08306.title: 13C-HMQC-NOESY
08306.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one carbon and two hydrogen dimensions.

08307.title: 13C-NOESY-HSQC
08307.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one carbon and two hydrogen dimensions.

08308.title: 15N-NOESY-HSQC
08308.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one nitrogen and two hydrogen dimensions.

08309.title: 15N-TOCSY-HSQC
08309.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one nitrogen and two hydrogen dimensions.

08310.title: 180° pulse
08310.definition: Pulsed radiofrequency signal in NMR that rotates the bulk magnetization vector (\(\boldsymbol{M}_{0}\)) of a nuclear spin to its opposing direction, effectively inverting the signal, (e.g., from the \(+z\) to \(-z\) axis).

11395.title: 1D property descriptor
11395.definition: An observed or calculated property of the whole molecule.

11396.title: 1D structure
11396.definition: The structure of a molecule encoded into a string such as SMILES or InChI.

11577.title: 2-amino-3-(3-hydroxy-5-methyl-1,2-oxazol-4-yl)propanoic acid receptor
11577.definition: Glutamate receptor in the central nervous system activated by the synthetic glutamate analog, AMPA.

09522.title: 2-photon lithography
09522.definition: Photolithography within a thick photoresist film, within which the photochemically-induced solubility change results from the simultaneous absorption of two photons.

15518.title: 2,3-bis(sulfanyl)propan-1-ol
15518.definition: Metal chelator that has been used in the treatment of arsenic, antimony, gold, mercury, and lead poisoning.

11397.title: 2D property
11397.definition: A molecular property that is calculated from the structure diagram of the molecule.

11399.title: 2D quantitative structure-activity relationships
11399.definition: A computational model of the quantitative relationship between the observed independent 1D property of a set of compounds and their dependent 1D properties or 2D properties.

11398.title: 2D structure
11398.definition: The structure of a molecule presented as a drawing or a file that contains a description of the topology, stereochemistry, and atomic symbol of its atoms and the bonds connecting them, but no explicit information about its three-dimensional structure.

09521.title: 3D lithography
09521.definition: Lithography performed in three dimensions, typically carried out using nanoimprint patterning or 2-photon lithography.

11400.title: 3D property
11400.definition: A property that is observed or calculated from a 3D representation of a molecule, which may depend on one or more conformations of the molecule.

11401.title: 3D searching
11401.definition: A virtual screening method that processes a chemical database to discover those compounds that match a query that either contains a 3D pharmacophore, a molecular shape or field, the 3D structure, or a combination of these.

11402.title: 3D structure
11402.definition: The structure of the conformation of a molecule presented as a drawing or a file that describes atomic symbols of its atoms and the bonds connecting them as well as their coordinates in three-dimensional space.

11403.title: 3D structure generation
11403.definition: A method to generate one or more 3D structures, conformations, of a molecule from its topological molecular graph.

11404.title: 4D quantitative structure-activity relationships
11404.definition:
A computational model of the quantitative relationship between the target observed independent 1D properties for a set of compounds and the 3D properties of
 several of their conformations.

11815.title: 5-hydroxytryptamine
11815.definition: Neurotransmitter found in the digestive tract, platelets and central nervous system.

11169.title: 5α-reductase
11169.definition: Enzyme (EC 1.3.99.5) that converts testosterone to 5\(\upalpha\)-dihydrotestosterone in peripheral tissues.

11170.title: 5α-reductase deficiency
11170.definition: Condition caused by a mutation of the $\ce{5\upalpha\!\mbox{-}reductase}$ type II gene, with autosomal recessive inheritance.

08311.title: 90° pulse
08311.definition: Pulsed radiofrequency signal that rotates the bulk magnetization vector (\(\boldsymbol{M}_{0}\)) of a nuclear spin to its orthogonal plane.

A00012.title: 'A' value
A00012.definition: The conformational preference of an equatorial compared to an axial substituent in a monosubstituted cyclohexane. This steric substituent parameter equals \(\Delta _{\rm{r}}G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) in \(\pu{kcal mol-1}\) for the equatorial to axial equilibration on cyclohexane. The values are also known as 'Winstein–Holness' A values.

12219.title: (z + 1)-average molar mass
12219.definition:
The equation for (z + 1)-average molar mass is \[M_{\rm{z+1}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{M} w_{M}M^{3}}{\sum\limits_M w_{M}M^{2}}\]
The equation for (z + 1)-average molecular weight is \[M_{\rm{r,z+1}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}}M^{3}}{\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}}M^{2}}\]

13924.title: artificial organ
13924.definition: Medical device that replaces, in part or in whole, the function of one of the organs of the body.

12328.title: a-ion
12328.definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{N}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{C-C}\) bond.

13951.title: aerobic biodegradation
13951.definition: Biodegradation in the presence of molecular oxygen.

13952.title: anaerobic biodegradation
13952.definition: Biodegradation in the absence of oxygen.

12329.title: alkyl cation
12329.definition: Even-electron positively charged saturated hydrocarbon ion containing no aromatic groups, a special case of carbenium ions.

12330.title: all-glass heated inlet system
12330.definition: All-glass inlet system for ion sources operating under vacuum that can be heated to about \(\pu{500^{\circ}C}\) and allows low vapor pressure materials to be introduced into the mass spectrometer without breaking vacuum.

12331.title: allyl cation
12331.definition: Even-electron ion formulated as \(\ce{R^{1}R^{2}C=CR^{3}C+R^{4}R^{5}}\) and its resonance forms.

12332.title: ambient ionization
12332.definition: Desorption of molecules and formation of ions outside the mass spectrometer directly from samples in their native environment with no or minimal sample preparation.

12333.title: ambient mass spectrometry
12333.definition: Mass spectrometry analysis performed using an ambient ionization technique.

12334.title: angle resolved mass spectrometry
12334.definition: Technique used to investigate details of the collisional excitation process by studying trends relating scattering angle of the precursor ion, internal energy transferred, and the masses of the ion and its collision partner.

12335.title: anionized molecule
12335.definition: Ion formed by the association of an anion with a molecule, \(\ce{M}\).

12325.title: accelerating potential
12325.definition: Electrical potential difference used to impart translational energy to ions.

14206.title: axial advancement per constitutional repeating unit
14206.definition: Projected length of a constitutional repeating unit (CRU) on the chain axis.

14217.title: anticlined stems
14217.definition: Stems in a crystal having opposite side-group orientations with respect to the chain axis (see (a) in figure).(a) Pairs of anticlined stems and (b) pairs of isoclined stems of regioregular poly(3-butylthiophene), i.e., poly(3-n-butylthiophene-2,5-diyl). Since regioregular poly(3-n-butylthiophene-2,5-diyl) is also a directional chain, (a) is an example of antidirectional packing of two chains, while (b) is an example of isodirectional packing.

14218.title: antidirectional packing
14218.definition: In a parallel-chain crystal, the crystalline packing of directional stems with opposite chain axis orientations.

12336.title: atmospheric pressure chemical ionization
12336.definition: Chemical ionization of a sample that is a gas or nebulized liquid, using an atmospheric pressure corona discharge or beta emitter such as \(\ce{^{63}Ni}\).

12337.title: atmospheric pressure matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization
12337.definition: Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization in which the sample target is at atmospheric pressure.

12338.title: atmospheric pressure photoionization
12338.definition: Direct ionization of molecules at atmospheric pressure by electron detachment induced by photons forming \(\ce{M^{+.}}\), or atmospheric pressure chemical ionization in which the reactant ions are generated by photoionization of suitable dopant species and subsequent ion/molecule reactions of their molecular ions.

12339.title: autodetachment
12339.definition: Process whereby a negative ion in a discrete state with energy greater than the detachment threshold loses an electron spontaneously without further interaction with an energy source.

12340.title: auxiliary gas
12340.definition: Gas used in a spray ion source in addition to the nebulizing gas to aid in solvent removal.

12341.title: average mass
12341.definition: Mass of an ion or molecule weighted for its isotopic composition.

12342.title: axial ejection
12342.definition: Ejection of an ion from an ion trap in a direction parallel to the longitudinal axis of the trap.

12343.title: axialization
12343.definition: Technique used in Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometers to limit the translational motion of the trapped ions so that they occupy a small volume near the trap center, thus optimizing performance criteria including resolving power.

14247.title: amorphous domain
14247.definition: Phase domain consisting of matter in the amorphous state.

13870.title: artificial
13870.definition: Qualifier for something that is made by human activity, rather than occurring naturally.

12326.title: accurate mass
12326.definition: Experimentally determined mass of an ion of known charge.

13871.title: artificial polymer
13871.definition: Man-made polymer that is not a biopolymer.

12327.title: accurate mass tag
12327.definition: Value of the mass of a peptide from a protein that has been chemically or enzymatically cleaved into fragments. The mass is recorded with sufficiently high accuracy and precision that it can be used in identification of the protein.

10317.title: A/D ratio
10317.definition: Ratio of the adult toxic dose to the developmentally toxic dose.

14330.title: ab initio emulsion polymerisation
14330.definition: Emulsion polymerization in which no seed particles are added.

AT06983.title: ab initio quantum mechanical methods
AT06983.definition: Methods of quantum mechanical calculations independent of any experiment other than the determination of fundamental constants. The methods are based on the use of the full Schrödinger equation to treat all the electrons of a chemical system. In practice, approximations are necessary to restrict the complexity of the electronic wavefunction and to make its calculation possible.

A00013.title: abatement
A00013.definition: Action taken to reduce air pollution which involves the use of control equipment or some new process. This refers to a reduction or lessening as opposed to elimination of a type of discharge or pollutant.

10318.title: abdominal cavity
10318.definition: Body cavity between the diaphragm and pelvis that contains the abdominal organs.

A00014.title: abeo-
A00014.definition: Bond migration, i.e. the formal transfer of one end of a skeletal bond to another position, with a compensating transfer of a hydrogen atom, can be indicated by a prefix of the form '\(x(y\rightarrow z)abeo-\)'. The prefix is compiled as follows: a numeral denoting the stationary (unchanged) end of the migrating bond (x) is followed by parentheses enclosing the locant denoting the original position (y) from which the other end of this bond has migrated, an arrow, and the locant (z) denoting the new position to which the bond has moved. The closing parenthesis is followed by the italicized prefix abeo- (Latin: I go away) to indicate bond migration. The original numbering is retained for the new compound and is used for the numbers x, y and z. It is always necessary to specify the resulting stereochemistry.

A00016.title: abiotic
A00016.definition: Not associated with living organisms. Synonymous with abiological.

15433.title: abiotic degradation
15433.definition: Process in which a substance is converted to simpler products by physical or chemical mechanisms.

A00017.title: abiotic transformation
A00017.definition: Process in which a substance in the environment is modified by non-biological mechanisms.

12827.title: ABL oncogene
12827.definition: Gene resulting from a chromosomal translocation (9;22) that fuses sequences from the BCR (breakpoint cluster region) gene with the ABL gene.

08443.title: ablation by sputtering
08443.definition: Bombardment of a sample surface with ions resulting in the removal of atoms from their lattice sites, and thus an ongoing discharge process that causes continuous ablation of the sample.

08444.title: ablation efficiency
08444.definition: Mass of sample removed in laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy divided by the energy delivered by the laser beam.

08445.title: ablation rate
08445.definition: Depth of sample layer removed in the glow discharge process per unit time.

08446.title: ablation threshold fluence
08446.definition: Minimum fluence required to achieve ablation of the sample.

12828.title: ABO blood group system
12828.definition: System of antigens expressed on erythrocytes and used for typing human blood for transfusion.

15434.title: abortifacient
15434.definition: Substance that causes pregnancy to end prematurely and causes an abortion.

10320.title: abortion
10320.definition: Premature termination of pregnancy with the death of the embryo or fetus.

A00018.title: absolute activation analysis
A00018.definition: A kind of activation analysis in which the elemental concentrations in the material are calculated from known nuclear constants, irradiation and measurement parameters, rather than by comparing with known standards.

A00019.title: absolute activity
A00019.definition: The exponential of the ratio of the chemical potential, \(\mu\), to \(R\,T\) where \(R\) is the gas constant and \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature, \(\lambda=\rm{e}^{\,\mu/RT}\).

15141.title: absolute bioavailability
15141.definition: Fraction of the administered dose of a drug from a dosage form absorbed intact into the systemic circulation.

A00020.title: absolute configuration
A00020.definition: The spatial arrangement of the atoms of a chiral molecular entity (or group) and its stereochemical description, e.g., R or S.

08711.title: absolute counting efficiency
08711.definition: Number of particles or photons counted by a radiation detector divided by the number emitted by a radiation source.

A00021.title: absolute counting
A00021.definition: A measurement under such well-defined conditions that the activity of a sample can be derived directly from the observed counting rate.

A00022.title: absolute electrode potential
A00022.definition: The electrode potential of a metal measured with respect to a universal reference system (not including any additional metal/solution interface).

09216.title: absolute elemental sensitivity factor
09216.definition: Coefficient for an element by which the measured intensity for that element is divided to yield the atomic concentration or atomic fraction of the element present in the sample.

A00023.title: absolute full energy peak efficiency
A00023.definition: Of a radiation spectrometer, the counting efficiency when considering only the events recorded in the full energy peak.

A00024.title: absolute lethal concentration
A00024.definition: Lowest concentration of a substance in an environmental medium which kills 100% of test organisms or species under defined conditions. This value is dependent on the number of organisms used in its assessment.

A00025.title: absolute lethal dose
A00025.definition: Lowest amount of a substance which kills 100% of test animals under defined conditions. This value is dependent on the number of organisms used in its assessment.

A00026.title: absolute photopeak efficiency
A00026.definition: Of a γ-ray spectrometer, the counting efficiency when only the events recorded in the photopeak are considered.

A00027.title: absolute preconcentration
A00027.definition: An operation (process) as the result of which microcomponents are transferred from the sample of larger mass into the sample of smaller mass, so that the concentration of the microcomponents is increased. Examples include the decrease in solvent volume during distillation or evaporation, and the transfer of microcomponents from an aqueous solution into a smaller volume of organic solvent by extraction.

12324.title: absolute quantitation of proteins
12324.definition: Method for absolute quantitation of proteins via measurements on constituent proteolytic peptides using chemically synthesized isotope-labeled peptides as surrogate internal standards for mass spectrometry.

14104.title: absorbance assay
14104.definition: Assay in which response is determined by the detection of light absorption by an assay component.

A00029.title: absorbance matching
A00029.definition: A procedure where the concentration of a known analyte may be determined by diluting the sample with solvent until the absorbance matches the absorbance of the analyte in the reference cell. This method is particularly useful if the Beer-Lambert law does not hold.

A00028.title: absorbance
A00028.definition: Logarithm of the ratio of incident to transmitted radiant power through a sample (excluding the effects on cell walls). Depending on the base of the logarithm a decadic and Napierian absorbance are used.

14413.title: absorbate
14413.definition: Substance that enters and is retained inside a solid or semisolid matrix (absorbent).

AT07312.title: absorbed photon flux density
AT07312.definition: Number of photons of a particular wavelength per time interval (spectral photon flux, number basis, \(q_{\rm{p},\lambda }\), or spectral photon flux, amount basis, \(q_{n,\rm{p},\lambda }\)) absorbed by a system per volume, \(V\). On number basis, SI unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{m}^{-4}\), and the  common unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{cm}^{-3}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\). On amount basis, SI unit is \(\pu{mol s-1 m-4}\), and a common unit is \(\pu{einstein s-1 cm-3 nm-1}\).

AT07313.title: absorbed radiant power density
AT07313.definition: Spectral radiant energy per time interval (spectral radiant power, \(P_{\lambda}\)) absorbed by a system per volume, \(V\). SI unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-4}\); common unit is \(\rm{W cm}^{-3}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\).

A00030.title: absorbed dose
A00030.definition: Amount of a substance absorbed into an organism or into organs and tissues of interest.

A00031.title: absorbed dose
A00031.definition: Energy imparted to matter by ionizing radiation in a suitable small element of volume divided by the mass of that element of volume.

A00032.title: absorbed electron coefficient
A00032.definition: Number of absorbed electrons per primary electron.

A00033.title: absorbed electrons
A00033.definition: The (excess) electrons present in a specimen under electron bombardment which are led to ground and measured as specimen current. The number of absorbed electrons per unit time (or the specimen current) equals the number of primary electrons minus the number of back scattered, secondary and transmitted electrons per unit time. Therefore the fraction of electrons being absorbed depends on many parameters, including the composition and thickness of the specimen, the primary electron energy, the electron incidence angle and local electrostatic fields when present.

13986.title: absorbed local spectral photon flux density
13986.definition: Local value of the spectral photon radiance, or spectral photon flux density, defined for a three-dimensional space, often in terms of napierian properties.

13987.title: absorbed local spectral radiance
13987.definition: Local value of the spectral radiance, or energy density absorption rate, defined for a three-dimensional space, often in terms of napierian properties.

13988.title: absorbed radiant density
13988.definition: Monochromatic radiant energy, per time interval (spectral radiance) coming from all directions and absorbed by a system integrated over the whole volume and averaged per volume \(V\), \(\langle L_{\lambda}^{\rm{a}}\left(t \right) \rangle_{V}\).

14414.title: absorbent
14414.definition: Solid or semisolid matrix that is able to accommodate and retain an absorbate.

A00034.title: absorber
A00034.definition: A device used commonly for sampling by absorption in which a gaseous or liquid material is removed from another gas or liquid by selective absorption; these include: scrubber, impinger, packed column, spray chamber, etc.

A00035.title: absorptance
A00035.definition: Ratio of the absorbed to the incident radiant power. When \(\alpha \leq 1\), \(\alpha \approx A_{\rm{e}}\), where \(A_{\rm{e}}\) is the Napierian absorbance.

A00036.title: absorption
A00036.definition: The process of one material (absorbate) being retained by another (absorbent); this may be the physical solution of a gas, liquid, or solid in a liquid, attachment of molecules of a gas, vapour, liquid, or dissolved substance to a solid surface by physical forces, etc. In spectrophotometry, absorption of light at characteristic wavelengths or bands of wavelengths is used to identify the chemical nature of molecules, atoms or ions and to measure the concentrations of these species.

A00037.title: absorption coefficient
A00037.definition: Linear decadic (\(a\),\(K\)) and Napierian absorption coefficients (\(\alpha \)) are equal to the corresponding absorbances divided by the optical path length through the sample. The molar absorption coefficients (decadic \(\varepsilon\), Napierian \(\kappa \)) are the linear absorption coefficients divided by the amount concentration.

AT06797.title: absorption coefficient
AT06797.definition: Ratio of the absorbed quantity (uptake) of a substance to the administered quantity (intake).

A00038.title: absorption cross-section
A00038.definition: Molar Napierian absorption coefficient divided by the Avogadro constant. When integrated against the logarithm of wavenumber (or frequency) it is called the integrated absorption cross-section.

08220.title: absorption index
08220.definition: Imaginary part of the complex refractive index describing absorption of electromagnetic radiation.

A00040.title: absorption intensity
A00040.definition: Differently defined physical quantities describing the absorption of radiation by a sample.

09435.title: absorption length
09435.definition: Distance over which the transmitted X-ray intensity falls by \(1/e\), where \(e\) is the base of the natural logarithm.

A00041.title: absorption line
A00041.definition: A narrow range of wavelengths in which a substance absorbs light; a series of discrete absorption lines can be used as an unambiguous identification for many relatively simple chemical species.

A00042.title: absorption pathlength
A00042.definition: The length of the radiation path through the absorbing medium; it is equal to the cell path length, \(l\), in the case of single-pass cells at normal incidence of radiation.

A00043.title: absorption spectrum
A00043.definition: The wavelength dependence of the absorption cross-section (or absorption coefficient); usually represented as a plot of absorption cross-section versus wavelength \(\lambda\) (or \(\frac{1}{\lambda}\)) of the light.

A00044.title: absorptivity
A00044.definition: Absorptance divided by the optical path length. For very low attenuance it approximates the absorption coefficient [within the approximation \((1 - e^{-A}) \sim A\)]. The use of this term is not recommended.

A00045.title: abstraction
A00045.definition: A chemical reaction or transformation, the main feature of which is the bimolecular removal of an atom (neutral or charged) from a molecular entity. For example:  (proton abstraction from acetone)  (hydrogen abstraction from methane)

A00046.title: abstraction process
A00046.definition: In abstraction and extraction processes, an adsorptive or adsorbate species extracts an adsorbed atom or a lattice atom respectively. Abstraction process: Extraction process:

14415.title: abundance
14415.definition:
Total number of individual organisms in a population, seen over a defined period of time in a certain place.Note: For fish, an estimate of total weight may replace number.
Total number of organisms per unit of habitat space seen over a defined period.
Amount of an element that exists in nature, usually expressed in relative terms as a percentage of the total amount of all elements in a given medium (e.g., the Earth’s crust).
Amount of an isotope of an element that exists in nature, usually expressed in relative terms as a percentage of the total amount of all isotopes of the element.

A00048.title: abundance sensitivity
A00048.definition: The ratio of the maximum ion current recorded at a mass \(m\) to the ion current arising from the same species recorded at an adjacent mass (\(m\pm 1\)).

14416.title: abundant element
14416.definition: Element which is of common occurrence in the Earth’s crust.

15435.title: abuse
15435.definition: Improper use of drugs or other substances.

12829.title: abzyme
12829.definition: Antibody or antibody construct with catalytic activity.

09130.title: AC voltammetry
09130.definition: Voltammetry in which a sinusoidal alternating potential of small amplitude (\(\pu{10 to 50 mV}\)) of constant frequency (\(\pu{10 Hz to 100 kHz}\)) is superimposed on a slowly and linearly varying potential ramp. The resulting alternating current is plotted versus imposed DC potential. The obtained AC voltammogram is peak-shaped.Waveform for AC voltammetry. The applied potential as a function of time is a sinusoidal alternating potential superimposed on a linearly increasing ramp.

15436.title: acaricide
15436.definition: Substance intended to kill mites, ticks, or other Acaridae.

A00050.title: accelerating voltage scan
A00050.definition: This is an alternative method of producing a momentum (mass) spectrum in magnetic deflection instruments by varying the accelerating voltage. This scan can also be used, in conjunction with a fixed radial electric field, to produce an ion kinetic energy spectrum.

A00053.title: acceleration of free fall
A00053.definition: Acceleration of free fall in vacuum due to gravity. Also called acceleration due to gravity.

A00051.title: acceleration
A00051.definition: Vector quantity equal to the derivative of velocity with respect to time. For the acceleration of free fall the symbol \(g\) is used.

08712.title: accelerator mass spectrometry
08712.definition: Mass spectrometry technique in which atoms and molecules from a sample are ionized, accelerated to mega-electron volt (\(\pu{1 MeV} = \pu{1.602176634E-13 J}\)) energies, and separated according to their momentum, charge, and energy, allowing high discrimination for the measurement of nuclide abundances.

AT06799.title: acceptable daily intake
AT06799.definition: Estimate by JECFA of the amount of a food additive, expressed on a body-weight basis, that can be ingested daily over a lifetime without appreciable health risk.

15437.title: acceptable residue level
15437.definition: Acceptable concentration of a residue that has been established for an antibiotic found in human or animal foods.

15438.title: acceptable risk
15438.definition: Probability of suffering disease or injury that is considered to be sufficiently small to be 'negligible'.

08052.title: acceptance interval
08052.definition: Interval of permissible measured quantity values.

08053.title: acceptance limit
08053.definition: Specified upper or lower bound of permissible measured quantity values.

15439.title: accepted risk
15439.definition: Probability of suffering disease or injury that is accepted by an individual.

A00056.title: acceptor number
A00056.definition: A quantitative measure of Lewis acidity.

10164.title: acceptor phase
10164.definition: Component of a multi-phase system into which the target analytes are extracted.

14417.title: accessible
14417.definition: Capable of being entered or reached; easy of access; such as one can go to, come into the presence of, reach, or lay hold of; get-at-able.

12830.title: accessory cell
12830.definition: Cell that assists in the adaptive immune response but does not directly mediate specific antigen recognition.

12831.title: accessory molecule
12831.definition: Molecule other than immunoglobulin (Ig), T-cell receptor (TCR), or major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecule that participates in T lymphocyte recognition and response to antigen.

10323.title: accessory rib
10323.definition: Rib arising from a cervical vertebra (cervical rib), or supernumerary rib arising from a thoracic or lumbar vertebra.

10324.title: accessory sex gland
10324.definition: Any gland, other than a gonad, associated with the genital tract, such as the bulbourethral gland and prostate.

10325.title: accessory sex organ
10325.definition: Organ or structure other than the gonads that matures at puberty and assists indirectly in sexual reproduction by nurturing and transporting gametes.

11306.title: accessory thyroid tissue
11306.definition: Ectopic thyroid tissue arising from remnants of the thyroglossal duct.

08221.title: accidental degeneracy
08221.definition: Condition that occurs when two or more normal transitions have the same energy as a matter of coincidence, as opposed to because of symmetry conditions.

15440.title: accidental exposure
15440.definition: Unintended contact with a substance or change in the physical environment (including, e.g., radiation) resulting from an accident.

11556.title: acclimation
11556.definition: Adjustment, physiologically and (or) behaviorally, of an organism to its environment or circumstances, e.g., thermoregulation, psychological adjustment.

14418.title: acclimatisation
14418.definition:
Processes, including selection and adaptation, by which a population of microorganisms develops the ability to degrade a substance, or develops a tolerance to it.
In experimental systems, allowing an organism to adjust to its environment prior to undertaking a study.
Modification of biological processes or structures in the maintenance of homeostasis in response to change in some environmental quality such as temperature, salinity, light, radiation, or toxicant concentration. Note: It is an expression of phenotypic plasticity of individuals in response to a sublethal change in some environmental factor.

A00057.title: accommodation coefficient
A00057.definition: A measure of the efficiency of capture of molecules or atoms which collide with aerosol particles, cloud droplets, etc. The accommodation coefficient is the fraction of the collisions which result in the capture of the molecules (atoms, radicals, etc.) by the particle, cloud droplet, etc.; fraction of colliding molecules which are not reflected but which enter the surface of an aqueous aerosol. Synonymous with sticking coefficient.

08054.title: accreditation of a laboratory
08054.definition: Third-party attestation related to a laboratory conveying formal demonstration of its competence to carry out specific conformity assessment tasks.

A00058.title: accretion
A00058.definition: The process by which aerosols grow in size by external addition of various chemical species; a form of agglomeration.

09150.title: accumulation in stripping voltammetry
09150.definition: Transfer of an analyte from a test solution to an electrode surface as the first step in stripping voltammetry.

13989.title: accumulation layer
13989.definition: Subsurface space where the majority carriers accumulate near the surface of a semiconductor because of band bending caused by the surface potential.

A00059.title: accuracy
A00059.definition: Ability of a measuring instrument to give responses close to a true value.

A00060.title: accuracy
A00060.definition: Closeness of the agreement between the result of a measurement and a true value of the measurand.

A00061.title: acenes
A00061.definition: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons consisting of fused benzene rings in a rectilinear arrangement.

A00062.title: acetals
A00062.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R2C(OR')2}$ ($\ce{R'} \neq \ce{H}$) and thus diethers of geminal diols. Originally, the term was confined to derivatives of aldehydes (one $\ce{R = H}$), but it now applies equally to derivatives of ketones (neither $\ce{R = H}$). Mixed acetals have different $\ce{R'}$ groups.

A00064.title: acetonides
A00064.definition: Cyclic acetals derived from acetone and diols, usually vicinal diols, or polyhydroxy compounds. E.g.

11557.title: acetylcholine
11557.definition: Substance that functions as a neurotransmitter between nerve cells and between nerves and muscles.

11559.title: acetylcholine receptor
11559.definition: Integral membrane protein that allows the cell to respond to the binding of acetylcholine.

A00065.title: acetylene black
A00065.definition: A special type of carbon black formed by an exothermic decomposition of acetylene. It is characterized by the highest degree of aggregation and crystalline orientation when compared with all types of carbon black.

A00066.title: acetylenes
A00066.definition: Acyclic (branched or unbranched) and cyclic (with or without side chain) hydrocarbons having one or more carbon–carbon triple bonds.

A00067.title: acetylides
A00067.definition: Compounds arising by replacement of one or both hydrogen atoms of acetylene (ethyne) by a metal or other cationic group. E.g., $\ce{NaC#CH}$ monosodium acetylide. By extension, analogous compounds derived from terminal acetylenes, $\ce{RC#CH}$.

A00068.title: Acheson graphite
A00068.definition: A synthetic graphite made by the Acheson process.

10327.title: achondroplasia
10327.definition: Inherited disorder where ossification of cartilage is retarded, especially affecting growth of long bones, resulting in very short limbs and a comparatively large head. Type of dwarfism.

A00085.title: aci-nitro compounds
A00085.definition: A class name for hydrocarbylideneazinic acids, $\ce{R2C=N^{+}(–O^{−})OH}$. The use of aci-nitro as a prefix in systematic nomenclature to name specific compounds is abandoned.

A00071.title: acid
A00071.definition: A molecular entity or chemical species capable of donating a hydron (proton) (see Brønsted acid) or capable of forming a covalent bond with an electron pair (see Lewis acid).

A00072.title: acid anhydrides
A00072.definition: Compounds consisting of two acyl groups bonded to the same oxygen atom acyl-O-acyl. Symmetric and mixed anhydrides have identical and different acyl groups, respectively. Examples,acetic anhydride  acetic benzenesulfonic anhydride  (thiobenzoic) anhydride

A00077.title: acid deposition
A00077.definition: The acids deposited by transfer from the atmosphere either by precipitation (rain, fog, snow, etc.), called wet deposition, or by direct transfer to the surface of the earth induced by the flow of acid-containing air masses over the earth's surface, called dry deposition.

10232.title: acid digestion
10232.definition: Process in which the sample (analyte and matrix) is dissolved by an acid.

15441.title: acid dissociation constant
15441.definition: Equilibrium constant for the following reaction of an acid \(\ce{HB}\): \[\begin{gathered} \ce{HB(aq)  H^{+}(aq) + B^{-}(aq)} \\ K_{\rm{a}} = [\ce{H^{+}}][\ce{B^{-}}]/[\ce{HB}]c^{\rm{o}} \end{gathered}\] where \(c^{\rm{o}} = \pu{1 mol L-1}\) is the standard amount concentration and activity coefficients have been neglected.

14419.title: acid precipitation
14419.definition: Rain, fog, snow, sleet, or other particulate matter from the atmosphere with a _000078_ below \(\pu{5.6}\) deposited from the air.

A00083.title: acid rain
A00083.definition: Rain with \(\rm{pH}\) values < about 5; commonly results from acids formed from pollutants. 'Pure' rain water equilibrated with atmospheric $\ce{CO2}$ and naturally occurring acids in relatively clean air usually has a \(\rm{pH} > 5\).

08447.title: acid transient effects
08447.definition: Increase in signal equilibration time or in wash out time caused by a modification in inorganic acid concentration.

AT06794.title: acid-labile sulfur
AT06794.definition: Refers to sulfido ligands, e.g., the bridging ligands in iron-sulfur proteins, which are released as $\ce{H2S}$ at acid pH.

14420.title: acid-volatile sulfide
14420.definition: Soil- and sediment-associated solid-phase sulfides extractable with cold hydrochloric acid.

A00075.title: acid–base indicator
A00075.definition: An acid or base which exhibits a colour change on neutralization by the basic or acidic titrant at or near the equivalence point of a titration.

A00079.title: acidity
A00079.definition: Of a compound: For Brønsted acids the tendency of a compound to act as a hydron donor. It can be quantitatively expressed by the acid dissociation constant of the compound in water or some other specified medium. For Lewis acids it relates to the association constants of Lewis adducts and π adducts.Of a medium: The use of the term is mainly restricted to a medium containing Brønsted acids, where it means the tendency of the medium to hydronate a specific reference base. It is quantitatively expressed by the appropriate acidity function.

A00080.title: acidity constant
A00080.definition: The equilibrium constant \(K_{\rm{a}n}\) for splitting off the nth proton from a charged or uncharged acid, to be defined. One may write \(K_{\rm{a}}\) for \(K_{\rm{a}1}\).

A00081.title: acidity function
A00081.definition: Any function that measures the thermodynamic hydron-donating or -accepting ability of a solvent system, or a closely related thermodynamic property, such as the tendency of the lyate ion of the solvent system to form Lewis adduct. (The term 'basicity function' is not in common use in connection with basic solutions.) Acidity functions are not unique properties of the solvent system alone, but depend on the solute (or family of closely related solutes) with respect to which the thermodynamic tendency is measured. Commonly used acidity functions refer to concentrated acidic or basic solutions. Acidity functions are usually established over a range of composition of such a system by UV/VIS spectrophotometric or NMR measurements of the degree of hydronation (protonation or Lewis adduct formation) for the members of a series of structurally similar indicator bases (or acids) of different strength: the best known of these functions is the Hammett acidity function \(H_{0}\) (for uncharged indicator bases that are primary aromatic amines).

A00082.title: acidosis
A00082.definition: Pathological condition in which the hydrogen ion substance concentration of body fluids is above normal and hence the pH of blood falls below the reference interval.

10328.title: acinus
10328.definition:
Small sac-like cavity in a gland, surrounded by secretory cells.
Terminal region of the airways of the lung where gas exchange occurs.

10329.title: acoustic meatus
10329.definition: Either of two passages in the ear, one leading to the tympanic membrane (external acoustic meatus), and one for passage of nerves and blood vessels (internal acoustic meatus).

11560.title: acoustic neuroma
11560.definition: Non-malignant intracranial tumor of the eighth cranial nerve.

12089.title: acoustic startle response test
12089.definition: Neurophysiological examination in which an animal is exposed to a brief (e.g., \(\pu{40 ms}\)) acoustic stimulus, followed by measurement of the animal’s motor reaction.

12832.title: acquired immunity
12832.definition: State of protection against pathogen-induced injury, with rapid immune elimination of pathogenic invaders owing to previous immunization or vaccination.

12833.title: acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
12833.definition: Disease caused by infection with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), assuming clinical relevance when an infected patient has lost most of his/her CD4+ T cells, so that infections with opportunistic pathogens occur.

08312.title: acquisition time
08312.definition: Duration of the digitization of a free induction decay.

10330.title: acrania
10330.definition: Rare congenital disorder that occurs in the human fetus, in which the flat bones in the cranium are either completely or partially absent.

10503.title: acrocentric centromere
10503.definition: Having the centromere very close to one end.

10331.title: acrocephaly
10331.definition: Type of cephalic disorder where the top of the skull is pointed or conical due to premature closure of the coronal suture plus any other suture.

10332.title: acromegaly
10332.definition: Abnormal enlargement of the hands, feet, and face in adults, caused by overproduction of growth hormone by the pituitary gland.

11561.title: acroparesthesia
11561.definition: Abnormal feeling of numbness, tingling, or burning of the skin, typically in the extremities.

10333.title: acrosome
10333.definition: Organelle that develops over the anterior half of the head in the spermatozoon.

10334.title: acrosome reaction
10334.definition: Process that occurs in the acrosome of the sperm as it contacts the egg, leading to structural changes that facilitate fusion.

15244.title: acrylic polymer
15244.definition: Polymer prepared from acrylic acid or a derivative of acrylic acid.

A00086.title: actinic flux
A00086.definition: The quantity of light available to molecules at a particular point in the atmosphere and which, on absorption, drives photochemical processes in the atmosphere. It is calculated by integrating the spectral radiance \(L \left(\lambda,\,\theta,\,\varphi\,\right)\) over all directions of incidence of the light, \(S_{\lambda} = \int _{\theta}\, \int _{\phi} \{L\left (\lambda,\theta,\varphi \right)/(hc/\lambda)\}\, \rm{sin}\,\theta\: \rm{d}\theta\: \rm{d}\varphi\). If the radiance is expressed in \(\pu{J m-2 s-1 st-1 nm-1}\) and \(hc/\lambda\) is the energy per quantum of light of wavelength \(\lambda\), the actinic flux has units of \(\rm{quanta cm}^{-2}\ \rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\). This important quantity is one of the terms required in the calculation of j-values, the first order rate coefficients for photochemical processes in the sunlight-absorbing, trace gases in the atmosphere. The actinic flux is determined by the solar radiation entering the atmosphere and by any changes in this due to atmospheric gases and particles (e.g. Rayleigh scattering absorption by stratospheric ozone, scattering and absorption by aerosols and clouds), and reflections from the ground. It is therefore dependent on the wavelength of the light, on the altitude and on specific local environmental conditions. The actinic flux has borne many names (e.g. flux, flux density, beam irradiance, actinic irradiance, integrated intensity) which has caused some confusion. It is important to distinguish the actinic flux from the spectral irradiance, which refers to energy arrival on a flat surface having fixed spatial orientation (\(\pu{J m-2 nm-1}\)) given by: \[E_{\lambda} = \int _{\theta}\, \int _{\phi} L\left (\lambda,\theta,\varphi \right )\, \rm{cos}\,\theta  \: \rm{sin}\,\theta\: \rm{d}\theta\: \rm{d}\varphi\] The actinic flux does not refer to any specific orientation because molecules are oriented randomly in the atmosphere. This distinction is of practical relevance: the actinic flux (and therefore a j-value) near a brightly reflecting surface (e.g. over snow or above a thick cloud) can be a factor of three higher than that near a non-reflecting surface. The more descriptive name of spectral spheradiance is suggested for the quantity herein called actinic flux.

AT07315.title: actinism
AT07315.definition: Chemical changes on living and non-living materials caused by optical radiation.

A00087.title: actinometer
A00087.definition: A chemical system or physical device which determines the number of photons in a beam integrally or per unit time. This name is commonly applied to devices used in the ultraviolet and visible wavelength ranges. For example, solutions of iron(III) oxalate can be used as a chemical actinometer, while bolometers, thermopiles, and photodiodes are physical devices giving a reading that can be correlated to the number of photons detected.

15442.title: action level
15442.definition:
Concentration of a substance in air, soil, water, or other defined medium at which specified emergency counter-measures, such as the seizure and destruction of contaminated materials, evacuation of the local population or closing down the sources of pollution, are to be taken.
Concentration of a pollutant in air, soil, water, or other defined medium at which some kind of preventive action (not necessarily of an emergency nature) is to be taken.

11562.title: action potential
11562.definition: Brief, spike-like depolarization associated with the passage of an impulse without decrement along the membrane of a muscle cell or nerve cell.

A00088.title: action spectrum
A00088.definition: A plot of a relative biological or chemical photoresponse (= \(\Delta y\)) per number of incident photons against wavelength or energy of radiation under the same radiant power of light. This form of presentation is frequently used in the studies of biological or solid state systems, where the nature of the absorbing species is unknown. This type of action spectrum is sometimes called spectral responsivity or sensitivity spectrum. The precise action spectrum is a plot of the spectral or quantum effectiveness. By contrast, a plot of the biological or chemical change or response per absorbed photon (quantum efficiency) versus wavelength is the efficiency spectrum.

A00089.title: activated adsorption process
A00089.definition: If the temperature coefficient of the rate of adsorption is substantial, an adsorption process is said to be activated (i.e. to have a significant activation energy). In this case, the sticking coefficient is small. In general, the activation energy of activated adsorption is a function of coverage and it usually increases with increasing coverage.

A00090.title: activated carbon
A00090.definition: A porous carbon material, a char which has been subjected to reaction with gases, sometimes with the addition of chemicals, e.g. $\ce{ZnCl2}$, before, during or after carbonization in order to increase its adsorptive properties.

A00091.title: activated charcoal
A00091.definition: A traditional term for activated carbon.

A00092.title: activated complex
A00092.definition: An activated complex, often characterized by the superscript ‡, is defined as that assembly of atoms which corresponds to an arbitrary infinitesimally small region at or near the col (saddle point) of a potential energy surface.

08936.title: activated monomer
08936.definition: Reactive species generated reversibly from a monomer.

09807.title: activated nucleotide sugar
09807.definition: Activated form of monosaccharide linked to a nucleotide to be available in a high-energy state for glycosyl transfer.

08141.title: activated state
08141.definition: In theories of unimolecular reactions an energized chemical species, often characterized by the superscript \(^{\ddagger}\), where the excitation is specific and the molecule is poised for reaction.

08907.title: activated-monomer polymerization
08907.definition: Chain polymerization in which propagation involves reaction between a growing-chain end and an activated monomer.

A00093.title: activation
A00093.definition: This word is used in different senses:   Input of external energy into a chemical system is said to bring about activation of the system.   An added substance that increases the rate of a catalysed reaction is known as an activator, and the effect is called activation. The degree of activation \(\varepsilon_{\rm{a}}\) is defined by: \[\varepsilon_{\rm{a}}=\frac{v\,-\,v_{0}}{v_{0}} = \frac{v}{v_{0}} - 1\] where \(v_{0}\) is the rate of the catalysed reaction in the absence of the activator and \(v\) is the rate of the catalysed reaction in the presence of the activator.  When some of the energy required for a reaction to occur is provided by a previous exothermic chemical reaction there is said to be chemical activation.

A00096.title: activation analysis
A00096.definition: A kind of elemental or isotopic analysis based on the measurement of characteristic radiation from nuclides formed directly or indirectly by activation of the test portion. In general, a specification is added of the type of the incident radiation (e.g. neutron, photon) and its energy (e.g. thermal, fast).

A00101.title: activation cross-section
A00101.definition: The cross-section for the formation of a radionuclide by a specified reaction.

A00102.title: activation energy
A00102.definition: An empirical parameter characterizing the exponential temperature dependence of the rate coefficient, \(k\), \(E_{a} = R\, T^{2}\frac{\rm{d(ln}k\rm{)}}{\rm{d}T}\), where \(R\) is the gas constant and \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature. The term is also used for threshold energies in electronic potential surfaces, in which case the term requires careful definition.

A00094.title: activation
A00094.definition: The process of transition from the passive to the active state by removal of the passivating film. A necessary condition for activation is an electrode potential negative to the equilibrium potential of formation of the passivating film. Activation is achieved by cathodic currents, by a reduced substance in the adjacent solution, or by contact with an electronic conductor having a suitably negative corrosion potential.

A00095.title: activation
A00095.definition: The process of inducing radioactivity by irradiation. In general, a specification is added of the type of incident radiation (e.g. nuclear, neutron, photon) or its energy (e.g. thermal, fast).

A00103.title: activation reaction
A00103.definition: Process leading from the reactants to the formation of an activated complex or transition state.

12834.title: activation-induced cell death
12834.definition: Process by which immune responses end in the death of most of the responding lymphocytes, leaving only a small number of resting memory cells.

A00104.title: activator
A00104.definition: A substance, other than the catalyst or one of the substrates, that increases the rate of a catalysed reaction without itself being consumed; the process is called activation. An activator of an enzyme-catalysed reaction may be called enzyme activator, if it acts by binding to the enzyme.

14105.title: active
14105.definition: Sample that produces a response or signal above a defined threshold at a tested concentration in a single assay or screen.

11563.title: active avoidance test
11563.definition: Fear-motivated associative avoidance test based on presentation of an adverse stimulus (e.g., an electric current) as a source of discomfort, to create an environment from which the animal or subject would prefer to escape.

12835.title: active immunization
12835.definition: Immunization with antigen, as distinct from the transfer of antibody to an unimmunized individual, which is called passive immunization.

15443.title: active ingredient
15443.definition: Component of a mixture responsible for the biological effects of the mixture.

15444.title: active metabolite
15444.definition: Metabolite causing biological and (or) toxicological effects.

A00107.title: active metal
A00107.definition: A metal corroding in the active state.

10165.title: active sampling
10165.definition: Continuous extraction with movement of the sample matrix with respect to the extraction phase.

A00108.title: active site
A00108.definition: The term is often applied to those sites for adsorption which are the effective sites for a particular heterogeneous catalytic reaction. The terms active site and active centre are often used as synonyms, but active centre may also be used to describe an ensemble of sites at which a catalytic reaction takes place.

A00109.title: active solid
A00109.definition: A porous solid with adsorptive properties by means of which chromatographic separations may be achieved. The separations resulting from this action follow laws different from those deriving from the partitioning action of the liquid phase.

A00111.title: active state
A00111.definition: Corrosion in the active state occurs by direct transfer (which may involve one or several steps) of metal ions from the metallic phase to the adjacent electrolyte. The corrosion current of an active metal usually increases when the electrode potential is made more positive, other conditions remaining constant.

13990.title: active state
13990.definition: Electronically excited surface centre, or a surface centre (surface site) with a trapped photogenerated charge carrier that interacts with species at the solid/liquid, liquid/liquid, solid/gas, or liquid/gas interfaces with formation of, e.g., chemisorbed species.

13991.title: active state
13991.definition: Electronically excited surface centre, or a surface centre (surface site) with a trapped photogenerated charge carrier or reactive intermediate that interacts with molecular entities at an interface with the formation of reaction products or intermediates.

12836.title: active systemic anaphylaxis test
12836.definition: Test for determining whether a drug can cause anaphylactic reactions in an animal following immunization with the drug.

A00112.title: active transport
A00112.definition: The carriage of a solute across a biological membrane from low to high concentration which requires the expenditure of (metabolic) energy.

15142.title: active transport of drugs
15142.definition: Carriage of a solute across a biological membrane, which requires a suitable carrier and the expenditure of energy.

10335.title: activin
10335.definition: Growth factor of the transforming growth factor \(\upbeta\) (TGF-\(\upbeta\)) superfamily, originally identified as a gonadal factor that stimulated secretion of follicle-stimulating hormone, also involved in many aspects of development including mesodermal induction (see mesenchyme), hematopoiesis, and neuronal differentiation.

A00115.title: activity
A00115.definition: Defined by the equation \[a = e^{\frac{\mu - \mu^{o}}{R\,T}}\] where \(R\) is the gas constant, \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature, \(\mu\) the chemical potential and \(\mu^{o}\) the standard chemical potential the definition of which depends on the choice of the standard state.

15312.title: activity coefficient at infinite dilution
15312.definition: For a substance \(\ce{B}\), activity coefficient \(f_{\ce{B}}\) extrapolated to infinite dilution: \[\ln (f_{\ce{B}}^{\infty}) = \lim \limits_{x_{\ce{B}} \to 0} (\frac{\mu_{\ce{B}} - \mu_{\ce{B}}^{\ast}}{RT} - \ln x_{\ce{B}})\]

A00116.title: activity coefficient
A00116.definition: The activity coefficient \(f_{\rm{B}}\) of a substance B in a liquid or solid mixture containing mole fractions \(x_{\rm{B}}\), \(x_{\rm{C}}\), ... of the substances B, C, ... is a dimensionless quantity defined in terms of the chemical potential \(\mu _{\rm{B}}\) of B in the mixture by: \[R T \ln (x_{\ce{B}} f_{\ce{B}}) = \mu_{\ce{B}}({\ce{cd}},T,P,x) - \mu_{\ce{B}}^{\ast}({\ce{cd}},T,p)\] where \(x\) denotes the set of mole fractions \(x_{\rm{B}}\), \(x_{\rm{C}}\), ... . The activity coefficient \(\gamma _{\rm{B}}\) of a solute B in a solution (especially a dilute liquid solution) containing molalities \(m_{\rm{B}}\), \(m_{\rm{C}}\), ... of solutes B, C, ... in a solvent A is a dimensionless quantity defined in terms of the chemical potential \(\mu _{\rm{B}}\) by: \[R\ T\ \ln \left(\frac{m_{\rm{B}}\ \gamma _{\rm{B}}}{m^{\ominus}}\right)=\mu _{\rm{B}}- \left\{\mu _{\rm{B}}- R\ T\ \ln \left(\frac{m_{\rm{B}}}{m^{\ominus }}\right)\right\}^{\infty }\]

14106.title: activity distribution
14106.definition: Graphical representation of the number of samples present in each activity range.

08713.title: activity growth curve
08713.definition: Graph of the activity of a radioactive nuclide as a function of time and showing the increase of activity through the decay of the precursor or as a result of activation.

A00114.title: activity
A00114.definition: The number of nuclear decays occurring in a given quantity of material in a small time interval, divided by that time interval. Often, this term is referred to as absolute activity. Symbol \(A=- \frac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Synonymous with disintegration rate or decay rate.

08773.title: actuator
08773.definition: Transducer that converts the energy supplied or taken from the surroundings into some mechanical motion.

14421.title: acute
14421.definition:
Of short duration, in relation to exposure or effect; the effect usually shows a rapid onset.
Note 1: In regulatory toxicology, 'acute' refers to studies where dosing is either single or limited to one day although the total study duration may extend to two weeks to permit appearance of toxicity in susceptible organ systems.
Note 2: In aquatic ecotoxicology, exposure of the test organisms is typically continuous and of four days or less.
In clinical medicine, sudden and severe, having a rapid onset.

16229.title: acute effect
16229.definition: Effect of finite duration occurring rapidly (usually in the first \(\pu{24 h}\) or up to \(\pu{14 d}\)) following a single dose or short exposure to a substance or radiation.

12837.title: acute lymphoblastic leukemia
12837.definition: Highly aggressive, undifferentiated form of lymphoid malignancy derived from a progenitor cell that is thought to be able to give rise to both T- and B-cell lineages.

12838.title: acute myelogenous leukemia
12838.definition: Cancer characterized by rapid growth of abnormal granulocytes that accumulate in the bone marrow.

12841.title: acute rejection
12841.definition: Rejection of a tissue or organ graft from a genetically unrelated donor, typically occurring within 10 to 13 days of transplantation.

12842.title: acute respiratory distress syndrome
12842.definition: Acute lung failure characterized by alveolar and interstitial edema, perivascular pulmonary edema, and hyaline membrane formation, resulting from a variety of underlying diseases that result in increased pulmonary vascular permeability.

AT06800.title: acute toxicity
AT06800.definition: Adverse effects of finite duration occurring within a short time (up to $\pu{14 d}$) after administration of a single dose (or exposure to a given concentration) of a test substance or after multiple doses (exposures), usually within $\pu{24 h}$ of a starting point (which may be exposure to the toxicant, or loss of reserve capacity, or developmental change, etc.)Ability of a substance to cause adverse effects within a short time of dosing or exposure.

15445.title: acute toxicity test
15445.definition: Study in which organisms are observed during only a short part of the life span and in which there is often only a single exposure to the test agent at the beginning of the study.

12839.title: acute-phase protein
12839.definition: Serum protein, mostly produced in the liver, which rapidly changes in concentration (some acute-phase proteins increase, some decrease) during the initiation of an inflammatory response.

12840.title: acute-phase response
12840.definition: Physiological response stimulated by cytokines including interleukin-1, interleukin-6, interferons, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF), characterized by increased vascular permeability, fever, and increased levels of proteins (thus called acute-phase proteins) such as C-reactive protein (CRP), occurring within a few hours of initiation.

14422.title: acute-to-chronic toxicity ratio
14422.definition: Numerical dimensionless quantity that is the ratio of an acute toxicity test result (e.g., \(\pu{LC_{50}}\)) to a chronic toxicity test result (e.g., maximum acceptable toxicant concentration, MATC) where both are expressed in the same units (e.g., \(\pu{mg L-1}\)). Ideally, the data are for the same chemical species.

15378.title: acyclic diene metathesis polymerisation
15378.definition: Metathesis polymerization of an acylic diene monomer.

A00121.title: acyl carbenes
A00121.definition: Any compound . In organic chemistry, an unspecified acyl carbene is commonly a carboxylic acyl carbene, .

A00123.title: acyl groups
A00123.definition: Groups formed by removing one or more hydroxy groups from oxoacids that have the general structure $\ce{R_{k}E(=O)_{l}(OH)_{m}}$ ($l \neq 0$), and replacement analogues of such acyl groups. In organic chemistry an unspecified acyl group is commonly a carboxylic acyl group. E.g.

A00124.title: acyl halides
A00124.definition: Compounds consisting of an acyl group bonded to halogen, e.g. $\ce{CH3S(=O)2Cl}$, methanesulfonyl chloride; $\ce{CH3COCl}$, acetyl chloride; cyclohexanecarboximidoyl chloride,

AT07317.title: acyl shift
AT07317.definition: Photochemical process with skeletal isomerization by shift of an acyl group from position 1 to position 2 or 3.

A00129.title: acyl species
A00129.definition: Acyl intermediates include acyl anions, acyl radicals and acyl cations (synonym acylium ions) which are formally derived from oxoacids $\ce{R_{k}E(=O)_{l}(OH)_{m}}$ ($l \neq 0$) by removal of a hydroxyl cation $\ce{HO^{+}}$, a hydroxyl radical $\ce{HO^{.}}$ or a hydroxyl anion $\ce{HO^{-}}$, respectively, and replacement analogues of such intermediates. Acyl anions, radicals and cations can formally be represented by canonical forms having a negative charge, an unpaired electron or a positive charge on the acid-generating element of the oxoacid.Acyl anions, e.g. Acyl radicals, e.g. Acyl cations, e.g.

A00119.title: acylals
A00119.definition: Diesters of geminal diols; i.e.  E.g. benzylidene diacetate:

A00126.title: acyloins
A00126.definition: $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}Hydroxy}$ ketones, $\ce{RCH(OH)C(=O)R}$. So named from the fact that they are formally derived from reductive coupling of carboxylic acyl groups.

A00127.title: acyloxyl radicals
A00127.definition: Oxygen-centered radicals consisting of an acyl radical bonded to an oxygen atom. E.g. .

14319.title: ad-micelle
14319.definition: Surfactant bilayer formed on a charged adsorbing surface.

10337.title: adactyly
10337.definition: Congenital absence of fingers or toes.

15446.title: adaptation
15446.definition:
Change in an organism, in response to changing conditions of the environment (specifically chemical), which takes place without any irreversible disruptions of the given biological system and without exceeding normal (homeostatic) capacities of its response.
Process by which an organism stabilizes its physiological condition after an environmental change.Note: If this process exceeds the homeostatic range, it becomes pathological and results in symptoms of disease (adverse effects).

12843.title: adaptive immune response
12843.definition: Immune response based on the principle of clonal recognition, such that upon first exposure to an antigen, primed lymphocytes either differentiate into immune effector cells or form an expanded pool of memory cells that respond to secondary exposure to the same antigen by mounting an amplified and more rapid response.

12844.title: adaptive immune system
12844.definition: Part of the immune system responsible for the adaptive immune response.

15447.title: added risk
15447.definition: Difference between the incidence of an adverse effect in a treated group (of organisms or a group of exposed humans) and a control group (of the same organisms or the spontaneous incidence in humans).

11564.title: addiction
11564.definition: Compulsive, uncontrolled reward-seeking behavior, especially referring to substance use.

12845.title: Addison disease
12845.definition: Adrenocortical hypofunction characterized by hypotension, weight loss, anorexia, and weakness. The most common form is idiopathic Addison disease, mediated by autoimmune mechanisms. Autoantibodies specific to the adrenal cortex are specific diagnostic markers of this form.

A00132.title: addition
A00132.definition: Refers to addition reaction or addition transformation.Loosely, the formation of an adduct. (For an example, see Lewis acid.)Loosely, any association or attachment.

A00133.title: addition reaction
A00133.definition: A chemical reaction of two or more reacting molecular entities, resulting in a single reaction product containing all atoms of all components, with formation of two chemical bonds and a net reduction in bond multiplicity in at least one of the reactants. The reverse process is called an elimination reaction. The addition may occur at only one site (α-addition, 1/1/addition), at two adjacent sites (1/2/addition) or at two non-adjacent sites (1/3/- or 1/4/addition, etc.). For example:   If the reagent or the source of the addends of an addition are not specified, then it is called an addition transformation.

08937.title: addition-fragmentation chain transfer
08937.definition: Chain-transfer process that proceeds by a propagating species adding to a chain-transfer agent to form an intermediate that then fragments to provide an initiating species.

08448.title: additional gases
08448.definition: Gases added to a combustion mixture.

A00134.title: additive
A00134.definition: A substance added to a sample for any of a variety of purposes.

14423.title: additive effect
14423.definition: Consequence that follows exposure to two or more physicochemical agents that act jointly but do not interact: the total effect is the simple sum of the effects of separate exposures to the agents under the same conditions.

14424.title: additive index
14424.definition: Quantification of the joint action of toxicants in mixture by adding measures of their toxicity calculated in relation to the toxicity of a reference toxicant.

08005.title: additive matrix effect
08005.definition: Matrix effect that is independent of the measured quantity value of the measurand.

A00135.title: additive name
A00135.definition: The formal assembly of names for the components of a compound without loss of atoms or groups of atoms from any componentThe addition or attachment of atoms or groups of atoms.

A00136.title: additivity
A00136.definition: The process by which each chemical species present in the ion source at a certain partial pressure makes a contribution to the total mass spectrum which is the same as that which it would give if that chemical species alone were present in the ion source at a pressure equal to this certain partial pressure.

A00137.title: additivity principle
A00137.definition: The hypothesis that each of several structural features of a molecular entity makes a separate and additive contribution to a property of the substance concerned. More specifically, it is the hypothesis that each of the several substituent groups in a parent molecule makes a separate and additive contribution to the standard Gibbs energy change (or Gibbs energy of activation) corresponding to a particular equilibrium (or rate of reaction).

12846.title: addressin
12846.definition: Extracellular protein of the venular endothelium serving as a ligand to a homing receptor for lymphocytes.

A00138.title: adduct
A00138.definition: A new chemical species AB, each molecular entity of which is formed by direct combination of two separate molecular entities A and B in such a way that there is change in connectivity, but no loss, of atoms within the moieties A and B. Stoichiometries other than 1:1 are also possible, e.g. a bis-adduct (2:1). An intramolecular adduct can be formed when A and B are groups contained within the same molecular entity. This is a general term which, whenever appropriate, should be used in preference to the less explicit term complex. It is also used specifically for products of an addition reaction. For examples, see Lewis adduct, Meisenheimer adduct, π-adduct.

A00139.title: adduct ion
A00139.definition: An ion formed by interaction of two species, usually an ion and a molecule, and often within the ion source, to form an ion containing all the constituent atoms of one species as well as an additional atom or atoms.

10338.title: adenocarcinoma
10338.definition: Malignant tumor formed from glandular epithelial tissue or formed in a glandular pattern.

11565.title: adenoma
11565.definition: Benign tumor arising from epithelial cells in glandular tissue.

12847.title: adenosine deaminase deficiency
12847.definition: Lack of the enzyme adenosine deaminase (ADA), which catalyzes the deamination of adenosine and deoxyadenosine to produce inosine and deoxyinosine, respectively. Affected individuals have a form of severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).

11566.title: adenosine receptor
11566.definition: Any of four types of purinergic receptors that respond to the nucleoside, adenosine, two of which are involved in release of the neurotransmitters, dopamine and glutamate.

14425.title: adenylate energy charge
14425.definition: Index reflecting the balance of energy transfer between catabolic and anabolic processes, calculated from the equation \[\rm{AEC} = ([\ce{ATP}] + ½[\ce{ADP})/([\ce{ATP}] + [\ce{ADP}] + [\ce{AMP}])\] where \(\ce{ATP}\), \(\ce{ADP}\), and \(\ce{AMP}\) are the amount concentrations of adenosine tri-, di-, and monophosphate, respectively.

11545.title: adhesion
11545.definition: Attachment of interfaces between phases or components that is maintained by intermolecular forces, chain entanglements, or both.

10340.title: adhesion factor
10340.definition: Substance contributing to selective cell-cell and cell-matrix binding.

12848.title: adhesion molecule
12848.definition: Molecule belonging mainly to the immunoglobulins, integrin superfamily (e.g., LFA-1, ICAM-1) or selectins, expressed on the cell membrane of various cells including those of the immune system. Interaction of adhesion molecules with each other as receptor and corresponding ligand facilitates cooperation (cross-talk) of cells, signal transduction, and information transfer between cells.

09445.title: adhesion promoter
09445.definition: Interfacial agent comprised of molecules possessing two or more functional groups, each of which exhibits preferential interactions with the various types of phase domains in a composite.

A00140.title: adhesional wetting
A00140.definition: A process in which an adhesional joint is formed between two phases.

A00141.title: adiabatic
A00141.definition: This word is used with various different meanings, and when it is used it should be defined. In thermodynamics 'adiabatic' is used in a macroscopic sense to refer to a process occurring in a thermally insulated system, so that there is no flow of heat to or from the surroundings. In reaction dynamics, the word has been used in a microscopic sense, with a range of meanings which have only a tenuous relationship to the thermodynamic meaning or the etymology. Whereas the thermodynamic meaning relates to conditions imposed on a process by an observer, the microscopic meaning relates to conditions under which the process occurs naturally. The microscopic meanings, as used in reaction dynamics, all have in common the feature that quantum states remain unchanged during the course of reaction. Different quantum states may be referred to: A reaction that is not adiabatic is referred to as nonadiabatic or diabatic, and some workers make a distinction between the two words.A reaction in which there is no change of electronic state or multiplicity has been called adiabatic, or more specifically electronically adiabatic. A reaction in which there is no change of vibrational state during the course of reaction has been said to be vibrationally adiabatic. More loosely, the expression has been applied to a process in which excess vibrational energy in the reactants appears as vibrational energy in the products, or in which ground-state vibration in the reactants leads to ground state vibration in the products.A reaction in which excess rotational energy in the reactants appears as rotational energy in the products, or in which ground-state rotation in the reactants leads to ground-state rotation in the products, has been referred to as rotationally adiabatic.In the Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel–Marcus (RRKM) theory of unimolecular reactions, a degree of freedom whose quantum number is more or less preserved during energization and subsequent reaction has been called 'adiabatic'; the word 'inactive' has also been applied to it.

A00142.title: adiabatic electron transfer
A00142.definition: Electron transfer process in which the reacting system remains on a single electronic surface in passing from reactants to products. For adiabatic electron transfer the electronic transmission factor is close to unity.

A00143.title: adiabatic ionization
A00143.definition: A process whereby an electron is either removed from or added to an atom or molecule producing an ion in its ground state.

A00144.title: adiabatic lapse rate
A00144.definition: The rate of decrease in temperature with increase in altitude of an air parcel which is expanding slowly to a lower atmospheric pressure without exchange of heat; for a descending parcel it is the rate of increase in temperature with decrease in altitude. Theory predicts that for dry air it is equal to the acceleration of gravity divided by the specific heat of dry air at constant pressure (approximately \(9.8\ ^{\unicode{x26ac}} \rm{C}\ \rm{km}^{-1}\)). The moist adiabatic lapse rate is less than the dry adiabatic lapse rate and depends on the moisture content of the air mass.

A00145.title: adiabatic photoreaction
A00145.definition: Within the 'Born-Oppenheimer' approximation, a reaction of an excited state species that occurs on a single 'potential-energy surface'.

08313.title: adiabatic pulse
08313.definition: Radiofrequency pulse that inverts spins by using a frequency sweep during the pulse.

A00146.title: adiabatic transition-state theory
A00146.definition: A form of transition-state theory in which the system is assumed to preserve its internal quantum states as it moves over the potential-energy surface. A detailed state-to-state scattering theory version of adiabatic transition-state theory has been referred to as the adiabatic channel model.

A00147.title: adiabatic treatments of reaction rates
A00147.definition: These are treatments of reaction rates in which the system is assumed to remain on a single potential-energy surface during the entire course of reaction, or to remain in a conserved internal state.

10341.title: aditus
10341.definition: Entrance or opening to some interior space or cavity.

A00148.title: adjacent re-entry model
A00148.definition: A model of crystallinity in which chain folds regularly connect adjacent stems.

10037.title: adjusted retention time
10037.definition: Total retention time (\(t_{\rm{R}}\)) minus hold-up time (\(t_{\rm{M}}\)). \(t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime} = t_{\rm{R}} - t_{\rm{M}}\)

A00150.title: adjuvant
A00150.definition: In pharmacology, a substance added to a drug to speed or increase the action of the main component.In immunology, a substance (such as aluminium hydroxide) or an organism (such as bovine tuberculosis bacillus) which increases the response to an antigen.

12849.title: adjuvant arthritis
12849.definition: Experimental model of immunopathology with features of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), induced in rats by injection with bacterial products, which may be used to study anti-inflammatory therapies.

12615.title: ADMET
12615.definition: Acronym referring to the absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity profile or processes for a xenobiotic upon its administration in vivo.

15143.title: administration
15143.definition: Introduction of a substance to an organism by a defined route.

15144.title: administration of drugs ocular route
15144.definition: Administration of drugs through the eye.

15145.title: administration of drugs oral route
15145.definition: Administration of drugs through the mouth to swallow.

15146.title: administration of drugs parenteral route
15146.definition: Method of introducing substances into an organism, avoiding the gastrointestinal tract.

15147.title: administration of drugs rectal route
15147.definition: Administration of drugs into the rectal cavity or through the rectum.

15148.title: administration of drugs respiratory route
15148.definition: Delivery to the lower respiratory tract in order to obtain a local or systemic effect.

15149.title: administration of drugs topical route
15149.definition: Administration of drugs on surfaces of the body.

15150.title: administration of drugs transdermal route
15150.definition: Introduction of products through unbroken skin by means of a specific drug delivery system (such as a patch containing a semi-solid formulation of the drug) for systemic and/or prolonged drug effect.

15151.title: administration of drugs vaginal route
15151.definition: Introduction of products into the vagina normally for local effect.

10342.title: adolescence
10342.definition: Stage of human development beginning with puberty and ending with adulthood.

12850.title: adoptive transfer
12850.definition: Transfer, by transplantation of immunocompetent cells, of the capacity to mount an immune response.

10343.title: adrenal 4 binding protein
10343.definition: Transcription factor that regulates the expression of the enzymes of steroid synthesis and is expressed primarily in steroidogenic cells.

10344.title: adrenal gland
10344.definition: Either of two small endocrine glands, one located above each kidney, consisting of a cortex, which secretes several steroid hormones, and a medulla, which secretes adrenaline and noradrenaline.

11567.title: adrenalin
11567.definition: Catecholamine hormone secreted by the adrenal glands that increases heart rate, breathing rate, blood pressure, and carbohydrate metabolism.

10345.title: adrenaline
10345.definition: Catecholamine hormone secreted by the adrenal glands that increases heart rate, breathing rate, blood pressure, and carbohydrate metabolism.

11568.title: adrenergic
11568.definition:
Relating to or denoting secretion of and (or) response to adrenalin, noradrenalin or related substances; in particular referring to sympathetic nerve fibers.
Relating to or denoting an agent that mimics the activity of adrenalin, noradrenalin or related substances.

10346.title: adrenocortocotropic hormone
10346.definition: Hormone secreted by the pituitary gland and stimulating the adrenal cortex (see adrenal gland).

A00152.title: adsorbate
A00152.definition: A molecular species of gas, dissolved substance or liquid which adheres to or is adsorbed in an extremely thin surface layer of a solid substance.

A00153.title: adsorbent
A00153.definition: A condensed phase at the surface of which adsorption may occur.

A00154.title: adsorber
A00154.definition: Solid material used to capture either a gas or liquid; often activated carbon is employed as the solid because of its high surface area per unit mass.

A00155.title: adsorption
A00155.definition: An increase in the concentration of a dissolved substance at the interface of a condensed and a liquid phase due to the operation of surface forces. Adsorption can also occur at the interface of a condensed and a gaseous phase.
