A00156.title: adsorption capacity
A00156.definition: For strongly adsorbed solutes of limited solubility, the value of the amount of adsorbed substance reached in a saturated solution is called the adsorption capacity of the adsorbent for a specific solute; its value depends also, in general, on the nature and, in the case of more than two components, on the relative composition of the bulk liquid.

A00157.title: adsorption chromatography
A00157.definition: Chromatography in which separation is based mainly on differences between the adsorption affinities of the sample components for the surface of an active solid.

A00158.title: adsorption complex
A00158.definition: The entity constituted by the adsorbate and the part of the adsorbent to which it is bound.

A00159.title: adsorption current
A00159.definition: A faradaic current whose magnitude depends on the applied potential, and, at any particular applied potential, on the rate or extent of the adsorption of an electroactive substance (or the product obtained from the reduction or oxidation of an electroactive substance) onto the surface of the indicator or working electrode.

14426.title: adsorption factor
14426.definition: Ratio of the amount of substance adsorbed at the interface of a condensed layer and a liquid or gaseous phase to the total amount of the substance available for adsorption.

A00161.title: adsorption hysteresis
A00161.definition: Adsorption hysteresis is said to occur when adsorption and desorption values deviate from one another.

A00162.title: adsorption indicator
A00162.definition: A substance which is adsorbed or desorbed with concomitant colour change at or near the equivalence point of a titration.

A00163.title: adsorption isobar
A00163.definition: The function relating the amount, mass, or volume, or corresponding excess of substance adsorbed by a given amount of solid, to the temperature at constant pressure.

A00164.title: adsorption isostere
A00164.definition: The function relating the equilibrium pressure to the temperature at a constant value of the amount, or excess amount, of substance adsorbed by a given amount of solid.

AT06934.title: adsorption isotherm
AT06934.definition: Isotherm describing adsorption of the sample component on the surface of the stationary phase from the mobile phase.

A00166.title: adsorptive
A00166.definition: The material that is present in one or other (or both) of the bulk phases and capable of being adsorbed.

09151.title: adsorptive stripping voltammetry
09151.definition: Stripping voltammetry involving pre-concentration by adsorption of the analyte (in contrast to electrochemical accumulation).

10347.title: adult
10347.definition: Person or animal that is fully grown, developed and sexually mature.

A00168.title: advection
A00168.definition: The transport of air, its properties (such as heat), trace materials, fog, cold air, etc., solely by mass motion of the atmosphere, generally in a horizontal direction.

09305.title: adventitious carbon referencing
09305.definition: In X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, measurement of the charging potential of a particular sample from a comparison of the experimentally measured \(\ce{C 1s}\) binding energy, arising from adsorbed hydrocarbons on the sample, with a standard binding energy value.

12851.title: adverse drug reaction
12851.definition: Appreciably harmful or unpleasant reaction resulting from an intervention related to the administration of a pharmaceutical product.

AT06809.title: adverse effect
AT06809.definition: Change in biochemistry, morphology, physiology, growth, development, or lifespan of an organism which results in impairment of functional capacity or impairment of capacity to compensate for additional stress or increase in susceptibility to other environmental influences.

15448.title: adverse event
15448.definition: Occurrence that causes an adverse effect.

12852.title: adverse immunostimulation
12852.definition: Antigen-non-specific, inappropriate, or unintended activation of a component of the immune system.

A00169.title: aeration
A00169.definition: The process by which a volume filled with a liquid becomes permeated with air or another gas; aeration is often accomplished by spraying the liquid into the air, bubbling air through a liquid or agitating the liquid to promote surface absorption of air.

09446.title: aerial image
09446.definition: Image of a mask pattern that is projected onto the photoresist coated wafer by an optical system.

12853.title: aeroallergen
12853.definition: Any airborne particle, such as a pollen grain or spore, that triggers an allergic reaction in sensitive individuals.

A00170.title: aerobe
A00170.definition: An organism that needs oxygen for respiration and hence for growth.

A00172.title: aerobic conditions
A00172.definition: Conditions for growth or metabolism in which the organism is sufficiently supplied with oxygen.

15449.title: aerodynamic diameter
15449.definition: Diameter of a spherical particle with relative density equal to unity that has the same settling velocity in air as the particle in question.

A00173.title: aerogel
A00173.definition: Gel comprised of a microporous solid in which the dispersed phase is a gas.

A00174.title: aerometer
A00174.definition: Instrument used to measure the density of gases.

A00175.title: aerometric measurement
A00175.definition: A measurement of the temperature, pressure, air motion (velocity vectors), or other physical measurement to characterize an air mass.

A00176.title: aerosol
A00176.definition: Sol in which the dispersed phase is a solid, a liquid or a mixture of both and the continuous phase is a gas (usually air).

AT07606.title: aerosol hydrolysis
AT07606.definition: Hydrolysis of the dispersed component of an aerosol.

08449.title: aerosol transport phenomena
08449.definition: Processes occurring inside the spray chamber or desolvation system responsible for the modification of the primary aerosol to finally yield the tertiary aerosol.

11571.title: afferent
11571.definition: Inflowing. Of nerves, those that conduct impulses toward the central nervous system.

AT07591.title: affine chain behaviour
AT07591.definition: Behaviour of a polymer network in which the junction points deform uniformly with the macroscopic deformation of the network.

09661.title: affinity
09661.definition: Strength of association between a single antibody and a single epitope of antigen.

A00177.title: affinity chromatography
A00177.definition: An expression characterizing the particular variant of chromatography in which the unique biological specificity of the analyte and ligand interaction is utilized for the separation.

12854.title: affinity maturation
12854.definition: Increase in antibody affinity for an antigen observed as the humoral immune response progresses.

A00178.title: affinity of reaction
A00178.definition: Negative partial derivative of Gibbs energy with respect to extent of reaction at constant pressure and temperature. It is positive for spontaneous reactions.

A00179.title: after mass analysis
A00179.definition: The sum of all the separate ion currents carried by the different ions contributing to the spectrum.

15450.title: after-effect of a poison
15450.definition: Ability of a poison to produce a change in an organism after cessation of contact.

14427.title: age class
14427.definition: Group of organisms of the same age within a population.

14428.title: age composition
14428.definition: Distribution of organisms among the various age classes present in the population. The sum of the number of individuals in all age classes equals the population size.

14429.title: age distribution
14429.definition: Composition of a population in terms of how its abundance is distributed across age classes.

15451.title: age sensitivity
15451.definition: Quantitative and qualitative age dependence of an effect.

10350.title: age-specific birth rate
10350.definition: Mean number of offspring born to a female in a specific age class in a given year, expressed per \(\pu{1000}\) females in that age class.

14430.title: age-specific death rate
14430.definition: Mean number of deaths as tabulated for a life table interval or for a specific age class in a given year, expressed per \(\pu{1000}\) in that interval or age class.

A00180.title: ageing of precipitate
A00180.definition: The time-dependent change of those properties of a precipitate, e.g. loss of water, growth of crystals, recrystallization, decrease of the specific surface, loss of coprecipitated substances, which generally improve the filtering properties. The process of ageing is very often promoted by maintaining the precipitate and precipitation medium together at elevated temperatures for a period of time. The terms chemical, physical and thermal ageing may be used in cases in which some of the (usually combined) effects named above are to be emphasized specifically.

10349.title: agenesis
10349.definition: Absence or partial development of an organ or body part observed at birth.

AT07502.title: agglomerate
AT07502.definition: Cluster of molecules or particles that results from agglomeration.

A00182.title: agglomeration
A00182.definition: Process of contact and adhesion whereby dispersed particles are held together by weak physical interactions ultimately leading to phase separation by the formation of precipitates of larger than colloidal size.

AT07607.title: agglomeration
AT07607.definition: Process in which dispersed molecules or particles assemble rather than remain as isolated single molecules or particles.

A00183.title: agglutination
A00183.definition: An immunochemical reaction leading to the aggregation of particulate matter such as bacteria, erythrocytes or other cells, or synthetic particles such as plastic beads coated with antigens or antibodies.

09662.title: agglutination inhibition
09662.definition: Type of agglutination in which particulate and soluble antigen compete for soluble antibody.

A00184.title: aggregate
A00184.definition: Certain materials used as catalysts or supports consist of spheroids smaller than \(10\ \rm{nm}\) in diameter, cemented into larger entities. A primary particle should be defined as the smallest discrete identifiable entity and the method of identification should be mentioned (e.g. transmission electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy). An assemblage of such primary particles exhibiting an identifiable collective behaviour (e.g. chemical nature of the aggregated primary particles, texture of the aggregate, resistance to mechanical separation upon grinding) constitutes an aggregate. When describing the aggregates the criterion of identification should be mentioned. Strongly bonded aggregates are called agglomerates.

AT07608.title: aggregation
AT07608.definition: Process whereby dispersed molecules or particles form aggregates.

10351.title: aggregation chimera
10351.definition: Organism made by combining cells from two embryos of different genotypes.

14431.title: aggregation error
14431.definition: Error in Bayesian probability analysis of model systems resulting from the use of a single set of parameters to represent a collection of distinct entities, such as individuals, in a population.

AT06849.title: aging
AT06849.definition: Processes that occur in a polymeric material during a specified period of time, and that usually result in changes in physical and/or chemical structure and the values of the properties of the material.

A00185.title: aglycon
A00185.definition: The non-sugar compound remaining after replacement of the glycosyl group from a glycoside by a hydrogen atom.

10352.title: agnathia
10352.definition: Congenital absence or partial absence of the lower jaw.

11572.title: agnosia
11572.definition: Impaired ability to recognize or comprehend the meaning of various sensations, not attributable to faulty sensory input or general intellect.

A00186.title: agonist
A00186.definition: Substance which binds to cell receptors normally responding to naturally occurring substances and which produces a response of its own.

A00187.title: agostic
A00187.definition: The term designates structures in which a hydrogen atom is bonded to both a carbon atom and a metal atom. The term is also used to characterize the interaction between a $\ce{CH}$ bond and an unsaturated metal centre, and to describe similar bonding of a transition metal with $\ce{Si–H}$ compounds. The expression '$\mu$-hydrido-bridged' is also used to describe the bridging hydrogen.

AT06984.title: agostic interaction
AT06984.definition: The manner of interaction (termed according to the Greek 'to hold or clasp to oneself as a shield') of a coordinatively unsaturated metal atom with a ligand, when the metal atom draws the ligand towards itself. An important type of agostic interaction is the C–H–Metal coordination providing for the activation of the C–H bond in transition metal complexes.

A00188.title: agranular carbon
A00188.definition: A monogranular or monolithic carbon material with homogeneous microstructure which does not exhibit any structural components distinguishable by optical microscopy.

12855.title: agranulocytosis
12855.definition: Failure of the bone marrow to make sufficient granulocytes, especially neutrophils.

A00190.title: air contaminant
A00190.definition: A substance, gaseous material or aerosol, which is present in an air mass at levels greater than in clean air. An air contaminant has been added commonly by anthropogenic activity.

A00192.title: air mass
A00192.definition: A qualitative term to describe a widespread body of air with approximately uniform characteristics which had been identified at a given time over a particular region of the earth's surface. Sometimes an air mass is marked by inert tracers such as $\ce{SF6}$ which may be added to it. The composition of a given air mass undergoes alteration as it migrates, chemical changes occur, compounds are removed by dry and wet deposition and new impurities are added to the mass.

A00193.title: air monitoring station
A00193.definition: A site at which monitoring of the concentration of one or more pollutants is carried out (e.g. the BAPMoN stations, Background Air Pollution Monitoring Network of the WMO, World Meteorological Organization).

A00194.title: air pollutant
A00194.definition: A substance, gaseous material or aerosol which has been introduced into the air (either by human activity or by natural processes) in sufficient concentration to produce a measurable effect on humans, animals, vegetation or materials (monuments, etc.): $\ce{SO2}$, $\ce{NO2}$, $\ce{H2S}$, $\ce{CO}$, hydrocarbons, etc.

A00195.title: air pollution
A00195.definition: Usually the presence of substances in the atmosphere, resulting either from human activity or natural processes, present in sufficient concentration, for a sufficient time and under circumstances such as to interfere with comfort, health or welfare of persons or the environment.

15452.title: air pollution control system
15452.definition:
Network of organizations that monitor air pollution.
Group of measures or processes used to minimize or prevent air pollution.

A00196.title: air pollution index
A00196.definition: A mathematical combination of the concentrations of air pollutants (weighted in some fashion to reflect the estimated health impact of the specific pollutant) which gives an approximate numerical measure of the quality of the air at a given time. These indices have little scientific basis but have been used to inform the public (in a qualitative fashion) of the degree of pollution present at a given time. It is recommended that the actual measured pollutant concentrations be used by all information services when possible with simultaneous reference given to the corresponding concentrations which are considered by health authorities to be hazardous to human health.

A00197.title: air pollution survey
A00197.definition: A study of the concentrations and geographical distribution of specified air pollutants in a given area and an assessment of the damage, if any, which the pollutants have caused.

14432.title: air pollution tolerance index
14432.definition: Empirical index used to assess the tolerance of individual plants to contaminated air. The numerical value of \(T_{\rm{I}}\) is obtained by combining various quantities according to the recipe \([A (T + P) + R]/10\), where \(A\) is the mass of ascorbic acid divided by the dry mass of a leaf, expressed as \(\pu{mg/g}\), \(T\) is the total mass of chlorophyll divided by the fresh mass, expressed as \(\pu{mg/g}\), \(P\) is the pH of a leaf extract, and \(R\) is the mass of water in the leaf divided by the wet mass, expressed as percent.

A00198.title: air quality characteristic
A00198.definition: One of the quantifiable properties relating to an air sample: concentration of a constituent, wind speed, temperature, etc. The quantity of air quality characteristic is the true value of the characteristic being investigated; it is recognized that in practice, this value can only be approximated by existing methods.

A00199.title: air resource management
A00199.definition: The detailed planning and the implementation of air pollution control programs designed to preserve the health and welfare of the people in the region, the plant and animal life, physical property, good visibility and other factors which determine the air quality and the maintenance of an aesthetically acceptable environment.

A00200.title: air sampling network
A00200.definition: A number of air sampling stations which are established in a given geographical region at which measurements of both pollutant concentrations and meteorological quantities (wind speed, direction, rain fall, humidity, etc.) are made to determine the extent and the nature of the air pollution and to establish trends in the concentrations of the air pollutants with time.

A00191.title: air-lift bioreactor
A00191.definition: A bioreactor in which the reaction medium is kept mixed and gassed by introduction of air or another gas (mixture) at the base of a column-like reactor equipped either with a draught tube or another device (e.g. external tube) by which the reactor volume is separated into a gassed and an ungassed region thus generating a vertically circulating flow.

A00201.title: Aitken particles
A00201.definition: Aerosol particles below \(0.1\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) in diameter. These generally are the most numerous among all particles in the air. Their concentrations can be determined with the Aitken counter which measures total particle number density. Owing to their small size, Aitken particles contribute little to the total mass concentration of all aerosol particles; this is determined primarily by particles of diameter \(> 0.1\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\).

10353.title: alar plate
10353.definition: Part of the dorsal side of neural tube in the embryo, involved in general somatic and visceral sensory communication.

A00202.title: albedo
A00202.definition: The fraction of the energy of electromagnetic radiation reflected from a body (or surface) relative to the energy incident upon it. The reflection of light from a surface is, of course, dependent on the wavelength of the light, the nature of the surface and its angle of incidence with the surface. The term albedo usually connotes a broad wavelength band (visible, ultraviolet or infrared), whereas the terms reflectivity and spectral albedo are used to describe the reflection of monochromatic (single wavelength or small band of wavelengths) radiation.

10354.title: albinism
10354.definition: Congenital disorder characterized by the complete or partial absence of pigment in the skin, hair and eyes, due to an absence of or defect in tyrosinase, a copper-containing enzyme involved in the production of melanin.

AT06761.title: albumin
AT06761.definition: A type of protein, especially a protein of blood plasma which transports various substances, including metal ions, drugs and xenobiotics.

15453.title: albuminuria
15453.definition: Presence of albumin, derived from plasma, in the urine.

AT07516.title: alcogel
AT07516.definition: Gel in which the swelling agent consists predominantly of an alcohol or a mixture of alcohols.

10355.title: alcohol-related neurodevelopmental disabilities
10355.definition: Spectrum of functional neurologic (behavioral) defects resulting from exposure in utero to alcohol.

A00203.title: alcoholates
A00203.definition: Synonymous with alkoxides. Alcoholate should not be used for solvates derived from an alcohol such as $\ce{CaCl2.nROH}$, for the ending -ate often occurs in names for anions.

A00204.title: alcohols
A00204.definition: Compounds in which a hydroxy group, $\ce{-OH}$, is attached to a saturated carbon atom $\ce{R3COH}$. The term 'hydroxyl' refers to the radical species, $\ce{HO^{.}}$.

A00206.title: aldaric acids
A00206.definition: Polyhydroxy dicarboxylic acids having the general formula $\ce{HOC(=O)[CH(OH)]_{n}C(=O)OH}$, formally derived from an aldose by oxidation of both terminal carbon atoms to carboxyl groups.

A00208.title: aldehydes
A00208.definition: Compounds $\ce{RC(=O)H}$, in which a carbonyl group is bonded to one hydrogen atom and to one $\ce{R}$ group.

A00210.title: alditols
A00210.definition: Acyclic polyols having the general formula $\ce{HOCH2[CH(OH)]nCH2OH}$ (formally derivable from an aldose by reduction of the carbonyl group).

A00211.title: aldoketoses
A00211.definition: A now less preferred synonym for ketoaldoses.

A00212.title: aldonic acids
A00212.definition: Polyhydroxy acids having the general formula $\ce{HOCH2[CH(OH)]_{n}C(=O)OH}$ and therefore derived from an aldose by oxidation of the aldehyde function, e.g. ᴅ-gluconic acid.

A00213.title: aldoses
A00213.definition: Aldehydic parent sugars (polyhydroxyaldehydes $\ce{H[CH(OH)]_{n}C(=O)H}$, $n \ge 2$) and their intramolecular hemiacetals.

A00215.title: alert levels
A00215.definition: Designated concentrations of certain key pollutants at which some degree of danger to public health is expected. In many areas in which a relatively high level of pollution is often encountered, several levels of alert are often established. For example, a first alert may signify a potential problem exists; a second alert becomes a signal for the curtailment of certain significant emission sources; the third alert signifies the need for some specified emergency action which must be taken to ensure the public safety.

14433.title: alga
14433.definition: Any of various chiefly aquatic, eukaryotic, photosynthetic organisms, ranging in size from single-celled forms to the giant kelp.

14434.title: algal bloom
14434.definition: Rapid increase in the abundance of phytoplankton or benthic algae in a given area, often as a result of an increased availability of nutrients or light, or increase in temperature (e.g., the spring bloom).

11405.title: algorithm
11405.definition: A step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or performing a function, usually by a computer.

10065.title: alias structure
10065.definition: List of combinations of effects that are aliased (confounded).

10066.title: aliased effects
10066.definition: In a fractional-factorial design, effects for which the information obtained are identical.

A00216.title: alicyclic compounds
A00216.definition: Aliphatic compounds having a carbocyclic ring structure which may be saturated or unsaturated, but may not be a benzenoid or other aromatic system.

09363.title: aligned incidence spectrum
09363.definition: Backscattering spectrum recorded with the analysing beam aligned with crystallographic axes or planes of the sample that produce channelling.

A00217.title: aliphatic compounds
A00217.definition: Acyclic or cyclic, saturated or unsaturated carbon compounds, excluding aromatic compounds.

A00218.title: aliquot
A00218.definition: A known amount of a homogeneous material, assumed to be taken with negligible sampling error. The term is usually applied to fluids. The term 'aliquot' is usually used when the fractional part is an exact divisor of the whole; the term 'aliquant' has been used when the fractional part is not an exact divisor of the whole (e.g. a \(15\ \rm{ml}\) portion is an aliquant of \(100\ \rm{ml}\)). When a laboratory sample or test sample is 'aliquoted' or otherwise subdivided, the portions have been called split samples.

09835.title: alkaline degradation
09835.definition: Treatment with alkaline solution (e.g. hydrazine, \(\ce{KOH}\), \(\ce{NaOH}\)) useful for the cleavage of fatty acids.

09034.title: alkalinity
09034.definition: Measure of the capacity of aqueous media to react with hydrogen ions.

A00220.title: alkaloids
A00220.definition: Basic nitrogen compounds (mostly heterocyclic) occurring mostly in the plant kingdom (but not excluding those of animal origin). Amino acids, peptides, proteins, nucleotides, nucleic acids, amino sugars and antibiotics are not normally regarded as alkaloids. By extension, certain neutral compounds biogenetically related to basic alkaloids are included.

A00221.title: alkalosis
A00221.definition: Pathological condition in which the hydrogen ion substance concentration of body fluids is below normal and hence the pH of blood rises above the reference interval.

A00222.title: alkanes
A00222.definition: Acyclic branched or unbranched hydrocarbons having the general formula $\ce{C_{n}H_{2n+2}}$, and therefore consisting entirely of hydrogen atoms and saturated carbon atoms.

A00223.title: alkanium ions
A00223.definition: Carbocations derived from alkanes by $C$-hydronation containing at least one pentacoordinate carbon atom, e.g. $\ce{^{+}CH5}$ methanium, $\ce{[C2H7]^{+}$ ethanium.

AT07318.title: alkene photocycloaddition
AT07318.definition: Photochemical process leading to formation of a cyclobutane upon addition of an electronically excited alkene to another ground-state alkene or of an electronically excited $\ce{\upalpha\!,\upbeta\!\mbox{-}unsaturated}$ carbonyl compound to a ground-state alkene. The latter is called a de Mayo reaction.

AT07319.title: alkene photodimerization
AT07319.definition: Photochemical process leading to the formation of a cyclobutane from two identical alkenes, i.e., from the photocycloaddition of an electronically excited alkene to a ground-state alkene.

AT07320.title: alkene photoisomerization
AT07320.definition: Photochemical process with geometrical isomerization of a carbon–carbon double bond.

AT07321.title: alkene photorearrangement
AT07321.definition: Photochemical process leading to the skeletal rearrangement of an alkene.

A00224.title: alkenes
A00224.definition: Acyclic branched or unbranched hydrocarbons having one carbon–carbon double bond and the general formula $\ce{C_{n}H_{2n}}$. Acyclic branched or unbranched hydrocarbons having more than one double bond are alkadienes, alkatrienes, etc.

A00225.title: alkoxides
A00225.definition: Compounds, $\ce{ROM}$, derivatives of alcohols, $\ce{ROH}$, in which $\ce{R}$ is saturated at the site of its attachment to oxygen and $\ce{M}$ is a metal or other cationic species.

A00226.title: alkoxyamines
A00226.definition: O-Alkyl hydroxylamines (with or without substitution on $\ce{N}$) $\ce{R'ONR2}$ ($\ce{R'\neq H}$).

A00228.title: alkyl groups
A00228.definition: Univalent groups derived from alkanes by removal of a hydrogen atom from any carbon atom $\ce{–C_{n}H_{2n+1}}$. The groups derived by removal of a hydrogen atom from a terminal carbon atom of unbranched alkanes form a subclass of normal alkyl ($n$-alkyl) groups $\ce{H(CH2)_{n}}$. The groups $\ce{RCH2}$, $\ce{R2CH}$ ($\ce{R \neq H}$), and $\ce{R3C}$ ($\ce{R \neq H}$) are primary, secondary and tertiary alkyl groups, respectively.

A00235.title: alkyl radicals
A00235.definition: Carbon-centered radicals derived formally by removal of one hydrogen atom from an alkane, e.g. $\ce{CH3CH2C^{.}H2}$ propyl.

15454.title: alkylating agent
15454.definition: Substance that introduces an alkyl substituent into a compound.

A00227.title: alkylenes
A00227.definition: An old term, which is not recommended, for alkenes, especially those of low molecular weight.An old term for alkanediyl groups commonly but not necessarily having the free valencies on adjacent carbon atoms, e.g. $\ce{–CH(CH3)CH2\bond{–}}$ propylene (systematically called propane-1,2-diyl).

A00232.title: alkylidene groups
A00232.definition: The divalent groups formed from alkanes by removal of two hydrogen atoms from the same carbon atom, the free valencies of which are part of a double bond, e.g. $\ce{(CH3)2C=}$ propan-2-ylidene.

A00230.title: alkylideneaminoxyl radicals
A00230.definition: Radicals having the structure $\ce{R2C=N–O^{.}}$. Synonymous with iminoxyl radicals.

A00231.title: alkylideneaminyl radicals
A00231.definition: Radicals having the structure $\ce{R2C=N^{.}}$. Synonymous with iminyl radicals.

A00233.title: alkylidenes
A00233.definition: Carbenes $\ce{R2C{:}}$ formed by mono or dialkyl substitution of methylene, $\ce{H2C{:}}$, e.g. $\ce{CH3CH2CH{:}}$ propylidene.

A00234.title: alkylidynes
A00234.definition: Carbenes $\ce{R2C…}$ containing a univalent carbon atom, atom, e.g. $\ce{CH3CH2C…}$ propylidyne

A00236.title: alkynes
A00236.definition: Acyclic branched or unbranched hydrocarbons having a carbon-carbon triple bond and the general formula $\ce{C_{n}H_{2n-2}}$, $\ce{RC#CR}$. Acyclic branched or unbranched hydrocarbons having more than one triple bond are known as alkadiynes, alkatriynes, etc.

11540.title: all-solid-state ion-selective electrode
11540.definition: Ion-selective electrode in which the ion-selective membrane contacts the electronic conductor without internal electrolyte solution.

11255.title: allantoic stalk
11255.definition: Narrow connecting tube between the intra- and extra-embryonic parts of the allantois.

10356.title: allantois
10356.definition: Extra-embryonic membrane formed early in development as an outpouching of the yolk sac into the area of the future umbilical cord.

A00237.title: allele
A00237.definition: One of several alternate forms of a gene which occur at the same locus on homologous chromosomes and which become separated during meiosis and can be recombined following fusion of gametes.

12856.title: allelic exclusion
12856.definition: Phenomenon whereby, following successful rearrangement of one allele of an antigen receptor gene, rearrangement of the other parental allele is suppressed, thereby ensuring each lymphocyte expresses only a single specificity of antigen receptor.

A00238.title: allenes
A00238.definition: Hydrocarbons (and by extension, derivatives formed by substitution) having two double bonds from one carbon atom to two others $\ce{R2C=C=CR2}$. (The simplest member, propadiene, is known as allene).

12857.title: allergen
12857.definition: Immunostimulant antigenic substance that may or may not cause a clinically significant effect but which is capable of producing an immune reaction, often immediate-type hypersensitivity.

12859.title: allergy
12859.definition: Symptoms or signs occurring in sensitized individuals following exposure to a previously encountered substance (allergen) that would otherwise not cause such symptoms or signs in non-sensitized individuals. The most common forms of allergy are rhinitis, urticaria, asthma, and contact dermatitis.

A00239.title: allo-
A00239.definition: Amino acids with two chiral centres were named in the past by allotting a name to the first diastereoisomer to be discovered. The second diastereoisomer, when found or synthesized, was then assigned the same name but with the prefix allo-. This method can be used only with trivial names but not with semisystematic or systematic names. It is now recommended that allo should be used only for alloisoleucine and allothreonine.

12860.title: alloantibody
12860.definition: Antibody produced against an antigen from another member of the same species.

12861.title: alloantigen
12861.definition: Antigen, present in some but not all individuals of a particular species, that arises from polymorphisms at the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) loci and stimulates intense reactions to allograft tissues from other individuals of the same species that do not produce it.

12862.title: allogeneic
12862.definition: Genetically different, referring to individuals of the same species.

14437.title: allogenic succession
14437.definition: Sequential appearance of species driven by external influences that alter local conditions; e.g., silt deposits changing a marshland to woodland.

12863.title: allograft
12863.definition: Tissue or organ graft between allogeneic individuals.

AT06803.title: allometric
AT06803.definition: Pertaining to a systematic relationship between growth rates of different parts of an organism and its overall growth rate.

15455.title: allometric growth
15455.definition: Regular and systematic pattern of growth such that the mass or size of any organ or part of a body can be expressed in relation to the total mass or size of the entire organism according to the allometric equation: \[Y = b{x^{\alpha}}\] where \(Y\) = mass of the organ, \(x\) = mass of the organism, \(\alpha\) = growth coefficient of the organ, and \(b\) is a constant.

15456.title: allometric scaling
15456.definition:
Adjustment of data to allow for change in proportion between an organ or organs and other body parts during the growth of an organism.
Adjustment of data to allow for differences and make comparisons between species having dissimilar characteristics (e.g., in size, shape, and metabolism).

15457.title: allometry
15457.definition: Measurement of the rate of growth of a part or parts of an organism relative to the growth of the whole organism.

15458.title: allomone
15458.definition: Semiochemical that is produced by an organism inducing a response in an organism of another species that is favorable to the emitter.

12865.title: alloreactivity
12865.definition: Reactivity of an antibody with an alloantigen.

12616.title: allosteric antagonist
12616.definition: Compound that binds to a receptor at a site separate from, but actively coupled to, that of the endogenous agonist to reduce actively receptor signals.

A00240.title: allosteric enzymes
A00240.definition: Enzymes which contain regions to which small, regulatory molecules (cf. effector) may bind in addition to and separate from substrate binding sites. On binding the effector, the catalytic activity of the enzyme towards the substrate may be enhanced, in which case the effector is an activator, or reduced, in which case it is an inhibitor.

14107.title: allosteric site
14107.definition: Binding site on a protein, distinct from the site recognized by an endogenous agonist (i.e., the orthosteric site) in the case of a receptor, or substrate in the case of an enzyme, that when occupied by a ligand effects a conformational change in the protein, thus altering its signaling, catalytic properties, or its capability to interact with other macromolecules.

A00241.title: allostery
A00241.definition: A phenomenon whereby the conformation of an enzyme or other protein is altered by combination, at a site other than the substrate-binding site, with a small molecule, referred to as an effector, which results in either increased or decreased activity by the enzyme.

A00243.title: allotropes
A00243.definition: Different structural modifications of an element.

A00244.title: allotropic transition
A00244.definition: A transition of a pure element, at a defined temperature and pressure, from one crystal structure to another which contains the same atoms but which has different properties. Examples: The transition of graphite to diamond, that of body-centred-cubic iron to face-centred-cubic iron, and the transition of orthorhombic sulfur to monoclinic sulfur.

12864.title: allotype
12864.definition: Allelic variant of an antigen that, because it is not present in all individuals, may be immunogenic in members of the same species that have a different version of the allele.

A00245.title: allylic groups
A00245.definition: The group $\ce{CH2=CHCH2}$ (allyl) and derivatives formed by substitution. The term 'allylic position' or 'allylic site' refers to the saturated carbon atom. A group, such as $\ce{–OH}$, attached at an allylic site is sometimes described as 'allylic'.

A00246.title: allylic intermediates
A00246.definition: Carbanions, carbenium ions or radicals, formally derived by detachment of one hydron, hydride or hydrogen from the $\ce{CH3}$ group of propene or derivatives thereof. E.g. $\ce{H2C=CHCH2^{+}}$ allyl cation.

A00247.title: allylic substitution reaction
A00247.definition: A substitution reaction occurring at position 1/ of an allylic system, the double bond being between positions 2/ and 3/. The incoming group may be attached to the same atom 1/ as the leaving group, or the incoming group becomes attached at the relative position 3/, with movement of the double bond from 2/3 to 1/2. For example:  (written as a transformation).

10357.title: alopecia
10357.definition: Hairlessness; absence or thinning of hair from areas of skin where it is usually present.

12740.title: alpha relaxation
12740.definition: Highest-temperature or lowest-frequency relaxation in the loss curve of a polymer.

12741.title: alpha relaxation peak
12741.definition: Highest-temperature peak or lowest-frequency peak in the loss curve of a polymer.

10358.title: alpha-fetoprotein
10358.definition: Protein coded by the AFP gene and produced by fetal tissues, an abnormally high amount of which in the amniotic fluid or maternal serum may indicate a neural tube defect, or some other loss of structural integrity in the fetus.

12617.title: alpha-helix
12617.definition: Secondary 3D structure of a protein or peptide containing a right-handed coiled or spiral conformation, in which every backbone \(\ce{N-H}\) group donates a hydrogen bond to the backbone \(\ce{C=O}\) group of the amino acid four residues earlier.

11573.title: alpha-synuclein
11573.definition: Protein abundant in the human brain, thought to regulate the release of dopamine.

09217.title: altered layer
09217.definition: Surface region of a material under particle bombardment where the chemical state or physical structure is modified by the effects of the bombardment.

AT06985.title: alternancy symmetry
AT06985.definition: A topological property of the molecular graphs of alternant hydrocarbons which allows the carbon atoms to be divided into two subsets in such a way that no two atoms of the same subset are adjacent. A consequence of this property is the symmetrical arrangement of the energy levels of bonding and antibonding Hückel MOs relative to the level of a nonbonding orbital (energy level of the p AO of a carbon atom).

A00249.title: alternant
A00249.definition: A conjugated system of $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electrons}$ is termed alternant if its atoms can be divided into two sets so that no atom of one set is directly linked to any other atom of the same set.

A00250.title: alternating copolymer
A00250.definition: A copolymer consisting of macromolecules comprising two species of monomeric units in alternating sequence.

A00251.title: alternating copolymerization
A00251.definition: A copolymerization in which an alternating copolymer is formed.

A00252.title: alternating current
A00252.definition: Current with sinusoidal wave forms; all other wave forms should be termed 'periodic'.

10083.title: alternating least squares regression
10083.definition: Solution to the multivariate decomposition of a data matrix in which iteratively a solution of one output matrix is used to compute the second matrix, after the application of constraints.

A00254.title: alternating voltage
A00254.definition: This term should be applied only to sinusoidal phenomena; the term periodic voltage should be used for other wave forms.

12866.title: alternative pathway
12866.definition: Activation pathway involving complement components C3, Factor B, Factor D, and properdin that, in the presence of a stabilizing activator surface such as microbial polysaccharide, generates the alternative pathway C3 convertase C3bBb.

09734.title: alternative splicing
09734.definition: Process occurring during gene expression that allows the generation of multiple protein molecules from one gene. It generally involves the processing of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) via elimination of introns.

A00256.title: altocumulus cloud
A00256.definition: A dappled layer of patch or cloud composed of flattened globules that may be arranged in groups, lines or waves collectively known as billows; \(\rm{2000–6000 m}\); vertical velocities of \(\rm{0.05–0.1 m s}^{-1}\).

A00257.title: altostratus cloud
A00257.definition: A grey, uniform, striated or fibrous sheet but without halo phenomena, and through which the sun is seen only as a diffuse, bright patch or not at all; usually at elevations \(\rm{2000–6000 m}\); vertical velocities of \(\rm{0.05–0.1 m s}^{-1}\).

12867.title: alveolar macrophage
12867.definition: Macrophage found in the lung alveoli; it may remove and sometimes retain inhaled particulate matter.

16261.title: alveolar period
16261.definition: Phase in lung development beginning in utero (about \(\pu{32}\) to \(\pu{36}\) weeks in the human fetus) and lasting until about eight years of age.

12868.title: alveolitis
12868.definition:
1) Inflammation of alveoli.
2) Inflammation of a tooth socket.

10359.title: alveolus
10359.definition: Any of the many terminal air sacs of the airways in the lungs necessary for rapid gaseous exchange with the blood.

11574.title: Alzheimer disease
11574.definition: Common and progressive neurodegenerative disease leading to loss of memory, orientation, and judgment.

A00312.title: AM 0 sunlight
A00312.definition: Solar irradiance in space just above the atmosphere of the earth on a plane perpendicular to the direction of the sun (air mass, AM, zero). Also called extraterrestrial irradiance.

A00313.title: AM 1 sunlight
A00313.definition: Solar irradiance at sea level, i.e., traversing the atmosphere, when the direction of the sun is perpendicular to the surface of the earth. Also called terrestrial global irradiance.

AT07326.title: amalgam lamp
AT07326.definition: Intense source of ultraviolet (\(185\) and \(253.7\ \rm{nm}\)) radiation produced by an electrical discharge in a lamp with the inner side covered by an amalgam of mercury with another element such as indium or gallium to control the vapour pressure of the mercury. These lamp have 2-3 times the UV output for the same wavelength as the standard low-pressure mercury lamp.

10360.title: amastia
10360.definition: Congenital absence of one or both mammary glands.

A00258.title: ambident
A00258.definition: A description applied to a chemical species whose molecular entities each possess two alternative and strongly interacting distinguishable reactive centres, to either of which a bond may be made in a reaction: the centres must be connected in such a way that reaction at either site stops or greatly retards subsequent attack at the second site. The term is most commonly applied to conjugated nucleophiles, for example the enolate ion:  (which may react with electrophiles either at the $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}carbon atom}$ or at oxygen) or $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}pyridones}$, and also to the vicinally ambident cyanide ion, cyanate ion, thiocyanate ion, sulfinate ion, nitrite ion and unsymmetrical hydrazines. Ambident electrophiles are exemplified by carboxylic esters $\ce{RC(=O)OCR3}$ which react with nucleophiles either at the carbonyl carbon or the alkoxy carbon. Molecular entities, such as dianions of dicarboxylic acids, containing two non-interacting (or feebly interacting) reactive centres, are not generally considered to be ambident and are better described as 'bifunctional'. The Latin root of the word implies two reactive centres, but the term has in the past also incorrectly been applied to chemical species with more than two reactive centres. For such species the existing term 'polydent' (or, better, 'multident') is more appropriate.

14438.title: ambient
14438.definition: Surrounding (applied to environmental media such as air, water, sediment, or soil).

A00259.title: ambient air
A00259.definition: The outdoor air in the particular location.

A00260.title: ambient air quality
A00260.definition: A general term used to describe the quality of the outside air. Usually adjectives such as good, fair, bad, etc. are used by the media to describe this; often some form of air pollution or air quality index is employed to determine the specific descriptive term to be used. These are very qualitative terms of little or no scientific value.

14439.title: ambient monitoring
14439.definition: Continuous or repeated measurement of agents in the environment to evaluate ambient exposure and health risk by comparison with appropriate reference values based on knowledge of the probable relationship between exposure and resultant adverse health effects.

10361.title: ambisexual
10361.definition:
Pertaining to or characterized by hermaphroditism.
Denoting sexual characteristics common to both sexes, e.g., pubic hair.

A00261.title: ambo
A00261.definition: A prefix used to indicate that a molecule with two (or more) chiral elements is present as a mixture of the two racemic diastereoisomers in unspecified proportions. For example, the dipeptide formed from ʟ-alanine and ᴅʟ-leucine is ʟ-alanyl-ambo-leucine.

10362.title: amelia
10362.definition: Lacking one or more limbs or having a shrunken or deformed limb as a birth defect.

10363.title: ameloblast
10363.definition: Epithelial cell that deposits enamel during tooth development.

10364.title: amelogenesis imperfecta
10364.definition:
Hereditary yellow, brown, or grey tooth enamel.
Developmental disorder of the teeth in which they are covered with thin, abnormal enamel resulting from defective structure or processing of enamel proteins.

10365.title: amenorrhea
10365.definition: Absence or abnormal stoppage of menstruation.

A00262.title: Ames/salmonella test
A00262.definition: A screening test employed in predicting the mutagenic and the potential carcinogenic activities of chemicals in the environment. It employs Ames test strains of salmonella bacteria ($\ce{his^{-}}$) which lack the ability to produce histidine. The compound to be tested, the bacteria and a small amount of histidine (insufficient to permit colony growth but enough to allow sufficient growth for expression of mutations) are added to agar. The bacteria are allowed to incubate for about \(63\ \rm{h}\) at \(37\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\). If a significant increase in colonies above background is observed in the sample containing the test compound, then it is concluded that the chemical tested is a direct mutagen for the particular Ames strain of bacteria. This is taken as a qualitative indication of the possible carcinogenic activity of this chemical in other biological systems. This procedure seems to be of qualitative value in a preliminary screening of potential carcinogens.

A00263.title: amic acids
A00263.definition: Carbamoyl carboxylic acids, i.e. compounds containing a carboxy and a carboxamide group, e.g. 5-carbamoylnicotinic acid.

A00265.title: amide oximes
A00265.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RC(NH2)=NOH}$ and derivatives formed by substitution; formally the oximes of carboxamides.

A00266.title: amides
A00266.definition: Derivatives of oxoacids $\ce{R_{k}E(=O)_{l}(OH)_{m}}\ (l \neq 0)$ in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group. Chalcogen replacement analogues are called thio-, seleno- and telluro-amides. Compounds having one, two or three acyl groups on a given nitrogen are generically included and may be designated as primary, secondary and tertiary amides, respectively, e.g.  benzamide, N,N-dimethylmethanesulfonamide,  secondary amides (see imides),  tertiary amides,  phenylphosphonamidic acid.Notes:Amides with $\ce{NH2}$, $\ce{NHR}$ and $\ce{NR2}$ groups should not be distinguished by means of the terms primary, secondary and tertiary.Derivatives of certain acidic compounds $\ce{R_{n}E(OH)_{m}}$, where $\ce{E}$ is not carbon (e.g. sulfenic acids, $\ce{RSOH}$, phosphinous acids, $\ce{R2POH)}$, having the structure $\ce{R_{n}E(NR2)_{m}}$ may be named as amides but do not belong to the class amides proper, e.g. $\ce{CH3CH2SNH2}$ ethanesulfenamide or ethylsulfanylamine.The term applies also to metal derivatives of ammonia and amines, in which a cation replaces a hydrogen atom on nitrogen. Such compounds are also called azanides, e.g.  lithium diisopropylamide, synonym lithium diisopropylazanide.See also: carboxamides, lactams, peptides, phosphoramides, sulfonamides

A00267.title: amidines
A00267.definition: Derivatives of oxoacids $\ce{R_{n}E(=O)OH}$ in which the hydroxy group is replaced by an amino group and the oxo group is replaced by $\ce{=NR}$. Amidines include carboxamidines, sulfinamidines and phosphinamidines, $\ce{R2P(=NR)NR2}$. In organic chemistry an unspecified amidine is commonly a carboxamidine.

A00268.title: amidium ions
A00268.definition: Cations formally derived by the addition of one hydron to the $\ce{N}$ or $\ce{O}$ atom of an amide and $N$-hydrocarbyl derivatives thereof. In organic chemistry an unspecified amidium ion is commonly a carboxamidium ion  or  The term does not imply knowledge concerning the position of the cationic centre, e.g. $\ce{PhC(=O)N^{+}Me3}$ N,N,N-trimethylbenzamidium.

A00269.title: amidrazones
A00269.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RC(=NH)NHNH2}$ or $\ce{RC(NH2)=NNH2}$, formally derived from carboxylic acids. These tautomers are named hydrazide imides and amide hydrazones, respectively. Also included are $N$-hydrocarbyl derivatives.

A00270.title: aminals
A00270.definition: Compounds having two amino groups bonded to the same carbon, $\ce{R2C(NR2)2}$. Also called geminal diamines. [The term aminal has also been used, with consequent ambiguity, for $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}amino}$ ethers (hemiaminal ethers); such use is discouraged.]

A00271.title: amine imides
A00271.definition: Compounds formally derived from the attachment of an amine $\ce{R3N}$ to a nitrene $\ce{RN{:}}$ . The structure $\ce{R3N^{+}–N−R}$ expresses the 1,2-dipolar character of amine imides. They may be named systematically as substituted diazan-2-ium-1-ides, e.g. $\ce{Me3N^{+}–N−Me}$, 1,2,2,2-tetramethyldiazan-2-ium-1-ide or trimethylamine $N$-methylimide.

A00273.title: amine oxides
A00273.definition: Compounds derived from tertiary amines by the attachment of one oxygen atom to the nitrogen atom $\ce{R3N^{+}–O^{−}}$. By extension the term includes the analogous derivatives of primary and secondary amines.

A00274.title: amines
A00274.definition: Compounds formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups, and having the general structures $\ce{RNH2}$ (primary amines), $\ce{R2NH}$ (secondary amines), $\ce{R3N}$ (tertiary amines).

A00277.title: aminium ions
A00277.definition: Cations $\ce{HR3N^{+}}$ formed by hydronation of an amine $\ce{R3N}$. 'Non-quaternary ammonium ions' is a synonymous term, e.g. prolinium, $\ce{PhN^{+}HMe2}$, $N,N$-dimethylanilinium.

A00278.title: aminiumyl radical ions
A00278.definition: Radicals cations, $\ce{R3N^{.+}}$, derivable from aminium ions, $\ce{R3NH^{+}}$, by removal of a hydrogen atom. Aminiumyl radical ions are, except for $\ce{H3N^{.+}}$, synonymous with the ammoniumyl radical ions. As the term ammonium is well known, ammoniumyl radical ions is the more desirable class name.

15245.title: amino polymer
15245.definition: Polymer prepared by polycondensation of an amino component such as amine or amide with an aldehyde, or by curing reactive oligomers prepared from an amino component and an aldehyde.

A00283.title: amino sugars
A00283.definition: Monosaccharides having one alcoholic hydroxy group (commonly but not necessarily in position 2) replaced by an amino group; systematically known as $x$-amino-$x$-deoxymonosaccharides. (Glycosylamines are excluded.) E.g. ᴅ-glucosamine or 2-amino-2-deoxy-ᴅ-glucopyranose.

A00279.title: amino-acid residue
A00279.definition: When two or more amino acids combine to form a peptide, the elements of water are removed, and what remains of each amino acid is called an amino-acid residue. $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}Amino-acid}$ residues are therefore structures that lack a hydrogen atom of the amino group ($\ce{–NH–CHR–COOH}$), or the hydroxyl moiety of the carboxyl group ($\ce{NH2–CHR–CO\bond{–}}$), or both ($\ce{–NH–CHR–COO\bond{–}}$); all units of a peptide chain are therefore amino-acid residues. (Residues of amino acids that contain two amino groups or two carboxyl groups may be joined by isopeptide bonds, and so may not have the formulas shown.) The residue in a peptide that has an amino group that is free, or at least not acylated by another amino-acid residue (it may, for example, be acylated or formylated), is called N-terminal; it is at the N-terminus. The residue that has a free carboxyl group, or at least does not acylate another amino-acid residue, (it may, for example, acylate ammonia to give $\ce{–NH–CHR–CO–NH2}$), is called C-terminal.

A00284.title: aminoxides
A00284.definition: The anion $\ce{H2N–O^{−}}$, aminoxide and its $\ce{N}$ hydrocarbyl derivatives $\ce{R2N–O^{−}}$; formally derived from hydroxylamines, $\ce{R2N–OH}$, by removing a hydron from the hydroxy group, e.g. $\ce{(CH3)2N–O^{−}}$ dimethylaminoxide.

A00285.title: aminoxyl radicals
A00285.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R2N–O^{.}  R2N^{.+}–O^{−}}$; they are radicals derived from hydroxylamines by removal of the hydrogen atom from the hydroxy group, and are in many cases isolable. The synonymous terms 'nitroxyl radicals' and 'nitroxides' erroneously suggest the presence of a nitro group; their use is not desirable. Example, $\ce{(ClCH2)2N–O^{.}}$ bis(chloromethyl)aminoxyl.

08917.title: aminoxyl-mediated radical polymerization
08917.definition: Stable-radical-mediated polymerization in which the deactivation of the radicals involves reversible coupling with aminoxyl radicals.

A00289.title: aminyl radicals
A00289.definition: The nitrogen-centered radical $\ce{H2N^{.}}$, formally derived by the removal of a hydrogen atom from ammonia, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives $\ce{R2N^{.}}$.

A00293.title: ammoniumyl radical ions
A00293.definition: $\ce{H3N^{.+}}$ and its hydrocarbyl derivatives, e.g. $\ce{(CH3)3N^{.+}}$ trimethylammoniumyl, $\ce{PhN^{.+}H2}$ phenylammoniumyl or benzenaminiumyl.

11578.title: amnesia
11578.definition: Partial or total, transient or permanent loss of memory.

11579.title: amnesic shellfish poisoning
11579.definition: Human illness caused by consumption of the marine toxin domoic acid that may lead to dizziness, confusion, motor weakness and seizures, with permanent cognitive impairment and short term memory loss.

10366.title: amniocentesis
10366.definition: Transabdominal procedure in which amniotic fluid is sampled by means of a needle inserted into the amniotic sac.

10367.title: amniochorionic membrane
10367.definition: Composite membrane, formed by fusion of the amnion, interiorly, with the outer chorion that surrounds the developing fetus.

10368.title: amnion
10368.definition: Membrane that lines the amniotic cavity (amniotic sac) and encloses the embryo of a mammal, bird, or reptile.

10369.title: amniote
10369.definition: Any vertebrate animal, such as a reptile, bird, or mammal, that possesses an amnion, chorion, and allantois during embryonic development.

10370.title: amniotic cavity
10370.definition: Fluid-filled space that surrounds the developing embryo of a mammal, bird, or reptile, bounded by the amniotic sac.

09635.title: amniotic fluid
09635.definition: Fluid that surrounds the foetus in the amniotic sac.

10371.title: amniotic sac
10371.definition: Membranous structure in amniotes, within which the embryo and fetus develop.

A00294.title: amorphous carbon
A00294.definition: A carbon material without long-range crystalline order. Short-range order exists, but with deviations of the interatomic distances and/or interbonding angles with respect to the graphite lattice as well as to the diamond lattice.

08565.title: amorphous material transmitting infrared radiation
08565.definition: Amorphous glasses made from elements of groups 4, 5 and 6 of the Periodic Table that transmit infrared radiation.

12743.title: amorphous state
12743.definition: State of matter characterised by the absence of long-range molecular order.

A00295.title: amount concentration
A00295.definition: Amount of a constituent divided by the volume of the mixture. Also called amount-of-substance concentration, substance concentration (in clinical chemistry) and in older literature molarity. For entities B it is often denoted by \(\left[\rm{B}\right]\). The common unit is mole per cubic decimetre (\(\pu{mol dm-3}\)) or mole per litre (\(\pu{mol L-1}\)) sometimes denoted by \(M\).

A00296.title: amount fraction
A00296.definition: Amount of a constituent divided by the total amount of all constituents in the mixture. It is also called mole fraction. Amount fraction is equal to the 'number fraction': the number of entities of one constituent divided by the total number of entities in the mixture.

A00297.title: amount of substance
A00297.definition: The amount of substance, symbol \(n\), of a system is a measure of the number of specified elementary entities. An elementary entity may be an atom, a molecule, an ion, an electron, any other particle or specified group of particles.

A00300.title: ampere
A00300.definition: The ampere, symbol \(\rm{A}\), is the SI unit of electric current. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the elementary charge \(e\) to be \(1.602\ 176\ 634\times10^{-19}\) when expressed in the unit \(\rm{C}\), which is equal to \(\rm{A s}\), where the second is defined in terms of ΔνCs.

A00301.title: amperometric detection method
A00301.definition: A detection method in which the current is proportional to the concentration of the species generating the current.

09128.title: amperometry
09128.definition: Electrochemical measurement principle based on measurement of current at a controlled applied potential.

10372.title: amphibian metamorphosis assay
10372.definition: Procedure in which a frog (often _027793_) is exposed to a substance starting at the tadpole stage, and the growth and development of the animals is studied.

A00302.title: amphipathic
A00302.definition: The property of surface activity is usually due to the fact that the molecules of the substance are amphipathic or amphiphilic, meaning that each contains both a hydrophilic and a hydrophobic (lipophilic) group. This assumes that one of the two phases is aqueous, and the other non-aqueous. If both are non-aqueous (e.g. oil/air), molecules containing organophilic and organophobic groups may be amphipathic and surface active.

13795.title: amphiphile
13795.definition: Substance made up of molecules containing groups that are solvophilic and other groups that are solvophobic with respect to a given solvent.

A00303.title: amphiphilic
A00303.definition:
A term used to describe a compound containing a large organic cation or anion which possesses a long unbranched hydrocarbon chain, e.g. 
$\ce{CH3(CH2)_{n}CO2^{−}M^{+}}$$\ce{CH3(CH2)_{n}N^{+}(CH3)3X^{−}}$ ($n \gt 7$)$\ce{CH3(CH2)_{n}SO3^{−}M^{+}}$.The existence of distinct polar (hydrophilic) and nonpolar (hydrophobic) regions in the molecule promotes the formation of micelles in dilute aqueous solution.

A00304.title: amphiprotic solvent
A00304.definition: Self-ionizing solvent possessing both characteristics of Brønsted acids and bases, for example $\ce{H2O}$ and $\ce{CH3OH}$, in contrast to aprotic solvent.

AT07196.title: ampholytic polymer
AT07196.definition: Polyelectrolyte composed of macromolecules containing both cationic and anionic groups, or corresponding ionizable groups.

A00306.title: amphoteric
A00306.definition: A chemical species that behaves both as an acid and as a base is called amphoteric. This property depends upon the medium in which the species is investigated: $\ce{H2SO4}$ is an acid when studied in water, but becomes amphoteric in superacids.

09685.title: amplification of deoxyribonucleic acid
09685.definition: Process of producing multiple copies of a deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequence by the repeated copying of a DNA segment.

A00307.title: amplification reaction
A00307.definition: A reaction which replaces the conventional reaction used in a particular determination so that a more favourable measurement can be made. The sequence can be repeated to provide a further favourable increase in measurement.

08566.title: amplitude modulation
08566.definition: Modulation of the amplitude of a beam of electromagnetic radiation; by the movement of a moving mirror in a rapid scan Fourier-transform spectrometer or by a mechanical chopper in other spectrometers.

A00310.title: amplitude of alternating current
A00310.definition: Half the peak-to-peak amplitude of a sinusoidal alternating current.

A00311.title: amplitude of alternating voltage
A00311.definition: This term should denote half of the peak-to-peak amplitude. Peak-to-peak and r.m.s. amplitudes should be so specified.

10373.title: ampulla
10373.definition: Flask-like dilatation of a canal or duct.

11580.title: amygdala
11580.definition: Brain nucleus located in the median temporal lobe that is part of the limbic system and plays an important role in emotional responses.

12869.title: amyloid
12869.definition: Fibrous protein secreted into the extracellular space where it forms amorphous deposits in multiple organs in some pathological states.

11582.title: amyloid plaque
11582.definition: Structure representing extracellular deposition of $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}amyloid protein}$ in the gray matter of the brain that occurs with aging and in increased amount in Alzheimer disease.

11583.title: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
11583.definition: Debilitating degenerative disease of the motor neurons characterized by progressive muscle weakness, muscle atrophy and fasciculations, muscle spasticity, difficulty speaking (dysarthria), difficulty swallowing (dysphagia), and difficulty breathing (dyspnea).

A00314.title: anabolism
A00314.definition: The processes of metabolism that result in the synthesis of cellular components from precursors of low molecular weight.

14441.title: anadromy
14441.definition: Life-history pattern that is characterized by egg incubation and early juvenile development in freshwater, migration to seawater for adult development, and a return to freshwater for spawning.

A00315.title: anaerobe
A00315.definition: An organism that does not need free-form oxygen for growth. Many anaerobes are even sensitive to free oxygen. Obligate (strict) anaerobes grow only in the absence of oxygen. Facultative anaerobes can grow either in the presence or in the absence of molecular oxygen.

A00317.title: anaesthetic
A00317.definition: Substance which produces loss of feeling or sensation: general anaesthetic produces loss of consciousness; local or regional anaesthetic renders a specific area insensible to pain.

10374.title: anal canal
10374.definition: Terminal part of the large intestine between the rectum and anus.

10375.title: anal membrane
10375.definition: In the embryo, dorsal part of the cloacal membrane after its division of the urorectal septum.

A00318.title: analgesic
A00318.definition: Substance which relieves pain, without causing loss of consciousness.

12618.title: analogue
12618.definition: Chemical compound having structural similarity to a reference compound.

A00319.title: analogue metabolism
A00319.definition: Process by which a normally non-biodegradable compound is biodegraded in the presence of a structurally similar compound which can induce the necessary enzymes.

A00320.title: analogue to digital converter (pulse)
A00320.definition: A pulse amplitude analyser which, for each pulse processed, produces an integer proportional to the height of that pulse.

12619.title: analogue-based drug discovery
12619.definition: Strategy for drug discovery and/or optimization in which structural modification of an existing drug provides a new drug with improved chemical and/or biological properties.

09392.title: analyser blanking
09392.definition: Action to prevent secondary ions from travelling through the mass spectrometer and being detected.

09218.title: analysis area
09218.definition: Two-dimensional region of a sample surface measured in the plane of that surface, from which the entire analytical signal or a specified fraction of that signal is detected.

09219.title: analysis area
09219.definition: Two-dimensional region of a sample surface at the analytical point, but set in the plane at right angles to the spectrometer axis, from which the entire analytical signal or a specified fraction of that signal is detected.

14442.title: analysis plan
14442.definition: Scheme that defines the exact format and design of the assessment, explicitly states the data needed, and describes the methods and design for analyzing these data.

A00331.title: analyte
A00331.definition: The component of a system to be analysed.

08450.title: analyte transport rate
08450.definition: Mass of analyte reaching the plasma per unit time.

15459.title: analytic study
15459.definition: Study designed to examine associations, commonly putative or hypothesized causal relationships.

08003.title: analytical chemistry
08003.definition: Scientific discipline that develops and applies strategies, instruments, and procedures to obtain information on the composition and nature of matter in space and time.

A00332.title: analytical function
A00332.definition: A function which relates the measured value \(\hat{C}_{\rm{a}}\) to the instrument reading, \(X\), with the value of all interferants, \(C_{i}\), remaining constant. This function is expressed by the following regression of the calibration results. \[\hat{C}_{\rm{a}} = f\left(X\right)\] The analytical function is taken as equal to the inverse of the calibration function.

A00333.title: analytical instrument
A00333.definition: A device or a combination of devices used to carry out an analytical process. The analytical process is all or part of the analytical procedure that encompasses all steps from the introduction of the sample or the test portion to the production of the result. An analytical instrument may carry out single or multiple analytical procedures. In the latter case it may be selective, i.e. designed to carry out any requested combination of procedures within the set, on each specimen.

A00334.title: analytical intercomparison
A00334.definition: A procedure which gives insight to the accuracy of results of analytical procedures by comparing the results obtained in the analyses of identical samples at different laboratories and preferably with different analytical methods.

15313.title: analytical method
15313.definition: Class of experimental procedures for solubility determination in which a saturated solution is prepared and then analyzed to determine composition.

A00336.title: analytical pyrolysis
A00336.definition: The characterization, in an inert atmosphere, of a material or a chemical process by a chemical degradation reaction(s) induced by thermal energy.

A00337.title: analytical quality control
A00337.definition: Procedures which give insight into the precision and accuracy of analysis results.

A00338.title: analytical radiochemistry
A00338.definition: That part of analytical chemistry in which the application of radioactivity is an essential step in the analytical procedures. Synonymous with radioanalytical chemistry.

08006.title: analytical run
08006.definition: Set of measurements of the same quantity performed under repeatability conditions of measurement.

08055.title: analytical selectivity
08055.definition: Selectivity of a measuring system in analytical chemistry.

A00342.title: analytical unit
A00342.definition: An assembly of subunits comprising: suitable apparatus permitting the introduction and removal of the gas, liquid or solid to be analysed and/or calibration materials; a measuring cell or other apparatus which, from the physical or chemical properties of the components of the material to be analysed, gives signals allowing their identification and/or measurement; signal processing devices (amplification, recording) or, if need be, data processing devices.

12870.title: anamnestic
12870.definition: Describing immunological memory that gives rise to a rapid increase in immunological response after reexposure to antigen.

10376.title: anamniote
10376.definition: Any vertebrate animal, such as a fish or amphibian, that lacks an amnion, chorion, and allantois during embryonic development.

10377.title: anaphase
10377.definition: Stage of mitosis and meiosis in which the chromosomes move from the equatorial plate toward opposite ends of the nuclear spindle.

10378.title: anaphase lag
10378.definition: Slowing or stopping of normal migration of chromosomes during anaphase, resulting in chromosomes being excluded from one of the daughter cells causing aneuploidy.

12871.title: anaphylactic shock
12871.definition: Immediate overreaction of the immune system to a drug or other agent in an individual who has previously encountered the agent and has produced antibodies to that agent.

12873.title: anaphylatoxin
12873.definition: Complement-derived protein fragment (e.g., C3a, C4a, or C5a) capable of directly triggering mast cell degranulation, chemotaxis, smooth muscle contraction, and inflammation.

12874.title: anaphylaxis
12874.definition: Life-threatening type I hypersensitivity allergic reaction occurring in a person or animal exposed to an antigen or hapten to which they have previously been sensitized.

15460.title: anaplasia
15460.definition: Loss of normal cell differentiation, a feature characteristic of most malignancies.

10379.title: anasarca
10379.definition: Generalized edema in the subcutaneous connective tissue.

10380.title: anastomosis
10380.definition: Connection creating continuity between two tubular body structures, e.g. blood vessels or loops of bowel.

AT06766.title: anation
AT06766.definition: Replacement of the ligand water by an anion in a coordination entity.

10382.title: anchoring villus
10382.definition: Chorionic villus that is attached to the region of the endometrium (see also decidua) that interacts with the trophoblast during development of the placenta.

10383.title: androblastoma
10383.definition: Rare benign tumor of the testis histologically resembling the fetal testis: the epithelium contains Sertoli cells that may produce estrogen and cause feminization.

10384.title: androgen
10384.definition: Substance, such as a naturally occurring steroid hormone, that binds to androgen receptors to activate the male accessory sex organs and induce male secondary sexual characteristics.

10386.title: androgen receptor
10386.definition: Nuclear receptor that is activated by binding of testosterone or dihydrotestosterone.

10387.title: androstenedione
10387.definition: Steroid hormone produced in the adrenal glands and gonads as a common precursor of male (testosterone) and female (estrogen) sex hormones.

10388.title: anemia
10388.definition: Decrease in the number of erythrocytes or total hemoglobin in the blood that results in a decrease in the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood, sometimes inducing pallor and fatigue.

10389.title: anencephalus
10389.definition: Fetus lacking all or most of the neural tissues of brain.

10390.title: anencephaly
10390.definition: Congenital absence of a major portion of the brain and its meninges, skull, and scalp that results from abnormal embryonic development.

12875.title: anergy
12875.definition: Lack of an immune response, usually taken as lack of response to common recall antigens.

A00344.title: aneroid barometer
A00344.definition: An instrument for monitoring the atmospheric pressure in which no liquid is employed, but rather changes in pressure between the atmosphere and a closed vessel bend a diaphram which moves a pointer on a scale.

11585.title: anesthetic
11585.definition: Substance that reduces the experience of pain with or without loss of consciousness.

10391.title: anestrus
10391.definition: Interval of sexual inactivity between two periods of estrus.

10393.title: aneuploid
10393.definition: Referring to a cell or organism with missing or extra chromosomes or parts of chromosomes, and thus an abnormal number of chromosomes that is not an exact multiple of the haploid number.

10395.title: aneurysm
10395.definition: Abnormal bulging of the wall of an artery or a chamber of the heart.

A00345.title: Anger camera
A00345.definition: A camera in which a large diameter scintillator is coupled to an array of photomultiplier tubes by fibre optics. X-ray imaging may also be achieved in multi-crystal cameras where many small crystals individually scintillate.

10396.title: angioblast
10396.definition:
Cell taking part in blood vessel formation.
Primordial mesenchymal tissue from which embryonic blood cells and vascular endothelium are differentiated.

12876.title: angioedema
12876.definition: Swelling that occurs in the tissue just below the surface of the skin, most often around the lips and eyes, the mucous membranes and occasionally the viscera.

10397.title: angiogenesis
10397.definition: Development of new blood vessels in the embryo or from pre-existing vessels; formation of capillary networks.

11586.title: angiography
11586.definition: Radiography of blood or lymph vessels, following the introduction of a radio-opaque substance.

10398.title: angiotensin converting enzyme
10398.definition: Enzyme (EC 3.4.15.1) that converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II, causing blood vessels to constrict thus increasing blood pressure.

A00346.title: angle
A00346.definition: The angle between two half-lines terminating at the same point is the ratio of the length of the included arc of the circle (with its centre at that point) to the radius of the circle. Symbols: \(\alpha \), \(\beta \), \(\gamma \) ... This is a quantity of dimension one with the SI unit radian (\(\pu{rad}\)), but very often degrees of arc are used.

09220.title: angle lapping
09220.definition: Sample preparation in which a sample is mechanically polished at an angle to the original surface.

09221.title: angle of emission
09221.definition: Angle between the trajectory of a particle or photon, as it leaves a surface, and the local or average surface normal.

08222.title: angle of incidence
08222.definition: Angle between a beam of electromagnetic radiation and a line normal to a surface.

A00348.title: angle of optical rotation
A00348.definition: Angle through which plane polarized light is rotated clockwise, as seen when facing the light source, in passing through an optically active medium.

15152.title: angle of repose
15152.definition: Characteristic angle of slope formed with the horizontal by the side of a static conical mound of powder.

A00349.title: angle strain
A00349.definition: Strain due to a departure in bond angle from 'normal' values. The term is often used in the context of non-aromatic cyclic compounds in which the internal angles differ from the regular tetrahedral angle of \(109^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\,28^{\prime }\); in this sense angle strain is also known as 'Baeyer strain'.

A00351.title: angular distribution
A00351.definition: With reference to the center of mass, the products of a bimolecular reaction are scattered with respect to the initial velocity vector, and the distribution of scattering angles is known as the angular distribution.

A00352.title: angular frequency
A00352.definition: Frequency multiplied by $2\uppi\!$. Also called pulsatance. It was formerly called circular frequency.

A00353.title: angular momentum
A00353.definition: Angular momentum, or moment of momentum of a particle about a point is a vector quantity equal to the vector product of the position vector of the particle and its momentum, \(L=r\times p\). For special angular momenta of particles in atomic and molecular physics different symbols are used.

AT06986.title: angular overlap model
AT06986.definition: A method of description of transition metal–ligand interactions and main group stereochemistry, whose basic assumption is that the strength of a bond formed using atomic orbitals on two atoms is related to the magnitude of overlap of the two orbitals.

A00355.title: anhydro bases
A00355.definition: Compounds resulting from internal acid–base neutralization (with loss of water) in iminium hydroxides containing an acidic site conjugated with the iminium function.

A00356.title: anilides
A00356.definition: Compounds derived from oxoacids $\ce{R_{k}E(=O)_{l}(OH)_{m}}\ (l \neq 0)$ by replacing an $\ce{OH}$ group by the NHPh group or derivative formed by ring substitution; N-phenyl amides, e.g. $\ce{CH3C(=O)NHPh}$ acetanilide.See: amidesSalts formed by replacement of a nitrogen-bound hydron of aniline by a metal or other cation, e.g. $\ce{NaNHPh}$ sodium anilide.

A00357.title: anils
A00357.definition: A term for the subclass of Schiff bases $\ce{R2C=NR'}$, where $\ce{R'}$ = phenyl or substituted phenyl group. Thus, $N$-phenyl imines.

A00358.title: anion
A00358.definition: A monoatomic or polyatomic species having one or more elementary charges of the electron.

A00359.title: anion exchange
A00359.definition: The process of exchanging anions between a solution and an anion exchanger.

A00360.title: anion exchanger
A00360.definition: Ion exchanger with anions as counter-ions. The term anion-exchange resin may be used in the case of solid organic polymers. The base form of an anion exchanger is the ionic form in which the counter-ions are hydroxide groups ($\ce{OH–}$ form) or the ionogenic groups form an uncharged base, e.g. $\ce{-NH2}$.

08989.title: anion-activated-monomer polymerization
08989.definition: Activated-monomer polymerization where the propagating species is an electrophile and activating species is anionic.

08977.title: anionic group-transfer polymerization
08977.definition: Anionic polymerization in which a specific atom or group is intramolecularly transferred to remain associated with the active chain-end during the course of polymerization.

AT07198.title: anionic polymer
AT07198.definition: Polymer composed of negatively charged macromolecules and an equivalent amount of counter-cations.

A00361.title: anionic polymerization
A00361.definition: An ionic polymerization in which the kinetic-chain carriers are anions.

08978.title: anionic ring-opening polymerization
08978.definition: Anionic polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

A00362.title: anionotropic rearrangement
A00362.definition: A rearrangement in which the migrating group moves with its electron pair from one atom to another.

08223.title: anisotropic
08223.definition: Having properties that depend on direction.

08567.title: anisotropic Raman scattering
08567.definition: Raman scattering by the anisotropic part of the derived polarizability tensor.

AT06776.title: anisotropy
AT06776.definition: The property of molecules and materials to exhibit variations in physical properties along different molecular axes of the substance.

10399.title: ankyloglossia
