10399.definition: Congenital oral anomaly, in which the lingual frenulum (the membrane connecting the underside of the tongue to the floor of the mouth) is unusually short and thick.

12877.title: ankylosing spondylitis
12877.definition: Chronic inflammatory disease affecting the spine, sacroiliac joints, and large peripheral joints, having a major genetic predisposition.

09447.title: annealing
09447.definition: Thermal treatment of a solid polymer material at a fixed or changing temperature that leads to desired changes in its physical structure and properties without involving complete melting or dissolution.

A00365.title: annelation
A00365.definition: Alternative, but less desirable term for annulation. The term is widely used in the German and French languages.

A00366.title: annihilation
A00366.definition: An interaction between a particle and its antiparticle in which they both disappear.

A00367.title: annulation
A00367.definition: A transformation involving fusion of a new ring to a molecule via two new bonds. Some authors use the term 'annelation' for the fusion of an additional ring to an already existing one, and 'annulation' for the formation of a ring from one or several acyclic precursors, but this distinction is not made generally.

A00368.title: annulenes
A00368.definition: Mancude monocyclic hydrocarbons without side chains of the general formula $\ce{C_{n}H_{n}}$ ($n$ is an even number) or $\ce{C_{n}H_{n+1}}$ ($n$ is an odd number). In systematic nomenclature an annulene with seven or more carbon atoms may be named [$n$]annulene, where $n$ is the number of carbon atoms, e.g. annulene for cyclonona-1,3,5,7-tetraene.

A00369.title: annulenylidenes
A00369.definition: Carbenes, derived by formal insertion of a divalent carbon atom into an even-membered annulene, e.g. cycloheptatrienylidene:

11587.title: annulus
11587.definition: Tough outer ring of an intervertebral disc.

A00370.title: anode
A00370.definition: Electrode at which oxidation takes place.

09152.title: anodic stripping voltammetry
09152.definition: Stripping voltammetry in which material accumulated at the working electrode is electrochemically oxidized in the stripping step.

A00371.title: anodic transfer coefficient
A00371.definition: Defined by analogy with cathodic transfer coefficient.

10400.title: anodontia
10400.definition: Congenital absence of all primary or permanent teeth.

10401.title: anogenital distance
10401.definition: Distance along the perineum between the anus and the base of the vagina or penis, or in the fetus between the anus and the base of the genital tubercle.

08568.title: anomalous dispersion
08568.definition: Changes in real refractive index of a material in the vicinity of an absorption band in which real refractive index decreases markedly with decreasing wavenumber on the high wavenumber side of an absorption band, then increases rapidly through the band centre and decreases markedly on the low wavenumber side of the band, before resuming normal dispersion at wavenumbers far from the band.

16244.title: anomalous liquid junction potential
16244.definition: Electrochemical potential that arises at the reference electrode–measurement solution interface when, during a potentiometric measurement, the filling solution of the salt bridge of the reference electrode contacts the charged particles of a suspension.

08569.title: anomalously polarized Raman band
08569.definition: Raman band with a depolarization ratio greater than \(\pu{0.75}\), as is frequently observed in surface-enhanced resonance Raman spectroscopy.

A00372.title: anomeric effect
A00372.definition: Originally the thermodynamic preference for polar groups bonded to C-1 (the anomeric carbon of a glycopyranosyl derivative) to take up an axial position.  This effect is now considered to be a special case of a general preference (the generalized anomeric effect) for synclinal (gauche) conformations about the bond C–Y in the system X–C–Y–C where X and Y are heteroatoms having nonbonding electron pairs, commonly at least one of which is nitrogen, oxygen or fluorine. For example in chloro(methoxy)methane the anomeric effect stabilizes the synclinal conformation.  In alkyl glycopyranosides the anomeric effect operates at two sites (i) along the endocyclic C-1 oxygen bond (endo-anomeric effect) and (ii) along the exocyclic C-1 oxygen bond (exo-anomeric effect). The opposite preference is claimed for some systems, e.g., glycopyranosyltrialkylammonium salts, and has been referred to as the reverse anomeric effect.

09808.title: anomeric hydroxy group
09808.definition: Hydroxy group that originates from the aldehydic or ketonic group of a monosaccharide after ring closure.

A00373.title: anomers
A00373.definition: Diastereoisomers of glycosides, hemiacetals or related cyclic forms of sugars, or related molecules differing in configuration only at C-1 of an aldose, C-2 of a 2-ketose, etc.

10404.title: anophthalmia
10404.definition: Congenital absence of one or both eyeballs.

10405.title: anorchism
10405.definition: Congenital absence of one or both testes.

10406.title: anorectal
10406.definition: Relating to the anus and rectum.

11588.title: anorexia
11588.definition: Eating disorder characterized by self-imposed food restriction.

11589.title: anorexia nervosa
11589.definition: Eating disorder characterized by obsessive desire to lose weight by reducing food intake or by repeated vomiting.

11590.title: anosmia
11590.definition: Loss of the sense of smell, either total or selective.

10407.title: anotia
10407.definition: Congenital absence of the (outer ear) pinna, often with narrowing or absence of the ear canal.

10408.title: anovulation
10408.definition: Failure of the ovaries to produce, to facilitate maturation of, or to release ova.

A00374.title: ansa compounds
A00374.definition: Benzene derivatives having para positions (or meta) bridged by a chain (commonly 10 to 12 atoms long) (Latin ansa, handle). By extension, any arene bridged by a chain constrained to lie over one of the two faces of the arene.

A00375.title: antagonism
A00375.definition: Combined effect of two or more factors which is smaller than the solitary effect of any one of those factors. In bioassays, the term may be used when a specified response is produced by exposure to either of two factors but not by exposure to both together.

A00376.title: antagonist
A00376.definition: Substance that reverses or reduces the effect induced by an agonist.Substance that attaches to and blocks cell receptors that normally bind naturally occurring substances.

A00377.title: antarafacial
A00377.definition: When a part of a molecule ('molecular fragment') undergoes two changes in bonding (bond-making or bond-breaking), either to a common centre or to two related centres, external to itself, these bonding changes may be related in one of two spatially different ways. These are designated as 'antarafacial' if opposite faces of the molecular fragment are involved, and 'suprafacial' if both changes occur at the same face. The concept of 'face' is clear from the diagrams in the cases of planar (or approximately planar) frameworks with isolated or interacting p-orbitals [diagrams (a) and (b)].  The terms antarafacial and suprafacial are, however, also employed in cases in which the essential part of the molecular fragment undergoing changes in bonding comprises two atoms linked only by a $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bond}$. In these cases it is customary to refer to the phases of the local $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bonding}$ orbital: occurrence of the two bonding changes at sites of like orbital phase is regarded as suprafacial, whereas that at two sites of opposite phase is antarafacial. The possibilities are shown for $\ce{C–C}$ and $\ce{C–H}$ $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bonds}$ in diagrams (c) and (d). There may be two distinct and alternative stereochemical outcomes of a suprafacial process involving a $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bond}$ between saturated carbon atoms, i.e. either retention or inversion at both centres. The antarafacial process results in inversion at one centre and retention at the second. For examples of the use of these terms, see cycloaddition, sigmatropic rearrangement.

A00378.title: anthelmintic
A00378.definition: Substance intended to kill parasitic intestinal worms, such as helminths.

A00379.title: anthocyanidins
A00379.definition: Aglycons of anthocyanins; they are oxygenated derivatives of flavylium (2-phenylchromenylium) salts.

A00380.title: anthocyanins
A00380.definition: Plant pigments of the flavonoid class; they are glycosides that on hydrolysis yield coloured aglycons called anthocyanidins.

15461.title: anthracosis
15461.definition: Form of pneumoconiosis caused by accumulation of anthracite carbon deposits in the lungs due to inhalation of smoke or coal dust.

14443.title: anthropogenic
14443.definition:
Caused by or influenced by human activities.
Describing a conversion factor used to calculate a dose or concentration affecting a human that has been derived from data obtained with another species, e.g., the rat.

A00381.title: anti
A00381.definition: In the representation of stereochemical relationships 'anti' means 'on opposite sides' of a reference plane, in contrast to 'syn' which means 'on the same side', as in the following examples.Two substituents attached to atoms joined by a single bond are anti if the torsion angle (dihedral angle) between the bonds to the substituents is greater than $\pu{90\!^{\circ}}$, or syn if it is less than $\pu{90\!^{\circ}}$. (A further distinction is made between antiperiplanar, synperiplanar, anticlinal and synclinal.)In the older literature the terms anti and syn were used to designate stereoisomers of oximes and related compounds. That usage was superseded by the terms 'trans' and 'cis' or E and Z, respectively.When the terms are used in the context of chemical reactions or transformations, they designate the relative orientation of substituents in the substrate or product:Addition to a carbon-carbon double bond:  Alkene-forming elimination:  In the examples described under (1) and (2) anti processes are always antarafacial, and syn processes are suprafacial.

A00390.title: anti-Compton γ-ray spectrometer
A00390.definition: A gamma-ray spectrometer in which the effect of the Compton scattering is at least partly compensated.

12883.title: anti-DNA antibody
12883.definition: Antibody directed against single-stranded or double-stranded DNA.

12884.title: anti-erythrocyte antibody
12884.definition: Antibody against molecules of the red blood cell, usually against membrane proteins, causing lysis of the red blood cells.

12893.title: anti-idiotypic antibody
12893.definition: Antibody raised against antigenic determinants unique to the variable region of a single antibody.

12894.title: anti-isotypic antibody
12894.definition: Antibody against universal features of a given constant (C) region isotype (such as $\upgamma\!$ or $\upmu\!$) of one species that is made by immunizing a member of another species with that isotype.

10413.title: anti-Müllerian hormone
10413.definition: Protein that inhibits the development of the Müllerian ducts (paramesonephric ducts) in the male embryo.

09450.title: anti-reflective coating
09450.definition: Material used in lithography or in other technologies that is applied to a surface in order to reduce reflection.

12900.title: anti-sheep red blood cell IgM response assay
12900.definition: Test to determine T-cell-dependent antibody response, usually by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Sheep red blood cells (SRBCs) are used as an antigen. Often referred to as the plaque assay.

08570.title: anti-Stokes Raman scattering
08570.definition: Raman scattering of electromagnetic radiation in which the scattered radiation has greater energy (greater wavenumber) than the exciting radiation.

A00408.title: anti-Stokes type radiation
A00408.definition: Fluorescence radiation occurring at shorter wavelengths than absorption.

A00382.title: antiaromatic compounds
A00382.definition: Compounds that contain \(4\ n\) (\(n\neq 0\)) $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electrons}$ in a cyclic planar, or nearly planar, system of alternating single and double bonds, e.g. cyclobuta-1,3-diene.

AT06987.title: antiaromaticity
AT06987.definition: Those cyclic molecules for which cyclic electron delocalization provides for the reduction (in some cases, loss) of thermodynamic stability compared to acyclic structural analogues are classified as antiaromatic species. In contrast to aromatic compounds, antiaromatic ones are prone to reactions causing changes in their structural type, and display tendency to alternation of bond lengths and fluxional behavior (see fluxional molecules) both in solution and in the solid. Antiaromatic molecules possess negative (or very low positive) values of resonance energy and a small energy gap between their highest occupied and lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals. In antiaromatic molecules, an external magnetic field induces a paramagnetic electron current. Whereas benzene represents the prototypical aromatic compound, cyclobuta-1,3-diene exemplifies the compound with most clearly defined antiaromatic properties.

A00383.title: antibiotic
A00383.definition: Substance produced by, and obtained from, certain living cells (especially bacteria, yeasts and moulds), or an equivalent synthetic substance, which is biostatic or biocidal at low concentrations to some other form of life, especially pathogenic or noxious organisms.

A00384.title: antibody
A00384.definition: A protein (immunoglobulin) produced by the immune system of an organism in response to exposure to a foreign molecule (antigen) and characterized by its specific binding to a site of that molecule (antigenic determinant or epitope).

12881.title: antibody therapy
12881.definition: Use of an antibody to target specific cells (often tumor cells) or signal transduction pathways (often via chemokines/cytokines) in the treatment of disease.

12879.title: antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity
12879.definition: Cytotoxic reaction in which an antibody-coated target cell is directly killed by an Fc receptor-bearing leukocyte, e.g., NK cell, macrophage, neutrophil, or eosinophil.

12880.title: antibody-forming cell assay
12880.definition: Assay that measures the humoral immune response mediated by the concerted actions of antigen-presenting cells, T lymphocytes, and B lymphocytes, generally by determination of murine primary IgM or IgG antibodies directed against the T-cell-dependent sheep red blood cell (SRBC) surface antigens after in vivo sensitization.

AT06988.title: antibonding molecular orbital
AT06988.definition: The molecular orbital whose occupation by electrons decreases the total bonding (as usual, increases the total energy) of a molecule. The energy level of an antibonding MO lies higher than the average of the valence atomic orbitals of the atoms constituting the molecule.

A00385.title: anticholinergic
A00385.definition: (adjective). Preventing transmission of parasympathetic nerve impulses.(noun). Substance which prevents transmission of parasympathetic nerve impulses.

A00386.title: anticircular elution
A00386.definition: The opposite of circular development. Here the sample as well as the mobile phase is applied at the periphery of a circle and both move towards the centre.

15462.title: anticoagulant
15462.definition: Substance that prevents blood clotting (e.g., warfarin).

A00389.title: anticodon
A00389.definition: A sequence of three nucleotides in the anticodon-loop of a tRNA, which recognizes and binds the complementary triplet sequence (codon) of the mRNA.

11591.title: anticonvulsant
11591.definition: Substance used to prevent or reduce the severity of convulsions.

A00391.title: anticyclone
A00391.definition: A large system of winds that rotate about a centre of high atmospheric pressure, clockwise (viewed from above) in the northern hemisphere and counterclockwise in the southern hemisphere.

15463.title: antidote
15463.definition: Substance capable of specifically counteracting or reducing the effect of a potentially toxic substance in an organism by a relatively specific chemical or pharmacological action.

11593.title: antiemetic
11593.definition: Substance used to prevent nausea and vomiting (emesis).

A00394.title: antigen
A00394.definition: A substance that stimulates the immune system to produce a set of specific antibodies and that combines with the antibody through a specific binding site or epitope.

12887.title: antigen presentation
12887.definition: Display of antigen as peptide fragments bound to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules on the surface of a cell.

12890.title: antigen processing
12890.definition: Cleavage of protein antigens in antigen-presenting cells (APCs).

12891.title: antigen receptor
12891.definition: Specific antigen-binding receptor on T or B lymphocytes that is transcribed and translated following rearrangements and translocation of V, D, and J genes.

12892.title: antigen recognition
12892.definition: Ability of highly specialized proteins of the immune system to recognize antigens and specifically bind to them.

12888.title: antigen-presenting cell
12888.definition: Cell, such as a dendritic cell or macrophage, that is responsible for making antigens accessible to lymphocytes and other immune effector and regulatory cells, making possible specific recognition by receptors on the cell surface.

12889.title: antigen-presenting groove
12889.definition:
1) Pocket in a major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecule that binds antigen for antigen presentation.
2) Hydrophobic binding region in the CD1 protein that anchors lipid-containing antigens causing exposure of the peptide or carbohydrate moiety in a position enabling T-cell receptor (TCR) contact.

12885.title: antigenic
12885.definition: Capable of stimulating lymphocytes to produce antibodies.

09663.title: antigenic determinant
09663.definition: Part of the structure of an antigen molecule that is responsible for specific interaction with antibody molecules evoked by the same or a similar antigen.

12886.title: antigenicity
12886.definition: Ability of an antigen to bind to a specific antibody or T-cell receptor (TCR); often a measure of its ability to produce immunity.

15464.title: antihistamine
15464.definition: Substance that blocks or counteracts the action of histamine.

A00398.title: antimetabolite
A00398.definition: Substance, structurally similar to a metabolite, which competes with it or replaces it, and so prevents or reduces its normal utilization.

12895.title: antimitochondrial antibody
12895.definition: Autoantibody producing a mitochondrial staining pattern on sections of various tissues and on tumor cell monolayers.

10412.title: antimitotic
10412.definition: Referring to inhibition of cell division by mitosis.

A00399.title: antimony–xenon lamp
A00399.definition: An intense source of ultraviolet, visible, and near infra-red radiation produced by an electrical discharge in a mixture of antimony vapour and xenon under high pressure. Its output in the ultraviolet region is higher than that of the mercury–xenon arc.

15465.title: antimuscarinic
15465.definition:
n., Substance inhibiting or preventing the actions of muscarine and muscarine-like agents (e.g., atropine) on the muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.
adj., Inhibiting or preventing the actions of muscarine and muscarine-like agents on the muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.

A00400.title: antimycotic
A00400.definition: Substance used to kill a fungus or to inhibit its growth. Synonymous with fungicide.

11594.title: antineuralgic
11594.definition: Substance used to alleviate the pain of neuralgia.

12896.title: antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibody
12896.definition: Antibody against antigens in the cytoplasm of neutrophils.

12897.title: antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibody associated vasculitis
12897.definition: One of a group of autoimmune systemic vasculitides associated with antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibodies (ANCAs), e.g., Wegener granulomatosis (WG), microscopic polyangiitis, and Churg–Strauss syndrome.

15466.title: antinicotinic
15466.definition:
n., Substance inhibiting or preventing the actions of nicotine and nicotine-like agents (e.g., suxamethonium chloride) on the nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
adj., Inhibiting or preventing the actions of nicotine and nicotine-like agents on the nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.

11595.title: antinociception
11595.definition: Blockage of the perception of pain.

12898.title: antinuclear antibody
12898.definition: Antibody, detectable in the blood, that has the capability of binding to a substance, e.g., DNA, within the nucleus of the cells.

A00401.title: antiparticle
A00401.definition: Of a given particle, a particle with the same rest mass, where the two can annihilate.

12899.title: antiphospholipid syndrome
12899.definition: One of the most common autoimmune diseases, characterized by thrombosis, recurrent spontaneous abortions, and the presence of antiphospholipid antibodies.

A00404.title: antiprismo-
A00404.definition: An affix used in names to denote eight atoms bound into a rectangular antiprism.

11596.title: antipsychotic
11596.definition: Psychoactive substance used to manage psychotic behavior or psychotic ideation.

15467.title: antipyretic
15467.definition: Substance that relieves or reduces fever.

A00405.title: antiresistant
A00405.definition: Substance used as an additive to a pesticide formulation in order to reduce the resistance of insects to the pesticide.

A00406.title: antiserum
A00406.definition: Serum containing antibodies to a particular antigen either because of immunization or after an infectious disease.

08774.title: antisoliton
08774.definition: Soliton with the negative amplitude or opposite spin with respect to a given soliton.

11597.title: antispasmodic
11597.definition: Substance used to prevent muscle spasms.

14444.title: antisymmetry
14444.definition: Quality of a population of bilaterally symmetrical individuals in which the difference in measurement of a trait made from the right and left sides of individuals from that population produces a bimodal distribution.

AT06989.title: antisymmetry principle
AT06989.definition: The postulate that electrons must be described by wavefunctions which are antisymmetric with respect to interchange of the coordinates (including spin) of a pair of electrons. A corollary of the principle is the Pauli exclusion principle. All particles with half-integral spin (fermions) are described by antisymmetric wavefunctions, and all particles with zero or integral spin (bosons) are described by symmetric wavefunctions.

12901.title: antitoxin
12901.definition: Antibody specific for exotoxins produced by certain microorganisms such as the causative agents of diphtheria and tetanus.

10414.title: antrum
10414.definition: Cavity or chamber, often in bone, with specific meanings in some hollow organs (e.g., the pyloric end or gastric antrum of the stomach).

10415.title: anus
10415.definition: External opening of the rectum to the body surface, controlled by the anal sphincter.

11598.title: anxiolytic
11598.definition: Agent that reduces anxiety without causing excessive sedation.

10416.title: aorta
10416.definition: Great artery arising from the left ventricle, being the main trunk from which the systemic arterial system proceeds

10417.title: aorta-gonad-mesonephros region
10417.definition: Region of the vertebrate embryonic mesoderm that gives rise to the genitourinary tract and its blood supply.

10418.title: aortic arch
10418.definition: Curved portion of the aorta between its ascending portion exiting the heart and its descending portion that proceeds to the arteries of the thoracic and abdominal cavities and the lower body.

10419.title: aortopulmonary septum
10419.definition: Spiral septum that, during development, separates the truncus arteriosus into a ventral pulmonary trunk and the ascending aorta dorsally.

A00412.title: apex current
A00412.definition: In measurement of non-faradaic admittance (or tensammetry), a plot of alternating current against applied potential shows a minimum or maximum when a non-electroactive substance undergoes adsorption or desorption at the surface of the indicator electrode. Such a maximum or minimum may be called an 'apex' to emphasize its non-faradaic origin and distinguish it from a 'summit', which would result from a charge-transfer process. The highest value of the current on such an apex may be called an 'apex current', and the corresponding applied potential may be called an 'apex potential'.

10420.title: aphakia
10420.definition: Absence of the lens of the eye, occurring as a congenital defect or as a result of trauma or surgery.

11599.title: aphasia
11599.definition: Difficulty with, or loss of the use of language in reading, writing or speaking owing to specific lesions in the brain.

15468.title: aphid
15468.definition: Common name for a harmful plant parasite in the family Aphididae, some species of which are vectors of plant virus diseases.

A00415.title: apical
A00415.definition: In trigonal bipyramidal structures (e.g. a five-coordinate trigonal bipyramid with phosphorus as central atom) the term apical refers to the two positions that are collinear with the central atom or to the bonds linking these positions to the central atom. The three equivalent bonds (or positions) in a plane passing through the central atom and perpendicular to the direction of the apical bonds are described as equatorial.  The term apical is also used for the bond pointing from the atom at or near the centre of the base to the apex of a pyramidal structure. The positions at or near the base of the pyramid, or the bonds linking those positions to the central atom of the base are described as 'basal'. The apical bonds have also been called axial.

AT06990.title: apicophilicity
AT06990.definition: In trigonal bipyramidal structures with a five-coordinate central atom, the stabilization achieved through a ligand changing its position from equatorial to apical (axial). The apicophilicity of an atom or a group is evaluated by either the energy difference between the stereoisomers (permutational isomers) containing the ligand in apical and equatorial positions or the energy barrier to permutational isomerization (see also Berry pseudorotation). In general, the greater the electronegativity and the stronger the $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$-withdrawing properties of a ligand (as for $\ce{Cl}$, $\ce{F}$, $\ce{CN}$), the higher is its apicophilicity. The notion of apicophilicity has been extended to four-coordinate bisphenoidal and three-coordinate T-shaped structures, which can be viewed as trigonal bipyramidal species where, respectively, one or two vertices are occupied by phantom ligands (lone electron pairs).

15469.title: aplasia
15469.definition: Lack of development of an organ or tissue, or of the cellular products from an organ or tissue.

12902.title: aplastic anemia
12902.definition: Greatly decreased formation of erythrocytes and hemoglobin, usually associated with pronounced granulocytopenia and thrombocytopenia, as a result of hypoplastic or aplastic bone marrow.

11602.title: apneusis
11602.definition: Abnormal breathing pattern consisting of a pause at full inspiration.

A00416.title: apo-
A00416.definition: An unitalicized prefix, preceded by a locant, used to indicate that all of the molecule beyond the carbon atom corresponding to that locant has been replaced by hydrogen atoms.

08224.title: apodization
08224.definition: Technical term for changing the shape of a mathematical function, electrical signal, or optical transmission to remove or smooth a discontinuity at the edges, literally meaning 'removing the foot'.

A00417.title: apoenzyme
A00417.definition: The protein part of an enzyme without the cofactor necessary for catalysis. The cofactor can be a metal ion, an organic molecule (coenzyme), or a combination of both.

AT06767.title: apoprotein
AT06767.definition: A protein without its characteristic prosthetic group or metal.

AT06804.title: apoptosis
AT06804.definition: Active process of programmed cell death requiring metabolic energy, often characterised by fragmentation of DNA, and without associated inflammation.

A00418.title: apparent
A00418.definition: A term, indicated by a superscript ', which means that a process is not well known or that its value carries uncertainties which are not known, e.g. \(\Delta G^{\circ}{'}\) is the apparent standard Gibbs energy change. In the context of partial molar quantities the word is used in a different sense; as a symbol for 'apparent' in this connection the use of subscript \(\varphi \), as in \(Y_{\varphi}\), is recommended. Other notations employed for this property include \(^{\varphi}X\) and \(\varphi_{X}\).

12221.title: apparent molar mass
12221.definition: Molar mass, molecular weight, relative molar mass, or relative molecular mass calculated from experimental data without the application of appropriate corrections.

11535.title: apparent monomer
11535.definition: Monomer which from the name of a polymer appears to have been used in the synthesis of the latter when it has actually been prepared from different precursor(s).

15379.title: apparent rate constant of polymerisation
15379.definition: Measured rate of polymerization divided by the concentration of the reactant (if there is only one) or the product of concentrations of the presumed reactants.

A00420.title: apparent viscosity
A00420.definition: The ratio of stress to rate of strain, calculated from measurements of forces and velocities as though the liquid were Newtonian. If the liquid is actually non-Newtonian, the apparent viscosity depends on the type and dimensions of the apparatus used.

A00421.title: appearance energy
A00421.definition: Refers to ionization of a molecule or atom by electron collision or photon absorption. In mass spectrometry it has often been reported as the voltage which corresponds to the minimum energy of the electrons in the ionizing beam necessary for the production of a given fragment ion. In photoionization it is the minimum energy of the quantum of light which produces ionization of the absorbing molecule.

A00423.title: appearance temperature
A00423.definition: The temperature of the atomization surface at which the analyte signal/noise (S/N) ratio reaches a value of 3 when the quantity of analyte in the atomizer is one hundred times the characteristic mass for peak high absorption.

10421.title: appendicular skeleton
10421.definition: Bones and cartilage that support the appendages, including the bones of the shoulders, upper limbs, pelvis, and lower limbs.

10422.title: appendix
10422.definition:
Tube-shaped sac ('vermiform appendix') attached to and opening into the upper end of the large intestine (cecum) in humans and some other mammals.
Appendage, blind sac, or diverticulum.

15153.title: appertisation
15153.definition: Process by which food is rendered free from pathogenic, toxigenic, and spoilage organisms.

11406.title: applicability domain
11406.definition: The property or structure space for which the predictions of a computational model are considered to be reliable.

A00424.title: applied potential
A00424.definition: The difference of potential measured between identical metallic leads to two electrodes of a cell. The applied potential is divided into two electrode potentials, each of which is the difference of potential existing between the bulk of the solution and the interior of the conducting material of the electrode, an \(i\ R\) or ohmic potential drop through the solution, and another ohmic potential drop through each electrode. In the electroanalytical literature this quantity has often been denoted by the term voltage, whose continued use is not recommended.

11603.title: apraxia
11603.definition: Neurological condition characterized by loss of the ability to perform skilled or purposeful movement that a person is nevertheless physically able and willing to do.

A00425.title: aprotic solvent
A00425.definition: Non-protogenic (in a given situation). (With extremely strong Brønsted acids or bases, solvents that are normally aprotic may accept or lose a proton. For example, acetonitrile is in most instances an aprotic solvent, but it is protophilic in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid and protogenic in the presence of potassium tert-butoxide. Similar considerations apply to benzene, trichloromethane, etc.)

AT07517.title: aquagel
AT07517.definition: Hydrogel in which the network component is a colloidal network.

15314.title: aquamolality
15314.definition: For a solute \(\ce{B}\) in a system containing solvent \(\ce{A}\) and a reference solvent \(\ce{C}\), \[m_{\ce{B}}^{(\ce{C})} = m_{\ce{B}} \overline M/M_{\ce{C}}\] where \(m_{\ce{B}}\) is the molality of \(\ce{B}\), \(M_{\ce{C}}\) is the molar mass of a reference component, and \(\overline{M}\) is the average molar mass of a mixed solvent, defined for a system containing two solvents as \[\overline M = x_{\nu,\ce{A}} M_{\ce{A}} + (1 - x_{\nu,\ce{A}}) M_{\ce{C}}\] the solvent amount fraction of solvent \(\ce{A}\).

A00426.title: aquation
A00426.definition: The incorporation of one or more integral molecules of water into another species with or without displacement of one or more other atoms or groups. For example, the incorporation of water into the inner ligand sphere of an inorganic complex is an aquation reaction.

A00427.title: arachno-
A00427.definition: An affix used in names to designate a boron structure intermediate between nido- and hypho- in degree of openness.

10423.title: arachnodactyly
10423.definition: Extreme length and slenderness of the fingers or toes.

10424.title: arachnoid membrane
10424.definition: Web like membrane that lies between the outer (and much thicker) dura mater and the deeper pia mater, and which covers the brain.

10425.title: arachnoid villus
10425.definition: Small projection of the arachnoid membrane into some of the venous sinuses of the dura mater.

11604.title: arachnoiditis
11604.definition: Inflammation of the arachnoid membrane, often characterized by perception of burning pain in the legs.

15470.title: arboricide
15470.definition: Substance intended to kill trees and shrubs.

11605.title: arborization
11605.definition: Terminal branching of a neuron into a treelike structure of the dendrites.

A00428.title: Archibald's method
A00428.definition: A sedimentation method based on the fact that at the meniscus and at the bottom of the centrifuge cell there is never a flux of the solute across a plane perpendicular to the radial direction and the equations characterizing the sedimentation equilibrium always apply there, even though the system as a whole may be far from equilibrium. The use of the term 'approach to sedimentation equilibrium' for Archibald's method is discouraged, since it has a more general meaning.

14445.title: arcsine square root transformation
14445.definition: \(\arcsin \sqrt{P}\), where \(P\) is the value of a measured effect, e.g., the proportion of exposed organisms in a population.

A00429.title: area
A00429.definition: This is understood to be the geometrical or projected area, and to ignore surface roughness.

A00430.title: area of interface
A00430.definition: In all measurements it is desirable that quantities like the charge and the capacity be related to unit, true, surface area of the interface. While this is relatively simple for a liquid-liquid interface, there are great difficulties when one phase is solid. In any report of these quantities it is essential to give a clear statement as to whether they refer to the true or the apparent (geometric) area and, especially if the former is used, precisely how it was measured.

11407.title: area under the curve
11407.definition:
The area under a graph curve, such as the number of actives identified by an algorithm as a function of the number of compounds tested, commonly used as a
 measure of the discriminating ability of an algorithm to correctly classify a test molecule.

15472.title: area under the moment curve
15472.definition: Area between a curve and the abscissa (horizontal axis) in a plot of (concentration \(\times\) time) vs. time.

13992.title: area-related parameters
13992.definition: Quantities expressed in terms of 'per area' are denoted as area-related parameters.

A00432.title: areic
A00432.definition: Attribute to a physical quantity obtained by division by area. Areic charge is the charge on a surface divided by the surface area.

09223.title: areic dose
09223.definition: Number, \(N\), of energetic particles of a specified type introduced into a solid through a surface area \(A\) divided by \(A\). \(D = N/A\).

09222.title: areic dose rate
09222.definition: Areic dose introduced into a solid in time interval \(t\) divided by \(t\).

09224.title: areic surface energy
09224.definition: Energy required to increase a surface area at thermodynamic equilibrium divided by that increase in area.

A00433.title: arene epoxides
A00433.definition: Epoxides derived from arenes by 1,2-addition of an oxygen atom to a formal double bond, e.g. 5,6-epoxycyclohexa-1,3-diene.  (Common usage has extended the term to include examples with the epoxy group bridging nonadjacent atoms.)

A00436.title: arenium ions
A00436.definition: Cations derived formally by the addition of a hydron or other cationic species to any position of an arene, e.g. $\ce{C6H7^{+}}$, benzenium. The term includes:Arenium σ-adduct (sigma-adduct) (Wheland intermediates) (which are considered to be intermediates in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions) and other cyclohexadienyl cations. Arenium π-adduct (pi-adduct), such as:

10426.title: areola
10426.definition:
A circular area of different color surrounding a central point, such as that surrounding the nipple of the breast, the part of the iris surrounding the pupil of the eye, or an area surrounding a vesicle.
Any minute space or interstice in a tissue.

A00439.title: argon ion laser
A00439.definition: A CW or pulsed laser emitting lines from \(334\) to \(529\ \rm{nm}\) from singly ionized argon. Principal emissions are at \(488.0\) and \(514.5\ \rm{nm}\).

15473.title: argyria
15473.definition: Pathological condition characterized by gray-bluish or black pigmentation of tissues (such as skin, retina, mucous membranes, internal organs) caused by the accumulation of metallic silver, due to reduction of a silver compound which has entered the organism during (prolonged) administration or exposure.

A00440.title: arithmetic mean
A00440.definition: The sum of a series of observations divided by the number of observations. Symbol: \(\bar{x}\). It can be calculated by the formula: \[\bar{x}=\frac{\sum x_{i}}{n}\]

10427.title: Arnold–Chiari malformation
10427.definition: Congenital herniation of the brainstem and lower cerebellum through the foramen magnum into the cervical vertebral canal.

10428.title: aromatase
10428.definition: Enzyme (EC 1.14.14.1) of the cytochrome P450 superfamily that converts testosterone to 17\(\upbeta\)-estradiol and androstenedione to estrone.

A00441.title: aromatic
A00441.definition: In the traditional sense, 'having a chemistry typified by benzene'.A cyclically conjugated molecular entity with a stability (due to delocalization) significantly greater than that of a hypothetical localized structure (e.g. Kekulé structure) is said to possess aromatic character. If the structure is of higher energy (less stable) than such a hypothetical classical structure, the molecular entity is 'antiaromatic'. The most widely used method for determining aromaticity is the observation of diatropicity in the $\ce{^{1}H}$ NMR spectrum.See also: Hückel (4n + 2) rule, Möbius aromaticityThe terms aromatic and antiaromatic have been extended to describe the stabilization or destabilization of transition states of pericyclic reactions The hypothetical reference structure is here less clearly defined, and use of the term is based on application of the Hückel (4n + 2) rule and on consideration of the topology of orbital overlap in the transition state. Reactions of molecules in the ground state involving antiaromatic transition states proceed, if at all, much less easily than those involving aromatic transition states.

AT07327.title: aromatic photocycloaddition
AT07327.definition: Inter- and intramolecular photochemical processes involving the addition of a $\ce{C–C}$ double (or triple) bond (i) to the 1,2-positions of an arene in which case it is called an ortho photocycloaddition, with formation of a benzocyclobutene (or a benzocyclobutadiene) derivative, (ii) to the 1,3-positions of an arene in which case it is called a meta photocycloaddition, with formation of tricyclo[3.3.0.02,8]oct-3-ene (or octa-3,6-diene) derivatives, or (iii) to the 1,4-positions of an arene in which case it is called a para photocycloaddition, with formation of bicyclo[2,2,2]oct-2-ene (or octa-2,5-diene) derivatives.

A00442.title: aromaticity
A00442.definition: The concept of spatial and electronic structure of cyclic molecular systems displaying the effects of cyclic electron delocalization which provide for their enhanced thermodynamic stability (relative to acyclic structural analogues) and tendency to retain the structural type in the course of chemical transformations. A quantitative assessment of the degree of aromaticity is given by the value of the resonance energy. It may also be evaluated by the energies of relevant isodesmic and homodesmotic reactions. Along with energetic criteria of aromaticity, important and complementary are also a structural criterion (the lesser the alternation of bond lengths in the rings, the greater is the aromaticity of the molecule) and a magnetic criterion (existence of the diamagnetic ring current induced in a conjugated cyclic molecule by an external magnetic field and manifested by an exaltation and anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility). Although originally introduced for characterization of peculiar properties of cyclic conjugated hydrocarbons and their ions, the concept of aromaticity has been extended to their homoderivatives (see homoaromaticity), conjugated heterocyclic compounds (heteroaromaticity), saturated cyclic compounds ($\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}aromaticity}$) as well as to three-dimensional organic and organometallic compounds (three-dimensional aromaticity). A common feature of the electronic structure inherent in all aromatic molecules is the close nature of their valence electron shells, i.e., double electron occupation of all bonding MOs with all antibonding and delocalized nonbonding MOs unfilled. The notion of aromaticity is applied also to transition states.

08226.title: array detector
08226.definition: Photoelectric detector in which a large number of pixels are distributed, usually in regularly spaced lines and usually over a rectangular area.

A00443.title: arrester
A00443.definition: Equipment designed to remove particles from a gaseous medium.

A00446.title: Arrhenius equation
A00446.definition: An equation that represents the dependence of the rate constant \(k\) of a reaction on the absolute temperature \(T\): \[k = A\ \rm{e}^{\frac{-E_{\rm{a}}}{R\ T}}\] In its original form the pre-exponential factor \(A\) and the activation energy \(E_{\rm{a}}\) are considered to be temperature-independent.

11606.title: arrhythmia
11606.definition: Condition in which there is an irregular or abnormal heart beat.

A00447.title: arsanes
A00447.definition: The saturated hydrides of tervalent arsenic, having the general formula $\ce{As_{n}H_{n+2}}$. Individual members having an unbranched arsenic chain are named arsane, diarsane, triarsane, etc. The name of a saturated hydride of arsenic where one or more arsenic atoms have bonding number 5 is formed by prefixing locants and \(\lambda ^{5}\) symbols to the name of the corresponding arsane, e.g. $\ce{H2AsAsHAsH2}$ triarsane, $\ce{H4AsAsH3AsH4}$ 1\(\lambda ^{5}\),2\(\lambda ^{5}\),3\(\lambda ^{5}\)-triarsane. Hydrocarbyl derivatives of $\ce{AsH3}$ belong to the class arsines.

A00448.title: arsanylidenes
A00448.definition: Recommended name for carbene analogues having the structure $\ce{R–As{:}}$ (former IUPAC name is arsinediyls). A common non-IUPAC synonym is arsinidenes.

A00449.title: arsanylium ions
A00449.definition: The arsanyl cation, $\ce{H2As^{+}}$, and derivatives by substitution. The name arsinylium (systematically derived from arsine) is not applied as it already designates $\ce{H2As(=O)^{+}}$, the acylium ion derived from arsinic acid.

A00450.title: arsenides
A00450.definition: Compounds obtained from arsines $\ce{AsR3}$ by replacing one or more hydrogen atoms by a metal, e.g. $\ce{CaAsPh}$ calcium phenylarsenide.

A00451.title: arsine oxides
A00451.definition: $\ce{H3As=O}$ and its hydrocarbyl derivatives (analogously arsine imides and arsine sulfides), e.g. $\ce{(CH3)3As=O}$ trimethylarsine oxide or trimethylarsane oxide.

A00452.title: arsines
A00452.definition: AsH3 and compounds derived from it by substituting one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups: $\ce{R3As}$, $\ce{RAsH2}$, $\ce{R2AsH}$, $\ce{R3As}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$) are called primary, secondary and tertiary arsines, respectively. A specific arsine is preferably named as a substituted arsane, e.g. $\ce{CH3CH2AsH2}$ ethylarsane.

A00453.title: arsinic acids
A00453.definition: $\ce{H2As(=O)OH}$ and its $\ce{As}$-hydrocarbyl derivatives, e.g. $\ce{Me2As(=O)OH}$, dimethylarsinic acid.

A00457.title: arsonium compounds
A00457.definition: Salts (including hydroxides) $\ce{[R4As]^{+}X^{−}}$ containing tetracoordinate arsonium ion and the associated anion.

A00459.title: arsoranes
A00459.definition: The mononuclear hydride $\ce{AsH5}$, systematically named \(\lambda ^{5}\)-arsane, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives. By extension the term also applies to arsonium ylides.

10429.title: arteriogenesis
10429.definition: Increase in the diameter of arterial vessels that leads to the formation of large conductance arteries from pre-existing arterioles.

11607.title: arteriolovenular anastomosis
11607.definition: Communication in which blood is shunted from arterioles to venules without passing through capillaries.

15476.title: arteriosclerosis
15476.definition: Hardening and thickening of the walls of the arteries.

11608.title: arteriovenous
11608.definition: Relating to both arteries and veins.

11609.title: arteriovenous anastomosis
11609.definition: Communication between an artery and a vein by collateral channels.

11610.title: arteriovenous fistula
11610.definition: Abnormal communication between an artery and a vein.

11611.title: arteriovenous malformation
11611.definition: Web of blood vessels with one or more abnormal communications between arteries and veins that bypass the capillary system.

10430.title: arteriovenous shunt
10430.definition: Connection between the arterial and venous sides of the circulation that bypasses the capillary beds.

12903.title: arthritis
12903.definition: Inflammation of a joint or joints.

12904.title: Arthus reaction
12904.definition: Local antibody-mediated hypersensitivity reaction in which antigen-antibody complexes which fix complement are deposited in the walls of small vessels, often in the skin, causing acute inflammation with an infiltration of neutrophils.

14108.title: artifact
14108.definition: Observation, effect, or result that is inaccurate because it is produced by the methodology used in scientific investigation or by experimental error.

10431.title: artificial insemination
10431.definition: Introduction of semen into the cervix, uterus or Fallopian tubes by means other than the natural one.

14284.title: artificial latex
14284.definition: Latex obtained by emulsification of a polymer or oligomer solution in a liquid or by emulsification of a liquid polymer or liquid oligomer in a liquid.

AT06947.title: artificial neural networks
AT06947.definition: Artificial neural networks (ANN) are algorithms simulating the functioning of human neurons and may be used for pattern recognition problems, e.g., to establish quantitative structure-activity relationships.

13993.title: artificial photosynthesis
13993.definition: Photocatalytic production of substances from simple compounds (e.g., \(\ce{H2}\) and \(\ce{O2}\) from water, \(\ce{H2}\) from hydrogen sulfide, etc.) using ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation absorbed by chromophoric systems, often included in microheterogeneous media, mimicking the action of antennae and reaction centres in natural photosynthetic organisms.

14446.title: artificial soil test
14446.definition: Test with earthworms in which the toxicity of a substance by skin and gut uptake is determined by adding the earthworms to an artificial soil made of sand, clay mineral, and peat, containing the substance of concern.

14447.title: artisol test
14447.definition: Test with earthworms in which the toxicity of a substance by skin and gut uptake is determined by placing the worms in an artificial substrate consisting of silica, water, and glass balls, containing the substance of concern.

A00462.title: aryl cations
A00462.definition: Carbocations formally derived by removal of a hydride ion from a ring carbon atom of an arene. E.g. phenyl cation or phenylium:

A00464.title: aryl groups
A00464.definition: Groups derived from arenes by removal of a hydrogen atom from a ring carbon atom. Groups similarly derived from heteroarenes are sometimes subsumed in this definition. E.g. o-tolyl:

14448.title: aryl hydrocarbon hydroxylase
14448.definition: Enzyme activity attributed to cytochrome P-450 monooxygenase isoforms and often measured in units of benzo[a]pyrene hydroxylation.

10432.title: aryl hydrocarbon receptor
10432.definition: Ligand-activated transcription factor involved in the regulation of biological responses to planar aromatic hydrocarbons.

10433.title: aryl hydrocarbon receptor nucleotide translocator protein
10433.definition: Protein coded for by a gene on chromosome 1q21 that forms a complex with ligand-bound aryl hydrocarbon receptor, resulting in translocation of the ligand-binding subunit to the nucleus.

A00463.title: arylene groups
A00463.definition: Bivalent groups derived from arenes by removal of a hydrogen atom from two ring carbon atoms. A synonym is arenediyl groups. E.g. o-phenylene or benzene-1,2-diyl:

A00465.title: aryne
A00465.definition: A hydrocarbon derived from an arene by abstraction of two hydrogen atoms from adjacent carbon atoms; thus 1,2-didehydroarene. Arynes are commonly represented with a formal triple bond. The analogous heterocyclic compounds are called heteroarynes or hetarynes. For example, benzyne:  Arynes are usually transient species.

14449.title: as low as reasonably achievable
14449.definition: Describing the situation in which everything practicable is done to reduce risks to the minimum with the approval of the regulatory authorities.

15480.title: asbestosis
15480.definition: Form of pneumoconiosis caused by inhalation of asbestos fibers.

A00466.title: ascending elution
A00466.definition: A mode of operation in which the paper or plate is in a vertical or slanted position and the mobile phase is supplied to its lower edge; the upward movement depends on capillary action.

A00467.title: ash
A00467.definition: The solid residue which remains after the combustion of a fuel such as coal. Ash consists largely of heat treated mineral matter, but it may contain some products of the incomplete combustion of the fuel as well.

A00468.title: ashing
A00468.definition: Dry or wet mineralization as a method of preconcentration of trace substances.

09451.title: aspect ratio
09451.definition: Proportional relationship between the width and height of an image produced by exposing a resist.

15482.title: asphyxia
15482.definition: Condition resulting from insufficient intake of oxygen.

15483.title: asphyxiant
15483.definition: Substance that blocks the transport or use of oxygen by living organisms.

A00469.title: aspirator
A00469.definition: Any apparatus that produces a movement of a fluid by suction (e.g. a squeeze bulb, pump, Venturi, etc.)

A00470.title: assay
A00470.definition: A set of operations having the object of determining the value of a quantity. In analytical chemistry, this term is synonymous with measurement.

A00471.title: assay kit
A00471.definition: A set of components (reagents and other necessary materials) and procedural instructions packaged together and designed for the estimation in vitro of a value of a specified quantity, when used according to the instructions.

14109.title: assay validation
14109.definition: Experiments conducted to verify that the output measurements of the assay are consistently reflective of the activity against the target.

14450.title: assemblage
14450.definition: Set of coexisting populations defined by phylogeny, location, or life style. Assemblages are intermediate between populations and communities.

14451.title: assessment endpoint
14451.definition: Ecological property that is to be protected and the precise parameter to be measured for this property.

08056.title: assessor
08056.definition: Person, assigned by an accreditation body, with relevant professional expertise and experience who can determine the competence of a laboratory.

08057.title: assigned value
08057.definition: Value attributed to a particular property of an item and that serves as an agreed reference for comparison.

15484.title: assimilation
15484.definition: Uptake and incorporation of substances by a living organism.

A00472.title: association
A00472.definition: The assembling of separate molecular entities into any aggregate, especially of oppositely charged free ions into ion pairs or larger and not necessarily well-defined clusters of ions held together by electrostatic attraction. The term signifies the reverse of dissociation, but is not commonly used for the formation of definite adducts by colligation or coordination.

14452.title: Association Française de Normalisation test
14452.definition: Commercially available test kit, certified by AFNOR as valid and equivalent to a standardized method.

A00473.title: association reaction
A00473.definition: The reaction of a (slow moving) ion with a neutral species wherein the reactants combine to form a single ionized species.

11612.title: associative avoidance test
11612.definition: Avoidance test in which the test animal has learned to develop an association between the stimulus and the delivery of an aversive event.

A00475.title: associative ionization
A00475.definition: This occurs when two excited gaseous atoms or molecular moieties interact and the sum of their internal energies is sufficient to produce a single, additive ionic product.

11613.title: associative learning
11613.definition: Process in which a new behavior arises as a consequence of association with a particular stimulus, sometimes restricted to learning through classical conditioning.

15485.title: asthenia
15485.definition: Weakness; lack or loss of strength.

12905.title: asthma
12905.definition: Chronic respiratory disease characterized by bronchoconstriction, excessive mucus secretion, and edema of the pulmonary alveoli, resulting in difficulty in exhaling, wheezing, and cough.

15486.title: astringent
15486.definition:
adj., Causing contraction, usually locally after topical application.
n., Substance causing cells to shrink, thus causing tissue contraction or stoppage of secretions and discharges; such substances may be applied to skin to harden and protect it.

11614.title: astrocyte
11614.definition: Glial cell of ectodermal origin in the central nervous system, characterized by filamentous protoplasmic extensions.

11616.title: astrocytic scar
11616.definition: Clustering of reactive astrocytes separating a localized brain injury from surrounding uninjured tissue.

11617.title: astrocytoma
11617.definition: Tumor within the substance of the brain or spinal cord made up of astrocytes.

11618.title: astrogliosis
11618.definition: Localized site of reactive astrocytes, distinct from an astrocytic scar.

A00477.title: asym-
A00477.definition: An affix used in names to denote asymmetrical.

A00478.title: asymmetric
A00478.definition: Lacking all symmetry elements (other than the trivial one of a one-fold axis of symmetry), i.e. belonging to the symmetry point group \(C_{1}\). The term has been used loosely (and incorrectly) to describe the absence of a rotation–reflection axis (alternating axis) in a molecule, i.e. as meaning chiral, and this usage persists in the traditional terms asymmetric carbon atom, asymmetric synthesis, asymmetric induction, etc.

A00479.title: asymmetric carbon atom
A00479.definition: The traditional name (van 't Hoff) for a carbon atom that is attached to four different entities (atoms or groups), e.g. Cabcd.

09588.title: asymmetric enantiomer-differentiating polymerization
09588.definition: Asymmetric polymerization in which, starting from a mixture of enantiomeric monomer molecules, only one enantiomer is polymerized.

A00482.title: asymmetric film
A00482.definition: A film bounded by two different bulk phases. When the bulk phases are identical the film is described as symmetric.

A00483.title: asymmetric induction
A00483.definition: The traditional term describing the preferential formation in a chemical reaction of one enantiomer or diastereoisomer over the other as a result of the influence of a chiral feature present in the substrate, reagent, catalyst or environment.

AT06862.title: asymmetric membrane
AT06862.definition: Membrane constituted of two or more structural planes of non-identical morphologies.

AT07328.title: asymmetric photochemistry
AT07328.definition: Photochemical process leading to a chiral substance from an achiral precursor such that one enantiomer predominates over the other.

09589.title: asymmetric polymerization
09589.definition: Polymerization that proceeds in an unsymmetrical manner in terms of chirality under the influence of chiral features present in one or more components of the reaction system.

A00484.title: asymmetric synthesis
A00484.definition: A traditional term used for stereoselective synthesis of chiral compounds.

08571.title: asymmetric top
08571.definition: Rotor whose three principal moments of inertia are all different.

A00485.title: asymmetric transformation
A00485.definition: The conversion of a racemate into a pure enantiomer or into a mixture in which one enantiomer is present in excess, or of a diastereoisomeric mixture into a single diastereoisomer or into a mixture in which one diastereoisomer predominates. This is sometimes called deracemization. If the two enantiomers of a chiral substrate A are freely interconvertible and if an equal amount or excess of a non-racemizing second enantiomerically pure chemical species, say ($R$)-B, is added to a solution of racemic A, then the resulting equilibrium mixture of adducts A·B will, in general, contain unequal amounts of the diastereoisomers ($R$)-A$\cdot$($R$)-B and ($S$)-A$\cdot$($R$)-B. The result of this equilibration is called asymmetric transformation of the first kind. If, in such a system, the two diastereoisomeric adducts differ considerably in solubility so that only one of them, say ($R$)-A$\cdot$($R$)-B, crystallizes from the solution, then the equilibration of diastereoisomers in solution and concurrent crystallization will continue so that all (or most) of the substrate A can be isolated as the crystalline diastereoisomer ($R$)-A$\cdot$($R$)-B. Such a 'crystallization-induced asymmetric transformation' is called an asymmetric transformation of the second kind.

09931.title: asymmetrical flow field-flow fractionation
09931.definition: Flow field-flow fractionation in which only one channel wall is permeable, meaning there is one channel inlet for the flow during the run and some of the channel flow is directed through the accumulation wall.

09902.title: asymmetry factor
09902.definition: Width of a peak (\(f + b\)) divided by twice the width of the front of the peak (\(f\)), measured at \(\pu{10\%}\) of the peak height (see figure). \[A_{\rm{s}} = \frac{(f + b)}{2f}\] Peak asymmetry (schematic). \(R_{\rm{D}}\) is the response of the detector.Peak asymmetry (schematic). \(R_{\rm{D}}\) is the response of the detector.

09306.title: asymmetry parameter
09306.definition: In X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy factor which characterizes the intensity distribution, \(L(\gamma)\), of photoelectrons ejected by X-rays from isolated atoms at an angle \(\gamma\) from the incident X-ray direction. In the dipole approximation, \(L(\gamma) = 1 + ½\beta [3(\sin^{2}\gamma)/2-1]\).

A00487.title: asymmetry potential
A00487.definition: The measured potential difference of a symmetrical cell with identical solutions and reference electrodes on each side of the glass membrane. There is rarely the need, nor the possibility, of measuring the asymmetry potential of commercial glass electrodes. Drifts in glass electrode potentials with time and variations from day to day in the potential measured in a standard buffer may be attributed to changes in asymmetry potential.

14453.title: asymptotic threshold concentration
14453.definition: Concentration of a chemical at which some percentage of a population of test organisms is in a state of approximate homeostasis for a prolonged period of time (\(\pu{48 h}\) or more).

10294.title: at-line extraction
10294.definition: Flow system with extraction device employing a local detector.

A00488.title: atactic macromolecule
A00488.definition: A regular macromolecule in which the configurational (base) units are not all identical.

A00489.title: atactic polymer
A00489.definition: A polymer composed of atactic macromolecules.

11619.title: ataxia
11619.definition: Loss of muscular coordination (see motor coordination) resulting in abnormal clumsiness.

12906.title: ataxia telangiectasia
12906.definition: Disease characterized by staggering gait, multiple disorganized blood vessels, and an immunodeficiency, associated with a protein called ataxia telangiectasia-mutated (ATM), a protein kinase thought to be important in detection of double-stranded DNA breaks.

10434.title: atelectasis
10434.definition:
Total or partial collapse of the lung.
Congenital condition characterized by the incomplete expansion of the lungs at birth.

10435.title: athelia
10435.definition: Congenital absence of one or both nipples.

15487.title: atherosclerosis
15487.definition: Pathological condition in which there is thickening, hardening, and loss of elasticity of the walls of blood vessels, characterized by a variable combination of changes of the innermost layer consisting of local accumulation of lipids, complex carbohydrates, blood and blood components, fibrous tissue, and calcium deposits. In addition, the outer layer becomes thickened and there is fatty degeneration of the middle layer.

11620.title: athetosis
11620.definition: Condition in which inappropriate muscle contraction causes involuntary writhing movements.

10436.title: athymia
10436.definition: Congenital absence of functioning thymus tissue.

A00491.title: atmosphere
A00491.definition: The entire mass of air surrounding the earth which is composed largely of nitrogen, oxygen, water vapour, clouds (liquid or solid water), carbon dioxide, together with trace gases and aerosols.

14454.title: atmospheric deposition
14454.definition: Process that transfers a chemical from the atmosphere to the Earth’s surface (land, water, or vegetation) by either dry impingement or by transport in rain or snow.

A00492.title: atmospheric pressure ionization
A00492.definition: An ambiguous term; in essence, it is used to describe chemical ionization at atmospheric pressure. It is recommended that use of the term be discontinued.

A00493.title: atom
A00493.definition: Smallest particle still characterizing a chemical element. It consists of a nucleus of a positive charge (\(Z\) is the proton number and \(e\) the elementary charge) carrying almost all its mass (more than 99.9%) and \(Z\) electrons determining its size.

AT06992.title: atom-atom polarizability
AT06992.definition: A quantity used in perturbation HMO theory as a measure of the change in electron density, \(q\), of atom \(s\) caused by a change in the electronegativity (or coulomb integral) of atom \(r\): \[\pi _{\rm{sr}}=\frac{\partial q_{\rm{s}}}{\partial a_{\rm{r}}}\]

AT06993.title: atom-bond polarizability
AT06993.definition: A quantity used in perturbation HMO theory as a measure of the change in electron density, \(q\), of atom \(m\) caused by a change in the resonance integral, \(\beta \), of bond \(rs\): \[\pi _{\rm{m,rs}}=\frac{\partial q_{\rm{m}}}{\partial \beta _{\rm{rs}}}\]

08924.title: atom-transfer radical polymerization
08924.definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization in which the deactivation of the radicals involves reversible atom-transfer or reversible group transfer to usually, though not exclusively, transition-metal complexes.

A00510.title: atom–molecule complex mechanism
A00510.definition: A mechanism that sometimes applies to the combination of atoms, but rarely of free radicals. In this mechanism the atom A first combines with a third body or chaperon, $$\ce{A + M -> AM}$$ and the complex AM then forms $\ce{A2 + M}$ by collision with another atom $\ce{A}$. Contrast the energy-transfer mechanism.

08451.title: atomic absorption spectroscopy
08451.definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy for measuring the amount of a chemical element based on the measurement of the absorption of characteristic electromagnetic radiation by atoms in the vapour phase.

AT06994.title: atomic charge

08452.title: atomic emission spectroscopy
08452.definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy for measuring the amount of a chemical element based on the measurement of the intensity of characteristic electromagnetic radiation emitted by atoms or molecules.

08453.title: atomic excitation source
08453.definition: Atomizer intended to convert free atoms to an excited state.

A00494.title: atomic fluorescence
A00494.definition: A combined process of photon absorption by an atom followed by spontaneous photon emission.

08454.title: atomic fluorescence spectroscopy
08454.definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy for measuring the amount of a chemical element based on the measurement of the re-emission of characteristic electromagnetic radiation by atoms, following the absorption of radiation in the vapour phase.

09452.title: atomic force microscopy
09452.definition: High-resolution scanning probe microscopy that maps a surface with a demonstrated resolution of the order of fractions of a nanometer.

A00495.title: atomic laser
A00495.definition: A gas laser which is pumped using energy transfer from other atoms or molecules. Examples are the helium-neon ($\ce{HeNe}$) and the copper vapour laser.

A00497.title: atomic mass constant
A00497.definition: One twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom in its nuclear and electronic ground state, \(m_{\rm{u}} = \pu{1.6605402(10)E-27 kg}\). It is equal to the unified atomic mass unit.

A00496.title: atomic mass
A00496.definition: Rest mass of an atom in its ground state. The commonly used unit is the unified atomic mass unit.

09225.title: atomic mixing
09225.definition: Migration of sample atoms due to energy transfer with incident particles in the surface region.

A00499.title: atomic number
A00499.definition: The number of protons in the atomic nucleus.

A00500.title: atomic orbital
A00500.definition: One-electron wavefunction obtained as a solution of the Schrödinger equation for an atom.

08572.title: atomic polar tensor
08572.definition: 3 × 3 tensor that gives the change in the components of the molecular dipole moment when the atom is displaced in three-dimensional space.

A00502.title: atomic spectral lines
A00502.definition: Atomic and ionic spectral lines originate from specified electronic transitions between energy levels of atoms and ions, respectively. In the past it has been common usage to denote atomic lines as arc lines and ionic lines as spark lines. This usage is now considered to be incorrect. The correct way to indicate that lines are due to atomic or ionic transitions is: Element symbol I wavelength, e.g., Cu I \(324.7\ \rm{nm}\); and Element symbol II wavelength, e.g., Cu II \(213.6\ \rm{nm}\). Similarly for higher states of ionization, the type of line is represented by III, IV, etc.

08216.title: atomic spectroscopy
08216.definition: Measurement principle of spectroscopy for the study of electromagnetic radiation absorbed and emitted by atoms.

A00503.title: atomic symbol
A00503.definition: One, two or three letters used to represent the atom in chemical formulae.

A00504.title: atomic units
A00504.definition: The units designed to simplify the form of the fundamental equations of quantum mechanics by eliminating from them fundamental constants. The atomic unit of length is the Bohr radius, \(a_{\rm{o}}=\frac{h^{2}}{4\ \pi ^{2}\ m\ e^{2}}=5.291\ 77249\times 10^{-11}\ \rm{m}\) (\(0.529177249\ \mathring{\rm{A}}\)). Energy is measured in hartrees, where \(1\ \rm{hartree} = \frac{e^{2}}{a_{\rm{o}}}=4.359\ 7482\times 10^{-18}\ \rm{J}\). Masses are specified in terms of atomic mass unit, \(\pu{amu} = \pu{1.6605402E-27 kg}\) and of the electron mass unit, \(m_{\rm{e}} = \pu{0.910953E-30 kg}\). The advantage of atomic units is that if all calculations are directly expressed in such units, the results do not vary with any revision of the numerical values of the fundamental constants.

08455.title: atomic vapour
08455.definition: Vapour containing free atoms of analyte.

08456.title: atomization curve
08456.definition: Graph of absorbance against atomization temperature.

A00506.title: atomization
A00506.definition: The conversion of volatilized analyte into free atoms.

A00507.title: atomization surface temperature
A00507.definition: The temperature of the support from which the sample is atomized.

A00508.title: atomize
A00508.definition: To subdivide a liquid into very small particles; methods include: impact with a jet of gas, use of a spinning disk generator, vibrating orifice generator, etc.

A00509.title: atomizer
A00509.definition: Any system which is capable of converting the analyte into atomic vapour.

12907.title: atopic allergy
12907.definition: Immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated hypersensitivity, including asthma, eczema, hay fever, and food allergy.

12908.title: atopic dermatitis
12908.definition: Inflammation of the skin in atopic individuals.

12909.title: atopic eczema
12909.definition: Chronic skin disease, often localized on flexural surfaces, in individuals with propensity to develop immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated allergy.

12910.title: atopy
12910.definition: Of, relating to, or caused by a hereditary predisposition toward developing certain hypersensitivity reactions, such as hay fever, asthma, or chronic urticaria, upon exposure to specific antigens.

12620.title: ATP binding cassette protein
12620.definition: Large gene family of transporter proteins that bind ATP and use the energy to transport substrates (e.g., sugars, amino acids, metal ions, peptides, proteins, and a large number of hydrophobic compounds and metabolites) across lipid membranes.

10437.title: atresia
10437.definition: Congenital absence or abnormal narrowing of a normal opening or normally patent lumen.

10438.title: atrial-septal defect
10438.definition: Defect in the septum between the atria of the heart, due to failure of normal closure of the foramen ovale in the perinatal period.

10439.title: atrichia congenita
10439.definition: Congenital baldness caused by an abnormality of the hairless gene.

10440.title: atrioventricular
10440.definition: Relating to the atrial and ventricular chambers of the heart.

10441.title: atrium
10441.definition: Each of the two upper chambers of the heart from which blood is passed to the ventricles.

10442.title: atrophy
10442.definition: Wasting away of the body or of an organ or tissue, involving a decrease in size and (or) numbers of cells.

A00511.title: atropisomers
A00511.definition: A subclass of conformers which can be isolated as separate chemical species and which arise from restricted rotation about a single bond, e.g. ortho-substituted biphenyl, 1,1,2,2-tetra-tert-butylethane.

A00512.title: attachment
A00512.definition: A transformation by which one molecular entity (the substrate) is converted into another by the formation of one (and only one) two-centre bond between the substrate and another molecular entity and which involves no other changes in connectivity in the substrate. For example, the formation of an acyl cation by attachment of carbon monoxide to a carbenium ion ($\ce{R^{+}}$):  The product of an attachment may also be the adduct of the two reactants, but not all adducts can be represented as the products of an attachment. (For example, the Diels–Alder cycloaddition:  results in an adduct of buta-1,3-diene and ethene, but the reaction cannot be described as an attachment since bonds are formed between more than two centres.)

11622.title: attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
11622.definition: Neuropsychiatric disorder of childhood characterized by decreased attention span, impulsiveness and hyperactivity.

A00514.title: attenuance filter
A00514.definition: An optical device (filter) which reduces the radiant power of a light beam by a constant factor over all wavelengths within its operating range. Sometimes called attenuator or neutral density filter.

A00513.title: attenuance
A00513.definition: Analogous to absorbance, but taking into account also the effects due to scattering and luminescence. It was formerly called extinction.

08227.title: attenuated total reflection
08227.definition: Internal reflection from an absorbing material at angles of incidence at or above the critical angle.

09195.title: attenuated total reflection infrared spectroscopy
09195.definition: Attenuated total reflection spectroscopy in which the infrared absorption spectrum of a sample in contact with a prism is measured.

08573.title: attenuated total reflection spectroscopy
08573.definition: Measurement method of vibrational spectroscopy based on internal reflection from an absorbing material at angles of incidence at or above the critical angle (attenuated total reflection).

12911.title: attenuated vaccine
12911.definition: Vaccine made from a live organism that targets cells of the immune system but has been engineered or weakened so as not to cause disease.

A00515.title: attenuation
A00515.definition: The reduction of a radiation quantity upon passage of radiation through matter resulting from interactions of the radiation with the matter it traverses.

A00516.title: attenuation coefficient
A00516.definition: Analogous to absorption coefficient but taking into account also the effects due to scattering and luminescence. It was formerly called extinction coefficient.

A00519.title: attractive potential-energy surface
A00519.definition: A potential-energy surface for a process A + B–C in which the initial descent of the system into the product valley is associated with a substantial decrease in the A–B distance and with little separation between the products A–B and C. In terms of a potential-energy profile, the energy barrier occurs in the early stage of the reaction path. Attractive surfaces are also called early-downhill surfaces, and the barrier in such a surface is called a Type-I barrier.

A00518.title: attractive–mixed–repulsive classification
A00518.definition: A classification of potential-energy surfaces in which a highly attractive surface is at one extreme and a highly repulsive surface is at the other. The energy release in intermediate cases is referred to as mixed.

AT06805.title: attributable risk
AT06805.definition: Part of a risk that is identified as due to exposure to a defined substance.

12621.title: attrition rate
12621.definition: Rate of loss of drug candidates during progression through the optimisation and developmental stages while on route to the marketplace.

12912.title: atypical interstitial pneumonia
12912.definition: Acute or chronic respiratory distress in cattle, in the absence of toxemia or other systemic signs that are characteristic of other pneumonias.

08058.title: audit
08058.definition: Systematic, independent, and documented process for obtaining objective evidence and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which the audit criteria are fulfilled.

10443.title: auditory tube
10443.definition: Narrow channel connecting the middle ear and the nasopharynx.

AT06996.title: aufbau principle
AT06996.definition: A rule for building up the electronic configuration of atoms and molecules. It states that a maximum of two electrons are put into orbitals in the order of increasing orbital energy: the lowest-energy orbitals are filled before electrons are placed in higher-energy orbitals.

14456.title: aufwuchs
14456.definition: Floral and (or) or faunal communities attached to submerged surfaces in aquatic ecosystems.

A00520.title: Auger effect
A00520.definition: The emission of an electron from an atom accompanying the filling of a vacancy in an inner electron shell.

A00521.title: Auger electron
A00521.definition: Electron originating in the Auger effect.

A00522.title: Auger electron spectroscopy
A00522.definition: Any technique in which a specimen is bombarded with \(\mathrm{keV}\)-energy electrons or X-rays, and the energy distribution of the electrons produced through radiationless de-excitation of the atoms in the sample (Auger electrons) is recorded. The derivative curve may also be recorded.

09307.title: Auger electron spectrum
09307.definition: Plot of intensity of Auger electrons as a function of the electron kinetic energy, usually as part of the energy distribution of detected electrons.

A00523.title: Auger electron yield
A00523.definition: The fraction of the atoms having a vacancy in an inner orbital which relax by emission of an Auger electron.

09226.title: Auger neutralization
09226.definition: Process in which an electron, tunnelling from the conduction band of a solid, neutralizes an incoming ion and an electron is ejected from a surface atom.

09308.title: Auger parameter
09308.definition: Kinetic energy of a narrow Auger electron peak in a spectrum minus the kinetic energy of the most intense X-ray photoelectron peak from the same element.

09173.title: Auger photoelectron coincidence spectroscopy
09173.definition: Detection of an Auger electron and a core-level photoelectron, emitted from a solid irradiated by mono-energetic X-rays, within a sufficiently short time that the Auger electron shall arise from the decay of the particular core-hole associated with the photoelectron.

09172.title: Auger spectroscopy
09172.definition: Measurement method of electron emission spectroscopy that utilizes Auger electrons emitted from the target following excitation with an electron beam or X-ray beam.

09309.title: Auger vacancy satellite
09309.definition: Emission of an Auger electron in which additional spectator holes are present in the initial state or the final state) for the transition.

A00524.title: Auger yield
A00524.definition: For a given excited state of a specified atom the probability that the de-excitation occurs by the Auger effect.

11623.title: aura
