11623.definition: Constellation of symptoms experienced before a migraine headache or seizure.

10444.title: auricle
10444.definition: An appendage to the atrium of the heart.

09975.title: aurones
09975.definition: Aurones are compounds derived from (2$Z$)-2-benzylidene-1-benzofuran-3(2$H$)-one [alternative name: (2$Z$)-2-(phenylmethylidene)-1-benzofuran-3(2$H$)-one] (aurone, compound 14).

AT06796.title: autacoid
AT06796.definition: A biological substance secreted by various cells whose physiological activity is restricted to the vicinity of its release; it is often referred to as a local hormone.

11624.title: autism
11624.definition: Neurodevelopmental disorder, present from early childhood, characterized by great difficulty in communicating and forming relationships with other people and in using abstract concepts.

15380.title: auto-acceleration
15380.definition: Increase in the rate of polymerization with increasing conversion of the reactant(s).

A00526.title: auto-ionization
A00526.definition: This occurs when an internally supra-excited atom or molecular moiety loses an electron spontaneously without further interaction with an energy source. (The state of the atom or molecular moiety is known as a pre-ionization state.)

12913.title: autoantibody
12913.definition: Immunoglobulin (Ig) antibody that is directed against the organism’s own antigen(s).

12914.title: autoantigen
12914.definition: Antigenic component of an individual’s tissues which may be a target of autoimmune responses by autoreactive B cells (autoantibodies) or T cells, including proteins (e.g., enzymes, structural proteins), glycoproteins (e.g., 2-glycoprotein I), nucleic acids, (e.g., double-stranded DNA), phospholipids (e.g., cardiolipin), and glycosphingolipids (e.g., gangliosides).

A00525.title: autocatalytic reaction
A00525.definition: A chemical reaction in which a product (or a reaction intermediate) also functions as a catalyst. In such a reaction the observed rate of reaction is often found to increase with time from its initial value.

10043.title: autocorrelation
10043.definition: Correlation of a variable with itself over a successive time or space intervals (lags).

11408.title: autocorrelation vector
11408.definition:
A vector that describes a molecular structure in which each element corresponds to a distance (number of bonds in a 2D structure or a binned interatomic
 distance in a 3D structure) between atoms of a particular type and the count of the number of times that distance is found in the structure.

12916.title: autocrine
12916.definition: Type of signaling in which a cell secretes a chemical messenger that binds to receptors on the same cell, leading to changes in the cell.

14457.title: autogenic succession
14457.definition: Sequential appearance of species driven by processes operating within the community environment (compare allogenic succession), e.g., primary and secondary successions that occur on newly exposed land.

12917.title: autograft
12917.definition: Tissue transplant from one site to another in an individual.

12918.title: autoimmune
12918.definition: Of or relating to an immune response by the body against one of its own cells or tissues.

12919.title: autoimmune disease
12919.definition: Pathological condition resulting when an organism produces antibodies or specific cells that bind to constituents of its own tissues (autoantigens) and cause tissue injury.

12920.title: autoimmune hemolytic anemia
12920.definition: Autoimmune disease in which antibodies initiate complement lysis of erythrocytes.

12921.title: autoimmune hepatitis
12921.definition: Chronic autoimmune-mediated hepatic inflammation usually characterized by antinuclear (ANA), smooth muscle (SMA)/anti-F-actin, liver-kidney microsomal (LKM), and/or soluble liver antigen (SLA) antibodies.

12922.title: autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome
12922.definition: Disease characterized by lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, autoimmune cytopenias, and hypergammaglobulinemia.

12923.title: autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1 or 2
12923.definition: Heterogeneous group of rare diseases characterized by autoimmune activity against more than one endocrine organ, although non-endocrine organs can also be affected.

12924.title: autoimmune regulator
12924.definition: DNA-binding protein involved in immunoregulation (probably in the establishment and maintenance of tolerance).

12925.title: autoimmunity
12925.definition: Immune response to 'self' tissues or components.

12622.title: autoinduction
12622.definition: Capacity of a drug to induce enzymes that mediate its own metabolism.

12926.title: autoinflammatory disease
12926.definition: Unregulated inflammation without significant levels of autoantibodies or autoactivated T cells, or evidence of infection, but rather caused by genetic disturbance of the mechanisms that initiate and control inflammation.

12928.title: autologous antibody
12928.definition: Antibody derived from a specific individual, acting within that individual.

14110.title: automated device
14110.definition: Device that performs one or more functions without human intervention by means of direct control or by programmed operations.

10295.title: automated extraction
10295.definition: Extraction in a mechanical device regulated by feed-back of information without human intervention.

10296.title: automatic extraction
10296.definition: Extraction according to manually preselected conditions without further human intervention.

A00527.title: automation
A00527.definition: Mechanization with process control, where process means a sequence of manipulations. One or several functions in an analytical instrument may be automated. The corresponding adjective is automated and the verb is automate.

11739.title: autonomic dysreflexia
11739.definition: Over-activity of the autonomic nervous system causing an abrupt onset of excessively high blood pressure, tachycardia, and constriction of peripheral blood vessels.

11625.title: autonomic nervous system
11625.definition: Part of the peripheral nervous system controlling the bodily functions that are not consciously directed, e.g., breathing, heart rate, and digestive processes.

15489.title: autophagosome
15489.definition: Membrane-bound body (secondary lysosome) in which parts of the cell are digested.

12929.title: autophagy
12929.definition: Digestion and breakdown in lysosomes of a cell’s own proteins and/or organelles.

A00529.title: autophobicity
A00529.definition: If adsorption equilibrium and mutual saturation of the phases is not achieved instantly, it is possible to distinguish the initial spreading tension, \(\sigma _{\rm{i}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }\), from the final spreading tension, \(\sigma _{\rm{i}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }\), when equilibrium has been reached. In the case in which \(\sigma _{\rm{i}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }\) is positive, while \(\sigma _{\rm{i}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }\) is negative, the system is said to exhibit autophobicity.

A00531.title: autoprotolysis
A00531.definition: A proton (hydron) transfer reaction between two identical molecules (usually a solvent), one acting as a Brønsted acid and the other as a Brønsted base. For example:

A00532.title: autoprotolysis constant
A00532.definition: The product of the activities (or, more approximately, concentrations) of the species produced as the result of autoprotolysis. For solvents in which no other ionization processes are significant the term is synonymous with 'ionic product'. The autoprotolysis constant for water, \(K_{\rm{w}}\), is equal to the product of activities: \[a\left(\rm{H}_{3}\rm{O}^{\rm{+}}\right)\ a\left(\rm{OH}^{\rm{-}}\right) = 1.0\times 10^{-14}\] at \(25\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\).

10445.title: autopsy
10445.definition: Postmortem examination of the human organs and body tissue to determine cause of death or pathological condition.

A00533.title: autoradiograph
A00533.definition: A radiograph of an object containing radioactive substance, produced by placing the object adjacent to a photographic plate or film or a fluorescent screen.

A00534.title: autoradiolysis
A00534.definition: Radiolysis of a radioactive material resulting directly or indirectly from its radioactive decay.

10084.title: autoregression
10084.definition: Stochastic process in which future values are estimated based on a weighted sum of past values.

10446.title: autosite
10446.definition: Independent twin of a pair of conjoined twins; the other twin is a parasitic twin.

10447.title: autosomal dominant mutation
10447.definition: Change in an autosomal gene capable of expression when carried by only one of a pair of homologous chromosomes.

10448.title: autosomal recessive mutation
10448.definition: Change in an autosomal gene that produces an effect in the organism only when it is homozygous.

10449.title: autosome
10449.definition: Any chromosome that is not a sex chromosome.

14458.title: autotroph
14458.definition: Organism that is independent of outside sources for organic food materials and manufactures its own organic material from inorganic sources.

14459.title: autotrophic succession
14459.definition: Sequential appearance of species in a location principally involving plants.

15490.title: autoxidation
15490.definition: Reaction with dioxygen at moderate temperatures.

15491.title: autoxidation
15491.definition: Apparently spontaneous, usually slow reaction of foodstuff components with dioxygen in an aerobic environment at moderate temperatures.

A00535.title: auxiliary electrode
A00535.definition: Three-electrode cells comprise (1) an indicator (or test) electrode or a working electrode, at the surface of which processes that are of interest may occur, (2) a reference electrode and (3) a third electrode, the auxiliary or counter electrode, which serves merely to carry the current flowing through the cell, and at the surface of which no processes of interest occur. If processes of interest occur at both the anode and the cathode of a cell (as in differential amperometry or controlled current potentiometric titration with two indicator electrodes), the cell should be said to comprise two indicator (or test) working electrodes.

A00536.title: auxochrome
A00536.definition: An atom or group which, when added to or introduced into a chromophore, causes a bathochromic shift and/or a hyperchromic effect in a given band of the chromophore, usually in that of lowest frequency. This term is obsolete.

15492.title: auxotroph
15492.definition: Organism unable to synthesize an organic molecule which is required for its growth: When the compound is given to the organism with the other nutrients it requires, growth of the organism may occur.

A00537.title: auxotrophy
A00537.definition: The inability of an organism to synthesize a particular organic compound required for its growth.

09227.title: average beam current
09227.definition: Electric charge of specified polarity in a beam passing in time interval \(t\), divided by \(t\).

A00539.title: average current density
A00539.definition: The average current density, \(j\), is defined by \[j = A^{-1}\ \int _{A}j_{x}\ \rm{d}A\] where \(A\) is the electrode area, \(j_{x}\) is the local current density and \(\rm{d}A\) is an infinitesimal surface element.

A00540.title: average degree of polymerization
A00540.definition: Any average, \(\bar{X}_{\rm{k}}\), of the degree of polymerization, where \(\rm{k}\) specifies the type of average.

A00541.title: average life
A00541.definition: Defined for an atom or nuclear system in a specified state. For an exponentially decaying system, it is the average time for the number of atoms or nuclei in a specified state to decrease by a factor e. Synonymous with mean lifetime.

09310.title: average matrix relative sensitivity factor
09310.definition: Coefficient, proportional to the intensity, calculated for an element in an average matrix, by which the measured intensity for that element is divided in calculations to yield the atomic concentration or atomic fraction of the element present in the sample.

14356.title: average number of radicals per particle
14356.definition: Ratio of the total number of radicals in particles to the number of particles.

A00542.title: average rate of flow
A00542.definition: The ratio of the mass of a drop, at the instant when it is detached from the tip of the capillary, to the drop time \(t_{1}\); the average value of the instantaneous rate of flow over the entire life of the drop.

09664.title: avidity
09664.definition: Net affinity of all binding sites of all antibodies in the antiserum under specified physicochemical reaction conditions.

A00543.title: Avogadro constant
A00543.definition: The Avogadro constant, \(N_{\rm{A}} = \pu{6.02214076E23 mol-1}\), is a proportionality constant between the quantity amount of substance (\(n\), with unit mole) and the quantity for counting entities (\(N\) with unit one, symbol 1), \(N = N_{\rm{A}}\ n\).

11626.title: avoidance test
11626.definition: Associative learning pairing an adverse event with a non-specific stimulus such that the animal learns to respond in a manner to avoid the adverse event.

A00544.title: avoided crossing
A00544.definition: Frequently, two Born–Oppenheimer electronic states (A, B) change their energy order as molecular geometry (x) is changed continuously along a path. In the process their energies may become equal at some points (the surfaces are said to cross, dotted lines in the figure), or only come relatively close (the crossing of the surfaces is said to be avoided). If the electronic states are of the same symmetry, the surface crossing is always avoided in diatomics and usually avoided in polyatomics.   Synonymous with intended crossing.

A00545.title: Avrami equation
A00545.definition: An equation, describing crystallization kinetics, of the form: \[1 - \varphi _{c} = \rm{e}^{K\ t^{n}}\] where \(\varphi _{c}\) is the crystalline volume fraction developed at time \(t\) and constant temperature, \(K\) and \(n\) are suitable parameters. \(K\) is temperature dependent. According to the original theory, \(n\) should be an integer from 1 to 4, the value of which should depend only on the type of the statistical model; however, it has become customary to regard it as an adjustable parameter that may be non-integral.

14460.title: axenic culture
14460.definition: Growth of organisms of a single species in the absence of cells or living organisms of any other species.

A00546.title: axial
A00546.definition: In the chair form of cyclohexane ring bonds to ring atoms (and molecular entities attached to such bonds) are termed axial or equatorial according to whether the bonds make a relatively large or small angle, respectively, with the plane containing or passing closest to a majority of the ring atoms. Thus the axial bonds are approximately parallel to the $C_{3}$ axis and the equatorial bonds approximately parallel to two of the ring bonds. These terms are also used for the chair form of other saturated six-membered rings. The corresponding bonds occurring at the allylic positions in mono-unsaturated six-membered rings are termed pseudo-axial (or quasi-axial) and pseudo-equatorial (or quasi-equatorial). The terms axial and equatorial have similarly been used in relation to the puckered conformation of cyclobutane, crown conformer of cyclooctane, etc. and the terms pseudo-axial and pseudo-equatorial in the context of the non-planar structures of cyclopentane and cycloheptane.  See apical for an alternative use of axial and equatorial with bipyramidal structures.

A00547.title: axial chirality
A00547.definition: Term used to refer to stereoisomerism resulting from the non-planar arrangement of four groups in pairs about a chirality axis. It is exemplified by allenes $\ce{abC=C=Ccd}$ (or $\ce{abC=C=Cab}$) and by the atropisomerism of ortho-substituted biphenyls. The configuration in molecular entities possessing axial chirality is specified by the stereodescriptors $R_{\rm{a}}$ and $S_{\rm{a}}$ (or by $P$ or $M$).

10451.title: axial skeleton
10451.definition: Bones of the body axis, including the skull, spinal column, ribs and sternum.

08457.title: axial viewing mode
08457.definition: Inductively-coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer configuration in which the entrance slit is aligned with the main plasma axis.

A00548.title: axialite
A00548.definition: A multilayer aggregate, consisting of lamellar crystals splaying out from a common edge.

11627.title: axon
11627.definition: Long thread-like process of a neuron along which impulses are conducted from the cell body to the nerve ending.

11628.title: axonal degeneration
11628.definition: Progressive loss of structure and function of an axon, typically in a peripheral-to-central direction.

11629.title: axonal transport
11629.definition: Movement of organelles and biomolecules to (retrograde) and from (anterograde) a neuron’s cell body, within the cytoplasm of its axon (the axoplasm).

11630.title: axonopathy
11630.definition: Damage (peripheral neuropathy) to multiple nerves in roughly the same areas on both sides of the body, causing weakness, numbness, and paresthesia.

AT07329.title: aza-di-π-methane rearrangement
AT07329.definition: Photochemical reaction of a 1-aza-1,4-diene or a 2-aza-1,4-diene in the triplet excited state to form the corresponding cyclopropylimine.

A00553.title: azanes
A00553.definition: Saturated acyclic nitrogen hydrides having the general formula $\ce{N_{n}H_{n+2}}$.

15381.title: azeotropic copolymerisation
15381.definition: Binary copolymerization in which the two monomer reactivity ratios, \(r_{12}\) and \(r_{21}\) are not both equal to unity yet the copolymerization forms a copolymer with its molar ratio of monomer units equal to the molar ratio of monomers in the monomer feed.

15315.title: azeotropic point
15315.definition: For a mixture, temperature and pressure (the azeotropic temperature and pressure) at which the compositions of the liquid and vapor phases become equal (the azeotropic composition), but the intensive properties of the two phases (such as molar volume) are different.

A00555.title: azides
A00555.definition: Compounds bearing the group $\ce{N3}$, viz. $\ce{–N=N^{+}=N^{-}}$; usually attached to carbon, e.g. $\ce{PhN3}$ phenyl azide or azidobenzene.Salts of hydrazoic acid, $\ce{HN3}$, e.g. $\ce{NaN3}$ sodium azide.

A00557.title: azines
A00557.definition: Condensation products, $\ce{R2C=NN=CR2}$, of two moles of a carbonyl compound with one mole of hydrazine  (this term should not be confused with the ending -azine appearing in Hantzsch–Widman names for some heterocycles).

A00558.title: azinic acids
A00558.definition: Derivatives of the parent structure $\ce{H2N^{+}(O^{−})OH}$, of which the alkylidene derivatives, $\ce{R2C=N^{+}(O^{−})OH}$ (tautomers of nitroalkanes), are the most commonly encountered. The alkylideneazinic acids are known as nitronic acids, or synonymously as aci-nitro compounds, e.g. $\ce{CH2=N^{+}(O^{−})OH}$ methylideneazinic acid.

A00559.title: azlactones
A00559.definition: Oxazol-5(4$H$)-ones I, compounds derived by cyclization of $N$-acyl $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}amino}$ carboxylic acids, $\ce{RC(=O)NHCR2C(=O)OH}$, through formal loss of the elements of water. 4-Hydrocarbylideneazlactones II are often referred to as 'unsaturated azlactones'.

A00560.title: azo compounds
A00560.definition: Derivatives of diazene (diimide), $\ce{HN=NH}$, wherein both hydrogens are substituted by hydrocarbyl groups, e.g. $\ce{PhN=NPh}$ azobenzene or diphenyldiazene.

A00561.title: azo imides
A00561.definition: N-Imides of azo compounds, analogous to azoxy compounds, having a delocalized structure  commonly but undesirably referred to as 'azimines'.

A00562.title: azomethine imides
A00562.definition: The 1,3-dipolar N-imides of azomethines having the structure   The term azo ylides, derived from the second resonance form, has also been used.

A00564.title: azomethines
A00564.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RN=CR2}$ ($\ce{R\neq H}$). Many consider the term to include the compounds $\ce{RN=CRH}$ ($\ce{R\neq H}$), thus making azomethines synonymous with Schiff bases.

A00566.title: azonic acids
A00566.definition: $N$-Hydrocarbyl derivatives of the parent structure $\ce{HN^{+}(O^{−})(OH)2}$. Cf. phosphonic acids.

10452.title: azoospermia
10452.definition: Absence of viable spermatozoa in the semen.

A00567.title: azoxy compounds
A00567.definition: $N$-Oxides of azo compounds of structure $\ce{RN=N^{+}(O^{−})R}$, e.g. $\ce{PhN=N^{+}(O^{−})Ph}$ azoxybenzene or diphenyldiazene oxide.

12965.title: autoimmune bullous skin disease
12965.definition: Any of several autoimmune diseases characterized by intraepidermal or subepidermal blisters (e.g., pemphigus vulgaris, bullous pemphigoid) and highly specific autoantibodies against components of the desmosome or hemidesmosome (e.g., desmoglein 3, BP180).

13037.title: allergic conjunctivitis
13037.definition: Irritation of the ocular conjunctiva, resulting from the activation of conjunctival mast cells by airborne allergens such as pollens or house dust.

13166.title: autoimmune gastritis
13166.definition: Autoimmune-mediated destruction of the gastric mucosa that may result in the development of pernicious anemia.

13332.title: autoimmune infertility
13332.definition: Infertility caused by sperm antibodies, autoimmune ovarian inflammation (oophoritis), or autoimmune orchitis.

13481.title: acquired myasthenia gravis
13481.definition: Autoimmune disease characterized by muscle weakness usually affecting ocular and oropharyngeal muscles due to an autoimmune attack against components of the neuromuscular junction (e.g., the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor).

13491.title: autoimmune myositis
13491.definition: Rare systemic inflammatory myopathy, including primary polymyositis, primary dermatomyositis, myositis associated with malignancy, childhood dermatomyositis, and myositis with multisystem autoimmune disease [e.g., mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), systemic sclerosis (SSc)].

13506.title: autoimmune nephritis
13506.definition: Inflammation of the kidney due to immunological reaction to renal antigens.

13507.title: autoimmune neuropathy
13507.definition: Autoimmune disease of the nervous system.

13555.title: autoimmune peripheral neuropathy
13555.definition: Acute or chronic inflammatory neuropathy leading to demyelination and axonal damage of nerves and nerve roots associated with high-titeredautoantibodies against gangliosides [e.g., Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS), Miller–Fisher syndrome, acute sensory ataxic neuropathy].

16208.title: aromatic substitution photochemical electrophile-olefin combination
16208.definition: Photosubstitution in electron-rich aromatic compounds, upon reaction with electron-deficient olefins, occurring in polar solvents through an electron-transfer pathway.

16210.title: aromatic substitution photochemical radical-olefin combination
16210.definition: Regioselective combination of a radical, an olefin, and an arene via a photoinduced electron-transfer pathway.

13587.title: autoimmune polyendocrinopathy
13587.definition: Autoimmune disease affecting multiple endocrine organs.

13654.title: allergic rhinitis
13654.definition: Nasal discharge resulting from an allergic response.

13741.title: autoimmune thyroiditis
13741.definition: Inflammatory destruction of the thyroid gland (ranging from a mild focal thyroiditis to extensive lymphocytic infiltration and scarring) often associated with goiter and hypothyroidism.

08143.title: α
08143.definition:
1) Designation applied to the carbon to which a functional group is attached.
2) In carbohydrate nomenclature, a stereochemical designation of the configuration at the anomeric carbon.
3) Parameter in a Brønsted relation expressing the sensitivity of the rate of protonation to acidity.
4) Parameter in Leffler’s relation expressing the sensitivity of changes in Gibbs activation energy to changes in overall Gibbs energy for an elementary reaction.

A00003.title: α, β
A00003.definition: Stereodescriptors, used in a number of different ways.Relative stereodescriptors used in carbohydrate nomenclature to describe the configuration at the anomeric carbon by relating it to the anomeric reference atom. For simple cases the anomeric reference atom is the same as the configurational reference atom. Thus in $\ce{\upalpha\!{-ᴅ-glucopyranose}}$ the reference atom is $\ce{C-5}$ and the $\ce{OH}$ at $\ce{C-1}$ is on the same side as the $\ce{OH}$ at $\ce{C-5}$ in the Fischer projection.Relative stereodescriptors used by Chemical Abstracts Service to describe the configuration of a cyclic molecule (including suitable polycyclic systems) with several stereogenic centres whereby the $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ side of the reference plane is the side on which the substituent with CIP priority lies at the lowest numbered stereogenic centre. The other side is $\ce{\upbeta\!}$. Absolute stereodescriptors originally devised for steroid nomenclature. However in this sense it is only meaningful if there is an agreed absolute configuration and orientation of the structure so as to define the plane and which way up the molecule is represented. Substituents above the plane of the steroid are described as $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ and are shown as a solid line ( or ); those below the plane are described as $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ and are shown by a broken line ( or ). The extension of this system to tetrapyrroles has been documented and it has been widely used elsewhere.

R00002.title: α-ray spectrometer
R00002.definition: A measuring assembly incorporating a radiation detector and a pulse amplitude, used for determining the energy spectrum of $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ ($\ce{\upbeta\!}$, $\ce{\upgamma\!}$) radiation.

A00001.title: α-addition
A00001.definition: A chemical reaction resulting in a single reaction product from two or three reacting chemical species, with formation of two new chemical bonds to the same atom in one of the reactant molecular entities. The synonymous term 1/1/addition is also used. For example:  (This particular example can also be viewed as an insertion reaction.). In inorganic chemistry such $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}addition}$ reactions, generally to a metallic central atom, are known as 'oxidative additions'. $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}Addition}$ is the reverse of α-elimination or 1/1/elimination.

11569.title: α-adrenergic receptor
11569.definition: Class of adrenergicreceptor mainly functioning in vasoconstriction and modulation of glandular secretions.

A00004.title: α-cleavage
A00004.definition: The fission of a bond originating at an atom which is adjacent to one assumed to bear the charge; the definition of $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}}$, $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}}$ cleavage then follows automatically. The process:  would thus be described as $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}fission}$ of a ketone with expulsion of a radical $\ce{R^{1.}}$ The carbon atoms of the radical $\ce{R^{1.}}$ are called the $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}}$, $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}}$, $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}carbons}$, starting with the atom nearest the functional group.

A00005.title: α-decay
A00005.definition: Radioactive decay in which an alpha particle is emitted.

A00006.title: α-effect
A00006.definition: A positive deviation of an $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}nucleophile}$ (a nucleophile bearing an unshared pair of electrons on an atom adjacent to the nucleophilic site) from a Brønsted-type plot of \(\log k_{\rm{nuc}}\) vs. \({\rm{p}}K_{\rm{a}}\) constructed for a series of related normal nucleophiles. More generally, it is the influence of the atom bearing a lone pair of electrons on the reactivity at the adjacent site.

A00007.title: α-elimination
A00007.definition: A transformation of the general type:  where the central atom Z is commonly carbon. The reverse reaction is called α-addition.

E00008.title: α-expulsion
E00008.definition: A general reaction by which a group attached to the alpha carbon of an excited chromophore is expelled either as an odd electron species or as an anionic species. This reaction should be distinguished from an α-(alpha-)cleavage.

12826.title: α:β T cell
12826.definition: Lymphocyte whose T-cell receptor (TCR) is a heterodimer of an \(\upalpha\) chain and a \(\upbeta\) chain.

12825.title: α:β T-cell receptor
12825.definition: T-cell receptor (TCR) consisting of a heterodimer of two different glycoprotein chains, designated \(\upalpha\) and \(\upbeta\), assembled into an \(\upalpha{:}\upbeta\) heterodimer.

A04388.title: π-adduct
A04388.definition: An adduct formed by electron-pair donation from a $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}orbital}$ into a $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}orbital}$, or from a $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}orbital}$ into a $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}orbital}$, or from a $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}orbital}$ into a $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}orbital}$. For example:  Such an adduct has commonly been known as a '$\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}complex}$', but, as the bonding is not necessarily weak, it is better to avoid the term complex.

A05436.title: σ-adduct
A05436.definition: The product formed by the attachment of an electrophilic or nucleophilic entering group or of a radical to a ring carbon of an aromatic species so that a new $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bond}$ is formed and the original conjugation is disrupted. (This has generally been called a '$\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}complex}$', but adduct is more appropriate than complex according to the definitions given.) The term may also be used for analogous adducts to unsaturated (and conjugated) systems in general.

08149.title: β, βnuc, βlg
08149.definition: Parameter in a Brønsted relation expressing the sensitivity of the rate of deprotonation to basicity.

13873.title: bioactivity
13873.definition: Capability of a substance, such as a drug or a vaccine, to provoke a response from a living matter.

13925.title: biomedical
13925.definition: Qualifier for a domain grouping scientific and practical activities related to therapy.

13926.title: bioprosthesis
13926.definition: Implantable prosthesis that consists totally or substantially of nonviable, treated donor tissue.

13927.title: bioresorbability
13927.definition: Ability to be eliminated from an animal or human body through natural pathways.

13874.title: bioadhesion
13874.definition: Adhesion of cells or tissues to the surface of a material.

13928.title: bioresorption
13928.definition: Disappearance of a substance from an organism by processes of metabolism, secretion, or excretion.

13929.title: bone cement
13929.definition: Synthetic, self-curing organic or inorganic material used to fill up a cavity or to create a mechanical fixation.

13875.title: bioalteration
13875.definition: Cell-mediated chemical modification without main chain scission.

13953.title: bioplastic
13953.definition: Biobased polymer derived from the biomass or issued from monomers derived from the biomass and which, at some stage in its processing into finished products, can be shaped by flow.

13877.title: biodegradability
13877.definition: Capability of being degraded by biological activity.

13878.title: biodisintegration
13878.definition: Disintegration resulting from the action of cells.

13879.title: biofilm
13879.definition: Aggregate of microorganisms in which cells that are frequently embedded within a self-produced matrix of extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) adhere to each other and/or to a surface.

13880.title: biofragmentation
13880.definition: Fragmentation resulting from the action of cells.

13881.title: biomaterial
13881.definition: Material exploited in contact with living tissues, organisms, or microorganisms.

13883.title: biostability
13883.definition: Resistance to the deleterious action of living systems that allows preservation of the initial characteristics of a substance.

13884.title: biotic
13884.definition: Pertaining to, or produced by, living cells or organisms.

13885.title: bulk degradation
13885.definition: Homogeneous degradation affecting the volume of a sample.

12344.title: base peak chromatogram
12344.definition: Chromatogram obtained by plotting the signal of the ions represented by the base peak detected in each of a series of mass spectra recorded as a function of retention time.

12345.title: beam mass spectrometer
12345.definition: Mass spectrometer in which an ion beam accelerated from the ion source is transmitted through a m/z analyzer, or analyzers, to the detector.

12346.title: benzyl ion
12346.definition: Even-electron ion \(\ce{C7H7^{+}}\) with the same carbon skeleton as toluene that has lost a hydrogen atom from the methyl side-chain that carries the positive charge.

14248.title: bundle crystal
14248.definition: Crystal in which the chains predominantly extend from the crystal surface, resulting in a fringed-micelle model morphology.

12347.title: b-ion
12347.definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{N}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{C-N}\) bond.

12348.title: blackbody infrared radiative dissociation
12348.definition: Special case of infrared multiphoton dissociation wherein excitation of the reactant ion is caused by absorption of infrared photons radiating from heated blackbody surroundings, which are usually the walls of a vacuum chamber.

12349.title: Brubaker lens
12349.definition: Additional set of four short, cylindrical electrodes, mounted co-linearly with a transmission quadrupole mass spectrometer that is excited with some fraction of the AC potential but not the DC potential applied to the main quadrupole. The Brubaker lens thus acts as a high-pass filter for ion m/z, but the resulting delay in application of the DC potential component also results in a reduction in defocusing by fringe fields and thus significantly improves overall ion transmission efficiency at a given mass resolution.

12350.title: buffer gas
12350.definition: Inert gas used for collisional reduction of the internal or translational energy of ions, such as in ion traps.

13872.title: bioactive
13872.definition: Qualifier for a substance that provokes any response from a living system.

12937.title: B lymphocyte
12937.definition: Bone marrow-derived lymphocyte, expressing an antigen-receptor complex composed of membrane-bound immunoglobulin (Ig) and associated molecular chains.

12932.title: B-1/B-2 cells
12932.definition: Two major subpopulations of B lymphocytes.

12934.title: B-cell linker protein
12934.definition: Adaptor protein operating in B cells that, upon phosphorylation, recruits signaling molecules to membrane lipid rafts.

12936.title: B-cell receptor
12936.definition: Receptor on the surface of a B cell consisting of transmembrane immunoglobulin (Ig) that recognizes a specific antigen.

12935.title: B-cell stimulatory factor
12935.definition: Generic name given to B-cell-specific growth and differentiation factors involved in the T-cell-dependent activation of B cells. Many are now identified as specific interleukins (ILs).

12938.title: B-lymphocyte chemokine
12938.definition: Chemokine that attracts B cells and activated T cells into the follicles of peripheral lymphoid tissues.

12939.title: B-lymphocyte-induced maturation protein 1
12939.definition: Transcriptional repressor in B cells, that switches off genes required for B cell proliferation in the germinal center, and for class switching and affinity maturation.

12933.title: B7 molecule
12933.definition: Co-stimulatory molecule on the surface of T-cell-activating antigen-presenting cells (APCs), allowing full activation of T cells that are bound to major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-peptide complexes.

12940.title: bacille Calmette–Guérin
12940.definition: Attenuated Mycobacterium tuberculosis used both as a specific vaccine for tuberculosis and as an adjuvant.

BT06997.title: back donation
BT06997.definition: A description of the bonding of $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}conjugated}$ ligands to a transition metal which involves a synergic process with donation of electrons from the filled $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}orbital}$ or lone electron pair orbital of the ligand into an empty orbital of the metal (donor–acceptor bond), together with release (back donation) of electrons from an nd orbital of the metal (which is of $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}symmetry}$ with respect to the metal–ligand axis) into the empty $\ce{\uppi\!^{\ast}\mbox{-}antibonding orbital}$ $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}complex}$ of the ligand.

B00575.title: back electron transfer
B00575.definition: A term often used to indicate thermal reversal of excited state electron transfer restoring the donor and acceptor in their original oxidation level. In using this term one should also specify the resulting electronic state of the donor and acceptor.

B00582.title: back scatter coefficient
B00582.definition: Number of back scattered electrons (BSEs) generated per primary electron for a given specimen and experimental condition. It depends on (mean) atomic number of the excited area of the sample, angle between electron beam and sample surface, primary electron energy and thickness of the sample.

B00583.title: back scattered electrons
B00583.definition: All primary electrons which are scattered out of the original direction and retransmitted through the surface of the solid. In practice, electrons emitted from the surface of a solid under electron bombardment which have a kinetic energy in the range between \(50\ \rm{eV}\) and excitation energy (\(E_{0}\)).

09035.title: back titration
09035.definition: Titration of remaining reagent after addition of excess reagent to the titrand.

15494.title: back-mutation
15494.definition: Process that reverses the effect of a mutation which had inactivated a gene; thus, it restores the wild phenotype.

12623.title: back-up compound
12623.definition: Molecule selected as a replacement for the lead drug candidate should this subsequently fail during further preclinical evaluation or in clinical studies.

15382.title: backbiting
15382.definition: Chain transfer from an active center on a macromolecule to another part of the same macromolecule.

BT06885.title: backflush
BT06885.definition: Temporary reversal of the direction of the permeable flow.

B00578.title: background concentration
B00578.definition: The concentration of a given species in a pristine air mass in which anthropogenic impurities of a relatively short lifetime are not present. The background concentrations of relatively long-lived molecules, methane, carbon dioxide, halocarbons ($\ce{CF3Cl}$, $\ce{CF2Cl2}$, etc.) and some other species continue to rise due to anthropogenic input, so the composition of background air is undergoing continual change. Background concentration of a given species is sometimes considered to be the concentration of that impurity in a given air mass when the contribution from anthropogenic sources under study is absent. Synonymous with baseline concentration.

08458.title: background continuum emission
08458.definition: Intense continuous background usually observed in laser-induced breakdown spectra.

08459.title: background equivalent concentration
08459.definition: Concentration of a given element measured at a given wavelength providing the same intensity as the background.

08007.title: background indication
08007.definition: Indication obtained from a phenomenon, body, or substance similar to the one under investigation but for which a quantity of interest is supposed not to be present or is not contributing to the indication.

B00579.title: background mass spectrum
B00579.definition: The mass spectrum observed when no sample is intentionally introduced into the mass spectrometer or spectrograph.

B00577.title: background
B00577.definition: The term employed to designate the value indicated by a radiation measuring device in the absence of the source whose radiation is to be measured, when the device is placed under its normal conditions of operation.

B00580.title: background radiation
B00580.definition: Radiation from any source other than the one it is desired to detect or measure.

B00581.title: backscatter
B00581.definition: Scattering of radiation in a generally backward direction. In the assay of radioactivity, it applies to the scattering of radiation into the radiation detector from any material except the sample and the detector. In light scattering, it is said to occur when the scattering angle, \(\theta \), is \(180^{\unicode{x26ac}}\). Conversely, forward scattering occurs when \(\theta \) is \(0^{\unicode{x26ac}}\).

09311.title: backscattered electron
09311.definition: Electron, originating in the incident beam, which is emitted after interaction with the sample.

08714.title: backscattering analysis
08714.definition: Measurement principle in which the backscattering of nuclear radiation impinging on a sample is applied to measure the structure and composition of materials.

09312.title: backscattering correction factor
09312.definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy, factor equal to the total Auger-electron current arising from ionizations in the sample caused by both primary electrons and backscattered electrons divided by the Auger-electron current arising directly from the primary electrons.

09228.title: backscattering energy
09228.definition: Energy of a particle from the primary beam after it has undergone a backscattering collision and escaped from the sample.

09313.title: backscattering fraction
09313.definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy, Auger-electron current arising from ionizations in the sample caused by backscattered electrons divided by Auger-electron current arising directly from the primary electrons.

09364.title: backscattering spectrum
09364.definition: Plot of backscattering yield versus backscattering energy.

09314.title: backscattering yield
09314.definition: Number of electrons emitted from the sample with energies greater than \(\pu{50 eV}\) divided by the number of electrons incident at a given energy and angle of incidence.

10117.title: backward chaining
10117.definition: Inference method from hypothesis to data that supports the hypothesis

10118.title: backward propagation
10118.definition: Supervised classification method for an artificial neural network in which weights of connections between nodes are calculated from the known output layer back to the input layer.

10119.title: backward stepwise linear discriminant analysis
10119.definition: Linear discriminant analysis in which variables to build the discriminant functions are removed one at a time to minimise the loss of discrimination, until there is a significant loss.

15495.title: bacterial artificial chromosome
15495.definition: DNA vector into which large DNA fragments can be inserted and cloned in a bacterial host.

B00587.title: baffle chamber
B00587.definition: A chamber used in incinerator design to promote the settling of fly ash and coarse particulate matter by changing the direction and/or reducing the velocity of the gases produced by the combustion of the refuse.

B00588.title: bag filter
B00588.definition: A large bag constructed of a suitable fabric which is often tubular in shape, into which a particle-containing air stream flows. Modern bags are constructed of a fabric which is capable of collecting all but very fine particles in the gas stream. The efficiency of the removal of particles of various size ranges changes with the amount of particles captured by the filter and the filtering time. The bag operates on the same principle as the one on a household vacuum cleaner.

15497.title: bagassosis
15497.definition: Lung disease caused by the inhalation of dust from sugar-cane residues.

B00589.title: baghouse
B00589.definition: An installation which contains many bag filters in parallel so that the resistance to air flow in a large installation is not seriously increased by the addition of these controls.

B00590.title: Bainite transition
B00590.definition: A term that is sometimes used in metallurgy for the martensitic transition that describes the transition between a face-centred-cubic lattice and a body-centred-tetragonal lattice. Example: The transition between the face-centred-cubic lattice of austenite and the body-centred-tetragonal lattice of a martensite.

B00591.title: baking
B00591.definition: The process in which the carbonaceous binder, usually coal tar pitch or petroleum pitch, as part of a shaped carbon mix is converted to carbon yielding a rigid carbon body by the slow application of heat. The process can take as little as \(14\ \rm{days}\) in coarse-grained, electrothermic grades (low binder level) and as long as \(36\ \rm{days}\) in ultra-fine-grained, specialty grades (high binder level). The final baking temperature can be in the range of \(1100{-}1500\ \rm{K}\), depending on the grade.

12941.title: BALB/c mouse
12941.definition: Inbred albino mouse strain, substrains of which produce plasmacytomas on injection with mineral oil, useful for the production of monoclonal antibodies.

B00592.title: Baldwin's rules
B00592.definition: A set of empirical rules for certain formations of 3- to 7-membered rings. The predicted pathways are those in which the length and nature of the linking chain enables the terminal atoms to achieve the proper geometries for reaction. The disfavoured cases are subject to severe distortions of bond angles and bond distances.

09229.title: ball cratering
09229.definition: Procedure in which the sample is abraded by a sphere in order to expose compositional changes in layers below the original surface, with the intent that the depth of those layers can be related to the lateral position in the crater created by the abrasion.

08574.title: band shape
08574.definition: Description of the profile of a spectral band.

B00595.title: band spectra
B00595.definition: The combination of many different spectral lines resulting from vibrational, rotational and electronic transitions. Unresolved band spectra may appear as a spectral continuum.

13994.title: band-to-band recombination
13994.definition: Recombination of charge carriers occurring via a one-step electron transition from the conduction band to the valence band in a semiconductor or insulator.

B00593.title: bandgap energy
B00593.definition: The energy difference between the bottom of the conduction band and the top of the valence band in a semiconductor or an insulator.

B00594.title: bandpass filter
B00594.definition: An optical device which permits the transmission of radiation within a specified wavelength range and does not permit transmission of radiation at higher or lower wavelengths. It can be an interference filter.

11631.title: bar test
11631.definition: Test for catalepsy in which a mouse is placed on a bar oriented parallel to and approximately \(\pu{2.5 cm}\) off the ground. Typically, if the mouse remains immobile on the bar for more than 20 seconds, it is considered to be cataleptic.

B00597.title: barbiturates
B00597.definition: Pyrimidine-2,4,6(1H,3H,5H)-trione (trivial name barbituric acid) and derivatives:  (keto tautomeric form)Salts of barbituric acid and its derivatives.

12942.title: bare lymphocyte syndrome
12942.definition: Rare, recessive genetic condition in which the products of one or more genes required to switch on major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I or MHC class II genes are defective or absent. As a consequence, MHC class I (BLS1) or MHC class II (BLS2) genes are not expressed, leading to severe immunodeficiency.

B00598.title: barn
B00598.definition: Non-SI unit of area, \(\rm{b} = 10^{-28}\ \rm{m}^{2}\), used to express cross sections in nuclear reactions.

11632.title: Barnes maze
11632.definition: Circular platform equipped with some 20 equidistant holes near the outer rim, one of which is marked by visual cues and is an escape hole for a rodent that is placed near the middle of the platform and subjected to an adverse stimulus, e.g., bright light.

13797.title: barotropic mesophase
13797.definition: Mesophase formed by varying the pressure at constant temperature.

B00599.title: Barton reaction
B00599.definition: Photolysis of a nitrite to form a $\ce{\updelta\!\mbox{-}nitroso alcohol}$. The mechanism is believed to involve a homolytic $\ce{RO–NO}$ cleavage, followed by $\ce{\updelta\!\mbox{-}hydrogen}$ abstraction and radical coupling.

10453.title: basal ganglia
10453.definition: Complex structure at the base of the brain consisting of several groups of neurons, the caudate nucleus, the putamen, the globus pallidus, and the substantia nigra.

15498.title: basal lamina
15498.definition: Triple-layered structure on which epithelium sits: It consists of an electron-dense layer (lamina densa) between two electron-transparent layers (lamina lucida). The lamina densa is composed of type IV collagen, and the lamina lucida contains the glycoprotein laminin.

B00601.title: base
B00601.definition: A chemical species or molecular entity having an available pair of electrons capable of forming a covalent bond with a hydron (proton) (see Brønsted base) or with the vacant orbital of some other species (see Lewis base).

B00603.title: base kind of quantity
B00603.definition: A kind of quantity considered dimensionally independent of other kinds of quantities, i.e. it is not defined by an equation containing other kinds of quantities, e.g. length, mass, amount of substance.

09686.title: base pair
09686.definition: Pair of two nucleobases, consisting of one purine and one pyrimidine base, held together by hydrogen bonds.

B00607.title: base pairing
B00607.definition: The specific association between two complementary strands of nucleic acids that results from the formation of hydrogen bonds between the base components of the nucleotides of each strand: A=T and G=C in DNA, A=U and G=C (and sometimes G=U) in RNA (the lines indicate the number of hydrogen bonds). Single-stranded nucleic acid molecules can adopt a partially double-stranded structure through intrastrand base pairing.

B00608.title: base peak
B00608.definition: The peak in a mass spectrum corresponding to the separated ion beam which has the greatest intensity. This term may be applied to the spectra of pure substances or mixtures.

B00609.title: base quantity
B00609.definition: One of the quantities that, in a system of quantities, are conventionally accepted as functionally independent of one another. In the SI, these are: length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity. All other physical quantities (and units) are regarded as being derived from these base quantities (and base units).

09453.title: base quencher
09453.definition: Base added to a chemical amplification resist to neutralize low levels of acid that might diffuse into nominally unexposed regions and cause blur.

09687.title: base sequence analysis
09687.definition: Method for determining the nucleotide sequence.

B00610.title: base unit
B00610.definition: Unit of measurement of a base quantity in a given system of quantities. By international agreement, a set of seven dimensionally independent units form the SI base units: the metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela.

B00606.title: baseline error
B00606.definition: An error which arises if the two beams in a double-beam spectrometer are not fully equivalent in transmitted power nor are corrected to be so (e.g. due to unmatched cells).

B00604.title: baseline
B00604.definition: The portion of the chromatogram recording the detector response when only the mobile phase emerges from the column.

14461.title: baseline toxicity
14461.definition: General, nonspecific, reversible mode of toxic action that can be produced in most living organisms by the presence of sufficient amounts of many organic chemicals.

10454.title: basement membrane
10454.definition: Thin layer of connective tissue underlying an attached epithelial cell layer.

09688.title: basic local alignment search tool
09688.definition: Computer algorithm that finds regions of local similarity between deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or protein sequences.

B00611.title: basicity
B00611.definition: For Brønsted bases, the tendency of a compound to act as hydron (proton) acceptor. The basicity of a chemical species is normally expressed by the acidity of the conjugate acid (see conjugate acid–base pair). For Lewis bases it relates to the association constants of Lewis adducts and π-adducts.

BT06998.title: basis function
BT06998.definition: A one-electron function used in the expansion of the molecular orbital function. Basis functions are commonly represented by atomic orbitals (see also Slater-type orbital or Gaussian-type orbital) centered on each atom of the molecule.

BT06999.title: basis set
BT06999.definition: A set of basis functions employed for the representation of molecular orbitals. One may distinguish the minimal basis set (includes one basis function for each SCF occupied atomic orbital with distinct principal and angular momentum quantum numbers); split valence basis set (includes two or more sizes of basis function for each valence orbital); double zeta (DZ) basis set (a split valence basis set that includes exactly twice as many functions as the minimal basis set); extended basis set (the set larger than the double zeta basis set); polarized basis set (incorporates basis functions of higher angular quantum number beyond what is required by the atom in its electronic ground state; allows orbitals to change not only a size, but also a shape); basis set with diffuse functions and others.

11409.title: basis set superposition error
11409.definition: An artifactual increase in calculated stability of the supersystem (the system formed by noncovalent interaction between two or more molecular entities, e.g. hydrogen bond system) resulting from the basis set of the supersystem being larger than for the component subsystems. The BSSE arises from a lowering of the quantum mechanical energy when the electron density of each subsystem spreads into the basis functions provided by the other subsystems.

12943.title: basophil
12943.definition: Type of granulocyte found in the blood and resembling the tissue mast cell.

12944.title: basophilic degranulation
12944.definition: Loss of granules in basophilic cells, associated with the release of active substances from the cells, characteristic of type I immediate hypersensitivity.

09457.title: basting solvent
09457.definition: Solvent in which a resist or additional thin-film component (typically a BARC) is dissolved for the coating process.

14331.title: batch emulsion polymerisation
14331.definition: Emulsion polymerization in which all the ingredients are placed in a reactor prior to reaction.

10166.title: batch extraction
10166.definition: Extraction in which the extraction phase and the sample are confined in an extraction vessel and processed according to a defined procedure.

B00613.title: batch
B00613.definition: A quantity of material which is known or assumed to be produced under uniform conditions. Some vocabularies assume 'lot' and 'batch' to be synonymous. The distinction made here with respect to knowledge of production history permits a lot to consist of one or more batches and is useful in interpreting the results of analysis.

B00615.title: batch operation
B00615.definition: The operation of an analytical instrument in such a way that one or more analytical procedures must be completed for a sequence of samples before the next sequence can be started. This term batch usually implies a sequence of a variably sized group of samples, the size of which is not related to a particular type of instrument.

B00616.title: batch reactor
B00616.definition: In a batch reactor the reactants and the catalyst are placed in the reactor which is then closed to transport of matter and the reaction is allowed to proceed for a given time whereupon the mixture of unreacted material together with the products is withdrawn. Provision for mixing may be required.

15499.title: Bateman function
15499.definition: Equation expressing the build up and decay in concentration of a substance (usually in plasma) based on first-order uptake and elimination in a one-compartment model, having the form \[C = [fDk_{\rm{a}}/V(k_{\rm{a}} - k_{\rm{e}})] [\exp(-k_{\rm{e}}t) - \exp(-k_{\rm{a}}t)] \]where \(C\) is the concentration and \(D\) the dose of the substance, \(f\) the fraction absorbed, and \(V\) the volume of distribution. \(k_{\rm{a}}\) and \(k_{\rm{e}}\) are the first-order rate constants of uptake and elimination, respectively, and \(t\) is time.

B00618.title: bathochromic shift
B00618.definition: Shift of a spectral band to lower frequencies (longer wavelengths) owing to the influence of substitution or a change in environment. It is informally referred to as a red shift and is opposite to hypsochromic shift (blue shift).

11412.title: Bayes’s theorem
11412.definition: A method for calculating prior probability estimates of an event that can be revised in accordance with new observations.

14462.title: Bayesian
14462.definition: Attributed to Thomas Bayes (1702–1761), English mathematician. The term is used to designate concepts relating to inverse probability, especially Bayes’ theorem, a theorem expressing the probability of one of a number of mutually exclusive events \(H_{\rm{i}}\), given some other event \(E\), in terms of the probabilities of all the \(H_{\rm{i}}\) independently of \(E\) and the probabilities of \(E\) given each \(H_{\rm{i}}\).

14463.title: Bayesian probability
14463.definition: Subjective or objective concept of probability as a 'measure of the state of knowledge'.

11410.title: Bayesian regularized neural network
11410.definition: A feed-forward neural network that uses Bayesian statistics to optimize the complexity and predictive power of the model.

11411.title: Bayesian statistics
11411.definition: A branch of statistics in which the evidence of the state of a system is expressed in terms of degrees of belief (probabilities).

11633.title: Bayley scale
11633.definition: Range of scores on play tasks performed by infants age 0–3 years, intended to assess development of motor, cognitive, and language skills against norms for age-matched normal child development.

12945.title: Bcl-2
12945.definition: Member of the Bcl protein family that protects cells from apoptosis by binding to the mitochondrial membrane.

10297.title: bead injection
10297.definition: Fully renewable (disposable) packed sorbent bed for solid-phase extraction in a flow manifold or mesofluidic platform using programmable flow extraction.Bead-injection protocols for automated solid phase microextraction with sorbent renewal for each assay [Reproduced from  https://www.flowinjectiontutorial.com].a) Injection of a metered amount of particles or beads with reactive surfaces in the flow system followed by mechanical trapping or capture with the aid of external energy sources; b) Injection of a metered volume of sample; c) Interaction of analyte(s) with sorptive surfaces; d) Preconcentration of analyte(s) followed by detection of native species or derivatization products; e) Automatic removal of sorptive surfaces.

B00619.title: bead-rod model
B00619.definition: A model simulating the hydrodynamic properties of a chain macromolecule consisting of a sequence of beads, each of which offers hydrodynamic resistance to the flow of the surrounding medium and is connected to the next bead by a rigid rod which does not. The mutual orientation of the rods is random.

B00620.title: bead-spring model
B00620.definition: A model simulating the hydrodynamic properties of a chain macromolecule consisting of a sequence of beads, each of which offers hydrodynamic resistance to the flow of the surrounding medium and is connected to the next bead by a spring which does not contribute to the frictional interaction but which is responsible for the elastic and deformational properties of the chain. The mutual orientation of the springs is random.

11634.title: beading
11634.definition: Focal bead-like swellings in dendrites and axons.

09393.title: beam bunching
09393.definition: Reduction in the spread of arrival times of an ion pulse by reduction in the speed of the leading ions or acceleration of those at the trailing edge of the pulse.

09365.title: beam chopper
09365.definition: Electrostatic or electromagnetic device used to generate pulses of ions from a continuous ion beam.

B00621.title: beam current
B00621.definition: The number of primary electrons reaching the surface of the specimen per unit time expressed as electrical current. Recommended symbol: \(i_{\rm{B}}\); unit: \(\rm{A}\); typical range: \(\mathrm{nA}\). Recommended measurement technique: Faraday cage.

B00622.title: beam diameter
B00622.definition: Diameter of the beam between which 68% of the electrons fall. For Gaussian beam shapes this corresponds to the 2\(\sigma \)-value of the intensity distribution of the beam. Measurement can be carried out by scanning a beam across a sufficiently sharp edge and recording the transmitted electrons.

09436.title: beam footprint
09436.definition: Area on the specimen irradiated by X-rays in X-ray reflectrometry.

09437.title: beam spill-off
09437.definition: Fraction of the incident X-ray beam in X-ray reflectrometry missing the specimen.

08228.title: beam splitter
08228.definition: Device to split a beam of electromagnetic radiation into two parts.

11635.title: beam walking test
11635.definition: Assessment of the ability of an animal to remain upright and to walk on an elevated and relatively narrow beam.

B00624.title: becquerel
B00624.definition: SI derived unit of radioactivity equal to one disintegration per second; admitted for reasons of safeguarding human health, symbol: \(\rm{Bq}\).

B00625.title: bed volume
B00625.definition: Synonymous with column volume for a packed column.

B00626.title: Beer–Lambert law
B00626.definition: The absorbance of a beam of collimated monochromatic radiation in a homogeneous isotropic medium is proportional to the absorption path length, \(l\), and to the concentration, \(c\), or — in the gas phase — to the pressure of the absorbing species. The law can be expressed as: \[A = \rm{log}_{10}\left ( \frac{P_{\lambda }^{0}}{P_{\lambda }} \right ) = \varepsilon \:c\:l\] or \[P_{\lambda }=P_{\lambda }^{0}10^{-\varepsilon \: c\: l}\] where the proportionality constant, \(\varepsilon\), is called the molar (decadic) absorption coefficient. For \(l\) in \(\pu{cm}\) and \(c\) in \(\pu{mol dm-3}\) or \(\rm{M}\), \(\varepsilon\) will result in \(\pu{dm3 mol-1 cm-1}\) or \(\rm{M}^{-1}\ \rm{cm}^{-1}\), which is a commonly used unit. The SI unit of \(\varepsilon\) is \(\pu{m2 mol-1}\). Note that spectral radiant power must be used because the Beer–Lambert law holds only if the spectral bandwidth of the light is narrow compared to spectral linewidths in the spectrum.

B00627.title: before mass analysis
B00627.definition: The sum of all the separate ion currents for ions of the same sign (usually positive) before mass analysis.

14464.title: behavioural teratology
14464.definition: Study of behavioral abnormalities in otherwise apparently normal individuals after exposure in the embryonic state to a substance or physical agent.

14465.title: behavioural toxicology
14465.definition: Study of abnormal behavior produced by exposure to a substance or physical agent.

12946.title: Behcet disease
12946.definition: Chronic vasculitis of unknown origin, characterized by ulcerations and skin rash and treated by immunosuppression.

11413.title: belief theory
11413.definition: A method to combine probability estimate states that given two or more probabilities \(P_{i}\) that a particular event is true, the combined probability of the event is given by: \[P = 1 - \Pi (1 - {P_{i}})\]

10455.title: bell stage
10455.definition: Period in which the developing tooth takes on a bell shape in cross section, immediately preceding the 'advanced bell stage', in which the hard tissues (dentin and enamel) form the crown of the tooth.

B00628.title: Bell–Evans–Polanyi principle
B00628.definition: The linear relation between energy of activation \((E_{\rm{a}})\) and enthalpy of reaction \((\Delta H_{\rm{r}})\) sometimes observed within a series of closely related reactions. \[E_{\rm{a}} = A + B\ \unicode[Times]{x394}H_{\rm{r}}\]

12947.title: Bence–Jones protein
12947.definition: Excess circulating kappa ($\kappa$)-light chain found in the urine of patients with multiple myeloma.

16233.title: benchmark concentration
16233.definition: Statistical lower CL on the concentration that produces a defined response (called the benchmark response or BMR, usually \(\pu{5\%}\) or \(\pu{100\%}\)) for an adverse effect compared to background, defined as \(\pu{0\%}\).Dose–response curve showing BMC and BMCL (BMC 10 % lower CL).

BT06899.title: benchmark dose
BT06899.definition: The statistical lower bound on a dose corresponding to a specified level of risk.

15500.title: benchmark guidance value
15500.definition: Biological monitoring guidance value set at the \(90^{\rm{th}}\) percentile of available biological monitoring results collected from a representative sample of workplaces with good occupational hygiene practices.

15501.title: benchmark response
15501.definition: Response, expressed as an excess of background, at which a benchmark dose or benchmark concentration is set.

B00629.title: bending of energy bands
B00629.definition: The distribution of potential in the space charge region of a semiconductor results in a change in the electron energy levels with distance from the interface. This is usually described as 'bending of the energy bands'. Thus the bands are bent, upwards if \(\sigma >0\) and downwards if \(\sigma

14466.title: beneficial metal
14466.definition: Non-essential metal which in some form (chemical species) at an appropriate dose can improve health of defined organisms, commonly human beings.

14467.title: benefit
14467.definition: Advantage to, or improvement in condition of, an individual, a population, a species, an assemblage, a community, or an ecosystem.

15502.title: benign
15502.definition:
Of a disease, producing no persisting harmful effects.
Tumor that does not invade other tissues (see metastasis ), having lost growth control but not positional control.Note: Such a tumor is not carcinogenic but may cause mechanical damage to adjacent tissues.

12948.title: benign monoclonal gammopathy
12948.definition: Nonmalignant overproduction of $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}globulin}$ by a single clone of lymphocytes.

BT07000.title: Bent's rule
BT07000.definition: In a molecule, smaller bond angles are formed between electronegative ligands since the central atom, to which the ligands are attached, tends to direct bonding hybrid orbitals of greater p character towards its more electronegative substituents.

14468.title: benthic
14468.definition: Living on the bottom of an aquatic system.

11636.title: Benton test
11636.definition: Procedure in which patterns on cards are memorized by a test subject who then attempts to recognize them on other cards presented subsequently.

B00630.title: benzenium ions
B00630.definition: Arenium ions, derived from benzene or substituted derivatives.

B00632.title: benzylic groups
B00632.definition: Arylmethyl groups and derivatives formed by substitution: $\ce{ArCR2^{–}}$, Benzyl, $\ce{C6H5CH2^{–}}$, is the prototype. The term 'benzylic position' or 'benzylic site' refers to the saturated carbon atom. A group, such as $\ce{–OH}$, attached at a benzylic site is sometimes referred to as 'benzylic'.

B00633.title: benzylic intermediates
B00633.definition: Carbanions, carbenium ions or radicals, derived formally by detachment of one hydron, hydride or hydrogen, respectively, from the $\ce{CH3}$ group of toluene or substitution derivatives thereof, e.g. $\ce{C6H5CH2^{.}}$, benzyl radical.

B00634.title: benzynes
B00634.definition: 1,2-Didehydrobenzene (the aryne derived from benzene) and its derivatives formed by substitution; see arynes, dehydroarenes. The terms m- and p-benzyne are occasionally, but erroneously, used for 1,3- and 1,4-didehydrobenzene, respectively.

09590.title: Bernoullian distribution
09590.definition: The Bernoullian distribution is a discrete distribution having two possible outcomes labelled by \(n = 0\) and \(n = 1\), in which \(n = 1\) ('success') occurs with probability $p$ and \(n = 0\) ('failure') occurs with probability \(q = 1 - p\), where $0 \lt p \lt 1$. It is a special case of a binomial distribution corresponding to a random distribution.

15503.title: beryllium disease
15503.definition: Serious and usually permanent lung damage resulting from chronic inhalation of beryllium.

12624.title: best-in-class
12624.definition: Drug acting on a specific molecular target that provides the best balance between efficacy and adverse effects.

12744.title: beta relaxation
12744.definition: Second-highest-temperature or second-lowest-frequency relaxation in the loss curve of a polymer.

12745.title: beta relaxation peak
12745.definition: Second-highest-temperature or second-lowest-frequency peak in the loss curve of a polymer.

12625.title: beta-barrel
12625.definition: Secondary 3D protein structure containing a large beta-sheet that twists and coils to form a closed structure in which the first-strand hydrogen bonds to the last.

12626.title: beta-sheet
12626.definition: Secondary 3D structure of a protein that takes on a flat, pleated appearance.

12627.title: beta-sheet breaker
12627.definition: Compound that on binding to a protein disrupts beta-sheet formation.

B00637.title: betaines
B00637.definition: Originally, the compound betaine, $\ce{(CH3)3N^{+}–CH2C(=O)O^{−}}$ $N,N,N$-trimethylammonioacetate, and similar zwitterionic compounds derived from other amino acids. By extension, neutral molecules having charge-separated forms with an onium atom which bears no hydrogen atoms and that is not adjacent to the anionic atom. Betaines cannot be represented without formal charges. E.g.

B00638.title: betweenanenes
B00638.definition: Bicyclic alkenes having a double bond between the bridgehead atoms and a trans attachment of each branch to the double bond. Thus trans-bicyclo[m.n.0]alk-1 (m+2)-enes.

B00640.title: biased linear pulse amplifier
B00640.definition: A pulse amplifier which, within the limits of its normal operating characteristics, has a constant gain for that portion of an input pulse that exceeds the threshold value and that produces no output for pulses whose amplitude is below the threshold.

15504.title: biased sample
15504.definition: Any sample that is not a random sample.

10456.title: bicornate uterus
10456.definition: Uterus that is divided into two lateral horns as a result of imperfect fusion of the paired embryonic tubes from which the uterus is formed.

BT07331.title: bicycle rearrangement
BT07331.definition: Photochemical rearrangement of unsaturated substrates by group migration over a $\ce{\uppi\! perimeter}$ following the movement of a bicycle pedal. An example is:

BT07330.title: bicycle-pedal mechanism
BT07330.definition: Volume-conserving mechanism proposed for the photoisomerization of conjugated double bonds. Two alternating double bonds rotate concertedly with only the two $\ce{CH}$ units turning in and out of the plane of the molecule.

08144.title: bidentate
08144.definition: Feature of a ligand with two potential binding sites.

11637.title: Biel water maze
11637.definition: A water labyrinth, described by Biel (1940), where rodents are forced to swim until they find a small underwater platform that allows them to escape.

09978.title: biflavonoids
09978.definition: Biflavonoid and other flavonoid oligomers, which occur widely in nature, are exemplified and named in this recommendation (Flv-3.8).

B00642.title: bifunctional catalysis
B00642.definition: Catalysis (usually for hydron transfer) by a bifunctional chemical species involving a mechanism in which both functional groups are implicated in the rate-controlling step, so that the corresponding catalytic coefficient is larger than that expected for catalysis by chemical species containing only one of these functional groups. The term should not be used to describe the concerted action of two different catalysts ('concerted catalysis').

08145.title: bifurcation
08145.definition: Feature on a potential-energy surface whereby a minimum-energy reaction path (MERP) emanating from a saddle point (corresponding to a transition structure) splits in two and leads to alternative products without intervening minima or secondary barriers to overcome. A bifurcation arises when the curvature of the surface in a direction perpendicular to the MERP becomes zero and then negative; it implies the existence of a lower-energy transition structure with a transition vector orthogonal to the original MERP.

10457.title: bilaminar embryo
10457.definition: Early blastula having only two of the three primary germ layers that it will ultimately have; the two layers present are the cells of the epiblast that will give rise to the ectoderm and those of the hypoblast that will become the endoderm during gastrulation - both attached to a basement membrane before the mesoderm has formed.

11414.title: bilinear equation
11414.definition: A QSAR equation that describes the non-linear dependence of the relative biological potency (\(\log 1/C\)) of a molecule on log P by the following form: \[log(1/{C_i}) = a\log P_{i} - b \log (\beta P_{i} + 1) + c\]

15505.title: bilirubin
15505.definition: Orange-yellow pigment, a breakdown product of heme-containing proteins (hemoglobin, myoglobin, cytochromes), which circulates in the blood plasma bound to albumin or as water-soluble glucuronide conjugates, and is excreted in the bile by the liver.

09104.title: bimetallic electrode
09104.definition: Electrode containing two different metals (e.g. platinum and ruthenium) on its surface (e.g. to modify its electrocatalytic properties).

B00644.title: bimodal distribution
B00644.definition: The occurrence of two maxima in a frequency distribution.

BT07564.title: bimodal network
BT07564.definition: Polymer network comprising polymer chains having two significantly different molar-mass distributions between adjacent junction points.

15383.title: binary copolymerisation
15383.definition: Copolymerization involving two species of monomer.

09230.title: binary elastic scattering
09230.definition: Collision between a moving particle and a second particle in which total kinetic energy and total momentum are conserved.

09366.title: binary elastic scattering peak
09366.definition: In ion-scattering spectrometry, increase in the spectrometer detection system response above the background signal, which can be attributed to the binary elastic scattering of an incident ion by a surface atom of a particular mass.

B00646.title: binder
B00646.definition: Usually a coal tar pitch or petroleum pitch (but may include thermosetting resins or mesophase pitch powders) which, when mixed with a binder coke or a filler, constitutes a carbon mix. This is used in preparation of the formation of shaped green bodies and subsequently carbon artifacts.

B00648.title: binder coke
B00648.definition: A constituent of a carbon (or ceramic) artifact resulting from carbonization of the binder during baking.

B00647.title: binder
B00647.definition: An additive used to hold the solid stationary phase to the inactive plate or sheet in thin-layer chromatography.

14111.title: binding assay
14111.definition: Assay in which the specific physical association or interaction between two molecules (e.g., ligand–receptor, antibody–antigen, protein–protein, ligand–transport protein) is measured.

09665.title: binding capacity
09665.definition: Amount of a ligand that binds to a receptor expressed in operational units.

BT07001.title: binding energy
BT07001.definition: The difference between the total energy of a molecular system and the sum of the energies of its isolated $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}}$ and $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bonds}$. The value of binding energy depends upon the geometrical arrangement of the isolated subunits (molecules). According to another definition, the term to be subtracted from the total energy is the sum of the energies of the separate atoms in the corresponding valence states, which compose the molecule.

14112.title: binding isotherm
14112.definition: Graphical representation of the relationship between the amount of ligand that is specifically bound to a receptor per mass of binding material and the amount of free ligand.

B00649.title: binding site
B00649.definition: A specific region (or atom) in a molecular entity that is capable of entering into a stabilizing interaction with another molecular entity. An example of such an interaction is that of an active site in an enzyme with its substrate. Typical forms of interaction are by hydrogen bonding, coordination and ion pair formation. Two binding sites in different molecular entities are said to be complementary if their interaction is stabilizing.

B00650.title: Bingham flow
B00650.definition: Many colloidal dispersions show Bingham flow which is characterized by a $\upsigma\!$-D diagram as shown. At rates of shear greater than that at point A, the following relation applies: \[\sigma - \sigma _{\rm{B}}=\eta _{\Delta }\ D\] where \(\sigma _{\rm{B}}\) (or \(\tau _{\rm{B}}\)) is called the Bingham yield stress, \(\eta _{\Delta }\) is the differential viscosity, \(D\) is the shear rate, and \(\sigma \) is the average of three normal stress components if the deformation is purely dilatational.

12240.title: binodal
12240.definition: Curve in the isobaric temperature-composition plane for a mixture defining the region of composition and temperature across which a transition occurs from miscibility of the components to conditions where single-phase mixtures are metastable or unstable.

10298.title: bioaccessibility
10298.definition: Fraction of analytes desorbed from a sample potentially available to organisms.

14469.title: bioaccessible
14469.definition: Able to come in contact with a living organism and perhaps interact with it with the possibility of absorption into the organism.

14470.title: bioaccumulation
14470.definition: Progressive increase in the amount of a substance in an organism or part of an organism that occurs because the rate of intake from all contributing sources and by all possible routes exceeds the organism’s ability to eliminate the substance from its body.

14471.title: bioaccumulation factor
14471.definition: Ratio of tissue chemical residue to chemical concentration in an external environmental phase (e.g., sediment, water, soil, air, or food). BAF is measured at a steady state in situations where organisms are exposed to multiple sources (e.g., water, sediment, food), unless noted otherwise.

15506.title: bioaccumulation potential
15506.definition: Ability of living organisms to concentrate a substance obtained either directly from the environment or indirectly through its food.

14472.title: bioactivation
14472.definition: Metabolic conversion of a xenobiotic to a more toxic derivative or to one that has more of an effect on living organisms.

09632.title: bioanalytical chemistry
09632.definition: Sub-field of analytical chemistry dealing with analysis of biomolecules.

B00651.title: bioassay
