B00651.definition: A procedure for determining the concentration or biological activity of a substance (e.g. vitamin, hormone, plant growth factor, antibiotic) by measuring its effect on an organism or tissue compared to a standard preparation.

09591.title: bioassimilation
09591.definition: Conversion of a substance into biomass by biochemical processes.

BT06847.title: bioavailability
BT06847.definition: Extent of absorption of a substance by a living organism compared to a standard system.

BT06813.title: bioavailability
BT06813.definition: Ratio of the systemic exposure from extravascular (ev) exposure to that following intravenous (iv) exposure as described by the equation: \[F=\frac{A_{\rm{ev}}\ D_{\rm{iv}}}{B_{\rm{iv}}\ D_{\rm{ev}}}\] where \(F\) is the bioavailabilty, \(A\) and \(B\) are areas under the (plasma) concentration-time curve following extravascular and intravenous administration, respectively, and \(D_{\rm{ev}}\) and \(D_{\rm{iv}}\) are the administered extravascular and intravenous doses.

14473.title: bioavailable
14473.definition: Able to be absorbed by living organisms.

09592.title: biobased
09592.definition: Composed of or derived from, in whole or in part, biological products derived from the biomass (including plant, animal, and marine or forestry materials).

B00652.title: biocatalyst
B00652.definition: An enzyme or enzyme complex consisting of, or derived from, an organism or cell culture (in cell-free or whole-cell forms) that catalyses metabolic reactions in living organisms and/or substrate conversions in various chemical reactions.

14474.title: biocenosis
14474.definition: All the interacting organisms living together in a specified habitat.

15507.title: biochemical mechanism
15507.definition: Reaction or series of reactions, usually enzyme-catalyzed, associated with a specific physiological event in a living organism.

B00653.title: biochemical oxygen demand
B00653.definition: The amount of oxygen, divided by the volume of the system, taken up through the respiratory activity of microorganisms growing on the organic compounds present in the sample (e.g. water or sludge) when incubated at a specified temperature (usually \(\pu{20^{\circ}C}\)) for a fixed period (usually \(\rm{5\ days}\), \(\rm{BOD}_{5}\)). It is a measure of that organic pollution of water which can be degraded biologically. In practice, it is usually expressed in milligrams \(\ce{O2}\) per litre.

B00654.title: biochip
B00654.definition: An integrated circuit whose electrical and logical functions are performed by protein molecules appropriately manipulated.

14475.title: biocide
14475.definition:
Substance intended to kill living organisms.
Nonagricultural pesticide used to control the severity and incidence of pests or diseases, e.g., algicide, slimicide, or disinfectant for the control of algal, fungal, or bacterial growth.

10262.title: biocompatible solid-phase microextraction
10262.definition: Extraction by a matrix-compatible immersion solid-phase microextraction device where the extraction phase and support are chosen to eliminate matrix interferences.

14476.title: bioconcentration
14476.definition: Process leading to a higher concentration of a substance in an organism than in environmental media to which it is exposed.

14477.title: bioconcentration factor
14477.definition: Measure of the tendency for a substance in water to accumulate in aquatic organisms defined as the ratio of the concentration of the substance of concern in the organism to the concentration in water at equilibrium.

BT06756.title: bioconjugate
BT06756.definition: A molecular species produced by living systems of biological origin when it is composed of two parts of different origins, e.g. a conjugate of a xenobiotic with some groups, e.g. glutathione, sulfate or glucuronic acid, to make it soluble in water or compartmentalized within the cell.

09593.title: biodegradable
09593.definition: Qualifier for a substance or device that undergoes biodegradation.

BT07169.title: biodegradable polymer
BT07169.definition: Polymer susceptible to degradation by biological activity, with the degradation accompanied by a lowering of its molar mass.

B00656.title: biodegradation
B00656.definition: Breakdown of a substance catalysed by enzymes in vitro or in vivo. This may be characterized for purposes of hazard assessment as:Primary. Alteration of the chemical structure of a substance resulting in loss of a specific property of that substance.Environmentally acceptable. Biodegradation to such an extent as to remove undesirable properties of the compound. This often corresponds to primary biodegradation but it depends on the circumstances under which the products are discharged into the environment.Ultimate. Complete breakdown of a compound to either fully oxidized or reduced simple molecules (such as carbon dioxide/methane, nitrate/ammonium and water).It should be noted that the products of biodegradation can be more harmful than the substance degraded.

14479.title: biodiversity
14479.definition: Occurrence of a number of species within a given ecosystem or biome, or the presence of a number of community types in a given area.

14480.title: biodiversity action plan
14480.definition: Internationally recognized program designed to protect and restore biological systems containing threatened species and habitats.

B00657.title: bioelectronics
B00657.definition: The application of biomolecular principles to microelectronics such as in biosensors and biochips.

15508.title: bioelimination
15508.definition: Removal, usually from the aqueous phase, of a test substance in the presence of living organisms by biological processes supplemented by physicochemical reactions.

15154.title: bioequivalence
15154.definition:
Relationship between two preparations of the same drug in the same dosage form that have a similar bioavailability.
Dosage forms containing the same drug are said to be bioequivalent if they do not differ significantly in the bioavailability (e.g., AUC, \(c_{\rm{max}}\), \(t_{\rm{max}}\)) of the active constituent/ingredient, when administered in the same dose under similar experimental conditions.

09594.title: bioerosion
09594.definition: Surface degradation resulting from the action of cells.

14481.title: biogeochemical cycle
14481.definition: Movement of elements or molecules among organisms and nonliving compartments of the atmosphere, lithosphere, and hydrosphere.

15509.title: bioinactivation
15509.definition: Metabolic conversion of a xenobiotic to a less toxic derivative.

09654.title: bioinformatics
09654.definition: Discipline encompassing the development and utilisation of computational tools to store, analyse, and interpret biological data.

BT06798.title: bioisostere
BT06798.definition: A compound resulting from the exchange of an atom or group of atoms with another, broadly similar, atom or group of atoms.

15510.title: biokinetics
15510.definition: Science of the movements involved in the distribution of substances.

12949.title: biolistics
12949.definition: Use of small particles, e.g., colloidal gold, as a vehicle for carrying agents (drugs, nucleic acid, etc.) into a cell.

12628.title: biological agent
12628.definition: Biopolymer-based pharmaceutical, such as a protein, applicable to the prevention, treatment, or cure of diseases or injuries to man.

15511.title: biological cycle
15511.definition: Complete circulatory process through which a substance passes in the biosphere. It may involve transport through the various media (air, water, soil), followed by environmental transformation, and carriage through various ecosystems.

14483.title: biological determinant
14483.definition: Property of living organisms that affects human or environmental health.

BT06900.title: biological effect monitoring
BT06900.definition: Continuous or repeated measurement of early biological effects of exposure to a substance to evaluate ambient exposure and health risk by comparison with appropriate reference values based on knowledge of the probable relationship between ambient exposure and biological effects.

BT06901.title: biological exposure index
BT06901.definition: Reference values intended as guidelines for the evaluation of potential health hazards in the practice of industrial hygiene. BEIs represent the levels of determinants that are most likely to be observed in specimens collected from a healthy worker who has been exposed to chemicals to the same extent as a worker with inhalation exposure to the TLV.

B00658.title: biological half life
B00658.definition: For a substance the time required for the amount of that substance in a biological system to be reduced to one half of its value by biological processes, when the rate of removal is approximately exponential.

14482.title: biological indicator
14482.definition: Any biological species or group of species whose performance, abundance, or population status is used to determine the health of an environment or ecosystem by systematic monitoring of chemical, physiological, or behavioral changes.

BT06902.title: biological monitoring
BT06902.definition: Continuous or repeated measurement of potentially toxic substances or their metabolites in tissues, secreta, excreta, expired air, or any combination of these to evaluate occupational or environmental exposure and health risk by comparison with appropriate reference values based on knowledge of the probable relationship between ambient exposure and resultant health effects. Sometimes also called 'biomonitoring'.

15512.title: biological preparation
15512.definition: Compound derived from living organisms and their products for use in medicine or as a pesticide, etc.

15155.title: biological product
15155.definition: Virus, therapeutic serum, toxin, antitoxin, or analogous product applicable to the prevention, treatment, or cure of diseases or injuries in humans and/or animals.

09655.title: biological recognition element
09655.definition: Component of biological origin that translates information from the biochemical domain into a physical or chemical domain with a defined selectivity.

15513.title: biological specimen
15513.definition:
Organ, tissue (including blood), secretion, or excretion product taken from an organism as a sample reflecting the state of the whole organism.
Organism taken as a sample reflecting the state of a population or their environment.

BT06903.title: biological tolerance values for working materials
BT06903.definition: The maximum permissible quantity of a chemical compound or its metabolites, or any deviation from the norm of biological parameters induced by those substances in exposed humans.

15514.title: biological warfare
15514.definition: Military operations using any organism (bacteria, virus, or other disease-causing organism) or toxin found in nature, to kill, injure, or incapacitate human beings, animals, or plants.

09634.title: biomacromolecule
09634.definition: Macromolecule (including proteins, nucleic acids, and polysaccharides) formed by living organisms.

14484.title: biomagnification
14484.definition:
Sequence of processes by which higher concentrations of a substance are attained in organisms at higher trophic levels.
Result of these processes of bioconcentration and bioaccumulation by which tissue concentrations of bioaccumulated chemicals increase as the chemical passes up through two or more trophic levels.
Note: Biomagnification occurs in a food chain as a consequence of efficient transfer of a substance from food to consumer accompanied by the lack of, or very slow, excretion or degradation of the substance.

14485.title: biomagnification factor
14485.definition: Ratio of concentrations of a compound at two consecutive trophic levels at steady state. It can also be expressed in terms of a rate constant-based bioaccumulation model \[B = C_{n}/C_{n-1} = \alpha f/k_{\rm{e}}\] where \(\alpha\) is assimilation efficiency, \(f\) is feeding rate, and \(k_{\rm{e}}\) is the first-order elimination constant. \(B\) can be calculated from field data on assumed trophic relations or from laboratory feeding experiments.

BT06904.title: biomarker
BT06904.definition: A parameter that can be used to identify a toxic effect in an individual organism and can be used in extrapolation between species, or as an indicator signalling an event or condition in a biological system or sample and giving a measure of exposure, effect, or susceptibility. The term 'biomarker' is generally used in scientific publications. In occupational hygiene and health, 'biological monitoring' and 'biological effect monitoring' are used with the meaning 'monitoring biomarkers'.

14486.title: biomarker of effect
14486.definition: Biomarker that, depending upon the magnitude, can be recognized as associated with an established or possible health impairment or disease.

14487.title: biomarker of exposure
14487.definition: Biomarker that relates exposure to a xenobiotic to the levels of the substance or its metabolite, or of the product of an interaction between the substance and some target molecule or cell, that can be measured in a compartment within an organism.

14488.title: biomarker of susceptibility
14488.definition: Biomarker of an inherent or acquired ability of an organism to respond to exposure to a specific substance.

B00660.title: biomass
B00660.definition: Material produced by the growth of microorganisms, plants or animals.

14489.title: biome
14489.definition: Set of plants and animals that occupy a certain geographic area.

BT06768.title: biomimetic
BT06768.definition: Refers to a laboratory procedure designed to imitate a natural chemical process. Also refers to a compound that mimics a biological material in its structure or function.

14490.title: biomodification
14490.definition: Alteration of the chemical or physical properties of a substance by the action of living organisms.

14491.title: biomonitor
14491.definition:
n. Organism that provides quantitative information on the quality of the environment around it.Note: The ideal substance biomonitor would indicate the presence of a specific pollutant and provide additional information about the amount present.
v. To use organisms to monitor pollutants and to deduce possible effects on biota or routes of toxicant exposure to humans.

14492.title: biomonitoring type 1
14492.definition: Determination of community changes along a gradient or among sites differing in levels of pollution.

14493.title: biomonitoring type 2
14493.definition: Determination of bioaccumulation in organisms among sites notionally varying in the level of contamination.

14494.title: biomonitoring type 3
14494.definition: Determination of effects on organisms using tools such as biochemical markers in sentinel species or some measure of diminished fitness or condition of individuals.

14495.title: biomonitoring type 4
14495.definition: Determination of genetically based resistance in populations of contaminated areas.

12950.title: biopanning
12950.definition: Technique for selection of peptides with high affinity binding to a chosen target.

14496.title: biopesticide
14496.definition: Biological agent with pesticidal activity, e.g., the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis when used to kill insects.

15156.title: biopharmaceutics
15156.definition: Branch of pharmaceutical science that deals with the fate of drugs in the living system; particularly the release of the drug from its dosage form into a biological medium, its passage across membranes into the systemic circulation, metabolism, and elimination, and the application of this knowledge to obtain the desired therapeutic effect.

B00661.title: biopolymers
B00661.definition: Macromolecules (including proteins, nucleic acids and polysaccharides) formed by living organisms.

15515.title: biopsy
15515.definition: Excision of a small piece of living tissue for microscopic or biochemical examination; usually performed to establish a diagnosis.

B00662.title: bioreactor
B00662.definition: An apparatus used to carry out any kind of bioprocess; examples include fermenter or enzyme reactor.

09092.title: biorecognition
09092.definition: Detection principle for a chemically modified electrode (CME) in which the electrode is modified by a biological recognition element.

09595.title: biorelated
09595.definition: Qualifier for actions or substances that are connected to living systems.

14497.title: bioremediation
14497.definition: Use of biological organisms such as plants or microbes to aid in removing hazardous substances from an area.

09596.title: bioresorbable
09596.definition: Qualifier used to indicate that a compound or a device is bioresorbed, i.e., totally eliminated or bioassimilated by an animal or a human body.

B00663.title: biosensor
B00663.definition: A device that uses specific biochemical reactions mediated by isolated enzymes, immunosystems, tissues, organelles or whole cells to detect chemical compounds usually by electrical, thermal or optical signals.

B00664.title: biosphere
B00664.definition: That part of the globe that encompasses all forms of life on the earth. It extends from the ocean depths to a few thousand metres of altitude in the atmosphere, and includes life forms at the earth's surface, in soils and constituents which exchange materials with atmospheres, oceans or surfaces.

15516.title: biostatic
15516.definition: Adjective applied to a substance that arrests the growth or multiplication of living organisms.

B00665.title: biosynthesis
B00665.definition: The production of a chemical compound by a living organism (cf. biotransformation).

15517.title: biota
15517.definition: All living organisms as a totality.

14498.title: biota-sediment accumulation factor
14498.definition: Ratio of lipid-normalized tissue chemical residue to carbon-normalized sediment substance concentration (units of mass lipid/mass organic carbon).

B00666.title: biotechnology
B00666.definition: The integration of natural sciences and engineering sciences in order to achieve the application of organisms, cells, parts thereof and molecular analogues for products and services.

14499.title: biotic index
14499.definition: One of several ranking systems calculated from the presence or abundance of sensitive species relative to tolerant species.

14500.title: biotic ligand
14500.definition: Component of a living organism to which an ion or other substance in aqueous solution can bind, usually with subsequent beneficial or harmful effect on the physiology of the organism.

14501.title: biotic ligand model
14501.definition: Model that integrates the interactions of metals with ligands in water to calculate the speciation (based on hardness, salinity, and presence of other metals) and the concentration of ionic species producing toxicity. The BLM chemically and mathematically models the organism’s target site as ligand(s) competing with nonbiotic ligands, based on the concept that toxicity occurs when a metal-(biotic ligand) complex reaches a critical concentration.

14502.title: biotic score
14502.definition: Weighted measurement of organisms present—the weighted part is determined by each group’s pollution tolerance or intolerance. As pollution increases in a stream, the biotic score value tends to increase.

14503.title: biotope
14503.definition: Habitat shared by many species, most often an area that is uniform in environmental conditions and in its distribution of animal and plant life.

B00667.title: biotransformation
B00667.definition: Any chemical conversion of substances that is mediated by living organisms or enzyme preparations derived therefrom.

14504.title: bioturbation
14504.definition: Group of processes whereby organisms affect the structure of sediment.

14505.title: biphasic dose–effect model
14505.definition:
Model of adverse effect vs. dose relationship that, owing to hormesis, dips down from the control level before increasing with the dose; individuals exposed to low, but nontoxic concentrations are healthier than individuals not exposed to the chemical.Note: Biphasic dose–effect curves occur for any nutrient. Hormesis is a phenomenon associated with compounds that have no nutrient properties.
Model of adverse effect vs. dose relationship that changes slope owing to a change in the mechanism of toxic action.Note: This may, e.g., be due to saturation of a transport or metabolic system.

10205.title: biphasic system
10205.definition: Equilibrium system containing two or more solvents forming two phases with a single interface.

B00668.title: biphotonic excitation
B00668.definition: Simultaneous (coherent) absorption of two photons (either same or different wavelength), the energy of excitation being the sum of the energies of the two photons. Also called two-photon excitation.

10085.title: biplot
10085.definition: Combination plot of a scores plot as points and loadings plot as vectors for common factors.

11638.title: bipolar disorder
11638.definition: Psychiatric illness characterized by mood shifts with periods of severe depressive illness and one or more episodes of exaggerated activity levels (manic behavior).

BT07334.title: bipolarons
BT07334.definition: Bound pairs of polarons mutually attracted by the lattice distortion in a solid.

B00671.title: biradical
B00671.definition: An even-electron molecular entity with two (possibly delocalized) radical centres which act nearly independently of each other, e.g.  Species in which the two radical centres interact significantly are often referred to as 'biradicaloids'. If the two radical centres are located on the same atom, the species are more properly referred to by their generic names: carbenes, nitrenes, etc. The lowest-energy triplet state of a biradical lies below or at most only a little above its lowest singlet state (usually judged relative to \(k_{\rm{B}}\ T\), the product of the Boltzmann constant \(k_{\rm{B}}\) and the absolute temperature \(T\)). The states of those biradicals whose radical centres interact particularly weakly are most easily understood in terms of a pair of local doublets. Theoretical descriptions of low-energy states of biradicals display the presence of two unsaturated valences (biradicals contain one fewer bond than permitted by the rules of valence): the dominant valence bond structures have two dots, the low energy molecular orbital configurations have only two electrons in two approximately nonbonding molecular orbitals, two of the natural orbitals have occupancies close to one, etc. Although this term has been recommended in the past for diradicals, specialists working in the field prefer the latter term.

10458.title: birth
10458.definition: Start of life as a physically separate being, e.g., the emergence of a baby from the body of its mother, or the hatching of an egg.

10459.title: birth defect
10459.definition: Physical or biochemical abnormality that is present at birth, and that may either be inherited or be the result of environmental influence.

14506.title: birth rate
14506.definition:
(in demography) Number of live births in a defined administrative jurisdiction in a calendar year divided by a midyear population of the jurisdiction, with the customary multiplier of \(\pu{1000}\) to produce a whole number rather than a decimal or a fraction. Note: An alternative statistic is total fertility rate, the average number of children born to each woman over the course of her life. In general, the total fertility rate is a better indicator of fertility rates because, unlike the crude birth rate, it is not affected by the age distribution of the population.
(in ecology) Number of births, \(B\), in a population of a defined size, \(N\), during a specified time interval \(\Delta t\). The rate is calculated from the formula \[B = \Delta N/\Delta t\] where \(\Delta N\) is the change in the number of births in a limited time period \(\Delta t\).

B00673.title: bisecting conformation
B00673.definition: For a structure containing the grouping $\ce{R3C–C(Y)=X}$ (with identical or different groups $\ce{R}$) the conformation in which the torsion angle is such that $\ce{X}$ is antiperiplanar to one of the groups $\ce{R}$, and, in a Newman projection, the double bond $\ce{C=X}$ bisects one of the $\ce{R–C–R}$ angles. In this conformation the bond $\ce{C–Y}$ eclipses one of the $\ce{C–R}$ bonds. The other conformation, in which $\ce{X}$ is synperiplanar to one of the groups $\ce{R}$, is called an eclipsing conformation.

B00674.title: bismuthanes
B00674.definition: The saturated hydrides of tervalent bismuth, having the general formula $\ce{Bi_{n}H_{n+2}$. Hydrocarbyl derivatives of $\ce{BiH3}$ belong to the class bismuthines.

B00675.title: bismuthines
B00675.definition: $\ce{BiH3}$ and compounds derived from it by substituting one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups: $\ce{R3Bi}$, $\ce{RBiH2}$, $\ce{R2BiH}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{RH}$) are called primary, secondary and tertiary bismuthines, respectively. A specific bismuthine is preferably named as a substituted bismuthane, e.g. $\ce{(CH3)3Bi}$ trimethylbismuthane.

12951.title: bispecific antibody
12951.definition: Artificially produced hybrid antibody in which each of the two antigen-binding arms is specific for a different antigenic epitope. Such antibodies, which can be produced either by chemical cross-linkage or by recombinant DNA techniques, can be used to link together two different antigens or cells, e.g., a cytotoxic T lymphocyte and a tumor cell.

B00676.title: bisphenols
B00676.definition: By usage, the methylenediphenols, $\ce{HOC6H4CH2C6H4OH}$, commonly $p,p$-methylenediphenol, and their substitution products (generally derived from condensation of two equivalent amounts of a phenol with an aldehyde or ketone).

11415.title: bit string
11415.definition:
A description of a molecule in a fixed length vector, each element of which is set from corresponding structural keys or calculated by hashing a molecular
 fingerprint.

B00677.title: bivane
B00677.definition: A wind vane used in turbulence studies to obtain horizontal and vertical components of the wind vector.

13995.title: black body
13995.definition: Idealised object absorbing all incident radiant power, regardless of wavelength and transforming it all into heat. No electromagnetic radiation passes through it and none is reflected. A black body is a perfect absorber of radiant energy. Therefore, it is also a perfect emitter of radiation. The wavelength distribution of the radiation of a black body depends only on its temperature and not on its internal nature or structure.

B00678.title: black film
B00678.definition: A film thinner than about \(\frac{1}{4}\) wavelength of visible light. Black films are often equilibrium film, but equilibrium films may be considerably thicker under some conditions. In soap films, two types of equilibrium film are often observed: the one characterized by thickness of the order of \(7\ \rm{nm}\) or more which varies significantly with minor changes in composition such as ionic strength is called 'common black film'.

13996.title: black-body-like photocatalytic reactor
13996.definition: Reactor used to determine quantum yields of photoadsorption and photocatalysed reactions when the catalyst is in the form of a powdered layer (or powder dispersion). The incident photons are (nearly) all absorbed by the catalyst, provided that the dispersion layer is sufficiently thick (or the dispersion is sufficiently concentrated).

10263.title: blade format
10263.definition: Solid-phase microextraction device where the extraction phase (sorbent) is dispersed in the form of a thin coating on the surface of a blade.

08008.title: blank correction
08008.definition: Step in a measurement procedure in which the effect of a blank indication is removed from an indication.

08009.title: blank indication
08009.definition: Indication obtained from a sample of blank material under the measurement conditions for the measurand.

08010.title: blank material
08010.definition: Material which contains no, or as little as possible, of the analyte of interest used in measurement to establish a blank indication.

09992.title: blank nominal indication
09992.definition: Nominal indication obtained from an object similar to the one under investigation, except that the nominal property of interest is supposed not to be present, or is not contributing to the nominal indication.

09036.title: blank titration
09036.definition: Titration performed with titrand containing no analyte.

B00679.title: blank value
B00679.definition: A reading or result originating from the matrix, reagents and any residual bias in the measurement device or process, which contributes to the value obtained for the quantity in the analytical procedure.

12952.title: blast
12952.definition: Immature stage in cell development, before the appearance of the definitive characteristics of the cell; used also as a word termination, as in erythroblast, etc.

10460.title: blastema
10460.definition: Mass of cells from which an organ or a body part develops, either in normal development or in the regeneration of a lost body part.

10461.title: blastocoel
10461.definition: Fluid-filled cavity in the blastula of a developing embryo.

10462.title: blastocyst
10462.definition: Modified blastula that is characteristic of placental mammals.

10463.title: blastomere
10463.definition: Any of the cells formed by cleavage of a fertilized egg.

10464.title: blastula
10464.definition: Hollow mass of cells formed after a zygote has undergone approximately six cell divisions.

10465.title: blastulation
10465.definition: Process by which the early embryo transforms from the morula into the blastula.

12953.title: Blau syndrome
12953.definition: Rare familial inflammatory disease characterized by arthritis, dermatitis, and uveitis.

B00680.title: blaze-angle
B00680.definition: The angle (\(\beta \)) between the operating facet of the grooves and the overall plane of a grating.

B00681.title: bleaching
B00681.definition: The loss of absorption or emission intensity.

12232.title: blob
12232.definition: Hypothetical spherical volume element occupied by a subchain of a macromolecule between two neighbouring entanglements on the same macromolecule.

08314.title: Bloch equations
08314.definition: Set of coupled differential equations which can be used to describe the behaviour of a magnetization vector under any conditions.

08315.title: Bloch–Siegert shift
08315.definition: Frequency difference seen for a nuclear magnetic resonance signal when a radiofrequency field is applied during the acquisition time.

B00682.title: block
B00682.definition: A portion of a macromolecule, comprising many constitutional units that has at least one feature which is not present in the adjacent portions. Where appropriate, definitions relating to 'macromolecule' may also be applied to 'block'.

B00683.title: block copolymer
B00683.definition: A copolymer that is a block polymer. In the constituent macromolecules of a block copolymer, adjacent blocks are constitutionally different, i.e. adjacent blocks comprise constitutional units derived from different species of monomer or from the same species of monomer but with a different composition or sequence distribution of constitutional units.

09454.title: block copolymer lithography
09454.definition: Process in which a thin film of block copolymer is formed into a regular nanoscale pattern.

11536.title: block homopolymer
11536.definition: Homopolymer that is composed of macromolecules comprising blocks that have at least one constitutional or configurational feature which is not present in the adjacent portions.

B00684.title: block macromolecule
B00684.definition: A macromolecule which is composed of blocks in linear sequence.

B00685.title: block polymer
B00685.definition: A polymer composed of block macromolecules.

12629.title: blockbuster drug
12629.definition: Drug that generates annual sales of USD 1 billion (\(\$\pu{E9}\)) or more.

09666.title: blocking
09666.definition: Coating of an immunospecific surface (e.g. serum, tissues, cells, biological macromolecules, biosensor surface) to form an active cover with selectivity or an inert layer.

12954.title: blocking antibody
12954.definition: Antibody that prevents other antibodies from combining with a specific antigen but does not itself produce an immunological response when combined with that antigen.

09367.title: blocking geometry
09367.definition: Experimental arrangement wherein the atom rows or planes of a single-crystal target are aligned parallel to a vector from the sample to the detector.

09636.title: blood
09636.definition: Fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries, and veins.

09637.title: blood cell
09637.definition: Any cellular element of the blood, including erythrocytes, leucocytes, and platelets.

09638.title: blood cell count
09638.definition: Number of red blood cells and white blood cells per unit volume in a specimen of venous blood.

12955.title: blood dyscrasia
12955.definition: Presence of abnormal material in the blood, usually applied to diseases affecting blood cells or platelets.

09639.title: blood group
09639.definition: Red cell phenotypes classified by their antigenic structural characteristics, which are under the control of various allelic genes.

12956.title: blood group antigen
12956.definition: Surface antigen on erythrocytes, detectable with a specific antibody from other individuals.

11640.title: blood–brain barrier
11640.definition: Selectively permeable structure that restricts the exit of blood cells and many substances from the brain capillaries into the extracellular space of the brain.

11641.title: blood–cerebrospinal fluid barrier
11641.definition: Functional restriction by cells of the choroid plexus of transit of substances from the cerebrospinal fluid into the extracellular space of the brain.

12957.title: blood–placenta barrier
12957.definition: Physiological interface between maternal and fetal blood circulations that filters out some substances that could harm the fetus while favoring the passage of others such as nutrients.

11642.title: blood–retinal barrier
11642.definition: Functional restriction of transit of substances from the blood to the retina by non-fenestrated endothelial cells with tight junctions.

10466.title: blood–testis barrier
10466.definition: Occluding barrier, formed by the Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubules, that separates the more mature cells of spermatogenesis from blood-borne products.

12958.title: Bloom syndrome
12958.definition: Disease caused by mutations in a DNA helicase and characterized by low T cell numbers, reduced antibody levels, and an increased susceptibility to respiratory infections, cancer, and radiation damage.

B00686.title: blotting
B00686.definition: A technique used for transferring DNA, RNA or protein from gels to a suitable binding matrix, such as nitrocellulose or Nylon paper, while maintaining the same physical separation.

B00687.title: blowdown
B00687.definition: Hydrocarbons purged during refinery shutdowns and startups which should be piped to storage systems for safe venting, flaring or recovery. This term also applies to the purging of water in boiler operation, and serves in the control of dissolved solids in the boiler water.

BT06905.title: body burden
BT06905.definition: Total amount of substance of a chemical present in an organism at a given time.

09640.title: body fluids
09640.definition: Liquids originating from the bodies of living or dead humans, animals, and other organisms.

B00692.title: Bohr magneton
B00692.definition: Electromagnetic fundamental physical constant: \[\mu _{\rm{B}} = \frac{e\ \mathrm{\hslash }}{2\ m_{\rm{e}}} = 9.274\hspace{0.5em}0154\hspace{0.25em}\left(31\right)\times 10^{-24}\ \mathrm{J}\ \mathrm{T}^{-1}\] where \(e\) is the elementary charge, \(\mathrm{\hslash}\) the Planck constant divided by \(2\ \pi \) and \(m_{\rm{e}}\) the electron rest mass.

B00693.title: Bohr radius
B00693.definition: Atomic fundamental physical constant used as atomic unit of length: \[a_{0}=\frac{4\ \pi \ \varepsilon_{0}\ \mathrm{\hslash }^{2}}{m_{\rm{e}}\ e^{2}}=5.291 \ 772\ 49\ (24)\times 10^{-11}\ \rm{m}\] where \(e\) is the elementary charge, \(\mathrm{\hslash}\) is the Planck constant divided by \(2\ \pi \) and \(m_{\rm{e}}\) is the electron rest mass.

13796.title: boloamphiphile
13796.definition: Amphiphile, the constituent molecules of which have solvophilic groups at each end of a solvophobic chain.

B00694.title: bolometer
B00694.definition: A detector constructed from a material having a large temperature coefficient of resistance. Absorption of radiation gives rise to a change in resistance. A bolometer is named according to its active component, e.g. thermistor bolometer, semiconductor bolometer, superconductor bolometer.

B00695.title: Boltzmann constant
B00695.definition: The Boltzmann constant, \(k\), is one of seven fixed constants defining the International System of Units, the SI, with \(k = \pu{1.380649E-23 J K-1}\). The Boltzmann constant is a proportionality constant between the quantities temperature (with unit kelvin) and energy (with unit joule).

08316.title: Boltzmann distribution of nuclear spins
08316.definition: Distribution of nuclear spins among their possible energy levels at thermal equilibrium.

11416.title: Boltzmann enhanced discrimination of receiver operating characteristic
11416.definition: A generalization of the area under the ROC curve to weight more heavily the early recognition of active compounds.

15519.title: bolus
15519.definition:
Single dose of a substance, originally a large pill.
Dose of a substance administered by a single rapid intravenous injection.
Concentrated mass of food ready to be swallowed.

B00696.title: bomb-digestion
B00696.definition: Materials which are not fully dissolved by acid-digestion at atmospheric pressure may require a more vigorous treatment in pressure vessels lined with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) glass, silica or vitreous (glassy) carbon or in sealed silica tubes; this treatment is called bomb-digestion. The test sample and acids are heated in such a closed vessel, so that the digestion is carried out at higher temperature and pressure.

B00697.title: bond
B00697.definition: There is a chemical bond between two atoms or groups of atoms in the case that the forces acting between them are such as to lead to the formation of an aggregate with sufficient stability to make it convenient for the chemist to consider it as an independent 'molecular species'.

B00698.title: bond dissociation
B00698.definition: (In ordinary usage the term refers to homolysis only.)

B00701.title: bond energy
B00701.definition: The average value of the gas-phase bond dissociation energies (usually at a temperature of \(298\ \rm{K}\)) for all bonds of the same type within the same chemical species. The mean bond energy for methane, for example, is one-fourth the enthalpy of reaction for:  Tabulated bond energies are generally values of bond energies averaged over a number of selected typical chemical species containing that type of bond.

BT07002.title: bond energy
BT07002.definition: The energy required to break a given type of bond between atoms in certain valence states. An averaged bond energy is commonly derived by dissecting the heat of atomization of a molecule into contributions of individual bonds. For molecules with localized bonds, the heats of atomization (formation) are usually well approximated by the sum of pertinent averaged bond energies.

08147.title: bond enthalpy
08147.definition: Average value of the gas-phase bond-dissociation enthalpies (usually at a temperature of \(\pu{298 K}\)) for all bonds of the same type within the same chemical species.

BT07003.title: bond length
BT07003.definition: The distance between atomic centers involved in a chemical bond. The notion of bond length is defined differently in various experimental methods of determination of molecular geometry; this leads to small (usually \(0.01{-}0.02\ \mathring{\rm{A}}\)) differences in bond lengths obtained by different techniques. For example, in gas-phase electron-diffraction experiments, the bond length is the interatomic distance averaged over all occupied vibrational states at a given temperature. In an X-ray crystal structural method, the bond length is associated with the distance between the centroids of electron densities around the nuclei. In gas-phase microwave spectroscopy, the bond length is an effective interatomic distance derived from measurements on a number of isotopic molecules, etc. A number of empirical relationships between bond lengths and bond orders in polyatomic molecules were suggested, see, for example, fractional bond number (the Pauling's bond order).

B00705.title: bond number
B00705.definition: The number of electron-pair bonds between two nuclei in any given Lewis formula. For example, in ethene the bond number between the carbon atoms is two, and between the carbon and hydrogen atoms it is one.

BT07004.title: bond orbital
BT07004.definition: A localized molecular orbital related to a certain $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}}$, $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}}$, or $\ce{\updelta\!\mbox{-}bond}$.

BT07005.title: bond order

B00707.title: bond order
B00707.definition: Theoretical index of the degree of bonding between two atoms relative to that of a single bond, i.e. the bond provided by one localized electron pair. In molecular orbital theory it is the sum of the products of the corresponding atomic orbital coefficients (weights) over all the occupied molecular spin-orbitals.

BT07006.title: bond-dissociation energy
BT07006.definition: For a diatomic molecule, the maximum vibrational energy that a molecule can have prior to its decomposition into the ground electronic states of the constituent atoms (spectroscopic bond-dissociation energy, \(D_{\rm{e}}\)). The \(D_{\rm{e}}\) value is related to the chemical dissociation energy: \(D_{\rm{0}}=D_{\rm{e}}- \mathrm{E}_{\rm{vib}}\left(0\right)\), where \(\mathrm{E}_{\rm{vib}}\left(0\right)\) is zero-point vibrational energy. This definition is usually extended to the dissociation of polyatomic molecules into certain molecular fragments through homolytic or heterolytic bond cleavages.

B00699.title: bond-dissociation energy
B00699.definition: The enthalpy (per mole) required to break a given bond of some specific molecular entity by homolysis, e.g. for , symbolized as \(D\left(\rm{CH}_{3}\,-\rm{H}\right)\) (cf. heterolytic bond dissociation energy).

08146.title: bond-dissociation enthalpy
08146.definition: Standard molar enthalpy required to break a given bond of some specific molecular entity by homolysis.

B00702.title: bond-energy-bond-order method
B00702.definition: An empirical procedure for estimating activation energies, involving empirical relationships between bond length, bond dissociation energy, and bond order.

08148.title: bond-stretch isomers
08148.definition: Two (or more) molecules with the same spin multiplicity but with different lengths for one or more bonds.

B00700.title: bonded phase
B00700.definition: A stationary phase which is covalently bonded to the support particles or to the inside wall of the column tubing.

BT07007.title: bonding molecular orbital
BT07007.definition: The molecular orbital whose occupation by electrons increases the total bonding (usually, lowers the total energy) of a molecule. Generally, the energy level of a bonding MO lies lower than the average of the valence orbitals of the atoms constituting the molecule.

B00703.title: bonding number
B00703.definition: The bonding number \(n\) of a skeletal atom is the sum of the total number of bonding equivalents (valence bonds) of that skeletal atom to adjacent skeletal atoms in a parent hydride, if any, and the number of attached hydrogen atoms, if any. Examples: $\ce{SH2}$: for $\ce{S}$, \(n=2\); $\ce{SH6}$: for $\ce{S}$, \(n=6\).

10467.title: bone age
10467.definition: Average age at which children reach a given stage of bone maturation, denoting the stage of skeletal development of an individual fetus or child.

12959.title: bone marrow
12959.definition: Soft fatty vascular substance in the cavity of bone where blood cells are formed.

12960.title: bone marrow transplantation
12960.definition: Transfer of bone marrow from a donor to a recipient whose bone marrow has been ablated.

10468.title: bone morphogenetic protein
10468.definition: Any of a family of growth factors involved in bone and cartilage formation and, more generally, in orchestrating tissue architecture through morphogenetic signals.

10469.title: bone morphogenetic protein-4
10469.definition: Bone morphogenetic protein member of the transforming growth factor \(\upbeta\) (TGF-\(\upbeta\)) superfamily.

14507.title: boomerang effect
14507.definition: Delayed damage from earlier environmental contamination.

12961.title: booster
12961.definition: Portion of an immunizing agent given at a later time to stimulate the effects of a previous dose of the same agent.

11417.title: bootstrap resampling
11417.definition: A procedure to evaluate the accuracy of the statistics of a model, such as the overall R2 or the contribution of particular properties, by systematically recomputing the statistics generated from many models developed using sample sets that contain the same number of observations as the original set, but for which certain observations are randomly omitted and other observations are included more than once.

10086.title: bootstrapping
10086.definition: Estimation of parameters by multiple re-sampling from measured data to approximate its distribution.

B00709.title: boranes
B00709.definition: The molecular hydrides of boron, e.g. $\ce{B5H9}$ pentaborane(9).

B00710.title: boranylidenes
B00710.definition: The species $\ce{RB{:}}$ containing an electrically neutral univalent boron atom with two formally non-bonding electrons.

B00711.title: borderline mechanism
B00711.definition: A mechanism intermediate between two extremes, for example a nucleophilic substitution intermediate between \(\rm{S}_{\rm{N}}1\) and \(\rm{S}_{\rm{N}}2\), or intermediate between electron transfer and \(\rm{S}_{\rm{N}}2\).

14508.title: borderline metal ions
14508.definition: Metal ions intermediate in properties between class a and class b metal ions.

BT07008.title: Born–Oppenheimer approximation
BT07008.definition: Representation of the complete wavefunction as a product of an electronic and a nuclear part, \[\Psi \left(\rm{r,R}\right)=\Psi _{\rm{e}}\left(\rm{r,R}\right)\ \Psi _{\rm{N}}\left(\rm{R}\right)\] where the two wave-functions may be determined separately by solving two different Schroedinger equations. The validity of the Born–Oppenheimer approximation is founded on the fact that the ratio of electronic to nuclear mass (\(\frac{m}{M}\cong 5\times 10^{-4}\)) is sufficiently small and the nuclei, as compared to the rapidly moving electrons, appear to be fixed. The approximation breaks down near a point where two electronic states acquire the same energy (see Jahn–Teller effect). The BO approximation is often considered as being synonymous with the adiabatic approximation. More precisely, the latter term denotes the case when \(\Psi _{\rm{e}}\) diagonalize the electronic Hamiltonian. Thus, the adiabatic approximation is an application of the BO approximation.

09091.title: boron-doped diamond electrode
09091.definition: Electrode composed of a boron-doped diamond film on an electron-conducting substrate.

B00716.title: boson
B00716.definition: Particle of integer spin quantum number following Bose–Einstein statistics.

11643.title: Boston naming test
11643.definition: Procedure in which 60 pictures are shown to a subject who has to name them quickly.

15520.title: botanical pesticide
15520.definition: Substance with activity against pests, that is produced naturally within a plant and may act as a defense against predators.

09455.title: bottom anti-reflective coating
09455.definition: Layer placed between a photoresist and a substrate to prevent reflection from the latter resulting in a reduction in photoresist pattern quality, as characterized by resolution, line edge roughness, etc.

14509.title: bottom-up ecotoxicological study
14509.definition: Approach to investigating ecotoxicological effects that starts with a determination of the presence and nature of any adverse effects via responses at the suborganismal (cellular and biochemical) levels of organization rather than via the community and (or) ecosystem levels of organization.

09735.title: bottom-up proteomics
09735.definition: Approach to identify proteins and characterise their amino acid sequences or post-translational modifications by sequential combination of proteolysis (enzymatic proteolysis and chemical proteolysis) prior to mass spectrometric analysis of the resulting proteolytic peptides.

15521.title: botulism
15521.definition: Acute food poisoning caused by botulinum toxin produced in food by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum and characterized by muscle weakness and paralysis; disturbances of vision, swallowing, and speech; and a high mortality rate.

B00718.title: bound fraction
B00718.definition: The fraction of the incubation mixture which, after separation, contains the analyte bound to the binding reagent.

09667.title: bound/free ratio
09667.definition: Amount of analyte bound by a label divided by amount of unbound (free) analyte

B00717.title: boundary layer
B00717.definition: That well-mixed region of the lower atmosphere in which the turbulence is maintained largely by convective buoyancy induced by the upward heat flux originating from the solar-heated surface of the earth. During the afternoon this often extends from \(1\ \rm{km}\) to \(5\ \rm{km}\) in height. The surface boundary layer is that region of the lower atmosphere where the shearing stress is constant. It is separated by the Ekman layer from the free atmosphere, where the behaviour of the atmosphere approaches that of an ideal fluid in approximate geostrophic equilibrium (horizontal coriolis force balances the horizontal pressure force at all points in the field).

10160.title: boundary layer thickness
10160.definition: Distance from the interface beyond which mass transfer is determined by convection.

B00719.title: bowsprit
B00719.definition: In the boat form of cyclohexane and related structures there are two ring atoms lying out of the plane of the other four; exocyclic bonds to these two atoms pointing in a direction roughly parallel to that plane are called bowsprit, the other two are called flagpole.

16228.title: bowtie entanglement
16228.definition: Chain entanglement with topology similar to that of a bowtie.

11644.title: brachial plexus
11644.definition: Bundle of nerve fibers that begins in the spine at the base of the neck, travels through the axilla (armpit region), and into the arm.

10470.title: brachydactyly
10470.definition: Congenital abnormal shortness of fingers and toes.

15522.title: brady-
15522.definition: Prefix meaning slow as in bradycardia or bradypnoea.

12962.title: bradykinin
12962.definition: Vasoactive peptide and inflammatory mediator produced at sites of tissue damage.

08575.title: Bragg filter
08575.definition: Optical filter used, for example, to attenuate Rayleigh scattering while transmitting light subject to Raman shift.

09231.title: Bragg’s rule
09231.definition: Empirical rule formulated by W.H. Bragg and R. Kleeman that states that the stopping cross section of a compound sample is equal to the sum of the products of the elemental stopping cross sections for each constituent and its atomic fraction. \[S_{\ce{AB}}(\varepsilon) = xS_{\ce{A}}(\varepsilon) + yS_{\ce{B}}(\varepsilon)\] where \(S_{\ce{AB}}(\varepsilon)\) is the stopping cross section of the compound \(\ce{A}_{x}\ce{B}_{y}\), and \(S_{\ce{A}}(\varepsilon)\) and \(S_{\ce{B}}(\varepsilon)\) are the stopping cross sections of elements \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\), respectively.

11647.title: brain
11647.definition: That part of the central nervous system contained within the cranium.

11649.title: brain herniation
11649.definition: Movement of part of the brain across structures within the skull such as a shift across such structures as the falx cerebri, the tentorium cerebelli, and even sometimes through the foramen magnum in the base of the skull (through which the spinal cord connects with the brain).

11650.title: brain slice
11650.definition: Slice of brain tissue immersed in artificial cerebrospinal fluid, used in electrophysiology experiments to allow study of a synapse or neural circuit in isolation from the rest of the brain, and in metabolic studies, under controlled physiological conditions.

11648.title: brain-derived neurotrophic factor
11648.definition: Protein secreted by the brain that acts on neurons in the central and peripheral nervous systems; a member of the neurotrophin family of growth factors, related to the nerve growth factor (NGF).

11651.title: brainstem
11651.definition: Unpaired subdivision of the brain, continuous with the spinal cord, that includes the thalamus, hypothalamus, pons, medulla oblongata, and the mesencephalon.

B00720.title: branch
B00720.definition: An oligomeric or polymeric offshoot from a macromolecular chain.

09602.title: branch constitutional repeating unit
09602.definition: Constitutional repeating unit of connectivity three or more connected at least to three other constitutional repeating units.

B00728.title: branch point
B00728.definition: Point on a polymer chain at which a branch is attached.

B00729.title: branch unit
B00729.definition: A constitutional unit containing a branch point.

B00721.title: branched chain
B00721.definition: A chain with at least one branch point intermediate between the boundary units.

B00722.title: branched polymer
B00722.definition: A polymer the molecules of which are branched chains.

10471.title: branchial
10471.definition: Of, relating to, or resembling the gills of a fish or the homologous embryonic structures and their derivatives in higher animals.

10472.title: branchial arch
10472.definition:
In embryology, one of several arches, resembling the gill arches of a fish, found in the embryo of a higher vertebrate; these arches develop into structures of the ear and neck.
In biology, one of several bony or cartilaginous arches located on either side of the pharynx and supporting the gills in fish and amphibians.

B00723.title: branching chain reaction
B00723.definition: A chain reaction which includes a propagation step or steps in which there is an increase in the number of active intermediates; for example,  is a branching reaction since one active intermediate ($\ce{H}$) gives rise to two ($\ce{OH}$ and $\ce{O}$).

B00724.title: branching decay
B00724.definition: Nuclear decay which can proceed in two or more different ways.

B00725.title: branching fraction
B00725.definition: In branching decay the fraction of nuclei which decay in a specified way.

B00726.title: branching index
B00726.definition: A parameter, \(g\), characterizing the effect of long-chain branches on the size of a branched macromolecule in solution and defined as the ratio of the mean-square radius of gyration of a branched molecule, \(< s_{\rm{b}}^{2} >\), to that of an otherwise identical linear molecule, \(< s _{\rm{l}}^{2} >\), with the same relative molecular mass in the same solvent and at the same temperature, i.e. \(g = \frac{< s_{\rm{b}}^{2} >}{< s_{\rm{l}}^{2} >}\).

BT07335.title: branching plane
BT07335.definition: At a conical intersection point, the plane spanned by the gradient difference vector (\(\boldsymbol{x_{1}}\)) and the gradient of the interstate coupling vector (\(\boldsymbol{x_{2}}\)): \[x_{1} = \frac{\delta(E_{2}-E_{1})}{\delta Q}\boldsymbol{q}\] \[x_{2} = \boldsymbol{q}\] where \(\boldsymbol{C_{1}}\) and \(\boldsymbol{C_{2}}\) are the configuration interaction eigenvectors (i.e., the excited and ground-state adiabatic wavefunctions) in a conical intersection problem, \(H\) is the conical intersection Hamiltonian, \(\textbf{Q}\) represents the nuclear configuration vector of the system, and thus \(\textbf{q}\) is a unit vector in the direction of vector \(\textbf{q}\). \(E_{1}\) and \(E_{2}\) are the energies of the lower and upper states, respectively.

B00727.title: branching ratio
B00727.definition: The ratio of alternative products formed in a reaction (e.g. the $\ce{HF}$/$\ce{DF}$ ratio in the reaction between $\ce{F}$ and $\ce{HD}$).

B00730.title: break
B00730.definition: The process involving the coalescence of gas bubbles.

B00731.title: break
B00731.definition: The flocculation of an emulsion, viz. the formation of aggregates may be followed by coalescence. If coalescence is extensive it leads to the formation of a macrophase and the emulsion is said to break.

08460.title: breakdown threshold fluence
08460.definition: Minimum fluence required to achieve measurable emission signals

14380.title: breaking of an emulsion
14380.definition: Formation of a system with separate macrophases from an emulsion.

10161.title: breakthrough volume
10161.definition: Sample volume at which a defined amount of an analyte pumped continuously through an extraction device will begin to be eluted. Typical breakthrough curve indicating the breakthrough volume \(V_{\rm{B}}\) and the sample volume corresponding to the saturation capacity of the sorbent \(V_{\rm{C}}\) (\(V_{\rm{R}}\) corresponds to the chromatographic elution volume and \(\upsigma_{\rm{v}}\) the standard deviation of the derivative of the curve).Typical breakthrough curve indicating the breakthrough volume \(V_{\rm{B}}\) and the sample volume corresponding to the saturation capacity of the sorbent \(V_{\rm{C}}\) (\(V_{\rm{R}}\) corresponds to the chromatographic elution volume and \(\upsigma_{\rm{v}}\) the standard deviation of the derivative of the curve).

15524.title: breathing zone
15524.definition: Space within a radius of \(\pu{0.5 m}\) from a person’s face.

B00732.title: Bredt's rule
B00732.definition: A double bond cannot be placed with one terminus at the bridgehead of a bridged ring system unless the rings are large enough to accommodate the double bond without excessive strain. For example, while bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-1-ene is only capable of existence as a transient, its higher homologues having a double bond at the bridgehead position have been isolated: e.g.

B00733.title: breeching
B00733.definition: The passage or conduit through which the exhaust products of combustion are carried to the stack or chimney.

B00734.title: breeze
B00734.definition: A term sometimes used to describe very fine particles of coke. Also a meteorological term for a gentle wind.

B00735.title: Bremsstrahlung
B00735.definition: X-radiation emitted as a result of the retardation of high energy particles by matter.

BT07336.title: Brewster angle
BT07336.definition: When an unpolarized planar electromagnetic wavefront impinges on a flat dielectric surface, there is a unique angle (\(\theta_{\rm{B}}\)), commonly referred to as Brewster angle, at which the reflected waves are all polarized into a single plane.

B00736.title: bridge
B00736.definition: A valence bond or an atom or an unbranched chain of atoms connecting two different parts of a molecule. The two tertiary carbon atoms connected through the bridge are termed bridgeheads.

B00739.title: bridge index
B00739.definition: In a coordination entity, the number of central atoms linked by a particular bridging ligand.

B00740.title: bridge solution
B00740.definition: Solution of high concentration of inert salt, preferably comprising cations and anions of equal mobility, optionally interposed between the reference electrode filling and both the test and standard solution, when the test solution and filling solution are chemically incompatible. This procedure introduces into the operational cell a second liquid junction formed usually in a similar way to the first. (This definition refers to a bridge solution of a double junction reference electrode.)

B00737.title: bridged carbocation
B00737.definition: A carbocation (real or hypothetical) in which there are two (or more) carbon atoms that could in alternative Lewis formulae be designated as carbenium centres but which is instead represented by a structure in which a group (a hydrogen atom or a hydrocarbon residue, possibly with substituents in non-involved positions) bridges these potential carbenium centres. One may distinguish 'electron-sufficient bridged carbocations' and 'electron-deficient bridged carbocations'. Examples of the former are phenyl-bridged ions (for which the trivial name 'phenonium ion' has been used), such as (A). These ions are straightforwardly classified as carbenium ions. The latter type of ion necessarily involves three-centre bonding. Structures (C) and (D) contain five-coordinate carbon atoms. The 'hydrogen-bridged carbocation' (B) contains a two-coordinate hydrogen atom. hypercoordination, which includes two-coordination for hydrogen and five- but also higher coordination for carbon is generally observed in bridged carbocations.

16247.title: bridgehead atom
16247.definition: Atom that is part of two or more rings in a polycyclic molecule and that is separated from another bridgehead atom by bridges all of which contain at least one other atom.

B00741.title: bridging ligand
B00741.definition: A ligand attached to two or more, usually metallic, central atoms.

BT07337.title: brightness
BT07337.definition: Obsolete term. This term is reserved for non-quantitative reference to physiological perception of light and is not recommended as a quantitative measure of the radiance of an emitting device, e.g., a lamp.

BT07338.title: brightness
BT07338.definition: Product of the fluorescence quantum yield (\(\varPhi _{\rm{f}}\)) of a dye and the molar decadic absorption coefficient at the excitation wavelength, \(\varepsilon\left(\lambda \right)\), i.e., \(\varPhi _{\rm{f}}\ \varepsilon\left(\lambda \right)\).

14510.title: Brillouin index
14510.definition: Quantitative value for community species diversity calculated as \[H_{\rm{B}} = (\ln N! - \sum \ln n_{i}!)/N\] where \(N\) is the total number of individuals and \(n_{i}\) is the number of individuals in the \(i^{\rm{th}}\) species.

11652.title: Broca area
11652.definition: Region in the frontal lobe of one of the hemispheres (the speech-dominant hemisphere, usually the left) of the hominid brain that is involved in motor functions of speech production.

12963.title: bronchial provocation test
12963.definition: Test of alteration of lung function induced by inhalation of an allergen or airway-constricting agent, providing information on bronchial responsiveness.

15525.title: bronchoconstriction
15525.definition: Narrowing of the air passages through the bronchi of the lungs.

15526.title: bronchodilation
15526.definition: Expansion of the air passages through the bronchi of the lungs.

10475.title: bronchopulmonary segment
10475.definition: Largest subdivision of a lobe of the lung with its air supply from a major branch of the bronchus and having its own arterial blood supply.

15527.title: bronchospasm
15527.definition: Intermittent violent contraction of the air passages of the lungs.

14511.title: broodstock
14511.definition: Adult fish producing either eggs or sperm.

B00747.title: Brooks and Taylor structure
B00747.definition: The structure of the anisotropic spheres which precipitate from isotropic pitch during pyrolysis. The structure of the spheres consists of a lamellar arrangement of aromatic molecules in parallel layers which are perpendicular to the polar axis of the sphere and which are perpendicular to the mesophase-isotropic phase interface.

09932.title: Brownian field-flow fractionation mode
09932.definition: Mechanism of field-flow fractionation of sub-micron particles that relies on Brownian motion.

B00748.title: Brownian motion
B00748.definition: The movement of particles in a colloidal system such as an aerosol caused by collision with the molecules in the fluid in which the particles are imbedded.

B00744.title: Brønsted acid
B00744.definition: A molecular entity capable of donating a hydron (proton) to a base, (i.e. a 'hydron donor') or the corresponding chemical species. For example: $\ce{H2O}$, $\ce{H3O^{+}}$, $\ce{CH3CO2H}$, $\ce{H2SO4}$, $\ce{HSO4^{−}}$, $\ce{HCl}$, $\ce{CH3OH}$, $\ce{NH3}$.

B00745.title: Brønsted base
B00745.definition: A molecular entity capable of accepting a hydron (proton) from an acid (i.e. a 'hydron acceptor') or the corresponding chemical species. For example: $\ce{OH−}$, $\ce{H2O}$, $\ce{CH3CO2^{−}}$, $\ce{HSO4^{−}}$, $\ce{SO4^{2−}}$, $\ce{Cl^{−}}$.

B00746.title: Brønsted relation
B00746.definition: The term applies to either of the equations: \[\frac{k_{\rm{HA}}}{p} = G\left ( \frac{q\ K_{\rm{HA}}}{p} \right )^{\alpha}\] \[\frac{k_{\rm{A}}}{q} = G\left ( \frac{q\ K_{\rm{HA}}}{p} \right )^{-\beta} \] (or their logarithmic forms) where \(\alpha\), \(\beta\) and \(G\) are constants for a given reaction series (\(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are called 'Brønsted exponents'), \(k_{\rm{HA}}\) and \(k_{\rm{A}}\) are catalytic coefficients (or rate coefficients) of reactions whose rates depend on the concentrations of $\ce{HA}$ and/or of $\ce{A^{-}}$. \(K_{\rm{HA}}\) is the acid dissociation constant of the acid $\ce{HA}$, \(p\) is the number of equivalent acidic protons in the acid $\ce{HA}$, and \(q\) is the number of equivalent basic sites in its conjugate base $\ce{A^{-}}$. The chosen values of \(p\) and \(q\) should always be specified. (The charge designations of $\ce{H}$ and $\ce{A}$ are only illustrative.) The Brønsted relation is often termed the 'Brønsted catalysis law' (or the 'Catalysis law'). Although justifiable on historical grounds, this name is not recommended, since Brønsted relations are known to apply to many uncatalysed and pseudo-catalysed reactions (such as simple proton (hydron) transfer reactions). The term 'pseudo-Brønsted relation' is sometimes used for reactions which involve nucleophilic catalysis instead of acid–base catalysis. Various types of Brønsted parameters have been proposed such as \(\beta_{\rm{lg}}\), \(\beta_{\rm{nuc}}\), \(\beta_{\rm{eq}}\) for leaving group, nucleophile and equilibrium constants, respectively.

13997.title: Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface area
13997.definition: Specific surface area (\(\pu{m2 kg-1}\)) determined from the adsorption isotherm of a gas with the help of the Brunauer, Emmett, and Teller model using the conventional value for the molecular cross-section.

11653.title: bruxism
11653.definition: Involuntary habitual grinding of the teeth, frequently during sleep.

B00750.title: bubble column
B00750.definition: A bioreactor, in the shape of a column, in which the reaction medium is kept mixed and aerated by introduction of air into the bottom (cf. air lift bioreactor).

B00751.title: bubbler
B00751.definition: An apparatus used to absorb certain water soluble components in a gas stream for later analysis. Usually it involves the use of a glass fritted tube which forces the air into small bubbles of high surface area during operation.

15157.title: buccal tablet
15157.definition: Usually a small, flat, and soft tablet, which is designed to be placed inside the cheek to be directly absorbed through the mucosa for systemic effect.

10476.title: buccopharyngeal membrane
10476.definition: Membrane present in fetal life that separates the nasal cavities from the pharynx.

10477.title: bud
10477.definition: Small protuberance resembling the bud of a plant and having the potential for growth and differentiation.

12964.title: Buehler assay
12964.definition: Skin sensitization test for contact allergic dermatitis in which a test substance is applied to the shaved flank of a guinea pig in an occlusive patch for 6 h at 0, 1, and 2 weeks, followed by challenge of the untreated flank at 4 weeks.

B00752.title: buffer-addition technique
B00752.definition: A technique in which an additive (called a spectrochemical buffer) is added to both the sample and reference solutions for the purpose of making the measure of the analyte less sensitive to variations in interferent concentration.

15528.title: builder
15528.definition: Material that enhances or maintains the cleaning efficiency of a surfactant, in a detergent, principally by inactivating water hardness; complex phosphates (especially sodium tripolyphosphate, i.e., pentasodium triphosphate), sodium carbonate, and sodium silicate are the builders most commonly used.

10479.title: bulbourethral gland
10479.definition: One of two small glands located on each side of, and inferior to, the prostate, draining to the urethra. Bulbourethral glands secrete a fluid component of the seminal fluid

10480.title: bulbus cordis
10480.definition: Outflow tract of the embryonic heart between the primitive ventricle and the aorta.

B00753.title: bulk concentration
B00753.definition: In any technique that involves the establishment of a concentration gradient, either within the material from which an electrode is made or in the solution that is in contact with an electrode, the bulk concentration of a substance B is the total or analytical concentration of B at points so remote from the electrode-solution interface that the concentration gradient for B is indistinguishable from zero at the instant under consideration. In common practice the bulk concentration of B is taken to be the total or analytical concentration of B that would be present throughout the electrode or solution if there were no current flowing through the cell and if the electrode and solution did not interact in any way. In the absence of any homogeneous reaction or other process that produces or consumes B, the bulk concentration of B is the total or analytical concentration of B that is present before the excitation signal is applied.

15158.title: bulk density
15158.definition: Characteristic of a powder rather than of individual particles given by the mass of powder occupying a known volume.

B00754.title: bulk mesophase
B00754.definition: A continuous anisotropic phase formed by coalescence of mesophase spheres. Bulk mesophase retains fluidity and is deformable in the temperature range up to about \(770\ \rm{K}\), and transforms into green coke by further loss of hydrogen or low-molecular-weight species. This bulk mesophase can sometimes be formed directly from the isotropic pitch without observation of intermediate spheres.

15384.title: bulk polymerisation
15384.definition: Polymerization of an undiluted liquid monomer.

B00755.title: bulk rheology
B00755.definition: Rheology may be conveniently divided into bulk rheology, in which effects due to the surface of the system can be neglected, and surface rheology, in which such effects are predominant. It should be noted that in surface rheology the neglect of bulk behaviour is permissible only in exceptional circumstances, such as for very thin films surrounded by a gas.

B00756.title: bulk sample
B00756.definition: The sample resulting from the planned aggregation or combination of sample units.

09394.title: buncher
09394.definition: Device to shorten the time length of a pulse of ions so that they arrive at a point over a reduced time interval.

10481.title: bundle of His
10481.definition: Band of specialized cardiac muscle fibers connecting the atria with the ventricles of the heart.

B00758.title: Bunnett–Olsen equations
B00758.definition: The equations for the relation between \(\log _{10}(\frac{\rm{[SH}^{+}\rm{]}}{[S]})+\rm{H}_{0}\) and \(\log _{10}\rm{[H}^{+}\rm{]}+\rm{H}_{0}\) for base S in aqueous mineral acid solution, where \(\rm{H}_{0}\) is Hammett's acidity function and \(\log _{10}\rm{[H}^{+}\rm{]}+\rm{H}_{0}\) represents the activity function \(\frac{\log _{10}(\gamma _{S}\ \gamma _{H^{+}})}{\gamma _{\rm{SH}^{+}}}\) for the nitroaniline reference bases to build \(\rm{H}_{0}\). \[\log _{10}(\frac{[\rm{SH}^{+}]}{[\rm{S}]})- \log _{10}[\rm{H}^{+}]=(\varPhi - 1)\ (\log _{10}\rm{[H}^{+}\rm{]}+\rm{H}_{0})+pK_{\rm{SH}^{+}}\] \[\log _{10}(\frac{[\rm{SH}^{+}]}{[\rm{S}]})+H_{0}=\varPhi \ (\log _{10}[\rm{H}^{+}]+\rm{H}_{0})+pK_{\rm{SH}^{+}}\]

B00759.title: Bunsen burner
B00759.definition: Premix burners are distinguished as Bunsen-, Meker-, or slot-burners according to whether they have one large hole, a number of small holes, or a slot as outlet port(s) for the gas mixture, respectively. When several parallel slots are present, they are identified as multislot burners (e.g. a three-slot burner).

15317.title: Bunsen coefficient
15317.definition: Volume \(V^{\rm{g}}\) of an amount \(n_{\ce{B}}^{\rm{l}}\) of a gas dissolved at a given standard temperature \(T^{^⦵\!}\) (usually \(\pu{273.15 K}\)) and given standard (partial) pressure \(p_{\ce{B}}^{_{^⦵\!}}\) (\(\pu{1 bar} = \pu{0.1 MPa}\) or, in older literature, \(\pu{1 atm}\)) divided by the volume of the solvent \(V^{\rm{l}}\) containing an amount \(n_{\ce{A}}\) of solvent at temperature \(T\) and the given total pressure \(p^{_{^⦵\!}}\).

B00760.title: Bunte salts
B00760.definition: Salts (usually sodium salts) of $S$-alkylthiosulfuric acid, of general structure $\ce{RSS(=O)2O^{−}M^{+}}$. Use of this term is discouraged.

12966.title: Burkitt lymphoma
12966.definition: Lymphoma caused by Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), occurring mainly in sub-Saharan Africa.

B00763.title: burn-up
B00763.definition: Induced nuclear transformation of atoms during reactor operation.

B00764.title: burn-up fraction
B00764.definition: The fraction of an initial quantity of a given nuclide that has undergone burn-up.

B00762.title: burning velocity
B00762.definition: The mean velocity of the flame front (in \(\rm{mm s}^{-1}\)) towards the unburnt gas mixture (usually vertically downwards). The quantity applies to gas mixtures and not to injection burners, and depends on the flame temperature and the solvent nebulized.

11654.title: burr hole surgery
11654.definition: Medical intervention in which a hole is drilled or scraped into the human skull, exposing the dura mater, to gain access during surgery, to relieve intracranial pressure, to evacuate a subdural hematoma, etc.

10482.title: bursa
10482.definition: Padlike fluid-filled sac or sac-like cavity, especially one reducing friction at a joint.

12967.title: bursa of Fabricius
12967.definition: Primary lymphoid organ in avian species, located at the cloacal-hind gut junction; it is the site of B-cell maturation.

11655.title: butyrylcholinesterase
11655.definition: Enzyme, found mainly in the liver, that hydrolyzes choline esters; it is non-specific and distinct from acetylcholinesterase.

B00766.title: bypass injector
B00766.definition: A sample injector by means of which the eluent (carrier gas) may be temporarily diverted through a sample chamber so that the sample is carried to the column.

15529.title: byssinosis
15529.definition: Pneumoconiosis caused by inhalation of dust and associated microbial contaminants and observed in cotton, flax, and hemp workers.

12968.title: bystander effect
12968.definition: Positive or negative effect on the immune system seen after exposure to certain drugs, radiation, and other agents, induced by non-immune mechanisms.

15530.title: bystander exposure
15530.definition: Liability of members of the general public to come in contact with substances arising from operations or processes carried out by other individuals in their vicinity.

12969.title: bystander suppression
12969.definition: Suppression of an immune response to an antigen due to tolerance to an unrelated (hence bystander) antigen.

13753.title: blood transfusion
13753.definition: Transference of blood or blood-based products from one individual into the circulation of another.

11570.title: β-adrenergic receptor
11570.definition: Member of a class of G protein-coupled receptors that are targets of the catecholamines, especially adrenalin, noradrenalin, and related substances.

11581.title: β-amyloid
11581.definition: Extracellular aggregate of misfolded fibrous proteins, typically with cross-linked $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}sheet}$ structure.

11639.title: β-blocker
11639.definition: Any of a class of drugs that targets the $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}adrenergic receptor}$, interferes with binding of adrenalin and other related substances to the receptor, and weakens their effects.

B00571.title: β-cleavage
B00571.definition: Fission next but one to a heteroatom or functional group producing a radical and an ion.

B00572.title: β-decay
B00572.definition: Nuclear decay in which a β-particle is emitted or in which orbital electron capture occurs.

08150.title: β-elimination
08150.definition: Transformation of the general type \[\ce{XABY -> A=B + XY (or X + Y, or X^{+} + Y^{-})}\] where the central atoms \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\) are commonly, but not necessarily, carbon.

10326.title: β-N-acetylhexosaminidase
10326.definition: Hydrolytic enzyme (EC 3.2.1.52) that acts on ganglioside \(\rm{G}_{\rm{M2}}\), producing N-acetyl-D-galactosamine and ganglioside \(\rm{G}_{\rm{M3}}\).

B00573.title: β-particle
B00573.definition: Electron ejected from a radioactive nucleus.

12931.title: β2-microglobulin
12931.definition: Small (\(\pu{12 kDa}\)) protein forming part of the structure of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I-encoded molecules.

C00950.title: chain conformational repeating unit
C00950.definition: The smallest structural unit of a polymer chain with a given conformation that is repeated along that chain through symmetry operations.

11658.title: Caenorhabditis elegans
11658.definition: Nematode with a well defined small neural network and homologues of human neurotransmitters, used as a model organism for studying normal development as well as neurotoxicity.

12372.title: conversion dynode
12372.definition: Surface that is held at high potential so that ions striking the surface produce secondary charged particles that are subsequently detected.

12373.title: corona discharge
12373.definition: Electric discharge generated in a gas, usually at atmospheric pressure, surrounding a conductor carrying a sufficiently high potential that the electric field around it ionizes the gas so as to form a plasma in the immediate vicinity of the conductor without causing complete electric breakdown or arcing.

12374.title: corona discharge ionization
12374.definition: Formation of ions in a corona discharge.

12375.title: counter-current gas
12375.definition: Stream of inert gas, often heated, that is used in an electrospray or other spray ionization source to aid in the evaporation of solvent from the sprayed particles. The flow of the gas is in the direction opposite to that of the spray.

12376.title: counter electrode
12376.definition: Counter electrode in an electrospray ionization ion source is one of two electrodes between which the high electric potential is applied, the other electrode being the electrospray needle.

12377.title: cross-flow nebulizer
12377.definition: Pneumatic nebulizer in which the dispersion gas flows at an angle, usually \(\pu{90\!^{\circ}}\), with respect to the column of liquid emerging from a capillary.

12378.title: curved field reflectron
12378.definition: Reflectron designed to provide a decelerating field strength that varies with depth of ion penetration and thus with ion translational energy, permitting energy focusing of ions with a range of translational energies such as those formed as product ions from post-source decay of metastable ions.

12379.title: cyclotron motion
