12379.definition: Circular motion of a charged particle moving perpendicularly to the direction of a magnetic field that results from the Lorentz force.

13930.title: carcinogenicity
13930.definition: Ability or tendency to produce cancer.

13954.title: compost
13954.definition: Solid product resulting from the decomposition of organic wastes by fermentation.

13955.title: conditioning film
13955.definition: Film that is rapidly formed on the surface of a solid in contact with a biological system (in the widest sense) that conditions the surface for subsequent interaction with constituents of the biological system.

14219.title: crystal polymorph
14219.definition: One of the different crystalline phases in which a given substance is able to crystallize.

14233.title: crystalline polymer-inclusion complex
14233.definition: Crystal comprising a polymer guest within a low-molar-mass host.

14234.title: crystalline-polymer molecular complex
14234.definition: Crystalline molecular complex between different polymers.

14243.title: chain-extended crystal
14243.definition: Folded-chain crystal in which each macromolecule makes one, or, at most, a few folds.

13886.title: controlled delivery
13886.definition: Supply of a substance according to desired rate and amount over time.

14261.title: cellulation
14261.definition: Division of the growth front of individual or groups of dominant lamellae into divergent 'cells', with the impurities and the less crystallizable molecules segregated between the cells and at the spherulite boundaries.

14262.title: confined-spaces crystallisation
14262.definition: Polymer crystallization occurring inside elongated cavities, spheres, galleries, or layers formed by a host material different from the polymer.

12351.title: centroid acquisition
12351.definition: Procedure of recording mass spectra in which an automated computer-based system detects peaks, calculates the centroid based on the average m/z value weighted by the intensity, and assigns m/z values based on a calibration file. Only the centroid m/z value and the peak magnitude are stored.

12352.title: charged residue model
12352.definition: Theoretical model for production of highly charged macromolecules by electrospray ionization in which the excess charges on electrosprayed droplets are transferred to and remain on molecules enclosed within the droplets after solvent evaporation.

12353.title: charge inversion reaction
12353.definition: Reaction of an ion with a neutral, surface, or ion of opposite polarity, in which the charge on the product ion is reversed in sign with respect to the reactant ion.

12354.title: charge-mediated fragmentation
12354.definition: Fragmentation of an ion in which the cleavage of one of its bonds is induced by the charge site. The cleaved bond is adjacent to the apparent charge site, and its cleavage involves movement of the electron pair forming that bond to the original charge site and thus migration of the charge to the released fragment.

12355.title: charge remote fragmentation
12355.definition: Fragmentation of an ion in which the cleaved bond is isolated from the apparent charge site by a distance of several bond lengths.

12356.title: charge site derivatization
12356.definition: Chemical derivatization of molecules to introduce a fixed charge site, thus improving ionization efficiency by electrospray ionization or matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization and directing subsequent ion fragmentation in a manner that facilitates structure identification.

12357.title: c-ion
12357.definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{N}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{N-C}\) bond.

12358.title: coaxial reflectron
12358.definition: Reflectron that is arranged such that its main axis is coaxial with the ion source and first stage of the time-of-flight analyzer.

12359.title: collector slit
12359.definition: Slit installed in a magnetic sector mass spectrometer to allow only those m/z separated ions with a specific m/z into the detector system.

12360.title: collisional focusing
12360.definition: Effect where collisions with a buffer gas in a radio-frequency ion trap or transmission quadrupole causes ions to lose translational energy and concentrate at the center of the trap or axis of the linear quadrupole. The effect increases with gas pressure up to a point where ion scattering becomes the dominant process.

12361.title: collision cell
12361.definition: Chamber in the ion path between m/z separation elements, or between ion source acceleration region and the first analyzer, in tandem mass spectrometry in space configurations.

12362.title: collision gas
12362.definition: Inert gas used for collisional excitation or a reactive gas used for ion/molecule reactions.

12363.title: collision quadrupole
12363.definition: Transmission quadrupole to which an oscillating radio frequency potential is applied so as to focus a beam of ions through a collision gas or buffer gas with no m/z separation other than low m/z cut-off.

12364.title: collision reaction cell
12364.definition: Collision cell for removal of interfering ions by ion/neutral reactions in inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry.

12365.title: concentric nebulizer
12365.definition: Pneumatic nebulizer in which the liquid flows through a central capillary and dispersion gas flows through a surrounding outer tube.

12366.title: consecutive reaction monitoring
12366.definition: Multiple-stage mass spectrometry experiment with three or more stages of m/z separation in which products of sequential fragmentation or bimolecular reactions are selected for detection.

12367.title: constant neutral mass gain spectrum
12367.definition: Spectrum formed of all precursor ions that have undergone a selected m/z increase corresponding to the mass of a particular neutral species divided by the charge number of the precursor. The ions detected are the product ions produced by gain of a preselected neutral species mass following ion/molecule reactions of the precursor ions with a reactant gas in a collision cell.

12368.title: constant neutral mass loss spectrum
12368.definition: Spectrum of all precursor ions that have undergone a selected m/z decrement corresponding to the mass of a particular neutral divided by the charge number of the precursor. The ions detected are the product ions produced by loss of a preselected neutral mass following collision-induced dissociation of the precursor ions in a collision cell.

12369.title: continuous dynode particle multiplier
12369.definition: Ion-to-electron detector in which the ion strikes the inner surface of a continuous tube device and induces the production of secondary electrons that, in turn, impinge on the inner surfaces of the device to produce more secondary electrons. This avalanche effect produces an increase in the final measured current pulse.

12370.title: continuous-flow fast atom bombardment
12370.definition: Variant of fast atom bombardment in which the mixture of analyte and liquid matrix is continuously supplied to the sample probe tip.

12371.title: continuous-flow matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization
12371.definition: Variant of matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization in which the analyte is dissolved in a liquid matrix that is continuously supplied to the sample probe tip.

12982.title: C-reactive protein
12982.definition: Serum protein produced by liver cells as part of the acute-phase response, which acts as a stimulus of the classical pathway of complement activation.

09736.title: C-terminal analysis
09736.definition: Chemical method for C-terminal sequencing of proteins and peptides starting at their C-terminus.

09737.title: C-terminus
09737.definition: End of an amino acid chain (protein or polypeptide), terminated by a carboxylic group.

12983.title: C-type lectin
12983.definition: Any of a large family of \(\ce{Ca^{2+}}\)-dependent lectins; members of this family share primary structural homology in their carbohydrate-recognition domains and include many endocytic receptors, many proteoglycans, and all known collectins and selectins.

12970.title: C1 inhibitor
12970.definition: Plasma glycoprotein secreted primarily by the liver and acting as a serine proteinase inhibitor (serpin), inhibiting C1 components of the complement system.

11656.title: CA1-pyramidal cell
11656.definition: Pyramidal neuron located in the cornu ammonis area 1, in the hippocampus.

11657.title: CA3-pyramidal cell
11657.definition: Pyramidal neuron located in the cornu ammonis area 3, in the hippocampus.

15531.title: cacosmia
15531.definition: Imagined perception of vile odors, including coprosmia (smelling feces) and necrosmia (the smell of death).

12984.title: cadherin
12984.definition: Calcium-dependent, transmembrane glycoprotein occurring in cell-cell contacts (desmosomes) and functioning as an adhesion molecule.

10483.title: Caesarian section
10483.definition: Surgical operation for delivering a child by opening the mother’s abdominal wall and uterus.

C00769.title: cage
C00769.definition: An aggregate of molecules, generally in the condensed phase, that surrounds the fragments formed, for example, by thermal or photochemical dissociation. Because the cage hinders the separation of the fragments by diffusion, they may preferentially react with one another ('cage effect') but not necessarily to reform the precursor species. For example:

C00770.title: cage compound
C00770.definition: A polycyclic compound having the shape of a cage. The term is also used for inclusion compounds.

C00771.title: cage effect
C00771.definition: When in a condensed phase, or in a dense gas, reactant molecules come together, or species are formed in proximity to one another, and are caged in by surrounding molecules, they may undergo a set of collisions known as an encounter; the term 'cage effect' is then applied.The cage effect is also known as the Franck–Rabinowitch effect.

16199.title: caged compound
16199.definition: Molecular species that can rapidly be converted from inactive into active form by light. Typically, photocaged compounds have a covalently attached group that can be photocleaved by electromagnetic radiation of a specific wavelength.

13798.title: calamitic
13798.definition: Having a rod- or lath-like shape.

15532.title: calcification
15532.definition: Form of mineralization in which organic tissue becomes hardened by deposition of calcium salts within its substance.

C00773.title: calcination
C00773.definition: Heating to high temperatures in air or oxygen.

C00774.title: calcined coke
C00774.definition: A petroleum coke or coal-derived pitch coke obtained by heat treatment of green coke to about \(1600\ \rm{K}\). It will normally have a hydrogen content of less than \(0.1\ \rm{wt.}\%\).

12985.title: calcineurin inhibitor
12985.definition: Any member of a group of immunomodulating drugs that bind to the cytosolic protein cyclophilin of T lymphocytes, thus inhibiting the phosphatase calcineurin, an inducer of interleukin-2 (IL-2) formation.

14512.title: calcinosis
14512.definition: Any pathological condition characterized by the deposition of calcium salts in tissues.

14513.title: calcium sink
14513.definition: Tissue such as arthropod cuticle, bivalve shell, or vertebrate bone that renders calcium or elements with similar biological behavior (such as lead or cadmium) less bioavailable during trophic interactions, thus providing a mechanism for trophic dilution.

11418.title: calculated molar refractivity
11418.definition: The calculated molar refractivity of a molecule or substituent used as a measure of size and polarizability in 2D-QSAR.

10167.title: calibrant in extraction phase
10167.definition: Internal standard that is incorporated in the extraction phase for calibration.

08011.title: calibration certificate
08011.definition: Document issued by a technically competent organization providing information about a calibration.

C00776.title: calibration component
C00776.definition: A component of a calibration mixture, present in the gaseous or vapour state, quantitatively and qualitatively defined, and used directly for testing and for calibration.

C00778.title: calibration function
C00778.definition: The functional (not statistical) relationship for the chemical measurement process, relating the expected value of the observed (gross) signal or response variable \(E(y)\) to the analyte amount \(x\). The corresponding graphical display for a single analyte is referred to as the calibration curve. When extended to additional variables or analytes which occur in multicomponent analysis, the 'curve' becomes a calibration surface or hypersurface.

C00779.title: calibration gas mixture
C00779.definition: A gas mixture of known composition, generally comprising one or more calibration components and a complementary gas.

C00775.title: calibration
C00775.definition: The set of operations which establish, under specified conditions, the relationship between values indicated by the analytical instrument and the corresponding known values of an analyte.

08012.title: calibration interval
08012.definition: Time period between calibrations over which the performance of the measuring system may be expected to meet specified requirements.

C00780.title: calibration material
C00780.definition: A material of known composition or properties which can be presented to the analytical instrument for calibration purposes.

C00781.title: calibration mixture
C00781.definition: A gaseous or liquid mixture of known composition, generally comprising one or more calibration components and an inert diluent, used directly for testing and calibration of analytical instruments.

C00782.title: calibration sample
C00782.definition: The test portion or test solution used for calibration of an analytical procedure. The calibration sample is normally of known weight or volume and is prepared according to specifications.

08716.title: calibration, k0 method
08716.definition: Calibration method of neutron activation analysis in which the \(k_{0}\) proportionality factors, together with a value of the neutron flux (as a function of the neutron energy) and with a value of the radiation detector's response for gamma radiation (as a function of the gamma-ray energy) are used for establishing a relationship between the number of counts measured and the corresponding amounts of elements in a material.

08717.title: calibrator
08717.definition: Measured amount of an element with stated measurement uncertainty that is simultaneously irradiated with the sample during activation analysis.

11659.title: california verbal learning test
11659.definition: Procedure in which some common words are read aloud and the test subject is asked to recall as many of these as possible.

C00783.title: calixarenes
C00783.definition: Originally macrocyclic compounds capable of assuming a basket (or 'calix') shaped conformation. They are formed from p-hydrocarbyl phenols and formaldehyde. The term now applies to a variety of derivatives by substitution of the hydrocarbon cyclo{oligo[(1,3-phenylene)methylene]}.

C00784.title: calorie
C00784.definition: Non-SI unit of energy. There are three differently defined calories: thermochemical calorie (\(\rm{cal}_{\rm{th}} = 4.184\ \rm{J}\)), international steam table calorie (\(\rm{cal}_{\rm{IT}} = 4.1868\ \rm{J}\)), \(15\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\) calorie (\(\rm{cal}_{15} = 4.1855\ \rm{J}\)), however only the symbol \(\rm{cal}\) is usually used.

C00785.title: calorimetric titration
C00785.definition: A titration performed in a calorimeter which produces a plot of heat change versus volume of titrant. This is the preferred term for experiments in which the main goal is the measurement of thermodynamic parameters. Because such experiments may be performed in any of a variety of types of calorimeters with varying degrees of calorimetric accuracy, it is important that the reporting of such results include an assessment of accuracy and precision. The term stands in contrast to the main emphasis in enthalpimetric analysis.

C00786.title: calorimetry
C00786.definition: A general term describing any experiment in which heat is measured as some chemical reaction or physical process occurs.

10484.title: canal
10484.definition: In biology and medicine, a relatively narrow tubular passage or channel.

10485.title: cancer
10485.definition: Disease resulting from the development of a malignant tumor.

C00787.title: candela
C00787.definition: The candela, symbol \(\pu{cd}\), is the SI unit of luminous intensity in a given direction. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the luminous efficacy of monochromatic radiation of frequency \(\pu{540E12 Hz}\), \(K_{\rm{cd}}\), to be \(683\) when expressed in the unit \(\pu{lm W^{-1}}\), which is equal to \(\pu{cd sr W^{-1}}\), or \(\pu{cd sr kg-1 m-2 s3}\), where the kilogram, metre and second are defined in terms of h, c and ΔνCs.

08059.title: candidate certified reference material
08059.definition: Reference material subjected to a process of reference material certification.

08060.title: candidate reference material
08060.definition: Material subjected to the procedures necessary to show its fitness for intended use (see fitness for purpose).

12986.title: candidiasis
12986.definition: Infection with a fungus of the genus Candida, especially C. albicans, that usually occurs in the skin and mucous membranes of the mouth, respiratory tract, or vagina but may invade the bloodstream, especially in immunocompromised individuals.

C00789.title: canonical rate constant
C00789.definition: The rate constant for a system in which the reactants are in thermal equilibrium at a given temperature. In statistical mechanics the expression 'canonical ensemble' is used to refer to a closed system in thermal equilibrium, the species being present in a statistical distribution. By contrast, a microcanonical ensemble is composed of systems all having the same energy: a canonical ensemble therefore consists of a statistical distribution of microcanonical ensembles. The canonical or thermal rate constant can be obtained from the microcanonical rate constant by summing over the energy, taking into account the statistical distribution.

11419.title: canonical structure representation
11419.definition:
A unique representation of the chemical structure of a molecule that is independent of the sequence in which the atoms were ordered in the original input file
 but is dependent on the algorithm used for the canonicalization.

10087.title: canonical variables
10087.definition: Linear combinations of data with the greatest correlation.

10088.title: canonical variate analysis
10088.definition: Multivariate technique which finds linear combinations of two sets of data that are most highly correlated.

C00790.title: canonical variational transition-state theory
C00790.definition: A development of transition-state theory in which the position of the dividing surface is varied so as to minimize the rate constant at a given temperature.

08061.title: capability
08061.definition: Ability of an object to realize an output that will fulfil the requirements for that output.

C00792.title: capacitance hygrometer
C00792.definition: Hygrometer using the capacitance variations of a capacitor whose dielectric medium consists of the gas or of a material in contact with this gas.

C00791.title: capacitance
C00791.definition: The charge on a plate divided by the potential difference between the plates.

10486.title: capacitation
10486.definition: Sum of biochemical changes undergone by mammalian spermatozoa in the female genital tract that enables them to penetrate and fertilize (see fertilization) an egg.

08461.title: capacitive microwave plasma
08461.definition: Plasma generated by a capacitor in presence of a microwave field.

09911.title: capillary affinity electrophoresis
09911.definition: Capillary electrophoresis in which the background electrolyte contains substances capable of specific, often biospecific, interactions with the analytes.

C00793.title: capillary column
C00793.definition: A general term for columns having a small diameter. A capillary column may contain a packing or have the stationary phase supported on its inside wall. The former case corresponds to packed capillary column while the latter case corresponds to an open-tabular column. Due to the ambiguity of this term its use without an adjective is discouraged.

C00794.title: capillary condensation
C00794.definition: Capillary condensation is said to occur when, in porous solids, multilayer adsorption from a vapour proceeds to the point at which pore spaces are filled with liquid separated from the gas phase by menisci. The concept loses its sense when the dimensions of the pores are so small that the term meniscus ceases to have a physical significance. Capillary condensation is often accompanied by hysteresis.

09912.title: capillary electrochromatography
09912.definition: Liquid chromatography, where the movement of the mobile phase through a capillary, filled, packed, or coated with a stationary phase, is achieved by electroosmotic flow (which may be assisted by pressure).

09913.title: capillary electrophoresis
09913.definition: Separation method based solely on the differences in the electrophoretic mobilities of charged species in capillaries.

09914.title: capillary gel electrophoresis
09914.definition: Capillary sieving electrophoresis in which the capillary is filled with a gel.

09915.title: capillary isoelectric focusing
09915.definition: Electrophoretic technique for the separation of analytes according to their isoelectric points by an electric field along a pH gradient formed in a capillary.

09916.title: capillary isotachophoresis
09916.definition: Electrophoretic separation technique in a discontinuous buffer system in which analytes migrate according to their electrophoretic mobilities, forming a chain of adjacent zones moving with equal speed (velocity) between two solutions, leading and terminating electrolytes, bracketing the mobility range of the analytes.

09917.title: capillary sieving electrophoresis
09917.definition: Electrophoretic separation technique, which takes place in a capillary containing a medium in the background electrolyte that retains molecules and particles based on their size and shape.

12987.title: capping
12987.definition: Active process whereby cross-linking of cell surface molecules (e.g., by antibody) leads to aggregation and subsequent migration of the molecules to one pole of the cell.

15159.title: capsule
15159.definition: Small edible package made usually from gelatin or other materials that can be filled with drugs (solids or liquids) to produce a unit dose, mainly for oral use. Hard capsules consist of two pieces that fit one inside the other which are produced empty and filled in a separate operation, and soft, liquid-filled capsules, which are manufactured and filled in one operation.

C00795.title: captodative effect
C00795.definition: Effect on the stability of a carbon-centred radical determined by the combined action of a captor (electron withdrawing) and a dative (electron releasing) substituent, both attached to the radical centre. The term is also used for certain unsaturated compounds.

C00796.title: capture
C00796.definition: A process in which an atomic or nuclear system acquires an additional particle. In general, a specification is added of the type of the captured particle or its energy.

09865.title: capture probe
09865.definition: Specifically-designed single-stranded nucleic acid with a defined (known) nucleotide sequence immobilised on a surface.

C00800.title: capture γ-radiation
C00800.definition: The γ-radiation emitted in radiative capture.

10487.title: caput epididymis
10487.definition: Upper and larger extremity of the epididymis.

C00802.title: carbaboranes
C00802.definition: A class of boron compound of general formula $\ce{[(CH)_{a}(BH)_{m}H_{b}]^{c}}$ where $c$ can be positive, negative or zero. The $\ce{CH}$ groups occupy polyhedron vertices, and other hydrogen atoms are either bridging or terminal.

C00803.title: carbamates
C00803.definition: Salts or esters of carbamic acid, $\ce{H2NC(=O)OH}$, or of $N$-substituted carbamic acids $\ce{R2NC(=O)OR'}$, ($\ce{R'}$ = hydrocarbyl or a cation). The esters are often called urethanes or urethans, a usage that is strictly correct only for the ethyl esters.

C00804.title: carbanion
C00804.definition: Generic name for anions containing an even number of electrons and having an unshared pair of electrons on a tervalent carbon atom (e.g. $\ce{Cl3C^{−}}$ or $\ce{HC#C^{−}}$) or — if the ion is mesomeric (see mesomerism) — having at least one significant contributing structure with an unshared pair of electrons on a tervalent carbon atom, for example:

C00807.title: carbene analogues
C00807.definition:
The electrically neutral mononuclear hydrides of group 14 having two non-bonding electrons, the electrically neutral mononuclear hydrides of group 15 having four non-bonding electrons, and also the compound $\ce{HB{:}}$ . The names of a number of these are shown below.

$\ce{RB{:}}$boranylidenes$\ce{RAs{:}}$arsanylidenes
$\ce{RN{:}}$nitrenes$\ce{R2Sn{:}}$stannylidenes
$\ce{R2Si{:}}$silylenes$\ce{RSb{:}}$stibanylidenes
$\ce{RP{:}}$phosphanylidenes$\ce{R2Pb{:}}$plumbylidenes
$\ce{R2Ge{:}}$germylidenes

Note that if $\ce{R} = \ce{H}$, these compounds are parent hydrides; derivatives formed by substitution are named accordingly. However, if the substituent's first atom, bearing the free valence, is of the same element as the atom of the carbene analogue, other parent compounds may be required (see carbenes), e.g. $\ce{HN{:}}$ nitrene; $\ce{CH3N{:}}$ methylnitrene; $\ce{H2NN{:}}$ diazanylidene (synonym isodiazene, not aminonitrene).

C00809.title: carbene radical anions
C00809.definition: Species $\ce{R2C^{_{\vdots}−}}$, having three non-bonding electrons, formally derived by addition of an electron to a carbene.

C00810.title: carbene radical cations
C00810.definition: Species $\ce{R2C^{.+}}$ having one non-bonding electron, formally derived by subtraction of an electron from a carbene, e.g. $\ce{H2C^{.+}}$ methyliumyl.

C00806.title: carbenes
C00806.definition: The electrically neutral species $\ce{H2C{:}}$ (methylene) and its derivatives, in which the carbon is covalently bonded to two univalent groups of any kind or a divalent group and bears two nonbonding electrons, which may be spin-paired (singlet state) or spin-non-paired (triplet state). In systematic name formation, carbene is the name of the parent hydride $\ce{C{:}H2}$ hence, the name dichlorocarbene for $\ce{C{:}Cl2}$. However, names for acyclic and cyclic hydrocarbons containing one or more divalent carbon atoms are derived from the name of the corresponding all-\(\lambda ^{4}\)-hydrocarbon using the suffix -ylidene. E.g. prop-2-en-1-ylidene, $\ce{H2C=CHCH{:}}$ ethenylidene, $\ce{H2C=C{:}}$; cyclohexylidene,Subclasses of carbenes include acyl carbenes , imidoyl carbenes,  and vinyl carbenes.

C00811.title: carbenium centre
C00811.definition: The three-coordinate carbon atom in a carbenium ion to which the excess positive charge of the ion (other than that located on heteroatoms) may be formally considered to be largely attributed, i.e. which has one vacant p-orbital. (N.B. It is not always possible to uniquely identify such an atom.) This formal attribution of charge often does not express the real charge distribution.

C00812.title: carbenium ion
C00812.definition: A generic name for carbocations, real or hypothetical, that have at least one important contributing structure containing a tervalent carbon atom with a vacant p-orbital. (The name implies a protonated carbene or a substitution derivative thereof.) The term was proposed (and rejected) as a replacement for the traditional usage of the name carbonium ion. To avoid ambiguity, the name should not be used as the root for the systematic nomenclature of carbocations. The corresponding difficulty confused carbonium ion nomenclature for many years. For example, the term 'ethylcarbonium ion' has at times been used to refer either to $\ce{CH3CH2^{+}}$ (ethyl cation) or (correctly) to $\ce{CH3CH2CH2^{+}}$ (propyl cation).

C00813.title: carbenoids
C00813.definition: Complexed carbene-like entities that display the reactivity characteristics of carbenes, either directly or by acting as sources of carbenes.

CT07609.title: carbo-reduction
CT07609.definition: Process in which a metal oxide is reduced in the presence of carbon or a carbon-containing compound.

C00817.title: carbocation
C00817.definition: A cation containing an even number of electrons with a significant portion of the excess positive charge located on one or more carbon atoms. This is a general term embracing carbenium ions, all types of carbonium ions vinyl cations, etc. Carbocations may be named by adding the word 'cation' to the name of the corresponding radical. Such names do not imply structure (e.g. whether three-coordinated or five-coordinated carbon atoms are present).

C00818.title: carbocyclic compounds
C00818.definition: Cyclic compounds in which all of the ring members are carbon atoms, e.g. 1,2-dihydronaphthalene.

09809.title: carbohydrate
09809.definition: Monosaccharide, oligosaccharide and polysaccharide substances, as well as substances derived from a monosaccharide by reduction of the carbonyl group (alditol), by oxidation, including the oxidation of one or more terminal groups of a carboxylic acid, or by replacement of one or more hydroxy groups by a hydrogen atom, an amino group, a thiol group, or by similar heteroatomic groups. This term also includes derivatives of these of these compounds.

C00820.title: carbohydrates
C00820.definition: Originally, compounds such as aldoses and ketoses having the stoichiometric formula $\ce{C_{n}(H2O)_{n}}$ hence 'hydrates of carbon'. The generic term carbohydrate includes monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides as well as substances derived from monosaccharides by reduction of the carbonyl group (alditols), by oxidation of one or more terminal groups to carboxylic acids, or by replacement of one or more hydroxy group(s) by a hydrogen atom, an amino group, thiol group or similar groups. It also includes derivatives of these compounds.

C00821.title: carbon
C00821.definition: Element number 6 of the periodic table of elements (electronic ground state \(1\rm{s}^{2}2\rm{s}^{2}2\rm{p}^{2}\)). For a description of the various types of carbon as a solid the term carbon should be used only in combination with an additional noun or a clarifying adjective.

C00823.title: carbon artifact
C00823.definition: An 'artificially produced' solid body which consists mainly of carbonaceous material in a distinct shape.

C00826.title: carbon cenospheres
C00826.definition: Porous or hollow carbonaceous sphere-like particles (frequently in the size range of a few to several hundreds of µm diameter) formed during pyrolysis, also in the course of combustion, of carbonaceous liquid droplets (e.g. heavy fuel) or solid particles (e.g. coal).

C00827.title: carbon cloth
C00827.definition: A textile material consisting of carbon fibres oriented at least in two directions. Carbon cloth is not necessarily woven.

C00828.title: carbon dioxide laser
C00828.definition: A continuous or pulsed source of coherent radiation normally tunable through the $\ce{CO2}$ vibration–rotation band centred near \(10.6\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\).

C00829.title: carbon electrode
C00829.definition: An electrode for an electrical application. In its green state it comprises granular carbon material bound with pitch. The granular carbon material may be either needle coke, fine-grained or isotropic coke or reclaimed graphite powder. Electrodes for use in steel production can only be manufactured from needle coke, and the green electrodes are fired at temperatures above around \(2800\ \rm{K}\) to produce highly graphite electrodes. The other granular carbon materials may be used for aluminium electrodes where the duty is not so severe, and the green electrodes are generally fired to lower temperatures.

C00830.title: carbon felt
C00830.definition: A textile material consisting of, in approximation, randomly oriented and intertwined carbon fibres.

C00831.title: carbon fibre
C00831.definition: Fibres (filaments, tows, yarns, rovings) consisting of at least $\pu{92\%}$ (mass fraction) carbon, usually in the non-graphitic state.

C00832.title: carbon fibre fabrics
C00832.definition: Woven textile materials made of carbon fibres.

C00833.title: carbon fibres type HM
C00833.definition: Carbon fibres type HM (high modulus) are carbon fibres with a value of Young's modulus (tensile modulus) larger than \(300\ \rm{GPa}\) (nearly $\pu{30\%}$ of the \(C_{11}\) elastic constant of a graphite single crystal).

C00834.title: carbon fibres type HT
C00834.definition: Carbon fibres type HT are carbon fibres with values of Young's modulus between \(150\) and \(275\) to \(300\ \rm{GPa}\). The term HT, referring to high tensile strength, was early applied because fibres of this type display the highest tensile strengths.

C00835.title: carbon fibres type IM
C00835.definition: Carbon fibres type IM (intermediate modulus) are related to carbon fibres type HT because of the comparable values of tensile strength, but are characterized by greater stiffness (Young's modulus up to approximately $\pu{35\%}$ of the theoretical \(C_{11}\) value).

C00836.title: carbon fibres type LM
C00836.definition: Carbon fibres type LM (low modulus) are carbon fibres with isotropic structure, tensile modulus values as low as $\pu{10\%}$ of the \(C_{11}\) values of the graphite single crystal, and low strength values.

C00837.title: carbon fibres type UHM
C00837.definition: Carbon fibres type UHM (ultra-high modulus) designates a class of carbon fibres having very high values of Young's modulus larger than \(600\ \rm{GPa}\) (i.e. greater than $\pu{55\%}$ of the theoretical \(C_{11}\) value of graphite).

09097.title: carbon ink electrode
09097.definition: Development of a carbon paste electrode that is screen printed using a carbon/polymer mixture of suitable composition.

CT06917.title: carbon loading
CT06917.definition: Mass fraction of the packing material which is carbon. Usually taken as a guide to the extent of alkyl substitution on the surface. Usually reported as percentage carbon determined using elemental analysis.

C00841.title: carbon material
C00841.definition: A solid high in content of the element carbon and structurally in a non-graphitic state.

C00842.title: carbon mix
C00842.definition: A mixture of filler coke, e.g. grains and/or powders of solid carbon materials and a carbonaceous binder and selected additives, prepared in heated mixers at temperatures in the range of \(410{-}445\ \rm{K}\) as a preliminary step for the formation of shaped green bodies.

09096.title: carbon paste electrode
09096.definition: Electrode of a composite of carbon powder and a pasting liquid (including mineral oil, Nujol, bromoform, bromonaphthalene).

C00825.title: carbon–carbon composite
C00825.definition: A carbon fibre-reinforced carbon matrix material. The carbon matrix phase is typically formed by solid, liquid or gaseous pyrolysis of an organic precursor material. The matrix is either a graphitizable carbon or non-graphitizable carbon, and the carbonaceous reinforcement is fibrous in form. The composite may also contain other components in particulate or fibrous forms.

C00822.title: carbonaceous mesophase
C00822.definition: A liquid-crystalline state of pitch which shows the optical birefringence of disc-like (discotic) nematic liquid crystals. It can be formed as an intermediate phase during thermolysis (pyrolysis) of an isotropic molten pitch or by precipitation from pitch fractions prepared by selective extraction. Generally, the spherical mesophase precipitated from a pyrolysing pitch has the Brooks and Taylor structure. With continuous heat treatment the carbonaceous mesophase coalesces to a state of bulk mesophase before solidification to green coke with further loss of hydrogen or low-molecular-weight compounds.

C00838.title: carbonitriles
C00838.definition: In systematic nomenclature, the suffix -carbonitrile is used to name compounds $\ce{RC#N}$ where the suffix includes the carbon atom of the $\ce{–CN}$. However, carbonitrile is not a class name for nitriles.

C00839.title: carbonium ion
C00839.definition: The term should be used with great care since several incompatible meanings are currently in use. It is not acceptable as the root for systematic nomenclature for carbocation.In most of the existing literature the term is used in its traditional sense for what is here defined as carbenium ion.A carbocation, real or hypothetical, that contains at least one five-coordinate carbon atom.A carbocation, real or hypothetical, whose structure cannot adequately be described by two-electron two-centre bonds only. (The structure may involve carbon atoms with a coordination number greater than five.)

C00840.title: carbonization
C00840.definition: A process by which solid residues with increasing content of the element carbon are formed from organic material usually by pyrolysis in an inert atmosphere.

08923.title: carbonothioyl-mediated radical polymerization
08923.definition: Reversible-addition-fragmentation radical polymerization mediated by a carbonothioyl compound.

C00844.title: carbonyl compounds
C00844.definition: Compounds containing the carbonyl group, $\ce{C=O}$. The term is commonly used in the restricted sense of aldehydes and ketones, although it actually includes carboxylic acids and derivatives.Metal carbonyls, in which carbon monoxide is a formal ligand.

C00847.title: carbonyl oxides
C00847.definition: 1,3 dipolar compounds having the structure  Also called peroxo compounds.

15533.title: carbonylhemoglobin
15533.definition: Compound that is formed between carbon monoxide and hemoglobin in the blood of animals and humans and is incapable of transporting oxygen.

C00850.title: carboxamides
C00850.definition: Amides of carboxylic acids, having the structure $\ce{RC(=O)NR2}$. The term is used as a suffix in systematic name formation to denote the $\ce{–C(=O)NH2}$ group including its carbon atom.

C00851.title: carboxamidines
C00851.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RC(=NR)NR2}$. The term is used as a suffix in systematic nomenclature to denote the $\ce{–C(=NH)NH2}$ group including its carbon atom, e.g. acetamidine, $\ce{CH3C(=NH)NH2}$; 2-butyl-4,5-dihydroimidazole:

C00852.title: carboxylic acids
C00852.definition: Oxoacids having the structure $\ce{RC(=O)OH}$. The term is used as a suffix in systematic name formation to denote the $\ce{–C(=O)OH}$ group including its carbon atom.

C00854.title: carbynes
C00854.definition: The neutral species $\ce{HC_{^\vdots}}$ (methylidyne) and its derivatives formed by substitution in which a univalent carbon atom is covalently bonded to one group and also bears three nonbonding electrons. (This term carries no implication about spin-pairing).

C00856.title: carbynium ions
C00856.definition: The cationic species $\ce{H2C^{.+}}$ or substitution derivatives thereof, formally derived by adding a hydron to a carbyne or subtracting an electron from a carbene.

13799.title: carceplex
13799.definition: Host-guest complex formed by a carcerand and a completely entrapped guest.

13800.title: carcerand
13800.definition: Host molecule that completely entraps a guest molecule.

12988.title: carcinoembryonic antigen
12988.definition: Membrane glycoprotein epitope normally present in the fetal gastrointestinal tract and elevated in many patients with various carcinomas.

12630.title: carcinogen
12630.definition: Agent (chemical, physical, or biological) that is capable of increasing the incidence of malignant neoplasms, thus causing cancer.

10488.title: carcinogenesis
10488.definition: Induction, by chemical, physical, or biological agents, of malignant neoplasms and thus of cancer.

15534.title: carcinogenicity test
15534.definition: Long-term (chronic) test designed to detect any possible carcinogenic effect of a test substance.

11660.title: carcinoma
11660.definition: Malignant tumor of an epithelial cell.

10490.title: cardiac jelly
10490.definition: Gelatinous substance, present between the endothelium and myocardium of the heart in early embryos, that develops into the connective tissue of the endocardium.

10491.title: cardiogenesis
10491.definition: Development of the heart in the embryo.

10492.title: cardiogenic
10492.definition:
Originating in the heart; describing anything caused by normal or abnormal function of the heart.
Pertaining to cardiogenesis.

12989.title: cardiolipin
12989.definition: 1,3-Bis(sn-3-phosphatidyl)-sn-glycerol, the main target of antiphospholipid antibodies.

15535.title: cardiotoxic
15535.definition: Chemically harmful to the cells of the heart.

10493.title: cardiovascular
10493.definition: Pertaining to the heart and blood vessels.

15309.title: cardo polymer
15309.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules consisting of a single-strand main chain and many ring units, each having one atom in common with the main chain.

C00858.title: carotenoids
C00858.definition: Tetraterpenoids ($\ce{C40}$), formally derived from the acyclic parent, $\ce{\uppsi\!,\!\uppsi\!-carotene}$ I by hydrogenation, dehydrogenation, cyclization, oxidation, or combination of these processes. This class includes carotenes, xanthophylls and certain compounds that arise from rearrangement of the skeleton of I or by loss of part of this structure. retinoids are excluded.

11661.title: carotid artery
11661.definition: One of two paired large arteries on either side of the neck that supplies most of the cerebralhemisphere.

11662.title: carpel tunnel syndrome
11662.definition: Median nerve entrapment neuropathy that causes paresthesia, pain, and numbness due to compression of the nerve at the wrist in the carpal tunnel.

C00859.title: carrier
C00859.definition: A substance in appreciable amount which, when associated with a trace of a specified substance, will carry the trace with it through a chemical or physical process.

C00861.title: carrier atom
C00861.definition: A participant atom which is neither core nor peripheral and which carries other groups to and from the molecule containing the core atom(s) but which does not itself become covalently attached to that molecule.

C00863.title: carrier gas
C00863.definition: A gas introduced in order to transport a sample for analytical purposes. In gas chromatography it is the gas which is passed continuously through the column and whose passage promotes the elution of the components of the sample. The carrier gas together with the portions of the sample present in this phase constitutes the mobile phase.

C00860.title: carrier
C00860.definition: A substance in appreciable amount which, when associated with a tracer of a specified substance, will carry the tracer with it through a chemical or physical process, or prevent the tracer from undergoing nonspecific processes due to its low concentration.

CT06814.title: carrier protein
CT06814.definition: Protein to which a specific ligand or hapten is conjugated.Unlabeled protein introduced into an assay at relatively high concentrations which distributes in a fractionation process in the same manner as labeled protein analyte, present in very low concentrations.Protein added to prevent non-specific interaction of reagents with surfaces, sample components, and each other.Protein found in cell membranes, which facilitates transport of a ligand across the membrane.

15537.title: carrier substance
15537.definition: Substance that binds to another substance and transfers it from one site to another.

15536.title: carrier-linked prodrug
15536.definition: Compound that contains a temporary linkage between a given active substance and a transient carrier group, the latter producing improved physicochemical or pharmacokinetic properties and easily removable in vivo.

15160.title: carrier-mediated drug transport
15160.definition: Transfer of a drug across a membrane by a transporter (often a protein) constituent of the cytosol membrane. Also known as active transport as opposed to passive diffusion/absorption.

C00866.title: carry-over
C00866.definition: A process by which materials are carried into a reaction mixture to which they do not belong. These materials can be either parts of a specimen, or reagents including the diluent or wash solution. In such cases, carry-over means the transfer of material (specimen or reagents) from one container, or from one reaction mixture, to another one. It can be either unidirectional or bidirectional in a series of specimens or assays. The term carry-over effect is used for carry-over from specimen to specimen.

14514.title: carrying capacity
14514.definition: Maximum population size expressed as total number of individuals, biomass, or population density that a given unit of habitat is capable of sustaining.

10494.title: cartilage
10494.definition: Specialized, fibrous connective tissue present in adults, forming the temporary skeleton in the embryo, providing a model in which the bones develop, and constituting a part of the organism’s growth mechanism.

10238.title: cartridge
10238.definition: Short disposable column containing a bed of porous particles immobilized between two porous frits.

C00869.title: cascade impactor
C00869.definition: An instrument used for the classification of aerosols according to size and for possible subsequent chemical analysis. Air is drawn through a series of orifices of decreasing size; the air flow is normal to collecting surfaces on which aerosols are collected by inertial impaction. The particles, separated stepwise by their momentum differences into a number of size ranges, are collected simultaneously.

09232.title: cascade mixing
09232.definition: Diffusion-like process in which atoms of material are moved randomly by energy deposited by incident particles slowing down in the sample surface region.

15538.title: case cohort study
15538.definition: Variant of the case control study in which the controls are drawn from the same cohort as the cases but are identified before the cases develop; some of the controls may later become cases.

15539.title: case control study
15539.definition: Study that starts with the identification of persons with the disease (or other outcome variable) of interest, and a suitable control (comparison, reference) group of persons without the disease. The relationship of an attribute to the disease is examined by comparing the diseased and non-diseased with regard to how frequently the attribute is present or, if quantitative, the levels of the attribute, in the two groups.

12990.title: caspase
12990.definition: Any member of a family of intracellular cysteine proteinases that cleave proteins at specific aspartic acid residues to initiate or promote apoptosis.

11663.title: cassavism
11663.definition: Epidemic paralytic disease, mainly affecting women and children, occurring in remote rural areas of African and Latin American countries, where cassava root is an important food.

10495.title: castration
10495.definition: Removal of the testicles or ovaries.

C00870.title: catabolism
C00870.definition: Reactions involving the oxidation of organic substrates to provide chemically available energy (e.g. ATP) and to generate metabolic intermediates.Generally, the process of breakdown of complex molecules into simpler ones, often providing biologically available energy.

C00871.title: catabolite repression
C00871.definition: A decrease in the activity of certain auxiliary catabolic enzymes when a surplus of an (easily metabolizable) substrate is available. Commonly this effect is caused by glucose (glucose repression) or by metabolites produced from glucose.

14516.title: catadromy
14516.definition: Life-history pattern that is characterized by egg incubation and early juvenile development in seawater, migration to freshwater for adult development, and return to seawater for spawning.

14517.title: catagenesis
14517.definition: Long-term geochemical alteration to organic matter, involving high temperatures and pressures deep below the surface of the Earth.

08151.title: Catalán solvent parameters
08151.definition: Quantitative measure of solvent polarity, based on the solvent’s hydrogen-bond-donor ability, hydrogen-bond-acceptor ability, polarizability, and dipolarity.

CT06762.title: catalase
CT06762.definition: A hemeprotein which catalyses the disproportionation of dihydrogen peroxide to $\ce{O2}$, and water; it also catalyses the oxidation of other compounds, such as ethanol, by dihydrogen peroxide.

C00872.title: catalymetric titration
C00872.definition: A titration process, which involves a catalyst, where the end-point is detected by the sudden increase or decrease of the rate of a reaction.

14000.title: catalysed photochemical reaction
14000.definition: Enhancement (alteration) of efficiency of photochemical reactions upon direct excitation of photoactive reactants via an intermediate interaction of these reactants with certain compounds that act as catalysts (promoters) of the appropriate chemical transformations of the reactants.

C00873.title: catalysed rate of reaction
C00873.definition: The observed rate of reaction, \(\xi \), minus the spontaneous rate of reaction, \(\xi _{0}\), observed under otherwise similar conditions in the absence of added catalytic material.

C00876.title: catalyst
C00876.definition: A substance that increases the rate of a reaction without modifying the overall standard Gibbs energy change in the reaction; the process is called catalysis. The catalyst is both a reactant and product of the reaction. The words catalyst and catalysis should not be used when the added substance reduces the rate of reaction (see inhibitor). Catalysis can be classified as 'homogeneous catalysis', in which only one phase is involved, and 'heterogeneous catalysis', in which the reaction occurs at or near an interface between phases. Catalysis brought about by one of the products of a reaction is called autocatalysis. Catalysis brought about by a group on a reactant molecule itself is called intramolecular catalysis. The term catalysis is also often used when the substance is consumed in the reaction (for example: base-catalysed hydrolysis of esters). Strictly, such a substance should be called an activator.

C00878.title: catalyst ageing
C00878.definition: Catalyst deactivation resulting from changes in the structure or in the texture of the catalyst. Changes of this kind are usually irreversible and the catalyst cannot be regenerated.

C00880.title: catalyst decay
C00880.definition: The conversion in a catalytic reaction performed under constant conditions of reaction often decreases with time of run or time on stream. This phenomenon is called catalyst deactivation or catalyst decay.

C00877.title: catalyst
C00877.definition: A substance included in the solvent to increase the rate of transfer without affecting the position of equilibrium. The term accelerator may also be used but kinetic synergist is not recommended.

13998.title: catalyst photoactivation
13998.definition: Generation or alteration of the catalytic activity (selectivity) of a substance after its interaction with light.

08938.title: catalyst precursor
08938.definition: Coordination compound that by reaction with an activator or cocatalyst provides an active catalyst during initialization of coordination polymerization.

09011.title: catalyst-transfer cross-coupling polymerization
09011.definition: Catalyst-transfer polymerization where the propagation steps comprise cross-coupling reactions.

09010.title: catalyst-transfer polymerization
09010.definition: Catalysed condensative chain polymerization where the catalyst is transferred from reactant polymer to product polymer with high efficiency.

C00882.title: catalytic activity concentration
C00882.definition: Catalytic activity of the component divided by the volume of the system.

C00883.title: catalytic activity content
C00883.definition: Catalytic activity of the component divided by the mass of the system.

C00884.title: catalytic activity fraction
C00884.definition: Quotient of the catalytic activity of the isozyme and the catalytic activity of all the isozymes of the same enzyme in the system.

C00881.title: catalytic activity
C00881.definition: Increase in the rate of reaction of a specified chemical reaction that an enzyme produces in a specific assay system.

08940.title: catalytic chain termination
08940.definition: Chain termination process involving transfer of a group to a reagent (the catalyst) that in turn transfers that group to a propagating species to terminate a chain and regenerate the original reagent.

08939.title: catalytic chain transfer
08939.definition: Chain-transfer process involving transfer of an atom or group to a reagent (the catalyst) that in turn transfers that group to a monomer to reinitiate polymerization and regenerate the original reagent.

C00885.title: catalytic coefficient

C00889.title: catalytic current
C00889.definition: The faradaic current that is obtained with a solution containing two substances B and A may exceed the sum of the faradaic currents that would be obtained with B and A separately, but at the same concentrations and under the same experimental conditions. In either of the two following situations the increase is termed a catalytic current. B is reduced or oxidized at the electrode-solution interface to give a product B' that then reduces or oxidizes A chemically. The reaction of B with A may yield either B or an intermediate in the overall half-reaction by which B' was obtained from B. In this situation the increase of current that results from the addition of A to a solution of B may be termed a regeneration current. The presence at the electrode-solution interface of one substance, which may be either A or the product A' of its reduction or oxidation, decreases the over-potential for the reduction or oxidation of B. In either case the magnitude of the catalytic current depends on the applied potential. If the current observed with a mixture of A and B is smaller than the sum of the separate currents, the term non-additive current should be used.

08153.title: catalytic cycle
08153.definition: Sequence of reaction steps in the form of a loop. One step is binding of a reactant to the active catalyst (sometimes formed from a precatalyst), and another step is the release of product and regeneration of the catalyst.

C00891.title: catalytic dehydrocyclization
C00891.definition: A reaction in which an alkane is converted into an aromatic hydrocarbon and hydrogen. For example,

C00892.title: catalytic domain of a polypeptide
C00892.definition: Any part of a polypeptide chain that possesses a catalytic function. It may contain more than one structural domain.

C00894.title: catalytic graphitization
C00894.definition: The transformation of non-graphitic carbon into graphite by heat treatment in the presence of certain metals or minerals.

C00895.title: catalytic hydrocracking
C00895.definition: A process similar to catalytic cracking in its industrial purpose but effected under hydrogen pressure and on a catalyst containing an ingredient with a hydrogenating function.

C00896.title: catalytic hydrodesulfurization
C00896.definition: A process in which, in the presence of hydrogen, sulfur is removed as hydrogen sulfide.

C00897.title: catalytic hydrogenolysis
C00897.definition: Ordinarily, a reaction in which $\ce{A + H2}$ gives $\ce{B}$.   For example,    The term may also be used for cleavage of bonds other than $\ce{A}$, e.g.

C00898.title: catalytic methanation
C00898.definition: A process for removing carbon monoxide from gas streams or for producing methane by the reaction

C00899.title: catalytic reforming
C00899.definition: A process for increasing the octane number of naphthas. It involves isomerization of alkanes, dehydrogenation of cyclohexanes to aromatic hydrocarbons, isomerization and dehydrogenation of alkylcyclopentanes, and dehydrocyclization of alkanes.

13999.title: catalytic site
13999.definition: Site at which catalysed chemical transformations take place.

10496.title: cataract
10496.definition: Partial or complete opacity (clouding) of the lens of the eye.

15540.title: catatonia
15540.definition: Behavior marked by excessive and sometimes violent motor activity and excitement, or by generalized inhibition or stupor, that may occur in schizophrenia, mood disorders, or organic brain syndromes.

10045.title: categorical data
10045.definition: Data, values of which are one of a fixed number of nominal categories.

09981.title: category
09981.definition: Kind-of-nominal-property indicating a class among nominal properties ordered according to nominal property values of a specified nominal property value set without relation to size.

C00903.title: catena-
C00903.definition: An affix used in inorganic nomenclature to denote a chain structure; often used to designate linear polymeric substances.

15310.title: catenane polymer
15310.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules consisting of physically catenated macrorings that have no atom in common and cannot be separated unless chemical bonds are broken.

C00904.title: catenanes
C00904.definition: Hydrocarbons having two or more rings connected in the manner of links of a chain, without a covalent bond. More generally, the class catena compounds embraces functional derivatives and hetero analogues, e.g:

C00905.title: cathode
C00905.definition: Electrode at which reduction takes place.

09153.title: cathodic stripping voltammetry
09153.definition: Stripping voltammetry in which material accumulated at the working electrode is electrochemically reduced in the stripping step. See figure.Applied potential against time during the accumulation and stripping steps in cathodic stripping voltammetry.

C00906.title: cathodic transfer coefficient
C00906.definition: For a reaction with a single rate-determining step \[\frac{\alpha _{\rm{c}}}{\nu } = -\frac{R\ T}{n\ F}\ (\frac{\partial (\ln (|I_{\rm{c}}|))}{\partial E})_{T,p,c_{i},...}\] where \(\alpha _{\rm{c}}\) is the cathodic transfer coefficient (number), \(R\) is the gas constant, \(T\) is the thermodynamic temperature, and \(\nu \) the stoichiometric number giving the number of identical activated complexes formed and destroyed in the completion of the overall reaction as formulated with the transfer of \(n\) electrons.

C00907.title: cation
C00907.definition: A monoatomic or polyatomic species having one or more elementary charges of the proton.

C00908.title: cation exchange
C00908.definition: The process of exchanging cations between a solution and a cation exchanger.

C00909.title: cation exchanger
C00909.definition: Ion exchanger with cations as counter-ions. The term cation-exchange resin may be used in the case of solid organic polymers. The acid form of a cation exchanger is the ionic form of a cation exchanger in which counter-ions are hydrogen ions (H-form) or the ionogenic groups have added a proton forming an undissociated acid.

08990.title: cation-activated-monomer polymerization
08990.definition: Activated-monomer polymerization where the propagating species is a nucleophile and the activating species is cationic.

08154.title: cation-π interaction
08154.definition: Noncovalent attractive force between a positive ion (metal cation, protonated Brønsted base, etc.) and a \(\ce{\uppi\ electron}\) system.

CT07200.title: cationic polymer
CT07200.definition: Polymer composed of positively charged macromolecules and an equivalent amount of counter-anions.

C00910.title: cationic polymerization
C00910.definition: An ionic polymerization in which the kinetic-chain carriers are cations.

08984.title: cationic ring-opening polymerization
08984.definition: Cationic polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

11542.title: cationized molecule
11542.definition: Ion formed by the association of a cation with a molecule \(\ce{M}\).

08229.title: Cauchy function
08229.definition: Function \(y = a/(b^{2} + x^{2})\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants.

10497.title: cauda epididymis
10497.definition: Tail of the epididymis that opens into the ductus deferens; part of the reservoir of spermatozoa.

11664.title: cauda equina
11664.definition: Bundle of long spinal nerve roots arising from the end of the spinal cord and filling the lower part of the spinal canal (from approximately the thoraco-lumbar junction downwards).

10498.title: caudal
10498.definition: Situated more toward the cauda, or tail, than some specified reference point; toward the inferior (in humans) or posterior (in animals) end of the body.

11665.title: caudate nucleus
11665.definition: Crescent-shaped mass of gray matter forming part of the corpus striatum and part of the basal ganglia.

08062.title: cause-and-effect diagram
08062.definition: Diagram indicating the causes of a specific event or condition.

12991.title: caveola
12991.definition: Invagination on the cell surface (plasma membrane), enriched in caveolin proteins, cholesterol, and glycosphingolipids, important in various processes including pinocytosis and signal transduction.

C00914.title: cavitands
C00914.definition: Compounds constrained by structure to having or accommodating a cavity large enough to host other molecules.

10499.title: cavitation
10499.definition: Formation of a cavity, as in formation of the amnion in mammalian development.

C00915.title: cavity dumping
C00915.definition: Periodic removal of coherent radiation from a laser cavity.

08317.title: CBCA(CO)NH/HN(CO)CACB
08317.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

08318.title: CBCANH/HNCACB
08318.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

08319.title: CC(CO)NH
08319.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

12971.title: CD1
12971.definition: Cell surface protein of antigen-presenting cells (APCs) involved in presentation of lipopeptide or glycolipid antigens.

12978.title: CD16
12978.definition: Low-affinity $\ce{Fc\mbox{-}\upgamma\! receptor}$ ($\ce{Fc\mbox{-}\upgamma\!\mbox{-}RIII}$) expressed mainly on natural killer (NK) cells, granulocytes, and macrophages, mediating antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC).

12979.title: CD23
12979.definition: Low-affinity ${\rm{Fc\mbox{-}}}\upvarepsilon\!$ receptor induced by interleukin-4 (IL-4) and expressed on see activated B cells and macrophages.

12972.title: CD3
12972.definition: Molecule composed of five polypeptide chains associated with the heterodimer T-cell receptor (TCR), forming the T-cell receptor complex (TCR/CD3); CD3 transduces the activating signals when antigen binds to the TCR.

12973.title: CD4
12973.definition: Cell surface antigen belonging to the immunoglobulin (Ig) superfamily of molecules and a marker of T helper cells.

12974.title: CD4+/CD25+ T cell
12974.definition: Subtype of CD4+ regulatory T cell (Treg) with potential role in the regulation of immune homeostasis.

12981.title: CD40 ligand
12981.definition: Essential molecule for normal switching signaling through binding to CD40 on B cells. The interaction of CD40L and CD40 is also critical for optimal T cell function.

12975.title: CD5+ B lymphocyte
12975.definition: Lymphocyte of type B-1a, which is predominant in fetal lymphoid organs and in neonatal cord blood.

12976.title: CD8
12976.definition: Cell surface molecule belonging to the immunoglobulin (Ig) superfamily of molecules found, among others, on cytotoxic T cells, which binds to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules.

12977.title: CD8+ T suppressor cell
12977.definition: Outdated term for CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL, Tc). The term 'suppressor T cell' is nowadays reserved for regulatory T cell (Treg).

10500.title: cecum
10500.definition: Pouch connected to the junction of the small and large intestines.

15385.title: ceiling temperature
15385.definition: Temperature above which, in a given chain polymerization, polymer of high molar mass is not formed.

CT06815.title: ceiling value
CT06815.definition: Airborne concentration of a potentially toxic substance which should never be exceeded in a worker’s breathing zone.

C00917.title: ceilometer
C00917.definition: An automatic, recording instrument for reading the height of the cloud-base.

12992.title: celiac disease
12992.definition: Autoimmune disorder occurring in genetically predisposed individuals, characterized by immune intolerance to the \(\ce{\upalpha\mbox{-}gliadin}\) component of gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye. Resultant inflammation of the mucosa of the upper small intestine is associated with malabsorption of nutrients and a wasting illness follows from this.

C00918.title: cell constant
C00918.definition: Defined as: \[\kappa _{\rm{cell}} = \kappa \ R\] where \(R\) is the measured resistance of the cell and \(\kappa \) is the conductivity (formerly called the specific conductance).

15541.title: cell cycle
15541.definition: Regulated biochemical steps that cells go through involving DNA replication and cell division, usually depicted as a sequential cyclical series of events.

C00922.title: cell error
C00922.definition: The error which results if the incident beam does not fall perpendicularly to the windows of the cell, or if the cell windows are contaminated or have some other imperfection.

CT06816.title: cell line
CT06816.definition: Defined unique population of cells obtained by culture from a primary source through numerous generations.

14114.title: cell membrane preparation
14114.definition: Preparation from tissue or cells, in which the membranous elements, generally the cell membrane, are enriched in relation to other cellular constituents.

14115.title: cell mortality
14115.definition: Ratio of counted dead cells to the total number of observed cells.

15544.title: cell strain
15544.definition: Cells having specific properties or markers derived from a primary culture or cell line.

14116.title: cell viability
14116.definition: Ratio of counted live cells to the total number of observed cells.

14113.title: cell-based assay
14113.definition: Assay in which the response of live cells to a test sample is measured.

12993.title: cell-mediated cytotoxicity
12993.definition: Lysis of a target cell initiated by a T lymphocyte binding to surface antibodies or antigen-bound major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules.

15542.title: cell-mediated hypersensitivity
15542.definition: State in which an individual reacts with allergic effects caused by the reaction of antigen-specific T-lymphocytes following exposure to a certain substance (allergen) after having been exposed previously to the same substance or chemical group.

12994.title: cell-mediated immune response
12994.definition: Specific immune response in which T lymphocytes mediate the effects, either through the release of cytokines or through cytotoxicity.

12995.title: cell-mediated immunity
12995.definition: Immune response mediated by antigen-specific T lymphocytes, either through the release of cytokines or through cytotoxicity, in contrast with humoral immunity, which is antibody-mediated.

C00928.title: Celsius temperature
C00928.definition: Thermodynamic temperature minus \(273.15\ \rm{K}\), invariably expressed in the SI unit degree Celsius (\(\pu{^{\circ}C}\)) which is equal to the kelvin. Sometimes the misnomer centigrade temperature is used for Celsius temperature.

15545.title: censored data
15545.definition: Sample observations for which the complete distribution is not known.

C00930.title: central atom
C00930.definition: The atom in a coordination entity which binds other atoms or groups of atoms (ligands) to itself, thereby occupying a central position in the coordination entity.

10501.title: central nervous system
10501.definition: Part of an animal’s nervous system that exerts control over the rest of the nervous system; in vertebrates, the brain and spinal cord protected within the dorsal body cavity (cranial and spinal cavities).

12996.title: central tolerance
12996.definition: Specific immunological tolerance due to the induction of lymphocyte apoptosis or anergy within the primary lymphoid organs (bone marrow in the case of B cell tolerance and the thymus for T cells).

08576.title: centre burst
08576.definition: Spectral region of an interferogram around zero-path-difference where intensity is greatest.

C00931.title: centre
C00931.definition: The centre of a Mössbauer spectrum is defined as the Doppler-velocity at which the resonance maximum is (or would be) observed when all magnetic dipole, electric quadrupole, etc. hyperfine interactions are (or would be) absent. The contribution of the second order Doppler shift (\(\delta _{\rm{T}}\)) should be indicated, if possible.

C00933.title: centrifugal acceleration
C00933.definition: The acceleration of a component as a result of a uniform rotational motion. Centrifugal acceleration is a vector quantity.

C00934.title: centrifugal barrier
C00934.definition: In a reaction without an electronic energy barrier, or its reverse, the rotational energy of the transition state gives rise to a reaction barrier, which is known as the centrifugal barrier.

C00936.title: centrifugal force
C00936.definition: Fictitious force acting on a body as a result of centripetal acceleration.

C00937.title: centrifugal radius
C00937.definition: The radius at which a component is spinning at the end of the period of centrifugation. For a component sedimented from a dilute suspension, it can be equated with radius of rotation at the bottom of the centrifuge tube.

10502.title: centromere
10502.definition: Constricted region of a chromosome that joins the two chromatids to each other and attaches to spindle fibers in mitosis and meiosis.

11666.title: cephalic
11666.definition: In or relating to the head.

C00938.title: cephalins
C00938.definition: Compounds derived from glycerol in which a primary and the secondary hydroxy groups are esterified with long-chain fatty acids, and the remaining primary one with the mono(2-aminoethyl) ester of phosphoric acid, or with the monoserine ester of phosphoric acid. The term is not recommended. These compounds are preferably designated as (3-phosphatidyl)ethanolamines and (3-phosphatidyl)serines respectively.

C00939.title: cephalosporins
C00939.definition: Cephems having the basic structure shown.

C00940.title: cephams
C00940.definition: Natural and synthetic antibiotics containing the 5-thia-1-azabicyclo[4.2.0]octan-8-one nucleus; generally assumed to have the 6R configuration, unless otherwise specified. The numbering used differs from that of the von Baeyer named bicyclic system. Where they differ, the von Baeyer numbering is shown in parentheses.

CT07539.title: ceramer
CT07539.definition: Chemically bonded hybrid material which is a crosslinked organic–inorganic polymer.

CT07540.title: ceramic
CT07540.definition: Rigid material that consists of an infinite three-dimensional network of sintered crystalline grains comprising metals bonded to carbon, nitrogen or oxygen.

C00942.title: ceramic filter
C00942.definition: A component of a stack sampling system which is suitable for high temperature use; also known as a ceramic thimble.

CT07541.title: ceramic precursor
CT07541.definition: Material that is converted to a ceramic through pyrolysis.

CT07543.title: ceramic yield
CT07543.definition: Mass of ceramic expressed as a percentage of the mass of the ceramic precursor used in the ceramization process.

CT07542.title: ceramic-reinforced polymer
CT07542.definition: Polymer composite consisting of a polymer continuous phase and disperse phase domains of microscopic ceramic particles.

11667.title: ceramide
11667.definition: Family of lipid molecules, each one composed of sphingosine and a fatty acid.

CT07610.title: ceramization
CT07610.definition: Process in which a ceramic precursor is converted into a ceramic.

11668.title: cerebellar tonsillar herniation
11668.definition: Abnormal protrusion of a portion of the cerebellum through the foramen magnum of the skull.

11669.title: cerebellum
11669.definition: Lower part of the brain that is beneath the posterior portion of the cerebrum, regulating the unconscious coordination of movement.

10562.title: cerebral cortex
10562.definition: Outer layer of the cerebrum, composed of folded grey matter, playing an important role in consciousness.

10504.title: cerebral hemisphere
10504.definition: Right or left half of the brain in sagittal section.

10505.title: cerebral palsy
10505.definition: Condition marked by lack of muscle control, resulting from brain damage before, at, or shortly after birth.

11670.title: cerebroside
11670.definition: Member of a group of glycosphingolipids called monoglycosylceramides which are important components in animal nerve and muscle cell membranes and the myelin sheath.

09641.title: cerebrospinal fluid
09641.definition: Clear, colourless fluid that fills spaces within and around the central nervous system.

11671.title: cerebrum
11671.definition: Principal part of the brain in vertebrates, located frontwards in the skull, consisting of the two hemispheres of the cerebral cortex separated by a fissure, and certain subcortical structures such as the hippocampus, basal ganglia, and the olfactory bulb.

C00943.title: Cerenkov detector
C00943.definition: A charged particle detector based on the Cerenkov effect.

C00944.title: Cerenkov effect
C00944.definition: Emission of radiation in the visible and ultraviolet spectrum arising when a charged particle crosses a medium with a velocity greater than that of light in the same medium.

C00945.title: Cerenkov radiation
C00945.definition: Radiation resulting from the Cerenkov effect.

09037.title: cerimetric titration
09037.definition: Redox titration using cerium(IV), in which an iron(II)-1,10-phenanthroline complex (ferroin) color change indicates the end-point.

08063.title: certification
08063.definition: Third-party attestation related to products, processes, systems, or persons.

10035.title: certified nominal reference material
10035.definition: Nominal reference material accompanied by documentation issued by an authoritative body and providing one or more specified nominal property values with examination uncertainty and examination traceability, using valid examination procedures.

08013.title: certified property value
08013.definition: Property value of a reference material, accompanied by statements of associated uncertainty and traceability and identified as a certified property value in the reference material certificate.

15546.title: certified reference material
15546.definition: Reference material, accompanied by documentation issued by an authoritative body and referring to valid procedures used to obtain a specified property value with uncertainty and traceability.

10506.title: cervical rib
10506.definition: Supernumerary rib arising from a cervical vertebra.

11672.title: cervical spine
11672.definition: Part of the spine immediately inferior to the skull and connecting to the thoracic spine, made up of seven vertebrae.

11673.title: cervical vertebra
11673.definition: Any of seven vertebrae that provide strength and structure to the cervical spine and support the head, allowing for its rotation and flexion.

10507.title: cervix
10507.definition: Narrow lower end of the uterus that opens into the vagina.

14518.title: cetaceans
14518.definition: Whales, dolphins, and porpoises, in the order Cetacea.

08941.title: chain activation
08941.definition: Unimolecular dissociation of a dormant species to form a mediating agent and a propagating species.

08942.title: chain activation
08942.definition: Reaction of an activator with a dormant species to form a deactivator and a propagating species.

C00947.title: chain axis
C00947.definition: The straight line parallel to the direction of chain extension, connecting the centres of mass of successive blocks of chain units, each of which is contained within an identity period.

C00948.title: chain branching
C00948.definition: When in a chain reaction there is a net increase in the number of chain carrier there is said to be chain branching. A simple example of a chain-propagating reaction leading to chain branching is:  in which there is one chain carrier (an oxygen atom) on the left and two chain carriers (a hydrogen atom and a hydroxyl radical) on the right.

C00949.title: chain carrier
C00949.definition: A species, such as an atom or free radical, which is involved in chain-propagating reactions is known as a chain carrier.

12188.title: chain conformation
12188.definition: Conformation of a chain as defined by its sequence of bond-conformational states.

15386.title: chain copolymerisation
15386.definition: Chain polymerization in which a copolymer is formed.

08943.title: chain deactivation
08943.definition: Conversion of a chain carrier into an inactive species.

15387.title: chain depropagation
15387.definition: Chemical reaction that results in the formation of a monomer molecule at an active center on the terminal unit of a chain carrier and decreases the degree of polymerization of the chain carrier by one.

CT07593.title: chain entanglement
CT07593.definition: Interlocking of polymer chains in a polymer material forming a transient or permanent network junction over the time-scale of the measurement.

C00952.title: chain fission yield
C00952.definition: The fraction of fissions giving rise to nuclei of a particular mass number.

C00953.title: chain folding
C00953.definition: The conformational feature in which a loop connects two parallel stems belonging to the same crystal.

C00946.title: chain
C00946.definition: The whole or part of a macromolecule, an oligomer molecule or a block, comprising a linear or branched sequence of constitutional units between two boundary constitutional units, each of which may be either an end-group, a branch point or an otherwise-designated characteristic feature of the macromolecule.

C00955.title: chain initiation
C00955.definition: The process in a chain reaction that is responsible for the formation of a chain carrier.

C00956.title: chain length
C00956.definition: In a chain reaction, the average number of times the closed cycle of reactions (involving the chain-propagating reactions) is repeated. It is equal to the rate of the overall reaction divided by the rate of the initiation reaction.

15547.title: chain of custody
15547.definition: Sequence of responsibility for a substance from the manufacturer to the distributor, to the user, or to the person(s) ultimately responsible for waste disposal. This term is also used in controlled transmission of samples from collection to analysis, especially of samples of materials used for medico-legal or forensic purposes.

C00958.title: chain polymerization
