C01097.title: clathrates
C01097.definition: Inclusion compounds in which the guest molecule is in a cage formed by the host molecule or by a lattice of host molecules.

CT07555.title: clay hybrid
CT07555.definition: Organic–inorganic composite material in which one of the components is a clay, the particles of which are dispersed in a polymer.

C01099.title: clean surface
C01099.definition: An experimental surface having no surface contamination observable by means of the used method.

C01100.title: clean up
C01100.definition: A process caused by sputtering, trapping (or adsorbing) metallic atoms, gas atoms or molecules on the walls of the vessel or anode. This has the effect of reducing the gas pressure in sealed lamps, and may be useful for cleaning up or gettering unwanted gases.

CT06860.title: clearance
CT06860.definition: Volume of blood or plasma or mass of an organ effectively cleared of a substance by elimination (metabolism and excretion) divided by time of elimination.Note:Total clearance is the sum of the clearances of each eliminating organ or tissue for a given substance.(in pulmonary toxicology) Volume or mass of lung cleared divided by time of elimination; used qualitatively to describe removal of any inhaled substance which deposits on the lining surface of the lung.(in renal toxicology) Quantification of the removal of a substance by the kidneys by the processes of filtration and secretion; clearance is calculated by relating the rate of renal excretion to the plasma concentration.

09458.title: clearance dose
09458.definition: Dose of radiation required to completely remove a positive-tone resist from a large area.

CT01101.title: clearance
CT01101.definition: Product of the concentration of a component in an output system and the volume flow rate of that output system divided by the concentration of this component in the input system.

CT06857.title: clearing point
CT06857.definition: The temperature at which the transition between the mesophase with the highest temperature range and the isotropic phase occurs.

10528.title: cleavage
10528.definition: First few divisions of a fertilized egg.

10531.title: cleft
10531.definition: Gap in soft tissue, bone, or both.

10532.title: cleft
10532.definition: Split, divided, or partly divided into two.

10533.title: cleft lip
10533.definition: Congenital malformation consisting of one or more clefts in the upper lip, the result of failed closure in the embryo of the maxillary and median nasal processes.

10534.title: cleft palate
10534.definition: Congenital fissure along the midline of the hard palate, that may extend into the soft palate.

10535.title: cleft sternum
10535.definition: Rare congenital malformation resulting from defective fusion in the embryo of paired mesodermal bands in the ventral midline.

14528.title: climax community
14528.definition: Community of plants and animals in a steady state due to ecological succession resulting in a composition of the community best adapted to average conditions in the area. The term is sometimes applied to soil development.

15567.title: clinical toxicology
15567.definition: Scientific study involving research, education, prevention, and treatment of diseases caused by substances such as drugs and toxins.

10536.title: clitoris
10536.definition: Erectile body in the female genitalia, homologous with the penis in the male.

10537.title: cloaca
10537.definition: Common cavity at the end of the digestive tract in vertebrates (apart from most mammals) into which are released both excretory and genital products.

10538.title: cloacal membrane
10538.definition: Membrane that covers the embryonic cloaca during the development of urinary and reproductive organs in those vertebrates where the cloaca occurs.

11423.title: clog P
11423.definition: Calculated log of the octan-1-ol/water partition coefficient.

CT06949.title: CLOGP values
CT06949.definition: CLOGP values are calculated 1-octanol/water partition coefficients, frequently used in structure-property correlation or quantitative structure-activity relationship (SPC/QSAR) studies.

13012.title: clonal anergy
13012.definition: Form of self-tolerance developing as a consequence of negative selection during thymic selection processes. Clones of thymocytes whose antigen receptors [T-cell receptors (TCRs)] bind with high affinity to self-antigens in association with major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules are inactivated.

13013.title: clonal deletion
13013.definition: Process by which contact with antigen (e.g., self-antigen) at an early stage of lymphocyte differentiation leads to cell death by apoptosis.

13014.title: clonal expansion
13014.definition: Proliferation of B lymphocytes and T lymphocytes activated by clonal selection in order to produce a clone of identical cells.

13015.title: clonal indifference
13015.definition: Failure of B or T cells expressing anti-self-receptors to interact with antigen (e.g., by low valency, low concentration, or sequestration of antigens; low receptor avidity; or lack of co-stimulatory molecules).

13016.title: clonal selection
13016.definition: Selection and activation by antigen of a lymphocyte, bearing a complementary receptor, which then proliferates to form an expanded clone.

C01103.title: clone
C01103.definition: A population of genetically identical cells produced from a common ancestor. Sometimes, 'clone' is also used for a number of recombinant DNA molecules all carrying the same inserted sequence.

15568.title: clonic
15568.definition: Pertaining to alternate muscular contraction and relaxation in rapid succession.

09689.title: cloning
09689.definition: Specialised deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) technology for the production of multiple exact copies of a single gene or another segment of DNA.

09690.title: cloning vector
09690.definition: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) molecule into which another DNA fragment of appropriate size can be integrated without the loss of its capacity for self-replication.

11683.title: clonus
11683.definition:
Alternate involuntary muscular contraction and relaxation in rapid succession.
Continuous rhythmic reflex tremor initiated by the spinal cord below an area of spinal cord injury, set in
motion by reflex testing.

CT07010.title: closed shell molecular systems
CT07010.definition: Even-electron atomic or molecular systems whose electron configurations consist of doubly occupied orbitals.

10191.title: closed-loop extraction
10191.definition: Extraction by a fixed volume of gas continuously recycled through the sample and a sorbent trap by a pump in a closed-circuit arrangement.Typical apparatus for closed-loop stripping analysis.

10233.title: closed-vessel acid digestion
10233.definition: Type of acid digestion performed in a closed vessel at elevated pressure.

C01106.title: closo-
C01106.definition: An affix used in names to denote a cage or closed structure, especially a boron skeleton that is a polyhedron having all triangular faces.

C01107.title: cloud
C01107.definition: An aerosol of the atmosphere which is dense enough to be perceptible to the eye. Usually refers to an assembly of water droplet aerosols suspended in the atmosphere, although dust clouds are also recognized.

12241.title: cloud point
12241.definition: Point in the isobaric temperature-composition plane of a binary or multicomponent mixture at which a decrease in transparency is observed due to the turbidity caused by phase separation.

10207.title: cloud point extraction
10207.definition: Coacervative extraction at a temperature above the cloud point temperature.

12242.title: cloud-point curve
12242.definition: Curve of temperature vs. composition defined by the cloud points over range of compositions of two substances.

10539.title: clover disease
10539.definition: Condition caused by the continued ingestion of low but toxic levels of estrogens.

10540.title: clubfoot
10540.definition: Deformed foot that is twisted out of shape or position, usually congenital (congenital talipes equinovarus (CTEV)).

CT06769.title: cluster
CT06769.definition: A number of metal centres grouped close together which can have direct metal bonding interactions or interactions through a bridging ligand, but are not necessarily held together by these interactions.

CT06950.title: cluster analysis
CT06950.definition: Cluster analysis is the clustering, or grouping, of large data sets (e.g., chemical and/or pharmacological data sets) on the basis of similarity criteria for appropriately scaled variables that represent the data of interest. Similarity criteria (distance based, associative, correlative, probabilistic) among the several clusters facilitate the recognition of patterns and reveal otherwise hidden structures.

11424.title: cluster centroid
11424.definition: The geometric center of a cluster, often exemplified as the object that is closest to the center.

13017.title: cluster determinant
13017.definition: Cluster of antigens representing a cell surface marker with which antibodies react. Not to be confused with cluster of differentiation (CD) antigen.

C01115.title: cluster ion
C01115.definition: An ion formed by the combination of more ions or atoms or molecules of a chemical species often in association with a second species. For example, $\ce{[(H2O)_{n}H]^{+}}$ is a cluster ion.

13018.title: cluster of differentiation antigen
13018.definition: Any of a family of molecular markers on cell surfaces that may be used operationally to define phenotype, origin, and activation state of the cell.

15569.title: cluster sampling
15569.definition:
A method of sampling in which the population is divided into aggregates (or clusters) of items bound together in a certain manner. A sample of these clusters is taken at random, and all the items which constitute them are included in the sample.
A sampling method in which each unit selected is a group of persons (all persons in a city block, a family, etc.) rather than an individual.

13801.title: co-assembly
13801.definition: Self-assembly of two or more self-assembling species that might or might not incorporate a non-assembling component into an ordered structure.

12637.title: co-drug
12637.definition: Two chemically linked synergistic drugs designed to improve the drug delivery properties of one or both drugs.

C01141.title: co-ions
C01141.definition: Ions of low relative molecular mass with a charge of the same sign as that of a given colloidal ion.

12236.title: co-nonsolvency
12236.definition: Decrease in solubility of a polymer in a solvent comprising more than one component, each component of which by itself is a solvent for the polymer.

C01321.title: co-oligomer
C01321.definition: An oligomer derived from more than one species of monomer.

C01322.title: co-oligomerization
C01322.definition: Oligomerization in which a co-oligomer is formed.

C01361.title: co-solvency
C01361.definition: The dissolution of a polymer in a solvent comprising more than one component, each component of which by itself is a non-solvent for the polymer.

13051.title: co-stimulation
13051.definition: Delivery of a second signal, in addition to that of antigen binding or antigen presentation, that is required for lymphocyte proliferation.

C01116.title: coacervation
C01116.definition: The separation into two liquid phases in colloidal systems. The phase more concentrated in colloid component is the coacervate, and the other phase is the equilibrium solution.

10208.title: coacervative extraction
10208.definition: Extraction by a surfactant-rich, water-immiscible phase formed by adding a dehydrating agent to a colloidal solution of the sample and a surfactant above its critical micelle concentration.

C01117.title: coagulation
C01117.definition: When a sol is colloidally unstable (i.e. the rate of aggregation is not negligible) the formation of aggregates is called coagulation or flocculation.

13019.title: coagulation system
13019.definition: Proteolytic cascade of plasma enzymes that triggers blood clotting when blood vessels are damaged.

14368.title: coagulative nucleation
14368.definition: A process combining nucleation by any mechanism with subsequent coagulation being a significant event in formation of colloidally stable particles.

C01121.title: coal tar pitch
C01121.definition: A residue produced by distillation or heat treatment of coal tar. It is a solid at room temperature, consists of a complex mixture of numerous predominantly aromatic hydrocarbons and heterocyclics, and exhibits a broad softening range instead of a defined melting temperature.

C01118.title: coal-derived pitch coke
C01118.definition: The primary industrial solid carbonization product obtained from coal tar pitch mainly produced in chamber or delayed coking processes.

C01119.title: coalescence
C01119.definition: The disappearance of the boundary between two particles (usually droplets or bubbles) in contact, or between one of these and a bulk phase followed by changes of shape leading to a reduction of the total surface area. The flocculation of an emulsion, viz. the formation of aggregates, may be followed by coalescence.

C01120.title: coalification
C01120.definition: A geological process of formation of materials with increasing content of the element carbon from organic materials that occurs in a first, biological stage into peats, followed by a gradual transformation into coal by action of moderate temperature (about \(500\ \rm{K}\)) and high pressure in a geochemical stage.

08157.title: coarctate
08157.definition: Feature of a concerted transformation in which the primary changes in bonding occur within a cyclic array of atoms but in which two nonbonding atomic orbitals on an atom interchange roles with two bonding orbitals.

10541.title: coarctation
10541.definition: Narrowing or constriction of a short section of a blood vessel, commonly of the aorta.

15161.title: coating
15161.definition: Technological process consisting of the application of a substance, which forms a layer (e.g., to protect the drug and/or the tablet, to mask taste, to control the rate of drug release (e.g., film coating, sugar coating).

08918.title: cobalt-mediated radical polymerization
08918.definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization mediated by a cobalt complex.

15570.title: cocarcinogen
15570.definition: Chemical, physical, or biological factor that intensifies the effect of a carcinogen.

10542.title: cochlea
10542.definition: Spiral cavity of the inner ear containing the organ of Corti that transduces sound into nerve impulses.

10067.title: coded experimental design
10067.definition: Matrix of runs by factor levels in which each level is denoted by a code that represents the relative magnitude of the level.

15571.title: Codex Alimentarius
15571.definition: Collection of internationally adopted food standards drawn up by the Codex Alimentarius Commission, the principal body implementing the joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Program.

C01123.title: codon
C01123.definition: The sequence of three consecutive nucleotides that occurs in mRNA which directs the incorporation of a specific amino acid into a protein and includes also the starting or termination signals of protein synthesis.

C01124.title: coefficient
C01124.definition: Proportionality constant between two quantities of different dimension.

C01125.title: coefficient of haze
C01125.definition: One technique of measurement of the amount of filterable particulate matter suspended in air which has been used in the past depends upon drawing a measured sample of air (usually 1 000 linear feet) through a paper or membrane filter. A measurement is made of the intensity of light transmitted through the dust spot formed relative to that transmitted through an identical clean filter. The dirtiness of the air is reported in terms of the \(\rm{COH}\) unit. This relates to the quantity of particulate material which produces an optical density, \[\log_{10}(\frac{I_{0}}{I})\] of 0.01 when measured by light transmission at \(\pu{400 nm}\) and relative to the transmission of an identical dust-free filter taken as 100%. Thus a filter which transmitted 50% relative to the clean filter has an absorbance of 0.301 or 30.1 \(\rm{COH}\) units. This is not a recommended measure of filterable particulate matter since the size, colour and other properties of the aerosol and the air in which it is suspended affect the results.

14001.title: Coekelbergs effect
14001.definition: Adsorption at the surface of a pre-irradiated adsorbent (the photocatalyst) occurring in the dark, after the irradiation in the presence of the photoadsorbate entities is terminated, i.e., after preliminary photoadsorption.

10543.title: coelom
10543.definition: Body cavity, found in many animals, lined with mesodermal epithelium and containing the digestive tract and other visceral organs

C01126.title: coenzyme
C01126.definition: The dissociable, low-relative-molecular-mass active group of an enzyme which transfers chemical groups, hydrogen or electrons. A coenzyme binds with its associated protein (apoenzyme) to form the active enzyme (holoenzyme).

15320.title: coexistence curve
15320.definition: Boundary of stable phase separation (limits of solubility) in a liquid or solid system of two or more components.

C01127.title: coextraction
C01127.definition: Formation of mixed-species aggregates in a low-polarity organic phase.

C01128.title: cofactors
C01128.definition: Organic molecules (cf. coenzymes) or ions (usually metal ions) that are required by an enzyme of its activity. They may be attached either loosely or tightly prosthetic group) to the enzyme. A cofactor binds with its associated protein (apoenzymes), which is functionally inactive, to form the active enzyme (holoenzyme).

13020.title: cognate T cell
13020.definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) primed by the same antigen as the B cell to which it gives help.

11684.title: cognition
11684.definition: Sum of the mental processes by which sensory input is stored, recovered, and used by the consciousbrain, including attention, memory, language usage, learning, reasoning, problem solving, and decision making.

C01129.title: coherence length
C01129.definition: The distance over which order is maintained. As an example, there can be long-range atomic or molecular order, i.e. coherence. Coherence lengths are significantly larger than molecular size. Normally, coherence length is estimated from electron, neutron or X-ray scattering and scales the size of ordered domains in material where long range ordering occurs (as in liquid crystals, for example). The term coherence length is also used for the scale characterizing the profile of molecular axis orientation in the distorted, so-called, transition layers formed at a solid/liquid-crystal boundary when an appropriate external field is applied (e.g. when the orientation of anchored surface molecules of a nematic liquid crystal is unaffected by an external field -- magnetic or electric -- whereas the bulk molecules reorient freely). This scale is referred to as electric coherence length, \(\zeta _{\rm{E}}\) or magnetic coherence length, \(\zeta _{\rm{M}}\), depending on the nature of the applied field.

C01135.title: coherent unit
C01135.definition: Derived unit of measurement that may be expressed as a product of powers of base units with the proportionality factor one.

08579.title: coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy

C01130.title: coherent radiation
C01130.definition: Radiation emitted by a source when all the elementary waves emitted have a phase difference constant in space and time.

C01131.title: coherent scattering
C01131.definition: Scattering is coherent whenever the phases of the signals arising from different scattering centres are correlated and incoherent whenever these phases are uncorrelated.

C01132.title: coherent source
C01132.definition: Those sources where the radiation has a constant phase relationship between waves spatially as well as temporally, e.g. lasers. Non-coherent optical sources emit radiation which is randomly distributed in phase, spatially as well as temporally. Most sources which are used in spectroscopy and for spectrochemical analysis conform to this latter group.

C01133.title: coherent structure
C01133.definition: If the net of an ordered adsorbed phase is in registry with the lattice of the adsorbent the structure is called coherent, if not it is called incoherent.

C01134.title: coherent system of units of measurement
C01134.definition: System of units of measurement in which all of the derived units are coherent.

15572.title: cohort
15572.definition: Component of the population born during a particular period and identified by period of birth so that its characteristics (such as causes of death and numbers still living) can be ascertained as it enters successive time and age periods. The term 'cohort' has broadened to describe any designated group of persons followed or traced over a period of time, as in the term cohort study (prospective study).

15573.title: cohort analysis
15573.definition: Tabulation and analysis of morbidity or mortality rates in relationship to the ages of a specific group of people (cohort), identified by their birth period, and followed as they pass through different ages during part or all of their life span. In certain circumstances such as studies of migrant populations, cohort analysis may be performed according to duration of residence in a country rather than year of birth, in order to relate health or mortality experience to duration of exposure.

15574.title: cohort study
15574.definition: Analytic study in epidemiology in which subsets of a defined population can be identified who are, have been, or in the future may be exposed or not exposed, or exposed in different degrees, to a factor or factors hypothesized to influence the probability of occurrence of a given disease or other outcome. The main feature of the method is observation of a large population for a prolonged period (years), with comparison of incidence rates of the given disease in groups that differ in exposure levels.

13802.title: coil-to-globule transition
13802.definition: Change in conformation of a macromolecular chain in solution from that of a coil to a relatively compact structure in which the chain has collapsed upon itself in response to an external stimulus.

09933.title: coiled-tube field-flow fractionation
09933.definition: Field-flow fractionation in a long (usually \(\pu{10 m}\) or more) rotating coiled column under the action of asymmetrical centrifugal field.

C01136.title: coincidence circuit
C01136.definition: An electronic circuit which produces a usable output pulse only when each of its inputs receives a pulse within a specified time interval.

C01139.title: coincidence resolving time
C01139.definition: The greatest time interval that can elapse between the occurrence of two or more consecutive signal pulses, in order that the measuring device processes them as a coincidence.

C01142.title: coke
C01142.definition: A solid high in content of the element carbon and structurally in the non-graphitic state. It is produced by pyrolysis of organic material which has passed, at least in part, through a liquid or liquid-crystalline state during the carbonization process. Coke can contain mineral matter.

C01143.title: coke breeze
C01143.definition: A by-product of coke manufacture; it is the residue from the screening of heat-treated coke. The particle size is less than \(10\ \rm{mm}\). Generally, coke breeze has a volatile matter content of \(

C01144.title: coking
C01144.definition: Many reactions involving hydrocarbons and particularly those run at higher temperatures lead to the deposition on the catalyst of high molecular weight compounds of carbon and hydrogen which deactivate the catalyst. This phenomenon is called coking or fouling. Catalysts so deactivated can often be regenerated.

C01145.title: col
C01145.definition: A mountain-pass in a potential-energy surface is known as a col or saddle point. It is a point at which the gradient is zero along all coordinates, and the curvature is positive along all but one coordinate, which is the reaction coordinate, along which the curvature is negative.

13021.title: cold autoantibody type
13021.definition: Autoantibody that reacts optimally at low temperatures (\(\pu{{0}{-}{5} ^{\circ}C}\)) with surface antigens of erythrocytes.

14529.title: cold condensation theory
14529.definition: Theory that pollutants with high vapor pressure, e.g., mercury or persistent organic pollutants (POPs), in the air will condense onto soil, water, and biota at cool temperatures. Consequently, the ratios for POP concentrations in the air and on condensed phases decrease as one moves from warmer to cooler climates.

12748.title: cold crystallisation
12748.definition: Polymer crystallisation brought about from a glass, from a liquid-crystalline state, or a state displaying a low degree of crystallinity at temperatures a little above the glass-transition temperature.

10265.title: cold fibre solid-phase microextraction
10265.definition: Solid-phase microextraction in the fibre format with a sorbent temperature maintained below that of the sample matrix during extraction.

C01147.title: cold neutrons
C01147.definition: Neutrons with a neutron temperature considerably lower than normal room temperature.

13022.title: collagen arthritis
13022.definition: Autoimmune model of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), arising from combined cellular immunity and humoral immunity against collagen type II, and characterized by rapid and severe erosions of cartilage and bone.

10544.title: collagenous
10544.definition: Rich in the fibrous connective tissue protein, collagen.

13023.title: collectin
13023.definition: Any member of a structurally related family of calcium-dependent carbohydrate-binding proteins or lectins containing collagen-like sequences, e.g., mannose-binding lectin (MBL).

C01148.title: collection
C01148.definition: The planned removal from solution of a micro- or macro-component by the intentional formation of a contaminated host precipitate, or by the adsorption or entrapment of the component by an added solid.

C01149.title: collection efficiency
C01149.definition: A term which characterizes an entire sampling and sample pretreatment procedure, usually represented as a percentage of the original amount of the analyte which is left for measurement (signal formation) after having passed through this procedure. This term also applies to the efficiency of collection of an air pollutant by an arrestment plant. For particulates, the collection efficiency is size related.

C01150.title: collection gas flow system
C01150.definition: A system in which the analyte is carried to a collecting device called the collector which may be an amalgamator for mercury, a cold trap for some of the more stable hydrides, an absorbing solution in which the analyte is absorbed by some chemical reaction, an electrothermal atomizer or a reservoir.

C01152.title: collector
C01152.definition: A solid substance added to or formed within a solution to collect a micro- or macro-component.

C01151.title: collector
C01151.definition: A device for removing and retaining contaminants from air or other gases; a term which is often applied to cleaning devices in exhaust systems. Also used to designate a device for removing and retaining samples from media in different environmental compartments to be investigated. A collector is sometimes used to describe a scavenger.

10545.title: collembolan reproduction test
10545.definition: Procedure in which collembolans (small soil-inhabiting insects) are exposed to soil that has been treated with a test substance, and adult mortality and reproductive output are studied.

C01153.title: colligation
C01153.definition: The formation of a covalent bond by the combination or recombination of two radicals (the reverse of unimolecular homolysis).

C01154.title: collimation
C01154.definition: The limiting of a beam of radiation to the required dimensions and angular spread.

C01155.title: collimator
C01155.definition: An arrangement of absorbers used for collimation.

C01156.title: collinear reaction
C01156.definition: This is a reaction assumed to occur via an activated complex in which all of the atoms directly involved in the process lie along a straight line.

11425.title: collinearity
11425.definition:
A linear relationship between two or more of the descriptors in a model, which can lead to difficulties in interpreting the relative importance of these
 descriptors.

09238.title: collision cascade
09238.definition: Sequential energy transfer between atoms in a solid as a result of bombardment by an energetic species.

C01160.title: collision complex
C01160.definition: An ensemble formed by two reaction partners for which the distance is the sum of their van der Waals radii. As such it constitutes a subclass of the species indicated as encounter complex.

C01161.title: collision cross-section
C01161.definition: In simple hard sphere collision theory the area of the circle with radius equal to the collision diameter.

C01162.title: collision density
C01162.definition: Total collision frequency for all molecules within a volume divided by that volume.

C01163.title: collision diameter
C01163.definition: In simple hard sphere collision theory the sum of radii of two colliding spherical particles.

C01164.title: collision efficiency
C01164.definition: The collision efficiency, or de-energization efficiency, is defined by: \[k_{\rm{-1}} = B_{\rm{c}}\ k_{\rm{-1}}^{\rm{sc}}\] where \(k_{-1}\) is the rate constant for a particular substance \(\rm{M}\) when it brings about the de-energization process  and \(k_{-1}^{\rm{sc}}\) is the corresponding rate constant for a reference molecule \(\rm{M}_{\rm{r}}\) that de-energizes \(\rm{A}^{*}\) on every collision; that is, the reference molecule \(\rm{M}_{\rm{r}}\) undergoes strong collisions, and by definition has a collision efficiency \(B_{\rm{c}}\) of unity. The species \(\rm{A}^{*}\) is usually in a vibrationally-excited state, and \(\rm{A}\) has energy less than that required for reaction to occur.

C01166.title: collision frequency
C01166.definition: Average number of collisions experienced by a molecule A with other molecules A (or B) in a time interval divided by that time interval.

C01170.title: collision theory
C01170.definition: Various collision theories, dealing with the frequency of collision between reactant molecules, have been put forward. In the earliest theories reactant molecules were regarded as hard spheres, and a collision was considered to occur when the distance \(d\) between the centres of two molecules was equal to the sum of their radii. For a gas containing only one type of molecule, A, the collision density is given by simple collision theory as: \[Z_{\mathrm{AA}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}\ \pi \ \sigma ^{2}\ u\ N_{\rm{A}}^{2}}{2}\] Here \(N_{\rm{A}}\) is the number density of molecules and \(u\) is the mean molecular speed, given by kinetic theory to be \(\sqrt{\frac{8\ k_{\rm{B}}\ T}{\pi \ m}}\), where \(m\) is the molecular mass, and \(\sigma =\pi \ d_{\mathrm{AA}}^{2}\). Thus: \[Z_{\mathrm{AA}}=2\ N_{\rm{A}}^{2}\ \sigma ^{2}\ \sqrt{\frac{\pi \ k_{\rm{B}}\ T}{m}}\] The corresponding expression for the collision density \(Z_{\mathrm{AB}}\) for two unlike molecules A and B, of masses \(m_{\rm{A}}\) and \(m_{\rm{B}}\) is: \[Z_{\mathrm{AB}}=N_{\rm{A}}\ N_{\rm{B}}\ \sigma ^{2}\ \sqrt{\frac{\pi \ k_{\rm{B}}\ T}{\mu }}\] where \(\mu \) is the reduced mass \(\frac{m_{\rm{A}}\ m_{\rm{B}}}{m_{\rm{A}}+m_{\rm{B}}}\), and \(\sigma =\pi \ d_{\mathrm{AB}}^{2}\). For the collision frequency factor these formulations lead to the following expression: \[z_{\mathrm{AA}}\quad \rm{or}\quad z_{\mathrm{AB}}=L\ \sigma ^{2}\ \sqrt{\frac{8\ \pi \ k_{\rm{B}}\ T}{\mu }}\] where \(L\) is the Avogadro constant. More advanced collision theories, not involving the assumption that molecules behave as hard spheres, are known as generalized kinetic theories.

C01167.title: collision-induced dissociation
C01167.definition: An ion/neutral species process wherein the projectile ion is dissociated as a result of interaction with a target neutral species. This is brought about by conversion of part of the translational energy of the ion to internal energy in the ion during the collision.

C01157.title: collisional activation
C01157.definition: An ion/neutral species process wherein excitation of a projectile ion of high translational energy is brought about by the same mechanism as in collision-induced dissociation. (The ion may decompose subsequently.)

C01158.title: collisional broadening
C01158.definition: Collisions of the emitting or absorbing particle with other particles cause collisional broadening as well as collisional shift of the spectral line. When collisions occur between unlike, neutral particles the term foreign-gas broadening is used, or van der Waals' broadening when both collision partners are neutral. When the colliding particles are of the same species, the term resonance broadening is employed. The term Lorentz broadening was previously used for neutral particle collision broadening, and Holtsmark broadening for cases of van der Waals' broadening when collisions took place with like particles. Both terms are now discouraged. Stark broadening refers to collisions with charged particles or particles with a strong permanent electrical dipole moment. Whereas a strong chaotic electrical field causes Stark broadening, an applied static electrical field induces a Stark shift.

C01159.title: collisional excitation
C01159.definition: An ion/neutral species process wherein there is an increase in the reactant ion's internal energy at the expense of the translational energy of either (or both) of the reacting species. The scattering angle may be large.

C01171.title: colloid
C01171.definition: A short synonym for colloidal system.

C01178.title: colloid osmotic pressure
C01178.definition: The pressure difference which has to be established between a colloidal system and its equilibrium liquid to prevent material transfer between the two phases when they are separated by a membrane, permeable to all components of the system, except the colloidal ones.

14312.title: colloid stabiliser
14312.definition: Compound increasing stability of a colloid.

C01172.title: colloidal
C01172.definition: The term refers to a state of subdivision, implying that the molecules or polymolecular particles dispersed in a medium have at least in one direction a dimension roughly between \(1\ \rm{nm}\) and \(1\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\), or that in a system discontinuities are found at distances of that order.

C01173.title: colloidal carbon
C01173.definition: A particulate carbon with particle sizes below ca.\(1000\ \rm{nm}\) in at least one dimension.

13803.title: colloidal crystal
13803.definition: Two- or three-dimensional ordered array of molecules or nanoparticles having a dimension roughly between \(\pu{1 nm}\) and \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\) in at least one direction.

C01174.title: colloidal dispersion
C01174.definition: A system in which particles of colloidal size of any nature (e.g. solid, liquid or gas) are dispersed in a continuous phase of a different composition (or state). The name dispersed phase for the particles should be used only if they have essentially the properties of a bulk phase of the same composition.

C01175.title: colloidal electrolyte
C01175.definition: An electrolyte which gives ions of which at least one is of colloidal size. This term therefore includes hydrophobic sols, ionic association colloids, and polyelectrolytes.

CT07518.title: colloidal gel
CT07518.definition: Gel in which the network component comprises particles of colloidal dimensions.

CT07563.title: colloidal network
CT07563.definition: Network comprising particles of colloidal dimensions.

CT07612.title: colloidal processing
CT07612.definition: Sol-gel processing in which a network of precipitated colloidal particles is treated by a conventional processing technique, such as cold pressing, hot pressing or sintering, in order to produce a ceramic article.

C01177.title: colloidal suspension
C01177.definition: A suspension in which the size of the particles lies in the colloidal range.

C01176.title: colloidally stable
C01176.definition: Particles which do not aggregate at a significant rate: the precise connotation depends on the type of aggregation under consideration. For example, a concentrated paint is called stable by some people because oil and pigment do not separate out at a measurable rate, and unstable by others because the pigment particles aggregate into a continuous network.

14395.title: colloidally stable system
14395.definition: System in which the particles essentially do not aggregate or sediment.

10546.title: coloboma
10546.definition: Any defect resulting from incomplete closure of the retinal fissure.

13024.title: colony-stimulating factor
13024.definition: Factor that permits the proliferation and differentiation of hematopoietic cells.

CT07342.title: color scale
CT07342.definition: Series of ordered numbers that represents observable gradations of a given attribute or gradations of a combination of attributes of color perception.

C01179.title: colorimeter
C01179.definition: An instrument used for colour measurement based on optical comparison with standard colours.

14002.title: colour centres
14002.definition: Lattice defects (typically vacancies) that trap one or more electrons or holes in ionic crystals. They constitute a long-lived deep trap with a low efficiency of trapping of a carrier of the opposite sign.

C01180.title: colour indicator
C01180.definition: An indicator which is classified as one- or two-colour, depending on whether it is colourless on one side of the transition interval or possesses a different colour on each side of this range.

CT07341.title: colourability
CT07341.definition: Ability of a colourless or slightly coloured photochromic material to develop colour.

C01182.title: column chromatography
C01182.definition: A separation technique in which the stationary bed is within a tube. The particles of the solid stationary phase or support coated with a liquid stationary phase may fill the whole inside volume of the tube (packed column) or be concentrated on or along the inside tube wall leaving an open, unrestricted path for the mobile phase in the middle part of the tube (open-tubular column).

09897.title: column diameter
09897.definition: Inner diameter of the column tubing.

C01181.title: column
C01181.definition: The tube and the stationary phase contained within, through which the mobile phase passes.

09898.title: column length
09898.definition: Length of that part of the column tube that contains the stationary phase.

C01183.title: column volume
C01183.definition: The geometric volume of the part of the tube that contains the packing: \[V_{\rm{c}} = A_{\rm{c}}\ L\] where \(A_{\rm{c}}\) is the internal cross-sectional area of the tube and \(L\) the length of the packed part of the column. In the case of wall-coated open-tubular columns the column volume corresponds to the geometric volume of the whole tube having a liquid or a solid stationary phase on its wall.

13804.title: columnar phase
13804.definition: Cylindrical assembly of molecules within a distinct series of layers in which the axes of the molecules lie in the planes of the layers and are identically aligned and oriented in adjacent layers.

11685.title: coma
11685.definition: State of profound unconsciousness lasting more than several hours in which one cannot respond to stimuli and from which one cannot be roused.

C01186.title: comb macromolecule
C01186.definition: A macromolecule comprising a main chain with multiple trifunctional branch points from each of which a linear side-chain emanates.

C01187.title: comb polymer
C01187.definition: A polymer composed of comb macromolecules.

08948.title: combination
08948.definition: Chain termination, in a chain polymerization, between two propagating macromolecules that gives rise to a single macromolecule of molar mass equal to the sum of the molar masses of the two macromolecules.

C01184.title: combination electrode
C01184.definition: An ion-selective electrode and an external reference electrode combined in a single unit, thereby avoiding the need for a separate external reference electrode.

08580.title: combination transition
08580.definition: Transition in which more than one vibration changes its degree of excitation; i.e., in which more than one vibrational quantum number changes.

13025.title: combinatorial diversity
13025.definition: Component of antibody and T-cell receptor (TCR) diversity that is generated by the recombination of variable (V), diversity (\(D\), for immunoglobulin heavy chains, and for TCR \(\upbeta\) and \(\ce{\updelta\ chains}\)), and joining (J) gene segments.

13026.title: combinatorial joining
13026.definition: Merging of DNA segments generating new genetic information.

14120.title: combinatorial library
14120.definition: Set of compounds prepared by combinatorial chemistry. It may consist of a collection of pools, or sublibraries. Its composition may be described by the chemset notation.

15575.title: combined effect of poisons
15575.definition: Simultaneous or successive effect of two or more poisons on the organism by the same route of exposure.

09113.title: combined electrode
09113.definition: Ion-selective electrode cell in which the ion-selective electrode and reference electrode are combined in a single sensor assembly, thereby avoiding the need for a separate external reference electrode.

10547.title: combined repeated dose toxicity study
10547.definition: Procedure to evaluate both general systemic toxicity, with an emphasis on neurological endpoints, and notably reproductive effects and developmental progression in rodents. Groups of males and females are administered a test substance in graded doses prior to mating, during the mating period, and subsequently (up to two weeks post-mating in males and four days post-delivery in females).

08321.title: combined rotation and multiple pulse spectroscopy
08321.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for obtaining high-resolution solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectra on nuclei with high gyromagnetic ratio such as \(\ce{^{1}H}\) and \(\ce{^{19}F}\).

C01185.title: combined sample
C01185.definition: A sample obtained by removing specific fractions by separation or selection techniques (e.g. heavy liquid, magnetic, sieving, etc.), analysing the fractions separately, and combining the results mathematically. When not combined, the sample is a modified sample. This term should not be confused with composite sample.

12284.title: combined technique
12284.definition: Application of two or more techniques to different samples at the same time. This can include thermal and nonthermal analytical techniques.

C01188.title: combustion gas
C01188.definition: A gas or vapour produced in furnaces, combustion chambers or in open burning.

15576.title: comet assay
15576.definition: Means of measuring DNA damage, particularly DNA strand breaks. A cell is embedded in agar and exposed to a DNA-damaging agent. The cell is then permeabilized with a detergent, and an electric field is applied. If the cell’s genomic DNA has been broken into small fragments, these fragments move out of the cell by electrophoresis and form a streak or 'tail' leading away from the cell which looks like a comet.

14530.title: cometabolism
14530.definition: Microbial transformation of a compound (that is normally unable to support cell replication) in the requisite presence of a transformable cosubstrate that supports cell replication.

C01189.title: commensurate–incommensurate transition
C01189.definition: A transition between two states having magnetic or crystallographic structures with a basic lattice and an imposed super-periodicity. In the commensurate (lock-in) state this super-periodicity is a simple rational multiple of the basic unit cell. In the incommensurate state the ratio of the super-periodicity repeat distance to the basic lattice repeat distance is irrational and may show continuous variation with variation in some degree of freedom (e.g. temperature, pressure, composition) of the system.

10089.title: common factor analysis
10089.definition: Factor analysis in which latent variables are calculated that maximise the correlation with observed variables.

13027.title: common variable immunodeficiency
13027.definition: Relatively common deficiency in antibody production, of unknown pathogenesis but strongly associated with genes mapping within the major histocompatibility complex (MHC).

C01191.title: common-ion effect
C01191.definition: A reduction in the rate of reaction of certain reactions of a substrate RX in solution [by a path that involves a pre-equilibrium with formation of $\ce{R^{+}}$ (or $\ce{R^{−}}$) ions as reaction intermediates] caused by the addition to the reaction mixture of an electrolyte solute containing the 'common ion' $\ce{X^{−}}$ (or $\ce{X+}$). For example, the rate of solvolysis of diphenylmethyl chloride in acetone-water is reduced by the addition of salts of the common ion $\ce{Cl^{−}}$ which causes a decrease in the quasi-equilibrium concentration of the diphenylmethyl cation in the scheme:   This phenomenon is a direct consequence of the mass-law effect on ionization equilibria in electrolytic solution. More generally, the common-ion effect is the influence of the 'common ion' on the reactivity due to the shift of the dissociation equilibrium. It may also lead to an enhancement of the rate of reaction.

11812.title: communicating hydrocephalus
11812.definition: Hydrocephalus where flow of cerebrospinal fluid is not blocked but there is failure of its reabsorption.

C01192.title: communities
C01192.definition: Naturally occuring groups of different (micro)organisms inhabiting a common environment, interacting with each other, especially through food relationships and relatively independent of other groups. Communities may be of varying sizes, and larger communities may contain smaller ones.

14531.title: community
14531.definition: Assembly of populations of different species of living organisms, usually interdependent on and interacting with each other, within a specified location in space and time.

14532.title: community conditioning hypothesis
14532.definition: Hypothesis that ecological communities retain information about events in their history and will not return to their original state after perturbation.

14534.title: community resilience
14534.definition: Ability of a community to return to its former state after perturbation.

14535.title: community resistance
14535.definition: Ability of a community to avoid displacement from its present state by a disturbance.

14533.title: community stability
14533.definition: Tendency of a community to return to its original state after a disturbance (competition, temporarily changing environment, etc.).

14536.title: community structure
14536.definition: Species present in a community and their relative abundances.

08064.title: commutability of a reference material
08064.definition: Property of a reference material, demonstrated by the closeness of agreement between the relation among the measurement results for a stated quantity in this material, obtained according to two given measurement procedures, and the relation obtained among the measurement results for other specified materials.

10548.title: compaction
10548.definition:
Complication of labor in twin births in which there is attempted simultaneous expulsion of both twins, so that the lower part of the mother’s pelvis is filled and further descent through the birth canal is prevented.
In embryology, process during which blastomeres change their shape and align themselves tightly against each other to form the compact morula.

15577.title: comparative genomics
15577.definition: Study of the relationship of genome structure and function across different biological species.

09810.title: comparative glycoproteomics
09810.definition: Field of glycoproteomics that studies that the changes in the structures and expression levels of glycoproteins under different conditions.

CT06951.title: comparative molecular field analysis
CT06951.definition: Comparative Molecular Field Analysis (CoMFA) is a 3D-QSAR method that uses statistical correlation techniques for the analysis of the quantitative relationship between the biological activity of a set of compounds with a special alignment, and their three-dimensional electronic and steric properties. Other properties, such as hydrophobicity and H-bonding, can also be incorporated into the analysis.

11426.title: comparative molecular similarity analysis
11426.definition:
A 3D-QSAR method similar to CoMFA that instead uses Gaussian-type functions to calculate the 3D properties of the molecules by the similarity of each molecule
 to each probe at each lattice position surrounding the molecules.

09811.title: comparative proteoglycomics
09811.definition: Field of proteoglycomics that studies the changes in the structures and expression levels of proteoglycans under different conditions.

C01194.title: comparator
C01194.definition: A known amount of element that is simultaneously irradiated with the test portion in the context of activation analysis. If one comparator is used (single comparator method), it is essentially identical to a flux monitor (except that this term is not necessarily linked to activation analysis).

14537.title: compartment
14537.definition:
Conceptualized part of the body (organs, tissues, cells, or fluids) considered as an independent system for purposes of modeling and assessment of distribution and clearance of a substance.
Part of an ecosystem considered as an independent system for purposes of assessment of uptake, distribution, and dissipation of a substance.

CT06818.title: compartmental analysis
CT06818.definition: Mathematical process leading to a model of transport of a substance in terms of compartments and rate constants, usually taking the form \[C=A\ \rm{e}^{-\alpha\ t}+B\ \rm{e}^{-\beta \ t}\rm{...}\] where each exponential term represents one experiment. \(C\) is the substance concentration; \(A\), \(B\),… are proportionality constants; \(\alpha \), \(\beta \),… are rate constants; and \(t\) is time.

14364.title: compartmentalisation behaviour
14364.definition: Zero-one behaviour wherein radicals are isolated, each being located within a different latex particle.

CT07581.title: compatible polymer blend
CT07581.definition: Immiscible polymer blend that exhibits macroscopically uniform physical properties.

C01197.title: compensation effect
C01197.definition: In a considerable number of cases plots of \(T\ \Delta ^{\ddagger }S\) vs. \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}H\), for a series of reactions, e.g. for a reaction in a range of different solvents, are straight lines of approximately unit slope. Therefore, the terms \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}H\) and \(T\ \Delta ^{\ddagger }S\) in the expression partially compensate, and \[\Delta ^{\ddagger}G = \Delta ^{\ddagger}H - T\ \Delta ^{\ddagger}S\] often is a much simpler function of solvent (or other) variation than \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}H\) or \(T\ \Delta ^{\ddagger }S\) separately.

C01195.title: compensation
C01195.definition: For the process: \[k = A\ \rm{e}^{\frac{-E}{R\ T}}\] where \(k\) is a rate constant, \(A\) the frequency factor and \(E\) the activation energy, \(A\) and \(E\) sometimes exhibit compensation, i.e. they change in the same direction with change in catalyst for a given reaction or with change in reaction for a given catalyst.

C01196.title: compensation
C01196.definition: For internal compensation, see compound.See: external compensation

08065.title: competence
08065.definition: Ability to apply knowledge and skills to achieve intended results.

15579.title: competent authority
15579.definition: In the context of European Community Council Directive 79/831/EEC, the Sixth Amendment to the European Community Council Directive 67/548/EEC relating to the Classification, Packaging and Labeling of Dangerous Substances, official government organization or group receiving and evaluating notifications of new substances.

15580.title: competent bacteria
15580.definition: Culture of bacteria (or yeast) treated in such a way that their ability to take up DNA molecules without transduction or conjugation has been enhanced.

C01199.title: competitive binding assay
C01199.definition: An assay based on the competition between a labelled and an unlabelled ligand in the reaction with a receptor binding agent (e.g. antibody, receptor, transport protein).

14538.title: competitive exclusion
14538.definition: Outcompetition from a niche of one species by another that uses the available resources of the niche more efficiently, eventually resulting in the exclusion of the outcompeted species.

13028.title: competitive inhibition assay
13028.definition: Method of measuring an antigen in a sample using a labeled species of the antigen as a competitive inhibitor of its binding in a specific antigen–antibody reaction.

C01200.title: competitive inhibition
C01200.definition: The reduction in rate due to reduction or loss of activity of a catalyst caused by adsorption of poison which is not greatly preferred to adsorption of reactant.

09668.title: complement
09668.definition: Array of serum proteins (some of which are enzymes) that become sequentially activated after the first member of the series is activated by either antigen-antibody complexes or microbial products.

13030.title: complement deficiency
13030.definition: Congenital deficiency in any of the various components of the complement system.

13031.title: complement reaction
13031.definition: Physiological reaction to the presence of a foreign microorganism in which a cascade of enzymatic reactions, triggered by molecular features of the microorganism, result in lysis or phagocytosis of the foreign material.

13032.title: complement receptor
13032.definition: Cell-surface protein that recognizes and binds complement proteins that have bound an antigen.

13033.title: complement system
13033.definition: Group of serum proteins with the capacity to interact with each other when activated in a chain reaction which results in formation of a lytic complex and the release of several biologically active peptides of low relative molecular mass (anaphylatoxins).

13029.title: complementarity-determining region
13029.definition: Hypervariable amino acid sequence within antibody and T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V) regions, which interacts with complementary amino acids on the antigen or major histocompatibility complex (MHC)–peptide complex.

C01202.title: complementary DNA
C01202.definition: A single-stranded DNA molecule with a nucleotide sequence that is complementary to an RNA molecule; cDNA is formed by the action of the enzyme reverse transcriptase on an RNA template. After conversion to the double-stranded form, cDNA is used for molecular cloning or for hybridization studies.

09691.title: complementary sequence
09691.definition: Nucleotide sequence that can form a double-stranded structure with another deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequence by following base-pairing (see base pair) rules.

CT07343.title: complete active space self-consistent field
CT07343.definition: Computational scheme employed in multiconfigurational SCF theory especially suitable for studies of reactivity of excited states. The wavefunction is defined by selecting the set of active orbitals involved in the excitation or chemical reaction under investigation and is constructed as a linear expansion in the set of configuration functions that can be generated by occupying the active orbitals in all ways consistent with an overall spin and space symmetry (full configuration interaction, CI).

CT07344.title: complete active space self-consistent field second-order perturbation theory
CT07344.definition: Theoretical scheme suitable for computations of accurate excitation energies and reaction barriers. In the first step, electron correlation is taken into account only to a certain extent by using a CASSCF formalism (the so called non-dynamic correlation), whereas the remaining electron correlation (the so called dynamic correlation) is included through the use of second-order perturbation theory.

09692.title: complete genome sequence
09692.definition: High-quality, low-error, gap-free deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequence of an entire genome of an organism.

10121.title: complete linkage
10121.definition: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the distance between two clusters is the distance between those two objects (one from each cluster) that are farthest apart.

15581.title: complete mineralisation
15581.definition: Complete breakdown of a complex organic compound to carbon dioxide, water, oxides, and oxidative inorganic products such as nitrate or sulfate.

C01203.title: complex
C01203.definition: A molecular entity formed by loose association involving two or more component molecular entities (ionic or uncharged), or the corresponding chemical species. The bonding between the components is normally weaker than in a covalent bond. The term has also been used with a variety of shades of meaning in different contexts: it is therefore best avoided when a more explicit alternative is applicable. In inorganic chemistry the term 'coordination entity' is recommended instead of 'complex'.

C01204.title: complex coacervation
C01204.definition: Coacervation caused by the interaction of two oppositely charged colloids.

C01205.title: complex mechanism
C01205.definition: This term is sometimes applied to an elementary reaction which proceeds via an intermediate species having a lifetime longer than a few rotational periods, in contrast to a direct reaction. However, in view of the danger of confusion with a reaction occurring in more than one step (a composite reaction) this usage is not to be recommended; it is better to use the terms complex-mode mechanism or complex-mode reaction.

C01206.title: complex-mode reaction
C01206.definition: An elementary reaction which proceeds via an intermediate species having a lifetime longer than a few rotational periods is known as a complex-mode reaction, or as an indirect reaction.

14539.title: complimentary niches
14539.definition: Niches where coexisting species occupy a similar position along one niche dimension, e.g., altitude, but differ along another, e.g., diet.

16268.title: component
16268.definition: Constituent whose amount or concentration can be varied independently in a mixture.

C01209.title: component
C01209.definition: Constituent of a mixture the amount or concentration of which can be varied independently. The number of components in a given system is the minimum number of independent species necessary to define the composition in all the phases of a system. It may vary with external conditions since additional chemical equilibria reduce the number of components. The term component is also often used in the more general sense as defined here under constituent.

CT07545.title: composite
CT07545.definition: Multicomponent material comprising multiple, different (non-gaseous) phase domains in which at least one type of phase domain is a continuous phase.

09038.title: composite alkalinity
09038.definition: Measurement by titration to the phenolphthalein end-point (pH 8.3) of that portion of alkalinity arbitrarily attributed to all the hydroxyl content and half the carbonate content of a titrand.

C01210.title: composite mechanism
C01210.definition: A reaction that involves more than one elementary reaction is said to occur by a composite mechanism. The terms complex mechanism, indirect mechanism, and step-wise mechanism are also commonly used. There are two main kinds of evidence for a composite mechanism: The kinetic equation for the reaction does not correspond to its stoichiometry.There is experimental evidence, direct or indirect, for intermediates of such a nature that it is necessary to conclude that more than one elementary reaction is involved. There are many types of composite mechanisms, for example: Reactions occurring in parallel, such as:  are called parallel reactions or simultaneous reactions. When there are simultaneous reactions there is sometimes  competition, as in the scheme:  where B and C compete with one another for A.Reactions occurring in forward and reverse directions are called opposing reactions: Reactions occurring in sequence, such as  are known as consecutive reactions.Reactions are said to exhibit feedback if a substance formed in one step affects the rate of a previous step. For example, in the scheme: The intermediate Y may catalyse the reaction  (positive feedback) or it may inhibit it (negative feedback).Chain reactions

CT06863.title: composite membrane
CT06863.definition: Membrane having chemically or structurally distinct layers.

C01211.title: composite reaction
C01211.definition: A chemical reaction for which the expression for the rate of disappearance of a reactant (or rate of appearance of a product) involves rate constants of more than a single elementary reaction. Examples are 'opposing reactions' (where rate constants of two opposed chemical reactions are involved), 'parallel reactions' (for which the rate of disappearance of any reactant is governed by the rate constants relating to several simultaneous reactions to form different respective products from a single set of reactants), and stepwise reactions.

C01212.title: composite sample
C01212.definition: Often prepared as a representative mixture of several different (usually bulk) samples, and from which the laboratory sample is taken.

C01214.title: composition of pure air
C01214.definition: The composition of air is variable with respect to several of its components (e.g. $\ce{CH4}$, $\ce{CO2}$, $\ce{H2O}$) so 'pure' air has no precise meaning; it is commonly considered to be air which is free of dust, aerosols and reactive gaseous contaminants of anthropogenic origin. The composition of the major components in dry air is relatively constant (percent by volume given): nitrogen, 78.084; oxygen, 20.946; argon, 0.934; carbon dioxide, 0.033; neon, 0.0018; helium, 0.000524; methane, 0.00016; krypton, 0.000114; hydrogen 0.00005; nitrous oxide, 0.00003; xenon, 0.0000087. The concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, the chlorofluorocarbons and some other species of anthropogenic origin are increasing measurably with time. Relative clean air which is free of most reactive anthropogenic pollution ($\ce{NO}$, $\ce{NO2}$, $\ce{SO2}$, non-methane hydrocarbons, etc.), often used as a reference sample in the calibration and operation of instruments, is purchased under the designation of zero air.

09239.title: compositional depth profile
09239.definition: Chemical composition measured as a function of distance normal to the surface.

C01213.title: compositional heterogeneity
C01213.definition: The variation in elemental composition from molecule to molecule usually found in copolymers.

09597.title: composting
09597.definition: Process of biological decomposition of organic matter performed by microorganisms, mostly bacteria and fungi.

14121.title: compound collection
14121.definition: Set of chemicals that has been assembled and annotated for easy storage and retrieval and that is available for screening.

15582.title: comprehensive effect of poisons
15582.definition: Simultaneous or successive effect made on an organism by poisons entering from different media, air, water, or food or through the skin.

09953.title: comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography
09953.definition: Type of two-dimensional chromatography in which all the effluent from the first separation step is transferred in fractions to a second separation step.

15162.title: compressed tablet
15162.definition: A solid dosage form prepared to a desired shape, usually in large-scale production, by means of high pressure in a punch and die.

C01216.title: compression factor
C01216.definition: Product of pressure and molar volume divided by the gas constant and thermodynamic temperature. For an ideal gas it is equal to 1.

C01217.title: comproportionation
C01217.definition: The reverse of disproportionation. The term 'symproportionation' is also used.

C01218.title: Compton effect
C01218.definition: The elastic scattering of a photon by an electron which afterwards occurs as a free electron. Part of the energy and momentum of the incident photon is transferred to the electron and the remaining part is carried away by the scattered photon. Synonymous with Compton scattering

C01219.title: Compton electron
C01219.definition: The energetic electron resulting from the Compton effect.

08720.title: Compton scattering analysis
08720.definition: Measurement principle in which wavelengths and angular distribution of Compton scattered electrons is applied in order to reconstruct X-ray and gamma-ray spectra.

CT06952.title: computational chemistry
CT06952.definition: Computational chemistry is a discipline using mathematical methods for the calculation of molecular properties or for the simulation of molecular behaviour. It also includes, e.g., synthesis planning, database searching, combinatorial library manipulation.

CT07345.title: computational photochemistry
CT07345.definition: Aspects of research that address the study of photochemical events by means of computer simulations using specialized software tools and strategies in order to get an understanding of the process at a microscopic level. The aim is to uncover the mechanism of known photochemical processes, design new photochemical systems, and predict molecular properties that are experimentally inaccessible.

15583.title: computational toxicology
15583.definition: Application of mathematical and computer models to predict adverse effects and to better understand the mechanism(s) through which a given chemical causes harm.

CT06953.title: computer-assisted drug design
CT06953.definition: Computer-assisted drug design involves all computer-assisted techniques used to discover, design and optimize biologically active compounds with a putative use as drugs.

CT06954.title: computer-assisted molecular design
CT06954.definition: Computer-assisted molecular design involves all computer-assisted techniques used to discover, design and optimize compounds with desired structure and properties.

CT06955.title: computer-assisted molecular modeling
CT06955.definition: Computer-assisted molecular modeling is the investigation of molecular structures and properties using computational chemistry and graphical visualization techniques.

10549.title: conal growth hypothesis
10549.definition: Hypothesis that explains transposition of the great arteries of the heart by failure of the aortopulmonary septum to follow a spiral course during partitioning of the bulbus cordis and truncus arteriosus in the process of forming the aorta and pulmonary trunk.

13034.title: concanavalin A
13034.definition: Hemagglutinin, isolated from jack bean (Canavalia ensiformis) meal, which reacts with polyglucosans in the blood of mammals, causing agglutination.

CT06938.title: concave isotherm
CT06938.definition: Distribution isotherm, the slope of which is continuously increasing.

12229.title: concentrated solution
12229.definition: Polymer solution in the concentration range at which the domains occupied by the dissolved macromolecules or entities overlap to such an extent that it is not possible to distinguish the individual domains from one another.

C01222.title: concentration
C01222.definition: Group of four quantities characterizing the composition of a mixture with respect to the volume of the mixture (mass, amount, volume and number concentration).Short form for amount-of-substance concentration ('substance concentration' in clinical chemistry).

14540.title: concentration–response curve
14540.definition: Graph of the relation between exposure concentration and the proportion of individuals in a population responding with a defined effect.

CT07346.title: concentration depolarization
CT07346.definition: Loss of emission anisotropy due to transfer of electronic excitation from photo-selected molecules to other molecules with different orientations.

C01225.title: concentration distribution ratio
C01225.definition: The ratio of the analytical concentration of a component in the stationary phase to its analytical concentration in the mobile phase. \[D_{\rm{c}} = \frac{\rm{amount\ of\ component}/\pu{cm3}\ \rm{of\ stationary\ phase}}{\rm{amount\ of\ component}/\pu{cm3}\ \rm{of\ mobile\ phase}}\]

C01227.title: concentration gradient
C01227.definition: Differential change in concentration of a component in a given direction in a small distance divided by the distance in that direction.

C01229.title: concentration in experimental surface
C01229.definition: The amount of the material of interest divided by the total amount of substances in the volume of interest. Concentration may be defined in terms of numbers of atoms (particles) (\(\rm{ppma}\)) or in terms of weight (\(\frac{\unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{g}}{\rm{g}}\)).

C01230.title: concentration overpotential
C01230.definition: The concentration overpotential of an electrode reaction at a given electrode current density (\(\rm{c.d.}\)) is basically the difference in equilibrium potentials across the diffusion layer. More precisely, it is the potential of a reference electrode (of the same electrode reaction as the working electrode) with the interfacial concentrations which establish themselves at \(\rm{c.d.}\), relative to the potential of a similar reference electrode with the concentrations of the bulk solution. From such a measured potential difference, with \(\rm{c.d.}\) flowing, one needs to subtract the ohmic potential drop prevailing between the two electrodes.

14122.title: concentration–response relationship
14122.definition: Association between compound concentration and the resultant magnitude of the continuously graded change produced, in an assay.

C01224.title: concentration-cell corrosion
C01224.definition: The local variation of the corrosion rate due to the action of a corrosion cell resulting from inhomogeneous composition of the environment.

15584.title: concentration–effect curve
15584.definition: Graph of the relation between exposure concentration and the magnitude of the resultant biological change.

15585.title: concentration–effect relationship
15585.definition: Association between exposure concentration and the resultant magnitude of the continuously graded change produced, either in an individual or in a population.

C01232.title: concentration-sensitive detector
C01232.definition: A device the response of which is proportional to the concentration of a sample component in the eluent.

10550.title: conception
10550.definition: Formation of a viable zygote by the union of a spermatozoon and an ovum.

14541.title: conceptual model
14541.definition: Linkage and interrelationship of assessment endpoint(s) and stressors.

14542.title: conceptual model diagram
14542.definition: Figure showing pathways of exposure of organisms and illustrating areas of uncertainty or concern.

14543.title: conceptual site model
14543.definition: Integration of information on contaminants of potential concern (COPCs), ecological resources, evaluated exposure routes, fate and transport mechanisms, evaluated COPC toxicity, identified assessment endpoints, and risk questions and hypotheses, into a description of all that is known and (or) expected about a contaminated site.

10551.title: conceptus
10551.definition: Embryo and associated membranes in the uterus, especially during the early stages of pregnancy.

C01234.title: concerted process
C01234.definition: Two or more primitive changes are said to be concerted (or to constitute a concerted process) if they occur within the same elementary reaction. Such changes will normally (though perhaps not inevitably) be 'energetically coupled'. (In the present context the term 'energetically coupled' means that the simultaneous progress of the primitive changes involves a transition state of lower energy than that for their successive occurrence.) In a concerted process the primitive changes may be synchronous or asynchronous.

CT07011.title: concerted reaction
CT07011.definition: A single-step reaction through which reactants are directly transformed into products, i.e., without involvement of any intermediates.

11427.title: concordance
11427.definition: The ability of a two-group classification model to correctly classify all molecules.

15586.title: concurrent validity
15586.definition: Measurement and its criterion refer to the same point in time.

C01235.title: condensation
C01235.definition: The physical process of converting a material from a gaseous or vapour phase to a liquid or solid phase; this commonly results when the temperature is lowered and/or the vapour pressure of the material is increased. The tendency exists for condensation to occur when the partial pressure of a given component of a gaseous mixture at a given temperature exceeds the vapour pressure of the liquid or solid form of that component at the given temperature.

C01236.title: condensation nuclei
C01236.definition: Particles, either liquid or solid, or ions upon which condensation of water vapour (or other substances) begins in the atmosphere. Condensation nuclei are usually very small hygroscopic aerosols (\(\pu{0.001 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{0.1 \upmu m}\) in diameter), but these are not as abundant as the smaller particles. The number of CN which are active (initiate condensation) in a given air mass may be a function of the relative humidity. Usually CN are counted as the active nuclei at about $\ce{300\%}$ relative humidity, while cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) are counted as the number of active nuclei at relative humidity less than or equal to $\ce{102\%}$.

C01237.title: condensation polymerization
C01237.definition: Polymerization by a repeated condensation process (i.e. with elimination of simple molecules).

C01238.title: condensation reaction
C01238.definition: A (usually stepwise) reaction in which two or more reactants (or remote reactive sites within the same molecular entity) yield a single main product with accompanying formation of water or of some other small molecule, e.g. ammonia, ethanol, acetic acid, hydrogen sulfide. The mechanism of many condensation reactions has been shown to comprise consecutive addition and elimination reactions, as in the base-catalysed formation of (E)-but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde) from acetaldehyde, via 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol). The overall reaction in this example is known as the aldol condensation. The term is sometimes also applied to cases where the formation of water or another simple molecule does not occur, as in 'benzoin condensation'.

08158.title: condensed formula
08158.definition: Linear representation of the structure of a molecular entity in which bonds are omitted.

14544.title: condition
14544.definition: State of health determining potential for reproduction and growth.

14545.title: condition factor
14545.definition: Parameter used to describe growth in fish. It reflects real growth and nutritional status better than simple measurement of body mass.

14546.title: condition index
14546.definition: Any quantitative measure of the condition in relation to a defined baseline.

C01240.title: conditional potential

C01241.title: conditional rate constant of an electrode reaction

11686.title: conditioned avoidance response test
11686.definition: Experimental procedure in which an adverse effect (e.g., foot shock, drug withdrawal) is delivered to rats or mice after presentation of a cue (e.g., light or sound); the rodents are trained to avoid rather than escape the shock after the start of its delivery.

12095.title: conditioned stimulus
12095.definition: Stimulus that comes to evoke a response after repetitive pairing with another stimulus that automatically elicits that response.

10239.title: conditioning solvent
10239.definition: Small volume of solvent used to prepare the sorbent for efficient sample processing.

CT07170.title: conducting polymer
CT07170.definition: Polymeric material that exhibits bulk electric conductivity.

CT07201.title: conducting polymer composite
CT07201.definition: Electrically-conducting composite comprising a non-conducting polymer matrix and an electrically-conducting material.

C01244.title: conduction band
C01244.definition: A vacant or only partially occupied set of many closely spaced electronic levels resulting from an array of a large number of atoms forming a system in which the electrons can move freely or nearly so. This term is usually used to describe the properties of metals and semiconductors.

C01245.title: conductivity
C01245.definition: Reciprocal of resistivity. This quantity is a tensor in an anisotropic medium. It was formerly called 'specific conductance'.

09165.title: conductometric titration
09165.definition: Titration in which the electric conductivity of a solution is measured as a function of the amount of titrant added.Conductimetric titration curve of conductance ($G$) against volume of titrant. The end-point of the titration is indicated by a change in slope of the graph.

09166.title: conductometry
09166.definition: Measurement principle in which the electric conductivity of a solution is measured.

08784.title: conductor
08784.definition: Material having the ability to transmit energy or charge carriers or both.

C01246.title: confidence level
C01246.definition: The probability of covering the expected value of an estimated parameter with an interval estimated for the parameter (symbol \(1 - \alpha\)). The confidence level can be expressed as a number between 0 and 1, or in percent. The complementary quantity is known as the significance level.

C01247.title: confidence limits
C01247.definition: Symmetric confidence limits (\(\pm C\)) about the estimated mean, which cover the population mean with probability \(1 - \alpha \). The quantity \(C\) is calculated by the formula: \[C = \frac{t_{\rm{p},v^{S}}}{\sqrt{n}}\] Here \(t_{\rm{p},v}\), is the critical value from the \(t\)- (or Student) distribution function corresponding to the confidence level \(1 - \alpha \) and degrees of freedom \(v\). The symbol \(p\) represents the percentile (or percentage point) of the \(t\)-distribution. For 1-sided intervals, \(p=1- \alpha \); for 2-sided intervals, \(p=1- \frac{\alpha }{2}\). In each case, the confidence level is \(1 - \alpha \). The confidence interval is given as \(\overline{x}\ \pm \ C\).

C01248.title: configuration
C01248.definition: A distribution of the electrons of an atom or a molecular entity over a set of one-electron wavefunctions called orbitals, according to the Pauli principle. From one configuration several states with different multiplicities may result. For example, the ground electronic configuration of the oxygen molecule ($\ce{O2}$) is: \(1\sigma _{\rm{g}}^{2}\), \(1\sigma _{\rm{u}}^{2}\), \(2\sigma _{\rm{g}}^{2}\), \(2\sigma _{\rm{u}}^{2}\), \(1\pi _{\rm{u}}^{4}\), \(3\sigma _{\rm{g}}^{2}\), \(1\pi _{\rm{g}}^{2}\) resulting in the \(^{3}\Sigma_{\rm{g}}\), \(^{1}\Delta_{\rm{g}}\) and \(^{1}\Sigma_{\rm{g}}^{+}\) multiplets.

C01249.title: configuration
