C01249.definition: In the context of stereochemistry, the term is restricted to the arrangements of atoms of a molecular entity in space that distinguishes stereoisomers, the isomerism between which is not due to conformation differences.

C01256.title: configuration interaction
C01256.definition: The mixing of many-electron wavefunctions constructed from different electronic configurations to obtain an improved many-electron state.

C01250.title: configurational base unit
C01250.definition: A constitutional repeating unit in a regular macromolecule, a regular oligomer molecule, regular block or a regular chain, the configuration of which is defined at least at one site of stereoisomerism in the main chain.

C01251.title: configurational disorder
C01251.definition: Structural disorder resulting from the statistical co-crystallization of different configurational repeating units.

C01252.title: configurational homosequence
C01252.definition: A constitutional homosequence in which the relative or absolute configuration is defined at one or more sites of stereoisomerism in each constitutional unit in the main chain of a polymer molecule.

C01253.title: configurational repeating unit
C01253.definition: The smallest set of successive configurational base units that prescribes configurational repetition at one or more sites of stereoisomerism in the main chain of a regular macromolecule, a regular oligomer molecule, a regular block or a regular chain.

C01254.title: configurational sequence
C01254.definition: The whole or part of a chain comprising one or more species of configurational unit(s) in defined sequence.

C01255.title: configurational unit
C01255.definition: A constitutional unit having at least one site of defined stereoisomerism.

14123.title: confirmed hit
14123.definition: Sample that produces activity above the hit threshold in an assay and whose structural identity has been confirmed.

08066.title: conformance probability
08066.definition: Probability that an item fulfils a specified requirement.

C01258.title: conformation
C01258.definition: The spatial arrangement of the atoms affording distinction between stereoisomers which can be interconverted by rotations about formally single bonds. Some authorities extend the term to include inversion at trigonal pyramidal centres and other polytopal rearrangements.

C01259.title: conformational analysis
C01259.definition: The assessment of the relative energies (or thermodynamic stabilities), reactivities, and physical properties of alternative conformations of a molecular entity, usually by the application of qualitative or semi-quantitative rules or by semi-empirical calculations.

CT06956.title: conformational analysis
CT06956.definition: Conformational analysis consists of the exploration of energetically favourable spatial arrangements (shapes) of a molecule (conformations) using molecular mechanics, molecular dynamics, quantum chemical calculations or analysis of experimentally-determined structural data, e.g, NMR or crystal structures.Molecular mechanics and quantum chemical methods are employed to compute conformational energies, whereas systematic and random searches, Monte Carlo, molecular dynamics, and distance geometry are methods (often combined with energy minimization procedures) used to explore the conformational space.

C01260.title: conformational disorder
C01260.definition: Structural disorder resulting from the statistical coexistence within the crystals of identical configurational units with different conformations.

12749.title: conformational enthalpy
12749.definition: Enthalpy change associated with conformational changes.

12750.title: conformational entropy
12750.definition: Entropy change associated with conformational changes.

13035.title: conformational epitope
13035.definition: Epitope on a protein antigen formed from several separate regions in the primary sequence of a protein brought together by protein folding.

12751.title: conformational melting
12751.definition: Step-like increase in the conformational entropy of macromolecules, or parts of macromolecules.

C01261.title: conformational repeating unit of a polymer

C01262.title: conformer
C01262.definition: One of a set of stereoisomers, each of which is characterized by a conformation corresponding to a distinct potential energy minimum.

08067.title: conformity assessment
08067.definition: Activity to determine whether specified requirements relating to a product, process, system, person, or body are fulfilled.

15587.title: confounding
15587.definition:
Situation in which the effects of two processes are not distinguishable from one another: The distortion of the apparent effect of an exposure on risk brought about by the association of other factors which can influence the outcome.
Relationship between the effects of two or more causal factors as observed in a set of data, such that it is not logically possible to separate the contribution which any single causal factor has made to an effect.
Situation in which a measure of the effect of an exposure on risk is distorted because of the association of exposure with other factor(s) which influence the outcome under study.

15588.title: confounding variable
15588.definition: Changing factor that can cause or prevent the outcome of interest, is not an intermediate variable, and is associated with the factor under investigation.

11689.title: confusion
11689.definition: Mental state of bewilderment or disorientation in which reactions to environmental stimuli may be inappropriate.

11428.title: confusion matrix
11428.definition: A table layout that shows the results of a two-class/binary classifier in which columns correspond to the predicted classifications from the model and rows correspond to the observed classifications.

CT06819.title: congener
CT06819.definition: One of two or more substances related to each other by origin, structure, or function.

13036.title: congenic
13036.definition: Differing at a single genetic locus.

10552.title: congenital
10552.definition: Present from birth, as of a disease or physical abnormality.

10553.title: congenital adrenal hyperplasia
10553.definition: Group of disorders caused by hyperplasia of the adrenal cortex or by malignant tumors, resulting in excess secretion of adrenocortical androgenic hormones, and characterized by masculinization of women, feminization of men, or precocious puberty in the male.

10473.title: congenital branchial cyst
10473.definition: Congenital cyst arising in the lateral aspect of the neck, from epithelial remnants of a pharyngeal groove.

10554.title: congenital malformation
10554.definition: Malformation existing at birth, or developing during the first month of life, regardless of the cause.

11182.title: congenital retinoschisis
11182.definition: Congenital splitting of the retina into two layers.

C01264.title: congruent transition
C01264.definition: A transition in which the two-phase equilibrium of melting, vaporization or allotropism of a compound involves phases of the same composition.

CT07347.title: conical intersection
CT07347.definition: Point of crossing between two electronic states of the same spin multiplicity (most commonly singlets or triplets).

C01265.title: coning and quartering
C01265.definition: The reduction in size of a granular or powdered sample by forming a conical heap which is spread out into a circular, flat cake. The cake is divided radially into quarters and two opposite quarters are combined. The other two quarters are discarded. The process is repeated as many times as necessary to obtain the quantity desired for some final use (e.g. as the laboratory sample or as the test sample). If the process is performed only once, coning and quartering is no more efficient than taking alternate portions and discarding the others.

10555.title: conjoined twin
10555.definition: One of a pair of identical twins fused together with varying degrees of union and of residual duplication of organs.

16250.title: conjugate
16250.definition: Molecule or compound designed to support, transport, and/or deliver one or several active species in order to take advantage of their specificity.

C01266.title: conjugate acid–base pair
C01266.definition: The Brønsted acid $\ce{BH^{+}}$ formed on protonation of a base $\ce{B}$ is called the conjugate acid of $\ce{B}$, and $\ce{B}$ is the conjugate base of $\ce{BH^{+}}$. (The conjugate acid always carries one unit of positive charge more than the base, but the absolute charges of the species are immaterial to the definition.) For example: the Brønsted acid $\ce{HCl}$ and its conjugate base $\ce{Cl^{−}}$ constitute a conjugate acid–base pair.

15321.title: conjugate phases
15321.definition: Two phases of variable composition in mutual thermodynamic equilibrium.

C01268.title: conjugate solutions
C01268.definition: Two solutions that co-exist in equilibrium at a given temperature and pressure and, at constant pressure (temperature), change their compositions and relative proportions with a variation of temperature (pressure). The term usually refers to two immiscible liquids, but it is also applicable to two immiscible solid solutions.

08785.title: conjugated polymer
08785.definition: A polymer composed of molecules whose backbone is a sequence of alternating single and multiple bonds:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\) and \(\ce{R^{2}}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl or heteroaryl and Ar is arenediyl (formerly: arylene) or heteroarenediyl (formerly: heteroarylene).

C01267.title: conjugated system
C01267.definition: In the original meaning a conjugated system is a molecular entity whose structure may be represented as a system of alternating single and multiple bonds: e.g. $\ce{CH2=CH–CH=CH2}$, $\ce{CH2=CH–C#N}$. In such systems, conjugation is the interaction of one p-orbital with another across an intervening $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bond}$ in such structures. (In appropriate molecular entities d-orbitals may be involved.) The term is also extended to the analogous interaction involving a p-orbital containing an unshared electron pair, e.g. $\ce{{:}Cl–CH=CH2}$.

C01270.title: conjugation
C01270.definition: The contact-dependent transfer of a part or all of its genome from one bacterial cell (donor) to another (recipient).

C01271.title: conjugation labelling
C01271.definition: Labelling of a substance by conjugation with a labelled molecule.

15589.title: conjunctiva
15589.definition: Mucous membrane that covers the eyeball and lines the under-surface of the eyelid.

C01273.title: conjunctive name
C01273.definition: A name for assemblies of functionalized acyclic parent hydrides and cyclic systems implying the loss of an appropriate number of hydrogen atoms from each.

10556.title: connective tissue
10556.definition: Extracellular matrix of fibrous proteins and glycoproteins, with associated cells such as fibroblasts, that fills the spaces between and within organs and tissues.

C01274.title: connectivity
C01274.definition: In a chemical context, the information content of a line formula, but omitting any indication of bond multiplicity.

CT07504.title: connectivity
CT07504.definition: Number of covalent bonds emanating from a constitutional unit of an oligomer molecule or a macromolecule.

11690.title: conscious
11690.definition: Aware of and responding to one’s surroundings.

C01276.title: consecutive reactions
C01276.definition: Reactions occurring in sequence, such as:  The overall process is said to occur by consecutive steps.

08015.title: consensus property value
08015.definition: Property value derived from a collection of results.

10033.title: conservation
10033.definition: Set of operations necessary to preserve the examinational properties of an examination standard within stated limits.

14547.title: conservation biology
14547.definition: Science applied to the conservation of genes, populations, species, and ecosystems.

14548.title: conservation ecology
14548.definition: Science of analyzing and protecting the Earth’s biological diversity.

CT07012.title: conservation of orbital symmetry
CT07012.definition: The orbital symmetry control of concerted reactions; this requires transformation of the molecular orbitals of reactants into those of products to proceed continuously by following a reaction path along which the symmetry of these orbitals remains unchanged. Reactions which adhere to this requirement are classified as symmetry-allowed reactions, and those which do not as symmetry-forbidden reactions.

15591.title: conservative assessment of risk
15591.definition: Assessment of risk that assumes the worst possible case scenario and therefore gives the highest possible value for risk: Risk management decisions based on this value will maximize safety.

C01278.title: consignment
C01278.definition: A quantity of material transferred on one occasion and covered by a single set of shipping documents. It may consist of one or more lots or portions of lots. The presence of different lots in a consignment is important from the point of view of the sampling plan and the interpretation of the results of analysis. The term 'population' is used as the general term for the quantity of parent material being sampled when it is immaterial if the parent body is a consignment, lot, batch, entity, etc.

C01279.title: consistency
C01279.definition: A general term to describe the property of a material by which it resists permanent change of shape.

13038.title: constant gene
13038.definition: Gene that encodes the constant (C) region of immunoglobulin (Ig) chains or T-cell receptor (TCR) chains.

12753.title: constant oscillation-amplitude method
12753.definition: Forced-resonance method to determine the viscoelastic properties of a material.

13039.title: constant region
13039.definition: Part of an immunoglobulin (Ig) or T-cell receptor (TCR) that is relatively constant in amino acid sequence among different Ig or TCR molecules.

08322.title: constant time evolution
08322.definition: Segment of a pulse sequence in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that allows evolution of chemical shift during a fixed time period rather than through the traditional symmetrical incremented delays.

C01281.title: constituent
C01281.definition: Chemical species present in a system; often called a component, although the term component has a more restricted meaning in physical chemistry.

16269.title: constituent
16269.definition: Chemical species present in a system.

C01282.title: constitution
C01282.definition: The description of the identity and connectivity (and corresponding bond multiplicities) of the atoms in a molecular entity (omitting any distinction arising from their spatial arrangement).

C01283.title: constitutional heterogeneity
C01283.definition: The variation in constitution from molecule to molecule in polymers with molecules uniform with respect to elemental composition. An example is a polymer composed of linear and branched molecules; another example is a statistical copolymer comprising two isomeric constitutional units.

C01284.title: constitutional homosequence
C01284.definition: A constitutional sequence which contains constitutional units of only one species and in one sequential arrangement.

C01285.title: constitutional isomerism
C01285.definition: Isomerism between structures differing in constitution and described by different line formulae e.g. $\ce{CH3OCH3}$ and $\ce{CH3CH2OH}$ .

C01286.title: constitutional repeating unit
C01286.definition: The smallest constitutional unit the repetition of which constitutes a regular macromolecule, a regular oligomer molecule, a regular block or a regular chain.

C01287.title: constitutional sequence
C01287.definition: The whole or part of a chain comprising one or more species of constitutional unit(s) in defined sequence.

C01288.title: constitutional unit
C01288.definition: An atom or group of atoms (with pendant atoms or groups, if any) comprising a part of the essential structure of a macromolecule, an oligomer molecule, a block or a chain.

12638.title: constitutive activity
12638.definition: Receptor or enzymatic function displayed in the absence of an agonist or activator.

C01289.title: constitutive enzymes
C01289.definition: Enzymes which are produced constitutively by the cell under all physiological conditions. Therefore, they are not controlled by induction or repression.

15592.title: construct validity
15592.definition: Extent to which a measurement corresponds to theoretical concepts (constructs) concerning the phenomenon under study; for example, if on theoretical grounds, the phenomenon should change with age, a measurement with construct validity would reflect such a change.

13040.title: contact allergen
13040.definition: Substance that causes a skin hypersensitivity reaction by direct contact.

C01290.title: contact angle
C01290.definition: When a liquid does not spread on a substrate (usually a solid), a contact angle \(\left(\theta\right) \) is formed which is defined as the angle between two of the interfaces at the three-phase line of contact. It must always be stated which interfaces are used to define \(\theta\). It is often necessary to distinguish between the 'advancing contact angle' \((\theta _{\rm{a}}) \), the 'receding contact angle' \((\theta _{\rm{r}}) \) and the 'equilibrium contact angle' \((\theta _{\rm{e}}) \). When \((\theta _{\rm{r}}) \neq (\theta _{\rm{a}}) \) the system is said to exhibit contact angle hysteresis

C01291.title: contact corrosion
C01291.definition: The enhancement of the corrosion rate of the material with the more negative corrosion cell resulting from the contact between different electron-conducting phases.

13041.title: contact dermatitis
13041.definition: Skin inflammation that occurs when the skin’s surface comes in contact with a substance originating outside the body.

09459.title: contact hole
09459.definition: Hole in a layer of a semiconductor device enabling contact with an underlying semiconductor layer.

13042.title: contact hypersensitivity
13042.definition: Immune response following skin contact with an antigen.

15593.title: contact poison
15593.definition:
Chemical that injures the target organism through physical contact and skin absorption rather than through ingestion or inhalation.
Pesticide (herbicide) that causes injury to only the plant tissue to which it is applied or which is not appreciably translocated within plants.

C01293.title: contact potential difference
C01293.definition: The electric potential difference between one point in the vacuum close to the surface of M1 and another point in the vacuum close to the surface of M2, where M1 and M2 are two uncharged metals brought into contact.

13043.title: contact sensitivity
13043.definition: State of immunological sensitization in which an eczematous epidermal reaction may occur when a hapten is applied to the skin of a sensitized individual.

13044.title: contact urticaria
13044.definition: Urticaria provoked by contact with inducing agents.

15594.title: containment
15594.definition: Process by which possible release, discharge, or spill of a toxic substance during normal use or after an accident is prevented by appropriate action.

14549.title: contaminant
14549.definition:
Minor impurity present in a substance.
Extraneous material inadvertently added to a sample prior to or during chemical or biological analysis.
In some contexts, as in relation to gas cleaning equipment, used as a synonym for 'pollutant', especially on a small scale.
Unintended component in food that may pose a hazard to the consumer.
Any undesirable solid, liquid, or gaseous matter occurring, as a result of human activities, in a solid, liquid, or gaseous environmental medium, even without adverse effects being observed.

C01295.title: contamination
C01295.definition: Carry-over from a preceding sample probe into a following specimen cup, which will influence not just one result, but all assays on that specimen, or with that reagent.

15595.title: content validity
15595.definition: Extent to which the measurement incorporates the domain of the phenomenon under study; for example, a measurement of functional health status should embrace activities of daily living, occupational, family, and social functioning, etc.

10046.title: contingency table
10046.definition: Type of table in a matrix format that displays the multivariate frequency distribution of variables.

C01297.title: continuity inversion
C01297.definition: A change in the mutual dispersion of two phases in contact.

C01298.title: continuous analyser
C01298.definition: An analyser in which subassemblies operate continuously.

CT06916.title: continuous bed packing
CT06916.definition: A column packing, which is a single entity, rather than being composed of individual particles.

14550.title: continuous effect
14550.definition: Change that can be measured on a continuum from zero (or even a negative value) to positive values such as growth and reproduction.

14332.title: continuous emulsion polymerisation
14332.definition: Emulsion polymerization in which all the ingredients are added continuously and the product latex is removed continuously.

10169.title: continuous extraction
10169.definition: Extraction in which the sample is continuously introduced into the extraction device.

C01301.title: continuous flow enthalpimetry
C01301.definition: A term used to describe methods wherein a reagent is continuously fed into a flowing analyte stream and the temperature difference is measured before and after a reactor (mixing chamber). Alternatively, the temperature may be measured in a differential manner between a reference and a reactor chamber. The analyte concentration is directly proportional to the measured temperature difference. Synonymous with continuous flow enthalpimetric analysis.

C01302.title: continuous indication analyser
C01302.definition: An analysis with a permanent indication related to the sample concentration. To obtain a continuous indication, the sampling and measuring cell need to be continuous. A time lag may exist between sampling and indication of measured concentration.

10209.title: continuous liquid-liquid extraction
10209.definition: Extraction in which a water-immiscible extraction solvent is continuously percolated through an aqueous solution and returned to the extraction solvent reservoir.Apparatus for continuous liquid–liquid extraction with a lighter-than-water extraction solvent (left) and a heavier-than-water extraction solvent (right). In each case the extraction solvent is contained in the round bottom flask and the aqueous sample in the vertical glass column.

C01304.title: continuous measuring cell
C01304.definition: A measuring cell which operates continuously.

C01305.title: continuous operation
C01305.definition: The operation of an analytical instrument in such a way that no analytical procedure needs to be completed on any sample before the next procedure can be started.

11691.title: continuous performance test
11691.definition: Any of several available neuropsychological procedures that measure a person’s sustained attention.

C01306.title: continuous precipitation
C01306.definition: A diffusional reaction in a multi-component system in which atoms are transported to the growing nuclei by diffusion over relatively large distances in the parent phase and during which the mean composition of the parent phase changes continuously towards its equilibrium value. Synonymous with nucleation and growth.

08581.title: continuous scan interferometer
08581.definition: Interferometer in which the optical path difference is continually changed.

CT07348.title: continuous wave laser
CT07348.definition: CW operation of a laser means that the laser is continuously pumped and continuously emits electromagnetic radiation. The emission can occur in a single cavity mode or on multiple modes.

C01300.title: continuous-flow cell
C01300.definition: A cell which allows liquid (or gaseous) samples to pass through the cell continuously while absorption measurements are made.

14327.title: continuous-phase concentration
14327.definition: Concentration of species within the continuous phase of a dispersion.

11429.title: continuum
11429.definition: The computational representation of a solvent as a continuous medium instead of individual explicit solvent molecules.

08463.title: continuum source
08463.definition: Source that emits electromagnetic radiation with relatively constant intensity over a broad spectral region.

C01308.title: contour length
C01308.definition: The maximum end-to-end distance of a linear polymer chain. For a single-strand polymer molecule, this usually means the end-to-end distance of the chain extended to the all-transconformation. For chains with complex structure, only an approximate value of the contour length may be accessible. The sum of the lengths of all skeletal bonds of a single-strand polymer molecule is occasionally termed 'contour length'. This use of this term is discouraged.

10557.title: contraceptive
10557.definition: Anything that prevents, or reduces the likelihood of pregnancy.

12639.title: contract research organisation
12639.definition: Commercial organisation that can be engaged to undertake specifically defined chemical, biological, safety, or clinical studies.

11692.title: contracture
11692.definition: Persistent shortening and tightening of muscle, tendon, or other tissue.

15596.title: contraindication
15596.definition: Any condition that renders some particular line of treatment improper or undesirable.

09460.title: contrast
09460.definition: Maximum of the absolute value of the gradient of a contrast curve taken as a measure of the ability of a resist to differentiate the regions that have been exposed to radiation from those that have not.

09461.title: contrast curve
09461.definition: Plot of the fraction of the original thickness that remains after the development of a uniformly irradiated resist versus the logarithm of the incident exposure dose.

11693.title: contrast medium
11693.definition: Any material (usually opaque to X-rays) employed to delineate or define a structure during a radiologic procedure.

C01309.title: contributing structure
C01309.definition: The definition is based on the valence-bond formulation of the quantum mechanical idea of the wavefunction of a molecule as composed of a linear combination of wavefunctions, each representative of a formula containing bonds that are only single, double or triple with a particular pairing of electron spins. Each such formula represents a contributing structure, also called 'resonance structure' to the total wavefunction, and the degree to which each contributes is indicated by the square of its coefficient in the linear combination. The contributing structures, also called 'canonical forms', themselves thus have a purely formal significance: they are the components from which wavefunctions can be built. Structures may be covalent (or non-polar) or ionic (or polar). The representation is frequently kept qualitative so that we speak of important or major contributing structures and minor contributing structures.

14551.title: control
14551.definition: Treatment in a toxicity test that duplicates all the conditions of the exposure treatments but contains no test material, in order to determine the absence of toxicity under basic test conditions (e.g., health of test organisms, quality of dilution water).

08068.title: control chart
08068.definition: Chart with control limits on which some statistical measure related to a series of samples is plotted in a particular order to steer the process with respect to that measure.

15597.title: control group
15597.definition: Selected subjects of study, identified as a rule before a study is done, which comprises humans, animals, or other species who do not have the disease, intervention, procedure, or whatever is being studied, but in all other respects are as nearly identical to the test group as possible.

08069.title: control limit
08069.definition: Value defining an intended level of stability for a process.

C01311.title: control material
C01311.definition: A material to be used for the assessment of the performance of an analytical procedure or part thereof.

C01312.title: control sample
C01312.definition: The test portion or test solution used for assessment of the performance of an analytical procedure.

08979.title: controlled anionic polymerization
08979.definition: Term indicating control of a certain kinetic feature of an anionic polymerization or structural aspect of the polymer molecules formed by anionic polymerization, or both.

C01310.title: controlled atmosphere
C01310.definition: A synthetic gaseous sample of pure air which may contain carefully determined amounts of certain contaminants; this may be used as a standard for the calibration of analytical techniques, as a simulated environment for the study of biological responses, or for other purposes.

08985.title: controlled cationic polymerization
08985.definition: Term indicating control of a certain kinetic feature of a cationic polymerization or structural aspect of the polymer molecules formed by cationic polymerization, or both.

08973.title: controlled ionic polymerization
08973.definition: Term indicating control of a certain kinetic feature of an ionic polymerization or structural aspect of the polymer molecules formed by ionic polymerization, or both.

08908.title: controlled polymerization
08908.definition: Term indicating control of a certain kinetic feature of a polymerization or structural aspect of the polymer molecules formed, or both.

08913.title: controlled radical polymerization
08913.definition: Term indicating control of a certain kinetic feature of a radical polymerization or structural aspect of the polymer molecules formed by radical polymerization, or both.

11539.title: controlled release
11539.definition: Detection principle for a chemically modified electrode (CME) in which an analyte or reagent accumulated at a CME undergoes quantitative release (egress, stripping, expulsion, or microdosing) to the test solution, under electrochemical or chemical control.

12286.title: controlled temperature program
12286.definition: Temperature history imposed on the sample during the course of the thermal analysis experiment.

12285.title: controlled-rate thermal analysis
12285.definition: Sample-controlled method where the feedback used to control the heating is the rate of transformation.

15163.title: controlled-release dosage form
15163.definition: Medication, which due to its special technological construction provides for drug release having predefined kinetics (zero order, \(t^{1/2}\), first order, etc.) at a sufficient rate to maintain the desired therapeutic level over an extended period of time.

C01313.title: convection
C01313.definition: Vertical motion of the air induced by the expansion of the air heated by the earth's surface and its resulting buoyancy.

C01314.title: convenience sample
C01314.definition: A sample chosen on the basis of accessibility, expediency, cost, efficiency or other reason not directly concerned with sampling parameters.

13045.title: conventional dendritic cell
13045.definition: Predominant type of dendritic cell active in antigen presentation to and activation of naïve T cells.

09039.title: conventional mass
09039.definition: Mass of a body that is balanced by a standard mass under conventionally chosen conditions.

10002.title: conventional nominal property value
10002.definition: Nominal property value attributed by agreement to a nominal property for a given purpose.

08016.title: conventional quantity value
08016.definition: Quantity value attributed by agreement to a quantity for a given purpose.

C01316.title: conventional true value
C01316.definition: Value attributed to a particular quantity and accepted, sometimes by convention, as having an uncertainty appropriate for a given purpose. Examples are the CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants.

13046.title: convergent evolution
13046.definition: Independent evolution of similarity between molecules or between species.

CT07349.title: conversion cross-section
CT07349.definition: Product of the quantum yield by the absorption cross-section, \(\sigma \ \varPhi \). SI unit is \(\pu{m2}\); commonly expressed in \(\pu{cm2}\).

C01317.title: conversion electron
C01317.definition: Electron ejected from the atom in the process of internal conversion.

C01319.title: conversion spectrum
C01319.definition: A plot of a quantity related to the absorption (absorbance, cross section, etc.) multiplied by the quantum yield for the considered process against a suitable measure of photon energy, such as frequency, \(\nu \), wavenumber, \(\sigma \), or wavelength, \(\lambda \), e.g. the conversion cross section, \(\sigma \varphi \), has the SI unit \(\mathrm{m}^{2}\).

13047.title: convertase
13047.definition: Enzyme activity that converts complement protein into its reactive form by cleaving it.

CT06937.title: convex isotherm
CT06937.definition: Distribution isotherm, the slope of which is continuously decreasing.

10558.title: convulsion
10558.definition: Sudden, violent, irregular movement of the body caused by involuntary contraction of muscles and associated with brain disorders, such as epilepsy, fever in children, or with drug or alcohol abuse.

12287.title: cooling curve
12287.definition: Experimental result of measuring the temperature of the sample as a function of time during cooling. Heating curves are obtained for temperature-time experiments during heating.

13048.title: Coombs test
13048.definition: Diagnostic test using anti-immunoglobulin (Ig) to agglutinate antibody-coated erythrocytes.

C01324.title: cooperative transition
C01324.definition: A transition that involves a simultaneous, collective displacement or change of state of the atoms and/or electrons in the entire system. Examples: An order–disorder transition of atoms or electrons, as in an alloy, a ferromagnet or superconductor; a Jahn–Teller or ferroic transition; a martensitic transition.

C01325.title: cooperativity
C01325.definition: Interaction between the substrate binding sites of an allosteric enzymes. Binding of a substrate molecule to one binding site changes the affinity of the binding sites on the other subunits (cf. allosteric enzymes) to the substrate by induction of a conformation change at the other binding sites. Cooperative enzymes typically display a sigmoid (S-shaped) plot of the reaction rate against substrate concentration.

C01329.title: coordination
C01329.definition: The formation of a covalent bond, the two shared electrons of which have come from only one of the two parts of the molecular entity linked by it, as in the reaction of a Lewis acid and a Lewis base to form a Lewis adduct; alternatively, the bonding formed in this way. In the former sense, it is the reverse of unimolecular heterolysis. 'Coordinate covalence' and 'coordinate link' are synonymous (obsolescent) terms. The synonym 'dative bond' is obsolete. (The origin of the bonding electrons has by itself no bearing on the character of the bond formed. Thus, the formation of methyl chloride from a methyl cation and a chloride ion involves coordination; the resultant bond obviously differs in no way from the $\ce{C–Cl}$ bond in methyl chloride formed by any other path, e.g. by colligation of a methyl radical and a chlorine atom.) The term is also used to describe the number of ligands around a central atom without necessarily implying two-electron bonds.

C01330.title: coordination entity
C01330.definition: An assembly consisting of a central atom (usually metallic) to which is attached a surrounding array of other groups of atoms (ligands).

12823.title: coordination network
12823.definition: A coordination compound extending, through repeating coordination entities, in one dimension, but with cross-links between two or more individual chains, loops, or spiro-links, or a coordination compound extending through repeating coordination entities in two or three dimensions.

C01331.title: coordination number
C01331.definition: The coordination number of a specified atom in a chemical species is the number of other atoms directly linked to that specified atom. For example, the coordination number of carbon in methane is four, and it is five in protonated methane, $\ce{CH5^{+}$. (The term is used in a different sense in the crystallographic description of ionic crystals.)

C01332.title: coordination polyhedron
C01332.definition: In a coordination entity, the solid figure defined by the positions of the ligand atoms directly attached to the central atom.

12822.title: coordination polymer
12822.definition: A coordination compound with repeating coordination entities extending in 1, 2, or 3 dimensions.

08995.title: coordination polymerization
08995.definition: Chain polymerization that involves the preliminary coordination of a monomer molecule with a chain carrier.

09000.title: coordination ring-opening polymerization
09000.definition: Coordination polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

08996.title: coordination-addition polymerization
08996.definition: Coordination polymerization of \(\ce{\upalpha\!,\!\upbeta\mbox{-}unsaturated}\) amides or esters that proceeds by sequential monomer coordination and Michael addition events.

08997.title: coordination-insertion polymerization
08997.definition: Coordination polymerization of olefins that proceeds by insertion of the olefin into a metal–carbon bond

09003.title: coordinative chain-transfer polymerization
09003.definition: Coordination polymerization in which a propagating chain is able to transfer reversibly between the catalyst and a chain-transfer agent, thereby converting the active species into a dormant species.

C01333.title: coordinatively saturated complex
C01333.definition: A transition metal complex that has formally 18 outer shell electrons at the central metal atom.

C01334.title: coordinatively unsaturated complex
C01334.definition: A transition metal complex that possesses fewer ligands than exist in the coordinatively saturated complex. These complexes usually have fewer than 18 outer shell electrons at the central metal atom.

08070.title: coordinator of an interlaboratory comparison
08070.definition: Person(s) with responsibility for organizing and managing all of the activities involved in the operation of an interlaboratory comparison.

14552.title: cooxidation
14552.definition: Cometabolism whereby growing microorganisms oxidize a compound without using either carbon or energy derived from the oxidation of that compound.

14553.title: copepod
14553.definition: Minute marine or freshwater crustacean, usually having six pairs of limbs on the thorax; some are abundant in plankton and others are parasitic on fish, marine mammals, and macro-invertebrates.

C01335.title: copolymer
C01335.definition: A polymer derived from more than one species of monomer.

C01337.title: copolymer micelle
C01337.definition: A micelle formed by one or more block or graft copolymer molecules in a selective solvent.

C01336.title: copolymerization
C01336.definition: Polymerization in which a copolymer is formed.

15391.title: copolymerisation composition equation
15391.definition: Equation relating the instantaneous composition of a binary copolymer to the monomer reactivity ratios and the ratio of instantaneous monomer concentrations.

C01338.title: copper vapour laser
C01338.definition: A pulsed source of coherent radiation emitting at \(578.2\ \rm{nm}\) and \(510.5\ \rm{nm}\) from excited copper atoms.

C01339.title: coprecipitation
C01339.definition: The simultaneous precipitation of a normally soluble component with a macro-component from the same solution by the formation of mixed crystals, by adsorption, occlusion or mechanical entrapment.

C01340.title: copy number
C01340.definition: The number of copies of a plasmid or a gene within a cell.

09642.title: cord blood
09642.definition: Blood contained in the vessels of the umbilical cord at the time of birth.

C01341.title: core atom
C01341.definition: The primary reference atom in a mechanistic change; usually either of the two atoms of a transformed multiple bond or the single atom at which substitution occurs.

10090.title: core consistency diagnostic
10090.definition: Method to assess the appropriateness of a PARAFAC model.

15599.title: core grade
15599.definition: Quality rating, based on standard evaluation criteria established by the U.S. Office of Pesticide Programs regulatory agencies, given to toxicological studies after submission by registrants.

09836.title: core oligosaccharide
09836.definition: Intermediate structural region between the O-polysaccharide and lipid A moiety of lipopolysaccharides (LPS).

09603.title: core unit
09603.definition: Constitutional unit in a dendrimer molecule, from which the dendron(s) emanate(s).

13805.title: core-crosslinked micelle
13805.definition: Core-shell structure formed by self-assembly of amphiphiles and subsequently covalently crosslinked through functionalities in the core.

14299.title: core-shell particle
14299.definition: Polymer particle comprising at least two phase domains, one of which (the core) lies within the other(s) that form the polymeric outer layer(s) (the shell(s)).

13806.title: core-shell structure
13806.definition: Molecular entity of spherical, elliptical, or cylindrical symmetry in which the constitution of the interior, the core, differs from that of the external surface, the shell.

13049.title: coreceptor
13049.definition: Cell surface protein receptor that recognizes a substance bound to a primary receptor, and binds to a signaling molecule that thereby enhances the activity of another receptor.

08582.title: Coriolis coupling
08582.definition: Coupling between rotational and vibrational molecular motion caused by Coriolis forces.

08583.title: Coriolis force
08583.definition: In vibrational theory, the motion of a polyatomic molecule is usually initially regarded as the independent superposition of a rotation and a vibration, with the vibration considered in a coordinate system that rotates with the molecule. This initial treatment must be corrected for centrifugal forces and for Coriolis forces. The Coriolis force on an atom is given by \(F_{\rm{Coriolis}} = 2m v_{\rm{a}} \omega \sin \varphi\), where \(m\) is the mass of the atom, \(v_{\rm{a}}\) is its apparent velocity in the rotating coordinate system, \(\omega\) is the angular velocity of the coordinate system, and \(\varphi\) is the angle between the velocity vector and the axis of rotation.

11695.title: coronal
11695.definition: Vertical (longitudinal) plane dividing the body into ventral and dorsal (front and back) sections.

11696.title: coronal suture
11696.definition: Transverse junction in the skull separating the frontal bone from the parietal bones.

11697.title: corpus callosum
11697.definition: Bundle of myelin-enriched neural fibers beneath the cortex connecting the two hemispheres of the brain.

10559.title: corpus cavernosum
10559.definition: Either of the two columns of erectile tissue forming the body of the clitoris (corpus cavernosum clitoridis) or penis (corpus cavernosum penis).

10560.title: corpus luteum
10560.definition: Glandular mass of yellowish tissue in the ovary, formed by a Graafian ovarian follicle that has matured and released its oocyte.

11698.title: corpus striatum
11698.definition: Striatum together with the globus pallidus.

C01343.title: corrected emission spectrum
C01343.definition: Obtained after correcting for instrumental and sample effects and usually represented by a graph of \(\mathit{\Phi} _{\lambda}\) against wavelength, where \(\mathit{\Phi} _{\lambda}\) is the spectral (radiant) energy flux.

C01344.title: corrected excitation spectrum
C01344.definition: Obtained if the photon flux incident on the sample is held constant. If the solution is sufficiently dilute that the fraction of the exciting radiation absorbed is proportional to the absorption coefficient of the analyte, and if the quantum yield is independent of the exciting wavelength, the corrected excitation spectrum will be identical in shape to the absorption spectrum.

C01345.title: corrected retention volume
C01345.definition: The corrected retention volume, \(V_{\rm{R}}^{0}\), is given by \[V_{\rm{R}}^{0}=j\ V_{\rm{R}}\] where \(j\) is the pressure gradient correction factor for a homogeneously filled column of constant diameter and \(V_{\rm{R}}\) is the retention volume. This quantity is of limited use because it is influenced by the volumes of the sample injector and detector, as well as the interstitial volume of the column.

C01346.title: correlation analysis
C01346.definition: The use of empirical correlations relating one body of experimental data to another, with the objective of finding quantitative estimates of the factors underlying the phenomena involved. Correlation analysis in organic chemistry often uses linear free-energy relations for rates or equilibria of reactions, but the term also embraces similar analysis of physical (most commonly spectroscopic) properties and of biological activity.

C01347.title: correlation coefficient

C01348.title: correlation diagram
C01348.definition: A diagram which shows the relative energies of orbitals, configurations, valence bond structures, or states of reactants and products of a reaction, as a function of the molecular geometry, or another suitable parameter. An example involves the interpolation between the energies obtained for the united atoms and the values for the separated atoms limits.

C01349.title: correlation energy
C01349.definition: The difference between the Hartree–Fock energy calculated for a system and the exact non-relativistic energy of that system. The correlation energy arises from the approximate representation of the electron-electron repulsions in the Hartree–Fock method.

08323.title: correlation spectroscopy
08323.definition: Homonuclear two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy correlation experiment showing cross peaks representing spin-spin coupling between pairs of nuclei.

08324.title: correlation spectroscopy through long-range coupling
08324.definition: Heteronuclear (typically \(\ce{^{13}C}\)) detected long range 2D correlation experiment in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that has mostly been superseded by heteronuclear multiple bond correlation (HMBC) experiments and its variants.

08325.title: correlation time
08325.definition: Parameter related to the mean time during which a molecule maintains its spatial geometry.

10091.title: correspondence factor analysis
10091.definition: Factor analysis applied to categorical data in which orthogonal factors are obtained from a contingency table.

C01350.title: corrinoids
C01350.definition: Derivatives of the corrin nucleus, which contains four reduced or partly reduced pyrrole rings joined in a macrocycle by three  groups and one direct carbon–carbon bond linking $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ positions.

C01351.title: corrosion
C01351.definition: An irreversible interfacial reaction of a material (metal, ceramic, polymer) with its environment which results in consumption of the material or in dissolution into the material of a component of the environment. Often, but not necessarily, corrosion results in effects detrimental to the usage of the material considered. Exclusively physical or mechanical processes such as melting or evaporation, abrasion or mechanical fracture are not included in the term corrosion.

C01352.title: corrosion cell
C01352.definition: A galvanic cell resulting from inhomogeneities in the material or in its environment.

C01357.title: corrosion potential
C01357.definition: The electrode potential spontaneously acquired by a corroding material in a particular environment.

C01358.title: corrosion rate
C01358.definition:
The amount of substance transferred per unit time at a specified surface. Using Faraday's law, the corrosion rate, \(
u_{\mathrm{cor}}\), can be formally expressed as an electric current which at the corrosion potential is called the corrosion current, \(I_{\mathrm{cor}}\), e.g. for the anodic dissolution of one component of a material with \(
u_{\mathrm{cor}}\) in \(\pu{mol s-1}\) and \(I_{\mathrm{cor}}\) in \(\mathrm{A}\) one obtains \(I_{\mathrm{cor}}=n\ F\ 
u_{\mathrm{cor}}\), \(n\) being the charge number of the electrode reaction and \(F\) the Faraday constant.

14554.title: corrosive
14554.definition:
n. Substance having the capability or tendency to cause slow destruction.
adj. Gradually destructive; steadily harmful.

10561.title: cortex
10561.definition: Outer layer of an organ such as the kidney, the cerebellum, or the adrenal gland.

13050.title: corticosteroid
13050.definition: Any of the family of steroid molecules that are produced in the adrenal cortex, or their synthetic analogs.

14556.title: cost-effectiveness analysis
14556.definition: Procedure for determining whether the expected beneficial effects of a defined course of action justify the cost when selecting among competing options for the use of limited resources.

14555.title: cost–benefit analysis
14555.definition: Procedure for determining the relationship of the expected benefits of a proposed action to the expected costs in order to decide whether the action provides the best option for the investment of limited resources.

C01364.title: cotectic
C01364.definition: The conditions of pressure, temperature and composition under which two or more solid phases crystallize at the same time from a single liquid over a finite range of decreasing temperature.

09069.title: Cottrell equation
09069.definition: Equation for diffusion current \(I_{\rm{d}}\) at time \(t\) at a large planar electrode in contact with a semi-infinite layer of unstirred solution containing excess supporting (inert) electrolyte and an electroactive substance of bulk concentration \(c\) when, at the instant \(t = 0\), the potential of the electrode is suddenly changed to a value at which a mass-transport limited electrochemical reaction occurs and the concentration of the electroactive species at the electrode is zero, \[I_{\rm{d}} = zFA{D^{1/2}}c/(\pi^{1/2} t^{1/2})\] where \(z\) is the electron number of an electrochemical reaction in the charge transfer step of the species (being positive for an oxidation and negative for a reduction), \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(A\) the electrode surface area, and \(D\) the diffusion coefficient of the electroactive substance.

14557.title: cough
14557.definition: Abrupt, periodic reversal of water flow over the gills that dislodges and eliminates excess mucus from the gills’ surfaces.

C01365.title: coulomb
C01365.definition: SI derived unit of electric charge, \(\rm{C} = \rm{A}\cdot \rm{s}\).

C01366.title: coulomb integral
C01366.definition: Integral over space of the type \(\int \psi _{r}\ast \ \hat{H}\ \psi _{r}\ \rm{d}\tau \) where \(\hat{H}\) is the hamiltonian operator containing electrostatic potential energy terms and \(\psi \) is a one-electron wavefunction.

08787.title: coulomb radius
08787.definition: Distance between two oppositely charged charge carriers at which the energy of their Coulombic attraction is equal to \(kT\), where \(k\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(T\) the absolute temperature.

CT07013.title: Coulomb repulsion
CT07013.definition: The potential energy component corresponding to the electrostatic interaction between each pair of charged particles: \[V=\frac{1}{4\: \pi\: \varepsilon_{0}}\ \sum _{i}\sum _{j \lt i}e_{i}\ e_{j}\ \Delta r_{ij}\] where \(\varepsilon _{0}\) is the permittivity of a vacuum, \(\Delta r_{ij}\) is the distance between the two particles, and \(e_{i}\) and \(e_{j}\) are the charges on particles \(i\) and \(j\). In molecular orbital theory, the electrostatic repulsion between the two electrons occupying the orbitals \(\Psi _{i}\) and \(\Psi _{j}\). In the Hartree–Fock method, the mean Coulomb repulsion is determined by the value of the coulomb integral \[J_{ij}=\int \int \Psi _{i\rm{*}}\left(\mathbf{r}_{1}\right)\ \Psi _{i}\left(\mathbf{r}_{1}\right)\ \left(\frac{e^{2}}{r_{12}}\right)\ \Psi _{j\rm{*}}\left(\mathbf{r}_{2}\right)\ \Psi _{j}\left(\mathbf{r}_{2}\right)  \ \mathrm{d}\mathbf{r}_{1} \ \mathrm{d}\mathbf{r}_{2} = \lt ij|ij \gt\]

09157.title: coulometer
09157.definition: Measuring instrument to obtain the electrical charge passed in an experiment, or to produce a known amount of substance in a titration.

C01367.title: coulometric detection method
C01367.definition: A detection method in which the current is directly proportional to the flow rate of the substance involved in the electrochemical reaction, and the amount of charge which flows is proportional to the amount of substances taking part in the reaction.

09159.title: coulometry
09159.definition: Electrochemical measurement principle in which the electric charge required to carry out a known electrochemical reaction is measured. By Faraday’s laws of electrolysis, the amount of substance is proportional to the charge.

C01369.title: coumarins
C01369.definition: 2H-Chromen-2-one (older name 1,2-benzopyrone), trivially named coumarin, and its derivatives formed by substitution.

15246.title: coumarone-indene polymer
15246.definition: Polymer prepared from a mixture containing 1-benzofuran (formerly coumarone) and indene.

C01370.title: count
C01370.definition: 1. Information corresponding to a pulse processed for counting.2. Number of pulses recorded during a measurement.

15600.title: count mean diameter
15600.definition: Mean of the diameters of all particles in a population.

15601.title: count median diameter
15601.definition: Calculated diameter in a population of particles in a gas or liquid phase above which there are as many particles with larger diameters as there are particles below it with smaller diameters.

C01373.title: counter tube
C01373.definition: Radiation detector consisting of a gas-filled tube or valve whose gas amplification is much greater than one, and in which the individual ionizing events give rise to discrete electrical pulses. Often an expression is added indicating the geometry (e.g. end window), composition of the gas (e.g. helium) or the physical process for its operation (e.g. proton recoil, fission).

CT06864.title: counter-current flow
CT06864.definition: Flow through a membrane module in which the fluids on the upstream and downstream sides of the membrane move parallel to the membrane surface but in opposite directions.

13052.title: counter-regulation hypothesis
13052.definition: Hypothesis that all types of infection early in childhood may protect against the development of atopy by driving the production of cytokines such as interleukin-10 (IL-10) and transforming growth factor $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ ($\ce{TGF\mbox{-}\upbeta\!}$), which downregulate both Th1 and Th2 responses.

14124.title: counter-screen
14124.definition: Screen in which test samples are assessed against a target for unwanted activity.

09887.title: countercurrent chromatography
09887.definition: Partition chromatography which uses two immiscible liquid phases and no solid support. One liquid acts as the stationary phase and the other as the mobile phase.

10170.title: countercurrent extraction
10170.definition: Extraction in which both phases are continuously added (or changed) and flow (or move) in opposite directions as the extraction progresses.

11430.title: counterpoise correction
11430.definition: A method to correct for basis set superposition error.

C01377.title: counting efficiency
C01377.definition: The ratio between the number of particles or photons counted with a radiation counter and the number of particles or photons of the same type and energy emitted by the radiation source.

C01378.title: counting loss
C01378.definition: A reduction of the counting rate resulting from phenomena such as the resolving time or the dead time.

C01379.title: counting rate
C01379.definition: The number of counts occuring in unit time.

C01380.title: coupled reaction
C01380.definition: A reaction which follows the (slower) reaction of kinetic interest, so as to provide means of monitoring the formation of a reaction product. This reaction is sometimes referred to as the indicator reaction.

CT07014.title: coupled cluster method
CT07014.definition: A method employed in ab initio quantum mechanical calculations providing for a higher-level treatment of electron correlation beyond MP4.

C01381.title: coupled simultaneous techniques
C01381.definition: The application of two or more techniques to the same sample when the two instruments involved are connected through an interface, e.g. simultaneous thermal analysis and mass spectrometry.

C01383.title: coupling constant
C01383.definition: A quantitative measure for nuclear spin-spin, nuclear-electron (hyperfine coupling) and electron-electron (fine coupling in EPR) coupling in magnetic resonance spectroscopy. The 'indirect' or scalar NMR coupling constants are in a first approximation independent of the external magnetic field and are expressed in \(\mathrm{Hz}\).

15392.title: coupling reaction
15392.definition: Linking of two macromolecules through chemical reaction.

C01384.title: covalent bond
C01384.definition: A region of relatively high electron density between nuclei which arises at least partly from sharing of electrons and gives rise to an attractive force and characteristic internuclear distance.

12640.title: covalent drug
12640.definition: Ligand that binds irreversibly to its molecular target through the formation of a new chemical bond.

C01386.title: Cox–Yates equation
C01386.definition: A modification of the Bunnett–Olsen equation of the form: \[\log_{10}(\frac{[\ce{SH^{+}}]}{[\ce{S}]}) - \log_{10}[\ce{H^{+}}] = m^{*}X + \pu{p}K_{\ce{SH}^{+}}\] is the activity function \[\log_{10}(\frac{\gamma_{\rm{S}}\ \gamma_{\rm{H}^{+}}}{\gamma_{\rm{SH}^{+}}})\] for an arbitrary reference base. The function \(X\) is called the excess acidity because it gives a measure of the difference between the acidity of a solution and that of an ideal solution of the same concentration. In practice \[X = -(\rm{H}_{0} + \log_{10}[\rm{H}^{+}])\] and \[m^{*} = 1 - \mathit{\Phi}\]

C01387.title: cracking
C01387.definition: The thermal or catalytic decomposition of a compound such as a hydrocarbon into chemical species of smaller molecular weight.

10210.title: Craig countercurrent distribution apparatus
10210.definition: Apparatus for extraction based on a multistage countercurrent distribution.

11699.title: cramp
11699.definition: Painful muscle spasm caused by prolonged tetanic contraction.

11700.title: cranial nerve
11700.definition: Each of 12 pairs of nerves that arise directly from the brain, not from the spinal cord, and pass through separate apertures in the skull.

10563.title: cranial placodes
10563.definition: Thickenings in the surface ectoderm of the embryo associated with future eye and ear regions.

10564.title: cranial suture
10564.definition: Line where the bony plates of the skull are joined together by fibrous bands of tissue, easily felt in the newborn before closure by ossification.

10565.title: craniofacial
10565.definition: Pertaining to the cranium and the face.

11701.title: craniopharyngioma
11701.definition: Congenital tumor arising from the pituitary gland in the embryonic tissue between the brain and pharynx.

10566.title: craniorachischisis
10566.definition: Neural tube defect in which both the cranium and vertebral column remain open.

10567.title: cranioschisis
10567.definition: Developmental failure of the cranial sutures to close completely, especially at the occiput, usually leading to grossly defective development of the brain.

10568.title: craniosynostosis
10568.definition: Premature closure of the cranial sutures.

10569.title: cranium
10569.definition: Bony structure surrounding the brain, excluding the bones of the face.

09240.title: crater depth
09240.definition: Average depth of the region of a crater from which the measured signal is derived.

CT06850.title: crazing
CT06850.definition: Formation of cavities, when a polymer is stressed, which contain load-bearing fibrils spanning the gap between the surfaces of each cavity.

10570.title: Cre/loxP
10570.definition: Bacterial system in which the Cre protein mediates DNA recombination between specific DNA sequences known as lox-P sites.

C01388.title: cream
C01388.definition: A highly concentrated emulsion formed by creaming of a dilute emulsion.

C01390.title: cream volume
C01390.definition: The volume of cream formed in an emulsion.

C01389.title: creaming
C01389.definition: The macroscopic separation of a dilute emulsion into a highly concentrated emulsion, in which interglobular contact is important, and a continuous phase under the action of gravity or a centrifugal field. This separation usually occurs upward, but the term may still be applied if the relative densities of the dispersed and continuous phases are such that the concentrated emulsion settles downward.

CT07546.title: creep
CT07546.definition: Time-dependent change of the dimensions of a material under a constant load.

15602.title: crepitations
15602.definition: Abnormal respiratory sounds heard on auscultation of the chest, produced by passage of air through passages which contain secretion or exudate or which are constricted by spasm or a thickening of their walls.

C01391.title: cresols
C01391.definition: The monomethylphenols and their derivatives formed by substitution on the ring with substituents other than $\ce{–OH}$.

10571.title: cretinism
10571.definition: Developmental disorder caused by deficiency of thyroid hormone, characterized by severe mental retardation and stunted physical growth, sometimes resulting from maternal iodine deficiency.

10572.title: cri du chat syndrome
10572.definition: Hereditary congenital syndrome due to deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5.

10573.title: crista
10573.definition: One of the inward projections or folds of the inner membrane of a mitochondrion.

15603.title: criterion
15603.definition: Validated set of data used as a basis for judgment.

15604.title: criterion validity
15604.definition: Extent to which the measurement correlates with an external criterion of the phenomenon under study.

08584.title: critical angle
08584.definition: Smallest angle of incidence at which total internal reflection occurs.

14558.title: critical body residue
14558.definition: Whole-body concentration of a chemical that is associated with a given adverse biological response.

14381.title: critical coagulation concentration
14381.definition: Minimum concentration of electrolyte at and above which rapid coagulation occurs.

15605.title: critical concentration
15605.definition: Concentration of a substance at and above which adverse functional changes, reversible or irreversible, occur in a cell or an organ.

09462.title: critical dimension
09462.definition: Length of the smallest geometrical features that can be formed in a lithographic process.

15606.title: critical dose
15606.definition: Dose of a substance at and above which adverse functional changes, reversible or irreversible, occur in a cell or an organ.

15607.title: critical effect
15607.definition: For deterministic effects, the first adverse effect that appears when the threshold (critical) concentration or dose is reached in the critical organ: Adverse effects with no defined threshold concentration are regarded as critical.

15608.title: critical end-point
15608.definition: Toxic effect used by the USEPA as the basis for a reference dose.

C01393.title: critical energy
C01393.definition: A chemical reaction cannot occur, except by quantum-mechanical tunnelling unless the total energy available is greater than a certain energy, which is known as the critical energy, or the threshold energy.

C01394.title: critical excitation energy
C01394.definition: Minimum energy to excite a specific analytical signal. The term is most frequently used in connection with the generation of X-ray spectra, designating the ionization (binding) energy of the orbital on which the transition ends.

15609.title: critical group
15609.definition: Part of a target population most in need of protection because it is most susceptible to a given toxicant.

15322.title: critical index
15322.definition: Index in the basic equation describing a coexistence curve \[\beta = \lim \limits_{T \to T_{\rm{c}}} \left(\frac{\partial \ln (x'' - x')}{\partial \ln \vert T - T_{\rm{c}}\vert} \right)\] where \(x''\), \(x'\) are the mole fractions of one component in the respective concentrated and dilute phases and \(T_{\rm{c}}\) is the critical solution temperature.

CT07202.title: critical ion-concentration in an ionomer
CT07202.definition: Concentration of ionic groups in an ionomer matrix above which ionic aggregation occurs.

14559.title: critical life-stage testing
14559.definition: Toxicity testing focused on the species life stage thought to be the most sensitive to the toxicant, such as newly hatched individuals.

C01395.title: critical micelle concentration
C01395.definition: There is a relatively small range of concentrations separating the limit below which virtually no micelle are detected and the limit above which virtually all additional surfactant molecules form micelles. Many properties of surfactant solutions, if plotted against the concentration, appear to change at a different rate above and below this range. By extrapolating the loci of such a property above and below this range until they intersect, a value may be obtained known as the critical micellization concentration (critical micelle concentration), symbol \(c_{\rm{M}}\), abbreviation cmc (or c.m.c.). As values obtained using different properties are not quite identical, the method by which the cmc is determined should be clearly stated.

15164.title: critical moisture content
15164.definition: A stage in the drying of solids, above which the drying rate (derived from the plot of the loss of moisture content against time) is linear, at which the drying rate ceases to be linear, until it reaches the equilibrium moisture content.

14357.title: critical oligomer degree of polymerisation for irreversible entry
14357.definition: Lowest degree of polymerization of aqueous-phase oligomer-radicals needed for irreversible capture by colloidal particles, micelles, or both during a polymerization.

14358.title: critical oligomer degree of polymerisation for precipitation
14358.definition: Lowest degree of polymerization of oligomer-radicals that precipitate from the continuous phase during a polymerization.

15610.title: critical organ
15610.definition: Organ that first attains the critical concentration of a substance and exhibits the critical effect under specified circumstances of exposure and for a given population.

15611.title: critical organ concentration
15611.definition: Mean concentration of a substance in the critical organ at the time the substance reaches its critical concentration in the most sensitive type of cell in the organ.

10574.title: critical period
10574.definition: Specific time in the development of a biological system when it is particularly vulnerable to injury or misdirection.

C01396.title: critical point
C01396.definition: The temperature and pressure at which the liquid and vapour intensive properties (density, heat capacity, etc.) become equal. It is the highest temperature (critical temperature) and pressure (critical pressure) at which both a gaseous and a liquid phase of a given compound can coexist.

C01397.title: critical pressure
C01397.definition: The minimum pressure which would suffice to liquefy a substance at its critical temperature. Above the critical pressure, increasing the temperature will not cause a fluid to vaporize to give a two-phase system.

C01400.title: critical solution point
C01400.definition: The point, with coordinates critical solution temperatures and critical composition, on a temperature-composition phase diagram at which the distinction between co-existent phases vanishes. In solid-solid, solid-liquid and liquid-liquid systems both upper and lower critical solution temperatures and corresponding 'critical solution compositions' can occur. Synonymous with consolute point.

CT06820.title: critical study
CT06820.definition: Investigation yielding the no observed adverse effect level that is used by the USEPA as the basis of the reference dose.

C01402.title: critical temperature
C01402.definition: That temperature, characteristic of each gas, above which it is not possible to liquefy a given gas.

C01403.title: critical thickness of a film
C01403.definition: A film often thins gradually to a thickness at which it either ruptures or converts abruptly to an equilibrium film. This thickness is sometimes well enough defined statistically to be considered a critical thickness, \(t_{\rm{c}}\) or \(h_{\rm{c}}\).

08017.title: critical value
08017.definition: Measured quantity value for a quantity of a component in a material, above which the component is declared to be present.

13053.title: Crohn disease
13053.definition: Chronic inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) thought to result from an abnormal overresponsiveness to commensal gut flora.

08327.title: cross polarization
08327.definition: Technique in solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that enables polarization from abundant spins such as \(\ce{^{1}H}\) or \(\ce{^{19}F}\) to be transferred to dilute spins such as \(\ce{^{13}C}\) or \(\ce{^{15}N}\) to enhance signal-to-noise ratio.

08326.title: cross polarization with magic angle spinning NMR
08326.definition: Combined use of cross polarization with magic-angle spinning for solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

C01411.title: cross reaction
C01411.definition: The ability of substances other than the analyte to bind to the binding reagent and the ability of substances other than the binding reagent to bind the analyte in competitive binding assays.

08721.title: cross reactivity
08721.definition: Ability of substances other than the analyte to bind to the binding reagent and ability of substances other than the binding reagent to bind the analyte in competitive binding assays.

08722.title: cross section
08722.definition: Characteristic area related to the probability of a specified interaction or reaction between an incident nuclear radiation and a target particle or system of particles.

13058.title: cross sensitivity
13058.definition: State of immunological hypersensitivity to one substance that predisposes an individual to sensitivity to other substances that are related in chemical structure (cross-reacting antigens).

C01404.title: cross-conjugation
C01404.definition: In a system $\ce{XC6H4GY}$ this is conjugation involving the substituent $\ce{X}$, the benzene ring and the side-chain connective-plus-reaction site $\ce{GY}$, i.e. either $\ce{X}$ is a $+R$ group and $\ce{GY}$ is a $-R$ group, or $\ce{X}$ is a $-R$ group and $\ce{GY}$ is a $+R$ group. In Hammett correlations this situation can lead to the need to apply exalted substituent constants \(\sigma ^{+}\) or \(\sigma ^{-}\), respectively, as in electrophilic or nucleophilic aromatic substitution, respectively. The term 'through resonance' is synonymous. Cross conjugation has also been used to describe the interactions occurring in 2-phenylallyl and similar systems.

C01407.title: cross-flow filtration
C01407.definition: Method of operating a filtration device where retained fluid is circulated over the membrane (filter) surface thus preventing undue build-up of filtered material on membrane (filter).

09867.title: cross-linking
09867.definition: Formation of a covalent bridge between two biomacromolecules or between two segments of the same biomacromolecule using reactive substances (e.g. formaldehyde, bifunctional aldehydes such as glutaraldehyde, or cisplatin) or photochemical processes.

13054.title: cross-matching
13054.definition:
1) Test for determining the compatibility between the blood of a donor and that of a recipient before transfusion; the clumping of erythrocytes indicates incompatibility.
2) Test for determining tissue compatibility between a transplant donor and the recipient before transplantation, in which the recipient’s serum is tested for antibodies that may react with the lymphocytes or other cells of the donor.
3) Process of performing one of these tests.

C01410.title: cross-over concentration
C01410.definition: The concentration range at which the sum of the volumes of the domains occupied by the solute molecules or particles in solution is approximately equal to the total volume of that solution. The term 'domain' refers to the smallest convex body that contains the molecule or particle in its average shape.

13055.title: cross-presentation
13055.definition: Activation of CD8+ lymphocytes by the presentation of exogenous antigens in association with major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules.

15393.title: cross-propagation
15393.definition: Propagation reaction in a copolymerization in which a chain carrier, bearing at its active end a monomer unit of one kind, reacts with a monomer molecule of another kind.

13056.title: cross-reacting antibody
13056.definition: Antibody that is able to react with an antigen that did not specifically stimulate its production.

13057.title: cross-reacting antigen
13057.definition:
Antigen that is able to react with an antibody induced by a different antigen.
Note: The two antigens may share the same antigenic determinants or carry determinants that are sufficiently alike stereochemically to enable the antibody to react with both.
Antigen that has an identical structure in two strains of microorganism, so that antibody raised against one strain will react with the other strain.

14560.title: cross-resistance
14560.definition: Condition in which enhanced tolerance to one toxicant also enhances tolerance to another.

09899.title: cross-sectional area of the column
09899.definition: Cross-sectional area of the empty tube: \(A_{\rm{c}} = \pi r_{\rm{c}}^{2} = \pi (d_{\rm{c}}/2)^{2}\), where \(d_{\rm{c}}\) is the column diameter.

15612.title: cross-sectional study
15612.definition: Study that examines the relationship between diseases (or other health-related characteristics) and other variables of interest as they exist in a defined population at one particular time.

09241.title: cross-sectioning
09241.definition: Sample preparation in which the sample is cleaved, cut, or polished in a plane perpendicular to the interface under study, so that associated compositional differences or gradients can be observed in that plane.

15394.title: cross-termination
15394.definition: Termination reaction in a copolymerization between two chain carriers with different chemical structures.

13059.title: cross-tolerance
13059.definition: State of immunological tolerance to one substance produced by priming an animal with another substance that bears a cross-reacting antigen.

10211.title: crosscurrent extraction
10211.definition: Extraction comprising a cascading series of states where the raffinate is brought into a subsequent stage and contacted with fresh solvent.

C01405.title: crossed electric and magnetic fields
C01405.definition: Electric and magnetic fields with the electric field direction at right angles to the magnetic field direction.

C01408.title: crossing over
C01408.definition: The usually reciprocal exchange of genetic material between chromosomes; part of natural genetic recombination.

C01409.title: crosslink
C01409.definition: A small region in a macromolecule from which at least four chains emanate, and formed by reactions involving sites or groups on existing macromolecules or by interactions between existing macromolecules.

CT07596.title: crosslink density
CT07596.definition: Number of crosslinks per unit volume in a polymer network.

CT07136.title: crosslinking
CT07136.definition: Reaction involving sites or groups on existing macromolecules or an interaction between existing macromolecules that results in the formation of a small region in a macromolecule from which at least four chains emanate.

CT07597.title: crosslinking site
CT07597.definition: Site on a macromolecule or region in a polymer material that takes part in the formation of chemical or physical crosslinks.

15165.title: crossover study
15165.definition: Type of comparative bioavailability study designed in such a way as to take into account differences in bioavailability arising from differences between patients suffering from disease, participating in the study.

10575.title: Crouzon syndrome
10575.definition: Group of autosomal dominant genetic diseases characterized by midfacial hypoplasia, craniosynostosis, exophthalmos, and a shortened head.

C01420.title: crowding
C01420.definition: The displacement of an impurity from an extract phase by contact with a solution containing the main extractable solute. The main solute need not be present in a pure solution but should have a higher distribution ratio than the impurities present.

C01421.title: crown
C01421.definition: A molecular entity comprising a monocyclic ligand assembly that contains three or more binding sites held together by covalent bonds and capable of binding a guest in a central (or nearly central) position. The adducts formed are sometimes known as 'coronates'. The best known members of this group are macrocyclic polyethers, such as '18-crown-6', containing several repeating units $\ce{–CR2–CR2O–}$ (where $\ce{R}$ is most commonly $\ce{H}$), and known as crown ethers.

C01422.title: crown conformation
C01422.definition: A conformation of a saturated cyclic molecular entity, containing an even number (≥8) of atoms in the ring, in which these atoms lie alternately in each of two parallel planes and are symmetrically equivalent (\(D_{4\rm{d}}\) for cyclooctane, \(D_{5\rm{d}}\) for cyclodecane etc). It is analogous to the chair conformation of cyclohexane.

C01423.title: crud
C01423.definition: A deposit or emulsion at the interface between two partially settled phases.

C01424.title: cryogenic
C01424.definition: Low temperature processes, apparatus, etc.; usually applied to systems operated at the temperature of liquid nitrogen, helium or other condensed gas which boils at a very low temperature (at atmospheric pressure).

C01425.title: cryogenic sampling
C01425.definition: The collection of trace compounds from gaseous media by co-condensation with a major constituent (e.g. water vapour, $\ce{CO2}$, $\ce{N2}$, $\ce{Ar}$) of the matrix.

10192.title: cryogenic trap
10192.definition: Device used to concentrate volatile analytes from the gas phase by condensation on a cold surface.

13060.title: cryoglobulin
13060.definition: Immunoglobulin (Ig) that forms insoluble aggregates at temperatures below body temperature.

13061.title: cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
13061.definition: Cutaneous or systemic vasculitis caused by cold-labile proteins (cryoglobulins, cryofibrinogen) that leads to increased viscosity, protein precipitation or gelatinification, complement activation, and endothelial cell damage, especially in the cold.

10576.title: crypt
10576.definition: Small tubular gland, pit, or depression.

C01426.title: cryptand
