Natural tendency shown by an individual or group of individuals, including any tendency to acquisition of specific diseases, often due to hereditary factors.
Total of the processes of absorption of a chemical into the circulatory systems, distribution throughout the body, biotransformation, and excretion.

D01799.title: disproportionation
D01799.definition: Any chemical reaction of the type , where A, A' and A'' are different chemical species. For example:  The reverse of disproportionation is called comproportionation. A special case of disproportionation (or 'dismutation') is 'radical disproportionation', exemplified by:  Reactions of the more general type:  are also loosely described as 'radical disproportionations'.

10611.title: disruption
10611.definition: Disturbance that interrupts a process or disorganizes a structure.

DT06866.title: disruptor
DT06866.definition: A chemical group used to disrupt the linearity of the backbone of molecules MCPLCs.

15646.title: dissipation
15646.definition: Reduction in the amount of a pesticide or other compound that has been applied to plants, soil, etc. (used when it is not clear whether this is by mineralization degradation, binding, or leaching).

D01801.title: dissociation
D01801.definition: The separation of a molecular entity into two or more molecular entities (or any similar separation within a polyatomic molecular entity). Examples include unimolecular heterolysis and homolysis, and the separation of the constituents of an ion pair into free ions.   The separation of the constituents of any aggregate of molecular entities.   In both senses dissociation is the reverse of association.

D01802.title: dissociation energy
D01802.definition: Energy required to dissociate a molecule into two parts. Subscripts 0 and e, i.e. \(D_{0}\) and \(D_{\rm{e}}\), are used to denote the dissociation from the ground state and potential energy minimum, respectively.

D01803.title: dissociative adsorption
D01803.definition: Adsorption with dissociation into two or more fragments, both or all of which are bound to the surface of the adsorbent. The process may be homolytic, as in the chemisorption of hydrogen: \[\rm{H}_{2}+2\rm{*}\rightarrow 2\rm{H}^{\rm{*}}\] where * represents a surface site, or heterolytic, as in: \[\rm{H}_{2}+\rm{M}^{n+}+\rm{O}^{2-}\rightarrow \rm{H}^{-}\rm{M}^{n+}+\rm{HO}^{-}\] where \(\rm{M}^{n+}\) and \(\rm{O}^{2- }\) are surface sites in which the ions are of lower coordination than the ions in the bulk phase. Associative desorption is the reverse of dissociative adsorption.

D01804.title: dissociative ionization
D01804.definition: An ionization process in which a gaseous molecule decomposes to form products, one of which is an ion.

D01805.title: dissociative surface reaction
D01805.definition: Dissociative surface reaction and its reverse, associative surface reaction, are defined by: \[2^{\rm{*}}+\rm{C}_{2}\rm{H}_{5}^{\rm{*}}\rightleftharpoons \rm{H}^{\rm{*}}+\,^{\rm{*}}{\rm{CH}_{2}\rm{CH}_{2}}^{\rm{*}}\] where * represents a surface site.

D01806.title: dissolution
D01806.definition: The mixing of two phases with the formation of one new homogeneous phase (i.e. the solution).

09472.title: dissolution inhibitor
09472.definition: Compound that, when included in a resist formulation, slows the rate of dissolution.

09473.title: dissolution promoter
09473.definition: Compound that, when included in a resist formulation, increases the rate of dissolution.

09474.title: dissolution rate
09474.definition: Rate at which resist is removed during development.

14595.title: dissolved organic carbon
14595.definition: Amount concentration of carbon found dissolved in water samples from aquatic systems, measured as total elemental carbon.

14597.title: dissolved organic matter
14597.definition: Analogous to dissolved organic carbon, but refers to the entire organic pool dissolved in water.

14596.title: dissolved oxygen content
14596.definition: Amount concentration of oxygen dissolved in water at a particular temperature and pressure.

D01808.title: dissymmetry of scattering
D01808.definition: The ratio of two Rayleigh ratios for different angles of observation, i.e. \[z(\theta _{1},\, \theta _{2}) = \frac{R(\theta _{1})}{R(\theta _{2})}\] \[\theta _{1} < \theta _{2}\] The angles must be specified; in light scattering it is customary to let \(\theta = 1 - \theta _{1}\) and, most frequently, \(\theta _{1} = 45 ^{\circ}\) and \(\theta _{2} = 135 ^{\circ}\).

10612.title: distal
10612.definition: Situated away from the centre of the body or from the point of attachment.

D01809.title: distonic radical cation
D01809.definition: A radical cation in which charge and radical sites are separated.

08163.title: distortion interaction model
08163.definition: Method for analyzing activation energy as the sum of the energies to distort the reactants into the geometries they have in transition states plus the energy of interaction between the two distorted reactants.

08331.title: distortionless enhancement by polarization transfer
08331.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy used for determining the presence of primary, secondary and tertiary heteronuclei.

D01810.title: distribuend
D01810.definition: The substance that is distributed between two immiscible liquids or liquid phases.

D01811.title: distribution
D01811.definition: The apportionment of a solute between two phases. The term partition or extraction may also be used in this sense where appropriate.

11550.title: distribution constant (exclusion)
11550.definition: Fraction of the intraparticle volume (the volume of the pores) available to the molecules of a particular sample component for diffusion: \[K_{0} = \frac{V_{\rm{R}} - V_0}{V_{\rm{i}}}\]

11551.title: distribution constant calibration
11551.definition: Calibration for extraction when close to equilibrium conditions, using a known for the distribution constant for the analyte.

D01814.title: distribution constant
D01814.definition: The concentration of a component in or on the stationary phase divided by the concentration of the component in the mobile phase. Since in chromatography a component may be present in more than one form (e.g. associated and dissociated forms), the analytical condition used here refers to the total amount present without regard to the existence of various forms. These terms are also called the distribution coefficients. However, the present term conforms more closely to the general usage in science.

D01815.title: distribution function
D01815.definition: A normalized function giving the relative amount of a portion of a polymeric substance with a specific value, or a range of values, of a random variable or variables.

DT06932.title: distribution isotherm
DT06932.definition: The equilibrium relation between the concentration of a sample component in the stationary phase \(c_{\rm{S}}\), and in the mobile phase \(c_{\rm{M}}\), expressed as a function \(c_{\rm{S}}=f(c_{\rm{M}})\). In some versions of chromatography, a distribution isotherm can be seen as a partition isotherm, an adsorption isotherm, or a combination of these, depending on the mechanism of separation.

D01817.title: distribution ratio
D01817.definition: The ratio of the total analytical concentration of a solute in the extract (regardless of its chemical form) to its total analytical concentration in the other phase.

15647.title: distribution volume
15647.definition: Theoretical volume of a body compartment throughout which a substance is calculated to be distributed.

14598.title: disturbance
14598.definition: Event that introduces, removes, or redistributes organisms, changing the colonization potential of a given environment.

09740.title: disulfide bond cleavage
09740.definition: Chemical reduction of protein disulfide bonds.

D01818.title: disyndiotactic polymer
D01818.definition: A syndiotactic polymer that contains two chiral or prochiral atoms with defined stereochemistry in the main chain of the configurational base unit.

D01819.title: ditactic polymer
D01819.definition: A tactic polymer that contains two sites of defined stereoisomerism in the main chain of the configurational base unit.

15648.title: diuresis
15648.definition: Excretion of urine, especially in excess.

D01822.title: diurnal variation
D01822.definition: Indicates variations which follow a distinctive pattern which recurs with a daily cycle.

12642.title: diversity
12642.definition: Unrelatedness of a set of molecules (e.g., building blocks or members of a compound library), as measured by properties such as atom connectivity, physical properties, or computationally generated descriptors.

13098.title: diversity gene
13098.definition: Small segment of immunoglobulin (Ig) heavy-chain or T-cell receptor DNA between the variable (V) gene and joining (J) gene segments, coding for the third hypervariable region of the receptors.

14599.title: diversity index
14599.definition: Mathematical descriptor of species variation within a community.

12643.title: diversity-oriented synthesis
12643.definition: Efficient production of a range of structures and templates with skeletal and stereochemical diversity as opposed to the synthesis of a specific target molecule.

10613.title: diverticulum
10613.definition: Outpouching of a hollow structure in the body, that may be acquired (as in colonic diverticulitis) or be present at birth (e.g., Meckel diverticulum or Zenker diverticulum).

15173.title: divided granule
15173.definition: Formulation in which individual doses of a granulated dosage form are separated (e.g., gelatin capsules).

15174.title: divided powder
15174.definition: Powder formulation in which individual doses of a powdered dosage form are separately wrapped (e.g., sachets, envelopes, or gelatin capsules).

08589.title: divided spinning cell
08589.definition: Measuring instrument for Raman spectroscopy incorporating a dish-shaped cell that is divided by a vertical partition through its middle to allow different liquids in its two halves. It is rotated about a vertical axis through its centre and the Raman scattered radiation from each half is measured alternately. With a standard liquid in one half and a sample in the other it is used to determine Raman scattering intensities relative to the standard.

D01823.title: dividing surface
D01823.definition: A surface, usually taken to be a hyperplane, constructed at right angles to the minimum-energy path on a potential-energy surface. In conventional transition-state theory it passes through the highest point on the minimum-energy path. In generalized versions of transition-state theory the dividing surface can be at other positions; in variational transition-state theory the position of the dividing surface is varied so as to get a better estimate of the rate constant.

D01824.title: DM-interference
D01824.definition: Interference in which the analytical signal is influenced by a different mechanism than the analyte e.g. the formation of non-dissociating species in emission spectroscopy.

D01826.title: DNA probe
D01826.definition: A short sequence of DNA labelled isotopically or chemically that is used for the detection of a complementary nucleotide sequence.

13077.title: DNA vaccination
13077.definition: Injection of DNA into muscle, followed by its transcription and translation into a protein or proteins that elicit antibody and T-cell responses.

D01827.title: Dobson unit
D01827.definition: Unit sometimes used in the description of the total ozone in a column of air overhead. It is given as the thickness (in units of \(10^{-3}\ \rm{cm}\) or \(10^{-5}\ \rm{m}\)) of that layer which would be formed by the total ozone in a column reduced to the pressure of \(760\ \rm{Torr}\) and temperature of \(0\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\).

11437.title: docking
11437.definition: Computational methods that optimize the placement of a ligand in a macromolecular binding site of known or proposed 3D structure and provide a score as to the quality of the fit.

DT06958.title: docking studies
DT06958.definition: Docking studies are computational techniques for the exploration of the possible binding modes of a substrate to a given receptor, enzyme or other binding site.

09475.title: doctor blading
09475.definition: Coating of solution or slurry drawn to uniform film by use of a knife edge or doctor blade.

D01828.title: dodecahedro-
D01828.definition: An affix used in names to denote eight atoms bound into a dodecahedron with triangular faces.

D01829.title: dolichols
D01829.definition: A group of prenol derivatives in which \(n\) in the general formula $\ce{H–[CH2–C(CH3)=CH–CH2]_{n}–OH}$ is greater than four and in which the residue that carries the hydroxy group is saturated, i.e. 2,3-dihydropolyprenols.

10614.title: dominant
10614.definition: Of a gene, determining the phenotype even when present only in one copy or inherited from only one parent.

15650.title: dominant half life
15650.definition: Half life of a fraction of a substance in a specific organ or compartment if it defines approximately the overall clearance rate for that substance at a specific time point.

11805.title: dominant hemisphere
11805.definition: Cerebralhemisphere containing the representation of speech and controlling arm and leg preference in skilled movements.

15651.title: dominant lethal mutation
15651.definition: Genetic change occurring in a germ cell that does not cause dysfunction of the gamete but which is lethal to the fertilized egg or developing embryo which develops from it.

11722.title: domoic acid
11722.definition: Neurotoxickainic acid analog produced by some algal blooms that causes amnesic shellfish poisoning.

08164.title: donicity
08164.definition: Quantitative experimental measure of the Lewis basicity of a molecule \(\ce{B}\), expressed as the negative enthalpy of the formation of the 1:1 complex \(\ce{B.SbCl5}\).

D01830.title: Donnan emf
D01830.definition: The potential difference \(E_{\rm{D}}\) at zero electric current between two identical salt bridges, usually saturated $\ce{KCl}$ bridges (conveniently measured by linking them to two identical electrodes) inserted into two solutions in Donnan equilibrium.

D01831.title: Donnan equilibrium
D01831.definition: The equilibrium characterized by an unequal distribution of diffusible ions between two ionic solutions (one or both of the solutions may be gelled) separated by a membrane which is impermeable to at least one of the ionic species present, e.g. because they are too large to pass through the pores of the membrane. The membrane may be replaced by other kinds of restraint, such as gelation, the field of gravity, etc., which prevent some ionic components from moving from one phase to the other, but allow other components to do so.

DT06889.title: Donnan exclusion
DT06889.definition: Reduction in concentration of mobile ions within an ion exchange membrane due to the presence of fixed ions of the same sign as the mobile ions.

D01833.title: donor number
D01833.definition: A quantitative measure of Lewis basicity.

10171.title: donor phase
10171.definition: In extraction, the sample or sample solution.

11723.title: dopamine
11723.definition: Naturally occurring substance functioning as a neurotransmitter in the sympathetic nervous system, and a metabolic precursor of other substances including adrenalin.

11724.title: dopaminergic
11724.definition: Relating to a nerve that releases or responds to dopamine as a neurotransmitter.

DT07203.title: dopant
DT07203.definition: Charge-transfer agent used to generate, by oxidation or reduction, positive or negative charges in an intrinsically conducting polymer.

09476.title: doping (p- and n-type)
09476.definition: Process that increases the thermal-equilibrium concentration of free charge carriers in a material to augment its electrical conductivity using chemical agents or additives (i.e. dopants).

D01834.title: doping
D01834.definition: The action of adding a small amount of foreign atoms to form a solid solution in the lattice of a non-metallic catalyst.

DT07204.title: doping
DT07204.definition: Oxidation or reduction process brought about by a dopant.

D01835.title: Doppler broadening
D01835.definition: Broadening due to the random motion of the emitting or absorbing atoms. A Doppler broadened line has a Gaussian shape.

10615.title: dorsal
10615.definition: On or relating to the upper side or back of an organism.

11725.title: dorsal root
11725.definition: Outgrowth of a spinal nerve that carries sensory signals to an appropriate integration center in the brain.

11726.title: dorsal root ganglion
11726.definition: Nodule on a dorsal root of the spine that consists of afferent sensory neuronal cell bodies.

15175.title: dosage form
15175.definition: Formulated preparation of molecules/drugs that are rarely if ever suitable for administration to patients without additives.

D01837.title: dosage
D01837.definition: As applied to an air pollutant in an exposure chamber, dosage is commonly defined as the concentration of the pollutant times the duration of exposure.

15176.title: dosage regimen
15176.definition: Dose and dosing interval of a drug.

DT07361.title: dose
DT07361.definition: Energy or amount of photons absorbed per volume (or per mass) by an irradiated object during a particular exposure time. SI units are \(\pu{J m-3}\) or \(\pu{J g-1}\) and \(\pu{mol m-3}\) or \(\pu{mol g-1}\), respectively. Common units are \(\pu{einstein m-3}\) or \(\pu{einstein g-1}\), respectively.

D01841.title: dose equivalent
D01841.definition: Product of the absorbed dose of ionizing radiation, a quality factor and a modifying factor to take into account the effect of radiation on different biological tissues.

D01839.title: dose
D01839.definition: A general term denoting the quantity of radiation or energy absorbed. For special purposes, it must be appropriately qualified e.g. absorbed, maximum permissible, mean lethal.

DT06810.title: dose
DT06810.definition: Total quantity of a substance administered to, taken up, or absorbed by an organism, organ, or tissue.

14600.title: dose–effect
14600.definition: Relation between dose and the magnitude of a measured biological change.

14601.title: dose–effect curve
14601.definition: Graph of the relation between dose and the magnitude of the biological change produced measured in appropriate units.

14602.title: dose–effect relationship
14602.definition: Association between dose and the resulting magnitude of a continuously graded change, either in an individual or in a population.

DT06906.title: dose-response and dose-effect relationships
DT06906.definition: The graph of the relation between dose and the proportion of individuals responding with an all-or-none effect; it is essentially the graph of the probability of an occurrence (or the proportion of a population exhibiting an effect) against dose. Typical examples of such all-or-none effects are mortality or the incidence of cancer. The dose-effect curve is the graph of the relation between dose and the magnitude of the biological change produced measured in appropriate units. It applies to measurable changes giving a graded response to increasing doses of a drug or xenobiotic. It represents the effect on an individual animal or person, when biological variation is taken into account. An example is the increased effect of lead on the haem synthesis, e.g., on activity of the enzyme 6-amino laevulinic acid dehydratase in blood serum or coproporphyrin levels in urine.

14603.title: dose–response curve
14603.definition: Graph of the relation between dose and the proportion of individuals in a population responding with a defined biological effect.

14604.title: dose–response relationship
14604.definition: Association between dose and the incidence of a defined biological effect in an exposed population usually expressed as percentage.

13100.title: dot plot
13100.definition: Two-dimensional graphical representation of individual data points.

D01843.title: double escape peak
D01843.definition: In a gamma-ray spectrum, the peak due to pair production in the detector and escape, from the sensitive part of the detector, of two photons of \(511\ \rm{keV}\) resulting from annihilation.

09478.title: double exposure
09478.definition: Lithographic process requiring two exposures to radiation for a single resist layer to form a finished pattern.

09703.title: double helix
09703.definition: The twisted shape of two complementary strands of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).

08792.title: double injection
08792.definition: Simultaneous injection of both types of charge carriers (electrons and holes) into a material or a device.

09479.title: double patterning
09479.definition: Printing of two distinct lines at the edges of a single resist line pattern by means of a deposit-etch process.

08332.title: double pulsed-field gradient spin-echo excitation
08332.definition: Pulse sequence in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in which pulsed-field gradients are applied to a doubled spin echo sequence to cleanly and precisely excite particular resonances.

08333.title: double resonance
08333.definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment where excitation is applied independently to two distinct frequency ranges.

D01842.title: double-beam spectrometer
D01842.definition: Double (spectral) beam spectrometers are used where two samples are to be excited by two different wavelengths. A double- (synchronous) beam spectrometer is a luminescence spectrometer in which both the excitation and emission monochromators scan the excitation and emission spectra simultaneously, usually with a fixed wavelength difference between excitation and emission.

D01844.title: double-focusing mass spectrograph
D01844.definition: An instrument which uses both direction and velocity focusing, and therefore an ion beam initially diverging in direction and containing ions of different kinetic energies is separated into beams according to the quotient mass/charge, these beams being focused on to a photographic plate or film.

D01845.title: double-focusing mass spectrometer
D01845.definition: An instrument which uses both direction and velocity focusing, and therefore an ion beam of a given mass/charge is brought to a focus when the ion beam is initially diverging and contains ions of the same mass and charge with different translational energies. The ion beam is measured electrically.

08334.title: double-labelled protein
08334.definition: Shorthand for a protein which has been uniformly \(\ce{^{15}N{-}}\) and \(\ce{^{13}C{-}labelled}\).

D01847.title: double-layer current
D01847.definition: The non-faradaic current associated with the charging of the electrical double layer at an electrode-solution interface, given by: \[i_{\mathrm{DL}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}(\sigma \ A)}{\mathrm{d}t}\] where \(\sigma \) = surface charge density of the double layer, \(A\) = area of the electrode-solution interface and \(t\) = time. Capital letters should be used as subscripts to avoid the possibility of confusing this symbol with that for the limiting diffusion current.

13101.title: double-negative cell
13101.definition: Immature T cell in the thymus that lacks expression of the two coreceptors, CD4 and CD8.

13102.title: double-positive cell
13102.definition: Immature T cell in the thymus that is characterized by expression of both CD4 and CD8 coreceptor proteins.

08467.title: double-pulse laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy
08467.definition: Measurement method of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy in which reactions are induced by the interaction of the evolved plasma and the remaining part of the laser pulse, or with a following laser pulse provided from a second laser system.

08335.title: double-quantum filtered correlation spectroscopy
08335.definition: Variant of the COSY experiment with a double quantum filter to remove, or at least reduce, impact of large singlet peaks on dynamic range and artefacts.

D01849.title: double-strand chain
D01849.definition: A chain that comprises constitutional unit connected in such a way that adjacent constitutional units are joined to each other through three or four atoms, two on one side and either one or two on the other side of each constitutional unit.

D01850.title: double-strand copolymer
D01850.definition: A copolymer the macromolecules of which are double-strand macromolecules.

D01851.title: double-strand macromolecule
D01851.definition: A macromolecule that comprises constitutional unit connected in such a way that adjacent constitutional units are joined to each other through three or four atoms, two on one side and either one or two on the other side of each constitutional unit.

D01852.title: double-strand polymer
D01852.definition: A polymer the macromolecules of which are double-strand macromolecules.

D01854.title: double-wavelength spectroscopy
D01854.definition: The effect of spectral background due to impurities, solvent or radiation scattering may be reduced if the difference in the absorbances of a sample measured at two selected wavelengths is obtained. This is often achieved by repetitively switching from one wavelength to the other. Double-wavelength spectroscopy does this automatically by allowing two beams of radiation of different wavelengths to pass through the cell. One beam is fixed at a longer wavelength and the other measures absorbance while being scanned over a limited wavelength range at shorter wavelengths.

D01853.title: doublet state
D01853.definition: A state having a total electron spin quantum number equal to \(\frac{1}{2}\).

D01855.title: doubling time
D01855.definition: The time (\(\min \), \(\mathrm{h}\)) required for a cell population to double either the number of cells or the active cell mass.

D01857.title: down-time
D01857.definition: The loss of time that should be available for analysis. This might be due to breakdown, maintenance or other factors.

DT07362.title: downconversion
DT07362.definition:
Process by which a photon with frequency \(
u _{1}\) interacts with a non-linear medium and splits into two simultaneously emitted photons with frequencies \(
u _{2}\) and \(
u _{3}\) so that the energy is conserved: \[
u _{1}=
u _{2}+
u _{3}\]

DT06874.title: downstream
DT06874.definition: Side of a membrane from which permeate emerges.

D01858.title: downwash
D01858.definition: As applied to the action of chimney gases, it is the downward motion of the chimney gases brought on by eddies which form in the lee of a chimney when the wind is blowing. It may result in bringing the flue gases to the ground prematurely.

13078.title: DP, DQ, and DR molecules
13078.definition: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II molecules occurring on human B lymphocytes and antigen-presenting cells (APCs).

14605.title: drainage basin
14605.definition: Area of land where water from rain or snow melt drains downhill into a body of water, such as a river, lake, dam, estuary, wetland, sea, or ocean.

13103.title: draining lymph node
13103.definition: Lymph node that is downstream of a site of infection and thus receives antigens and microbes from the site via the lymphatic system.

13104.title: Draize test
13104.definition:
Context: ocular; Test for potential to cause irritation to the eye in which the test substance is applied directly to the eye of restrained rabbits.
Note: Widely criticized as unethical. Now often replaced with an acute eye irritation test using cadaveric chicken eyes.
Context: skin; Test for the potential of a material to cause irritation or corrosion following local dermal application. Generally performed with rabbits.

D01859.title: drift
D01859.definition: A slow non-random change in signal with time.

08793.title: drift current
08793.definition: Electric current caused by electric drift.

08794.title: drift velocity
08794.definition: Average velocity that a charge carrier attains due to an applied electric field.

D01860.title: driving force
D01860.definition: The decrease in Gibbs energy on going from the reactants to the products of a chemical reaction (\(-\Delta G\)).

DT07363.title: driving force
DT07363.definition: Term widely used to indicate the negative of the standard Gibbs energy change for outer-sphere electron transfer (\(\Delta _{\rm{ET}}G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\)).

D01862.title: drop time
D01862.definition: The time that elapses between the instants at which two successive drops of liquid metal are detached from the tip of the capillary.

D01861.title: droplet
D01861.definition: A small liquid particle. The size of droplets encountered in the atmosphere extends over a wide range; e.g. liquid aerosol solutions which make up the fine particle fraction of continental tropospheric aerosol are usually \(2\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) in diameter. Cloud water droplets usually have diameters in the range of \(5{-}70\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\), while rain droplets commonly have diameters ranging from \(0.1{-}3\ \rm{mm}\).

09103.title: dropping mercury electrode
09103.definition: Mercury electrode formed by sequence of mercury drops falling from a small aperture.

DT07364.title: Drude–Nernst equation
DT07364.definition: Equation describing the contraction (\(\Delta V_{\rm{el}}\)) taking place in a dielectric medium of relative static permittivity \(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\) (formerly called dielectric constant) upon introduction of an ion of charge number \(z\) and radius \(r\): \[\Delta V_{\rm{el}} = -\frac{\left ( z\,e \right )^{2}}{2\,r\,\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}}\frac{\partial\left ( \rm{ln}\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\right)}{\partial\,p}\] with \(e\) the elementary charge.

D01863.title: drug
D01863.definition: Any substance which when absorbed into a living organism may modify one or more of its functions. The term is generally accepted for a substance taken for a therapeutic purpose, but is also commonly used for abused substances. Synonymous with medicine, pharmaceutical.

12644.title: drug cocktail
12644.definition:
­(in drug therapy) Administration of two or more distinct pharmacological agents to achieve a combination of their individual effects.
Note 1: The combined effect may be additive, synergistic, or designed to reduce side-effects.
Note 2: This term is often used synonymously with that of 'drug combination' but is preferred in order to avoid confusion with medications in which different drugs are included in a single formulation.
(in drug testing) Administration of two or more distinct compounds to test simultaneously their individual behaviours (e.g., pharmacological effects in high-throughput screens or drug metabolism).

12645.title: drug delivery
12645.definition: Process by which a drug is administered to its intended recipient.

15177.title: drug delivery system
15177.definition: Sophisticated dosage form, which, by its construction, is able to modify/control the availability of the drug substance to the body by temporal or spatial considerations.

DT06960.title: drug design
DT06960.definition: Drug design includes not only ligand design, but also pharmacokinetics and toxicity, which are mostly beyond the possibilities of structure- and/or computer-aided design. Nevertheless, appropriate chemometric tools, including experimental design and multivariate statistics, can be of value in the planning and evaluation of pharmacokinetics and toxicological experiments and results. Drug design is most often used instead of the correct term 'Ligand Design'.

12646.title: drug distribution
12646.definition: Measured amounts of an administered compound in various parts of the organism to which it is given.

12648.title: drug repurposing
12648.definition: Strategy that seeks to discover new applications for an existing drug that were not previously referenced and not currently prescribed or investigated.

12649.title: drug safety
12649.definition: Assessment of the nontolerable biological effects of a drug.

15178.title: drug-eluting stent
15178.definition: Refers to a stent with an active drug that is intended to produce a therapeutic effect (e.g., reduction of restenosis).

13105.title: drug-induced autoimmunity
13105.definition: Immune-mediated idiosyncratic drug reaction against self-antigens.

13106.title: drug-induced lupus
13106.definition: Idiosyncratic drug reaction similar in character to systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and having antinuclear antibodies (ANA), but generally milder in nature and resolving when drug exposure is discontinued.

11438.title: drug-likeness
11438.definition: An estimate of the probability that a chemical structure is similar to known drugs based on chemical or physical properties.

12647.title: druggability
12647.definition: Capacity of a molecular target to be modulated in a favourable manner by a small-molecule drug.

D01864.title: dry bulb temperature
D01864.definition: In psychrometry, the temperature of the gas measured by a dry bulb thermometer.

09480.title: dry deposition
09480.definition: Assembly of a layer on a substrate by the use of a solvent-free process, such as vapor deposition.

09481.title: dry development
09481.definition: Process in which a portion of a latent pattern in an exposed resist is removed to form the image without the use of a liquid developer.

09489.title: dry etching
09489.definition: Process of removal of material, typically of a masked pattern on a semiconductor, by exposing it to a bombardment of ions.

09482.title: dry-etch resistance
09482.definition: Facility of an exposed resist to withstand etching conditions, usually a plasma, determined in comparison to a reference standard.

D01865.title: drying agent
D01865.definition: A substance which removes water (liquid or gaseous).

DT07534.title: drying control chemical additive
DT07534.definition: Co-solvent included to facilitate the rapid drying of gels without cracking.

12650.title: dual binding site
12650.definition: Presence of two distinct ligand binding sites on the same molecular target.

DT07365.title: dual fluorescence
DT07365.definition: Systems or molecular species showing two fluorescence bands. Several non-trivial molecular properties may be at the basis of a dual fluorescence, such as conformational equilibrium in the ground state and a mixture of excited states.

D01866.title: dual substituent-parameter equation
D01866.definition: In a general sense, any equation which expresses substituent effects in terms of two parameters. However, in practice the term is used more specifically for an equation for summarizing the effects of meta- or para- substituents (i = m or p) $\ce{\textbf{X}}$ on chemical reactivity, spectroscopic properties, etc. of a probe site $\ce{\textbf{Y}}$ in benzene or other aromatic system. \[P^{\rm{i}} = \rho_{I}^{\rm{i}}\ \sigma_{I} + \rho_{R}^{\rm{i}} \sigma_{R}\] \(P\) is the magnitude of the property $\ce{\textbf{Y}}$ for substituent $\ce{\textbf{X}}$, expressed relative to the property for $\ce{X} = \ce{H}$; \(\sigma _{I}\) and \(\sigma _{R}\) are inductive or polar and resonance substituent constants, respectively, there being various scales for \(\sigma _{R};\,\rho _{I}\) and \(\rho _{R}\) are the corresponding regression coefficients.

08468.title: dual viewing mode
08468.definition: Inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer that allows axial viewing mode or radial viewing mode.

09397.title: dual-beam profiling
09397.definition: In secondary-ion mass spectrometry, sputter depth profiling involving two ion guns.

DT07366.title: dual-mode photochromism
DT07366.definition: Photochromism occurring in complex systems and triggered alternatively by two different external stimuli, such as light and an electric current. In such a case photochromism and 'electrochromism' are mutually regulated.

09483.title: dual-tone resist
09483.definition: Photoresist capable of being processed in either positive tone (aqueous base development) or negative tone (organic solvent development).

10617.title: duct
10617.definition: Vessel for transporting fluids such as lymph, or glandular secretions such as tears or bile.

10618.title: ductus arteriosis
10618.definition: Fetal blood vessel connecting the pulmonary artery to the proximal descending aorta.

10070.title: dummy factor
10070.definition: Factor that is known to have no effect on the response, used in an experimental design, to estimate repeatability standard deviation.

10619.title: dung fly test
10619.definition: Procedure using dung flies of the order Diptera where a test substance is mixed with bovine feces to which eggs of the fly are added; number, sex, and morphology are determined when the last adult has emerged.

10620.title: duodenum
10620.definition: First portion of the small intestine, between the stomach and the jejunum, where bile and pancreatic digestive juices enter the intestinal tract.

15652.title: duplicate portion sampling method
15652.definition: Study in which test persons consume their ordinary diet but, for each meal, they prepare for subsequent analysis a duplicate portion of all food as prepared, served, and consumed.

15653.title: duplicate samples
15653.definition: Two samples taken under the same or comparable conditions.

11727.title: dura mater
11727.definition: Outermost and most fibrous of the three membranes of the meninges (see meninx) covering the brain and the spinal cord.

D01868.title: dust collector
D01868.definition: A device for monitoring dust emissions. Also the equipment used to remove and collect dust from process exhaust gases; this may employ simply sedimentation (dustfall jars, coated slides, papers, etc.), inertial separation (cyclones, impactors, impingers, etc.), precipitation (thermal and electrostatic) or filtration.

D01869.title: dust fall
D01869.definition: Solid particles in the air which fall to the ground under the influence of gravity.

D01867.title: dust
D01867.definition: Small, dry, solid particles projected into the air by natural forces, such as wind, volcanic eruption and by mechanical or man-made processes such as crushing, grinding, milling, drilling, demolition, shoveling, conveying, screening, bagging and sweeping. Dust particles are usually in the size range from about \(1{-}100\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) in diameter and they settle slowly under the influence of gravity.

08336.title: dwell time
08336.definition: Time interval between sampled data points.

D01870.title: dye laser
D01870.definition: A CW or pulsed source of coherent radiation in which the active medium is usually a solution of a fluorescent organic molecule (the dye) pumped with a suitable pump laser or with a flash lamp. These lasers can be tuned over a large part of the fluorescence band of the dye.

13813.title: dynamer
13813.definition: Assembly or supramolecular assembly, the components of which are linked through reversible bondings that enable structural reassembly by reshuffling in response to changes in the chemical or physical environment.

10299.title: dynamic bioaccessibility
10299.definition: Leaching of analytes from a solid or semi-solid sample in a flow-through device to evaluate their bioaccessibility.

09321.title: dynamic emittance matching
09321.definition: Electron or ion optical method of steering a spectrometer axis to align with the impact area of the primary beam at all points of a raster scan on the sample surface.

14606.title: dynamic energy budget theory
14606.definition: Theory that simple quantitative rules may be applied to define the organization of metabolism of individual organisms.

10172.title: dynamic extraction
10172.definition: Extraction in which clean (or recycled) extraction phase is continuously passed through the sample.

D01871.title: dynamic fields mass spectrometer
D01871.definition: A mass spectrometer in which the separation of a selected ion beam depends essentially on the use of fields, or a field, varying with time. These fields are generally electric.

10194.title: dynamic headspace analysis
10194.definition: Continuous removal of headspace above a sample by a flow of inert gas over or through the sample until all or a significant portion of the analytes have been removed from the sample. Sample vapours are typically transferred to a sorbent trap or cryogenic trap for collection.Typical apparatus for analysis by dynamic headspace (purge and trap). The gas flow (sparging gas) enters at the bottom of the sample container transporting volatile compounds through the headspace and purge head to the desorption tube for collection.

12275.title: dynamic light scattering
12275.definition: Experimental method based on the measurement of the time autocorrelation function of the intensity of light scattered from a polymer solution or a dispersion of particles.

12763.title: dynamic mechanical analyser
12763.definition: Apparatus for conducting a dynamic mechanical analysis experiment.

12294.title: dynamic mechanical analysis
12294.definition: Technique where storage and loss viscoelastic moduli are determined with the help of a periodical stress.

DT06875.title: dynamic membrane formation
DT06875.definition: Process in which an active layer is formed on the membrane surface by the deposition of substances contained in the fluid being treated.

08165.title: dynamic NMR
08165.definition: NMR spectroscopy of samples undergoing chemical reactions.

14006.title: dynamic photoadsorption process
14006.definition: Simultaneous (or synchronous) formation of adsorbed species (adsorbate) via photoadsorption and detachment by photodesorption to yield the same species, both processes occurring under photoexcitation of the solid photocatalyst (adsorbent).

D01874.title: dynamic range
D01874.definition: The ratio between the maximum usable indication and the minimum usable indication (detection limit). A distinction may be made between the linear dynamic range, where the response is directly proportional to concentration, and the dynamic range where the response may be non-linear, especially at higher concentrations.

DT07021.title: dynamic reaction path
DT07021.definition: A classical trajectory method based on molecular orbital calculations which determines atomic accelerations, velocities and positions using the energy gradient, and does not require prior knowledge of the potential energy surface.

09183.title: dynamic secondary-ion mass spectrometry
09183.definition: Secondary-ion mass spectrometry analysis with primary ion current density sufficiently high for use in the analysis of sample surface layers in the depth direction.

08590.title: dynamic spectrum
08590.definition: Spectrum of a material under the influence of an applied external perturbation represented by a variable \(\tau\), relative to a reference spectrum.

14609.title: dynamic stability hypothesis
14609.definition: Hypothesis that long food chains are less stable than short food chains.

12280.title: dynamic structure factor
12280.definition: Function describing the temporal dependence of relative scattering intensity on the magnitude of the scattering vector, \(q\).

D01875.title: dynamic surface tension
D01875.definition: In certain circumstances, one may measure surface tensions that are different from the equilibrium value. Such a surface tension is called the dynamic surface (or interfacial) tension (\(\gamma ^{\rm{dyn}}\) or \(\sigma ^{\mathrm{dyn}}\)). The equilibrium value is then called the static surface (or interfacial) tension (\(\gamma ^{\rm{st}}\) or \(\sigma ^{\mathrm{st}}\)). The modifying signs may be omitted if there is no danger of ambiguity.

12293.title: dynamic technique
12293.definition: Indicates, especially in the mechanical analysis of materials, that a parameter changes continuously during the experiment.

D01876.title: dynamic thermomechanometry
D01876.definition: A technique in which the dynamic modulus and/or damping of a substance under oscillatory load is measured as a function of temperature while the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program.

10049.title: dynamic time warping
10049.definition: Process of synchronizing a data matrix so that it represents the same time shifts.

12764.title: dynamic viscometer
12764.definition: Apparatus that uses a forced, non-resonance method to determine the viscoelastic properties of a material sample.

D01877.title: dynamic viscosity
D01877.definition: For a laminar flow of a fluid the ratio of the shear stress to the velocity gradient perpendicular to the plane of shear.

12762.title: dynamic-load thermomechanical analysis
12762.definition: Thermomechanical analysis carried out using a sinusoidal stress.

14607.title: dynamically fragile community
14607.definition: Community that is stable for only a very limited range of environmental characteristics, e.g., a stable and predictable environment with respect to predator–prey ratios or disturbances caused by humans.

14608.title: dynamically robust community
14608.definition: Community that is stable within a wide range of conditions, e.g., in very variable and unpredictable environments.

11728.title: dynein
11728.definition: Protein associated with motile structures that exhibits adenosine triphosphatase activity; it forms 'arms' on the outer microtubules of cilia and flagella and functions as a molecular motor.

11729.title: dynorphin
11729.definition: Member of a class of opioid peptides that arise from the precursor protein prodynorphin.

D01879.title: dyotropic rearrangement
D01879.definition: An uncatalysed process in which two $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bonds}$ simultaneously migrate intramolecularly, e.g.

11730.title: dysaphia
11730.definition: Impairment of the sense of touch.

11731.title: dysarthria
11731.definition: Difficulty in speech owing to disturbances of muscular control resulting from central or peripheral nervous system damage or emotional stress.

11732.title: dysesthesia
11732.definition:
Condition in which a disagreeable sensation, especially of touch, is produced following damage to peripheral or central sensory pathways.
Abnormal sensation experienced in the absence of stimulation.

15654.title: dysfunction
15654.definition: Abnormal, impaired, or incomplete functioning of an organism, organ, tissue, or cell.

10621.title: dysgenesis
10621.definition: Defective or abnormal development of an organ.

11734.title: dyskinesia
11734.definition: Difficulty or abnormality in voluntary movement.

11736.title: dyslexia
11736.definition: Impairment in appreciation of spatial relations, often leading to difficulty in reading.

10624.title: dysmorphia
10624.definition: Abnormality of shape of a body part or organ, often referring to a birth defect.

10627.title: dysostosis
10627.definition: Defect in the normal ossification of fetal cartilage.

11738.title: dysphasia
11738.definition: Difficulty in the use of language owing to a brain lesion, without mental impairment.

10626.title: dysplasia
10626.definition: Abnormal development of an organ or tissue identified by morphological examination.

16264.title: dyspnea
16264.definition: Difficulty in breathing; shortness of breath.

15324.title: dystectic reaction
15324.definition: Isobaric, reversible melting or dissolution with either complete or partial dissociation on heating of a solid compound, \(\ce{A_{\rm{a}}B_{\rm{b}}}\), formed by components \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\) \[\ce{A_{\rm{a}}B_{\rm{b}}(s)  A_{\rm{a}}B_{\rm{b}}(l)  {\rm{a}}A(l) + {\rm{b}}B(l)}\] where the forward arrows indicate the direction of heating.

11740.title: dystonia
11740.definition: State of abnormal (either hypo- or hypertonic) muscle tone resulting in impairment of voluntary movement.

15325.title: dystonic reaction
15325.definition: Reversible dissolution in an isothermal, isobaric system of three or more components characterized by dissolution and saturation with a stoichiometric compound consisting of two or more of these components. The equilibrium process is, for example, \[\ce{AB.p H2O  A(aq, sat) + B(aq, sat) + p H2O(l)}\]

13712.title: drug-specific T cell
13712.definition: T-memory cell that is specific for a drug allergen.

D01511.title: Δ, Λ
D01511.definition: Designations of stereoisomers of tris(didentate) metal complexes and other octahedral complexes.

08473.title: Esum
08473.definition: Energy that must be supplied to an atom to transfer it from the ground atomic state to a given ionic excited state.

12400.title: einzel lens
12400.definition: Three-element charged particle lens in which the first and third elements are maintained at the same electric potential. Such a lens produces focusing without changing the translational energy of the particle.

12401.title: electrohydrodynamic ionization
12401.definition: Ionization process that produces charged droplets and gas-phase ions from a liquid under vacuum with the application of an electric field.

12402.title: electron capture dissociation
12402.definition: Process in which multiply protonated molecules interact with low-energy electrons followed by fragmentation. The capture of an electron by the even-electron cation \(\ce{[M + nH]^{n+}}\) liberates energy and reduces its charge state, thus producing the corresponding \(\ce{[M + nH]^{(n - 1)+.}}\) odd-electron ion, which readily fragments.

12403.title: electron capture ionization
12403.definition: Ionization of a gas-phase atom or molecule by attachment of a free electron to form molecular ions of the \(\ce{M^{-.}}\) type.

13956.title: ecotoxicity
13956.definition: Consequence of adverse effects caused by a substance on the environment and on organisms living in it.

13957.title: environmentally degradable polymer
13957.definition: Polymer that can be degraded by the action of the environment, through, for example, air, light, heat, or microorganisms.

13958.title: environmentally friendly
13958.definition: Qualifiers for a substance, device, or process that has minimal deleterious impact on the environment, which is air, water, minerals, living systems, etc.

12404.title: electrospray needle
12404.definition: Narrow bore tube from which highly charged droplets are emitted in electrospray ionization.

12405.title: electrostatic energy analyser
12405.definition: Device consisting of pairs of parallel conducting plates, concentric cylinders, or concentric spheres that separate charged particles according to their ratio of translational energy to charge by means of a potential difference applied between the pair.

12406.title: even-electron rule
12406.definition: Rule that states that even-electron ions tend to form even-electron fragment ions whereas odd-electron ions tend to dissociate to form either odd- or even-electron ions.

12407.title: exact mass
12407.definition: Calculated mass of an ion or molecule with specified isotopic composition.

12408.title: extracted ion chromatogram
12408.definition: Chromatogram created by plotting the intensity of the signal observed at a chosen m/z value or set of values in a series of mass spectra recorded as a function of retention time.

12409.title: extracted ion electropherogram
12409.definition: Electropherogram created by plotting the intensity of the signal observed at a chosen m/z value or set of values in a series of mass spectra recorded as a function of electrophoresis time.

12410.title: extracted ion profile
12410.definition: Any plot of signal intensity observed at a chosen m/z value or set of values in a series of mass spectra recorded as a function of time, including extracted ion chromatogram, extracted ion electropherogram, or from flow injection analysis or any other time-dependent sampling.

13905.title: enzymatic degradation
13905.definition: Degradation caused by the catalytic action of enzymes.

13906.title: erosion
13906.definition: Degradation that occurs at the surface and progresses from it into the bulk.

E01882.title: E, Z
E01882.definition: The approved stereodescriptors of stereoisomeric alkenes $\ce{R1R2C=CR3R4}$ ($\ce{R1} \neq \ce{R2} , \ce{R3} \neq \ce{R4}$); neither $\ce{R1}$ nor $\ce{R2}$ need be different from $\ce{R3}$ or $\ce{R4}$), cumulenes $\ce{R1R2C(=C=C)_{n}=CR3R4}$ and related systems e.g. $\ce{R1R2C=NOH}$, $\ce{HON=C\{[CH2]_{n}\}2C=NOH}$. The group of highest CIP priority attached to one of the terminal doubly bonded atoms of the alkene, oxime, etc. or cumulene (i.e. $\ce{R1}$ or $\ce{R2}$) is compared with the group of highest precedence attached to the other (i.e. $\ce{R3}$ or $\ce{R4}$). The stereoisomer is designated as $Z$ (zusammen = together) if the groups lie on the same side of a reference plane passing through the double bond and perpendicular to the plane containing the bonds linking the groups to the double-bonded atoms; the other stereoisomer is designated as $E$ (entgegen = opposite). The descriptors may be applied to structures with a fractional bond order between one and two; and to double bonds involving elements other than carbon. They are not used to describe ring substitution relationships.

ET07374.title: E/Z photoisomerization
ET07374.definition: General designation of a photoinduced geometrical isomerization of a C–C double bond.

10628.title: early life stage test
10628.definition: Toxicity test using an organism in an early life stage such as the embryo or larva, noting that this stage is often the most sensitive part of the species life cycle.

10629.title: earthworm reproduction test
10629.definition: Procedure in which adult worms (Eisenia sp.) are exposed to a test substance mixed into the soil; number, weight and behaviour of the adult worms are studied after four weeks and the number of juveniles hatched is counted after a further four weeks.

08337.title: echo time
08337.definition: In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, time interval between the middle of the first radiofrequency pulse and the peak of the spin echo.

10630.title: eclampsia
10630.definition: Acute, life-threatening complication of pregnancy characterized by tonic-clonic seizures (convulsions), usually in a woman who has developed pre-eclampsia.

E01884.title: eclipsed
E01884.definition: Two atoms or groups attached to adjacent atoms are said to be eclipsed if the torsion angle between the three bonds is zero (or approximately so).

E01886.title: eclipsing strain
E01886.definition: Intramolecular strain present due to nonbonded interactions between two eclipsed atoms or groups. It is, for example, one of the interactions responsible for the existence of a rotational barrier and hence restricted rotation about the $\ce{C–C}$ bond in ethane. It has also been called Pitzer strain, torsional strain and bond opposition strain.

10631.title: ecogenetics
10631.definition: Study of the influence of hereditary factors on the response of individuals or populations to environmental factors.

14611.title: ecological character
14611.definition: Sum of biological, physical, and chemical components of an ecosystem and their interactions that maintain the ecosystem and its products, functions, and attributes.

14612.title: ecological energetics
14612.definition: Study of the flow of energy within an ecological system from the time the energy enters the living system until it is irretrievably lost from the system as heat.

14613.title: ecological epidemiology
14613.definition: Application of epidemiological methods to determine the cause, incidence, prevalence, and distribution of adverse effects in nonhuman species inhabiting contaminated sites; it is frequently associated with retrospective ecological risk assessment.

14614.title: ecological imbalance
14614.definition: Change in any biological, physical, or chemical components of an ecosystem, or in their interactions, which result in change in ecological character and its functions and attributes.

14615.title: ecological mortality
14615.definition: Toxicant-related diminution of fitness of an individual functioning within an ecosystem that is of a magnitude sufficient to be equivalent to somatic death.

14616.title: ecological parameter
14616.definition: Measurable variable whose value is a determinant of the characteristics of an ecosystem.

14610.title: ecology
14610.definition: Branch of biology that studies the interactions between living organisms and all factors (including other organisms) in their environment. Such interactions encompass environmental factors that determine the distributions of living organisms.

14617.title: ecophysiology
14617.definition: Study of physiology and tolerance limits of species that enhances understanding of their distribution in relation to abiotic conditions.

14618.title: ecoregion
14618.definition:
Any of a number of regions into which a continent, country, etc., can be divided according to their distinct environmental conditions and habitat types.
Large area of land or water with a characteristic, geographically distinct assemblage of natural communities and species comprising a recurring pattern of ecosystems associated with characteristic combinations of soil and landform.Note: The biodiversity of ecosystems in an ecoregion is often distinct from that of other ecoregions.

14619.title: ecosystem
14619.definition: Grouping of organisms (microorganisms, plants, animals) interacting together, with and through their physical and chemical environments, to form a functional entity within a defined environment.

14620.title: ecotone
14620.definition: Area of gradual transition between two or more ecosystems.

14621.title: ecotoxicologically relevant concentration
14621.definition: Concentration of a pesticide (active ingredient, formulations, and relevant metabolites) that is likely to affect a determinable ecological characteristic of an exposed system.

14399.title: ecotoxicology
14399.definition: Study of the toxic effects of chemical and physical agents on all living organisms, especially on populations and communities within defined ecosystems; it includes transfer pathways of these agents and their interactions with the environment.

10632.title: ectoderm
10632.definition: In an embryo, outermost layer that develops into the epidermis of the skin and the nervous system.

15655.title: ectoparasiticide
15655.definition: Substance intended to kill parasites living on the exterior of the host.

10633.title: ectopia
10633.definition: Abnormal location or malpositioning of an organ or body part, usually congenital.

10634.title: ectopic expression
10634.definition: Expression of a gene in a tissue in which it is not normally expressed.

10635.title: ectopic pregnancy
10635.definition: Complication of pregnancy in which the embryo implants (see implantation) and develops outside the cavity of the uterus.

10636.title: ectrodactyly
10636.definition: Congenital absence or deficiency of one or more of the central digits of the hand or foot.

10637.title: ectrosyndactyly
10637.definition: Congenital absence or deficiency of one or more of the central digits of the hand or foot with fusion of the existing ones.

13107.title: eczema
13107.definition: Acute or chronic skin inflammation with erythema, papules, vesicles, pustules, scales, crusts, or scabs, alone or in combination, of varied etiology.

E01888.title: eddy
E01888.definition: In turbulent fluid motion, a blob of the fluid that has some definitive character and moves in some way differently from the main flow.

E01889.title: eddy dispersion
E01889.definition: The process by which substances are mixed in the atmosphere or in any fluid system due to eddy motion.

14623.title: eddy motion
14623.definition: Movement in a current of water or air, that is contrary to the direction of the main current, especially in a circular motion, leading to irregularity in the motion of molecules.

10638.title: edema
10638.definition: Presence of abnormally large amounts of fluid in body cavities and intercellular spaces of tissues.

09484.title: edge acuity
09484.definition: Degree to which the edge of an image appears sharp and precise.

14624.title: edge effect
14624.definition: Influence of the closeness of contrasting environments on an ecosystem, seen at boundaries between natural habitats, especially forests, and disturbed or developed land.

09741.title: Edman degradation
09741.definition: Method of N-terminal analysis in which the N-terminal amino acid residue is labelled and cleaved from the peptide without affecting other peptide bonds in the peptide chain.

E01890.title: educt
E01890.definition: Term used mainly in the German literature for starting material (reactant). It should be avoided in English, because there it means 'something that comes out' and not 'something that goes in'. The German use of the term is in fact also incorrect.

16237.title: effect
16237.definition: Change in biochemistry, morphology, physiology, growth, development, or lifespan of an organism which results in impairment of functional capacity or impairment of capacity to compensate for additional stress or increase in susceptibility to other environmental influences.

10068.title: effect of a factor
10068.definition: Coefficient of a term in a response model.

14625.title: effect time
14625.definition: Time taken for a substance to produce a precisely defined effect.

09322.title: effective attenuation length
09322.definition: Parameter that, when introduced in place of the electron inelastic mean free path into an expression derived for Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy on the assumption that elastic scattering effects are negligible for a given quantitative application, will correct that expression for elastic scattering effects.

12202.title: effective bond length
12202.definition: Square root of the ratio of the unperturbed mean-square end-to-end distance of a linear chain to its number of skeletal bonds, i.e., \[b = (\lt\!r_{\rm{o}}^{2}\!\gt\!/n)^{1/2}\]

E01891.title: effective cadmium cut-off energy
E01891.definition: In a given experimental configuration, the energy value determined by the condition that the detector response would be unchanged if the cadmium cover surrounding the detector was replaced by a fictitious cover opaque to neutrons with energy below this value and transparent to neutrons with energy above this value.

E01892.title: effective charge
E01892.definition: Change in effective charge is a quantity obtained by comparison of the polar effect of substituents on the free energies of rate or equilibrium processes with that on a standard ionization equilibrium. Provided the effective charges on the states in the standard equilibrium are defined, then it is possible to measure effective charges for states in the reaction or equilibrium under consideration.

E01893.title: effective chimney height
E01893.definition: A height used for the purposes of calculating the dispersion of emitted gases from a chimney, and which differs from the real chimney height by an amount which depends on such factors as the exit velocity, buoyancy effects and wind speed; it may also be affected by the local topography. It denotes the maximum height of the centre of a plume path above the level of the ground. The effective height may be above or below the actual chimney height, although the former case is most common.

12651.title: effective concentration
12651.definition: Concentration of a substance that produces a defined magnitude of response in a given system.

12652.title: effective dose
12652.definition: Dose of a substance that causes a defined magnitude of response in a given system.

E01894.title: effective half life
E01894.definition: For a radioactive substance, the time required for the amount of that substance in a biological system to be reduced to one half of its value by both radioactive decay and biological processes, when the rate of removal is approximately exponential.

09918.title: effective length of the capillary
09918.definition: Length of the capillary from the sample introduction point to the detection point.

E01896.title: effective molarity
E01896.definition: The ratio of the first-order rate constant of an intramolecular reaction involving two functional groups within the same molecular entity to the second-order rate constant of an analogous intermolecular elementary reaction. This ratio has the dimension of concentration. The term can also apply to an equilibrium constant.

09906.title: effective plate height
09906.definition: Column length (\(L\)) divided by effective plate number (\(N_{\rm{eff}}\)): \[H_{\rm{eff}} = \frac{L}{N_{\rm{eff}}}\]

09907.title: effective plate number
09907.definition: Number indicative of column performance, calculated from the ratios of measures of adjusted retention and peak width: \[\eqalign{& N_{\rm{eff}} = \left(\frac{V_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{\sigma} \right)^{2} = \left(\frac{t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{\sigma} \right)^{2} \cr & N_{\rm{eff}} = 16 \left(\frac{V_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{b}}} \right)^{2} = 16 \left(\frac{t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{b}}} \right)^{2} \cr & N_{\rm{eff}} \approx 5.545 \left(\frac{V_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{h}}} \right)^{2} \approx 5.545 \left(\frac{t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{h}}} \right)^{2}}\]

14007.title: effective radiation-catalytic activity
14007.definition: Number of product entities (atoms, molecules, or radicals) generated by each \(\pu{100 eV}\) of radiation incident on the system.

E01898.title: effective theoretical plate number
E01898.definition: A number indicative of column performance when resolution is taken into account: \[N=\frac{16\ R_{\rm{s}}^{2}}{(1- \alpha )^{2}}\] where \(R_{\rm{s}}\) is the peak resolution and \(\alpha \) is the separation factor.

E01899.title: effective thermal cross-section
E01899.definition: A fictitious cross-section for a specified reaction, which, when multiplied by the 2200 metre-per-second flux density, gives the correct reaction rate for thermal neutrons.

E01895.title: effectively infinite thickness
E01895.definition: Solid or liquid samples of one gram or more are generally used in X-ray spectroscopy. If the sample is thick enough so that the intensity of characteristic fluorescent radiation is not significantly modified by an increase in thickness, the sample is described as a bulk sample of effectively infinite thickness.

E01901.title: effector
E01901.definition: A small molecule which increases (activator) or decreases (inhibitor) the activity of an (allosteric) protein by binding to the protein at the regulatory site (which is different from the substrate-binding catalytic site).

13108.title: effector cell
13108.definition: Cell that carries out an immune function, e.g., cytokine release, cytotoxicity.

14626.title: effects assessment
14626.definition: Component of risk assessment concerned with quantifying the manner in which the frequency and intensity of effects increase with increasing exposure to a contaminant or other source of stress (also known as dose–response assessment or toxicity assessment).

11741.title: efferent
11741.definition: Carrying outward; of nerves, those that conduct impulses outward from the central nervous system.

10639.title: efferent duct
10639.definition: Seminal duct leading from the testis to the head of the epididymis.

15180.title: effervescent tablet
15180.definition: Solid preparation that on contact with water breaks apart by the effect of gas (usually \(\ce{CO2}\)) evolution, resulting commonly from the reaction of hydrogen carbonate with citric or tartaric acid, in order to facilitate dissolution or dispersion of the active ingredient before ingestion.

14126.title: efficacy
14126.definition: Extent to which a compound activates a receptor to produce a response in an assay under saturating conditions.

E01906.title: efficiency of atomization
E01906.definition: The ratio of the amount of analyte that passes through the flame cross-section at the observation height, as free neutral (or ionized) atoms, to the amount of analyte aspirated.

E01907.title: efficiency of nebulization
E01907.definition: The substance fraction of component entering the flame in the amount of component consumed. The efficiency of nebulization is related to the amount of component and not to the amount of solvent. It cannot be calculated directly from the ratio: volume rate of sample drained from the spray chamber divided by volume rate of fluid consumed. Corrections usually have to be made to take account of differences in component concentrations in the drained and consumed solutions, respectively, because of evaporation of some solvent from mist droplets deposited on the walls.

E01908.title: efficiency spectrum
E01908.definition: A plot of the efficiency of a step (\(\eta \)) against wavelength or photon energy.

E01902.title: efficiency
E01902.definition: The ratio between the useful energy delivered or bound and the energy supplied, i.e. energy output/energy input. It is also used in the sense of a quantitative measure of the relative rate of a given step involving a species with respect to the sum of the rates of all of the parallel steps which depopulate that species.

E01909.title: efflorescence
E01909.definition: The reverse of deliquescence: the drying of a salt solution when the vapour pressure of water in the saturated solution of a substance is greater than the partial pressure of water in the ambient air. Also refers to the loss of water of crystallization from a solid salt such as $\ce{Na2CO3.10H2O}$ .

15181.title: efflorescent
15181.definition: Substance that loses water to form a lower hydrate or becomes anhydrous spontaneously.

E01910.title: effluent
E01910.definition: Any spent liquors or other waste materials which are emitted by a source (waste from plating shops, pickling tanks, sewage treatment plants, chemical manufacturing plants, etc.).

E01911.title: effluent
E01911.definition: The mobile phase leaving the column.

12653.title: efflux pump
12653.definition: Transporter protein located in the membrane of cells that utilizes active transport to move a compound from the internal to the external environment.

10640.title: egg
10640.definition: Female gamete after completion of the second meiotic division.

E01913.title: eighteen-electron rule
E01913.definition: An electron-counting rule to which an overwhelming majority of stable diamagnetic transition metal complexes adhere. The number of nonbonded electrons at the metal plus the number of electrons in the metal-ligand bonds should be 18. The 18 electron rule in transition metal chemistry is a full analogue of the 'Lewis octet rule'.

E01914.title: einstein
E01914.definition: One mole of photons. Although widely used, it is not an IUPAC sanctioned unit. It is sometimes defined as the energy of one mole of photons. This use is discouraged.

ET06759.title: Einstein equation
ET06759.definition: In its most general form, the Einstein equation relates the atomic mobility \(b_{i}\) of a species \(i\) to the diffusion coefficient \(D_{i}\): i.e., \(D_{i}=k\ T\ b_{i}\).

09323.title: Einstein photoelectric equation
09323.definition:
Equation relating the kinetic energy of an electron, emitted from a conductor illuminated by monochromatic photons, and the photon energy and work function of the surface from which the photoelectron is emitted. \(½m_{m{e}} 
u_{m{max}}^{2} = h
u - \phi_{0}\), where \(m_{m{e}}\) is the mass of an electron, \(
u_{m{max}}\) the maximum velocity of the emitted electron, \(h\) the Planck constant, \(
u\) the frequency of the illuminating photons, and \(\phi_{0}\) the photoelectric work function of the surface.

10641.title: ejaculation
10641.definition: Expulsion of semen from the genital ducts and urethra, usually resulting from a reflex process during sexual stimulation

10642.title: ejaculatory duct
10642.definition: Passage formed by the junction of the duct of the seminal vesicles and the ductus deferens through which semen enters the urethra.

ET07369.title: El-Sayed rules
ET07369.definition: The rate of intersystem crossing is relatively large if the radiationless transition involves a change of orbital type.

E01915.title: elastic collision
E01915.definition: A particle (atom or molecule) can undergo a change in its state of excitation as a result of collisions with other particles. In an elastic collision an exchange only of kinetic energy takes place between the colliding species; in an inelastic collision there is an interchange between the kinetic energy and the internal energy of the particle.

09324.title: elastic peak
09324.definition: Peak in the electron spectrum, produced by quasi-elastically scattered electrons detected by an electron spectrometer.

09174.title: elastic peak electron spectroscopy
09174.definition: Measurement method in which an electron spectrometer is used to measure the energy, intensity, and/or energy broadening distribution of quasi-elastically scattered electrons from a solid or liquid surface.

09246.title: elastic scattering cross section
09246.definition: Cross section for binary elastic scattering.

E01916.title: elastic scattering
E01916.definition: When in a molecular collision there is no transfer of energy among different degrees of freedom, there is said to be elastic scattering.

E01917.title: elastic scattering
E01917.definition: Radiation may be scattered by its transmission through a medium containing particles. If the scatter results in no significant change in the wavelength relative to the primary radiation it is called elastic scattering. In cases where the scattering centres are small compared to the wavelength of the radiation the elastic scattering is called Rayleigh scattering and Mie scattering if this condition is not fulfilled.

ET07598.title: elastically active network chain
ET07598.definition: Segment of a chain between two successive crosslinks in a polymer network that is long enough to show entropic elasticity.

14627.title: elasticity
14627.definition: Ability of a community to return to its prestressed condition.

08795.title: electret
08795.definition: Dielectric material with a permanent or quasi-permanent electric dipole.

E01923.title: electric charge
E01923.definition: Integral of the electric current over time. The smallest electric charge found on its own is the elementary charge, \(e\), the charge of a proton.

08796.title: electric conductor
08796.definition: Material that is able to transmit electric current.

E01928.title: electric current density
E01928.definition: A vector quantity the scalar product of which with the cross sectional area vector is equal to the electric current. By magnitude it is the electric current divided by the cross sectional area.

E01927.title: electric current
E01927.definition: Base quantity in the system of quantities upon which SI is based.

E01929.title: electric dipole moment
E01929.definition: Vector quantity, the vector product of which with the electric field strength, \(E\), of a homogeneous field is equal to the torque. \(T=p\times E\). The direction of the dipole moment is from the negative to the positive charge.

08469.title: electric discharge
08469.definition: Transmission of electrical current by a plasma in an applied electric field through a normally non-conducting medium.

E01930.title: electric displacement
E01930.definition: Product of the permittivity and electric field strength.

08797.title: electric drift
08797.definition: Oriented flow of otherwise randomly moving charge carriers induced by an applied external electric field.

E01931.title: electric field
E01931.definition: Force acting on a charge divided by the charge.

E01932.title: electric mobility
E01932.definition: Speed of ions divided by the electric field strength in the phase concerned.

E01933.title: electric polarizability
E01933.definition: Tensor quantity relating the induced electric dipole moment, \(p_{\rm{i}}\), to the applied electric field strength, \(E\), \(p_{\rm{i}}=\alpha \ E\).

E01934.title: electric potential difference
E01934.definition: Difference in the potentials of electrodes on the right and left of a galvanic cell. When \(\Delta V\) is positive, positive charge flows from left to right through the cell.

E01935.title: electric potential
E01935.definition: At a point, the work required to bring a charge from infinity to that point in the electric field divided by the charge.

E01936.title: electric resistance
E01936.definition: To direct current, the potential difference divided by the current when there is no electromotive force in the conductor.

E01938.title: electric sector
E01938.definition: An arrangement of two conducting sheets forming a capactor and giving a radial electrostatic field which is used to deflect and focus ion beams of different energies. The capacitor may, for example, be cylindrical, spherical or toroidal.

08591.title: electrical anharmonicity
08591.definition: Influence of terms that are of \(2^{\rm{nd}}\) and higher order in the normal coordinate \(Q\) in the expansion of the electric dipole moment.

E01918.title: electrical arc
E01918.definition: A self-sustaining electrical discharge between at least two electrodes, characterized by a comparatively small cathode fall voltage, a low burning voltage and a relatively high current density. The burning voltage of an arc is the voltage across the electrode gap during an arc discharge.

14008.title: electrical double layer
14008.definition: Array of charged species and oriented dipoles existing at a solid-solution interface. The solid may be a metal or a semiconductor. Double refers to the fact that the surface charge and its counter charge at the solution side are included.

08592.title: electrical harmonicity
08592.definition: Influence of the linear term, \(\Sigma_{k} (\partial \boldsymbol{\mu}/\partial Q_{k}) Q_{k}\), in the expansion of the electric dipole moment. \(Q\) is the normal coordinate.

E01921.title: electrical hygrometer
E01921.definition: A hygrometer whose sensitive element has electrical properties which vary with the humidity of the gas which traverses the hygrometer.

ET07205.title: electrically conducting polymer
ET07205.definition: Polymeric material that exhibits bulk electric conductivity.

08798.title: electrically conducting polymer composite
08798.definition: Composite composed of a non-conducting polymer matrix in which irregular powdered or fibrous particles of an electrically conducting material are evenly dispersed in an amount exceeding the percolation threshold for electric conductivity and so the composite exhibits electric conductivity close to that of the conducting filler.

E01939.title: electrified interphase
E01939.definition: An interphase between phases containing free charged components which are usually accumulated or depleted in the surface region thus giving rise to net charges on the phase. This definition includes the special case when the net charge on each of the phases reduces to zero. Charged components may or may not cross the interface between two phases, so that interphases may be divided into the limiting types unpolarizable and polarizable, respectively. Ideally unpolarizable interphases are those for which the exchange of common charged particles between the phases proceeds unhindered. Ideally polarizable interphases are those for which there are no common components between the phases or the exchange of these is hindered. This condition may arise as a result of the equilibrium conditions or from the kinetics of charge transfer and leads to an interphase which is impermeable to electric charge. Real interphases may approach more or less well one of these idealized cases. Polarisibility or non-polarisibility is not an absolute property of an interphase but depends on a number of conditions, e.g. time scale of the experiment.

ET06890.title: electro-dialysis
