ET06890.definition: Membrane-based separation process in which ions are driven through an ion-selective membrane under the influence of an electric field.

08807.title: electro-optic effect
08807.definition: Change in the optical properties of a material in response to a change in an external electric field strength.

08594.title: electro-optic parameter
08594.definition: Characteristic quantity used in the analysis of absolute infrared intensity data chosen on the assumption that the electric dipole moment of the molecule can be described as the vector sum of bond dipole moments.

ET06891.title: electro-osmosis
ET06891.definition: Process in which water is transported across the thickness of an anion- exchange or cation-exchange membrane under an applied electric field.

ET06922.title: electro-osmotic hold-up time
ET06922.definition: Time required for a liquid in a capillary to move due to electro-osmosis through the effective length of the capillary, \(L_{\rm{eff}}\). This time is usually measured as the migration time of a neutral compound, called an electro-osmotic flow marker which is assumed to have an electro-osmotic mobility that is negligible compared to that of the analyte.

ET06923.title: electro-osmotic mobility
ET06923.definition: Electro-osmotic velocity divided by electric field (strength) \[\mu _{\rm{eo}}=\frac{\nu _{\rm{eo}}}{E}\]

E02017.title: electro-osmotic pressure
E02017.definition: The pressure difference \(\Delta p\) across the membrane, plug, etc., needed just to stop electro-osmotic volume flow. \(\Delta p\) is positive if the higher pressure is on the high potential side.

E02019.title: electro-osmotic volume flow
E02019.definition: The volume flow per unit time per unit field strength through the whole plug.

E01940.title: electroactive substance
E01940.definition: In voltammetry and related techniques, a substance that undergoes a change of oxidation state, or the breaking or formation of chemical bonds, in a charge-transfer step. If an electroactive substance B is formed, in the solution or electrode, by a chemical reaction from another substance C, the substance C should be called the precursor of B. In potentiometry with ion-selective electrodes, a material containing, or in ion-exchange equilibrium with, the sensed ion. The electroactive substance is often incorporated in an inert matrix such as poly(vinyl chloride) or silicone rubber.

E01941.title: electrocapillarity
E01941.definition: The dependence of the interfacial tension on the electrical state of the interphase.

E01942.title: electrocapillary equation
E01942.definition: A form of the Gibbs adsorption equation which includes an expression of the phenomenon of electrocapillarity: \[s\ \mathrm{d}T- \tau \ \mathrm{d}p+\mathrm{d}\gamma +\sigma ^{\alpha }\ \mathrm{d}E+\sum \mathit{\Gamma }_{j}\ \mathrm{d}\mu _{j}=0\] where \(s\) is the surface excess of entropy of unit area of interphase, \(T\) is the temperature, \(\tau \) is the thickness or excess volume of unit area of the interphase, \(p\) is the external pressure, \(\gamma \) is the interfacial tension, \(\sigma ^{\alpha }\) is the free surface charge density on phase \(\alpha \) (areal amount of charge on the surface of phase \(\alpha \)), \(E\) is the generalized potential, \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{j}\) is the surface excess, \(\mu _{j}\) is the chemical potential and \(j\) is an electrically neutral component of one or other of the phases; the sum is over all the components but one in each phase.

09094.title: electrocatalysis
09094.definition: Detection principle for a chemically modified electrode (CME) in which a charge transfer reaction between a CME and analyte proceeds at a lower overpotential than at the bare electrode. Usually, the effect of electrocatalysis is also an increase of faradaic current.

09071.title: electrochemical biosensor
09071.definition: Electrochemical sensor that has a biological recognition element.

09058.title: electrochemical cell
09058.definition: System that consists of at least two electron conductors (electrodes) in contact with ionic conductors (electrolytes).

09059.title: electrochemical constants
09059.definition: In May 2019, certain fundamental constants that had been measured in SI units have had their numerical values fixed, with no uncertainty, thus defining the units. Of importance to electroanalytical chemistry are the values of the Boltzmann constant, the elementary charge, and the Avogadro constant. These are given in the table below, with calculated values of the Faraday constant (\(F = e·N_{\rm{A}}\)) and gas constant (\(R = k\cdot\!N_{\rm{A}}\)).

09170.title: electrochemical detection in flowing systems
09170.definition: Electrochemical techniques (potentiometry, amperometry, voltammetry, coulometry, conductimetry) used for analyte detection in flowing systems.

E01943.title: electrochemical detector
E01943.definition: An electrochemical cell which responds to certain substances in the carrier gas eluting from the column. The electrochemical process may be an oxidation, reduction or a change in conductivity.

09168.title: electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
09168.definition: Electrochemical measurement method of the complex impedance of an electrochemical system as a function of the frequency of a small amplitude (normally \(\pu{5 to 10 mV}\)) sinusoidal voltage perturbation superimposed on a fixed value of applied potential or on the open circuit potential.

E01944.title: electrochemical method of detection
E01944.definition: A method in which either current or potential is measured during an electrochemical reaction. The gas or liquid containing the trace impurity to be analysed is sent through an electrochemical cell containing a liquid or solid electrolyte and in which an electrochemical reaction specific to the impurity takes place.

09162.title: electrochemical piezoelectric microgravimetry
09162.definition: Electrogravimetry using an electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance.

E01945.title: electrochemical potential
E01945.definition: Of a substance in a specified phase, the partial molar Gibbs energy of the substance at the specified electric potential.

09163.title: electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance
09163.definition: Electrochemical cell in which the working electrode is located on one surface of a piezoelectric quartz crystal, the oscillation frequency of which is measured.

09072.title: electrochemical sensor
09072.definition: Measuring system in which the response to an electrochemical reaction is converted, via a suitable transducer, into a measurable electrical signal.

14127.title: electrochemiluminescence assay
14127.definition: Assay in which light emitted by electrogenerated luminescence is detected and used to quantify a label, e.g., ruthenium(II) tris-(bipyridine), on one of the two assay binding components.

13814.title: electroclinic polymer
13814.definition: Polymer with constitutional units that are susceptible to a change in orientation under the influence of an electric field that causes the system to have induced polarity.

11742.title: electroconvulsive therapy
11742.definition: Therapeutic intervention in which seizures are electrically induced in patients with the aim of providing relief from a specific mental illness.

E01948.title: electrocyclic reaction
E01948.definition: A molecular rearrangement that involves the formation of a $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bond}$ between the termini of a fully conjugated linear $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$ system (or a linear fragment of a $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$ system) and a decrease by one in the number of , or the reverse of that process. For example:  The stereochemistry of such a process is termed 'conrotatory' or antarafacial if the substituents at the interacting termini of the conjugated system both rotate in the same sense, e.g.  or 'disrotatory' (or suprafacial) if one terminus rotates in a clockwise and the other in a counter-clockwise sense, e.g.

09060.title: electrode
09060.definition:
Electron conductor in an electrochemical cell connected to the external circuit.
Half-cell consisting of at least one electron conductor and at least one ionic conductor (electrolyte).

09114.title: electrode array
09114.definition: Assembly of linked electrodes (usually microelectrodes, ultramicroelectrodes or nanoelectrodes) acting as a single electrode.

09073.title: electrode coverage density
09073.definition: Amount of a chemical modifier at an electrode surface per unit area.

E01952.title: electrode current density
E01952.definition:
If the charging current is negligible, in the case of a single electrode reaction, the electrode current density (\(m{c.d.}\)) of the electric current flowing through the electrode is related to the flux density of a species B by the equation: \[j = n\ 
u _{m{B}}^{-1}\ F\ \left(N_{m{B}}ight)_{e}\] where \(\left(N_{m{B}}ight)_{e}\) is the normal component of the vector \(N_{m{B}}\) at the electrode-solution interface, \(n\) is the charge number of the electrode reaction and \(
u _{m{B}}\) is the stoichiometric number of species B. The ratio \( rac{n}{
u _{m{B}}}\) is to be taken as positive if the species B is consumed in a cathodic reaction or produced in an anodic reaction. Otherwise it is to be taken as negative. With the convention that the normal distance vector points into the electrolytic solution, a cathodic current is then negative, an anodic current positive.

E01956.title: electrode potential
E01956.definition: Electromotive force of a cell in which the electrode on the left is a standard hydrogen electrode and the electrode on the right is the electrode in question.

E01959.title: electrode process
E01959.definition: The totality of changes occurring at or near a single electrode during the passage of current.

E01960.title: electrode reaction
E01960.definition: For an electrode process at a given potential the current is controlled by the kinetics of a number of steps which include the transport of reactants to and from the interface and the interfacial reaction itself. The latter, which is called the electrode reaction, must always include at least one elementary step in which charge is transferred from one phase to the other, but may also involve purely chemical steps within the interfacial region.

E01961.title: electrode reaction rate constants

E01950.title: electrodecantation
E01950.definition: Electrodialysis may lead to local differences in concentration and density. Under the influence of gravity these density differences lead to large scale separation of sols of high and of low (often vanishingly low) concentrations. This process is called electrodecantation.

E01955.title: electrodeposition
E01955.definition: The deposition of dissolved or suspended material by an electric field on an electrode. (Includes electro-crystallization).

11743.title: electroencephalogram
11743.definition: Test or record of brain electrical activity detected by electroencephalography.

11744.title: electroencephalography
11744.definition: Recording of electrical activity from different parts of the brain.

E01965.title: electrofuge
E01965.definition: A leaving group that does not carry away the bonding electron pair. For example, in the nitration of benzene by $\ce{NO2^{+}}$, $\ce{H^{+}}$ is the electrofuge. The adjective of electrofuge is electrofugal.

E01966.title: electrogenerated chemiluminescence
E01966.definition: Luminescence produced by electrode reactions. Also called electroluminescence or electrochemiluminescence.

E01967.title: electrographite
E01967.definition: A synthetic graphite made by electrical heating of graphitizable carbon.

09164.title: electrogravimetry
09164.definition: Gravimetry in which the material to be weighed is obtained by electrochemical reaction.

08801.title: electroinjection
08801.definition: Process of charge carrier injection induced by an applied external electric field.

09919.title: electrokinetic chromatography
09919.definition: Separation method based on a combination of electrophoresis and interactions of the analytes with additives (e.g. surfactants), which form a dispersed phase moving at a different speed (velocity). In order to achieve separation, either the analytes or this secondary phase should be charged.

09920.title: electrokinetic injection
09920.definition: Injection of the analytical sample by applying a potential across the sample and capillary and using the electroosmotic flow to draw an aliquot into the end of the capillary tube. The sample is then replaced by the running electrolyte for the separation to take place.

E01968.title: electrokinetic potential
E01968.definition: Potential drop across the mobile part of the double layer, that is responsible for electrokinetic phenomena. \(\zeta \) is positive if the potential increases from the bulk of the liquid phase towards the interface. In calculating the electrokinetic potential from electrokinetic phenomena it is often asumed that the liquid adhering to the solid wall and the mobile liquid are separated by a sharp shear plane. As long as there is no reliable information on the values of the permittivity and the viscosity in the electrical double layer close to the interface, the calculation of the electrokinetic potential from electrokinetic experiments remains open to criticism. It is therefore essential to indicate in all cases which equations have been used in the calculation of \(\zeta \). It can be shown, however, that for the same assumptions about the permittivity and viscosity all electrokinetic phenomena must give the same value for the electrokinetic potential.

ET07171.title: electroluminescent polymer
ET07171.definition: Polymeric material that shows luminescence when an electric current passes through it such that charge carriers can combine at luminescent sites to give rise to electronically excited states of luminescent groups or molecules.

09061.title: electrolyte
09061.definition:
Conducting medium in which the flow of electric current is accompanied by the movement of ions.
Substance that provides ions on dissolution in a solvent or on melting.

09062.title: electrolytic cell
09062.definition: Electrochemical cell in which electrical energy is converted into chemical energy.

E01972.title: electrolytic hygrometer
E01972.definition: Hygrometer using a hygroscopic substance (for example, diphosphorus pentaoxide, $\ce{P2O5}$) which is transformed into an electrolyte (phosphoric acid, $\ce{H3PO4}$) in contact with the moisture in the gas. The electrolyte (phosphoric acid) is electrolysed continuously and the electrolysis current is measured. At a constant flow of the gas to be analysed, the electrolysis current is a linear function of the water concentration.

08802.title: electromagnetic field
08802.definition: Physical field composed of two interconnected, mutually orthogonal fields, an electric field and a magnetic field, which mediates interactions of charged, dipolar and multipolar objects.

08803.title: electromagnetic field responsive polymer
08803.definition: Polymer showing a noticeable response of its physical or chemical properties during or upon exposure to an electromagnetic field or one of its components: electric field and magnetic field.

08242.title: electromagnetic radiation
08242.definition: Flow of energy through space propagated as synchronized sinusoidal waves of the electric field, \(\boldsymbol{E}\), and the magnetic field \(\boldsymbol{H}\).

08243.title: electromagnetic transition
08243.definition: Transition accompanied by the emission or absorption of a photon.

10278.title: electromembrane extraction
10278.definition: Hollow-fibre liquid-phase microextraction in which the extraction is driven by an electrical potential sustained between the sample solution and the acceptor phase, separated by a supported liquid membrane.Typical experimental arrangement for electromembrane extraction of cations (anions extracted by reversing the polarity). SLM, supported liquid membrane in the form of a porous hollow fiber with solvent-filled pores.

E01973.title: electromeric effect
E01973.definition: A molecular polarizability effect occurring by an intramolecular electron displacement (sometimes called the 'conjugative mechanism' and, previously, the 'tautomeric mechanism') characterized by the substitution of one electron pair for another within the same atomic octet of electrons. It can be indicated by curved arrow symbolizing the displacement of electron pairs, as in:  which represents the hypothetical electron shift  The term has been deemed obsolescent or even obsolete (see mesomeric effect, resonance effect). It has long been custom to use phrases such as 'enhanced substituent resonance effect' which imply the operation of the electromeric effect, without using the term, and various modern theoretical treatments parametrize the response of substituents to 'electronic demand', which amounts to considering the electromeric effect together with the inductomeric effect.

ET06758.title: electromigration
ET06758.definition: The transport of particles under the influence of an electric field.

E01974.title: electromotive force
E01974.definition: Energy supplied by a source divided by the electric charge transported through the source. For a galvanic cell it is equal to the electric potential difference for zero current through the cell.

11745.title: electromyography
11745.definition: Recording of the electrical activity of muscle, or its representation as a visual display or audible signal, using electrodes attached to the skin or inserted into a muscle.

E01975.title: electron
E01975.definition: Elementary particle not affected by the strong force having a spin quantum number \(\frac{1}{2}\), a negative elementary charge and a rest mass of \(0.000\ 548\ 579\ 903(13)\ \rm{u}\).

E01976.title: electron acceptor
E01976.definition: A substance to which an electron may be transferred; for example 1,4-dinitrobenzene or the dication 1,1'-dimethyl-4,4'-bipyridyldiium.

E01977.title: electron affinity
E01977.definition: Energy required to detach an electron from the singly charged negative ion (energy for the process ). The equivalent more common definition is the energy released (\(E_{\rm{initial}} - E_{\rm{final}}\)) when an additional electron is attached to a neutral atom or molecule.

E01979.title: electron attachment
E01979.definition: The transfer of an electron to a molecular entity, resulting in a molecular entity of (algebraically) increased negative charge. It is not an attachment.

ET07367.title: electron back-transfer
ET07367.definition: Thermal inversion of excited-state electron transfer restoring the donor and acceptor in their original oxidation state. In using this term one should also specify the resulting electronic state of the donor and acceptor. This term is preferred to back electron-transfer.

ET07615.title: electron beam curing
ET07615.definition: Curing induced by electron beam irradiation.

09505.title: electron beam lithography
09505.definition: Lithography performed by exposing a resist to a beam of electrons.

09566.title: electron beam resist
09566.definition: Resist optimized for use under electron beam irradiation.

E01980.title: electron capture
E01980.definition: A nuclear transformation in which the nucleus captures an orbital electron. Often the shell, from which the electron is captured, is indicated. (K-, L-, etc.).

E01981.title: electron capture detector
E01981.definition: A small radioactive source containing $\ce{^{3}H}$ or $\ce{^{63}Ni}$ ionizes the molecules of the carrier gas (nitrogen or argon–methane), and a potential difference creates a small current. This current is reduced when an electronegative substance (such as a halocarbon) is introduced. The reduction in current is a measure of the concentration of the electronegative substance. The detection limit (threshold) varies greatly according to the substances to be analysed and can reach a mixing ratio of \(10^{-12}\). The linear dynamic range may be \(10^{4}\) but the maximum measuring value generally lies below \(1\ \rm{ppmv}\).

E01982.title: electron charge
E01982.definition: The negative electric charge which appears on the electron or univalent ions [ \(1.602\times 10^{-19}\) coulombs or \(4.803\times 10^{-10}\) electrostatic units (\(\mathrm{esu}\))].

E01984.title: electron correlation
E01984.definition: The adjustment of electron motion to the instantaneous (as opposed to time-averaged) positions of all the electrons in a molecular entity.

E01986.title: electron density
E01986.definition: If \(P(x,\,y,\,z)\ \rm{d}x\ \rm{d}y\ \rm{d}z\) is the probability of finding an electron in the volume element \(\rm{d}x\ \rm{d}y\ \rm{d}z\) at the point of a molecular entity with coordinates \(x,\,y,\,z\), then \(P(x,\,y,\,z)\) is the electron density at this point. For many purposes (e.g. X-ray scattering, forces on atoms) the system behaves exactly as if the electrons were spread out into a continuously distributed charge. The term has frequently been wrongly applied to negative charge population.

ET07024.title: electron density function
ET07024.definition: The electron probability distribution function, \(\rho \), defined as \[\rho (\mathbf{r}) = n\ \int \Psi ^{\rm{*}}\left[\mathbf{r}(1),\mathbf{r}(2)\,\rm{...}\,\mathbf{r}(n)\right]\ \Psi \left[\mathbf{r}(1),\mathbf{r}(2)\,\rm{...}\,\mathbf{r}(n)\right]\rm{d}\mathbf{r}(2)\,\rm{...}\,\rm{d}\mathbf{r}(n)\] where \(\Psi \) is an electronic wave-function and integration is made over the coordinates of all but the first electron of \(n\). The physical interpretation of the electron density function is that \(\rho \ \mathrm{d}\mathbf{\mathbf{r}}\) gives the probability of finding an electron in a volume element \(\mathrm{d}\mathbf{\mathbf{r}}\), i.e., electron density in this volume.

E01987.title: electron detachment
E01987.definition: The reverse of an electron attachment.

E01988.title: electron donor
E01988.definition: A molecular entity that can transfer an electron to another molecular entity, or to the corresponding chemical species.[obsolete] A Lewis base. This use is discouraged.

08244.title: electron emission spectrometry
08244.definition: Measurement principle of spectrometry for the study of electrons emitted by atoms.

09325.title: electron energy analyser
09325.definition: Measuring instrument for measuring the number of electrons, or an intensity proportional to that number, as a function of the electron kinetic energy.

E01991.title: electron energy
E01991.definition: The potential difference through which electrons are accelerated before they are used to bring about electron ionization.

08593.title: electron energy loss spectroscopy
08593.definition: Measurement method of vibrational spectroscopy in which a constant-energy beam of electrons passes through or is reflected from a sample and the energy distribution in the transmitted or reflected beam is analysed to give a spectrum of number of electrons against electron energy loss.

09326.title: electron energy loss spectrum
09326.definition: Energy spectrum of electrons from a nominally monoenergetic source emitted after inelastic interactions with the sample, often exhibiting peaks due to specific inelastic loss processes (see characteristic electron energy losses and plasmon).

09247.title: electron flooding
09247.definition: Irradiation of a sample with low-energy electrons in order to change or stabilize the charging potential.

09327.title: electron inelastic mean free path
09327.definition: Average distance that an electron with a given energy travels between successive inelastic collisions.

E01999.title: electron ionization
E01999.definition: This is the term used to describe ionization of any species by electrons. The process may, for example, be written:   for atoms or molecules: \[\rm{M} + e \rightarrow \rm{M}^{+\cdot } + 2e\]   for radicals: \[\rm{M}^{\cdot}  + e \rightarrow \rm{M}^{+} + 2e\]   The term 'electron impact' should not be used.

E02000.title: electron jump
E02000.definition: The term can be applied to a reaction in which there is an electron transfer with the formation of an ionic intermediate.

E02001.title: electron kinetic energy
E02001.definition: The difference between the energy of the exciting photon and the ionization energy.

08470.title: electron number density
08470.definition: Number of free electrons in vapour phase per volume unit.

09063.title: electron number of an electrochemical reaction
09063.definition: Number of electrons transferred in a charge transfer reaction between an electrode and a single entity (ion, radical-ion, or molecule) of an electroactive substance, whose identity must be specified.

E02005.title: electron paramagnetic resonance
E02005.definition: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and/or electron spin resonance (ESR) is defined as the form of spectroscopy concerned with microwave-induced transitions between magnetic energy levels of electrons having a net spin and orbital angular momentum. The term electron paramagnetic resonance and the symbol EPR are preferred and should be used for primary indexing.

E02006.title: electron probe microanalysis
E02006.definition: General term for methods using bombardment of a solid specimen by electrons which generate a variety of signals providing the basis for a number of different analytical techniques.

E02007.title: electron probe X-ray microanalysis
E02007.definition: Any analytical technique which uses the excitation and evaluation of the characteristic X-ray spectrum of a solid specimen by a focused electron beam (typically of a diameter of less than \(1\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\)). Qualitative and quantitative X-ray analysis is the main feature of EPXMA. For obtaining supplementary information the secondary, back scattered and absorbed electrons are also frequently observed. Qualitative and quantitative X-ray analysis is, however, the main feature of EPXMA.

08166.title: electron pushing
08166.definition: Method using curly arrows for showing the formal movement of an electron pair (from a lone pair or a \(\upsigma\) or \(\ce{\uppi\ bond}\)) or of an unpaired electron, in order to generate additional resonance forms or to denote a chemical reaction.

E02008.title: electron rest mass
E02008.definition: Atomic fundamental physical constant used as atomic unit of mass, \(m_{\rm{e}} = \pu{9.1093897(54)E-31 kg}\).

09328.title: electron retardation
09328.definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, measurement method for kinetic energy distribution by retarding the emitted electrons before or within the electron energy analyser.

09329.title: electron spectrometer
09329.definition: Measuring system, the essential part of which is an electron energy analyser.

E02009.title: electron spectroscopy for chemical analysis
E02009.definition: Type of spectroscopy involving the measurement of the kinetic energy of electrons emitted by chemical substances usually as a result of excitation by monochromatic X-rays.

E02010.title: electron stopping power
E02010.definition: When a beam of electrons strikes a target or specimen there are three ways in which the electrons may lose energy (low energy collisions, X-ray production, and formation of a spectral continuum). The average energy loss per unit distance travelled along the electron path is called electron stopping power, \(\frac{\rm{d}E}{\rm{d}x}\).

E02011.title: electron transfer
E02011.definition: The transfer of an electron from one molecular entity to another, or between two localized sites in the same molecular entity.

E02013.title: electron transfer photosensitization
E02013.definition: Photochemical process in which a reaction of a non-absorbing substrate is induced by electron transfer (not energy transfer) with an excited light-absorbing sensitizer. The overall process must be such that the sensitizer is recycled. Depending on the action of the excited sensitizer as electron donor or acceptor the sensitization is called reductive or oxidative.

08806.title: electron tunneling
08806.definition: Quantum mechanical effect of passing an electron through a potential energy barrier separating two energy equivalent regions.

E02015.title: electron work function
E02015.definition: The minimum work needed to extract electrons from the Fermi level of a metal M across a surface carrying no net charge. It is equal to the sum of the potential energy and the kinetic Fermi energy taken with the reverse sign: \[\mathit{\Phi}^{M} = -(V_{\rm{e}} + \varepsilon_{\rm{e}}^{F})\] where \(V_{\rm{e}}\) is the potential energy for electrons in metals and \(\varepsilon_{\rm{e}}^{\rm{F}}\) is the kinetic energy of electrons at the Fermi level.

09506.title: electron-beam direct-write lithography
09506.definition: Electron beam lithography whereby the pattern is written directly onto the photoresist without the use of a mask.

ET07022.title: electron-counting rules
ET07022.definition: Rules establishing correspondence between the topology of a molecular structure and the number of electrons which may be placed into its bonding molecular orbitals. In the origin of various electron-counting rules lies a general assumption that the completeness of the valence electron shell of a molecular entity belonging to a certain structural type serves as the major criterion of structural stability.

E01985.title: electron-deficient bond
E01985.definition: A single bond between adjacent atoms that is formed by less than two electrons, as in $\ce{B2H6}$:  The $\ce{B–H–B}$ bonds are called 'two-electron three-centre bonds'.

ET07023.title: electron-deficient compounds
ET07023.definition: Molecules or ions that contain too few electrons to allow their bonding to be described exclusively in terms of two-center, two-electron, i.e., covalent, bonds. Such molecules or certain fragments in these are often held together by the multicenter bonds.

08804.title: electron-deficient molecule
08804.definition: Molecule that has fewer valence electrons than required for forming normal two-center two-electron chemical bonds and thus contains multicenter chemical bonds.

08805.title: electron-rich molecule
08805.definition: Molecule that has more valence electrons than is needed to link its atoms by single covalent bonds.

E02012.title: electron-transfer catalysis
E02012.definition: The term indicates a sequence of reactions such as shown in equations (1)–(3), leading from $\ce{A}$ to $\ce{B}$:  \[\rm{A} + \rm{e}^{-} \rightarrow \rm{A}^{\cdot- }\]$\quad$(1)\[\rm{A}^{\cdot- } \rightarrow \rm{B}^{\cdot- }\]$\quad$(2)\[\rm{B}^{\cdot- } + \rm{A} \rightarrow \rm{B} + \rm{A}^{\cdot- }\]$\quad$(3) An analogous sequence involving radical cations ($\ce{A^{+.}}$, $\ce{B^{+.}}$) is also observed. The most notable example of electron-transfer catalysis is the \(\rm{S}_{\rm{RN}}1\) (or \(\rm{T}+\rm{D}_{\rm{N}}+\rm{A}_{\rm{N}}\)) reaction of aromatic halides. The term has its origin in a suggested analogy to acid-base catalysis, with the electron instead of the proton. However, there is a difference between the two catalytic mechanisms, since the electron is not a true catalyst, but rather behaves as the initiator of a chain reaction. 'Electron-transfer induced chain reaction' is a more appropriate term for the situation described by equations (1)–(3).

09742.title: electron-transfer dissociation
09742.definition: Ion fragmentation technique in mass spectrometry-driven proteomics based on the transfer of low energy electrons to the molecules selected for fragmentation.

08994.title: electron-transfer ring-opening metathesis polymerization
08994.definition: Ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) proceeding through one-electron redox processes in the absence of a metal carbene initiator.

09743.title: electron-transfer/higher-energy collision dissociation
09743.definition: Ion fragmentation technique in mass spectrometry-driven proteomics that is a combination of electron-transfer dissociation (ETD) and higher-energy collision dissociation (HCD) in Kingdon trap instruments (Orbitrap™).

E01990.title: electronegativity
E01990.definition: Concept introduced by L. Pauling as the power of an atom to attract electrons to itself. There are several definitions of this quantity. According to Mulliken it is the average of the ionization energy and electron affinity of an atom, but more frequently a relative scale due to Pauling is used where dimensionless relative electronegativity differences are defined on the basis of bond dissociation energies, \(E_{\rm{d}}\), expressed in electronvolts: \[\chi _{\rm{r}}\left(\rm{A}\right)- \chi _{\rm{r}}\left(\rm{B}\right)=\left(\rm{eV}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\ \sqrt{E_{\rm{d}}\left(\rm{AB}\right)- \frac{1}{2}\ [E_{\rm{d}}\left(\rm{AA}\right)+E_{\rm{d}}\left(\rm{BB}\right)]}\] The scale is chosen so as to make the relative electronegativity of hydrogen \(\chi _{\rm{r}} = 2.1\). The sign of the square root was chosen intuitively by Pauling.

11746.title: electroneurography
11746.definition: Non-invasive method used to examine the integrity and conductivity of a peripheral nerve, in which a brief electrical stimulation is given to the nerve at one point, while at the same time the induced electrical activity (compound action potentials) is recorded at another point of the nerve’s distribution and the interval is displayed on a video monitor.

E01992.title: electroneutrality principle
E01992.definition: The principle expresses the fact that all pure substances carry a net charge of zero.

ET07025.title: electronic chemical potential
ET07025.definition: The quantity that measures the escaping tendency of electrons from a species in its ground state. It is the negative of the absolute electronegativity.

E01996.title: electronic effect of substituents: symbols and signs
E01996.definition: The inductive effect has universally been represented by the symbol \(\rm{I}\). This is now commonly taken to include both through-bonds and through-space transmission, but \(\rm{I}\) is also used specifically for through-bonds transmission; through-space transmission is then symbolized as \(\rm{F}\) (for field effect). The symbols for the influence of substituents exerted through electron delocalization have variously been \(\rm{M}\) (mesomeric), \(\rm{E}\) (electromeric), \(\rm{T}\) (tautomeric), \(\rm{C}\) (conjugative), K (konjugativ) and \(\rm{R}\) (resonance). Since the present fashion is to use the term resonance effect, \(\rm{R}\) is the most commonly used symbol, although \(\rm{M}\) is still seen quite often. Both the possible sign conventions are in use. The Ingold sign convention associates electronegativity (relative to hydrogen atom) with a negative sign, electropositivity with a positive sign. Thus the nitro group is described as electronwithdrawing by virtue of its \(-\rm{I}\) and \(-\rm{M}\) effects; chloro is described as a \(-\rm{I}\), \(+\,\rm{M}\) substituent, etc. For correlation analysis and linear free-energy relationships this convention has been found inconvenient, for it is in contradiction to the sign convention for polar substituent constants ($\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}constants}$). Authors concerned with these fields often avoid this contradiction by adopting the opposite sign convention originally associated with Robinson, for electronic effects. This practice is almost always associated with the use of R for the electron delocalization effect: thus the nitro group is a \(+\,\rm{I}\), \(+\,\rm{R}\) substituent; chloro a \(+\,\rm{I}\), \(-\rm{R}\) substituent, etc.

E01997.title: electronic energy migration
E01997.definition: The movement of electronic excitation energy from one molecular entity to another of the same species, or from one part of a molecular entity to another of the same kind (e.g. excitation migration between the chromophores of an aromatic polymer). The migration can happen via radiative or radiationless processes.

08338.title: electronic reference to access in vivo concentrations
08338.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that generates an electronic signal in a nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometer which is detected simultaneously to the sample free induction decay during the acquisition.

ET07027.title: electronic stability
ET07027.definition: Unavailability of another electronic structure (different electronic state) of lower energy with the same number of electrons.

ET07026.title: electronic state
ET07026.definition: An arrangement allowed by the laws of quantum mechanics of electrons within an atom, molecule (or system of molecules).

09368.title: electronic stopping cross section
09368.definition: Stopping cross section arising from energy transfer to the electrons of the sample.

08245.title: electronic transition
08245.definition: Transition in an atom, ion, or molecule from an electronic energy level \(E_{1}\) to another energy level \(E_{2}\).

E01994.title: electronically excited state
E01994.definition: A state of an atom or molecular entity which has greater electronic energy than the ground state of the same entity.

09921.title: electroosmosis
09921.definition: Motion of a liquid through a capillary (or membrane or plug) because of the application of an electric field across the capillary (or membrane or plug).

09922.title: electroosmotic velocity
09922.definition: Effective length of the capillary (\(L_{\rm{eff}}\)) divided by the electroosmotic hold-up time (\(t_{\rm{eo}}\)). \[\boldsymbol{v}_{\rm{eo}} = L_{\rm{eff}}/t_{\rm{eo}}\]

09923.title: electroosmotic volume flow rate
09923.definition: Volume flow rate divided by electric field strength through the whole plug or capillary.

E02020.title: electrophile
E02020.definition: An electrophile (or electrophilic reagent) is a reagent that forms a bond to its reaction partner (the nucleophile) by accepting both bonding electrons from that reaction partner. An 'electrophilic substitution reaction' is a heterolytic reaction in which the reagent supplying the entering group acts as an electrophile. For example:  Electrophilic reagents are Lewis acids. 'Electrophilic catalysis' is catalysis by Lewis acids. The term 'electrophilic' is also used to designate the apparent polar character of certain radicals as inferred from their higher relative reactivities with reaction sites of higher electron density.

08986.title: electrophilic chain polymerization
08986.definition: Chain polymerization in which the active centres are electrophilic species.

08167.title: electrophilic substitution
08167.definition: Heterolytic reaction in which the entering group adds to a nucleophile and in which the leaving group, or electrofuge, relinquishes both electrons to its reaction partner, whereupon it becomes another potential electrophile.

E02021.title: electrophilicity
E02021.definition: The property of being electrophilic (see electrophile).The relative reactivity of an electrophilic reagent. (It is also sometimes referred to as 'electrophilic power'.) Qualitatively, the concept is related to Lewis acidity. However, whereas Lewis acidity is measured by relative equilibrium constants, electrophilicity is measured by relative rate constants for reactions of different electrophilic reagents towards a common substrate (usually involving attack at a carbon atom).

E02022.title: electrophoresis
E02022.definition: The motion of colloidal particles in an electric field. The term 'cataphoresis' should be abandoned.

E02024.title: electrophoretic mobility
E02024.definition: The observed rate of migration of a component (\(v\)) divided by electric field strength (\(E\)) in a given medium.

ET06925.title: electrophoretic velocity
ET06925.definition: The velocity of a charged analyte under the influence of an electric field relative to the background electrolyte. Also called rate of migration (in electrophoresis).

E02025.title: electrophotography
E02025.definition: Processes of photoimaging which are based on photo-induced changes of electric fields (photo-conductive or photo-electrostatic effects).

11747.title: electrophysiology
11747.definition: Study of the electrical properties of cells and tissues.

10643.title: electroporation
10643.definition: Means of introducing molecules into cells by transiently permeabilizing their membranes with brief electric field pulses.

11748.title: electroretinogram
11748.definition: Recording, with electrodes placed on the cornea or nearby skin, of the electrical activity of photoreceptors and other retinal cells in response to standardized, patterned stimuli with light and colour.

08809.title: electrorheological effect
08809.definition: Reversible change in the apparent viscosity of a liquid system such as suspension of polar or good polarizable microparticles in an oil, upon exposure of an electric field.

09744.title: electrospray ionisation
09744.definition: Soft ionisation technique in mass spectrometry-driven proteomics.

09184.title: electrospray laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry
09184.definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge quotient and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air via ablation by a focused pulsed laser while simultaneously directing an electrospray jet through the desorbed plume to enhance sample ionization.

09924.title: electrostacking
09924.definition: Methods that use differences in migration behaviour in spatially defined regions of the capillary of different field strengths (conductivities).

E02027.title: electrostatic filter
E02027.definition: Filters for which an electrostatic charge is applied to the filter element. A fibrous filter material is often pleated in between V-shaped supports consisting of electrostatically charged, metal rods which are insulated from the supporting frame.

E02028.title: electrostatic precipitator
E02028.definition: A device which separates particles from a gas stream by passing the carrier gas between pairs of electrodes across which a unidirectional, high-voltage potential is placed. The particles are charged before passing through the field and migrate to an oppositely charged electrode. These devices are very efficient collectors of small particles, and their use in removing particles from power plant plumes and in other industrial applications is widespread.

14396.title: electrostatic stabilisation
14396.definition: Stabilization of a colloid resulting from the mutual repulsion of the electrical double layers surrounding its particles.

14397.title: electrosteric stabilisation
14397.definition: Stabilization of a colloid that has both steric and electrostatic stabilization characteristics.

ET07368.title: electrostriction
ET07368.definition: Contraction of a dielectric in an electric-field gradient.

08471.title: electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy
08471.definition: Measurement method of atomic absorption spectroscopy in which the sample is atomized by an electrothermal atomizer.

E02029.title: electrothermal atomizer
E02029.definition: A device which is heated to the temperature required for analyte atomization by the passage of electrical current through its body. In open atomizers the sample vapour, together with analyte atoms, leaving the atomizer surface may move freely into the surrounding space. In confined atomizers the sample vapour is restricted by the atomizer wall except for the openings where the optical beam enters and leaves the atomizer and the sample introduction hole.

08472.title: electrothermal vaporization
08472.definition: Technique for sample introduction based on the use of a solid furnace heated at a controlled temperature to vaporize the sample prior to its introduction into an inductively-coupled plasma.

E02030.title: electroviscous effects
E02030.definition: For dispersions of charged particles, these are those components of the viscosity connected with the charge of the particles.

E02036.title: element effect
E02036.definition: The ratio of the rate constants of two reactions that differ only in the identity of the element of the atom in the leaving group, e.g. \(\frac{k_{\rm{Br}}}{k_{\rm{Cl}}}\). As for isotope effects, a ratio of unity is regarded as a 'null effect'.

09248.title: elemental map
09248.definition: Surface map using signals proportional to the amount of an element present in a sample.

09330.title: elemental relative sensitivity factor
09330.definition: In dynamic secondary-ion mass spectrometry, coefficient for an element by which the measured intensity of a mass peak for that element, divided by the measured intensity of a mass peak for the matrix, is multiplied to yield the atomic concentration of the element present in the sample.

E02032.title: elementary charge
E02032.definition: The elementary charge, \(e\), is one of seven fixed constants defining the International System of Units, the SI, with \(e = \pu{1.602176634E-19 C}\). The elementary charge \(e\) corresponds to a coupling strength of the electromagnetic force via the fine-structure constant and is considered as a fundamental constant of nature.

E02033.title: elementary entity
E02033.definition: Any countable object or event, but usually a molecule, an ion or a specified group of atoms.

E02034.title: elementary particle
E02034.definition: A particle in which, at the present, no structure can be observed at moderate energies.

E02035.title: elementary reaction
E02035.definition: A reaction for which no reaction intermediates have been detected or need to be postulated in order to describe the chemical reaction on a molecular scale. An elementary reaction is assumed to occur in a single step and to pass through a single transition state.

11749.title: elevated plus maze
11749.definition: Stage with four orthogonal side arms elevated above the floor, where two opposite arms have sidewalls and the other two arms have no walls; used as research tool for anxiety.

13109.title: elicitation
13109.definition: Production of a cell-mediated or antibody-mediated allergic response by exposure of a sensitized individual to an allergen.

E02038.title: elimination
E02038.definition: The reverse of an addition reaction or transformation. In an elimination two groups (called eliminands) are lost most often from two different centres (1/2/elimination or 1/3/elimination, etc.) with concomitant formation of an unsaturation in the molecule (double bond, triple bond) or formation of a new ring. If the groups are lost from a single centre ($\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}elimination}$, 1/1/elimination) the resulting product is a carbene or a 'carbene analogue'.

15656.title: elimination half life
15656.definition: Period taken for the plasma concentration of a substance to decrease by half.

16238.title: elimination rate
16238.definition: Derivative with respect to time of the concentration or amount of a substance in the body, or a part thereof, resulting from elimination.

15657.title: eliminator
15657.definition: Substance that contributes to the elimination of a poison from an organism.

15182.title: elixir
15182.definition: Sweet (often colored) dilute alcohol-based, 'hydroalcoholic', liquid used in the compounding of drugs to be taken by mouth in order to improve palatability.

09197.title: ellipsometry
09197.definition: Measurement method for the thickness of transparent surface films and layers and for the refractive index of a reflecting material.

08595.title: ellipticity
08595.definition: Degree to which linearly polarized incident electromagnetic radiation becomes elliptically polarized in an absorbing optically active medium. \[\tan\;\psi = (E_{\rm{R}} - E_{\rm{L}})/(E_{\rm{R}} + E_{\rm{L}}) = \tanh (k^{\rm{L}} - k^{\rm{R}})\pi l/\lambda\] where \(E_{\rm{R}}\) and \(E_{\rm{L}}\) are the electric vectors of right and left circularly polarized radiation, \(k^{\rm{L}}\) and \(k^{\rm{R}}\) are the absorption indices of the sample for left and right circularly polarized radiation, \(\lambda\) is the wavelength of the radiation and \(l\) is the path-length through the medium.

E02039.title: eluate
E02039.definition: The effluent from a chromatographic bed emerging when elution is carried out.

E02040.title: eluent
E02040.definition: The liquid or gas entering a chromatographic bed and used to effect a separation by elution.

E02041.title: elute
E02041.definition: To chromatograph by elution chromatography. This term is preferred to the term 'develop', which has been used in paper chromatography and in thin-layer chromatography. The process of elution may continue until the components have left the chromatographic bed.

E02046.title: elution chromatography
E02046.definition: A procedure for chromatographic separation in which the mobile phase is passed through the chromatographic bed after the application of the sample.

E02047.title: elution curve
E02047.definition: A chromatogram or part of a chromatogram recorded when elution techniques are used.

09943.title: elution mode
09943.definition: Method of introduction of the mobile phase (upper or lower) into the rotating coil (from the head or the tail). Of four combinations, only two elution modes should be used in high-speed counter-current chromatography, i.e. either the lower phase from the head toward the tail or the upper phase from the tail toward the head.

10240.title: elution solvent
10240.definition: Small volume of strong solvent used to displace target analytes from the sorbent bed.

12281.title: elution time
12281.definition: Time elapsed from the injection of the sample into a chromatography bed to the recording of a specified signal of the detector due to the sample having passed through the bed.

12282.title: elution volume
12282.definition: Volume of solvent that has passed through a chromatography bed from the injection of the sample to the recording of a specified signal of the detector due to the sample having passed through the bed.

14628.title: elutriate
14628.definition: Aqueous solution obtained after adding water to a solid substance (e.g., sediment, tailings, drilling mud, or dredging spoil), shaking the mixture, then centrifuging or filtering it or decanting the supernatant.

14629.title: elutriate test
14629.definition: Test in which a nonbenthic species, such as Daphnia magna, is exposed to an elutriate produced by mixing test sediment with water and then centrifuging the mixture.

E02053.title: elutriation
E02053.definition: The process of separating the lighter particles of a powder from the heavier ones by means of an upward directed stream of fluid (gas or liquid).

E02054.title: emanation thermal analysis
E02054.definition: A thermoanalytical technique in which the release of radioactive emanation from a substance (and/or its reaction product(s)) is measured as a function of temperature whilst the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature programme.

15183.title: embedding
15183.definition: Technological process, which consists of mixing or inclusion of the therapeutic substance with an excipient or their mixtures, typically as a matrix dosage form, in order to change the rate of release.

09485.title: embossing
09485.definition: Creating a pattern by pressing a master die into a malleable material.

E02055.title: embryo
E02055.definition: An aggregate of a small number of atoms, molecules or ions. An embryo of such a size that the Gibbs energy at constant pressure and temperature is a maximum is called a critical embryo. An embryo larger than a critical embryo is called a homogeneous nucleus. Colloidal sols may be formed by condensation methods. When a condensation method is applied, molecules (or ions) are deposited on nuclei which may be of the same chemical species as the colloid (homogeneous nucleation) or different (heterogeneous nucleation).

10647.title: embryo transfer
10647.definition: Process of implanting a fertilized ovum into a uterus.

10648.title: embryo transport rate analysis
10648.definition: Method to evaluate the potential for early embryonic loss in rodents caused by accelerated or retarded arrival of embryos into the uterus.

10644.title: embryogenesis
10644.definition: Development and growth of an embryo in the period from formation of the bilaminar embryo to the beginning of the fetal period (in humans, the second through the eighth week after conception).

10645.title: embryoid body
10645.definition: Structure resembling an embryo which is formed by embryonic stem cells or teratocarcinoma cells when they are removed from a growth-promoting medium.

10649.title: embryology
10649.definition: Science of the origin and development of the organism from fertilization of the oocyte to the beginning of fetal life (in humans, the end of the eighth week).

10609.title: embryonic disc
10609.definition: Bilayer plate of cells in the blastocyst from which the mammalian embryo develops.

10646.title: embryonic induction
10646.definition: Process whereby the development of one group of cells, called the competent region, is altered by an inducing factor from another group, called a signaling center or organizer.

10650.title: embryonic period
10650.definition: Period from fertilization to the end of major organogenesis.

10651.title: embryonic stem cell
10651.definition: Undifferentiated, pluripotent cell from an early stage of the pre-implantation embryo (inner cell mass of the blastocyst).

15658.title: embryotoxicity
15658.definition:
Production by a substance of toxic effects in progeny in the first period of pregnancy between conception and the fetal stage.
Any toxic effect on the conceptus as a result of prenatal exposure during the embryonic stages of development: These effects may include malformations and variations, malfunctions, altered growth, prenatal death, and altered postnatal function.

15659.title: embryotropic effect
15659.definition: Change in the embryo and the regulation of its development.

14630.title: emergent properties
14630.definition: New properties emerging with upward steps in hierarchical systems, such as ecological communities or ecosystems, that cannot be predicted solely from our limited understanding of the system’s parts or components.

11751.title: emetic
11751.definition:
n. Substance that produces vomiting.
adj. Producing vomiting.

E02056.title: emission
E02056.definition: Radiative deactivation of an excited state; transfer of energy from a molecular entity to an electromagnetic field.

15660.title: emission and exposure control
15660.definition: Technical and administrative procedures and specifications applied for the monitoring, reduction, or elimination of emissions from a source or exposure to a target.

ET07370.title: emission anisotropy
ET07370.definition: Used to characterize luminescence (fluorescence, phosphorescence) polarization resulting from photoselection. Defined as: \[r = \frac{I_{\parallel} - I_{\perp }}{I_{\parallel} + 2I_{\perp }}\] where \(I_{\parallel}\) and \(I_{\perp }\) are the intensities measured with the linear polarizer for emission parallel and perpendicular, respectively, to the electric vector of linearly polarized incident electromagnetic radiation (which is often vertical). The quantity \(I_{\parallel} + 2I_{\perp }\) is proportional to the total fluorescence intensity \(I\).

E02058.title: emission control equipment
E02058.definition: Air pollution control equipment which either converts the pollutant chemically to a non-polluting substance or collects the pollutant by some means including gravity settling chambers, inertial separators, cyclonic separators, filters, electrical precipitators, scrubbers, (spray towers, jet scrubbers, Venturi scrubbers, inertial scrubbers, mechanical scrubbers and packed scrubbers). Certain gases and odoriferous compounds are controlled by combustion, absorption (spray chambers, mechanical contactors, bubble cap or sieve plate contactors and packed towers) and adsorption units (packed beds or fluidized beds).

E02059.title: emission flux
E02059.definition: The emission per unit area of the appropriate surface of an emitting source.

E02057.title: emission
E02057.definition: The total rate at which a solid, liquid or gaseous pollutant is emitted into the atmosphere from a given source; usually expressed as mass per unit time. Primary emissions are those substances which are emitted directly to the atmosphere (e.g. $\ce{NO}$, $\ce{SO2}$, etc.), while secondary emissions are formed from the primary emissions through thermal or photochemical reactions (e.g. ozone, aldehydes, ketones, sulfuric acid, nitric acid, etc.). The point or area from which the discharge takes place is called the source; the area in which the emission or its transformed products (e.g. in the case of aerosols, acidic deposition, etc.) may be deposited is called the receptor area or sink. Emission may be applied to noise, heat, etc., as well as pollutants.

E02060.title: emission spectrum
E02060.definition: Plot of the emitted spectral radiant power (spectral radiant exitance) or of the emitted spectral photon irradiance (spectral photon exitance) against a quantity related to photon energy, such as frequency, \(\nu \), wavenumber, \(\sigma \), or wavelength, \(\lambda \). When corrected for wavelength-dependent variations in the equipment response, it is called a corrected emission spectrum.

14631.title: emission standard
14631.definition: Quantitative limit on the emission or discharge of a substance from a source, usually expressed in terms of a time-weighted average concentration or a ceiling value.

E02062.title: emittance
E02062.definition: Ratio of radiant exitance of a thermal radiator to that of a full radiator (black body) at the same temperature. In ISO this quantity is called emissivity.

E02063.title: empirical formula
E02063.definition: Formed by juxtaposition of the atomic symbols with their appropriate subscripts to give the simplest possible formula expressing the composition of a compound.

E02064.title: emulsifier
E02064.definition: A surfactant which when present in small amounts facilitates the formation of an emulsion, or enhances its colloidal stability by decreasing either or both of the rates of aggregation and coalescence.

14333.title: emulsifier-free emulsion polymerisation
14333.definition: Emulsion polymerization carried out without the addition of a colloid stabilizer.

E02065.title: emulsion
E02065.definition: A fluid colloidal system in which liquid droplets and/or liquid crystals are dispersed in a liquid. The droplets often exceed the usual limits for colloids in size. An emulsion is denoted by the symbol O/W if the continuous phase is an aqueous solution and by W/O if the continuous phase is an organic liquid (an 'oil'). More complicated emulsions such as O/W/O (i.e. oil droplets contained within aqueous droplets dispersed in a continuous oil phase) are also possible. Photographic emulsions, although colloidal systems, are not emulsions in the sense of this nomenclature.

14329.title: emulsion polymerisation
14329.definition: Polymerization whereby monomer(s), initiator, dispersion medium, and possibly colloid stabilizer constitute initially an inhomogeneous system resulting in particles of colloidal dimensions containing the formed polymer.

E02066.title: enamines
E02066.definition: Alkenylamines; by usage the term refers specifically to vinylic amines, which have the structure $\ce{R2NCR=CR2}$ .

E02069.title: enantiomer
E02069.definition: One of a pair of molecular entities which are mirror images of each other and non-superposable.

E02070.title: enantiomeric excess
E02070.definition: For a mixture of \(\left(+\right)\)- and \(\left(-\right)\)-enantiomers, with composition given as the mole or weight fractions \(F_{\left(\!+\!\right)}\) and \(F_{\left(\!-\!\right)}\) (where \(F_{\left(\!+\!\right)}\,+\,F_{\left(\!-\!\right)}=1\)) the enantiomer excess is defined as \(|F_{\left(\!+\!\right)} - F_{\left(\!-\!\right)}|\) (and the percent enantiomer excess by \(100\ |F_{\left(\!+\!\right)} - F_{\left(\!-\!\right)}|\)). Frequently this term is abbreviated e.e.

E02073.title: enantiomeric groups
E02073.definition: Chiral groups that are mirror images of one another.

E02075.title: enantiomeric ratio
E02075.definition: The ratio of the percentage of one enantiomer in a mixture to that of the other e.g. \(70\left(\!+\!\right)\,\colon\,30\left(\!-\!\right)\).

E02076.title: enantiomeric units
E02076.definition: Two configurational units that correspond to the same constitutional unit are considered to be enantiomeric if they are non-superposable mirror images.

E02071.title: enantiomerically enriched
E02071.definition: A sample of a chiral substance whose enantiomeric ratio is greater than \(50\ \colon\ 50\) but less than \(100\ \colon\ 0\).

E02072.title: enantiomerically pure
E02072.definition: A sample all of whose molecules have (within limits of detection) the same chirality sense. Use of homochiral as a synonym is strongly discouraged.

E02079.title: enantiomorph
E02079.definition: One of a pair of chiral objects or models that are non-superposable mirror images of each other. The adjective enantiomorphic is also applied to mirror-image related groups within a molecular entity.

09888.title: enantioselective chromatography
09888.definition: Separation of enantiomeric species due to the enantioselectivity of their interaction with the chiral selector(s) of a chromatographic (electrophoretic) system.

E02083.title: enantiotopic
E02083.definition: Constitutionally identical atoms or groups in molecules which are related by symmetry elements of the second kind only (mirror plane, inversion centre or rotation–reflection axis). For example the two groups c in a grouping Cabcc are enantiotopic. Replacement of one of a pair of enantiotopic groups forms one of a pair of enantiomers. Analogously, if complexation or addition to one of the two faces defined by a double bond or other molecular plane gives rise to a chiral species, the two faces are called enantiotopic.

ET06895.title: enantiotropic mesophase
ET06895.definition: A mesophase that is thermodynamically stable over a definite temperature or pressure range.

14334.title: encapsulating emulsion polymerisation
14334.definition: Emulsion polymerization leading to the encapsulation of a solid within polymer particles or liquid polymer droplets.

E02085.title: encapsulation
E02085.definition: Enzymes or cells which are of relatively large size may be entrapped in a maze of polymeric molecules (a gel). This procedure is called immobilization by inclusion. When the biocatalyst is enclosed inside a semipermeable membrane, usually approximately spherical, the method is known as encapsulation. In the process of reticulation the primary biocatalyst particles (individual enzyme molecules, cofactors or individual cells) are covalently attached to each other by organic chains, into a three-dimensional network. The term grafting is also used in this context. Attachment to the support by adsorption forces is called immobilization by adsorption.

10653.title: encephalocele
10653.definition: Congenital protrusion of brain tissue through a fissure or defect in the skull.

11752.title: encephalopathy
11752.definition: Any disorder of the brain that affects its functioning.

E02086.title: encounter
E02086.definition: A set of collisions between reactant molecules in solids, liquids or dense gases, occurring in rapid succession as a result of the cage effect.

E02087.title: encounter complex
E02087.definition: A complex of molecular entities produced at an encounter-controlled rate, and which occurs as an intermediate in a reaction mechanism. When the complex is formed from two molecular entities it is called an 'encounter pair'. A distinction between encounter pairs and (larger) encounter complexes may be relevant in some cases, e.g. for mechanisms involving pre-association.

E02089.title: encounter-controlled rate
E02089.definition: A rate of reaction corresponding to the rate of encounter of the reacting molecular entities. This is also known as 'diffusion-controlled rate' since rates of encounter are themselves controlled by diffusion rates (which in turn depend on the viscosity of the medium and the dimensions of the reactant molecular entities). For a bimolecular reaction between solutes in water at \(\pu{25^{\circ}C}\) an encounter-controlled rate is calculated to have a second-order rate constant of about \(\pu{E10 dm3 mol-1 s-1}\).

15398.title: end-capping
15398.definition: Reaction in which end-groups of a desired structure are intentionally formed.

E02092.title: end-group
E02092.definition: A constitutional unit that is an extremity of a macromolecule or oligomer molecule. An end-group is attached to only one constitutional unit of a macromolecule or oligomer molecule.

14128.title: end-point assay
14128.definition: Kinetic assay run for a set constant incubation time. Typically, at the end of the set incubation time, a reagent that stops the reaction is added to allow postponed measurement of the signal.

09041.title: end-point error
09041.definition: Difference in the volume or mass of titrant, or the corresponding difference in the volume or mass of titrand, between the end-point value and equivalence-point value.

E02097.title: end-to-end distance
E02097.definition: The length, \(r\), of the end-to-end vector.

E02098.title: end-to-end vector
E02098.definition: The vector, \(r\), connecting the two ends of a linear polymer chain in a particular conformation.

14632.title: endemic
14632.definition: Pertaining to a species found in a discrete geographical unit, such as an island, habitat type, or other defined area or zone.

14633.title: endemism
14633.definition: Ecological state of being unique to a place.

E02091.title: endergonic reaction
E02091.definition: This is usually taken to be a reaction for which the overall standard Gibbs energy change \(\Delta G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) is positive. Some workers use this term with respect to a positive value of \(\Delta H^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) at the absolute zero of temperature.

E02094.title: endo, exo, syn, anti
E02094.definition: Descriptors of the relative orientation of groups attached to non-bridgehead atoms in a bicyclo[x.y.z]alkane (x ≥ y > z > 0).  If the group is orientated towards the highest numbered bridge (z bridge, e.g. C-7 in example below) it is given the description exo; if it is orientated away from the highest numbered bridge it is given the description endo. If the group is attached to the highest numbered bridge and is orientated towards the lowest numbered bridge (x bridge, e.g. C-2 in example below) it is given the description syn; if the group is orientated away from the lowest numbered bridge it is given the description anti.

10654.title: endocardial cushion
10654.definition: Subset of cells in the primordial tube-like heart that is essential to the development of the ventricular septum and the atrioventricular valves of the heart.

10655.title: endocardium
10655.definition: Endothelial lining of the heart chambers, also containing small blood vessels and a few bundles of smooth muscle, continuous with the endothelium of the great blood vessels.

10656.title: endochondral ossification
10656.definition: Formation and growth of bone tissue (especially of the long bones) during fetal development of the mammalian skeletal system, and in repair of bone fractures, that takes place in the presence of cartilage.

15661.title: endocon
15661.definition: Portion of a conjugated metabolite that is derived from a natural product (such as a sugar, amino acid, or other organic acid) of the metabolizing organism.

10657.title: endocrine
10657.definition: Pertaining to hormones or to glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream.

10658.title: endocrine disrupter
10658.definition: Exogenous substance that, at some dose, alters function(s) of the endocrine system and consequently causes adverse health effects in an intact organism, its progeny, or (sub)populations.

11753.title: endocrine disruptor
11753.definition: Exogenous chemical that alters function(s) of the endocrine system and consequently causes adverse health effects in an intact organism, its progeny, or (sub)populations.

ET06822.title: endocytosis
ET06822.definition: Uptake of material into a cell by invagination of the plasma membrane and its internalisation in a membrane-bounded vesicle.

10659.title: endoderm
10659.definition: Innermost of the three primary germ layers of an embryo, developing into the gastrointestinal tract, the lungs, and associated structures.

E02093.title: endoenzymes
E02093.definition: Enzymes that cut internal bonds of a polymer. Endonucleases are able to cleave phosphodiester bonds within a nucleic acid chain by hydrolysis either randomly or at specific base sequences (cf. restriction enzymes).

13110.title: endogenous
13110.definition: Produced within or caused by factors within an organism.

09792.title: endometabolome
09792.definition: Complete set of metabolites inside a cell (intracellular metabolites).

10660.title: endometrium
10660.definition: Inner lining of the uterus that is shed during menstruation.

09704.title: endonuclease
09704.definition: Enzyme that cleaves nucleic acids by hydrolysing phosphodiester bonds between nucleotides within a nucleic acid molecule.

15662.title: endoplasmic reticulum
15662.definition: Intracellular complex of membranes in which proteins and lipids, as well as molecules for export, are synthesized and in which the biotransformation reactions of the monooxygenase enzyme systems occur.

11754.title: endorphin
11754.definition: One of several peptides (including the enkephalins) that activates the body’s opiate receptors, causing an analgesic effect; literally, endogenous morphine-like substance.

13111.title: endosome
13111.definition: Intracellular smooth surfaced vesicle in which endocytosed material passes on its way to the lysosomes.

15663.title: endothelial
15663.definition: Pertaining to the layer of flat cells lining the inner surface of blood and lymphatic vessels, and the surface lining of serous and synovial membranes.

10661.title: endothelium
10661.definition: Layer of flat cells that line the blood vessels, lymphatic vessels, and the chambers of the heart.

14634.title: endotherm
14634.definition: 'Warm-blooded organism' that regulates its body temperature to be (almost) constant.

E02095.title: endothermic reaction
E02095.definition: A reaction for which the overall standard enthalpy change \(\Delta H^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) is positive.

13112.title: endotoxin
13112.definition: Pathogenic cell wall-associated lipopolysaccharides of Gram-negative bacteria.

14635.title: endpoint
14635.definition: Objective of measurement of a toxicity test.

14636.title: endpoint assessment
14636.definition: Quantitative or quantifiable expression of the environmental value considered to be at risk in a risk analysis.

E02099.title: ene reaction
E02099.definition: The addition of a compound with a double bond having an allylic hydrogen (the 'ene') to a compound with a multiple bond (the 'enophile') with transfer of the allylic hydrogen and a concomitant reorganization of the bonding, as illustrated below for propene (the 'ene') and ethene (the 'enophile'). The reverse is a 'retro-ene' reaction.

15184.title: enemas
15184.definition: Solutions (aqueous or oily), emulsions, or suspensions for rectal administration of medicaments for cleansing, diagnostic, or therapeutic purposes.

E02100.title: energized species
E02100.definition: In an elementary process, a species having sufficient energy to become an activated complex, but which does not have the structure of the activated complex. If it is not inactivated by collisions it can become an activated complex and pass at once into products, after undergoing vibration.

08810.title: energy band
08810.definition: Quasi-continuous range of discrete energy levels that an electron is either allowed (an occupied band) or forbidden (forbidden band or band gap) to occupy in a molecule or solid.

08811.title: energy band theory
08811.definition: Theory describing the electronic structure of a solid in terms of energy intervals, called energy bands that are allowed or forbidden for occupation by electrons.

E02103.title: energy dispersion
E02103.definition: The separation of characteristic photons according to their energy.

E02105.title: energy dispersive X-ray fluorescence analysis
E02105.definition: A method of X-ray fluorescence analysis where element specificity is obtained by measuring the energy spectrum of the induced X-radiation.

09369.title: energy edge
09369.definition: Values of the backscattering energy for an element, or for an isotope, that is located at the surface of a sample.

E02106.title: energy flux density
E02106.definition: For mono-directional radiation, the energy traversing in a time interval over a small area perpendicular to the direction of the energy flow, divided by that time interval and by that area.

08812.title: energy gap
08812.definition: Energy interval in a lattice where no electronic state exists.

ET07028.title: energy gradient
ET07028.definition: First derivatives of the total energy with respect to nuclear coordinates, i.e., negative values of forces on the nuclei. Evaluation of energy gradient plays a central role in searching potential energy surfaces for stationary points. A widespread technique is based on the minimization of the gradient norm (the square of energy gradient).

ET07029.title: energy hypersurface
ET07029.definition: The notion of hypersurface is used to stress the multidimensionality of PESs. In a molecular system consisting of \(N\) atomic nuclei, the number of the independent coordinates that fully determine the PES is equal to \(3\ N-6\) (or \(3\ N-5\) if the system is linear).

08246.title: energy level
08246.definition: Set of one or more stationary quantum states of a free atom, ion, or molecule having a particular internal energy.

E02102.title: energy
E02102.definition: Energy of the individual particles or photons of which a radiation consists.

E02109.title: energy of activation
E02109.definition: This is defined by the equation: \[U^{\ddagger } = -R\ T\ (\frac{\partial (\ln I_{0})}{\partial T^{-1}})_{p,c_{j},...}\] where \(I_{0}\) is the exchange current. At any overpotential \(\eta \) it is defined by the equation: \[U^{\ddagger }\left(\eta \right) = -R\ (\frac{\partial (\ln (|I|))}{\partial T^{-1}})_{p,\eta ,c_{j},...}\] where \(I\) is the current passing from the electrode into the electrolyte.

11439.title: energy of the highest occupied molecular orbital
11439.definition:
The energy of the highest energy level in the ground state of a molecule that contains electrons, sometimes used as a measure of nucleophilicity in QSAR
 models.

11440.title: energy of the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital
11440.definition:
The energy of the lowest energy level of a molecule that contains no electrons in the ground state, sometimes used as a measure of electrophilicity in QSAR
 models.

E02113.title: energy resolution
E02113.definition: A measurement, at given energy, of the smallest difference between the energies of two particles or photons capable of being distinguished by a radiation spectrometer.

E02114.title: energy storage efficiency
E02114.definition: The rate of the Gibbs energy storage in an endothermic photochemical reaction divided by the incident irradiance.

E02115.title: energy threshold
E02115.definition: The limiting kinetic energy of a incident particle or energy of an incident photon below which a specified process cannot take place.

E02116.title: energy transfer
E02116.definition: From a phenomenological point of view, the term is used to describe the process by which a molecular entity absorbs light and a phenomenon originates from the excited state of another molecular entity. In mechanistic photochemistry the term has been reserved for the photophysical process in which an excited state of one molecular entity (the donor) is deactivated to a lower-lying state by transferring energy to a second molecular entity (the acceptor) which is thereby raised to a higher energy state. The excitation may be electronic, vibrational, rotational or translational. The donor and acceptor may be two parts of the same molecular entity, in which case the process is called intramolecular energy transfer.

E02117.title: energy transfer plot
E02117.definition: A plot of the quenching rate constant of an excited molecular entity by a series of quenchers versus the excited state energy of the quenchers. Alternatively, a plot of the rate constant for the sensitization of a reaction versus the excited state energy of different sensitizers. This type of plot is used to estimate the energy of the excited molecular entity quenched (in the former case) or produced (in the latter case).

E02118.title: energy yield of luminescence
E02118.definition: The ratio of the energy emitted as luminescence to the energy absorbed by a species.

E02101.title: energy
E02101.definition: In mechanics the sum of potential energy and kinetic energy. In thermodynamics the internal energy or internal energy increase, \(\Delta U\), is the sum of heat and work brought to the system. Only changes in energy are measurable. For photons \[E=h\ \nu \]where \(h\) is the Planck constant and \(\nu \) the frequency of radiation. In relativistic physics \[E=m\ c^{2}\] where \(c\) is the speed of light and \(m\) the mass.

E02119.title: enforced concerted mechanism
E02119.definition: Variation of reaction parameters in a series of reactions proceeding in non-concerted steps may lead to a situation where the putative intermediate will possess a lifetime shorter than a bond vibration, so that the steps become concerted. The transition state structure will lie on the coordinate of the More O'Ferrall–Jencks diagram leading to that of the putative intermediate.

09371.title: enhanced elastic cross section
09371.definition: Cross section of an atom for elastic scattering that is greater than the Rutherford cross section due to partial penetration of a nucleus in the sample by the incident particle.

E02120.title: enhanced phosphorescence analysis
E02120.definition: A use of luminescence quenching effects to enhance sensitivity. The strong depopulation of the fluorescing singlet excited state by external heavy atom perturbers can lead to a large population of the phosphorescing triplet excited state.

E02121.title: enhancement reaction
E02121.definition: A reaction which enables a favourable measurement to be made in which the constituent which is finally measured has not been magnified in any way (cf. amplification reaction).

E02122.title: enhancer
E02122.definition: A fluorescent compound which accepts energy and thus enhances or promotes the emission from a sample containing a chemically or enzymatically generated excited molecular entity.

13113.title: enhancing antibody
13113.definition: Antibody that binds to an antibody-antigen complex or idiotypic-anti-idiotypic antibody complex and strengthens the interaction.

11755.title: enkephalin
11755.definition: Either of two endogenous pentapeptides with opiate-like effects that are especially involved in modulating pain responses in the central nervous system.

E02123.title: enolates
E02123.definition: Salts of enols (or of the tautomeric aldehydes or ketones), in which the anionic charge is delocalized over oxygen and carbon, or similar covalent metal derivatives in which the metal is bound to oxygen.

E02124.title: enols
