ET07032.definition: A semi-empirical all-valence electron quantum mechanical method which uses the same approximations, apart from $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}approximation}$ and neglect of overlap integrals, as those of the Hückel molecular orbital theory. The method reproduces relatively well the shapes and the order of energy levels of molecular orbitals. The account for overlap makes it possible to describe the net destabilization caused by interaction of two doubly occupied orbitals, which effect is not reproduced by HMO theory.

E02280.title: extended X-ray absorption fine structure
E02280.definition: Structure in X-ray absorption spectra remote from the edge and extending to higher energies, due mainly to the scattering of the expelled electron by neighbouring atoms. Structure closer to the absorption edge is sometimes called near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS).

09198.title: extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy
09198.definition: X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy in the energy region from the core-level edge to an energy several hundred $\pu{eV}$ greater.

E02278.title: extended-chain crystal
E02278.definition: A polymer crystal in which the chains are in an essentially fully extended conformation.

ET07267.title: extender
ET07267.definition: Substance, especially a diluent or modifier, added to a polymer to increase its volume without substantially altering the desirable properties of the polymer.

E02281.title: extensive quantity
E02281.definition: Physical quantity whose magnitude is additive for subsystems.

E02282.title: extent
E02282.definition: A quantity measured by its area, \(A\) (or \(S\)). For solids, a real (true, actual) and a geometric surface (interface) area, \(A_{\rm{r}}\) and \(A_{\rm{g}}\), respectively, may be defined if asperities are present whose height is orders of magnitude greater than the atomic or molecular size. The geometric surface is the projection of the real surface on a plane parallel to the macroscopic, visible phase boundary. If asperities are of the order of the atomic size, the surface of the solid may be described as stepped. (High index faces of crystals are stepped surfaces but may be ideally smooth in the sense of the roughness factor.)

08818.title: extent of electron delocalization
08818.definition: Magnitude of the region in a molecule over which a molecular orbital occupied with delocalized electrons is extended.

E02283.title: extent of reaction
E02283.definition: Extensive quantity describing the progress of a chemical reaction equal to the number of chemical transformations, as indicated by the reaction equation on a molecular scale, divided by the Avogadro constant (it is essentially the amount of chemical transformations). The change in the extent of reaction is given by \(\mathrm{d}\xi =\frac{\mathrm{d}n_{\rm{B}}}{\nu _{\rm{B}}}\), where \(\nu _{\rm{B}}\) is the stoichiometric number of any reaction entity B (reactant or product) and \(\mathrm{d}n_{\rm{B}}\) is the corresponding amount.

10174.title: external calibration
10174.definition: Calibration employing a simplified sample matrix spiked with target analyte embodying a reference value of the measurand.

13817.title: external field
13817.definition: Field surrounding a molecular or ionic species emanating from a source external to that species.

16202.title: external quantum efficiency
16202.definition: Efficiency of light emission for solid-state light-emitting devices, such as organic light-emitting devices (OLEDs). Analogous to emission quantum yield.

08819.title: external quantum yield
08819.definition: Quantum yield relating to the whole device or the overall process involved.

08599.title: external reflection spectroscopy
08599.definition: Measurement method of spectroscopy in which radiation is reflected from a sample of higher refractive index than that of the incident medium.

E02290.title: external standard
E02290.definition: A compound present in a standard sample of known concentration and volume which is analysed separately from the unknown sample under identical conditions. It is used to facilitate the qualitative indentification and/or quantitative determination of the sample components. The volume of the external standard (standard sample) need not to be known if it is identical to that of the unknown sample.

08725.title: external standardization for quenching correction
08725.definition: Measurement method to obtain a quenching correction through the use of a gamma-radiation source to generate a spectrum of Compton electrons within the sample vial.

E02291.title: external surface
E02291.definition: When a porous solid consists of discrete particles it is inconvenient to describe the outer boundary of the particles as the external surface.

15701.title: external validity
15701.definition: Generalizability of the results of a particular study, beyond the limits of the population actually studied.

E02292.title: exterplex
E02292.definition: Termolecular analogue of an exciplex. Use of this term is discouraged.

14678.title: extinction probability
14678.definition:
Probability that a population will eventually become extinct.
Probability that a population will become extinct within a specified interval of time.

15705.title: extra risk
15705.definition: Probability that an agent produces an observed response, as distinguished from the probability that the response is caused by a spontaneous event unrelated to the agent.

E02295.title: extra-column volume
E02295.definition: The volume between the effective injection point and the effective detection point, excluding the part of the column containing the stationary phase. It is composed of the volumes of the injector, connecting lines and detector.

10699.title: extracellular matrix
10699.definition: Mesh of molecules, secreted by cells into the surrounding extracellular space.

15702.title: extracellular space
15702.definition: Volume within a tissue, outside cells, and excluding vascular and lymphatic space.

15703.title: extracellular volume
15703.definition: Volume of fluid outside the cells but within the outer surface of an organism.

E02296.title: extract
E02296.definition: The separated phase (often but not necessarily organic) that contains the material extracted from the other phase. Where appropriate the term 'loaded solvent' may be used, but is not recommended.

E02297.title: extract
E02297.definition: To transfer a solute from a liquid phase to another immiscible or partially miscible liquid phase in contact with it. The term is also applied to the dissolution of material from a solid phase with a liquid in which it is not wholly soluble (i.e. leaching).

E02298.title: extractability
E02298.definition: A property which qualitatively indicates the degree to which a substance is extracted. The term is imprecise and generally used in a qualitative sense. It is not a synonym for fraction extracted.

E02299.title: extractant
E02299.definition: The active component(s) primarily responsible for transfer of a solute from one phase to the other.

E02301.title: extraction
E02301.definition: Distribution and partition are often used as synonyms for the general phenomenon of extraction where appropriate.

E02304.title: extraction constant
E02304.definition: The extraction constant at zero ionic strength, \(K_{\rm{ex}}^{\rm{0}}\), is the equilibrium constant of the distribution reaction expressed in terms of the reacting species. Thus, for the gross reaction: \[\rm{M}_{\rm{aq}}^{n+} + n\rm{HL}_{\rm{org}} \rightleftharpoons  \rm{ML}_{n,\rm{org}} + n\rm{H}_{\rm{aq}}^{+}\] in which the reagent $\ce{HL}$ initially dissolved in an organic phase reacts with a metal ion $\ce{M^{n}}$ in aqueous solution to form a product $\ce{ML_{n}}$ which is more soluble in the organic phase than in water, \[K_{\rm{ex}}^{\rm{0}} = \frac{a_{\rm{ML } n,\rm{org}}\hspace{2pt}a_{\rm{H}^{+},\rm{aq}}^{n}}{a_{\rm{M}^{n+},\rm{aq}}\hspace{2pt}a_{\rm{HL},\rm{org}}^{n}}\]

E02305.title: extraction factor
E02305.definition: The ratio of the total mass of a solute in the extract to that in the other phase.

09398.title: extraction field
09398.definition: In secondary-ion mass spectrometry, electric field above a sample, operational during ion emission from the sample.

E02306.title: extraction fractionation
E02306.definition: A process in which a polymeric material, consisting of macromolecules differing in some characteristic affecting their solubility, is separated from a polymer-rich phase into fractions by successively increasing the solution power of the solvent, resulting in the repeated formation of a two-phase system in which the more soluble components concentrate in the polymer-poor phase.

E02302.title: extraction
E02302.definition: In connection with processes, this term often refers to the initial transfer step whereby the main solute, often together with impurities, is transferred from feed to solvent.

10175.title: extraction phase
10175.definition: Liquid, solid, or gas phase in contact with the sample for the purpose of removal of analytes from the sample matrix.

10176.title: extraction rate
10176.definition: Rate at which analytes are transferred from the sample to the extraction phase.

15704.title: extraction ratio
15704.definition: Amount of substance extracted from a source divided by the total contained within the source.

10195.title: extractive distillation
10195.definition: Separation of close-boiling liquids by fractional distillation in the presence of a low-volatility solvent or salt that selectively interacts with one or more components of the mixture, increasing the difference in vapour pressure of the sample components.

09185.title: extractive electrospray ionization mass spectrometry
09185.definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air as a result of an inert gas being passed over the sample to pick up the molecules, which are subsequently ionized by ionized solvent droplets generated by pneumatically assisted electrospray ionization.

09399.title: extractor voltage
09399.definition: Electric potential, referenced to the sample, of the electrode defining the field above the sample and used to facilitate introduction of emitted ions into the mass spectrometer.

10700.title: extraembryonic membrane
10700.definition: One of the membranes that surrounds the embryo, which include the yolk sac, allantois, amnion, and chorion.

10701.title: extraembryonic mesoderm
10701.definition: Cells outside the embryo that, although derived from the zygote, are not part of the embryo proper and contribute to the fetal membranes (yolk sac, allantois, amnion, and chorion).

15706.title: extraneous residue limit
15706.definition: Refers to a pesticide residue or contaminant arising from environmental sources (including former agricultural uses) other than the use of a pesticide or contaminant substance directly or indirectly on the commodity. It is the maximum concentration of a pesticide residue or contaminant that is recommended by the Codex Alimentarius Commission to be legally permitted or recognized as acceptable in or on food, agricultural commodity, or animal feed.

08600.title: extraordinary wave
08600.definition: In a uniaxial crystal electromagnetic radiation with electric vector oblique to the optic axis and which does not obey the normal laws of refraction.

E02309.title: extrapolated range
E02309.definition: The distance from a radiation source, calculated by extrapolation to zero of the flux density, of the tangent to the flux density versus distance curve, taken at the point where the flux density has decreased to one half of its initial value.

14679.title: extrapolation
14679.definition: Calculation, based on quantitative observations in exposed test species or in vitro test systems, of predicted dose–effect and dose–response relationships for a substance in the same species at other doses or in humans and other species at similar doses.

14680.title: extrapolation factor
14680.definition: Quantity used in effect and exposure assessments to adjust estimated exposures or concentrations/doses for uncertainties, to make corrections in the data, or to improve safety.

15707.title: extrapyramidal movement disorders
15707.definition: Involuntary movement disorders mediated by signaling through neurons outside the pyramidal (corticospinal) tract, often describing side effects of psychiatric medications.

13133.title: extravasation
13133.definition: Movement of cells or fluid from within blood vessels to the surrounding tissues.

09507.title: extreme ultraviolet lithography
09507.definition: Photolithography performed by exposing a resist to extreme ultraviolet (\(\pu{13 nm}\)) radiation.

E02310.title: extremophiles
E02310.definition: Organisms which require extreme physico-chemical conditions for their optimum growth and proliferation. Extremophilic microorganisms are e.g. thermophiles or psychrophiles, halophiles, alkalophiles or acidophiles, osmophiles and barophiles, based on their growth at extremes of temperature, salt concentration, pH, osmolarity or pressure, respectively.

14010.title: extrinsic absorption
14010.definition: Absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation in semiconductors and insulators corresponding to optical transitions of electrons from defect energy levels (within the bandgap energy) to conduction band levels, or holes to valence band levels (photoionisation of defects), or from the ground state level to excited levels of a given intrinsic defect of any sort.

14011.title: extrinsic defect
14011.definition: Imperfection in a solid semiconductor (or insulator) connected with surface defects of any sort involving extrinsic chemical units in relation to the chemical formula of the solid, particularly adsorbed species of any sort.

10702.title: extrinsic pathway
10702.definition: Apoptotic pathway of cell death initiated upon occupancy of so-called death receptors at the cell surface with their ligands, such as Fas/CD95 and tumor necrosis factor-\(\upalpha\), and involving activation of caspase 8.

09331.title: extrinsic plasmon
09331.definition: Plasmon excited as an electron travels through a condensed medium.

08820.title: extrinsic semiconductor
08820.definition: Semiconductor whose electric properties are largely determined by the dopant 'impurities' present.

E02311.title: extrusion transformation
E02311.definition: A transformation in which an atom or group $\ce{Y}$ connected to two other atoms or groups $\ce{X}$ and $\ce{Z}$ is lost from a molecule, leading to a product in which $\ce{X}$ is bonded to $\ce{Z}$, e.g.  or  The reverse of an extrusion is called insertion.

13134.title: exudate
13134.definition: Extravascular fluid containing proteins and cellular debris that accumulates during inflammation.

E04391.title: π-electron acceptor/donor group
E04391.definition: A substituent capable of a $\ce{+R}$ (e.g.$\ce{NO2}$) or $\ce{-R}$ (e.g. $\ce{OCH3}$) effect, respectively.

13932.title: foreign body reaction
13932.definition: Cellular response of the inflammatory and wound healing processes following introduction of a foreign object in a human or animal body.

12411.title: fast ion bombardment
12411.definition: Ionization of any species by the interaction of a focused beam of ions, with a translational energy of several thousand \(\pu{eV}\), with a solid or liquid sample.

12412.title: field-free region
12412.definition: Section of a mass spectrometer in which there are no electric or magnetic fields.

12413.title: first stability region
12413.definition: Stability region of a Mathieu stability diagram closest to the origin.

12414.title: fixed precursor ion spectrum
12414.definition: Spectrum obtained when data are acquired that determine the m/z values of product ions produced by the reaction of a selected precursor ion with a user-specified m/z value.

12415.title: flow injection mass spectrometry
12415.definition: Method of flow injection analysis in which an aliquot of sample is injected, without chromatographic separation, into a liquid carrier stream for on-line mass spectrometry.

12416.title: focal plane detector
12416.definition: Detector for m/z spatially dispersed ion beams in which all ions simultaneously impinge on the detector plane to produce spatially defined signals.

12417.title: forward geometry
12417.definition: Double-focusing mass spectrometer configuration in which the ion beam traverses the electric sector before the magnetic sector.

12418.title: forward library search
12418.definition: Procedure of comparing a mass spectrum of an unknown compound with a mass spectral library so that the unknown spectrum is compared in turn with the library spectra, considering only the m/z peaks that have intensities greater than a specific threshold in the unknown.

12419.title: Fourier-transform mass spectrometry
12419.definition: Mass spectrometry technique in which m/z values are represented by frequencies of ion motion and mass spectra are generated by Fourier transform mathematical operations from time domain transients produced by image current detection.

12420.title: fringe field
12420.definition: Electric or magnetic field that extends from the edge of an electric sector, magnetic sector, lens, or other ion optics element.

14220.title: frustration
14220.definition: Feature of crystalline packing characterized by different crystalline arrangements of chain stems at two (or more) sites that would be expected to be equivalent.

14244.title: fold period
14244.definition: Thickness of a lamellar parallel-chain crystal in the direction of its stems.

14012.title: F centres
14012.definition: Anion vacancies occupied by electrons in semiconductors.

F02351.title: f-functional branch point
F02351.definition: Branch point from which f linear chains emanate.

13136.title: F(ab')2 fragment
13136.definition: Bivalent antigen-binding fragment obtained following pepsin digestion of immunoglobulin. Consists of both light chains and the N-terminal part of both heavy chains linked by disulfide bonds.

10703.title: F1 generation
10703.definition: Indicating ‘first filial’ generation, denoting offspring from genotypically (see genotype) distinct parents.

13135.title: Fab fragment
13135.definition: Monovalent antigen-binding (‘ab’) fragment obtained following papain digestion of immunoglobulin (Ig). It consists of an intact light chain and the N-terminal VH and C H1 domains of the heavy chain.

F02313.title: fac-
F02313.definition: An affix used in names to designate three groups occupying the corners of the same face of an octahedral coordination sphere, not now generally recommended for precise nomenclature purposes.

10704.title: facial cleft
10704.definition: Congenital anomaly resulting from the failure of facial structures in the embryo to fuse properly.

10705.title: facies
10705.definition: In medicine, facial expression of an individual that is typical of a particular syndrome, disease, or condition.

14681.title: facilitated diffusion
14681.definition: Passive diffusion down a gradient, not requiring energy, but occurring at a rate faster than expected by simple diffusion alone.

11767.title: facilitation
11767.definition:
Neural facilitation: Increase in postsynaptic excitation as a result of very rapid firing of action potentials by a presynaptic neuron.
Presynaptic facilitation: Increase of presynaptic excitation when an excited neuron receives additional excitatory impulses from other neurons.

F02314.title: factor
F02314.definition: Proportionality constant between two quantities of the same dimension.

10093.title: factor analysis
10093.definition: Matrix decomposition of a data matrix (\(\boldsymbol{X}\)) into the product of a scores matrix (\(\boldsymbol{T}\)) and the transpose of the loadings matrix (\(\boldsymbol{P}^{\rm{T}}\)).

10072.title: factor level
10072.definition: Value of a factor in an experimental design.

10706.title: fallopian tube
10706.definition: One of a pair of tubes, on either side of the upper or outer extremity of the ovary, that provides a path by which an ovum travels from the ovary to the fundus of the uterus.

F02316.title: fallout
F02316.definition: A measurement of air contamination consisting of the mass rate at which solid particles deposit from the atmosphere.

11444.title: false negative
11444.definition: A model prediction of a negative result, such as no biological activity, when the true result is positive, i.e. activity.

11445.title: false positive
11445.definition: A model prediction of a positive result, such as biological activity, when the true result is negative, i.e. inactivity.

11768.title: falx
11768.definition: Continuation of dura mater between the right and left hemispheres of the brain.

13143.title: familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome
13143.definition: Episodic autoinflammatory disease, induced by exposure to cold, and caused by mutations in the gene CSA1, encoding cryopyrin.

13144.title: familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
13144.definition: Progressive and potentially lethal inflammatory disease caused by an inherited deficiency of perforin.

F02319.title: fanning
F02319.definition: In blast furnace operation, the idling period between the blowing periods when the blast pressure is reduced to a minimum. This also applies to plume behaviour under inversion conditions.

F02320.title: farad
F02320.definition: SI derived unit of electric capacitance, \(\pu{F} = \pu{C V-1} = \pu{m-2 kg-1 s4 A2}\).

F02321.title: faradaic current
F02321.definition: A current corresponding to the reduction or oxidation of some chemical substance. The net faradaic current is the algebraic sum of all the faradaic currents flowing through an indicator or working electrode.

F02322.title: faradaic current density
F02322.definition: Measures the rate of the interfacial reaction, the proportionality constant being the charge number of the reaction multiplied by the Faraday constant.

F02323.title: faradaic demodulation current
F02323.definition: Component of the current that is due to the demodulation associated with an electrode reaction and that appears if an indicator or working electrode is subjected to the action of two intermodulated applied potentials of different frequency.

F02324.title: faradaic rectification current
F02324.definition: A component of the current that is due to the rectifying properties of an electrode reaction and that appears if an indicator or working electrode is subjected to any periodically varying applied potential while the mean value of the applied potential is controlled.

F02325.title: Faraday constant
F02325.definition: Fundamental physical constant representing molar elementary charge: \(F = \pu{9.64853399(24)E4 C mol-1}\).

F02326.title: Faraday cup collector
F02326.definition: A hollow collector, open at one end and closed at the other, used to collect beams of ions.

09075.title: Faraday’s laws of electrolysis
09075.definition:
Faraday’s First Law of electrolysis: Mass \(m\) of electrochemically-transformed substance is proportional to the charge \(Q\) passed, \(m\! \propto\! Q\).
Faraday’s Second Law of electrolysis: When the same electric charge (quantity of electricity) \(Q\) is passed through several electrolytes, the mass \(m_{\rm{i}}\) of the substances deposited are proportional to their respective chemical equivalent molar mass, \(M_{\rm{i}}/z_{\rm{i}}\). \[m_{1}/m_{2} = (M_{1}/z_{1})/(M_{2}/z_{2})\]

13145.title: farmer’s lung
13145.definition: Hypersensitivity disease caused by the interaction of immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies with large amounts of an inhaled allergen in the alveolar wall of the lung, causing alveolar wall inflammation and compromising gas exchange.

13146.title: Fas
13146.definition: Member of the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) receptor gene family. Engagement of Fas on the surface of the cell by the Fas ligand (CD178) present on cytotoxic cells can trigger apoptosis in the Fas-bearing target cell.

11769.title: fasciculation
11769.definition: Involuntary contractions, or twitchings, of groups (fasciculi) of muscle fibers.

F02327.title: fast atom bombardment ionization
F02327.definition: This term is used to describe ionization of any species by causing interaction of the sample (which may be dissolved in a solvent matrix) and a beam of neutral atoms having high translational energy.

14384.title: fast coagulation rate
14384.definition: Rate of coagulation in the absence of any repulsive barrier between particles.

08342.title: fast field cycling NMR relaxometry
08342.definition: Relaxometry to measure the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate constant as a function of the applied magnetic field strength in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

12655.title: fast follower
12655.definition: Compound selected as a rapid successor to a lead drug candidate.

F02329.title: fast neutrons
F02329.definition: Neutrons of kinetic energy greater than some specified value. This value may vary over a wide range and will be dependent upon the application.

F02328.title: fast-atom bombardment mass spectrometry
F02328.definition: A method in which ions are produced in a mass spectrometer from non-volatile or thermally fragile organic molecules by bombarding the compound in the condensed phase with energy-rich neutral particles.

09400.title: fast-atom bombardment secondary ion mass spectrometry
09400.definition: Secondary ion mass spectrometry in which the primary-ion beam is replaced by a fast-atom beam.

15187.title: fast-dissolving tablet
15187.definition: A tablet formulation intended for a rapid release of its active agent.

14682.title: fate
14682.definition: Disposition of a material in various environmental compartments (e.g., soil or sediment, water, air, biota) as a result of transport, partitioning, transformation, and degradation.

FT07375.title: fatigue
FT07375.definition: Loss of performance over time, due to chemical degradation. The major cause of fatigue is oxidation.

F02330.title: fatty acids
F02330.definition: Aliphatic monocarboxylic acids derived from or contained in esterified form in an animal or vegetable fat, oil or wax. Natural fatty acids commonly have a chain of 4 to 28 carbons (usually unbranched and even-numbered), which may be saturated or unsaturated. By extension, the term is sometimes used to embrace all acyclic aliphatic carboxylic acids.

09837.title: fatty acyls
09837.definition: Diverse group of lipid molecules synthesised by chain elongation of an acetyl-CoA primer with malonyl-CoA (or methylmalonyl-CoA) groups.

13137.title: Fc fragment
13137.definition: Crystallizable, non-antigen-binding fragment of an immunoglobulin (Ig) molecule obtained following papain digestion. Consists of the C-terminal portion of both heavy chains, responsible for binding to Fc receptors and complement factor C1q.

13138.title: Fc receptor
13138.definition: Receptors expressed on a wide range of cells, interacting with the Fc portion of immunoglobulins (Ig) belonging to various isotypes.

13139.title: Fd fragment
13139.definition: Heavy chain portion of an immunoglobulin (Ig) N-terminal to the papain hydrolysis site, after reduction and separation of the light chain portion.

14683.title: feasibility study
14683.definition: Part of a remedial investigation that compares the various options available for remediation and identifies those that are practicable.

10708.title: fecundity
10708.definition:
Ability to produce offspring within a given period of time.
Quantity of reproductive output.

14684.title: fecundity selection
14684.definition: Component of the life cycle of an individual in which natural selection can occur, involving the production of more offspring by matings of certain genotype pairs than are produced by other genotype pairs.

10177.title: feed
10177.definition: Solution or gas containing analyte introduced into an extraction.

F02334.title: feed rate
F02334.definition: The amount of reactant fed per unit time to the inlet of the reactor.

F02333.title: feed-back inhibition
F02333.definition: A metabolic control mechanism in which the end product of a biochemical sequence is able to inhibit the activity of an early enzyme in the sequence, thereby controlling the metabolic flux through this pathway. As an example, isoleucine controls its own synthesis by inhibiting threonine deaminase; adenosine 5-triphosphate (ATP) and citrate control glycolysis by inhibiting phosphofructokinase.

F02331.title: feedback
F02331.definition: The process whereby the output of a device is used to modify the operation of an analytical instrument.

10710.title: female fertility
10710.definition:
Ability to conceive (see conception).
Production of live offspring.

10845.title: female fertility index
10845.definition: In rodents, number of pregnant females divided by the number of females mated, multiplied by 100.

10709.title: feminization
10709.definition: Development of female characteristics as part of normal female maturation, or, in a male, pathologically as a result of endocrine imbalance.

F02336.title: fenestranes
F02336.definition: Compounds of the general formula shown above. They may be considered to be spiro compounds having bridges of carbon atoms connecting the $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ and $\ce{\upalpha\!'}$ positions.

FT06786.title: Fenton reaction
FT06786.definition: $\ce{Fe^{2+} + H2O2 -> Fe^{3+} + OH^{.} + OH^{−}}$ . This is the iron-salt-dependent decomposition of dihydrogen peroxide, generating the highly reactive hydroxyl radical, possibly via an oxoiron(IV) intermediate. Addition of a reducing agent, such as ascorbate, leads to a cycle which increases the damage to biological molecules.

F02337.title: fermentation
F02337.definition: In metabolism, the dehydrogenating degradation of organic substance by organisms or cells under anaerobic conditions in which electrons are transferred to metabolites which accumulate and are excreted in reduced form. Fermentation is only possible if the organism is able to gain energy by this process.In microbiology, the process in which cells (microorganisms, plant or animal cells) are cultured in a bioreactor in liquid or solid medium to convert organic substances into biomass (growth) or into products.

F02338.title: fermenter
F02338.definition: A bioreactor which enables optimal fermentation conditions to be maintained, allowing addition of nutrients, removal of products and insertion of measuring and/or control probes as well as other necessary equipment (e.g. for heating, cooling, aeration, agitation, sterilization, etc.) under sterile conditions.

F02339.title: fermi
F02339.definition: Non-SI unit of length, \(\pu{f} = \pu{E-15 m}\), used in nuclear physics.

F02340.title: Fermi energy
F02340.definition: The total energy of an electron in an uncharged metal at the Fermi level.

09332.title: Fermi level referencing
09332.definition: Process for establishing the binding energy scale for a particular sample by assigning the kinetic energy corresponding to the Fermi level, as determined by analysis of the spectrum obtained from X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy or ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy, as the point of zero binding energy.

14013.title: Fermi level splitting
14013.definition: Splitting of the Fermi level in irradiated semiconductors and insulators into two Fermi quasi-levels for electrons \(E_{\rm{F}}^{\rm{e}}\) and for holes \(E_{\rm{F}}^{\rm{h}}\), displaced toward the bottom of the conduction band and toward the top of the valence band, respectively.

F02341.title: Fermi level
F02341.definition: The chemical potential of electrons in a solid (metals, semiconductors or insulators) or in an electrolyte solution.

08601.title: Fermi resonance
08601.definition: Cubic anharmonic resonance (see anharmonicity), i.e., any interaction caused by cubic terms in the vibrational potential energy.

F02342.title: fermion
F02342.definition: Particle of half-integer spin quantum number following Fermi–Dirac statistics.

FT06771.title: ferredoxin
FT06771.definition: A protein containing more than one iron and acid-labile sulfur, that displays electron-transfer activity but not classical enzyme function.

F02345.title: ferrocenophanes
F02345.definition: Compounds in which the two ring components of ferrocene are linked by one or more bridging chains.

F02346.title: ferroelastic transition
F02346.definition: A transition in which a crystal switches from one stable orientation state into another that is equally stable by the application of a mechanical stress along an appropriate direction.

F02347.title: ferroelectric transition
F02347.definition: A transition from a ferroelectric to either another ferroelectric, or a paraelectric, or an antiferroelectric state.

FT07172.title: ferroelectric polymer
FT07172.definition: Polymer in which spontaneous polarization arises when dipoles become arranged parallel to each other by electric fields.

F02348.title: ferroic transition
F02348.definition: A general term for ferroelastic, ferroelectric, antiferroelectric, ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic and ferrimagnetic transitions in which a suitable driving force switches a ferroic crystal from one orientation state, or domain state, to another.

FT07173.title: ferromagnetic polymer
FT07173.definition: Polymer that exhibits magnetic properties because it has unpaired electron spins aligned parallel to each other or electron spins that can easily be so aligned.

F02350.title: fertile
F02350.definition: Of a nuclide, capable of being transformed, directly or indirectly, into a fissile nuclide by neutron captureOf a material: containing one or more fertile nuclides.

15708.title: fertility
15708.definition: Ability to conceive and to produce offspring: For litter-bearing species, the number of offspring per litter is used as a measure of fertility.

10712.title: Fertility Assessment by Continuous Breeding
10712.definition: Reproductive toxicity test in rodents in which female animals are repeatedly mated and frequency and size of litter and other parameters are measured; second or later generation fertility is also studied.

15709.title: fertility toxicant
15709.definition: Produces abnormalities of male or female reproductive functions or impairs reproductive capacity.

10713.title: fertilization
10713.definition: In reproductive biology, union of male and female gametes to form a zygote from which an embryo can develop.

14685.title: fertilisation effect
14685.definition: Enhanced growth of plants as a result of exposure to low levels of pollutants such as nitrogen and sulfur oxides in acid precipitation.

14686.title: fertiliser
14686.definition: Substance applied to soil or hydroponic systems for improving the root nutrition of plants with the aim of increasing crop yields and (or) controlling production.

10714.title: fetal alcohol syndrome
10714.definition: Condition developing in the fetus and resulting in congenital abnormalities, caused by alcohol intake by the mother during pregnancy, typically characterized by decreased cognitive development, stunted growth and a characteristic facies.

10381.title: fetal anatomic position
10381.definition: Usual positioning of the developing fetus with the back curved forward, head bent forward, and limbs drawn in towards the body.

13147.title: fetal antigens
13147.definition: Human cancer cell antigens, which cross-react serologically with antigens normally expressed by embryonic tissue, e.g., carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), or $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}fetoprotein}$ (AFP).

10715.title: fetal pole
10715.definition: Thickening on the margin of the yolk sac of a fetus during pregnancy.

13148.title: fetal tolerance
13148.definition: Lack of rejection of a fetal allograft carrying paternal major histocompatibility complex (MHC) and minor histocompatibility antigens that differ from those of the mother.

10716.title: FETAX
10716.definition: Assay for teratogenicity using embryos of the frog, Xenopus laevis.

10717.title: fetoscopy
10717.definition: Procedure in which a fetus may be directly observed in utero, using a fiber-optic endoscope (fetoscope) introduced through a small incision in the abdomen under local anesthesia.

10718.title: fetus
10718.definition: Young mammal within the uterus of the mother, from the visible completion of characteristic organogenesis until birth.

10266.title: fibre format
10266.definition: Extraction phase in the form of a thin layer supported on a fibre made of inert material, such as fused silica, stainless steel, or nickel-titanium alloy.

FT07301.title: fibrillar morphology
FT07301.definition: Morphology in which phase domains have shapes with one dimension much larger than the other two dimensions.

11770.title: fibrillation
11770.definition: Rapid contractions or twitching of muscle fibrils, but not of the muscle as a whole.

13149.title: fibrinolysis
13149.definition: Enzymatic lysis of a fibrin clot.

13150.title: fibrinolytic
13150.definition: Pertaining to, characterized by, or causing the breakdown of fibrin (fibrinolysis), usually by the action of plasmin.

10719.title: fibroblast
10719.definition: Flat fibrous tissue cell, with stellate or spindle shape, associated with the formation of collagen fibers and intercellular extracellular matrix.

10720.title: fibroblast growth factor
10720.definition: Any member of a family of more than twenty protein growth factors involved in angiogenesis, wound healing, and, in early embryonic development, induction of mesoderm, patterning and morphogenesis, and development of the limbs and brain.

F02353.title: fibrous activated carbon
F02353.definition: An activated carbon in the form of fibres, filaments, yarns or rovings and fabrics or felts. Such fibres differ from carbon fibres used for reinforcement purposes in composites by their high surface area, high porosity and low mechanical strength.

F02355.title: fibrous crystal in polymers
F02355.definition: A type of crystal significantly longer in one dimension than in either of the other two. Fibrous crystals may comprise essentially extended chains parallel to the fibre axis; however, macroscopic polymer fibres containing chain-folded crystals are also known.

15712.title: fiducial limit
15712.definition: Form of confidence limit given as a stated probability, for example, \(P = \pu{0.95}\).

F02357.title: field desorption
F02357.definition: A term used to describe the formation of ions in the gas phase from a material deposited on a solid surface (known as an 'emitter') in the presence of a high electrical field. 'Field desorption' is an ambiguous term because it implies that the electric field desorbs a material as an ion from some kind of emitter on which the material is deposited. There is growing evidence that some of the ions formed are due to thermal ionization and some to field ionization of vapour evaporated from material on the emitter. Because there is generally little or no ionization unless the emitter is heated by an electric current, 'field desorption' is a misnomer. The term is, however, firmly implanted in the literature and most users undertand what is going on regardless of the implications of the term. In addition, no better simple term has been suggested to take its place and so, reluctantly, it is recommended that it be retained.

F02358.title: field effect
F02358.definition: An experimentally observable effect symbolized by \(F\) (on reaction rates, etc.) of intramolecular coulombic interaction between the centre of interest and a remote unipole or dipole, by direct action through space rather than through bonds. The magnitude of the field effect (or 'direct effect') depends on the unipolar charge/dipole moment, orientation of dipole, shortest distance between the centre of interest and the remote unipole or dipole, and on the effective dielectric constant.

F02360.title: field ionization
F02360.definition: The removal of electrons from any species by interaction with a high electrical field.

F02361.title: field level
F02361.definition: Logarithm of the ratio of two values of a field quantity, usually amplitude. Levels are expressed in different ways: \(L_{F}=\ln (\frac{F}{F_{0}})\ N_{\rm{p}}\), where \(N_{\rm{p}}\) is the symbol for the unit neper coherent with the SI, or \(L_{F}=20\ \log _{10}(\frac{F}{F_{0}})\ \mathrm{dB}\), where \(\mathrm{dB}\) is the symbol for the unit decibel.

08821.title: field-effect transistor
08821.definition: Transistor in which the flow of charge carriers from source to drain is controlled by the potential applied to the gate.

09934.title: field-flow fractionation
09934.definition: Separation based on the retention and elution of macromolecular, colloidal, and particulate matter achieved by the combined action of the non-uniform flow speed (velocity) profile of a carrier fluid (mobile phase) and a physical force field (e.g. gravitational, centrifugal, electrical) applied at right angles to a thin (\(\pu{0.05 mm}\) to \(\pu{0.5 mm}\)) channel (see figure). Basic principle of field-flow fractionation.Basic principle of field-flow fractionation.

09250.title: field-induced migration
09250.definition: Effect occurring in insulators or semi-conductors where internal electric fields cause the migration of sample atoms.

F02362.title: filamentous carbon
F02362.definition: A carbonaceous deposit from gaseous carbon compounds, consisting of filaments grown by the catalytic action of metal particles.

08822.title: fill factor
08822.definition: Ratio of the real maximum output power, \(P_{\rm{max}}\), that can be obtained with an actual solar cell to the product of the open-circuit potential, \(V_{\rm{oc}}\), and short-circuit photocurrent, \(I_{\rm{sc}}\): \[f_{\rm{FF}} = P_{\rm{max}}/V_{\rm{oc}}I_{\rm{sc}}\]

F02363.title: filler
F02363.definition: Filler (also called grist) is a petroleum- or coal-based coke fraction of a green, carbon mix or formulation. Coarse particles, \(>0.425\ \mathrm{mm}\), are sometimes referred to as tailings; fine particles, \(

F02364.title: filler coke
F02364.definition: The main constituent of a carbon artifact, introduced as solid component (predominantly in the form of particulate carbon) into the 'carbon mix' from which polygranular carbon and graphite materials are obtained by heat treatment.

F02365.title: filling solution
F02365.definition: Solution containing the anion to which the reference electrode of the operational pH cell is reversible, e.g. chloride for silver-silver chloride electrode. In the absence of a bridge solution, a high concentration of filling solution comprising cations and anions of almost equal mobility is employed as a means of maintaining the liquid junction potential small and approximately constant on substitution of test solution for standard solution(s).

F02366.title: film
F02366.definition: A generic term referring to condensed matter restricted in one dimension.

F02368.title: film badge
F02368.definition: A package containing one or more small photographic films for approximate measurement of radiation exposure, used for the purpose of monitoring personnel.

F02370.title: film element
F02370.definition: A small homogeneous part of a film including the two interfaces and any fluid between them.

F02381.title: film tension
F02381.definition: The contractile force per unit length, \(\unicode[Times]{x3A3}_{\rm{f}}\), exerted by an equilibrium film in contact with the bulk phase.

F02384.title: filter
F02384.definition: A porous material on which solid particles present in air or other fluid which flows through it are largely caught and retained. Filters are made with a variety of materials: cellulose and derivatives, glass fibre, ceramic, synthetic plastics and fibres. Filters may be naturally porous or be made so by mechanical or other means. membrane/ceramic filters are prepared with highly controlled pore size in a sheet of suitable material such as polyfluoroethylene, polycarbonate or cellulose esters. Nylon mesh is sometimes used for reinforcement. The pores constitute 80–85% of the filter volume commonly and several pore sizes are available for air sampling (\(0.45{-}0.8\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) are commonly employed).

F02385.title: filter
F02385.definition: Material interposed in the path of radiation to modify the spectral distribution of the radiation.

F02387.title: filter spectrometer
F02387.definition: A spectrometer which has one or more spectral filters for isolating one or more spectral bands.

F02388.title: filtration
F02388.definition: The process of segregation of phases; e.g. the separation of suspended solids from a liquid or gas, usually by forcing a carrier gas or liquid through a porous medium.

14687.title: final acute value
14687.definition: Estimate of the concentration of a substance corresponding to a cumulative probability of \(\pu{0.05}\) in the acute toxicity values for all species for which acceptable acute tests have been conducted on the material.

14688.title: final chronic value
14688.definition: Estimate of the concentration of a substance corresponding to a cumulative probability of \(\pu{0.05}\) in the chronic toxicity values for all genera for which acceptable chronic tests have been conducted on the material.

09333.title: final energy state
09333.definition: Energy state of an atom after a particular Auger, X-ray, or photoemission process.

14689.title: finding of no significant impact
14689.definition: Statement of no significant impact of a major federal action concluded after an environmental assessment (EA).

F02389.title: fine structure constant
F02389.definition: Atomic fundamental physical constant, \(\alpha =\frac{\mu _{0}\ e^{2}\ c_{0}}{2\ h} = 7.297\ 353\ 08\ \left(33\right)\times 10^{-3}\), where \(\mu _{0}\) is the permeability of vacuum, \(e\) the elementary charge, \(h\) the Planck constant, and \(c_{0}\) the speed of light.

08602.title: finesse
08602.definition: Free spectral range divided by resolution.

11771.title: finger tapping test
11771.definition: Procedure in which a test subject is asked to tap a finger at maximal rate on a surface, a higher rate of tapping indicating better neuromuscular function.

12656.title: fingerprint
12656.definition: Representation of a compound or chemical library by attributes (descriptors) such as atom connectivities, 3D structure, or physical properties.

08603.title: fingerprint bands
08603.definition: Infrared and Raman bands that are characteristic of a particular molecule rather than a functional group.

08604.title: fingerprint region
08604.definition: Region of a spectrum that contains fingerprint bands as well as bands with characteristic group frequencies.

14690.title: finite rate of increase
14690.definition: Rate of increase of population size measured over set intervals, such as between age classes of a life table or generations of a population with nonoverlapping generations, e.g., an annual plant.

13151.title: first line of defence
13151.definition: Surface tissues, notably the skin, respiratory tract, and gastrointestinal tract.

12657.title: first-in-class
12657.definition: First drug acting on a hitherto unaddressed molecular target to reach the market.

15713.title: first-order chemical reaction
15713.definition:
Chemical reaction where the initial rate is directly proportional to the concentration of one of the reactants.
Any process in which a variable decreases with time at a constant fractional amount.

F02390.title: first-order phase transition
F02390.definition: A transition in which the molar Gibbs energies or molar Helmholtz energies of the two phases (or chemical potentials of all components in the two phases) are equal at the transition temperature, but their first derivatives with respect to temperature and pressure (for example, specific enthalpy of transition and specific volume) are discontinuous at the transition point, as for two dissimilar phases that coexist and that can be transformed into one another by a change in a field variable such as pressure, temperature, magnetic or electric field. Example: The transition on heating $\ce{CsCl}$ to \(752\ \rm{K}\) at which it changes from the low-temperature, $\ce{CsCl}$-type structure to the high-temperature $\ce{NaCl}$-type structure. Synonymous with discontinuous phase transition.

FT06824.title: first-pass effect
FT06824.definition: Biotransformation and, in some cases, elimination of a substance in the liver after absorption from the intestine and before it reaches the systemic circulation.

F02391.title: Fischer projection
F02391.definition: A projection formula in which vertically drawn bonds are considered to lie below the projection plane and horizontal bonds to lie above that plane. Thus for the molecule Cabcd:

F02392.title: Fischer–Rosanoff convention
F02392.definition: An arbitrary convention according to which (+)-glyceraldehyde, now known to be (R)-2,3-dihydroxypropanal, was named ᴅ-glyceraldehyde (with the enantiomer ʟ-glyceraldehyde and its racemate ᴅʟ-glyceraldehyde) and taken to have the absolute configuration represented by the Fischer projection formula shown in the diagram.  The atom numbered 1 according to normal nomenclature rules is conventionally placed at the top of the main chain, which is drawn vertically and other groups are drawn on either side of that main chain. The convention is still in use for $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}amino acids}$ and for sugars.

14691.title: fish acute toxicity syndromes
14691.definition: Behavioral, physiological, and biochemical responses of fish used to classify chemicals by mode of action.

10721.title: fish embryo test
10721.definition: Procedure in which fish (often zebrafish, Danio rerio) eggs and embryos are exposed to a test chemical and subsequent development or death of the animals is studied.

10722.title: fish reproduction assay
10722.definition: Procedure in which sexually mature male and spawning female fish are exposed to a test substance and multiple endpoints, including egg production, endocrine activity, vitellogenin, and gonadal histopathology are measured.

10723.title: fish sexual development test
10723.definition: Procedure in which fish are exposed from the time of fertilization of the egg until sexual differentiation is completed and markers of possible endocrine disruptor activity are studied, including vitellogenin concentration, gonadal histopathology, sex ratios, and the occurrence of intersex.

F02394.title: fissile
F02394.definition: Of a nuclide: capable of undergoing fission by interaction with (slow) neutrons.Of a material: containing one or more fissile nuclides.

F02397.title: fission fragments
F02397.definition: Nuclei resulting from fission and possessing kinetic energy acquired from the fission process.

F02398.title: fission neutrons
F02398.definition: Neutrons originating in the fission process which have retained their original energy.

F02400.title: fission products
F02400.definition: Nuclides produced by fission and the daughter products of these nuclides.

F02401.title: fission yield
F02401.definition: The fraction of fissions leading to fission products of a given type.

10724.title: fistula
10724.definition: Permanent abnormal passage from an internal organ to the body surface or between two internal organs or structures.

14692.title: fitness advantage
14692.definition: Increased relative fitness of a resistant genotype in a polluted environment compared to a nonresistant genotype.

14693.title: fitness cost
14693.definition: Reduced relative fitness of a resistant genotype in an unpolluted environment compared to a nonresistant genotype.

08073.title: fitness for purpose
08073.definition: Ability of a product, process, or service to serve a defined purpose under specific conditions.

15328.title: fitting equation
15328.definition: Theoretically based or empirical equation for interpolation of data over a range of temperature, pressure, composition, or other variable.

15714.title: fixed dose procedure
15714.definition: Acute toxicity test in which a substance is tested initially at a small number (3 or 4) predefined doses to identify which produces evident toxicity without lethality: The test may be repeated at one or more higher or lower defined discriminating doses to satisfy the criteria.

F02402.title: fixed ions
F02402.definition: In an ion exchanger, the non-exchangeable ions which have a charge opposite to that of the counter-ions.

F02403.title: fixed neutral loss scan
F02403.definition: A scan which determines, in a single experiment, all the parent ion mass-to-charge ratios which react to the loss or gain of a selected neutral mass.

F02404.title: fixed neutral loss spectrum
F02404.definition: A spectrum obtained when data are acquired that determine all the parent ion mass-to-charge ratios that react by the loss (gain) of a selected neutral mass.

F02405.title: fixed precursor ion scan
F02405.definition: A scan which determines, in a single experiment, all the daughter ion mass-to-charge ratios that are produced by the reaction of a selected parent ion mass-to-charge ratio.

F02406.title: fixed product ion scan
F02406.definition: A scan which determines, in a single experiment, all the parent ion mass-to-charge ratios that react to produce a selected daughter ion mass-to-charge ratio (sometimes called a 'parent ion scan').

F02407.title: fixed product ion spectrum
F02407.definition: A spectrum obtained when data are acquired that determine all the parent ion mass-to-charge ratios that react to produce a selected daughter ion mass-to-charge ratio.

08476.title: flame
08476.definition: Continuously flowing mixture of hot gases with a stationary position that derives its heat content from a strongly exothermic, irreversible chemical reaction between a fuel and an oxidant.

08474.title: flame atomic spectrometer
08474.definition: Spectrometer to make measurements by flame atomic spectroscopy.

08475.title: flame atomic spectroscopy
08475.definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy that uses a flame to excite atoms.

F02410.title: flame ionization detector
F02410.definition: The gases emerging from the column are fed into a hydrogen flame across which an electrical potential is placed. Certain molecules ionize easily in the flame and the current produced is proportional to the instantaneous flow rate of the eluted component. The detector is relatively insensitive to inorganic molecules and is most used for organic compounds. Concentrations below \(1\ \rm{ppmv}\) are easily detected. The linear dynamic range is between \(10^{3}\) and \(10^{5}\).

F02411.title: flame photometric detector
F02411.definition: The eluent from the column is fed into a hydrogen-rich flame and produces light emission. Optical filters are used to select the wavelength range of the emission which is characteristic of specific atoms (usually sulfur or phosphorus). The detector is very specific, depending on the choice of optical filters. It can detect the S- and P-containing compounds down to \(10^{-3}\ \rm{ppmv}\), but the detector is non-linear.

F02412.title: flame photometry
F02412.definition: The use of emission spectroscopy in the ultraviolet and visible regions to identify and estimate the amounts of various elements which are excited in a flame, an arc or high voltage spark.

F02409.title: flame-in-tube atomizer
F02409.definition: An atomizer in which hydrogen, used as carrier gas, is partially combusted in the inlet arm of a T-shaped tube furnace by introducing a limited amount of oxygen or air.

10196.title: flash desorption
10196.definition: Thermal desorption where the temperature of a packed tube or cryogenic trap is rapidly increased to transfer condensed or sorbed compounds to the gas phase.

F02416.title: flash fluorimetry
F02416.definition: The term used when decay times luminescence are measured using a pulsed source of radiation. It is often necessary to separate the signal due to the light flash from luminescence emission signal by a deconvolution technique in order to obtain the correct decay curve for emission. Decay times corrected for this effect are termed corrected decay times of fluorescence or phosphorescence.

F02417.title: flash lamps
F02417.definition: Lamps which contain an inert gas which can be rapidly pulsed.

F02418.title: flash photolysis
F02418.definition: A technique of transient spectroscopy and transient kinetic studies in which a light pulse is used to produce transient species. Commonly, an intense pulse of short duration is used to produce a sufficient concentration of a transient species suitable for spectroscopic observation.

F02419.title: flash point
F02419.definition: The lowest temperature at which a substance, e.g. fuel oil, will give off a vapour that will flash or burn momentarily when ignited.

F02420.title: flash vacuum pyrolysis
F02420.definition: Thermal reaction of a molecule by exposing it to a short thermal shock at high temperature, usually in the gas phase.

F02421.title: flat band potential
F02421.definition: If effects of surface states are negligible, \(\Delta \varphi ^{\rm{sc}}\), the potential drop associated with the space charge in the semiconductor, vanishes as the charge on the semiconductor becomes zero. The potential of the semiconductor corresponding to this condition is the flat band potential, which plays the same role as the potential of zero charge for metals.

09967.title: flavans
09967.definition: Flavans are compounds with a 2-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran skeleton (1 in flavonoids), that may be substituted, and include flavan-3-ols (compounds derived from 2-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran-3-ol skeleton 2) and flavan-4-ones (compounds derived from 2-phenyl-2,3-dihydro-4\(H\)-1-benzopyran-4-one skeleton 3), which are generically designated as flavanols and flavanones, respectively. Compounds derived from 2-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran-3,4-diol skeleton 4 are flavan-3,4-diols, designated leukoanthocyanidins because these colourless compounds have their structure derived from that of an anthocyanidin, specifically they are dehydronated 3,4-dihydroxy-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroanthocyanidins.

F02423.title: flavins
F02423.definition: Derivatives of the dimethylisoalloxazine (7,8-dimethylbenzo[g]pteridine- 2,4(3H,10H)-dione) skeleton, with a substituent on the 10 position. (Riboflavin, having a 10-ᴅ-ribityl group, is the most prominent member).

09968.title: flavones
09968.definition: Flavones and 3-hydroxyflavones (flavonols) are compounds with a 2-phenyl-4\(H\)-1-benzopyran-4-one (2-phenyl-4\(H\)-chromen-4-one) skeleton 5.

F02424.title: flavonoids
F02424.definition: Flavonoids, isoflavonoids and neoflavonoids are natural products derived from 2-phenylchromen-4-one (flavone), 3-phenylchromen-4-one and 4-phenylcoumarin, respectively. Derivations include reduction of the 2(3) carbon-carbon double bond (flavanones), reduction of the keto group (flavanols), and hydroxylation at various positions.

09977.title: flavonolignans
09977.definition: Flavonolignans have structures based on flavonoids condensed with \(\ce{C6{-}C3}\) lignan precursors.

F02425.title: flavoproteins
F02425.definition: Flavins tightly bound or covalently attached to a protein chain, commonly through the 8-methyl carbon atom.

08343.title: flip angle
08343.definition: Rotation that the net magnetization experiences during the application of a radiofrequency pulse in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

F02428.title: floc
F02428.definition: When a sol is colloidally unstable the formation of aggregates is called coagulation or flocculation. Some authors distinguish between coagulation and flocculation, the latter implying the formation of a loose or open network which may or may not separate macroscopically. The loose structure formed in this way is called a floc.

F02430.title: floccule
F02430.definition: A small loosely aggregated mass of material suspended in or precipitated from a liquid; a cluster of particles.

15401.title: floor temperature
15401.definition: Temperature below which, in a given chain polymerization, polymer of high molar mass is not formed.

12264.title: Flory–Fox assumption
12264.definition: Assumption that the Kirkwood–Riseman theory can be applied to linear isolated macromolecules in solution, independent of whether they are in the theta state.

12265.title: Flory–Fox equation
12265.definition: Equation relating intrinsic viscosity, \(\eta\), and molar mass, \(M\), to the mean-square radius of gyration, with \[[\eta]M = \mathit{\Phi}^{\prime}\!\lt\!s^{2}\!\gt^{3/2}\] where \(\mathit{\Phi}^{\prime}\) is a parameter the value of which depends on the molar-mass distribution, macromolecular constitution, and chain expansion.

F02431.title: Flory–Huggins theory
F02431.definition: A thermodynamic theory of polymer solutions, first formulated independently by Flory and by Huggins, in which the thermodynamic quantities of the solution are derived from a simple concept of combinatorial entropy of mixing and a reduced Gibbs energy parameter, the 'χ parameter'.

F02432.title: flotation
F02432.definition: The removal of matter by entrainment at an interface.

F02433.title: flow analysis
F02433.definition: The generic name for all analytical methods that are based on the introduction and processing of test samples in flowing media.

13152.title: flow cytometry
13152.definition: Method of sorting and measuring types of cells by fluorescent labeling of markers on the surface of the cells. It is sometimes referred to as fluorescence-assisted (or activated) cell sorting (FACS) analysis.

14133.title: flow cytometry assay
14133.definition: Cell-based assay in which the response is dependent on the detection of the phenotype of cells as determined through the light-scattering properties of each cell, and, typically, the fluorescence intensity of a relevant probe.

09935.title: flow field-flow fractionation
09935.definition: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is a nonspecific hydrodynamic force field across the channel, generated by a secondary mobile phase cross-flow in addition to the normal channel flow.

F02436.title: flow injection
F02436.definition: The introduction of a sample or reagent into a continuous stream by use of a rapid delivery device.

F02437.title: flow injection enthalpimetry
F02437.definition: A term used to describe several related methods in which a transient temperature change in a flowing liquid stream, caused by a chemical reaction, is used to quantitatively determine an analyte. The analyte is introduced as a discrete liquid sample (i.e. test portion) into the flowing stream. This definition limits the scope to experiments with primarily an analytical emphasis, performed in a flow injection calorimeter. This maintains a clear distinction from classical flow calorimetric methods where reagents are combined continuously in flowing streams, or where the heat effect is measured via the flowing of a fluid over a reaction vessel. An acceptable synonym is enthalpimetric flow injection analysis. Other non-recommended terms which have been used in the literature include 'peak enthalpimetry' and 'enzyme thermistor'. Flow enthalpimetry has been used to describe the flow injection technique, but its use for this purpose is discouraged.

F02439.title: flow rate
F02439.definition: The volume of mobile phase passing through the column in unit time. The flow rate is usually measured at column outlet, at ambient pressure (\(p_{\rm{a}}\)) and temperature (\(T_{\rm{a}}\), in \(\rm{K}\)); this value is indicated with the symbol \(F\). If a water-containing flowmeter was used for the measurement (e.g. the so-called soap bubble flowmeter) then \(F\) must be corrected to dry gas conditions in order to obtain the mobile phase flow rate at ambient temperature (\(F_{\rm{a}}\)): \[F_{\rm{a}}=F\ (1- \frac{p_{\rm{w}}}{p_{\rm{a}}})\] where \(p_{\rm{w}}\) is the partial pressure of water vapour at ambient temperature. In order to specify chromatographic conditions in column chromatography, the flow-rate (mobile phase flow rate at column temperature, \(F_{\rm{c}}\)) must be expressed at \(T_{\rm{c}}\) (kelvin), the column temperature: \[F_{\rm{c}}=F_{\rm{a}}\ \frac{T_{\rm{c}}}{T_{\rm{a}}}\]

F02440.title: flow rate
F02440.definition: The volume rate of one component, $\ce{\textbf{X}}$ (e.g. air, $\ce{O2}$), of the unburnt gas mixture (such as $\ce{C2H2}$, $\ce{O2}$, etc.) in the burner tip. Ambient temperature and pressure must be stated.

F02441.title: flow rate
F02441.definition: Quantity \(X\) (e.g. heat, amount, mass, volume, ...) transferred in a time interval divided by that time interval. General symbols: \(q_{X}\), \(\overset{.}{X}\).

F02442.title: flow rate of unburnt gas mixture
F02442.definition: The volume rate of the gas mixture of the burner tip. It depends on operating conditions such as gas pressure; the ambient temperature and pressure should also be stated.

F02443.title: flow reactor
F02443.definition: A reactor through which the reactants pass while catalysis is in progress.

F02444.title: flow resistance parameter
F02444.definition: A term used to compare packing density and permeability of columns packed with different particles; it is dimensionless. \[\mathit{\Phi} = \frac{d_{\rm{p}}^{2}}{B_{0}}\] where \(d_{\rm{p}}\) is the average particle diameter. In open-tubular columns \(\mathit{\Phi} = 32\).

08477.title: flow spoiler
08477.definition: Component of a flame atomic spectrometer for creating turbulence in the stream of mist in the spray chamber and removing the largest droplets from this mist by deposition.

F02438.title: flow-programmed chromatography
F02438.definition: A procedure in which the rate of flow of the mobile phase is changed systematically during a part or the whole of the separation.

10300.title: flow-through extraction
10300.definition: Extraction by flow of sample through or over the extraction phase, or vice versa, to enhance the extraction rate.

10301.title: flow-through solid-phase spectrometry
10301.definition: Continuous optical interrogation of a packed-sorbent bed in a flow system at any stage of the extraction process prior to analyte elution and sorbent regeneration.

14694.title: flow-through system
14694.definition: Exposure system for aquatic toxicity tests in which the test material solutions and control water flow into and out of test chambers on a once-through basis either intermittently or continuously.

14695.title: flow-through test
14695.definition: Aquatic toxicity test performed in a flow-through system.

14696.title: fluctuating asymmetry
14696.definition: Deviation from perfect bilateral symmetry for a population of a bilaterally symmetrical species that is thought to reflect developmental instability.

F02446.title: flue gas
F02446.definition: Waste gas from the combustion process.

F02447.title: flue gas scrubber
F02447.definition: Equipment for removing fly ash and other objectionable materials from the products of combustion by means of sprays or wet baffles.

FT07376.title: fluence rate
FT07376.definition: Total radiant power, \(P\), incident from all directions onto a small sphere divided by the cross-sectional area of that sphere. SI unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-2}\).

F02448.title: fluence
F02448.definition: At a given point in space, the radiant energy incident on a small sphere divided by the cross-sectional area of that sphere. It is used in photochemistry to specify the energy delivered in a given time interval (for instance by a laser pulse).

F02449.title: fluid coke
F02449.definition: The carbonization product of high-boiling hydrocarbon fractions (heavy residues of petroleum or coal processing) produced by the fluid coking process.

14697.title: fluid feeder
14697.definition: Organism that feeds on the fluids of other animals or of plants.

F02451.title: fluidized bed
F02451.definition: A catalyst bed in which the flow of gases is sufficient to cause the finely divided particles to behave like a fluid.

13153.title: fluorescein isothiocyanate
13153.definition: Green fluorescent dye used to 'tag' antibodies for use in immunofluorescence.

F02453.title: fluorescence
F02453.definition: Luminescence which occurs essentially only during the irradiation of a substance by electromagnetic radiation.

14134.title: fluorescence correlation assay
14134.definition: Assay in which fluctuations in fluorescence intensity are detected and used to characterize a species that is labeled with a fluorescent probe.

F02455.title: fluorescence error
F02455.definition: Some samples are excited to fluorescence by the incident radiation beam. When added to the transmitted radiation beam this fluorescence results in an erroneous reading called the fluorescence error. It is particularly noticeable if the photodetector is situated close to the sample.

FT07377.title: fluorescence lifetime
FT07377.definition: Parameter describing the time evolution of the decay of the fluorescent radiant intensity.

14135.title: fluorescence polarisation
14135.definition: Dimensionless value determined from the fluorescence intensities (\(I\)) measured parallel (\(I_{\Vert}\)) and perpendicular (\(I_{\perp}\)) to the excitation plane: \[p = \frac{I_{\Vert} - I_{\perp}}{I_{\Vert} + I_{\perp}}\]

14136.title: fluorescence polarisation assay
14136.definition: Assay in which the association between an intrinsically fluorescent ligand, or a ligand linked to a fluorescent probe, and a larger macromolecule is detected.

FT07378.title: fluorescence resonance energy transfer
FT07378.definition: Term frequently and inappropriately applied to resonance energy transfer in the sense of Förster-resonance-energy transfer (FRET), which does not involve the emission of radiation.

14137.title: fluorescence resonance energy transfer assay
14137.definition: Assay based on the nonradiative energy transfer that occurs when the emission spectrum of a fluorescent donor molecule overlaps with the absorption spectrum of an energy acceptor molecule.

F02457.title: fluorescence yield
F02457.definition: For a given transition from an excited state of a specified atom, the ratio of the number of excited atoms which emit a photon to the total number of excited atoms.

09868.title: fluorescent in situ hybridization
09868.definition: Cytogenetic technique used to detect and localise the presence or absence of specific deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequences on chromosomes. It uses fluorescent probes that only bind to those parts of the chromosome with which they show a high degree of sequence complementarity.

13155.title: fluorescent antibody
13155.definition: Antibody conjugated to a fluorescent dye such as fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC).

F02458.title: fluorimeter
F02458.definition: An instrument used to measure the intensity and the wavelength distribution of the light emitted as fluorescence from a molecule excited at a specific wavelength or wavelengths within the absorption band of a particular compound. Characteristic fluorescence bands may be used to identify specific pollutants such as the polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons. Excitation spectra of impurities can be observed by scanning the wavelength of the excitation light which is incident on the sample over a range of wavelengths and observing the relative intensity of the fluorescence emitted at a given wavelength. These spectra are also characteristic of the impurity.

F02459.title: fluorocarbons
F02459.definition: Compounds consisting wholly of fluorine and carbon.

FT07379.title: fluorogenic
FT07379.definition: Property of a material in which fluorescence is induced or enhanced by the addition of another molecular entity.

13818.title: fluorophilic
13818.definition: Qualifier indicating attraction to fluorous compounds.

13820.title: fluorophobic
13820.definition: Qualifier indicating repulsion by fluorous compounds.

13821.title: fluorophobic interaction
13821.definition: Repulsive interaction of fluorous and non-fluorous structures.

FT07380.title: fluorophore
FT07380.definition: Molecular entity (often organic) that emits fluorescence.

08880.title: fluoropolymers
08880.definition: Polymers whose macromolecules are rich in fluorocarbon groups (structure-based polymer class name).

15715.title: fluorosis
15715.definition: Adverse effects of fluoride, as in dental or skeletal fluorosis.

13822.title: fluorous
13822.definition: Pertaining to the presence of a sufficient number of carbon-fluorine bonds as to cause a substance to be insoluble in water or common organic solvents but soluble in fluorocarbons.

10178.title: fluorous extraction
10178.definition: Extraction in a biphasic system in which the main component of one phase is a highly fluorinated solvent (liquid-liquid extraction) or highly fluorinated sorbent (solid-phase extraction).

F02462.title: flux depression
F02462.definition: The lowering of the particle (or photon) flux density in the neighbourhood of an object due to absorption of particles (or photons) in the object.

08726.title: flux monitor
08726.definition: Radiation detector to measure energy flux density.

09251.title: flux of a beam of particles
09251.definition: \(\mathit{\Phi} = {\rm{d}}N/{\rm{d}}t\), where \(N\) is number of particles of a specified type and \(t\) is time.

08727.title: flux perturbation
08727.definition: Change of energy flux density or energy distribution of particles or photons in an object as a result of effects such as flux depression and/or self-shielding.

F02461.title: flux
F02461.definition: Flow rate of X through a cross-section perpendicular to the flow divided by the cross-sectional area.

F02463.title: fluxional
F02463.definition: A chemical species is said to be fluxional if it undergoes rapid degenerate rearrangements (generally detectable by methods which allow the observation of the behaviour of individual nuclei in a rearranged chemical species, e.g. NMR, X-ray). Example: bullvalene (1 209 600 interconvertible arrangements of the ten CH groups).  The term is also used to designate positional change among ligands of complex compounds and organometallics. In these cases, the change is not necessarily degenerate.

09796.title: fluxomics
09796.definition: In vivo measurements of metabolic fluxes and integration of the results into stoichiometric network models.

F02465.title: fly ash
F02465.definition: Finely divided particles of ash entrained in flue gases resulting from the combustion of fuel.

13140.title: fMLP peptide
13140.definition: Formyl-methionyl-leucyl-phenylalanine, a chemoattractant (see chemotactic factor, chemotaxis) derived from degradation of bacterial or mitochondrial proteins. It causes neutrophil activation.

F02467.title: foam
F02467.definition: A dispersion in which a large proportion of gas by volume in the form of gas bubbles, is dispersed in a liquid, solid or gel. The diameter of the bubbles is usually larger than \(1\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\), but the thickness of the lamellae between the bubbles is often in the usual colloidal size range. The term froth has been used interchangeably with foam. In particular cases froth may be distinguished from foam by the fact that the former is stabilized by solid particles (as in froth flotation q.v.) and the latter by soluble substances.

F02468.title: foam fractionation
F02468.definition: A method of separation in which a component of the bulk liquid is preferentially adsorbed at the liquid/vapour (L/V) interface and is removed by foaming.

10241.title: foamed polyurethane sorbent
10241.definition: Sorbent consisting of spherical, micron-sized, agglomerated particles bound together in a rigid and highly porous structure used for the extraction of semi-volatile organic compounds from air in high-volume samplers.

F02469.title: foaming agent
F02469.definition: A surfactant which when present in small amounts facilitates the formation of a foam, or enhances its colloidal stability by inhibiting the coalescence of bubbles.

09613.title: focal unit
09613.definition: Core unit of a dendrimer molecule that comprises only one dendron

15716.title: foci
15716.definition: Small groups of cells distinguishable, in appearance or histochemically, from the surrounding tissue: indicative of an early stage of a lesion that may lead to the formation of a neoplastic nodule.

09493.title: focused ion beam
09493.definition: Technique used for the site-specific analysis, deposition, ablation, and micromachining of materials down to dimensions of \(\pu{10}\) to \(\pu{15 nm}\).

09252.title: focused ion beam system
09252.definition: Ion beam system used for machining small regions with sub-micron precision.

10727.title: foetus
10727.definition: Alternative spelling of fetus found in British English usage.

F02470.title: fog
F02470.definition: A general term applied to a suspension of droplets in a gas. In meteorology, it refers to a suspension of water droplets resulting in a visibility of less than \(1\ \rm{km}\).

F02471.title: fog horizon
F02471.definition: The top of a fog layer which is confined by a low-level temperature inversion and gives the appearance of the horizon (which it actually obscures) when viewed from above, against the sky.

F02472.title: folates
F02472.definition: A group of heterocyclic compounds based on the pteroic acid skeleton (below) conjugated with one or more ʟ-glutamate units.

F02474.title: fold domain
F02474.definition: A portion of a polymer crystal wherein the fold planes have the same orientation. The sectors of lamellar crystals frequently represent fold domains.

F02473.title: fold
F02473.definition: The loop connecting two different stems in a folded chain.

F02476.title: fold plane
F02476.definition: A crystallographic plane defined by a large number of stems that are connected by chain folds.

F02477.title: fold surface
F02477.definition: A surface approximately tangential to the folds.

13823.title: foldamer
13823.definition: Polymer or oligomer molecule that adopts a secondary structure stabilized by noncovalent interactions.

F02475.title: folded-chain crystal
F02475.definition: A polymer crystal consisting predominantly of chains that traverse the crystal repeatedly by folding as they emerge at its external surfaces. The re-entry of the chain into the crystal is assumed to be adjacent or near-adjacent within the lattice.

08248.title: folding
08248.definition: The appearance of peaks at incorrect frequencies in a mathematically-processed spectrum due to insufficient density of datapoints in the time-domain spectrum or from peaks outside of the sampled frequency range.This process can be simulated by folding a spectrum that shows the correct wavenumbers back onto itself at \(\tilde{\nu}_{\rm{M}}\) and its multiples.

10728.title: folic acid
10728.definition: Water-soluble B vitamin involved in breakdown of carbohydrates, releasing energy and promoting biosynthesis.

10729.title: follicle
10729.definition:
Small, secretory sac, such as the dental follicles that enclose the teeth before eruption or the hair follicles within the epidermis.
Fluid- or colloid-filled ball of cells in some glands such as the thyroid gland and the ovaries.

10730.title: follicle-stimulating hormone
10730.definition: Hormone secreted by the anterior pituitary that stimulates the Graafian follicles of the ovary and subsequent follicular maturation, and in the male contributes to inducing spermatogenesis.

10731.title: follicle-stimulating hormone releasing hormone
10731.definition: Hormone, released by the hypothalamus, inducing the secretion of follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone by the pituitary gland.

10732.title: follicular atresia
