10732.definition: Degeneration and resorption of an ovarian follicle before it reaches maturity and ruptures.

13156.title: follicular dendritic cell
13156.definition: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II-negative Fc receptor-positive dendritic cell which bears immune complexes on its surface and is probably involved in the generation of antibody-secreting cells and maintenance of B-cell memory (see memory cell) in germinal centers.

10733.title: follicular phase
10733.definition: First half of the human menstrual cycle, during which one or more follicles in the ovary may mature, culminating in ovulation.

12658.title: follow-on drug
12658.definition: Drug having a similar mechanism of action to an existing drug.

10734.title: fontanelle
10734.definition: Any of several soft spots in specific locations on the skull of the newborn where the bones have not yet fused and the brain is covered by skin and a tough membrane.

15717.title: food additive
15717.definition: Any substance, not normally consumed as a food by itself and not normally used as a typical ingredient of a given food, whether or not it has nutritive value, that is added intentionally to food for a technological (including organoleptic) purpose in the manufacture, processing, preparation, treatment, packing, packaging, transport, or holding of the food. Addition results, or may be reasonably expected to result (directly or indirectly), in the substance or its byproducts becoming a component of, or otherwise affecting, the characteristics of the food to which it is added.

15718.title: food allergy
15718.definition: Hypersensitivity reaction to substances in the diet to which an individual has previously been sensitized.

14698.title: food chain
14698.definition: Hierarchical sequence of transfer of substances from prey organism to predator organism.

15719.title: food intolerance
15719.definition: Physiologically based reproducible, unpleasant (adverse) reaction to a specific food or food ingredient that is not immunologically based.

14699.title: food-mass feeder
14699.definition: Animal that feeds on the body parts of other animals.

F02478.title: foot
F02478.definition: Non-SI unit of length, \(\pu{ft} = \pu{12 in} = \pu{0.3048 m}\).

13157.title: footpad test
13157.definition: Test for allergic contact dermatitis in which the test substance is injected into the front footpad of a guinea pig and challenge is performed seven days later.

10736.title: foramen magnum
10736.definition: Large foramen in the base of the skull, through which the spinal cord passes.

10737.title: foramen ovale
10737.definition:
In the fetal heart, opening that allows shunting of blood between the right and left atria and normally closes at birth.
One of the larger foramina in the base of the skull.

F02481.title: force constants
F02481.definition: The coefficients in an expansion of the intramolecular potential function in terms of a definite set of coordinates, the values of which define the deformation of the molecule away from its equilibrium configuration. In order to define force constants, one has to indicate both the definition of each coordinate and the expansion of the potential.

11446.title: force field
11446.definition: A set of mathematical functions and their associated parameters used in a molecular mechanics or dynamics calculation of conformations, flexibility, and interactions of molecules.

F02480.title: force
F02480.definition: Derivative of momentum with respect to time.

15721.title: forced diuresis
15721.definition: Method of stimulating diuresis based on performing hydrational therapy, sometimes with parallel introduction of diuretics, with the aim of achieving increased clearance of a toxic substance in urine.

12767.title: forced sinusoidal oscillation
12767.definition: Deformation of a material by the application of a small sinusoidal strain (\(\gamma\)) such that \[\gamma = \gamma_{0} \cos \omega t\] where \(\gamma_{0}\) and \(\omega\) are positive constants.

08169.title: formal charge
08169.definition: Quantity (omitted if zero) attached to each atom in a Lewis structure according to \[Z_{\rm{formal}} = N_{\rm{valence}} - N_{\rm{lonepairs}} - ½N_{\rm{bonds}}\]

09065.title: formal electrode potential
09065.definition: Equilibrium electrode potential under conditions of unit concentration of species involved in the electrode reaction. \[E_{\rm{eq}} = E^{\circ\prime} - (RT/zF) \mathop \sum \limits_{i} \nu_{i} \ln(c_{i}/c^{\circ)\] where \(E_{\rm{eq}}\) is the equilibrium electrode potential, \(R\) the gas constant, \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature, \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(z\) the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, \(\nu_{\rm{i}}\) the stoichiometric coefficients (numbers of species) in the equation of the electrode reaction (positive for products and negative for reactants), and \(c_{\rm{i}}\) are the amount concentrations of the species involved (most usually ions).

F02484.title: formamidine disulfides
F02484.definition: The compound $\ce{H2NC(=NH)SSC(=NH)NH2}$ and its derivatives formed by substitution at nitrogen.

F02485.title: formation constant
F02485.definition: For a mononuclear binary complex, if a central atom (central group) $\ce{M}$ (the 'metal') and a ligand $\ce{L}$ have been defined, then in the following expressions \(K_{n}\) is the stepwise formation constant, and \(\beta_{n}\) is the cumulative formation constant for the complex $\ce{ML_{n}}$. They can both be referred to as stability constants (stepwise and cumulative). \[K_{n}=K(\rm{ML}_{n- 1}+\rm{L}\rightleftharpoons \rm{ML}_{n})\] \[\beta_{n} = K(\rm{M}+n\rm{L}\rightleftharpoons \rm{ML}_{n})\]

F02486.title: formazans
F02486.definition: The parent compound $\ce{H2NN=CHN=NH}$ and its derivatives formed by substitution at carbon and/or nitrogen.

15188.title: formulation
15188.definition: Summary of operations carried out to convert a pharmacologically active compound into a dosage form suitable for administration.

13158.title: Forssman antigen
13158.definition: Glycolipid heterophile antigen (globopentosylceramide) expressed on cell surfaces during embryonic and adult life in rodents and other mammals, and found in many pathogens, but probably not in humans.

F02487.title: Förster cycle
F02487.definition: An indirect method of determination of excited state equilibria, such as \(\rm{p}K^{\rm{*,a}}\) values, based on ground state thermodynamics and electronic transition energies. This cycle considers only the difference in molar enthalpy change (\(\Delta \Delta H\)) of reaction of ground and excited states, neglecting the difference in molar entropy change of reaction of those states (\(\Delta \Delta S\)).

F02488.title: Förster excitation transfer
F02488.definition: A mechanism of excitation transfer which can occur between molecular entities separated by distances considerably exceeding the sum of their van der Waals radii. It is described in terms of an interaction between the transition dipole moments (a dipolar mechanism). The transfer rate constant \(k_{D \rightarrow  A}\) is given by: \[k_{\ce{D -> A}} = \frac{K^{2}J \pu{8.8E-28 mol}}{n^{4} \tau_{0} r^{6}}\] where \(K\) is an orientation factor, \(n\) the refractive index of the medium, \(\tau _{0}\) the radiative lifetime of the donor, \(r\) the distance (cm) between donor (D) and acceptor (A), and \(J\) the spectral overlap (in coherent units \(\pu{cm6 mol-1}\)) between the absorption spectrum of the acceptor and the fluorescence spectrum of the donor. The critical quenching radius, \(r_{0}\), is that distance at which \(k_{D \rightarrow  A}\) is equal to the inverse of the radiative lifetime.

FT07381.title: Förster-resonance-energy transfer
FT07381.definition: Non-radiative excitation transfer between two molecular entities separated by distances considerably exceeding the sum of their van der Waals radii. It describes the transfer in terms of the interaction between the transition (dipole) moments of the entities in the very weak dipole-dipole coupling limit. It is a Coulombic interaction frequently called a dipole-dipole coupling. The transfer rate constant from donor to acceptor, \(k_{\rm{T}}\), is given by \[k_{\rm{T}} = k_{\rm{D}}\left ( \frac{R_{0}}{r} \right )^{6}=\frac{1}{\tau _{D}^{0}}\left ( \frac{R_{0}}{r}\right )^{6}\] where \(k_{\rm{D}}\) and \(\tau_{\rm{D}}^{0}\) are the emission rate constant and the lifetime of the excited donor in the absence of transfer, respectively, \(r\) is the distance between the donor and the acceptor and \(R_{0}\) is the critical quenching radius or Förster radius, i.e., the distance at which transfer and spontaneous decay of the excited donor are equally probable (\(k_{\rm{T}} = k_{\rm{D}}\)) (see Note 3). \(R_{0}\) is given by \[R_{0} = Const.\left ( \frac{\kappa^{2}\mathit{\Phi}_{D}^{0}J }{n^{4}} \right )^{1/6}\] where \(\kappa\) is the orientation factor, \(\mathit{\Phi} _{D}^{0}\) is the fluorescence quantum yield of the donor in the absence of transfer, \(n\) is the average refractive index of the medium in the wavelength range where spectral overlap is significant, \(J\) is the spectral overlap integral reflecting the degree of overlap of the donor emission spectrum with the acceptor absorption spectrum and given by \[J = \int _{\lambda }I_{\lambda}^{D}(\lambda)\epsilon _{A}\left ( \lambda \right )\lambda^{4}\rm{d}\lambda\] where \(I_{\lambda}^{D}(\lambda)\) is the normalized spectral radiant intensity of the donor so that \(\int_{\lambda}I_{\lambda}^{D}(\lambda)\rm{d}\lambda = 1\). \(\varepsilon_{\rm{A}}({\lambda})\) is the molar decadic absorption coefficient of the acceptor. See Note 3 for the value of \(Const.\).

10125.title: forward chaining
10125.definition: Inference method from data to hypothesis.

10738.title: forward genetics
10738.definition: Approach to genetic investigation in which the aim is to identify the gene that governs a particular function.

10126.title: forward stepwise linear discriminant analysis
10126.definition: Linear discriminant analysis in which variables to build the discriminant functions are introduced one at a time to maximise the discrimination, until there is no significant improvement.

10739.title: fossa
10739.definition: In anatomy, a depression or hollow, often in a bone.

10740.title: fossa ovalis
10740.definition: Oval depression in the heart, on the lower part of the septum of the right atrium.

14700.title: fossil
14700.definition: Mineralized or otherwise preserved remnant or trace (such as a footprint) of an animal, plant, and other organism.

F02490.title: fossil fuel
F02490.definition: A fuel such as coal, oil and natural gas which has formed over many years through the decomposition of deposited vegetation which was under extreme pressure of an overburden of earth.

F02491.title: fouling agent
F02491.definition: Fouling agents (or mechanical inhibitors) are inhibitory substances bound by neither covalent nor other strong bonds to the active centres: the interaction is usually of the van der Waals, H-bond or sometimes ionic, type. They form protective layers or block pores, thus physically impeding access of reactants to the active centres. The fouling agents which cause real problems are those which have a long standing effect and do not disappear spontaneously. Carbon deposits act, partially or totally, this way (see coking). Other examples are vanadium and nickel sulfide deposits in hydrotreating catalysts.

FT06876.title: fouling
FT06876.definition: Process resulting in loss of performance of a membrane due to the deposition of suspended or dissolved substances on its external surfaces, at its pore openings, or within its pores.

15722.title: founder effect
15722.definition: Changes in allelic frequencies that occur when a small group is separated from a large population and establishes a colony in a new location.

F02492.title: Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometer
F02492.definition: A high-frequency mass spectrometer in which the cyclotron motion of ions, having different mass/charge ratios, in a constant magnetic field is excited essentially simultaneously and coherently by a pulse or a radio-frequency electric field applied perpendicular to the magnetic field. The excited cyclotron motion of the ions is subsequently detected on so-called receiver plates as a time domain signal that contains all the cyclotron frequencies that have been excited. Fourier transformation of the time domain signal results in the frequency domain FT-ICR signal which, on the basis of the inverse proportionality between frequency and the mass/charge ratio, can be converted into a mass spectrum. The term is sometimes contracted to Fourier transform mass spectrometer (FT-MS).

F02493.title: Fourier transform spectrometer
F02493.definition: A scanning interferometer, containing no principal dispersive element, which first splits a beam into two or more components, then recombines these with a phase difference. The spectrum is obtained by a Fourier transformation of the output of the interferometer.

08605.title: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
08605.definition: Infrared spectroscopy in which a Fourier-transform spectrometer is used to separate the transmitted electromagnetic radiation into its component wavenumbers.

08606.title: Fourier-transform Raman spectroscopy
08606.definition: Raman spectroscopy in which a Fourier-transform spectrometer is used to separate the scattered electromagnetic radiation into its component wavenumbers.

FT07382.title: Fourier-transform spectroscopy
FT07382.definition: Measurement technique whereby spectra are collected based on measurements of the temporal coherence of a radiative source, using time-domain measurements of the electromagnetic radiation or other type of radiation.

13141.title: Foxp3
13141.definition: Transcription repressor that is specifically expressed in CD4+CD25+ T cells.

FT07549.title: fractal agglomerate
FT07549.definition: Agglomerate having the same fractal dimension as the constituent particles.

FT07550.title: fractal dimension
FT07550.definition: Parameter that provides a mathematical description of the fractal structure of a polymer network, an aggregated particulate sol, or of the particles that comprise them.

F02494.title: fraction
F02494.definition: In general, a ratio of two quantities of the same kind, the numerator quantity applying to one constituent (or part) of the system and the denominator to the sum of quantities for all constituents (parts) of the system. When applied to mixtures fractions represent a group of three quantities: mass fraction, volume fraction, and amount fraction (or amount fraction equal to the number fraction).

F02501.title: fraction collector
F02501.definition: A device for recovering fractional volumes of the column effluent.

F02503.title: fraction extracted
F02503.definition: The fraction of the total quantity of a substance extracted (usually by the solvent) under specified conditions, i.e. \(E_{\rm{A}} = \frac{Q_{\rm{A}}}{Q_{\rm{A}}^{'}}\) where \(Q_{\rm{A}}\) is the mass of A extracted and \(Q_{\rm{A}}^{'}\) is the total mass of A present at the start.

F02495.title: fractional change of a quantity
F02495.definition: A term which may be expressed infinitesimally at time \(t\) by the differential \(\frac{\rm{d}Q(t)}{Q(t)}\). For a finite time interval the quotient is \[\frac{\Delta Q\left(t_{1};t_{2}\right)}{Q\left(t_{1}\right)} = \frac{\left[Q\left(t_{2}\right)\,-\,Q\left(t_{1}\right)\right]}{Q\left(t_{1}\right)}\] The quantities \(Q(t_{1})\) and \(Q(t_{2})\) are of the same kind and have the same type of component. Fractional change has dimension one. Examples are: mass fractional change, \(\frac{\rm{d}m(t)}{m(t)}\); amount of substance fractional change, \(\frac{\rm{d}n(t)}{n(t)}\).

09401.title: fractional ion yield
09401.definition: Number of ions of a particular species sputtered from a sample divided by number of particles of that species sputtered from that sample.

F02496.title: fractional selectivity
F02496.definition: The term selectivity (\(S\)) is used to describe the relative rates of two or more competing reactions on a catalyst. Such competition includes cases of different reactants undergoing simultaneous reactions or of a single reactant taking part in two or more reactions. For the latter case, \(S\) may be defined in two ways. The first of these defines a fractional selectivity, \(S_{\rm{F}}\), for each product by the equation \[S_{\rm{F}}=\frac{\xi _{i}}{\sum \xi _{i}}\] The second defines relative selectivities, \(S_{\rm{R}}\), for each pair of products by \[S_{\rm{R}}=\frac{\xi _{i}}{\xi _{j}}\] In each case, \(\xi _{i}\) and \(\xi _{j}\) are the rates of increase of the extent of reactions i and j respectively, i.e. \[\xi _{i}=\frac{\mathrm{d}\xi _{i}}{\mathrm{d}t}\] and \[\xi _{j}=\frac{\mathrm{d}\xi _{j}}{\mathrm{d}t}\] where \(\xi _{i}\) and \(\xi _{j}\) are the extents of reactions \(i\) and \(j\) respectively.

09253.title: fractional sputtering yield
09253.definition: Number of atoms and ions of a particular species sputtered from a sample divided by the total number of atoms and ions sputtered from the sample.

10073.title: fractional-factorial design
10073.definition: Experimental design obtained from a full-factorial design in which experiments are systematically removed to fulfill stated statistical requirements.

FT06825.title: fractionation
FT06825.definition: Process of classification of an analyte or a group of analytes from a sample according to physical (e.g., size, solubility) or chemical (e.g., bonding, reactivity) properties.

F02497.title: fractionation
F02497.definition: A process by means of which macromolecular species differing in some characteristic (chemical composition, relative molecular mass, branching, stereoregularity, etc.) are separated from each other.

12768.title: fragile glass
12768.definition: Glass characterised by a large value of the fragility index (m).

12769.title: fragility index
12769.definition: Quantity characterising the fragility or the strength of a glass at a given temperature \[m = \left (\frac{\rm{d} \log_{10} \tau}{{\rm{d}} (T_{\rm{g}}/T)} \right)_{T = T_{\rm{g}}}\] \(\tau\) = relaxation time [\(\pu{s}\)]; \(T_{\rm{g}}\) = glass-transition temperature [\(\pu{K}\)]; \(T\) = temperature [\(\pu{K}\)].

12659.title: fragment
12659.definition: Low-molar-mass ligand (typically smaller than \(\pu{200 Da}\)) that binds to a target with low affinity but high ligand efficiency.

F02508.title: fragment ion
F02508.definition: An electrically charged dissociation product of an ionic fragmentation. Such an ion may dissociate further to form other electrically charged molecular or atomic moieties of successively lower formula weight.

11447.title: fragment keys
11447.definition:
Description of the structure of a molecule as the presence or absence of each of a pre-determined set of molecular substructures, usually associated with a
 particular location in a bit string.

12660.title: fragment-based lead discovery
12660.definition: Screening libraries of low-molar-mass compounds (typically \(\pu{120\!{-}\! 250 Da}\)) using sensitive biophysical techniques capable of detecting weakly binding lead compounds.

F02506.title: fragmentation
F02506.definition: The heterolytic cleavage of a molecule according to the general reaction:  where $\ce{{a}-b}$ is an electrofuge and $\ce{X}$ is a nucleofuge (which may emerge from the reaction in combined form), and the middle group affords the unsaturated fragment $\ce{c=d}$. For example, The breakdown of a radical into a diamagnetic molecule or ion and a smaller radical, e.g. The breakdown of a radical ion in a mass spectrometer or in solution, forming an ion of lower molar mass and a radical, e.g.

F02507.title: fragmentation reaction
F02507.definition: A fragmentation reaction may be written: \[\rm{M}_{1}^{+}\rightarrow \rm{M}_{2}^{+}+\rm{M}_{3}\] The decomposition of a metastable ion of mass-to-charge ratio \(\frac{m_{1}}{z_{1}}\) into an ion of mass-to-charge ratio \(\frac{m_{2}}{z_{2}}\) after electric acceleration of the metastable ion and before magnetic deflection gives rise to a peak in the mass spectrum at an apparent mass, \(\frac{m_{2}^{2}\ z_{1}}{m_{1}\ z_{2}^{2}}\). The symbol \(m^{*}\) should be used to indicate the apparent mass of the product ions giving rise to this peak. Traditionally, the peak itself has been called a metastable peak and this should preferably be expressed as metastable ion peak. It is nevertheless recommended that the former term should be retained. The word metastable should never be used as a noun. Its use as an adjective should be limited to such terms as metastable ion, where it is used correctly, and to the special case of metastable peak discussed above. It should never be used in such terms as metastable reaction, metastable decomposition, metastable studies, etc. It should be clear that the metastable ion is the ion that undergoes fragmentation; it is not detected. When a reaction is written with an asterisk above the arrow as shown: \[\rm{M}_{1}^{+}\overset{\rm{*}}{\rightarrow }\rm{M}_{2}^{+}+\rm{M}_{3}\] this means that the reaction has been confirmed by the observation of a metastable peak. The textual description of such a process may be written as, for example, (\(m^{*}\), \(43\rightarrow 28\), calcd. 18.2, obsd. 18.3) meaning 'for the fragmentation \(\frac{m}{z}\ 43\rightarrow \frac{m}{z}\ 28\) a metastable peak at \(\frac{m}{z}\) 18.3 (calculated 18.2) has been observed'.

F02509.title: frame-shift mutation
F02509.definition: A point mutation involving either the deletion or insertion of a nucleotide in a gene. By the frame-shift mutation, the normal reading frame used when decoding the nucleotide triplets in the gene is altered to another reading frame.

13159.title: framework region
13159.definition: One of several relatively conserved amino acid sequences that flank the hypervariable regions in immunoglobulin (Ig) and T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V) regions and maintain a common overall structure for all V region domains.

16203.title: Franck–Condon factor
16203.definition: Squared modulus of the overlap integral between the vibrational wave functions (\(\mathit{\Theta}\)) for the initial (0) and final (\(\rm{e}\)) state of a given electronic transition. \[\left\vert \int \mathit{\Theta} _{\rm{v'}}^{(\rm{e})} \mathit{\Theta} _{\rm{v}}^{(0)} dQ \right\vert^{2}\] where the integration is over all nuclear coordinates.

F02510.title: Franck–Condon principle
F02510.definition: Classically, the Franck–Condon principle is the approximation that an electronic transition is most likely to occur without changes in the positions of the nuclei in the molecular entity and its environment. The resulting state is called a Franck–Condon state, and the transition involved, a vertical transition. The quantum mechanical formulation of this principle is that the intensity of a vibronic transition is proportional to the square of the overlap integral between the vibrational wavefunctions of the two states that are involved in the transition.

14014.title: free charge carriers
14014.definition: Applies to free electrons or free holes.

F02513.title: free charge density on the interface
F02513.definition: The physical charge density believed to occur on either side of the electrical double-layer.

08823.title: free charge-carrier photogeneration
08823.definition: Generation of free charge carriers by photons.

F02514.title: free electron laser
F02514.definition: Source of coherent radiation in which the active medium is an electron beam moving at speeds close to the speed of light in the spatially periodic magnetic field produced by an array of magnets (the wiggler). The emitted wavelength, \(\lambda _{\rm{L}}\), is approximately given by \[\frac{\lambda _{\omega }}{4\ E^{2}}\] with \(\lambda _{\omega }\) being the wiggler period and \(E\) the electron's energy in \(\mathrm{MeV}\).

14015.title: free electrons
14015.definition: Photoexcited electrons from the valence band into the conduction band in semiconductors and insulators.

11448.title: free energy perturbation
11448.definition: A method that uses molecular dynamics or Metropolis Monte Carlo simulations to compute the relative free energy differences between two conditions, typically the solution and bound states of a ligand-protein system.

08249.title: free induction decay
08249.definition: Indication from a pulsed spectroscopy experiment that takes the form of damped sine waves arising from the excited system returning to equilibrium.

15402.title: free ion
15402.definition: Ion whose behavior is independent of the influence of a counterion.

14701.title: free ion activity model
14701.definition: Model for acute metal toxicity to aquatic organisms based on the idea that toxicity occurs when the concentration of the free metal cation in solution reaches a certain level.

12770.title: free oscillation
12770.definition: Oscillatory deformation of a material specimen with the motion generated without the continuous application of an external force.

F02520.title: free rotation
F02520.definition: In a stereochemical context the rotation about a bond is called 'free' when the rotational barrier is so low that different conformations are not perceptible as different chemical species on the time scale of the experiment. The inhibition of rotation of groups about a bond due to the presence of a sufficiently large rotational barrier to make the phenomenon observable on the time scale of the experiment is termed hindered rotation or restricted rotation.

08607.title: free spectral range
08607.definition: For a Fabry-Perot or laser cavity, wavenumber interval between successive longitudinal cavity modes of vibration; \(\Delta \tilde{\nu} = 1/(2nl)\), where \(l\) is the cavity spacing and \(n\) is the refractive index of the material in the cavity.

12234.title: free volume
12234.definition: Difference between specific volume of an amorphous polymer and that of its perfect crystalline form.

12254.title: free-draining
12254.definition: Adjective describing the undisturbed flow of solvent through the domain of a dissolved macromolecule.

F02521.title: free-running laser
F02521.definition: A term applied to a pulsed laser, meaning that the laser emission lasts as long as the pumping process is sufficient to sustain lasing conditions. Typical pulse durations are in the \(\pu{\upmu s}\)-\(\pu{ms}\) range, depending on the pumping source. When the operation mode of a pulsed laser is not specified as mode-locked, Q-switched, or anything else, it must be considered as free-running.

F02516.title: freely draining
F02516.definition: An adjective referring to a chain macromolecule the segments of which produce such small frictional effects when moving in a medium that the hydrodynamic field in the vicinity of a given segment is not affected by the presence of other segments. Thus, the solvent can flow virtually undisturbed through the domain occupied by a freely draining macromolecule.

F02517.title: freely jointed chain
F02517.definition: A hypothetical linear chain molecule consisting of infinitely thin rectilinear segments uniform in length; each segment can take all orientations in space with equal probability, independently of its neighbours. For models in which the segments are not all uniform in length, the name 'random-walk chain' has been used.

F02518.title: freely rotating chain
F02518.definition: A hypothetical linear chain molecule, free from short-range and long-range interactions, consisting of infinitely thin rectilinear segments (bonds) of fixed length, jointed at fixed bond angles; the torsion angles of the bonds can assume all values with equal probability.

F02523.title: freezing
F02523.definition: The conversion of a liquid to a solid by lowering the temperature and/or the application of pressure.

F02524.title: freezing out
F02524.definition: A term used in combustion for the analysis of incinerator flue gas components (largely the organic fraction) in which a series of traps at progressively lower temperatures is employed. In more general use, the term implies the removal of a condensable gas or liquid by condensation in a trap at low temperatures.

F02526.title: frequency distribution
F02526.definition: If the range of observed measurement values is subdivided into a regular sequence of smaller intervals, this distribution is a plot of the frequency of occurrence of values falling into each interval.

FT07384.title: frequency-domain fluorometry
FT07384.definition: Technique that permits recovery of the parameters characterizing a fluorescence decay. Instead of using an exciting visible, UV, or infrared radiation pulse (see single-photon timing), the sample is excited by sinusoidally modulated radiation at high frequency. The fluorescence response is sinusoidally modulated at the same frequency as, but delayed in phase and partially demodulated with respect to the excitation.

FT07383.title: frequency
FT07383.definition: The number of waveperiods per time interval. The linear frequency, \(\nu\), is the number of cycles per time interval. SI unit \(\rm{Hz =  s}^{-1}\).

12661.title: frequent hitter
12661.definition: Structural feature that regularly results in a positive response in a variety of high-throughput or primary screens.

08250.title: Fresnel reflection
08250.definition: Reflection of radiation from a surface that is smooth and large with respect to the wavelength of the radiation. A reflected beam, of intensity governed by the Fresnel equations, is produced at an angle of reflection equal to the angle of incidence.

13160.title: Freund’s adjuvant
13160.definition: Complete Freund’s adjuvant is an emulsion of aqueous antigen in mineral oil that contains heat-killed Mycobacteria.

14702.title: Freundlich adsorption isotherm
14702.definition: Empirical equation that describes the adsorption of a contaminant to soil. The equation is \[x/m = (K_{\rm{f}} C_{\rm{e}}) \exp (1/n)\] where \(x/m\) is the mass ratio of concentrations of adsorbed substance at equilibrium divided by the concentration of the contaminant in soil, \(C_{\rm{e}}\) is the contaminant concentration in the aqueous phase at equilibrium, \(K_{\rm{f}}\) is the equilibrium constant (the Freundlich adsorption constant), and \(1/n\) is a contaminant specific exponent.

F02530.title: friction factor
F02530.definition: Quotient of frictional force and normal force, for a sliding body. Formerly called frictional coefficient or coefficient of friction.

F02528.title: frictional coefficient
F02528.definition: A tensor correlating the frictional force, \(F\), opposing the motion of a particle in a viscous fluid and the velocity \(u\) of this particle relative to the fluid. In the case of an isolated spherical particle in a viscous isotropic fluid, \(f\) is a constant and \(F=f\ u\).

F02531.title: fringed-micelle model
F02531.definition: A model of crystallinity in which the crystallized segments of a macromolecule belong predominantly to different crystals.

F02535.title: front surface geometry
F02535.definition: A system where excitation and observation are from the same face of the sample (\(\alpha\ \angle\ 90^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\), \(\beta\ \angle\ 180^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) where \(\alpha \) = angle of incidence of the exciting beam on the plane surface of the sample, and \(\beta \) = angle between the exciting direction and observation direction.)

F02532.title: frontal chromatography
F02532.definition: A procedure in which the sample (liquid or gas) is fed continuously into the chromatographic bed. In frontal chromatography no additional mobile phase is used.

11773.title: frontal lobe
11773.definition: Most anterior of the four major lobes of each cerebral hemisphere, containing the primary motor cortex.

F02533.title: frontier orbitals
F02533.definition: The Highest-energy Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO) (filled or partly filled) and Lowest-energy Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO) (completely or partly vacant) of a molecular entity. Examination of the mixing of frontier molecular orbitals of reacting molecular entities affords an approach to the interpretation of reaction behaviour; this constitutes a simplified perturbation molecular orbital theory of chemical behaviour.

F02534.title: fronting
F02534.definition: Asymmetry of a peak such that, relative to the baseline, the front is less steep than the rear. In paper chromatography and thin-layer chromatography, it refers to the distortion of a spot showing a diffuse region in front of the spot in the direction of flow.

10741.title: frontonasal dysplasia
10741.definition: Congenital malformation of the midface in which the nose has a flat, wide appearance, the eyes may be wide-set, and there is a groove of varying size, running down the middle of the face across the nose.

11774.title: frontotemporal dementia
11774.definition: Neurodegenerative disease characterized by progressive neuronal defects in the frontal and temporal lobes of the brain, leading to dementia.

F02536.title: frost point hygrometer
F02536.definition: Instrument in which the sample is passed over a cooled surface. The temperature at which frost forms on it is a function of the water content of the gas passing over the surface.

F02537.title: froth flotation
F02537.definition: The removal of particulate matter by foaming.

F02538.title: Frumkin effect
F02538.definition: In an electrode reaction, when reactants or intermediates are adsorbed, the rate of reaction may no longer be related to the concentration by a simple law. The deviation may be due to either entropic or energetic effects or both. The situation best understood is that where a reactant is non-specifically adsorbed in the outer Helmholtz plane (inner boundary of the diffuse layer). The effect of such adsorption on electrode kinetics is usually termed the Frumkin effect. Rate constants, transfer coefficients etc. corrected for this effect are frequently called 'true' rate constants etc. It would be preferable to describe them as 'corrected for the Frumkin effect', but in any case, if such a correction is carried out, the basis on which it is made should be clearly described.

08170.title: frustrated Lewis acid-base pair
08170.definition: Acid and base for which adduct formation is prevented by steric hindrance.

F02540.title: fuel cycle
F02540.definition: The sequence of steps, such as utilization, reprocessing, and refabrication, through which nuclear fuel may pass.

F02541.title: fuel element
F02541.definition: The smallest structurally discrete part of a reactor which has fuel as its principal constituent.

F02542.title: fuel reprocessing
F02542.definition: The processing of nuclear fuel, after its use in a reactor, to remove fission products and recover fissile and fertile material.

F02544.title: fugacity coefficient
F02544.definition: Ratio of fugacity to the partial pressure of a gaseous constituent.

F02543.title: fugacity
F02543.definition: Of a substance B, \(f_{\rm{B}}\) or \(\tilde{p}_{\rm{B}}\), in a gaseous mixture is defined by \(f_{\rm{B}}=\lambda _{\rm{B}}\ \lim _{p\rightarrow 0}\frac{p_{\rm{B}}}{\lambda _{\rm{B}}}\), where \(p_{\rm{B}}\) is the partial pressure of B and \(λ_{\rm{B}}\) its absolute activity.

F02546.title: full energy peak
F02546.definition: Of a spectrum of radiation, the part of the spectral response curve corresponding to the total absorption in a detecting material of the energy of the detected radiation.

10197.title: full-evaporation headspace analysis
10197.definition: Small volume of sample in a headspace vessel maintained at a temperature sufficient to cause complete evaporation of analytes.

10074.title: full-factorial design
10074.definition: Experimental design with all possible combinations of factor levels.

F02547.title: fullerenes
F02547.definition: Compounds composed solely of an even number of carbon atoms, which form a cage-like fused-ring polycyclic system with twelve five-membered rings and the rest six-membered rings. The archetypal example isfullerene, where the atoms and bonds delineate a truncated icosahedron. The term has been broadened to include any closed cage structure consisting entirely of three-coordinate carbon atoms.

F02548.title: fulminates
F02548.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RON=C{:}}$. So called because fulminic acid (actually $\ce{HC#N^{+}–O^{−}}$ formonitrile oxide) was previously considered to be $\ce{HON=C{:}}$.Salts of fulminic acid, e.g. $\ce{Na^{+}[–C#N^{+}O^{−}]}$.

F02549.title: fulvalenes
F02549.definition: The hydrocarbon fulvalene and its derivatives formed by substitution (and by extension, analogues formed by replacement of one or more carbon atoms of the fulvalene skeleton by a heteroatom).

F02550.title: fulvenes
F02550.definition: The hydrocarbon fulvene and its derivatives formed by substitution (and by extension, analogues formed by replacement of one or more carbon atoms of the fulvene skeleton by a heteroatom).

14703.title: fulvic acid
14703.definition: Humic substance that is soluble at all \(\rm{pH}\)s.

F02551.title: fume
F02551.definition: Fine solid particles (aerosol), predominantly less than \(1\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) in diameter, which result from the condensation of vapour from some types of chemical reaction. Usually this is formed from the gaseous state generally after volatilization from melted substances and often accompanied by chemical reactions such as oxidation.

F02552.title: fumes
F02552.definition: In popular usage, a term often taken to mean airborne effluents, unpleasant and malodorous, which might arise from chemical processes.

15723.title: fumigant
15723.definition: Substance that is vaporized in order to kill or repel pests.

F02553.title: fumigation
F02553.definition: An atmospheric phenomenon in which pollution, retained by an inversion layer near its level of emission, is brought rapidly to ground level as the inversion breaks up. This term also applies to the exposure of material (e.g. grain) to chemicals to kill insects, etc.

14138.title: functional assay
14138.definition: Assay in which the biological or physiological activity of the target is measured.

11449.title: functional class fingerprints
11449.definition:
Hashed circular fingerprints that encode each atom according to its property (hydrophobic, hydrogen bond donor, hydrogen bond acceptor, negatively charged, or
 positively charged) for path length 2, FCFP2; path length 4, FCFP4; and path length 6, FCFP6.

F02554.title: functional class name
F02554.definition: A name that expresses the characteristic group as a class term written as a separate word following the name of a parent structure or a name derived from a parent structure. In the latter case, when the derived name is that for a substituent group (formerly called a 'radical'), the method has been called 'radicofunctional nomenclature'.

11775.title: functional domain
11775.definition: In the brain, referring to the concept that discrete regions are involved in specific aspects of cognitive function, thus giving rise to modularity.

10742.title: functional genomics
10742.definition: Development and implementation of technologies to characterize the mechanisms through which genes and their products function and interact with each other and with the environment.

F02555.title: functional group
F02555.definition: Organic compounds are thought of as consisting of a relatively unreactive backbone, for example a chain of \(\rm{sp}^{3}\) hybridized carbon atoms, and one or several functional groups. The functional group is an atom, or a group of atoms that has similar chemical properties whenever it occurs in different compounds. It defines the characteristic physical and chemical properties of families of organic compounds.

11776.title: functional observational battery
11776.definition: Structured set of tests to examine changes in neuromuscular, arousal, autonomic and sensory functions that assesses the presence, absence or severity of specific neurological signs.

F02556.title: functional parent
F02556.definition: A structure the name of which implies the presence of one or more characteristic groups and which has one or more hydrogen atoms attached to at least one of its skeletal atoms or one of its characteristic groups, or in which at least one of its characteristic groups can form at least one kind of functional modification.

FT07174.title: functional polymer
FT07174.definition: Polymer that bears specified chemical groups.Polymer that has specified physical, chemical, biological, pharmacological, or other uses which depend on specific chemical groups.

09746.title: functional proteomics
09746.definition: Field of study in proteomics studying protein interactions on different levels: protein-protein interactions (interactomics), the formation of protein complexes, and the interaction of proteins with other biomolecules.

14704.title: functional redundancy
14704.definition: Apparently unaltered maintenance of community function despite changes in structure.

14705.title: functional response
14705.definition: Change in some predator function, such as prey consumption rate, in response to changes in prey density.

FT07505.title: functionality
FT07505.definition: Number of covalent bonds that a monomer molecule or monomeric unit in a macromolecule or oligomer molecule can form with other reactants.

14016.title: fundamental absorption
14016.definition: Absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation in semiconductors and insulators inducing optical transitions of electrons originating exclusively from the valence band to the conduction band to yield free electron-hole pairs and/or exciton absorption bands.

14017.title: fundamental absorption edge
14017.definition: High wavelength limit of the fundamental absorption band in the spectrum of semiconductors and of insulators.

14706.title: fundamental niche
14706.definition: Environmental conditions under which a species can thrive.

10743.title: fundus
10743.definition: Part of a hollow organ (e.g., the uterus) that is furthest from its opening.

15724.title: fungus preparation
15724.definition: Substance obtained from fungi that has an insecticidal effect reflecting the pathogenicity of the fungi for insects.

15248.title: furan polymer
15248.definition: Polymer prepared from furan or a furan derivative.

F02559.title: furanoses
F02559.definition: Cyclic hemiacetal forms of monosaccharides in which the ring is five-membered (i.e. a tetrahydrofuran skeleton).

F02561.title: furnace pyrolysis
F02561.definition: A flowing stream of gas (hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, chlorine, etc.) required to produce volatile species of the elements being determined, is passed over the test sample in a heated furnace. The analytes leave the furnace in the gas stream, or are entrained by a carrier gas. The analytes in the gas stream may be collected in an absorbing solution, on a carbon or other filter or by condensation on a cool surface. In the case of mercury this can also be done by amalgamation with a noble metal. The analytes may then be swept and released from the trap, by heating, into a sampling source for analysis.

F02562.title: furocoumarins
F02562.definition: Derivatives (mostly of natural origin) of the linear furocoumarin skeleton, psoralen, or its angular isomer, angelicin, variously substituted with hydroxy, methoxy, alkyl, or hydroxymethyl groups, among others.

11777.title: fused in sarcoma transcription factor
11777.definition: Nuclear DNA- and RNA-binding protein involved in transcription, splicing, and RNA-transport.

F02563.title: fusion
F02563.definition: The amalgamation of two distinct cells or macromolecules into a single integrated unit.

F02564.title: fusion name
F02564.definition: A composite name for a polycyclic parent structure having the maximum number of non-cumulative double bonds and at least one ortho fusion. Name formation involves the dissection of the structure into contiguous components having recognized trivial or semisystematic names, one of which is selected as the 'base component'. attachment of the other components is described by prefixes.

10127.title: fuzzy clustering
10127.definition: Classification in which membership of an object in each possible class is given a weight between zero and one.

13142.title: Fv fragment
13142.definition: Variable (V) region fragment of an antibody heavy chain or light chain.

13959.title: green polymer
13959.definition: Polymer that conforms to the concept of green chemistry.

12421.title: gas chromatography-mass spectrometry
12421.definition: Technique by which a mixture is separated into individual components by gas chromatography, followed by detection with a mass spectrometer.

12422.title: glow discharge ionization
12422.definition: Formation of ions from gaseous atoms or molecules or from the vapor of a solid sample at the cathode by applying a potential difference between two electrodes immersed in a low-pressure inert gas environment.

12423.title: gridless reflectron
12423.definition: Reflectron design in which the decelerating/accelerating field is produced without the use of wire-mesh grids.

13907.title: genetic engineering
13907.definition: Process of inserting new genetic information into existing cells in order to modify a specific organism for the purpose of changing its characteristics.

09402.title: g index
09402.definition: Power for the ratio of mass intensities in two mass spectra measured for two different primary ion conditions, used to generate the G-SIMS spectrum.

11795.title: G protein-coupled receptor
11795.definition: Seven-transmembrane-domain receptor that interacts with guanosine triphosphate/diphosphate (GTP/GDP) binding proteins to initiate signal transduction.

G02571.title: G value
G02571.definition: The number of specified chemical events in an irradiated substance produced per \(100\ \rm{eV}\) of energy absorbed from ionizing radiation.

12212.title: g-factor
12212.definition: Ratio of the mean-square radius of gyration of a branched molecule, \(\lt\!s_{\rm{b}}^{2}\!\gt\), to that of an otherwise identical linear molecule, \(\lt\!s_{\rm{l}}^{2}\!\gt\), of the same relative molecular mass in the same solvent at the same temperature, i.e., \(g = \lt\!s_{\rm{b}}^{2}\!\gt\!/\!\lt\!s_{\rm{l}}^{2}\!\gt\).

10094.title: G-fold cross validation
10094.definition: Cross validation of a data set of \(N\) objects in which \(N/G\) objects are removed at each iteration of the procedure.

12662.title: G protein
12662.definition: Member of a family of membrane-associated proteins which on activation by cellular receptors lead to signal transduction.

09186.title: G-SIMS
09186.definition: Variant of static secondary-ion mass spectrometry in which the intensities for each mass in two spectra from the same area, recorded with different beam energies or different bombarding ions, are ratioed to each other and the result is used to scale one of the spectra to generate a new spectrum.

09403.title: G-SIMS with fragmentation pathway mapping
09403.definition: Development of G-SIMS in which the g index is varied in order to deduce the linkages between product ions and precursor ion.

12213.title: g′-factor
12213.definition: Ratio of the intrinsic viscosity of a branched molecule, \([\eta_{\rm{b}}]\), to that of an otherwise identical linear molecule, \([\eta_{\rm{l}}]\), of the same relative molecular mass in the same solvent at the same temperature, i.e., \(g^{\prime} = [\eta_{\rm{b}}]/[\eta_{\rm{l}}]\).

11778.title: GABAergic
11778.definition: Pertaining to the action of $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}aminobutyric acid}$ or to neural or metabolic pathways in which it functions as a neurotransmitter.

14707.title: Gaia hypothesis
14707.definition: Hypothesis proposed by James Lovelock that the Earth’s temperature, albedo, and surface chemistry are homeostatically regulated by the sum of all the biota of the Earth.

G02572.title: gain
G02572.definition: The gain of a photomultiplier is given by the equation \(G=k\ \sigma ^{n}\), where \(k\) is the efficiency of collection of photoelectrons on the first dynode, \(\sigma \) is the secondary emission ratio, i.e. the number of secondary electrons emitted for each electron incident on the dynode and \(n\) is the number of dynodes.

10744.title: gall bladder
10744.definition: Pear-shaped muscular sac underneath the liver that stores bile secreted by the liver before its release into the duodenum.

G02574.title: Galvani potential difference
G02574.definition: An electric potential difference between points in the bulk of two phases. It is measurable only when the two phases have identical composition (e.g. two copper wires). It is the difference of inner electric potentials in two phases. Symbol: \(\Delta _{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\phi \).

09066.title: galvanic cell
09066.definition: Electrochemical cell in which chemical reactions occur spontaneously and chemical energy is converted into electrical energy.

09076.title: galvanostat
09076.definition: Instrument which controls the electric current between the working electrode and the auxiliary electrode.

10745.title: gamete
10745.definition: Reproductive cell (e.g., sperm or egg) containing a haploid set of chromosomes.

10746.title: gamete intrafallopian transfer
10746.definition: Technique of assisted reproduction by placing eggs and sperm into a woman’s Fallopian tubes in order that fertilization may occur there.

14708.title: gametic selection
14708.definition: Natural selection resulting from differential success of gametes produced by heterozygotes.

10747.title: gametogenesis
10747.definition: Development of male or female gametes to maturity.

12771.title: gamma relaxation
12771.definition: Third-highest-temperature or third-lowest-frequency relaxation in the loss curve of a polymer.

12772.title: gamma relaxation peak
12772.definition: Third-highest-temperature or third-lowest-frequency peak in the loss curve of a polymer.

08728.title: gamma-ray spectrometry
08728.definition: Measurement principle of the quantitative study of the energy spectra of gamma-ray sources.

13165.title: gammaglobulin
13165.definition: One of a group of serum proteins, mostly immunoglobulins (Ig), which have the greatest mobility towards the cathode during electrophoresis.

11779.title: ganglion
11779.definition:
Cluster of nerve cell bodies located outside the brain and spinal cord, i.e., in the peripheral nervous system.Note: Ganglia interconnect to form a complex network known as a plexus and serve as relay stations where different neurons can modulate the signals of each other. Compare: basal ganglion.
Fibrous cyst usually attached to a tendon sheath.

11781.title: ganglioside
11781.definition: Glycosphingolipid chemically similar to cerebrosides but containing one or more sialic (N-acetylneuraminic or N-glycolylneuraminic) acid residues, found principally in nerve tissue, spleen, and thymus.

15189.title: gargle
15189.definition: Aqueous solution used for the prevention and treatment of mouth and throat infections.

G02576.title: gas analysis installation
G02576.definition: An assembly for the purpose of determining one or more components in a gaseous mixture. It generally comprises the following elements: sample probe, region of primary treatment of the gases, region of secondary treatment of gases, points for venting to the atmosphere and for calibration sample injection, transfer line and the analytical unit.

G02577.title: gas black
G02577.definition: Finely divided carbon (graphite) produced by incomplete combustion or thermal decomposition of natural gas.

G02578.title: gas chromatography
G02578.definition: A separation technique in which the mobile phase is a gas. Gas chromatography is always carried out in a column.

G02579.title: gas constant
G02579.definition: Fundamental physical constant, \(R = \pu{8.314472(15) J K-1 mol-1}\).

12295.title: gas flow
12295.definition: Passage of gas from one part of the system to another. The gas may be either inert (carrier gas) or reactive, either introduced into the system or evolving from the sample.

G02585.title: gas laser
G02585.definition: A laser in which the active medium is a gas containing a laser active species. It is typically composed of a plasma discharge tube containing a gas that can be excited with an electric discharge.

G02590.title: gas sensing electrode
G02590.definition: A sensor composed of an indicator and a reference electrode in contact with a thin film of solution which is separated from the bulk of the sample solution by a gas-permeable membrane or an air gap. This intermediate solution interacts with the gaseous species (penetrated through the membrane or an air gap) in such a way as to produce a change in a measured constituent (e.g. the $\ce{H^{+}}$ activity) of the intermediate solution. This change is then sensed by the ion-selective electrode and is related to the partial pressure of the gaseous species in the sample. [Note: In electrochemical literature the term gas electrode is used for the classical, redox-equilibrium-based gas electrodes as well, such as the hydrogen or the chlorine gas electrodes ($\ce{Pt(s)}$|$\ce{H2(g)}$|$\ce{H^{+}(aq)}$ or $\ce{Pt(s)}$|$\ce{Cl2(g)}$|$\ce{Cl^{-}(aq)}$]. These electrodes respond both to the partial pressure of the gas ($\ce{H2}$ or $\ce{Cl2}$) and to the ionic activities ($\ce{H^{+}}$ or $\ce{Cl^{-}}$). The Clark oxygen electrode fits under this classification although, in contrast to other gas sensors, it is an amperometric and not a potentiometric device.

G02581.title: gas-filled phototube
G02581.definition: Similar in construction to a vacuum phototube except that it is filled with a noble gas (usually $\ce{Ar}$) at a pressure of about \(10\ \rm{Pa}\). Photoelectrons accelerated by the anode electric potential ionize gas atoms. The additional electrons provide a substantial intrinsic gain.

G02582.title: gas-filled X-ray detector
G02582.definition: A cylindrical cathode with a window, an axial wire anode and an ionizable gas. The gas may be continuously replenished giving a flow-through detector or the detector may be sealed. Following an original ionizing event, electron multiplication occurs through a process of gas amplification in the high electric field surrounding the anode wire. The gain of this process is defined as the number of electrons collected on the anode wire for each primary electron produced. For X-rays having energies higher than the excitation potential of the detector gas, the spectral responsivity function has a second peak in addition to the main peak that is called the escape peak. The escape peak has a mean pulse height proportional to the difference between the photon energy of the incident X-rays and of the spectral characteristic line of the detector gas. A quenching gas, a molecular gas, is added to the detector gas in order to neutralize the detector gas ions and to absorb secondary electrons as well as UV radiation resulting from neutralization of detector gas ions. According to the potential applied to the anode, the detector can work as an ionization chamber, proportional counter, or Geiger counter.

G02586.title: gas-liquid chromatography
G02586.definition: Comprises all gas-chromatographic methods in which the stationary phase is a liquid dispersed on a solid support. Separation is achieved by partition of the components of a sample between the phases.

G02587.title: gas-phase acidity
G02587.definition: The negative of the Gibbs energy (\(\Delta G_{\rm{r}}^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\)) change for the reaction:  in the gas phase.

G02588.title: gas-phase basicity
G02588.definition: The negative of the Gibbs energy (\(\Delta G_{\rm{r}}^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\)) change associated with the reaction: in the gas phase.  Also called absolute or intrinsic basicity.

G02589.title: gas-phase-grown carbon fibres
G02589.definition: Carbon fibres grown in an atmosphere of hydrocarbons with the aid of fine particulate solid catalysts such as iron or other transition metals and consisting of graphitizable carbon.

G02591.title: gas-solid chromatography
G02591.definition: Comprises all gas chromatographic methods in which the stationary phase is an active solid (e.g. charcoal, molecular sieves). Separation is achieved by adsorption of the components of a sample. In gas chromatography the distinction between gas-liquid and gas-solid may be obscure because liquids are used to modify solid stationary phases, and because the solid supports for liquid stationary phases affect the chromatographic process. For classification by the phases used, the term relating to the predominant effect should be chosen.

G02580.title: gaseous diffusion separator
G02580.definition: Instrumentation to separate a gas mixture into its components by means of differences in the diffusion rates of the component molecules. This method has been used in separation of various isotopes of uranium (by means of $\ce{UF6}$) and hydrogen ($\ce{H2O}$, $\ce{HDO}$, $\ce{D2O}$, $\ce{HTO}$, etc.)

15190.title: gastric emptying rate
15190.definition: Pace at which a drug along with the stomach content leaves and enters the duodenum.

15726.title: gastroenteritis
15726.definition: Inflammation of the stomach and intestine.

15727.title: gastrointestinal
15727.definition: Pertaining to or communicating with the stomach and intestine.

14709.title: gastrointestinal excretion
14709.definition: Excretion through the intestinal mucosa by active or passive processes.

10748.title: gastroschisis
10748.definition: Congenital defect characterized by a fissure in the anterior abdominal wall through which the small and (or) large intestine protrude.

10749.title: gastrula
10749.definition: Embryonic stage that develops from two to three germ layers during gastrulation.

10750.title: gastrulation
10750.definition: Stage of embryo development in which the two-layered blastula transforms into the gastrula by developing ectoderm and endoderm, as well as a third layer (mesoderm), through the movement of specific cells.

08478.title: gate delay
08478.definition: Time between the application of a laser pulse and the start of detection in laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy.

08344.title: gated decoupling
08344.definition: Application of spin decoupling only during selected time periods in a pulse experiment in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

GT07386.title: gated photochromism
GT07386.definition: Special form of photochromism in which one or both forms of a photochromic system are transformed reversibly, either chemically or electrochemically, into a non-photochromic form.

G02592.title: gated photodetector
G02592.definition: Where photodetectors are switched on (or off) usually in a repetitive manner employing electronic switches, they are described as gated.

G02593.title: gauche
G02593.definition: Synonymous with a synclinal alignment of groups attached to adjacent atoms.

G02595.title: gauche effect
G02595.definition: The stabilization of the gauche (synclinal) conformation in a two carbon unit bonded vicinally to electronegative elements e.g. 1,2-difluoroethane.The destabilization of the gauche (synclinal) conformation in a two carbon unit bonded vicinally to large, soft and polarizable elements such as sulfur and bromine.

G02596.title: gauss
G02596.definition: emu unit of magnetic flux density, \(\rm{G}=10^{-4}\ \rm{T}\).

08252.title: Gaussian band

G02597.title: Gaussian band shape
G02597.definition:
A band shape described by the Gaussian function: \[F\left(
u - 
u _{0}ight) =  rac{a}{\sqrt{\pi }}\ m{e}^{-a^{2}\ (
u - 
u _{0})^{2}}\] In this equation, \(a^{-1}\) is proportional to the width of the band, and \(
u _{0}\) is the frequency of the band maximum.

08171.title: Gaussian orbital
08171.definition: Function centered on an atom of the form \(\phi(r) \propto x^{i} y^{j} z^{k} \exp (-\zeta r^{2})\), used to approximate atomic orbitals in the LCAO-MO method.

15728.title: gavage
15728.definition: Administration of materials directly into the stomach by esophageal intubation.

08479.title: GD-OES spectrometers with simultaneous detection
08479.definition: Spectrometers for glow discharge optical emission spectroscopy that allow simultaneous monitoring of selected spectral ranges or the whole emission spectra.

G02598.title: Geiger counter
G02598.definition: A gas-filled X-ray detector in which gas amplification reaches saturation and proportionality no longer exists. The output signal does not depend on the incident energy. The time taken for the counter to recover from the saturation is called dead time.

G02599.title: Geiger–Muller counter tube
G02599.definition: A counter tube operated under such conditions that the magnitude of each pulse is independent of the amount of energy deposited in it.

G02600.title: gel
G02600.definition: Non-fluid colloidal network or polymer network that is expanded throughout its whole volume by a fluid.

GT07620.title: gel aging
GT07620.definition: Time-dependent changes in the chemical or the physical structure and the properties of a gel.

09747.title: gel electrophoresis
09747.definition: Separation technique used to separate or fractionate proteins and larger peptides according to their relative molecular mass using an electric field in polyacrylamide gel (PAGE).

GT07551.title: gel fraction
GT07551.definition: Mass fraction of the network material resulting from a network-forming polymerization or crosslinking process.

14281.title: gel microparticle
14281.definition: Particle of gel of any shape with an equivalent diameter of approximately \(\pu{0.1 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{100 \upmu m}\).

14282.title: gel nanoparticle
14282.definition: Particle of gel particle of any shape and an equivalent diameter of approximately \(\pu{1 nm}\) to \(\pu{100 nm}\).

GT07535.title: gel point
GT07535.definition: Point of incipient network formation in a process forming a chemical or physical polymer network.

GT07536.title: gel time
GT07536.definition: Time interval from the start of a network-forming process to the gel point.

GT07621.title: gelation
GT07621.definition: Process of passing through the gel point to form a gel or network.

GT07537.title: gelation temperature
GT07537.definition: Temperature threshold for the formation of a thermoreversible gel.

13167.title: Gell and Coombs classification
13167.definition: Classification of immune mechanisms of tissue injury into four types: type I, immediate-type hypersensitivity reactions, mediated by interaction of immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibody and antigen causing the release of histamine and other mediators; type II, antibody-mediated hypersensitivity reactions, due to antibody–antigen interactions on cell surfaces; type III, immune complex, local or general inflammatory responses due to formation of circulating immune complexes and their deposition in tissues; and type IV cell-mediated hypersensitivity reactions, initiated by sensitized T lymphocytes either by release of lymphokines or by T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity [see cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL)].

GT07387.title: geminate ion pair
GT07387.definition: Ion pair formed from a precursor that constitutes a single kinetic entity, i.e., by electron transfer or ion transfer in an encounter complex (cf. collision complex) or by ionic dissociation of a single molecular entity.

G02602.title: geminate pair
G02602.definition: Pair of molecular entities in close proximity in solution within a solvent cage and resulting from reaction (e.g. bond scission, electron transfer, group transfer) of a precursor that constitutes a single kinetic entity.

15730.title: generally regarded as safe
15730.definition: Phrase used to describe the USFDA philosophy that justifies approval of food additives that may not meet the usual test criteria for safety but have been used extensively and have not demonstrated that they cause any harm to consumers.

G02614.title: generation time
G02614.definition: The average time required by a cell for the completion of one cell cycle.

08480.title: generator coupling efficiency
08480.definition: Fraction of the energy generated being used for creating and maintaining the plasma in an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer.

15192.title: generic
15192.definition: Drug(s) or formulation(s) of drug(s) or dosage forms, which no longer have patent protection.

14711.title: genetic adaptation
14711.definition: Result of random genetic variation due to mutation and (or) to changes in allele frequencies, causing variation in the survival and reproductive success of individuals and hence of groups of organisms, with the consequence that those best adjusted to their environment flourish.

GT06961.title: genetic algorithm
GT06961.definition: A genetic algorithm is an optimization algorithm based on the mechanisms of Darwinian evolution which uses random mutation, crossover and selection procedures to breed better models or solutions from an originally random starting population or sample.

G02615.title: genetic code
G02615.definition: The set of rules which governs the relationship between the linear order of the nucleotides in an mRNA molecule and the sequence of the amino acids in the protein which it encodes. The genetic code is a triplet code, nearly universal. It is not overlapping: a mutation which alters only a single nucleotide in a gene can change only one amino acid in the encoded protein. It is degenerate: it assigns each of the 20 amino acids to one or more of 61 of the 64 possible nucleotide triplets (cf. codon) that can be constructed from four nucleotides. The remaining three triplets are used to signal the termination of a genetic message.

14712.title: genetic drift
14712.definition: Evolutionary process of change in the allele frequencies in a population due to random changes in the frequency by which different alleles are transferred to the next generation.

16224.title: genetic epidemiology
16224.definition: Study of the correlations between phenotypic trends and genetic variation across population groups and the application of the results of such a study to control of health problems.

14713.title: genetic hitchhiking
14713.definition: Situation in which a scored locus is acting only as a marker for a closely linked gene that is actually responsible for the difference in tolerance among genotypes. More generally, it is the condition 'in which a given allele changes in frequency as a result of linkage or gametic phase disequilibrium with another selected locus'.

15732.title: genetic polymorphism
15732.definition: Existence of inter-individual differences in DNA sequences coding for one specific gene, giving rise to different functional and (or) morphological traits.

11167.title: genetic recombination
11167.definition:
Referring to new gene sequences, and thus to new heritable information, caused by gene crossovers, occurring naturally in either meiosis or mitosis, or constructed artificially for the purpose of introducing a new trait into an organism or cell line.
In immunology, random scrambling of specific gene sequences to produce the vast array of possible immunoglobulin and T cell receptor sequences required to recognize, potentially, all possible antigens.

14714.title: genetic risk
14714.definition: Risk to the progeny of an exposed individual of an adverse effect associated with heritable genetic damage, e.g., damage to germ cells leading to a nonviable fetus or an offspring with a birth defect.

15733.title: genetic susceptibility
15733.definition: Predisposition to a particular disease or sensitivity to a substance due to the presence of a specific allele or combination of alleles in an individual’s genome.

15734.title: genetic toxicology
15734.definition: Study of chemically or physically induced changes to the structure of DNA, including epigenetic phenomena or mutations that may or may not be heritable.

15731.title: genetically modified organism
15731.definition: Bacterium, plant, or animal whose DNA has been deliberately altered.

10754.title: genital
10754.definition:
Of or relating to human or animal reproduction.
Of or relating to the genital organs.
Of or relating to the final stage of psychosexual maturation.

10756.title: genital fold
10756.definition: Embryonic structure that will develop into the penis and scrotum in males or the labia in females.

10757.title: genital organ
10757.definition: Organ of reproduction or generation, both external and internal to the body.

10758.title: genital tract
10758.definition: Genital passages of the urogenital apparatus.

10759.title: genital tubercle
10759.definition: Primordium of the penis or clitoris.

10755.title: genitalia
10755.definition:
Plural of genital.
Externally visible sex organs.

G02616.title: genome
G02616.definition: The complete set of chromosomal and extrachromosomal genes of an organism, a cell, an organelle or a virus; the complete DNA component of an organism.

GT06826.title: genomics
GT06826.definition: Science of using DNA- and RNA-based technologies to demonstrate alterations in gene expression.Method providing information on the consequences for gene expression of interactions of the organism with environmental stress, xenobiotics, etc.

10760.title: genotoxic
10760.definition: Capable of causing a change to the structure of the genome.

G02617.title: genotype
G02617.definition: The genetic constitution of an organism as revealed by genetic or molecular analysis, i.e. the complete set of genes, both dominant and recessive, possessed by a particular cell or organism.

14716.title: genus
14716.definition: Low-level taxonomic rank used in the classification of living and fossil organisms.

14717.title: geographic information system
14717.definition: Computerized system to handle spatial data at a reasonable cost; most allow one to archive, organize, integrate, statistically analyze, and display many kinds of spatial information using a common coordinate system.

G02621.title: geometric mean
G02621.definition: The nth root of the product of the absolute values of the observations, taken with the proper sign. It can be calculated with the formula: \[\bar{x}_{\rm{g}} = (\Pi |x_{i}|)^{\frac{1}{n}}\] The \(\mathit{\Pi}\) product is taken from i = 1 to n.

G02619.title: geometric attenuation
G02619.definition: The reduction of a radiation quantity due to the effect only of the distance between the point of interest and the source, excluding the effect of any matter present.

G02618.title: geometrical equivalence
G02618.definition: The symmetry correspondence among units belonging to the same chain. The symmetry elements always bear a special relationship to the chain axis.

G02623.title: geometry
G02623.definition: A term used colloquially to signify the arrangement in space of the various components in an experiment, particularly the source and the detector in radiation measurements.

G02624.title: geometry factor
G02624.definition: The average solid angle in steradians at source subtended by the aperture or sensitive volume of the detector, divided by $4\uppi\!$.

10761.title: germ cell gene mutation assay
10761.definition: Procedure in which mutations induced by an agent are studied in germ line cells or somatic stem cells from a transgenic animal (rodent), containing reporter genes for detection of various mutations.

10763.title: germ layer
10763.definition: Any of three distinct layers of cells (endoderm, ectoderm, and mesoderm) that become recognizable as the embryo develops.

13171.title: germ line
13171.definition: Referring to genes in their unrearranged state rather than those rearranged for production of immunoglobulin (Ig) or T-cell receptor (TCR) molecules.

10762.title: germ line cell
10762.definition: Gamete or an embryonic cell that can develop into a gamete.

13170.title: germ-free
13170.definition: Descriptor applied to animals (usually mice) raised in the complete absence of intestinal and other microorganisms.

15735.title: germ-free animal
15735.definition: Animal grown under sterile conditions in the period of postnatal development: Such animals are usually obtained by Caesarean operation and kept in special sterile boxes in which there are no viable microorganisms (sterile air, food, and water are supplied).

13172.title: germinal center
13172.definition: Discrete area within lymph nodes and spleen where B-cell maturation and memory development occur.

G02626.title: germylidenes
G02626.definition: Carbene analogues having the structure $\ce{R2Ge{:}}$. The older synonym germylenes is no longer recommended.

10764.title: gestation
10764.definition: Period between conception and birth during which an embryo or fetus is carried in the uterus of a female mammal.

10846.title: gestation index
10846.definition: In rodents, number of females with live born offspring divided by number of females with evidence of pregnancy, multiplied by \(\pu{100}\).

10765.title: gestation period
10765.definition: Time from conception to birth, during which a fetus develops.

11782.title: giant axon
11782.definition: Very large axon (typically \(\pu{0.5 mm}\) in diameter) that functions in the propulsion system of the squid.

11783.title: giant axonal neuropathy
11783.definition: Rare human genetic neurological disorder in which the neurofilaments become disordered, resulting in abnormal size and shape of neurons.

13173.title: giant cell
13173.definition: Large multinucleate cell derived from fused macrophages and often present in granulomas.

G02627.title: Gibbs adsorption
G02627.definition: The surface excess amount or Gibbs adsorption of component \(i\), \(n_{i}^{\sigma }\), which may be positive or negative, is defined as the excess of the amount of this component actually present in the system over that present in a reference system of the same volume as the real system and in which the bulk concentrations in the two phases remain uniform up to the Gibbs dividing surface. That is \[n_{i}^{\sigma }=n_{i}- V^{\alpha }\ c_{i}^{\alpha }- V^{\beta }\ c_{i}^{\beta }\] where \(n_{i}\) is the total amount of the component \(i\) in the system, \(c_{i}^{\alpha }\) and \(c_{i}^{\beta }\) are the concentrations in the two bulk phases \(\alpha \) and \(\beta \), and \(V^{\alpha }\) and \(V^{\beta }\) are the volumes of the two phases defined by the Gibbs surface.

G02629.title: Gibbs energy
G02629.definition: Enthalpy minus the product of thermodynamic temperature and entropy. It was formerly called free energy or free enthalpy.

G02630.title: Gibbs energy diagram
G02630.definition: A diagram showing the relative standard Gibbs energies of reactants, transition state, reaction intermediates and products, in the same sequence as they occur in a chemical reaction. These points are often connected by a smooth curve (a 'Gibbs energy profile', commonly still referred to as a 'free energy profile') but experimental observation can provide information on relative standard Gibbs energies only at the maxima and minima and not at the configurations between them. The abscissa expresses the sequence of reactants, products, reaction intermediates and transition states and is usually undefined or only vaguely defined by the reaction coordinate (extent of bond breaking or bond making). In some adaptations the abscissas are however explicitly defined as bond orders, Brønsted exponents, etc. Contrary to statements in many text books, the highest point on a Gibbs energy diagram does not necessarily correspond to the transition state of the rate-limiting step. For example, in a stepwise reaction consisting of two reaction steps:  one of the transition states of the two reaction steps must (in general) have a higher standard Gibbs energy than the other, whatever the concentration of D in the system. However, the value of that concentration will determine which of the reaction steps is rate-limiting. If the particular concentrations of interest, which may vary, are chosen as the standard state, then the rate-limiting step is the one of highest Gibbs energy.

G02631.title: Gibbs energy of activation
G02631.definition: The standard Gibbs energy difference between the transition state of a reaction (either an elementary reaction or a stepwise reaction) and the ground state of the reactants. It is calculated from the experimental rate constant \(k\) via the conventional form of the absolute rate equation: \[\Delta ^{\ddagger}G = R\ T\ \left[\ln (\frac{k_{\rm{B}}}{h}) - \ln (\frac{k}{T})\right]\] where \(k_{\rm{B}}\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(h\) the Planck constant (\(\frac{k_{\rm{B}}}{h} = 2.083\ 58\times 10^{10}\ \rm{K}^{-1}\ \rm{s}^{-1}\)). The values of the rate constants, and hence Gibbs energies of activation, depend upon the choice of concentration units (or of the thermodynamic standard state).

GT07388.title: Gibbs energy of photoinduced electron transfer
GT07388.definition: For photoinduced electron transfer between an acceptor (\(\ce{A}\)) and a donor (\(\ce{D}\)) (either one of them may be the electronically excited molecular entity) of any charge type, \(z(\ce{A})\) and \(z(\ce{D})\), the change in standard Gibbs energy can be approximated as (the notation is for the case of neutral species \(\ce{D}\) and \(\ce{A}\)) \[\Delta_{\rm{ET}} G^{\circ} = N_{\rm{A}} \left\{e [E^{\circ}(\ce{D^{+.}}/\ce{D}) - E^{\circ}(\ce{A}/\ce{A^{-.}})] + w(\ce{D^{+.}}\ce{A^{-.}}) - w(\ce{DA}) \right\} - \Delta E_{0,0}\] where \(e = \pu{1.602176487E-19 C}\) is the elementary charge, \(N_{\rm{A}} = \pu{6.02214076E23 mol-1}\) is the Avogadro constant, \(E^{\circ}(\ce{D^{+.}}/\ce{D})/\pu{V}\) is the standard electrode potential of the donor cation radical resulting from the electron transfer, \(E^{\circ}(\ce{A}/\ce{A^{-.}})/\pu{V}\) is the standard electrode potential of the acceptor (both relative to the same reference electrode) and \(\Delta E_{0,0}/\pu{J mol-1}\) is the vibrational zero electronic energy of the excited partner (provided that a vibrationally equilibrated excited state at energy \(E_{0,0}\) takes part in the reaction), all data referring to the same solvent. \(w(\ce{D^{+.}}\ce{A^{-.}})\) and \(w(\ce{DA})\) are the electrostatic work terms that account for the effect of Coulombic attraction in the products and reactants, respectively \[w(\ce{D^{+.}A^{-.}})/\pu{J} = \frac{z(\ce{D^{+.}})z(\ce{A^{-.}})e^{2}}{4\pi \epsilon_{0} \epsilon_{r} a}\] \[w(\ce{DA})/\pu{J} = \frac{z(\ce{D})z(\ce{A})e^{2}}{4\pi \epsilon_{0} \epsilon_{r} a}\] where \(a\) is the distance of the charged species after electron transfer, \(\varepsilon_{r}\) is the relative medium static permittivity (formerly called dielectric constant), \(\varepsilon_{0} \approx \pu{8.854E-12 C2 J-1 m-1}\) is the electric constant (vacuum permittivity), and \(z(\ce{X})\) the charge of the species \(X\).  In SI units the factor \(\frac{e^{2}}{4\pi \varepsilon_{0}} = \pu{2.307E-28 J m}\). For the case of neutral species \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{D}\), \(z(\ce{D}) = z(\ce{A}) = 0\).

G02632.title: Gibbs energy of repulsion
G02632.definition: Indicated by \(G_{\rm{r}}\) or \(G_{\rm{el}}\) if the repulsion is due to electric effects (\(g_{\rm{r}}\) or \(g_{\rm{el}}\) is taken for unit area of each of two flat and parallel surfaces). \(G_{\rm{r}}\) (or \(G_{\rm{el}}\)) is defined as \[G_{\rm{r}} ({\rm{or\ }} G_{\rm{el}}) = \left[\int \limits_{\rm{final\ distance}}^{\infty} {\rm{Force.d (distance)}}\right]_{T,p}\]

15330.title: Gibbs energy of transfer
15330.definition: Change in Gibbs energy at a given temperature and pressure for transfer of a substance between two different phases.

G02634.title: Gibbs film elasticity
