G02634.definition: Pertains to a film element of a soap film changing in area at constant mass and is the differential change of its surface tension with relative change in area \(A\), \[E=A\ (\frac{\partial \sigma }{\partial A})_{T,p,n_{i}}\] where \(T\) is the thermodynamic temperature, \(p\) is the pressure, and \(n_{i}\) is the amount of substance of the species \(i\).

G02635.title: Gibbs surface
G02635.definition: A geometrical surface chosen parallel to the interface and used to define the volumes of the bulk phases in the calculation of the extent of adsorption, and of other surface excess properties. Also referred to as Gibbs dividing surface.

15329.title: Gibbs–Duhem equation
15329.definition: Equation relating the intensive variables \(T\), \(p\) and the \(C\) chemical potentials \(\mu_{i}\) in a phase \[S{\rm{d}}T - V{\rm{d}}p + \sum \limits_{i=1}^{C} n_{i} {\rm{d}}\mu_{i} = 0\] where \(C\) is the total number of components, \(i\) in a phase.

15331.title: Gibbs–Konovalov equations
15331.definition: Pair of equations for a binary mixture of components \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\) that relate the variables \(T\), \(p\), in one phase of variable composition, \(\upalpha\), to the variables \(T\), \(p\), in a coexisting equilibrium phase of variable composition, \(\upbeta\): \[\begin{array}{c} -\frac{\left(1 - x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} \right)\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta} H_{\ce{A}} + x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} \Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta} H_{\ce{B}}}{T}{\rm{d}}T + \left[\left(1 - x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} \right)\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta}V_{\ce{A}} + x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta}\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta}V_{\ce{B}} \right]{\rm{d}}p +\left(x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} - x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} \right)\left(\frac{\partial^{2} G_{\rm{m}}^{\alpha}}{\partial x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha 2}} \right)_{T,p} {\rm{d}}x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} = 0 \\ -\frac{\left(1 - x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} \right)\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta} H_{\ce{A}} + x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} \Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta} H_{\rm{B}}}{T}{\rm{d}}T + \left[\left(1 - x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} \right)\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta}V_{\ce{A}} + x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha}\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta}V_{\ce{B}} \right]{\rm{d}}p +\left(x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} - x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} \right)\left(\frac{\partial^{2} G_{\rm{m}}^{\alpha}}{\partial x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta 2}} \right)_{T,p} {\rm{d}}x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} = 0 \end{array}\] where \(\Delta_{\upalpha}^{\upbeta} H_{\ce{A}} = H_{\ce{A}}^{\upbeta} - H_{\ce{A}}^{\upalpha}\), \(\Delta_{\upalpha}^{\upbeta} V_{\ce{A}} = V_{\ce{A}}^{\upbeta} - V_{\ce{A}}^{\upalpha}\) are the enthalpy and volume of transfer of component \(\ce{A}\) from phase \(\upalpha\) to phase \(\upbeta\), and similarly for component \(\ce{B}\).

10766.title: gigantism
10766.definition: Condition of abnormal size or overgrowth of the entire body or of any of its parts.

10767.title: gland
10767.definition: Organized aggregation of cells functioning as a secretory or excretory organ.

10768.title: glans
10768.definition: Any small rounded mass or gland-like body.

10769.title: glans clitoridis
10769.definition: Rounded mass of sensitive erectile tissue that forms the head of the clitoris.

10770.title: glans penis
10770.definition: Rounded mass of sensitive erectile tissue at the distal end (head) of the penis, analogous to the glans clitoridis.

12773.title: glass
12773.definition: Amorphous matter in the glassy state, i.e., below its glass-transition temperature.

G02637.title: glass electrode error
G02637.definition: Deviation of a glass electrode from the hydrogen-ion response function. An example often encountered is the error due to sodium ions at alkaline \(\rm{pH}\) values, which by convention is regarded as positive.

G02638.title: glass laser
G02638.definition: A solid state laser in which the active medium is a glass host that supports the active species. The neodymium-doped phosphate glass laser is one example.

09115.title: glass pH-sensitive electrode
09115.definition: pH-sensitive electrode, usually consisting of a bulb, or other suitable form, of special glass attached to a stem of high-resistance glass, complete with an internal reference electrode and internal filling solution system.

G02640.title: glass transition
G02640.definition: A second-order transition in which a supercooled melt yields, on cooling, a glassy structure. Below the glass-transition temperature the physical properties vary in a manner similar to those of the crystalline phase. Example: Lithium disilicate crystals melt at \(1305\ \rm{K}\); the melt can be supercooled to the glass-transition temperature at approximately \(773\ \rm{K}\) below which the viscous liquid freezes to a rigid amorphous glass.

G02639.title: glass-like carbon
G02639.definition: An agranular non-graphitizable carbon with a very high isotropy of its structural and physical properties and with a very low permeability for liquids and gases. The original surfaces and the fracture surfaces have a pseudo-glassy appearance.

G02641.title: glass-transition temperature
G02641.definition: The temperature at which the viscosity of the glass is \(10^{13}\ \rm{dPa}\ \rm{s}\).

09088.title: glassy carbon electrode
09088.definition: Electrode made of glassy carbon material with an intertwined graphitic ribbon structure, formed by pyrolysis of a resol precursor at temperatures up to \(\pu{3000^{\circ}C}\).

12774.title: glassy state
12774.definition: State of amorphous matter below its glass-transition temperature.

10771.title: glaucoma
10771.definition: Disease of the eye characterized by increased intraocular pressure, resulting in atrophy of the optic nerve.

11784.title: glia
11784.definition: Non-neuronal cellular elements of the central and peripheral nervous system having metabolic and support functions.

11785.title: glial cell
11785.definition: Cellular component of the glia, including oligodendroglial cells, astrocytes, ependymal cells and microglial cells.

11787.title: glial fibrillary acidic protein
11787.definition: Cytoskeletal intermediate filament protein found in mature fibrillary astrocytes and in neural progenitor cells.

11786.title: glial-derived neurotrophic factor
11786.definition: Protein that promotes and guides the growth of neurons and facilitates the survival of mature neurons by suppressing cell death.

11788.title: glioblastoma
11788.definition: Glioma consisting chiefly of undifferentiated anaplastic cells of astrocytic origin.

11789.title: glioma
11789.definition: Neoplasm originating from any of the glia cells in the brain and spinal cord.

GT07389.title: global analysis
GT07389.definition: Method for kinetic analysis of time-resolved emission or absorption data.

14718.title: global distillation
14718.definition: Process by which persistent and relatively volatile organochlorine compounds are distilled from warmer regions of use to cooler regions of the globe.

14719.title: global fractionation
14719.definition: Process by which some persistent organic pollutants (POPs) move more rapidly than others toward the polar regions. Because POPs differ in their individual rates of degradation, vapor pressure, and lipophilicity, a fractionation occurs. The net result is a redistribution of the different POPs from the equator or site of origin toward the cold polar regions of the Earth.

11450.title: global model
11450.definition:
A computational model designed to cover all of chemistry space although it typically includes a measure of if the molecule for which the properties are to be
 predicted is within or outside the applicability domain of the model.

14720.title: global warming
14720.definition: Heating up of the Earth’s climate thought to result from the increased atmospheric carbon dioxide (\(\ce{CO2}\)) concentrations from fossil fuel burning, release of other greenhouse gases, and the worldwide destruction of forests.

08345.title: globally optimized alternating-phase rectangular pulses
08345.definition: Spin decoupling pulse sequence in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy used to provide decoupling over a large frequency range.

11791.title: globoside
11791.definition: Glycosphingolipid, specifically a ceramide tetrasaccharide (tetraglycosylceramide), isolated from kidney and erythrocytes.

G02642.title: globular-chain crystal
G02642.definition: A type of crystal comprised of macromolecules having globular conformations. Globular-chain crystals usually occur with globular proteins.

13824.title: globule
13824.definition: Conformation of a macromolecule in which the constitutional units collectively arrange into a compact ovoid or spherical shape.

15737.title: glomerular
15737.definition: Pertaining to a tuft or cluster, as of a plexus of capillary blood vessels or nerve fibers, especially referring to the capillaries of the glomerular of the kidney.

15738.title: glomerular filtration
15738.definition: Formation of an ultrafiltrate of the blood occurring in the glomerulus of the kidney.

15739.title: glomerular filtration rate
15739.definition: Volume of ultrafiltrate formed in the kidney tubules from the blood passing through the glomerular capillaries divided by time of filtration.

13174.title: glomerulonephritis
13174.definition: Any of a group of kidney diseases involving inflammation of the renal glomeruli, often as a result of antibody–antigen complexes that localize in the kidney.

13175.title: glomerulonephropathy
13175.definition: Disease of the renal glomeruli, which may show either thickening of the glomerular basement membrane due to the accretion of proteins or a minimal change disease, in which there is functional damage but little structural change by light microscopy.

10772.title: glomerulus
10772.definition: Tuft or a cluster, as of a plexus of capillary blood vessels or nerve fibers (e.g., capillaries of the filtration apparatus of the kidney).

G02643.title: glove box
G02643.definition: An enclosure in which material may be manipulated in isolation from the operator's environment. This manipulation is effected by gauntlet gloves or flexible plastic devices fixed to ports in the walls of the box.

08481.title: glow discharge source
08481.definition: Component of an atomic emission spectrometer employing a glow electric discharge used in atomic emission spectroscopy for qualitative and quantitative analysis of solid materials.

08482.title: glow electric discharge
08482.definition: Electric discharge in gas at low pressure (\(\pu{100}\) to \(\pu{1000 Pa}\)).

08483.title: glow-discharge optical emission spectroscopy
08483.definition: Optical emission spectroscopy in which a glow electric discharge excites atoms at the surface of a sample, which is made the cathode of the discharge.

10773.title: glucocorticoid
10773.definition: Any of a group of steroid hormones, such as cortisone, produced by the adrenal cortex, inhibiting inflammation, and mediating a response to stress that alters protein, fat, and carbohydrate metabolism.

15740.title: glue-sniffing
15740.definition: Inhalation of solvent vapor from plastic cements or other adhesives in order to become intoxicated.

11793.title: glutamate-induced excitotoxicity
11793.definition: Form of excitotoxicity where excess glutamate release in synapses (glutamatergic storm) leads to overstimulation, followed by excess cellular calcium uptake, cytotoxicity and apoptosis.

13176.title: glutamic acid decarboxylase
13176.definition: Main autoantigen in diabetes mellitus type 1 and stiff-person syndrome (a neurological autoimmune disease).

13177.title: gluten
13177.definition:
1) Any of the prolamins found in cereal grains, especially the prolamins in wheat, rye, barley, and possibly oats, which cause digestive disorders, notably celiac disease.
2) In wheat, mixture of water-insoluble proteins, including gliadins, that give wheat dough its elastic texture.

09812.title: glycan microarray
09812.definition: Glycans attached to a surface of a microarray.

09813.title: glycan profiling
09813.definition: Determination of the diversity of glycan structures expressed on glycoconjugates or cells.

09814.title: glycan-binding protein
09814.definition: Protein that recognises and binds to specific glycans and mediates their biological function.

G02645.title: glycans
G02645.definition: Synonymous with polysaccharides. Glycans composed of a single type of monosaccharide residue (homopolysaccharide, synonym homoglycan) are named by replacing the ending '-ose' of the sugar by '-an', e.g. mannans, fructans, xylans, arabinans. dextrans and dextrins belong to the class glucans.

G02647.title: glycerides
G02647.definition: Esters of glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) with fatty acids, widely distributed in nature. They are by long-established custom subdivided into triglycerides, 1,2- or 1,3-diglycerides, and 1- or 2-monoglycerides, according to the number and position of acyl groups (not, as one might suppose, the number of glycerol residues). The recommended method for naming individual glycerides is mono-, di- or tri-O-acylglycerol, as appropriate.

09838.title: glycerolipids
09838.definition: Esters, ethers, and other O-derivatives of glycerol with alkyls or alkenyls, including mono-, di-, and tri-substituted glycerols.

G02648.title: glycerophospholipid
G02648.definition: Any derivative of glycerophosphoric acid that contains at least one O-acyl, or O-alkyl, or O-(1-alkenyl) group attached to the glycerol residue.

09839.title: glycerophospholipids
09839.definition: Lipids with glycerol backbone esterified with one or two fatty acids in position \(\ce{C-1}\) and/or \(\ce{C-2}\) and with phosphoric acid at position \(\ce{C-3}\). The phosphate group is usually esterified with an alcohol (choline, ethanolamine, serine, inositol, glycerol) to form the 'lipid head group'.

G02650.title: glyco-amino-acid
G02650.definition: A saccharide attached to a single amino acid by any kind of covalent bond. A glycosyl-amino-acid is a compound consisting of saccharide linked through a glycosyl linkage (O-, N-, or S-) to an amino acid.

G02651.title: glycoconjugate
G02651.definition: A type of compound consisting of carbohydrate units covalently linked with other types of chemical constituent.

09815.title: glycoform
09815.definition: Specific form of a glycoprotein containing a distinct glycan structure per glycosylation site.

09816.title: glycogene
09816.definition: Gene encoding an enzyme or other functional protein for glycan synthesis.

09817.title: glycolipid
09817.definition: Compound containing a glycan covalently linked to a lipid aglycon.

G02653.title: glycolipids
G02653.definition: Naturally occurring 1,2-di-O-acylglycerols joined at oxygen 3 by a glycosidic linkage to a carbohydrate part (usually a mono-, di- or tri-saccharide). Some substances classified as bacterial glycolipids have the sugar part acylated by one or more fatty acids and the glycerol part may be absent.

G02654.title: glycols
G02654.definition: Dihydric alcohols, also known as diols, in which the two hydroxy groups are on different carbon atoms, usually but not necessarily adjacent. E.g. $\ce{HOCH2CH2OH}$ 'ethylene glycol' (ethane-1,2-diol), $\ce{HO[CH2]4OH butane-1,4-diol}$.

10774.title: glycolysis
10774.definition: Biochemical breakdown of glucose into pyruvic acid with the production of ATP.

09818.title: glycome
09818.definition: Complete set of glycans and glycoconjugates produced by a species, tissue, or cell in a specified time, space, and environment.

09819.title: glycomics
09819.definition: Complex and comprehensive study of the glycome.

09820.title: glycone
09820.definition: Carbohydrate part of a glycoconjugate or a glycoside.

G02656.title: glycopeptides
G02656.definition: Compounds in which a carbohydrate component is linked to a peptide/protein component.

09821.title: glycoprotein
09821.definition: Protein with one or more covalently bound glycans.

G02658.title: glycosamines
G02658.definition: A term synonymous with amino sugars; now restricted to some trivial names.

G02659.title: glycosaminoglycan
G02659.definition: The carbohydrate units in proteoglycans are polysaccharides that contain amino sugars; these polysaccharides are known as glycosaminoglycans.

G02660.title: glycoses
G02660.definition: A less frequently used term for monosaccharides.

09823.title: glycosidase
09823.definition: Enzyme that catalyses the hydrolysis of glycosidic linkages.

G02661.title: glycosides
G02661.definition: Originally mixed acetals resulting from the attachment of a glycosyl group to a non-acyl group $\ce{RO– (which itself may be derived from a saccharide and chalcogen replacements thereof ($\ce{RS\bond{–}}$, $\ce{RSe\bond{–}}$).  The bond between the glycosyl group and the $\ce{OR}$ group is called a glycosidic bond. By extension, the terms N-glycosides and C-glycosides are used as class names for glycosylamines and for compounds having a glycosyl group attached to a hydrocarbyl group respectively.   These terms are misnomers and should not be used. The preferred terms are glycosylamines and C-glycosyl compounds, respectively.

09825.title: glycosidic linkage
09825.definition: Linkage of a monosaccharide to another residue via the anomeric hydroxy group.

09826.title: glycosyl
09826.definition: Monosaccharide ring without the anomeric oxygen.

G02665.title: glycosyl group
G02665.definition: The structure obtained by removing the hydroxy group from the hemiacetal function of a monosaccharide and, by extension, of a lower oligosaccharide.

G02663.title: glycosylamines
G02663.definition: Compounds having a glycosyl group attached to an amino group, $\ce{NR2}$; less elegantly called N-glycosides, e.g. N,N-dimethyl-$\upbeta\!$-ᴅ-glucopyranosylamine.

09827.title: glycosylation
09827.definition: Covalent attachment of a saccharide to a protein, lipid, polynucleotide, saccharide, or other organic compound, generally catalysed by enzymes glycosyltransferases.

09828.title: glycosyltransferase
09828.definition: Enzyme that catalyses the transfer of a saccharide from a nucleotide di(mono)phosphate-activated sugar to an acceptor molecule.

15741.title: gnotobiota
15741.definition: Specifically and entirely known microfauna and microflora of a specially reared laboratory animal.

15742.title: gnotobiote
15742.definition: Specially reared laboratory animal whose microflora and microfauna are specifically known in their entirety.

15743.title: goiter
15743.definition: Noncancerous enlargement of the thyroid gland, visible as a swelling at the front of the neck, that is often associated with iodine deficiency.

15744.title: goitrogen
15744.definition: Any substance (such as thiouracil) that induces the formation of a goiter.

09099.title: gold electrode
09099.definition: Foil, wire or disc electrode made of gold which is easily fabricated into a variety of electrode geometries.

11794.title: Golgi staining
11794.definition: Method of silver staining of histological sections of tissue from the nervous system, in which a limited number of neurons stain in their entirety upon formation of microcrystals of silver chromate, thus allowing visualization in the light microscope of some individual neurons in densely packed tissue.

10775.title: gonad
10775.definition: Organ in animals that produces gametes, i.e., the testis or the ovary.

15745.title: gonadotropic
15745.definition: Pertaining to effects on sex glands and on the systems that regulate them.

10776.title: gonadotropin
10776.definition: Glycopeptide hormone, produced by the fetal placenta, that maintains the function of the corpus luteum during the first few weeks of pregnancy.

10777.title: gonadotropin-releasing hormone
10777.definition: Any factor from the hypothalamus that stimulates the anterior pituitary to release both follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone.

15746.title: good agricultural practice
15746.definition: Nationally authorized safe uses of pesticides under actual conditions necessary for effective and reliable pest control.

08074.title: good laboratory practice
08074.definition: Quality system concerned with the organizational process, and conditions under which non-clinical health and environmental safety studies are planned, performed, monitored, recorded, archived, and reported.

14721.title: good laboratory practice principles
14721.definition: Fundamental rules incorporated in Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) guidelines and national regulations concerned with the process of effective organization and the conditions under which laboratory studies are properly planned, performed, monitored, recorded, and reported.

08075.title: good manufacturing practice
08075.definition: Combination of manufacturing and quality procedures aimed at ensuring that products are consistently manufactured to their specified requirements and to avoid contamination of the product by internal or external sources.

13178.title: Goodpasture syndrome
13178.definition: Autoimmune disease of humans in which glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage are produced by complement-mediated tissue damage caused by antibodies directed against the renal glomerular and alveolar basement membranes.

13164.title: gp120
13164.definition: Viral glycoprotein, non-covalently associated with gp41 in the viral envelope of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

10778.title: Graafian follicle
10778.definition: Mature ovarian follicle within which an oocyte attains full size and which ruptures during ovulation to release the ovum.

G02668.title: grab sampling
G02668.definition: The taking of a sample (often in an evacuated bulb) in a very short time; preferred terms are instantaneous sampling or instantaneous sampling.

14722.title: graded effect
14722.definition: Consequence that can be measured on a graded scale of intensity or severity and its magnitude related directly to the dose or concentration of the substance producing it.

G02669.title: gradient
G02669.definition: A differential ratio; the change in a quantity such as the mixing ratio of an impurity in air, the temperature of the air, etc., with height or distance.

G02670.title: gradient elution
G02670.definition: A procedure in which the composition of the mobile phase is changed continuously or stepwise during the elution process.

G02671.title: gradient layer
G02671.definition: The chromatographic bed used in thin-layer chromatography in which there is a gradual transition in some property.

08346.title: gradient-selected experiment
08346.definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment where pulsed-field gradients are employed to filter out unwanted resonances from a spectrum rather than the classic phase-cycling approach.

G02672.title: gradientless reactor
G02672.definition: Stirred flow or recirculation reactors, characterized ideally by very small concentration and temperature gradients within the catalyst region.

G02674.title: gradual potential-energy surface
G02674.definition: These terms relate to the steepness of the energy rise along the reaction path of a potential-energy surface.

G02675.title: graft copolymer
G02675.definition: A copolymer that is a graft polymer.

G02676.title: graft copolymerization
G02676.definition: Polymerization in which a graft copolymer is formed.

11537.title: graft homopolymer
11537.definition: Homopolymer composed of macromolecules with one or more species of block connected to the main chain as side chains, these side chains having constitutional or configurational features that differ from those in the main chain.

G02678.title: graft macromolecule
G02678.definition: A macromolecule with one or more species of block connected to the main chain as side chains, these side chains having constitutional or configurational features that differ from those in the main chain.

G02679.title: graft polymer
G02679.definition: A polymer composed of graft macromolecules.

13179.title: graft rejection
13179.definition: Destruction of grafted tissue by host lymphocytes following an adaptive immune response.

13180.title: graft-versus-host disease
13180.definition: Disease that occurs following bone marrow transplantation between genetically non-identical people and in which mature T cells in the transplanted bone marrow attack and destroy the recipients tissues.

13181.title: graft-versus-host reaction
13181.definition: Reaction occurring when T lymphocytes present in a graft recognize and attack host cells.

GT07138.title: grafting
GT07138.definition: Reaction in which one or more species of block are connected to the main chain of a macromolecule as side-chains having constitutional or configurational features that differ from those in the main chain.

G02680.title: gram
G02680.definition: cgs base unit of mass, \(\pu{g} = \pu{E-3 kg}\).

G02681.title: Gram stain
G02681.definition: A set of two stains that are used to stain (crystal violet and iodine) and counterstain (fuchsin) bacteria. gram-negative bacteria are completely decolorized after treating the stained bacteria with ethanol or acetone and can be visualized by the counterstain. They have a complex cell wall in which the peptidoglycan layer is covered by lipopolysaccharides in an outer membrane structure. gram-positive bacteria resist decolorization by ethanol or acetone, they retain the initial gram stain. They have a cell wall consisting predominantly of peptidoglycan not overlayed by an outer membrane.

15747.title: graminicide
15747.definition: Pesticide (herbicide) used for the control of weedy grasses (Gramineae).

G02682.title: granular carbon
G02682.definition: The term granular carbon is equivalent to coarse particulate carbon. This is a carbon material consisting of separate particles or grains which are monolithic, on the average larger than about \(100\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) in diameter, but smaller than about \(1\ \rm{cm}\).

15194.title: granulation
15194.definition: Process in which powder particles are made to aggregate to larger particles called granules.

11796.title: granule cell
11796.definition: One of several types of neurons with small cell bodies, involved in neural networks in several regions of the brain, including the cerebellum, hippocampus, and cerebral cortex.

15193.title: granules
15193.definition: Powder particles, which have been aggregated to form larger irregular particles, usually of \(\pu{0.5\!{-}\! 2 mm}\) diameter.

10779.title: granulocyte
10779.definition: White blood cell, distinct from a lymphocyte, containing cytoplasmic granules.

13182.title: granulocyte colony-stimulating factor
13182.definition: Hematopoietic (see hematopoiesis) factor augmenting the production of neutrophils in the bone marrow.

13183.title: granulocyte–macrophage colony-stimulating factor
13183.definition: Cytokine that stimulates production of granulocytes and monocytes from stem cells.

13185.title: granuloma
13185.definition: Mass or nodule of granulation tissue, with actively growing fibroblasts and capillary buds, characterized by the presence of aggregates of modified macrophages resembling epithelial cells (epithelioid histiocytes), and lymphocytes, surrounded by a rim of giant multinucleate cells, either of the Langerhans or foreign body type.

10780.title: granulosa
10780.definition: Pertaining to cells of the cumulus oophorus.

13186.title: granzyme
13186.definition: Member of a family of serine esterases present in the granules of cytotoxic T lymphocytes and natural killer (NK) cells. They induce apoptosis in the target cell that they enter through perforin channels inserted into the target cell membrane by the cytotoxic lymphocyte.

11451.title: graph-based method
11451.definition: A computational method that converts the problem to be solved into a graph characterized by the character of the objects, such the atoms of a molecule or molecules in a database, and the distances between them.

08172.title: graphene
08172.definition: Allotrope of carbon, whose structure is a one-atom-thick planar sheet of \(\ce{sp^{2}{-}bonded}\) carbon atoms in a honeycomb (hexagonal) crystal lattice.

G02683.title: graphene layer
G02683.definition: A single carbon layer of the graphite structure, describing its nature by analogy to a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon of quasi infinite size.

G02684.title: graphite
G02684.definition: An allotropic form of the element carbon consisting of layers of hexagonally arranged carbon atoms in a planar condensed ring system graphene layers The layers are stacked parallel to each other in a three-dimensional crystalline long-range order. There are two allotropic forms with different stacking arrangements, hexagonal and rhombohedral. The chemical bonds within the layers are covalent with \(\rm{sp}^{2}\) hybridization and with a C–C distance of \(141.7\ \rm{pm}\). The weak bonds between the layers are metallic with a strength comparable to van der Waals bonding only.

G02686.title: graphite fibres
G02686.definition: Carbon fibres consisting mostly of synthetic graphite for which three-dimensional crystalline order is confirmed by X-ray diffraction.

G02687.title: graphite material
G02687.definition: A material consisting essentially of graphitic carbon.

G02688.title: graphite whiskers
G02688.definition: Thin, approximately cylindrical filaments in which graphene layers are arranged in a scroll-like manner. There is, at least in part, a regular stacking of the layers as in the graphite lattice, giving rise to h,k,l, X-ray reflections. The physical properties of graphite whiskers approach, along the cylinder axis, those of graphite.

G02689.title: graphitic carbon
G02689.definition: All varieties of substances consisting of the element carbon in the allotropic form of graphite irrespective of the presence of structural defects.

G02690.title: graphitizable carbon
G02690.definition: A non-graphitic carbon which upon graphitization heat treatment converts into graphitic carbon.

G02691.title: graphitization
G02691.definition: A solid-state transformation of thermodynamically unstable non-graphitic carbon into graphite by means of heat treatment.

G02692.title: graphitization heat treatment
G02692.definition: A process of heat treatment of a non-graphitic carbon industrially performed at temperatures in the range between \(2500\) and \(3300\ \rm{K}\), to achieve transformation into graphitic carbon.

G02693.title: graphitized carbon
G02693.definition: A graphitic carbon with more or less perfect three-dimensional hexagonal crystalline order prepared from non-graphitic carbon by graphitization heat treatment.

14723.title: grasshopper effect
14723.definition: Global distillation of persistent organic pollutants (POPs) involving seasonal cycling of temperatures such that movement toward the higher latitudes occurs in annual pulses.

13187.title: Graves disease
13187.definition: Hyperthyroidism associated with diffuse hyperplastic goitre resulting from production of a thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor (TSHR)-binding autoantibody.

09043.title: gravimetric analysis
09043.definition: Measurement principle of quantitative chemical analysis based on measurement of mass.

09044.title: gravimetric factor
09044.definition: Mass fraction of analyte in a precipitate (see precipitation) obtained in a gravimetric analysis.

G02694.title: gravimetric method
G02694.definition: A determination by weight; e.g. in the older method of $\ce{Cl^{−}}$ ion determination, a weighed amount of sample is dissolved in water, $\ce{AgNO3}$ solution added, $\ce{AgCl}$ is precipitated, dried and weighed. From the known mass fraction of silver in $\ce{AgCl}$, the weights of the initial sample and that of the $\ce{AgCl}$ precipitated, the percentage of chlorine in the sample can be calculated readily.

G02695.title: gravitational constant
G02695.definition: Universal fundamental physical constant in Newton's law of gravitation, \(G = \pu{6.67259(85)E-11 m3 kg-1 s-2}\).

09936.title: gravitational field-flow fractionation
09936.definition: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is the Earth’s gravitational field.

G02696.title: gray
G02696.definition: SI derived unit of energy imparted to an element of matter by ionizing radiation divided by the mass of that element (absorbed dose of radiation) equal to one joule per kilogram and admitted for reasons of safeguarding human health, \(\pu{Gy} = \pu{J kg-1}\).

08608.title: grazing incidence
08608.definition: Angle of incidence of a beam of electromagnetic radiation greater than \(\pu{70\!^{\circ}}\).

09199.title: grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering analysis
09199.definition: Measurement method in which the elastically scattered intensity of X-rays from a reflecting surface is measured for small-angle deflections at grazing incidence.

11035.title: greater omentum
11035.definition: Omentum passing from the greater curvature of the stomach in front of the small intestine, folding back on itself to fuse into four layers of peritoneal membrane, and ascending to the transverse colon.

GT07552.title: green body
GT07552.definition: Object formed from a preceramic material prior to pyrolysis.

12663.title: green chemistry
12663.definition: Invention, design, and application of chemical products and processes to reduce or eliminate the use and generation of hazardous substances.

G02697.title: green coke
G02697.definition: Green coke (raw coke) is the primary solid carbonization product from high boiling hydrocarbon fractions obtained at temperatures below \(900\ \rm{K}\). It contains a fraction of matter that can be released as volatiles during subsequent heat treatment at temperatures up to approximately \(1600\ \rm{K}\). This mass fraction, the so-called volatile matter, is in the case of green coke between 4 and 15 wt.%, but it depends also on the heating rate.

G02698.title: greenhouse effect
G02698.definition: Heating effect produced by certain gases (e.g. $\ce{CO2}$, $\ce{O3}$, etc.), which by virtue of their characteristic infrared absorption, lower the earth to space transmission of long wavelength radiation but allow transmission of shorter wavelength radiation inward from the sun to the earth.

14724.title: greenhouse gases
14724.definition: Atmospheric gases that are relatively transparent to sunlight entering the atmosphere but absorb infrared radiation generated at the Earth’s surface. They include water vapor, carbon dioxide (\(\ce{CO2}\)), methane, dinitrogen oxide (nitrous oxide), chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), chloroethane (methylchloroform), carbon tetrachloride, and the fire retardant, halon. Ozone in the troposphere can also act as a greenhouse gas.

10781.title: grey matter
10781.definition: Regions of the brain and spinal cord that are made up primarily of cell bodies and dendrites of nerve cells rather than of myelinated axons.

G02699.title: Grignard reagents
G02699.definition: Organomagnesium halides, $\ce{RMgX, having a carbon–magnesium bond (or their equilibrium mixtures in solution with $\ce{R2Mg}$ + $\ce{MgX}$).

08484.title: Grimm-type cathode
08484.definition: Cathode for a glow electric discharge consisting of a flat sample, which is cooled during the discharge process so that thermal volatilization is suppressed and the sample material is removed by sputtering only.

G02701.title: grit
G02701.definition: Airborne solid particles in the atmosphere which are of natural or manmade origin and which remain in suspension for some time; in the United Kingdom the size of the grit particles is defined as greater than \(75\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) in diameter (retained on a 200 mesh British Standard sieve).

09869.title: groove binding
09869.definition: Process in which molecules are bound within a minor or major groove of the deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) double helix.

G02702.title: ground level concentration
G02702.definition: The concentration of a chemical species, normally a pollutant, in air; usually measured at a specific height above the ground.

G02703.title: ground level inversion
G02703.definition: The inversion of the normal temperature gradient in the atmosphere; the temperature of the air increases with increasing height of the air above the ground. This leads to poor mixing of gases released below the inversion.

G02704.title: ground state
G02704.definition: The state of lowest Gibbs energy of a system.

15748.title: ground treatment of plants
15748.definition: Dusting or spraying of plants with pesticides by hand, by special machines, or by apparatus fixed to tractors or driven by them.

G02705.title: group
G02705.definition: A defined linked collection of atoms or a single atom within a molecular entity. This use of the term in physical organic and general chemistry is less restrictive than the definition adopted for the purpose of nomenclature of organic compounds.

08609.title: group frequency
08609.definition: Frequency in vibrational spectroscopy that is characteristic of a particular chemical functional group.

G02707.title: group preconcentration
G02707.definition: An operation (process) as a result of which several microcomponents are isolated in one step. This may be achieved in one of two ways, by transportation either of the matrix or of the microcomponents into a second phase. The first method is widely used in the analysis of relatively simple substances and materials.

08910.title: group-transfer polymerization
08910.definition: Chain polymerization in which a specific atom or group is intramolecularly transferred to remain associated with the active chain-end during the course of polymerization.

G02708.title: growth curve
G02708.definition: Curve giving the activity of a radioactive nuclide as a function of time and showing the increase of the activity through the decay of the precursor or as a result of activation.

14726.title: growth dilution
14726.definition: Decrease in contaminant concentration in a growing organism because the amount of tissue in which the contaminant is distributed is increasing.

10782.title: growth factor
10782.definition: Naturally occurring or genetically engineered protein or steroid hormone that binds to a receptor to regulate cell growth, proliferation, or differentiation.

10783.title: growth hormone
10783.definition: Peptide hormone secreted by the anterior pituitary that stimulates growth, energy metabolism, and cell proliferation.

10784.title: growth hormone releasing factor
10784.definition: Substance produced in the hypothalamus that regulates release of growth hormone by the anterior pituitary.

G02709.title: growth rate
G02709.definition: The measure (\(\rm{h}^{-1}\),\(\rm{d}^{-1}\)) of the rate of growth or multiplication of an organism or a culture, usually expressed as specific growth rate (the increase of mass or cell number per time unit referred to the unit of mass, \(\frac{\rm{d}(\ln X)}{\rm{d}t}\)).

G02710.title: Grunwald–Winstein equation
G02710.definition: The linear free energy relation: \[\log _{10}(\frac{k_{\rm{s}}}{k_{0}}) = m\ Y\] expressing the dependence of the rate of solvolysis of a substrate on ionizing power of the solvent. The rate constant \(k_{0}\) applies to the reference solvent (ethanol–water, 80:20, v/v) and \(k_{\rm{s}}\) to the solvent s, both at \(25\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\). The parameter \(m\) is characteristic of the substrate and is assigned the value unity for tert-butyl chloride. The value \(Y\) is intended to be a quantitative measure of the ionizing power of the solvents. The equation was later extended to the form: \[\log _{10}(\frac{k_{\rm{s}}}{k_{0}}) = m\ Y+l\ N\] where \(N\) is the nucleophilicity of the solvent and \(l\) its susceptibility parameter. The equation has also been applied to reactions other than solvolysis.

08076.title: guard band
08076.definition:
Interval between a tolerance limit and a corresponding acceptance limit.
Figure 1: Guarded acceptance. Two-sided acceptance interval created by reducing the tolerance interval on either side by a guard band, thus reducing the probability of falsely accepting a non-conforming item.Figure 2: Guarded rejection. Two-sided acceptance interval created by increasing the tolerance interval on either side by a guard band, thus reducing the probability of falsely rejecting a conforming item.

10785.title: gubernaculum
10785.definition: Fetal mesenchyme ligament that passes through the anterior abdominal wall and connects the lower pole of each developing gonad with the developing scrotum in men, and with the developing labia majora in women.

G02711.title: guest
G02711.definition: An organic or inorganic ion or molecule that occupies a cavity, cleft or pocket within the molecular structure of a host molecular entity and forms a complex with it or that is trapped in a cavity within the crystal structure of a host.

15749.title: guideline for exposure limits
15749.definition: Scientifically judged quantitative value (a concentration or number) of an environmental constituent that ensures aesthetically pleasing air, water, or food and from which no adverse effect is expected concerning noncarcinogenic endpoints, or that gives an acceptably low estimate of lifetime cancer risk from those substances which are proven human carcinogens or carcinogens with at least limited evidence of human carcinogenicity.

15750.title: guideline value
15750.definition: Quantitative measure (a concentration or a number) of a constituent of an environmental medium that ensures aesthetically pleasing air, water, or food and does not result in a significant risk to the user.

15751.title: guides to air quality
15751.definition: Sets of atmospheric concentrations and exposure times that are associated with specific effects of varying degrees of pollution on humans, animals, vegetation, and the environment in general.

15752.title: guides to environmental quality
15752.definition: Sets of concentrations, numbers and exposure times that are associated with the specific effects of factors in environmental media on humans, animals, vegetation, and the environment in general.

14727.title: guild
14727.definition: Group of functionally similar species whose members interact strongly with one another but weakly with the remainder of the community.

11797.title: Guillain–Barré syndrome
11797.definition: Type of idiopathic polyneuritis in which autoimmunity to peripheral nerve, myelin leads to a condition characterized by chronic demyelination of the spinal roots (see spinal cord), peripheral nerves, and cranial nerves.

13188.title: guinea pig maximization test
13188.definition: Skin sensitization test for allergic contact dermatitis in which shaved guinea pig skin is exposed to intradermal injections of a test agent together with complete Freund’s adjuvant, followed by an occlusive patch for boosting for \(\pu{48 h}\) beginning on day 7, and challenged on day 21.

G02712.title: Guinier plot
G02712.definition: A diagrammatic representation of data on scattering from large particles, obtained at different angles but at the same concentration, constructed by plotting \(\log _{10}\Delta R\left(\theta \right)\) or \(\log _{10}P\left(\theta \right)\) versus \((\sin \frac{\theta}{2})^{2}\) or \(q^{2}\) and (usually) used for the evaluation of the radius of gyration. \(\Delta R(\theta)\) is the excess Rayleigh ratio, \(P\left(\theta \right)\) the particle scattering function, \(\theta \) the scattering angle and \(q\) the length of the scattering vector.

G02713.title: gustiness
G02713.definition: Intensity of turbulence; the ratio of the root mean square of wind velocity fluctuations to the mean wind velocity.

13189.title: gut-associated lymphoid tissue
13189.definition: Lymphoid cells and tissues lining the mucosa that seem to serve as the first point of antigen contact via this route, including Peyer’s patches, the appendix, tonsils, adenoids, and mesenteric lymph nodes.

GT07553.title: hybrid material
GT07553.definition: Material composed of an intimate mixture of inorganic components, organic components, or both types of component.

11575.title: γ-aminobutyric acid
11575.definition: Major neurotransmitter at inhibitory synapses in the central nervous system of mammals.

11576.title: γ-aminobutyric acid receptor
11576.definition: Transmembrane receptor protein that binds and responds to the inhibitory neurotransmitter $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}aminobutyric acid}$.

G02566.title: γ-cascade
G02566.definition: Two or more different gamma rays emitted successively from one nucleus when it passes through one or more energy levels.

13163.title: γ-interferon
13163.definition: Member of a group of cytokines, the interferons, which has as its primary action the activation of macrophages and can induce cells to resist viral replication.

13161.title: γ:δ T cell
13161.definition: Lymphocyte whose T-cell receptor (TCR) is a heterodimer of a \(\ce{\upgamma\mbox{-}chain}\) and a \(\ce{\updelta\mbox{-}chain}\).

13162.title: γ:δ T-cell receptor
13162.definition: T-cell receptor (TCR) composed of two different glycoprotein chains, designated \(\upgamma\) and \(\updelta\), assembled in a \(\ce{\upgamma\mbox{:}\updelta\ heterodimer}\).

13933.title: host response
13933.definition: Reaction of a living system to the presence of a substance or a material.

13934.title: hybrid artificial organ
13934.definition: Artificial organ that is a combination of viable cells and one or more biomaterials.

12424.title: hard ionization
12424.definition: Formation of gas-phase ions accompanied by extensive fragmentation.

12425.title: high-field asymmetric waveform ion mobility spectrometry
12425.definition: Separation of ions at atmospheric pressure between two electrodes due to simultaneous application of a high potential asymmetric waveform, whereby ions migrate towards one of the two electrodes depending on the ratio of the high- to low-field mobility of the ion. A variable compensating DC potential is used to selectively transmit ions of interest.

12426.title: hybrid mass spectrometer
12426.definition: Mass spectrometer that combines m/z analyzers of different types to perform tandem mass spectrometry or higher-order \({\rm{MS}}^{n}\) experiment.

12427.title: hydrogen/deuterium exchange
12427.definition: Exchange of hydrogen atoms with deuterium atoms in a chemical species in solution prior to introduction into a mass spectrometer, or by ion/molecule reaction with a neutral gas inside a mass spectrometer.

12428.title: hydrogen shifts
12428.definition: Sigmatropic reactions of ions in which the \(\ce{\upsigma\mbox{-}bonds}\) broken and formed involve hydrogen atoms, and are subject to the Woodward–Hofmann rules resulting from orbital symmetry considerations.

12429.title: hyphenated mass spectrometry technique
12429.definition: Analytical technique in which mass spectrometry is interfaced with a pretreatment step, most often chromatographic separation but many other combinations are possible.

14209.title: helix pitch
14209.definition: Distance between successive helical windings projected on the chain axis.

14237.title: homopolymer isomorphism
14237.definition: Macromolecular isomorphism involving two homopolymers with different constitutional repeating units.

14249.title: hedrite
14249.definition: Polyhedral aggregate of lamellar crystals resulting in a morphology that resembles that of a polymer single crystal, at least from one viewing direction.

14264.title: heteroepitaxy
14264.definition: Epitaxy between crystals of different substances.

14265.title: homoepitaxy
14265.definition: Epitaxy between crystals of the same substance.

13190.title: H-2
13190.definition: Region of mouse chromosome 17 coding the major histocompatibility complex (MHC).

13191.title: H-2 complex
13191.definition: Mouse major histocompatibility complex (MHC) coded by H-2.

08347.title: H(CCO)NH
08347.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one nitrogen, and two hydrogen dimensions.

HT06787.title: Haber–Weiss reaction
HT06787.definition: The Haber–Weiss cycle consists of the following two reactions: $\ce{H2O2 + OH^{.} -> H2O + O2^{−} + H^{+}}$and$\ce{H2O2 + O2^{-} -> O2 + OH^{-} + OH^{.}}$ The second reaction achieved notoriety as a possible source of hydroxyl radicals. However, it has a negligible rate constant. It is believed that iron(III) complexes can catalyse this reaction: first, Fe(III) is reduced by superoxide, followed by oxidation by dihydrogen peroxide.

14728.title: habitat
14728.definition:
Spatial area (geographical area) where a particular species population lives, large enough to comprise a breeding population.
Note: A microhabitat or microenvironment is the immediate surroundings and other physical factors of an individual plant or animal within its habitat.
Physical conditions that surround a species, or species population, or assemblage of species, or community.

11798.title: habituation
11798.definition: Decrease or cessation of a response to a stimulus after its repeated presentation.

08253.title: Hadamard transform spectrometer
08253.definition: Multiplexing spectrometer that uses the optical components of a dispersive spectrometer with a Hadamard encoding mask.

13192.title: hairy cell leukemia
13192.definition: B-cell neoplasm, usually occurring during middle age, constituting about \(\pu{2\%}\) of all leukemias and responding well to chemotherapy. The neoplastic cells have fine, hairlike surfaces.

HT07207.title: halato-telechelic polymer
HT07207.definition: Polymer composed of linear macromolecules having ionic or ionizable end-groups.

H02717.title: half life
H02717.definition: For a single radioactive decay process, the time required for the activity to decrease to half its value by that process.

H02716.title: half life
H02716.definition: For a given reaction the half life \(t_{1/2}\) of a reactant is the time required for its concentration to reach a value that is the arithmetic mean of its initial and final (equilibrium) values. For a reactant that is entirely consumed it is the time taken for the reactant concentration to fall to one half its initial value: The half life of a reaction has meaning only in special cases:  For a first-order reaction, the half life of the reactant may be called the half life of the reaction.  For a reaction involving more than one reactant, with the concentrations of the reactants in their stoichiometric ratios, the half life of each reactant is the same, and may be called the half life of the reaction.   If the concentrations of reactants are not in their stoichiometric ratios, there are different half lives for different reactants, and one cannot speak of the half life of the reaction.

H02721.title: half thickness
H02721.definition: The thickness of a specified substance which, when introduced into the path of a given beam of radiation, reduces the value of a specified radiation quantity by one half.

H02715.title: half-chair
H02715.definition: The conformation of a six-membered ring structure in which four contiguous atoms are in a plane and the other two atoms lie on opposite sides of the plane.

HT07390.title: half-life
HT07390.definition: Time necessary for thermal bleaching to half of the absorbance of the coloured form of a photochromic compound at a specific wavelength during one cycle.

HT07391.title: half-life
HT07391.definition: Time needed for a concentration of the entity to decrease to \(1/2\) of its original value.

H02720.title: half-peak potential
H02720.definition: In linear-sweep voltammetry, triangular-wave voltammetry, cyclic triangular-wave voltammetry, and similar techniques, the potential of the indicator electrode at which the difference between the total current and the residual current is equal to one-half of the peak current. This potential is attained in the interval in which the rate of the charge-transfer process, and hence the (absolute value of the) current, increase monotonically with time.

08729.title: half-value thickness
08729.definition: Thickness of a specified material that, when introduced into the path of a given beam of radiation, reduces the intensity of a specified radiation by one half.

H02722.title: half-wave potential
H02722.definition: The potential of a polarographic or voltammetric indicator electrode at the point, on the rising part of a polarographic or voltammetric wave, where the difference between the total current and the residual current is equal to one-half of the limiting current. The quarter-wave potential, the three-quarter-wave potential, etc., may be similarly defined.

H02723.title: half-width
H02723.definition: The full width of a spectral band at a height equal to half of the height at the band maximum. Also known as full width at half maximum (FWHM). The dimension of band width should be either inverse length (wavenumbers) or inverse time (frequencies) so that the values give an indication of the energies. Note the hyphen in half-width. Half bandwidth has the meaning of half-width at half maximum.

11799.title: hallucination
11799.definition: The apparent, often strong, subjective perception of an external object or event when no such stimulus or situation is present.

H02725.title: halochromism
H02725.definition: The colour change which occurs on addition of acid (or base, or a salt) to a solution of a compound. A chemical reaction (e.g. ion formation) transforms a colourless compound into a coloured one.

08173.title: halogen bond
08173.definition: Association between a Lewis-acidic halogen atom in a molecular entity and a Lewis-basic region in another, or the same, molecular entity, which acts as an electron-pair donor, such that the balance of forces of attraction and repulsion results in net stabilization.

H02727.title: halohydrins
H02727.definition: A traditional term for alcohols substituted by a halogen atom at a saturated carbon atom otherwise bearing only hydrogen or hydrocarbyl groups (usually used to mean $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}halo alcohols}$). E.g. $\ce{BrCH2CH2OH}$ 'ethylene bromohydrin' (2-bromoethanol), $\ce{ClCH2CH2CH2OH}$ 'trimethylene chlorohydrin' (3-chloro-propan-1-ol), $\ce{PhCH(OH)CH2Cl}$ 'styrene chlorohydrin' (2-chloro-1-phenylethanol).

H02728.title: halonium ions
H02728.definition: Ions of the form $\ce{R2X^{+}}$, where $\ce{X}$ is any halogen ($\ce{X} = \ce{Br^{+}}$, bromonium ions; $\ce{X} = \ce{Cl^{+}}$, chloronium ions; $\ce{X} = \ce{F^{+}}$, fluoronium ions; $\ce{X} = \ce{I^{+}}$, iodonium ions). They may be open-chain or cyclic.

H02729.title: halophiles
H02729.definition: Organisms which require a minimum concentration of sodium chloride in their environment (cf. extremophiles).

H02730.title: hamiltonian operator
H02730.definition: Quantum mechanical operator of total energy.

H02732.title: Hammett equation
H02732.definition: The equation in the form: \[\log _{10}(\frac{k}{k_{0}}) = \rho \ \sigma \] or \[\log _{10}(\frac{K}{K_{0}}) = \rho \ \sigma \] applied to the influence of meta- or para-substituents $\ce{X}$ on the reactivity of the functional group $\ce{Y}$ in the benzene derivative m- or $\ce{p-XC6H4Y}$. \(k\) or \(K\) is the rate or equilibrium constant, respectively, for the given reaction of m- or $\ce{p-XC6H4Y}$; \(k_{0}\) or \(K_{0}\) refers to the reaction of $\ce{C6H5Y}$, i.e. $\ce{X} = \ce{H}$; is the substituent constant characteristic of m- or $\ce{p-X}$: is the reaction constant characteristic of the given reaction of $\ce{Y}$. The equation is often encountered in a form with \(\log _{10}k_{0}\) or \(\log _{10}K_{0}\) written as a separate term on the right hand side, e.g. \[\log _{10}k = \rho \ \sigma +\log _{10}k_{0}\] or \[\log _{10}K = \rho \ \sigma +\log _{10}K_{0}\] It then signifies the intercept corresponding to $\ce{X} = \ce{H}$ in a regression of \(\log _{10}k\) or \(\log _{10}K\) on \(\sigma \).

H02734.title: Hammond principle
H02734.definition: The hypothesis that, when a transition state leading to an unstable reaction intermediate (or product) has nearly the same energy as that intermediate, the two are interconverted with only a small reorganization of molecular structure. Essentially the same idea is sometimes referred to as 'Leffler's assumption', namely, that the transition state bears the greater resemblance to the less stable species (reactant or reaction intermediate/product). Many text books and physical organic chemists, however, express the idea in Leffler's form, but attribute it to Hammond. As a corollary, it follows that a factor stabilizing a reaction intermediate will also stabilize the transition state leading to that intermediate. The acronym 'Bemahapothle' (Bell, Marcus, Hammond, Polanyi, Thornton, Leffler) is sometimes used in recognition of the principal contributors towards expansion of the original idea of the Hammond postulate.

H02735.title: handedness
H02735.definition: This term has been used in two ways, either chirality or chirality sense

HT06962.title: Hansch analysis
HT06962.definition: Hansch analysis is the investigation of the quantitative relationship between the biological activity of a series of compounds and their physicochemical substituent or global parameters representing hydrophobic, electronic, steric and other effects using multiple regression correlation methodology.

H02736.title: Hansch constant
H02736.definition: A measure of the capability of a solute for hydrophobic lipophilic interaction based on the partition coefficient \(P\) for distribution of the solute between octan-1-ol and water. The most general way of applying \(P\) in correlation analysis, QSAR, etc. is as log \(P\), but the behaviour of substituted benzene derivatives may be quantified by a substituent constant scale, \(\pi \), which is defined in a way analogous to the Hammett $\ce{\upsigma\!}$ scale. There are various scales, depending on the substrate series used as reference.

11452.title: Hansch equation
11452.definition: A QSAR equation that describes the relationship between the logarithm of the relative biological potency of a molecule (\(\log (1/C_{i})\)) and its electronic and hydrophobic properties: \[\log (1/C_{i}) = \rho \sigma_{i} + b\,\log P_{i} - c\,(\log P_{i})^{2}\] in which fitting to the square term provides a parabola with an associated optimum log P.

11453.title: Hansch–Fujita π-constant
11453.definition: A constant that describes the contribution of a substituent to the octan-1-ol-water log P of a compound.]

H02737.title: Hantzsch–Widman name
H02737.definition: A name for a heteromonocyclic parent hydride having no more than ten ring members formed by the citation of 'a' prefixes denoting the heteroatoms followed by an ending (the 'stem') defining the size of the ring.

10786.title: haploid
10786.definition: State in which a cell contains only one set of chromosomes.

13193.title: haplotype
13193.definition: Set of allelic variants present at a given genetic region.

H02738.title: hapten
H02738.definition: A low-molecular weight molecule which contains an antigenic determinant but which is not itself antigenic unless complexed with an antigenic carrier. Examples of haptens are dinitrophenols, phosphorylcholine and dextran.

13194.title: haptenic
13194.definition: Able to act as a hapten.

08174.title: hapticity
08174.definition: Topological description for the number of contiguous atoms of a ligand that are bonded to a central metal atom.

H02740.title: hard acid
H02740.definition: A Lewis acid with an acceptor centre of low polarizability. Other things being approximately equal, complexes of hard acids and bases or soft acids and bases have an added stabilization (sometimes called 'HSAB' rule). For example the hard O- (or N-) bases are preferred to their S- (or P-) analogues by hard acids. Conversely a soft acid possesses an acceptor centre of high polarizability and exhibits the reverse preference for coordination of a soft base. These preferences are not defined in a quantitative sense.

H02741.title: hard amorphous carbon films
H02741.definition: A synonym for diamond-like carbon films

09494.title: hard bake
09494.definition: High temperature annealing to solidify any resist material remaining after development in order to provide a durable protective layer for etching.

H02742.title: hard base
H02742.definition: A Lewis base with a donor centre (e.g. an oxygen atom) of low polarizability the converse applies to soft bases.

14730.title: hard water
14730.definition: Water that contains mineral salts of divalent cations, commonly calcium and magnesium and sometimes iron(II) (ferrous) ions, principally as hydrogencarbonates, chlorides, and sulfates.

HT07293.title: hard-segment phase domain
HT07293.definition: Phase domain of microscopic or smaller size, usually in a block, graft, or segmented copolymer, comprising essentially those segments of the polymer that are rigid and capable of forming strong intermolecular interactions.

14729.title: hardness
14729.definition: Concentration of all metallic cations, except those of the alkali metals, present in water.

14731.title: Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium
14731.definition: State of a population if the frequencies of different alleles of all genes in the genome remain constant between generations.

14732.title: harm
14732.definition: Adverse effect to an ecosystem, community, population, species, individual organism, organ, tissue, or cell.

15753.title: harmful occupational factor
15753.definition: Component of the work environment, the effect of which on a worker under certain conditions leads to ill health or reduction of working ability.

15754.title: harmful substance
15754.definition: Substance that, following contact with an organism, can cause ill health or adverse effects either at the time of exposure or later in the life of the present and future generations.

HT07041.title: harmonic approximation

08610.title: harmonic constant
08610.definition: Coefficient of (\(\nu + ½\)) in the vibrational term value, determined by the harmonic terms in the vibrational potential energy.

H02744.title: harmonic frequency generation
H02744.definition: Production of coherent radiation of frequency \(k\ \nu \) (\(k=2,3,...\)) from coherent radiation of frequency. In general, this effect is obtained through the interaction of laser light with a suitable optical medium with non-linear polarizability. The case \(k=2\) is referred to as frequency doubling, \(k=3\) is frequency tripling and \(k=4\) is frequency quadrupling. Even higher integer values of \(k\) are possible.

H02745.title: harmonic mean
H02745.definition: The number of observations, divided by the sum of reciprocals of the observations. Symbol: \(\bar{x}_{\rm{h}}\). It can be calculated with the formula: \[\bar{x}_{\rm{h}} = \frac{n}{\sum x_{j}^{-1}}\]

H02746.title: harpoon mechanism
H02746.definition: Reaction sequence (thermal or photoinduced) between neutral molecular or atomic entities in which long-range electron transfer is followed by a considerable reduction of the distance between donor and acceptor sites as a result of the electrostatic attraction in the ion pair created.

H02748.title: Hartree energy
H02748.definition: Atomic fundamental physical constant used as atomic unit of energy: \(E_{\rm{h}}=\frac{\mathrm{\hslash }^{2}}{m_{\rm{e}}\ a_{0}^{2}} = 4.359\ 7482(26)\times 10^{-18}\ \rm{J}\), where \(\mathrm{\hslash}\) is the Planck constant divided by \(2\ \pi \), \(m_{\rm{e}}\) the electron rest mass and \(a_{0}\) the Bohr radius.

13195.title: Hashimoto thyroiditis
13195.definition: Autoimmune disease where the body’s own antibodies attack the cells of the thyroid.

11454.title: hashing
11454.definition: An algorithm that maps data of variable length, such as the raw descriptors of path or circular fingerprints or InChIs, to a smaller fixed length vector.

H02749.title: Haworth representation
H02749.definition: The Haworth representation of the cyclic forms of monosaccharides can be derived from the Fischer projection, as follows. The monosaccharide is depicted with the carbon-chain horizontal and in the plane of the paper, the potential carbonyl group being to the right. The oxygen bridge is then depicted as being formed behind the plane of the paper. The heterocyclic ring is therefore located in a plane approximately perpendicular to the plane of the paper and the groups attached to the carbon atoms of that ring are above and below the ring. The carbon atoms of the ring are not shown. Groups that appear to the right of the vertical chain in the Fischer projection (structures $\ce{A}$, $\ce{D}$) then appear below the plane of the ring in the Haworth representation (structures $\ce{B}$, $\ce{C}$, $\ce{E}$). However, at the asymmetric carbon atom ($\ce{C-5}$ in $\ce{A}$; $\ce{C-4}$ in $\ce{D}$) involved via oxygen in ring formation with the carbon atom of the carbonyl group a formal double inversion must be envisaged to obtain the correct Haworth representation. In the pyranose forms of ᴅ-aldohexoses $\ce{C-6}$ will always be above the plane, In the furanose forms of ᴅ-aldohexoses the position of $\ce{C-6}$ will depend on the configuration at $\ce{C-4}$; it will, for example, be above the plane in ᴅ-glucofuranoses (e.g. $\ce{C}$) but below the plane in ᴅ-galactofuranoses (e.g. $\ce{E}$).

13196.title: hay fever
13196.definition: Allergic condition affecting the mucous membranes of the upper respiratory tract and the eyes, characterized by nasal discharge, sneezing, and itchy, watery eyes; and usually caused by an abnormal sensitivity to airborne pollen.

HT06827.title: hazard
HT06827.definition: Set of inherent properties of a substance, mixture of substances, or a process involving substances that, under production, usage, or disposal conditions, make it capable of causing adverse effects to organisms or the environment, depending on the degree of exposure; in other words, it is a source of danger.

14733.title: hazard assessment
14733.definition: Determination of factors controlling the likely effects of a hazard such as the dose–effect and dose–response relationships, variations in target susceptibility, bioaccumulation potential, persistence, and mechanism of toxicity.

15755.title: hazard communication standard
15755.definition: U.S. OSHA standard requiring all employers to inform employees of the hazard of substances in the workplace and the steps necessary to avoid harm.

14734.title: hazard evaluation
14734.definition: Identification and assessment of the potential adverse effects that could result from manufacture, use, and disposal of a material in a specified quantity and manner.

14735.title: hazard identification
14735.definition: Determination of substances of concern, their adverse effects, target populations, and conditions of exposure, taking into account toxicity data and knowledge of effects on human health, other organisms, and their environment.

14736.title: hazard index
14736.definition: Sum of the hazard quotients for substances that affect the same target organ or organ system.

14737.title: hazard quotient
14737.definition: Ratio of toxicant exposure (estimated or measured) to a reference value regarded as corresponding to a threshold of toxicity; often this is determined as the predicted environmental concentration (PEC) divided by the predicted no-effect concentration (PNEC).

14738.title: hazardous concentration
14738.definition: Concentration of a substance producing a defined effect on \(\pu{\textit{p} \%}\) (usually \(\pu{5\%}\)) of species of concern, derived by means of a statistical extrapolation procedure.

15756.title: hazardous production factor
15756.definition: Production factor the effect of which on a worker under certain conditions results in injury or some impairment of health.

H02751.title: haze horizon
H02751.definition: The top of a haze layer which is confined by a low-level temperature inversion so that it gives the appearance of the horizon which it may obscure.

H02750.title: haze
H02750.definition: A state of reduced visibility (\(1{-}2\ \rm{km}\)) resulting from the increased light scatter due to the presence of fine dust or aerosol particles ($\ce{H2SO4}$, $\ce{NH4HSO4}$, products of the ozone-terpene reactions, etc.).

08175.title: HBA solvent
08175.definition: Strongly or weakly basic solvent capable of acting as a hydrogen-bond acceptor (HBA) and forming strong intermolecular solute-solvent hydrogen bonds.

08176.title: HBD solvent
08176.definition: Solvent with a sizable permanent dipole moment that bears suitably acidic hydrogen atoms to form strong intermolecular solvent-solute hydrogen bonds.

08348.title: HBHA(CO)NH
08348.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one nitrogen and two hydrogen dimensions.

08349.title: HCCH-COSY
08349.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one carbon and two hydrogen dimensions.

08350.title: HCCH-TOCSY
08350.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one carbon and two hydrogen dimensions.

08824.title: head-tail isomerism
08824.definition: Constitutional isomerism of polymeric (oligomeric) chains composed of identical non symmetric repeating units consisting in different orientations of the units.

11800.title: headache
11800.definition: Pain in one or more parts of the cranium, not confined to the area of distribution of any nerve.

10198.title: headspace
10198.definition: Volume of gas phase above a sample in a closed container.

10267.title: headspace solid-phase microextraction
10267.definition: Solid-phase microextraction where the extraction phase is placed in the headspace above the sample.

15757.title: health
15757.definition:
State of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.
State of dynamic balance in which an individual’s or a group’s capacity to cope with the circumstances of living is at an optimal level.
State characterized by anatomical, physiological, and psychological integrity; ability to perform personally valued family, work, and community roles; ability to deal with physical, biological, psychological, and social stress; a feeling of well-being; and freedom from the risk of disease and untimely death.
In ecology, a sustainable steady state in which humans and other living organisms can coexist indefinitely.

15758.title: health advisory level
15758.definition: In the United States, nonregulatory health-based reference level of chemical traces (usually in ppm, i.e., \(\pu{mg L-1}\)) in drinking water at which there are no adverse health risks when ingested over various periods of time.

15760.title: health hazard
15760.definition: Any factor or exposure that may adversely affect health.

HT06908.title: health surveillance
HT06908.definition: The procedure for effects of work on the health of employees.

15759.title: health-based exposure limit
15759.definition: Maximum concentration or intensity of exposure that can be tolerated without significant effect (based on only scientific and not economic evidence concerning exposure levels and associated health effects).

15761.title: healthy worker effect
15761.definition: Epidemiological phenomenon observed initially in studies of occupational diseases: Workers usually exhibit lower overall disease and death rates than the general population, due to the fact that the old, severely ill, and disabled are ordinarily excluded from employment. Death rates in the general population may be inappropriate for comparison, if this effect is not taken into account.

09954.title: heart-cut separations
09954.definition: Type of two-dimensional chromatography in which selected fractions from the first separation step are transferred to a second separation step.

H02754.title: heat capacity of activation
H02754.definition: A quantity related to the temperature coefficient of \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}H\) (enthalpy of activation) and \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}S\) (entropy of activation) according to the equations: \[\Delta ^{\ddagger}C_{p} = (\frac{\partial \Delta ^{\ddagger }H}{\partial T})_{p}=T\ (\frac{\partial \Delta ^{\ddagger }S}{\partial T})_{p}\] If the rate constant is expressible in the form \[\ln k = \frac{a}{T}+b+c\ \ln T + \rm{d}T,\] then: \[\Delta ^{\ddagger}C_{p} = (c - 1)\ R+2\ \rm{d}(R\ T)\] SI unit: \(\pu{J mol-1 K-1}\).

H02753.title: heat capacity
H02753.definition: Heat brought to a system to increase its temperature divided by that temperature increase. At constant volume \(C_{V}=(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T})_{V}\) at constant pressure \(C_{p}=(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T})_{p}\), where \(U\) is the internal energy and \(H\) the enthalpy of the system.

H02755.title: heat flux
H02755.definition: Heat transferred through a cross section perpendicular to the flow in a small time interval divided by that time interval and the cross sectional area.

15403.title: heat of polymerisation
15403.definition: Heat absorbed or given off from the conversion of a specified amount of monomer into polymer.

12291.title: heat-flow differential scanning calorimetry
12291.definition: Technique where the difference between the heat-flow rates into a sample and a reference material is measured.

13197.title: heat shock proteins
13197.definition: Evolutionarily conserved proteins, found in many organisms, that are induced upon exposure of cells to various types of stress, including heat, oxidative or hypoxic stress, and deprivation of nutrients or essential ions.

H02752.title: heat
H02752.definition: Energy transferred from a hotter to a cooler body due to a temperature gradient.

H02756.title: heavy atom effect
H02756.definition: The enhancement of the rate of a spin-forbidden process by the presence of an atom of high atomic number, which is either part of, or external to, the excited molecular entity. Mechanistically, it responds to a spin–orbit coupling enhancement produced by a heavy atom.

H02757.title: heavy atom isotope effect
H02757.definition: An isotope effect due to isotopes other than those of hydrogen.

13198.title: heavy chain
13198.definition: Larger of the two types of polypeptide chain found in immunoglobulin (Ig) molecules.

14739.title: heavy metal
14739.definition: Term used commonly but erroneously when referring to metal toxicity.

H02758.title: heavy water
H02758.definition: Water containing a significant fraction (up to 100 per cent) of deuterium in the form of $\ce{D2O}$ or $\ce{HDO}$.

H02761.title: height equivalent to a theoretical plate
H02761.definition: The column length divided by the theoretical plate number.

H02760.title: height equivalent to an effective theoretical plate
H02760.definition: The column length divided by the effective theoretical plate number.

15311.title: helical polymer
15311.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules that adopt partly or completely a helical conformation.

H02762.title: helicenes
H02762.definition: ortho-Fused polycyclic aromatic or heteroaromatic compounds in which all rings (minimum five) are angularly arranged so as to give helically shaped molecules, which are thus chiral, e.g. hexahelicene.

H02763.title: helicity
H02763.definition: The chirality of a helical, propeller or screw-shaped molecular entity. A right-handed helix is described as P (or plus), a left-handed one as M (or minus).    The application of this system to the description of conformations considers the torsion angle between two specified (fiducial) groups that are attached to the atoms linked by that bond. The sign of the smaller torsion angle between the fiducial groups defines the chirality sense of the helix. Rules for the selection of fiducial groups according to priority are given by R.S. Cahn, C.K. Ingold and V. Prelog, Angew. Chem. 78, 413-447 (1966), Angew. Chem. Internat. Ed. Eng. 5, 385-415, 511 (1966).

HT07392.title: heliochromism
HT07392.definition: Applied to photochromic compounds possessing a high efficiency for colouring with near-ultraviolet radiation and a low efficiency for bleaching with visible radiation, but a moderate efficiency for thermal fading at ambient temperature. These compounds are activated by unfiltered sunlight and deactivated under diffuse daylight conditions, therefore being suitable for sun-lens applications.

H02766.title: helium dead-space
H02766.definition: The position of the Gibbs surface is often defined experimentally as that surface which encloses the volume of space from which the solid excludes helium gas (the so-called helium dead-space), and is associated with the assumptions that the volume of the solid is unaffected by the adsorption of component i, and that helium is not adsorbed by the solid. This requires that the measurement of the helium dead-space be made at a sufficiently high temperature.

H02767.title: helium ionization detector
H02767.definition: A weak beta source and a high potential raise the helium atom of the carrier gas to a metastable state. All other substances having an ionization potential lower than \(18\ \rm{eV}\) are ionized, and the current that results is used to measure the components. The detector is usually employed to measure inorganic compounds at concentrations between \(0.1\) and \(10\ \rm{ppmv}\). It has a linear range of about \(10^{2}\) but is somewhat unstable and requires great care to ensure the helium purity and to eliminate all leaks in the system.

H02765.title: helium–cadmium laser
H02765.definition: A continuous wave laser emitting mainly at \(325.0\) and \(441.6\ \rm{nm}\) from singly ionized cadmium.

H02768.title: helium–neon laser
H02768.definition: A continuous wave laser emitting mainly at \(632.8\ \rm{nm}\), \(1152.3\ \rm{nm}\), and \(3391.3\ \rm{nm}\) from excited neutral $\ce{Ne}$ atoms.

H02769.title: helix
H02769.definition: The molecular conformation of a spiral nature, generated by regularly repeating rotations around the backbone bonds of a macromolecule.

H02770.title: helix residue
H02770.definition: The smallest set of one or more successive configurational base units that generates the whole chain through helical symmetry.

H02771.title: helix sense
H02771.definition: The right-handed sense of a helix traces out a clockwise rotation moving away from the observer; the left-handed sense of a helix traces out a counterclockwise rotation moving away from the observer, e.g. the ...\(\mathrm{TG}^{+}\) \(\mathrm{TG}^{+}\) \(\mathrm{TG}^{+}\) … helix of isotactic poly(propylene) is left-handed.

H02772.title: Helmholtz energy
H02772.definition: Internal energy minus the product of thermodynamic temperature and entropy. It was formerly called free energy.

13199.title: helper T lymphocyte
13199.definition: Member of a subclass of T lymphocytes that provides help (in the form of cytokines and/or cognate interactions) necessary for the expression of effector function by other cells in the immune system.

09670.title: hemagglutination
09670.definition: Agglutination reactions in which the particles used are erythrocytes.

10787.title: hemal
10787.definition:
Pertaining to blood or blood vessels.
Situated, in common with the heart and major blood vessels, on the ventral side of the body with respect to the vertebral column or its embryonic precursors.

10788.title: hemangioma
10788.definition: Benign tumor formed by a vascular malformation present at birth or developing during life, in which proliferation of blood vessels leads to a vascular tangle.

11803.title: hematoma
11803.definition: Region of bleeding into a tissue or organ.

10789.title: hematopoiesis
10789.definition: Development of each of the types of blood cell from common precursor cells, located mainly in the bone marrow.

13201.title: hematopoietic stem cell
13201.definition: Self-renewing stem cell that is capable of giving rise to all of the formed elements of the blood (i.e., leukocytes, erythrocytes, and platelets).
