15763.title: hematotoxicity
15763.definition: Adverse changes in blood caused by exposure to chemicals.

15764.title: hematuria
15764.definition: Presence of blood in the urine.

H02773.title: hemes
H02773.definition: Complexes consisting of an iron ion coordinated to a porphyrin acting as a tetradentate ligand, and to one or two axial ligands.

14318.title: hemi-micelle
14318.definition: Type of micelle that exists in relatively small numbers below the critical micelle concentration.

H02775.title: hemiaminals
H02775.definition: $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}Amino}$ alcohols, improperly called carbinolamines (the adducts of ammonia, or of primary or secondary amines to the carbonyl group of aldehydes and ketones) $\ce{R2C(OH)NR2}$. Compounds of structure $\ce{R2C(OR')NR2}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$) are hemiaminal ethers, or $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}amino}$ ethers.

13826.title: hemicarceplex
13826.definition: Complex formed by a hemicarcerand and an entrapped guest.

13827.title: hemicarcerand
13827.definition: Host molecule that allows guest molecules to enter and exit its cavities in accordance with a change in the equilibrium conditions.

H02776.title: hemiketals
H02776.definition: Hemiacetals having the structure $\ce{R2C(OH)OR}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$), derived from ketones by formal addition of an alcohol to the carbonyl group. This term, once abandoned, has been reinstated as a subclass of hemiacetals.

10790.title: hemimelia
10790.definition: Congenital partial absence of all or part of the distal half of a limb.

11804.title: hemiplegia
11804.definition: Paralysis of one side of the body, including the arm, trunk and leg.

10791.title: hemivertebra
10791.definition: Congenital defect of the vertebral column in which one side of a vertebra fails to develop completely due to failure of the chondrification center to form on that side.

15766.title: hemochromatosis
15766.definition: Hereditary disorder affecting iron metabolism in which excessive amounts of iron accumulate in the body tissues.

H02779.title: hemochromes
H02779.definition: Iron–porphyrin complexes, having one or two basic ligands (e.g. piperidine, amines).

HT06886.title: hemodialysis
HT06886.definition: Dialysis process in which undesired metabolites and toxic by-products, such as urea and creatine, are removed from blood.

H02780.title: hemoglobins
H02780.definition: Heme derivatives having a protein chain as axial ligand.

15767.title: hemoglobinuria
15767.definition: Presence of free hemoglobin in the urine.

15768.title: hemolysin
15768.definition: Substance that damages the membrane of erythrocytes causing the release of hemoglobin.

15769.title: hemolysis
15769.definition: Release of hemoglobin from erythrocytes, and its appearance in the plasma.

13202.title: hemolytic anemia
13202.definition: Anemia resulting from the lysis of erythrocytes.

10792.title: hemolytic disease of the newborn
10792.definition: Severe form of anemia in a fetus or newborn infant caused by incompatibility with the mother’s blood type, typically when the mother is rhesus factor negative (Rh -ve) and produces antibodies which attack (Rh +ve) fetal blood through the placenta.

15770.title: hemoperfusion
15770.definition: Passing blood through a column of charcoal or adsorbent resin for the removal of drugs or toxins.

11806.title: hemorrhage
11806.definition: Copious escape of blood from a disrupted blood vessel.

15771.title: hemosiderin
15771.definition: Insoluble iron(III) hydroxide-based pigment deposited in cells in conditions of iron overload.

11807.title: hen test
11807.definition: Procedure using birds to study acute and delayed neurotoxicity, notably of organophosphates.

H02781.title: Henderson–Hasselbalch equation
H02781.definition: An equation of the form: \[\rm{pH} = \rm{p}K_{\rm{a}}- \log _{10}(\frac{\left[\rm{HA}\right]}{\left[\rm{A}^{-}\right]})\] for the calculation of the \(\rm{pH}\) of solutions where the ratio \(\frac{\left[\rm{HA}\right]}{\left[\rm{A}^{-}\right]}\) is known.

H02782.title: henry
H02782.definition: SI derived unit of inductance, \(\pu{H} = \pu{V A-1 s} = \pu{m2 kg s-2 A-2}\).

H02783.title: Henry's law
H02783.definition: The partial pressure (fugacity) of a solute (B) in a solution is directly proportional to the rational chemical activity (\(a_{x}\)) of the solute; this relationship is called Henry's law: \[p_{\rm{B}}=\frac{a_{x,\rm{B}}}{\alpha _{x,\rm{B}}^{\infty }}\] where \(\alpha _{x,\rm{B}}^{\infty }\) is the rational solubility coefficient for infinite dilution, i.e. for pure solvent. For the solvent (A) the relationship is called Raoult's law, and the proportionality factor is the fugacity of the pure solvent, \(\overset{˜}{p}_{\rm{A}}^{\ast }\): \[p_{\rm{A}}=\overset{˜}{p}_{\rm{A}}^{\ast }\ a_{\rm{A}}\]

09020.title: Henry’s law constant
09020.definition: Proportionality factor describing the equilibrium distribution of a chemical species between the gas phase and a liquid solution at infinite dilution of the solute according to Henry’s law. It is an umbrella term for the reciprocal quantities Henry’s law solubility constant and Henry’s law volatility constant. Because of its ambiguity, it is strongly recommended to specify whether a solubility or volatility constant is intended.

09021.title: Henry’s law solubility constant
09021.definition: Umbrella term for all variants of Henry’s law constants that are defined in such a way that the numerical value increases with increasing solubility of the solute. Variants include \(H_{\rm{s}}^{cp}\), \(H_{\rm{s}}^{xp}\), \(H_{\rm{s}}^{bp}\), and \(H_{\rm{s}}^{cc}\), as discussed elsewhere in this section.

09026.title: Henry’s law solubility constant (via b and p)
09026.definition: Molality \(b\) of a species divided by the partial pressure \(p\) of that species in the gas phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{s}}^{bp}: = \underset{b \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{b}{p}\]

09024.title: Henry’s law solubility constant (via c and p)
09024.definition: Amount concentration \(c_{\rm{l}}\) of a species in the liquid phase divided by the partial pressure \(p\) of that species in the gas phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{s}}^{cp}: = \underset{c_{\rm{l}} \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{c_{\rm{l}}}{p}\]

09025.title: Henry’s law solubility constant (via x and p)
09025.definition: Amount fraction \(x\) of a species in the liquid phase divided by the partial pressure \(p\) of that species in the gas phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{s}}^{xp}: = \underset{x \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{x}{p}\]

09022.title: Henry’s law volatility constant
09022.definition: Umbrella term for all variants of Henry’s law constants that are defined in such a way that the numerical value increases with increasing volatility of the solute. Variants include \(H_{\rm{v}}^{pc}\), \(H_{\rm{v}}^{px}\), \(H_{\rm{v}}^{pw}\), and \(H_{\rm{v}}^{cc}\), as discussed elsewhere in this section.

09023.title: Henry’s law volatility constant (via p and c)
09023.definition: Partial pressure \(p\) of a species in the gas phase divided by the amount concentration \(c_{\rm{l}}\) of that species in the liquid phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{v}}^{pc}: = \underset{c_{\rm{l}} \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{p}{c_{\rm{l}}}\]

09028.title: Henry’s law volatility constant (via p and w)
09028.definition: Partial pressure \(p\) of a species in the gas phase divided by the mass fraction \(w\) of that species in the liquid phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{v}}^{pw}: = \underset{w \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{p}{w}\]

09027.title: Henry’s law volatility constant (via p and x)
09027.definition: Partial pressure \(p\) of a species in the gas phase divided by the amount fraction \(x\) of that species in the liquid phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{v}}^{px}: = \underset{x \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{p}{x}\]

13203.title: heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
13203.definition: Most frequent antibody-mediated drug-induced thrombocytopenia, which occurs in \(\pu{1-}\pu{2\%}\) of patients treated with heparin intravenously for longer than four days.

10726.title: hepatic flexure
10726.definition: Bend between the ascending colon and the transverse colon.

10793.title: hepatosplenomegaly
10793.definition: Enlargement of the liver and spleen.

13204.title: hereditary angioneurotic edema
13204.definition: Clinical name for a genetic deficiency of the C1 inhibitor of the complement system.

10794.title: hermaphrodite
10794.definition: Having the reproductive organs and many of the secondary sex characteristics of both sexes.

10796.title: hernia
10796.definition: Protrusion of an organ or structure through an abnormal opening in connective tissue or in the muscle wall of the cavity in which it is normally enclosed.

10798.title: herpes
10798.definition: Family of viruses including herpes simplex types 1 and 2, and herpes zoster (also called varicella zoster).

10799.title: Hershberger bioassay
10799.definition: Short-term in vivo procedure in which the androgenic or antiandrogenic effects of a test substance are studied in castrated, peripubertal male rodents, as indicated by changes in the weights of androgen-dependent tissues.

H02785.title: hertz
H02785.definition: SI derived unit of frequency equal to one cycle per second, \(\rm{Hz} = \rm{s}^{-1}\).

H02786.title: Herz compounds
H02786.definition: 1,2$\uplambda\!$4,3-Benzodithiazolium chlorides (formed in the reaction of aniline and derivatives thereof with disulfur dichloride).

H02790.title: heteroalkenes
H02790.definition: Analogues of alkenes in which a doubly bonded carbon atom is replaced by a heteroatom, e.g. $\ce{H2Si=CH2}$ methylidenesilane (silene less preferred), $\ce{MeN=CH2}$ N-methylmethanimine.

13205.title: heteroantigen
13205.definition: Identical or similar cross-reacting antigen shared by several species (e.g., Forssman antigen).Antibodies produced against one of these antigens will also react with the other antigens of the set even though these are derived from a different species; such antibodies are also called heterophile antibodies.

H02791.title: heteroarenes
H02791.definition: Heterocyclic compounds formally derived from arenes by replacement of one or more methine ($\ce{–C=}$) and/or vinylene ($\ce{–CH=CH\bond{–}}$) groups by trivalent or divalent heteroatoms, respectively, in such a way as to maintain the continuous $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$ system characteristic of aromatic systems and a number of out-of-plane $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electrons}$ corresponding to the Hückel rule (\(4\ n+2\)); an alternative term is hetarenes.

H02792.title: heteroaryl groups
H02792.definition: The class of heterocyclyl groups derived from heteroarenes by removal of a hydrogen atom from any ring atom; an alternative term is hetaryl. E.g.

H02793.title: heteroarynes
H02793.definition: Compounds derived from heteroarenes by replacement of a formal carbon-carbon double bond by a formal triple bond (with loss of two hydrogen atoms). Also known as hetarynes and as 1,2-didehydroheteroarenes. E.g.

H02794.title: heterobimetallic complex
H02794.definition: A metal complex having two different metal atoms.

H02795.title: heterochain polymer
H02795.definition: A class of polymer in which the main chain is constructed from atoms of two or more elements. Heterochain polymers are named by placing the names or symbols of all the elements in the main chain, immediately before the expresssion '-chain polymer', e.g. (oxygen, carbon)-chain polymer or (O, C)-chain polymer; (oxygen, nitrogen, carbon)-chain polymer or (O, N, C)-chain polymer.

14382.title: heterocoagulation
14382.definition: Coagulation of particles of different kinds or sizes, or both.

H02796.title: heteroconjugation
H02796.definition:
[obsolete] Association between a base and the conjugate acid of a different base through a hydrogen bond ($\ce{B'\bond{...}HB^{+}}$ or $\ce{A'H\bond{...}A^{-}}$). The term has its origin in the conjugate acid–base pair and is in no way related to conjugated systems of orbitals. Heteroassociation is a more appropriate term.
[obsolete] Some authors refer to conjugated systems containing a heteroatom, e.g. pyridine, as 'heteroconjugated systems'. This usage is discouraged since it inappropriately suggests an analogy to homoconjugation, and conflicts with the currently accepted definition of that term.

H02797.title: heterocumulenes
H02797.definition: Cumulenes in which one or more carbon atoms of the cumulative bond system have been replaced by heteroatoms. E.g. $\ce{O=C=C=C=O}$, but not $\ce{CH2=C=O}$, ketene, nor $\ce{O=C=O}$, carbon dioxide, which are heteroallenes.

H02798.title: heterocyclic compounds
H02798.definition: Cyclic compounds having as ring members atoms of at least two different elements, e.g. quinoline, 1,2-thiazole, bicyclo[3.3.1]tetrasiloxane.

H02799.title: heterocyclyl groups
H02799.definition: Univalent groups formed by removing a hydrogen atom from any ring atom of a heterocyclic compound. E.g.

H02800.title: heterodetic cyclic peptide
H02800.definition: A peptide consisting only of amino-acid residues, but in which the linkages forming the ring are not solely eupeptide bonds; one or more is an isopeptide, disulfide, ester, or other bond.

H02801.title: heterodisperse
H02801.definition: Describes a colloidal system in which all the particles are of different sizes.

14139.title: heterogeneous assay
14139.definition: Assay in which the response is detected only after the physical separation by methods such as filtration or centrifugation of one or more assay components.

14140.title: heterogeneous binding assay
14140.definition: Assay in which one binding component is immobilized to a surface (e.g., cellular membrane, glass, gold, bead, or biopolymer layer) while its binding partner is freely diffusible.

09004.title: heterogeneous catalysis coordination polymerization
09004.definition: Coordination polymerization making use of a heterogeneous catalyst.

09109.title: heterogeneous crystalline membrane electrodes
09109.definition: ISE prepared of an active substance, or mixture of active substances, mixed with an inert matrix (such as silicone rubber or \(\ce{PVC}\)), or placed on hydrophobized graphite or conducting epoxy resin, to form a heterogeneous sensing membrane.

09116.title: heterogeneous crystalline membrane ion-selective electrode
09116.definition: Ion-selective electrode in which the ion-selective membrane is a crystalline material mixed with an inert matrix (such as silicone rubber or polyvinyl chloride), or placed on hydrophobized graphite or conducting epoxy resin, to form a heterogeneous sensing membrane.

09599.title: heterogeneous degradation
09599.definition: Degradation or biodegradation occurring at different rates depending on the location within a matrix.

H02805.title: heterogeneous diffusion rate constant
H02805.definition: Defined by the equation: \[k_{\rm{d}}=\frac{I_{\rm{l}}}{n\ F\ c\ A}\] where the limiting current \(I_{\rm{l}}\) is assumed to be due to the diffusion species of concentration \(c\) and of diffusion coefficient \(D\). \(n\) is the charge number of the cell reaction written so that the stoichiometric coefficient of this species is unity. \(A\) is usually taken as the geometric area of the electrode, and \(F\) is the Faraday constant.

14018.title: heterogeneous photocatalysis
14018.definition: Photocatalysis taking place at the interfacial boundary between two phases (solid/liquid, solid/gas, liquid/gas).

14019.title: heterogeneous radiation catalysis
14019.definition: Radiation catalysis taking place in heterogeneous systems.

08825.title: heterojunction
08825.definition: Interface between dissimilar crystalline or amorphous solid phases that have unequal bandgap levels.

H02808.title: heteroleptic
H02808.definition: Transition metal or Main Group compounds having more than one type of ligand.

13206.title: heterologous antibody
13206.definition: Antibody derived from another individual of the same species or another species.

13207.title: heterologous antigen
13207.definition: Antigen that reacts with an antibody other than the one whose formation it induced.

H02809.title: heterolysis
H02809.definition: The cleavage of a covalent bond so that both bonding electrons remain with one of the two fragments between which the bond is broken, e.g.  Heterolytic bond fission is a feature of many bimolecular reactions in solution (e.g.electrophilic substitution, nucleophilic substitution).

H02810.title: heterolytic bond-dissociation energy
H02810.definition: The energy required to break a given bond of some specific compound by heterolysis. For the dissociation of a neutral molecule $\ce{AB}$ in the gas phase into $\ce{A^{+}}$ and $\ce{B^{−}}$ the heterolytic bond-dissociation energy $D(\ce{A^{+}B^{−}})$ is the sum of the bond dissociation energy, $D(\ce{A–B})$, and the adiabatic ionization energy of the radical $\ce{A^{.}}$; minus the electron affinity of the radical $\ce{B^{.}}$.

H02811.title: heterolytic dissociative adsorption
H02811.definition: Relates in the usual sense to the formal nature of the cleavage of a single bond. If in the bond of the adsorptive $\ce{A:B}$, $\ce{A}$ or $\ce{B}$ retains the electron pair, the adsorption is heterolytic dissociative adsorption.

08351.title: heteronuclear decoupling
08351.definition: Spin decoupling in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy between two different nuclei (e.g., \(\ce{^{13}C}\) and \(\ce{^{1}H}\)) by appropriate excitation of the decoupled nucleus.

08352.title: heteronuclear multiple bond correlation NMR
08352.definition: Two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that gives correlations between carbons and protons that are separated by two, three, and, sometimes in conjugated systems, four bonds.

08353.title: heteronuclear multiple-bond correlation over two bonds
08353.definition: Variant of the heteronuclear single quantum correlation (HSQC) and heteronuclear multiple bond correlation (HMBC) experiment in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that almost exclusively correlates \(\ce{^{1}H}\) nuclei with heteronuclei separated by two covalent bonds.

08354.title: heteronuclear multiple-quantum correlation NMR
08354.definition: Simplest implementation of an inverse detected \(\ce{^{1}H}\) heteronuclear correlation nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment.

08355.title: heteronuclear multiple-quantum correlation with additional TOCSY transfer
08355.definition: Variant of heteronuclear multiple bond correlation (HMBC) spectroscopy that shows correlations from a heteronucleus (e.g., \(\ce{^{13}C}\)) to not only its directly bound \(\ce{^{1}H}\) but also to all other \(\ce{^{1}H}\) nuclei within the spin system.

08356.title: heteronuclear Overhauser effect spectroscopy
08356.definition: Heteronuclear variant of nuclear Overhauser effect spectroscopy (NOSEY) showing through space interaction between \(\ce{^{1}H}\) and a heteronucleus, typically \(\ce{^{13}C}\).

08357.title: heteronuclear shift correlation NMR
08357.definition: Directly-observed one-bond heteronuclear correlation experiment in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

08358.title: heteronuclear single quantum correlation
08358.definition: \(\ce{^{1}H}\) (inverse) detected two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy heteronuclear experiment that correlates \(\ce{^{1}H}\) nuclei with their directly coupled nucleus through a single bond.

08359.title: heteronuclear single quantum correlation with additional TOCSY transfer
08359.definition: Variant of the heteronuclear single quantum correlation (HSQC) experiment that shows correlations from a heteronucleus (e.g., \(\ce{^{13}C}\)) to not only its directly bound \(\ce{^{1}H}\) but also to all other \(\ce{^{1}H}\) nuclei within the spin system.

08360.title: heteronuclear single quantum multiple-bond correlation
08360.definition: Variant of the heteronuclear single quantum correlation (HSQC) experiment that provides pure absorption, antiphase line shapes for precise, direct measurement of \(^{n}J(\ce{C,H})\) spin-spin coupling constants.

13208.title: heterophagy
13208.definition: Digestion of exogenous material taken up by a cell by phagocytosis or pinocytosis, following fusion of the phagocytic or pinocytic vacuole with a lysosome.

13209.title: heterophile antibody
13209.definition: Antibody raised against an antigen from one species, which also reacts against antigens from other species.

13210.title: heterophile antigen
13210.definition: Antigen that stimulates production in a vertebrate of antibodies capable of reacting with tissue components having related antigens in a wide range of other species.

H02812.title: heteropolysaccharide
H02812.definition: The class name for polysaccharides composed of two or more different kinds of monomeric units (i.e. monosaccharides).

09587.title: heterotactic macromolecule
09587.definition: Regular macromolecule having a configurational repeating unit comprising four configurational base units, the first two stereogenic units of which are identical and enantiomorphic to the last two.

14740.title: heterotherm
14740.definition: Animal that partially regulates body temperature, sometimes maintaining its body temperature at a certain level, e.g., when active, but at other times allowing it to fluctuate with the environment.

14741.title: heterotroph
14741.definition: Organism obtaining organic food by eating other organisms or their excreta.

H02816.title: heterotrophic
H02816.definition: Descriptive of organisms which are not able to synthesize cell components from carbon dioxide as sole carbon source. Heterotrophic organisms use preformed oxidizable organic substrates such as glucose as carbon and energy sources.

14742.title: heterotrophic succession
14742.definition: Temporal sequential appearance of different heterotrophic species at a location, most often decomposer organisms.

15775.title: heterozygote
15775.definition: Organism that has different allelic forms of a specified gene on each of a pair of homologous chromosomes or describing the genome of that organism.

14743.title: heterozygote advantage
14743.definition: Greater Darwinian fitness (reproductive output) from heterozygous than from homozygous individuals of a species. This tends to preserve variation in the population gene pool.

13211.title: heterozygous
13211.definition: Possessing different alleles at a given locus on the two homologous chromosomes.

H02818.title: hexagonal graphite
H02818.definition: The thermodynamically stable form of graphite with an ABAB stacking sequence of the graphene layers. The exact crystallographic description of this allotropic form is given by the space group \(d_{6h}^{4} - P6_{3}/\rm{mmc}\) (unit cell constants: \(a=245.6\ \mathrm{pm}\), \(c=670.8\ \mathrm{pm}\)). Hexagonal graphite is thermodynamically stable below approximately \(2600\ \rm{K}\) and \(6\ \rm{GPa}\).

13828.title: hexagonal mesophase
13828.definition: Columnar mesophase characterized by a hexagonal packing of the molecular column.

H02819.title: hexahedro-
H02819.definition: An affix used in names to denote eight atoms bound into a hexahedron (e.g. cube).

H02820.title: hexaprismo-
H02820.definition: An affix used in names to denote twelve atoms bound into a hexagonal prism.

09137.title: Heyrovský–Ilkovič equation
09137.definition: The relationship that describes the electrode potential as a function of the current of a reversible redox system (reversible electrode reaction) in the steady state in voltammetry \[E = E^{\circ\prime} - \frac{RT}{zF} \ln \left(\frac{D_{\rm{red}}}{D_{\rm{ox}}}\right)^{s} \pm \frac{RT}{zF} \ln\!\left(\frac{I_{\rm{d,lim}} - I}{I}\right)\] where \(E^{\circ\prime}\) is the formal electrode potential, \(z\) the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, \(D_{\rm{red}}\) and \(D_{\rm{ox}}\) the diffusion coefficients of the reduced and oxidized forms of the electroactive substance, respectively, \(I_{\rm{d,lim}}\) is the limiting diffusion current, and \(I\) is the current at the potential being applied. The value of the exponent \(s\) is ½ for a stationary or dropping mercury electrode, ⅔ for a hydrodynamic electrode (see hydrodynamic voltammetry), or 1 for a microelectrode. In the equation, the last term is added for reduction and subtracted for oxidation.

10797.title: hiatal hernia
10797.definition: Hernia of a part of the stomach through a rupture of the diaphragm at the esophageal opening.

10128.title: hidden layer
10128.definition: Group of nodes in an artificial neural network between input layer and output layer.

10129.title: hierarchical clustering
10129.definition: Pattern recognition in which objects are linked together by use of an appropriate measure of distance between pairs of objects, and a linkage criterion, which specifies the dissimilarity of sets as a function of the pairwise distances between objects.

13212.title: high endothelial venule
13212.definition: Specialized venule in lymphoid tissues that has walls permeable to migrating lymphocytes, allowing them to move from blood into the lymphoid tissues.

14143.title: high throughput
14143.definition: Relative term, applied to the generation of a large number of results in a short timeframe (e.g., \(\pu{E5}\) in a week or a month).

14141.title: high-content screening assay
14141.definition: A cell-based assay that produces multiple biological readouts.

13214.title: high-mobility group box protein
13214.definition: Any of a group of universal sensors of nucleic acids, required for the induction of transmembrane and cytoplasmic receptor-mediated innate immune responses.

08255.title: high-pass filter
08255.definition:
Optical filter that excludes radiation of wavenumber lower (wavelength higher) than a certain value and passes radiation of wavenumber above (wavelength lower) than this value.
Electrical filter that blocks signal with a modulation frequency lower than a certain cut-on value and passes signals of frequency above this value.

14142.title: high-performance liquid chromatography assay
14142.definition: Assay in which response is determined after the physical separation of assay components using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) with concurrent detection, usually by monitoring absorbance at an appropriate wavelength.

H02824.title: high-pressure graphitization
H02824.definition: A term which refers to the solid-state transformation of non-graphitic carbon into graphite by heat treatment under elevated pressure (e.g. \(100\) to \(1000\ \rm{MPa}\)) so that a definitely higher degree of graphitization is achieved at lower temperature and/or for a shorter heat treatment time than in heat treatment of the same non-graphitic material at atmospheric pressure.

H02825.title: high-pressure mercury lamp
H02825.definition: Radiation source containing mercury at a pressure of ca. \(8\ \rm{MPa}\) (ca. \(80\ \rm{bar}\)) or higher which emits lines over a background continuum between about \(200\) and \(1400\ \rm{nm}\).

09944.title: high-speed counter-current chromatography
09944.definition: Counter-current chromatography system using a multilayer coil separation column, which undergoes a type-J synchronous planetary motion (see figure).Type-J planetary motion of a multilayer coil separation column. The column holder rotates about its own axis and revolves around the centrifuge axis at the same angular velocity (ω) in the same direction. This planetary motion prevents twisting of the bundle of flow tubes, allowing continuous elution through a rotating column without risk of leakage and contamination.

08177.title: high-throughput screening
08177.definition: Automated method to quickly assay large libraries of chemical species for the affinity of small organic molecules toward a target of interest.

09748.title: higher-energy collision dissociation
09748.definition: Ion fragmentation technique in mass spectrometry-driven proteomics used mostly in Kingdon trap (Orbitrap™) instruments. It does not have low mass cut-off of collision-induced dissociation (CID) and therefore is used for the tandem mass tag of stable isotope labels.

15332.title: higher-order system
15332.definition: System containing more than three components.

H02822.title: higher-order transition
H02822.definition: A general term used to describe a transition in which the first and second derivatives of the molar Gibbs energy or molar Helmholtz energy (or chemical potential) with respect to temperature and pressure are continuous, but derivatives of some higher order are discontinuous at the transition point. Synonymous with smooth transition.

13213.title: highly active antiretroviral therapy
13213.definition: Approach to the treatment of acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) patients involving a combination of nucleoside analogs, which prevent reverse transcription, with drugs that inhibit responses to the virus.

H02823.title: highly oriented pyrolytic graphite
H02823.definition: Highly oriented pyrolytic graphite (HOPG) is a pyrolytic graphite with an angular spread of the c-axes of the crystallites of less than 1 degree.

09089.title: highly oriented pyrolytic graphite electrode
09089.definition: Graphite electrode of material produced by high temperature deposition of carbon on a ceramic surface and subject to graphitization at \(\pu{3000^{\circ}C}\)

08256.title: Hilbert transforms

H02827.title: Hildebrand parameter
H02827.definition: A parameter measuring the cohesion of a solvent (energy required to create a cavity in the solvent).

15776.title: Hill plot
15776.definition: Graphical method for analyzing binding of a molecule \(\ce{A}\) to a macromolecule \(\ce{P}\) with \(n\) binding sites. A Hill plot of \(\log[\theta/(1 - \theta)]\) vs. \(\log[\ce{A}]\) has a slope of 1 if binding is noncooperative and \(\gt 1\) for cooperative binding, where \(\theta = [\ce{A}]_{\rm{bound}}/n[\ce{P}]_{\rm{total}}\) is the fraction of sites occupied.

13215.title: hinge region
13215.definition: Amino acids between the Fab and Fc regions of immunoglobulin (Ig) that permit flexibility of the molecule.

HT07622.title: hipping
HT07622.definition: Isostatic pressing process carried out at elevated temperatures.

11808.title: hippocampal slice culture
11808.definition: Maintenance in vitro of fresh prepared slices of the hippocampus.

10800.title: hippocampus
10800.definition: Structural component of the limbic system of the vertebrate brain involved in short-term and long-term memory and spatial navigation.

10801.title: Hirschsprung syndrome
10801.definition: Absence of nerve ganglia throughout all or part of the gastrointestinal tract, causing dysregulation of intestinal motility.

10802.title: hirsutism
10802.definition: Presence of excessive bodily and facial hair.

11809.title: histamine
11809.definition: Bioactive metabolite produced in living organisms by deamination of the amino acid histidine.

11810.title: histaminergic
11810.definition: Pertaining to the action of histamine or to neural pathways in which it functions as a neurotransmitter.

13216.title: histaminosis
13216.definition: Histamine intolerance, which may contribute to food intolerance as part of a pseudoallergic reaction.

13217.title: histocompatibility
13217.definition: Relationship between a tissue or organ donor and a recipient who have sufficient similarity in major histocompatibility complex (MHC) antigens to avoid rejection of a graft.

15777.title: histogenic origin
15777.definition: Germ cell layer of the embryo from which a given adult tissue develops.

13218.title: histoincompatibility
13218.definition: Relationship between a tissue or organ donor and a recipient who have sufficient differences in major histocompatibility complex (MHC) antigens to cause rejection of a graft.

15778.title: histology
15778.definition: Study (usually microscopic) of the anatomy of tissues and their cellular and subcellular structure.

H02829.title: histones
H02829.definition: A class of basic proteins associated with DNA in the chromosomes of eukaryotic cells forming the nucleosome as the basic subunit of chromatin. They contain an unusually large proportion of the basic amino acids arginine and lysine.

15779.title: histopathology
15779.definition: Microscopic pathological study of the anatomy and cell structure of tissues in disease to reveal abnormal or adverse structural changes.

12664.title: hit
12664.definition: Molecule that produces reproducible activity above a defined threshold in a biological assay and whose structural identity has been established.

12665.title: hit expansion
12665.definition: Generation of additional compound sets that contain chemical motifs and scaffolds that have activity in the primary screen.

14144.title: hit rate
14144.definition: Proportion of hits from a screen that displays confirmed activity beyond a minimum defined level, the hit threshold. It is expressed as a percentage of the number of samples screened.

14145.title: hit threshold
14145.definition: Minimum activity that defines actives in a primary screen.

15780.title: hit-and-run effect
15780.definition: Toxicity that follows a single exposure to a substance.

12666.title: hit-to-lead chemistry
12666.definition: Process by which a proven molecule or series derived from high-throughput screening or primary screens is chemically optimised to a viable lead or series.

13219.title: hives
13219.definition: Vascular reaction pattern of the skin marked by the transient appearance of smooth, slightly elevated patches (wheals) that are either more red or more pale than the surrounding skin and are accompanied by severe itching.

08361.title: HN(CA)CO
08361.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

08362.title: HN(CO)CA
08362.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

08363.title: HNCA
08363.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

08364.title: HNCO
08364.definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

13220.title: Hodgkin disease
13220.definition: Immune system tumor characterized by large cells called Reed–Sternberg cells that derive from mutated B-lineage cells.

12775.title: Hoffman–Weeks plot
12775.definition: Plot of melting temperature, \(T_{\rm{m}}\), vs. crystallisation temperature, \(T_{\rm{cr}}\).

H02830.title: Hofmann rule
H02830.definition: 'The principal olefin formed in the decomposition of quaternary ammonium hydroxides that contain different primary alkyl groups is always ethylene, if an ethyl group is present.' Originally given in this limited form by A. W. Hofmann, the rule has since been extended and modified as follows: 'When two or more alkenes can be produced in a $\upbeta\!$-elimination reaction, the alkene having the smallest number of alkyl groups attached to the double bond carbon atoms will be the predominant product.' This orientation described by the Hofmann rule is observed in elimination reactions of quaternary ammonium salts and tertiary sulfonium salts, and in certain other cases.

H02831.title: hold-back carrier
H02831.definition: A carrier used to prevent a particular species from following other species in a chemical or physical operation.

10038.title: hold-up time
10038.definition: Time required to elute a component which is not retained by the stationary phase.

H02833.title: hold-up volume
H02833.definition: The volume of the mobile phase (or the corresponding time) required to elute a component the concentration of which in the stationary phase is negligible compared to that in the mobile phase. In other words, this component is not retained at all by the stationary phase. Thus, the hold-up volume (time) is equal to the retention volume (time) of an unretained compound. The hold-up volume (time) includes any volumes contributed by the sample injector, the detector, and connectors. \[t_{\rm{M}}=\frac{V_{\rm{M}}}{F_{\rm{c}}}\] In gas chromatography this term is also called the gas hold-up volume (time). The corrected gas hold-up volume (\(V_{\rm{M}}^{\rm{o}}\)) is the gas hold-up volume multiplied by the compression (compressibility) correction factor (\(j\)): \[V_{\rm{M}}^{\rm{o}}=V_{\rm{M}}\ j\] Assuming that the influence of extra column volume on \(V_{\rm{M}}\) is negligible, \[V_{\rm{M}}^{\rm{o}}=V_{\rm{G}}\]

H02832.title: hold-up volume
H02832.definition: The volume of eluent required to elute a component, the concentration of which in the stationary phase is negligible compared to that in the mobile phase.

08826.title: hole
08826.definition: Quasiparticle, a conceptual charge carrier opposite to electron, defined as the absence of electron at a position where it should be present if a lattice is in its ground state (valence band normally filled).

H02834.title: hole burning
H02834.definition: The photo bleaching of a feature, normally a narrow range, within an inhomogeneous broader absorption or emission band. The holes are produced by the disappearance of resonantly excited molecules as a result of photophysical or photochemical processes. The resulting spectroscopic technique is site-selection spectroscopy.

H02835.title: hole transfer
H02835.definition: Charge migration process in which the majority carriers are positively charged.

08827.title: hole-transporting material
08827.definition: Material, typically a semiconductor, in which holes are predominant mobile charge carriers.

10279.title: hollow fibre
10279.definition: Narrow cylindrical tube prepared from a porous polymer.

08485.title: hollow-cathode discharge source
08485.definition: Glow discharge source with a graphite cathode, into which the sample is inserted in the form of drillings, a pressed pellet or a dry solution residue.

08486.title: hollow-cathode lamp
08486.definition: Glow discharge source of spectral lines of an atom in which the cathode is made of the desired element.

10280.title: hollow-fibre liquid-phase microextraction
10280.definition: Liquid-phase microextraction of analytes from a liquid (or gaseous) sample by a supported liquid membrane in the form of a porous hollow fibre with solvent-filled pores. The analytes are transferred to an acceptor phase contained in the cavity of the hollow fibre.Typical experimental arrangement for hollow-fiber supported liquid membrane (SLM) for liquid-phase microextraction.

H02836.title: holoenzyme
H02836.definition: An active enzyme consisting of the apoenzyme and coenzyme.

10803.title: holoprosencephaly
10803.definition: Birth defect in which the embryonic forebrain fails to divide completely to form the cerebral hemispheres.

10804.title: homeobox
10804.definition: Any of a class of closely similar DNA sequences occurring in various genes and involved in regulating pattern formation, segmentation, and morphogenesis during embryonic development in many species.

10806.title: homeosis
10806.definition: Replacement of part of one segment of an insect or other segmented animal by a structure characteristic of a different segment, especially through mutation.

14744.title: homeostasis
14744.definition: Totality of processes occurring in an open system or a closed system, especially a living organism, enabling it to regulate its internal environment to maintain stable, constant conditions or the outcome of these processes.

13221.title: homing
13221.definition: Movement of leukocytes to specific locations in the body.

13222.title: homing receptor
13222.definition: Cell surface molecule that directs leukocytes to specific locations in the body.

H02838.title: homo
H02838.definition: a) An acronym for Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO). See: frontier orbitals.b) A prefix (consisting of lower case letters, homo), used to indicate a higher homologue of a compound.

H02839.title: homoaromatic
H02839.definition: Whereas in an aromatic molecule there is continuous overlap of p-orbitals over a cyclic array of atoms, in a homoaromatic molecule there is a formal discontinuity in this overlap resulting from the presence of a single \(\rm{sp}^{3}\) hybridized atom at one or several positions within the ring; p-orbital overlap apparently bridges these \(\rm{sp}^{3}\) centres, and features associated with aromaticity are manifest in the properties of the compound. Pronounced homoaromaticity is not normally associated with neutral molecules, but mainly with species bearing an electrical charge, e.g. the 'homotropylium' cation, ($\ce{C8H9^{+}}$):  In bis, tris, (etc.) homoaromatic species, two, three, (etc.) single \(\rm{sp}^{3}\) centres separately interrupt the $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$ system.

H02840.title: homochain polymer
H02840.definition: A class of polymer in which the main chain is constructed from atoms of a single element. Homochain polymers are named by placing the name or symbol of the element in the main chain immediately before the expression '-chain polymer', e.g. carbon-chain polymer or C-chain polymer; sulfur-chain polymer or S-chain polymer.

14383.title: homocoagulation
14383.definition: Coagulation of colloidal particles of the same size and kind.

H02842.title: homoconjugation
H02842.definition: [obsolete] Association between a base and its conjugate acid through a hydrogen bond ($\ce{B\bond{...}HB^{+}}$ or $\ce{AH\bond{...}A^{-}}$). Homoassociation is a more appropriate term for this phenomenon.The orbital overlap of two $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}systems}$ separated by a non-conjugating group, such as $\ce{CH2}$.

H02843.title: homocyclic compounds
H02843.definition: Cyclic compounds having as ring members atoms of the same element only, e.g. benzene, pentazole, cyclohexasilane.

13223.title: homocytotropic antibody
13223.definition: Antibody that binds preferentially to cells from the same species rather than to cells from other species.

HT07048.title: homodesmotic reaction
HT07048.definition: A subclass of isodesmic reactions in which reactants and products contain equal numbers of carbon atoms in corresponding states of hybridization; moreover, there is matching of the carbon-hydrogen bonds in terms of the number of hydrogen atoms joined to the individual carbon atoms. To achieve all this matching, one should significantly extend the number and types of reference molecules. In the aliphatic series of hydrocarbons these are propane, isobutane and neopentanes as well as propene and isobutene; for aromatics—buta-1,3-diene, 2-vinylbutadiene (3-methylidenehexa-1,5-diene) and 2,3-divinylbutadiene (3,4-bismethylidenehexa-1,5-diene). Thus to assess strain energy of cyclopropane and aromatic stabilization of benzene the following homodesmotic reactions are to be respectively analysed.$\ce{c-(CH2)3 + 3CH3–CH3 -> 3CH3CH2CH3}$\(\Delta H_{\exp}^{\circ} = \pu{-26.5 kcal/mol}\) (\(\pu{110.9 kJ/mol}\)).$\ce{C6H6 + 3CH2=CH2 -> 3CH2=CH–CH=CH2}$(trans)\(\Delta H_{\rm{calc}}^{\circ} \rm{(MP2/6{-}31G^{**})} = \pu{23.9 kcal/mol}\) (\(\pu{100.0 kJ/mol}\)) Due to closer matching of the hybridization states of the atoms of reactants and products as compared to isodesmic reactions, the homodesmotic reactions give more accurate estimates of the intrinsic strain and the cyclic delocalization. The definition may be extended to molecules with heteroatoms.

H02844.title: homodetic cyclic peptide
H02844.definition: A cyclic peptide in which the ring consists solely of amino-acid residues in eupeptide linkage.

H02845.title: homogeneity
H02845.definition: The degree to which a property or a constituent is uniformly distributed throughout a quantity of material. A material may be homogeneous with respect to one analyte or property but heterogeneous with respect to another. The degree of heterogeneity (the opposite of homogeneity) is the determining factor of sampling error.

14146.title: homogeneous assay
14146.definition: Assay in which all reagents and reactants are of a uniform phase (typically, liquid phase) and assay response is detected without the need for physical separation of assay components.

14147.title: homogeneous binding assay
14147.definition: Single-phase system used to qualitatively discriminate between specific and nonspecific interactions or quantitatively determine the concentration of a component part of a mixture.

09005.title: homogeneous catalysis coordination polymerization
09005.definition: Coordination polymerization making use of a homogeneous catalyst.

09108.title: homogeneous crystalline membrane electrodes
09108.definition: ISE in which the membrane is a crystalline material prepared from either a single compound or a homogeneous mixture of compounds.

09117.title: homogeneous crystalline membrane ion-selective electrode
09117.definition: Ion-selective electrode in which the ion-selective membrane is a crystalline material prepared from either a single compound or homogeneous mixture of compounds.

09600.title: homogeneous degradation
09600.definition: Degradation that occurs at the same rate regardless of the location within a polymeric item.

08611.title: homogeneous line-broadening
08611.definition: Line-broadening by mechanisms that affect every molecule of the same species in the sample in the same way.

14366.title: homogeneous micellisation nucleation
14366.definition: Formation of primary particles as a result of micelle formation from surface-active oligomer radicals formed in a polymerization.

14297.title: homogeneous particle
14297.definition: Particle that is spatially uniform with respect to chemical composition of the constituent polymer(s).

14020.title: homogeneous photocatalysis
14020.definition: Photocatalysis taking place in homogeneous systems.

HT07582.title: homogeneous polymer blend
HT07582.definition: Polymer blend that is a single-phase structure.

09045.title: homogeneous precipitation
09045.definition: Precipitation in gravimetric analysis in which the precipitating agent is produced from a homogeneously dissolved precursor to minimise local excesses and supersaturation.

14021.title: homogeneous radiation catalysis
14021.definition: Radiation catalysis taking place in homogeneous systems.

08828.title: homojunction
08828.definition: Interface occurring between two similar semiconductors with equal bandgaps.

H02850.title: homoleptic
H02850.definition: Transition metal or Main Group compounds having only one type of ligand are said to be homoleptic, e.g. $\ce{TaMe5}$.

10807.title: homologous
10807.definition:
Having the same relationship, relative position, or structure.
(Of organs) Similar in position, structure, and evolutionary origin but not necessarily in function.
(Of chromosomes) Pairing at meiosis and having the same structural features and pattern of genes.
(Of a series of chemical compounds) Having the same functional group(s) but differing in structure by a fixed group of atoms.

HT07232.title: homologous polymer blend
HT07232.definition: Mixture of two or more fractions of the same polymer, each of which has a different molar-mass distribution.

10808.title: homologous recombination
10808.definition: Crossing over between two similar or identical strands of DNA, resulting in exchange of corresponding stretches of DNA between two sister chromosomes.

15781.title: homology
15781.definition:
Similarity of anatomical structures in different species because of shared ancestry
Similarity of DNA or RNA nucleotide sequences, or of protein amino-acid sequences, supporting the hypothesis that they share a common ancestor.Note: Homology among DNA or RNA nucleotide sequences, or among protein amino-acid sequences, is often concluded on the basis of sequence similarity. In general, if there are almost identical sequences, it is likely that they are homologous. However, it is possible that highly similar sequences were not derived from a common ancestor, i.e., they are similar but not homologous.

12667.title: homology model
12667.definition: Computational representation of a protein built from the 3D structure of a similar protein or proteins using alignment techniques and homology arguments.

H02851.title: homolysis
H02851.definition: The cleavage of a bond ('homolytic cleavage' or 'homolytic fission') so that each of the molecular fragments between which the bond is broken retains one of the bonding electrons. A unimolecular reaction involving homolysis of a bond (not forming part of a cyclic structure) in a molecular entity containing an even number of (paired) electrons results in the formation of two radicals:  It is the reverse of colligation. Homolysis is also commonly a feature of bimolecular substitution reactions (and of other reactions) involving radicals and molecules.

H02852.title: homolytic dissociative adsorption
H02852.definition: Relates in the usual sense to the formal nature of the cleavage of a single bond. If the electron pair in the bond of the adsorptive $\ce{A{:}B}$ is divided in the course of its dissociative adsorption, the adsorption is homolytic dissociative adsorption.

08365.title: homonuclear decoupling
08365.definition: Spin decoupling in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy between two signals of the same nuclear isotope.

H02854.title: homopolymer
H02854.definition: A polymer derived from one species of (real, implicit or hypothetical) monomer.

H02855.title: homopolymerization
H02855.definition: Polymerization in which a homopolymer is formed.

H02856.title: homopolysaccharide
H02856.definition: The class name for polysaccharides composed of only one kind of monosaccharide.

15404.title: homopropagation
15404.definition: Addition of a monomer to a chain carrier bearing a terminal group derived from the same monomer species.

H02857.title: homotopic
H02857.definition: Atoms or groups of a molecule which are related by an n-fold rotation axis (n = 2, 3, etc.) are called homotopic. For example, chiral tartaric acid (\(C_{2}\) axis), chloroform (\(C_{3}\) axis) and cyclohexaamylose ($\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}cyclodextrin}$, \(C_{6}\) axis) have respectively two homotopic carboxyl groups, three homotopic chlorine atoms and six homotopic ᴅ-glucose residues.

15782.title: homozygote
15782.definition: Organism that has the same allelic form of a specified gene on each of a pair of homologous chromosomes or describing the genome of that organism.

13224.title: homozygous
13224.definition: Possessing the same allele at a given locus on the two homologous chromosomes.

10809.title: honey bee larval toxicity test
10809.definition: Procedure in which larvae of the honey bee (Apis mellifera) are exposed to a test chemical in the diet and subsequent mortality is recorded daily up to the \(\pu{72\!\!{-}\!h}\) \(\pu{LD_{50}}\).

13829.title: honeycomb polymer film
13829.definition: Hexagonal array of holes in a polymer film.

08829.title: hopping transport
08829.definition: Incoherent transport of charge carriers by hopping between adjacent energetically nearly equivalent localized sites.

H02858.title: horizontal elution
H02858.definition: A mode of operation in which the paper or plate is in a horizontal position and the mobile-phase movement along the plane depends on capillary action.

14745.title: hormesis
14745.definition: Unexpected and unexplained but favorable biological response to low-level exposure to a substance or physical agent generally considered to be harmful.

10810.title: hormone
10810.definition: Substance formed in one organ or part of the body and carried in the blood to another organ or part where it selectively alters functional activity.

13225.title: horror autotoxicus
13225.definition: Term (Latin: dread of self-poisoning) to describe the body’s innate aversion to immunological self destruction.

08077.title: Horwitz equation
08077.definition: Empirical relationship providing a standard deviation under reproducibility conditions of measurement (\(s_{\rm{R,H}}\)) to be expected for typical measurements of the mass fraction (\(w\)) of a component in a material: \(s_{\rm{R,H}} = 0.02 w^{0.8495}\).

08078.title: Horwitz ratio
08078.definition:
Standard deviation of a mass fraction of a component under reproducibility conditions of measurement divided by the corresponding standard deviation calculated from the Horwitz equation.
Figure 1: Horwitz curve (trumpet, horn). Expected relative standard deviation under reproducibility conditions of measurement, \(\pm s_{\rm{R,H}}/w\) plotted against logarithm of mass fraction, \(w\).

H02859.title: host
H02859.definition: A molecular entity that forms complexes with organic or inorganic guests, or a chemical species that can accommodate guests within cavities of its crystal structure. Examples include cryptands and crowns (where there are ion-dipole attractions between heteroatoms and positive ions), hydrogen-bonded molecules that form 'clathrates' (e.g. hydroquinone and water), and host molecules of inclusion compounds (e.g. urea or thiourea). van der Waals forces and hydrophobic interactions bind the guest to the host molecule in clathrates and inclusion compounds.

13226.title: host defense
13226.definition: Ability of an individual to resist invasion by opportunistic agents and production of disease associated with exposure to microorganisms, foreign tissue, and particulates, as well as certain types of neoplasia. Host defense may be either nonspecific (innate or natural immunity) or specific (adaptive or acquired immunity) in nature.

13227.title: host-resistance assay
13227.definition: Evaluation of host resistance in rodents to in vivo challenge with an infectious organism under normal conditions and after pharmacological and nutritional alterations of the immune system.

H02860.title: host-vector system
H02860.definition: A compatible combination of host (e.g. bacteria) and vector (e.g. plasmid) that allows propagation of DNA.

H02861.title: hot atom
H02861.definition: An atom in an excited energy state or having kinetic energy above the ambient thermal level, usually as a result of nuclear processes.

H02862.title: hot cell
H02862.definition: A heavily shielded enclosure for highly radioactive materials. It may be used for their handling or processing by remote means or for their storage.

08830.title: hot electron
08830.definition: Electron that is out of the thermal equilibrium with its environment and has enough kinetic energy to overcome potential barriers to travel between different regions of a molecule or lattice.

H02863.title: hot ground state reaction
H02863.definition: A hot state reaction of the ground electronic state.

H02865.title: hot state reaction
H02865.definition: A reaction proceeding from an ensemble of molecular entities possessing a higher average vibrational, rotational or translational energy than they would at thermal equilibrium with the surrounding medium.

08612.title: hot transition
08612.definition: Electronic transition between an excited state and a state in which all vibrational quantum numbers are the same or greater.

H02867.title: Hückel (4n + 2) rule
H02867.definition: Monocyclic planar (or almost planar) systems of trigonally (or sometimes digonally) hybridized atoms that contain $\ce{(4n + 2) \uppi\!\mbox{-}electrons}$ (where $n$ is a non-negative integer) will exhibit aromatic character. The rule is generally limited to $n = 0 – 5$. This rule is derived from the Hückel MO calculation on planar monocyclic conjugated hydrocarbons $\ce{(CH)_{m}}$ where $m$ is an integer equal to or greater than 3 according to which $\ce{(4n + 2) \uppi\!\mbox{-}electrons}$ are contained in a closed-shell system. Examples of systems that obey the Hückel rule include:  Systems containing $\ce{4n\;\uppi\!\mbox{-}electrons}$ (such as cyclobutadiene and the cyclopentadienyl cation) are 'antiaromatic'.

HT07035.title: Hückel molecular orbital theory
HT07035.definition: The simplest molecular orbital theory of $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}conjugated}$ molecular systems. It uses the following approximations: $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$ approximation; LCAO representation of the $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}molecular orbitals}$; neglect of electron-electron and nuclear-nuclear repulsions (in fact, the assumption that these cancel). The diagonal elements of the effective Hamiltonian, coulombic integrals, and the off-diagonal elements, resonance integrals, (accounted for only directly bonded atoms) are chosen as empirical parameters, all overlap integrals being neglected.

H02868.title: Huggins coefficient
H02868.definition: A parameter in the Huggins equation.

H02869.title: Huggins equation
H02869.definition: The equation describing the dependence of the reduced viscosity, \(\frac{\eta _{\rm{i}}}{c}\), on the mass concentration of a polymer, \(c\), for dilute polymer solutions of the form: \[\frac{\eta _{\rm{i}}}{c} = \left[\eta \right]+k_{\rm{H}}\ \left[\eta \right]^{2}\ c\] where \(k_{\rm{H}}\) is the Huggins coefficient and \([\eta]\) is the intrinsic viscosity.

HT07393.title: hula-twist mechanism
HT07393.definition: Volume-conserving mechanism of photoisomerization of a double bond in a conjugated system involving simultaneous configurational and conformational isomerization, e.g., the photoinitiated concerted rotation of two adjacent double and single bonds.

11228.title: human chorionic somatomammotropin
11228.definition: Placental hormone that affects maternal metabolism and supports fetal growth by making more glucose and fatty acids available to the fetus.

15783.title: human ecology
15783.definition: Interrelationship between humans and the entire environment—physical, biological, socioeconomic, and cultural, including the interrelationships between individual humans or groups of humans and other human groups or groups of other species.

15784.title: human equivalent dose
15784.definition: Human dose of an agent that is believed to induce the same magnitude of a toxic effect that the known animal dose has induced.

15785.title: human exposure threshold
15785.definition: Generic value of exposure to a substance, or a group of substances falling within a defined structural class, below which there is expected to be no appreciable risk to human health.

10811.title: Human Genome Project
10811.definition: International research project that started in 1990 with the goal of determining the base-pair sequence of the human genome. The project was declared complete in 2003.

13228.title: human immunodeficiency virus
13228.definition: Causative agent of acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS).

13230.title: human leukocyte antigen
13230.definition: Antigen coded by genes of the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC).

13231.title: human leukocyte antigen polymorphism
13231.definition: Discontinuous genetic variation in the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) that results in the occurrence of several different forms of MHC molecules among people.

13232.title: human leukocyte antigen type I
13232.definition: Molecules that enable the body to recognize infected cells and tumor cells and destroy them with cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs).

13233.title: human leukocyte antigen type II
13233.definition: Molecules that enable CD4+ lymphocytes to recognize epitopes of exogenous antigens and discriminate self from non-self.

13229.title: humanized antibody
13229.definition: Genetically engineered monoclonal antibody of non-human origin in which all but the antigen-binding complementarity-determining region (CDR) sequences have been replaced with sequences derived from human antibodies.

14746.title: humic substances
14746.definition: Nonvolatile organic anionic polyelectrolytes, of biological origin, in the molecular mass range \(\pu{500\!{-}\! 5000}\), which have complex structures and are variable in composition.

H02870.title: humidity
H02870.definition: A general term referring to the water content of a gas.

13234.title: humoral
13234.definition: Pertaining to extracellular fluid such as plasma and lymph.

13235.title: humoral immune response
13235.definition: Immune response in which specific antibodies induce the effector functions (such as phagocytosis and activation of the complement system).

13236.title: humoral immunity
13236.definition: Specific immune response that is mediated primarily by humoral factors circulating in solution in the blood plasma and lymph (i.e., antibodies and complement).

H02871.title: Hund rules
H02871.definition: Of the different multiplets resulting from different configurations of electrons in degenerate orbitals of an atom those with greatest multiplicity have the lowest energy (multiplicity rule).Among multiplets having the same multiplicity, the lowest-energy one is that with the largest total orbital angular momentum (angular momentum rule) (valid if the total orbital angular momentum is a constant of motion).In configurations containing shells less than half full of electrons, the term having the lowest total angular momentum \(J\) lies lowest in energy, whereas in those with shells more than half filled, the term having the largest value of \(J\) lies lowest (fine structure rule). Hund rules apply if the 'Russell–Saunders' coupling scheme is valid. Sometimes the first rule is applied with questionable validity to molecules.

11811.title: Huntington disease
11811.definition: Genetic autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disease resulting from a mutation in the Huntingtin gene and resulting notably in decline of cognitive function and a characteristic chorea.

14747.title: Hutchinsonian niche
14747.definition: Intersection of ranges of tolerances for sets of resources utilized by organisms, represented mathematically by a multidimensional hypervolume whose dimensions correspond to environmental variables. Any species is considered unimodally distributed, i.e., confined to a habitat in the niche.

14748.title: hybrid
14748.definition:
Result of interbreeding between two animals or plants of different taxa.Note: Hybrids between different species within the same genus are sometimes known as interspecific hybrids or crosses. Hybrids between different subspecies within a species are known as intra-specific hybrids. Hybrids between different genera are sometimes known as intergeneric hybrids.
Cross-breed between populations, breeds, or cultivars within a single species.Note: Hybridization is often used in plant and animal breeding to obtain desirable characteristics not found or inconsistently present in the parent individuals or populations.

14285.title: hybrid latex
14285.definition:
Latex comprising a polymer of relatively high molar mass and an oligomer or an alkyd resin, in which there is usually chemical bonding between the two components, formed either during latex synthesis or subsequently after formation of a film from the latex.
Latex comprising multicomponent particles that contain both organic and inorganic material phases.

HT07049.title: hybrid orbital
HT07049.definition: An atomic orbital derived through hybridization of atomic orbitals with different angular momentum quantum numbers located at a given atom.

HT07556.title: hybrid polymer
HT07556.definition: Polymer or polymer network comprised of inorganic and organic components.

H02874.title: hybridization
H02874.definition: Linear combination of atomic orbitals on an atom. Hybrid orbitals are often used in organic chemistry to describe the bonding molecules containing tetrahedral (\(\mathrm{sp}^{3}\)), trigonal (\(\mathrm{sp}^{2}\)) and digonal (\(\mathrm{sp}\)) atoms.

09870.title: hybridization assay
09870.definition: Assay with specifically designed single-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) probe with a defined (known) nucleotide sequence usually immobilised on a surface (in such a case, the nucleic acid probe is called the capture probe).

H02875.title: hybridoma
H02875.definition: A hybrid cell line resulting from the fusion of a specific antibody-producing spleen cell (lymphocyte) with a myeloma cell, which has the growth characteristics of the myeloma component and the antibody-secreting characteristics of the lymphocyte, and will multiply to become a source of pure monoclonal antibody.

10812.title: hydatidiform mole
10812.definition: Vesicular or polycystic mass resulting from the proliferation of the trophoblast, with hydropic degeneration and avascularity of the chorionic villi.

10813.title: hydranencephaly
10813.definition: Rare condition in which the brain’s cerebral hemispheres are replaced by sacs filled with cerebrospinal fluid.

15195.title: hydrate
15195.definition: Crystalline form of a compound in which water molecules are part of the crystal structure.

H02876.title: hydration
H02876.definition: Addition of water or of the elements of water (i.e. H and OH) to a molecular entity. For example, hydration of ethene:  The term is also used in a more restricted sense for the process:

H02879.title: hydrazides
H02879.definition: Compounds derived from oxoacids $\ce{R_{k}E(=O)_{l}(OH)_{m}}$ ($l \neq 0$) by replacing $\ce{–OH}$ by $\ce{–NRNR2}$ ($\ce{R}$ groups are commonly $\ce{H}$), as in carbohydrazides, $\ce{RC(=O)NHNH2}$, sulfonohydrazides, $\ce{RS(=O)2NHNH2}$, and phosphonic dihydrazides, $\ce{RP(=O)(NHNH2)2}$.

H02880.title: hydrazidines
H02880.definition: Compounds, $\ce{RC(NHNH2)2=NNH2}$, derived from carboxylic acids by replacing $\ce{–OH}$ by $\ce{–NHNH2}$ (or N-substituted analogues) and $\ce{=O}$ by $\ce{=NNH2}$ (or substituted analogues). A specific hydrazidine is named as a hydrazide hydrazone, e.g. hexanohydrazide hydrazone.

H02881.title: hydrazines
H02881.definition: Hydrazine (diazane), $\ce{H2NNH2}$, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives. When one or more substituents are acyl groups, the compound is a hydrazide. N-Alkylidene derivatives are hydrazones.

H02883.title: hydrazo compounds
H02883.definition: Compounds containing the divalent hydrazo group, $\ce{–NHNH\bond{–}}$, such as hydrazoarenes (1,2-diarylhydrazines or 1,2-diaryldiazanes, usually with both aryl groups the same) and their N-substituted derivatives $\ce{ArNRNRAr}$.

H02884.title: hydrazones
H02884.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R2C=NNR2}$, formally derived from aldehydes or ketones by replacing $\ce{=O}$ by $\ce{=NNH2}$ (or substituted analogues).

H02885.title: hydrazonic acids
H02885.definition: Compounds derived from oxoacids $\ce{R_{k}E(=O)_{l}(OH)_{m}}$ ($l \neq 0$) by replacing a double-bonded oxygen atom by $\ce{=NNR2}$, as in carbohydrazonic acids, $\ce{RC(OH)=NNH2}$ and sulfonohydrazonic acids, $\ce{RS(=O)(=NNH2)OH}$.

H02889.title: hydrocarbons
H02889.definition: Compounds consisting of carbon and hydrogen only.

H02891.title: hydrocarbyl groups
H02891.definition: Univalent groups formed by removing a hydrogen atom from a hydrocarbon, e.g. ethyl, phenyl.

H02890.title: hydrocarbylene groups
H02890.definition: Divalent groups formed by removing two hydrogen atoms from a hydrocarbon, the free valencies of which are not engaged in a double bond, e.g. 1,3-phenylene, $\ce{–CH2CH2CH2–}$ propane-1,3-diyl, $\ce{–CH2–}$ methylene.

H02892.title: hydrocarbylidene groups
H02892.definition: Divalent groups, $\ce{R2C=}$, formed by removing two hydrogen atoms from the same carbon atom of a hydrocarbon, the free valencies of which are engaged in a double bond.

H02893.title: hydrocarbylidyne groups
H02893.definition: Trivalent groups, $\ce{RC#}$, formed by removing three hydrogen atoms from the same carbon atom of a hydrocarbon, the free valencies of which are engaged in a triple bond.

H02894.title: hydrocarbylsulfanyl nitrenes
H02894.definition: Nitrenes substituted with hydrocarbyl sulfanyl groups, . Sulfenyl nitrenes is an older synonymous term. E.g. MeSN methylsulfanylnitrene or methylthionitrene. The synonymous term 'thiazynes' (from the third canonical form; confusable with the hetarynes derivable from 1,2- and 1,4-thiazine) is best avoided.

10814.title: hydrocele
10814.definition: Accumulation of serous fluid in a sacculated cavity; specifically, such an accumulation in the space of the tunica vaginalis testis, or in a separate pocket along the spermatic cord.

10815.title: hydrocephalus
10815.definition: Accumulation of excess cerebrospinal fluid within the ventricles of the brain; head enlargement and brain damage may occur.

H02895.title: hydrocracking unit
H02895.definition: Used in the thermal decomposition of heavy (high molecular weight) hydrocarbons to smaller (low molecular weight) hydrocarbons; high pressures of hydrogen and a special catalyst are employed. Sulfur compounds in the fuel are reduced to $\ce{H2S}$, and the final hydrocarbon product can be obtained relatively sulfur-free.

09889.title: hydrodynamic chromatography
09889.definition: Liquid chromatography for the separation of macromolecules and particles based on the difference in the speed of the mobile phase flow between the column axis and column wall and the specific size-dependent distribution of particles across the column cross-section.

09925.title: hydrodynamic injection
09925.definition: Introduction of the analytical sample into a capillary by a pressure difference between the ends of the capillary.

12253.title: hydrodynamic interaction
12253.definition: In a solution or dispersion, the perturbation of the flow of the solvent continuum or dispersing medium continuum around a solute molecule, a segment of a dissolved macromolecule or dispersed entity caused by the presence of the other solute molecules, segments, or dispersed entities.

09138.title: hydrodynamic voltammetry
09138.definition: Voltammetry with forced flow of the solution towards the electrode surface.

H02897.title: hydrodynamic volume
H02897.definition: The volume of a hydrodynamically equivalent sphere.

H02896.title: hydrodynamically equivalent sphere
H02896.definition: A hypothetical sphere, impenetrable to the surrounding medium, displaying in a hydrodynamic field the same frictional effect as an actual polymer molecule. The size of a hydrodynamically equivalent sphere may be different for different types of motion of the macromolecule, e.g. for diffusion and for viscous flow.

HT07519.title: hydrogel
HT07519.definition: Gel in which the swelling agent is water.

H02898.title: hydrogen
H02898.definition: The general name for the atom $\ce{H}$, without regard for its nuclear mass, either for hydrogen in its natural abundance or where it is not desired to distinguish between the isotopes. The systematic name for atomic hydrogen is monohydrogen.

H02899.title: hydrogen bond
H02899.definition: A form of association between an electronegative atom and a hydrogen atom attached to a second, relatively electronegative atom. It is best considered as an electrostatic interaction, heightened by the small size of hydrogen, which permits proximity of the interacting dipoles or charges. Both electronegative atoms are usually (but not necessarily) from the first row of the Periodic Table, i.e. $\ce{N}$, $\ce{O}$ or $\ce{F}$. Hydrogen bonds may be inter-molecular or intramolecular. With a few exceptions, usually involving fluorine, the associated energies are less than \(\pu{20\!-\! 25 kJ mol-1}\) (\(\pu{5\!{-}\! 6 kcal mol-1}\)).

HT07050.title: hydrogen bond
HT07050.definition: A particular type of multicenter (three center - four electron) $\ce{X–H...Y}$ in which the central hydrogen atom covalently linked to an electronegative atom $\ce{X}$ ($\ce{C}$, $\ce{N}$, $\ce{O}$, $\ce{S}$...) forms an additional weaker bond with atom $\ce{Y}$ ($\ce{N}$, $\ce{O}$, $\ce{S}$...) in the direction of its lone electron pair orbital. The energy of hydrogen bonds, which is usually in the range of \(\pu{3\!{-}\! 15 kcal/mol}\) (\(\pu{12\!{-}\! 65 kJ/mol}\)), results from the electrostatic interaction and also from the orbital interaction of the antibonding $\upsigma^{\ast}(\ce{XH})MO$ of the molecule acting as the hydrogen donor and the non-bonding lone electron pair $MO{\rm{n}}_{\rm{Y}}$ of the hydrogen acceptor molecule.

H02900.title: hydrogen gas electrode
H02900.definition: A thin foil of platinum electrolytically coated with a finely divided deposit of platinum or palladium metal, which catalyses the electrode reaction: \[\rm{H}^{+}+\rm{e}\rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\rm{H}_{2}\] in solutions saturated with hydrogen gas.

H02901.title: hydrolases
H02901.definition: Enzymes that catalyse the cleavage of $\ce{C–O}$, $\ce{C–N}$, $\ce{C–C}$ and other bonds by reactions involving the addition or removal of water.

HT07623.title: hydrolysis ratio
HT07623.definition: Mole ratio of water to alkoxy groups used in sol-gel processing of metal alkoxides.

H02903.title: hydrometeor
H02903.definition: Any condensed water particle in the atmosphere of sufficient size to be potentially capable of undergoing precipitation (in fogs, clouds, some hazes, raindrops, snowflakes, etc.).

11814.title: hydromyelia
11814.definition: Pathological dilation of the spinal cord due to expansion of the cerebrospinal fluid-filled central canal of the cord.

H02904.title: hydron
H02904.definition: The general name for the cation $\ce{H^{+}}$; the species $\ce{H^{−}}$ is the hydride anion and $\ce{H}$ is the hydro group. These are general names to be used without regard to the nuclear mass of the hydrogen entity, either for hydrogen in its natural abundance or where it is not desired to distinguish between the isotopes.

08179.title: hydronation
08179.definition: Attachment of the ion \(\ce{H^{+}}\) either in natural abundance or where it is not desired to distinguish between the isotopes.

10817.title: hydronephrosis
10817.definition: Swelling of the funnel-shaped part of the kidney, where urine is collected to enter the ureter.

H02905.title: hydroperoxides
H02905.definition: Monosubstitution products of hydrogen peroxide (dioxidane), $\ce{HOOH}$, having the skeleton $\ce{ROOH}$, in which $\ce{R}$ is any organyl group. Compounds in which $\ce{R}$ is acyl are known as peroxy acids.

15196.title: hydrophile-lipophile balance system
15196.definition: Empirical scale (of \(0\!-\!20\)) used to classify surfactants and emulsifying agents.

H02906.title: hydrophilic
H02906.definition: 'Water loving'. The capacity of a molecular entity or of a substituent to interact with polar solvents, in particular with water, or with other polar groups.

13830.title: hydrophilic interaction
13830.definition: Attractive interaction between hydrophilic groups, molecules, or substances.

09890.title: hydrophilic-interaction liquid chromatography
09890.definition: Liquid chromatography in which the molecules are partitioned between a water-enriched layer, which is immobilised on a hydrophilic (polar) stationary phase, and a less-polar mobile phase, containing water and organic solvent.

HT06963.title: hydrophilicity
HT06963.definition: Hydrophilicity is the tendency of a molecule to be solvated by water.

13831.title: hydrophobic
13831.definition: Qualifier indicating capacity of a molecular entity or of a substituent to interact repulsively with polar molecules, in particular with water or with polar groups.

12668.title: hydrophobic fragmental constant
12668.definition: Representation of the lipophilicity contribution of a constituent part of a structure to the total lipophilicity.

H02907.title: hydrophobic interaction
H02907.definition: The tendency of hydrocarbons (or of lipophilic hydrocarbon-like groups in solutes) to form intermolecular aggregates in an aqueous medium, and analogous intramolecular interactions. The name arises from the attribution of the phenomenon to the apparent repulsion between water and hydrocarbons. However, the phenomenon ought to be attributed to the effect of the hydrocarbon-like groups on the water-water interaction. The misleading alternative term 'hydrophobic bond' is discouraged.

09891.title: hydrophobic-interaction chromatography
09891.definition: Chromatography in which molecules are separated by interactions between their hydrophobic moieties and hydrophobic sites on the surface of the stationary phase.

HT06964.title: hydrophobicity
HT06964.definition: Hydrophobicity is the association of non-polar groups or molecules in an aqueous environment which arises from the tendency of water to exclude non-polar molecules.

H02908.title: hydropolysulfides
H02908.definition: Compounds having the structures $\ce{RS2H}$, $\ce{RS3H}$ ... $\ce{RSnH}$, in which $\ce{Sn}$ is a chain of sulfur atoms, and $\ce{R}$ is hydrocarbyl. Some people exclude hydrodisulfides from the class hydropolysulfides.

10818.title: hydrops
10818.definition: Gross edema of the entire body, with severe anemia, occurring in hemolytic disease of the newborn.

H02909.title: hydrosphere
H02909.definition: The gaseous, liquid and solid water of the earth (oceans, ice caps, lakes, rivers, etc.) as distinguished from the lithosphere and the atmosphere.

H02910.title: hydrosulfides
H02910.definition: Term used in radicofunctional nomenclature of thiols. Hydrosulfides is not commonly used as a class name for thiols.

10819.title: hydroureter
10819.definition: Dilation of a ureter with fluid.

H02911.title: hydroxamic acids
H02911.definition: Compounds, $\ce{RC(=O)NHOH}$, derived from oxoacids $\ce{R_{k}E(=O)_{l}(OH)_{m}}$ ($l \neq 0$) by replacing $\ce{–OH}$ by $\ce{–NHOH}$, and hydrocarbyl derivatives thereof. Specific examples are preferably named as N-hydroxy amides.

H02912.title: hydroximic acids
H02912.definition: Compounds derived from oxoacids $\ce{R_{k}E(=O)_{l}(OH)_{m}}$ ($l \neq 0$) by replacing $\ce{=O}$ by $\ce{=NOH}$ ($\ce{=NOR}$), as in carbohydroximic acids, $\ce{RC(OH)=NOH}$, and sulfonohydroximic acids, $\ce{RS(=O)(=NOH)OH}$.

15786.title: hygiene
15786.definition: Science of health and its preservation.

10820.title: hygroma
10820.definition: Accumulation of fluid in a sac, cyst, or bursa.

H02914.title: hygrometer
H02914.definition: Instrument used to measure the water vapour content of the atmosphere.

H02922.title: hygrometry
H02922.definition: The measurement or indication of the water content of the ambient air or of a sample of gas.

15197.title: hygroscopicity
15197.definition: Tendency of a substance to absorb water from the atmosphere.

10821.title: hymen
10821.definition: Thin, membranous fold of highly variable appearance that, before its rupture, partly occludes the opening of the vagina.

10822.title: hyoid arch
10822.definition: Second pharyngeal or branchial arch of the developing embryo, from which different tissues around the neck, ear, and face will develop.

10823.title: hypaxial
10823.definition: Ventral to the long axis of the body.

15787.title: hyper-
15787.definition: Prefix meaning above or excessive: when used with the suffix '-emia' refers to blood and with the suffix '-uria' refers to urine, for example, 'hyperbilirubinemia'.

08613.title: hyper-Raman spectroscopy
08613.definition: Raman spectroscopy in which scattering occurs through hyperpolarizabilities. A two-photon technique in which an intense pulsed beam of electromagnetic radiation is focused onto the sample. When sufficient power is present in the pulse, two photons may interact with the one molecule to create a virtual state at double the frequency of the laser excitation. Raman scattering from this virtual state to an excited vibrational state of the ground state then occurs.

15789.title: hyperalimentation
15789.definition: Ingestion or administration of nutrients in excess of optimal amounts.

15790.title: hyperbilirubinemia
15790.definition: Excessive concentration of bilirubin in the blood.

09615.title: hyperbranched macromolecule
