09615.definition: Highly branched macromolecule, the constitutional repeating units of which are in substantial part branch constitutional repeating units and terminal constitutional repeating units.

09616.title: hyperbranched oligomer
09616.definition: Substance composed of hyperbranched oligomer molecules.

09617.title: hyperbranched oligomer molecule
09617.definition: Highly branched oligomer molecule, the constitutional repeating units of which are in substantial part branch constitutional repeating units and terminal constitutional repeating units.

15791.title: hypercalcemia
15791.definition: Excessive concentration of calcium in the blood.

11816.title: hypercapnia
11816.definition: Abnormally increased carbon dioxide concentration in the blood resulting in a increased rate and depth of breathing.

H02923.title: hyperchromic effect
H02923.definition: The increase in the intensity of a spectral band due to substituents or interactions with the molecular environment.

H02924.title: hyperconjugation
H02924.definition: In the formalism that separates bonds into $\ce{\upsigma\!}$ and $\ce{\uppi\! types}$, hyperconjugation is the interaction of $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bonds}$ (e.g. $\ce{C–H}$, $\ce{C–C}$, etc.) with a $\ce{\uppi\!}$ network. This interaction is customarily illustrated by contributing structure, e.g. for toluene (below), sometimes said to be an example of 'heterovalent' or 'sacrificial hyperconjugation', so named because the contributing structure contains one two-electron bond less than the normal Lewis formula for toluene:  At present, there is no evidence for sacrificial hyperconjugation in neutral hydrocarbons. The concept of hyperconjugation is also applied to carbenium ions and radicals, where the interaction is now between $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bonds}$ and an unfilled or partially filled $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}}$ or p-orbital. A contributing structure illustrating this for the tert-butyl cation is:  This latter example is sometimes called an example of 'isovalent hyper-conjugation' (the contributing structure containing the same number of two-electron bonds as the normal Lewis formula). Both structures shown on the right hand side are also examples of 'double bond-no-bond resonance'. The interaction between filled $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}}$ or p-orbitals and adjacent antibonding  $\ce{\upsigma\!^{\ast}\mbox{-}orbitals}$ is referred to as 'negative hyperconjugation', as for example in the fluoroethyl anion:

HT07051.title: hypercoordination
HT07051.definition: A property of main-group atoms in molecular entities to acquire coordination numbers greater than four (which would comply with the Lewis octet rule). Hypercoordination may be associated with hypervalency, but usually is referred to peculiar atomic centres in the electron-deficient species with multicentre $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bonding}$, in which the bonding power of a pair of electrons is spread over more than two atoms. An example of a hypercoordinated atom is the five-coordinate carbon atom in the methanium cation, where three $\ce{C–H}$ bonds may be regarded as normal two center - two electron bonds and the bonding in the remaining $\ce{CH2}$ fragment is governed by the three-centre, two-electron bond. A particular case of a hypercoordinated atom is the hydrogen atom included into a hydrogen bond.

15788.title: hyperemia
15788.definition: Excessive amount of blood in any part of the body.

11817.title: hyperesthesia
11817.definition: Excessive sensitivity to touch, pain, or other sensory stimuli.

10824.title: hyperextension
10824.definition: Extension of a limb or part of a limb beyond the normal limit.

HT07394.title: hyperfine
HT07394.definition: Interaction between the electron spin S and the nuclear spin I.

HT07052.title: hyperfine coupling
HT07052.definition: The interaction between the spin magnetic moment of an unpaired electron and the nuclear spin magnetic moments resulting in the splitting of the $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ (spin up) and $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ (spin down) energy levels in an external magnetic field and, thus, in the multiplet pattern of the ESR spectra of radical-like species and transition metal compounds. Two main contributions to the hyperfine coupling are usually considered, Fermi contact and dipolar interactions. The contact interaction is isotropic and related to the unpaired spin density at the nucleus, \(|\psi _{\unicode[Times]{x3C3}}|^{2}\). The dipolar interaction is anisotropic, and related to \(r^{-3}\), where \(r\) is the distance between the atom holding the unpaired electron and the nucleus with non-zero spin.

10825.title: hyperflexion
10825.definition: Flexion of a limb or part of a limb beyond the normal limit.

13237.title: hypergammaglobulinemia
13237.definition: Increase of gammaglobulins in the blood by paraproteinemia or increased production of immunoglobulins (Ig).

15792.title: hyperglycemia
15792.definition: Excessive concentration of glucose in the blood.

13238.title: hyperimmunoglobulin E syndrome
13238.definition: Rare primary immunodeficiency syndrome characterized by recurrent severe staphylococcal skin abscesses (hence Job syndrome), lung infections, and markedly elevated serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) levels.

13239.title: hyperimmunoglobulin M syndrome
13239.definition: Primary T cell defect due to mutations in the CD40 ligand (CD40L), characterized by recurrent (opportunistic) infections and very low levels of immunoglobulin G (IgG) and immunoglobulin A (IgA).

15793.title: hyperkalemia
15793.definition: Excessive concentration of potassium in the blood.

09937.title: hyperlayer focusing field-flow fractionation
09937.definition: Mechanism of field-flow fractionation of particles greater than \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\) in diameter relying on hydrodynamic lift forces near the channel wall to move particles into faster flowing streams.

15794.title: hypernatremia
15794.definition: Excessive concentration of sodium in the blood.

15795.title: hyperparathyroidism
15795.definition: Abnormally increased parathyroid gland activity that affects, and is affected by, plasma calcium concentration.

10826.title: hyperplasia
10826.definition: Abnormal multiplication or increase in the number of normal cells in a tissue or organ.

HT07053.title: hyperpolarizability
HT07053.definition: The energy of a molecule in an external electrostatic field can be expanded as \[E=E^{\rm{o}}- \unicode[Times]{x3BC}_{i}\ F_{i}- \frac{1}{2}\ \unicode[Times]{x3B1} _{ij}\ F_{i}\ F_{j}- \frac{1}{6}\ \unicode[Times]{x3B2} _{ijk}\ F_{i}\ F_{j}\ F_{k}- \frac{1}{24}\ \unicode[Times]{x3B3} _{ijkl}\ F_{i}\ F_{j}\ F_{k}\ F_{l}- \rm{...}\] where \(E^{\rm{o}}\) is the unperturbed energy, \(F_{i}\) is the component of the field in the i direction, \(\unicode[Times]{x3BC}_{i}\) is the permanent dipole moment, \(\unicode[Times]{x3B1}_{ij}\) is the polarizability tensor, and \(\unicode[Times]{x3B2}_{ijk}\) and \(\unicode[Times]{x3B3}_{ijkl}\) are the first and second hyperpolarizability tensors, respectively. \(\unicode[Times]{x3B2}\) is a third order symmetric tensor that measures the second order response of the molecular electric dipole moment to the action of an external electric field and is thus often referred to as dipole hyperpolarizability.

11818.title: hyperpolarization
11818.definition: Transient increase in membrane polarization of nerve cells or muscle cells; the opposite of depolarization.

13240.title: hyperreactivity
13240.definition: Abnormally increased response to a stimulus.

13241.title: hypersensitivity
13241.definition: State in which an individual reacts with allergic effects following exposure to a certain substance (allergen) after having been exposed previously to the same substance. It is sometimes used loosely for any increased response.

13242.title: hypersensitivity pneumonitis
13242.definition: Immune-mediated inflammatory disease of the lung parenchyma caused by exposure to an inhaled chemical allergen or organic dust.

13243.title: hypersensitization
13243.definition: Development of excessive immune reactivity to an antigen.

08614.title: hyperspectral imaging
08614.definition: Measurement method to obtain information about the spatial composition of a sample by obtaining a spectrum at each spatially resolved point of the sample.

13244.title: hypersusceptibility
13244.definition: Adverse immunological effects in an individual occurring under conditions of exposure to an allergen that result in no effects in the great majority of the population, or an individual exhibiting exaggerated effects in comparison with the great majority of those showing some adverse effects.

10827.title: hypertelorism
10827.definition: Abnormally wide space between two organs, especially referring to the eyes.

15796.title: hypertension
15796.definition: Persistently high blood pressure in the arteries or in a circuit, for example, pulmonary hypertension or hepatic portal hypertension.

11820.title: hypertonia
11820.definition: Extreme tension of the muscles or arteries.

10828.title: hypertrophy
10828.definition: Enlargement of an organ or tissue as a result of the increase in the size of its cells.

HT07054.title: hypervalency
HT07054.definition: The ability of an atom in a molecular entity to expand its valence shell beyond the limits of the Lewis octet rule. Hypervalent compounds are common for the second and subsequent row elements in groups 15–18 of the periodic table. A description of the hypervalent bonding implies a transfer of the electrons from the central (hypervalent) atom to the nonbonding molecular orbitals which it forms with (usually more electronegative) ligands. A typical example of the hypervalent bond is a linear three-centre, four-electron bond, e.g. that of $\ce{F_{ap}–P–F_{ap}}$ fragment of $\ce{PF5}$.

13245.title: hypervariable region
13245.definition: Amino acid sequence within the immunoglobulin (Ig) and T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V) regions that shows the greatest variability and contributes most to the antigen or peptide-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecule binding site.

15797.title: hypervitaminosis
15797.definition: Condition resulting from the ingestion of an excess of one or more vitamins.

H02926.title: hypho-
H02926.definition: An affix used in names to designate an open structure, especially a boron skeleton, more closed than a klado structure but more open than an arachno structure.

11821.title: hypnotic
11821.definition: Agent that may reduce anxiety and induces sleep.

15798.title: hypo-
15798.definition: Prefix meaning under, deficient: when used with the suffix '-emia' refers to blood and with the suffix '-uria' refers to urine, for example, 'hypocalcemia'.

H02928.title: hypo-phase
H02928.definition: The denser phase in an extraction system. This term is often used when two non-aqueous phases are present or when the solvent is an aqueous phase.

10829.title: hypoblast
10829.definition: Innermost of the three primary germ layers, adjacent to the blastocyst cavity, that develops into the endoderm.

15799.title: hypocalcemia
15799.definition: Abnormally low calcium concentration in the blood.

11822.title: hypocapnia
11822.definition: Abnormally decreased carbon dioxide concentration in the blood.

H02927.title: hypochromic effect
H02927.definition: The opposite of hyperchromic effect (i.e. a decrease in intensity).

13246.title: hypogammaglobulinemia
13246.definition: Immunodeficiency state marked by abnormally low levels of all classes of immunoglobulins (Ig), associated with increased susceptibility to infectious diseases.

10830.title: hypogonadism
10830.definition: Inadequate functioning of the testes or ovaries as manifested by deficiencies in gametogenesis or in secretion of gonadal hormones.

15800.title: hypokalemia
15800.definition: Abnormally low potassium concentration in the blood.

15801.title: hypomagnesemia
15801.definition: Abnormally low magnesium concentration in the blood.

15802.title: hyponatremia
15802.definition: Abnormally low sodium concentration in the blood.

11823.title: hypophysectomy
11823.definition: Surgical removal of the pituitary gland (hypophysis).

10831.title: hypoplasia
10831.definition: Underdevelopment or atrophy of a tissue or organ.

13247.title: hyposensitization therapy
13247.definition: Dermal application of a selected allergen to an allergic person in stepwise increasing dosage, with the aim of reducing the immune system’s tendency for the corresponding allergic reaction.

10832.title: hypospadias
10832.definition: Birth defect in which the urethra opens on the underside of the penis, or into the vagina.

11825.title: hypotension
11825.definition:
Subnormal arterial blood pressure.Note: Hypotension can be a cause of dizziness, weakness and fainting.
Lower than normal pressure or tension of any kind (used less commonly).

10833.title: hypothalamus
10833.definition: Region at the base of the brain containing specialized nerve cells that help activate, control, and integrate peripheral autonomic mechanisms, endocrine activities, and some somatic functions such as body temperature, sleep, and appetite.

11826.title: hypotonia
11826.definition:
Condition in which there is a diminution or loss of muscle tone.
Relaxation of the arteries.
Lower than normal tension in any part, as in intraocular pressure of the eyeball.

15803.title: hypovolemic
15803.definition: Pertaining to an abnormally decreased volume of circulating fluid (plasma) in the body.

10834.title: hypoxia
10834.definition:
Abnormally low dioxygen content or tension.
Deficiency of dioxygen in the inspired air, in blood, or in tissues, short of anoxia.

H02929.title: hypsochromic shift
H02929.definition: Shift of a spectral band to higher frequency or shorter wavelength upon substitution or change in medium. It is informally referred to as blue shift.

H02930.title: hysteresis
H02930.definition: Regarding a material quantity or instrument's reading; the dependence of a value on the direction of change from a previous characteristic value. It may be quantified by the difference between the upscale and downscale variation starting from fixed lower and upper measurement points (inversion).

H01881.title: η
H01881.definition: An affix giving a topological indication of the bonding between a $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$ ligand and the central atom in a coordination entity. A right superscript numerical index indicates the number of ligating atoms in the $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$ system of the ligand which bind to the central atom.

I00954.title: identity period
I00954.definition: The shortest distance along the chain axis for translational repetition of the chain structure. The chain identity period is usually denoted by \(c\). Synonymous with (chain) repeating distance.

08731.title: in-vivo neutron activation analysis
08731.definition: Measurement method of neutron activation analysis in which a living organism is exposed to neutrons to measure the concentrations of elements in that living organism.

13935.title: immunogenicity
13935.definition: Ability of a material or substance to elicit a cellular immune response and/or antibody production.

13936.title: implant
13936.definition: Medical device made from one or more biomaterials that is intentionally placed within the body, either totally or partially buried beneath an epithelial surface.

12430.title: image current detection
12430.definition: Method of ion detection by measuring the current that results from the image charge induced by a coherent motion of ions passing near a conductor.

12431.title: imaging mass spectrometry
12431.definition: Procedure used to form chemically selective images of an object based on the mass spectrometric detection of ions desorbed from its surface.

12433.title: infrared multiphoton dissociation
12433.definition: Dissociation of a reactant ion as a result of the absorption of multiple infrared photons.

12434.title: in-source collision-induced dissociation
12434.definition: Dissociation of an ion as a result of collisional excitation during ion transfer from an atmospheric pressure ion source to the vacuum chamber of the mass spectrometer.

12435.title: internal fragment
12435.definition: Fragment ion of a peptide ion precursor formed by a double backbone cleavage that contains neither the original \(\ce{C}\)- or \(\ce{N}\)-terminal residues. Typically a combination of b- and y-type cleavages or occasionally an a- and y-type combination.

12436.title: ion desolvation
12436.definition: Removal of solvent molecules clustered around a gas-phase ion by means of heating and/or collisions with gas molecules.

12437.title: ion enhancement
12437.definition: Phenomenon in which the ionization efficiency of a compound is increased by the presence of another compound.

12438.title: ion evaporation model
12438.definition: Mechanism for production of gas-phase ions from highly charged fine liquid droplets as in electrospray ionization that involves direct ejection of the ions from the droplet surface.

12439.title: ion funnel
12439.definition: Series of stacked ring electrodes with progressively decreasing inner diameter to which a combined radio frequency and fixed potential is applied. The resulting field focuses ions travelling along the central axis.

12440.title: ion gate
12440.definition: Set of plates or grid of wires in an ion mobility spectrometer, time-of-flight mass spectrometer, or other mass spectrometer that is used to apply a pulsed electric field with the purpose of selectively deflecting charged particles.

12441.title: ion/ion reaction
12441.definition: Reaction between two ions, generally of opposite polarity.

12442.title: ion mobility spectrometry
12442.definition: Separation of ions according to their velocity through a buffer gas under the influence of an electric field.

12443.title: ion/neutral complex
12443.definition: Weakly bound species formed from an ion and neutral.

12444.title: ion optics
12444.definition: Devices designed to control the formation, focusing, and deflection of charged particle beams in a vacuum under the influence of electric and magnetic fields.

12445.title: ion suppression
12445.definition: Phenomenon in which the ionization efficiency of a species is lowered by the presence of a different species.

12446.title: ion-to-photon detector
12446.definition: Detector in which ions strike a conversion dynode to produce electrons that in turn strike a phosphor and the resulting photons are detected by a photomultiplier.

12447.title: ion trap
12447.definition: Device for spatially confining ions using electric and magnetic fields alone or in combination.

12448.title: isobaric tag for relative and absolute quantitation
12448.definition: Chemical labeling reagents used for relative or absolute quantitation in proteomics, based on covalent labeling of the \(\ce{N}\)-terminus and side-chain amines of peptides from protein digestions with tags of varying mass.

12449.title: isotope cluster
12449.definition: Group of peaks representing ions of the same elemental composition, but different isotopic compositions.

12450.title: isotope coded affinity tag
12450.definition: Chemical labeling reagents used for relative quantitation in proteomics, consisting of a reactive group capable of labeling a defined amino acid side-chain, an isotopically coded linker, and a tag for the affinity isolation of labeled proteins and peptides.

12451.title: isotope dilution mass spectrometry
12451.definition: Quantitative mass spectrometry technique in which an isotopically enriched compound is used as a surrogate internal standard.

12452.title: isotope ratio
12452.definition: Ratio of the number of atoms of one isotope to the number of atoms of another isotope of the same chemical element in the same system.

12453.title: isotope ratio mass spectrometry
12453.definition: Measurement and study of the relative abundances of the different isotopes of an element in a material using a mass spectrometer.

12454.title: isotopolog ions
12454.definition: Ions that differ only in the isotopic composition of one or more of the constituent atoms.

12455.title: isotopomeric ion
12455.definition: Isomeric ions having the same numbers of each isotopic atom but differing in their positions within the ion.

14210.title: ideal crystalline chain conformation
14210.definition: Minimum energy conformation of an isolated polymer chain constructed according to the equivalence postulate and approximating the conformation found in a crystalline phase.

14223.title: isodirectional packing
14223.definition: In a parallel-chain crystal, the crystalline packing of directional stems with the same chain axis orientation.

14221.title: isochiral stem packing
14221.definition: Crystalline packing of stems having the same helicity.

14222.title: isoclined stems
14222.definition: Stems in a crystal having the same side-group orientation with respect to the chain axis (see figure (b) in anticlined stems).

14235.title: isomorphous polymer co-crystal
14235.definition: Crystal consisting of two or more structurally different polymers, resulting in macromolecular isomorphism.

14241.title: irregular adjacent re-entry model
14241.definition: Adjacent re-entry model in which the fold period can vary.

14266.title: isothermal crystallisation
14266.definition: Crystallization taking place at constant temperature.

13069.title: immune cytolysis
13069.definition:
1) Cell lysis caused by a lesion produced by the action of complement proteins on the antibody-coated plasma membrane of a cell.
2) Cell lysis following plasma membrane reaction with perforins released by natural killer (NK) cells.

13088.title: immune complex deposition
13088.definition: Precipitation of immune complex in organs and tissues, often causing local inflammation.

13248.title: Ia antigen
13248.definition: Isoantigen encoded by the Ia region of the mouse major histocompatibility complex (H-2 complex).

15804.title: iatrogenic
15804.definition: Any adverse condition resulting from medical treatment.

IT07396.title: IC
IT07396.definition: Frequently used acronym for internal conversion.

12669.title: inhibitory concentration at 50%
12669.definition: The concentration of an enzyme inhibitor or receptor antagonist that reduces the enzyme activity or agonist response by \(\pu{50\%}\).

10835.title: ichthyosis
10835.definition: Congenital disorder of keratinization, characterized by dryness and scaling of the skin, often associated with other defects and with abnormalities of lipid metabolism.

I02931.title: icosahedro-
I02931.definition: An affix used in names to denote twelve atoms bound into a triangular icosahedron.

I02932.title: icosanoids
I02932.definition: Unsaturated $\ce{C20}$ fatty acids and skeletally related compounds. The spelling icosanoids is preferred over the spelling eicosanoids for consistency with icosanoic acid. Specialists working in this field commonly use eicosanoids, however.

IT07398.title: intramolecular charge transfer emission
IT07398.definition: Electronic emission from an ICT state.

15805.title: icterus
15805.definition: Excess of bile pigment in the blood and consequent deposition and retention of bile pigment in the skin and the sclera.

I02933.title: ideal adsorbed state
I02933.definition: The adsorbed state in a system following Langmuir's isotherm.

15405.title: ideal binary copolymerisation
15405.definition: Binary copolymerization in which the relative rates of incorporation of the two types of monomer into the copolymer are independent of the nature of the monomer unit at the end of a propagating chain.

IT06941.title: ideal chromatography
IT06941.definition: Chromatographic process, where no peak-broadening effects (such as diffusion, slow mass transfer, etc.) operate.

15406.title: ideal copolymerisation
15406.definition: Copolymerization in which all types of propagating species show the same relative reactivity toward the monomers present.

I02934.title: ideal dilute solution
I02934.definition: Dilute solution in which the solute may be regarded as obeying Henry's law, so that all the solute activity coefficients may be approximated to 1.

I02935.title: ideal gas
I02935.definition: Gas which obeys the equation of state \(p\, V=n\, R\, T\) (the ideal gas law; \(p\) is the pressure, \(V\) the volume, \(n\) the amount of molecules, \(R\) the gas constant and \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature). For an ideal gas the fugacity, \(f\), of each constituent B is equal to its partial pressure, \(p_{\rm{B}}\), \(f_{\rm{B}}=p_{\rm{B}}=x_{\rm{B}}\ p\), where \(x_{\rm{B}}\) is the amount fraction of B.

I02938.title: ideal mixture
I02938.definition: A mixture of substances B, C, ... is called an ideal mixture when \(a_{\rm{B}}=x_{\rm{B}}\), \(a_{\rm{C}}=x_{\rm{C}}\), ... or \(f_{\rm{B}}=1\), \(f_{\rm{C}}=1\) where \(a_{\rm{B}}\) and \(f_{\rm{B}}\) are the relative activity and the activity coefficient, respectively, of a substance B in a liquid or solid mixture.

IT06944.title: ideal, non-linear chromatography
IT06944.definition: Chromatographic process, where only the curvature of the distribution isotherm determines the shape of the peaks while other peak-broadening processes are neglected.

10836.title: identical twins
10836.definition: Twins resulting from one zygote that, at an early stage of embryonic development, separated into two independently growing cell aggregations giving rise to two individuals of the same sex and identical genetic constitution.

I02940.title: identity reaction
I02940.definition: A chemical reaction whose products are chemically identical with the reactants, for example the bimolecular self exchange reaction of $\ce{CH3I}$ with $\ce{I^{-}}$.

13249.title: idiopathic
13249.definition: Term that describes a 'primary' symptom or disease in which no underlying cause or associated disorder can be found.

13250.title: idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura
13250.definition: Thrombocytopenia of unknown cause, probably related to the production of anti-platelet antibodies, and leading to bruising (purpura).

15806.title: idiosyncrasy
15806.definition: Genetically based unusually high sensitivity of an organism to the effect of certain substances.

13251.title: idiosyncratic drug reaction
13251.definition: Rare and unpredictable adverse drug reaction occurring only in susceptible individuals.

13252.title: idiotype
13252.definition: The combined antigenic determinants (idiotopes) expressed in the variable (V) region of immunoglobulins (Ig) of an individual that determine antibody specificity to a particular antigen.

13253.title: idiotype network
13253.definition: Regulatory network based on interactions of anti-idiotypic antibodies and idiotypes present on antibodies and T-cell receptors (TCRs), resulting in feedback inhibition of ongoing B cell or T cell responses.

10837.title: ileocecal
10837.definition: Relating to the ileum and the cecum.

10838.title: ileum
10838.definition: Third portion of the small intestine, between the jejunum and the cecum.

09139.title: Ilkovič equation
09139.definition: Equation relating electric current at a dropping mercury electrode under purely diffusional control, \(I_{{\rm{d,}}t}\), the amount concentration of an electroactive substance at the drop surface \(c\), and the concentration in bulk solution \(c_{\rm{0}}\), \[I_{{\rm{d}},t} = -k\,z\,F\,D^{1/2}q_{\rm{m}}^{2/3} t^{1/6}(c - c_{0})\] where \(k\) is a numerical constant, $z$ the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(D\) the diffusion coefficient of the electroactive substance, \(q_{\rm{m}}\) the mass flux of mercury at the dropping electrode, and \(t\) the time elapsed from the beginning of the drop.

I02941.title: illuminance
I02941.definition: Luminous flux received by a surface divided by the area of that surface.

09495.title: image
09495.definition: Pattern produced in or on a substrate during a lithographic process.

09497.title: image blur
09497.definition: Broadening during the development of a lithographic image.

I02942.title: image converter tube
I02942.definition: An electron tube that produces on its fluorescent screen an image of the irradiation pattern of its photosensitive input surface. An image converter which produces an image with enhanced radiance is sometimes called an image intensifier.

09254.title: image depth profile
09254.definition: Three-dimensional representation of the spatial distribution of a particular elemental or molecular species, as indicated by emitted secondary ions or electrons, as a function of depth or material removed by sputtering.

I02943.title: image dissection tube
I02943.definition: A two-dimensional radiation detector in which the electron image produced by a photo-emitting surface, usually a photocathode, is focused in the plane of a defining aperture. Magnetic or electric fields scan this image across the defining aperture.

14148.title: image-based assay
14148.definition: Assay in which image analysis algorithms that determine the compartmentalization of fluorescent probes give topological as well as quantitative information.

08366.title: imaginary NMR spectrum
08366.definition: In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, one of two equally sized blocks of frequency data \(\pu{90\!^{\circ}}\) out of phase to each other produced by Fourier transformation of the time domain signal.

I02944.title: imaging
I02944.definition: The use of a photosensitive system for the capture, recording and retrieval of information associated with an object using electromagnetic energy.

I02945.title: imbalance
I02945.definition: The situation in which reaction parameters that characterize different bond forming or bond breaking processes in the same reaction have developed to different extents as the transition state is approached along some arbitrarily defined reaction coordinate. For example, in the nitroalkane anomaly, the Brønsted \(\beta \) exponent for proton removal is smaller than the Brønsted \(\alpha \) for the nitroalkane, because of imbalance between the amount of bond breaking and resonance delocalization in the transition state. Imbalance is common in reactions such as elimination, addition and other complex reactions that involve proton (hydron) transfer.

I02946.title: imbibition
I02946.definition: The uptake of a liquid by a gel or porous substance. It may or may not be accompanied by swelling.

I02948.title: imides
I02948.definition:
Diacyl derivatives of ammonia or primary amines, especially those cyclic compounds derived from diacids, e.g. 
In additive nomenclature, in which imide is analogous to oxide, the term is used to name compounds of the type $\ce{R3Y^{+}-N^{-}R}$ ($\ce{Y = N, P}$) and $\ce{R2Z^{+}-N^{-}R}$ ($\ce{Z = O, S, Se, Te}$), which are the products of formal attachment of an $\ce{RN=}$ group to $\ce{N}$, $\ce{P}$, $\ce{O}$, $\ce{S}$, $\ce{Se}$, $\ce{Te}$. E.g. amine imides, azomethine imides.Salts having the anion $\ce{RN^{2−}}$.

I02949.title: imidic acids
I02949.definition: Compounds derived from oxoacids $\ce{R_{k}E(=O)_{l}(OH)_{m}}$ ($l \neq 0$) by replacing $\ce{=O}$ by $\ce{=NR}$; thus tautomers of amides. In organic chemistry an unspecified imidic acid is generally a carboximidic acid, $\ce{RC(=NR)(OH)}$. E.g. $\ce{RS(=NH)2(OH)}$ a sulfonodiimidic acid.

I02950.title: imidines
I02950.definition: Analogues of cyclic acid anhydrides in which $\ce{=O}$ has been replaced by $\ce{=NR}$ and $\ce{–O\bond{–}}$ by $\ce{–NR\bond{–}}$.

I02953.title: imidoyl carbenes
I02953.definition: Carbenes having the structure $\ce{RC(=NR)C{:}–R}$. Imidoyl is a shortened but imprecise term for carboximidoyl, $\ce{RC(=NH)\bond{–}}$.

I02957.title: imines
I02957.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RN=CR2}$ ($\ce{R} = \ce{H}$, hydrocarbyl). Thus analogues of aldehydes or ketones, having NR doubly bonded to carbon; aldimines have the structure $\ce{RCH=NR}$, ketimines have the structure $\ce{R'2C=NR}$ ($\ce{R'} \neq \ce{H}$). Imines include azomethines and Schiff bases. Imine is used as a suffix in systematic nomenclature to denote the $\ce{C=NH}$ group excluding the carbon atom.An obsolete term for azacycloalkanes.

I02958.title: iminium compounds
I02958.definition: Salts in which the cation has the structure $\ce{R2C=N^{+}R2}$. Thus N-hydronated imines and their N-substituted derivatives. The synonymous terms imonium compounds and immonium compounds are irregularly formed and should not be used.

I02959.title: imino acids
I02959.definition: An obsolete term, which should not be used, for imidic acids.Any carboxylic acids having an imino substituent, $\ce{HN=}$, replacing two hydrogens. A shortened form of imino carboxylic acid.Obsolescent term for azaalkanoic acids and azacycloalkane-2-carboxylic acids, e.g. proline:

I02960.title: imino carbenes
I02960.definition: This term systematically means carbenes bearing an imino or N-substituted imino group, $\ce{RN=}$, somewhere in the molecule. E.g. $\ce{R–C:–CH2C(=NR)R}$. It is listed here in order to warn against its misuse for alkylideneamino carbenes.

I02962.title: iminoxyl radicals
I02962.definition: Synonymous with alkylideneaminoxyl radicals. The term can be regarded as a contraction of iminyloxyl radicals.

I02965.title: iminyl radicals
I02965.definition: Radicals having the structure $\ce{R2C=N^{.}}$. A contraction of alkaniminyl radicals, e.g. $\ce{CH3–CH=N^{.}}$, ethaniminyl. A synonymous term is alkylideneaminyl radicals.

I02964.title: iminylium ions
I02964.definition: Cations having the structure $\ce{R2C=N^{+}}$. A contraction of alkaniminylium ions. Alkylideneaminylium ions is a synonymous term. A subclass of nitrenium ions.

13254.title: immature
13254.definition: Describing cells that are not fully developed and unable to participate immediately in an immune response.

15198.title: immediate-release tablet
15198.definition: Dosage form that releases the drug immediately.

13255.title: immediate-type hypersensitivity
13255.definition: Reaction provoked by re-exposure to an antigen (allergen) that causes plasma cells to secrete immunoglobulin E (IgE) which binds to Fc receptors on the surface of tissue mast cells and blood basophils, sensitizing them, so that later exposure to the same allergen cross-links the bound IgE, leading to degranulation and the secretion of pharmacologically active mediators such as histamine, leukotriene, and prostaglandin that act immediately on the surrounding tissues.

15807.title: immediately-dangerous-to-life-or-health-concentration
15807.definition: According to the U.S. NIOSH, the maximum exposure concentration from which one could escape within \(\pu{30 min}\) without any escape-impairing symptoms or any irreversible health effects.

09498.title: immersion fluid
09498.definition: High refractive index liquid medium used in immersion lithography that replaces the air gap between the lens and the resist surface in conventional photolithography.

09508.title: immersion lithography
09508.definition: Photolithography that provides resolution enhancement by immersing a resist-coated substrate in a fluid during the exposure process.

10268.title: immersion solid-phase microextraction
10268.definition: Solid-phase microextraction where the extraction phase is immersed directly into the sample.

I02966.title: immersional wetting
I02966.definition: A process in which a solid or liquid, $\ce{\upbeta\!}$, is covered with a liquid, $\ce{\upalpha\!}$, both of which were initially in contact with a gas or liquid, $\ce{\updelta\!}$, without changing the area of the $\ce{\upalpha\!\updelta\!\mbox{-}}$interface.

IT07239.title: immiscibility
IT07239.definition: Inability of a mixture to form a single phase.

I02968.title: immission dose
I02968.definition: The integral of the immission flow into the receptor over the exposure period.

I02969.title: immission flux
I02969.definition: The immission rate divided by the unit surface area of the receptor.

I02967.title: immission
I02967.definition: A Germanic term, pronounced in English, 'eye-mission'; the transfer of pollutants from the atmosphere to a 'receptor'; for example, pollutants retained by the lungs. It does not have the same meaning as ground level concentration, but is the opposite in meaning to emission. This term has not been used commonly in the English language.

I02970.title: immission rate
I02970.definition: The mass (or other physical quantity) of pollutant transferring per unit time into a receptor.

I02971.title: immobile adsorption
I02971.definition: A situation in which the freedom of molecules of adsorbate to move about the surface is limited. Adsorption is immobile when \(k\ T\) is small compared to \(\Delta E\), the energy barrier separating adjacent sites. The adsorbate has little chance of migrating to neighbouring sites and such adsorption is necessarily localized.

I02973.title: immobilization
I02973.definition: The technique used for the physical or chemical fixation of cells, organelles, enzymes, or other proteins (e.g. monoclonal antibodies) onto a solid support, into a solid matrix or retained by a membrane, in order to increase their stability and make possible their repeated or continued use. The principle is also used for affinity chromatography.

I02976.title: immobilized enzyme
I02976.definition: A soluble enzyme bound to an insoluble organic or inorganic matrix, or encapsulated within a membrane in order to increase its stability and make possible its repeated or continued use.

14149.title: immobilised metal ion affinity-based fluorescence polarisation assay
14149.definition: Assay in which the interaction between nanoparticles coated with triply charged metal ions and phosphate groups on a substrate that carries a fluorescent tag is detected.

I02972.title: immobilized phase
I02972.definition: A stationary phase in which is immobilized on the support particles, or on the inner wall of the column tubing e.g. by in situ polymerization (cross-linking) after coating.

09886.title: immobilized stationary phase
09886.definition: Stationary phase which has been immobilized on the support particles or on the inner wall of the column, e.g. by a physical attraction (coated stationary phase), by chemical bonding (bonded stationary phase), or by in situ polymerisation (cross-linked stationary phase) after coating.

13256.title: immune adherence
13256.definition: Attachment of particulate antigen coated with C3b (see complement) to cells expressing C3b receptors, which results in enhanced phagocytosis of bacteria by macrophages.

13257.title: immune complex
13257.definition: Product of an antigen–antibody reaction, which may also contain components of the complement system.

13258.title: immune complex disease
13258.definition: Illness resulting from deposition of antigen–antibody complexes in tissues.

13259.title: immune deviation
13259.definition: Regulatory mechanism of the preferential activation of one aspect (cellular or humoral) of the adaptive immune system at the expense of the other.

13260.title: immune elimination
13260.definition: Removal of pathogens or tumor cells by the immune system; the first step of immunoediting of tumors.

13261.title: immune enhancement
13261.definition: Therapeutic stimulation of the immune response, especially in tumor therapy.

13262.title: immune equilibrium
13262.definition: State in carcinogenesis where there is an equilibrium between elimination of tumor cells by the immune system and growth of non-immunogenic tumor cells; the second step in immunoediting.

13263.title: immune escape
13263.definition: Biological feature of an infectious agent or of a tumor cell that prevents its elimination by the immune system. Such a feature can be acquired by a selection process. Immune escape is the third step in immunoediting of tumors.

13264.title: immune evasion
13264.definition: Property of a pathogen that results in avoidance of attack by the immune system, e.g., because of reduced phagocytosis, lack of recognition by the innate immune system, or suppression of the immune response.

13265.title: immune modulation
13265.definition: Alteration of the immune response to alleviate harmful effects of the immune system or to promote its activity by changes in regulatory factors; often part of deliberate therapeutic intervention.

13266.title: immune regulation
13266.definition: Capacity of the immune system to regulate itself so that an immune response does not become excessive and cause tissue damage, autoimmune reactions, or allergic reactions.

13267.title: immune reserve hypothesis
13267.definition: Hypothesis that the immune response involves multiple redundancies that are capable of compensating for acute reductions in certain immune functions.

I02977.title: immune response
I02977.definition: Selective reaction of the body to substances that are foreign to it, or that the immune system identifies as foreign, shown by the production of antibodies and antibody-bearing cells or by a cell-mediated hypersensitivity reaction.

13269.title: immune response genes
13269.definition: Genes, including those within the major histocompatibility complex (MHC), that together determine the overall level of immune response to a given antigen.

13268.title: immune response-associated protein
13268.definition: Protein found in antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and B lymphocytes in mice.

13270.title: immune surveillance
13270.definition: Recognition, and in some cases elimination, of tumor cells by the immune system before they become clinically detectable.

13271.title: immune system
13271.definition: Integrated network of organs, glands, and tissues that has evolved to protect the body from foreign substances, including bacteria, viruses, and other infection-causing parasites and pathogens.

13272.title: immunity
13272.definition: Inherited, acquired, or induced resistance to infection by a specific pathogen.

I02978.title: immunization
I02978.definition: The administration of an antigen to an animal in order to stimulate the production of antibodies by that organism. Also, the administration of antigens, antibodies or lymphocytes to an animal to generate the corresponding active, passive or adaptive immunity.

13273.title: immunoactivation
13273.definition: Activation of the immune system as a whole to react more rapidly to antigens.

13274.title: immunoactivator
13274.definition: Substance that activates the immune system as a whole to react more rapidly to antigens.

13275.title: immunoadsorption
13275.definition: Method for removal of antibody or antigen by allowing it to bind to a corresponding antigen or antibody immobilized in the solid phase.

I02979.title: immunoassay
I02979.definition: A ligand-binding assay that uses a specific antigen or antibody, capable of binding to the analyte, to identify and quantify substances. The antibody can be linked to a radiosotope (radioimmunoassay, RIA), or to an enzyme which catalyses an easily monitored reaction (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, ELISA), or to a highly fluorescent compound by which the location of an antigen can be visualized (immunofluorescene).

13276.title: immunoblot
13276.definition: Supporting substrate [often a nitrocellulose, nylon, or poly(vinylidene fluoride) membrane] onto which proteins that have been separated by gel electrophoresis are transferred and then identified by the binding of specific antibodies.

09671.title: immunoblotting
09671.definition: Technique that uses antibodies (or other specific ligands in related techniques) to identify target proteins among a number of unrelated protein species.

09672.title: immunochemical specificity
09672.definition: The extent to which the immunoassay responds only to (all subsets of) a specific analyte and not to other substances of similar structure that are present in the sample.

I02980.title: immunochemistry
I02980.definition: Study of biochemical and molecular aspects of immunology, especially the nature of antibodies, antigens and their interactions.

13277.title: immunocompetence
13277.definition: Having the ability to exhibit an immune response.

09673.title: immunocomplex
09673.definition: Product of an antigen-antibody reaction that may also contain components of the complement.

13278.title: immunocompromised
13278.definition: Unable to mount a full or effective immune response.

13279.title: immunoconjugate
13279.definition: Antibody or antibody fragment to which a functional molecule, such as a drug, has been chemically linked.

13280.title: immunocytokine
13280.definition: Antibody or antibody fragment to which a cytokine has been chemically linked.

13281.title: immunodeficiency
13281.definition: Inability to produce a normal repertoire of antibodies or immunologically sensitized T lymphocytes, especially in response to specific antigens.

13282.title: immunodominant epitope
13282.definition: Epitope in an antigen that is preferentially recognized by T cells, which then come to dominate the immune response.

13283.title: immunodysregulation–polyendocrinopathy–enteropathy, X-linked
13283.definition: X-linked syndrome characterized by immunodysregulation, polyendocrinopathy (diabetes mellitus type 1, thyroiditis), hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, dermatitis, and enteropathy, caused by mutations in the gene encoding Foxp3.

13284.title: immunoediting
13284.definition: Process of continuing immunosuppression of immunogenic tumor cells, which may finally result in the selection of non-immunogenic tumor cells. It consists of the steps immune elimination, immune equilibrium, and immune escape.

09926.title: immunoelectrophoresis
09926.definition: Biochemical methods for separation and characterization of proteins based on electrophoresis and reaction with antibodies.

13285.title: immunofluorescence
13285.definition: Technique for detection of cell- or tissue-associated antigens by the use of a fluorescently tagged ligand, e.g., an anti-immunoglobulin (Ig) conjugated to fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC).

I02981.title: immunogen
I02981.definition: A substance that elicits a cellular immune response and/or antibody production (cf. antigen).

I02982.title: immunoglobulin
I02982.definition: A protein of the globulin-type found in serum or other body fluids that possesses antibody activity. An individual Ig molecule is built up from two light (L) and two heavy (H) polypeptide chains linked together by disulfide bonds. Igs are divided into five classes based on antigenic and structural differences in the H chains.

13286.title: immunoglobulin A
13286.definition: Class of immunoglobulin (Ig) characterized by $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ heavy chains.

09674.title: immunoglobulin class
09674.definition: Classification of immunoglobulins based on antigenic and structural differences of the heavy peptide chain.

13287.title: immunoglobulin D
13287.definition: Class of immunoglobulin (Ig) characterized by $\updelta\!$ heavy chains.

13288.title: immunoglobulin E
13288.definition: Class of immunoglobulin (Ig) characterized by $\upvarepsilon\!$ heavy chains.

13290.title: immunoglobulin E-binding Fc receptors
13290.definition: High-affinity IgE-binding ${\rm{Fc\mbox{-}}}\upvarepsilon\!{\rm{\mbox{-}R}}$ type I receptors are expressed on mast cells and basophils and interact with IgE antibodies with high affinity.

13291.title: immunoglobulin E-mediated hypersensitivity
13291.definition: State in which an individual reacts with allergic effects caused fundamentally by the reaction of antigen-specific immunoglobulin E (IgE) following exposure to a certain substance (allergen) after having been exposed previously to the same substance.

13292.title: immunoglobulin G
13292.definition: Class of immunoglobulin (Ig) characterized by \(\upgamma\) heavy chains.

13294.title: immunoglobulin gene superfamily
13294.definition: Genes encoding proteins containing one or more immunoglobulin (Ig) domains (homology units) that are homologous to either Ig variable (V) region or constant (C) region domains. Cell surface and soluble molecules mediating recognition, adhesion, or binding functions in and outside the immune system, derived from the same precursor, belong to this family of molecules (e.g., immunoglobulin, T-cell receptor (TCR), major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I and class II molecules, CD4, CD8, and $\ce{Fc\upgamma\!R}$).

13293.title: immunoglobulin M
13293.definition: Class of immunoglobulin (Ig) characterized by \(\upmu\) heavy chains.

13295.title: immunoglobulin superfamily
13295.definition: Large family of proteins characterized by possession of 'immunoglobulin-type' domains of approximately 110 amino acids folded into two \(\ce{\upbeta\mbox{-}pleated sheets}\). Members include immunoglobulins \(A\), \(E\), \(G\), \(M\) (IgA, IgE, IgG, and IgM), T-cell receptors (TCRs), and human leukocyte antigen (HLA) major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules.

13296.title: immunohistochemistry
13296.definition: Detection of cell-associated molecules in the light microscope with antibodies labeled with enzymes that change a substrate into a colored precipitate.

13297.title: immunological ignorance
13297.definition: Absence of a pathogenic autoimmune response in spite of the concomitant presence in the host of the autoantigen and T cells bearing the specific autoreactive T-cell receptor (TCR).

13298.title: immunological incompetence
13298.definition: Inability of the immune system to function in a normal fashion.

13300.title: immunological memory
13300.definition: Ability of the immune system to respond faster and more effectively to subsequent exposures to an antigen following a primary immune response to the same antigen.

13301.title: immunological synapse
13301.definition: Contact point between the T cell and antigen-presenting cell (APC) that is generated by reorganization and clustering of cell surface molecules in lipid rafts. The synapse facilitates interactions between T-cell receptor (TCR) and major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules, and between adhesion molecules, thereby potentiating a TCR-mediated activation signal.

13302.title: immunological tolerance
13302.definition: Persistent specific immunological unresponsiveness toward a substance that would normally be expected to elicit an immune response, resulting from previous non-sensitizing exposure to an antigen.

13299.title: immunologically privileged site
13299.definition: Any of various sites in the body where foreign tissue grafts do not induce an immune reaction.

13303.title: immunology
13303.definition: Science that deals with the immune system including cell-mediated immunity (CMI) and humoral aspects of immunity and immune responses.

13304.title: immunomagnetic separation
13304.definition: Method of separating specific cell types or macromolecules with the aid of cell-specific antibodies coupled to paramagnetic beads.

13305.title: immunomodulation
13305.definition: Modification of the functioning of the immune system by the action of a substance that increases or reduces the ability to produce an immune response.

13306.title: immunopathology
13306.definition:
1) Study of diseases of the immune system.
2) The occurrence of such diseases.

13308.title: immunopharmacology
13308.definition:
1) Study of the immune system using drugs as diagnostic tools.
2) Use of pharmaceutical molecules to support and stimulate the immune system in patients with immunodeficiency, or to suppress or specifically influence the reactivity of the immune system in order to control a pathological immune reaction or disease.

13309.title: immunophenotyping
13309.definition: Use of a panel of antibodies to determine a subset of proteins expressed on the surface of a cell or heterogeneous group of cells, often for diagnostic purposes, e.g., identifying the presence of leukemia cells in a population of lymphocytes.

13310.title: immunophilin
13310.definition: Any of a group of cytoplasmic proteins in T cells that are targets of the immunosuppressant drugs cyclosporin A, tacrolimus (fujimycin), rapamycin, and related compounds.

13311.title: immunopotentiation
13311.definition: Enhancement of the capacity of the immune system to produce an effective response.

13312.title: immunoprecipitate
13312.definition: Precipitate formed in an antigen–antibody reaction.

09675.title: immunoprecipitation
09675.definition: Isolation and concentration of an antigen by forming a precipitate with an antibody.

I02983.title: immunoradiometric assay
I02983.definition: An assay based on the reversible and non-covalent binding of an antigen by a specific antibody labelled with a radioactive nuclide as a tracer.

09676.title: immunoreactivity
09676.definition: Kinetic property of the immune response caused by an antigen.

13313.title: immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motif
13313.definition: Consensus sequence for src-family tyrosine kinases, found in the cytoplasmic domains of several signaling molecules including the signal transduction units of lymphocyte antigen receptors and of Fc receptors.

13314.title: immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibitory motif
13314.definition: Consensus sequence present in the cytoplasmic domains of certain cell surface molecules [e.g., Fc \(\upgamma\) RIIB, inhibitory natural killer (NK) cell receptors] and which mediates inhibitory signals.

13316.title: immunosensitizer
13316.definition: Substance that makes the immune system more reactive to antigens.

09677.title: immunosensor
09677.definition: Biosensor where one of the immunointeracting partners (an antibody or an antigen as the analyte) is immobilised on the surface of a physicochemical transducer.

10242.title: immunosorbents
10242.definition: Porous material with surface bound monoclonal or polyclonal antibodies capable of selective extraction of target analytes by formation of reversible antibody-antigen (compound) binding complexes.

13317.title: immunostimulating complex
13317.definition: Immunological adjuvant composed of saponin, cholesterol, phospholipid, and an immunogen, usually protein.

13318.title: immunostimulation
13318.definition: Increase in immune function, e.g., by use of bacille Calmette–Guérin (BCG) vaccine or drugs.

13319.title: immunosuppressant
13319.definition: Substance that depresses the function of the immune system.

I02984.title: immunosuppression
I02984.definition: Reduction in the functional capacity of the immune response; may be due to:  Inhibition of the normal response of the immune system to an antigen.   Prevention, by chemical or biological means, of the production of an antibody to an antigen by inhibition of the processes of transcription, translation or formation of tertiary structure.

13320.title: immunosuppressive
13320.definition: Causing depression of the normal function of the immune system.

13321.title: immunosurveillance
13321.definition: Mechanisms by which the immune system is able to recognize and destroy malignant cells before the formation of an overt tumor.

13322.title: immunotherapy
13322.definition: Treatment or prevention of a disease using agents that can modify the immune response.

13324.title: immunotoxicant
13324.definition: Substance that is harmful to the immune system.

14409.title: immunotoxicity
14409.definition: Ability of a physical, chemical, or biological agent to induce adverse effects in the immune system.

13325.title: immunotoxicology
13325.definition: Discipline applying cardinal principals of both immunology and toxicology to study the ability of certain substances to alter the immune response.

13326.title: immunotoxin
13326.definition: Biochemical conjugate, or recombinant fusion protein, consisting of an immune targeting molecule such as an antibody or antibody fragment together with a cytotoxic molecule.

09255.title: impact energy
09255.definition: Kinetic energy of particles on impact with a sample surface.

08831.title: impact ionization
08831.definition: Charge carrier generation by another charge carrier possessing a high kinetic energy, which knocks an electron out of the HOMO into the LUMO or still higher state so creating a new electron-hole pair.

I02987.title: impact parameter
I02987.definition: In simple hard sphere collision theory the distance of closest approach that would result for two particles in a collision if the particle trajectories were undeflected by the collision.

IT07175.title: impact-modified polymer
IT07175.definition: Polymeric material whose impact resistance and toughness have been increased by the incorporation of phase microdomains of a rubbery material.

I02985.title: impaction
I02985.definition: A forcible contact of particles of matter with a surface.

I02988.title: impedance
I02988.definition: Complex representation of potential difference divided by the complex representation of the current.

09169.title: impedimetry
09169.definition: Measurement principle in which the complex electric impedance of a system is measured, usually as a function of a small amplitude sinusoidal electrode potential.

10840.title: imperforate anus
10840.definition: Congenital absence of an anal opening due to the persistence of epithelial plug (persistence of the anal membrane) or to complete absence of the anal canal.

12255.title: impermeable
12255.definition: Adjective describing the flow behaviour of a macromolecule in solution or a dispersed entity when, due to hydrodynamic interaction, the solvent or dispersion medium within the domain of the macromolecule or dispersed entity is essentially immobilised and moves with the dissolved macromolecule or dispersed entity.

I02989.title: impingement
I02989.definition: Equivalent to impaction; often refers to impaction on a liquid surface.

I02990.title: impinger
I02990.definition: A sampling instrument employing impingement for the collection of particulate matter. Common types are: the midget impinger employing impingement in \(1{-}10\ \rm{cm}^{3}\) water,  the standard impinger employing impingement in \(75\ \rm{cm}^{3}\) water and  dry impingers.  Impingers are also suitable for sampling certain gases and vapours.

10841.title: implantation
10841.definition: Embedding of the early embryo in the lining of the uterus.

09256.title: implanted areic dose
09256.definition: Number, \(N_{\rm{imp}}\), of energetic particles of a specified type incident on a solid within a surface area \(A\) and stopped within the solid divided by \(A\). \(D_{\rm{imp}} = N_{\rm{imp}}/A\).

10842.title: imposex
10842.definition: Pseudohermaphroditic condition in female gastropods (snails) manifested by the development (imposition) of male characteristics such as a penis or vas deferens.

I02991.title: imprecision
I02991.definition: Variation of the result in a set of replicate measurements. This can be expressed, e.g. as the standard deviation or coefficient of variation (relative standard deviation). This term may have a more general meaning, e.g. if the replicates constitute a batch or involve different instruments, laboratories and analyst.

I02992.title: impregnation
I02992.definition: The modification of the separation properties of the chromatographic bed used in planar chromatography by appropriate additives.

IT07246.title: impregnation
IT07246.definition: Penetration of monomeric, oligomeric, or polymeric liquids into an assembly of fibres.

09509.title: imprint lithography
09509.definition: Patterns created by mechanical deformation of an imprint resist and a subsequent curing process.

10843.title: imprinting
10843.definition: Differential expression of a gene, depending on whether it was transmitted through the sperm or the egg.

08615.title: improper rotation axis
08615.definition: In spectroscopy, a rotation-reflection axis, which is a symmetry element such that rotation by \(2\pi/n\) about the axis followed by reflection through a plane perpendicular to the axis transforms an object into itself.

I02993.title: improved canonical variational transition-state theory
I02993.definition: A modification of canonical variational transition-state theory in which, for energies below the threshold energy, the position of the dividing surface is taken to be that of the microcanonical threshold energy. This forces the contributions to rate constant to be zero below the threshold energy. A compromise dividing surface is then chosen so as to minimize the contributions to the rate constant made by reactants having higher energies.

15808.title: in silico
15808.definition: Phrase applied to data generated and analyzed using computer modeling and information technology.

I03060.title: in situ micro-X-ray diffraction
I03060.definition: Any technique which utilizes the diffraction of X-rays generated in a microstructural domain of a solid under bombardment with a finely focused electron beam, thus providing an X-ray diffraction pattern of this microstructural domain. The pattern can be recorded with a film either on the reflection or transmission side of the specimen (in the latter case the crystalline sample has to be a thin film or a small particle).

I03059.title: in situ microanalysis
I03059.definition: Term used for direct analytical investigation of the microstructural domains of a solid by focused beams of particles and radiation. Analytical characterization includes obtaining information about type, quantity and distribution of the elements, their state of chemical bonding, morphology and crystalline (geometric) and electronic structure of the individual phases. The combination of this information serves as a basis for the property-relevant characterization of solids.

I03153.title: in vitro
I03153.definition: In glass, referring to a study in the laboratory usually involving isolated organ, tissue, cell, or biochemical systems.

10681.title: in vitro estrogen activity assay
10681.definition:
Procedure in which a tumor cell line is exposed to a test substance and activation of the estrogen receptor is studied by a reporter molecule in order to assess the estrogen-sensitivity of the tumor.
Test using estrogen-sensitive cells to evaluate estrogenic activity of a substance or environmental sample.

10866.title: in vitro fertilization
10866.definition: Fertilization outside the body, used as a treatment for infertility.

I03154.title: in vivo
I03154.definition: In the living body, referring to a study performed on a living organism.

08079.title: in-house reference material
08079.definition: Reference material produced and used by an analytical laboratory.

I03045.title: in-laboratory processing
I03045.definition: The selection, removal and preparation of the test (or analytical) portions from the laboratory sample. The processing may include a reduction in the size of the unit(s) (division) and particle size (reduction), as well as mixing to achieve homogeneity.

10302.title: in-line extraction
10302.definition: Coupling of a flow system with extraction device to a detector without flow interruption.

10269.title: in-needle capillary adsorption trap
10269.definition: In-tube format device with a sorbent-coated capillary placed inside a needle.

I03055.title: in-out isomerism
I03055.definition: Isomerism found in bicyclic systems having long enough bridges to allow the bridgehead exocyclic bond or lone pair of electrons to point either inside the structure or outside.

14023.title: in-scattering
14023.definition: Physical phenomenon considering scattered radiative energy from rays in any direction \(\mathit{\Omega}'\) into the direction \(\mathit{\Omega}\) of the rays considered in the radiative transfer equation (RTE).

IT07624.title: in situ composite formation
IT07624.definition: Process for preparing a polymer composite by  forming the filler or reinforcement in an existing polymer or  polymerizing monomers in the presence of dispersed filler.

10303.title: in-syringe microextraction
10303.definition: Batch-type extraction in which the barrel of a syringe pump is used as the device for liquid-phase microextraction or dispersive solid-phase microextraction.

10270.title: in-tube solid-phase microextraction
10270.definition: Extraction utilizing a coated open tubular or packed capillary tube as the extraction phase in a flow system.

I02995.title: inaccuracy
I02995.definition: A quantitative term to describe the (lack of) accuracy of a chemical measurement process; comprises the imprecision and the bias. Inaccuracy must be viewed as a two-component quantity (vector); imprecision and bias should never be combined to give a scalar measure for chemical measurement process inaccuracy. (One or the other component may, however, be negligible under certain circumstances.) Inaccuracy should not be confused with uncertainty. Inaccuracy (imprecision, bias) is characteristic of the measurement process, whereas error and uncertainty are characteristics of a result. (The latter characteristic, of course, derives from the imprecision and bounds for bias of the chemical measurement process.)

13327.title: inactivated vaccine
13327.definition: Vaccine formulated from the whole microorganism that has been rendered unable to reproduce or cause disease, often by mutation or heat denaturation.

15199.title: inactivation factor
15199.definition: Number that expresses the reduction in the numbers of a microorganism, brought about by a sterilization process.

14150.title: inactive
14150.definition: Sample that, at the tested concentration, does not produce a response above the hit threshold in an assay.

10844.title: inbred strain
10844.definition: Strain of an animal that has been inbred by brother-sister matings for more than \(\pu{20}\) generations, and consequently all the individuals of the strain are more than \(\pu{98\%}\) genetically identical.

11455.title: InChIKey
11455.definition: A fixed length (character) condensed digital representation of the InChI that is not human-understandable.

IT06828.title: incidence
IT06828.definition: Number of occurrences of illness commencing, or of persons falling ill, during a given period in a specific population: usually expressed as a rate.

15809.title: incidence rate
15809.definition: Measure of the frequency at which new events occur in a population.

08487.title: incident power
08487.definition: Power supplied by a generator to the plasma.

I02997.title: incinerator
I02997.definition: Equipment in which solid, liquid or gaseous combustible wastes are ignited and burned. Types include flue-fed and multiple-chamber incinerators with several stages of combustion.

14751.title: incipient LC50
14751.definition: Concentration of a chemical which is lethal to \(\pu{50\%}\) of the test organisms as a result of exposure for periods long enough for acute lethal action to cease; in other words, the concentration below which \(\pu{50\%}\) of individuals will have a normal lifespan despite the previous exposure to a toxicant.

11828.title: inclusion body
11828.definition: Particle in a cell, detectable under the light microscope.

I02998.title: inclusion compound
I02998.definition: A complex in which one component (the host) forms a cavity or, in the case of a crystal, a crystal lattice containing spaces in the shape of long tunnels or channels in which molecular entities of a second chemical species (the guest) are located. There is no covalent bonding between guest and host, the attraction being generally due to van der Waals forces. If the spaces in the host lattice are enclosed on all sides so that the guest species is 'trapped' as in a cage, such compounds are known as clathrates or 'cage compounds'.

I02999.title: incoherent radiation
I02999.definition: Not having the properties of coherent radiation.

08367.title: incredible natural-abundance double-quantum transfer experiment
08367.definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment designed to show homonuclear spin-spin coupling correlations between low natural abundance nuclei such as \(\ce{^{13}C}\).

I03003.title: increment
I03003.definition: An individual portion of material collected by a single operation of a sampling device. Increments may be reduced individually or tested either (a) individually or (b) combined with other increments with the resulting composite reduced in size and tested as a single unit. Increments are created by the sampling operation and are usually taken from parts of a lot separated in time or space. Increments of a bulk population correspond to units of a packaged population.

14752.title: incremental unit risk estimate
14752.definition: For an air pollutant, the additional lifetime cancer risk occurring in a hypothetical population in which all individuals are exposed continuously from birth throughout their lifetimes to a concentration of \(\pu{1 \upmu g m-3}\) of the pollutant in the air they breathe.

14753.title: independent joint action
14753.definition: Production of an effect by each toxicant in a given exposure that is independent of the others and occurs by a different mode of action.

14754.title: index of biological integrity
14754.definition: Composite index combining 12 qualities of fish communities of warm-water, low-gradient streams to determine the level of stream degradation.

I03004.title: indicated hydrogen
I03004.definition: Under certain circumstances it is necessary to indicate in the name of a ring, or ring system, containing the maximum number of non-cumulative double bonds, one or more positions where no multiple bond is attached. This is done by specifying the presence of an 'extra' hydrogen atom at such positions by citation of the appropriate numbered locant followed by an italicized capital H.Example:  A second type of indicated hydrogen (sometimes referred to as 'added hydrogen') describes hydrogen atoms added to a specific structure as a consequence of the addition of a suffix or a prefix describing a structural modification. This type of indicated hydrogen is normally cited in parentheses after the locant of the additional feature.Example:

15810.title: indication
15810.definition: Quantity value provided by a measuring instrument or a measuring system.

09046.title: indicator consumption error
09046.definition: Systematic measurement error from the reaction of a visual indicator with a reactant in a titration.

I03006.title: indicator electrode
I03006.definition: An electrode that serves as a transducer responding to the excitation signal (if any) and to the composition of the solution being investigated, but that does not affect an appreciable change of bulk composition within the ordinary duration of a measurement.

14755.title: indicator species
14755.definition: Species whose presence shows the occurrence of defined environmental conditions.

I03008.title: indifferent absorbing ion
I03008.definition: An ion which absorbs through coulomb forces only and which is hence only repelled by surfaces of like sign, attracted by surfaces of opposite sign, and is not absorbed on an uncharged surface.

14756.title: indigenous
14756.definition: Native to a given region or ecosystem.

09678.title: indirect agglutination
09678.definition: Agglutination in which antigen is first immobilised artificially onto the particulate surfaces, either by physical adsorption or by chemical and/or immunochemical linkers.

I03010.title: indirect amplification
I03010.definition: A type of amplification reaction where the constituent required is associated with some other constituent which is then amplified and measured.

14022.title: indirect bandgap semiconductor
14022.definition: Semiconductor or dielectric materials with a first band-to-band transition from the highest level in the valence band to the lowest level in the conduction band requiring the change of electron momentum, that is \(\boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{max}} \neq \boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{min}}\), where \(\boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{max}}\) and \(\boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{min}}\) are the momentum vectors of electrons of the highest level in the valence band and the lowest level in the conduction band, respectively.

14757.title: indirect ecological effect
14757.definition:
Effect resulting from imposed biotic or abiotic factors which alter ecosystem properties that in turn favor or disfavor an ecological component of importance (e.g., a species) and thus indirectly lead to improved or reduced fitness of that species.
Result of imposed biotic or abiotic factors allowing indigenous or new species to dominate, thereby affecting ecosystem composition.

15811.title: indirect exposure
15811.definition:
Exposure to a substance in a medium or vehicle other than the one originally receiving the substance.
Exposure of people to a substance by contact with a person directly exposed.

13328.title: indirect immunofluorescence
13328.definition: Method of visualizing an antigen in which an unlabeled antibody against the antigen is reacted with it first, and then is detected by staining with a second fluorescently tagged immunoglobulin G (IgG) directed against the first antibody.

14758.title: indirect photolysis
14758.definition: Degradation of a contaminant through interaction with other molecules in solution that have absorbed light energy. This can occur through energy transfer or by chemical reaction with short-lived reactive species.

I03011.title: indirect reaction
I03011.definition: A chemical process in which the reactive complex has a lifetime that is longer than its period of rotation is called an indirect reaction (in contrast to a direct reaction). In a molecular-beam experiment the products of such reactions are scattered at random with reference to the centre of mass of the system. Indirect reactions are also called complex-mode reactions. (They are sometimes called complex reactions, but this usage is not recommended in view of the danger of confusion with composite reactions, which occur in more than one step).

14759.title: indirect toxicity
14759.definition: Adverse effects that result from agent(s) acting on and producing changes in the chemical, physical, and (or) biological environment external to the organisms under study (e.g., decrease in food for predatory species due to direct toxicity from a chemical to prey may produce adverse effects in the predator species due to starvation rather than inducing any direct chemical toxicity in predator organisms).

08730.title: indirectly-ionizing radiation
08730.definition: Beam of electrically neutral particles that cause ionization by interacting with atoms in a material, producing electrically-charged particles that subsequently cause direct ionization in the material.

14761.title: individual effective dose
14761.definition: Concept forming the basis for most dose–response models, which holds that there exists a smallest dose needed to kill any particular individual. The IED is a characteristic of an individual.

IT07055.title: individual gauge for localized orbitals
IT07055.definition: A method of calculation of nuclear shieldings, in which localized molecular orbitals associated with inner shell, bonding orbitals, and lone pairs have unique origins for the calculation of diamagnetic and paramagnetic terms. With this method, satisfactory estimates of NMR chemical shifts for elements in the first and second rows can be achieved in ab initio calculations with basis sets of moderate size provided sufficiently accurate molecular geometries are used.

I03014.title: individual perception threshold
I03014.definition: A term used in odour testing which signifies the lowest concentration of a particular species at which a subject indicates both an initial positive and repeated response.

15812.title: individual protective device
15812.definition: Device for individual use for protection of the whole body, eyes, respiratory pathways, or skin of workers against hazardous and harmful production factors.

15813.title: individual risk
15813.definition: Probability that an individual person will experience an adverse effect.

13329.title: indolamine-2,3-dioxygenase
13329.definition: Enzyme catalyzing the initial rate-limiting step of tryptophan degradation.

10321.title: induced abortion
10321.definition: Intentional termination of a pregnancy with death of the embryo or fetus.

10849.title: induced pluripotent stem cell
10849.definition: Pluripotent stem cell that is generated from an adult cell by genetic reprogramming.

I03016.title: induced reaction
I03016.definition: A reaction which occurs or is accelerated only if another reaction is simultaneously occurring in the same system. The substance, which causes an induced reaction, is termed inductor. The inductor, unlike the catalyst, is used up irreversibly during the process.

I03017.title: inducer
I03017.definition: A small molecule that triggers gene transcription by binding to a regulator protein (cf. enzyme induction). It acts by combining with the corresponding repressor protein to bring about an allosteric change so that the repressor is made incapable of combining with the operator of the system.

13330.title: inducible co-stimulatory protein
13330.definition: Highly specific receptor for the protein B7H/B7RP-1 that is expressed on the surface of B cells and macrophages, and also appears on the surface of T cells during the process of T-cell activation.

I03018.title: induction
I03018.definition: An increase in the rate of synthesis of an (inducible) enzyme in response to the action of an inducer or environmental conditions. An inducer is often the substrate of the inducible enzyme or a structurally similar substance (gratuitous inducer) that is not metabolized.The experimental elicitation of lytic growth by a prophage from lysogenic bacteria.

I03019.title: induction period
I03019.definition: The initial slow phase of a chemical reaction which later accelerates. Induction periods are often observed with radical reactions, but they may also occur in other systems (for example before steady-state concentration of the reactants is reached).

I03021.title: inductive effect
I03021.definition: In strict definition, an experimentally observable effect (on rates of reaction, etc.) of the transmission of charge through a chain of atoms by electrostatic induction. A theoretical distinction may be made between the field effect, and the inductive effect as models for the coulomb interaction between a given site within a molecular entity and a remote unipole or dipole within the same entity. The experimental distinction between the two effects has proved difficult, except for molecules of peculiar geometry, which may exhibit 'reversed field effects'. Ordinarily the inductive effect and the field effect are influenced in the same direction by structural changes in the molecule and the distinction between them is not clear. This situation has led many authors to include the field effect in the term 'inductive effect'. Thus the separation of values into inductive and resonance components does not imply the exclusive operation of a through-bonds route for the transmission of the non-conjugative part of the substituent effect. To indicate the all-inclusive use of the term inductive, the phrase 'so-called inductive effect' is sometimes used. Certain modern theoretical approaches suggest that the 'so-called inductive effect' reflects a field effect rather than through-bonds transmission.

08488.title: inductively-coupled plasma
08488.definition: Plasma produced by induction by means of a high-frequency (about \(\pu{2500 Hz}\)) electromagnetic field. The region of gas at high temperature and free from the field is taken as the region of observation.

08490.title: inductively-coupled plasma mass spectrometry
08490.definition: Measurement method of atomic spectrometry that uses an inductively-coupled plasma to excite and ionize atoms with measurement of the number and kind of ions in the plasma using mass spectrometry.
