08491.title: inductively-coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy
08491.definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy that uses an inductively-coupled plasma to excite and ionize atoms with measurement of the number and kind of ions in the plasma from their emission of electromagnetic radiation (see optical emission spectroscopy).

08492.title: inductively-coupled plasma robustness
08492.definition: Ability of an inductively-coupled plasma to withstand slight modification in the operating conditions and/or matrix composition with no significant changes in its fundamental characteristics (i.e., temperatures, electron number density) or the analytical figures of merit (i.e., sensitivity, detection limits or signal-to-noise ratio)

08489.title: inductively-coupled plasma spectrometry
08489.definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy that uses an inductively-coupled plasma to excite and ionize atoms.

08493.title: inductively-coupled plasma thermal pinch
08493.definition: Decrease in the inductively-coupled plasma volume normally caused when an organic volatile solution is delivered to it. Organic vapours diffuse towards the outermost area of the plasma and its volume decreases.

08494.title: inductively-coupled plasma torch
08494.definition: Quartz component of an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer where the plasma is generated and stabilized.

I03022.title: inductomeric effect
I03022.definition: A molecular polarizability effect occurring by the inductive mechanism of electron displacement. The consideration of such an effect and the descriptive term have been regarded as obsolescent or even obsolete, but in recent years theoretical approaches have reintroduced substituent polarizability as a factor governing reactivity, etc. and its parametrization has been proposed.

14762.title: industrial ecology
14762.definition: Study of the flows of materials and energy in the industrial environment and the effects of these flows on natural systems.

14763.title: industrial melanism
14763.definition: Gradual increase to predominance of melanic forms in populations from industrialized regions.

09334.title: inelastic electron scattering background
09334.definition: Intensity distribution in a spectrum for particles originally at one energy but which are emitted at lower energies due to one or more inelastic scattering processes.

09335.title: inelastic electron scattering background subtraction
09335.definition: Subtraction of a chosen inelastic electron scattering background from a measured spectrum in Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.

08616.title: inelastic electron tunnelling spectroscopy
08616.definition: Measurement method of vibrational spectroscopy to obtain spectra of molecules on metal oxide surfaces.

I03025.title: inelastic scattering
I03025.definition: If in a molecular collision there is transfer of energy among degrees of freedom, but no chemical reaction occurs, there is said to be inelastic scattering.

09336.title: inelastic scattering cross section
09336.definition: Cross section for inelastic scattering by an electron traversing a material.

I03026.title: inert
I03026.definition: Stable and unreactive under specified conditions.

15814.title: inert chemical
15814.definition: Substance that is not generally reactive.

I03027.title: inert gas
I03027.definition: A non-reactive gas under particular conditions. For example, nitrogen at ordinary temperatures and the noble gases (helium, argon, krypton, xenon and radon) are unreactive toward most species.

15815.title: inert ingredient
15815.definition: Any intentionally added ingredient of a mixture that does not contribute to the desired biological effect: This definition does not include impurities and does not imply that the inert ingredient has no biological effects.

I03028.title: inertial defect
I03028.definition: Difference of principal moments of inertia \(\mathit{\Delta} = I_{C} - I_{A} - I_{B}\). For planar molecules it is close to zero and for non-planar molecules it is negative.

I03029.title: inertial separator
I03029.definition: Any dry type collector which utilizes the relatively greater inertia of particles to effect their removal from a gas stream; e.g. cyclonic and impingement separators, gravity settling chambers and high-velocity gas reversal chambers.

14765.title: infauna
14765.definition: Animals living in the sediment of aquatic systems but not on the surface.

13331.title: infectious tolerance
13331.definition: Continuing state of tolerance that can be transferred by T lymphocytes from a tolerant animal.

11829.title: inferior cerebellar peduncle
11829.definition: Part of the cerebellum that is important for a number of motor functions, including balance, position sensing and coordination of movement.

10850.title: infertility
10850.definition: Persistent inability of either a male or a female to achieve conception or to produce offspring.

15333.title: infinite dilution
15333.definition: Limiting composition or other variable in a solution obtained by extrapolating to a value of zero for the variable describing the composition of the solution.

15334.title: infinite miscibility
15334.definition: Property of a system of forming a single phase at all relative proportions of its components.

I03030.title: infinite source thickness
I03030.definition: For a specified radiation, the minimum thickness of a flat preparation of a radioactive material where the intensity of the specified radiation at the surface does not increase when the thickness is increased by adding more of similar radioactive material.

13333.title: inflammasome
13333.definition: High-molecular-weight complex that activates inflammatory caspases and the cytokines interleukin-1$\ce{\upbeta\!}$ ($\ce{IL\mbox{-}1\upbeta\!}$) and IL-18.

11830.title: inflammation
11830.definition: Reaction of the body to injury or to infectious, allergic, or chemical irritation; characterized by redness, swelling, heat, and pain resulting from dilation of the blood vessels accompanied by loss of plasma and leukocytes into the tissues.

13334.title: inflammatory bowel disease
13334.definition: Group of chronic inflammatory conditions resulting in the inappropriate and persistent activation of the mucosal immune system of the bowel.

09987.title: influence nominal property
09987.definition: Nominal property that, in an examination, does not affect the nominal property that is actually examined, but affects the relation between the nominal indication on the examining system and the examination result.

09257.title: information depth
09257.definition: Maximum depth, normal to the surface, from which useful information is obtained.

09258.title: information radius
09258.definition: Maximum radius of a circular region, in the plane of the surface, from which useful information is obtained.

I03032.title: information theory
I03032.definition: As applied in reaction dynamics, information theory analyses the deviations of experimentally-determined energy distributions from predictions made on the basis of equal a priori probabilities for all possible outcomes.

IT07399.title: infrared
IT07399.definition: Region of the electromagnetic spectrum extending from \(780\ \rm{nm}\) to about \(20\,000\ \rm{nm}\).According to the CIE, the range between \(780\ \rm{nm}\) and \(1\ \rm{mm}\) is subdivided into:IR-A \(780\)–\(1400\ \rm{nm}\)IR-B \(1.4\)–\(3\ \unicode[times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\)IR-C \(3\ \unicode[times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\)–\(1\ \rm{mm}\)

08617.title: infrared radiation
08617.definition: Electromagnetic radiation of wavelength between approximately \(\pu{780 nm}\) and \(\pu{1000 \upmu m}\) or of wavenumber between approximately \(\pu{13000 cm-1}\) and \(\pu{10 cm-1}\).

08618.title: infrared spectroscopy
08618.definition: Measurement principle of vibrational spectroscopy using infrared radiation.

10851.title: infundibulum
10851.definition: Anatomical funnel-shaped opening, often referring to the hollow stalk that connects the hypothalamus and the posterior pituitary gland, or to the portion of the Fallopian tube that receives the ovum.

15816.title: infusion
15816.definition: Therapeutic introduction of a fluid other than blood, as a (usually saline) solution, into a vein.

15817.title: ingestion
15817.definition:
Process of taking food and drink into the body by mouth.
Process of taking in particles by a phagocytic cell.

10852.title: inguinal canal
10852.definition: Passage in the lower anterior abdominal wall, which in men conveys the spermatic cord and in women the round ligament of the uterus.

15818.title: inhalation
15818.definition: Act of drawing in of air, vapor, or gas and any suspended particulates into the lung.

15200.title: inhalation therapy
15200.definition: Administration of drugs directly to the respiratory tract, mostly by aerosols.

I03033.title: inherent viscosity
I03033.definition: The ratio of the natural logarithm of the relative viscosity, \(\eta _{\rm{r}}\), to the mass concentration of the polymer, \(c\), i.e. \[\eta _{\rm{inh}}\equiv \eta _{\ln} = \frac{\ln \eta _{\rm{r}}}{c}\] The quantity \(\eta _{\ln }\), with which the inherent viscosity is synonymous, is the logarithmic viscosity number.

15819.title: inherently biodegradable
15819.definition: Class of compounds for which there is unequivocal evidence of biodegradation (primary or ultimate) in any test of biodegradability.

10853.title: inhibin
10853.definition: Any of a group of peptide hormones secreted by the follicular granulosa cells of the ovary and the Sertoli cells of the testis, inhibiting follicle-stimulating hormone secretion by the anterior pituitary.

I03034.title: inhibition
I03034.definition: The decrease in rate of reaction brought about by the addition of a substance inhibitor), by virtue of its effect on the concentration of a reactant, catalyst or reaction intermediate. For example, molecular oxygen and p-benzoquinone can react as 'inhibitors' in many reactions involving radicals as intermediates by virtue of their ability to act as scavengers toward these radicals. If the rate of a reaction in the absence of inhibitor is \(v_{0}\) and that in the presence of a certain amount of inhibitor is \(v\), the degree of inhibition (\(i\)) is given by: \[i=\frac{v_{0}- v}{v_{0}}\]

12670.title: inhibition constant
12670.definition:
Equilibrium dissociation constant of an enzyme-inhibitor complex: \(K_{\rm{i}} = [\ce{E}][\ce{I}]/[\ce{EI}]\).
The equilibrium dissociation constant of a receptor-ligand complex.

I03035.title: inhibitor
I03035.definition: A substance that diminishes the rate of a chemical reaction; the process is called inhibition. Inhibitors are sometimes called negative catalysts, but since the action of an inhibitor is fundamentally different from that of a catalyst, this terminology is discouraged. In contrast to a catalyst, an inhibitor may be consumed during the course of a reaction. In enzyme-catalysed reactions an inhibitor frequently acts by binding to the enzyme, in which case it may be called an enzyme inhibitor.

I03036.title: inhibitory concentration
I03036.definition: Concentration of a substance that causes a defined inhibition of a given system: \(\rm{IC}_{50}\) is the median concentration that causes 50% inhibition.

I03037.title: inhibitory dose
I03037.definition: Dose of a substance that causes a defined inhibition of a given system: \(\rm{ID}_{50}\) is the median dose that causes 50% inhibition.

11832.title: inhibitory post-synaptic potential
11832.definition: Referring to a more negative membrane potential at the postsynaptic side of the synaptic cleft that renders the postsynaptic neuron less likely to generate an action potential.

I03038.title: inhomogeneity error
I03038.definition: An error due to inhomogenous distribution of absorbing species in the analytical sample. It may be observed by probing the sample volume with an incident beam of radiation of reduced cross-section.

08619.title: inhomogeneous broadening
08619.definition: Line-broadening by mechanisms that arise from an ensemble of spectroscopically non-equivalent molecules of the same species. Such molecules exist, for example, when molecules occupy non-equivalent sites in a condensed phase, and when gaseous molecules have different velocities and, thus, shift the observed wavenumber differently through the Doppler effect.

10854.title: iniencephaly
10854.definition: Malformation producing a cranial defect at the occiput, with the brain exposed, often combined with a cervical rachischisis and retroflexion.

08954.title: inifer
08954.definition: Substance that combines the properties of an initiator and a reversible chain-transfer agent.

08955.title: iniferter
08955.definition: Substance that combines the properties of an initiator, a reversible chain-transfer agent and a chain terminator or reversible deactivator.

08919.title: iniferter process
08919.definition: Stable-radical-mediated polymerization where the initiator and dormant species are iniferters.

14378.title: inisurf
14378.definition: Initiator with the properties of a surfactant.

I03041.title: initial state correlations
I03041.definition: These are correlations between the states of the products of a reaction and the initial states of the reactants. The correlations may relate to energy levels, quantum numbers, and symmetries.

09337.title: initial energy state
09337.definition: Core-hole excited state of an atom prior to Auger transition or to X-ray emission.

09338.title: initial energy state
09338.definition: Ground state of an atom prior to photoelectron emission.

08495.title: initial plasma radiation zone
08495.definition: Inductively-coupled plasma volume in inductively-coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy where the analytically-relevant light emission begins to be observed.

I03040.title: initial rate method
I03040.definition: A mode of measurement in a kinetic method of analysis, in which the initial reaction rate is determined (usually by the slope method) and utilized for the measurement of concentration.

09339.title: initial-state Auger parameter
09339.definition: \(\beta = 3E_{\rm{B}} + E_{\rm{K}}\), where \(E_{\rm{B}}\) and \(E_{\rm{K}}\) are, respectively, the binding energy of a photoelectron peak and the Fermi level referenced (see Fermi level referencing) kinetic energy of an Auger electron peak, each involving the same initial core level of the same element.

08956.title: initialization
08956.definition: Process for converting a starting coordination complex or precatalyst into an active catalyst.

16249.title: initialisation
16249.definition: Process for converting a starting initiator or chain transfer agent into a macro-initiator or macro-chain-transfer agent during reversible-deactivation polymerization (RDP).

08958.title: initialization efficiency
08958.definition: Efficiency of conversion of a starting initiator or transfer agent into a macro-initiator or macro-chain-transfer agent.

08957.title: initializer
08957.definition: Starting initiator or transfer agent in reversible-deactivation polymerization (RDP).

14766.title: initiating event
14766.definition: Specific action that results in a risk being incurred.

08959.title: initiating species
08959.definition: Species to which monomer adds or becomes inserted to start a chain polymerization.

I03042.title: initiation
I03042.definition: A reaction or process generating free radicals (or some other reactive reaction intermediates) which then induce a chain reaction. For example, in the chlorination of alkanes by a radical mechanism the initiation step is the dissociation of molecular chlorine.

I03043.title: initiator
I03043.definition: A substance introduced into a reaction system in order to bring about an initiation reaction.

08960.title: initiator efficiency
08960.definition: Number of growing chains initiated divided by the number of active-centers generated from initiator molecules.

15201.title: injection
15201.definition: Delivery of a generally sterile liquid medication into the body, or a vessel, tissue, or organ via syringe and needle.

I03044.title: injection temperature
I03044.definition: The temperature at the point of injection.

13335.title: innate immunity
13335.definition: Immunity that is not intrinsically affected by prior contact with antigen, i.e., all aspects of immunity not directly mediated by lymphocytes.

I03046.title: inner electric potential
I03046.definition: Quantity the gradient of which is equal to the negative of the electric field strength within the phase concerned. It can be calculated from the model of the phase. It is sometimes called the Galvani potential.

I03047.title: inner filter effect
I03047.definition: In an emission experiment, an apparent decrease in emission quantum yield and/or distortion of bandshape as a result of reabsorption of emitted radiation.During a light irradiation experiment, absorption of incident radiation by a species other than the intended primary absorber.

I03048.title: inner Helmholtz plane
I03048.definition: The locus of the electrical centres of specifically adsorbed ions.

I03049.title: inner layer
I03049.definition: The region between the outer Helmholtz plane and the interface.

I03050.title: inner orbital X-ray emission spectra
I03050.definition: X-ray spectral lines generated by the transition of electrons between 'inner orbitals'. The term 'inner orbital' serves to designate the sharp, not degenerate electronic levels of atoms in a solid and therefore is a general term for all orbitals except the valence band.

I03052.title: inner-sphere electron transfer
I03052.definition: Historically an electron transfer between two metal centres sharing a ligand or atom in their respective coordination shells. The definition has more recently been extended to any situation in which the interaction between the donor and acceptor centres in the transition state is significant (\(\pu{\gt 20 kJ mol-1}\)).

08925.title: inner-sphere electron transfer atom-transfer radical polymerization
08925.definition: Atom-transfer radical polymerization where the activation step involves direct atom or group transfer.

I03053.title: inoculation
I03053.definition: The introduction of a small sample of organisms (microbial, plant or animal cells) into a culture medium to act as a seed for the production of large numbers of the same organism by growth and propagation.

10243.title: inorganic oxide adsorbent
10243.definition: Adsorbent with site-specific polar and ion exchange functional groups that extract analytes from a gas or liquid phase by their complementary interactions with the surface.

IT07515.title: inorganic polymer
IT07515.definition: Polymer or polymer network with a skeletal structure that does not include carbon atoms.

IT07514.title: inorganic–organic polymer
IT07514.definition: Polymer or polymer network with a skeletal structure comprising inorganic and organic units.

I03056.title: input rate
I03056.definition: The number of samples that are processed by the instrument divided by time of operation. It should be stated if the residence time is included or not.

10856.title: insemination
10856.definition: Delivery of sperm into the female reproductive system for the purpose or with the result of causing pregnancy.

08368.title: insensitive nuclei enhanced by polarization transfer
08368.definition: Pulse sequence in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that involves the transfer of nuclear spin polarization from spins with large Boltzmann population differences to nuclear spins of interest with low Boltzmann population differences.

I03057.title: insert
I03057.definition: A sequence of foreign DNA introduced into a restriction site (insertion site, cloning site) of a vector DNA.

I03058.title: insertion
I03058.definition: A chemical reaction or transformation of the general type: $$\ce{X-Z + Y -> X-Y-Z}$$ in which the connecting atom or group $\ce{Y}$ replaces the bond joining the parts $\ce{X}$ and $\ce{Z}$ of the reactant $\ce{XZ}$. An example is the carbene insertion reaction:  The reverse of an insertion is called an extrusion.

08911.title: insertion polymerization
08911.definition: Chain polymerization in which monomer units are sequentially inserted into a specific site within a polymer structure with retention of chain-end functionality.

11834.title: insomnia
11834.definition: Inability to sleep during the period when sleep should normally occur.

08080.title: inspection
08080.definition: Examination of a product, process, service, or installation or their design and determination of conformity with specific requirements or on the basis of professional judgment, with general requirements.

I03061.title: instability
I03061.definition: A change which takes place in an instrument reading over a stated period of unattended operation for a given value of the air quality characteristic. It can be characterized by the variation with time of its mean, specifying the drift and by the dispersion. Span instability is the change which takes place in instrument span over a stated period of unattended operation. Zero instability is the change in instrument reading in response to a zero sample over a stated period of unattended operation.

IT07056.title: instability of Hartree–Fock solution
IT07056.definition: Existence of additional solutions to the equations of the Hartree–Fock method occurring usually in the case when potential energy surfaces of different electronic states are drawn close together. Within the spin-restricted Hartree–Fock method (RHF), singlet and triplet instabilities are distinguished. The former involves the existence of another solution with lower energy and the electron distribution of lower symmetry. It may be regarded as an indication that the initially assumed molecular shape needs correction. The triplet instability involves rejection of the condition of double occupancy of molecular orbitals and thus transition to the spin-unrestricted Hartree–Fock method (UHF). The triplet instability is a necessary, but insufficient, condition for the conclusion as to the biradical character of the ground state of a given system.

I03064.title: instantaneous sampling
I03064.definition: Obtaining a sample of the atmosphere in a period which is short compared with the duration of the sampling exercise. Such samples are often called 'grab' samples, a term not recommended. These are useful for the analysis of hydrocarbons and other complicated mixtures of trace gases which are relatively stable in a stainless steel canister or tank and can be transported back to the laboratory for chromatographic or other analysis which cannot be done satisfactorily in the field.

I03062.title: instantaneous current
I03062.definition: At a dropping electrode, the total current that flows at the instant when a time \(t\) has elapsed since the fall of the preceding drop. At any other electrode, the total current that flows at the instant when a time \(t\) has elapsed since the beginning of an electrolysis. The instantaneous current is usually time-dependent and may have the character of an adsorption, catalytic, diffusion, double-layer, or kinetic current, and may include a migration current. A plot of the dependence of instantaneous current on time is commonly called an 'i-t curve'.

I03063.title: instantaneous rate of flow
I03063.definition: The rate of increase of the mass of a drop at a particular instant \(t\) seconds after it has begun to form.

08257.title: instrument line shape
08257.definition: Idealized form of a feature in a spectrometer corresponding to a transition.

I03065.title: instrumental activation analysis
I03065.definition: A kind of activation analysis in which element specificity is obtained by using appropriate irradiation conditions, radiation measurement techniques and mathematical techniques for the interpretation of the measurement results.

I03066.title: instrumental dependability
I03066.definition: This relates to the frequency of failures which interrupt the operation of an instrument. It can be quantified, e.g. by the infrequency of breakdowns or by the availability of the instrument for use when required.

09259.title: instrumental depth resolution
09259.definition: Depth resolution in a sample arising from parameters of the instrument.

I03067.title: instrumental indication
I03067.definition: The observed deflection or rest point multiplied by the value of the division for the load in question.

15820.title: intake
15820.definition: Amount of a substance that is taken into the body, regardless of whether or not it is absorbed: The total daily intake is the sum of the daily intake by an individual from food, drinking-water, and inhaled air.

I03068.title: integral capacitance
I03068.definition: Integral capacitance (per unit area of electrode) is given by \[K=\frac{Q}{E- E_{Q=0}}\] where \(Q\) is the electric charge (per unit area of electrode), \(E\) is the potential of the electrode with respect to a reference electrode, and \(E_{Q=0}\) is the potential at the point of zero charge.

I03069.title: integral detector
I03069.definition: A device which measures the accumulated quantity of sample component(s) reaching the detector.

15821.title: integral indicator of toxic effect
15821.definition: Parameter (such as body weight or temperature) characterizing the overall changes in the general state of the organism exposed to a toxic substance.

08258.title: integrated intensity
08258.definition: Area under a spectral band in an absorption spectrum where the absorption is linearly proportional to the amount of absorber in unit area.

14767.title: integrated risk information system
14767.definition: USEPA database containing reference doses, slope factors, and drinking-water health advisories (one-day, ten-day, longer-term, and lifetime advisories), and associated information.

I03070.title: integrating sphere
I03070.definition: A hollow sphere having a highly reflecting inside surface used as a device to collect, with very high efficiency, light scattered or emitted from a sample contained in it or located outside and near one of the ports. Small ports allow the entrance of light and access to a detector.

08259.title: integration range
08259.definition: Frequency or wavenumber range over which the integrated intensity of an absorption band is measured by numerical integration of the area under the band.

10857.title: integrin
10857.definition: Any of a family of cell membrane glycoproteins that mediate cell-to-cell and cell-to-extracellular matrix interactions.

11835.title: intelligence quotient
11835.definition: Numeric measure of a person’s cognitive function based on one of several standardized tests of a problem-solving nature.

I03071.title: intended crossing
I03071.definition: Synonymous with avoided crossing. The term 'intended' should not be used in this context since it is an anthropomorphic term.

08260.title: intensified charge coupled device detector
08260.definition: Charge coupled device with a prior amplification system to improve sensitivity.

I03072.title: intensity
I03072.definition: The traditional term for photon flux, fluence rate, irradiance or radiant power (radiant flux). In terms of an object exposed to radiation, the term should now be used only for qualitative descriptions.

I03073.title: intensity
I03073.definition: The ratio of intensity of a separated ion beam to the intensity of the separated ion beam which has the greatest intensity. This ratio is generally equated to the normalized ratio of the heights of the respective peaks in the mass spectrum, with the height of the base peak being taken as 100.

I03074.title: intensive quantity
I03074.definition: Physical quantity whose magnitude is independent of the extent of the system.

I03075.title: interaction distance
I03075.definition: The farthest distance of approach of two particles at which it is discernible that they will not pass at the impact parameter.

10075.title: interaction effect
10075.definition: Effect of a factor where the term is the product of two or more factors.

09872.title: interactomics
09872.definition: Complex and comprehensive study of the interactions between various proteins and between protein and other molecules within a cell, such as nucleic acids and metabolites, as well as the consequences of these interactions.

09340.title: interatomic Auger process
09340.definition: Auger transition in which at least one of the final electron vacancies is localized in valence levels or molecular orbitals of atoms adjacent to the atom in which the initial vacancy occurred.

I03076.title: intercalation compounds
I03076.definition: Compounds resulting from reversible inclusion, without covalent bonding, of one kind of molecule in a solid matrix of another compound, which has a laminar structure. The host compound, a solid, may be macromolecular, crystalline or amorphous.

IT07248.title: intercalation
IT07248.definition: Process by which a substance becomes transferred into pre-existing spaces of molecular dimensions in a second substance.

I03077.title: intercalation reaction
I03077.definition: Reaction, generally reversible, that involves the penetration of a host material by guest species without causing a major structural modification of the host.

13336.title: intercellular adhesion molecule
13336.definition: Member of the immunoglobulin superfamily that interacts with integrins and is found on the surface of several cell types, including antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and T cells.

IT07139.title: interchange reaction
IT07139.definition: Reaction that results in an exchange of atoms or groups between a polymer and low-molar-mass molecules, between polymer molecules, or between sites within the same macromolecule.

13337.title: interclonal competition
13337.definition: Process which favors survival of foreign-specific lymphocytes at the expense of self-specific lymphocytes and is a secondary mechanism involved in the induction and maintenance of self-tolerance.

I03080.title: interconal region
I03080.definition: The region of a Bunsen flame where the combustion zone has the form of a cone.

I03081.title: interconvertible enzyme
I03081.definition: An enzyme existing in at least two well defined, reversibly convertible forms, produced by covalent modifications of amino acid side chains under biological conditions. Covalent modifications that occur as intermediates in the catalytic process are not included in this definition.

I03082.title: interface
I03082.definition: The plane ideally marking the boundary between two phases.

09341.title: interface core-level shift
09341.definition: Energy shift observed in core-level photoelectron spectroscopy arising from the changed bonding and/or from the displacements of atoms from their bulk positions near an interface between two materials.

IT07253.title: interfacial adhesion
IT07253.definition: Adhesion in which interfaces between phases or components are maintained by intermolecular forces, chain entanglements, or both, across the interfaces.

I03083.title: interfacial concentration
I03083.definition: The interfacial concentration \(c_{\rm{B},\rm{e}}\) (or simply \(c_{\rm{e}}\)) of a species B is the concentration of that species at the boundary of the electrical double-layer facing the solution, i.e. just outside the region where the departures from the electroneutrality of the solution are significant. This concept is mainly used in the usual case where the thickness of the electric double layer is very small as compared to that of the diffusion layer. It is often calculated from theory or derived from measurements of the limiting current.

I03084.title: interfacial double-layer
I03084.definition: The Coulombic interaction of interfacial charges (e.g. ions) and the magnetic or electrostatic interaction of interfacial molecules lead to particularly complex interfacial structures. Complex interfacial profiles that can be approximated by two distinct sub-layers with different physical properties (e.g. structure and/or nature and/or composition), are referred to as interfacial double-layers. Examples of such approximated complex profiles are: the electrical double-layer consisting of a surface charge layer (i.e. a two dimensional distribution of one type of ions) and a diffuse charge layer (counter-ions distributed over the space region next to the surface); the approximated profile of the orientation angle of anisotropic liquid molecules within a 'double-layer' consisting of a distribution of so-called anchored molecules which are perturbed (strongly bound and orientated) by the surface, and the adjacent, so-called, transition layer, i.e. the region where the surface perturbation is damped.

I03085.title: interfacial layer
I03085.definition: The inhomogeneous space region intermediate between two bulk phases in contact, and where properties are significantly different from, but related to, the properties of the bulk phases. Examples of such properties are: compositions, molecular density, orientation or conformation, charge density, pressure tensor, electron density, etc. The interfacial properties vary in the direction normal to the surface. Complex profiles of interfacial properties occur in the case of multicomponent systems with coexisting bulk phases where attractive/repulsive molecular interactions involve adsorption or depletion of one or several components. This interfacial region may also be regarded as a distinct, though not autonomous, phase and be called the interphase.

I03086.title: interfacial layer width
I03086.definition: The characteristic length defined by the variance of the Gaussian function fitted to the gradient of the electron density profile established by X-ray specular reflectivity studies of the liquid interface.

15407.title: interfacial polycondensation
15407.definition: Polycondensation involving two monomers separately dissolved in immiscible solvents, forming a twophase system, with polycondensation taking place at (or near) an interface between the two phases.

14768.title: interference competition
14768.definition: Interspecies competition in which one species interferes with another, as might occur with territoriality or aggressive behavior.

08496.title: interference curve
08496.definition: Graph of absorbance or intensity plotted as a function of the concentration of an interfering element in an atomic spectroscopy experiment.

08620.title: interference fringes
08620.definition: Sinusoidal intensity variation due to interference of electromagnetic radiation that undergoes multiple reflection between two flat and parallel surfaces.

I03089.title: interference
I03089.definition: A systematic error in the measure of a signal caused by the presence of concomitants in a sample.

09511.title: interference lithography
09511.definition: Technique for patterning regular arrays of fine features without the use of complex optical systems or photomasks.

08621.title: interference record
08621.definition: Record of the signal from the detector of a two-beam interferometer as the optical path difference between the two beams is varied.

08019.title: interferent
08019.definition: Component of the matrix that embodies an influence quantity.

I03092.title: interfering lines
I03092.definition: Radiation from nearby spectral lines may perturb the measurement of the intensity of the line wanted. These lines are termed interfering lines.

I03093.title: interfering substance
I03093.definition: Any substance, other than the ion being measured, whose presence in the sample solution affects the measured emf of a cell. Interfering substances fall into two classes: 'electrode/electrochemical' interferences and 'chemical' interferences. Examples of the first class include:Those substances which give a similar response to the ion being measured and whose presence generally results in an apparent increase in the activity (or concentration) of the ion to be determined (e.g. $\ce{Na^{+}}$ for the $\ce{Ca^{2+}}$ electrode).Electrolytes present at a high concentration that give rise to appreciable liquid junction potential differences or results in a significant activity coefficient decrease, or incipient Donnan exclusion failure. The second class of substances that should be recognized as chemical interferences includes: Species that interact with the ion being measured so as to decrease its activity or apparent concentration. The electrode continues to report the true activity (e.g. $\ce{CN^{−}}$ present in the measurement of $\ce{Ag^{+}}$), but a considerable gap will occur between the activity and concentration of the ions even in very dilute solutions. Under these circumstances the determination of ionic concentration may be problematic. Substances interacting with the membrane itself, blocking the surface or changing its chemical composition [i.e. organic solvents for the liquid or poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) membrane electrodes] are grouped as interferences or electrode poisons.

08622.title: interferogram
08622.definition: Pattern formed by wave interference produced by an interferometer, especially one represented on a screen or chart recorder.

I03095.title: interferons
I03095.definition: A class of glycoproteins (with sugar groups attached at specific locations) important in immune function. They are able to inhibit the multiplication of viruses in cells.

08081.title: interlaboratory comparison
08081.definition: Organization, performance, and evaluation of measurements or tests on the same or similar items by two or more laboratories in accordance with predetermined conditions.

13338.title: interleukin
13338.definition: Member of a group of immunoregulatory glycoproteins, also called lymphokines, monokines, or cytokines.

I03096.title: intermediate
I03096.definition: A molecular entity with a lifetime appreciably longer than a molecular vibration (corresponding to a local potential energy minimum of depth greater than \(R\ T\)) that is formed (directly or indirectly) from the reactants and reacts further to give (either directly or indirectly) the products of a chemical reaction; also the corresponding chemical species.

10009.title: intermediate examination precision
10009.definition: Examination precision under intermediate precision condition of examination.

10858.title: intermediate filament
10858.definition: Any of a group of fibrous proteins (including keratin fibres, neurofilaments, desmin, and vimentin) that make up part of the cytoskeleton of most eukaryotic cells; so named because, at about \(\pu{10 nm}\) diameter, they are intermediate in thickness between actin filaments and microtubules.

08020.title: intermediate measurement precision
08020.definition: Measurement precision under intermediate precision conditions of measurement.

I03097.title: intermediate neutrons
I03097.definition: Neutrons of kinetic energy between the energies of slow and fast neutrons. In reactor physics, the range might be \(1\ \rm{eV}\) to \(0.1\ \rm{MeV}\).

09994.title: intermediate precision condition
09994.definition: Condition of examination out of a set of conditions that includes the same examination procedure, same location, and replicate examinations on the same or similar objects over an extended period of time, but may include other conditions involving changes.

15822.title: intermittent effect
15822.definition: Biological change that comes and goes at intervals.

I03098.title: intermolecular
I03098.definition: Descriptive of any process that involves a transfer (of atoms, groups, electrons, etc.) or interactions between two or more molecular entities.Relating to a comparison between different molecular entities.

15408.title: intermolecular chain transfer
15408.definition: Chain transfer from an active center on a macromolecule to a different macromolecule.

09873.title: intermolecular interactions
09873.definition: Interactions between (parts of) two biomolecule chains (e.g. base pairing in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) double helix, or the interactions between two polypeptide chains, or between a DNA and a protein molecule).

08261.title: internal absorbance
08261.definition: Absorbance in the absence of reflection, scattering or luminescence.

I03100.title: internal absorptance
I03100.definition: Absorptance when surface effects and effects of the cuvette such as reflection losses are excluded.

I03102.title: internal conversion
I03102.definition: A photophysical process. An isoenenergetic radiationless transition between two electronic states of the same multiplicity. When the transition results in a vibrationally excited molecular entity in the lower electronic state, this usually undergoes deactivation to its lowest vibrational level, provided the final state is not unstable to dissociation.

I03103.title: internal energy
I03103.definition: Quantity the change in which is equal to the sum of heat, \(q\), brought to the system and work, \(w\), performed on it, \(\Delta U=q+w\). Also called thermodynamic energy.

I03105.title: internal filling solution
I03105.definition: Aqueous electrolyte solution, which may be gelled, containing fixed concentration of hydrogen ions, e.g. $\ce{HCl}$ or a buffer solution, and a fixed concentration of the ion to which the internal reference electrode is reversible, e.g. chloride ion in the case of silver-silver chloride, or calomel electrodes.

13339.title: internal image
13339.definition: Epitope on an anti-idiotype that binds in a way that structurally and functionally mimics the antigen.

08082.title: internal quality control
08082.definition: Quality control within a specified laboratory.

08832.title: internal quantum yield
08832.definition: Quantum yield relating to a single component or a part of a device or a partial step of an overall process.

I03106.title: internal reference electrode
I03106.definition: An 'inner' reference electrode which is contained inside an ion-selective electrode assembly.

08623.title: internal reflection
08623.definition: Reflection of electromagnetic radiation from a material of lesser refractive index than that of the incident medium.

08624.title: internal reflection element
08624.definition: Transparent or semi-transparent material of high refractive index that carries infrared radiation to a sample in internal reflection and attenuated total reflection measurements.

I03108.title: internal standard
I03108.definition: A compound added to a sample in known concentration to facilitate the qualitative indentification and/or quantitative determination of the sample components.

I03109.title: internal surface
I03109.definition: With respect to porous solids, the surface associated with pores communicating with the outside space. Since the accessibility of pores may depend on the size of the fluid molecules, the extent of the accessible internal surface may depend on the size of the molecules comprising the fluid, and may be different for the various components of a fluid mixture (molecular sieve effect).

I03111.title: internal valence force field
I03111.definition: A force field expressed in terms of bond-stretching, angle-bending, torsional and other displacements directly connected to the structural parameters of the molecule: \[V=\frac{1}{2}\ \sum k_{ij}\ R_{i}\ R_{j}\] or \[V=\frac{1}{2}\ \sum K_{ij}\ R_{i}\ R_{j}\] where \(k\) (or \(K\)) are the force constants and \(R\) the internal valence coordinates.

15823.title: internal validity
15823.definition: Selection and comparison of index and comparison groups in such a manner that, apart from sampling error, the observed differences between these groups with respect to dependent variables under study may be attributed only to the hypothesized effect under investigation.

11456.title: International Chemical Identifier
11456.definition:
A non-proprietary canonical identifier of chemical substances that can be used in printed and electronic data sources to enable easier linking of diverse data
 compilations.

10024.title: international examination standard
10024.definition: Examination standard recognized by signatories to an international agreement and intended to serve worldwide.

I03114.title: international unit
I03114.definition: The unit of enzyme activity proposed by the International Union of Biochemistry in 1964. Specifically, it is the amount of enzyme that catalyses the conversion of one micromole of substrate per minute under the specified conditions of the assay method.

14024.title: interparticle electron transfer
14024.definition: Electron transfer taking place from a photoexcited semiconductor onto another semiconductor (or insulator) in its ground state leading to vectorial (irreversible) charge transfer.

I03115.title: interparticle porosity
I03115.definition: The interparticle volume of a packed column per unit column volume: \[\varepsilon = \frac{V_{0}}{V_{\rm{c}}}\] It is also called the interstitial fraction of the column.

I03116.title: interparticle volume of the column
I03116.definition: The volume occupied by the mobile phase between the particles in the packed section of a column. It is also called the interstitial volume or the void volume of the column. In liquid chromatography, the interparticle volume is equal to the mobile-phase hold-up volume (\(V_{\rm{M}}\)) in the ideal case, neglecting any extra-column volume. In gas chromatography, the symbol \(V_{\rm{G}}\) may be used for the interparticle volume of the column. In the ideal case, neglecting any extra-column volume, \(V_{\rm{G}}\) is equal to the corrected gas hold-up volume (\(V_{\rm{M}}^{\rm{o}}\)). \[V_{\rm{G}}=V_{\rm{M}}^{\rm{o}}=V_{\rm{M}j}\]

I03117.title: interpenetrating polymer network
I03117.definition: Polymer comprising two or more networks that are at least partially interlaced on a molecular scale but not covalently bonded to each other and cannot be separated unless chemical bonds are broken.

I03119.title: interphase transition
I03119.definition: A transition that occurs at boundaries between phases. Example: The precipitation of second phases or the initiation of new phase growth at an interface.

15824.title: interpolation
15824.definition: Estimation of a value between two known data points.

15825.title: interpretation
15825.definition: Evaluation of the observations from an investigation or study in order to determine their significance for human health, for the environment or for both.

IT07400.title: intersection space
IT07400.definition: (3N − 8)-dimensional subspace of the (3N − 6)-dimensional nuclear coordinate space consisting of an infinite number of conical intersection points (N is the number of nuclei).

10859.title: intersexuality
10859.definition: Condition of having both male and female characteristics: thus, the state of being intermediate between the sexes.

14769.title: interspecies competition
14769.definition: Interference with or inhibition of one species by another.

15826.title: interspecies dose conversion
15826.definition: Process of extrapolating from the doses of one animal species to another, for example, from rodent dose to human equivalent.

14770.title: interspecific competition
14770.definition: Competition by different species for the same (limited) resources.

14771.title: interspecific interaction
14771.definition: Relations between different species in a community.

15827.title: interstitial fluid
15827.definition: Aqueous solution filling the narrow spaces between cells.

I03120.title: interstitial fraction
I03120.definition: The interstitial volume per unit volume of a packed column. Defined by: \(\varepsilon_{\rm{I}}=\frac{V_{\rm{I}}}{X}\) where \(V_{\rm{I}}\) is the interstitial volume and \(X\) the column volume.

15828.title: interstitial pneumonia
15828.definition: Chronic form of pneumonia involving increase of the interstitial tissue and decrease of the functional lung tissue.

I03121.title: interstitial velocity
I03121.definition: The linear velocity of the mobile phase inside a packed column calculated as the average over the entire cross section. This quantity can, under idealized conditions, be calculated from the equation: \[u=\frac{F}{\varepsilon_{\rm{I}}}\] where \(F\) is the nominal linear flow and \(\varepsilon_{\rm{I}}\) the interstitial fraction

I03122.title: interstitial volume
I03122.definition: The volume \(V_{\rm{G}}\) of the column not occupied by the liquid phase and its solid support, or by the active solid. It does not include any volume external to the column, such as the volume of the sample injector or of the detector.

14772.title: interstitial water
14772.definition: Water in sediment or soil that surrounds the solid particles. The amount of interstitial water is calculated and expressed as the percentage ratio of the mass of water in the sediment to the mass of the wet sediment.

I03123.title: intersystem crossing
I03123.definition: A photophysical process. An isoenergetic radiationless transition between two electronic states having different multiplicities. It often results in a vibrationally excited molecular entity in the lower electronic state, which then usually deactivates to its lowest vibrational level.

14360.title: interval 1 in emulsion polymerisation
14360.definition: Period in a batch ab initio emulsion polymerization during which the formation of particles takes place.

14361.title: interval 2 in emulsion polymerisation
14361.definition: Period in an emulsion polymerization during which no new particles are formed and monomer droplets are present.

14362.title: interval 3 in emulsion polymerisation
14362.definition: Period in an emulsion polymerization during which no new particles are formed and no monomer droplets are present.

I03124.title: interval analysis
I03124.definition: A method to estimate uncertainties in the results of a least-squares procedure. The input data are primary values plus limits of intervals expressing their uncertainty. The output consists of derived values plus limits of intervals expressing a pessimistic estimate of maximal uncertainty.

I03125.title: intervalence charge transfer
I03125.definition: Electron transfer (thermal or photoinduced) between two metal sites differing only in oxidation state. Quite often such electron transfer reverses the oxidation states of the sites. The term is frequently extended to the case of metal-to-metal charge transfer between non-equivalent metal centres.

14359.title: intervals in emulsion polymerisations
14359.definition: Periods in an emulsion polymerization defined by the formation of polymer particles, and the presence or absence of monomer droplets in the polymerizing mixture.

15829.title: intervention study
15829.definition: Epidemiological investigation designed to test a hypothesized cause–effect relationship by intentional change of a supposed causal factor in a population.

11720.title: intervertebral disc
11720.definition: Flat circular structure, consisting of a tough, fibrous exterior and a gelatinous core, interposed between adjacent vertebrae.

I03126.title: interzonal region
I03126.definition: The region of the Bunsen flame confined by the inner and outer zones, where in many instances the conditions for flame analysis are optimum.

15830.title: intestinal reabsorption
15830.definition: Absorption further down the intestinal tract of a substance or substances that have been absorbed before and subsequently excreted into the intestinal tract, usually through the bile.

13340.title: intolerance
13340.definition: Extreme sensitivity or allergy to a drug, food, or other substance.

15831.title: intoxication
15831.definition:
Poisoning: pathological process with clinical signs and symptoms caused by a substance of exogenous or endogenous origin.
Drunkenness following consumption of beverages containing ethanol or other compounds affecting the central nervous system.

I03128.title: intra-
I03128.definition: The prefix for an elementary reaction or some part thereof indicating that the bond(s) undergoing primitive changes form part of a ring in the transition state of the elementary reaction. This prefix is used for nonpericyclic processes only and is replaced by 'cyclo' for pericyclic processes.

13342.title: intra-epithelial lymphocyte
13342.definition: Lymphocyte found in the epithelial layer of mammalian mucosal linings, such as those of the gastrointestinal and reproductive tracts.

10860.title: intracytoplasmic sperm injection
10860.definition: Infertility treatment in which the sperm is injected through the membrane of the egg into its cytoplasm.

13341.title: intradermal test
13341.definition: Diagnostic test for a possible cause of hypersensitivity in an individual in which a small drop of antigen is placed on a scarified skin surface or injected intradermally.

08083.title: intralaboratory comparison
08083.definition: Organization, performance, and evaluation of measurements or tests on the same or similar items within the same laboratory in accordance with predetermined conditions.

10861.title: intramembrous ossification
10861.definition: Creation of bone tissue during fetal development of jawed vertebrates, as well as during the healing of bone fractures; the tissue forms from mesenchymal stem cells residing in an extracellular matrix devoid of collagen.

I03130.title: intramolecular
I03130.definition: Descriptive of any process that involves a transfer (of atoms, groups, electrons, etc.) or interactions between different parts of the same molecular entity.Relating to a comparison between atoms or groups within the same molecular entity.

I03131.title: intramolecular catalysis
I03131.definition: The acceleration of a chemical transformation at one site of a molecular entity through the involvement of another functional ('catalytic') group in the same molecular entity, without that group appearing to have undergone change in the reaction product. The use of the term should be restricted to cases for which analogous intermolecular catalysis by chemical species bearing that catalytic group is observable. intramolecular catalysis can be detected and expressed in quantitative form by a comparison of the reaction rate with that of a comparable model compound in which the catalytic group is absent, or by measurement of the effective molarity of the catalytic group.

IT07401.title: intramolecular charge transfer
IT07401.definition: Process that changes the overall charge distribution in a molecule.

09874.title: intramolecular interactions
09874.definition: Interactions between (neighbouring or distant) segments within the same biomolecule chain (e.g. base pairing in hairpin or monomolecular tetraplex structures of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA), the interactions stabilizing the secondary or tertiary structures of proteins, etc.).

I03132.title: intramolecular isotope effect
I03132.definition: A kinetic isotopic effect observed when a single substrate, in which the isotopic atoms occupy equivalent reactive positions, reacts to produce a non-statistical distribution of isotopomeric products. In such a case the isotope effect will favour the pathway with lower force constants for displacement of the isotopic nuclei in the transition state.

11549.title: intraparticle volume of the column
11549.definition: Volume of the mobile phase within the pores of the particles in the stationary phase.

I03133.title: intraphase transition
I03133.definition: A transition that occurs within a phase. Example: initiation of phase growth at an intragranular feature, such as twin planes and dislocations in steels.

14773.title: intraspecific competition
14773.definition: Competition by individuals of the same species (population) for the same (limited) resources.

11837.title: intrathecal
11837.definition: Within a sheath, as within either the subarachnoid or the subdural space.

10863.title: intrauterine growth restriction
10863.definition: Subnormal, poor growth of the fetus.

I03134.title: intrinsic activation energy
I03134.definition: If \(E_{\rm{a,1}}\) and \(E_{\rm{a,- 1}}\) are the activation energies for a reaction in forward and reverse directions, the lesser of the two is sometimes called the intrinsic activation energy. It is the activation energy for the reaction in the exothermic direction.

15832.title: intrinsic activity
15832.definition: Maximal stimulatory effect induced by a compound in relation to that of a given reference compound.

I03135.title: intrinsic barrier
I03135.definition: The Gibbs energy of activation (\(\Delta ^{\ddagger}G\)) in the limiting case where \(\Delta G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}} = 0\), i.e. when the effect of thermodynamic driving force is eliminated. According to the Marcus equation, the intrinsic barrier is related to the reorganization energy, \(\lambda \), of the reaction by the equation: \[\Delta ^{\ddagger}G = \frac{\lambda }{4}\]

15833.title: intrinsic clearance
15833.definition: Volume of plasma or blood from which a substance is completely removed in a period of time under unstressed conditions.

14026.title: intrinsic defects
14026.definition: Imperfections connected with surface point defects (zero-dimensional), linear defects (one-dimensional), or square defects (two-dimensional) not including extrinsic chemical units in relation to the chemical formula of the solid.

I03136.title: intrinsic detector efficiency
I03136.definition: The ratio of the number of particles or photons detected to the number of similar particles or photons which have struck the envelope limiting the sensitive volume of a radiation detector.

14025.title: intrinsic emission
14025.definition: Band-to-band recombination of electrons and holes (or exciton decay) in a semiconductor or insulator leading to luminescence.

10032.title: intrinsic examination standard
10032.definition: Examination standard based on a reproducible nominal property of a phenomenon or substance.

15834.title: intrinsic factor
15834.definition: Specific protein required for the absorption of \(\ce{vitamin B_{12}}\) and secreted by cells in the gastric glands of the stomach.

I03138.title: intrinsic full energy peak efficiency
I03138.definition: The detector efficiency when considering only events where the total energy of the radiation is absorbed in the sensitive volume of the detector.

10864.title: intrinsic pathway
10864.definition: Apoptotic pathway of cell death initiated from within the cell by signals initiated by mitochondrial damage and (or) DNA damage, a defective cell cycle, detachment from the extracellular matrix, hypoxia, loss of cell survival factors, or other types of severe cell stress; characterized by the activation of caspase 9.

I03139.title: intrinsic photopeak efficiency
I03139.definition: The detector efficiency when only counts resulting from the photoelectrical effect are considered.

09342.title: intrinsic plasmon
09342.definition: Plasmon excited at the same time as the excitation of a core-level photoelectron or an Auger electron associated with the same locality as the excitation of the photoelectron or Auger electron.

14775.title: intrinsic rate of increase
14775.definition: Rate of increase in the size of a population growing under no constraints.

IT07057.title: intrinsic reaction coordinate
IT07057.definition: A minimum-energy reaction path on a potential energy surface in mass-weighted coordinates, connecting reactants to products via the transition state.

08833.title: intrinsic semiconductor
08833.definition: Semiconductor in which mobile charge carriers are generated solely by thermal excitation of electrons.

12672.title: intrinsic solubility
12672.definition: Equilibrium solubility of the uncharged form of an ionisable compound at a pH where it is fully unionised. \[\ce{HA(s)  HA(aq)} \quad (1)\] \[\ce{HA(aq)  H^{+}(aq) + A^{-}(aq)} \quad (2)\]

I03140.title: intrinsic viscosity
I03140.definition: The limiting value of the reduced viscosity, \(\frac{\eta _{\rm{i}}}{c}\) or the inherent viscosity, \(\eta _{\rm{inh}}\), at infinite dilution of the polymer, i.e. \[[\eta] = \lim _{c\rightarrow 0}\frac{\eta _{\rm{i}}}{c}=\lim _{c\rightarrow 0}\eta _{\rm{inh}}\]

IT07208.title: intrinsically conducting polymer
IT07208.definition: Electrically conducting polymer composed of macromolecules having fully conjugated sequences of double bonds along the chains.

I03141.title: intron
I03141.definition: An intervening section of DNA occuring almost exclusively within a eukaryotic gene but which is not translated to amino acid sequences in the gene product. The introns are removed from the premature mRNA through a process called splicing to form an active mRNA.

13343.title: invariant chain
13343.definition: Protein (\(\pu{31 kDa}\)) of the endoplasmic reticulum lumen that binds to newly formed major histocompatibility complex (MHC) heterodimeric proteins, preventing binding of endogenous peptides to their groove.

14151.title: inverse agonist
14151.definition: Ligand that decreases signaling through a receptor below the level of constitutive activity.

08497.title: inverse Bremsstrahlung
08497.definition: Absorption of photon energy by free electrons.

14335.title: inverse emulsion polymerisation
14335.definition: Emulsion polymerization in a nonaqueous medium in which the dispersed phase is usually an aqueous solution, initially of monomer(s), and finally of polymer.

I03142.title: inverse isotope effect
I03142.definition: A kinetic isotope effect in which \(\frac{k^{\rm{l}}}{k^{\rm{h}}}1\). The isotope effect will normally be 'normal' when the frequency differences between the isotopic transition state are smaller than in the reactants. Conversely, an inverse isotope effect can be taken as evidence for an increase in the corresponding force constants on passing from the reactant to the transition state.

14286.title: inverse latex
14286.definition: Nonaqueous latex in which the dispersed phase comprises hydrophilic polymer usually swollen with water.

14343.title: inverse micro-emulsion polymerisation
14343.definition: Emulsion polymerization in which the starting system is a micro-emulsion and the final system is composed of an organic continuous phase with an aqueous polymer solution as the dispersed phase.

14346.title: inverse mini-emulsion polymerisation
14346.definition: Emulsion polymerization in which the starting system is a mini-emulsion and the final system is composed of an organic continuous phase with an aqueous polymer solution as the dispersed phase.

13832.title: inverse opal
13832.definition: Colloidal crystal of spherical voids with a periodic structure within a solid polymer continuum.

08625.title: inverse Raman scattering

08626.title: inverse spatially offset Raman spectroscopy
08626.definition: Variant of spatially offset Raman spectroscopy in which a sample is illuminated with a ring of laser light and the Raman scattering is collected from the centre of the ring.

I03145.title: inverse square law
I03145.definition: The intensity of radiation from a point source in free space is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source. Presence of absorbers necessitates corrections to this law.

I03146.title: inversion
I03146.definition: A symmetry operation involving a centre of inversion (\(i\)).

I03147.title: inversion height
I03147.definition: The height above ground level at which there is change in sign of the normal temperature 'lapse rate', \(\frac{\rm{d}T}{\rm{d}z}\) (the rate of change of the temperature with height). Several temperature inversions may be present in the air over a given site at different altitudes as result of various meteorological factors.

14027.title: inversion layer
14027.definition: Layer formed when band bending places the Fermi level on the surface close to the band of the bulk minority charge carriers. This leads to a higher concentration of the minority charge carriers on the surface relative to the concentration of the majority charge carriers, an opposite situation to that in the bulk.

I03149.title: inversion point
I03149.definition: The temperature (pressure) at which one polymorph of a solid phase changes into another at constant pressure (temperature).

08369.title: inversion pulse
08369.definition: Pulse in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that completely inverts the magnetization of a spin, e.g., \(+z\) to \(-z\).

08370.title: inversion recovery sequence
08370.definition: Spin echo sequence preceded by a \(\pu{180\!^{\circ}}\) inversion pulse used to determine spin-lattice relaxation times in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

08371.title: inversion time
08371.definition: Time between the inversion pulse and the sampling pulse(s) in an inversion recovery sequence.

14300.title: inverted core-shell particle
14300.definition: Core-shell particle in which polymer synthesized in the second stage is located in the core of the particle and polymer constituting the initial seed is located in the shell.

I03151.title: inverted micelle
I03151.definition: The reversible formation of association colloids from surfactants in non-polar solvents leads to aggregates termed inverted (or inverse, reverse or reversed) micelle. Such association is often of the type: \[\rm{Monomer}\rightleftarrows \rm{Dimer}\rightleftarrows \rm{Trimer}\rightleftarrows \rm{ ... }n\rm{-mer}\] and the phenomenon of critical micelle concentration (or an analogous effect) is consequently not observed. In an inverted micelle the polar groups of the surfactants are concentrated in the interior and the lipophilic groups extend towards and into the non-polar solvent.

I03152.title: inverted region
I03152.definition: In plots relating rate constants to charges in standard Gibbs energy (\(\Delta G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\)) for electron transfer a region may occur in which the rate constants decrease as the exergonicity of the reaction increases. This region is often referred to as the inverted region and its presence is predicted by the theory developed for outer sphere electron transfer for the case \(-\Delta G^{\circ} \gt \lambda \) in the Marcus equation, \(\lambda\) being the reorganization energy. Note the similarity to the energy gap law for radiationless conversion of an excited state.

12673.title: investigational new drug
12673.definition: Drug not yet approved for general use by the national authority, such as the Food and Drug Administration of the United States of America, but undergoing clinical investigation to assess its safety and efficacy.

08930.title: iodine-transfer polymerization
08930.definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization mediated by an iodo-compound.

I03158.title: ion
I03158.definition: An atomic or molecular particle having a net electric charge.

09260.title: ion beam
09260.definition: Directed flux of charged atoms or molecules.

08732.title: ion beam analysis
08732.definition: Measurement principle in which elementary particles resulting from nuclear reactions of charged particles with nuclei in a material are applied in order to measure the amount and depth distribution of elements in materials.

09404.title: ion beam ratio
09404.definition: Intensity of analyte ion divided by intensity of matrix ion, both corrected for isotopic abundance.

09567.title: ion beam resist
09567.definition: Resist optimized for use under ion beam irradiation.

11838.title: ion channel
11838.definition: Pore-forming transmembrane protein that can gate the transmembrane flux of small ions.

11839.title: ion channelopathy
11839.definition: Neuromuscular disease resulting from a genetic defect in an ion channel.

I03161.title: ion collector
I03161.definition: Device for the capture of selected ions such as a Faraday cup collector (with a d.c. amplifier) or an electron multiplier.

I03162.title: ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometer
I03162.definition: A high-frequency mass spectrometer in which the ions to be detected, with a selected value of the quotient mass/charge, absorb maximum energy through the effect of a high-frequency electric field and a constant magnetic field perpendicular to the electric field. Maximum energy is gained by the ions which satisfy the cyclotron resonance condition and as a result they are separated from ions of different mass/charge.

I03165.title: ion energy loss spectra
I03165.definition: Spectra that show the loss of translational energy of ions involved in ion/neutral species reactions.

I03167.title: ion exchange
I03167.definition: In surface chemistry, if the adsorption of one or several ionic species is accompanied by the simultaneous desorption (displacement) of an equivalent amount of one or more other ionic species, this process is called ion exchange.

I03171.title: ion exchanger
I03171.definition: A solid or liquid, inorganic or organic substance containing exchangeable ions with others of the same charge, present in a solution in which the ion exchanger is considered to be insoluble. It is recognized that there are cases where liquid exchangers are employed and where it may be difficult to distinguish between the separation process as belonging to ion exchange or liquid-liquid distribution, but the broad definition given here is regarded as that which is most appropriate. A monofunctional ion exchanger contains only one type of ionogenic group, a bifunctional ion exchanger two types and a polyfunctional ion exchanger more than one type. In a macroporous ion exchanger the pores are large compared to atomic dimensions.

09261.title: ion implantation
09261.definition: Injection of ions into a sample.

I03218.title: ion kinetic energy spectrum
I03218.definition: A spectrum obtained when a beam of ions is separated according to the translational energy-to-charge ratios of the ionic species contained within it. A radial electric field (E) achieves separation of the various ionic species in this way.

I03219.title: ion laser
I03219.definition: A gas laser in which the active species is an ion formed in the electric discharge. Most practically important lasers of this type have continuous wave (CW) output. Examples are the argon ion, krypton ion and helium-cadmium (HeCd) lasers.

I03221.title: ion microscopy
I03221.definition: Use of the secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) technique to obtain micrographs of the elemental (or isotopic) distribution at the surface of a sample with a spatial resolution of \(2\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) or better.

I03231.title: ion pair
I03231.definition: A pair of oppositely charged ions held together by coulomb attraction without formation of a covalent bond. Experimentally, an ion pair behaves as one unit in determining conductivity, kinetic behaviour, osmotic properties, etc. Following Bjerrum, oppositely charged ions with their centres closer together than a distance: \[q = \frac{8.36\times 10^{6}\ z^{+}\ z^{-}}{\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\ T}\ \rm{pm}\] are considered to constitute an ion pair ('Bjerrum ion pair'). [\(z^{+}\) and \(z^{-}\) are the charge numbers of the ions, and \(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\) is the relative permittivity (or dielectric constant) of the medium.] An ion pair, the constituent ions of which are in direct contact (and not separated by an intervening solvent or other neutral molecule) is designated as a 'tight ion pair' (or 'intimate' or 'contact ion pair'). A tight ion pair of $\ce{X^{+}}$ and $\ce{Y^{−}}$ is symbolically represented as $\ce{X^{+}Y^{−}}$. By contrast, an ion pair whose constituent ions are separated by one or several solvent or other neutral molecules is described as a 'loose ion pair', symbolically represented as $\ce{X^{+}}\,\|\,\ce{Y^{−}}$. The members of a loose ion pair can readily interchange with other free or loosely paired ions in the solution. This interchange may be detectable (e.g. by isotopic labelling) and thus afford an experimental distinction between tight and loose ion pairs. A further conceptual distinction has sometimes been made between two types of loose ion pairs. In 'solvent-shared ion pairs' the ionic constituents of the pair are separated by only a single solvent molecule, whereas in 'solvent-separated ion pairs' more than one solvent molecule intervenes. However, the term 'solvent-separated ion pair' must be used and interpreted with care since it has also widely been used as a less specific term for 'loose' ion pair.

I03233.title: ion pair return
I03233.definition: The recombination of a pair of ions $\ce{R^{+}}$ and $\ce{Z^{−}}$ formed from ionization of $\ce{RZ}$. If the ions are paired as a tight ion pair and recombine without prior separation into a loose ion pair this is called 'internal ion-pair return':   It is a special case of 'primary geminate recombination'. If the ions are paired as a loose ion pair and form the covalent chemical species via a tight ion pair, this is called 'external ion-pair return':  It is a special case of 'secondary geminate recombination'. When the covalent molecule RZ is reformed without direct evidence of prior partial racemization or without other direct evidence of prior formation of a tight ion pair, (e.g. without partial racemization if the group R is suitably chiral) the internal ion-pair return is sometimes called a 'hidden return'. External (unimolecular) ion-pair return is to be distinguished from 'external (bimolecular) ion return', the (reversible) process whereby dissociated ions are converted into loose ion pairs:

I03238.title: ion probe microanalysis
I03238.definition: Any technique in which the specimen is bombarded by a focused beam of (primary) ions (diameter less than \(10\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\)) and the (secondary) ions ejected from the specimen are detected after passage through a mass spectrometer.

IT06773.title: ion pumps
IT06773.definition: Ion pumps enable ions to flow through membranes in a thermodynamically uphill direction by the use of an energy source such as ATP or light. They consist of sugar-containing hetero-peptide assemblies, which open and close upon the binding and subsequent hydrolysis of ATP, usually transporting more than one ion towards the outside or the inside of the membrane.

I03243.title: ion scattering spectrometry
I03243.definition: Any technique using low energy (\(10\ \rm{keV}\)) ions in which the bombarding particles scattered by the sample are detected and recorded as a function of energy and/or angle. This technique is used mainly for determining the composition and structure of the first few atomic layers of a sample.

I03247.title: ion source
I03247.definition: Generally an assembly composed of: (i) an ionization chamber in which a stream of electrons flows from a hot filament across a stream of gas to collector (the potential between filament and collector is usually between 50 and 70 \(\rm{V}\)); (ii) a device for the acceleration of these ions.

I03249.title: ion trap mass spectrometer
I03249.definition: An arrangement in which ions with a desired range of quotients mass/charge are first made to describe stable paths under the effect of a high-frequency electric quadrupole field, and are then separated and presented to a detector by adjusting the field so as to selectivity induce path instability according to their respective mass/charge ratios.

08834.title: ion-conducting polymer
08834.definition: Conducting polymer in which ionic species are mobile charge carriers.

I03168.title: ion-exchange chromatography
I03168.definition: Chromatography in which separation is based mainly on differences in the ion-exchange affinities of the sample components. Present day ion-exchange chromatography on small particle high efficiency columns, and usually utilizing conductometric or spectroscopic detectors, is often referred to as ion chromatography (IC).

I03169.title: ion-exchange isotherm
I03169.definition: The concentration of a counter-ion in the ion exchanger expressed as a function of its concentration in the external solution under specified conditions and at constant temperature.

IT07155.title: ion-exchange polymer
IT07155.definition: Polymer that is able to exchange ions (cations or anions) with ionic components in solution.

10244.title: ion-exchange sorbent
10244.definition: Porous sorbent material  containing fixed ionic sites with a complementary charge to that of the target analyte(s).

09892.title: ion-exclusion chromatography
09892.definition: Exclusion chromatography in which ionized compounds are excluded from the pores of the support and elute first, while weakly ionized and non-ionic compounds elute later.

I03173.title: ion-free layer
I03173.definition: An interphase in which only non-specifically adsorbed ions are present.

09893.title: ion-pair chromatography
09893.definition: Liquid chromatography in which the mobile liquid phase contains an ionized additive (an ion-pair reagent) that can form an ion pair with an analyte molecule.

10162.title: ion-pair extraction
10162.definition: Transfer of ions from an aqueous phase to an immiscible liquid (or solid) phase by adding an ion of complementary charge to the aqueous phase.

I03232.title: ion-pair formation
I03232.definition: Involves an ionization process in which a positive fragment ion and a negative fragment ion are among the products.

09373.title: ion-scattering spectrum
09373.definition: Plot of the intensities of ions, scattered from a sample, as a function of the scattered-ion energy divided by the incident-ion energy.

I03244.title: ion-selective electrode
I03244.definition: An electrochemical sensor, based on thin films or selective membranes as recognition elements, and an electrochemical half-cell equivalent to other half-cells of the zeroth (inert metal in a redox electrolyte), 1st, 2nd and 3rd kinds. These devices are distinct from systems that involve redox reactions (electrodes of zeroth, 1st, 2nd and 3rd kinds), although they often contain a 2nd kind electrode as the 'inner' or 'internal' reference electrode. The potential difference response has, as its principal component, the Gibbs energy change associated with permselective mass transfer (by ion-exchange, solvent extraction or some other mechanism) across a phase boundary. The ion-selective electrode must be used in conjunction with a reference electrode (i.e. 'outer' or 'external' reference electrode) to form a complete electrochemical cell. The measured potential differences (ion-selective electrode vs. outer reference electrode potentials) are linearly dependent on the logarithm of the activity of a given ion in solution. Comment: The term 'ion-specific electrode' is not recommended. The term 'specific' implies that the electrode does not respond to additional ions. Since no electrode is truly specific for one ion, the term 'ion-selective' is recommended as more appropriate. 'Selective ion-sensitive electrode' is a little-used term to describe an ion-selective electrode. 'Principal' or 'primary' ions are those which an electrode is designed to measure. It is never certain that the 'principal' ion is most sensitively measured, e.g. nitrate ion-selective electrodes.

I03245.title: ion-selective electrode cell
I03245.definition: An ion-selective electrode in conjunction with a reference electrode. Generally, the cell contains two reference electrodes, internal and external, and the thin film or membrane recognition-transduction element. However, besides this conventional type of cell (with solution contact on both sides of the membrane) there are cell arrangements with wire contact to one side of the membrane (all solid state and coated wire types).

09118.title: ion-selective field effect transistor
09118.definition: Electrochemical sensor based on the principle of the field effect transistor (FET) in which the surface of the gate is modified in a way that makes the response ion-selective.

09119.title: ion-selective membrane
