09119.definition: Membrane with controlled permeability to a particular ion covering an electrode, or separating two electrolyte solutions.

I03223.title: ion/molecule reaction
I03223.definition: An ion/neutral species reaction in which the neutral species is a molecule. The use of ion-molecule reaction is not recommended; the hyphen suggests a reaction of a species that is both an ion and a molecule and is not the intended meaning.

I03225.title: ion/neutral species exchange reaction
I03225.definition: In this reaction an association reaction is accompanied by the subsequent or simultaneous liberation of a different neutral species as product.

I03226.title: ion/neutral species reaction
I03226.definition: A process wherein a charged species interacts with a neutral reactant to produce either chemically different species or changes in the internal energy of one or both of the reactants. The contrasting expression ion/neutral reaction is not ideal, simply because the word neutral is not a noun. However, any alternatives such as ion/neutral species reaction are so clumsy as to mitigate against their general acceptance

IT07210.title: ionene
IT07210.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules in which ionized or ionic groups are parts of main chains.

IT07212.title: ionic aggregates in an ionomer
IT07212.definition: Domains enriched with ionic groups within an ionomer matrix.

IT07058.title: ionic bond
IT07058.definition: The bond between atoms with sharply different electronegativities. In strict terms, an ionic bond refers to the electrostatic attraction experienced between the electric charges of a cation and an anion, in contrast with a purely covalent bond. In practice, it is preferable to consider the amount of ionic character of a bond rather than referring to purely ionic or purely covalent bonds. The relationship was proposed (L. Pauling) for the estimation of ionic character of a bond between atoms A and B: \[\rm{Amount of ionic character} = 1 - e^{-1/4}\ (\chi _{\rm{A}}\,-\,\chi_{\rm{B}})\] where \(\chi _{\rm{A}}\) and \(\chi _{\rm{B}}\) are the Pauling electronegativities of atoms A and B. This type of bonding is realized mostly in solids.

08498.title: ionic cloud
08498.definition: Gas phase containing free ions of analyte.

I03175.title: ionic conductivity
I03175.definition: Defined for ionic species $\ce{B}$ by \(\lambda = |z_{\rm{B}}|\ F\ u_{\rm{B}}\) where \(z_{\rm{B}}\) is the charge number of the ionic species $\ce{B}$, \(F\) is the Faraday constant, and \(u_{\rm{B}}\) is the electric mobility of species $\ce{B}$. In most current practice \(z_{\rm{B}}\) is taken as unity, i.e. ionic conductivity is taken as that of species such as $\ce{Na^{+}}$, $\ce{Ca^{2+}}$/2, $\ce{La^{3+}}$/3 etc. To avoid ambiguity the species considered should be clearly stated, e.g. as \(\lambda (\rm{Ca}^{\rm{2+}}/2)\).

I03176.title: ionic copolymerization
I03176.definition: A copolymerization which is an ionic polymerization.

I03177.title: ionic dissociation
I03177.definition: The decomposition of an ion into another ion of lower mass and one or more neutral species.

08180.title: ionic liquid
08180.definition: Liquid that consists exclusively or almost exclusively of equivalent amounts of oppositely charged ions.

15335.title: ionic mole fraction

IT07213.title: ionic polymer
IT07213.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing ionic or ionizable groups, or both, irrespective of their nature, content, and location. Synonym: ion-containing polymer.

I03178.title: ionic polymerization
I03178.definition: A chain polymerization in which the kinetic-chain carriers are ions or ion pairs.

08974.title: ionic ring-opening polymerization
08974.definition: Ionic polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

I03180.title: ionic strength
I03180.definition: On a molality basis, \[I_{m} = \frac{1}{2}\ \sum m_{\rm{B}}\ z_{\rm{B}}^{2}\] where the sum goes over all the ions B. \(z_{\rm{B}}\) is the charge number of ion B. The ionic strength on a concentration basis is defined analogously \[I_{c} = \frac{1}{2}\ \sum c_{\rm{B}}\ z_{\rm{B}}^{2}\]

I03181.title: ionic transport number
I03181.definition: Quotient of the current carried by an ionic component and the total current.

I03183.title: ionization
I03183.definition: The generation of one or more ions. It may occur, e.g. by loss of an electron from a neutral molecular entity, by the unimolecular heterolysis of such an entity into two or more ions, or by a heterolytic substitution reaction involving neutral molecules, such as:    The loss of an electron from a singly, doubly, etc. charged cation is called second, third, etc. ionization. This terminology is used especially in mass spectroscopy.

I03188.title: ionization buffer
I03188.definition: A buffer added to increase the free-electron concentration by the flame gases, thus repressing and stabilizing the degree of ionization.

I03189.title: ionization by sputtering
I03189.definition: Ionization by bombardment of a solid specimen with accelerated ions or electrons or fast neutrals.

I03190.title: ionization chamber
I03190.definition: A radiation detector which employs an electric field for the collection at the electrodes of charges associated with the ions produced in the sensitive volume by ionizing radiation, without charge multiplication. The solid angle ($\ce{2\Uppi\!}$, $\ce{4\uppi\!}$) subtended when using the detector, is sometimes specified.

I03194.title: ionization cross-section
I03194.definition: A measure of the probability that a given ionization process will occur when an atom or molecule interacts with an electron or a photon.

I03196.title: ionization efficiency
I03196.definition: The ratio of the number of ions formed to the number of electrons or photons used in an ionization process.

I03197.title: ionization efficiency curve
I03197.definition: The number of ions produced as a function of the energy of the electrons or photons used to produce ionization.

I03199.title: ionization energy
I03199.definition: Minimum energy required to eject an electron out of a neutral atom or molecule in its ground state. The adiabatic ionization energy refers to the formation of the molecular ion in its ground vibrational state and the vertical ionization energy applies to the transition to the molecular ion without change in geometry. This quantity was formerly called 'ionization potential'. The second ionization energy of an atom is the energy required to eject the second electron from the atom (energy for the process $\ce{X^{+} -> X^{2+} + e^{-}}$).

11840.title: ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1
11840.definition: Protein that is expressed in several tissues, but in brain is a specific immunomarker for microglia.

I03214.title: ionizing collision
I03214.definition: An ion/neutral species interaction in which an electron or electrons are stripped from the ion and/or the neutral species in the collision. Generally, this term has come to be used to describe collisions of fast-moving ions with a neutral species in which the neutral species is ionized with no change in the number of charges carried by the ion. Care should be taken when this term is used to emphasize if charge stripping of the ion has taken place.

I03215.title: ionizing power
I03215.definition: A term to denote the tendency of a particular solvent to promote ionization of an uncharged or, less often, charged solute. The term has been used both in a kinetic and in a thermodynamic context.

I03216.title: ionizing radiation
I03216.definition: Any radiation consisting of directly or indirectly ionizing particles or a mixture of both, or photons with energy higher than the energy of photons of ultraviolet light or a mixture of both such particles and photons.

I03217.title: ionizing voltage
I03217.definition: The voltage difference through which electrons are accelerated before they are used to bring about electron impact ionization. To obtain the true ionizing voltage, corrections for any contact or surface potentials must be made.

I03228.title: ionogenic groups
I03228.definition: The fixed groupings in an ion exchanger which are either ionized or capable of dissociation into fixed ions and mobile counter-ions.

I03229.title: ionomer
I03229.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules in which a small but significant proportion of the constitutional units has ionic or ionizable groups, or both.

IT07215.title: ionomer cluster
IT07215.definition: Ionic aggregate, in a polymer matrix of low polarity, formed through interactions of ionomer multiplets.

I03230.title: ionomer molecule
I03230.definition: A macromolecule in which a small but significant proportion of the constitutional units have ionizable or ionic groups, or both. Some protein molecules may be classified as ionomer molecules.

IT07216.title: ionomer multiplet
IT07216.definition: Ionic aggregate, in a polymer matrix of low polarity, formed through the association of ion-pairs in an ionomer.

IT06772.title: ionophore
IT06772.definition: A compound which can carry specific ions through membranes of cells or organelles.

12674.title: ionotropic receptor
12674.definition: Transmembrane ion channel that opens or closes in response to the binding of a ligand.

I03251.title: ipso-attack
I03251.definition: The attachment of an entering group to a position in an aromatic compound already carrying a substituent group (other than hydrogen). The entering group may displace that substituent group but may also itself be expelled or migrate to a different position in a subsequent step. The term 'ipso-substitution' is not used, since it is synonymous with substitution. For example:   where E + is an electrophile and Z is a substituent (other than hydrogen).

I03253.title: iridoids
I03253.definition: Cyclic monoterpenoids having the iridane skeleton (1-isopropyl-2,3-di-methylcyclopentane), the traditional, but not undisputed, numbering of which is shown in the diagram.

IT06779.title: iron-sulfur cluster
IT06779.definition: A unit comprising two or more iron atoms and bridging sulfur ligands in an iron-sulfur protein. The recommended designation of a cluster consists of the iron and sulfur content, in square brackets, for example, $\ce{[2\! Fe-2\! S]}$, $\ce{[3\! Fe-4\! S]}$. The possible oxidation levels are indicated by the net charge excluding the ligands, for example $\ce{[4\! Fe-4\! S]^{2+}}$; $\ce{[4\! Fe-4\! S]^{+}}$ or ($\ce{[4\! Fe-4\! S]^{2+;1+}}$) cluster.

IT06780.title: iron-sulfur proteins
IT06780.definition: Proteins in which non-haem iron is coordinated with cysteine sulfur and usually also with inorganic sulfur. Divided into three major categories: rubredoxins; 'simple iron-sulfur proteins', containing only iron-sulfur clusters; and 'complex iron-sulfur proteins', containing additional active redox centres such as flavin, molybdenum or haem. In most iron-sulfur proteins, the clusters function as electron-transfer groups, but in others they have other functions, such as catalysis of hydratase/dehydratase reactions, maintenance of protein structure, or regulation of activity.

I03254.title: irradiance
I03254.definition: Radiant power, \(P\), of all wavelengths incident from all upward directions on a small element of surface containing the point under consideration divided by the area of the element. SI unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-2}\).

09619.title: irregular dendrimer
09619.definition: Substance composed of irregular dendrimer molecules.

09620.title: irregular dendrimer molecule
09620.definition: Dendrimer molecule that contains either different types of regular dendrons or at least one irregular dendron.

09621.title: irregular dendron
09621.definition: Dendron composed of either different types of constitutional units, different types of end-groups or any combination of these.

I03256.title: irregular macromolecule
I03256.definition: A macromolecule the structure of which essentially comprises the repetition of more than one type of constitutional unit or a macromolecule the structure of which comprises constitutional units not all connected identically with respect to directional sense.

I03257.title: irregular polymer
I03257.definition: A polymer composed of irregular macromolecules.

15835.title: irreversible alteration
15835.definition: Change from normal structure or function that persists or progresses after cessation of exposure of the organism.

I03258.title: irreversible transition
I03258.definition: A transition that changes the state of a system which cannot be readily reversed to restore the system to its original state. Example: The conversion of $\ce{TiO2}$ (anatase) to $\ce{TiO2}$ (rutile).

15836.title: irritant
15836.definition:
n., Substance that causes inflammation following immediate, prolonged, or repeated contact with skin, mucous membrane, or other biological material.
Note: A substance capable of causing inflammation on first contact is called a primary irritant.
adj., Causing inflammation following immediate, prolonged, or repeated contact with skin, mucous membrane, or other tissues.

08627.title: IRTRAN™
08627.definition: Kinds of crystal transparent to infrared radiation used as windows and filters in infrared spectroscopy.

11841.title: Irwin battery
11841.definition: Set of neurobehavioral tests, including observations of behavior in novel environments, of reactions, and of motor functions; used in various modifications and resembling the functional observational battery.

IT07403.title: ISC
IT07403.definition: Frequently used acronym for intersystem crossing.

10867.title: ischemia
10867.definition: Local deficiency of blood supply, and hence of dioxygen, to an organ or tissue, caused by constriction or obstruction of the blood vessels.

15372.title: Ising model
15372.definition: Theory of coexistence curves or other discontinuities in the properties of phases (such as order-disorder or magnetic transitions) in binary systems, based on a one-, two-, or three-dimensional statistical mechanical nearest-neighbor lattice theory.

11457.title: ISIS keys
11457.definition:
Predefined fragment keys that are used in 2D substructure and similarity searching with the ISIS software but are also generated by many other software
 programs and used for 2D-QSAR or cluster analysis of molecules.

13344.title: islet cell antibodies
13344.definition: Autoantibodies reacting with endocrine (pancreatic islet) cells and detectable by indirect immunofluorescence on pancreatic cryostat sections.

I03260.title: isobar
I03260.definition: Lines on a plot joining points of equal barometric pressure in the atmosphere.

I03261.title: isobaric mass-change determination
I03261.definition: A technique in which the equilibrium mass of a substance at constant partial pressure of the volatile product(s) is measured as a function of temperature while the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program. The record is the isobaric mass-change curve. The mass should be plotted on the ordinate decreasing downwards and temperature on the abscissa increasing from left to right.

I03262.title: isobaric separation
I03262.definition: Chromatographic separation carried out using constant inlet and outlet pressure conditions.

I03263.title: isobars
I03263.definition: Different nuclides of equal mass number.

14776.title: isobole approach
14776.definition: Approach used to visualize or quantify joint action of chemical mixtures by plotting a graph (isobologram) of equally effective dose pairs (isoboles) for a single effect level. A particular effect level is selected, such as \(\pu{50\%}\) of the maximum, and doses of drugs \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\) (each alone) that give this effect are plotted as axial points in a Cartesian plot. The straight line connecting \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\) is the locus of points (dose pairs) that will produce this effect in a simply additive combination. This line of additivity allows a comparison with the actual dose pair that produces this effect level experimentally.

I03265.title: isoclinic point
I03265.definition: A wavelength, wavenumber, or frequency at which the first derivative of an absorption spectrum of a sample does not change upon a chemical reaction or physical change of the sample.

IT07059.title: isoconjugate systems
IT07059.definition: Molecular entities with similar conjugate networks which have the same number of $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electrons}$, e.g. cyclopentadienide anion and pyrrole or benzene and pyridine.

I03267.title: isocoumarins
I03267.definition: Isocoumarin (1H-isochromen-1-one) and its derivatives formed by substitution.

I03268.title: isocratic analysis
I03268.definition: A procedure in which the composition of the mobile phase remains constant during the elution process.

09896.title: isocratic elution
09896.definition: Chromatography in which the composition of the mobile phase remains constant during elution.

I03269.title: isocyanates
I03269.definition: The isocyanic acid tautomer, $\ce{HN=C=O}$, of cyanic acid, $\ce{HOC≡N}$ and its hydrocarbyl derivatives RN=C=O.

I03270.title: isocyanides
I03270.definition: The isomer $\ce{HN+\!#C^{-}}$ of hydrocyanic acid, $\ce{HC#N}$, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives $\ce{RNC}$ ($\ce{RN^{+}\!#C^{-}}$).

I03271.title: isocyclic compounds
I03271.definition: A less preferred synonym for homocyclic compounds.

I03272.title: isodesmic reaction
I03272.definition: A reaction (actual or hypothetical) in which the types of bonds that are made in forming the products are the same as those which are broken in the reactants, e.g.   Such processes have advantages for theoretical treatment. The Hammett equation as applied to equilibria [cf. (a)] essentially deals with isodesmic processes.

I03273.title: isodiazenes
I03273.definition: Compounds having the structure . These compounds can also be called diazanylidenes or hydrazinylidenes. They have also been called by the trivial name azamines and the incorrectly formed name 1,1-diazenes. They should not be called 'aminonitrenes'.

I03274.title: isoelectric
I03274.definition: A macro-ion of a polyampholyte (in particular a protein) is said to be isoelectric if it exhibits no electrophoresis.

09749.title: isoelectric focusing
09749.definition: Separation technique used to separate or fractionate proteins and peptides in a gel (or similar type of media) according to their isoelectric point.

I03275.title: isoelectric point
I03275.definition: The \(\rm{pH}\) value at which the net electric charge of an elementary entity is zero. \(\rm{pI}\) is a commonly used symbol for this kind-of-quantity. It should be replaced by \(\rm{pH(I)}\) because it is a \(\rm{pH}\) determined under that particular condition.

I03276.title: isoelectronic
I03276.definition: Two or more molecular entities are described as isoelectronic if they have the same number of valence electrons and the same structure, i.e. number and connectivity of atoms, but differ in some of the elements involved. Thus: $\ce{CO}$, $\ce{N2}$ and $\ce{NO^{+}}$ are isoelectronic. $\ce{CH2=C=O}$ and $\ce{CH2=N=N}$ are isoelectronic. $\ce{CH3COCH3}$ and $\ce{CH3N=NCH3}$ have the same number of electrons, but have different structures, hence they are not described as isoelectronic.

I03277.title: isoemissive point
I03277.definition: Wavelength, wavenumber or frequency at which the total intensity of emission of light by a sample does not change during a chemical reaction or physical change. The terms isolampsic and isostilbic are sometimes used.

I03278.title: isoentropic
I03278.definition: A reaction series is said to be isoentropic if the individual reactions of the series have the same standard entropy of activation.

I03279.title: isoenzyme
I03279.definition: One of a group of related enzymes catalysing the same reaction but having different molecular structures and characterized by varying physical, biochemical and immunological properties.

I03280.title: isoequilibrium relationship
I03280.definition: A relationship analogous to the isokinetic relationship but applied to equilibrium data. The equation defining the isoequilibrium temperature \(\beta \) is: \[\Delta _{\rm{r}}H - \beta\ \Delta _{\rm{r}}S = \rm{constant}\] where \(\Delta H\) and \(\Delta S\) are enthalpy and entropy of reaction, respectively.

09970.title: isoflavans
09970.definition: Isoflavans are compounds with a 3-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran skeleton (see isoflavonoids). They may be substituted.

09971.title: isoflavones
09971.definition: Isoflavones are compounds with a 3-phenyl-4$H$-1-benzopyran-4-one (3-phenyl-4$H$-chromen-4-one) skeleton 9. They may be substituted.

13345.title: isograft
13345.definition: Tissue transplanted (see graft) between two genetically identical individuals.

IT07060.title: isogyric reaction
IT07060.definition:
A reaction in which the number of electron pairs is conserved, for example: 
$$\ce{CH4(^{1}\textit{A}_{1}) + H(^{2}\textit{S}) -> CH3(^{2}\textit{A}^{'}_{2}) + H2(^{1}\Sigma^{+}_{\rm{g}})}$$

13346.title: isohemagglutinin
13346.definition: Naturally occurring immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibody specific for the erythrocyte antigens of the ABO blood groups, thought to result from immunization by bacteria in the gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts.

I03282.title: isoionic
I03282.definition: A macro-ion of a polyampholyte (in particular a protein) is said to be isoionic if besides the polyampholyte and $\ce{H^{+}}$ or $\ce{OH^{−}}$ ions (in general ions of the solvent) no other ions are present in the system.

I03283.title: isoionic point
I03283.definition: The \(\rm{pH}\) value at which the net electric charge of an elementary entity in pure water equals zero.

I03284.title: isokinetic line
I03284.definition: A line in a given surface connecting points with equal wind speed; also called isotach or isovel.

I03285.title: isokinetic relationship
I03285.definition: When a series of structurally related substrates undergo the same general reaction or when the reaction conditions for a single substrate are changed in a systematic way, the enthalpies and entropies of activation sometimes satisfy the relation: \[\Delta ^{\ddagger}H - \beta \ \Delta ^{\ddagger }S = \rm{constant}\] where the parameter \(\beta \) is independent of temperature. This equation (or some equivalent form) is said to represent an 'isokinetic relationship'. The temperature \(T=\beta \) (at which all members of a series obeying the isokinetic relationship react at the same rate) is termed the 'isokinetic temperature'. Supposed isokinetic relationships as established by direct correlation of \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}H\) with \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}S\) are often spurious and the calculated value of \(\beta \) is meaningless, because errors in \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}H\) lead to compensating errors in \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}S\). Satisfactory methods of establishing such relationships have been devised.

I03286.title: isokinetic sampling
I03286.definition: A technique for collecting airborne particulate in which the sampling device has a collection efficiency of unity for all sizes of particles in sampled air, regardless of wind velocity and direction of the instrument. The air stream entering the collector has a velocity (speed and direction) equal to that of the air in the gas stream just ahead of the sampling port of the collector.

I03287.title: isolated double bonds
I03287.definition: Those bonds which are neither conjugated nor cumulative as in  or the B ring of

I03288.title: isolobal
I03288.definition: The term is used to compare molecular fragments with each other and with familiar species from organic chemistry. Two fragments are isolobal if the number, symmetry properties, approximate energy and shape of the frontier orbitals and the number of electrons in them are similar.

I03289.title: isomer
I03289.definition: One of several species (or molecular entities) that have the same atomic composition (molecular formula) but different line formulae or different stereochemical formulae and hence different physical and/or chemical properties.

I03296.title: isomer shift
I03296.definition: Measure of the energy difference between the source (\(E_{\rm{s}}\)) and the absorber (\(E_{\rm{a}}\)) transition. The measured Doppler velocity shift, \(\delta \), is related to the energy difference by \[E_{\rm{a}}- E_{\rm{s}}=\frac{\delta \ E_{\gamma }}{c}\] where \(E_{\gamma }\) is the Mössbauer gamma energy and \(c\) is the speed of light in vacuum.

I03290.title: isomerases
I03290.definition: Enzymes that catalyse intramolecular rearrangements. Isomerases are classified into racemases and epimerases, cis-trans isomerases, intramolecular lyases and other isomerases.

I03292.title: isomeric state
I03292.definition: A nuclear state having a mean lifetime long enough to be observed.

I03293.title: isomeric transition
I03293.definition: A spontaneous transition between two isomeric states of a nucleus.

I03295.title: isomerization
I03295.definition: A chemical reaction, the principal product of which is isomeric with the principal reactant. An intramolecular isomerization that involves the breaking or making of bonds is a special case of a molecular rearrangement. Isomerization does not necessarily imply molecular rearrangement (e.g. in the case of the interconversion of conformational isomers).

I03298.title: isometric
I03298.definition: Two molecular entities that are superposable or can be made superposable by reflection of one of them in a mirror are isometric; otherwise they are anisometric.

IT07233.title: isomorphic polymer blend
IT07233.definition: Polymer blend of two or more different semi-crystalline polymers that are miscible in the crystalline state as well as in the molten state.

I03299.title: isomorphous structures
I03299.definition: In the crystalline state, polymer chains are generally parallel to one another but neighbouring chains of equivalent conformation may differ in chirality and/or orientation. Chains of identical chirality and conformation are isomorphous. Chains of opposite chirality but equivalent conformation are enantiomorphous. For example, two ...$\ce{TG^{+}TG^{+}TG^{+}}$... helices of isotactic poly(propylene) are isomorphous. Isotactic poly(propylene) chains of the ...$\ce{TG^{+}TG^{+}TG^{+}}$... and ...$\ce{G^{+}TG^{+}TG^{+}T}$... types are mutually enantiomorphous. With regard to orientation, consider a repeating side group originating at atom \(A_{1}^{i}\), the first atom of the side group being \(B_{\alpha }^{i}\). For certain chain symmetries (helical, for instance) the bond vectors \(\overset{\rightarrow }{\mathbf{b}}(A_{1}^{i},B_{\alpha }^{i})\) have the same components (positive or negative) \(\frac{\overset{\rightarrow }{\mathbf{b}}\cdot \overset{\rightarrow }{\mathbf{c}}}{|\overset{\rightarrow }{\mathbf{c}}|}\) along the c axis for every \(i\).  Two equivalent (isomorphous or enantiomorphous) chains in the crystal lattice, having identical components of the bond vectors along $c$, both positive or both negative, are designated isoclined; two equivalent chains having bond vectors along $c$ of the same magnitude but opposite sign are designated anticlined.

I03302.title: isooptoacoustic point
I03302.definition: Wavelength, wavenumber or frequency at which the total energy emitted by a sample as heat does not change upon a chemical reaction in or a physical change of the sample. Its position depends on the experimental conditions.

15336.title: isopleth
15336.definition: Line joining points of equal composition on a phase diagram.

I03304.title: isopotential point
I03304.definition: For an ion-selective electrode cell, there is often a particular activity of the measured ion for which the emf of the cell is independent of temperature. That activity, and the corresponding potential difference, defines the isopotential point. The specification of the ion-selective electrode and outer reference electrode must be described. Comment: When an isothermal cell is used with identical reference electrodes, the isopotential point is the activity of sensed species that gives zero net membrane potential, e.g. sensed activity is the same in the inner and outer (test) solution. Calibration lines for different cell temperatures have different slopes, but intersect at a common activity point. Cells with temperature gradients are not recommended.

I03306.title: isoprenoids
I03306.definition: Compounds formally derived from isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene), the skeleton of which can generally be discerned in repeated occurrence in the molecule. The skeleton of isoprenoids may differ from strict additivity of isoprene units by loss or shift of a fragment, commonly a methyl group. The class includes both hydrocarbons and oxygenated derivatives.

I03307.title: isopycnic
I03307.definition: An adjective describing components of a multicomponent system with equal partial specific volumes.

I03308.title: isopycnic separation
I03308.definition: Chromatographic separations carried out using constant density conditions. The temperature and pressure may be altered during the run (originally the term 'isoconfertic separation' was used but this term is not recommended).

I03309.title: isorefractive
I03309.definition: An adjective describing components of a multicomponent system having zero refractive index increments with respect to each other.

I03310.title: isosbestic point
I03310.definition: Wavelength, wavenumber or frequency at which the total absorbance of a sample does not change during a chemical reaction or a physical change of the sample.

I03311.title: isoselective relationship
I03311.definition: A relationship analogous to the isokinetic relationship, but applied to selectivity data of reactions. At the isoselective temperature, the selectivities of the series of reactions following the relationship are identical.

IT07625.title: isostatic pressing
IT07625.definition: Application of a hydrostatic pressure through a liquid to achieve densification prior to the production of a uniform compact monolith through ceramization of the densified liquid.

I03313.title: isosteric enthalpy of adsorption
I03313.definition: When the addition of the differential amount of component \(i\) \(\mathrm{d}n_{i}^{\sigma }\) or \(\mathrm{d}n_{i}^{\rm{s}}\) is effected at constant pressure \(p\), the differential molar enthalpy of adsorption, \(\Delta _{a}H_{i}^{\sigma}\) or \(\Delta _{a}H_{i}^{\rm{s}}\) also called the isosteric enthalpy of adsorption (\(q^{\rm{st}}\)) is defined as: \[\Delta _{a}H_{i}^{\sigma} = -q^{\rm{st},\sigma} = U_{i}^{\sigma} - H_{i}^{\rm{g}}\] \[\Delta _{a}H_{i}^{\rm{s}} = -q^{\rm{st},\sigma} = H_{i}^{\sigma} - H_{i}^{\rm{g}}\] where \(H_{i}^{\rm{s}}=(\frac{\partial H^{\rm{s}}}{\partial n_{i}^{\rm{s}}})_{T,p,m,n_{j}^{\rm{s}}}\) and \(H_{i}^{\rm{g}}\) is the partial molar enthalpy of component \(i\) in the gas phase, i.e. \((\frac{\partial H^{\rm{g}}}{\partial n_{i}^{\rm{g}}})_{T,p,n_{i}^{\rm{g}}}\)

IT07061.title: isostructural reaction
IT07061.definition: A ligand exchange reaction, where the structural type of the metal complex remains the same. $$\ce{ML_{n} + X -> ML_{n-1}X + L + \Delta\textit{E}}$$ Although these types of reactions are not necessarily isodesmic reactions, a substantial degree of error cancellation for the calculated energy, $\Delta E$, is achieved because the coordination sphere of the metal atom $\ce{M}$ is conserved.

I03315.title: isotactic macromolecule
I03315.definition: A tactic macromolecule, essentially comprising only one species of configurational base unit, which has chiral or prochiral atoms in the main chain in a unique arrangement with respect to its adjacent constitutional units.

I03316.title: isotactic polymer
I03316.definition: A polymer composed of isotactic macromolecules.

I03318.title: isotherm
I03318.definition: Lines joining points of equal temperature in the atmosphere.

I03319.title: isothermal chromatography
I03319.definition: A procedure in which the temperature of the column is kept constant during the separation.

12296.title: isothermal technique
12296.definition: Applied to a technique to indicate that the temperature is maintained constant throughout the experiment.

I03321.title: isotones
I03321.definition: Nuclides having the same neutron number but different atomic numbers.

15837.title: isotonic
15837.definition: Denoting a liquid exerting the same osmotic pressure or chemical potential of water (water potential) as another liquid with which it is being compared.

I03322.title: isotope dilution
I03322.definition: Mixing of a given nuclide with one or more of its isotopes.

I03323.title: isotope dilution analysis
I03323.definition: A kind of quantitative analysis based on the measurement of the isotopic abundance of a nuclide after isotope dilution with the test portion.

I03327.title: isotope effect
I03327.definition: The effect on the rate or equilibrium constant of two reactions that differ only in the isotopic composition of one or more of their otherwise chemically identical components is referred to as a kinetic isotope effect or a thermodynamic (or equilibrium) isotope effect, respectively.

I03328.title: isotope exchange
I03328.definition: A chemical reaction in which the reactant and product chemical species are chemically identical but have different isotopic composition. In such a reaction the isotope distribution tends towards equilibrium (as expressed by fractionation factors) as a result of transfers of isotopically different atoms or groups. For example:

I03329.title: isotope exchange analysis
I03329.definition: A kind of quantitative analysis based on the isotope exchange between isotopes of the element to be determined and other isotopes of this element in different valency states or in different molecules.

I03330.title: isotope pattern
I03330.definition: Set of peaks related to ions with the same chemical formula but containing different isotopes; e.g. the 16 and 17 mass/charge peaks in a $\ce{CH4}$ sample arising from $\ce{^{12}CH4^{+}}$ and $\ce{^{13}CH4^{+}}$ ions.

I03331.title: isotopes
I03331.definition: Nuclides having the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

I03332.title: isotopic abundance
I03332.definition: The relative number of atoms of a particular isotopes in a mixture of the isotopes of an element, expressed as a fraction of all the atoms of the element.

I03340.title: isotopic carrier
I03340.definition: A carrier which differs only in isotopic composition from the trace it has to carry.

14777.title: isotopic discrimination
14777.definition: The differential behavior of isotopes occurring if the rate or extent of participation in some biological or chemical process depends significantly on the mass of the isotope. Also called the isotope effect.

I03341.title: isotopic enrichment
I03341.definition: Any process by which the isotopic abundance of a specified isotopes in a mixture of isotopes of an element is increased.

I03342.title: isotopic enrichment factor
I03342.definition: For a material enriched in a specified isotope, the ratio between the isotopic abundance and the natural abundance of that isotope.

I03343.title: isotopic fractionation factor
I03343.definition:
The ratio \[\frac{(x_{1}/x_{2})_{\rm{A}}}{(x_{1}/x_{2})_{\rm{B}}}\] where \(x\) is the abundance, expressed as the atom fraction of the isotope distinguished by the subscript numeral, when the two isotopes are equilibrated between two different chemical species $\ce{A}$ and $\ce{B}$ (or between specific sites A and B in the same or different chemical species). The term is most commonly met in connection with deuterium solvent isotope effects, when the fractionation factor \(\mathit{\Phi}\) expresses the ratio: \[\varPhi = \frac{(x_{\rm{D}}/x_{\rm{H}})_{\rm{solute}}}{(x_{\rm{D}}/x_{\rm{H}})_{\rm{solvent}}}
\] for the exchangeable hydrogen atoms in the chemical species (or sites) concerned. The concept is also applicable to transition states.

I03344.title: isotopic ion
I03344.definition: Any ion containing one or more of the less abundant naturally occurring isotopes of the elements that make up its structure, e.g. $\ce{CH2D^{+}}$.

08733.title: isotopic label
08733.definition: Radioactive or stable isotope of a specified element distinguishable by the observer but not by the system used to identify an isotopic tracer.

I03345.title: isotopic labelling
I03345.definition: Labelling in which the resulting product is only different from the initial one by its isotopic composition.

I03346.title: isotopic molecular ion
I03346.definition: A molecular ion containing one or more of the less abundant naturally occurring isotopes of the atoms that make up the molecular structure. Thus, for ethyl bromide there exist isotopic molecular ions such as: $\ce{^{13}CCH5Br^{+.}}$, $\ce{C2H4DBr^{+.}}$, $\ce{C2H5^{81}Br^{+.}}$, $\ce{^{13}C2H5^{81}Br^{+.}}$, etc.

I03348.title: isotopic scrambling
I03348.definition: The achievement, or the process of achieving, an equilibrium distribution of isotopes within a specified set of atoms in a chemical species or group of chemical species (for an example, see diagram).

I03349.title: isotopic separation
I03349.definition: An operation for the purpose of modifying an isotopic abundance in a mixture of isotopes.

I03350.title: isotopic tracer
I03350.definition: A tracer which only differs in isotopic composition from the substance to be traced.

I03334.title: isotopically deficient
I03334.definition: An isotopically labelled compound may be designated as isotopically deficient when the isotopic content of one or more elements has been depleted, i.e. when one or more nuclide(s) is (are) present in less than a natural ratio.

I03335.title: isotopically enriched ions
I03335.definition: When the abundance of a particular nuclide is increased above the level at which it occurs in nature and is incorporated in a molecule, the term 'isotopically enriched ion' is used to describe any ion enriched in the isotope.

I03336.title: isotopically labelled
I03336.definition: Describes a mixture of an isotopically unmodified compound with one or more analogous isotopically substituted compound(s).

I03337.title: isotopically modified
I03337.definition: Describes a compound that has a macroscopic composition such that the isotopic ratio of nuclides for at least one element deviates measurably from that occurring in nature. It is either an isotopically substituted compound or an isotopically labelled compound.

I03338.title: isotopically substituted
I03338.definition: Describes a compound that has a composition such that essentially all the molecules of the compound have only the indicated nuclide at each designated position. For all other positions, the absence of nuclide indication means that the nuclide composition is the natural one.

I03339.title: isotopically unmodified
I03339.definition: Describes a compound that has a macroscopic composition such that its constituent nuclides are present in the proportions occurring in nature.

I03351.title: isotopologue
I03351.definition: A molecular entity that differs only in isotopic composition (number of isotopic substitutions), e.g. $\ce{CH4}$, $\ce{CH3D}$, $\ce{CH2D2}$.

I03352.title: isotopomer
I03352.definition: Isomers having the same number of each isotopic atom but differing in their positions. The term is a contraction of 'isotopic isomer'. Isotopomers can be either constitutional isomers (e.g. $\ce{CH2DCH=O}$ and $\ce{CH3CD=O}$) or isotopic stereoisomers [e.g. $\ce{(\textit{R})-}$ and $\ce{(\textit{S})-CH3CHDOH}$ or $\ce{(\textit{Z})-}$ and $\ce{(\textit{E})-CH3CH=CHD}$].

10868.title: isotretinoin
10868.definition: Vitamin A-like medication (13-cis retinoic acid) used, among other things, for acne treatment.

I03353.title: isotropic
I03353.definition: A quantity which is independent of direction. Anisotropic and nonisotropic refer to quantities which are direction dependent.

I03354.title: isotropic carbon
I03354.definition: A monolithic carbon material without preferred crystallographic orientation of the microstructure.

I03355.title: isotropic pitch-based carbon fibres
I03355.definition: Carbon fibres obtained by carbonization of isotropic pitch fibres after these have been stabilized (i.e. made non-fusible).

12776.title: isotropisation temperature
12776.definition: Temperature at which a transition from any anisotropic state to an isotropic liquid occurs.

13347.title: isotype
13347.definition: Class of antibody that differs from others in the constant region of the heavy chain (Fc portion).

13348.title: isotype control
13348.definition: Antibody exhibiting the non-specific characteristics of the antibody-isotype but lacking any specificity for the antigen in question; used as a negative control in antibody-antigen detection assays, notably in flow cytometry.

13349.title: isotype switch
13349.definition: Process by which a B cell switches from making antibody of one isotype to another without altering the specificity of the antibody, producing an isotype with the same variable (V) regions but a different heavy chain constant (C) region.

I03356.title: isoureas
I03356.definition: The imidic acid tautomer of urea, $\ce{H2NC(=NH)OH}$, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives.

15838.title: itai-itai disease
15838.definition: Illness (renal osteomalacia) observed in the Toyama prefecture of Japan, resulting from the ingestion of cadmium-contaminated rice.

14778.title: iteroparous species
14778.definition: Species that reproduces more than once.

13406.title: immunoglobulin or T-cell receptor lymphocyte repertoire
13406.definition: Profile of immunoglobulins (Ig) or T-cell receptors (TCRs) available within a specified group of cells.

12456.title: jet separator
12456.definition: Gas chromatograph-to-mass spectrometer interface where the gas chromatography effluent expands into a lower-pressure region and then through a downstream orifice. The low mass carrier gas molecules diffuse from the jet axis, leaving the sample stream enriched in the heavier analyte molecules.

08372.title: J-modulated spin-echo
08372.definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance pulse sequence that refocuses spin vectors that have fanned out due to field inhomogeneity or chemical shift differences.

08373.title: J-resolved spectroscopy
08373.definition: Two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy resolving chemical shift information in one dimension and spin-spin coupling in the second.

J03359.title: j-value
J03359.definition: An effective first order rate constant for a photochemical reaction (photodecomposition, etc.) of light-absorbing impurities in the atmosphere.

J03360.title: Jablonski diagram
J03360.definition: Originally, a diagram showing that the fluorescent state of a molecular entity is the lowest excited state from which the transition to the ground state is allowed, whereas the phosphorescent state is a metastable state below the fluorescent state, which is reached by radiationless transition. In the most typical cases the fluorescent state is the lowest singlet excited state and the phosphorescent state the lowest triplet state, the ground state being a singlet. Presently, modified Jablonski diagrams are frequently used and are actually state diagrams in which molecular electronic states, represented by horizontal lines displaced vertically to indicate relative energies, are grouped according to multiplicity into horizontally displaced columns. Excitation and relaxation processes that interconvert states are indicated in the diagram by arrows. Radiative transitions are generally indicated with straight arrows (→), while radiationless transitions are generally indicated with wavy arrows ⇝.

11458.title: jackknifing
11458.definition: A procedure to evaluate the accuracy of the statistics of a model, such as the overall R2 or the contribution of particular properties, by systematically recomputing the statistics generated from models developed by leaving out one or more observations at a time from the sample set.

08628.title: Jacquinot stop
08628.definition: Aperture in the optics of a Fourier-transform spectrometer, typically between the source and the interferometer, designed to be the limiting aperture when no other optical element such as the detector serves this purpose.

J03361.title: Jahn–Teller effect
J03361.definition: Molecular distortions due to an electronically degenerate @G02704-1@ state. For non-linear molecular entities in a geometry described by a point symmetry group possessing degenerate irreducible representations there always exists at least one non-totally symmetric vibration that makes electronically degenerate states unstable at this geometry. The nuclei are displaced to new equilibrium positions of lower symmetry causing a splitting of the originally degenerate states (first-order Jahn–Teller effect).

J03362.title: Jahn–Teller transition
J03362.definition: A displacive crystal distortion to lower symmetry that cooperatively removes a localized-electron orbital degeneracy at an array of like atoms so as to leave the atoms in the centre of symmetry of their distorted sites. Example: The crystallographic distortion in $\ce{Mn3O4}$.

13350.title: JAK/STAT signaling pathway
13350.definition: Mechanism that transmits information from chemical signals outside the cell to gene promoters on the DNA in the cell nucleus. The mechanism is activated by the binding of Janus-family tyrosine kinase (JAK) to the nonpolypeptide portion of occupied receptors for some interleukins (IL). JAK phosphorylates signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) proteins apart from STAT 5a and 5b.

13351.title: JAM test
13351.definition: Method which uses labeled nucleotide precursors to estimate DNA fragmentation during cell-mediated cytotoxicity or apoptosis.

15373.title: Jänecke coordinates
15373.definition: Coordinates used mainly in representation of multicomponent phase diagrams that distinguish solutes and a single solvent. The mole or mass fractions of the \(s\) solutes are chosen as the primary composition variables and the mole or mass fraction of solvent as a secondary variable, so that the solute amount (mass) fractions may be represented, for example, in ternary and quaternary systems, as linear (ternary) or planar triangular or square planar (quaternary) diagrams, with the solvent amount or mass fraction along an axis perpendicular to the chosen diagram of solute variables. Quantitatively, \[x_{{\rm{s}},{\ce{B}}} = x_{\ce{B}}/\sum \limits_{i=1}^{s}x_{i}\] where the summation is over the \(s\) solute substances. Note that \(\sum \limits_{i=1}^{s}x_{{\rm{s}},{\ce{B}}} = 1\).

13352.title: Janus-family tyrosine kinase
13352.definition: Tyrosine kinase activated by cytokines binding to cell receptors.

15839.title: jaundice
15839.definition: Pathological condition characterized by deposition of bile pigment in the skin and mucous membranes, including the conjunctivae, resulting in yellow appearance of the patient or animal.

10869.title: jejunum
10869.definition: Second part of the small intestine between the duodenum and ileum.

13353.title: joining chain
13353.definition: Polypeptide that forms part of the polymeric structure of pentameric immunoglobulin M (IgM) and dimeric immunoglobulin A (IgA).

13354.title: joining gene
13354.definition: Gene coding for a joining segment that connects variable (V) regions and constant (C) regions of immunoglobulin (Ig) or T-cell receptor (TCR) chains that, upon gene rearrangement, encodes part of the third hypervariable region of the antigen receptors.

15840.title: joint effect
15840.definition: Simultaneous or successive effect of factors of diverse types (chemical, physical, biological) on an organism.

J03363.title: joule
J03363.definition: SI derived unit of energy, \(\pu{J} = \pu{N m} = \pu{kg m2 s-2}\).

J03364.title: junction point
J03364.definition: Branch point in a polymer network.

J03365.title: junction unit
J03365.definition: A non-repeating atom or non-repeating group of atoms between blocks in a block macromolecule.

JT07602.title: junction-point density
JT07602.definition: Number of junction points per unit volume in a polymer network.

13355.title: junctional diversity
13355.definition: Diversity of the splice junctions in the recombined variable (V) gene, diversity (D) gene [for immunoglobulin (Ig) heavy chains, and for TCR b and d chains], and joining (J) gene segments of antibody and T-cell receptor (TCR) genes.

12457.title: kinetic energy release
12457.definition: Translational energy of fragments resulting from dissociation of a metastable ion measured relative to the center-of-mass.

12458.title: kinetic energy release distribution
12458.definition: Distribution of values of translational energies in the center-of-mass reference for an ensemble of metastable ions undergoing a specific dissociation reaction.

12459.title: kinetic shift
12459.definition: Excess energy above the thermochemical threshold required to observe dissociation of a precursor ion within the timeframe of a particular mass spectrometry experiment.

12460.title: Kingdon trap
12460.definition: Ion trapping device that consists of an outer barrel-like electrode and a coaxial inner spindle-like electrode that form an electrostatic field with a quadro-logarithmic potential distribution.

10130.title: k-means clustering
10130.definition: Unsupervised classification method which partitions objects into \(k\) groups, in which each object belongs to the group with the nearest mean.

10131.title: k-nearest neighbour
10131.definition: Non-parametric supervised classification method for objects based on the closest training examples in the variable space.

14782.title: k-strategy
14782.definition: Equilibrium strategy for species involving effective interactions with each other in the community, allowing coexistence of many species. Equilibrium species are more effective competitors than opportunistic species.

11842.title: kainic acid
11842.definition: Natural amino acid produced by some seaweeds that activates a subclass of glutamate receptors ('kainate receptors') to produce excitotoxicity.

15841.title: kairomone
15841.definition: Semiochemical that is produced by one organism inducing a response in an organism of another species that is unfavorable to the emitter.

13356.title: kallikrein
13356.definition: Any of a group of enzymes found in the blood and body fluids that acts on certain plasma globulins to produce bradykinins.

K03367.title: Kamlet–Taft solvent parameters
K03367.definition: Parameters of the Kamlet–Taft solvatochromic relationship which measure separately the hydrogen bond donor ($\ce{\upalpha\!}$), hydrogen bond acceptor ($\ce{\upbeta\!}$), and dipolarity/polarizability ($\ce{\uppi\!^{\ast}}$) properties of solvents as contributing to overall solvent polarity.

14779.title: Kamofsky’s law
14779.definition: Any agent will be teratogenic if it is present at concentrations or intensities producing cell toxicity.

13357.title: Kaposi sarcoma
13357.definition: Form of skin cancer that can involve internal organs. It is most often found in patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) and can be fatal.

13358.title: kappa-light chain
13358.definition: Smaller of the two types of light chain found in human immunoglobulins (Ig), the other type being a lambda ($\uplambda\!$)-light chain.

K03369.title: Kaptein–Closs rules
K03369.definition: Rules used to predict the sign of CIDNP effects.

10870.title: karyolysis
10870.definition: Dissolution of a cell nucleus, especially during mitosis and meiosis but also following necrosis.

10871.title: karyorrhexis
10871.definition: Irreversible fragmentation of the nucleus of a dying cell following karyolysis, whereby its chromatin is distributed irregularly throughout the cytoplasm.

10872.title: karyotype
10872.definition:
Characterization of the number, form, and size of the chromosomes of an individual or a species.
Photomicrograph of an individual’s chromosomes, arranged according to a standard classification for the species.

K03370.title: Kasha rule
K03370.definition: Polyatomic molecular entities luminesce with appreciable yield only from the lowest excited state of a given multiplicity. There are exceptions to this rule.

K03371.title: Kasha–Vavilov rule
K03371.definition: The quantum yield of luminescence is independent of the wavelength of exciting radiation. There are exceptions to this rule.

K03372.title: katal
K03372.definition: Unit for catalytic activity coherent with the SI, equal to the catalytic activity that catalyses a reaction rate of one mole per second in an assay system. \(\pu{1 kat} = \pu{1 mol s-1}\). The katal is recommended for use in the specific context of enzymes and clinical chemistry.

12777.title: Kauzmann temperature
12777.definition: Temperature at which the extrapolation of the entropy of a super-cooled liquid is equal to the entropy of its crystalline state.

K03373.title: Kekulé structure
K03373.definition: A representation of an aromatic molecular entity (such as benzene), with fixed alternating single and double bonds, in which interactions between multiple bonds are assumed to be absent. For benzene:  are the Kekulé structures.

K03374.title: kelvin
K03374.definition: The kelvin, symbol \(\pu{K}\), is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Boltzmann constant \(k\) to be \(\pu{1.380649E-23}\) when expressed in the unit \(\pu{J K-1}\), which is equal to \(\pu{kg m2 s-2 K-1}\), where the kilogram, metre and second are defined in terms of h, c and ΔνCs.

10873.title: keratin
10873.definition: Fibrous protein forming the main structural constituent of hair, feathers, hoofs, claws, horns, etc.

10874.title: keratinization
10874.definition: Replacement of the outer epithelial layer of cells, especially in skin, with keratin-rich structures.

11460.title: kernel method
11460.definition:
Algorithms for pattern analysis that use functions such as Gaussians to enable them to operate in a high-dimensional descriptor space without ever computing
 the coordinates of the data in that space.

K03376.title: ketals
K03376.definition: Acetals derived from ketones by replacement of the oxo group by two hydrocarbyloxy groups $\ce{R2C(OR)2}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$). This term, once abandoned, has been reinstated as a subclass of acetals.

K03378.title: ketenes
K03378.definition: Compounds in which a carbonyl group is connected by a double bond to an alkylidene group $\ce{R2C=C=O}$.

K03379.title: ketenimines
K03379.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R2C=C=NR}$. Thus imino analogues of ketenes.

K03385.title: keto carbenes
K03385.definition: The term has imprecisely been used to designate carboxylic acyl carbenes. keto carbenes are carbenes bearing an oxo function at an unspecified site.

08181.title: keto-enol tautomerization
08181.definition: Interconversion of ketone and enol tautomers by hydron migration, accelerated by acid or base catalysis.

10875.title: ketoacidosis
10875.definition: Acidosis, as in diabetes, pregnancy, or starvation, accompanied by the accumulation of ketone bodies in body tissues and fluids.

K03383.title: ketoaldonic acids
K03383.definition: Monosaccharides in which a structure containing a keto group and a carboxylic acid group is in equilibrium with a hemiacetal structure. Specific compounds are named using the -ulosonic acid suffix.

K03384.title: ketoaldoses
K03384.definition: Monosaccharides which contain both an aldehydic and a ketonic carbonyl group in equilibrium with intramolecular hemiacetal forms.

10876.title: ketone body
10876.definition: Ketone that is an intermediate product of the breakdown of fats in the body; any of three compounds, acetoacetic acid, acetone, and (or) \(\upbeta\)-hydroxybutanoic acid, found in excess in blood and urine of persons with metabolic disorders.

K03386.title: ketones
K03386.definition: Compounds in which a carbonyl group is bonded to two carbon atoms $\ce{R2C=O}$ (neither $\ce{R}$ may be $\ce{H}$).

K03387.title: ketoses
K03387.definition: Ketonic parent sugars (polyhydroxyketones $\ce{H–[CHOH]_{n}–C(=O)[CHOH]_{m}–H}$ with three or more carbon atoms) and their intramolecular hemiacetals. The oxo group is usually at $\ce{C-2}$. E.g. ᴅ-fructose:

15843.title: ketosis
15843.definition: Pathological increase in the production of ketone bodies, for example, following blockage or failure of carbohydrate metabolism.

K03389.title: ketyls
K03389.definition: Radical anions (or the corresponding salts) derived from ketones by addition of an electron $\ce{R2C^{.}–O^{−}  R2C^{−}–O^{.}}$.

14780.title: keystone habitat
14780.definition: High-quality habitat patch essential to maintaining the vitality of the metapopulation.

14781.title: keystone species
14781.definition: Species, usually a top predator, that influences the ecological community by its activity or role, not its numerical dominance.

13360.title: killer activatory receptor
13360.definition: Receptor found on natural killer (NK) cells, and some $\ce{\upgamma\!{:}\updelta\!}$ and $\ce{\upalpha\!{:}\upbeta\! T cells}$.

13361.title: killer cell
13361.definition: Cell that displays cell-mediated cytotoxicity, including cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL, Tc), natural killer (NK) cells, and natural killer T (NKT) cells. Some also consider activated macrophages, monocytes, and interferon (IFN)-activated neutrophils to be killer cells.

13362.title: killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptor
13362.definition: Receptor expressed on natural killer (NK) cells that binds to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules on target cells; binding MHC class I inhibits the signaling that would otherwise lead to target cell killing.

13363.title: killer lectin-like receptor
13363.definition: Killer cell receptor that binds to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules and, like the C-type lectin receptors also found on these cells, can either inhibit or activate the killer cells.

K03391.title: kilogram
K03391.definition: The kilogram, symbol \(\pu{kg}\), is the SI unit of mass. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant \(h\) to be \(\pu{6.62607015E-34}\) when expressed in the unit \(\pu{J s}\), which is equal to \(\pu{kg m2 s-1}\), where the metre and the second are defined in terms of c and ΔνCs.

12675.title: kinase
12675.definition: Enzyme that transfers a phosphate group from high-energy donor molecules, such as ATP, to specific target molecules.

09980.title: kind-of-nominal-property
09980.definition: Defining aspect, common to mutually comparable nominal properties.

K03392.title: kind-of-property
K03392.definition: An attribute of phenomena, bodies or substances that may be distinguished qualitatively. Examples: Colour (value: green, blue), transparency, length (value: long, short; \(2\ \rm{m}\), \(5\ \rm{m}\)), amount-of-substance (value: \(\pu{2 mol}\), \(\pu{5 mol}\)). Kind-of-property includes the concept kind-of-quantity. All kinds-of-property may be related to nominal (e.g. green, blue) and ordinal scales (e.g. small, large), but kinds-of-quantity are generally related to difference [e.g. \(10\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\) (i.e. \(10\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\) more than an arbitrary zero)] or ratio scales (length \(2\ \rm{m}\) or \(5\ \rm{m}\)).

K03393.title: kind-of-quantity
K03393.definition: Abstract property common to several real quantities.

11843.title: kindling
11843.definition: Increase of epileptogenic activities as a result of repeated, longer-lasting subthreshold brain stimulation, e.g., with electrical stimuli.

09374.title: kinematic factor
09374.definition: Particle energy after an elastic collision divided by the energy before the collision, in the laboratory frame of reference.

K03395.title: kinematic viscosity
K03395.definition: Dynamic viscosity divided by the density of the fluid.

K03394.title: kinematics
K03394.definition: The study of the properties of motion that are independent of the nature of the forces. In reaction dynamics the term is often applied in particular to effects that occur when atomic masses are changed, the forces remaining the same.

K03396.title: kinetic activity factor
K03396.definition: A factor involving activity coefficients that appears as a multiplier in the rate equation. For a bimolecular reaction the factor is \[\frac{y_{\rm{A}}\ y_{\rm{B}}}{y_{\ddagger}}\] where \(y_{\rm{A}}\), \(y_{\rm{B}}\) and \(y_{\ddagger }\) are the activity coefficients for the reactants A and B and the activated complex, respectively. For a unimolecular reaction the factor is \[\frac{y_{\rm{A}}}{y_{\ddagger}}\] and for a trimolecular reaction it is \[\frac{y_{\rm{A}}\ y_{\rm{B}}\ y_{\rm{C}}}{y_{\ddagger}}\]

14152.title: kinetic assay
14152.definition: Assay in which the time dependence of the signal intensity is measured. Signal values are typically acquired at several time intervals in order to calculate kinetic parameters.

K03398.title: kinetic control
K03398.definition: The term characterizes conditions (including reaction times) that lead to reaction products in a proportion governed by the relative rates of the parallel (forward) reactions in which the products are formed, rather than by the respective overall equilibrium constants.

08629.title: kinetic coupling
08629.definition: Coupling of vibrational displacements through terms in the vibrational kinetic energy.

K03399.title: kinetic current
K03399.definition: A faradaic current that corresponds to the reduction or oxidation of an electroactive substance formed by a prior chemical reaction from another substance that is not electroactive, and that is partially or entirely controlled by the rate of that reaction. The reaction may be heterogeneous, occurring at an electrode-solution interface (surface reaction), or it may be homogeneous, occurring at some distance from the interface (volume reaction).

K03401.title: kinetic electrolyte effect
K03401.definition: The general effect of an added electrolyte (i.e. an effect other than, or in addition to, that due to its possible involvement as a reactant or catalyst) on the observed rate constant of a reaction in solution. At low concentrations (when only long-range coulombic forces need to be considered) the effect on a given reaction is determined only by the ionic strength of the solution and not by the chemical identity of the ions. For practical purposes, this concentration range is roughly the same as the region of validity of the Debye–Hückel limiting law for activity coefficients. At higher concentrations, the effect of an added electrolyte depends also on the chemical identity of the ions. Such specific action can usually be interpreted as the incursion of a reaction path involving an ion of the electrolyte as reactant or catalyst, in which case the action is not properly to be regarded just as a kinetic electrolyte effect. Kinetic electrolyte effects are usually (too restrictively and therefore incorrectly) referred to as 'kinetic salt effects'. A kinetic electrolyte effect ascribable solely to the influence of the ionic strength on activity coefficients of ionic reactants and transition states is called a 'primary kinetic electrolyte effect'. A kinetic electrolyte effect arising from the influence of the ionic strength of the solution upon the pre-equilibrium concentration of an ionic species that is involved in a subsequent rate-limiting step of a reaction is called a 'secondary kinetic electrolyte effect'. A common case encountered in practice is the effect on the concentration of hydrogen ion (acting as catalyst) produced from the ionization of a weak acid in a buffer solution. Synonymous with kinetic equivalence.

K03402.title: kinetic energy
K03402.definition: Energy of motion: for a body of mass \(m\), \[E_{\rm{k}}=\frac{m\ v^{2}}{2}\] where \(v\) is the speed.

K03403.title: kinetic equivalence
K03403.definition: Two reaction schemes are kinetically equivalent if they imply the same rate law. For example, consider the two schemes (i) and (ii) for the formation of $\ce{C}$ from $\ce{A}$: \[(\rm{i}) \qquad \ce{A [k_{1},\ce{OH^{-}}][k_{-1},\ce{OH^{-}}] B ->[k_{2}] C}\] Providing that $\ce{B}$ does not accumulate as a reaction intermediate. \[\frac{\rm{d}[\ce{C}]}{\rm{d}t} = \frac{k_{1} k_{2}[\ce{A}][\ce{OH^{-}}]}{k_{2} + k_{-1} [\ce{OH^{-}}]}\] \[(\rm{ii}) \qquad \ce{A [k_{1}][k_{-1}] B ->[k_{2}][\ce{OH^{-}}] C}\] Providing that $\ce{B}$ does not accumulate as a reaction intermediate: \[\frac{\rm{d}[\ce{C}]}{\rm{d}t} = \frac{k_{1} k_{2}[\ce{A}][\ce{OH^{-}}]}{k_{-1} + k_{2} [\ce{OH^{-}}]}\] Both equations for \(\frac{\rm{d}[\ce{C}]}{\rm{d}t}\) are of the form: \[\frac{\rm{d}[\ce{C}]}{\rm{d}t} = \frac{r [\ce{A}][\ce{OH^{-}}]}{1 + s [\ce{OH^{-}}]}\] where \(r\) and \(s\) are constants (sometimes called 'coefficients in the rate equation'). The equations are identical in their dependence on concentrations and do not distinguish whether $\ce{OH^{−}}$ catalyses the formation of $\ce{B}$, and necessarily also its reversion to $\ce{A}$, or is involved in its further transformation to $\ce{C}$. The two schemes are therefore kinetically equivalent under conditions to which the stated provisos apply.

K03405.title: kinetic isotope effect
K03405.definition: The effect of isotopic substitution on a rate constant is referred to as a kinetic isotope effect. For example, in the reaction:  the effect of isotopic substitution in reactant $\ce{A}$ is expressed as the ratio of rate constants \(\frac{k^{\rm{l}}}{k^{\rm{h}}}\), where the superscripts \(\rm{l}\) and \(\rm{h}\) represent reactions in which the molecules $\ce{A}$ contain the light and heavy isotopes, respectively. Within the framework of transition state theory in which the reaction is rewritten as:  and with neglect of isotopic mass on tunnelling and the transmission coefficient, \(\frac{k^{\rm{l}}}{k^{\rm{h}}}\) can be regarded as if it were the equilibrium constant for an isotope exchange reaction between the transition state $\ce{[TS]^{\ddagger}}$ and the isotopically substituted reactant $\ce{A}$, and calculated from their vibrational frequencies as in the case of a thermodynamic isotope effect. Isotope effects like the above, involving a direct or indirect comparison of the rates of reaction of isotopologues, are called 'intermolecular', in contrast to intramolecular isotope effects, in which a single substrate reacts to produce a non-statistical distribution of isotopomeric product molecules.

K03406.title: kinetic method
K03406.definition: An analytical method in which the rate of a reaction or a related quantity is measured and utilized to determine concentrations.

K03407.title: kinetic resolution
K03407.definition: The achievement of partial or complete resolution by virtue of unequal rates of reaction of the enantiomers in a racemate with a chiral agent (reagent, catalyst, solvent, etc.).

12676.title: kinetic solubility
12676.definition: Composition of a solution with respect to a compound when its induced precipitate first appears.

15409.title: kinetic-chain length
15409.definition: In a chain polymerization, the rate of chain propagation divided by the sum of the rates of all of the chain-termination processes.

15842.title: kinetics
15842.definition: Branch of chemistry concerned with measuring and studying rates of chemical reactions.

13364.title: kinin
13364.definition: Any of a family of polypeptides that is released during inflammatory responses and that increases vascular permeability and smooth muscle contraction.

12263.title: Kirkwood–Riseman theory
12263.definition: Theory, based on the pearl-necklace model, that describes the translational diffusive and viscous flows of an isolated linear macromolecule in solution in the theta state and accounts for the gradual change from free-draining behaviour at lower molecular weights to impermeable behaviour at higher molecular weights.

K03410.title: klado-
K03410.definition: An affix used in names to designate a very open polyboron structure.

10877.title: Klinefelter syndrome
10877.definition: Syndrome in males resulting from a genetic defect in which an extra female X chromosome (thus an XXY genotype) is present in a male, characterized by small testes, long legs, enlarged breasts, reduced sperm production, and mental retardation.

08374.title: Knight shift
08374.definition: Frequency shift in the nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum of a paramagnetic species that refers to the relative shift \(\boldsymbol{K}\) in NMR frequency for atoms in a metal (e.g., sodium) compared with the same atoms in a nonmetallic environment (e.g., as a salt).

15844.title: knock-down
15844.definition: Technique used to decrease the expression of a particular gene in a cell or living organism in order to define its function.

15845.title: knock-in
15845.definition: Technique used to express an exogenous gene or to overexpress an endogenous gene in a living organism in order to define its function.

15846.title: knock-out
15846.definition: Technique used to inactivate a particular gene in a living organism in order to define its function.

13365.title: knockout
13365.definition: Use of homologous genetic recombination in embryonic stem cells to replace a functional gene with a defective copy of the gene.

13366.title: knockout mouse
13366.definition: Mouse produced from embryonic cells containing DNA that has been genetically engineered so that it does not express a particular gene or group of genes.

10878.title: knockout mutation
10878.definition: Mutation that leads to the loss of function of a particular gene.

12778.title: Kohlrausch–Williams–Watts equation
12778.definition: Equation describing the enthalpy relaxation, \(\Delta H\) which is observed during the annealing of polymers in the glassy state at a temperature, \(T_{\rm{a}}\), lower than \(T_{\rm{g}}\) \[\Delta H(t_{\rm{a}}) = \Delta c_{p}(T_{\rm{g}} - T_{\rm{a}}) \exp\!\left[- \left (\frac{t_{\rm{a}}}{\tau} \right)^{\beta} \right]\] \(\Delta H\) = difference of the enthalpy in the initial, glassy state, and the enthalpy of the glassy state after annealing; \(t_{\rm{a}}\) = time of annealing; \(\Delta c_{p}\) = difference in heat capacity at the glass-transition temperature, \(T_{\rm{g}}\), and the starting temperature of the annealing process, \(T_{\rm{a}}\); \(\tau\) = relaxation time at \(T_{\rm{a}}\); \(\beta\) = exponential factor.

10132.title: Kohonen network
10132.definition: Type of self-organising map with low dimensional grid.

K03411.title: Koopmans' theorem
K03411.definition: Directly relates experimental ionization potentials with energy levels of molecular orbitals. The theorem states that the ionization potential required to remove an electron from the orbital \(\Psi _{\rm{i}}\) is given by the negative value of the energy of the orbital, \(-\varepsilon_{\rm{i}}\), as calculated within the Hartree–Fock approximation. The theorem is not applied to localized molecular orbitals, which are not eigenfunctions of the effective hamiltonian.

K03412.title: Koppel–Palm solvent parameters
K03412.definition: Parameters to measure separately the ability of a solvent to enter into non-specific solvent–solute interactions (permittivity \(\varepsilon\) and refractive index \(\eta _{\rm{D}}\)) and specific solvent–solute interaction (solvent basicity or nucleophilicity \(B\) and solvent acidity or electrophilicity \(E\)) as contributing to overall solvent polarity.

12251.title: Kraemer equation
12251.definition: Equation describing the dependence of the inherent viscosity, \(\eta_{\rm{inh}}\), of a dilute solution on the mass concentration of the solute, \(c\), with \[\eta_{\rm{inh}} = (\ln \eta_{\rm{r}})/c = [\eta] + k_{\rm{K}}[\eta]^{2} c\] where \(k_{\rm{K}}\) is the Kraemer coefficient and \([\eta]\) is the intrinsic viscosity.

K03415.title: Krafft point
K03415.definition: The temperature (more precisely, narrow temperature range) above which the solubility of a surfactant rises sharply. At this temperature the solubility of the surfactant becomes equal to the critical micelle concentration. It is best determined by locating the abrupt change in slope of a graph of the logarithm of the solubility against \(t\) or \(\frac{1}{T}\).

08263.title: Kramers–Kronig transforms

K03416.title: Kratky plot
K03416.definition: A diagrammatic representation of scattering data on large particles, obtained at different angles but at the same concentration, constructed by plotting \((\sin \frac{\theta }{2})^{2}\ \Delta R\left(\theta \right)\) vs. \((\sin \frac{\theta}{2})^{2}\), or \(q^{2}\ \Delta R\left(\theta \right)\) vs. \(q\) and used for the determination of molecular shape. \(\Delta R(\theta)\) is the excess Rayleigh ratio, \(P(\theta)\) the particle scattering function, \(\theta \) the scattering angle and \(q\) the length of the scattering vector.

08630.title: KRS-5
08630.definition: Eutectic (\(\pu{42 \% TlBr, 58 \% TlI}\)) mixture of thallium bromide and thallium iodide transparent to infrared radiation used as window in infrared spectroscopy.

K03417.title: krypton ion laser
K03417.definition: A CW or pulsed laser emitting lines from \(337\) to \(859\ \rm{nm}\) from singly ionized krypton. Principal emissions are at \(530.9\), \(568.2\), \(647.1\) and \(752.5\ \rm{nm}\).

08631.title: Kubelka–Munk function
08631.definition: \(f(R_{\infty}) = (1 – R_{\infty})^{2}/2R_{\infty}\), where \(R_{\infty}\) is the diffuse reflectance from a sample of infinite depth.

15374.title: Kuenen coefficient
15374.definition: Volume \(V^{\rm{g}}\) of an amount \(n_{\ce{B}}^{\rm{l}}\) of a dissolved gas at a given standard temperature \(T^{^⦵\!}\) (usually \(\pu{273.15 K}\)) and given standard pressure \(p^{_{^⦵\!}}\) (\(\pu{1 bar} = \pu{0.1 MPa}\) or, in older literature, \(\pu{1 atm}\)) divided by the mass \(m^{\rm{l}}\) of the dissolving liquid containing an amount $n_{\ce{A}}$ of solvent at temperature $T$ and the given pressure \(p^{_{^⦵\!}}\).

12204.title: Kuhn segment
12204.definition: Segment or link of an equivalent freely jointed chain.

13367.title: Kupffer cell
13367.definition: Fixed tissue macrophage found lining the blood sinuses in the liver.

13368.title: Kveim reaction
13368.definition: Test for sarcoidosis, eliciting a granuloma at the site of intrradermal injection of a lymph node extract from a person with active disease. Generally considered non-specific.

10879.title: kyphosis
10879.definition: Rearward curvature or convexity of the spine in excess of normal, resulting in a protuberant upper back.

K03366.title: κ
K03366.definition: An affix in the name of a polydentate chelate complex indicating single ligating atom attachments of a polyatomic ligand to a coordination centre. A right superscript numerical index indicates the number of such attachments.

13960.title: life cycle assessment
13960.definition: Investigation and valuation of the environmental impacts of a given product or service caused or necessitated by its existence.

12461.title: label-free quantitation
12461.definition: Method for determining the concentration of proteins through a combination of protein digestion and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) without relying on stable isotope labeling. Protein quantification is achieved by measuring the signal intensity of peptide ions corresponding to a protein or by counting and comparing the number of fragment mass spectra identifying peptides of a given protein.

12462.title: laser desorption
12462.definition: Formation of gas-phase species from a solid or liquid sample surface upon activation using a short pulse of photons from a laser.

12463.title: laser desorption ionization
12463.definition: Formation of gas-phase ions by the interaction of a laser with a solid or liquid material.

12464.title: laser microprobe mass spectrometry
12464.definition: Laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry, particularly emphasizing spatially resolved composition information.

12465.title: linear ion trap
12465.definition: Two-dimensional Paul ion trap in which ions are confined in the axial dimension by means of a static electric potential.

12466.title: liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry
12466.definition: Technique by which a mixture of analytes is separated into individual components by liquid chromatography (typically high-performance liquid chromatography), followed by detection with a mass spectrometer.

12467.title: liquid ion evaporation
12467.definition: Spray ionization interface in which droplets are dispersed from a pneumatic nebulizer toward a high potential electrode that produces a static charge on the droplets leading to ion formation after solvent evaporation.

12468.title: liquid junction interface
12468.definition: Means of coupling capillary electrophoresis to a mass spectrometer in which a liquid reservoir surrounds the separation capillary and transfer capillary to the mass spectrometer and provides electric contact for the capillary electrophoresis.

12469.title: liquid secondary ionization
12469.definition: Ionization of any species by the interaction of a focused beam of ions or atoms with a sample that is dissolved in a solvent matrix.

12470.title: liquid sheath
12470.definition: Flow of make-up liquid in a sheath flow interface.

12471.title: lock mass
12471.definition: Mass of an ion of known m/z value, derived from a suitable standard compound introduced into an ion source together with the sample to be analyzed, which permits real-time recalibration by correction of m/z shifts arising from instrumental drift.

12472.title: low-energy collision-induced dissociation
12472.definition: Collision-induced dissociation process wherein the precursor ion has laboratory-frame translational energy lower than a given value, often taken to be \(\pu{1 keV}\).

14211.title: left-handed helix
14211.definition: Helix in which the continuous helical line, approximating the sequence of bonds along the polymer main chain, winds clockwise moving towards the observer, i.e., seen from the positive axis direction (see the figures in chain identity period).

14250.title: lamellar crystal sector
14250.definition: Portion of a lamellar crystal, often bounded by a well-defined crystal face.

14251.title: long period
14251.definition: Average periodicity (repeating distance) of the layers of lamellar crystals in a stacked assembly.

12882.title: lupus anticoagulant
12882.definition: Autoantibody that binds to phospholipids and/or proteins of the cell membrane in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and can interfere with blood clotting and tests of clotting function.

14478.title: lipid-based bioconcentration factor
14478.definition: Ratio of the concentration of the substance of concern in the lipid fraction of the test organism to the concentration in the ambient water.

L03422.title: l
L03422.definition: An obsolete prefix for (−)-,See: d, l, dlFor like and unlike diastereoisomersSee: l, u

13369.title: L-selectin
13369.definition: Any of a group of leukocyte surface adhesion molecules; they are classed as CD62 in the cluster of differentiation (CD) antigen marker system. All have lectin family carbohydrate binding domains and epidermal growth factor (EGF) repeats.

L03423.title: l, u
L03423.definition: Stereodescriptors of diastereoisomers with two chirality elements. When the two chirality elements are both R or both S the molecular entity is described as having an l relationship (l = like), when one chirality element is R and the other S the molecular entity is described as having a u relationship (u = unlike).
