L03594.definition: Non-SI unit of volume, \(\pu{L} = \pu{E-3 m3}\). The other allowed symbol is \(\mathrm{l}\).

10897.title: litter
10897.definition: Multiple offspring produced by a mammal from one pregnancy.

14807.title: littoral
14807.definition:
Belonging to the shore of a lake, river, pond, or especially the sea.
Intertidal zone, sometimes referring specifically to the shallow well-lit region along the shore.

14808.title: littoral enclosures
14808.definition: Isolated shore regions of freshwater ponds separated from the main body of water by plastic dividers used for ecotoxicological testing. These test systems generally have a volume of \(\pu{1000 L}\) to \(\pu{5E4 L}\) and a maximum depth of \(\pu{2 m}\).

13391.title: live attenuated vaccine
13391.definition: Vaccine prepared from living attenuated organisms or from viruses that have been attenuated but can still replicate in the cells of the host organism.

L03595.title: live time
L03595.definition: For a measurement, the time during which a radiation measuring assembly is capable of processing events occurring in the radiation detector. It equals the clock time minus the integrated resolving or dead time (to be distinguished from 'life time').

13392.title: liver-kidney microsomal antibodies
13392.definition: Autoantibodies directed against cytochrome P450 and uridine diphosphate (UDP)-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT) antigens typically found in patients with immune-mediated hepatitis.

08980.title: living anionic polymerization
08980.definition: Anionic polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

08987.title: living cationic polymerization
08987.definition: Cationic polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

09012.title: living condensative chain polymerization
09012.definition: Condensative chain polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

08998.title: living coordination polymerization
08998.definition: Coordination polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

L03596.title: living copolymerization
L03596.definition: A copolymerization which is a living polymerization.

08975.title: living ionic polymerization
08975.definition: Ionic polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

LT07156.title: living polymer
LT07156.definition: Polymer with stable, polymerization-active sites formed by a chain polymerization in which irreversible chain transfer and chain termination are absent.

08961.title: living polymer chain
08961.definition: Polymer chains that possess the potential for chain growth under the polymerization conditions.

L03597.title: living polymerization
L03597.definition: A chain polymerization from which chain transfer and chain termination are absent. In many cases, the rate of chain initiation is fast compared with the rate of chain propagation, so that the number of kinetic-chain carriers is essentially constant throughout the polymerization.

08914.title: living radical polymerization
08914.definition: Radical polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

08991.title: living ring-opening metathesis polymerization
08991.definition: Ring-opening metathesis polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

L03598.title: load
L03598.definition: The total weight acting, after counterbalancing, upon the terminal bearing which carries the object being weighed.

14809.title: loading
14809.definition: Ratio of animal biomass to the volume of test solution in an exposure chamber.

L03599.title: loading capacity
L03599.definition: The maximum concentration of solute(s) that a solvent can contain under specified conditions.

15203.title: loading dose
15203.definition: Initial, typically larger than the maintenance dose of a drug given to a patient at the start of pharmacotherapy.

11466.title: loading of a property
11466.definition: The contribution of the property to a principal component or partial least squares latent variable.

10096.title: loadings
10096.definition: Projection of a factor onto the variables.

10097.title: loadings plot
10097.definition: Plot of one loading against variable number, or two or three loadings against each other.

11854.title: lobe
11854.definition: One of the four main regions of the cerebral cortex.

L03600.title: local conformation
L03600.definition: The conformation of a macromolecule at the scale of the constitutional units. In the polymer literature, local conformation is sometimes referred to as microconformation.

14028.title: local differential absorption
14028.definition: Absorption term in the radiative transfer equation (RTE). Mathematical expression is \[\alpha_{\lambda} (\boldsymbol{x},t) L_{\mathit{\Omega},\lambda} (\boldsymbol{x}/t)\] with \(\alpha_{\lambda} (\boldsymbol{x},t)\) the space- and time-dependent linear napierian absorption coefficient and \(L_{\mathit{\Omega},\lambda} (\boldsymbol{x},t)\) the spectral radiance arriving at position \(x\) and time \(t\) from every possible angular directions \(\mathit{\Omega}\).

16239.title: local effect
16239.definition: Change occurring at the site of contact between an organism and a toxicant.

L03602.title: local efficiency of atomization
L03602.definition: The substance fraction of atomized component in the component consumed. The efficiency of atomization is measured in a given part of the flame, usually the observation space; \(\varepsilon_{\rm{a}} = \varepsilon_{\rm{n}}\ \chi _{\rm{s}}\ \chi _{\rm{v}}\ \chi _{\rm{a}}\). The signal is a function of the product \(q_{\rm{v}}\ \varepsilon_{\rm{a}}\), but \(\varepsilon_{\rm{a}}\) is also a function of \(q_{\rm{v}}\), usually decreasing at high volume rates.

L03603.title: local flame temperature
L03603.definition: The effective thermodynamic temperature in the observation space as measured by a specific sensor for a specified element (in \(\rm{K}\)). The temperature of a flame (or other plasma) is not homogeneous. It is usually lower at the borders of the flame. It is therefore appropriate to speak of an effective temperature which represents an average value of all temperatures throughout the observation space. The flame temperature depends on several factors such as: kind of plasma, kind of gas or gas mixture and concentration gradient of the thermometric species in the observation space.

L03604.title: local fraction atomized
L03604.definition: The substance fraction of the atomized component in the total volatilized component. This quantity is measured in a defined part of the flame, usually the observation space. The fraction atomized is the result of chemical reactions in the gaseous state. It depends on the bond strength of the compounds that the component may form within the flame and on the composition and temperature of the flame. When analysing elements that tend to become oxidized in the flame, it may be advisable to use as fuel gas mixtures with a reducing component such as $\ce{C2H2}$ or $\ce{N2O}$.

L03605.title: local fraction desolvated
L03605.definition: The amount-of-substance fraction of component in a desolvated state in the amount of component entering the flame. This quantity is measured in a defined part of the flame, usually the observation space. Because it varies with height in the flame as a result of progressive evaporation of aerosol droplets, it is appropriate to term the expression local. The fraction desolvated does not account for losses by incomplete volatilization of the dry aerosol (which largely depends upon the nature and concentration of the component). Such losses are described by local fraction volatilized, which usually depends on the solute. Since \(\chi _{\rm{s}}\) varies markedly with the height in the flame, its observed value represents an average. Local fraction desolvated depends on the solvent, the temperature of the flame and the time the component takes to travel from the tip of the burner to the height in the flame considered.

L03606.title: local fraction volatilized
L03606.definition: The substance fraction of the volatilized component in the total desolvated component. The gaseous state includes free atoms, molecules and radicals. This quantity is measured in a defined part of the flame, usually the observation space. The fraction volatilized varies inversely with the size of the desolvated particles. Since \(\chi _{\rm{v}}\) varies markedly with the height in the flame, its observed value represents an average.

08633.title: local mode
08633.definition: Mode of vibration localized in one type of bond.

11467.title: local model
11467.definition: A computational model that applies to only a subset of molecules, typically a closely related series.

08634.title: local molar polarizability

LT07066.title: localized molecular orbitals
LT07066.definition: The molecular orbitals located on certain fragments of a molecular system and spatially separated from each other as much as possible. The LMOs are derived from the electron occupied canonical molecular orbitals by subjecting them to a unitary transformation determined by an appropriate physical criterion, e.g. by maximizing the sum of squares of the centroids of occupied MOs (the Foster–Boys procedure) or by minimizing the sum of the exchange (or Coulomb) repulsion integrals between the occupied MOs (the Edmiston–Ruedenberg procedure).

L03608.title: localized-itinerant transition
L03608.definition: A transition of either of two types: (a) a Mott transition (single-valent systems). (b) a small-polaron to itinerant-electron transition (mixed-valent systems).

09014.title: locant
09014.definition: Numeral or letter or a combination of both that identifies position(s) in a structure.

08267.title: lock-in amplifier
08267.definition: Amplifier that amplifies only those signals that have, within a specified spectral bandwidth, the same frequency as, and a specified phase relation with, the selected reference signal.

10898.title: locus
10898.definition: Specific location of a gene or DNA sequence on a chromosome.

10899.title: LOD score
10899.definition: Ratio of the likelihood of two or more loci remaining together when chromosomes recombine (true linkage) to the likelihood of this occurring by chance alone.

11468.title: log D
11468.definition: The logarithm of the ratio of the total concentration (neutral and charged species) of a compound in a nonpolar phase, traditionally water-saturated octan-1-ol, to that in water at a given \(\pu{pH}\).

11469.title: log P
11469.definition:
The logarithm of the ratio of the concentration of the uncharged form of a compound in a nonpolar phase, traditionally water-saturated octan-1-ol, to that in
 water.

L03614.title: log-normal distribution
L03614.definition: A distribution function \(F(y)\), in which the logarithm of a quantity is normally distributed, i.e. \(F(y)=f_{\rm{gauss}}(\ln y)\) where \(f_{\rm{gauss}}(x)\) is a Gaussian distribution. The size distributions of atmospheric aerosols are often described using this distribution function, although the term also applies to gaseous pollutants.

14813.title: log-normal transformation
14813.definition: Transformation of data with a logarithmic function that results in a normal distribution.

12780.title: logarithmic decrement
12780.definition: Natural logarithm of the ratio of the displacement of a damping curve separated by one period of the displacement.

L03611.title: logarithmic normal distribution
L03611.definition: A continuous distribution with the differential mass-distribution function of the form: \[f_{\rm{w}}(x)\ \rm{d}x = \frac{1}{a\ \sqrt{\pi \ x}}\ \exp (- \frac{1}{a^{2}}\ \ln ^{2}\frac{x}{b})\ \rm{d}x\] where \(x\) is a parameter characterizing the chain length, such as relative molecular mass or degree of polymerization and \(a\) and \(b\) are positive adjustable parameters.

14810.title: logistic curve
14810.definition: Function, often applied to growth curves, fitting the general equation \[y = k/(1 + e^{a+bt})\] where \(t\) represents time, \(y\) the body weight or population size, \(k\) the rate of growth, and \(a\) and \(b \gt 0\) are constants. In the logistic equation the percentage rate of increase decreases linearly as size increases. The resulting curve continually rises, slowly at first, more rapidly in the middle phase, and slowly again near the end of growth.

14811.title: logistic growth
14811.definition: Growth of a population under environmental constraints that set a maximum population size, giving an S-shaped curve.

L03613.title: logit
L03613.definition: In competitive binding assays, the logit-log dose relationship, in which the response is defined by: \(R=\mathrm{logit}\left(y\right)=\log _{10}(\frac{y}{1- y})\) where \(y=\frac{b}{b_{0}}\) with \(b\) = fraction of tracer bound and \(b_{0}\) = value of \(b\) with no unlabelled ligand in the system. Logit transformed assay data frequently yield straight-line dose-response curves, amenable to statistical analysis.

14812.title: logit transformation
14812.definition: In competitive binding assays, the logit-log dose relationship, in which the response is defined by \[R = {\rm{logit}}\,(y) = \ln [y/(1 - y)]\] where \(y = b/b_{0}\), \(b\) is fraction of tracer bound and \(b_{0}\) is the value of \(b\) with no unlabelled ligand in the system.

L03617.title: London forces
L03617.definition: Attractive forces between apolar molecules, due to their mutual polarizability. They are also components of the forces between polar molecules. Also called 'dispersion forces'.

L03615.title: London–Eyring–Polanyi method
L03615.definition: A semiempirical method of calculating a potential-energy surface, based on a simplified quantum-mechanical equation (the London equation).

L03616.title: London–Eyring–Polanyi–Sato method
L03616.definition: A modification of the London–Eyring–Polanyi proposed in 1955 by S. Sato.

L03618.title: lone pair
L03618.definition: Two paired electrons localized in the valence shell on a single atom. Lone pairs should be designated with two dots. The term 'nonbonding electron pair' is more appropriate, and is found in many modern text books.

L03619.title: long chain
L03619.definition: A chain of high relative molecular mass.

L03624.title: long spacing
L03624.definition: The average separation between stacked lamellar crystals, usually measured by small-angle X-ray or neutron diffraction.

L03622.title: long-lived collision complex
L03622.definition: When a potential-energy surface is such that the system performs a number of vibrations and rotations in the region of a col, the corresponding intermediate is known as a long-lived collision complex, and the reaction is said to be indirect.

L03623.title: long-range intramolecular interaction
L03623.definition: An interaction between segments, widely separated in sequence along the chain, that occasionally approach one another during molecular flexing. This type of interaction is closely related to the excluded volume of a segment, the latter quantity reflecting interactions involving segments and solvent molecules. If no confusion can occur, the word 'intramolecular' may be omitted.

12017.title: long-term potentiation
12017.definition: Potentiation lasting up to several months.

L03621.title: longitudinal order
L03621.definition: Order in the atomic positions along the chains of a linear polymer.

L03625.title: loose end
L03625.definition: Polymer chain within a network which is connected by a junction-point at one end only.

14814.title: Lorax incongruity
14814.definition: Delusion of selfless motivation in environmental stewardship or advocacy.

10900.title: lordosis
10900.definition: Forward (ventral) curvature of the spine in the lumbar and cervical regions.

L03628.title: Lorentzian band shape
L03628.definition:
This band shape is described by the function: \[F\left(
u - 
u _{0}ight) =  rac{1}{\pi }\ \gamma \ ((
u - 
u _{0})^{2}+\gamma ^{2})^{-1}\] where \(
u_{0}\) is the mean band position, \(\gamma \) is the half band width at half maximum, and \(F\ (
u - 
u _{0})\) is the frequency distribution function.

L03629.title: Lorenz–Mie theory
L03629.definition: Theory of light scattering by isotropic, homogeneous spheres.

12781.title: loss curve
12781.definition: Plot of loss tangent (\(\tan \delta\)) vs. the temperature or the frequency of the forced sinusoidal oscillation.

12782.title: loss modulus
12782.definition: Ratio of the amplitude of the stress \(\pu{90\!^{\circ}}\) out of phase with the strain (\(\sigma_{0} \sin \delta\)) to the amplitude of the strain (\(\gamma_{0}\)) in the forced sinusoidal oscillation of a material. \[M^{\prime\prime} = \frac{\sigma_{0} \sin \delta}{\gamma_{0}}\]

14815.title: loss of life expectancy
14815.definition: Calculated estimate of loss in lifetime associated with a risk factor; it is estimated as the simple difference between life expectancy without the risk factor and life expectancy with the risk factor.

12783.title: loss tangent
12783.definition: Tangent of the phase angle (\(\delta\)) between stress and strain during a forced sinusoidal oscillation.

L03630.title: lot
L03630.definition: A quantity of material which is assumed to be a single population for sampling purposes.

14816.title: lotic
14816.definition: Related to flowing continental waters, such as rivers and streams.

14817.title: lotic mesocosms
14817.definition: Streams of various sizes used to evaluate the effects of substances. Unlike lentic systems, no standardized design has been developed for flowing-water test systems.

14818.title: lotic water
14818.definition: Flowing continental waters, such as rivers and streams.

15204.title: lotion
15204.definition: Solution, emulsion, or suspension to be applied to the skin.

L03631.title: low energy electron diffraction
L03631.definition: Any technique which measures the angular intensity distribution of electrons reflected from a crystalline surface under bombardment with low energy electrons (\(E_{0} < 500\ \rm{eV}\)) in larger angles of incidence. The diffraction pattern also provides very surface sensitive information on the atomic arrangement of the top layers of a solid.

L03636.title: low pressure electrical discharge
L03636.definition: Low pressure electrical discharge sources are radiation sources in which radiation is produced by electrical discharges in gases at low pressures, i.e. pressures from \(10^{2}\ \rm{Pa}\) to \(10^{-3}\ \rm{Pa}\).

08505.title: low sample consumption system
08505.definition: Liquid-sample introduction system to an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer adapted to work at sample flow rates below \(\pu{100 \upmu L min-1}\).

L03638.title: low temperature UV–VIS absorption spectroscopy
L03638.definition: The measurement of the absorption of UV–VIS radiation by a solute in a highly viscous or solid matrix at low temperature.

09176.title: low-energy ion scattering spectrometry
09176.definition: Measurement method to elucidate the composition and structure of the very outermost atomic layers of a solid material, in which principally monoenergetic, singly-charged probe ions scattered from the surface are detected and recorded as a function of their energy, angle of scattering, or both.

08268.title: low-pass filter
08268.definition:
Optical filter that excludes radiation of wavenumber greater (wavelength lower) than a certain value and passes radiation of wavenumber below (wavelength greater than) this value.
Electrical filter that blocks signal with a modulation frequency above a certain cut-on value and passes signals of frequency below this value.

L03637.title: low-pressure mercury lamp
L03637.definition: Resonance lamp that contains mercury vapour at pressures of about \(0.1\ \rm{Pa}\) (\(0.75\times 10^{-3}\ \rm{Torr}\); \(1\ \rm{Torr} = 133.33\ \rm{Pa}\)). At \(\pu{25^{\circ}C}\), such a lamp emits mainly at \(253.7\) and \(184.9\ \rm{nm}\). They are also called germicidal lamps. There are cold- and hot-cathode as well as cooled electrode-less (excited by microwaves) low-pressure mercury lamps. The Wood lamp is a low-pressure mercury arc with an added fluorescent layer that emits in the UV-A spectral region (\(315\)-\(400\ \rm{nm}\)).

10245.title: low-specificity sorbents
10245.definition: Sorbent with a non-selective surface used almost exclusively to extract analytes from an aqueous solution. The sorbent has a largely passive role in the extraction, with the driving force being the expulsion of the organic contaminants from waterto minimize disruption of the water structure.

LT06788.title: low-spin
LT06788.definition: In any coordination entity with a particular $\rm{d^{n}}$ ($1 \lt \pu{n} \lt 9$) configuration and a particular geometry, if the n electrons are distributed so that they occupy the lowest possible energy levels, the entity is a low-spin complex. If some of the higher energy d orbitals are occupied before all the lower energy ones are completely filled, then the entity is a high-spin complex.

LT07067.title: low-spin state
LT07067.definition: When the separation between the highest occupied and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals is not large, two alternative electronic states may be considered. The state with two electrons paired up in the HOMO is called a low-spin state. The low-spin state is the ground state when the one-electron energy needed to promote an electron to the LUMO is larger than the Coulomb and exchange repulsion energies required to pair up two electrons in the HOMO.

12244.title: lower critical solution temperature
12244.definition: Critical temperature below which a mixture is miscible at any composition.

11855.title: lower motor neuron
11855.definition: Neuron that receives impulses from an upper motor neuron and whose axons innervate the skeletal muscles.

14819.title: lowest effective dose
14819.definition: Lowest dose of a chemical inducing a specified effect in a specified fraction of exposed individuals.

LT06909.title: lowest observed adverse effect level
LT06909.definition: Lowest concentration or amount of a substance, found by experiment or observation, which causes an adverse alteration of morphology, functional capacity, growth, development, or life span of a target organism distinguishable from normal (control) organisms of the same species and strain under defined conditions of exposure.

08837.title: lowest unoccupied molecular orbital
08837.definition: Lowest-energy molecular orbital that is unoccupied in the ground state but occupied by one or more electrons if the molecular entity occurs in its first electronically excited state.

14820.title: lowest-observed-effect concentration
14820.definition: Lowest concentration of a material used in an aquatic toxicity test that has a statistically significant adverse effect on the exposed population of test organisms compared with controls.

L03634.title: lowest-observed-effect-level
L03634.definition: Lowest concentration or amount of a substance, found by experiment or observation, that causes any alteration in morphology, functional capacity, growth, development, or life span of target organisms distinguishable from normal (control) organisms of the same species and strain under the same defined conditions of exposure.

15205.title: lozenge
15205.definition: Tablet, which does not contain a disintegrant and which is sucked to dissolve in the mouth to produce either a local (e.g., antiseptic) or systemic (e.g., vitamins) effect.

15206.title: lubricant
15206.definition: Used as processing aid in tablet and capsule manufacturing, to facilitate the movement of the formulation into the dye and punch and to reduce the energy of compression.

10901.title: lumbar puncture
10901.definition: Piercing into the subarachnoid space of the lumbar region in order to obtain spinal fluid for diagnostic purposes or to inject a drug.

11856.title: lumbar spine
11856.definition: Portion of the vertebral column of the lower back between the thoracic spine and sacrum, in humans consisting of five vertebrae designated L1 to L5.

L03639.title: lumen
L03639.definition: SI derived unit of luminous flux, \(\rm{lm} = \rm{cd sr}\).

L03640.title: luminance
L03640.definition: Photometric counterpart of radiance, producing the visual sensation called brightness. Typical units are: \(\pu{candela m-2}\) (\(\mathrm{nit}\)), \(\pu{candela cm-2}\) (\(\mathrm{stilb}\)), \(\mathrm{foot}\ \mathrm{lambert}\) (\(2.426\ \rm{nit}\)). As with all photometric quantities, luminance does not refer to a specific wavelength, but applies to light emitted by a standard source (formerly a 'standard international candle', now a blackbody radiator emitting at the temperature of solidifying platinum, \(2042\ \rm{K}\)). Conversion from photometric units to radiometric units (e.g. \(\rm{J s}^{-1}\)) requires convolution over wavelength of the relative spectral response of the human eye (photopic response tables).

L03641.title: luminescence
L03641.definition: Spontaneous emission of radiation from an electronically or vibrationally excited species not in thermal equilibrium with its environment.

14160.title: luminescence assay
14160.definition: Assay in which response is measured by the detection of light of a nonradiative origin, such as bioluminescence or chemiluminescence.

L03644.title: luminescence quenching
L03644.definition: Radiationless redistribution of excitation energy via interaction (electronic energy or charge transfer) between an emitting species and the quencher.

L03645.title: luminescence spectrometer
L03645.definition: The instrument used to measure luminescence emission spectra.

L03646.title: luminous flux
L03646.definition: Of a source of luminous intensity \(I\) in an element of solid angle \(\rm{d}\varOmega\) is given by \(\rm{d}\varPhi = I\ \rm{d}\varOmega\).

L03647.title: luminous intensity
L03647.definition: Base quantity in the system of quantities upon which SI is based.

L03648.title: luminous quantities
L03648.definition: Group of quantities characterizing visible light in terms of the appearance to the human eye. The symbols of luminous quantities may be distinguished by adding a subscript v. The units for luminous quantities are derived from the SI base unit candela.

L03649.title: lumiphore
L03649.definition: A part of a molecular entity (or atom or group of atoms) in which electronic excitation associated with a given emission band is approximately localized. (Analogous to chromophore for absorption spectra).

10902.title: luteal phase
10902.definition: Phase of the human menstrual cycle, usually lasting \(\pu{14 days}\), beginning with formation of the corpus luteum and ending, in the absence of fertilization, with the onset of menstruation.

10903.title: luteinizing hormone
10903.definition: Hormone made by the pituitary gland that acts on the ovary to control egg maturation and to trigger ovulation. The same hormone acts in the testes to trigger production of testosterone.

L03651.title: lux
L03651.definition: SI derived unit of illuminance, \(\rm{lx} = \rm{lm m}^{-2}=\rm{cd sr m}^{-2}\).

14821.title: lx life table or schedule
14821.definition: Life table that summarizes mortality data for populations.

14822.title: lxmx life table
14822.definition: Life table that summarizes both mortality and natality data for populations.

13370.title: Ly-6
13370.definition: Family of multi-gene-encoded, small, generally glycosylphosphatidyl inositol-anchored membrane proteins thought to be involved in cell adhesion and signaling, and in antigen-independent activation of lymphocytes.

L03652.title: lyases
L03652.definition: Enzymes cleaving $\ce{C–C}$, $\ce{C–O}$, $\ce{C–N}$ and other bonds by other reactions than by hydrolysis or oxidation. Lyases catalyse the addition of molecules to unsaturated compounds or the elimination of molecules creating an unsaturated residue.

L03653.title: lyate ion
L03653.definition: The anion produced by hydron removal from a solvent molecule. For example, the hydroxide ion is the lyate ion of water.

09643.title: lymph
09643.definition: Yellowish, slightly basic fluid circulating through the lymphatic system.

13397.title: lymph node
13397.definition: Any of the small rounded gland-like structures of the lymphatic system, which occur along the lymphatic vessels and which are responsible for removing bacteria, viruses, and foreign molecules from the lymph stream and for producing lymphocytes and antibodies.

13394.title: lymphangion
13394.definition: Morphological or functional unit of lymphatic vessels consisting of the region between adjacent lymphatic valves.

10904.title: lymphatic
10904.definition: Relating to lymph or its secretion.

13395.title: lymphatic system
13395.definition: Describing vessels whose special function is the collection of lymph and its ultimate conveyance to the blood circulation and thoracic duct.

13396.title: lymphatic tissue
13396.definition: Tissue involved in the collection, production, and handling of lymph, including the lymphatic vessels and lymph nodes.

13398.title: lymphoblast
13398.definition: Abnormal cell with a large nucleus and scanty cytoplasm, thought to be the precursor of the lymphocyte, found in blood and blood-forming organs in patients with lymphoblastic leukemia.

13399.title: lymphocyte
13399.definition: Small leucocyte found in the blood, lymph, and lymphoid tissues that has a single round nucleus and little or no granulation in the cytoplasm.

13401.title: lymphocyte activation
13401.definition: Sum of the biochemical processes necessary to stimulate a resting lymphocyte to become an immune effector cell, requiring antigen and co-stimulatory molecules.

13402.title: lymphocyte function-associated antigen-1
13402.definition: Adhesion molecule found on lymphocytes, macrophages, and neutrophils, involved in adhesion of lymphocytes to antigen-presenting cells (APCs).

13403.title: lymphocyte homing
13403.definition: Process that directs lymphocyte subsets to specialized microenvironments that control their differentiation, regulate their survival, and target immune effector cells to sites of antigenic or microbial invasion.

13404.title: lymphocyte homing receptor
13404.definition: Cell surface glycoprotein on lymphocytes and other leukocytes that mediates adhesion to specialized blood vessels, the high endothelial venules.

13405.title: lymphocyte proliferation test
13405.definition: Test of immune sensitization in which white blood cells are exposed in vitro to an antigen and multiply if already sensitized to that antigen.

13407.title: lymphocyte subpopulation
13407.definition: Population forming part of the whole population of lymphocytes, usually characterized by sensitivity to a given antigen.

13408.title: lymphocyte transformation test
13408.definition: Test for increased DNA synthesis followed by cell division and differentiation of lymphocytes in response to antigens or mitogens; an in vitro test of lymphocyte function.

13409.title: lymphocytopenia
13409.definition: Deficiency of lymphocytes in the blood compared with normal values.

13410.title: lymphocytosis
13410.definition: Condition characterized by an abnormal increase in the number of lymphocytes in blood, usually a result of infection or inflammation.

10905.title: lymphoid
10905.definition: Relating to or denoting tissue responsible for producing lymphocytes and antibodies.

13412.title: lymphoid follicle
13412.definition: Region of clustered B cells, allowing the selection of antigen-binding B cells by dendritic cells during adaptive immune responses.

13413.title: lymphoid stem cell
13413.definition: Stem cell giving rise to the lineage of lymphocytes.

13414.title: lymphoid tissue
13414.definition: Vertebrate tissue that is made up predominantly of lymphocytes, e.g., lymph, lymph nodes, spleen, thymus, Peyer’s patches, adenoids, pharyngeal tonsils, and, in birds, bursa of Fabricius and cecal tonsils.

13416.title: lymphokine-activated killer cell
13416.definition: Killer (K) cell or natural killer (NK) cell activated in vitro by interleukin (IL)-2 to give enhanced killing of target cells.

13417.title: lymphoma
13417.definition: Neoplasm, usually malignant, of the lymphatic tissues.

13419.title: lymphoproliferation
13419.definition: Proliferation of lymphocytes in response to stimulation with cellular activators, including antigens or mitogens.

13420.title: lymphosum
13420.definition: Sum of B cells + T cells + natural killer (NK) cells determined separately (by flow cytometry), compared to the total number of lymphocytes.

13421.title: lymphotoxin
13421.definition: T-cell-derived cytokine that is cytotoxic for certain tumor cells and also has immunoregulatory functions.

10906.title: Lyon hypothesis
10906.definition: Hypothesis (named after Mary Lyon) that random inactivation of all but one X chromosome occurs in each female mammalian cell in early development, thus explaining why the effect of the X chromosome on phenotype is the same in males with one copy as in females with two copies.

L03654.title: lyonium ion
L03654.definition: The cation produced by hydronation of a solvent molecule. For example, ($\ce{CH3OH2^{+}}$) is the lyonium ion of methanol.

L03655.title: lyophilic
L03655.definition: The terms lyophilic (hydrophilic, lipophilic, oleophilic, etc.) and lyophobic (lipophobic, etc.) may be used to describe the character of interaction of a particular atomic group with the medium. In this usage the terms have the relative qualitative meaning of 'solvent preferring' (water-preferring, fat-preferring, etc.) and 'solvent rejecting' (water-rejecting, fat-rejecting, etc.) respectively.

L03656.title: lyophilic sols
L03656.definition: These comprise both association colloids in which aggregates of small molecules are formed reversibly and macromolecules in which the molecules themselves are of colloidal size.

LT06896.title: lyotropic mesophase
LT06896.definition: A mesophase formed by dissolving an amphiphilic mesogen in a suitable solvent, under appropriate conditions of concentration, temperature, and pressure.

L03658.title: lysimeter
L03658.definition: Laboratory column of selected representative soil or a protected monolith of undisturbed field soil with which it is possible to sample and monitor the movement of water and substances.

10907.title: lysosomal storage disease
10907.definition: One of a group of rare inherited metabolic disorders resulting from a defect in lysosomal function, commonly a deficiency of enzymes required for the metabolism of lipids, glycoproteins, or mucopolysaccharides, resulting in their accumulation in the cell.

13422.title: lysosome
13422.definition: Cytoplasmic granule containing hydrolytic enzymes involved in the digestion of phagocytosed material.

13937.title: macromolecular prodrug
13937.definition: Prodrug in which the temporary chemical entity is a macromolecule.

13938.title: medical device
13938.definition: Instrument, apparatus, implement, machine, contrivance, in vitro reagent, or other similar or related article, including any component, part of accessory, which is intended for use in the diagnosis of disease or other conditions, or in the cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease in man.

13961.title: mulching film
13961.definition: Polymer film aimed at covering seeded area in order to protect the growing plants from weeds and cold and preserve humidity.

12473.title: magnetic sector
12473.definition: Device that produces a magnetic field perpendicular to a charged particle beam that deflects the beam to an extent that is proportional to the ratio of particle momentum and charge.

12474.title: magnetron motion
12474.definition: Slow rotation of the center of cyclotron motion around the central axis of a Penning ion trap that results from a drift of the cyclotron centre along the electric equipotential lines perpendicular to the magnetic field direction.

12475.title: make-up liquid
12475.definition: Solvent that is mixed with the sample flow in a liquid introduction mass spectrometry interface in order to adjust the flow rate or solvent characteristics of the system, for example, to promote ionization efficiency.

12476.title: mass-analyzed ion kinetic energy spectrometry
12476.definition: Procedure by which translational energy spectra are obtained from a sector mass spectrometer that incorporates at least one magnetic sector plus one electric sector in reverse geometry (a magnetic sector followed by an electric sector).

14212.title: multiple helix
14212.definition: Helical arrangement comprising two or more intertwined helical chains sharing the same axis.

12477.title: mass calibration
12477.definition: Means of determining m/z values of ions from experimentally detected signals using a theoretical or empirical relational equation.

12478.title: mass defect
12478.definition: Difference between the nominal mass and the monoisotopic mass of an atom, molecule, or ion.

12479.title: mass discrimination
12479.definition: Differences in overall detection sensitivities for ions of different m/z values in a mass spectrum, caused by variations in ionization efficiency, transmission efficiency through the interface between the ion source and the analyzer vacuum system, analyzer, and detector response.

12480.title: mass gate
12480.definition: Ion gate used to transmit ions in a given m/z range.

12481.title: mass limit
12481.definition: Value of m/z above or below which ions cannot be detected in a mass spectrometer.

12482.title: mass selective axial ejection
12482.definition: Use of mass selective instability to eject ions of selected m/z values from an ion trap along the trap axis.

12483.title: mass selective instability
12483.definition: Unstable trajectories in an ion trap for ions within a particular range of m/z values caused by an appropriate combination of oscillating electric fields.

12484.title: mass spectral library
12484.definition: Collection of mass spectra of different compounds, usually represented as arrays of signal intensity vs. the m/z values.

12485.title: mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry
12485.definition: Acquisition and study of the spectra of the product ions or precursor ions of m/z selected ions, or of precursor ions of a selected neutral mass loss.

12486.title: Mathieu stability diagram
12486.definition: Graphical representation expressed in terms of dimensionless reduced coordinates that describes the stability or instability of charged particle motion in a transmission quadrupole mass spectrometer or Paul ion trap, based on an appropriate form of the Mathieu differential equation.

12487.title: membrane introduction mass spectrometry
12487.definition: Mass spectrometry measurement that uses a semi-permeable membrane separator that permits the passage of analytes directly from solutions or ambient air to the mass spectrometer ion source.

12488.title: membrane separator
12488.definition: GC-MS interface with a polymer membrane that selectively passes analyte molecules in preference to the carrier gas thereby enriching the analyte in the gas stream.

12489.title: microchannel plate
12489.definition: Thin plate that contains a closely spaced array of channels each of which acts as a continuous dynode particle multiplier. A fast charged or neutral particle, or a photon, that strikes the plate causes a cascade of secondary electrons that ultimately exits the opposite side of the plate.

12490.title: microelectrospray
12490.definition: Electrospray ionization at a low solvent flow rate, typically several microliters per minute (\(\pu{\upmu L min-1}\)) or lower, where a pump is used to provide the sample flow.

12491.title: molecular beam mass spectrometry
12491.definition: Mass spectrometry measurement in which the sample is introduced into the ion source of the mass spectrometer as a collimated beam of molecules with a narrow velocity distribution.

12492.title: molecular effusion separator
12492.definition: GC-MS interface that subjects the GC effluent to effusive flow through a porous glass tube. The lighter carrier gas passes out of the tube, leaving the gas within the tube enriched in analyte.

12493.title: momentum separator
12493.definition: Mass spectrometer interface to inlets including chromatography and spray-based ion sources that enriches the sample by selecting the central part of the effluent or spray using an orifice or skimmer. Particles with a higher forward momentum diverge less from the spray axis for a given radial momentum.

12494.title: monodisperse aerosol generating interface for chromatography
12494.definition: Particle beam interface that incorporates a monodisperse aerosol generator.

12495.title: monoisotopic mass
12495.definition: Exact mass of an ion or molecule calculated using the mass of the most abundant isotope of each element.

12496.title: moving belt interface
12496.definition: Liquid sample mass spectrometer interface that uses two or more pulleys and a continuous loop of material. Samples are sprayed or deposited from solution onto the belt where they are transported into the vacuum system for vaporization or desorption and ionization.

12497.title: MS/MS spectrum
12497.definition: Mass spectrum obtained using tandem mass spectrometry.

12498.title: MSn
12498.definition: Symbol for multiple-stage mass spectrometry experiments designed to record product ion spectra where \(n\) is the number of product ion stages (nth-generation product ions).

12499.title: multicollector mass spectrometer
12499.definition: Mass spectrograph based on a double-focusing magnetic analyzer that spatially disperses ions of different m/z values on to an array of Faraday cup detectors, generally used with inductively coupled plasma ion sources for isotopic composition measurements.

12500.title: multiple reaction monitoring
12500.definition: Application of selected reaction monitoring to multiple product ions from one or more precursor ions.

12501.title: multiple-stage mass spectrometry
12501.definition: Multiple stages of precursor ion m/z selection followed by product ion detection for successive nth-generation product ions.

13908.title: maximum degree of biodegradation
13908.definition: Greater value of the degree of biodegradation that can be reached under selected experimental conditions.

13909.title: microcapsule
13909.definition: Hollow microparticle composed of a solid shell surrounding a core-forming space available to permanently or temporarily entrapped substances.

13910.title: microparticle
13910.definition: Particle with dimensions between \(\pu{1E-7}\) and \(\pu{1E-4 m}\).

13911.title: microsphere
13911.definition: Microparticle of spherical shape without membrane or any distinct outer layer.

13912.title: mineralization
13912.definition: Process through which an organic substance becomes impregnated by or turned into inorganic substances.

15598.title: matched control
15598.definition: Control (individual or group or case) selected to be similar to a study individual or group, or case, in specific characteristics: some commonly used matching variables are age, sex, race, and socioeconomic status.

M03751.title: E/2 mass spectrum
M03751.definition: Processes of the charge-stripping type: \[\rm{M}^{+}+\rm{X}\rightarrow \rm{M}^{2+}+\rm{X}+\rm{e}\] occuring in a collision cell (containing a gas, X) located in a field-free region preceding a magnetic and electric sector combination placed in either order, may be detected as follows. If the instrument slits are wide and if the electric sector field \(E\) is set to half the value required to transmit the main ion-beam, the only ions to be transmitted will be those with a kinetic energy/charge ratio half, or almost exactly half, that of the main ion beam. The product ions of the charge-stripping process fulfil this condition. If the magnetic field \(B\) is scanned, a mass spectrum of such doubly-charged product ions, and thus of their singly-charged precursors, is obtained. Such a spectrum is called an \(\frac{E}{2}\) mass spectrum. Interference from product ions from processes of the type: \[\rm{M}_{1}^{+}+\rm{X}\rightarrow \rm{M}_{2}^{+}+\rm{X}+\rm{M}_{3}\] where \(m_{1}\), \(m_{2}\), and (\(m_{1}- m_{2}\)) are the masses of \(\rm{M}_{1}^{+}\), \(\rm{M}_{2}^{+}\) and \(\rm{M}_{3}\), respectively, and where \(m_{2}=0.5\ m_{1}\), can arise in \(\frac{E}{2}\) mass spectra.

09585.title: m diad
09585.definition: Pair of adjacent constitutionally equivalent stereogenic units that are of like configuration.

14823.title: MacArthur–Wilson model
14823.definition: Model of island colonization giving the mathematical relationship \[S(t) = S_{\rm{EQ}}(1 - e^{-Gt})\] where \(S(t)\) is the number of species present at time \(t\), \(S_{\rm{EQ}}\) is the equilibrium number of species for the island, and \(G\) is the rate constant for colonization of the island.

11470.title: machine learning
11470.definition:
A computer algorithm that generates empirical models, such as a model of biological potency as a function of the properties of the molecules, that is derived
 from the analysis of a training set for which all the necessary data are available.

14315.title: macro-emulsion
14315.definition: Emulsion in which the particles of the dispersed phase have diameters from approximately \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{100 \upmu m}\).

13423.title: macroautophagy
13423.definition: Sequestration and breakdown of organelles and long-lived proteins in a double-membrane vesicle, called an autophagosome or autophagic vacuole, inside the cell.

10908.title: macrocephaly
10908.definition: Congenital disorder characterized by an abnormally large head and (or) brain.

M03662.title: macrocycle
M03662.definition: A cyclic macromolecule or a macromolecule cyclic portion of a macromolecule.

13965.title: macrocyclic component
13965.definition: Molecule that has at least one ring (cycle) large enough to allow it to be threaded onto a linear subchain of another molecule.

09083.title: macroelectrode
09083.definition: Electrode with smallest dimension of order millimetre or greater.

10909.title: macroglossia
10909.definition: Congenital disorder characterized by an abnormally enlarged tongue.

10910.title: macrognathia
10910.definition: Congenital disorder characterized by enlargement or elongation of the jaw.

M03663.title: macrolides
M03663.definition: Macrocyclic lactones with a ring of twelve or more members.

10911.title: macromelia
10911.definition: Congenital disorder characterized by an abnormally large limb or limbs.

M03664.title: macrometeorology
M03664.definition: Study of the largest-scale aspects of the atmosphere, e.g. general global circulation.

12207.title: macromolecular coil
12207.definition: Depiction of a macromolecule in which its segments are distributed about some point in space.

13966.title: macromolecular component
13966.definition: Macromolecule that is part of a rotaxane assembly.

11471.title: macromolecular crystallographic information file
11471.definition: A file that describes in detail the features of a macromolecular structure and the X‑ray diffraction experiment that was used to derive that structure.

M03666.title: macromolecular isomorphism
M03666.definition: Statistical co-crystallization of different constitutional repeating units which may either belong to the same copolymer chains (copolymer isomorphism) or originate from different homopolymer chains (homopolymer isomorphism). Isomorphism is a general term: in the strict sense, the crystal structure is essentially the same throughout the range of compositions; in isodimorphism or isopolymorphism, there are two or more crystal structures, respectively, depending on composition.

13967.title: macromolecular pseudorotaxane
13967.definition: Pseudorotaxane, at least one component of which is a macromolecule.

13968.title: macromolecular rotaxane
13968.definition: Rotaxane, at least one component of which is a macromolecule.

M03667.title: macromolecule
M03667.definition: A molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

M03668.title: macromonomer
M03668.definition: Polymer or oligomer the molecules of which each have one end-group that acts as a monomer molecule, so that each polymer or oligomer molecule contributes only a single monomer unit to a chain of the product polymer.

M03670.title: macromonomer molecule
M03670.definition: A macromolecule that has one end-group which enables it to act as a monomer molecule, contributing only a single monomeric unit to a chain of the final macromolecule.

M03669.title: macromonomeric unit
M03669.definition: The largest constitutional unit contributed by a single macromonomer molecule to the structure of a macromolecule.

14825.title: macronutrient
14825.definition: Imprecise term referring to a nutrient required for survival, or present in biological fluids or compartments at a level easily measured by existing analytical techniques.

13424.title: macrophage
13424.definition: Large (\(\pu{10\!{-}\! 20 \upmu m}\) diameter) ameboid and phagocytic cell found in many tissues, especially in areas of inflammation, derived from blood monocytes and playing an important role in host defense mechanisms.

13426.title: macrophage function test
13426.definition: Any assay suitable to characterize the effect of substances on macrophage function in in vivo or in vitro.

13427.title: macrophage mannose receptor
13427.definition: Receptor involved in pathogen recognition, in clearance of endogenous serum glycoproteins, and in antigen presentation.

14826.title: macrophyte
14826.definition: Aquatic plant large enough to be seen easily with the naked eye (as distinct from phytoplankton and small algae).

13428.title: macropinocytosis
13428.definition: 'High-volume' pinocytosis by which dendritic cells engulf relatively large volumes of fluid from their surroundings, enabling them to take in many antigens nonspecifically.

M03672.title: macropore
M03672.definition: Pore with width exceeding about \(0.05\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) or \(50\ \rm{nm}\) (\(500\ \rm{Å}\)).

14304.title: macroporous particle
14304.definition: Particle containing pores of diameters exceeding about \(\pu{50 nm}\).

MT07177.title: macroporous polymer
MT07177.definition: Glass or rubbery polymer that includes a large number of macropores (\(50\ \rm{nm}\)–\(1\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) in diameter) that persist when the polymer is immersed in solvents or in the dry state.

M03673.title: macroradical
M03673.definition: A macromolecule which is also a free radical.

M03674.title: macroscopic cross-section
M03674.definition: The cross-section per unit volume of a given material for a specified process. For a pure nuclide, it is the product of the microscopic cross-section and the number of target nuclei per unit volume; for a mixture of nuclides, it is the sum of such products.

M03676.title: macroscopic film
M03676.definition: A film which has lateral dimensions above \(100\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\).

M03677.title: macroscopic kinetics
M03677.definition: A term applied to a kinetic study in which the interest is in the behaviour of bulk systems, e.g. in changes in concentrations of reactants and products.

15860.title: macroscopic pathology
15860.definition: Study of changes associated with disease that are visible to the naked eye without the need for a microscope.

10912.title: macrosomia
10912.definition: Congenital disorder characterized by an abnormally large body or body part.

10913.title: macrostomia
10913.definition: Congenital disorder characterized by an abnormally large size of the mouth.

MT07419.title: magic angle
MT07419.definition: Upon excitation of an 'isotropic' sample (assuming an ultra short excitation pulse) the relationship between the fluorescence intensity detected at a time \(t\) and through a polarization analyser oriented at an angle \(\beta\) with respect to the electric polarization of the exciting beam is given by \[I(t,\beta ) \propto  N(t)\left [ 1 + (3\, \rm{cos}^{2}\, \beta - 1)R(t) \right ]\] where \(R(t)\) is the degree of alignment of the emitting transition dipole in the laboratory frame and \(N(t)\) is the excited-state population, both at time \(t\). For \(\beta = 54.7^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) (the magic angle), the dipole-alignment contribution vanishes and \(I(t,\,\beta = 54.7^{\,\unicode{x26ac}} ) \propto N(t)\).

08377.title: magic angle spinning
08377.definition: Technique in solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy to remove or reduce the influence of anisotropic interactions by rapid sample rotation about the magic angle, where \(\boldsymbol{B_{0}}\) is external magnetic induction and \(\uptheta\) is the axis of rotation of the sample at an angle of approx. \(\pu{54.74\!^{\circ}}\) to the external magnetic induction.

MT06778.title: magnetic circular dichroism
MT06778.definition: Magnetic circular dichroism is observed when a sample differentially absorbs left- and right- circularly polarized light in a magnetic field parallel to the light beam.

M03680.title: magnetic deflection
M03680.definition: The deflection of an ion beam as a result of the motion of the ions in a magnetic field (magnetic sector). Generally the direction of motion of the ions is at right angles to the direction of the magnetic field, and the motion is uniform.

M03681.title: magnetic equivalence
M03681.definition: Nuclei having the same resonance frequency in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and also identical spin-spin interactions with the nuclei of a neighbouring group are magnetically equivalent. The spin-spin interaction between magnetically equivalent nuclei does not appear, and thus has no effect on the multiplicity of the respective NMR signals. Magnetically equivalent nuclei are necessarily also chemically equivalent, but the reverse is not necessarily true.

M03682.title: magnetic field scan
M03682.definition: The usual method of producing a momentum (mass) spectrum, by varying the strength of the magnetic field.

M03683.title: magnetic field strength
M03683.definition: Magnetic flux density divided by the permeability.

M03685.title: magnetic flux density
M03685.definition: Magnetic flux density at the nucleus (from experiment) in those cases in which the magnetic hyperfine interaction can be described by an effective field. In other cases the vector components of the magnetic hyperfine interaction should be reported if possible.

M03686.title: magnetic flux density
M03686.definition: Magnetic induction is a vector characterizing a magnetic field. The force acting on a moving charge in a magnetic field is the charge multiplied by the vector product of the velocity and magnetic flux density. This quantity is sometimes loosely called the magnetic field.

M03684.title: magnetic flux
M03684.definition: Scalar product of magnetic flux density and area.

09524.title: magnetic mask
09524.definition: Mask with a pattern defined by a paramagnetic metal.

M03688.title: magnetic moment
M03688.definition: Vector quantity, the vector product of which with the magnetic flux density of a homogeneous field is equal to the torque.

10246.title: magnetic nanoparticle sorbent
10246.definition: Sorbent consisting of nanometre-sized, spherical particles with a magnetic or magnetisable core surrounded by a sorbent shell.

MT06795.title: magnetic resonance imaging
MT06795.definition: The visualisation of the distribution of nuclear spins (usually water) in a body by using a magnetic field gradient (NMR imaging). A similar technique, but less widely used, is to visualise the distribution of paramagnetic centres (EPR imaging).

11857.title: magnetic resonance spectroscopy
11857.definition: Noninvasive method based on nuclear spin alignment that allows localization of levels and measurement of kinetics of an injected labeled substances in living tissue.

MT06781.title: magnetic susceptibility
MT06781.definition: For paramagnetic materials, the magnetic susceptibility may be measured experimentally and used to give information on the molecular magnetic dipole moment, and hence on the electronic structure of the molecules in the material. The paramagnetic contribution to the molar magnetic susceptibility of a material, \(\chi \), is related to the molecular magnetic dipole moment \(m\) by the curie relation: \(\chi = \frac{\rm{constant x}\ m^{2}}{T}\).

M03690.title: magnetic transition
M03690.definition: A transition between disordered and ordered arrays of atomic magnetic moments. Where the ordered phase has a net spontaneous magnetization, \(M_{\rm{S}}\), the magnetic-ordering temperature is called a curie temperature, \(T_{\rm{C}}\); where the net spontaneous magnetization of the ordered phase remains zero, the ordering temperature is called a Néel temperature, \(T_{\rm{N}}\). The temperature at which the two ferromagnetic subarrays of a ferrimagnet just cancel each other is called the compensation point. Materials exhibit ferromagnetic behaviour when unpaired electron spins are aligned in parallel, antiferromagnetic behaviour when the alignment is antiparallel, and ferrimagnetic behaviour if the alignment of the spins is antiparallel with unequal numbers in the two orientations or if the spins are canted. Therefore, ferromagnetic, ferrimagnetic and weak ferromagnetic transitions involve a net magnetic moment change, whereas antiferromagnetic transitions have zero net magnetic moment change.

M03691.title: magnetizability
M03691.definition: Tensor quantity relating the induced magnetic moment, \(m_{\rm{i}}\), to the applied magnetic flux density \(B\), \(m_{\rm{i}}=\xi \ B\).

M03692.title: magnetization transfer
M03692.definition: NMR method for determining kinetics of chemical exchange by perturbing the magnetization of nuclei in a particular site or sites and following the rate at which magnetic equilibrium is restored. The most common perturbations are saturation and inversion, and the corresponding techniques are often called 'saturation transfer' and 'selective inversion-recovery'.

M03693.title: magnetogyric ratio
M03693.definition: Ratio of the magnetic moment to the angular momentum. It is often misleadingly called the gyromagnetic ratio.

09512.title: magnetolithography
09512.definition: Lithography for direct patterning of surfaces based on the application of a magnetic field to the substrate using paramagnetic metal masks.

08839.title: magnetoresistance
08839.definition: Change in the electric resistance of a material in response to an external magnetic field.

10134.title: Mahalanobis distance
10134.definition: Distance (\(d_{i,j}\)) between an object characterised by vector of variables \(\boldsymbol{x}_{i}\) and the centroid of a class \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{j}\) with covariance matrix \(\boldsymbol{S}\) calculated as \[d_{i,j} = \sqrt {(\boldsymbol{x}_{i} - \boldsymbol{\mu}_{j})^T \boldsymbol{S}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{x}_{i} - \boldsymbol{\mu}_{j})}\] where \(\boldsymbol{S}\) is the covariance matrix of the variables.

M03694.title: main chain
M03694.definition: That linear chain to which all other chains, long or short or both, may be regarded as being pendant.

10076.title: main effect
10076.definition: Effect of a factor where the term is a single factor.

15430.title: main ring
15430.definition: Macrocycle in a bridged polycyclic macromolecule or polycyclic macromolecular portion that contains the subunits of highest seniority.

13969.title: main-chain macromolecular rotaxane
13969.definition: Macromolecular rotaxane in which rotaxane constitutional units are exclusively located within the main macromolecular chain.

MT06869.title: main-chain polymer liquid crystal
MT06869.definition: A polymer, whose molecules have mesogenic units only in their main chains.

13970.title: main-chain rotaxane polymer
13970.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecular assemblies that are main-chain macromolecular rotaxanes.

MT07140.title: main-chain scission
MT07140.definition: Chemical reaction that results in the breaking of main-chain bonds of a polymer molecule.

13855.title: main-chain self-assembly
13855.definition: Inter- or intra-molecular self-assembly of constitutional units within the backbones of polymer molecules.

15861.title: mainstream smoke
15861.definition: Smoke that is inhaled by the smoker.

13429.title: major basic protein
13429.definition: Small basic arginine-rich peptide (\(\pu{pI 10.9}\), molecular mass of \(\pu{13.8 kDa}\)) in the granules of eosinophils that kills helminths and protozoa.

13430.title: major histocompatibility complex
13430.definition: Cluster of genes encoding cell surface molecules involved in antigen presentation to T cells. In humans, they are found on chromosome 6 and in mice on chromosome 17. They are polymorphic and code for antigens that lead to rapid graft rejection between members of a single species that differ at these loci.

13431.title: major histocompatibility complex class I molecule
13431.definition: Surface protein encoded by the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) expressed on all nucleated cells, presenting antigen-derived peptides.

13432.title: major histocompatibility complex class II molecule
13432.definition: Surface protein encoded by the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) expressed on antigen-presenting cells (APCs), presenting antigen-derived peptides.

13433.title: major histocompatibility complex class III molecule
13433.definition: Antigen encoded by the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) including several complement factors, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) $\ce{\upalpha\!}$, and lymphotoxin.

13434.title: major histocompatibility complex molecule
13434.definition: Any of the cell-surface glycoprotein alloantigens encoded by the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) that are involved in the regulation of immune responses and can cause the rejection of grafted tissues, cells, and tumors bearing them.

13435.title: major histocompatibility complex restriction
13435.definition: Necessity that T cells recognize processed antigen only when presented by major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules of the original haplotype associated with T-cell priming.

10847.title: male fertility index
10847.definition: In rodents, number of males impregnating females divided by number of males mated, multiplied by \(\pu{100}\).

14827.title: male-mediated toxicity
14827.definition: Disease or birth defects produced by a father’s exposure to a physical or chemical agent.

10914.title: malformation
10914.definition: Structural defect as a result of abnormal development.

15863.title: malignancy
15863.definition: Population of cells showing both uncontrolled growth and a tendency to invade and destroy other tissues.

10915.title: malignant
10915.definition:
Occurring in a severe form, tending to become progressively worse, resistant to treatment, and likely to result in death.
In cancer, cells showing both uncontrolled growth and a tendency to invade and destroy other tissues.

14828.title: Malthusian theory
14828.definition: Model, developed by Thomas R. Malthus (1766–1834), implying that, unchecked by environmental or social constraints, human populations would double every 25 years, regardless of the initial population size. Thus, if \(X_{i}\) denotes the population size during time period \(i\) and \(r\) the population growth rate, the Malthusian population model gives the relationship \[X(I + 1) = (1 + r)X_{i}\]

13436.title: mammalian target of rapamycin
13436.definition: Intracellular signaling molecule (phosphoinositide-3-kinase) involved in control of cell growth, whose activity is negatively influenced by the immunosuppressive drug rapamycin.

M03695.title: mancude-ring systems
M03695.definition: Rings having (formally) the maximum number of noncumulative double bonds, e.g. benzene, indene, indole, 4H-1,3-dioxine. Also called mancunide-ring systems.

11858.title: manganism
11858.definition: Condition of manganese poisoning, usually after chronic inhalation exposure to manganese fumes.

15864.title: mania
15864.definition: Emotional disorder (mental illness) characterized by an expansive and elated state (euphoria), rapid speech, flight of ideas, decreased need for sleep, distractibility, grandiosity, poor judgment, and increased motor activity.

M03697.title: manipulator
M03697.definition: A hand-operated or -controlled device for remotely handling radioactive materials.

13437.title: mannan-binding lectin-associated serine peptidase-1 and -2
13437.definition: Complement-dependent bactericidal factors that bind to the Ra and R2 polysaccharides expressed by certain enterobacterium strains, such as Ra chemotype strains of Salmonella.

13438.title: mannose-binding protein
13438.definition: Member of the collectin family of calcium-dependent lectins, and an acute-phase protein.

13439.title: mantle zone
13439.definition: Outer ring of small lymphocytes surrounding the center of a lymphatic nodule (lymphoid follicle). It contains transient lymphocytes and is the location of the lymphoma in mantle cell lymphoma.

M03698.title: manual
M03698.definition: Refers to physical human intervention in an analytical procedure.

M03699.title: mapping
M03699.definition: The determination of the relative positions of genes within the chromosomes of restriction sites along a DNA molecule.

M03700.title: Marangoni effect
M03700.definition: Motions of the surface of a liquid are coupled with those of the subsurface fluid or fluids, so that movements of the liquid normally produce stresses in the surface and vice versa. The movement of the surface and of the entrained fluid(s) caused by surface tension gradients is called the Marangoni effect.

M03702.title: Marcus equation
M03702.definition: Relation between the rate of outer-sphere electron transfer and the thermodynamics of this process. Essentially, the rate constant within the encounter complex (or the rate constant of intramolecular transfer) is given by the Eyring equation: \[k_{\mathrm{ET}}=\frac{\kappa _{\mathrm{ET}}\ k\ T}{h}\ \exp (- \frac{\Delta G^{\ddagger }}{R\ T})\] where \(k\) is the Boltzmann constant, \(h\) the Planck constant, \(R\) the gas constant and \(\kappa _{\rm{ET}}\) the so-called electronic transmission factor (\(\kappa _{\rm{ET}}\sim 1\) for adiabatic and \(

M03701.title: Marcus–Coltrin path
M03701.definition: A path trajectory over a potential-energy surface which corresponds to the outermost vibrational turning points for the molecular species involved. This path was suggested as a device for calculating the probability of quantum-mechanical tunnelling: the trajectory for the system is considered to follow this path.

M03703.title: Marcus–Hush relationship
M03703.definition: Relationship between the barrier (\(\Delta G^{\ddagger}\)) to thermal electron transfer, the energy of a corresponding optical charge-transfer transition (\(\Delta E_{\rm{op}}\)), and the overall change in standard Gibbs energy accompanying thermal electron transfer (\(\Delta G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\)). Assuming a quadratic relation between the energy of the system and its distortions from equilibrium (harmonic oscillator model) the expression obtained is: \[\Delta G^{\ddagger} = \frac{\Delta E_{\rm{op}}^{2}}{4\ (\Delta E_{\rm{op}}\,-\,\Delta G^{o})}\] The simplest form of this expression obtains for degenerate electron transfer (\(\Delta G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\)) in e.g. symmetrical mixed valence systems: \[\Delta G^{\ddagger} = \frac{\Delta E_{\rm{op}}}{4}\] Note that for this situation the Marcus equation reads: \[\Delta G^{\ddagger} = \frac{\lambda }{4}\]

10917.title: Marfan syndrome
10917.definition: Congenital connective tissue disorder associated with mutation of the fibrillin-1 gene FBN1.

15865.title: margin of exposure
15865.definition: Ratio of the no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) to the theoretical or estimated exposure dose (EED) or concentration (EEC).

13440.title: marginal zone
13440.definition: Outer area of the splenic periarteriolar lymphoid sheath (PALS) that is rich in B cells, particularly those responding to thymus-independent antigens.

13441.title: margination
13441.definition: Leukocyte adhesion to the endothelium of blood vessels in the early phase of an acute inflammatory response.

M03706.title: Mark–Houwink equation
M03706.definition: The equation describing the dependence of the intrinsic viscosity of a polymer on its relative molecular mass (molecular weight) and having the form: \[[\eta] = K\cdot M_{\rm{r}}^{a}\] where \([\eta]\) is the intrinsic viscosity, \(K\) and \(a\) are constants the values of which depend on the nature of the polymer and solvent as well as on temperature and \(M_{\rm{r}}\) is usually one of the relative molecular mass averages.

M03705.title: marker
M03705.definition: (DNA) A fragment of known size used as reference for analytical purposes.(genetic) A gene with known phenotype and mapped position.(chromatography) A reference substance co-chromatographed with the sample to assist in identifying the components.

M03707.title: Markownikoff rule
M03707.definition: 'In the addition of hydrogen halides to unsymmetrically constituted [unsaturated] hydrocarbons, the halogen atom becomes attached to the carbon bearing the lesser number of hydrogen atoms.' Originally formulated by Markownikoff (Markovnikov) to generalize the orientation in additions of hydrogen halides to simple alkenes, this rule has been extended to polar addition reaction as follows. 'In the heterolytic addition of a polar molecule to an alkene or alkyne, the more electronegative (nucleophilic) atom (or part) of the polar molecule becomes attached to the carbon atom bearing the smaller number of hydrogen atoms.' This is an indirect statement of the common mechanistic observation, that the more electropositive (electrophilic) atom (or part) of the polar molecule becomes attached to the end of the multiple bond that would result in the more stable carbenium ion (whether or not a carbenium ion is actually formed as a reaction intermediate in the addition reaction). Addition in the opposite sense is commonly called 'anti-Markovnikov addition'.

11472.title: Markush structure
11472.definition: A structure diagram that describes a set of related molecules with the structure of the common core and the structures of the substituents at each position.

M03708.title: martensitic transition
M03708.definition: A diffusionless transition (first studied in the steel alloy, Martensite), at constant composition, generated by coordinated atomic, ionic or molecular displacements over distances smaller than interatomic distances in the parent phase. The cooperative rearrangements of the crystal structure generally take place progressively by the movement of a two-dimensional interface through the solid. Examples: The face-centred-cubic to body-centred-tetragonal transition of iron containing some carbon; the transition of tetragonal $\ce{ZrO2}$ to monoclinic $\ce{ZrO2}$.

10918.title: masculinization
10918.definition: Development of male characteristics, such as facial hair, either as part of normal male maturation, or, pathologically, by people of either sex as a result of hormonal imbalance.

09523.title: mask
09523.definition: Transparent substrate pre-patterned with the desired image that is inserted into the incident beam in photo- and X-ray lithography.

09525.title: mask error enhancement factor
09525.definition: Increase in error of pattern edge location during pattern formation when the wavelength of light used to expose a resist is greater than the feature size.

09513.title: maskless lithography
09513.definition: Lithography that does not need a mask of the image to make a pattern.

M03727.title: mass of the stationary phase
M03727.definition: The mass (weight) of the liquid stationary phase or the active solid in the column. The mass (weight) of any solid support is not included. In the case of partition chromatography with a liquid stationary phase it is identical to the liquid phase mass (weight).

09406.title: mass accuracy
09406.definition: Measured mass minus reference value for that mass.

08184.title: mass action, law of
08184.definition: Statement that the velocity of a reaction depends on the active mass, i.e., the concentrations of the reactants.

M03710.title: mass analysis
M03710.definition: A process by which a mixture of ionic or neutral species is identified according to the mass-to-charge (\(\frac{m}{z}\)) ratios (ions) or their aggregate atomic masses (neutrals). The analysis may be qualitative and/or quantitative.

14829.title: mass balance equation
14829.definition: Equation that expresses the total mass of a chemical in terms of all the various forms and concentrations in different environmental compartments (including biota) in which it occurs.

M03712.title: mass balance
M03712.definition: Summation of the masses of a given element in its various compounds before and after reaction (changes) in the atmosphere; provides a test of the completeness of the accounting of the various reaction paths for this element which can be had through the compounds which have been analysed.

M03713.title: mass concentration
M03713.definition: Mass of a constituent divided by the volume of the mixture.

M03715.title: mass density gradient
M03715.definition: Change in mass density in a small distance divided by that distance.

M03718.title: mass distribution ratio
M03718.definition: The fraction (\(1 - R\)) of a component in the stationary phase divided by the fraction (\(R\)) in the mobile phase: \[D_{\rm{m}} = \frac{\rm{amount\ of\ substance\ in\ the\ stationary\ phase}}{\rm{amount\ of\ component\ in\ the\ mobile\ phase}}\] This term is recommended in preference to the term capacity factor frequently used in the chromatographic literature.

MT06929.title: mass distribution ratio
MT06929.definition: Defined analogously to mass distribution ratio (in micellar electrokinetic chromatography), \(k_{\rm{MEEKC}}\) by replacing terms for micelles with corresponding terms for micro-emulsion.

MT06928.title: mass distribution ratio
MT06928.definition: Defined as: \[k_{\rm{MEKC}} = \frac{n_{\rm{mc}}}{n_{\rm{aq}}} = K\cdot \frac{V_{\rm{mc}}}{V_{\rm{aq}}}\] where \(n_{\rm{mc}}\) and \(n_{\rm{aq}}\) are the chemical amounts of the analyte in the micellar and aqueous phases, respectively, \(K\) is the distribution constant and \(V_{\rm{mc}}\) and \(V_{\rm{aq}}\) are the corresponding volumes of the phases.

M03719.title: mass excess
M03719.definition: Mass of an atom minus the product of mass number and atomic mass constant.

09750.title: mass fingerprinting
09750.definition: Protein analysis where an unknown protein is chemically or enzymatically cleaved into peptide fragments whose masses are determined by mass spectrometry. The peptide masses are compared to peptide masses calculated for known proteins in a database and analysed statistically to determine the best match.

M03720.title: mass flow rate
M03720.definition: Mass of a material crossing a surface divided by the time.

M03722.title: mass fraction
M03722.definition: Mass of a constituent divided by the total mass of all constituents in the mixture.

15866.title: mass mean diameter
15866.definition: Diameter of a spherical particle with a mass equal to the mean mass of all the particles in a population.

15867.title: mass median diameter
15867.definition: Diameter of a spherical particle with the median mass of all the particles in a population.

M03726.title: mass number
M03726.definition: Total number of heavy particles (protons and neutrons jointly called nucleons) in the atomic nucleus. Also called nucleon number. Symbol \(m\) in mass spectrometry.

M03728.title: mass peak
M03728.definition: A record of the ion current, at a specific mass to charge ratio, received by the collector.

15375.title: mass percent
15375.definition: Deprecated term that includes both a quantity and a unit. Replace by mass fraction expressed as percent.

M03729.title: mass range
M03729.definition: The range of mass numbers which can be characterized by a mass spectrometer with sufficient resolution to differentiate adjacent peaks.

15337.title: mass ratio
15337.definition: Mass of one constituent \(\ce{A}\) divided by the mass of a second constituent \(\ce{B}\) in the same system. \[\zeta_{\ce{A,B}} = m_{\ce{A}}/m_{\ce{B}}\]

M03730.title: mass resolving power
M03730.definition: Commonly and also acceptably defined in terms of the overlap (or 'valley') between two peaks. Thus for two peaks of equal height, masses \(m_{1}\) and \(m_{2}\), when there is overlap between the two peaks to a stated percentage of either peak height (10% is recommended), then the resolving power is defined as \(\frac{m_{1}}{m_{1} - m_{2}}\). The percentage overlap (or 'valley') concerned must always be stated.

15338.title: mass solubility
15338.definition: Obsolete term for molality of a saturated solution of a gas.

M03731.title: mass spectrograph
M03731.definition: An instrument in which beams of ions are separated (analysed) according to the quotient mass/charge, and in which the deflection and intensity of the beams are recorded directly on photographic plate or film.

M03732.title: mass spectrometer
M03732.definition: An instrument in which beams of ions are separated (analysed) according to the quotient mass/charge, and in which the ions are measured electrically. This term should also be used when a scintillation detector is employed.

M03733.title: mass spectrometer
M03733.definition: A mass spectrometer in which the ions to be separated absorb maximum energy through the effect of alternating electric fields which are parallel to the path of the ions. These ions are then separated from other ions with different mass/charge by an additional electric field.

M03736.title: mass spectrometer focusing system
M03736.definition: An assembly permitting the separation of ions according to their mass-to-charge ratio.

M03745.title: mass spectrometric detector
M03745.definition: A mass spectrometer used as a detector to give qualitative and quantitative data on the various eluted substances. The mass spectrum of the eluted compounds provides evidence beyond the elution time as to the chemical nature of the species.

M03746.title: mass spectrometry
M03746.definition: The branch of science dealing with all aspects of mass spectroscopes and the results obtained with these instruments.

M03748.title: mass spectroscopy
M03748.definition: The study of systems by causing the formation of gaseous ions, with or without fragmentation, which are then characterized by their mass-to-charge ratios and relative abundances.

M03749.title: mass spectrum
M03749.definition: A spectrum which is obtained when a beam of ions is separated according to the mass-to-charge (\(\frac{m}{z}\)) ratios of the ionic species contained within it.

M03754.title: mass transfer coefficient
M03754.definition:
The heterogeneous diffusion rate constant defined for the case of the limiting current. A more general definition in terms of the electrode current densities is: \[k_{m{d}}= rac{j\ 
u }{n\ F\ (c_{m{e}}- c_{0})}\] or \[k_{m{d}} =  rac{j\ 
u \ (1- t_{m{B}}\ n\ 
u ^{-1}\ z_{m{B}}^{-1})}{n\ F\ (c_{m{e}}- c_{0})}\] where \(j\) is the electrode current density, \(
u \) is the stoichiometric number, \(n\) is the charge number of the electrode reaction, \(F\) is the Faraday constant, \(c_{m{e}}\) is the interfacial concentration, \(c_{0}\) is the bulk concentration, \(t_{m{B}}\) is the transport number of species B, and \(z_{m{B}}\) is the charge number of species B.

M03753.title: mass transfer
