M03753.definition: Spontaneous (irreversible) process of transfer of mass across non-homogeneous fields. The driving force can be difference in concentration (in liquids) or partial pressure (in gases) of the component. In fluids, mass transfer may be enhanced by turbulent flow. In biological systems, mass transfer through membranes may result from normal diffusion, facilitated diffusion or active transport.

12217.title: mass-average molar mass
12217.definition:
The equation for mass-average molar mass is \[M_{\rm{m}} \equiv M_{\rm{w}} = \sum\limits_{M} w_{M}M\]
The equation for mass-average molecular weight  is \[M_{\rm{r,m}} \equiv {M_{\rm{r,w}}} = \sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}} M_{\rm{r}}\]

14293.title: mass-average particle diameter
14293.definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[\left\langle d_{\rm{m}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{m}} = \frac{\Sigma {N_{i}} {d_{i}^{4}}}{\Sigma {N_{i}} {d_{i}^{3}}}\]

M03711.title: mass-average velocity

M03716.title: mass-distribution function
M03716.definition: A distribution function in which the relative amount of a portion of a substance with a specific value, or a weight distribution range of values, of the random variable(s) is expressed in terms of mass fraction.

M03721.title: mass-flow sensitive detector
M03721.definition: A device the response of which is proportional to the amount of sample component reaching the detector in unit time.

M03725.title: mass-law effect
M03725.definition: At equilibrium, the product of the activities (or concentrations) of the reacting species is constant. Thus for the equilibrium: \[\alpha\,\rm{A}\,+\,\beta\,\rm{B}\rightleftharpoons \gamma\,\rm{C}\,+\,\delta\,\rm{D}\] \[K=\frac{\left[\rm{C}\right]^{\gamma }\ \left[\rm{D}\right]^{\delta }}{\left[\rm{A}\right]^{\alpha }\ \left[\rm{B}\right]^{\beta }}\]

M03752.title: mass-to-charge ratio
M03752.definition: The abbreviation \(\frac{m}{z}\) is used to denote the dimensionless quantity formed by dividing the mass number of an ion by its charge number. It has long been called the mass-to-charge ratio although \(m\) is not the ionic mass nor is \(z\) a multiple or the elementary (electronic) charge, \(e\). The abbreviation \(\frac{m}{e}\) is, therefore, not recommended. Thus, for example, for the ion ($\ce{C7H7^{2+}}$), \(\frac{m}{z}\) equals 45.5.

M03755.title: mass-transfer-controlled electrolyte rate constant
M03755.definition: In controlled-potential coulometry and related techniques, the empirically evaluated constant of proportionality defined by the equation \[s_{\rm{B}}=- \frac{1}{c_{\rm{B}}}\ \frac{\mathrm{d}c_{\rm{B}}}{\mathrm{d}t}\] where \(c_{\rm{B}}\) is the bulk concentration of the substance B, and \(\frac{\rm{d}c_{\rm{B}}}{\rm{d}t}\) is the rate of change of that concentration, resulting from the consumption of B by reduction or oxidation at the working electrode.

M03709.title: mass
M03709.definition: Base quantity in the system of quantities upon which SI is based.

M03723.title: massic
M03723.definition: Attribute to a physical quantity obtained by division by mass; synonymous with specific.

M03724.title: massive transition
M03724.definition: A transition in which a crystal structure is changed into a new structure during cooling or heating, predominantly by interface-controlled reactions and the usual nucleation and growth characteristics associated with thermal diffusion.

13442.title: mast cell
13442.definition: Large connective tissue cell that contains inflammatory substances such as histamine, proteases (including tryptases, chymases, and carboxypeptidase A), heparin and chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans, and eicosanoid lipid mediators (the precursors of leukotrienes and prostaglandins). These substances are released in allergic reactions or in response to injury or inflammation.

13443.title: mast cell activation disorder
13443.definition: Disorder or syndrome in which there is evidence of systemic, inappropriate release of mast cell mediators.

13444.title: mast cell stabilizer
13444.definition: Non-steroidal medication that reduces the release of substances from mast cells, e.g., sodium cromoglycate.

12784.title: master curve
12784.definition: Viscoelastic spectrum of a polymer or polymer material constructed using the time–temperature superposition (TTS) principle, so that the spectrum covers a wide range of lengths of time or frequencies of measurement.

13445.title: mastocytoma
13445.definition: Nodule of mast cells that can involve the skin, subcutaneous tissue, and sometimes muscle.

13446.title: mastocytosis
13446.definition: Rare disease characterized by the presence of too many mast cells in various organs and tissues. The condition can be a chronic, long-term illness or it can develop suddenly.

M03756.title: matched cells
M03756.definition: A pair of cells with closely similar optical properties are called matched cells. One cell is the sample cell while the other, the reference (or blank) cell contains the solvent or a reference solution. In double beam spectrometers, radiation is passed either simultaneously or alternately through the cells. In single beam instruments the cells are moved sequentially into the radiation beam.

12297.title: material
12297.definition: The substance which is studied and from which the sample is taken.

08085.title: material characterization study
08085.definition: Intralaboratory comparison or interlaboratory comparison with the aim of assigning a reference quantity value to a quantity with stated measurement uncertainty or value to a reference nominal property value with stated examination uncertainty.

08025.title: material homogeneity
08025.definition: Uniform structure or composition of a material with respect to one or more specified properties.

08026.title: material recovery
08026.definition: Mass (volume, amount of substance) of a specified component isolated from a system divided by the mass (volume, amount of substance) of the system prior to isolation.

M03757.title: material safety data sheet
M03757.definition: Compilation of information required under the US OSHA Hazard Communication Standard on the identity of hazardous substances, health and physical hazards, exposure limits and precautions.

08027.title: material stability
08027.definition: Constancy of a property of a material over time.

09032.title: materials chemistry
09032.definition: Materials chemistry is the scientific discipline that designs, synthesizes, and characterizes materials with particular interest on both their processing and the understanding of useful or potentially useful properties displayed by the materials designed and synthesized for specific applications.

10919.title: maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein
10919.definition: Protein made in the fetus that normally leaks, in small amounts, into the mother’s circulation.

M03759.title: matrix effect
M03759.definition: The combined effect of all components of the sample other than the analyte on the measurement of the quantity. If a specific component can be identified as causing an effect then this is referred to as interference.

09263.title: matrix factor
09263.definition: Factors, arising from the composition of the matrix, for multiplying the quotient of the measured intensity and the appropriate sensitivity factor in formulae to determine the composition using surface analytical techniques.

15207.title: matrix formulation
15207.definition: Specific case of drug embedding in insoluble excipients (typically in a polymer) in order to achieve extended release.

M03758.title: matrix
M03758.definition: The components of the sample other than the analyte.

M03760.title: matrix isolation
M03760.definition: A term which refers to the isolation of a reactive or unstable species by dilution in an inert matrix (argon, nitrogen, etc.), usually condensed on a window or in an optical cell at low temperature, to preserve its structure for identification by spectroscopic or other means.

08086.title: matrix reference material
08086.definition: Reference material that is characteristic of a real sample.

09188.title: matrix-assisted laser desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry
09188.definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities from a sample that has been mixed with a matrix whose role is enhancing the ion yield produced by laser ablation and electrospray ionization.

09189.title: matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry
09189.definition: Measurement method in which a time-of-flight mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ions emitted, as a result of a short pulse of laser illumination, from a sample whose analyte is contained in a matrix that assists the formation of ions.

10271.title: matrix-compatible solid-phase microextraction
10271.definition: Immersion solid-phase microextraction where the extraction phase is designed to minimize sorption of particles or macromolecules present in the sample matrix.

10180.title: matrix-matched calibration
10180.definition: Calibration employing external calibration in which standard solutions of target are prepared in a solution of analyte-free matrix.

10224.title: matrix-solid phase dispersion
10224.definition: Extraction in which samples are blended with an abrasive solid sorbent, forming a free flowing powder from which target analytes are recovered by solvent elution.Typical work flow scheme for solid-phase matrix dispersion. (i) Sample is blended with an abrasive sorbent, (ii) free flowing powder containing sample is packed in a short column, and (iii) target analytes are recovered by elution.

M03761.title: Mattauch–Herzog geometry
M03761.definition: An arrangement for a double-focusing mass spectrograph in which a deflection of \(\frac{\pi}{4\ \sqrt{2}}\) radians in a radial electrostatic field is followed by a magnetic deflection of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) radians.

13447.title: maturation
13447.definition: Process by which B cells produce antibodies with increased affinity for antigen during the course of an immune response.

13448.title: mature B cell
13448.definition: B cell with immunoglobulin M (IgM) and immunoglobulin D (IgD) on its surface.

14830.title: maturity index
14830.definition: Index for pollution based on the proportions of species in a soil nematode community that fall into various categories ranging from colonizers (\(r\mbox{-}\rm{strategists}\)) to persisters (\(k\mbox{-}\rm{strategists}\)).

14831.title: maulstick incongruity
14831.definition: Assignment of ecological or biological significance of a contaminant’s effect based primarily on statements of statistical significance but contrary to biological probability.

14832.title: maximum acceptable toxicant concentration
14832.definition: Geometric mean of the lowest exposure concentration that causes a statistically significant adverse effect (lowest-observed-effect concentration, LOEC) and the highest exposure concentration where no effect is observed (no-observed-effect concentration, NOEC) in a life-cycle (full chronic) or partial lifecycle (partial chronic) test.

15208.title: maximum additive concentration
15208.definition: Maximum concentration of a drug, which will form a clear solution with a given concentration of surfactant.

M03762.title: maximum allowable concentration
M03762.definition: The maximum concentration of a pollutant which is considered harmless to healthy adults during their working hours, assuming they breathe uncontaminated air at all other times.

15868.title: maximum average daily concentration of an atmospheric pollutant
15868.definition: Highest of the average daily concentrations recorded at a definite point of measurement during a certain period of observation.

15869.title: maximum contaminant level
15869.definition: Under the Safe Drinking Water Act (USA), primary MCL is a regulatory concentration for drinking water which takes into account both adverse effects (including sensitive populations) and technological feasibility (including natural background levels): Secondary MCL is a regulatory concentration based on 'welfare', such as taste and staining, rather than health, but also takes into account technical feasibility.

M03763.title: maximum emission concentration
M03763.definition: Standards for maximum concentration of air pollutant emission from stationary or mobile sources.

15870.title: maximum exposure limit
15870.definition: Occupational exposure limit legally defined in the United Kingdom under COSHH as the maximum concentration of an airborne substance, averaged over a reference period, to which employees may be exposed by inhalation under any circumstances, and set on the advice of the HSC Advisory Committee on Toxic Substances.

MT07068.title: maximum hardness principle
MT07068.definition: A chemical system at a given temperature will evolve to a configuration of maximum absolute hardness, $\upeta\!$, provided that the potential due to the nuclei, plus any external potential and the electronic chemical potential, remain constant. In terms of molecular orbital theory, the highest value of $\upeta\!$ reflects the highest possible energy gap between the lowest unoccupied and highest occupied molecular orbitals; this value correlates with the stability of a system.

MT06910.title: maximum latent period
MT06910.definition: The length of time after which no causal relationship can reasonably be established. This length of time is the period from the last exposure to the point of time at which an exposed person has demonstrated the initial signs or symptoms.

14833.title: maximum likelihood estimation
14833.definition: Parametric method used to fit dose- or concentration-effect data to the log-normal, log-logistic, or other models.

10098.title: maximum likelihood principal component analysis
10098.definition: Principal-component analysis that incorporates information about measurement uncertainty to develop models that are optimal in a maximum likelihood sense.

M03765.title: maximum permissible daily dose
M03765.definition: Maximum daily dose of substance whose penetration into a human body during a lifetime will not cause diseases or health hazards that can be detected by current investigation methods and will not adversely affect future generations.

M03766.title: maximum permissible level
M03766.definition: Level, usually a combination of time and concentration, beyond which any exposure of humans to a chemical or physical agent in their immediate environment is unsafe.

15871.title: maximum residue limit
15871.definition: Maximum contents of a pesticide residue (expressed as \(\pu{mg kg-1}\) fresh weight) recommended by the Codex Alimentarius Commission to be legally permitted in or on food commodities and animal feeds.

15872.title: maximum residue limit for veterinary drugs
15872.definition: Maximum contents of a drug residue (expressed as \(\pu{mg kg-1}\) or \(\pu{\upmu g kg-1}\) fresh weight) recommended by the Codex Alimentarius Commission to be legally permitted or recognized as acceptable in or on food commodities and animal feeds.

15209.title: maximum safe concentration
15209.definition: Concentration of a drug in the plasma, above which side effects are likely to occur in a patient.

M03767.title: maximum storage life
M03767.definition: Period during which there is no change in concentration in excess of the value of the uncertainty of the concentration.

M03768.title: maximum tolerable concentration
M03768.definition: Highest concentration of a substance in an environmental medium that does not cause death of test organisms or species (denoted by \(\rm{LC}_{0}\)).

M03769.title: maximum tolerable dose
M03769.definition: Highest amount of a substance that, when introduced into the body, does not kill test animals (denoted by \(\rm{LD}_{0}\)).

M03770.title: maximum tolerable exposure level
M03770.definition: Maximum amount or concentration of a substance to which an organism can be exposed without leading to an adverse effect after prolonged exposure time.

M03771.title: maximum tolerated dose
M03771.definition: High dose used in chronic toxicity testing that is expected on the basis of an adequate subchronic study to produce limited toxicity when administered for the duration of the test period. It should not induce: (a) overt toxicity, for example appreciable death of cells or organ dysfunction, or (b) toxic manifestations that are predicted materially to reduce the life span of the animals except as the result of neoplastic development or (c) 10% or greater retardation of body weight gain as compared with control animals. In some studies, toxicity that could interfere with a carcinogenic effect is specifically excluded from consideration.

15873.title: maximum velocity
15873.definition: In Michaelis–Menten kinetics, the maximum rate of conversion of a substrate when its concentration is not rate-limiting.

08185.title: Mayr–Patz equation
08185.definition: Rate constants for the reactions of \(\ce{sp^{2}{-}hybridized}\) electrophiles with nucleophiles can be expressed by the correlation \[\lg [k/(\pu{dm3 mol-1 s-1})] = s_{\rm{N}}(E + N)\] where \(E\) is the nucleophile-independent electrophilicity parameter, \(N\) is the electrophile-independent nucleophilicity parameter, and \(s_{\rm{N}}\) is the electrophile-independent nucleophile-specific susceptibility parameter.

11859.title: maze
11859.definition: Labyrinthine system, in which the ability of an animal (usually a rodent) to find a direct route from a starting point to a specific location is observed.

M03772.title: McLafferty rearrangement
M03772.definition: $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}Cleavage}$ with concomitant specific transfer of a $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}hydrogen atom}$ in a six-membered transition state in mono-unsaturated systems, irrespective of whether the rearrangement is formulated by a radical or an ionic mechanism, and irrespective of the position of the charge.

12681.title: me-too drug
12681.definition: Term applied to drug analogues that offer no significant advantage over the prototype compound.

M03773.title: mean
M03773.definition: The sum of a series of observations divided by the number of observations in the series.

14834.title: mean absorption time
14834.definition: Mean time required for absorption of a drug or contaminant calculated as the difference in mean residence time (MRT) of the material introduced by the (noninstantaneous) route of interest and the MRT for the same material injected intravenously.

M03774.title: mean activity of an electrolyte in solution
M03774.definition: Defined by the equation: \[a_{\pm }=\mathrm{e}^{(\mu _{\rm{B}}- \mu _{\rm{B}}^{\unicode{x29B5}})\ \nu \ R\ T}\] where \(\mu _{\rm{B}}\) is the chemical potential of the solute $\ce{B}$ in a solution containing B and other species. The nature of $\ce{B}$ must be clearly stated: it is taken as a group of ions of two kinds carrying an equal number of positive and negative charges, e.g. $\ce{Na^{+}} + \ce{NO3^{−}}$ or $\ce{Ba^{2+}} + \ce{2Cl^{−}}$ or $\ce{2Al^{3+}} + \ce{3SO4^{2−}}$. \(v\) is the total number of ions making up the group i.e. 2, 3 and 5 respectively in the above examples. \(\mu _{\rm{B}}^{\unicode{x29B5}}\) is the chemical potential of $\ce{B}$ in its standard state, usually the hypothetical ideal solution of concentration \(\pu{1 mol kg -1}\) and at the same temperature and pressure as the solution under consideration.

M03775.title: mean catalytic activity rate
M03775.definition: The catalytic activity of a specified component in or moved from a system divided by the time during which the component was changed or moved. This kind of quantity should not be confused with rate of reaction.

10053.title: mean centering
10053.definition: Data pre-processing in which the mean value of a variable is subtracted from data across all objects. \[a_{i,j}^{\ast} = a_{i,j} - \frac{1}{n} \sum \limits_{i\,=\,1}^{n} a_{i,j}\]

M03776.title: mean current density
M03776.definition: Defined as \[j=\frac{I}{A}\] where \(I\) is the electric current and \(A\) is usually taken as the geometric area of the electrode. However the nature of the area used in this calculation must be clearly stated. In interpreting the mean current density it is important to know whether the current is uniformly distributed over the electrode interface.

09264.title: mean escape depth
09264.definition: Average depth normal to the surface from which specified particles or radiations escape.

M03777.title: mean exchange current density
M03777.definition: Defined by \[j_{0}=\frac{I_{0}}{A}\] where \(I_{0}\) is the exchange current of the electrode reaction and \(A\) is usually taken as the geometric area of the electrode.

M03778.title: mean free path
M03778.definition: The average distance a molecule travels between collisions. For a molecule, \(\lambda = (\sqrt{2}\ \pi \ n\ d_{\rm{m}}^{2})^{-1}\), where \(n\) is the number of molecules per unit volume and \(d_{\rm{m}}\) is their mean diameter. For $\ce{O2}$ at one atmosphere and \(25\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\), this distance is only \(9.7\times 10^{-6}\ \rm{cm}\); at \(10^{-6}\) atmospheres and \(25\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\) it is \(9.7\ \rm{cm}\). For an aerosol particle, the mean free path, \(\lambda _{\rm{B}}\) in the Stokes region (see Stokes law) is given by: \(\lambda _{\rm{B}} = \sqrt{\frac{3\ k\ T}{m}}\ m\ B\) where \(m\) is the mass of the particle, \(k\) is the Boltzmann constant (\(1.381\times 10^{-23}\ \rm{J K}^{-1}\)), \(T\) is the temperature (\(\rm{K}\)) and \(B\) is the mobility.

14835.title: mean generation time
14835.definition: Average time interval required for a bacterial cell to divide or for the population to double under a defined set of conditions.

M03779.title: mean interstitial velocity of the carrier gas
M03779.definition: The interstitial velocity, \(u\) of the carrier gas multiplied by the pressure-gradient correction-factor, \(j\): \[\bar{u} = u\ j\] \[\bar{u} = \frac{F\ j}{\varepsilon_{\rm{I}}}\] where \(F\) is the nominal linear flow, \(\varepsilon_{\rm{I}}\) is the interstitial fraction.

M03782.title: mean linear range
M03782.definition: In a given material, for specified charged particles of a specified energy, the average displacement of the particles before they stop.

M03783.title: mean mass range
M03783.definition: The mean linear range multiplied by the mass density of the material.

M03784.title: mean mass rate
M03784.definition: The mass of a specified component changed in or moved to or from a system divided by the time during which the component was changed or moved.

M03785.title: mean residence time
M03785.definition: The mean time during which the molecules remain on the surface of the adsorbent, i.e. the mean time interval between impact and desorption.

10151.title: mean squared error of calibration
10151.definition: In calibration for \(N\) calibration data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the value predicted by the calibration function. \[E_{\rm{MSEC}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i} - c_{i})^2}{N}\]

10099.title: mean squared error of prediction
10099.definition: In multivariate calibration the average of the squared deviation of estimated values from the values of evaluation data. For \(N\) evaluation data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the predicted value. \[E_{\rm{MSEP}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i}\,-\, c_{i})^2}{N}\]

M03786.title: mean substance rate
M03786.definition: The amount of substance of a specified component changed in or moved to or from a system divided by the time during which the component was changed or moved. This kind of quantity usually should be preferred to mean mass rate or mean volume rate.

M03787.title: mean volume rate
M03787.definition: The volume of a specified component changed in or moved to or from a system divided by the time during which the component was changed or moved.

12235.title: mean-field theory
12235.definition: Theory reducing the difficult exact evaluation of interactions in a multi-body system to a simpler but approximate evaluation of an average effective interaction of one body with its surroundings.

12197.title: mean-square end-to-end distance
12197.definition: Statistical-mechanical mean-square end-to-end distance of a linear chain averaged over all chain conformations.

12201.title: mean-square end-to-end distance of a freely rotating chain
12201.definition: Mean-square end-to-end distance of a linear freely rotating chain.

12192.title: mean-square radius of gyration
12192.definition: For a flexible macromolecule composed of \(n\) mass elements, of masses \(m_{i}\) , \(i = 1, 2, \ldots, n\), located at statistical-mechanical mean-square distances \(\lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\) from the centre of mass, the mean-square radius of gyration is the mass average of \(\lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\) over all mass elements, i.e., \[\lt\!s^{2}\!\gt = \left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} m_{i} \lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\!/\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} m_{i} \right)\]

12199.title: mean-square unperturbed end-to-end distance
12199.definition: Mean-square end-to-end distance of a chain having unperturbed dimensions.

12194.title: mean-square unperturbed radius of gyration
12194.definition: Mean-square radius of gyration of a macromolecule having unperturbed dimensions.

M03788.title: measurable quantity
M03788.definition: An attribute of a substance which may be distinguished qualitatively and determined quantitatively. In the context of analytical chemistry, the attribute may refer to a physical quantity such as X- or $\upgamma\!\mbox{-}\rm{ray\ energy}$, or it may refer to a measure of amount such as mass or concentration.

M03790.title: measured excitation spectrum
M03790.definition: The spectrum observed by measuring the variation of the luminescence flux from an analyte as a function of the excitation wavelength.

M03793.title: measured value
M03793.definition: The observed value of weight, volume, meter-reading or other quantity, found in the analysis of a material.

M03794.title: measurement
M03794.definition: A description of a property of a system by means of a set of specified rules, that maps the property onto a scale of specified values, by direct or 'mathematical' comparison with specified reference(s). The demand for rules makes 'measurement' a scientific concept in contrast to the mere colloquial sense of 'description'. However, in the present definition, 'measurement' has a wider meaning than given in elementary physics. Even a very incomplete description of, for instance, a patient (at a stated time) has to be given by a set of measurements, that are easier to manage and grasp.

08087.title: measurement capability
08087.definition: Ability to measure a quantity in a specified interval of quantity values, embodied in a specified material, as demonstrated by measurement uncertainty.

08506.title: measurement efficiency
08506.definition: Number of detector events per atom in the sample.

14836.title: measurement endpoint
14836.definition: Measurable response to a stressor (e.g., fledglings produced per nest each year) that is related to the valued qualities of the assessment endpoint (e.g., reproductive success of bald eagles).

08088.title: measurement precision control material
08088.definition: Quality control material with or without reference quantity value used in quality control to assess measurement precision.

08028.title: measurement procedure
08028.definition: Detailed description of a measurement according to one or more measurement principles and to a given measurement method, based on a measurement model and including any calculation to obtain a measurement result.

08029.title: measurement procedure bias
08029.definition: Contribution to measurement bias that is attributed to systematic effects on measurement results made according to a measurement procedure.

08030.title: measurement procedure with standard addition
08030.definition: Measurement procedure in which indications are obtained for an analytical sample as well as for analytical samples with addition(s) of a measurement standard.

08031.title: measurement reproducibility
08031.definition: Measurement precision under reproducibility conditions of measurement.

M03795.title: measurement resolution
M03795.definition: The minimum value above which the difference of two values of air quality characteristic can be distinguished with 95% probability.

M03796.title: measurement result
M03796.definition: The outcome of an analytical measurement (application of the chemical measurement process), or value attributed to a measurand. This may be the result of direct observation, but more commonly it is given as a statistical estimate derived from a set of observations. The distribution of such estimates (estimator distribution) characterizes the chemical measurement process, in contrast to a particular estimate, which constitutes an experimental result. Additional characteristics become evident if we represent \(\hat{x}\) as follows: \[\hat{x} = \tau + e = \rlap{\underbracket{\phantom{\tau + \Delta}}_\mu }\tau + \overbracket{\Delta+\delta}^{e} = \mu + \delta\] The true value, \(\tau \), is the value \(x\) that would result if the chemical measurement process were error-free. The error, \(e\), is the difference between an observed (estimated) value and the true value; i.e. \(e=\hat{x}- \tau \) (signed quantity). The total error generally has two components, bias (\(\mathit{\Delta}\)) and random error (\(\delta \)), as indicated above. The limiting mean, \(\mu\), is the asymptotic value or population mean of the distribution that characterizes the measured quantity; the value that is approached as the number of observations approaches infinity. Modern statistical terminology labels this quantity the expectation value or expected value, \(E(\hat{x})\). The bias, \(\mathit{\Delta}\), is the difference between the limiting mean and the true value; i.e. \(\mathit{\Delta} = \mu - \tau \) (signed quantity). The random error, \(\delta \), is the difference between an observed value and the limiting mean; i.e. \(\delta = \hat{x} - \mu \) (signed quantity).

M03797.title: measurement solution
M03797.definition: The solution that is presented to the measuring device. It comprises the test solution, or an aliquot thereof, after it has undergone any treatment required prior to the presentation to the measuring device.

M03798.title: measurement threshold
M03798.definition: The minimum concentration of a substance which produces a quantifiable signal with a given uncertainty.

08089.title: measurement trueness control material
08089.definition: Quality control material with reference quantity value used in quality control to estimate a systematic measurement error.

08635.title: mechanical anharmonicity
08635.definition: Influence of cubic and higher-order terms in vibrational potential energy.

M03800.title: mechanical entrapment
M03800.definition: The process of random incorporation of comparatively small quantities of other phases (e.g. water, dust, particles, etc.) in the bulk of a precipitate during its formation.The deliberate capture of small quantities of such phases by the deliberate addition of solids to a liquid phase. (The term inclusion is not recommended).

08636.title: mechanical harmonicity
08636.definition: Influence of quadratic terms in vibrational potential energy.

M03801.title: mechanical hygrometer
M03801.definition: An apparatus containing an element (hair, goldbeater's skin, carbon-film) whose dimension or mass varies as a function of its water content.

12785.title: mechanical melting
12785.definition: Mechanically induced transition of matter in the crystalline or glassy state to its melt.

13837.title: mechanically interlocked molecular architecture
13837.definition: Supramolecular structure in which molecules are linked only as a consequence of their topology.

M03804.title: mechanism
M03804.definition: A detailed description of the process leading from the reactants to the products of a reaction, including a characterization as complete as possible of the composition, structure, energy and other properties of reaction intermediates, products and transition states. An acceptable mechanism of a specified reaction (and there may be a number of such alternative mechanisms not excluded by the evidence) must be consistent with the reaction stoichiometry, the rate law and with all other available experimental data, such as the stereochemical course of the reaction. Inferences concerning the electronic motions which dynamically interconvert successive species along the reaction path (as represented by curved arrows, for example) are often included in the description of a mechanism. It should be noted that for many reactions all this information is not available and the suggested mechanism is based on incomplete experimental data. It is not appropriate to use the term mechanism to describe a statement of the probable sequence in a set of stepwise reactions. That should be referred to as a reaction sequence, and not a mechanism.

M03805.title: mechanism-based inhibition
M03805.definition: Irreversible inhibition of an enzyme due to its catalysis of the reaction of an artificial substrate. Also called 'suicide inhibition'.

M03803.title: mechanization
M03803.definition: The use of devices to replace, refine, extend or supplement human effort. The corresponding verb is to mechanize.

10307.title: mechanized extraction
10307.definition: Extraction using a device with at least one movable part that replaces or supplements human effort in any (or all) steps of the process.

MT07141.title: mechano-chemical reaction
MT07141.definition: Chemical reaction that is induced by the direct absorption of mechanical energy.

10921.title: Meckel diverticulum
10921.definition: Congenital pouch in the ileum resulting from incomplete closure of the yolk sac.

10922.title: meconium
10922.definition: First intestinal discharges of the newborn infant, greenish in color and consisting of epithelial cells, mucus, and bile.

M03806.title: median
M03806.definition: Depending on whether the number of observations is even or odd, the median can be estimated as follows:   If \(n=2\ m+1\): The middle value of a series of observations, arranged in increasing or decreasing order.   If \(n=2\ m\): The arithmetic mean of the two middle values of a series of observations, arranged in increasing or decreasing order.   Comment: The use of the median when reporting results of chemical analysis is generally not recommended, because its statistical efficiency is less than that of the mean. In certain cases, however, especially when treating small sets of data, the median may offer advantages because it is a so-called 'robust statistic', i.e. it offers considerable resistance to the effects of isolated outliers.

M03807.title: median effective concentration
M03807.definition: Statistically derived concentration of a substance in an environmental medium expected to produce a certain effect in 50% of test organisms in a given population under a defined set of conditions.

M03808.title: median effective dose
M03808.definition: Statistically derived dose of a chemical or physical agent (radiation) expected to produce a certain effect in 50% of test organisms in a given population or to produce a half-maximal effect in a biological system under a defined set of conditions.

14837.title: median effective time
14837.definition: For sublethal or ambiguously lethal effects, the median time until \(\pu{50\%}\) of the exposed individuals respond.

14838.title: median inhibitory time
14838.definition: Time required for a toxicant to inhibit a specified process in \(\pu{50\%}\) of a population under test conditions.

M03809.title: median lethal concentration
M03809.definition: Statistically derived concentration of a substance in an environmental medium expected to kill 50% of organisms in a given population under a defined set of conditions.

M03810.title: median lethal dose
M03810.definition: Statistically derived dose of a chemical or physical agent (radiation) expected to kill 50% of organisms in a given population under a defined set of conditions.

M03811.title: median lethal time
M03811.definition: Statistically derived average time interval during which 50% of a given population may be expected to die following acute administration of a chemical or physical agent (radiation) at a given concentration under a defined set of conditions.

M03812.title: median narcotic concentration
M03812.definition: Statistically derived concentration of a substance in an environmental medium expected to cause narcotic conditions in 50% of a given population under a defined set of conditions.

M03813.title: median narcotic dose
M03813.definition: Statistically derived dose of a substance expected to cause narcosis in 50% of test animals under a defined set of conditions.

10923.title: median teratogenic concentration
10923.definition: Median concentration resulting in developmental malformations for \(\pu{50\%}\) of exposed test animals within a predetermined time, e.g., \(\pu{96 h}\).

14839.title: median time to death
14839.definition: Median time resulting in death for \(\pu{50\%}\) of the exposed organisms.

14840.title: median tolerance limit
14840.definition: Concentration of a substance in air, water, sediment, or soil at which \(\pu{50\%}\) of the test organisms survive after a specified time of exposure. The \(\pu{TL_{50}}\) (equivalent to the \(\pu{TL_{m}}\)) is usually expressed as a time-dependent value (e.g., \(\pu{24\!\mbox{-}h}\) or \(\pu{96\!\mbox{-}h}\) \(\pu{TL_{50}}\); the estimated concentration at which \(\pu{50\%}\) of test organisms survive after \(\pu{24 h}\) or \(\pu{96 h}\) of exposure).

10924.title: mediastinum
10924.definition: Region in the middle of the thorax between the two lungs, containing the regional vessels, trachea, esophagus, bronchi, lymph nodes, and heart.

08964.title: mediating agent
08964.definition: Species that mediates polymerization in reversible-deactivation polymerization.

M03814.title: medium
M03814.definition: The phase (and composition of the phase) in which chemical species and their reactions are studied in a particular investigation.

M03815.title: medium effect
M03815.definition: The medium effect on ionic species B due to transfer from solvent \(\rm{S}_{1}\) to solvent \(\rm{S}_{2}\) (number) is defined by \[R\ T\ \ln \gamma _{\rm{S}_{1}}^{\rm{S}_{2}}\left(\rm{B}\right)=\mu _{\rm{B}}^{\rm{o},\rm{S}_{2}}- \mu _{\rm{B}}^{\rm{o},\rm{S}_{1}}\] where \(R\) is the gas constant, \(T\) is the thermodynamic temperature and \(\mu _{\rm{B}}^{\rm{o},\rm{S}_{i}}\) is the standard chemical potential of B in solvent \(\rm{S}_{i}\) (where \(i\) = 1 or 2), the reference states being the same in both solvents. \(\gamma _{\rm{S}_{1}}^{\rm{S}_{2}}(\rm{B})\) is not an exactly measurable quantity.

09177.title: medium-energy ion scattering spectrometry
09177.definition: Measurement method to elucidate the composition and structure of the outermost atomic layers of a solid material, in which principally monoenergetic, singly-charged probe ions scattered from the surface are detected and recorded as a function of their energy, angle of scattering, or both.

M03816.title: medium-pressure mercury lamp
M03816.definition: Non-coherent radiation source containing mercury vapour at pressures ranging from \(50\) to several hundred \(\mathrm{kPa}\) (\(1\ \rm{atm} = 101.325\ \rm{kPa}\)). Emits mostly from \(200\) to \(1000\ \rm{nm}\) with the most intense lines approximately at \(218\), \(248\), \(254\), \(266\), \(280\), \(289\), \(297\), \(303\), \(313\), \(334\), \(366\), \(406\), \(408\), \(436\), \(546\) and \(578\ \rm{nm}\).

10925.title: medulla
10925.definition:
[medulla oblongata] Lower part of the brain stem continuous with the spinal cord, containing neural centers regulating the autonomic functions of breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure.
Middle (central) part of an organ, as in adrenal medulla, renal medulla, or the medulla of a lymph node.

11860.title: medulloblastoma
11860.definition: Highly malignant, invasive brain tumor of embryonal origin, arising in the posterior fossa, usually from the cerebellum.

10926.title: megacolon
10926.definition: Condition of extreme dilation of the colon that can be congenital (as in Hirschsprung disease) or acquired (as when children refuse to defecate).

10927.title: megadactyly
10927.definition: Disorder characterized by an abnormally large fingers and (or) toes.

14841.title: meiofauna
14841.definition: Small benthic invertebrates living in interstices of soil or sediment or in aquatic systems.

M03818.title: meiosis
M03818.definition: The reductive cell division which results in daughter cells containing one copy of each of the chromosome of the parent. The entire meiotic process involves two separate divisions (meiosis I and meiosis II). The first division is a true reductive division with the chromosome number being halved, whereas the second division resembles mitosis in many ways. Thus, a diploid parental cell will give rise to haploid daughter cells (cf. ploidy).

14842.title: meiotic drive
14842.definition: Any process that causes some alleles to be over-represented in the gametes which are formed during meiosis.

M03819.title: Meisenheimer adduct
M03819.definition: A cyclohexadienyl derivative formed as Lewis adduct from a nucleophile (Lewis base) and an aromatic or heteroaromatic compound, also called Jackson–Meisenheimer adduct. In earlier usage the term 'Meisenheimer complex' was restricted to the typical Meisenheimer alkoxide adduct of nitro-substituted aromatic ethers, e.g.  Analogous cationic adducts, such as:  considered to be reaction intermediates in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions, are called 'Wheland intermediates', and sometimes, inappropriately, $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}complexes}$.

14843.title: melanic forms
14843.definition: Individuals or subspecies with increased dark pigmentation.

14844.title: melanism
14844.definition: Increased black or nearly black pigmentation of skin, feathers, or hair of an organism, resulting from (increased) synthesis of melanin.

12786.title: melt
12786.definition: Matter in the amorphous state above its glass-transition temperature.

12787.title: melt flow index
12787.definition: Mass of a polymer in grams that flows through a calibrated orifice at constant temperature under a specified load over a \(\pu{10\!{-}min}\) period.

M03821.title: melting
M03821.definition: The conversion of a solid to a liquid by the application of heat and/or pressure.

M03822.title: melting point corrected
M03822.definition: The term originally signified that a correction was made (not made) for the emergent stem of the thermometer. In current usage it often means that the accuracy of the thermometer was (was not) verified. This current usage is inappropriate and should be abandoned.

12788.title: melting temperature
12788.definition: Temperature at which the last trace of crystallinity disappears upon heating.

MT06878.title: membrane
MT06878.definition: Structure, having lateral dimensions much greater than its thickness, through which transfer may occur under a variety of driving forces.

13450.title: membrane attack complex
13450.definition: Complex of complement components C5b–C9 that inserts as a pore into the membrane of target cells leading to cell lysis.

09849.title: membrane bilayer
09849.definition: Planar structure spontaneously formed by amphipathic lipids in a polar (aqueous) environment.

M03824.title: membrane emf
M03824.definition: The potential difference \(E_{\rm{m}}\) between two saturated $\ce{KCl}$ bridges inserted into two solutions separated by a membrane. The solutions need not be in equilibrium with one another and need not contain any colloidal material.

10281.title: membrane extraction
10281.definition: Extraction of analytes from a sample by permeation through a membrane.

10282.title: membrane extraction with sorbent interface
10282.definition: Membrane extraction with a sorbent trap for concentration of the permeate.

M03823.title: membrane
M03823.definition: A general term which refers to a continuous layer, usually consisting of a semi-permeable material, with controlled permeability covering a structure, such as carbon or an inert metal, or separating two electrolyte solutions. This latter case is the most general form of an ion-selective electrode. The membrane separates the internal components of the ion-selective electrode from the test solution. The membrane of an ion-selective electrode is responsible for the EMF response and selectivity of the entire electrode. Comment: Membranes of sensor electrodes are thought to be practically homogeneous, but an actual membrane may contain inhomogeneous regions, often at surfaces, and connected with materials and preparation methods used. Inhomogeneous regions include low dielectric polymer regions with few charge sites and regions with high local site densities. Surface regions of plasticized liquid membranes often are low in sites and high in plasticizer or exuded impurities.

11861.title: membrane polarization
11861.definition: Occurrence of a potential difference across a biological membrane.

09850.title: membrane rafts
09850.definition: Dynamic, nanometre-sized, highly ordered, membrane domains enriched in sterols and sphingolipids. They contain specific sets of membrane proteins that are sorted into rafts by their specific physical properties and specific lipid-protein interactions.

M03826.title: membrane sites
M03826.definition: Membranes frequently contain built-in 'fixed' charged sites (e.g. immobile $\ce{–(SO3^{−})}$ in polystyrenesulfonate), or intentionally added, hydrophobically trapped, 'mobile' sites [e.g. tetraphenylborate in plasticized poly(vinyl chloride)]. Such membranes with charged sites are named sited membranes. Ions of opposite sign in the membrane are 'counter-ions'. Ions of the same sign as sites are not present in significant quantities, and are co-ions. Sited membranes are 'permselective' to counter-ions i.e. only counter-ions exchange into the membrane and therefore have some mobility in the membrane bulk.

10272.title: membrane-protected solid-phase microextraction
10272.definition: Immersion solid-phase microextraction in which the extraction phase is surrounded by a permeable membrane that allows access of analytes to the extraction phase while shielding the extraction phase from matrix components with a potential to interfere in the extraction or subsequent analysis.

09112.title: membranes with mobile charged sites
09112.definition:
Kind of ion-selective membranes used in an ISE comprising:

Positively-charged, hydrophobic cations which, when dissolved in a suitable organic solvent and held in an inert support (e.g., poly(propylenecarbonate) filter or \(\ce{PVC}\)), provide membranes which are sensitive to changes in the activities of anions.
Negatively-charged hydrophobic anions which, when dissolved in a suitable organic solvent and held in an inert support (e.g., poly(propylene carbonate) filter or \(\ce{PVC}\)), provide membranes which are sensitive to changes of cation activities.
Uncharged “carrier” electrodes based on solutions of molecular complexing agents of cations and anions, which can be used for preparing ion exchanger membranes sensitive and selective to certain cations and anions.
Hydrophobic ion-pair electrodes of plasticized polymers (e.g., \(\ce{PVC}\)) containing a dissolved hydrophobic ion-pair respond to the ion activities of those components, which are relevant to the ion-pairs incorporated in the membrane. The responses can be Nernstian.

13451.title: memory
13451.definition: Characteristic of the acquired immune response (see acquired immunity) of lymphocytes whereby a second encounter with a given antigen produces a secondary immune response that is faster, greater, and longer lasting than the primary immune response.

13452.title: memory cell
13452.definition: Clonally expanded T cell or B cell produced during a primary immune response and which is primed to mediate a secondary immune response to the original antigen.

M03827.title: memory effect
M03827.definition: In instruments used for atmospheric trace component analysis, the dependence of an instrument reading on one or several previous sample(s).

13453.title: memory lymphocyte immunostimulation assay
13453.definition: Patented modification of the lymphocyte transformation test (LTT) based on the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) principle.

08840.title: memristor
08840.definition: Electric component that can be reversibly switched between stable low- and high-resistive states.

10928.title: menarche
10928.definition: First menstrual cycle of a woman.

10929.title: Mendelian gene
10929.definition: Gene located in a chromosome that obeys the laws of Mendelian inheritance.

10930.title: Mendelian inheritance
10930.definition: Inheritance in which stable and indivisible characteristics are controlled entirely or overwhelmingly by a single genetic locus and transmitted over many generations.

10931.title: Mendelian trait
10931.definition: Phenotype that shows a pattern of Mendelian inheritance.

14845.title: Mendelism
14845.definition: Fundamental principles of inheritance (especially the laws of segregation and independent assortment and the existence of dominant and recessive characters), propounded originally by Gregor Mendel (1822–1884) and forming the basis for the science of classical genetics.

11863.title: meningioma
11863.definition: Firm, often vascular, tumor arising from the meninges of the brain or spinal cord.

11864.title: meningitis
11864.definition: Inflammation or infection of the meninges.

10933.title: meningocele
10933.definition: Herniation of the membranes of the brain or spinal cord (see meninx) through a defect in the cranium or spinal column.

11865.title: meningoencephalitis
11865.definition: Inflammation of the brain and meninges.

11866.title: meningoencephalocele
11866.definition: Protrusion of both the meninges and brain tissue through a defect in the skull.

10934.title: meningomyelocele
10934.definition: Birth defect following failure of the neural tube to close, resulting in protrusion of a sac of nerve tissue and its covering membranes.

10932.title: meninx
10932.definition: Any of the three membranes (the dura mater, arachnoid, and pia mater) that line the skull and vertebral canal and enclose the brain and spinal cord.

10935.title: menopause
10935.definition: Cessation of reproductive capability in a woman, marked by declining ovarian function and an end to menses.

10936.title: menstrual cycle
10936.definition: The period, normally lasting \(\pu{28 days}\) in the human female, during which an ovum matures, is ovulated, and enters the uterus through the Fallopian tubes. If fertilization occurs, the cycle is interrupted by pregnancy; otherwise, the cycle ends with menstruation.

10937.title: menstruation
10937.definition: Cyclic endometrial shedding and discharge of a bloody fluid from the uterus during the menstrual cycle.

11867.title: mental retardation
11867.definition: Formerly used term to describe intellectual disability.

11868.title: mentation
11868.definition: Mental activity, conscious or unconscious, but especially referring to thinking and reasoning.

M03828.title: mer-
M03828.definition: An affix used in names to denote meridional; three groups occupying vertices of an octahedral coordination sphere in such a relationship that one is cis to the two others which are themselves trans, not now recommended for precise nomenclature purposes.

15874.title: mercurialism
15874.definition: Chronic poisoning caused by exposure to mercury, often by breathing its vapor but also by skin absorption and, less commonly, by ingestion.

09102.title: mercury electrode
09102.definition: Liquid metal electrode used in polarography.

M03834.title: mercury flow system
M03834.definition: For mercury released directly as atomic vapour, different direct transfer systems are used. In an open dynamic system the liberated analyte is transported by a carrier gas through the sampling or excitation source and swept away. In an open static system the equilibrated gaseous phase is forced into the absorption cell by displacement, e.g. by water. During measurement the gaseous phase is thus static. In a closed system the analyte and carrier gas are circulated through the absorption cell and the generator vessel until equilibrium between the liquid and gaseous phases is established.

M03835.title: mercury–xenon lamp
M03835.definition: Non-coherent intense source of ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared radiation produced by an electrical discharge in a mixture of mercury vapour and xenon under high pressure.

M03836.title: mero
M03836.definition: A prefix meaning part, partial or fragment, used in formation of compound words, e.g. merocyanines are compounds related to cyanines but have a nitrogen atom at only one end of the chromogenic system instead of at both ends.

10529.title: meroblastic cleavage
10529.definition: Partial cleavage of the egg, occurring in some animals, such as reptiles and birds, whose eggs have a large amount of yolk, resulting in unequal blastomeres and only part of the egg progressing to further cell division; the yolk mass remains and has nutritive value.

10938.title: meromelia
10938.definition: Congenital absence of a part of a limb, resulting in a shrunken and deformed extremity.

M03837.title: merry-go-round reactor
M03837.definition: An apparatus in which several samples are rotated around a radiation source in order to expose each to equal amounts of radiation.

10939.title: mesectoderm
10939.definition: Embryonic migratory cells derived from the neural crest of the head that contribute to the formation of the meninges (see meninx) and become pigment cells.

10940.title: mesencephalon
10940.definition: Part of the vertebrate brain that develops from the middle section of the embryonic neural tube.

10941.title: mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition
10941.definition: Process in which motile mesenchymal cells undergo a development to planar, polarized fixed cells, forming epithelia.

10942.title: mesenchyme
10942.definition: Meshwork of embryonic connective tissue in the mesoderm, from which are formed the bone, muscular, and connective tissues of the body and also the urogenital system, blood vessels, and lymph vessels.

13454.title: mesenteric lymph node
13454.definition: Lymph node lying between layers of the mesentery.

10943.title: mesentery
10943.definition: Membranous sheet attaching various organs to the body wall, especially the peritoneal fold attaching the intestine to the dorsal body wall.

12231.title: mesh size
12231.definition: Average distance between two adjacent entanglements on a given macromolecule in a semi-dilute solution, a concentrated solution, or bulk amorphous polymer.

M03838.title: meso
M03838.definition: A prefix to indicate the presence of a symmetry element of the second kind (see chirality) in a chemical species which is usually one of a set of diastereoisomers that also includes a chiral member.

M03856.title: meso structures
M03856.definition: Relative configurations of consecutive, but not necessarily contiguous, constitutionally equivalent carbon atoms that have a symmetrically-constituted connecting group (if any) are designated 'meso' or 'racemo', as appropriate. Examples:  (The symbol  represents a symmetrically-constituted connecting group, such as $\ce{–CH2\bond{–}}$, $\ce{–CH2–CH2\bond{–}}$, or $\ce{–CR2–CH2–CR2\bond{–}}$ .)

M03839.title: meso-compound
M03839.definition: A term for the achiral member(s) of a set of diastereoisomers which also includes one or more chiral members. For example:

14846.title: mesocosm
14846.definition: Enclosed and essentially self-sufficient (but not necessarily isolated) experimental environment or ecosystem that is on a larger scale than a laboratory microcosm.

10944.title: mesoderm
10944.definition:
Middle layer of cells in the embryo, lying between the ectoderm and the endoderm. It includes the following tissues:
Lateral mesoderm: peripheral portion of intraembryonic mesoderm.
Intermediate mesoderm: origin of the nephrogenic cord.
Parietal (somatic) mesoderm: cell source for the formation of the lateral and ventral body wall.
Visceral (branchial, pharyngeal, splanchnic) mesoderm: inner layer of lateral mesoderm that, with the endoderm, provides the cells from which the gut and lungs and their coverings arise.

10308.title: mesofluidic extraction device
10308.definition: Extraction device with channel widths from \(\pu{10 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{2 mm}\) integrated into a flow platform.

10945.title: mesogastrium
10945.definition: Part of the embryonic mesentery that is attached to the early stomach.

MT06870.title: mesogen
MT06870.definition: A compound that under suitable conditions of temperature, pressure, and concentration can exist as a mesophase or, in particular, as a liquid-crystal (LC) phase.

MT06858.title: mesogenic group
MT06858.definition: A part of a molecule or macromolecule endowed with sufficient anisotropy in both attractive and repulsive forces to contribute strongly to mesophase or, in particular, liquid-crystal mesophase formation in low-molar-mass and polymeric substances.

M03840.title: mesogenic monomer
M03840.definition: A monomer which can impart the properties of liquid crystals to the polymers formed by its polymerization.

M03841.title: mesogenic pitch
M03841.definition: A pitch with a complex mixture of numerous essentially aromatic hydrocarbons. It does not contain anisotropic particles detectable by optical microscopy. Mesogenic pitch is low in quinoline-insoluble fractions and capable of transforming into mesophase pitch during continuous heat treatment above \(750\ \rm{K}\) by the formation of optically detectable carbonaceous mesophase.

M03842.title: mesoionic compounds
M03842.definition: Dipolar five- (possibly six-) membered heterocyclic compounds in which both the negative and the positive charge are delocalized, for which a totally covalent structure cannot be written, and which cannot be represented satisfactorily by any one polar structure. The formal positive charge is associated with the ring atoms, and the formal negative charge is associated with ring atoms or an exocyclic nitrogen or chalcogen atom. Mesoionic compounds are a subclass of betaines.

M03843.title: mesolytic cleavage
M03843.definition: Cleavage of a bond in a radical ion whereby a radical and an ion are formed. The term reflects the mechanistic duality of the process, which can be viewed as homolytic or heterolytic depending on how the electrons are attributed to the fragments.

M03844.title: mesomeric effect
M03844.definition: The effect (on reaction rates, ionization equilibria, etc.) attributed to a substituent due to overlap of its p- or $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}orbitals}$ with the p- or $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}orbitals}$ of the rest of the molecular entity. delocalization is thereby introduced or extended, and electronic charge may flow to or from the substituent. The effect is symbolized by M. Strictly understood, the mesomeric effect operates in the ground electronic state of the molecule. When the molecule undergoes electronic excitation or its energy is increased on the way to the transition state of a chemical reaction, the mesomeric effect may be enhanced by the electromeric effect, but this term is not much used, and the mesomeric and electromeric effects tend to be subsumed in the term resonance effect of a substituent.

M03845.title: mesomerism
M03845.definition: Essentially synonymous with resonance. The term is particularly associated with the picture of $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electrons}$ as less localized in an actual molecule than in a Lewis formula. The term is intended to imply that the correct representation of a structure is intermediate between two or more Lewis formulae.

M03846.title: mesomorphic phase
M03846.definition: Often formed by concentrated systems of surfactants. These are states of matter in which anisometric molecules (or particles) are regularly arranged in one (nematic state) or two (smectic state) directions, but randomly arranged in the remaining direction(s).

MT06853.title: mesomorphic state
MT06853.definition: A state of matter in which the degree of molecular order is intermediate between the perfect three-dimensional, long-range positional and orientational order found in solid crystals and the absence of long-range order found in isotropic liquids, gases, and amorphous solids.

M03847.title: mesomorphic transition
M03847.definition: A transition that occurs between a fully-ordered crystalline solid and an isotropic liquid. Mesomorphic transitions can occur (i) from a crystal to a liquid crystal (ii) from a liquid crystal to another liquid crystal and (iii) from a liquid crystal to an isotropic liquid.

10946.title: mesonephric duct
10946.definition: Embryonic duct of the mesonephros, which in the male becomes the vas deferens and in the female becomes vestigial.

10947.title: mesonephros
10947.definition: Middle part of the embryonic kidney in vertebrates, becoming the adult kidney in fishes and amphibians and the epididymis in reptiles, birds, and mammals.

M03848.title: mesopause
M03848.definition: That region of the atmosphere between the mesosphere and the thermosphere at which the temperature is a minimum.

M03849.title: mesophase
M03849.definition: A phase occurring over a definite range of temperature, pressure, or concentration within the mesomorphic state.

M03850.title: mesophase pitch
M03850.definition: A pitch with a complex mixture of numerous essentially aromatic hydrocarbons containing anisotropic liquid-crystalline particles (carbonaceous mesophase) detectable by optical microscopy and capable of coalescence into the bulk mesophase.

M03851.title: mesophase pitch-based carbon fibres
M03851.definition: Mesophase pitch-based carbon fibres (MPP-based carbon fibres) are carbon fibres obtained from mesogenic pitch after it has been transformed into mesophase pitch (MPP) at least during the process of spinning, and after the spun mesophase pitch fibres have been made non-fusible (stabilized) and carbonized.

M03852.title: mesophiles
M03852.definition: Microorganisms which grow at moderate temperatures in the range \(20{-}45^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\), and which have an optimum growth temperature in the range \(30{-}39^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\).

M03853.title: mesopore
M03853.definition: Pore of intermediate size. [Those with widths exceeding about \(0.05\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) or \(50\ \rm{nm}\) (\(500\ \mathring{\rm{A}}\)) are called macropores; those with widths not exceeding about \(2\ \rm{nm}\) (\(20\ \mathring{\rm{A}}\)) are called micropores].

14305.title: mesoporous particle
14305.definition: Particle containing pores of diameters between approximately \(\pu{2 \upmu m}\) and \(\pu{50 \upmu m}\).

M03854.title: mesoscale
M03854.definition: In meteorology, the size or scale of phenomena smaller than ordinary cyclones or weather systems but larger than such microscale phenomena as the thickness of the boundary layer, the wakes of objects, etc. Thunderstorms involve mesoscale processes, and other meteorological events the size of cities are usually mesoscale processes.

M03855.title: mesosphere
M03855.definition: That region of the atmosphere which lies above the stratopause (about \(4752\ \rm{km}\)) and below the mesopause (about \(8090\ \rm{km}\)) and in which temperature decreases with increasing height; this is the region in which the lowest temperatures of the atmosphere occur.

15875.title: mesothelioma
15875.definition: Malignant tumor of the mesothelium of the pleura, pericardium, or peritoneum, that may be caused by exposure to asbestos fibers and some other fibers.

10948.title: mesothelium
10948.definition: Single layer of flattened cells forming an epithelium that lines serous cavities such as the peritoneum, pleura, and pericardium.

M03857.title: messenger RNA
M03857.definition: An RNA molecule that transfers the coding information for protein synthesis from the chromosomes to the ribosomes. mRNA is formed from a DNA template by transcription. It may be a copy of a single gene or of several adjacent genes (polycistronic mRNA). On the ribosome, the sequence is converted into the programmed amino acid sequence through translation.

14847.title: meta-analysis
14847.definition: Process of using statistical methods to combine the results of different studies. In the biomedical sciences, the systematic evaluation of a problem using information (commonly in the form of statistical tables and other data) from a number of independent studies.

13455.title: metabolic activation
13455.definition: Formation of one or more chemically reactive intermediate(s) as a result of modification of a molecule by the xenobiotic-metabolizing enzymes of liver and other organs.

15876.title: metabolic enzymes
15876.definition: Proteins that catalyze chemical transformations of body constituents and, in more common usage, of xenobiotics.

MT06830.title: metabolic half-life
MT06830.definition: Time required for one-half of the quantity of a substance in the body to be metabolised.

15877.title: metabolic model
15877.definition: Analysis and theoretical reconstruction of the way in which the body deals with a specific substance, showing the proportion of the intake that is absorbed, the proportion that is stored and in what tissues, the rate of breakdown in the body and the subsequent fate of the metabolic products, and the rate at which it is eliminated by different organs as unchanged substance or metabolites.

09799.title: metabolic pathway
09799.definition: All metabolic products of the main compound (e.g. phase 1 and phase 2 metabolites) with the routes of metabolism and the excreted metabolites in body fluids, e.g. in urine or blood.

15878.title: metabolic transformation
15878.definition: Biotransformation of a substance that takes place within a living organism.

M03858.title: metabolism
M03858.definition: The entire physical and chemical processes involved in the maintenance and reproduction of life in which nutrients are broken down to generate energy and to give simpler molecules (catabolism) which by themselves may be used to form more complex molecules (anabolism). In case of heterotrophic organisms, the energy evolving from catabolic processes is made available for use by the organism.

09800.title: metabolism quenching
09800.definition: Physical or chemical methodology used for rapidly breaking all biochemical processes in metabolomic samples.

M03859.title: metabolite
M03859.definition: Any intermediate or product resulting from metabolism.

09801.title: metabolite fingerprinting and footprinting
09801.definition: Unique pattern characterizing the metabolism in a given living phase that does not attempt to identify or quantify all the metabolites.

09802.title: metabolite profiling
09802.definition: Strategy to identify and quantify a particular set of metabolites belonging to a specific metabolic pathway or class of compounds.

10949.title: metabologen
10949.definition: Morphogen, including bone morphogenetic protein, that affects metabolism and homeostasis.

09803.title: metabolome
09803.definition: Complete set (from \(\pu{50}\) to \(\pu{1000}\) metabolites) of organic or inorganic compounds of low relative molecular mass, present in the cell or organism and which participate in the metabolic reactions required for growth, maintenance, and normal functioning.

09804.title: metabolomics
09804.definition: Complex and comprehensive study of metabolome; identification and quantification of the small molecule metabolic products of a biological system (cell, tissue, organ, biological fluid, or organism) at a specific point in time.

09805.title: metabonomics
09805.definition: Measurement of the dynamic multiparametric metabolic response of a living system to pathophysiological stimuli or genetic modification.

12680.title: metabotropic receptor
12680.definition: Receptor that modulates electric potential-gated channels via G-proteins.

M03868.title: metal to ligand charge transfer transition
M03868.definition: An electronic transition of a metal complex that corresponds to excitation populating an electronic state in which considerable electron transfer from the metal to a ligand has occurred.

M03869.title: metal to metal charge transfer transition
M03869.definition: An electronic transition of a bi- or poly-nuclear metal complex that corresponds to excitation populating an electronic state in which considerable electron transfer between two metal centres has occurred.

12824.title: metal-organic framework
12824.definition: A metal-organic framework, abbreviated to MOF, is a coordination network with organic ligands containing potential voids.

M03860.title: metal–carbene complexes
M03860.definition: Metal complexes of the type $\ce{R2CML_{n}}$ ($\ce{M}$ = metal, $\ce{L}$ = ligand) in which formally a carbene is coordinated to a metal, e.g.

M03861.title: metal–carbyne complexes
M03861.definition: Metal complexes of the type $\ce{RCML_{n}}$ ($\ce{M}$ = metal, $\ce{L}$ = ligand) in which formally a carbyne is coordinated to a metal, e.g.

M03863.title: metal–insulator transition
M03863.definition: A transition characterized by a sudden change in electrical transport properties (conductivity) due to a reversible change from localized to itinerant behaviour of the electrons. Example: The transition at \(339\ \rm{K}\) in $\ce{VO2}$ where it changes from a high-temperature metallic behaviour to a low-temperature semiconductor behaviour. Synonymous with metal–nonmetal transition.

M03864.title: metallacycloalkanes
M03864.definition: Monocyclic compounds containing a metal atom and saturated carbon atoms as ring members, e.g.:

08881.title: metallo-supramolecular polymer
08881.definition: Dynamic polymeric entity whose macromolecules are composed of alternating simple or oligomeric molecules with two or more chelate end-groups (so-called unimers) and metal ions (so-called ion couplers) that are linked to chains by reversible coordination bonds (structure-based polymer class name):

09006.title: metallocene polymerization
09006.definition: Coordination polymerization making use of a metallocene catalyst.

M03865.title: metallocenes
M03865.definition: Organometallic coordination compounds in which one atom of a transition metal such as iron, ruthenium or osmium is bonded to and only to the face of two cyclopentadienyl $\ce{[\upeta\!^{5}\mbox{-}(C5H5)]}$ ligands which lie in parallel planes. The term should not be used for analogues having rings other than cyclopentadienyl as ligands.

MT06765.title: metalloenzyme
MT06765.definition: An enzyme that, in the active state, contains one or more metal ions which are essential for its biological function.

13838.title: metallomesogen
13838.definition: Mesogen composed of molecules incorporating one or more metal atoms.

10950.title: metallothionein
10950.definition: One of a family of low-molecular mass proteins that binds metals such as zinc, copper, cadmium and mercury.

14848.title: metallothionein-like proteins
14848.definition: Poorly characterized, cysteine-rich metal-binding proteins or proteins not conforming precisely to the classic properties of metallothioneins.

M03866.title: metallurgical coke
M03866.definition: Metallurgical coke is produced by carbonization of coals or coal blends at temperatures up to \(1400\ \rm{K}\) to produce a macroporous carbon material of high strength and relatively large lump size.

M03870.title: metamagnetic transition
M03870.definition: An antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic transition for \(H_{\rm{applied}}>H_{\rm{c}}\) and/or \(T>T_{\rm{t}}\) where \(H_{\rm{c}}\) and \(T_{\rm{t}}\) refer to the critical magnetic field and transition temperature, respectively.

14849.title: metameter
14849.definition: Measurement or a transformation of a measurement used in the analysis of biological tests, e.g., the probit metameter.

10951.title: metanephros
10951.definition: Primordium of the permanent kidney, developing later than, and caudal to, the mesonephros.

10952.title: metaphase
10952.definition: Stage of mitosis or meiosis in which the chromosomes become aligned on the equatorial plate of the cell, separating the centromeres.

10953.title: metaplasia
10953.definition: Abnormal transformation of an adult, fully differentiated tissue of one kind into a differentiated tissue of another kind.

14850.title: metapopulation
14850.definition: Set of local populations which interact via dispersing individuals among local populations; though not all local populations in a metapopulation need interact directly with every other local population.

M03871.title: metastability
M03871.definition: A term that describes the state of a phase in which an energy barrier considerably higher than \(k\ T\) must be surmounted before this phase can transform to a phase of lower molar Gibbs energy and molar Helmholtz energy, where \(k\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature.

09407.title: metastable background
09407.definition: Intensity in a mass spectrum arising from ions that spontaneously fragment between emission and detection.

M03874.title: metastable ion
M03874.definition: An ion which is formed with sufficient excitation to dissociate spontaneously during its flight from the ion source to the detector.

M03875.title: metastable state
M03875.definition: An isomeric state in an energy state higher than the ground state.

M03876.title: metastable state
M03876.definition: Any excited state which in principle, by virtue of the selection rules, cannot radiatively combine with any lower state. It usually has a considerably longer lifetime than an ordinary excited state.

15879.title: metastasis
15879.definition:
Movement of bacteria or body cells, especially cancer cells, from one part of the body to another, resulting in change in location of a disease or of its symptoms from one part of the body to another.
Growth of pathogenic microorganisms or of abnormal cells distant from the site of their origin in the body.

15339.title: metatectic reaction
15339.definition: Isothermal reversible reaction of a solid mixture phase \(\upbeta\) which is transformed into a different solid phase \(\upalpha\) plus a liquid phase \(\ce{l}\) during cooling of a system. For a binary system, \[\ce{\upbeta  \upalpha + 1}\] where the forward arrow indicates the direction of cooling. The equilibrium transformation occurs along the metatectic line characterized by the metatectic temperature. The metatectic composition and temperature, isobaric invariants of the system, define the metatectic point, which lies between the compositions of liquid \(\ce{l}\) and solid phase \(\upalpha\).

M03878.title: metathesis
M03878.definition: A bimolecular process formally involving the exchange of a bond (or bonds) between similar interacting chemical species so that the bonding affiliations in the products are identical (or closely similar) to those in the reactants. For example:  (The term has its origin in inorganic chemistry with a different meaning, but this older usage is not applicable in physical organic chemistry.)

08992.title: metathesis polymerization
08992.definition: Polymerization in which unsaturated monomers are transformed into unsaturated polymers by a process of bond redistribution.

M03879.title: methanogens
M03879.definition: Strictly anaerobic archaebacteria, able to use only a very limited substrate spectrum (e.g. molecular hydrogen, formate, methanol, methylamine, carbon monoxide or acetate) as electron donors for the reduction of carbon dioxide to methane.

15880.title: methemoglobin
15880.definition: Derivative of hemoglobin that is formed when the iron(II) in the heme porphyrin is oxidized to iron(III); this derivative cannot transport dioxygen.

15882.title: methemoglobin-forming substance
15882.definition: Substance capable of oxidizing directly or indirectly the iron(II) in hemoglobin to iron(III) to form methemoglobin.

15881.title: methemoglobinaemia
15881.definition: Presence of methaemoglobin in the blood in greater than normal proportion.

M03880.title: method of isotopic perturbation
M03880.definition: NMR shift difference measurement of the isotope effect on a fast (degenerate) equilibrium between two species which are equivalent except for isotopic substitution. This can be used to distinguish a rapidly equilibrating mixture with time-averaged symmetry from a single structure with higher symmetry.

14851.title: method of multiple working hypotheses
14851.definition: Method proposed to reduce precipitate explanation by considering all plausible hypotheses simultaneously in testing so that equal amounts of effort and attention are provided to each.

08090.title: method performance study
08090.definition: Intra- or interlaboratory study of one or more performance characteristics of a measurement procedure.

10954.title: methylation
10954.definition: Attachment of a methyl group to a molecule.

M03883.title: methylotrophic microorganisms
M03883.definition: Organisms that use, as substrates for growth, $\ce{C}$ compounds containing carbon in a lower oxidation state than in carbon dioxide.

M03884.title: metre
M03884.definition: The metre, symbol \(\pu{m}\), is the SI unit of length. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the speed of light in a vacuum \(c\) to be \(\pu{299792458}\) when expressed in the unit \(\pu{m s-1}\), where the second is defined in terms of the caesium frequency \(\Delta \nu_{\ce{Cs}}\).

08032.title: metrological compatibility of measurement results
08032.definition: Property of a set of measurement results for a specified measurand, such that the absolute value of the difference of any pair of measured quantity values from two different measurement results is smaller than some chosen multiple of the standard measurement uncertainty of that difference.

08033.title: metrological equivalence of measurement results
08033.definition: Property of two or more measurement results for a given measurand which have metrological compatibility of measurement results, so that they are each acceptable for the same specified intended use.

14320.title: micellar aggregation number
14320.definition: Number of molecules constituting a micelle.

M03885.title: micellar catalysis
M03885.definition: The acceleration of a chemical reaction in solution by the addition of a surfactant at a concentration higher than its critical micelle concentration so that the reaction can proceed in the environment of surfactant aggregates (micelles). (Rate enhancements may be due, for example, to higher concentration of the reactants in that environment, more favourable orientation and solvation of the species, or enhanced rate constants in the micellar pseudophase of the surfactant aggregate.) Micelle formation can also lead to a decreased reaction rate.

14321.title: micellar charge
14321.definition: Combined charge of the surfactant ions and counterions tightly bound to a micelle.

09895.title: micellar chromatography
09895.definition: Reversed-phase liquid chromatography which uses a mobile phase containing a surfactant above its critical micellar concentration (cmc).

09927.title: micellar electrokinetic chromatography
