09927.definition: Electrokinetic chromatography, in which the secondary phase is a micellar dispersed phase in the capillary.

M03886.title: micellar mass
M03886.definition: The term usually refers to a neutral micelle and therefore includes an equivalent amount of counter-ions with the surfactant ions.

14367.title: micellar nucleation
14367.definition: Formation of primary particles as a result of polymerization within monomer-swollen micelles initiated by the capture of primary radicals or oligomer-radicals.

14344.title: micellar polymerisation
14344.definition: Polymerization of a polymerizable surfactant in solution above its critical micelle concentration.

14322.title: micellar relative molar mass
14322.definition: Mass of a mole of micelles divided by the molar mass constant. The relative molar mass of micelles (mic) is thus \(M_{\rm{r,mic}} = M_{\rm{mic}}/M_{\rm{u}}\).

13839.title: micellar rod
13839.definition: Rod-like mesogens with the capacity to form micellar aggregates.

M03887.title: micellar solubilization
M03887.definition: In a system formed by a solvent, an association colloid and at least one other component (the solubilizate), the incorporation of this other component into or on the micelles is called micellar solubilization, or, briefly, solubilization.

M03889.title: micelle
M03889.definition: Surfactants in solution are often association colloids, that is, they tend to form aggregates of colloidal dimensions, which exist in equilibrium with the molecules or ions from which they are formed. Such aggregates are termed micelles.

M03890.title: micelle charge
M03890.definition: Usually understood to include the net charge of the surfactant ions and the counterions bound to the micelle.

14388.title: micellisation
14388.definition: Process in which surface-active molecules or ions aggregate into micelles.

M03891.title: Michaelis constant
M03891.definition: Substance concentration of substrate at which the rate of reaction is equal to one half of the limiting rate (maximum rate).

11546.title: Michaelis–Menten equation
11546.definition: The relationship between the initial rate (velocity) of an enzyme-catalysed reaction \(v_{0}\) and the initial substrate concentration \([\ce{S}]_{0}\) in the form \[v_{0} = V[\ce{S}]_{0}/(K_{\rm{M}} + [\ce{S}]_{0})\] where \(V\) (the limiting rate) and \(K_{\rm{M}}\) (the Michaelis constant) are independent of the initial substrate concentration and constant at a given temperature and a given enzyme concentration. The reaction is then said to display Michaelis–Menten kinetics.

M03892.title: Michaelis–Menten kinetics
M03892.definition:
The dependence of an initial rate of reaction upon the concentration of a substrate S that is present in large excess over the concentration of an enzyme or other catalyst (or reagent) E with the appearance of saturation behaviour following the Michaelis-Menten equation: \[
u= rac{V\ \left[m{S}ight]}{K_{m{m}}+\left[m{S}ight]}\] where \(
u\) is the observed initial rate, \(V\) is its limiting value at substrate saturation (i.e. \(\left[m{S}ight]\gg K_{m{m}}\)), and \(K_{m{m}}\) the substrate concentration when \(
u =  rac{V}{2}\). The definition is experimental, i.e. it applies to any reaction that follows an equation of this general form. The symbols \(V_{\max }\) or \(
u_{\max }\) are sometimes used for \(V\). The parameters \(V\) and \(K_{m{m}}\) (the 'Michaelis constant') of the equation can be evaluated from the slope and intercept of a linear plot of \(
u^{-1}\) vs. \(\left[m{S}ight]^{-1}\) (a 'Lineweaver–Burk plot') or from slope and intercept of a linear plot of \(
u\) vs. \( rac{
u}{\left[m{S}ight]}\) ('Eadie–Hofstee plot'). A Michaelis–Menten equation is also applicable to the condition where E is present in large excess, in which case the concentration \(\left[m{E}ight]\) appears in the equation instead of \(\left[m{S}ight]\). The term has sometimes been used to describe reactions that proceed according to the scheme: \[m{E}+m{S}\overset{k_{1}}{\underset{k_{-1}}ightleftarrows }m{ES}\overset{k_{m{cat}}}{ightarrow }m{Products}\] in which case \(K_{m{m}} =  rac{k_{-1}+k_{m{cat}}}{k_{1}}\) (Briggs–Haldane conditions). It has more usually been applied only to the special case in which \(k_{-1}\gg k_{m{cat}}\) and \(K_{m{m}} =  rac{k_{-1}}{k_{1}}=K_{s}\); in this case \(K_{m{m}}\) is a true dissociation constant (Michaelis–Menten conditions).

M03893.title: Michaelis–Menten mechanism
M03893.definition: The Michaelis–Menten mechanism is the simplest mechanism that will explain Michaelis–Menten kinetics. According to the mechanism, a substrate A first combines with a molecule of enzyme E, and this process is followed by a step in which the enzyme-substrate complex EA breaks down (sometimes with the participation of the solvent) into enzyme and reaction products: \[\rm{E}+\rm{A}\overset{k_{1}}{\underset{k_{-1}}\rightleftharpoons }\rm{EA}\overset{k_{2}}{\rightarrow }\rm{E}+\rm{Products}\] If, as is usual, the substrate A is present in great excess of the enzyme it can be shown that steady-state conditions apply, and that the rate equation is: \[v = \frac{k_{2}\ \left[\rm{E}\right]_{0}\ \left[\rm{A}\right]}{\frac{k_{-1}\,+\,k_{2}}{k_{1}}\,+\,\left[\rm{A}\right]}\] where \(\left[\rm{E}\right]_{0}\) is the total concentration of enzyme. This equation is of the form of the Michaelis–Menten equation. Other, more complicated, mechanisms lead to the Michaelis–Menten equation, adherence to which therefore does not require that the Michaelis– Menten mechanism applies.

12298.title: micro- technique
12298.definition: Prefix used to denote that the technique measures small quantities, either with respect to the amount of sample studied, or with respect to the change in the properties measured.

14317.title: micro-emulsion
14317.definition: Dispersion made of water, oil, and surfactant(s) that is an isotropic and thermodynamically stable system with dispersed domain diameter varying approximately from \(\pu{1 nm}\) to \(\pu{100 nm}\), usually \(\pu{10 nm}\) to \(\pu{50 nm}\).

14342.title: micro-emulsion polymerisation
14342.definition: Emulsion polymerization in which the starting system is a micro-emulsion and the final latex comprises colloidal particles of polymer dispersed in an aqueous medium.

13815.title: micro-encapsulation
13815.definition: Confinement of microscopic particles with a host.

M03904.title: micro-network
M03904.definition: Polymer network that has dimensions of the order of \(1\ \rm{nm}\) to \(1\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\).

14355.title: micro-suspension polymerisation
14355.definition: Suspension polymerization in which the diameter of the monomer droplets is of the order of a few \(\pu{\upmu m}\).

15883.title: microalbuminuria
15883.definition: Chronic presence of albumin in slight excess in urine.

09659.title: microarray
09659.definition: Two-dimensional arrangement of a device for analysis of sub-microlitre sample volume.

13456.title: microautophagy
13456.definition: Process in which lysosomes directly engulf cytoplasm by invagination, protrusion, and/or septation of the lysosomal limiting membrane.

M03895.title: microbial leaching
M03895.definition: A process for the solubilization of metals, mostly from poor ores, by lithotrophic bacteria.

M03896.title: microcanonical rate constant
M03896.definition: A rate constant calculated by microcanonical variational transition-state theory and therefore a rate constant that relates to a fixed energy.

M03897.title: microcanonical variational transition-state theory
M03897.definition: A development of transition-state theory in which the dividing surface is varied so as to minimize the rate calculated for a fixed energy. The rate expressions obtained in a microcanonical treatment can be integrated over the energy, taking into account the statistical distribution over energy states, so as to give the canonical, or thermal, rates.

M03898.title: microcarrier
M03898.definition: A small, beaded material, derived from silica, glass, dextran or similar materials, used for the immobilization of biocatalysts or as a support for the culture of anchorage-dependent animal cell lines.

10955.title: microcephaly
10955.definition: Congenital occurrence of an abnormally small head.

10956.title: microcheiria
10956.definition: Congenital occurrence of abnormally small hands.

M03899.title: microclimatology
M03899.definition: The science that deals with the climate of restricted areas and investigates their phenomena and causes.

09526.title: microcontact printing
09526.definition: Form of soft lithography that uses micron-scale and smaller relief patterns on a master elastomer stamp to form images on the surface of a substrate through conformal contact.

14852.title: microcosm
14852.definition: Artificial multi-species test system that simulates major characteristics of the natural environment for the purposes of ecotoxicological effects and risk assessment; such systems are normally terrestrial or aquatic and may contain plants, animals (vertebrates and invertebrates), and microorganisms.

10283.title: microdialysis
10283.definition: Dialysis by a short length of hollow-fibre membrane used for sampling.

09084.title: microelectrode
09084.definition: Electrode with smallest dimension of less than 1 millimetre and greater than 1 micrometre.

M03900.title: microelectrophoresis
M03900.definition: The electrophoresis technique involving the movement of a mass of particles on a small scale (e.g. paper electrophoresis).

09928.title: microemulsion electrokinetic chromatography
09928.definition: Electrokinetic chromatography, where a microemulsion is employed as the dispersed phase.

14853.title: microevolution
14853.definition: Evolutionary change below the species level; a small change in the genetic make-up of a population from generation to generation.

11552.title: microextraction (methology)
11552.definition: Extraction method characterized by a low phase ratio, so that at equilibrium the fraction extracted is low (i.e. the extraction is not exhaustive).

11554.title: microextraction (packed sorbent)
11554.definition: Solid-phase extraction using a syringe with a short sorbent bed located between the plunger and the needle.

11553.title: microextraction (technique)
11553.definition: Extraction technique in which the volume (mass) of the extraction phase (liquid or solid) is substantially smaller than the sample volume (mass).

09527.title: microfabrication
09527.definition: Process whereby structures of micrometre scale and smaller are fabricated.

MT06887.title: microfiltration
MT06887.definition: Pressure-driven membrane-based separation process in which particles and dissolved macromolecules larger than \(0.1\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) are rejected.

10309.title: microflow injection analysis extraction device
10309.definition: Miniaturized flow injection analysis device for extraction with conduits of a diameter greater than \(\pu{0.1 mm}\).

10310.title: microfluidic extraction device
10310.definition: Extraction device with channel widths from \(\pu{100 nm}\) to \(\pu{10 \upmu m}\) integrated into a flow platform.

09528.title: microfluidics
09528.definition: Multi-disciplinary subject concerned with the behavior, precise control, and manipulation of fluids that are geometrically constrained within a small, typically sub-millimeter, scale channel.

13457.title: microfold cell
13457.definition: Cell found in the follicle-associated epithelium of the Peyer’s patch that has the unique ability to sample antigen from the lumen of the small intestine and deliver it via transcytosis to antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and lymphocytes located in a unique pocket-like structure on their basolateral side.

M03901.title: microgel
M03901.definition: Particle of gel of any shape with an equivalent diameter of approximately \(0.1\) to \(100\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\).

11872.title: microglial cell
11872.definition: Small glial cell; resident macrophage derived as a mononuclear phagocyte that populates the brain in early development.

11873.title: microgliosis
11873.definition: Morphological response of microglia to injury, characterized by hypertrophy and amoeboid morphology.

13458.title: microglobulin
13458.definition: Any small globular protein found on the surface of many cells, including lymphocytes, and in the blood plasma distinct from albumin.

10957.title: microglossia
10957.definition: Congenital occurrence of an abnormally small tongue.

10958.title: micrognathia
10958.definition: Congenital occurrence of abnormally small jaws, especially effecting the mandible.

M03902.title: microheterogeneity
M03902.definition: A particular glycoprotein may occur in forms that differ in the structure of one or more or its carbohydrate units, a phenomenon known as microheterogeneity.

09514.title: microlithography
09514.definition: Lithography or pattern formation at a resolution of the order of microns.

10959.title: micromass culture
10959.definition: Laboratory technique in which dispersed cells from an embryonic organ or tissue, such as the brain, limb bud, or cartilage, are allowed to reaggregate in culture.

15884.title: micromercurialism
15884.definition: Early or subclinical effects of exposure to elemental mercury detected at the low exposure levels.

M03903.title: micrometeorology
M03903.definition: The study of the meteorological processes on scales from a millimeter or less up to tens or hundreds of metres; e.g. meteorology of a local site that is usually small and often is confined to a shallow layer of air next to the ground.

09529.title: micromolding
09529.definition: Form of soft lithography that uses the relief patterns in a master template to make 3-dimensional structures.

10960.title: micronucleus test
10960.definition:
Test for mutagenicity in which animals are treated with a test agent, after which time the frequency of micronucleated cells is determined.
Note: If a test group shows significantly increased levels of micronucleated cells compared to a control group, the chemical is considered capable of inducing chromosomal damage.
Procedure to detect clastogenic or aneugenic agents by microscopic examination of chromosomes.
Note: The test can be performed in vivo in rodents, or in cell culture (in vitro mammalian cell micronucleus test).

M03905.title: microphotometer
M03905.definition: The optical instrument used to measure transmittance in atomic emission spectroscopy.

10962.title: microphthalmia
10962.definition: Congenital occurrence of abnormally small eyeballs.

14161.title: microplate
14161.definition: Any of a number of plates containing a series of wells which may be used for storage or to perform individual assays.

14162.title: microplate standards
14162.definition: Defined footprint, height, flanges, and well positions for 96-, 384-, and 1536-well microplates.

M03907.title: micropore filling
M03907.definition: The process in which molecules are adsorbed in the adsorption space within micropores.

M03906.title: micropore
M03906.definition: Pore with width not exceeding about \(2.0\ \rm{nm}\) (\(20\ \mathrm{Å}\)).

M03908.title: micropore volume
M03908.definition: Conventionally measured by the volume of the adsorbed material which completely fills the micropores expressed in terms of bulk liquid at atmospheric pressure and at the temperature of measurement.

M03909.title: microporous carbon
M03909.definition: A porous carbon material, usually a char or carbon fibres, which may or may not have been subjected to an activation process to increase its adsorptive properties. A microporous carbon is considered to have a major part of its porosity in pores of less than \(2\ \rm{nm}\) width and to exhibit apparent surface areas usually higher than \(200\ \) to \(300\ \rm{m}^{2}\ \rm{g}^{-1}\).

14306.title: microporous particle
14306.definition: Particle containing pores of diameters not exceeding \(\pu{2 nm}\).

15885.title: microproteinaemia
15885.definition: Chronic presence of microprotein (alpha-1 and beta-2 microglobulin) in blood, indicating proximal renal tubule damage.

12682.title: microRNA
12682.definition: Small single-stranded RNA molecules that play a significant role in the post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression.

10963.title: microsatellite
10963.definition: Non-coding segment of DNA consisting of short nucleotide sequences (\(\pu{2\!{-}\! 6}\) base pairs), typically occurring in \(\pu{10\!{-}\! 100}\) consecutive (tandem) repeats.

M03911.title: microscopic cross-section
M03911.definition: A measure of the probability of a specified interaction or reaction between an incident radiation and a target particle or system of particles. It is the reaction rate per target particle for a specified process divided by the flux of the incident radiation. In general, a specification is added of the type of radiation (e.g. neutron, photon), the energy of the incident radiation (e.g. thermal, epithermal, fast) and the type of interaction of reaction (e.g. activation, fission, scattering).

M03912.title: microscopic diffusion control
M03912.definition: The observable consequence of the limitation that the rate of a bimolecular chemical reaction in a homogeneous medium cannot exceed the rate of encounter of the reacting molecular entities. If (hypothetically) a bimolecular reaction in a homogeneous medium occurred instantaneously when two reactant molecular entities made an encounter, the rate of reaction would be an encounter-controlled rate, determined solely by rates of diffusion of reactants. Such a hypothetical 'fully diffusion controlled rate' is also said to correspond to 'total microscopic diffusion control', and represents the asymptotic limit of the rate of reaction as the rate constant for the chemical conversion of the encounter pair into product (or products) becomes large relative to the rate constant for separation (or dissociation) of the encounter pair. 'Partial microscopic diffusion control' is said to operate in a homogeneous reaction when the rates of chemical conversion and of separation are comparable. (The degree of microscopic diffusion control cannot usually be determined with any precision.)

M03913.title: microscopic electrophoresis
M03913.definition: A technique in which the electrophoresis of individual particles is observed with the aid of a microscope or ultra-microscope.

M03914.title: microscopic film
M03914.definition: A film which has lateral dimensions in the range \(0.1{-}100\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\).

M03915.title: microscopic kinetics
M03915.definition: This term applies to a kinetic study in which the emphasis is on the interpretation of the behaviour in terms of elementary reactions.

13459.title: microscopic polyangiitis
13459.definition: ANCA-associated necrotizing, pauci-immune vasculitis of the small vessels (capillaries, venules, arterioles) frequently associated with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and/or hemorrhagic alveolitis as well as autoantibodies against myeloperoxidase.

M03916.title: microscopic reversibility at equilibrium
M03916.definition: The principle of microscopic reversibility at equilibrium states that, in a system at equilibrium, any molecular process and the reverse of that process occur, on the average, at the same rate. This definition corresponds to the statement of the principle that was given by R.C. Tolman in 1924. However, many workers have interchanged the meanings of microscopic reversibility and detailed balance, and it seems best now to regard the two, which are closely related, as synonymous.

M03917.title: microsome
M03917.definition: Artefactual spherical particle, not present in the living cell, derived from pieces of the endoplasmic reticulum present in homogenates of tissues or cells: microsomes sediment from such homogenates when centrifuged at \(10^{6}\ \rm{g}\) and higher: the microsomal fraction obtained in this way is often used as a source of mono-oxygenase enzymes.

10964.title: microstomia
10964.definition: Congenital occurrence of an abnormally small opening of the mouth.

13840.title: microstructure
13840.definition: Structure of material in which at least one of the features repeats over distances of the order of micrometers.

MT07637.title: microsyneresis
MT07637.definition: Syneresis in which the exudation of the liquid is from microscopic regions within a network.

14855.title: Microtox® test
14855.definition: Test involving luminescent marine bacteria of the Vibrio sp. [e.g., V. (Photobacterium) phosphoreum, V. fischeri, V. harveyi]. A decrease in bioluminescence is thought to reflect toxic action.

10235.title: microwave acid digestion
10235.definition: Type of bomb acid digestion with microwave radiation used for sample heating.

08507.title: microwave cavity
08507.definition: Resonant cavity that permits focusing a microwave field inside a discharge tube thus giving rise to a standing wave.

10225.title: microwave-assisted extraction
10225.definition: Leaching using microwave energy to heat the solvent in contact with the sample or the sample directly.

08508.title: microwave-induced plasma
08508.definition: Plasma generated in a microwave cavity.

M03918.title: middle atmosphere
M03918.definition: The combined stratosphere and mesosphere in the atmosphere.

10965.title: midgut
10965.definition: Middle section of the digestive tract in a vertebrate embryo, from which the ileum, jejunum, and portions of the duodenum and colon develop.

15886.title: midstream sampling
15886.definition: Taking an aliquot of a flowing liquid, such as urine, avoiding initial and terminal flow periods which are likely to be unrepresentative.

M03919.title: Mie scattering
M03919.definition: The scattering of electromagnetic radiation by spherical particles of any size \(r\), relative to the wavelength, \(\lambda \). Since the cases \(r\ll \lambda \) and \(r\gg \lambda \) are covered by Rayleigh (dipole) scattering and geometric scattering theories, respectively, Mie scattering often refers to the case of \(r\approx \lambda \).

11874.title: migraine
11874.definition: Recurrent syndrome usually characterized by unilateral head pain accompanied by symptoms including nausea and vomiting, vertigo, photophobia and other visual phenomena.

11875.title: migrainous infarction
11875.definition: Stroke that occurs in connection with a migraine attack.

M03920.title: migration
M03920.definition: The (usually intramolecular) transfer of an atom or group during the course of a molecular rearrangement.The movement of a bond to a new position, within the same molecular entity is known as 'bond migration'. Allylic rearrangements, e.g.  exemplify both types of migration.

M03921.title: migration current
M03921.definition: The difference between the current that is actually obtained, at any particular value of the potential of the indicator or working electrode, for the reduction or oxidation of an ionic electroactive substance and the current that would be obtained, at the same potential, if there were no transport of that substance due to the electric field between the electrodes. The sign convention regarding current is such that the migration current is negative for the reduction of a cation or for the oxidation of an anion, and positive for the oxidation of a cation or the reduction of an anion. Hence the migration current may tend to either increase or decrease the total current observed. In any event the migration current approaches zero as the transport number of the electroactive substance is decreased by increasing the concentration of the supporting electrolyte, and hence the conductivity

MT06924.title: migration time
MT06924.definition: The time required for the analyte to move through the effective length of the capillary, \(L_{\rm{eff}}\), that is, from the sample introduction point to the detection point.

MT06927.title: migration time of micelles
MT06927.definition: Experimentally determined as the migration time of a compound that is completely retained in the micellar phase.

M03923.title: migratory aptitude
M03923.definition: The term is applied to characterize the relative tendency of a group to participate in a rearrangement. In nucleophilic rearrangements ( migration to an electron-deficient centre), the migratory aptitude of a group is loosely related to its capacity to stabilize a partial positive charge, but exceptions are known, and the position of hydrogen in the series is often unpredictable.

M03924.title: migratory insertion
M03924.definition: A combination of migration and insertion. The term is mainly used in organometallic chemistry.

M03926.title: milligram equivalent of readability
M03926.definition: The product of readability and the value of the scale division (in \(\rm{mg}\) per division).

M03927.title: millimetre of mercury
M03927.definition: Non-SI unit for pressure; \(\rm{mmHg}\approx 133.322\ \rm{Pa}\). This old unit is not recognized by CIPM or ISO, but it is used for blood pressure.

M03928.title: milling
M03928.definition: The mechanical reduction of the particle size of a sample by attribution (friction), impact or cutting. The required particle size of a sample is related to the size of the test portion and the number of particles required to ensure homogeneity among test portions. The reduction in particle size may sometimes result in particles of different hardness and density, which produces inhomogeneity during the preparation of the test sample or during the withdrawal of the test portion.

10966.title: Minamata disease
10966.definition: Neurological disease caused by methylmercury, first seen in subjects ingesting contaminated fish from Minamata Bay in Japan.

14856.title: mineral
14856.definition: Naturally occurring substance, usually crystalline, which has a particular chemical composition and specific physical properties.

14316.title: mini-emulsion
14316.definition: Emulsion in which the particles of the dispersed phase have diameters in the range from approximately \(\pu{50 nm}\) to \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\).

14345.title: mini-emulsion polymerisation
14345.definition: Polymerization of a mini-emulsion of monomer in which all of the polymerization occurs within preexisting monomer particles without the formation of new particles.

14163.title: miniaturisation
14163.definition: Experimental design aimed at decreasing the reaction volume of an assay and consequently the amount and cost of reagents.

15887.title: minimal risk level
15887.definition: Estimate of the daily human exposure to a hazardous substance that is likely to be without appreciable risk of adverse noncancer health effects over a specified duration of exposure: This substance-specific estimate is used by ATSDR health assessors to identify contaminants and potential health effects that may be of concern at hazardous waste sites.

14858.title: minimal time to effect or response
14858.definition: Minimum time required to get an effect or response. Regardless of the toxicant concentration, the effect, or response, cannot occur any faster than this minimum time.

M03929.title: minimum consumption time
M03929.definition: The time during which nebulization must be carried out in order to perform one analysis with a given precision. The minimum consumption time is equal to the minimum volume consumed of the prepared sample divided by the rate of fluid consumption in order to obtain a given precision. It can be reduced by means of integrating the signal or measuring the signal increments (kinetic methods).

M03930.title: minimum density of states criterion
M03930.definition: This is a criterion used in Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel–Marcus (RRKM) theory for locating the transition state. The reaction coordinate \(r\) at the transition state, according to this criterion, is given by \(\frac{\partial (N\left(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\right))}{\partial r}=0\), where \(N\left(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\right)\) is the density of states at an internal energy \(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\).

15210.title: minimum effective plasma concentration
15210.definition: Concentration of a drug that must be achieved in the plasma before any desired therapeutic or pharmacological effect can be obtained.

15211.title: minimum inhibitory concentration
15211.definition: Lowest concentration of an antibacterial drug necessary to inhibit the growth of a microorganism.

M03932.title: minimum lethal concentration
M03932.definition: Lowest concentration of a toxic substance in an environmental medium that kills individual organisms or test species under a defined set of conditions. Synonymous with lowest lethal concentration found.

M03933.title: minimum lethal dose
M03933.definition: Lowest amount of a substance that, when introduced into the body, may cause death to individual species of test animals under a defined set of conditions.

08034.title: minimum sample size
08034.definition: Lower limit of sample size stipulated in documentation taken for chemical analysis.

14857.title: minimum significant difference
14857.definition: Difference between groups (in tests with, e.g., salmonid fish, the difference in average weights or average mortality) that would have to occur before it could be concluded that there was a significant difference between the groups.

08186.title: minimum structural change, principle of
08186.definition: Principle that a chemical reaction is expected to occur with a minimum of bond changes or with a minimum redistribution of electrons (although more complex reaction cascades are also possible).

14859.title: minimum viable population
14859.definition: Smallest population size of a species allowing survival in the wild.

M03931.title: minimum-energy reaction path
M03931.definition: Path orthogonal to the equipotential contours of a potential energy surface that connects the energy minima through a saddle point (transition state) from which it slopes downwards along the steepest descending lines in \(3N-6\) configurational space (\(N\) is the number of nuclei in the reacting system).

10967.title: minisatellite
10967.definition: Non-coding segment of DNA, found throughout the genome, usually near the ends of chromosomes, that consists of tandem repeats of sequences of about \(\pu{10\!{-}\! 100}\) base pairs.

11876.title: Minnesota multiphasic personality inventory
11876.definition: Questionnaire type of psychological test for ages 18 and older. The RF version has 338 true–false statements with seven validity and ten personality scales that may be used in either an individual or group format.

13460.title: minor histocompatibility antigen
13460.definition: Non-major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-encoded cell surface processed peptide which, in association with MHC-encoded molecules, contributes to graft rejection, albeit not usually as severe as that due to MHC mismatch.

11877.title: miosis
11877.definition: Abnormal contraction of the pupil of the eye to less than \(\pu{2 mm}\).

MT07230.title: miscibility
MT07230.definition: Capability of a mixture to form a single phase over certain ranges of temperature, pressure, and composition.

MT07270.title: miscibility gap
MT07270.definition: Area within the coexistence curve of an isobaric phase diagram (temperature vs composition) or an isothermal phase diagram (pressure vs composition).

15888.title: miscible
15888.definition: Liquid substances capable of mixing without separation into two phases; refers to liquid mixtures.

10135.title: misclassification rate
10135.definition: Fraction of objects incorrectly assigned to a group in supervised classification.

11878.title: misfolded protein
11878.definition: Protein that has the same amino acid sequence as the normal, functional protein but exhibits a deviant tertiary structure and lacks normal function.

M03936.title: mist
M03936.definition: A qualitative term applied to a suspension of droplets in a gas. In the atmosphere a mist produces a generally thin, greyish veil over the landscape. It reduces visibility to a lesser extent than fog but somewhat more than haze (visibility of less than \(2\ \rm{km}\) but greater than \(1\ \rm{km}\)).

M03937.title: mitochondria
M03937.definition: Organelles appearing in all eukaryotic cells which produce ATP as useful energy for the cell by oxidative phosphorylation. The proteins for the adenosine 5'-triphosphate (ATP)-generating electron transport of the respiration chain are located in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Mitochondria contain many enzymes of the citric acid cycle and for fatty acid $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}oxidation}$. Many of them are coded for by nuclear DNA.

11879.title: mitochondrial membrane potential
11879.definition: Membrane potential across the inner membrane of the mitochondrion generated by the electron transport chain.

15890.title: mitochondrion
15890.definition: Eukaryote cytoplasmic organelle that is bounded by an outer membrane and an inner membrane; the inner membrane has folds called cristae that are the center of ATP synthesis in oxidative phosphorylation in the animal cell and supplement ATP synthesis by the chloroplasts in photosynthetic cells.

13461.title: mitogen
13461.definition: Substance that induces lymphocyte transformation or, more generally, mitosis and cell proliferation.

13462.title: mitogen-activated protein kinase
13462.definition: Member of a kinase network in which 'upstream' kinases activate 'downstream' kinases that, in response to phosphorylation, translocate to the nucleus and activate transcription factors.

13463.title: mitophagy
13463.definition: Autophagy-related pathway specific for mitochondria; it can be subdivided into macromitophagy and micromitophagy depending upon the degree of mitophagy.

M03938.title: mitosis
M03938.definition: The process whereby a cell nucleus divides into two daughter nuclei, each having the same genetic complement as the parent cell.

MT07533.title: mixed ceramic
MT07533.definition: Ceramic material consisting of co-continuous interpenetrating networks of two or more metal carbides, nitrides or oxides.

13465.title: mixed connective tissue disease
13465.definition: Human autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body, producing symptoms that combine features of polymyositis, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and systemic scleroderma, and thus being considered as an overlap syndrome.

M03940.title: mixed crystal
M03940.definition: A crystal containing a second constituent which fits into and is distributed in the lattice of the host crystal. (The use of 'solid solution' for amorphous materials is not recommended.)

M03941.title: mixed energy release
M03941.definition: This is an effect found in a process A + BC when the attacking species A is heavy. Because A is heavy the A–B distance continues to decrease while the repulsive energy of B–C is being released.

M03942.title: mixed indicator
M03942.definition: An indicator containing a supplementary dye selected to heighten the overall colour change.

M03943.title: mixed labelled
M03943.definition: A specifically labelled compound is referred to as mixed labelled when the isotopically substituted compound has more than one kind of modified atom e.g. $\ce{CH3–CH2–[^{18}O][^{2}H]}$.

13464.title: mixed lymphocyte response
13464.definition: T-cell-proliferative response induced by cells expressing allogeneic major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules.

11880.title: mixed neuropathy
11880.definition: Dysfunction or degeneration of both motor and sensory nerves.

M03944.title: mixed potential

10247.title: mixed-mode sorbent
10247.definition: Porous sorbent material with surface co-bonded ion exchange and alkyl functional groups.

M03946.title: mixing control
M03946.definition: The experimental limitation of the rate of reaction in solution by the rate of mixing of solutions of the two reactants. It can occur even when the reaction rate constant is several powers of 10 less than that for an encounter-controlled rate. Analogous (and even more important) effects of the limitation of reaction rates by the speed of mixing are encountered in heterogeneous (solid/liquid, solid/gas, liquid/gas) systems.

M03947.title: mixing height
M03947.definition: The height to which significant mixing of added pollutants occurs within the atmosphere. In reference to stack gases, it is considered the height at which stack effluent begins mixing with the atmosphere as it leaves the stack.

M03945.title: mixing
M03945.definition: The combining of components, particles or layers into a more homogeneous state. The mixing may be achieved manually or mechanically by shifting the material with stirrers or pumps or by revolving or shaking the container. The process must not permit segregation of particles of different size or properties. homogeneity may be considered to have been achieved in a practical sense when the sampling error of the processed portion is negligible compared to the total error of the measurement system.

M03948.title: mixing ratio
M03948.definition: In meteorology, the dimensionless ratio of the mass of a substance (such as water vapour) in an air parcel to the mass of the remaining substances in the air parcel. For trace substances, this is approximated by the ratio of the mass of the substance to the mass of air. However, in the case of water vapour the mass of dry air is used. In atmospheric chemistry, mixing ratios (molecular, molar, by volume, as well as by weight) are used to describe relative concentrations of atmospheric trace gases and impurities.

14860.title: mixing zone
14860.definition: Area where an effluent discharge undergoes initial dilution and is extended to cover the secondary mixing in the ambient water body.

M03949.title: mixture
M03949.definition: Portion of matter consisting of two or more chemical substances called constituents.

16270.title: mixture
16270.definition: Gaseous, liquid, or solid phase containing more than one substance, when all the substances are treated in the same way.

M03950.title: MLCT
M03950.definition: Abbreviation for Metal to Ligand Charge Transfer.

M03951.title: mobile adsorption
M03951.definition: A situation in which molecules of adsorbate are free to move about the surface. Mobility of the adsorbate will increase with temperature and mobile adsorption may be either localized or non-localized. In localized mobile adsorption the adsorbate spends most of the time on the adsorption sites but can migrate or be desorbed and readsorbed elsewhere. In non-localized adsorption the mobility is so great that a small fraction of the adsorbed species is on the desorption sites and a large fraction at other positions on the surface.

M03952.title: mobile phase
M03952.definition: A fluid which percolates through or along the stationary bed, in a definite direction. It may be a liquid (liquid chromatography) or a gas (gas chromatography) or a supercritical fluid (supercritical-fluid chromatography). In gas chromatography the expression carrier gas may be used for the mobile phase. In elution chromatography the expression 'eluent' is also used for the mobile phase.

10036.title: mobile-phase speed
10036.definition: Linear velocity of the mobile phase across the average cross-section of the column.

M03954.title: mobile-phase velocity
M03954.definition: The linear velocity of the mobile phase across the average cross-section of the chromatographic bed or column.

09945.title: mobile-phase volume
09945.definition: Volume of the liquid mobile phase contained in the column in counter-current chromatography \[V_{\rm{M}} = V_{\rm{C}} - V_{\rm{S}}\] where \(V_{\rm{C}}\) is the total volume of the column and \(V_{\rm{S}}\) is the volume of the liquid stationary phase in the column.

MT06760.title: mobility
MT06760.definition: Mass transport is described by a mobility \(b\), defined by: \[b_{i} = \frac{\nu _{i}}{\boldsymbol{F}_{i}}\] where \(\nu _{i}\) is the average drift velocity and \(\boldsymbol{F}_{i}\) is the force on particle \(i\).

M03956.title: mobility
M03956.definition: The velocity of a particle per unit applied force.

M03955.title: mobility
M03955.definition: Drift velocity of electrons or holes divided by the electric field strength.

M03957.title: Möbius aromaticity
M03957.definition: A monocyclic array of orbitals in which there is a single out-of-phase overlap (or, more generally, an odd number of out-of-phase overlaps) reveals the opposite pattern of aromatic character to Hückel systems; with \(4\, n\) electrons it is stabilized (aromatic), whereas with \(4\, n+2\) it is destabilized (antiaromatic). In the excited state \(4\, n+2\) Möbius $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$ systems are stabilized, and \(4\, n\) systems are destabilized. No examples of ground-state Möbius $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$ systems are known, but the concept has been applied to transition states of pericyclic reactions. The name is derived from the topological analogy of such an arrangement of orbitals to a Möbius strip.

M03958.title: mode
M03958.definition: The value of the variable occurring with the greatest frequency in the series of observations. A bimodal distribution is one which contains two maxima. The use of mode when reporting results of chemical analysis is generally not recommended.

M03959.title: mode-locked laser
M03959.definition: A laser in which many resonant modes are coupled in phase, to yield a train of very short pulses (e.g. ps pulses). The coupling of the modes is obtained by modulation of the gain in the resonator, and can be active (electro-optic modulation of the losses or of the pump intensity), or passive (with a saturable absorber).

10077.title: model
10077.definition: Equation describing the response as a function of values of the factors.

14861.title: model error
14861.definition: Elements of uncertainty associated with the discrepancy between the model and the real world.

MT07568.title: model network
MT07568.definition: Polymer network synthesized using a reactant or reactants of known molar mass or masses and chemical structure.

M03960.title: moderation
M03960.definition: Reduction of the neutron energy by scattering without appreciable capture.

M03961.title: moderator
M03961.definition: A material used to reduce the neutron energy by scattering without appreciable capture.

M03962.title: modified active solid
M03962.definition: An active solid the sorptive properties of which have been changed by some treatment.

M03963.title: modified Arrhenius equation
M03963.definition: This is an extension of the simple Arrhenius equation in which the pre-exponential factor is proportional to \(T^{n}\) where \(T\) is the temperature and \(n\) a constant: \[k = B\ T^{n}\ \exp(-E_{\rm{a}}/RT)\] \(B\) is a temperature-independent constant.

09343.title: modified Auger parameter
09343.definition: Sum of the Fermi level referenced (see Fermi level referencing) kinetic energy of a narrow Auger electron peak in the spectrum and the binding energy of the most intense photoelectron peak from the same element.

15212.title: modified release
15212.definition: Release of a drug from a dosage form that it is not immediate (e.g., sustained release, retarded release, delayed-action preparations, controlled release, extended release, etc.).

M03964.title: modified sample
M03964.definition: A sample or a known fraction of the parent population in which the analyte has been isolated or (usually) concentrated before being submitted to the laboratory. If the isolation or concentration occurs in the laboratory, the procedure is usually considered part of the preparation of the test sample from the laboratory sample (in-laboratory processing).

M03965.title: modifier
M03965.definition: A substance added to a solvent to improve its properties e.g. by increasing the solubility of an extractant, changing interfacial parameters or reducing adsorption losses. Additives used to enhance extraction rates should be called accelerators or catalysts.

12789.title: modulated heat flow
12789.definition: Heat flow in a modulated-temperature DSC experiment.

12299.title: modulated technique
12299.definition: Indicates that a parameter changes in a periodic manner during the experiment.

12300.title: modulated temperature technique
12300.definition: Applied to the technique name to indicate that a temperature modulation has been applied to the temperature program.

12790.title: modulated-temperature DSC
12790.definition: DSC experiment in which a small sinusoidal modulation overlays the change in temperature with time.

09955.title: modulation frequency
09955.definition: Number of modulations in a given time interval.

09956.title: modulation number
09956.definition: Number of modulations for a given first-dimension peak.

09957.title: modulation period
09957.definition: Duration of a complete cycle of modulation in a system for comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography.

09958.title: modulator
09958.definition: Interface device between the two columns in a system for comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography that accumulates or samples narrow bands from the effluent of the first column for fast re-injection into the second column.

14164.title: module
14164.definition: Individual automated device within a fully automated assay system that usually performs a complete single assay step or procedure.

M03966.title: modulus of elasticity
M03966.definition: The normal stress divided by linear strain.

M03967.title: Mohr amplification process
M03967.definition: The process in which iodide is oxidized to iodate to achieve a more favourable measurement.

M03968.title: moiety
M03968.definition: In physical organic chemistry moiety is generally used to signify part of a molecule, e.g. in an ester $\ce{R1COOR2}$ the alcohol moiety is $\ce{R2O}$. The term should not be used for a small fragment of a molecule.

15213.title: moistening agents
15213.definition: Usually water or low-molecular-weight alcohols or compounds, used in topical applications and in wet granulation, for the production of tablets.

MT06966.title: MOL file format
MT06966.definition: The MOL file format is used to encode chemical structures, substructures and conformations as text-based connection tables. It is used by MDL Information Systems Inc. (e.g., in their MACCS or ISIS programs).

M03970.title: molality
M03970.definition: Amount of entities of a solute divided by the mass of the solvent.

M03971.title: molar
M03971.definition: Adjective before the name of an extensive quantity generally meaning division by amount of substance to make it intensive. Molar volume is volume divided by amount of substance. In a few special cases molar is used to denote division by amount concentration (e.g. molar absorption coefficient).

M03972.title: molar absorption coefficient
M03972.definition: Absorbance divided by the absorption pathlength, \(l\), and the amount concentration, \(c\): \[\varepsilon(\lambda) = \frac{1}{c\, l}\, \rm{lg}\! \left ( \frac{P_{\lambda}^{0}}{P_{\lambda}}\right ) = \frac{A(\lambda)}{c\, l}\] where \(P_{\lambda}^{0}\) and \(P_{\lambda}\) are, respectively, the incident and transmitted spectral radiant power.

16253.title: molar activity (material)
16253.definition: Activity of a specified radionuclide (\(\ce{R}\)) in a material (\(\ce{M}\)) divided by amount of substance of that material.

M03974.title: molar activity
M03974.definition: For a specified isotope, the activity of the compound divided by the amount of the material in moles: \(A_{\rm{m}}=\frac{A}{n}\).

08269.title: molar decadic absorption coefficient
08269.definition: Decadic absorbance (\(A_{10}\)) divided by path-length (\(l\)) and amount concentration (\(c\)). \(\varepsilon = A_{10}/(cl)\).

08638.title: molar ellipticity
08638.definition: Ellipticity divided by the amount concentration of the optically active absorbing material and by the path-length at temperature (\(t\)) and wavelength (\(\lambda\)).

12214.title: molar mass
12214.definition: Mass divided by amount of substance.

08270.title: molar Napierian absorption coefficient
08270.definition: Napierian absorbance (\(A_{\rm{e}}\)) divided by path-length (\(l\)) and amount concentration (\(c\)). \(\kappa = A_{\rm{e}}/(cl)\).

M03979.title: molar refraction
M03979.definition: Function of the refractive index, \(n\), given by \(R = V_{\rm{m}}\ \frac{n^{2}\,-\,1}{n^{2}\,+\,2}\), where \(V_{\rm{m}}\) is the molar volume.

12215.title: molar-mass average
12215.definition: Any average of the molar mass, molecular weight, relative molar mass, or relative molecular mass for a non-uniform polymer, with the symbol \(\rm{k}\) specifying the type of average.

12224.title: molar-mass dispersity
12224.definition: Ratio of the mass-average molar mass, \(M_{\rm{m}}\), molecular weight, relative molar mass, or relative molecular mass, \(M_{\rm{r,m}}\), to the number-average molar mass, \(M_{\rm{n}}\), molecular weight, relative molar mass, or relative molecular mass, \(M_{\rm{r,n}}\). \[Ð\!_{\rm{M}} = M_{\rm{m}}/M_{\rm{n}} = M_{\rm{r,m}}/M_{\rm{r,n}}\]

M03978.title: molar-mass exclusion limit
M03978.definition: The maximum value of the molar mass or molecular weight of molecules or particles, in a specific polymer solvent system, that can enter into the pores of the porous non-adsorbing material used in size-exclusion chromatography. For particles with molar mass or molecular weight larger than the exclusion limit the separation effect of the size-exclusion chromatography vanishes.

M03977.title: molarity
M03977.definition: Term sometimes used for amount concentration.

M03980.title: mole
M03980.definition:
The mole, symbol mol, is the SI unit of amount of substance. One mole contains exactly \(\pu{6.02214076E23}\) elementary entities. This number is the fixed numerical value of the Avogadro constant, \(N_{\rm{A}}\), when expressed in the unit \(\pu{mol-1}\) and is called the Avogadro number.
The amount of substance, symbol \(n\), of a system is a measure of the number of specified elementary entities. An elementary entity may be an atom, a molecule, an ion, an electron, any other particle or specified group of particles.

15340.title: mole percent
15340.definition: Deprecated term that includes both a quantity and a unit. Replace by mole fraction expressed as percent.

15341.title: mole ratio
15341.definition: Amount of one constituent divided by the amount of a second constituent in the same system. For constituents 1 and 2, \[r_{12} = n_{1}/n_{2}\]

M03982.title: molecular beams
M03982.definition: A molecular beam is produced by allowing a gas at higher pressure to expand through a small orifice into a container at lower pressure. The result is a beam of particles (atoms, free radicals, molecules or ions) moving at approximately equal velocities, with few collisions occurring between them. In a crossed molecular-beam experiment a reaction is studied using collimated beams of reactant molecules. For a bimolecular reaction, beams of the two reactants are caused to impinge on one another, often at an angle of 90°. In a beam-gas scattering experiment a collimated beam is introduced into a gas, and the scattering patterns are observed.

M03984.title: molecular conformation
M03984.definition: The conformation of the macromolecule as a whole. In the polymer literature, molecular conformation is sometimes referred to as macroconformation. In molecular conformations involving parallel stems, the latter may be confined to the same crystal or may also extend over several crystals.

MT06967.title: molecular connectivity index
MT06967.definition: A molecular connectivity index is a numeric descriptor derived from molecular topology.

12683.title: molecular descriptor
12683.definition: Parameter that characterizes a specific structural or physicochemical aspect of a molecule.

MT06968.title: molecular design
MT06968.definition: Molecular design is the application of all techniques leading to the discovery of new chemical entities with specific properties required for the intended application.

11473.title: molecular diversity
11473.definition: A measure of the spread of various properties or chemotypes within a set of compounds.

MT06969.title: molecular dynamics
MT06969.definition: Molecular dynamics is a simulation procedure consisting of the computation of the motion of atoms in a molecule or of individual atoms or molecules in solids, liquids and gases, according to Newton's laws of motion. The forces acting on the atoms, required to simulate their motions, are generally calculated using molecular mechanics force fields.

13816.title: molecular encapsulation
13816.definition: Confinement of an individual molecule within a larger molecule.

M03986.title: molecular entity
M03986.definition: Any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, ion pair, radical, radical ion, complex, conformer etc., identifiable as a separately distinguishable entity. Molecular entity is used in this Compendium as a general term for singular entities, irrespective of their nature, while chemical species stands for sets or ensembles of molecular entities. Note that the name of a compound may refer to the respective molecular entity or to the chemical species, e.g. methane, may mean a single molecule of $\ce{CH4}$ (molecular entity) or a molar amount, specified or not (chemical species), participating in a reaction. The degree of precision necessary to describe a molecular entity depends on the context. For example 'hydrogen molecule' is an adequate definition of a certain molecular entity for some purposes, whereas for others it is necessary to distinguish the electronic state and/or vibrational state and/or nuclear spin, etc. of the hydrogen molecule.

10969.title: molecular epidemiology
10969.definition: Use in epidemiological studies of techniques of molecular biology, such as DNA profiling and genetic analysis, with the aim of detecting genetic patterns characteristic of susceptible populations or of groups at risk of disease.

11474.title: molecular fingerprints
11474.definition: Descriptions of the structure of a molecule calculated from the properties of each of its atoms and bonds that are then usually condensed into a fixed-length string by a hashing algorithm.

M03987.title: molecular formula
M03987.definition: For compounds consisting of discrete molecules, a formula according with the relative molecular mass (or the structure).

09408.title: molecular fragment
09408.definition: Ion or neutral particle that was part of a larger molecular structure and contains information about that structure.

09530.title: molecular glass
09530.definition: Assembly of small molecules that vitrify, rather than crystallize, when cooled.

MT07069.title: molecular graph
MT07069.definition: The graph with differently labelled (coloured) vertices (chromatic graph) which represent different kinds of atoms and differently labelled (coloured) edges related to different types of bonds. Within the topological electron distribution theory, a complete network of the bond paths for a given nuclear configuration.

MT07070.title: molecular graph theory
MT07070.definition: The theory which deals with analyses of all consequences of connectivities inherent in molecular structure and chemical transformations. The theory does not produce numerical data but uses available data and searches for regularities that can be attributed to combinatorial and topological origins.

MT06970.title: molecular graphics
MT06970.definition: Molecular graphics is a technique for the visualization and manipulation of molecules on a graphical display device.

09409.title: molecular image
09409.definition: Image of a surface formed from ions characteristic of a particular molecule.

14165.title: molecular imprinted polymers
14165.definition: Synthetic polymers in which well-defined volume cavities (imprints) created by template molecules mimic a biomolecular specific ligand–receptor interaction.

13841.title: molecular imprinting
13841.definition: Technique to create templated cavities in polymer matrices with memory of the template molecules to be used in molecular recognition.

M03988.title: molecular ion
M03988.definition: An ion formed by the removal from (positive ions) or addition to (negative ions) a molecule of one or more electrons without fragmentation of the molecular structure. The mass of this ion corresponds to the sum of the masses of the most abundant naturally occurring isotopes of the various atoms that make up the molecule (with a correction for the masses of the electron(s) lost or gained). For example, the mass of the molecular ion of ethyl bromide $\ce{C2H5^{79}Br}$ will be \(2\times 12\) plus \(5\times 1.0078246\) plus 78.91839 minus the mass of the electron (\(m_{\rm{e}}\)). This is equal to \(107.95751\ \rm{u}-m_{\rm{e}}\), \(u\) being the unified atomic mass unit based on the standard that the mass of the isotope $\ce{^{12}C}$ = \(12\ \rm{u}\) exactly.

M03990.title: molecular kinetics
M03990.definition: This term is applied to a kinetic study in which there is emphasis on the behaviour of the system at the molecular level.

M03991.title: molecular laser
M03991.definition: A gas laser which makes use of electronic, vibrational or rotational energy levels in molecules. The molecules can be excited by an electric discharge, as in the case of the $\ce{N2}$ or $\ce{CO2}$ laser, by chemical reactions, as in the $\ce{HF}$ or $\ce{DF}$ lasers, or by another laser, as in the $\ce{CH3F}$ far IR laser.

09531.title: molecular logic gate
09531.definition: Molecule that acts as a device performing a logical operation based on one or more physical or chemical inputs and a single output.

M03993.title: molecular mechanics calculation
M03993.definition: An empirical calculational method intended to give estimates of structures and energies for conformations of molecules. The method is based on the assumption of 'natural' bond lengths and angles, deviation from which leads to strain, and the existence of torsional interactions and attractive and/or repulsive van der Waals and dipolar forces between non-bonded atoms. The method is also called '(empirical) force-field calculations'.

M03994.title: molecular metal
M03994.definition: A non-metallic material whose properties resemble those of metals, usually following oxidative doping; e.g. polyacetylene following oxidative doping with iodine.

13466.title: molecular mimicry
13466.definition: Concept that identity or similarity of epitopes expressed by a pathogen and by a self molecule may lead to production of antibodies reacting to the self-antigen.

MT06971.title: molecular modeling
MT06971.definition: Molecular modeling is the investigation of molecular structures and properties using computational chemistry and graphical visualization techniques in order to provide a plausible three-dimensional representation under a given set of circumstances.

M03995.title: molecular nucleation
M03995.definition: The initial crystallization of a small portion of a macromolecule, after which further crystallization is thermodynamically favoured. Molecular nucleation may give rise to a new crystal or increase the size of a pre-existing one.

M03996.title: molecular orbital
M03996.definition: A one-electron wavefunction describing an electron moving in the effective field provided by the nuclei and all other electrons of a molecular entity of more than one atom. Such molecular orbitals can be transformed in prescribed ways into component functions to give 'localized molecular orbitals'. Molecular orbitals can also be described, in terms of the number of nuclei (or 'centres') encompassed, as two-centre, multi-centre, etc. molecular orbitals, and are often expressed as a linear combination of atomic orbitals. An orbital is usually depicted by sketching contours on which the wavefunction has a constant value (contour map) or by indicating schematically the envelope of the region of space in which there is an arbitrarily fixed high (say 96%) probability of finding the electron occupying the orbital, giving also the algebraic sign (+ or −) of the wavefunction in each part of that region.

08841.title: molecular orbital theory
08841.definition: Theory of quantum mechanics in which electrons in a molecule (lattice) are not assigned to particular bonds between atoms but move under the influence of all atoms.

MT07422.title: molecular orientation
MT07422.definition: Absorption probability (referred to electric dipolar absorption) for a molecular transition with its electric transition moment at an angle \(\theta\) with the electric vector of the light is proportional to \(\cos^{2}\theta\). For the whole sample it is proportional to the orientation factor \(K_{\theta} = \:< \cos^{2}\theta >\), averaged over all sample molecules. This average is \(1\) for a sample with all transition moments perfectly aligned along the electric vector of the light, \(1/3\) for an isotropic sample and \(0\) for a sample where all transition moments are perpendicular to the electric vector.

M03997.title: molecular rearrangement
M03997.definition: The term is traditionally applied to any reaction that involves a change of connectivity (sometimes including hydrogen), and violates the so-called 'principle of minimum structural change'. According to this oversimplified principle, chemical species do not isomerize in the course of a transformation, e.g. substitution, or the change of a functional group of a chemical species into a different functional group is not expected to involve the making or breaking of more than the minimum number of bonds required to effect that transformation. For example, any new substituents are expected to enter the precise positions previously occupied by displaced groups. The simplest type of rearrangement is an intramolecular reaction in which the product is isomeric with the reactant (one type of 'intramolecular isomerization'). An example is the first step of the Claisen rearrangement:  The definition of molecular rearrangement includes changes in which there is a migration of an atom or bond (unexpected on the basis of the principle of minimum structural change), as in the reaction:  where the rearrangement stage can formally be represented as the '1,2-shift' of hydride between adjacent carbon atoms in the carbocation:  Such migrations occur also in radicals, e.g.:  The definition also includes reactions in which an entering group takes up a different position from the leaving group, with accompanying migration. An example of the latter type is the 'allylic rearrangement':  A distinction is made between 'intramolecular rearrangements' (or 'true molecular rearrangements') and 'intermolecular rearrangements' (or 'apparent rearrangements'). In the former case the atoms and groups that are common to a reactant and a product never separate into independent fragments during the rearrangement stage (i.e. the change is intramolecular), whereas in an 'intermolecular rearrangement' a migrating group is completely free from the parent molecule and is re-attached to a different position in a subsequent step, as in the Orton reaction:

08187.title: molecular recognition
08187.definition: Attraction between specific molecules through noncovalent interactions that often exhibit electrostatic and stereochemical complementarity between the partners.

MT07071.title: molecular Rydberg state
MT07071.definition: An excited electronic state which is composed primarily of atomic orbitals with principal quantum numbers greater than that of the ground state and the valence excited states. Such electronic states typically have a large polarizability.

MT06972.title: molecular shape
MT06972.definition: The molecular shape is an attribute of a molecule dealing with spatial extension, form, framework, or geometry. It is often described by, e.g., principal axes, ovality, or connectivity indices.

09851.title: molecular shape of lipids
09851.definition: Specific structure of lipid molecules (glycerophospholipids) in aqueous environments and membranes as a function of the ratio between the cross-sections of their polar heads and hydrophobic tails.

13971.title: molecular shuttle
13971.definition: Rotaxane or pseudorotaxane comprising a threading component upon which is threaded a macrocyclic component that, depending on the conditions, can reside at either a specific recognition site on the threading component or away from any recognition site.

M03998.title: molecular sieve effect
M03998.definition: With respect to porous solids, the surface associated with pores communicating with the outside space may be called the internal surface. Because the accessibility of ores may depend on the size of the fluid molecules, the extent of the internal surface may depend on the size of the molecules comprising the fluid, and may be different for the various components of a fluid mixture. This effect is known as the molecular sieve effect.

11475.title: molecular similarity
11475.definition: The degree to which two molecules resemble one another as calculated from their respective 2D or 3D properties, molecular fingerprints, fragment keys, or superimposed 3D structures that usually ranges from 1 (identical) to 0 (dissimilar).

M03999.title: molecular spectra
M03999.definition: Spectra formed by bands consisting of rotational lines originating from rotational, vibrational and electronic transitions of molecules. These may be emission or absorption spectra.

08217.title: molecular spectroscopy
08217.definition: Measurement principle of spectroscopy for the study of rotational, vibrational, and electronic transitions of molecules.

08842.title: molecular switch
08842.definition: Molecule that can be reversibly switched between two or more stable states in response to a change in, e.g., its microenvironment (pH, the presence of a ligand, temperature etc.), illumination or electric current.

12684.title: molecular target
12684.definition: Protein (e.g., receptor, enzyme, or ion channel), RNA, or DNA that is implicated in a clinical disorder or the propagation of any untoward event.

09532.title: molecular template
09532.definition: Molecular structure that transfers a pattern to or organizes another molecular scale structure.

09533.title: molecular wires
09533.definition: Molecular-scale objects that conduct electrical current.

M03989.title: molecularity
M03989.definition: The number of reactant molecular entities that are involved in the 'microscopic chemical event' constituting an elementary reaction. (For reactions in solution this number is always taken to exclude molecular entities that form part of the medium and which are involved solely by virtue of their solvation of solutes.) A reaction with a molecularity of one is called 'unimolecular', one with a molecularity of two 'bimolecular' and of three 'termolecular'.

10248.title: molecularly imprinted polymer sorbent
10248.definition: Porous polymer sorbent with synthetic recognition sites with a high specificity for the sorption of a targeted compound or group of structurally-related compounds.

M04002.title: molecule
M04002.definition: An electrically neutral entity consisting of more than one atom (\(n>1\)). Rigorously, a molecule, in which \(n>1\) must correspond to a depression on the potential energy surface that is deep enough to confine at least one vibrational state.

MT06973.title: molfile
MT06973.definition: A molfile is a table containing atom type, connectivity and a more or less arbitrary 2D or 3D information about a molecule. Well-known file formats include the MOLfile used by MDL Information Systems Inc. (e.g., in the database MACCS), the MOL2 file used by Tripos Associates (e.g., in the modeling package SYBYL), or the CSSR format.

M04004.title: molozonides
M04004.definition: 1,2,3-Trioxolanes, the primary products of the reaction of ozone at a carbon–carbon double bond.

M04005.title: moment of a force
M04005.definition: About a point is the vector product of the radius vector from this point to a point on the line of action of the force and the force, \(M=r\times F\).

M04006.title: moment of inertia
M04006.definition: Of a body about an axis is the sum of the products of its mass elements and the squares of their distances to the axis. principal moments of inertia of a molecule are chosen so that \(I_{A}\leq I_{B}\leq I_{C}\).

M04008.title: momentum spectrum
M04008.definition: A spectrum which is obtained when a beam of ions is separated according to the momentum-to-charge ratios of the ionic species contained within it. A sector magnetic field achieves separation of the various ionic species in this way. If the ion beam is homogeneous in translational energy, as is the case with sector instruments, separation according to the \(\frac{m}{z}\) ratios is also achieved and a mass spectrum is obtained.

M04007.title: momentum
M04007.definition: Vector quantity equal to the product of mass and velocity.

MT06831.title: monitoring
MT06831.definition: Continuous or repeated observation, measurement, and evaluation of health and/or environmental or technical data for defined purposes, according to prearranged schedules in space and time, using comparable methods for sensing and data collection.

14862.title: monitoring test
14862.definition: Test designed to be applied on a routine basis, with some degree of control, to ensure that the quality of an environmental compartment, biological endpoint, or effluent has not exceeded some prescribed criteria range. In a biomonitoring test, organisms are used as 'sensors' to detect changes in the quality of water or effluent. A monitoring test implies generation of information, on a continuous or other regular basis.

M04013.title: mono-energetic radiation
M04013.definition: Radiation consisting of particles of a single kinetic energy or photons of a single energy.

M04009.title: monochromator
M04009.definition: Optical device that transmits a mechanically selectable narrow band of wavelengths of electromagnetic radiation chosen from a wider range of wavelengths available at the input.

09680.title: monoclonal
09680.definition: Arising from a single clone of cells.

M04010.title: monoclonal antibodies
M04010.definition: A single species of immunoglobulin molecules produced by culturing a single clone of a hybridoma cell. MAbs recognize only one chemical structure, i.e. they are directed against a single epitope of the antigenic substance used to raise the antibody.

13467.title: monocyte
13467.definition: Mononuclear phagocyte found in blood and which is the precursor of the tissue macrophage.

M04011.title: monodisperse medium
M04011.definition: A colloidal system in which all particles are of (nearly) the same size.

08735.title: monoisotopic element
08735.definition: Chemical element having only one stable nuclide.

M04014.title: monoisotopic mass spectrum
M04014.definition: A spectrum containing only ions made up of the principal isotopes of atoms making up the original molecule.

13468.title: monokine
13468.definition: Alternative name for a cytokine produced by monocytes.

M04015.title: monolayer
M04015.definition: A single, closely packed layer of atoms or molecules. The term floating monolayer is used for certain spread monolayers or films which are in the condensed — often solid — state. The term 'Langmuir monolayer' has recently been coined for spread monolayers. This usage is not recommended.

M04016.title: monolayer capacity
M04016.definition: For chemisorption the amount of adsorbate which is needed to occupy all adsorption sites as determined by the structure of the adsorbent and by the chemical nature of the absorptive. For physisorption, the amount needed to cover the surface with a complete monolayer of atoms or molecules in close-packed array, the kind of close packing having to be stated explicitly when necessary.

MT07559.title: monolith
MT07559.definition: Shaped, fabricated, intractable article with a homogeneous microstructure which does not exhibit any structural components distinguishable by optical microscopy.

09901.title: monolithic column
09901.definition: Column packed with a single piece of solid material (monolith) composed of interconnected skeletons (forming macropores) and interconnected flow paths (mesopores) as a stationary phase material.

M04017.title: monomer
M04017.definition: A substance composed of monomer molecules.

M04019.title: monomer molecule
M04019.definition: A molecule which can undergo polymerization thereby contributing constitutional units to the essential structure of a macromolecule.

15410.title: monomer reactivity ratios
15410.definition: In binary copolymerization, (a) the ratio (\(r_{12}\)) of the rate constant (\(k_{11}\)) for the homopropagation of monomer \(\rm{M}_{1}\) to the rate constant (\(k_{12}\)) for the cross-propagation of the chain carrier \(\ldots -{\rm{m}}_{1}^{\ast}\) with the monomer \(\rm{M}_{2}\) and (b) the ratio (\(r_{21}\)) of the rate constant (\(k_{22}\)) for the homopropagation of monomer \(\rm{M}_{2}\) to the rate constant for the cross-propagation (\(k_{21}\)) of the chain carrier \(\ldots -{\rm{m}}_{2}^{\ast}\) with monomer \(\rm{M}_{1}\). Thus, \(r_{12} = k_{11}/k_{12}, r_{21} = k_{22}/k_{21}\).

15411.title: monomer reactivity scale
15411.definition: Relative scale defined by the values of the rate constants for the addition of monomers to a reference active center.

14336.title: monomer-flooded emulsion polymerisation
14336.definition: Semi-continuous emulsion polymerization in which the monomer(s) is(are) fed to the reactor at a rate that exceeds the rate of polymerization.

14337.title: monomer-starved emulsion polymerisation
14337.definition: Semi-continuous emulsion polymerization in which the polymerization rate is controlled by the feed rate(s) of monomer(s), in such a way that, for most of the process, the polymerization rate equals the monomer(s) feed rate(s).

M04018.title: monomeric unit
M04018.definition: The largest constitutional unit contributed by a single monomer molecule to the structure of a macromolecule or oligomer molecule.

13469.title: mononuclear phagocyte system
13469.definition: Network of phagocytic cells throughout the body. System comprising blood monocytes and tissue macrophages.

15892.title: monooxygenase
15892.definition: Enzyme that catalyzes reactions between an organic compound and molecular oxygen in which one atom of the oxygen molecule is incorporated into the organic compound and one atom is reduced to water; involved in the metabolism of many natural and foreign compounds giving both unreactive products and products of different or increased toxicity from that of the parent compound.

M04021.title: monosaccharides
M04021.definition: A term which includes aldoses, ketoses and a wide variety of derivatives. Derivation includes oxidation, deoxygenation, introduction of other substituents, alkylation and acylation of hydroxy groups, and chain branching. E.g.

10971.title: monosomy
10971.definition: Disorder in which body cells have only one pair instead of the normal two pairs of a particular chromosome.

09681.title: monospecificity
09681.definition: Immunoreactivity of an antiserum with its designated antigen.

M04022.title: monotectic reaction
M04022.definition: The reversible transition, on cooling, of a liquid to a mixture of a second liquid and a solid: \[\rm{liquid}_{1}\rightleftarrows \rm{liquid}_{2}+\rm{solid}\]

M04023.title: monotectoid reaction
M04023.definition: A reaction in a system containing two solid solution phases, \(\alpha\mathit{'}\) and \(\alpha\mathit{''}\) in which \(\alpha\mathit{'}\) decomposes into \(\alpha\mathit{''}\) and a new phase \(\beta \): \[\alpha\mathit{'}\rightleftharpoons \alpha\mathit{''}+\beta \]

M04024.title: monotectoid temperature
M04024.definition: The maximum temperature at which a monotectoid reaction can occur.

M04028.title: monotropic transition
M04028.definition: The irreversible transition from a metastable polymorphic form to the stable polymorph. Example: The transition of metastable $\ce{CaCO3}$ (aragonite-type) to the stable $\ce{CaCO3}$ (calcite-type).

11881.title: Monro–Kellie hypothesis
11881.definition: Hypothesis that the intracranial volume is unchangeable and therefore a constant intracranial pressure requires that the sum of the volumes of the three compartments blood, brain tissue and cerebrospinal fluid remains constant.

MT07072.title: Monte Carlo method
MT07072.definition: In mathematics, a method originally used for calculating multiple integrals by means of a random sample. The method is used for numerical modelling of many-particle chemical systems, in particular liquids; it is based on the equilibrium statistical mechanics theory. Observables A are calculated as mean values over a great number (\(\cong\rm{10}^{\rm{5}}-\rm{10}^{\rm{6}}\)) of instant configurations as determined by coordinates of the particles. \[< A >\ = \frac{1}{N}\sum _{i=1}^{N}A\{r_{i}\}\] where \(N\) is the number of configurations. At the first stage, various configurations are randomly generated and then those energetically unrealizable eliminated. An efficient search for the most probable configurations to be entered into the above expression is provided by the Metropolis algorithm based on the principle of Markov's chain theory. While being elaborated for the study of equilibrium chemical systems, MC method is also applied to studies of the dynamics of chemical reactions.

MT06832.title: Monte Carlo study
MT06832.definition: Simulation and analysis of a sequence of events using random numbers to generate possible outcomes in an iterative process.

14863.title: Montreal protocol
14863.definition: Officially the Protocol on Substances That Deplete the Ozone Layer, a treaty signed on 16 September 1987, in Montreal by 25 nations; there are now 168 subscribing nations. The protocol sets limits on the production of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), halons, and related substances that release chlorine or bromine to the ozone layer of the atmosphere.

09534.title: Moore’s law
09534.definition: Empirical observation by Gordon E. Moore, co-founder of Intel, that, over the history of computing hardware, the number of transistors on integrated circuits doubles approximately every two years.

15893.title: morbidity
15893.definition: Any departure, subjective or objective, from a state of physiological or psychological well-being: In this sense, 'sickness', 'illness', and 'morbid condition' are similarly defined and synonymous.

15894.title: morbidity rate
15894.definition: Term (to be avoided) used loosely to refer to incidence or prevalence rates of disease.

15895.title: morbidity survey
15895.definition: Method for the estimation of the prevalence and (or) incidence of a disease or diseases in a population.

M04029.title: mordant
M04029.definition: Substance that fixes a dyestuff in or on a material by combining with the dye to form an insoluble compound, used to fix or intensify stains in a tissue or cell preparation.

M04030.title: More O'Ferrall–Jencks diagram
M04030.definition: Visualization of the potential energy surfaces for a reacting system, as a function of two chosen coordinates. It is particularly useful to discuss structural effects on the transition state geometry for processes occurring either by stepwise or concerted routes. The use of such diagrams, first suggested for elimination reactions, was later extended to acid–base catalysis and to certain other reactions.

M04031.title: Morin transition
M04031.definition: A transition specific to $\ce{\upalpha-Fe2O3}$ in which there is a change in the direction of the atomic magnetic moments in the antiferromagnetic state from parallel to perpendicular to the c-axis. Synonymous with spin-flop transition.

11882.title: morphine
