11882.definition: The major phenanthrene alkaloid of opium, used as an analgesic, sedative, and anxiolytic.

14864.title: morphodynamics
14864.definition: Study of the interaction and adjustment of the seafloor topography and fluid hydrodynamic processes, seafloor morphologies, and sequences of change dynamics involving the motion of sediment.

10972.title: morphogen
10972.definition: Any of various signalling factors in embryonic tissue that influences the movement and organization of cells during morphogenesis by forming a concentration gradient.

10973.title: morphogenesis
10973.definition: Shaping of an organism during embryological development by differentiation of cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems, according to the genetic program of the organism, and influenced by morphogens and environmental conditions.

MT07285.title: morphology
MT07285.definition: Shape, optical appearance, or form of phase domains in substances, such as high polymers, polymer blends, composites, and crystals.

MT07284.title: morphology coarsening
MT07284.definition: Process by which phase domains increase in size during the aging of a multiphase material.

M04032.title: morphotropic transition
M04032.definition: An abrupt change in the structure of a solid solution with variation in composition.

MT07073.title: Morse potential
MT07073.definition: The empirical function relating the potential energy of a molecule to the inter-atomic distance r accounting for the anharmonicity of bond stretching: \[E\left(r\right) = D_{\rm{e}}\ (1- \rm{e}^{-a\ (r- r_{\rm{e}})})^{2}\] where \(D_{\rm{e}}\) is the bond-dissociation energy, \(r_{\rm{e}}\) is the equilibrium bond length, and \(a\) is a parameter characteristic of a given molecule.

14865.title: mortality
14865.definition: Death rate, the number of dead individuals per unit time.

15896.title: mortality study
15896.definition: Investigation dealing with death rates or proportion of deaths attributed to specific causes as a measure of response.

10975.title: morula
10975.definition: Early multi-celled stage of the embryo from which the blastocyst is formed.

10976.title: mosaicism
10976.definition: Condition in which an individual or an organism that develops from a single zygote has two or more cell populations that differ in genetic constitution.

M04033.title: Mössbauer effect
M04033.definition: Resonance absorption of γ-radiation by nuclei arranged in a crystal lattice in such a way that the recoil momentum is shared by many atoms.

08736.title: Mössbauer spectrometry
08736.definition: Measurement method in which recoil-less resonance gamma ray scattering and absorption in solids is applied to measure the nuclear environment of atoms of elements in a material.

M04034.title: Mössbauer thickness
M04034.definition: The effective thickness of a source (\(t_{s}\)) or absorber (\(t_{a}\)) in the optical path.

M04035.title: most probable distribution
M04035.definition: A discrete distribution with the differential mass-distribution function of the form: \[f_{\rm{w}}(x) = a^{2}\ x\ (1- a)^{x- 1}\] where \(x\) is a parameter characterizing the chain length, such as relative molecular mass or degree of polymerization and \(a\) is a positive adjustable parameter. For large values of \(x\), the most probable distribution converges to the particular case of the Schulz–Zimm distribution with \(b=1\). In the literature, this distribution is sometimes referred to as the Flory distribution or the Schulz–Flory distribution.

14866.title: most-sensitive-species approach
14866.definition: Ecotoxicological approach in which results for the most sensitive of all tested species are used as an indicator of the toxicant concentration below which the entire community is protected from adverse effects.

11883.title: motor activity
11883.definition: Physical activity and performance of an animal.

11884.title: motor coordination
11884.definition: Cooperation of the motor neurons and the involved muscles to perform a body movement precisely according to spatiotemporal requirements.

11885.title: motor cortex
11885.definition: Region of the cerebral cortex, located primarily in the frontal lobe, involved in coordinating motor activity.

11886.title: motor endplate
11886.definition: Complex structure by which the axon of a motor neuron establishes synaptic contact with a skeletal muscle fiber.

11887.title: motor neuron
11887.definition: Nerve cell in the spinal cord having an axon that leaves the central nervous system to establish a functional connection with an effector (muscle or glandular) tissue.

11888.title: motor neuron disease
11888.definition: Generic term for a heterogeneous group of disorders, all affecting motor neurons in the brain, spinal cord, or both.

11889.title: motor system
11889.definition: Part of the central nervous system responsible for control of movement, consisting of the pyramidal system controlling voluntary movement and the extrapyramidal system coordinating involuntary movement.

M04037.title: Mott transition
M04037.definition: A transition occurring only in 'single-valent' systems from strongly correlated (\(U > W\)) to weakly correlated (\(U < W\)) electrons as a result of a change of bandwidth \(W\). \(W\) reflects the strength of the interatomic interactions in a periodic array of like atoms and \(U\) is a measure of the intra-atomic interactions, i.e. the electrostatic energy involved in the creation of polar states by transferring an electron from one atom to the next, as shown schematically by the disproportionation reaction: \[\rm{M}^{n+}+\rm{M}^{n+}\rightarrow \rm{M}^{(n+1)+}+\rm{M}^{(n- 1)+}\] A \(U > W\) produces a magnetic semiconductor; a \(U < W\) gives rise to a metal (normally nonmagnetic). Note also that \(U\) and \(W\) can be altered by changes in interatomic distances, brought about through temperature or pressure variations or by introducing an alloying element. Synonymous with Mott–Hubbard transition.

13471.title: mouse ear-swelling test
13471.definition: Test for sensitization in which the test substance is applied topically to the ear of a mouse for three consecutive days. The change in ear thickness is then measured following challenge on day 8.

13470.title: mouse IgE test
13470.definition: Procedure in which serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) levels are measured in mice following topical exposure to a test substance. Substances that cause a significant increase in IgE are considered to be potential respiratory allergens.

14867.title: moving average method
14867.definition: Method of estimating \(\pu{LC_{50}}\), \(\pu{EC_{50}}\), or \(\pu{LD_{50}}\). It can be implemented with straightforward equations if the toxicant concentrations are set in a geometric series and there are equal numbers of individuals exposed in each treatment.

09751.title: MS/MS data based identification
09751.definition: Mass spectrometric method used for protein/peptide identification based on protein sequencing.

15897.title: mucociliary transport
15897.definition: Process of removal of particles from the bronchi of the lungs in a mucus stream moved by cilia, thus contributing to uptake from the gastrointestinal tract.

13472.title: mucocutaneous
13472.definition: Pertaining to or affecting the mucous membranes and/or the skin.

M04041.title: mucopolysaccharides
M04041.definition: Polysaccharides composed of alternating units from uronic acids and glycosamines, and commonly partially esterified with sulfuric acid.

13473.title: mucosa
13473.definition: Moist tissue that lines some organs and body cavities, including the nose, mouth, lungs, and digestive tract.

13474.title: mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue
13474.definition: Secondary lymphoid tissue present in the surface mucosa of the respiratory tract and bronchus (BALT), gastrointestinal tract (GALT), nasal passages (NALT), larynx (LALT), conjunctiva (CALT), and genitourinary tract, and in the skin sub-epidermis (SALT).

13475.title: mucosal addressin cell adhesion molecule-1
13475.definition: Protein involved in trafficking of lymphocytes to mucosal endothelium.

13476.title: mucosal tolerance
13476.definition: State of lymphocyte hyporesponsiveness to protein antigens applied across mucosal surfaces by oral or nasal instillation.

10978.title: mucous membrane
10978.definition: Layer of epithelial tissue with a thin underlying layer of connective tissue (the lamina propria) that lines many body cavities, including the gut, respiratory passages, and tubular organs; it secretes, and is covered in, mucus.

10979.title: mucus
10979.definition: Slippery viscous fluid, consisting largely of water and glycoproteins, secreted by mucous membranes.

MT07074.title: Mulliken population analysis
MT07074.definition: A partitioning scheme based on the use of density and overlap matrixes of allocating the electrons of a molecular entity in some fractional manner among its various parts (atoms, bonds, orbitals). As with other schemes of partitioning the electron density in molecules, MPA is arbitrary and strongly dependent on the particular basis set employed. However, comparison of population analyses for a series of molecules is useful for a quantitative description of intra-molecular interactions, chemical reactivity and structural regularities.

M04042.title: multi-centre bond
M04042.definition: Representation of some molecular entities solely by localized two-electron two-centre bonds appears to be unsatisfactory. Instead, multi-centre bonds have to be considered in which electron pairs occupy orbitals encompassing three or more atomic centres. Examples include the three-centre bonds in diborane, the delocalized $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}bonding}$ of benzene and bridged carbocations.

M04043.title: multi-centre reaction
M04043.definition: A synonym for pericyclic reaction. The number of 'centres' is the number of atoms not bonded initially, between which single bonds are breaking or new bonds are formed in the transition state. This number does not necessarily correspond to the ring size of the transition state for the pericyclic reaction. Thus, a Diels–Alder reaction is a 'four-centre reaction'. This terminology has largely been superseded by the more detailed one developed for the various pericyclic reactions.

M04044.title: multi-channel pulse height analyser
M04044.definition: A pulse amplitude analyser which includes a storage function to record the number of pulses received per channel.

09568.title: multi-component resist
09568.definition: Resist comprising more than one active component.

09959.title: multi-dimensional chromatography
09959.definition: Chromatography in which parts or all of the separated sample components are subjected to additional separation steps.

M04066.title: multi-strand chain
M04066.definition: A chain that comprises constitutional unit connected in such a way that adjacent constitutional units are joined to each other through more than four atoms, more than two on at least one side of each constitutional unit.

M04067.title: multi-strand macromolecule
M04067.definition: A macromolecule that comprises constitutional unit connected in such a way that adjacent constitutional units are joined to each other through more than four atoms, more than two on at least one side of each constitutional unit.

10056.title: multi-way data
10056.definition: Multivariate data having two or more kinds of explanatory variable per object.

MT07307.title: multicoat morphology
MT07307.definition: Morphology observed in a blend of a block copolymer with the homopolymer of one of the blocks and characterized by alternating concentric shells of the copolymer and the homopolymer.

10311.title: multicommutation flow extraction
10311.definition: Programmable flow extraction device with microsolenoid valves for processing microliter sample volumes.

15214.title: multicompartment formulation
15214.definition: Dosage form (capsule, tablet) comprising several elements (e.g., microspheres or coated pellets) differing in the rate of drug release.

15898.title: multicompartment model
15898.definition: Product of a compartmental analysis requiring more than two compartments.

14298.title: multicomponent particle
14298.definition: Inhomogeneous particle consisting of two or more immiscible components.Examples of two-phase particle morphology.

MT07075.title: multiconfiguration SCF method
MT07075.definition: Configuration-interaction method in which simultaneous optimization of both the shapes of molecular orbitals and contributions from different electronic configurations is carried out by using the variational method.

10980.title: multicotyledonary placentation
10980.definition: Formation of a placenta with many lobes.

09752.title: multidimensional protein identification technology
09752.definition: Non-gel step-wise multidimensional technique for separating and identifying individual components of complex protein and peptide mixtures. It combines fractionation of proteolytic peptides in steps on a strong cation exchanger (SAX) using ion exchange chromatography (IEC); each step uses higher elution force. Then, each fraction is separated on reversed phase liquid chromatography and analysed using mass spectrometry.

11476.title: multidimensional scaling
11476.definition:
A visualization method that converts a dataset of distances between molecules in property space into coordinates in lower dimension space with emphasis on
 preserving the relative distances between dissimilar molecules.

12685.title: multidrug resistance
12685.definition: Characteristic of cells that confers resistance to the effects of several different classes of drugs.

M04046.title: multienzyme
M04046.definition: A protein possessing more than one catalytic function contributed by distinct parts of a polypeptide chain ('domains'), or by distinct subunits, or both.

M04047.title: multienzyme complex
M04047.definition: A multienzyme with catalytic domains on more than one type of polypeptide chain.

M04048.title: multienzyme polypeptide
M04048.definition: A polypeptide chain containing at least two types of catalytic domains.

15899.title: multifactorial disease
15899.definition: Illness with pathogenesis dependent on complex interplay of genetic and (or) environmental factors.

10981.title: multifactorial inheritance
10981.definition: Transmission from parents to offspring of a trait that is determined by multiple genetic and environmental factors, each with a small effect.

10982.title: multigenerational study
10982.definition:
Animal test of reproductive toxicity in which two to three generations of the test organism are exposed to the substance being assessed.
Animal test of reproductive toxicity in which only one generation is exposed and effects on subsequent generations are assessed.

M04049.title: multilayer
M04049.definition: A system of adjacent layers or monolayers. The term bilayer applies to the particular case of a multilayer two monolayers thick. Monolayers and multilayers may be alternatively named 'films' provided boundaries can be defined for them.

M04050.title: multilayer adsorption
M04050.definition: Adsorption such that the adsorption space accommodates more than one layer of molecules, and not all adsorbed molecules are in contact with the surface layer of the adsorbent.

M04051.title: multilayer aggregate
M04051.definition: A stack of lamellar crystals generated by spiral growth at one or more screw dislocations. The axial displacement over a full turn of the screw (Burgers vector) is usually equal to one lamellar thickness.

09946.title: multilayer coil
09946.definition: Separation column used for high-speed counter-current chromatography.

15215.title: multilayer tablet
15215.definition: Consists of several different layers that are compressed on top of each other, to form a single tablet composed of two or more layers.

14301.title: multilayered particle
14301.definition: Multicomponent particle made of at least two different polymers, with an inner core of one polymer and with at least two layers of different polymers.

10152.title: multilinear least squares regression
10152.definition: Multivariate calibration in which the coefficients of the regression are calculated directly from the indications and values of standards.

11477.title: multiobjective optimization
11477.definition:
The search for those combinations of properties that produces the best compromise between the various objectives of the search, for example properties of
 compounds that are the best trade-off between potency, bioavailability, and selectivity.

12686.title: multiparameter optimisation
12686.definition: Drug-likeness penetrability algorithm derived from CLOGP, clogD, molar mass, topological polar surface area, number of hydrogen-bond donors, and \(\pu{p}K_{\rm{a}}\).

M04053.title: multiphoton ionization
M04053.definition: Occurs when an atom or molecule and their concomitant ions have energy states whereby the energy in two or more photons is absorbed.

M04054.title: multiphoton process
M04054.definition: A process involving interaction of two or more photons with a molecular entity.

08271.title: multiple attenuated total reflection
08271.definition: Process in which attenuated total reflection occurs sequentially several times with the same sample.

11890.title: multiple chemical sensitivity
11890.definition: Intolerance condition attributed to extreme sensitivity of individuals to various environmental chemicals, found in air, food, water, building materials, or fabrics.

10199.title: multiple headspace extraction
10199.definition: Dynamic gas extraction carried out stepwise, with sequential analysis of a number of headspace samples taken from the same vial.

14868.title: multiple heterosis
14868.definition: Higher fitness of an individual as a composite or summed effect of heterozygote superiority (heterosis) at each of a series of loci.

MT07309.title: multiple inclusion morphology
MT07309.definition: Multiphase morphology in which dispersed phase domains of one polymer contain and completely encapsulate many phase domains of a second polymer that may have the same composition as the continuous phase domain.

13477.title: multiple myeloma
13477.definition: Plasma cell malignancy resulting in high levels of monoclonal immunoglobulin (Ig) in serum and of free light chains (Bence–Jones protein) in urine.

M04057.title: multiple peak scanning
M04057.definition: An alternative to multiple ion detection which emphasizes that monitoring of peaks rather than detection of ions is the important feature.

M04058.title: multiple scattering
M04058.definition: Successive rescattering of radiation within the scattering medium.

11891.title: multiple sclerosis
11891.definition: Common demyelinating (see demyelination) disorder of the central nervous system, causing patches of sclerosis (plaques) in the brain and spinal cord.

15900.title: multiple screening
15900.definition: Procedure that has evolved by combining single screening tests, and is the logical corollary of mass screening.

M04056.title: multiple-pass cell
M04056.definition: Permits multiple passage of radiation to increase the absorption pathlength. It is constructed in such a way that mirrors either form part of the cell or are mounted in the sample cell holder.

08378.title: multiple-quantum magic angle spinning NMR
08378.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy used to obtain high-resolution NMR spectra of quadrupolar nuclei by removal of the anisotropy of the quadrupole interaction, involving creating a triple-quantum (or \(5{\rm{Q}}\)) coherence.

08379.title: multiplet
08379.definition: Feature in a nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum that is split but is too complex to easily interpret.

08639.title: multiplex advantage
08639.definition: Decrease in measurement uncertainty obtained by measuring intensity at many different wavelengths simultaneously, as is done, for example, in Fourier-transform spectroscopy.

14166.title: multiplex assay
14166.definition: Assay in which the activity of a single sample against more than one target is measured in a single test.

13478.title: multiplex immunoassay
13478.definition: Type of particle immunoassay employing sets of microspheres with various physicochemical features, each labeled with a different antibody. The method allows detection in a single measurement of an array of 100 or more proteins.

M04059.title: multiplex spectrometer
M04059.definition: A spectrometer in which a single photodetector simultaneously receives signals from different spectral bands which are specifically encoded. In the case of frequency multiplexing, each spectral band is modulated at a specific frequency. Decoding is achieved by filtering out, by electronic means, the corresponding signals. Frequency multiplexing may be realized by changing the path difference between the two interfering beams at a uniform rate. Fourier transform of the interferogram so obtained yields the spectrum. This method is called Fourier transform spectrometry (FTS).

12791.title: multiplexing
12791.definition: Technique used in dynamic mechanical analysis in which a specimen is subjected to the superposition of a number of forced sinusoidal oscillations of different frequencies.

08035.title: multiplicative matrix effect
08035.definition: Matrix effect that is proportional to the measured quantity value of the measurand.

M04061.title: multiplicative name
M04061.definition: A name that expresses the multiple occurrence of identical parent structures, two or more of which are connected by a symmetrical structure expressible by means of a multivalent simple or composite prefix.

10054.title: multiplicative scatter correction
10054.definition: Data pre-processing in which a constant and a multiple of a reference data set is subtracted from data.

M04062.title: multiplicity
M04062.definition: The number of possible orientations, calculated as \(2\ S+1\), of the spin angular momentum corresponding to a given total spin quantum number (\(S\)), for the same spatial electronic wavefunction. A state of singlet multiplicity has \(S=0\) and \(2\ S+1=1\). A doublet state has \(S=\frac{1}{2}\), \(2\ S+1=2\), etc. Note that when \(S>L\) (the total orbital angular momentum possible) there are only \(2\ L+1\) orientations of total angular momentum possible.

M04063.title: multiply labelled
M04063.definition: A selectively labelled compound may be multiply labelled when in the unmodified compound there is more than one atom of the same element at the position where the isotopic modification occurs, e.g. $\ce{H}$ in $\ce{CH4}$, or there are several atoms of the same element at different positions where the isotopic modification occurs, e.g. $\ce{C}$ in $\ce{C4H8O}$.

15901.title: multipotent
15901.definition: Of a cell, capable of giving rise to several different kinds of structure or types of cell.

13479.title: multipotent progenitor cell
13479.definition: Undifferentiated stem cell, obtained from adult bone marrow or other non-embryonic tissue sources, that possesses the ability to differentiate into a variety of cell types, especially into cells of a closely related family of cells that are expanded in vitro and deposited in master cell banks for 'off-the-shelf' use, with potential hematopoiesis-inducing and immunomodulating activities.

MT07424.title: multireference configuration interaction
MT07424.definition: Configuration-interaction method in which the configurations are built by excitation out of a wavefunction obtained by using, e.g., the multiconfiguration SCF method.

15902.title: multistage cluster sampling
15902.definition: Cluster sampling with more than two stages, each sampling being made on aggregates (or clusters) in which the clusters already obtained by the preceding sampling have been divided.

10217.title: multistage countercurrent distribution
10217.definition: Multistage countercurrent separation based on a discontinuous, differential migration process employing stepwise extraction.

15903.title: multistage model
15903.definition: Dose–response model for cancer death estimation of the form \[P = 1 - \exp [-(q_{0} + q_{1}d_{1} + q_{2}d_{2} + \ldots + q_{k}d_{k})]\] where \(P\) is the probability of cancer death from a continuous dose rate, \(d_{i}\) , of group (or stage) \(i = 0, 1, 2 \ldots\), the \(q\)’s are constants, and \(k\) is the number of dose groups (or, if less than the number of dose groups, \(k\) is the number of biological stages believed to be required in the carcinogenesis process). With the multistage model, it is assumed that cancer is initiated by cell mutations in a finite series of steps.

M04065.title: multistage sampling
M04065.definition: Samples taken in a series of steps with the sampling portions constituting the sample (units or increments) at each step being selected from the larger or greater number of portions of the previous step, or from a primary or composite sample. The first set of portions (units or increments) taken from the population available for sampling is the primary sample. The subsequent samples (secondary, tertiary, etc.) are the sets of subsamples, units, items, individuals or increments taken from the preceding step. The units may be different steps of multistage sampling (e.g. pallets, cases, packages).

12688.title: multitarget drug discovery
12688.definition: Deliberate design of compounds that act on more than one molecular target.

12687.title: multitarget-directed ligand
12687.definition: Ligand acting on more than one distinct molecular target. Targets may be of the same or different mechanistic classes.

10153.title: multivariate calibration
10153.definition: Calibration in which the indications are multivariate data.

10100.title: multivariate curve resolution
10100.definition: Factor analysis for the decomposition of multicomponent data into a linear sum of chemically-meaningful components when little or no prior information about the composition is available.

10055.title: multivariate data
10055.definition: Data having two or more variables per object.

MT06974.title: multivariate statistics
MT06974.definition: Multivariate statistics is a set of statistical tools to analyze data (e.g., chemical and biological) matrices using regression and/or pattern recognition techniques.

10249.title: multiwell extraction plate
10249.definition: Regular array of wells in a single moulded body with a short sorbent bed or disc embedded at the base of each well.Multiwell extraction plate.

10181.title: multiwell sample plate
10181.definition: Plate with multiple wells for individual samples.

M04068.title: munchnones
M04068.definition: Mesoionic compounds having a 1,3-oxazole skeleton bearing an oxygen atom attached to the 5-position with the following delocalized structure:

08737.title: muon induced X-ray emission analysis
08737.definition: Measurement method of X-ray analysis in which characteristic X-radiation emitted upon irradiation of a material with a beam of muons of certain energy is used to measure the chemical composition and chemical state of an element.

M04069.title: muonium
M04069.definition: Atom-like particle consisting of a positive muon and an electron.

12689.title: Murcko assembly
12689.definition: Core scaffold of a molecule that remains after all chain substituents that do not terminate in a ring are removed. Single atoms connected by a double bond are typically also retained.

15904.title: murine
15904.definition: Of or belonging to the family of rats and mice (Muridae).

13480.title: murine local lymph node assay
13480.definition: Predictive test of sensitization in which a test substance is applied topically to the skin of mice (usually three times at daily intervals) and the weight of the local draining lymph nodes is measured at six days. Usually lymphoproliferation in the nodes is measured following injection of [\(\ce{^{3}H}\)]thymidine or bromodeoxyuridine.

11892.title: muscarinic
11892.definition: Referring to agents that stimulate the postganglionicparasympatheticreceptor, named after the prototypical mushroom alkaloid, muscarine [2,5-anhydro-1,4,6-trideoxy-6-(trimethylammonio)-D-ribo-hexitol].

11893.title: muscarinic receptor
11893.definition: One of the two main classes of acetylcholine receptors that responds to muscarinic agents.

11894.title: muscle spindle
11894.definition: Sensory organ in the body of a striated muscle containing afferent and efferentnerve fibers that detect passive muscle stretch and convey information to the central nervous system to cause reflex resistance to this stretch.

M04071.title: mustards
M04071.definition: Compounds having two $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}haloalkyl groups}$ bound to a sulfur atom, as in $\ce{(XC2H2C2H2)2S}$, and their analogues, the nitrogen (and phosphorus) mustards, $\ce{(XC2H2C2H2)2NR}$. Compounds having one $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}haloalkyl group}$ and one $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}hydroxyalkyl group}$ on $\ce{S}$ are termed hemi- or semi-mustards by some chemists.

MT06833.title: mutagen
MT06833.definition: Agent that can induce heritable changes (mutations) of the genotype in a cell as a consequence of alterations or loss of genetic material.

M04072.title: mutagenesis
M04072.definition: The introduction of permanant heritable changes i.e. mutations into the DNA of an organism.

14400.title: mutagenicity
14400.definition: Ability of a physical, chemical, or biological agent to induce (or generate) heritable changes (mutations) in the genotype in a cell as a consequence of alterations or loss of genes or chromosomes (or parts thereof).

M04073.title: mutarotation
M04073.definition: The change in optical rotation accompanying epimerization. In sugar chemistry this term usually refers to epimerization at the hemiacetal carbon atom.

M04074.title: mutation
M04074.definition: A heritable change in the nucleotide sequence of genomic DNA (or RNA in RNA viruses), or in the number of genes or chromosomes in a cell, which may occur spontaneously or be brought about by chemical mutagens or by radiation (induced mutation).

M04075.title: mutation rate
M04075.definition: The frequency (\(\rm{h}^{-1}\)) with which a mutation occurs within a organism or gene. In general, rates of spontaneous mutation vary between one in \(10^{4}\) and one in \(10^{8}\) per gene per generation, and can be considerably increased by mutagens.

M04076.title: mutual inductance
M04076.definition: For two thin conducting loops, the magnetic flux through one loop, caused by an electric current in the other loop, divided by that current.

15342.title: mutual solubility
15342.definition: In a system of two or more liquid or solid components, solubility of all components in all phases.

14869.title: mutualism
14869.definition: Interaction between two or more species, giving fitness benefit to all the involved species, e.g., increased carrying capacity.

15905.title: myalgia
15905.definition: Pain or tenderness in a muscle or group of muscles.

10983.title: mycoplasma
10983.definition: Very small infectious microorganism, related to bacteria, but without a cell wall.

10984.title: myelencephalon
10984.definition: Part of the brain in the embryo that gives rise to the medulla oblongata.

11896.title: myelin
11896.definition: Electrically insulating lipoprotein layers that are produced by glial cells and surround the axons of the neurons.

11897.title: myelin basic protein
11897.definition: Major component of myelin, that helps organizing the correct assembly of the lipids and proteins in myelin sheets.

M04077.title: Myelin cylinders
M04077.definition: Birefringent cylinders which form spontaneously from lipid-containing material in contact with water.

11899.title: myelin sheath
11899.definition: Concentric layers of myelin surrounding the axons of some neurons.

11898.title: myelin-associated glycoprotein
11898.definition: Transmembrane glycoprotein that plays an important role in the interaction between axons and myelin and affects myelination during nerve regeneration.

10985.title: myelination
10985.definition: The acquisition, development, or formation of a myelin sheath around a nerve fiber.

10986.title: myeloblast
10986.definition: Immature bone marrow cell that is a precursor of the granulocyte series.

13482.title: myelodysplastic syndrome
13482.definition: Diverse collection of hematological conditions united by ineffective production (or dysplasia) of myeloid blood cells and risk of transformation to acute myelogenous leukemia (AML). Anemia requiring chronic blood transfusion is frequently present.

11900.title: myelogram
11900.definition: X-ray of the spinal canal following injection of a contrast material into the surrounding cerebrospinal fluid spaces.

13484.title: myeloid
13484.definition: Referring to the nonlymphocytic groups of white blood cells, including granulocytes, monocytes, and platelets.

13485.title: myeloid stem cell
13485.definition: One of two groups of stem cells produced in the bone marrow. Myeloid stem cells may mature into several types of blood cells, including acidic basophils, eosinophils, erythrocytes, macrophages, megakaryocytes, and neutrophils.

13486.title: myeloid tissue
13486.definition: Tissue within red bone marrow that produces the blood cells. It is found around the blood vessels and contains various cell types that are precursors of the blood cells.

13483.title: myeloma
13483.definition: Tumor composed of cells derived from hematopoietic cells (see hematopoiesis) of the bone marrow, or from mast cells.

13487.title: myeloma protein
13487.definition: Monoclonal antibody secreted by myeloma cells.

11901.title: myelomeningocele
11901.definition: Protrusion of the spinal cord and its coverings through a defect in the vertebral column.

11902.title: myelopathy
11902.definition:
Any functional or pathologic disturbance in the spinal cord.
Disorder of the myelopoietic tissues of the bone marrow.

13488.title: myeloperoxidase
13488.definition: Enzyme found in azurophilic granules of neutrophils, the major target of antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibody (ANCA).

13489.title: myelopoiesis
13489.definition: Process of formation and development of myeloid blood cells in the bone marrow.

13490.title: myelosuppression
13490.definition: Decrease in myeloid cells, including pancytopenia, anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia, and other blood dyscrasias.

10987.title: myelotoxic
10987.definition: Harming bone marrow or any of its components.

10988.title: myoblast
10988.definition: Mononucleate cell that is committed to differentiate into muscle.

10993.title: myotome
10993.definition: In the embryo, that part of a somite that develops into skeletal muscle.

11904.title: myotonia
11904.definition: Prolonged contraction or delayed relaxation of a muscle after mechanical or brief electrical stimulation.

M03659.title: µ-
M03659.definition: An affix used in names to signify that a group so designated bridges two or more centres of coordination.

14882.title: "no action" alternative
14882.definition: Scenario in which one assesses if the contaminants at the waste site pose, or will pose in the future, a risk if left alone.

11869.title: N-methyl-D-aspartate
11869.definition: Excitotoxic non-essential amino acid used experimentally to identify a specific subset of glutamatereceptors.

11870.title: N-methyl-D-aspartate-type glutamate receptor
11870.definition: One of the various types of receptors of the neurotransmitterglutamate.

14238.title: nanoporous polymer crystal
14238.definition: Polymer crystal presenting empty volume elements that can host low-molar-mass guest species.

12502.title: nanoelectrospray
12502.definition: Electrospray ionization at a very low solvent flow rate, typically hundreds of nanoliters per minute of sample solution or lower, often without the use of an external solvent delivery system.

12503.title: negative ion chemical ionization
12503.definition: Chemical ionization that results in the formation of negative ions.

12504.title: neutralization-reionization mass spectrometry
12504.definition: Procedure by which neutral species are formed from m/z selected ions by charge transfer to a collision gas or by dissociation. The neutral species are separated from the remaining ions and ionized through collisions with a second gas.

12505.title: neutral loss
12505.definition: Loss of an uncharged species from an ion during dissociation.

12506.title: neutral loss scan
12506.definition: Scan used to generate a constant neutral loss spectrum.

12507.title: nitrogen rule
12507.definition: Rule stating that a neutral organic molecule containing one or more atoms of the elements \(\ce{C}\), \(\ce{H}\), \(\ce{O}\), \(\ce{N}\), \(\ce{S}\), \(\ce{P}\), or any halogen has an odd nominal mass if it contains an odd number of nitrogen atoms.

12508.title: nozzle-skimmer dissociation
12508.definition: Collisionally activated dissociation that is caused by collisions in the region between the nozzle and skimmer of an atmospheric pressure ionization source such as electrospray or atmospheric pressure chemical ionization.

12509.title: nozzle-skimmer voltage
12509.definition: Electric potential difference applied between the electrospray needle and the skimmer, which is typically held at the same potential as the counter electrode.

12510.title: nth-generation product ion
12510.definition: Serial product ions from dissociation or bimolecular reaction of selected precursor ions where \(n\) refers to the number of stages of dissociation or bimolecular reaction in a series of consecutive reactions that involve successive product ions.

12511.title: nth-generation product ion spectrum
12511.definition: Mass spectrum recorded from any mass spectrometer in which the appropriate scan function can be set to record the appropriate generation product ion or ions of m/z selected precursor ions.

14245.title: non-parallel-chain crystal
14245.definition: Polymer crystal in which the stems are aligned along two or more different crystallographic directions.

16254.title: Nernstian response
16254.definition: Response of an ion-selective electrode according to a local thermodynamic equilibrium, over a given range of activity (or concentration) that follows the Nernst equation.

14267.title: non-isothermal crystallisation
14267.definition: Crystallization taking place under varying temperature conditions.

13913.title: nanocapsule
13913.definition: Hollow nanoparticle composed of a solid shell that surrounds a core-forming space available to entrap substances.

13914.title: nanosphere
13914.definition: Nanoparticle of spherical shape without membrane or any distinct outer layer.

N00350.title: ångström
N00350.definition: Non-SI unit of length, \(\rm{Å} = 10^{-10}\ \rm{m}\), widely used in molecular physics.

N04078.title: n → π* state
N04078.definition: An excited state related to the ground state by a n → π* transition.

N04079.title: n → π* transition
N04079.definition: An electronic transition described approximately as promotion of an electron from a 'non-bonding' (lone-pair) n orbital to an 'antibonding' $\ce{\uppi\! orbital}$ designated as $\ce{\uppi\!^{\ast}}$.

N04081.title: n → σ* transition
N04081.definition: An electronic transition described approximately as promotion of an electron from a 'non-bonding' (lone-pair) n orbital to an 'antibonding' $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}orbital}$ designated as $\ce{\upsigma\!^{\ast}}$. Such transitions generally involve high transition energies and appear close to or mixed with Rydberg transitions.

13493.title: N-nucleotides
13493.definition: Non-templated nucleotides added to the junctions between antibody and T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V) gene, diversity (D) gene, and joining (J) gene segments during gene rearrangement.

13495.title: N-region
13495.definition: Highly variable region on the H-chain of immunoglobulins.

09753.title: N-terminal analysis
09753.definition: Chemical method for N-terminal sequencing of proteins and peptides starting at their N-terminus.

09754.title: N-terminus
09754.definition: The end of an amino acid chain (protein or polypeptide), terminating in a free primary amine group.

N04080.title: n-σ* delocalization
N04080.definition: Delocalization of a free electron pair (n) into an antibonding $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}orbital}$ ($\ce{\upsigma\!^{\ast}}$).

13492.title: NACHT domain-, leucine-rich repeat (LRR)-, and pyrin (N-terminal homology) domain (PYD)-containing protein 3
13492.definition: NOD-like receptor (NLR), found in certain inflammasomes, that binds to aggregated proteins and the peptides that compose them. Its activation leads to the generation of inflammatory cytokines, such as interleukin (IL)-1, and neurotoxic factors.

13496.title: naïve lymphocyte
13496.definition: Mature T cell or B cell that has not yet been activated (see lymphocyte activation) by encounter with antigen.

NT07243.title: nanocomposite
NT07243.definition: Composite in which at least one of the phase domains has at least one dimension of the order of nanometres.

09535.title: nanodevice
09535.definition: Device in which the manufactured size is between \(\pu{1}\) and \(\pu{100 nm}\).

13842.title: nanodomain
13842.definition: Region of a self-assembled entity with an equivalent diameter of approximately \(\pu{(1\!-\! 100) nm}\).

09086.title: nanoelectrode
09086.definition: Electrode with smallest dimension less than 1 micrometre

09536.title: nanoelectromechanical systems
09536.definition: Devices that integrate electrical and mechanical functionality at the nanoscale. A miniaturization of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS).

15216.title: nanoencapsulation
15216.definition: Formation of nanoparticles encapsulating a drug.

NT06888.title: nanofiltration
NT06888.definition: Pressure-driven membrane-based separation process in which particles and dissolved macromolecules smaller than \(2\ \rm{nm}\) are rejected.

NT07521.title: nanogel
NT07521.definition: Particle of gel of any shape with an equivalent diameter of approximately \(1\) to \(100\ \rm{nm}\).

09510.title: nanoimprint lithography
09510.definition: Subset of imprint lithography that allows for the fabrication of nanometer scale patterns.

09515.title: nanolithography
09515.definition: Umbrella term that is used to describe all lithographic techniques that allow for the fabrication of nanometer scale patterns.

08188.title: nanomaterial
08188.definition: Substance whose particles are in the size range of 1 to \(\pu{100 nm}\).

09538.title: nanoparticle
09538.definition: Particle of any shape with an equivalent diameter of approximately \(\pu{1}\) to \(\pu{100 nm}\).

09539.title: nanopattern
09539.definition: Patterns on a substrate with lesser dimensions of between \(\pu{1}\) to \(\pu{100 nm}\).

09540.title: nanophotonics
09540.definition: Study of the interaction of light with particles or substances on a scale less than the wavelength of the light.

N04083.title: nanoscopic film
N04083.definition: A film which has lateral dimensions in the range of \(0.1{-}100\ \rm{nm}\).

13843.title: nanoscopic polymer film
13843.definition: Polymer film that has lateral dimensions in the range of \(\pu{(1\!-\! 100) nm}\).

09516.title: nanosphere lithography
09516.definition: Lithography in which material is deposited into the interstices of a 2D array of nanospheres that are subsequently removed to form a pattern.

09541.title: nanostructure
09541.definition: Structure or feature of size between \(\pu{1}\) and \(\pu{100 nm}\).

09542.title: nanotechnology
09542.definition: Manipulation of matter on an atomic and molecular scale.

15908.title: nanotoxicology
15908.definition: Scientific discipline involving the study of the actual or potential danger presented by the harmful effects of nanoparticles on living organisms and ecosystems, of the relationship of such harmful effects to exposure, and of the mechanisms of action, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of intoxications.

N04084.title: naphthenes
N04084.definition: Cycloalkanes especially cyclopentane, cyclohexane and their alkyl derivatives. The term seems to be obsolescent, except in the petrochemical industry.

N04085.title: naphthenic acids
N04085.definition: Acids chiefly monocarboxylic, derived from naphthene. The term seems to be obsolescent, except in the petrochemical industry.

08272.title: Napierian absorbance
08272.definition: Absorbance calculated with logarithm base \(e\) (natural or Napierian logarithm).

N04086.title: narcissistic reaction
N04086.definition: A chemical reaction that can be described as the conversion of a reactant into its mirror image, without rotation or translation of the product, so that the product enantiomer actually coincides with the mirror image of the reactant molecule. Examples of such reactions are cited under the entries fluxional and degenerate rearrangement.

11906.title: narcosis
11906.definition: Nonspecific, reversible depression of central nervous system function, marked by stupor or unconsciousness.

11907.title: narcotic
11907.definition:
Nonspecific usage – an agent that produces insensibility or stupor.
Specific usage – any natural or synthetic substance that has morphine-like actions.

10995.title: natality
10995.definition: Rate of birth, the number of newborn individuals per unit time.

14870.title: National Academy of Sciences paradigm of risk assessment
14870.definition: Model for risk assessment with four components—hazard identification, exposure assessment, dose–response assessment, and risk characterization.

10025.title: national examination standard
10025.definition: Examination standard recognized by national authority to serve in a state or economy as the basis for assigning nominal property values to other examination standards for the same kind-of-nominal-property.

15909.title: natriuretic
15909.definition: Substance increasing the rate of excretion of sodium ion in the urine.

NT07076.title: natural atomic orbital
NT07076.definition: A valence-shell atomic orbital whose derivation involves diagonalising the localized block of the full density matrix of a given molecule associated with basis functions \(\chi _{i}\left(\rm{A}\right)\) on that atom. A distinguishing feature of NAOs is that they meet the simultaneous requirement of orthonormality and maximum occupancy. For isolated atoms, NAOs coincide with natural orbitals. In a polyatomic molecule the NAOs (in contrast to natural orbitals that become delocalised over all nuclear centres) mostly retain one-centre character, and thus are optimal for describing the molecular electron density around each atomic centre.

13497.title: natural autoantibodies
13497.definition: Part of the naturally occurring repertoire of polyreactive antibodies that bind to autoantigens with low affinity. They are mainly of immunoglobulin M (IgM) isotype and produced by CD5+ B lymphocytes.

NT07077.title: natural bond orbital
NT07077.definition: The orbital which is formed from natural hybrid orbitals. For a localized $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bond}$ between atoms $\ce{A}$ and $\ce{B}$, the NBO is: \[\sigma _{\rm{AB}}=c_{\rm{A}}\ \rm{h}_{\rm{A}}+c_{\rm{B}}\ \mathrm{h}_{\rm{B}}\] where \(\rm{h}_{\rm{A}}\) and \(\rm{h}_{\rm{B}}\) are the natural hybrids centered on atoms $\ce{A}$ and $\ce{B}$. NBOs closely correspond to the picture of localized bonds and lone pairs as basic units of molecular structure, so that is possible to conveniently interpret ab initio wave-functions in terms of the classical Lewis structure concepts by transforming these functions to NBO form.

N04087.title: natural broadening
N04087.definition: Broadening which has its origin in the finite optical lifetime of one or both levels involved in the transition.

N04088.title: natural graphite
N04088.definition: A mineral found in nature. It consists of graphitic carbon regardless of its crystalline perfection.

NT07078.title: natural hybrid orbital
NT07078.definition: Symmetrically orthogonalised directed hybrid orbital derived through unitary transformation of natural atomic orbitals centred on a particular atom.

13498.title: natural immunity
13498.definition: Host defense mechanisms that do not require prior exposure to antigen.

N04089.title: natural isotopic abundance
N04089.definition: Of a specified isotope of an element, the isotopic abundance in the element as found in nature.

13499.title: natural killer cell
13499.definition: Large granular lymphocyte which does not rearrange nor express either immunoglobulin or T-cell receptor (TCR) genes but is able to recognize and destroy certain tumor and virally infected cells in a major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecule- and antibody-independent manner.

13500.title: natural killer cell activity assay
13500.definition: Immunotoxicity test in which lymphoid tissue or blood that has been treated with a test compound is co-incubated with target cells. The cytotoxic effect on target cells is measured, e.g., with the chromium release assay. It is used under circumstances where differences from untreated cells are attributed to natural killer (NK) cell activity.

13501.title: natural killer T cell
13501.definition: Lymphoid cells with a morphology and granule content intermediate between T cells and natural killer (NK) cells.

14288.title: natural latex
14288.definition: Latex, the dispersed phase of which is obtained from various plants.

08641.title: natural linewidth
08641.definition: Line width of a molecular spectral band that arises from the probability of spontaneous emission in the absence of radiation fields and interaction with other molecules or entities.

15910.title: natural occurrence
15910.definition: Presence of a substance in nature, as distinct from presence resulting from inputs from human activities.

NT07079.title: natural orbital
NT07079.definition: The orbitals defined (P. Lowdin) as the eigenfunctions of the spinless one-particle electron density matrix. For a configuration interaction (CI) wave-function constructed from orbitals \(\varPhi \), the electron density function, \(\unicode[Times]{x3C1}\), is of the form: \[\unicode[Times]{x3C1} = \sum_{i}\sum _{j}a_{ij}\,\varPhi_{i}^{*}\,\varPhi_{j}\] where the coefficients \(a_{ij}\) are a set of numbers which form the density matrix. The NOs reduce the density matrix \(\unicode[Times]{x3C1}\) to a diagonal form: \[\unicode[Times]{x3C1} = \sum _{k}b_{k}\mathit{\Phi}_{k}^{*}\mathit{\Phi}_{k}\] where the coefficients \(b_{k}\) are occupation numbers of each orbital. The importance of natural orbitals is in the fact that CI expansions based on these orbitals have generally the fastest convergence. If a CI calculation was carried out in terms of an arbitrary basis set and the subsequent diagonalisation of the density matrix \(\rm{a}_{ij}\) gave the natural orbitals, the same calculation repeated in terms of the natural orbitals thus obtained would lead to the wave-function for which only those configurations built up from natural orbitals with large occupation numbers were important.

14029.title: natural photosynthesis
14029.definition: Production of complex organic substances by higher plants, algae and photosynthesising bacteria from simple compounds (e.g., carbon dioxide and water, hydrogen sulfide, etc.) using ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation energy absorbed by, e.g., chlorophyll, chlorophyll-protein complexes, and natural chromoproteins.

NT07080.title: natural population analysis

14167.title: natural product
14167.definition:
Complex mixture derived from natural (biological) sources used in screening as a resource for identification of lead compounds.
Pure compound of natural (biological) origin (whether obtained by purification of natural mixtures or by laboratory synthesis), as opposed to compounds originating from synthetic chemistry.Note: Typical origins include extracts from microbes and higher organisms from terrestrial or marine environments.

14872.title: natural radiation background
14872.definition: Cosmic radiation emitted from stars and long-lived terrestrial radionuclides that are ubiquitously present in the Earth’s soils.

N04092.title: natural radioactivity
N04092.definition: Radioactivity of naturally occurring nuclide in materials where the isotopic abundance of that nuclide is natural.

13502.title: natural resistance-associated macrophage protein
13502.definition: Iron transporter that plays a critical role in macrophage activation and differentiation.

14871.title: natural selection
14871.definition: Evolutionary theory, originally proposed by Darwin, of the preferential survival and reproduction of organisms better adapted to their environment as a result of genetic adaptation.

08738.title: near edge X-ray absorption fine structure
08738.definition: Measurement method of X-ray absorption analysis similar to X-ray absorption near edge structure, but usually reserved for soft X-rays with photon energy less than \(\pu{1 keV}\).

09543.title: near-field scanning optical microscopy
09543.definition: Microscopy applied to the investigation of nanostructures that breaks the farfield resolution limit by exploiting the properties of evanescent waves.

08642.title: near-infrared radiation
08642.definition: Infrared radiation of which vacuum wavenumbers range from approximately \(\pu{12800 cm-1}\) to \(\pu{4800 cm-1}\) and wavelengths range from approximately \(\pu{780 nm}\) to \(\pu{2500 nm}\).

08509.title: nebulization
08509.definition: Conversion of a liquid into an aerosol consisting of droplets suspended in a gas stream.

10996.title: necropsy
10996.definition: Postmortem examination of the organs and body tissue of a non-human animal to determine cause of death or pathological condition.

NT06834.title: necrosis
NT06834.definition: Sum of morphological changes resulting from cell death by lysis and/or enzymatic degradation, usually affecting groups of cells in a tissue.

N04095.title: needle coke
N04095.definition: The commonly used term for a special type of coke with extremely high graphitizability resulting from a strong preferred parallel orientation of its turbostratic layer structure and a particular physical shape of the grains.

10250.title: needle trap
10250.definition: Gas-tight syringe with a sorbent-filled needle.

N04096.title: negative adsorption
N04096.definition: The depletion of one or more components in an interfacial layer.

14168.title: negative assay control
14168.definition: Experimental conditions designed to produce the signal reflective of the absence of the process under investigation.

NT07081.title: negative hyper-conjugation
NT07081.definition: The effect of donation of electron density from filled $\ce{\uppi\!}$ or $\ce{n_{\uppi\!}\mbox{-}orbitals}$ to the symmetry adapted $\ce{\upsigma\!^{\ast}\mbox{-}orbital(s)}$ of $\ce{\upsigma\!^{\ast}\mbox{-}bond(s)}$ of a molecular entity resulting in building $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}character}$ into bonds that nominally possess only $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}character}$. The consequences of the effect are, for example, in elongation of the $\ce{C–F}$ bond in the $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}fluoroethyl}$ anion and stabilization of the anti-periplanar conformation of fluoromethylamine.

N04098.title: negative ion
N04098.definition: An atom, radical, molecule or molecular moiety in the vapour phase which has gained one or more electrons thereby acquiring an electrically negative charge. The use of the term anion as an alternative is not recommended because of its connotations in solution chemistry.

13503.title: negative selection
13503.definition: Deletion by apoptosis in the thymus of T cells that recognize self-peptides presented by self-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules, thus preventing the development of autoimmune T cells. Negative selection of developing B cells is also thought to occur if they encounter high levels of self-antigen in the bone marrow.

09410.title: negative-ion yield
09410.definition: Number of negatively-charged secondary ions sputtered from a sample divided by total number of incident primary particles.

09544.title: negative-tone development
09544.definition: Process for revealing the latent image in a resist in which the exposed regions are less soluble in the developer than the unexposed regions.

12690.title: neglected disease
12690.definition: Term used to emphasise an imbalance between therapeutic needs and resource allocation.

15911.title: negligible risk
15911.definition:
Probability of adverse effects occurring that can reasonably be described as trivial.
Probability of adverse effects occurring that is so low that it cannot be reduced appreciably by increased regulation or investment of resources.

N04100.title: neighbouring group participation
N04100.definition: The direct interaction of the reaction centre (usually, but not necessarily, an incipient carbenium centre) with a lone pair of electrons of an atom or with the electrons of a $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}}$ or $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}bond}$ contained within the parent molecule but not conjugated with the reaction centre. A distinction is sometimes made between n-, $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}}$ and $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}participation}$. A rate increase due to neighbouring group participation is known as 'anchimeric assistance'. 'Synartetic acceleration' is the special case of anchimeric assistance ascribed to participation by electrons binding a substituent to a carbon atom in a $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}position}$ relative to the leaving group attached to the $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}carbon}$ atom. According to the underlying model, these electrons then provide a three-centre bond (or 'bridge') 'fastening together' (as the word 'synartetic' is intended to suggest) the $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}}$ and $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}carbon}$ atoms between which the charge is divided in the intermediate bridged ion formed (and in the transition state preceding its formation). The term synartetic acceleration is not widely used.

14873.title: nekton
14873.definition: Aggregate of actively swimming animals in a body of water ranging from microscopic organisms to whales.

14874.title: neo-Darwinism
14874.definition: Theory of biological evolution (widely accepted since the 1920s) based on Darwin’s theory of natural selection but incorporating the theories of later biologists regarding genes, inheritance, and mutation, particularly those of Weismann and Mendel.

13504.title: neoantigen
13504.definition: Antigen newly expressed on a tumor or virally infected cell, or arising after macromolecule-hapten binding.

11908.title: neocortex
11908.definition: Outer layer of the cerebral cortex that supports higher brain functions, especially cognitive function and language in humans.

N04103.title: neodymium laser
N04103.definition: A CW pulsed laser emitting radiation from excited The $\ce{Nd^{3+}}$ principally occurring around \(1.06\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) (the precise position depends on the matrix). The $\ce{Nd^{3+}}$ is present as a dopant in suitable crystals (e.g. yttrium–aluminium garnet, YAG) or in suitable glasses (phosphate, silicate, etc.).

09973.title: neoflavans
09973.definition: Neoflavans are compounds with a 4-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2$H$-1-benzopyran skeleton (see neoflavonoids). They may be substituted.

09974.title: neoflavones
09974.definition: Neoflavones are compounds with a 4-phenyl-2$H$-1-benzopyran-2-one (4-phenyl-2$H$-chromen-2-one) skeleton 11. They may be substituted.

13505.title: neonatal tolerance
13505.definition: Tolerance to specific foreign antigens induced by the exposure of a bird or mammal to the foreign antigens during embryonic or neonatal life, depending upon species.

10997.title: neonate
10997.definition: Newborn animal or human infant during the first four weeks of postnatal life.

14875.title: neophyte
14875.definition: Plant found newly in an area where it had not been recorded previously.

15913.title: neoplasia
15913.definition: New and abnormal formation of tissue as a tumor or growth by cell proliferation that is faster than normal and continues after the initial stimulus that initiated the proliferation has ceased.

10998.title: neoplasm
10998.definition: New and abnormal formation of tissue as a consequence of growth by cell proliferation, which may continue after the initial stimulus that initiated the proliferation has ceased, and which may develop into a tumor.

N04106.title: neper
N04106.definition: Unit, coherent with the SI, for expressing field levels, \(\rm{Np}=1\).

N04107.title: nephelometry
N04107.definition: Analytical methods which depend on the measurement of the intensity of scattered light emanating from an illuminated volume of an aerosol. The ratio of scattered intensity to illuminating intensity is compared with a standard of known properties.

15914.title: nephritis
15914.definition: Inflammation of the kidney, leading to kidney failure, usually accompanied by proteinuria, hematuria, edema, and hypertension.

15915.title: nephropathy
15915.definition: Any disease or abnormality of the kidney.

15916.title: nephrosis
15916.definition: Disease of the kidneys marked by degeneration of renal tubular epithelium.

15917.title: nephrotoxic
15917.definition: Chemically harmful to the cells of the kidney.

09068.title: Nernst equation
09068.definition: Fundamental equation in electrochemistry that describes the dependence of the equilibrium electrode potential on the composition of the contacting phases, written as a reduction: \[E_{\rm{eq}} = E^{\circ}\!-\!(RT/zF)\mathop \sum \limits_i \nu_i \ln(a_i)\] where \(E_{\rm{eq}}\) is the equilibrium electrode potential, \(E^{\circ}\) the standard electrode potential of the reaction, \(R\) the gas constant, \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature, \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(z\) the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, and \(\nu_{\rm{i}}\) are the stoichiometric coefficients (numbers of species) in the equation of the electrode reaction, positive for products and negative for reactants, while \(a_{\rm{i}}\) represents the activities of the species involved (most usually ions).

N04108.title: Nernst's diffusion layer
N04108.definition: A fictitious layer corresponding to the dotted straight lines of the diagram which shows the concentration profile along the direction perpendicular to an electrode surface. The thickness \(\delta \) of this layer is called the effective (or equivalent) thickness of the diffusion layer. Its definition is apparent from the figure. It is the thickness which the diffusion layer would have if the concentration profile were a straight line coinciding with the tangent to the true concentration profile at the interface, and that straight line were extended up to the point where the bulk concentration is reached. \(\delta \) has a formal significance only. It is simply another way of writing the mass transfer coefficient \(k_{\rm{d}}\) defined in terms of a resistivity instead of a conductivity. N04108.png

11909.title: nerve
11909.definition: Ensheathed bundle of nerve fibers that conveys information between the central nervous system and other regions of the body.

11910.title: nerve conduction study
11910.definition: Measure of the functional integrity of a nerve with a stimulating electrode, placed on the skin over the nerve, and a more distal recording electrode, to determine the velocity of the impulse that passes along the nerve between the electrodes.

11911.title: nerve conduction velocity
11911.definition: Rate of progression of a nerve impulse in a peripheral nerve or in its largest component nerve fibers.

11912.title: nerve fiber
11912.definition: Axon with its surrounding myelin sheath.

11913.title: nerve gas
11913.definition: Volatile chemical with neurotoxic features intended for use in warfare to disable or kill the organism rapidly after inhalation or skin contact, and classified as a prohibited weapon of mass destruction by The Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC).

11914.title: nerve growth factor
11914.definition: One of a family of proteins known as neurotropins that function as signaling molecules to induce axon growth, branching, elongation and survival of neurons.

11915.title: nerve root
11915.definition: Proximal end of a spinal nerve nearest its attachment to the spinal cord.

11916.title: nervous system
11916.definition: The entire neuronal apparatus, composed of both the central nervous system and the peripheral nervous system.

08273.title: net absorption cross-section
08273.definition: Molar Napierian absorption coefficient divided by the Avogadro constant. \(\sigma_{\rm{net}} = \kappa/N_{\rm{A}}\).

N04110.title: net current
N04110.definition: The sum of cathodic and anodic partial currents.

08380.title: net dephasing time
08380.definition: Measured time constant associated with spin-spin relaxation for loss of magnetization in the \(xy\) plane.

N04111.title: net electric charge
N04111.definition: The algebraic sum of the charges present at the surface of the particle divided by the elementary charge of the proton. The symbol \(z\) is also used for charge number of an ion.

09057.title: net faradaic current
09057.definition: Algebraic sum of faradaic currents flowing through an electrode.

N04109.title: net
N04109.definition: A two-dimensional lattice (in a particular range of surface coverage and temperature) into which the adsorbate is ordered, especially in some cases of localized adsorption.

14876.title: net reproductive rate
14876.definition: Expected number of females to be produced during the lifetime of a newborn female as estimated with a life table.

NT07626.title: net shaping
NT07626.definition: Production of an object in, or as close as possible to, its final shape prior to ceramization.

NT07562.title: network
NT07562.definition: Highly ramified structure in which essentially each constitutional unit is connected to each other constitutional unit and to the macroscopic phase boundary by many paths through the structure, the number of such paths increasing with the average number of intervening constitutional units; the paths must on average be co-extensive with the structure.

NT07604.title: network defect
NT07604.definition: Elastically ineffective chains in a polymer network.

N04112.title: network
N04112.definition: A highly ramified macromolecule in which essentially each constitutional unit is connected to each other constitutional unit and to the macroscopic phase boundary by many permanent paths through the macromolecule, the number of such paths increasing with the average number of intervening bonds; the paths must on the average be co-extensive with the macromolecule.

N04113.title: network polymer
N04113.definition: A polymer composed of one or more networks.

NT07603.title: network-chain molar mass
NT07603.definition: Number-average molar mass of polymer chains between two adjacent crosslinks or junction points in a polymer network.

10999.title: neural
10999.definition:
Pertaining to a nerve or to the nervous system.
Pertaining to the dorsal side of the vertebral bodies or to their precursors.

11917.title: neural activity
11917.definition: Metabolic and electrical activity of neurons.

11000.title: neural arch
11000.definition:
Dorsal bony covering of the spinal cord.
Cartilaginous structures surrounding the embryonicspinal cord.

11001.title: neural crest
11001.definition: Band of cells on either side of the neural tube.

11919.title: neural network
11919.definition: A functionally interconnected set of neurons, generally in the central nervous system.

11002.title: neural plate
11002.definition: Area in the middle of the early embryo that rolls up to form the neural tube.

11920.title: neural stem cell
11920.definition: Multipotent cell, with mitotic potential, that may serve as a precursor for neuroprogenitor cells.

11003.title: neural tube
11003.definition: Embryonic tubular structure that becomes the brain and spinal cord.

11004.title: neural tube defect
11004.definition: Failure of the neural tube to close properly during gastrulation.

11918.title: neuralgia
11918.definition: Paroxysmal pain extending along the course of one or more nerves.

11921.title: neurectomy
11921.definition: Excision of a nerve or part of a nerve.

11922.title: neurite
11922.definition: Outgrowth or projection of either an axon or a dendrite from the neuron cell body that is the structural basis of the neural network.

11923.title: neurite outgrowth
11923.definition: Phenomenon in which neurons tend to send out neurites to make contact with other nerve cells.

11925.title: neurobehavior core test battery
11925.definition: A set of seven tests, recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1983, to detect neurotoxicity in human populations

11005.title: neurobehavioral
11005.definition: Pertaining to the function of the nervous system as it relates to behavior.

11006.title: neuroblast
11006.definition: Cell derived from neural stem cell that will differentiate into a neuron.

11007.title: neuroblastoma
11007.definition: Malignant neoplasm consisting of poorly differentiated embryonic nerve cells (neuroblasts).

11926.title: neurodegenerative disease
11926.definition: Disease of the brain and (or) peripheral nervous system with progressive loss of neuronal function, accompanied by changes in morphology and subcellular organization of the nervous system.

11927.title: neurodevelopmental toxicity
11927.definition:
Adverse effect of a substance that disrupts developmental processes of the nervous system.
Toxicity in which the developing nervous system shows heightened sensitivity compared with the adult nervous system.

11008.title: neuroectoderm
11008.definition: Central region of the early embryonic ectoderm that will give rise to the brain and spinal cord, together with the neural crest cells that will form the peripheral nervous system.

11010.title: neuroendocrine
11010.definition: Pertaining to the nervous and endocrine systems in anatomical or functional relationship.

11009.title: neuroendocrine system
11009.definition: Combined cooperating network of the nervous system and hormonal systems.

11928.title: neurofibril
11928.definition: Part of a filamentous structure found in the cell body, axons, dendrites, and sometimes synaptic endings of neurons, consisting of bundles of neurofilaments and neurotubules.

11929.title: neurofibrillary tangle
11929.definition: Intracellular accumulation of aggregates of hyperphosphorylated tau protein or paired helical filaments consisting of the tau protein, a microtubule-associated protein that normally stabilizes the cytoskeleton.

11930.title: neurofibroma
11930.definition: Tumor of the peripheral nervous system representing an abnormal collection of Schwann cells and connective tissue.

11931.title: neurofilament
11931.definition: Class of intermediate filament of the neuronal cytoskeleton, providing support for the axon and dendrites.

11932.title: neurogenesis
11932.definition: Formation of nerve cells or of the nervous system.

11933.title: neurogenic
11933.definition:
Originating in, starting from, or caused by, the nervous system or nerve impulses.
Relating to neurogenesis.

11934.title: neurogenic shock
11934.definition: Condition of decreased blood pressure, slow heart rate and insufficient perfusion of the body with blood, caused by loss of autonomic control following acute trauma to the brain or spinal cord.

11011.title: neurohypophysis
11011.definition: Posterior lobe of the pituitary gland, involved in the storage and secretion of oxytocin and vasopressin.

11935.title: neuroimaging
11935.definition: Process of producing images of the structure or activity of the brain or other parts of the nervous system.

11936.title: neuroinflammation
11936.definition: Complex series of local immune responses within the nervous system to deal with a threat to the neural environment from infection, injury, or trauma.

11937.title: neuroleptic
11937.definition: Any of a class of psychotropic drugs used to treat psychosis, particularly schizophrenia.

11938.title: neurolysis
11938.definition:
Breakdown of nervous tissue from disease or injury.
Therapeutic destruction of a nerve or nerves to treat intractable pain.
Surgical freeing of a nerve from adhesions of the neural sheath.

11939.title: neuroma
11939.definition: Tumor made up largely of nerve cells.

11941.title: neuron-specific enolase
11941.definition: Enzyme of glucose metabolism, normally found in nervous tissue, that catalyzes the dehydration of 2-phosphoglycerate.

11940.title: neuronopathy
11940.definition: Disorder involving destruction of the cell bodies of neurons.

11984.title: neuropathic pain
11984.definition: Pain initiated by nerve injury, not mediated by nociception.

11942.title: neuropathological examination
11942.definition: Application of gross and histopathologic methods to study toxic changes in the morphology and histology of the nervous tissues and the brain.

11943.title: neuropathy
11943.definition: Pathological change in the peripheral nervous system.

11944.title: neuropathy target esterase
11944.definition: Enzyme that is phosphorylated by organophosphate compounds and is believed to be involved in the delayed neuropathy of organophosphates.

16265.title: neuropeptide
16265.definition: One of a group of small proteins (peptides) that serve as neurotransmitters in the brain, autonomic nervous system and neuroendocrine system.

11013.title: neuropore
11013.definition: Opening at either the cranial (caudal) or anterior (rostral) end of the neural tube before it completes closure in the early embryonic stage.

11945.title: neuroprogenitor cell
11945.definition: Precursor cell that is capable of differentiating into specific cell types of the nervous system.

11946.title: neuroprotective
11946.definition: Agent or property of an agent that protects neurons from damage and (or) from the process of aging or degeneration of the brain.

11947.title: neuropsychological testing
11947.definition: Assessment, under standardized conditions, of an individual’s brain function as it impacts upon cognitive function, thought processes, behavior and personality.

11948.title: neurotoxic
11948.definition: Poisonous to structures and (or) functions of the brain and nerves.

16266.title: neurotoxic esterase assay
16266.definition: Test in which delayed neuropathy resulting from hydrolytic cleavage of organophosphate esters is studied with measurement of the responsible enzyme activity,

11951.title: neurotoxic shellfish poisoning
11951.definition: Toxic shellfish poisoning characterized by nausea, vomiting, and mild neurological symptoms such as dysarthria, paresthesia, ataxia, and vertigo caused by ingestion of shellfish (specifically, bivalve molluscs) contaminated with the polyether brevetoxin and its derivatives produced by the dinoflagellate Karenia brevis.

11949.title: neurotoxicant
11949.definition: Substance that can produce functional or structural damage to the nervous system.

11950.title: neurotoxicology
11950.definition: Discipline applying principles of both neuroscience and toxicology to study the ability of certain substances to alter nervous system structure or function.

11952.title: neurotoxin
11952.definition: Any substance that has the potential to damage the nervous system.

11953.title: neurotransmission
11953.definition: Process by which a presynaptic cell, upon excitation, releases a specific agent (a neurotransmitter) that crosses the synapse to stimulate or inhibit the postsynaptic cell.

11955.title: neurotransmitter
11955.definition: Biochemical that is released upon excitation from a presynaptic membrane, crosses the synaptic space and binds to a receptor on the postsynaptic membrane, where it induces a signal that may be either stimulatory or inhibitory.

11014.title: neurotrophin
11014.definition: One of several protein growth factors that regulates development, maintenance, and function of the vertebrate nervous system.

11956.title: neurotropic
11956.definition: Having an affinity for nerve cells or tissues of the nervous system.

11958.title: neurovascular
11958.definition:
Relating to both the nervous system and the vascular system.
Relating to the vasomotor nerves that supply the walls of the blood vessels.

11015.title: neurulation
11015.definition: Formation of the embryonic neural plate and its rolling up into the neural tube.

12691.title: neutral antagonist
12691.definition: Ligand that blocks the responses of a receptor to both agonists and inverse agonists with the same intensity. It binds to the receptor without evoking any change of conformation or change to the ratio of activated to inactivated conformations.

13508.title: neutralization
13508.definition: Blocking by an antibody of the effects of a virus.

NT07522.title: neutralized gel
NT07522.definition: Gel containing acidic or basic groups that have been neutralized.

N04115.title: neutrino
N04115.definition: An elementary particle of negligible mass and zero electric charge. There are also a muon neutrino and tau neutrino.

N04116.title: neutron
N04116.definition: Nuclear particle of zero charge, spin quantum number \(\frac{1}{2}\) and a mass of \(1.008\ 664\ 904(14)\ \rm{u}\).

08739.title: neutron activation analysis
08739.definition: Activation analysis using neutrons as the incident particles.

N04117.title: neutron density
N04117.definition: The number of free neutrons divided by the containing volume. Partial densities may be defined for neutrons characterized by such parameters as energy and directions.

08740.title: neutron depth profiling
08740.definition: Measurement method of activation analysis for near-surface-depth light elements in which a thermal neutron or cold neutron (see: neutron energy) beam passes through a material with target nuclei that emit monoenergetic charged particles upon neutron absorption. The reduction of the energy of an emitted charged particle measures the depth of the target nuclei in a material.

08741.title: neutron diffraction analysis
08741.definition: Measurement method in which the diffraction of neutrons is applied to measure parameters of the atomic and/or magnetic structure of a material.

08742.title: neutron energy
08742.definition: Kinetic energy of a free neutron.

N04118.title: neutron multiplication
N04118.definition: The process in which a neutron produces on the average more than one neutron in a medium containing fissile material.

N04119.title: neutron number
N04119.definition: Number of neutrons in an atomic nucleus.

08743.title: neutron scattering analysis
08743.definition: Measurement method in which the elastic or inelastic scattering of neutrons by the target nuclei is applied to study the composition and structure of a material.

N04132.title: neutron temperature
N04132.definition: The temperature assigned to a population of neutrons when this population is approximated by a Maxwellian distribution.

13509.title: neutropenia
13509.definition: Abnormally low concentration of neutrophils in the blood.

13510.title: neutrophil
13510.definition: Granular leukocyte, the major circulating phagocytic polymorphonuclear granulocyte, having a nucleus with three to five lobes and fine cytoplasmic granules stainable by neutral dyes.

13511.title: neutrophil activation
13511.definition: Change in morphology and behavior of a neutrophil resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor.

N04133.title: neutrophilic organisms
N04133.definition: Organisms preferring a neutral medium for growth.

12692.title: new chemical entity
12692.definition: Drug that contains no active moiety previously approved for use by the national authority, such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

12693.title: new molecular entity
