12693.definition: Active ingredient that has never before been approved in any form by the national authority, such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

N04134.title: Newman projection
N04134.definition: A projection formula representing the spatial arrangement of bonds on two adjacent atoms in a molecular entity. The structure appears as viewed along the bond between these two atoms, and the bonds from them to other groups are drawn as projections in the plane of the paper. The bonds from the atom nearer to the observer are drawn so as to meet at the centre of a circle representing that atom. Those from the further atom are drawn as if projecting from behind the circle.

N04135.title: newton
N04135.definition: SI derived unit of force, \(\pu{N} = \pu{kg m s-2}\).

N04136.title: Newton black film
N04136.definition: In soap films, two types of equilibrium film are often observed, sometimes successively in the same system: one characterized by thicknesses of the order of \(7\ \rm{nm}\) or more which varies significantly with minor changes in composition such as ionic strength, and the other having a lesser thickness relatively independent of such changes. When a distinction is needed, the former are designated as common black films, and the latter as Newton black films. The current use of first or secondary for the common black film and of second, primary or Perrin's for the Newton black film is discouraged.

N04137.title: Newton diagram
N04137.definition: A vector diagram used to show the relationship between initial and final velocities or momenta in a two-particle scattering process. It is commonly used to relate laboratory and centre-of-mass coordinates.

N04138.title: Newtonian fluid
N04138.definition: A fluid in which the components of the stress tensor are linear functions of the first spatial derivatives of the velocity components. These functions involve two material parameters (taken as constants throughout the fluid, although depending on ambient temperature and pressure).

11905.title: NG2 cell
11905.definition: Glial cell of the central nervous system, distinct from an oligodendrocyte or astrocyte, that may serve as a precursor of oligodendrocytes, and that takes its name from expression of proteoglycan NG2.

14877.title: niche
14877.definition: Group of conditions and resources, facilitating but limiting survival, growth, and reproduction of a defined group of organisms or species.

14878.title: niche preemption
14878.definition: Rapid use and preemption of resources by a species that exploits them to the exclusion or severe disadvantage of another species.

14879.title: niche width
14879.definition: Term referring to the area which a species could physically inhabit.

11959.title: nicotinic
11959.definition: Referring to a substance or effect that mimics acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction, at autonomic ganglia and at other locations in the brain.

11960.title: nicotinic receptor
11960.definition: One of the two main classes of acetylcholine receptors, ligand-gated ion channels that open upon binding nicotine as well as acetylcholine.

N04140.title: nido-
N04140.definition: An affix used in names to denote a nest-like structure, especially a boron skeleton that is almost closed.

N04141.title: Nier–Johnson geometry
N04141.definition: An arrangement for a double-focusing mass spectrometer in which a deflection of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) radians in a radial electrostatic field analyser is followed by a magnetic deflection of \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) radians. The electrostatic analyser uses a symmetrical object-image arrangement and the magnetic analyser is used asymmetrically.

N04142.title: NIH shift
N04142.definition: The intramolecular hydrogen migration which can be observed in enzymatic and chemical hydroxylations of aromatic rings. It is evidenced by appropriate deuterium labelling, i.e.  In enzymatic reactions the NIH shift is generally thought to derive from the rearrangement of arene oxide intermediates, but other pathways have been suggested. (NIH stands for U.S. National Institutes of Health where the shift was discovered.)

09120.title: Nikolsky–Eisenman equation
09120.definition: Equation describing the contribution of interfering ions, \(i\), to the electrode potential of an ion-selective electrode that is mainly dominated by the primary ion \(\ce{X}\). \[E = {\rm{const}} + \frac{RT}{z_{\rm{X}}F} \ln \left(a_{\ce{X}} + \sum\limits_i K_{{\ce{X}},i}^{\rm{pot}}a_{i}^{(z_{\ce{X}}/z_i)} \right)\] where \(E\) is the measured electrode potential of an ISE when the only variables are activities in the test solution. \(R\) is the gas constant, \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature, \(z_{\rm{X}}\) and \(z_{\rm{i}}\) are the numbers of electrons transferred by the analyte ion \(\ce{X}\) and \(i\), respectively, \(F\) is the Faraday constant, \(a_{\rm{X}}\) and \(a_{\rm{i}}\) the activity of \(\ce{X}\) and \(i\), respectively, and \(K_{\ce{X},i}^{\rm{pot}}\) is the potentiometric selectivity coefficient for interfering ion \(i\) with respect to the primary ion \(\ce{X}\).

N04143.title: nimbostratus cloud
N04143.definition: An amorphous, dark grey, rainy cloud layer reaching almost to the ground; \(300{-}600\ \rm{m}\) vertical velocities of \(0.05{-}0.2\ \rm{m s}^{-1}\).

14880.title: not in my backyard principle
14880.definition: Public acceptance of necessary provisions (e.g., waste incinerators) provided they do not affect the individual’s quality of life.

14881.title: nine aspects of disease association
14881.definition: Nine aspects of evidence, defined by Bradford-Hill (1965), fostering the accuracy of linkage between a risk factor and disease: strength of association, consistency of association, specificity of association, temporal association, biological gradient (dose-response) in the association, biological plausibility, coherence of the association, experimental support of association, and analogy.

11961.title: nine-hole box test
11961.definition: Behavioral test based on the five-choice serial reaction time task, which allows the study of attention based on a test animal learning from which hole (typically one of five open holes in an arc of nine) a visual (light) cue was given, with a food pellet reward for nose-poking the correct hole.

11016.title: nipple
11016.definition: Projection on the apex of the breast through which the ducts of the milk-producing glands open.

11962.title: Nissl body
11962.definition: Granular structure consisting of rough endoplasmic reticulum, found in neurons.

N04144.title: nitramines
N04144.definition: Amines substituted at N with a nitro group (a contracted form of N-nitroamines); they are thus amides of nitric acid, and the class is composed of nitramide, $\ce{O2NNH2}$, and its derivatives formed by substitution.

N04145.title: nitrenes
N04145.definition: The neutral compound $\ce{HN{:}}$ having univalent nitrogen, and its derivatives $\ce{RN}$. Aminylenes is a recognized but less widely used synonym. Other names that have been used include aminediyls, imidogens, azenes. They may exist in either a singlet or a triplet electronic state (four spin-paired electrons, or two spin-paired and two with parallel spins, respectively), e.g. $\ce{CH3N{:}}$ methylnitrene.Until the 1960s, nitrenes had a totally different meaning: analogues of nitrones in which the double-bonded oxygen is replaced by double-bonded carbon, thus azomethine ylides.

N04146.title: nitrenium ions
N04146.definition: The cation ($\ce{H2N{:}^{+}}$) and its N-hydrocarbyl derivatives ($\ce{R2N{:}^{+}}$), in which the nitrogen has a positive charge, and two unshared electrons. A synonymous but less widely used term is aminylium ions. The alkylidene derivatives of ($\ce{H2N{:}^{+}}$), ($\ce{R2C=N{:}^{+}}$), still belong to the class nitrenium ions, but are more precisely designated by the term iminylium ions.

13512.title: nitric oxide
13512.definition: Generic term for nitrogen monoxide species, including nitrosonium ion, nitric oxide radical, etc., that can function in a cell-signaling capacity.

N04147.title: nitrification
N04147.definition: Sequential oxidation of ammonium salts to nitrite and nitrate by microorganisms.

N04148.title: nitrile imides
N04148.definition: Ylides having the structure . Also known as 'nitrile imines' or 'nitrilimines', especially in the German literature.

N04153.title: nitrile ylides
N04153.definition: 1,3-dipolar compounds having the structure:  The uncharged canonical form  is called an alkylidene- (or hydrocarbylidene-) amino carbene; the name iminyl carbene is incorrect because iminyl is not a recognized prefix for $\ce{–N=CR2}$.

N04151.title: nitriles
N04151.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RC#N}$; thus C-substituted derivatives of hydrocyanic acid, $\ce{HC#N}$. In systematic nomenclature, the suffix nitrile denotes the triply bound $\ce{#N}$ atom, not the carbon atom attached to it.

N04155.title: nitrilium betaines
N04155.definition: Derivatives of nitriles having the general structure $\ce{R–C#N^{+}–Y^{−}}$. A subclass of 1,3-dipolar compounds including nitrile imides, nitrile oxides, nitrile sulfides and nitrile ylides.

N04156.title: nitrilium ions
N04156.definition: Cations derived formally by attachment of one hydron to the nitrogen atom of a nitrile and hydrocarbyl derivatives thereof. E.g.  benzonitrilium.

N04157.title: nitrimines
N04157.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{O2NN=CR2}$ (also called N-nitroimines).

N04158.title: nitro compounds
N04158.definition: Compounds having the nitro group, $\ce{NO2}$ (free valence on nitrogen), which may be attached to carbon, nitrogen (as in nitramines), or oxygen (as in nitrates), among other elements (in the absence of specification, C-nitro compounds are usually implied).

N04159.title: nitrogen fixation
N04159.definition: The assimilation of atmospheric nitrogen by microbial reduction to ammonia and conversion into organonitrogen compounds such as amino acids. Only a limited number of microorganisms are able to fix nitrogen.

N04160.title: nitrogen laser
N04160.definition: A source of pulsed semi-coherent superradiance mainly around \(337\ \rm{nm}\). The lasing species is molecular nitrogen.

N04164.title: nitrones
N04164.definition: The N-oxides of imines, that have the structure $\ce{R2C=N+(O−)R'}$ ($\ce{R'} \neq \ce{H}$). Synonymous with azomethine oxides. N-Oxides $\ce{R2C=N+(O−)H}$ may be included.

N04166.title: nitrosamides
N04166.definition: Although this term has, regrettably, been used to mean the N-nitroso derivatives of amides, logically it refers to amides of nitrous acid; the unstable parent compound $\ce{H2NNO}$ is, in fact, named nitrosamide, but its derivatives formed by substitution with hydrocarbyl groups are by long custom called nitrosamines.

N04167.title: nitrosamines
N04167.definition: N-Nitroso amines, compounds of the structure $\ce{R2NNO}$. Compounds $\ce{RNHNO}$ are not ordinarily isolable, but they, too, are nitrosamines. The name is a contraction of N-nitrosoamine and, as such, does not require the N locant.

15918.title: nitrosative stress
15918.definition: Adverse effects occurring when the generation of reactive nitrogen species in a system exceeds the system’s ability to neutralize and eliminate them; nitrosative stress may lead to nitrosylation reactions that can alter protein structure, thus inhibiting normal function.

N04169.title: nitroso compounds
N04169.definition: Compounds having the nitroso group, $\ce{–NO}$. attached to carbon, or to another element, most commonly nitrogen or oxygen.

08168.title: NMR exchange spectroscopy
08168.definition: Two-dimensional NMR technique producing cross peaks corresponding to site-to site chemical exchange. The cross-peak amplitudes carry information about exchange rates.

N04174.title: no carrier added
N04174.definition: A preparation of a radioactive isotope which is essentially free from stable isotopes of the element in question.

NT06911.title: no observed adverse effect level
NT06911.definition: Greatest concentration or amount found by experiment or observation, which causes no detectable adverse alteration of morphology, functional capacity, growth, development, or life span of the target organism under defined conditions.

15919.title: no-acceptable-daily-intake-allocated
15919.definition: This expression is applicable to a substance for which the available information is not sufficient to establish its safety, or when the specifications for identity and purity are not adequate, or when the available data show that the substance is hazardous and should not be used.

15921.title: no-effect dose
15921.definition: Amount of a substance that has no effect on the organism.

15922.title: no-effect level
15922.definition: Maximum dose (of a substance) that produces no detectable changes under defined conditions of exposure.

N04176.title: no-load indication
N04176.definition: The deflection or rest point (no-load reading) multiplied by the value of the division for zero load (rider at zero); symbol \(i_{0}\).

14885.title: no-observed-effect concentration
14885.definition: Special case of the no-observed-effect level (NOEL), commonly used in aquatic toxicology.

N04209.title: no-observed-effect-level
N04209.definition: Greatest concentration or amount of a substance, found by experiment or observation, that causes no alterations of morphology, functional capacity, growth, development, or life span of target organisms distinguishable from those observed in normal (control) organisms of the same species and strain under the same defined conditions of exposure.

14886.title: no-response level
14886.definition: Maximum dose of a substance at which no specified response is observed in a defined population and under defined conditions of exposure.

11963.title: nociception
11963.definition: Physiological response to harmful stimuli by specialized nerve endings that transmit a signal perceived as pain by the brain.

13494.title: NOD-like receptor
13494.definition: Any of a large family of cytoplasmic proteins containing a nucleotide-binding domain and leucine-rich repeats (LRRs), involved in regulation of inflammation and apoptosis; many family members are thought to function as pattern recognition receptors (PRRs).

11017.title: nodal
11017.definition: Growth factor of the transforming growth factor \(\upbeta\) (TGF-\(\upbeta\)) superfamily, coded by a gene designated NODAL, that plays crucial roles in embryogenesis, particularly in signalling from the primitive streak to the mesoderm to establish left-right asymmetry as well as aspects of stem cell differentiation.

NT07082.title: nodal plane
NT07082.definition: A plane of a system in which the value of the orbital wave-function equals zero. This plane defines a region of zero electron density for the orbital.

10137.title: node
10137.definition: Locations in an artificial neural network that carry values that are calculated from values of connected nodes and weights by a transfer.

11964.title: node of Ranvier
11964.definition: Short interval in the myelin sheath of a nerve fiber where the axon is invested only by scant cytoplasmic processes of the neighboring Schwann cells or, in the central nervous system, of oligodendroglia cells.

15920.title: nodule
15920.definition: Small node or boss that is solid and can be detected by touch.

11018.title: noggin
11018.definition: Signaling protein released by the notochord, important in somite patterning and nervous system development.

N04175.title: noise
N04175.definition: The random fluctuations occurring in a signal that are inherent in the combination of instrument and method.

09991.title: nominal indication
09991.definition: Nominal property value provided by an examining system.

N04177.title: nominal linear flow
N04177.definition: The volumetric flowrate of the mobile phase divided by the area of the cross section of the column (\(\rm{cm min}^{-1}\)) i.e. the linear flowrate in a part of the column not containing packing.

11543.title: nominal mass
11543.definition: Mass of a molecular ion or molecule calculated using the isotope mass of the most abundant constituent element isotope of each element rounded to the nearest integer value and multiplied by the number of atoms of each element.

09979.title: nominal property
09979.definition: Property of a phenomenon, body, or substance, where the property has no size.

09996.title: nominal property value
09996.definition: Feature common to equivalent individual nominal properties.

10015.title: nominal property value coverage probability
10015.definition: Probability that the set of true nominal property values of an examinand is contained within a specified nominal property value coverage set.

10014.title: nominal property value coverage set
10014.definition: Subset of the nominal property value set containing the true nominal property value(s) of an examinand with a stated probability, based on the information available.

09997.title: nominal property value set
09997.definition: Set of possible nominal property values for nominal properties of a given kind-of-nominal-property.

10020.title: nominal reference material
10020.definition: Material, sufficiently homogeneous and stable with reference to a specified nominal property, that has been established to be fit for its intended use in an examination.

08274.title: nominal spectral resolution
08274.definition: Spectral resolution setting on an instrument that a user sets to record a spectrum.

N04178.title: nominally labelled tracer
N04178.definition: A tracer in which the label is present mainly in a specified position.

09929.title: non-aqueous capillary electrophoresis
09929.definition: Capillary electrophoresis, which uses water-free organic solutions and modifiers to produce ions in solution.

15923.title: non-bioenvironmental transformation
15923.definition: Change in the chemical or physical nature of a substance occurring as a result of physicochemical conditions and independent of any biological system.

N04184.title: non-calorimetric thermophysical measurements
N04184.definition: These include (\(p\),\(V\), \(T\)) measurements, saturated density measurements, and any other measurements which give information on the (\(p\),\(V\), \(T\)) surface of a fluid.

08036.title: non-certified property value
08036.definition: Property value that is provided for information only but is not certified by a reference material producer.

09875.title: non-covalent interactions
09875.definition: Interactions between biomolecules or within a biomolecule (e.g. hydrogen bonds, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals forces) taking part in the stabilization of proper biomolecule structure and intermolecular interactions.

NT07425.title: non-crossing rule
NT07425.definition: Electronic states of the same symmetry cannot cross along a reaction coordinate.

N04187.title: non-crystalline electrodes
N04187.definition: Electrodes in which a support matrix, containing an ion exchanger (either cationic or anionic), a plasticizer solvent, and possibly an uncharged, selectivity-enhancing species, forms the ion-selective membrane which is usually interposed between two aqueous solutions. The support used can be either macroporous [e.g. poly(propylene carbonate) filter, glass frit, etc.] or microporous (e.g. 'thirsty' glass or inert polymeric material such as PVC) yielding with the ion-exchanger and the solvent a 'solidified' homogeneous mixture. These electrodes exhibit a response due to the presence of the ion-exchange material in the membrane. The solvent-polymeric-membrane is an example.

09110.title: non-crystalline membrane
09110.definition: Kind of ion-selective membranes used in an ISE which is a support matrix, containing an ion exchanger (either cationic or anionic), a plasticizer solvent, and possibly an uncharged, selectivity-enhancing species, form the ion-selective membrane which is usually interposed between two aqueous solutions. The matrix can be either macroporous (e.g., poly(propylene carbonate) filter, glass frit, etc.) or microporous (e.g., “thirsty” glass or polymeric material such as \(\ce{PVC}\)) yielding with the ion-exchanger and the solvent a “solidified” homogeneous mixture.

N04188.title: non-destructive activation analysis
N04188.definition: An activation analysis procedure in which, after the irradiation, no chemical and physical operations are applied which cause a change of any properties of the sample.

08643.title: non-dispersive infrared spectroscopies
08643.definition: Kinds of infrared spectroscopy in which the effect of the sample on the radiation from the source is measured as a whole without exploring the dependence on wavenumber.

N04191.title: non-draining
N04191.definition: An adjective describing a chain macromolecule that behaves in a hydrodynamic field as though the solvent within the domain of the macromolecule were virtually immobilized with respect to the macromolecule.

N04192.title: non-equilibrium reaction
N04192.definition: If the reactants in a chemical reaction are not initially present in a Boltzmann distribution the reaction is referred to as a non-equilibrium reaction.

N04193.title: non-graphitic carbon
N04193.definition: All varieties of solids consisting mainly of the element carbon with two-dimensional long-range order of the carbon atoms in planar hexagonal networks, but without any measurable crystallographic order in the third direction (c-direction) apart from more or less parallel stacking.

N04194.title: non-graphitizable carbon
N04194.definition: A non-graphitic carbon which cannot be transformed into graphitic carbon solely by high-temperature treatment up to \(3300\ \rm{K}\) under atmospheric pressure or lower pressure.

13514.title: non-Hodgkin lymphoma
13514.definition: Any of various malignant lymphomas characterized by the absence of Reed–Sternberg cells and producing symptoms similar to those of Hodgkin disease.

NT06942.title: non-ideal chromatography
NT06942.definition: Chromatographic process with normal peak-broadening effects.

NT06943.title: non-ideal, linear chromatography
NT06943.definition: Chromatographic process, where the retention is governed by a linear distribution isotherm and normal peak-broadening takes place.

NT06945.title: non-ideal, non-linear chromatography
NT06945.definition: Chromatographic process, where both isotherm curvature and other peak-broadening processes (such as diffusion) contribute to the peak shape.

N04195.title: non-isotopic labelling
N04195.definition: Labelling in which the resulting product has a different chemical composition from the initial one.

NT07085.title: non-Kekulé molecules
NT07085.definition: Molecules that are fully conjugated, but each of whose Kekulé structures contains at least two atoms that are not $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}bonded}$. Examples of non-Kekule hydrocarbons are trimethylenemethane (2-methylidenepropane-1,3-diyl) 1, m-benzodiquinomethane (benzene-1,2-diyldimethyl) 2, and 1,2,4,5 - tetramethylenebenzene (benzene-1,2,4,5-tetrayltetramethyl) 3.

08190.title: non-Kekulé structure
08190.definition: Compound with unpaired electrons for which no Lewis structures are possible with all bonding electrons paired in single or double bonds.

NT06940.title: non-linear chromatography
NT06940.definition: Chromatographic process, where the retention is governed by a non-linear distribution isotherm.

NT06936.title: non-linear distribution isotherm
NT06936.definition: A distribution isotherm which is not linear.

10101.title: non-linear iterative partial least squares
10101.definition: Iterative decomposition of a data matrix to give principal components.

N04197.title: non-linear optical effect
N04197.definition: An effect brought about by electromagnetic radiation the magnitude of which is not proportional to the irradiance. Non-linear optical effects of importance to photochemistry are harmonic frequency generation, lasers, Raman shifting, upconversion, and others.

NT07178.title: non-linear optical polymer
NT07178.definition: Polymer that exhibits an optical effect brought about by electromagnetic radiation such that the magnitude of the effect is not proportional to the irradiance.

NT07426.title: non-linear optical techniques
NT07426.definition: Collective name applied to techniques related to non-linear optical effects.

N04196.title: non-linearity error
N04196.definition: An error caused by any deviation from linearity of the response of the detector to the measured radiant power.

08926.title: non-metal-mediated atom-transfer radical polymerization
08926.definition: Atom-transfer radical polymerization in which the deactivation of the radicals involves reversible atom transfer or reversible group transfer to a non-metallic reagent.

13515.title: non-obese diabetic mouse
13515.definition: Genetically modified mouse with a susceptibility to spontaneous development of automimmune diabetes mellitus type I.

N04199.title: non-polarized interphases
N04199.definition: Interphases for which the exchange of common charged components between the phases proceeds unhindered.

10284.title: non-porous membrane
10284.definition: Membrane in which permeation occurs by processes other than flow through pores.

N04200.title: non-radiative decay
N04200.definition: The disappearance of an excited species due to a radiationless transition.

08744.title: non-radiative quenching
08744.definition: Deactivation of an electronically-excited state by interaction with the external environment through a non-radiative process.

12792.title: non-reversing heat flow
12792.definition: In modulated-temperature DSC, the component of the total heat flow that is out-of-phase with the temperature modulation.

15343.title: non-saturating solute
15343.definition: Solute which forms an unsaturated solution.

13516.title: non-self
13516.definition: Of, relating to, or designating a cell or tissue that has not been produced by the individual organism.

N04204.title: non-specific adsorption
N04204.definition: Ions approach an interface differently depending on the forces in play. Ions are non-specifically adsorbed (positively or negatively) when they are subjected in the interphase only to long-range coulombic interactions (attraction or repulsion). They are believed to retain their solvation shell, and in the position of closest approach to the interface they are separated from it by one or more molecular layers.

09876.title: non-specific binding
09876.definition: Binding of a protein to deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) independent of the nucleotide sequence or the conformation of the DNA, often with a strong contribution of electrostatic interaction between the negatively charged sugar-phosphate backbone of the DNA and basic amino acid residues of the protein.

08511.title: non-specific emission or attenuation
08511.definition: Electromagnetic radiation, within the bandpass filter used, emitted by, or absorption caused by, atoms, molecules and radicals that are subject to the atomizer by all components, apart from the analyte, that are present there during measurement.

N04205.title: non-uniform corrosion
N04205.definition: Corrosion is non-uniform if the time average of the corrosion current through a unit area depends on its position on the surface. Non-uniform corrosion can be due to inhomogeneities of structure or of composition of the corroding material, or to inhomogeneities of the environment. Special cases of non-uniform corrosion such as pitting or intergranular corrosion are sometimes called localized corrosion.

12273.title: non-uniform dispersion
12273.definition: Dispersion of particles not identical with respect to size, shape, or constitution.

N04206.title: non-uniform polymer
N04206.definition: A polymer comprising molecules non-uniform with respect to relative molecular mass or constitution or both.

08381.title: non-uniform sampling
08381.definition: Technique employed within a high dimensionality nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment that acquires only a subset of the data points traditionally acquired linearly thus enabling a reduction in experiment time or an increased resolution in the resultant spectra.

N04207.title: non-vertical energy transfer
N04207.definition: Energy transfer process with a low Franck–Condon factor because the nuclear geometries of the minima on the ground- and excited-state potential energy surfaces of the donor or of the acceptor are strongly displaced.

N04180.title: nonadiabatic coupling
N04180.definition: This is momentum coupling between two adiabatic potential-energy surfaces.

14310.title: nonaqueous dispersion
14310.definition: Dispersion in which the continuous phase is nonaqueous.

N04183.title: nonbonded interactions
N04183.definition: Intramolecular attractions or repulsions between atoms that are not directly linked to each other, affecting the thermodynamic stability of the chemical species concerned.

NT07083.title: nonbonding molecular orbital
NT07083.definition: A molecular orbital whose occupation by electrons does not contribute (or contributes insignificantly) to the binding energy of the molecule. Generally, a nonbonding MO represents the highest occupied molecular orbital of a molecule.

N04185.title: nonclassical carbocation
N04185.definition: A carbocation the ground state of which has delocalized (bridged) bonding $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}}$ or $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}electrons}$. (N.B. Allylic and benzylic carbocations are not considered nonclassical.)

NT07084.title: nonclassical structure
NT07084.definition: The structure of molecules or molecular ions that escapes description in terms of conventional rules of valency and stereochemistry. Nonclassical structures are characteristic of carbonium ions with hypercoordinated (see hypercoordination) carbon atoms, e.g., methanium ion 1, pyramidal dication $\ce{C6H6^{2+}}$ 2 (isomeric to benzene dication), and the molecular species whose structure cannot be adequately represented by the equilibrium (2-norbornyl cation, 3) or resonance of two or more classical structures. From the stereochemical point of view, those structures are assigned to the nonclassical type for which all tetracoordinate carbon bonds extend into a single hemisphere, i.e., the valence angle of a carbon atom is greater than $\pu{180\!^{\circ}}$. A hypothetical example is pyramidane, 4, the structure of which corresponds to a local minimum on the $\ce{C5H4}$ potential energy surface.

12694.title: noncompetitive antagonist
12694.definition: Functional antagonist that either binds irreversibly to a receptor or to a site distinct from that of the natural agonist.

14169.title: noncompetitive binding assay
14169.definition: Assay in which the interaction of a ligand with a receptor is measured without a requirement for added competing agents. It can be homogeneous or heterogeneous.

13513.title: nondepleting antibody
13513.definition: Cell surface antibody that does not provoke attack by killer cells and thus does not provoke depletion of a group of cells in the body, usually referring to B cells.

11019.title: nondisjunction
11019.definition: Failure of chromosomes to separate during meiosis, resulting in an uneven distribution of chromosomes in the two gametes (\(\pu{24}\) and \(\pu{22}\) in humans).

15924.title: nonionising radiation
15924.definition: Electromagnetic radiation of low energy that is not capable of causing ionization.

10102.title: nonlinear mapping
10102.definition: Projection of objects defined in a multivariate space onto two- or three-dimensional space so that the distances between objects are preserved as well as possible.

15925.title: nonoccupational exposure
15925.definition: Environmental exposure outside the workplace to substances that are otherwise associated with particular work environments and (or) activities and processes that occur there.

N04202.title: nonselectively labelled
N04202.definition: An isotopically labelled compound is designated as nonselectively labelled when the position(s) and the number of the labelling nuclide(s) are both undefined.

14883.title: nonstochastic health effects
14883.definition: Effects that are dependent on the magnitude of the dose in excess of a threshold.

14884.title: nontarget organisms
14884.definition: Organisms that are not the intended targets of a particular use of a pesticide.

N04210.title: nor-
N04210.definition: Affix used to denote the elimination of one methylene group from a side chain of a parent structure (including a methyl group).

11020.title: noradrenaline
11020.definition: Catecholamine hormone acting as a postganglionic adrenergic mediator at $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}}$ and $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}adrenergic}$ receptors.

N04211.title: normal
N04211.definition: The term 'normal' in e.g. 'normal boiling temperature' means the value at a pressure of \(101325\ \rm{Pa}\).

08644.title: normal coordinate
08644.definition: Formal mathematical description of a normal vibration. When the potential energy, \(V\), is harmonic and the kinetic energy, \(T\), is calculated in the limit of infinitesimally small displacements, the normal coordinates are defined as independent entities such that '(for non-linear molecules)'\[V = ½\sum_{k=1}^{3N-6}\lambda_{k}Q_{k}^{2}\ {\rm{and}}\ T = ½\sum_{k=1}^{3N-6}\dot Q_{k}^{2}\]where \(\lambda_{k}\) is the \(k^{\rm{th}}\) eigenvalue and \(\dot {Q}\) is \(\partial Q/\partial t\). Normal coordinate \(Q_{k}\) is related to the internal displacement coordinates, \(R_{i}\), through the elements, \(L_{ik} = \partial R_{i}/\partial Q_{k}\) of the \(k^{\rm{th}}\) column of the eigenvector matrix \(\boldsymbol{L}\). Normal coordinates are not independent when the potential energy is anharmonic, or the displacements are not infinitesimal.

08645.title: normal coordinate analysis
08645.definition: Calculation of the normal modes of vibrations of a molecule or crystal under the assumptions that the potential energy is harmonic and the displacements from equilibrium are infinitesimal.

08646.title: normal dispersion of the refractive index
08646.definition: Slow decrease of real refractive index of a material in a non-absorbing spectral region far from regions of strong absorption as the wavenumber decreases.

15140.title: normal equivalent deviation
15140.definition: Proportion dying in a toxicity test expressed in terms of standard deviations from the mean of a normal curve.

08647.title: normal incidence
08647.definition: Incidence of a beam of electromagnetic radiation when the angle of incidence \(\theta = \pu{0\!^{\circ}}\), i.e., the incident radiation beam is normal to the surface.

08648.title: normal mode
08648.definition: One of the \(3N - 6\) (\(3N - 5\) for a linear molecule) modes of vibration that would add to give the total vibrational motion in a molecule if the interatomic potential were strictly quadratic in the displacements from equilibrium.

08512.title: normal plasma analytical zone
08512.definition: Inductively-coupled plasma volume mainly responsible for emission of analytically-useful light because processes leading to excited species, such as droplet desolvation, element vaporization, atomization (or ionization) and excitation have been completed.

09142.title: normal pulse voltammetry
09142.definition: Voltammetry in which potential pulses of amplitude increasing by a constant increment and with a pulse width of \(\pu{2 to 200 ms}\) are superimposed on a constant initial potential. The current is sampled at the end of the pulse and then plotted versus the potential of the pulse. Sigmoidal wave-shaped voltammograms are obtained. See figure.(a) Waveform for normal pulse voltammetry (not to scale). Typical values for pulse parameters are \(\tau = \pu{1 s}\), \(t_{\rm{p}} = \pu{50 ms}\), \(E_{\rm{p}} = \pu{2 mV}\), \(E_{\rm{step}} = \pu{2 mV}\). Sampling interval indicated by horizontal curly brackets is typically \(\pu{15 ms}\). (b) Normal pulse voltammogram.

N04215.title: normal region
N04215.definition: Region for which the rate constants increase with increasing exergonicity of the reaction in plots relating rate constants for electron transfer, or quantities related to it, with the standard Gibbs energy for the reaction (\(\Delta _{\rm{ET}}G^{\rm{o}}\)). This region is predicted by the Marcus theory for outer-sphere electron transfer for the case of \(-\Delta_{\rm{ET}} G^{\circ} \leq \lambda \) in the Marcus equation.

N04216.title: normal stress
N04216.definition: Force acting normally to a surface divided by the area of the surface.

N04214.title: normal-phase chromatography
N04214.definition: An elution procedure in which the stationary phase is more polar then the mobile phase. This term is used in liquid chromatography to emphasize the contrast to reversed-phase chromatography.

NT07086.title: normalization
NT07086.definition: A mathematical procedure which ensures that the integral of the square of modulus of a wave-function over all space equals 1. The constant required to ensure that a wave-function is normalized is termed the normalization constant.

09545.title: normalized image log slope
09545.definition: Measure of the information content of the aerial image and represents an energy (intensity) gradient at the position of the nominal line edge.

08649.title: normalized tunnelling intensity
08649.definition: Second differential of intensity with respect to bias voltage divided by first differential of intensity with respect to bias voltage.

14887.title: normit
14887.definition: Metameter equal to the normal equivalent deviation (NED). The resulting analysis of dose– or concentration-effect data with the normit metameter is often called normit analysis and is essentially equivalent to probit analysis.

N04219.title: Norrish Type I photoreaction
N04219.definition: $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}Cleavage}$ of an excited carbonyl compound leading to an acyl-alkyl radical pair (from an acyclic carbonyl compound) or an acyl-alkyl diradical (from a cyclic carbonyl compound) as a primary photoproduct.

N04218.title: Norrish Type II photoreaction
N04218.definition: Intramolecular abstraction of a $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}hydrogen}$ by an excited carbonyl compound to produce a 1,4-diradical as a primary photoproduct.

NT07427.title: Norrish–Yang reaction
NT07427.definition: Photochemical process leading to the formation of cyclobutanols from excited carbonyl compounds by intramolecular $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}hydrogen}$ abstraction (Norrish Type II photoreaction) and subsequent 1,4-diradical combination.

09708.title: Northern blot
09708.definition: Technique involving hybridization of nucleic acids  used to study gene expression at the level of ribonucleic acid (RNA).

11966.title: nose-poke test
11966.definition: Test allowing study of attention deficit based on noting the success of a test animal in gaining a food pellet reward for nosing the correct hole in a box.

15927.title: nosocomial
15927.definition: Associated with a hospital or infirmary, especially used of diseases that may result from treatment in such an institution.

11021.title: notochord
11021.definition: Rod-shaped structure of cells derived from mesoderm, lying ventral to the neural tube and defining the primitive axis of the embryo.

N04224.title: nth order phase transition
N04224.definition: A transition in which the molar Gibbs energy (or chemical potential) and its \((n - 1)\)th-order derivatives are continuous, whereas the \(n\)th-order derivatives with respect to temperature and pressure are discontinuous at the transition point.

10078.title: nth-order effect
10078.definition: Effect of a factor where the term is a factor raised to the power \(n\).

08745.title: nuclear capture
08745.definition: Process in which an atomic nucleus acquires an additional particle.

N04226.title: nuclear chemistry
N04226.definition: The part of chemistry which deals with the study of nuclei and nuclear reactions using chemical methods.

N04228.title: nuclear disintegration
N04228.definition: Nuclear decay involving a splitting into more nuclei or the emission of particles.

08382.title: nuclear electric quadrupole moment
08382.definition: Parameter that describes the effective shape of the ellipsoid of nuclear charge distribution.

13518.title: nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells
13518.definition: Protein complex that controls the transcription of genes involved in cytokine production, cellular adhesion, inflammation, and apoptosis.

13517.title: nuclear factor of activated T cells
13517.definition: Transcription factor involved in rapid cell response to stress, such as injury or invading pathogens, and in cell proliferation and survival.

N04229.title: nuclear fission
N04229.definition: The division of a nucleus into two or more parts with masses of equal order of magnitude, usually accompanied by the emission of neutrons, gamma radiation and, rarely, small charged nuclear fragments.

N04230.title: nuclear fuel
N04230.definition: Material containing fissile nuclides, which when placed in a reactor, enables a chain reaction to be achieved.

N04232.title: nuclear fusion reaction
N04232.definition: A reaction between two light nuclei resulting in the production of a nuclear species heavier than either initial nucleus.

N04233.title: nuclear graphite
N04233.definition: A polygranular graphite material for use in nuclear reactor cores consisting of graphitic carbon of very high chemical purity. High purity is needed to avoid absorption of low-energy neutrons and the production of undesirable radioactive species.

12695.title: nuclear hormone receptor
12695.definition: Ligand-activated transcription factor that regulates gene expression by interacting with specific DNA sequences upstream of its target gene(s).

N04234.title: nuclear isomers
N04234.definition: Nuclides having the same mass number and atomic number, occupying different nuclear energy states.

N04235.title: nuclear level
N04235.definition: One of the energy values at which a nucleus can exist for an appreciable time (\(> 10^{-22}\ \rm{s}\)).

08383.title: nuclear magnetic resonance relaxometry
08383.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy to measure nuclear relaxation variables.

08218.title: nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
08218.definition: Measurement principle of spectroscopy to measure the precession of magnetic moments placed in a magnetic induction based on absorption of electromagnetic radiation of a specific frequency by an atomic nucleus.

08384.title: nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum
08384.definition: Representation of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy data with at least one dimension a frequency domain.

N04236.title: nuclear magneton
N04236.definition: Electromagnetic fundamental physical constant \(\mu _{\rm{N}}=\frac{m_{\rm{e}}}{m_{\rm{p}}}\ \mu _{\rm{B}}=5.050\ 7866(17)\times 10^{-27}\ \rm{J T}^{-1}\), where \(m_{\rm{e}}\) is the electron rest mass, \(m_{\rm{p}}\) the proton rest mass and \(\mu _{\rm{B}}\) the Bohr magneton.

08385.title: nuclear Overhauser effect
08385.definition: Change of intensity of one resonance when the spin transitions of another are somehow perturbed from their equilibrium populations.

08386.title: nuclear Overhauser effect difference spectroscopy
08386.definition: One dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that yields, through subtraction of spectra generated with and without selective excitation of a specific resonance, the nuclear Overhauser enhancement of nuclei spatially close to a selectively excited nucleus.

08387.title: nuclear Overhauser effect spectroscopy
08387.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy based on the nuclear Overhauser effect to observe nuclei that are close to each other in space.

N04237.title: nuclear particle
N04237.definition: A nucleus or any of its constituents in any of their energy states.

N04238.title: nuclear quadrupole moment
N04238.definition: A parameter which describes the effective shape of the equivalent ellipsoid of the nuclear charge distribution, \(Q>0\) for prolate (e.g. $\ce{^{57}Fe}$, $\ce{^{19}7Au}$); \(Q

08388.title: nuclear quadrupole resonance spectroscopy
08388.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy where splitting of the nuclear spin states is determined by the electrostatic interaction of the nuclear charge density with the external electric potential of the surrounding electron cloud.

09375.title: nuclear reaction cross section
09375.definition: Cross section at a given beam energy and emission direction of the detected product for a particular nuclear reaction per atom.

N04239.title: nuclear reactor
N04239.definition: A device in which a self-sustaining nuclear fission chain reaction can be maintained and controlled. The term is sometimes applied to a device in which a nuclear fusion reaction can be produced and controlled.

11163.title: nuclear receptor
11163.definition: Receptor that encounters its ligand in the cytosol and translocates to the nucleus, where it binds DNA and acts as a factor regulating gene transcription.

11022.title: nuclear spindle
11022.definition: Structure, formed from microtubules, that draws the newly duplicated chromosomes apart during mitosis and meiosis.

09376.title: nuclear stopping cross section
09376.definition: Stopping cross section arising from energy transfer to atomic nuclei of the sample.

N04240.title: nuclear transformation
N04240.definition: The change of one nuclide into another with a different proton number or nucleon number.

N04241.title: nuclear transition
N04241.definition: For a nucleus a change from one quantized energy state into another or a nuclear transformation.

11023.title: nuclear type I receptor
11023.definition: Steroid hormone receptor, found in the cytosol, that upon ligand binding translocates into the nucleus and interacts with DNA as a homodimer to drive specific gene transcription.

11024.title: nuclear type II receptor
11024.definition: Steroid hormone receptor, found in the nucleus, that upon ligand binding interacts with DNA as a heterodimer (usually with the retinoid X receptor, RXR) to drive specific gene transcription.

NT06774.title: nuclearity
NT06774.definition: The number of central atoms joined in a single coordination entity by bridging ligands or metal-metal bonds is indicated by dinuclear, trinuclear, tetranuclear, polynuclear, etc.

14170.title: nuclease assay
14170.definition: Method used to determine the presence or quantify the amount of specific target nucleotide sequences.

N04242.title: nucleating agent
N04242.definition: A material either added to or present in a system, which induces either homogeneous or heterogeneous nucleation.

N04244.title: nucleation and growth
N04244.definition: A process in a phase transition in which nuclei of a new phase are first formed, followed by the propagation of the new phase at a faster rate.

N04243.title: nucleation
N04243.definition: The process by which nuclei are formed in solution. The condensation of a single chemical compound is called 'homogeneous nucleation'. The simultaneous condensation of more than one compound is called 'simultaneous nucleation'. The condensation of a compound on a foreign substance is called 'heterogeneous nucleation'.

NT07272.title: nucleation of phase separation
NT07272.definition: Initiation of phase domain formation through the presence of heterogeneities.

09709.title: nucleic acid aptamers
09709.definition: Single stranded (ss) oligonucleotides (mainly deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA)) originating from in vitro selection, which, starting from random sequence libraries, optimise the nucleic acids for high-affinity binding to a given target.

09877.title: nucleic acid–protein interaction
09877.definition: Formation of specific or non-specific complexes between deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins, mediated and stabilised by a network of non-covalent interactions.

N04245.title: nucleic acids
N04245.definition: Macromolecules, the major organic matter of the nuclei of biological cells, made up of nucleotide units, and hydrolysable into certain pyrimidine or purine bases (usually adenine, cytosine, guanine, thymine, uracil), ᴅ-ribose or 2-deoxy-ᴅ-ribose and phosphoric acid.

09710.title: nucleobase
09710.definition: Purine or pyrimidine nitrogenous base occurring in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA).

09711.title: nucleobase lesion
09711.definition: Product of chemical modification of a nucleobase.

N04246.title: nucleofuge
N04246.definition: A leaving group that carries away the bonding electron pair. For example, in the hydrolysis of an alkyl chloride, $\ce{Cl^{-}}$ is the nucleofuge. The tendency of atoms or groups to depart with the bonding electron pair is called nucleofugality. The adjective is nucleofugal.

N04247.title: nucleon
N04247.definition: Heavy nuclear particle: proton or neutron.

N04249.title: nucleophile
N04249.definition: A nucleophile (or nucleophilic reagent) is a reagent that forms a bond to its reaction partner (the electrophile) by donating both bonding electrons. A 'nucleophilic substitution reaction' is a heterolytic reaction in which the reagent supplying the entering group acts as a nucleophile. For example:  The term 'nucleophilic' is also used to designate the apparent polar character of certain radicals, as inferred from their higher relative reactivity with reaction sites of lower electron density. Nucleophilic reagents are Lewis bases.

NT07428.title: nucleophilic aromatic photosubstitution
NT07428.definition: Photosubstitution in aromatic compounds with the participation of nucleophiles.

N04250.title: nucleophilic catalysis
N04250.definition: Catalysis by a Lewis base, involving formation of a Lewis adduct as a reaction intermediate. For example, the hydrolysis of acetic anhydride in aqueous solution catalysed by pyridine:

08982.title: nucleophilic chain polymerization
08982.definition: Chain polymerization in which the active centres are nucleophilic species.

08191.title: nucleophilic substitution
08191.definition: Heterolytic reaction in which an entering group adds to the electrophilic part of the substrate and in which the leaving group, or nucleofuge, retains both electrons of the bond that is broken, whereupon it becomes another potential nucleophile.

N04251.title: nucleophilicity
N04251.definition: The property of being nucleophilic.The relative reactivity of a nucleophilic reagent. (It is also sometimes referred to as 'nucleophilic power'.) Qualitatively, the concept is related to Lewis basicity. However, whereas Lewis basicity is measured by relative equilibrium constants:  nucleophilicity of a Lewis base is measured by relative rate constants of different nucleophilic reagents towards a common substrate, most commonly involving formation of a bond to carbon:

N04252.title: nucleoproteins
N04252.definition: Proteins having nucleic acids as prosthetic groups, and thus yielding nucleic acids (or their cleavage products) as well as amino acids on hydrolytic cleavage.

N04253.title: nucleosides
N04253.definition: Ribosyl or deoxyribosyl derivatives (rarely, other glycosyl derivatives) of certain pyrimidine or purine bases. They are thus glycosylamines or N-glycosides related to nucleotides by the lack of phosphorylation. It has also become customary to include among nucleosides analogous substances in which the glycosyl group is attached to carbon rather than nitrogen ('C-nucleosides').

N04254.title: nucleotide bases
N04254.definition: The heterocyclic pyrimidine and purine compounds which are constituents of all nucleic acids. Adenine (A), guanine (G) and cytosine (C) are found in both DNA and RNA, thymine (T) is found (primarily) in DNA and uracil (U) only in RNA.

09712.title: nucleotide sequence
09712.definition: Order of nucleotides in a deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecule.

13519.title: nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing protein 1, 2
13519.definition: Members of a family of human intracellular proteins involved in the detection of invasive bacteria and activation of the $\ce{NF\kappa B}$ transcription factor pathway.

13520.title: nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing protein-like receptor
13520.definition: Cytosolic protein that contains a central nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain, an N-terminal effector-binding domain and C-terminal leucine-rich repeats (LRRs).

N04255.title: nucleotides
N04255.definition: Compounds formally obtained by esterification of the 3 or 5 hydroxy group of nucleosides with phosphoric acid. They are the monomers of nucleic acids and are formed from them by hydrolytic cleavage.

N04256.title: nucleus
N04256.definition: The positively charged central portion of an atom, excluding the orbital electrons.

N04257.title: nuclide
N04257.definition: A species of atom, characterized by its mass number, atomic number and nuclear energy state, provided that the mean lifetime in that state is long enough to be observable.

08746.title: nuclide precursor
08746.definition: Radionuclide which precedes a nuclide in a decay chain.

N04258.title: nuclidic mass
N04258.definition: The rest mass of a nuclide expressed in atomic mass units.

13521.title: nude mouse
13521.definition: Mouse that is T-cell-deficient due to a homozygous gene defect (\(nu/nu\)) resulting in the absence of a thymus (and also lack of body hair).

N04259.title: nuisance threshold
N04259.definition: That concentration of an air pollutant that is considered objectionable. In the case of a substance with an objectionable odour, it is the smallest concentration of the substance which can be detected by a human being (nose).

13522.title: null cell
13522.definition: Lymphocyte with neither T- nor B-cell differentiation antigens on its surface.

11026.title: nulliparous
11026.definition: Never having given birth to a live infant.

N04260.title: number concentration
N04260.definition: Number of entities of a constituent in a mixture divided by the volume of the mixture.

N04261.title: number content
N04261.definition: Number of defined particles, or elementary entities, of a component in a system divided by the mass of that system.

N04262.title: number density
N04262.definition: Number of particles divided by the volume they occupy.

N04264.title: number flow rate
N04264.definition: Number of defined particles, or elementary entities of a defined component, crossing a cross-section divided by the time.

N04266.title: number of entities
N04266.definition: Integer number obtained by counting of entities, which are usually molecules, atoms or ions.

09623.title: number of generations
09623.definition: Number of constitutional repeating units on the path from the free valence to any end-group of a dendron.

09624.title: number of generations
09624.definition: Number of generation of the dendrons of a regular dendrimer molecule.

09625.title: number of pseudo-generations
09625.definition: Number of generations of the hypothetical dendrimer molecule that would present the same ratio of constitutional repeating units to core unit.

12216.title: number-average molar mass
12216.definition:
The equation for number-average molar mass is \[M_{\rm{n}} = \frac{1}{\sum\limits_{M} (w_{M}/M)}\]
The equation for number-average molecular weight  is \[M_{\rm{r,n}} = \frac{1}{\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}}(w_{M_{\rm{r}}}/M_{\rm{r}})}\]

14291.title: number-average particle diameter
14291.definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[\left\langle d_{\rm{N}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{N}} = \frac{\Sigma N_{i} d_{i}}{\Sigma N_{i}}\]

N04263.title: number-distribution function
N04263.definition: A distribution function in which the relative amount of a portion of a substance with a specific value, or a range of values, of the random variable(s) is expressed in terms of mole fraction.

11967.title: numbness
11967.definition: Imprecise term for absent or reduced touch perception, as well as paresthesia.

16252.title: numerical aperture
16252.definition: For an optical fibre, \(n_{\rm{o}}\) sin \(\theta_{\alpha}\), where \(n_{\rm{o}}\) is the refractive index of the exterior medium and \(\theta_{\alpha}\) is the maximum input half angle that can support propagation.

14888.title: numerical response
14888.definition: Change in predator or grazer number through increased reproductive output, decreased mortality, or increased immigration in response to changes in prey or food densities.

N04269.title: numerical value
N04269.definition: Quotient of the value of a quantity and the unit used in its expression.

15928.title: nutritional table method
15928.definition: Procedure for evaluating the dietary intake of a large number of people.

15929.title: nychthemeral
15929.definition: Relating to or exhibiting a nychthemeron or \(\pu{24\!\mbox{-}h}\) period.

08275.title: Nyquist criterion
08275.definition: Result of information theory that a sine wave can be completely reconstructed if its ordinate is known at two or more points in a cycle.

08276.title: Nyquist frequency
08276.definition: Highest frequency or wavenumber that can be characterized by sampling at a given rate in order to be able to fully reconstruct the signal without artefacts.

11968.title: nystagmus
11968.definition: Involuntary rhythmic oscillation of the eyeballs.

15945.title: -omics, -omes
15945.definition: Neologism referring to the fields of study in biology ending in the suffix -omics, such as genomics or proteomics: The related neologism -omes are the objects of study of the field such as the genome or proteome, respectively.

14228.title: orientational disorder
14228.definition: Structural disorder at given crystallographic positions, resulting from the statistical coexistence within crystals of directional stems with opposite orientations.

12512.title: orthogonal electrospray
12512.definition: Configuration for electrospray ionization in which the axis of the spray is at a right angle to the axis of the sampling cone.

12513.title: orthogonal extraction
12513.definition: Pulsed acceleration of ions perpendicular to their original direction of travel into a mass spectrometer, typically time-of-flight.

09852.title: O-polysaccharide
09852.definition: Part of a lipopolysaccharide that consists of a polysaccharide chain extending outwards from the bacterial cell surface.

08037.title: object traceability
08037.definition: Ability to trace the history, application, or location of an object.

15930.title: objective environment
15930.definition: Actual physical, chemical, and social environment as described by objective measurements, such as noise levels in decibels and concentrations of air pollutants.

08389.title: observation frequency
08389.definition: Frequency corresponding to the centre of the spectrum window for a given nucleus under observation and the nominal frequency used to generate the hard, full spectrum pulses.

O04270.title: observation height
O04270.definition: The difference in height between the axis of the observed space (optical axis) and the burner tip (in \(\mathrm{mm}\)). The optical axis of the instrument should be the same as the optical axis of the observation space. Other definitions which express the observation height as a fraction of the whole flame height are not recommended because the height to the tip of the flame is not well defined. The observation height should be stated in the method.

O04271.title: observation pathlength
O04271.definition: The intersection of the optical axis and the observation space (in \(\mathrm{mm}\)).

O04272.title: observation space
O04272.definition: The intersection of the optical beam and that part of the flame where the net signal is at least half of the maximum net signal. The characteristics of the observation space depend on the temperature of the flame, the stoichiometry of the gases and the properties of the processed fluid (presence of proteins for instance). The observation space in atomic absorption is analogous to the observation space of a cuvette in molecular absorption spectrometry.

O04273.title: observation volume
O04273.definition: The volume of that part of the flame that is observed through the optical device (in \(\unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{l}\)).

09443.title: observed interface width
09443.definition: In secondary-ion mass spectrometry, Auger electron spectroscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, distance over which a change in signal intensity from \(\pu{16\%}\) to \(\pu{84\%}\), or from \(\pu{84\%}\) to \(\pu{16\%}\), is measured at the junction of two dissimilar matrices, the thicknesses of which are more than six times that distance

11813.title: obstructive hydrocephalus
11813.definition: Hydrocephalus where flow of the cerebrospinal fluid is blocked.

12696.title: obviousness
12696.definition: Term associated with intellectual property wherein the latter’s patentability is assessed relative to the combination of more than one item of 'prior art'.

11969.title: occipital lobe
11969.definition: One of the four major lobes of each cerebral hemisphere, situated within the occiput, containing most of the neural apparatus of visual processing.

11027.title: occiput
11027.definition: Back part of the head or skull.

14302.title: occluded particle
14302.definition: Multicomponent particle in which one polymer forms more than one phase domain within a matrix of another polymer.

O04275.title: occlusion
O04275.definition: The process of incorporation of foreign substances as molecular species within precipitates as they are formed.

09644.title: occult blood
09644.definition: Blood present in such small amounts that its presence can be ascertained only by chemical analysis or by spectroscopic or microscopic examination; particularly the blood found in stools.

15932.title: occupational exposure
15932.definition: Experience of substances, intensities of radiation, etc., or other conditions while at work.

15933.title: occupational exposure limit
15933.definition: Regulatory level of exposure to substances, intensities of radiation, etc., or other conditions, specified appropriately in relevant government legislation or related codes of practice.

15934.title: occupational exposure standard
15934.definition:
Level of exposure to substances, intensities of radiation, etc., or other conditions considered to represent specified good practice and a realistic criterion for the control of exposure by appropriate plant design, engineering controls, and, if necessary, the addition and use of personal protective clothing.
In UK, health-based exposure limit defined under COSHH Regulations as the concentration of any airborne substance, averaged over a reference period, at which, according to current knowledge, there is no evidence that it is likely to be injurious to employees, if they are exposed by inhalation, day after day, to that concentration, and set on the advice of the HSE Advisory Committee on Toxic Substances.

15935.title: occupational hygiene
15935.definition: Identification, assessment, and control of physicochemical and biological factors in the workplace that may affect the health or well-being of those at work and in the surrounding community.

15936.title: occupational medicine
15936.definition: Specialty devoted to the prevention and management of occupational injury, illness, and disability, and the promotion of the health of workers, their families, and their communities.

08843.title: occupied band
08843.definition: Energy band occupied by electrons, typically the valence band.

O04276.title: octahedro-
O04276.definition: An affix used in names to denote six atoms bound into an octahedron.

14889.title: octanol-air partition coefficient
14889.definition: Partition coefficient for a compound between octanol and air. Like \(K_{\rm{ow}}\), it is a measure of lipophilicity.

14890.title: octanol-water partition coefficient
14890.definition: Ratio of the solubility of a chemical in octanol to its solubility in water at equilibrium.

08192.title: octanol-water partition ratio
08192.definition: Equilibrium concentration of a substance in octan-1-ol divided by its equilibrium concentration in water.

14891.title: octaves
14891.definition: Log2 classes (e.g., 1–2, 2–4, 4–8, 8–16, 16–32,... individuals) used in species-abundance curves and representing doubling of the numbers of individuals in a species.

15938.title: odds
15938.definition: Ratio of the probability of occurrence of an event to that of non-occurrence, or the ratio of the probability that something is so, to the probability that it is not so.

15939.title: odds ratio
15939.definition: Quotient obtained by dividing one set of odds by another. The terms 'odds' or 'odds ratio' are defined differently according to the situation under discussion. Consider the following notation for the distribution of a binary exposure and a disease in a population or a sample. \[\begin{array}{l c c} & Exposed & Nonexposed \\ \rm{Disease} & a & b \\ \rm{No\ disease} & c & d \\ \end{array}\] The odds ratio (cross-product ratio) is \(ad/bc\).

O04278.title: optically detected magnetic resonance
O04278.definition: A double resonance technique in which transitions between spin sublevels are detected by optical means. Usually these are sublevels of a triplet and the transitions are induced by microwaves. For different types of optical detection the following expressions are used: ADMR (absorption), DEDMR (delayed emission, non-specified), DFDMR (delayed fluorescence), FDMR (fluorescence), PDMR (phosphorescence). If a reaction yield is followed the expression RYDMR (reaction yield detected magnetic resonance) is used.

11028.title: odontoblast
11028.definition: Dentin-forming cell of the pulp cavity of a tooth, arising from the mesenchyme of the neural crest.

15940.title: odor threshold
15940.definition: In principle, the lowest concentration of an odorant in the air that can be detected by a human being.

O04279.title: odour threshold
O04279.definition: The concentration of a compound which produces an odour which is detectable by a human being (nose). For certain compounds this threshold is very low (e.g. 1 part in \(10^{9}\) for certain sulfides).

09756.title: off peptide product ions
09756.definition: Protein/peptide sequencing approach using overlapping complementary information on a sequence acquired using proteolysis in bottom-up proteomic analysis by at least two different proteolytic approaches.

09755.title: off-gel isoelectric focusing
09755.definition: Separation technique used to fractionate proteins and peptides into discrete liquid fractions according to their isoelectric point.

14171.title: off-rate
14171.definition: Rate of dissociation of the enzyme-substrate (\(\ce{ES}\)) complex to enzyme (\(\ce{E}\)) and substrate (\(\ce{S}\)) or of ligand–receptor (\(\ce{LR}\)) to receptor (\(\ce{R}\)) and ligand (\(\ce{L}\)).

09200.title: off-specular X-ray reflectometry
09200.definition: X-ray reflectometry in which significant scattered intensity arises from imperfections in the specimen, the scattered intensity falling outside the specular condition (see specular X-ray reflectometry).

12697.title: off-target effect
12697.definition: Pharmacological action induced by any molecule at molecular/biological sites distinct from that for which it was designed.

11029.title: offspring
11029.definition: Child or children of a person, or the young of an animal, in relation to the parent(s).

O04280.title: ohm
O04280.definition: SI derived unit of electrical resistance, \(\Omega = \pu{V A-1} = \pu{m2 kg s-3 A-2}\).

08844.title: ohmic contact
08844.definition: Electric junction which exhibits linear and symmetric current-potential dependence.

15217.title: ointment
15217.definition: Greasy, semi-solid preparation for external application, often anhydrous, containing dissolved or dispersed medicaments.

14892.title: Oklo natural reactors
14892.definition: Naturally occurring nuclear reactors arising through biogeochemical processes approximately 1.8 billion years ago in Oklo (Gabon, Africa).

13523.title: OKT3
13523.definition: Brand name for muromonab-CD3, an immunosuppressant drug given intravenously to reverse acute rejection of transplanted organs, including the heart, kidneys, and liver.

O04281.title: olefins
O04281.definition: Acyclic and cyclic hydrocarbons having one or more carbon–carbon double bonds, apart from the formal ones in aromatic compounds. The class olefins subsumes alkenes and cycloalkenes and the corresponding polyenes.

15941.title: olf
15941.definition: Unit used to measure scent emission of people and objects; one olf is defined as the scent emission of an 'average person', a sitting adult who takes an average of \(\pu{0.7}\) baths per day and whose skin has a total area of \(\pu{1.8 m2}\); the scent emission of an object or person is measured by specially trained personnel comparing it to normed scents.

15942.title: olfactometer
15942.definition: Apparatus for testing the power of the sense of smell.

10478.title: olfactory bulb
10478.definition: Region of the frontal lobe of the brain, receiving input from neurons of the nasal mucosa and involved in the sense of smell.

O04282.title: oligo
O04282.definition: A prefix meaning 'a few', and used for compounds with a number of repeating units intermediate between those in monomers and those in high polymers. The limits are not precisely defined, and in practice vary with the type of structure being considered, but are generally from 3 to 10, e.g. oligopeptides, oligosaccharides.

13524.title: oligoclonal
13524.definition: Having a few different clones, or the product of a few different clones.

11030.title: oligodactyly
11030.definition: Congenital occurrence of fewer than the usual number of digits, resulting in humans having fewer than five fingers or toes on a hand or foot.

11971.title: oligodendrocyte
11971.definition: Type of glial cell that produces the myelin sheath in the central nervous system.

11031.title: oligodontia
11031.definition: Congenital absence of some of the teeth.

O04283.title: oligomer
O04283.definition: A substance composed of oligomer molecules. An oligomer obtained by telomerization is often termed a telomer.

O04286.title: oligomer molecule
O04286.definition: A molecule of intermediate relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises a small plurality of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of lower relative molecular mass.

O04285.title: oligomerization
O04285.definition: The process of converting a monomer or a mixture of monomers into an oligomer. An oligomerization by chain reaction carried out in the presence of a large amount of chain transfer agent, so that the end-groups are essentially fragments of the chain transfer agent, is termed telomerization.

11033.title: oligospermia
11033.definition: Subnormal concentration of sperm in the male ejaculate (see ejaculation).

14893.title: oligotrophic
14893.definition: Describing an environment having a low concentration of nutrients.

14894.title: oligotrophy
14894.definition:
State of being oligotrophic.
Obligate or facultative capacity to live in low-nutrient habitats.

15943.title: oligozoospermia
15943.definition: Sperm concentration less than a reference value.

15944.title: oliguria
15944.definition: Excretion of a diminished amount of urine in relation to fluid intake.

11034.title: omentum
11034.definition: Fold of peritoneal membrane passing between the stomach and another abdominal organ.

11037.title: omphalocele
11037.definition: Congenital herniation of abdominal viscera into the base of the umbilical cord.

11038.title: omphalosite
11038.definition: Lesser developed of two monozygotic twins that failed to separate completely during embryogenesis.

10312.title: on-line extraction
10312.definition: Coupling of a flow system with an extraction device to a detector via a discontinuous interface.

14172.title: on-rate
14172.definition: Rate of formation of the enzyme-substrate (\(\ce{ES}\)) or ligand–receptor (\(\ce{LR}\)) complex.

13525.title: oncofetal antigen
13525.definition: Antigen whose expression is normally restricted to the fetus but which may be expressed during malignancy in adults.

15946.title: oncogene
15946.definition: Gene that can cause neoplastic (see neoplasia) transformation of a cell; oncogenes are slightly changed equivalents of normal genes known as proto-oncogenes.

15948.title: oncogenic
15948.definition: Capable of producing tumors in animals, either benign (noncancerous) or malignant (cancerous).

OT07432.title: one-bond-flip
OT07432.definition: Photoisomerization of one double bond in a conjugated double bond system. It is a regular E/Z photoisomerization.  Compare with bicycle-pedal mechanism, hula-twist mechanism.

10136.title: one-class classification
10136.definition: Classification identifying objects of a specific class amongst all objects, by learning from training data containing only objects of the specific class.

15218.title: one-compartment model
15218.definition: Kinetic model, where the whole body is thought of as a single compartment in which a substance is distributed rapidly, achieving an equilibrium between blood and tissue immediately.

11039.title: one-generation reprotox study
11039.definition: Procedure in which male rodents are dosed with a test substance for at least one spermatogenic cycle, and females for two estrous cycles, and then further exposed during mating, pregnancy, and nursing; adverse effects on reproduction, parturition, lactation and postnatal growth are studied.

15949.title: one-hit model
15949.definition: Dose-response model of the form \[P = 1 - {\rm{e}}^{-bd}\] where \(P\) is the probability of cancer death from a continuous dose rate, \(d\), and \(b\) is a constant.

OT07433.title: one-photon photochromism
OT07433.definition: Photochromic process involving a one-photon mechanism. In this case, the photoproduct B is formed from the singlet or from the triplet state of the thermodynamically-stable molecular entity A.

OT07305.title: onion morphology
OT07305.definition: Multiphase morphology of roughly spherical shape that comprises alternating layers of different polymers arranged concentrically, all layers being of similar thickness.

O04291.title: onium compounds
O04291.definition: Cations (with their counter-ions) derived by addition of a hydron to a mononuclear parent hydride of the nitrogen, chalcogen and halogen families.$\ce{H4N^{+}}$ ammonium$\ce{H3O^{+}}$ oxonium$\ce{H2F^{+}}$ fluoronium$\ce{H4P^{+}}$ phosphonium$\ce{H3S^{+}}$ sulfonium$\ce{H2Cl^{+}}$ chloronium$\ce{H4As^{+}}$ arsonium$\ce{H3Se^{+}}$ selenonium$\ce{H2Br^{+}}$ bromonium$\ce{H4Sb^{+}}$ stibonium$\ce{H3Te^{+}}$ telluronium$\ce{H2I^{+}}$ iodonium$\ce{H4Bi^{+}}$ bismuthoniumDerivatives formed by substitution of the above parent ions by univalent groups. The number of substituted hydrogen atoms is, especially in the case of hydrocarbyl substituents, indicated by the adjectives primary, secondary, tertiary or quaternary. E.g. ($\ce{Cl2F^{+}}$) dichlorofluoronium, $\ce{(CH3)2S^{+}H}$ dimethylsulfonium (a secondary sulfonium ion), $\ce{Cl(CH3)3P^{+}}$ chlorotrimethylphosphonium, $\ce{(CH3CH2)4N^{+}}$ tetraethylammonium (a quaternary ammonium ion).See also: arsonium compounds, halonium ions, oxonium ions, phosphonium compounds, quaternary ammonium compounds, stibonium compounds, sulfonium compoundsDerivatives formed by substitution of the above parent ions by groups having two or three free valencies on the same atom. Such derivatives are, where possible, designated by a specific class name. E.g. $\ce{RC#O^{+}}$ hydrocarbylidyne oxonium ions, $\ce{R2C=N^{+}H2X^{−}}$ iminium compounds, $\ce{RC#NH^{+}}$ nitrilium ions.

15219.title: onset of drug action
15219.definition: Time required to achieve the minimum effective plasma concentration following administration of the dosage form.

15950.title: onycholysis
15950.definition: Loosening or detachment of the nail from the nail bed following some destructive process.

11040.title: oocyte
11040.definition: Immature precursor of the ovum resident in the ovary.

11043.title: oogenesis
11043.definition: Process of formation and development of an ovum.

11044.title: oogonium
11044.definition: Primitive germ cell that proliferates by mitosis and develops into a primary oocyte prior to birth.

09077.title: open circuit potential
09077.definition: Electrode potential of working electrode relative to the reference electrode when no potential or electric current is being applied to the electrochemical cell.

11973.title: open field test
11973.definition: Procedure to observe changes in motor activity and rearing, in which a rodent is placed on a surface and distance and patterns of movement are recorded.

O04294.title: open film
O04294.definition: A film in which mass transfer can occur between the film and the coexisting bulk phases, for all the components. The term partly open film applies to a film in which mass transfer can occur only for certain components. The term closed film applies to those films with fixed mass.

O04295.title: open hearth furnace
O04295.definition: Reverberatory furnace, containing a basin-shaped hearth, for melting and refining suitable types of pig iron, iron ore, and scrap for steel production. A large amount of dust from ore and other materials and splashings from slag are carried away by the waste gases; a supplementary chamber is commonly used for collecting slag and dust.

09713.title: open reading frame
09713.definition: Sequence of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA) nucleotides, located between the start-code sequence (initiation codon) and the stop-code sequence (termination codon), which is transcribed and translated to generate a protein.

OT07087.title: open-shell systems
OT07087.definition: Atomic or molecular systems in which the electrons are not completely assigned to orbitals in pairs.

O04297.title: open-tubular column
O04297.definition: A column, usually having a small diameter, in which either the inner tube wall, or a liquid or active solid held stationary on the tube wall acts as the stationary phase and there is an open, unrestricted path for the mobile phase.

10236.title: open-vessel acid digestion
10236.definition: Type of acid digestion performed at ambient pressure wherein the digestion temperature is limited by the boiling point of the acid.

11688.title: operant conditioning
11688.definition: Learning in which appropriate behavior is rewarded, or inappropriate behavior is punished; behavior is modified by learned association with antecedents and consequences.

O04298.title: operational pH cell
O04298.definition: An electrochemical cell which is the basis of practical pH measurement consisting of a hydrogen ion-responsive electrode (hydrogen gas, or glass) and a reference electrode immersed in the test solution.

O04299.title: operational pH standard
O04299.definition: Certain substances which meet the criteria of (i) preparation in highly pure state reproducibly and (ii) stability of solution over a reasonable period of time are designated as operational standards in aqueous solution of specified concentration. Their number is in principle unlimited but values are available now for 15 solutions. The values of operational pH standards, i.e. \(\mathrm{pH}\left(\rm{OS}\right)\), are assigned by comparison with the reference value pH standard, i.e. \(\mathrm{pH}\left(\rm{RVS}\right)\), in cells with liquid junction, the operational cells, where the liquid junctions are formed within vertical \(1\ \rm{mm}\) tubes.

O04301.title: operon
