P04437.definition: This term is not recommended and should not be used as a synonym for partition constant, partition ratio or distribution ratio.

P04438.title: partition constant
P04438.definition: The ratio of activity of a given species A in the extract to its activity in the other phase with which it is in equilibrium, thus: \[\left(K_{\rm{D}}^{\rm{o}}\right)_{\rm{A}} = \frac{a_{\rm{A,org}}}{a_{\rm{A,aq}}}\] Its value should not vary with composition but depends on the choice of standard states and on the temperature (and eventually the pressure).

P04439.title: partition function
P04439.definition: For a molecule the ratio of the total number of molecules to their number in the non-degenerate ground state.

PT06933.title: partition isotherm
PT06933.definition: Isotherm describing partition of the sample component between the bulk of a liquid stationary phase and a liquid, gaseous or supercritical mobile phase.

P04440.title: partition ratio
P04440.definition: The ratio of the concentration of a substance in a single definite form, A, in the extract to its concentration in the same form in the other phase at equilibrium, e.g. for an aqueous/organic system: \[\left (K_{\rm{D}} \right )_{A} = \frac{\left [ A \right ]_{\rm{org}}}{\left [ A \right ]_{\rm{aq}}}\]

11075.title: parturition
11075.definition: Process of giving birth by a maternal organism.

P04442.title: pascal
P04442.definition: SI derived unit of pressure, \(\pu{Pa} = \pu{N m-2} = \pu{kg m-1 s-2}\).

09344.title: pass energy
09344.definition: Mean kinetic energy of detected particles in the energy-dispersive portion of an electron energy analyser.

P04443.title: passivation
P04443.definition: The process of transition from the active to the passive state by formation of the passivating film. Passivation is achieved by an anodic current which at the respective electrode potential must be larger than the maximum current, or by the presence of an oxidized substance in the neighbouring solution which passivates by being reduced (passivator).

P04444.title: passivation potential
P04444.definition: The most negative electrode potential at which the passivating film is formed. The passivation potential is equal to or more positive than the equilibrium potential of formation of the phase constituting the film. Usually, the corrosion current goes through a maximum at the passivation potential.

12000.title: passive avoidance test
12000.definition: Fear-motivated test in which rodents learn to avoid an otherwise preferred environment in which they are exposed to an aversive stimulus.

13538.title: passive cutaneous anaphylaxis test
13538.definition: Assay for allergenicity in which an antibody is injected intradermally into a test animal followed at a later time (anywhere from \(\pu{3}\) to \(\pu{48 h}\)) with an intravenous injection of a mixture of a test antigen and a dye (typically Evans blue). Increased vascular permeability at the site of antigen-antibody reaction is visualized by extravasation of the dye.

13539.title: passive hemagglutination
13539.definition: Method of measuring antibody titer, in which antigen-coated erythrocytes are agglutinated by adding antibody specific for the antigen.

13540.title: passive immunization
13540.definition: Immunization of an individual by the transfer of antibody synthesized in another individual.

P04445.title: passive metal
P04445.definition: A metal corroding in the passive state.

P04446.title: passive sampler
P04446.definition: A device for preconcentration of trace substances from gaseous media based on molecular diffusion without controlled conveyance of the gas to be investigated (e.g. work place air).

10183.title: passive sampling
10183.definition: Extraction process driven by diffusion of analytes towards the extraction phase.

15964.title: passive smoking
15964.definition: Inhalation of sidestream smoke by people who do not smoke themselves.

P04447.title: passive state
P04447.definition: The passive state is characterized by a contiguous 'passivating film' of solid corrosion products separating the metallic phase from the adjacent electrolyte. Corrosion in the passive state involves growth of the passivating film and/or transfer of metal ions through the film into the electrolyte.

15220.title: paste
15220.definition: Ointment containing \(\gt \pu{0\%}\) of powder, dispersed in a fatty base.

13541.title: patch test
13541.definition: Test for allergy that is performed by placing the suspected allergen in direct contact with the skin or mucosa.

11076.title: patent ductus arteriosus
11076.definition: Congenital disorder wherein the ductus arteriosis fails to close after birth.

12702.title: patentability
12702.definition: Set of criteria that must be satisfied in order to achieve commercial exclusivity for an invention.

P04448.title: Paterno–Büchi reaction
P04448.definition: The photocycloaddition of an electronically excited carbonyl group to a ground state olefin yielding an oxetane.

11483.title: path fingerprints
11483.definition:
Vectors of Boolean arrays generated from the properties of the atoms and bonds in linear paths, typically two to seven bonds long, hashed into an integer of
 fixed determined length.

15431.title: path length
15431.definition: Number of polymer main-chain (backbone) atoms between two subunits.

08278.title: path-length
08278.definition: Length of the optical path through the sample.

13542.title: pathogen-associated molecular pattern
13542.definition: Describing repetitive motifs of molecules such as lipopolysaccharide (LPS), peptidoglycan, lipoteichoic acids, and mannans, which are widely expressed by microbial pathogens but are not present on host tissues. They are therefore utilized by the pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) of the immune system to distinguish pathogens from self-antigens.

14901.title: pathway
14901.definition: Sequence of enzymatic or other reactions by which one biological material is converted to another.

08657.title: pATR spectrum
08657.definition: \(-\log_{10}\) of the spectrum obtained in attenuated total reflection spectroscopy.

09546.title: pattern collapse
09546.definition: Destruction of pattern during and after development caused by the surface tension of the development solvent.

PT06976.title: pattern recognition
PT06976.definition: Pattern recognition is the identification of patterns in large data sets, using appropriate mathematical methodology. Examples are principal component analysis (PCA), SIMCA, partial least squares (PLS) and artificial neural networks (ANN).

13543.title: pattern recognition receptor
13543.definition: Receptor found on many different cell types in the immune system that enables them to recognize pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs). Amongst the large number of different PRRs are the mannose receptor (CD206), macrophage scavenger receptor (CD204), and the toll-like receptors (TLRs).

09547.title: pattern transfer
09547.definition: Transfer of the pattern of a developed lithographic image to an underlying substrate by processes such as etching.

15412.title: patterns of reactivity scheme
15412.definition: Method for the prediction of monomer reactivity ratios in binary copolymerization, based exclusively on experimentally determined parameters.

13544.title: pauci-immune
13544.definition: Referring to vasculitis characterized by relatively little deposition of immunoglobulin (Ig) and complement factors, usually describing a form of glomerulonephritis.

P04449.title: paucidisperse system
P04449.definition: A colloidal system in which only a few particle-sizes occur.

PT07089.title: Pauli exclusion principle
PT07089.definition: A rule, complementary to the aufbau principle, of building up the electronic configuration of atoms and molecules: a maximum of two electrons can occupy an orbital and then only providing that the spins of the electrons are paired, i.e. opposed. The principle demands that the wavefunction for a many-electron system must be asymmetric with respect to the permutation of the space-spin coordinates for every pair of electrons.

12001.title: paw-reaching test
12001.definition: Test used to reveal motor deficits, usually of central origin, exhibited on the contralateral side by reduced ability of a test animal to extend the forelimb.

12002.title: PC-12 cell
12002.definition: Cell of an established line originally derived from a pheochromocytoma of the rat adrenal medulla.

P04452.title: peak analysis
P04452.definition: The extraction of relevant peak parameters (i.e. position, area) from a measured spectrum.

P04453.title: peak area
P04453.definition: The area enclosed between the peak and the baseline.

P04454.title: peak area method
P04454.definition: A kind of peak analysis in which a peak area is calculated by subtracting an estimate of the underlying continuum in a relevant part of a measured spectrum.

P04455.title: peak base
P04455.definition: The interpolation, in a differential chromatogram, of the baseline between the extremities of the peak.

P04456.title: peak concentration
P04456.definition: The highest concentration of a given trace component which was measured with a continuous analyser during a specified sampling period.

P04457.title: peak current
P04457.definition: In linear-sweep voltammetry, triangular-wave voltammetry, cyclic triangular-wave voltammetry, and similar techniques, the maximum value of the faradaic current due to the reduction or oxidation of a substance B during a single sweep. This maximum value is attained after an interval during which the concentration of B at the electrode-solution interface decreases monotonically, while the faradaic current due to the reduction or oxidation of B increases monotonically, with time. It is attained before an interval during which this current decreases monotonically with time because the rate of transport of B toward the electrode-solution interface is smaller than the rate at which it is removed from the interface by electrolysis. The term has also been used to denote the maximum value of the faradaic current attributable to the reduction or oxidation of an electroactive substance in techniques such as ac polarography, differential pulse polarography, and derivative polarography. However, these techniques give curves that arise in ways different from that cited above, and the terms summit, summit current, and summit potential are therefore recommended for use in connection with such techniques.

P04458.title: peak elution volume
P04458.definition: The volume of mobile phase entering the column between the start of the elution and the emergence of the peak maximum, or the corresponding time. In most of the cases, this is equal to the total retention volume (time). There are, however, cases when the elution process does not start immediately at sample introduction. For example, in liquid chromatography, sometimes the column is washed with a liquid after the application of the sample to displace certain components which are of no interest and during this treatment the sample does not move along the column. In gas chromatography, there are also cases when a liquid sample is applied to the top of the column but its elution starts only after a given period. This term is useful in such cases.

09266.title: peak energy
09266.definition: Energy value corresponding to the intensity maximum in a direct spectrum or to the intensity minimum (i.e. the negative excursion) for a differential spectrum.

P04460.title: peak fitting
P04460.definition: A kind of peak analysis in which a relevant part of a spectrum is fitted with a theoretical response function.

P04462.title: peak height
P04462.definition: The distance between the peak maximum and the peak base, measured in a direction parallel to the axis representing the detector response.

P04451.title: peak
P04451.definition: The portion of a differential chromatogram recording the detector response when a single component is eluted from the column. If separation is incomplete, two or more components may be eluted as one 'unresolved peak'.

P04463.title: peak maximum
P04463.definition: The point on the peak at which the distance to the peak base, measured in a direction parallel to the axis representing the detector response, is a maximum.

P04464.title: peak potential
P04464.definition: In linear-sweep voltammetry, triangular-wave voltammetry, cyclic triangular-wave voltammetry, and similar techniques, the potential of the indicator electrode at which the peak current is attained.

P04465.title: peak resolution
P04465.definition: The separation of two peaks in terms of their average peak width at base (\(t_{\rm{R2}}>t_{\rm{R1}}\)): \[R_{\rm{s}}=\frac{t_{\rm{R2}}\,-\,t_{\rm{R1}}}{\frac{w_{\rm{b1}}\,+\,w_{\rm{b2}}}{2}}=\frac{2\ (t_{\rm{R2}}- t_{\rm{R1}})}{w_{\rm{b1}}\,+\,w_{\rm{b2}}}\] In the case of two adjacent peaks it may be assumed that \(w_{\rm{b1}}\approx w_{\rm{b2}}\), and thus, the width of the second peak may be substituted for the average value: \[R_{\rm{s}}\approx \frac{t_{\rm{R2}}\,-\,t_{\rm{R1}}}{w_{\rm{b2}}}\]

09903.title: peak width at base
09903.definition: Peak width at peak base intercepted by tangents to the chromatogram drawn at the inflection points on either side of the peak. Represented by the line AB in the peak height figure.

09904.title: peak width at half height
09904.definition: Peak width at \(\pu{50\%}\) of the peak height that terminates at the intersections with the peak.

P04466.title: peak widths
P04466.definition: Peak widths represent retention dimensions (time or volume) parallel to the baseline. If the baseline is not parallel to the axis representing time or volume, then the peak widths are to be drawn parallel to this axis. Three peak-width values are commonly used in chromatography. Peak width at base (\(w_{\rm{b}}\)) is the segment of the peak base intercepted by the tangents drawn to the inflection points on either side of the peak. Peak width at half height (\(w_{\rm{h}}\)) is the length of the line parallel to the peak base at 50% of the peak height that terminates at the intersection with the two limbs of the peak. Peak width at inflection points (\(w_{\rm{i}}\)) is the length of the line drawn between the inflection points parallel to the peak base. The peak width at base may be called the 'base width'. However, the peak width at half height must never be called the 'half width' because that has a completely different meaning. Also, the symbol \(w_{1/2}\) should never be used instead of \(w_{\rm{h}}\).

12262.title: pearl-necklace model
12262.definition: Model describing the flow behaviour of a dissolved chain macromolecule in terms of a freely jointed sequence of beads, each of which offers hydrodynamic resistance to the flow of the surrounding solvent continuum and is connected to the next bead by a rigid rod that offers no hydrodynamic resistance.

P04467.title: pectins
P04467.definition: Polyuronic acids mostly derived from ᴅ-galacturonic acid (abundant in some fruits).

14902.title: pedosphere
14902.definition: Part of the Earth made up of soils and where important soil processes are occurring.

PT07442.title: Peierls distortion
PT07442.definition: Distortion of a regular one-dimensional structure with a partially occupied band to give bond alternation, eventually leading to dimerization or oligomerization. The degree of oligomerization, \(\lambda \) depends on the electronic population of the conduction band indicated by the wave vector of the Fermi level \(k_{\mathrm{F}}\) \[\lambda = 2\ \pi /k_{\mathrm{F}}\]

P04468.title: Peierls transition
P04468.definition: A metal-insulator transition in quasi one-dimensional solids that occurs as a result of a band gap opening up at the Fermi energy due to a displacive distortion of the regular array increasing the unit cell length, usually a dimerization; the decrease in electronic energy outweighs the increase in lattice energy. Example: The transition in methylethylmorpholinium tetracyanoquinodimethanide at \(335\ \rm{K}\).

14903.title: pelagic
14903.definition: Of or relating to the open sea, as distinguished from the shallow water near the coast; dwelling on or near the surface of the open sea or ocean; oceanic. Now chiefly: (Ecology) designating, relating to, or inhabiting that region of the sea which consists of open water of any depth, away from or independent of both the shore and the sea floor (and so contrasted with the littoral and benthic regions).

15221.title: pellet
15221.definition:
Very small tablet or pilule.
Implantable polymeric matrix.
Spherical granule.

15222.title: pelletisation
15222.definition: Process of agglomeration that converts fine powders or granules of bulk drugs and excipients into small, free-flowing, spherical, or semi-spherical units, referred to as pellets.

P04469.title: pellicular packing
P04469.definition: In this case the stationary phase forms a porous outer shell on an impermeable particle.

11077.title: pelvic kidney
11077.definition: Congenital abnormality in which a kidney develops and remains in the pelvic area.

13545.title: pemphigus
13545.definition: Rare, serious autoimmune disease marked by successive outbreaks of blisters, which appear suddenly and disappear, leaving pigmented spots.

P04470.title: penams
P04470.definition: Natural and synthetic antibiotics containing the 4-thia-1-azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptan-7-one structure, generally assumed to have the 5R configuration unless otherwise specified. The numbering of the penam skeleton differs from that of the von Baeyer named bicyclic system. Where they differ the von Baeyer numbering is shown in parentheses in the example.

P04472.title: pendant group
P04472.definition: An offshoot, neither oligomeric nor polymeric from a chain.

13847.title: pendent chain
13847.definition: Oligomeric or polymeric offshoot from a macromolecular chain.

PT06879.title: penetrant
PT06879.definition: Entity from a phase in contact with one of the membrane surfaces that passes though the membrane.

15965.title: penetration
15965.definition:
Action of entering or passing through a cell membrane.
Ability or power to enter or pass through a cell membrane.

P04475.title: penicillins
P04475.definition: Substituted penams having the basic structure shown, including the natural penicillins and synthetic analogues.

08515.title: Penning excitation
08515.definition: Collisional excitation and ionization mechanism of inductively-coupled plasma spectrometry involving analyte atoms and metastable argon atoms.

P04476.title: Penning gas mixture
P04476.definition: A Penning gas mixture consists of a rare gas containing impurity atoms possibly at very low concentrations. The impurity atoms have an ionization potential \(V_{\rm{ion}}\) which is lower than or equal to the metastable potential (\(V_{\rm{meta}}\)) of the parent noble gas. The Penning effect in a Penning gas mixture is the ionization by charge transfer (charge exchange) during collision between a metastable atom and a neutral atom which decreases the average energy to form an ion pair, e.g.  In a glow discharge, this results in an increase of the the ionization coefficient (Townsend first coefficient), a decrease in breakdown potential and a lowering of the cathode fall potential. The magnetic Penning effect describes the increase of the ionization probability of gas in a low pressure electrical discharge resulting from the helical (spiral) movement of electrons in a magnetic field placed normal to the anode-cathode electrical field.

P04478.title: pentaprismo-
P04478.definition: An affix used in names to denote ten atoms bound into a pentagonal prism.

15413.title: penultimate-unit effect
15413.definition: Phenomenon that the penultimate monomer unit preceding the active center on the terminal unit of an active polymer chain affects the reactivity of that active center.

09757.title: peptide de novo sequencing
09757.definition: Analytical process that derives an amino acid sequence of a peptide from its tandem mass spectrum without the assistance of a sequence database.

09758.title: peptide fragment ion
09758.definition: Product ion which originates in a peptide precursor ion fragmentation process.

09759.title: peptide fragmentation technique
09759.definition: Mass spectrometric technique that serves to generate peptide fragment ions through the fragmentation of peptide precursor ions via different physicochemical processes in an ion source.

09714.title: peptide nucleic acid
09714.definition: Synthetic deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) mimic, which contains 2-aminoethylglycine linkages instead of the negatively charged phosphodiesteric backbone of oligonucleotides.

09760.title: peptide precursor ion
09760.definition: Peptide ion generated during the ionisation of peptides in an ion source or during tandem mass spectrometry of an intact protein in top-down proteomic analysis, selected for further analysis by means of tandem mass spectrometry.

13546.title: peptide tetramer
13546.definition: Structure consisting of four identical major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-encoded peptides, presenting four binding sites for biotin attached to the tail of the MHC molecule, and held together by fluorescent streptavidin.

13547.title: peptide vaccine
13547.definition: Preparation of an immunologically active peptide found in a disease-causing organism or substance, or any of their products, which is specially treated for use in vaccination.

13548.title: peptide-binding groove
13548.definition: Structural feature found in major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I and class II heterodimeric proteins that can bind endogenous peptides.

P04479.title: peptides
P04479.definition: Amides derived from two or more amino carboxylic acid molecules (the same or different) by formation of a covalent bond from the carbonyl carbon of one to the nitrogen atom of another with formal loss of water. The term is usually applied to structures formed from $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}amino acids}$, but it includes those derived from any amino carboxylic acid.  (R may be any organyl group, commonly but not necessarily one found in natural amino acids).

P04480.title: peptidoglycan
P04480.definition: A glycosaminoglycan formed by alternating residues of ᴅ-glucosamine and either muramic acid {2-amino-3-O-[(S)-1-carboxyethyl]-2-deoxy-ᴅ-glucose} or ʟ-talosaminuronic acid (2-amino-2-deoxy-ʟ-taluronic acid), which are usually N-acetylated or N-glycoloylated. The carboxyl group of the muramic acid is commonly substituted by a peptide containing residues of both ʟ- and ᴅ-amino acids, whereas that of ʟ-talosaminuronic acid is substituted by a peptide consisting of ʟ-amino acids only.

09761.title: peptidomics
09761.definition: Study of the set of peptides in an organism, its peptidome.

PT07642.title: peptization
PT07642.definition: Reversal of coagulation or flocculation, i.e., the dispersion of agglomerates to form a colloidally stable suspension or emulsion.

12703.title: peptoid
12703.definition: Peptide-like oligomer consisting of repeating \(N\)-substituted glycine units  where \(\ce{R1}\) to \(\ce{R4}\) are typically alkyl or aryl and may be the same or different.

14904.title: per capita birth rate
14904.definition: Average number of offspring per population member per time unit. Calculated from birth rate \(B\) and population size \(N\) as \[b = B/N\]

14905.title: per capita death rate
14905.definition: Average number of deaths per population member per time unit. Calculated from death rate \(D\) and population size \(N\) as \[m = D/N\]

14906.title: per capita rate of increase
14906.definition: Relative increase, \(r\), in the population per unit of time expressed per capita. \[r = b - m\] where \(b\) is per capita birth rate and \(m\) is per capita death rate.

P04485.title: percentage exposed
P04485.definition: The accessibility of the atoms of metal in metallic catalysts, supported or unsupported, depends upon the percentage of the total atoms of metal which are surface atoms. It is recommended that the term percentage exposed be employed for this quantity rather than the term dispersion which has been frequently employed.

P04486.title: percentage relative error
P04486.definition: The relative error expressed in percent. It can be calculated from the relative error by multiplying by 100. Comment: The term 'percentage relative error' should always be quoted in full, rather than 'error' or 'percentage error' to avoid confusion.

P04487.title: percentage standard deviation
P04487.definition: The value of the relative standard deviation, expressed in percent. It can be calculated from the relative standard deviation by multiplying by 100. Comment: It is recommended that the 'relative standard deviation' be reported, rather than the 'percentage standard deviation', in order to avoid confusion where results themselves are expressed as percentages. The term 'coefficient of variation' in place of 'relative standard deviation' is not recommended.

08516.title: percentage transmission
08516.definition: In atomic spectroscopy, flux of mass of sample divided by the flux of mass of solvent blank, measured under the same conditions, expressed as a percentage.

08847.title: percolation
08847.definition: Formation of the long-range (infinite) functional connectivity in a disperse system composed of small active particles evenly dispersed in an inactive matrix, which makes the system penetrable for a fluid or current.

08848.title: percolation threshold
08848.definition: Minimal volume fraction of functionally active small particles evenly dispersed in a non-active matrix, at which the long-range (infinite) functional connectivity in the system is achieved.

15966.title: percutaneous
15966.definition: Through the skin following application on the skin.

PT07570.title: perfect network
PT07570.definition: Polymer network composed of chains all of which are connected at both of their ends to different junction points.

P04490.title: perfectly polarized interphase
P04490.definition: Differences from the behaviour of interphases containing only neutral species arise when the interphase may be described as perfectly polarized. This term is used when no charged component is common to both phases adjoining the interphase. This may arise as a result of the equilibrium conditions or from the kinetics of charge transfer and leads to an interphase impermeable to electric charge.

13549.title: perforin
13549.definition: Molecule produced by cytotoxic T cells and natural killer (NK) cells that, like complement component C9, polymerizes to form a pore in the membrane of the target cell leading to cell death.

08094.title: performance characteristic of a measurement procedure
08094.definition: Aspect of a measurement procedure that may be quantitatively investigated and assessed as part of procedure validation.

08095.title: performance score
08095.definition: Statistic, derived from a result reported by a participant in a proficiency testing scheme, used in interpretation of participant performance and to allow comparison with defined objectives.

10286.title: perfusate
10286.definition: Stream of extraction phase entering a dialysis module.

15967.title: perfusion
15967.definition:
Act of pouring over or through, especially the passage of a fluid through the vessels of a specific organ.
Liquid poured over or through an organ or tissue.

PT06921.title: perfusion stationary phase
PT06921.definition: Stationary phase in which the mobile phase primarily travels through the pores of the stationary phase.

13550.title: periarteriolar lymphoid sheath
13550.definition: Lymphoid tissue that forms the white pulp of the spleen.

11078.title: pericardium
11078.definition: Serous membranous sac that surrounds the heart, consisting of an inner visceral layer (the epicardium), and an outer parietal pericardium that is attached to the sternum and diaphragm.

P04491.title: pericyclic reaction
P04491.definition: A chemical reaction in which concerted reorganization of bonding takes place throughout a cyclic array of continuously bonded atoms. It may be viewed as a reaction proceeding through a fully conjugated cyclic transition state. The number of atoms in the cyclic array is usually six, but other numbers are also possible. The term embraces a variety of processes, including cycloadditions, cheletropic reactions, electrocyclic reactions, sigmatropic rearrangements, etc. (provided they are concerted).

P04492.title: perikinetic aggregation
P04492.definition: The rate of aggregation is in general determined by the frequency of collisions and the probability of cohesion during collision. If the collisions are caused by Brownian motion, the process is called perikinetic aggregation.

14391.title: perikinetic coagulation
14391.definition: Coagulation due to collisions of particles caused by their Brownian motion.

11079.title: perinatal
11079.definition: Relating to the period from shortly before to shortly after birth, in humans usually from the 20th to the 29th week of gestation to one to four weeks after birth.

11080.title: perineum
11080.definition: Muscular structure of the lower pelvis, between the legs and extending from the anus to the pubic symphysis, or alternatively including the anus and vagina in the female and the region from the anus to the base of the scrotum in the male.

P04493.title: period
P04493.definition: Time for one cycle of a periodic phenomenon.

P04494.title: periodic copolymer
P04494.definition: A copolymer consisting of macromolecules comprising more than two species of monomeric units in regular sequence.

P04495.title: periodic copolymerization
P04495.definition: A copolymerization in which a periodic copolymer is formed.

P04496.title: periodic voltage
P04496.definition: This general term is applicable to square, triangular, and other wave forms.

13551.title: periodontitis
13551.definition: Inflammatory reaction of the tissues surrounding a tooth (periodontium), usually resulting from the extension of gingival inflammation (gingivitis) into the periodontium, and involving inflammation and infection of the ligaments and bones that support the teeth.

P04497.title: peripheral atom
P04497.definition: A secondary reference (non-core) atom which at some point in the mechanistic sequence is situated in the molecule containing the core atom(s).

09645.title: peripheral blood
09645.definition: Blood obtained from parts of the body that are located at some distance from the heart.

13552.title: peripheral blood leukocyte
13552.definition: Leukocyte derived from the peripheral circulatory system.

13553.title: peripheral blood mononuclear cell
13553.definition: Monocyte produced by the bone marrow from hematopoietic stem cell precursors, circulating in the bloodstream for about one to three days before moving into tissues throughout the body.

13554.title: peripheral lymphoid organ
13554.definition: Any of the lymphoid organs (see lymphoid tissue) other than the thymus.

12003.title: peripheral nervous system
12003.definition: One of the two major divisions of the nervous system, made up of the nerves and ganglia lying outside the brain and spinal cord that transmit sensory and motor signals to and from the central nervous system.

12004.title: peripheral neuropathy
12004.definition: Neuropathy affecting nerves of the peripheral nervous system.

13556.title: peripheral tolerance
13556.definition: Specific immunological tolerance occurring outside of the primary lymphoid organs (see lymphoid tissue).

14907.title: periphyton
14907.definition: Matrix of algae, microbes, and detritus attached to submerged surfaces in aquatic ecosystems.

P04499.title: periselectivity
P04499.definition: The differentiation between two symmetry-allowed processes, for example the [2+4] vs. [4+6] cycloaddition of cyclopentadiene to tropone.

12005.title: peristalsis
12005.definition: Progression of a wave of smooth muscle contraction followed by relaxation along the length of a muscular tube.

P04500.title: peritectic reaction
P04500.definition: An isothermal, reversible reaction between two phases, a liquid and a solid, that results, on cooling of a binary, ternary, ... , \(n\) system in one, two, ... (\(n- 1\)) new solid phases. Synonymous with incongruent reaction.

P04501.title: peritectoid reaction
P04501.definition: An isothermal, reversible reaction in the solid state, that, on cooling of a binary, ternary, ... , \(n\) system, results in one, two, ... (\(n-1\)) new solid phases. For example, in a binary system containing two solids \(\alpha'\) and \(\alpha''\) \[\alpha' + \alpha'' \rightarrow \beta\] Synonymous with metatectoid reaction.

P04502.title: peritectoid temperature
P04502.definition: The maximum temperature at which a peritectoid reaction can occur.

11081.title: peritoneal cavity
11081.definition: Potential space between the two layers (visceral and parietal) of the peritoneum.

15968.title: peritoneal dialysis
15968.definition: Method of artificial detoxication in which a toxic substance from the body is transferred into liquid that is instilled into the peritoneum.

11082.title: peritoneum
11082.definition: Thin double layer of mesothelium and irregular connective tissue that lines the abdominal cavity and covers most of the abdominal organs.

15344.title: peritonic reaction
15344.definition: Isothermal, isobaric reversible reaction between two phases, a saturated liquid and a solid, that results, on removal of the solvent component of a ternary system in one new solid phase. For example, \[\ce{l + \upalpha  \upbeta}\] where the forward arrow indicates the direction of removal of the solvent component. The system is in equilibrium along the peritonic line, on which is found the peritonic composition or point, an isothermal, isobaric invariant of the system which lies between the compositions of phases \(\ce{l}\) and \(\upalpha\).

PT07594.title: permanent crosslink
PT07594.definition: Crosslink formed by covalent bonds, intermolecular or intramolecular interactions that are stable under the conditions of use of the material formed.

08517.title: permanent modifier
08517.definition: Substance added together with the sample or standards in electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy that is refractory, or forms a refractory species (e.g., a carbide), and thus does not need to be renewed for several atomization cycles.

15969.title: permeability coefficient
15969.definition: Quantity defining the permeability of molecules across a cell membrane and expressed as \[P = \frac{KD}{\Delta x}\] where \(K\) is the partition coefficient, \(D\) is the diffusion coefficient, and \(\Delta x\) is the thickness of the cell membrane.

P04504.title: permeability of vacuum
P04504.definition: Fundamental physical constant by definition equal to \(4\ \pi \times 10^{-7}\ \rm{H m}^{-1}\), exactly.

P04503.title: permeability
P04503.definition: Permeability of vacuum multiplied by the relative permeability.

15970.title: permeable
15970.definition: Of a membrane, allowing a given substance to pass through.

PT06880.title: permeate
PT06880.definition: Stream containing penetrants that leaves a membrane module.

10287.title: permeation
10287.definition: Process by which mass transfer occurs through a membrane.

P04505.title: permeation chromatography
P04505.definition: Separation based mainly upon exclusion effects, such as differences in molecular size and/or shape (e.g. molecular-sieve chromatography) or in charge (e.g. ion-exclusion chromatography). The term gel-permeation chromatography is widely used for the process when the stationary phase is a gel. The term gel-filtration is not recommended.

P04506.title: permeation tube
P04506.definition: A device used for dynamic preparation of test gas mixtures by means of controlled permeation of a gaseous analyte out of a container through polymer material into a carrier gas stream. These devices containing certain condensable gases (e.g. $\ce{NO2}$, $\ce{SO2}$, etc.) when operated at closely controlled temperatures can be used as primary standards calibrated in terms of the weight loss per unit time.

15345.title: permil
15345.definition: One part in a thousand parts.

15971.title: permissible exposure limit
15971.definition: Recommendation by U.S. OSHA for a time-weighted average concentration that must not be exceeded during any \(\pu{8\!\mbox{-}h}\) work shift of a \(\pu{40\!\mbox{-}h}\) working week.

P04508.title: permittivity of vacuum
P04508.definition: Fundamental physical constant \(\varepsilon_{0}=\frac{1}{\mu _{0}\ c_{0}^{2}}\) exactly, where \(\mu_{0}\) is the permeability of vacuum and \(c_{0}\) the speed of light in vacuum. It is equal to \(8.854\ 187\ 817\,...\times\ 10^{-12}\ \rm{F m}^{-1}\).

P04507.title: permittivity
P04507.definition: Permittivity of vacuum multiplied by the relative permittivity.

P04509.title: permselectivity
P04509.definition: A term used to define the preferential permeation of certain ionic species through ion-exchange membranes.

13557.title: pernicious anemia
13557.definition: Disease in which the erythrocytes are abnormally formed, due to an inability to absorb vitamin \({\rm{B}}_{12}\). True pernicious anemia refers specifically to a disorder of atrophied parietal cells leading to absent intrinsic factor, resulting in an inability to absorb \({\rm{B}}_{12}\).

P04510.title: peroxides
P04510.definition: Compounds of structure $\ce{ROOR}$ in which $\ce{R}$ may be any organyl group (The term is also used in an inorganic sense to denote salts of the anion $\ce{O2^{2−}}$).

P04511.title: peroxisome
P04511.definition: Organelle, similar to a lysosome, characterized by its content of catalase (EC 1.11.1.6), peroxidase (EC 1.11.1.7) and other oxidative enzymes.

P04513.title: peroxy acids
P04513.definition: Acids in which an acidic $\ce{–OH}$ group has been replaced by an $\ce{–OOH}$ group, e.g. $\ce{CH3C(=O)OOH}$ peroxyacetic acid, $\ce{PhS(=O)2OOH}$ benzeneperoxysulfonic acid.

12261.title: Perrin equation
12261.definition: For an isolated dissolved molecule or dispersed entity, an equation relating the rotational diffusion coefficient, \(\mathit{\Theta}\), to the equivalent hydrodynamic radius in rotational diffusive flow, \(r_{\mathit{\Theta}}\), and to the viscosity of the solvent continuum or the dispersion medium continuum, \(\eta_{0}\), with \[D = kT/(6\pi \eta_{\rm{0}} r_{\mathit{\Theta}}^3)\] where \(k\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature.

P04515.title: persistence length
P04515.definition: The average projection of the end-to-end vector on the tangent to the chain contour at a chain end in the limit of infinite chain length. The persistence length (symbol a) is the basic characteristic of the worm-like chain.

P04516.title: persistent
P04516.definition: A term used to characterize radicals which have lifetimes of several minutes or greater in dilute solution in inert solvents. Persistence is a kinetic or reactivity property. In contrast, radical stability, which is a thermodynamic property, is expressed in terms of the $\ce{C–H}$ bond strength of the appropriate hydrocarbon. The lifetime of a radical is profoundly influenced by steric shielding of the radical centre by bulky substituents.

14908.title: persistent inorganic pollutant
14908.definition: Inorganic substance that is stable in the environment, is liable to long-range transport, may bioaccumulate in human and animal tissue, and may have significant impacts on human health and the environment.

14909.title: persistent organic pollutant
14909.definition: Organic chemical that is stable in the environment, is liable to long-range transport, may bioaccumulate in human and animal tissue, and may have significant impacts on human health and the environment.

15972.title: personal monitoring
15972.definition: Type of environmental monitoring in which an individual’s exposure to a substance is measured and evaluated.

15973.title: personal protective device
15973.definition: Equipment (clothing, gloves, hard hat, respirator, etc.) worn by an individual to prevent exposure to a potentially toxic substance.

15974.title: personal sampler
15974.definition: Compact, portable instrument for individual air sampling, measuring, or both, the content of a harmful substance in the respiration zone of a working person.

P04517.title: perspective formula
P04517.definition: A geometric representation of stereochemical features of a molecule or model which appears as a view from an appropriate direction.

PT06881.title: perstraction
PT06881.definition: Separation process in which membrane permeation and extraction phenomena occur by contacting the downstream with an extracting solvent.

PT07090.title: perturbation theory
PT07090.definition: Along with variational method, the second major quantum-mechanical approximation method. The methods of perturbation theory are based on representation of the Hamiltonian of a system under study, \(H\), through the Hamiltonian, \(H^{0}\), of a system, whose Schroedinger equation is solvable, and its relatively small perturbation \(H^{\rm{'}}\): \(H=H^{0}+H^{\rm{'}}\). Numerous techniques are derived allowing one to relate the unknown eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the perturbed system to the known eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the unperturbed system. As distinct from the variational method, the methods of perturbation theory are applicable to all the electronic states of an atom or molecule. When \(H^{\rm{'}}\) is time-dependent, the perturbed system does not have stationary states. In this case time-dependent perturbation theory, which is the method of approximate calculation of the expansion of wave-functions of the perturbed system over wave-functions of stationary states of the unperturbed system, must be employed. The applications of this method are associated mostly with studies of light emission and absorption by atoms and molecules.

08749.title: perturbed angular correlation spectrometry
08749.definition: Measurement method of gamma-ray spectrometry in which coincidence counting is used for the measurement of parameters describing hyperfine interactions, with internal or external electrical or magnetic field gradients, of the spin of an intermediate level between two gamma-ray transitions in cascade emitted in the decay of a radionuclide.

P04518.title: perturbed dimensions
P04518.definition: The dimensions of an actual polymer random coil not in a theta state.

PT06892.title: pervaporation
PT06892.definition: Membrane-based process in which the feed and retentate streams are both liquid phases while permeant emerges at the downstream face of the membrane as a vapour.

15975.title: pest
15975.definition: Organism that may harm public health, attacks food and other materials essential to mankind, or otherwise affects human beings adversely.

P04519.title: pesticide
P04519.definition: Strictly, a substance intended to kill pests: in common usage, any substance used for controlling, preventing, or destroying animal, microbiological or plant pests.

P04520.title: pesticide residue
P04520.definition: Any substance or mixture of substances in food for man or animals resulting from the use of a pesticide including any specified derivatives, such as degradation and conversion products, metabolites, reaction products and impurities considered to be of toxicological significance.

P04522.title: petroleum coke
P04522.definition: A carbonization product of high-boiling hydrocarbon fractions obtained in petroleum processing (heavy residues). It is the general term for all special petroleum coke products such as green, calcined and needle petroleum coke.

P04523.title: petroleum pitch
P04523.definition: A residue from heat treatment and distillation of petroleum fractions. It is solid at room temperature, consists of a complex mixture of numerous predominantly aromatic and alkyl-substituted aromatic hydrocarbons, and exhibits a broad softening range instead of a defined melting temperature.

13558.title: pexophagy
13558.definition: Autophagy selective for degradation of peroxisomes, which can be separated into macropexophagy and micropexophagy.

13559.title: Peyer’s patch
13559.definition: Part of the gut-associated lymphoid tissue (GALT) and found as a distinct lymphoid nodule, mainly in the small intestine.

P04524.title: pH
P04524.definition: The quantity pH is defined in terms of the activity of hydrogen(1+) ions (hydrogen ions) in solution: \[\rm{pH} = -\rm{lg}[a(\rm{H}^{+})] = -\rm{lg}[\rm{m}(\rm{H}^{+})\gamma_{\rm{m}}(\rm{H}^{+})/m^{\unicode{x29B5} }]\] where \(a(\rm{H}^{+})\) is the activity of hydrogen ion (hydrogen 1+) in aqueous solution, \(\rm{H}^{+}\rm{(aq)}\), \(\gamma_{\rm{m}}(\rm{H}^{+})\) is the activity coefficient of \(\rm{H}^{+}\rm{(aq)}\) (molality basis) at molality \(m(\rm{H}^{+})\), and \(m^{⦵} = \pu{1 mol kg-1}\) is the standard molality.

P04545.title: pH glass electrode
P04545.definition: A hydrogen-ion responsive electrode usually consisting of a bulb, or other suitable form, of special glass attached to a stem of high resistance glass complete with internal reference electrode and internal filling solution system. Other geometrical forms may be appropriate for special applications, e.g. capillary electrode for measurement of blood pH.

P04546.title: pH gradient
P04546.definition: The differential change of pH with distance (\(\frac{\rm{dpH}}{\rm{d}I}\)).

14912.title: pH-partition hypothesis
14912.definition: Hypothesis that bioavailability is governed by the diffusion of the unionized form of an ionizable substance through the gastrointestinal lumen, as determined by \(\pu{p}K_{\rm{a}}\) and \(\rm{pH}\).

P04660.title: pH-rate profile
P04660.definition: A plot of observed rate coefficient, or more usually its decadic logarithm, against pH of solution, other variables being kept constant.

09121.title: pH-sensitive electrode
09121.definition: Potentiometric electrochemical sensor that measures pH as a linear function of electrode potential.

09947.title: pH-zone-refining counter-current chromatography
09947.definition: Counter-current chromatography that produces a train of fused rectangular solute peaks called pH-zones, each with its specific pH. Each zone contains highly concentrated solute, often near saturation level, and is separated from the neighbouring zone by a narrow strip called a mixing zone, which contains a mixture of impurities.

P04525.title: pH0.5 or pH1/2
P04525.definition: That value of pH in an aqueous phase at which the distribution ratio is unity at equilibrium. 50% of the solute is extracted (\(E = 0.5\)) only when the phase ratio is unity.

11083.title: phage display
11083.definition: Method that enables the presentation of large peptide libraries on the surface of phage particles, from which proteins with desired functional properties can be selected rapidly.

13560.title: phagocyte
13560.definition: Cell, especially of monocyte/macrophage or neutrophil lineage, that is specialized for the engulfment of cellular and particulate matter.

13561.title: phagocytic activity assay
13561.definition: Method of quantifying phagocytosis in which yeast cells, stained with May–Grünwald stain, are incubated with macrophages, and subsequently, after a fixed time, yeast cells engulfed in the macrophages are counted.

13562.title: phagocytosis
13562.definition: Process by which particulate material is endocytosed by a cell.

13563.title: phagolysosome
13563.definition: Intracellular vacuole where killing and digestion of phagocytosed material occurs following the fusion of a phagosome with a lysosome.

13564.title: phagosome
13564.definition: Intracellular vacuole produced following invagination of the cell membrane around phagocytosed material.

PT07605.title: phantom chain behaviour
PT07605.definition: Hypothetical behaviour in which chains can move freely through one another when a network is deformed.

11985.title: phantom pain
11985.definition: Sensation that an amputated limb is still present, often associated with pain.

15223.title: pharmaceutical equivalence
15223.definition: To be pharmaceutically equivalent, the generic and proprietary formulations must (1) contain the same amount of active ingredient; (2) contain the same active ingredient in the same dosage form; (3) be intended for the same route of administration; and (4) generally be labeled for the same conditions of use.

15224.title: pharmaceutics
15224.definition: Science of preparation of drugs, dosage forms, and drug delivery systems taking into account the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the drug as well as its physical and chemical properties.

P04526.title: pharmacodynamics
P04526.definition: Study of pharmacological actions on living systems, including the reactions with and binding to cell constituents, and the biochemical and physiological consequences of these actions.

12705.title: pharmacogenetics
12705.definition: Study of inherited differences (variation) in drug metabolism and response.

12706.title: pharmacogenomics
12706.definition: General study of all of the many different genes that determine drug behaviour.

PT06835.title: pharmacokinetics
PT06835.definition: Process of the uptake of drugs by the body, the biotransformation they undergo, the distribution of the drugs and their metabolites in the tissues, and the elimination of the drugs and their metabolites from the body over a period of time.Study of such processes.

11485.title: pharmacophore
11485.definition:
A proposal for the ensemble of steric and electronic features that define the optimal supermolecular intermolecular interaction of a ligand with a specific
 biological target structure with the result that it triggers or blocks its biological response.

11084.title: pharyngeal groove
11084.definition: One of several paired grooves in the embryonic endoderm, lateral to the corresponding pharyngeal pouch in the ectoderm.

11085.title: pharyngeal pouch
11085.definition: One of several paired evaginations in the embryonic endoderm that develop into epithelial tissues and organs such as the thymus and thyroid gland.

11086.title: pharynx
11086.definition: Part of the digestive tube lying between the esophagus (below) and the mouth and nasal cavity (above and anterior).

P04528.title: phase
P04528.definition: An entity of a material system which is uniform in chemical composition and physical state.

12707.title: phase 0 clinical studies
12707.definition: Exploratory first-in-human trials that involve microdosing of drug to allow the assessment of pharmacokinetic parameters with limited drug exposure.

08391.title: phase correction
08391.definition: Linear combination of the real and imaginary parts of a 1-D nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum to produce peaks with pure absorption mode line shape.

08392.title: phase cycling
08392.definition: Component of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment that repeats a pulse sequence changing only the phases of the pulse(s) and the phase-sensitive detector reference.

15346.title: phase diagram
15346.definition: Graphical representation, by use of points, lines, and surfaces, of the phases present at chemical equilibrium in unary, binary, ternary, and higher-order systems containing two or more phases.

PT07286.title: phase domain
PT07286.definition: Region of a material that is uniform in chemical composition and physical state.

14031.title: phase function
14031.definition: Distribution function representing the fraction of photons scattered from any direction \(\mathit{\Omega}'\) into the direction \(\mathit{\Omega}\) under consideration in the radiative transfer equation (RTE). Dimension one.

12708.title: phase I clinical studies
12708.definition: Initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

PT06836.title: phase I reaction
PT06836.definition: Enzymic modification of a substance by oxidation, reduction, hydrolysis, hydration, dehydrochlorination, or other reactions catalyzed by enzymes of the cytosol, of the endoplasmic reticulum (microsomal enzymes) or of other cell organelles.

12709.title: phase II clinical studies
12709.definition: Controlled clinical studies conducted in a limited number of individuals to obtain some preliminary data on the effectiveness of an investigational new drug for a particular indication or indications in patients with the disease or condition.

PT06837.title: phase II reaction
PT06837.definition: Binding of a substance, or its metabolites from a phase I reaction, with endogenous molecules (conjugation), making more water-soluble derivatives that may be excreted in the urine or bile.

12710.title: phase III clinical studies
12710.definition: Expanded controlled and uncontrolled trials in humans.

15976.title: phase III reaction
15976.definition: Further metabolism of conjugated metabolites produced by phase II reactions.

PT07291.title: phase interaction
PT07291.definition: Molecular interaction between the components present in the interphases of a multiphase mixture.

P04530.title: phase inversion
P04530.definition: A term used in two senses which should be specified: density inversion or continuity inversion.

P04531.title: phase ratio
P04531.definition: The ratio of the volume of the mobile phase to that of the stationary phase in a column: \[\beta = \frac{V_{0}}{V_{\rm{s}}}\] In the case of open-tubular columns the geometric internal volume of the tube (\(V_{\rm{c}}\)) is to be substituted for \(V_{0}\).

P04532.title: phase ratio
P04532.definition: The ratio of the quantity of the solvent to that of the other phase.

P04533.title: phase rule
P04533.definition: The number of degrees of freedom, \(F\), that a system containing \(C\) components can have when \(P\) phases are in equilibrium, is given as: \[F=C- P+2\]

P04534.title: phase separation
P04534.definition: The process by which a single solid (liquid) phase separates into two or more new phases.

P04537.title: phase transition
P04537.definition: A change in the nature of a phase or in the number of phases as a result of some variation in externally imposed conditions, such as temperature, pressure, activity of a component or a magnetic, electric or stress field.

P04535.title: phase-space theory
P04535.definition: This is a theory applied to unimolecular or bimolecular reactions proceeding through long-lived complexes. The probability of reaction is assumed to be proportional to the number of states available to a particular product channel divided by the number of states corresponding to all product channels. The theory is used to predict rates, product energy distributions, product velocity distributions, and product angular momentum distributions.

P04536.title: phase-transfer catalysis
P04536.definition: The phenomenon of rate enhancement of a reaction between chemical species located in different phases (immiscible liquids or solid and liquid) by addition of a small quantity of an agent (called the 'phase-transfer catalyst') that extracts one of the reactants, most commonly an anion, across the interface into the other phase so that reaction can proceed. These catalysts are salts of 'onium ions' (e.g. tetraalkylammonium salts) or agents that complex inorganic cations (e.g. crown ethers). The catalyst cation is not consumed in the reaction although an anion exchange does occur.

14369.title: phase-transfer event in a dispersed system
14369.definition: Transport of any species (radical, monomer, chain-transfer agent, etc.) from the continuous to the discrete phase and vice-versa.

P04538.title: phenolates
P04538.definition: Synonymous with phenoxides. The term phenolate should not be used for solvates derived from a phenol, for the ending -ate often occurs in names for anions.

15249.title: phenolic polymer
15249.definition: Polymer prepared by the polycondensation of phenols and aldehydes or by curing reactive oligomers prepared from phenols and aldehydes.

P04539.title: phenols
P04539.definition: Compounds having one or more hydroxy groups attached to a benzene or other arene ring, e.g. 2-naphthol:

15977.title: phenome
15977.definition: Complete phenotypic description of an organism (by analogy with genome).

P04540.title: phenomenological equation
P04540.definition:
In the following only media which are isotropic with respect to mass transport (i.e. the transport coefficients are independent of direction) are being considered. In the linear range (not too far from equilibrium), for uniform temperature and neglecting external fields such as the earth's gravitational field, the flux density of species B is related to the gradients of the electrochemical potentials of all species by the phenomenological equation: \[N_{\rm{B}}- c_{\rm{B}}\ v_{\rm{A}}=- \sum _{\begin{array}{c}
i\\
i\neq A
\end{array}}L_{\rm{B}i}^{\rm{A}}\ \nabla \mu _{i}\] with \[i=\rm{B},\rm{C},...\] where \(\nabla \mu _{i}\) is the gradient of the electrochemical potential of species i. The proportionality factors \(L_{\rm{B}i}^{\rm{A}}\) are called phenomenological coefficients. Their values depend on the frame of reference. The latter is taken here to move with the velocity \(v_{\rm{A}}\) of species A, and hence: \[L_{\rm{A}i}^{\rm{A}}=0\]

P04541.title: phenonium ions
P04541.definition: The traditional generic name for those cyclohexadienyl cations that are spiro-annulated with a cyclopropane unit. Phenonium ions constitute a subclass of arenium ions.

P04542.title: phenotype
P04542.definition: The observable structural and functional characteristics of an organism determined by its genotype and modulated by its environment.

12712.title: phenotypic screening
12712.definition: Evaluation of compounds (small molecules, peptides, siRNA, etc.) in cells, tissues, or organisms for their ability to modify the system in a measurable manner.

P04543.title: phenoxides
P04543.definition: Salts or analogous metal derivatives of phenols; synonymous with phenolates. A preferable general term, however, is aryloxides.

11087.title: phenylketonuria
11087.definition: Autosomal recessive disorder resulting from mutations that impair the function of the enzyme phenylalanine 4-monooxygenase (EC 1.14.16.1).

12006.title: pheochromocytoma
12006.definition: Tumor of the chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla that results in excessive secretion of norepinephrine and other catecholamines.

P04544.title: pheromone
P04544.definition: Substance used in olfactory communication between organisms of the same species eliciting a change in sexual or social behaviour. Synonymous with ectohormone, feromone.

13565.title: Philadelphia chromosome
13565.definition: Chromosome resulting from a reciprocal translocation between human chromosomes 9 and 22, most commonly associated with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML).

11088.title: philtrum
11088.definition: Groove in the midline of the upper lip below the nose.

11089.title: phocomelia
11089.definition: Congenital abnormality in which one or more of the hands or feet is attached to an underdeveloped limb, and therefore too close to the body.

P04547.title: phonon
P04547.definition: Elementary excitation in the quantum mechanical treatment of vibrations in a crystal lattice. An energy bundle that behaves as a particle of energy \(h\ \nu \), with \(\nu \) the vibration frequency and \(h\) the Planck constant.

12007.title: phonophobia
12007.definition: Abnormal fear of loud sound, or occasionally of voices.

13566.title: phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate
13566.definition: Mitogenic phorbol ester that directly stimulates protein kinase C (PKC) and acts as a tumor promoter.

P04548.title: phosphanes
P04548.definition: The saturated hydrides of tervalent phosphorus having the general formula $\ce{P_{n}H_{n+2}}$. Individual members having an unbranched phosphorus chain are named phosphane, diphosphane, triphosphane, etc. The name of a saturated hydride of phosphorus wherein one or more phosphorus atoms have a bonding number of 5 is formed by prefixing locants and \(\lambda ^{5}\) symbols to the name of the corresponding phosphane. Hydrocarbyl derivatives of $\ce{PH3}$ belong to the class phosphines.

P04549.title: phosphanylidenes
P04549.definition: Recommended name for carbene analogues having the structure $\ce{RP{:}}$ (former IUPAC name is phosphinediyls). A common non-IUPAC synonym is phosphinidenes.

P04550.title: phosphatidic acids
P04550.definition: Derivatives of glycerol in which one hydroxy group, commonly but not necessarily primary, is esterified with phosphoric acid and the other two are esterified with fatty acids.

P04551.title: phosphazenes
P04551.definition: Compounds containing a phosphorus–nitrogen double bond, i.e. derivatives of $\ce{H3P=NH}$ and $\ce{HP=NH}$. A multiplicity of such bonds is present in various well-established chain, ring and cage compounds. E.g.

P04552.title: phosphine oxides
P04552.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R3P=O  R3P^{+}–O^{−}}$ (analogously, phosphine imides and phosphine sulfides).

P04553.title: phosphines
P04553.definition: $\ce{PH3}$ and compounds derived from it by substituting one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups $\ce{R3P}$. $\ce{RPH2}$, $\ce{R2PH}$ and $\ce{R3P}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$) are called primary, secondary and tertiary phosphines, respectively. A specific phosphine is preferably named as a substituted phosphane, e.g. $\ce{CH3PH2}$ methylphosphane.

P04557.title: phospho
P04557.definition: A prefix used in biochemical nomenclature in place of phosphono to denote the $\ce{-P(=O)(OH)2}$ group linked to a heteroatom, e.g. $\ce{Me3N^{+}-CH2CH2–OP(=O)(OH)O^{-}}$ phosphocholine.An infix used in biochemical nomenclature to name phosphoric diesters, e.g. glycerophosphocholine.

P04558.title: phosphoglycerides
P04558.definition: Phosphoric diesters, esters of phosphatidic acids, generally having a polar head group ($\ce{OH}$ or $\ce{N2}$) on the esterified alcohol which typically is 2-aminoethanol, choline, glycerol, inositol, serine. The term includes lecithins, cephalins. E.g.

13567.title: phospholipase Cγ
13567.definition: Enzyme that cleaves phosphatidylinositol bisphosphate into diacylglycerol and inositol trisphosphate, leading to the activation of two major cell signaling pathways.

P04559.title: phospholipids
P04559.definition: Lipids containing phosphoric acid as mono- or di-esters, including phosphatidic acids and phosphoglycerides.

P04561.title: phosphonitriles
P04561.definition: Compounds of stoichiometric composition $\ce{[X2PN]_{n}}$, in which $\ce{X}$ is alkoxy, halogen, or other electronegative group, and \(n\) is a variable integer, the value of which may not be known.

P04562.title: phosphonium compounds
P04562.definition: Salts (and hydroxides) $\ce{[R4P^{+}]X^{−}}$ containing tetracoordinate phosphonium ion and the associated anion.

P04563.title: phosphonium ylides
P04563.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R3P^{+}–C^{−}R2  R3P=CR2}$. Also known as Wittig reagents.

P04564.title: phosphono
P04564.definition: A prefix indicating the presence of the group $\ce{–P(=O)(OH)2}$.

P04566.title: phosphoramides
P04566.definition: Compounds in which one or more of the OH groups of phosphoric acid have been replaced with an amino or substituted amino group; commonly confined to the phosphoric triamides, $\ce{P(=O)(NR2)3, since replacement of one or two $\ce{OH}$ groups produces phosphoramidic acids $\ce{P(=O)(OH)(NR2)2}$, $\ce{P(=O)(OH)2(NR2)}$.

P04567.title: phosphoranes
P04567.definition: The mononuclear hydride $\ce{PH5}$, systematically named \(\lambda ^{5}\)-phosphane, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives. By extension, the literature also applies the term to phosphonium ylides.

P04568.title: phosphoranyl radicals
P04568.definition: A tetracoordinate phosphorus species which has nine valence-shell electrons $\ce{R4P^{.}}$.

P04569.title: phosphorescence
P04569.definition: From a phenomenological point of view, the term has been used to describe long-lived luminescence. In mechanistic photochemistry, the term designates luminescence involving change in spin multiplicity, typically from triplet to singlet or vice versa. The luminescence from a quartet state to a doublet state is also phosphorescence.

PT07443.title: phosphorescence lifetime
PT07443.definition: Parameter describing the time evolution of the decay of the phosphorescence radiant intensity.

P04571.title: phosphoroscope
P04571.definition: A mechanical device used to separate phosphorescence from fluorescence.

PT06790.title: phosphorylation
PT06790.definition: A process (catalysed by enzymes) involving the transfer of a phosphate group from a donor to a suitable acceptor; in general, an ester linkage is formed, for example: $\ce{ATP + alcohol -> ADP + phosphate ester}$.

12301.title: photo- technique
12301.definition: Indicates that the experiment involves the illumination of the sample or measures the amount of light emitted from a sample. Where possible, the wavelength range of the light should be specified.

PT07444.title: photo-Bergman cyclization
PT07444.definition: Intramolecular photoinduced cyclization of enediynes leading to aromatic compounds.

PT07449.title: photo-Claisen rearrangement
PT07449.definition: Rearrangement closely related to the photo-Fries rearrangement; it is experienced by aryl ethers (instead of aryl esters) and follows an analogous mechanism.

PT07180.title: photo-elastic polymer
PT07180.definition: Polymer that, under stress, exhibits birefringence.

P04614.title: photo-Fries rearrangement
P04614.definition: A photorearrangement of aryl or acyl esters to give the-rearranged product (as well as the-rearranged product):

16267.title: photo-induced toxicity
16267.definition: Toxicity of a chemical in the presence of light due to the production of toxic photolysis products.

15978.title: photo-irritation
15978.definition: Inflammation of the skin caused by exposure to light, especially that due to metabolites formed in the skin by photolysis.

09548.title: photoacid generator
09548.definition: Compound that on exposure to radiation gives rise to a proton.

P04574.title: photoacoustic detector
P04574.definition: A pressure-sensitive detector used to detect intermittent radiation absorbed in a black body or in the sample concerned. The resulting rapid temperature change produces a transient pressure oscillation that is observed with the help of a microphone, or a piezoelectric device.

P04575.title: photoacoustic effect
P04575.definition: Generation of heat after absorption of radiation, due to radiationless deactivation or chemical reaction.

08658.title: photoacoustic saturation
08658.definition: Condition in photoacoustic spectroscopy in which all bands with greater than a certain absorption intensity appear to have the same intensity.

P04576.title: photoacoustic spectroscopy
P04576.definition: A spectroscopic technique based on the photoacoustic effect. A photoacoustic spectrum consists of a plot of the intensity of the acoustic signal detected by a microphone or a 'piezoelectric' detector, against the excitation wavelength or another quantity related to the photon energy of the modulated excitation.

09549.title: photoactive compound
09549.definition: Compound that on exposure to radiation will release an active ionic or radical species.

14032.title: photoadsorbate
14032.definition: Entity (molecule, atom, or ion) bound to the surface of a solid (semiconductor or insulator) particle (typically to a photoadsorption centre) as the result of photoexcitation of either the solid or the entity (molecule, atom, or ion).

P04577.title: photoadsorption
P04577.definition: Irradiation by light (usually visible or ultraviolet) may affect adsorption. In a system containing adsorptive and adsorbent exposure to light may lead to increased adsorption (photoadsorption) or it may lead to desorption of an adsorbate (photodesorption).

14033.title: photoadsorption area number
14033.definition: Maximum amount of substance photoadsorbed per area on the uniformly irradiated surface of an adsorbent.

14034.title: photoadsorption capacity
14034.definition: Maximal number of entities (molecules, atoms, or ions) per regular surface site that can be photoadsorbed at a uniformly irradiated surface of an adsorbent, \(\theta_{\rm{max}} = N_{\rm{max}}/N^{\rm{ss}}\) where \(N_{\rm{max}}\) is the maximal number of entities photoadsorbed and \(N^{\rm{ss}}\) is the number of surface sites (mainly regular surface sites, i.e., regular lattice ions or atoms; typically, \(N^{\rm{ss}}\) ca. \(\pu{E15 cm-2}\)).

14035.title: photoadsorption centre
14035.definition: Surface site or defect in its active state after photoexcitation capable of photoadsorbing species by a chemical interaction with the adsorbate entities (molecules, atoms, or ions).

14036.title: photoadsorption efficiency
14036.definition: Ratio of the maximal (typically the initial) rate of photoadsorption of entities \(\ce{B}\) (molecules, atoms, or ions) to the integrated incident (superscript 0, zero) photon flux, \(\int_{\lambda_{1}}^{\lambda_{2}} q_{\rm{p},\lambda}^{0}{\rm{d}}\lambda = q_{\rm{p}}^{0} = {\rm{d}}N_{\rm{p}}^{0}/{\rm{d}}t\), in the wavelength range \(\lambda_{1}{-}\lambda_{2}\). Both rates should be measured under otherwise identical conditions (preferably as initial rates) in order to avoid concentration and/or surface area effects.

14037.title: photoadsorption fraction
14037.definition: Number of entities (atoms, molecules or ions) photoadsorbed per regular surface site at a uniformly irradiated surface of an adsorbent.

14038.title: photoadsorption photonic yield
14038.definition: Ratio of the maximal (typically the initial) rate of photoadsorption of entities \(\ce{B}\) (molecules, atoms, or ions) on a surface to the incident (superscript 0, zero) photon flux, \(q_{\rm{p},\lambda}^{0} = {\rm{d}}N_{\rm{p},\lambda}^{0}/{\rm{d}}t\) at a given wavelength. Both rates should be measured under otherwise identical conditions (preferably as initial rates) in order to avoid concentration and/or surface area effects.

14039.title: photoadsorption quantum yield
14039.definition: Ratio of the number of photoadsorbed entities \(\ce{B}\) (molecules, atoms, or ions) on a surface to the number of photons of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation (at a given wavelength \(\lambda\)) absorbed by the system (typically by the adsorbent) during the initial stage of irradiation.

P04578.title: photoaffinity labelling
P04578.definition: Technique by which a photochemically reactive molecular entity, specifically associated with a biomolecule, is photo-excited in order to covalently attach a label to the biomolecule, usually via intermediates. Identification of the resulting photo-crosslinked product provides structural information on the protein′s binding site.

13568.title: photoallergy
13568.definition: Type IV hypersensitivity reaction in which photoactivation of a substance produces a hapten that then acts as a sensitizer.

P04579.title: photoassisted catalysis
P04579.definition: Catalytic reaction involving production of a catalyst by absorption of light.

PT07445.title: photobiology
PT07445.definition: Branch of biology concerned with the biological and bioenvironmental effects of ultraviolet, visible or infrared radiation.

16206.title: photocaged fluorescent molecules
16206.definition: Caged fluorophores displaying a high fluorescent enhancement after photolysis.

14040.title: photocarrier
14040.definition: Nonequilibrium free electron or free hole generated in a solid by ultraviolet, visible, or infrared absorption and occupying energy levels in the conduction band or the valence band, respectively.

P04580.title: photocatalysis
P04580.definition: Change in the rate of a chemical reaction or its initiation under the action of ultraviolet, visible or infrared radiation in the presence of a substance—the photocatalyst—that absorbs light and is involved in the chemical transformation of the reaction partners.

PT07446.title: photocatalyst
PT07446.definition: Catalyst able to produce, upon absorption of light, chemical transformations of the reaction partners. The excited state of the photocatalyst repeatedly interacts with the reaction partners forming reaction intermediates and regenerates itself after each cycle of such interactions.

14041.title: photocatalytic active centre
14041.definition: Surface centre, i.e., either a surface defect or a regular surface site, at which a chemical transformation takes place after converting the centre into an active state by a photophysical process, e.g., by photoexcitation.

14042.title: photocatalytic activity
14042.definition: Number of entities (product) formed in a photocatalytic process (alternatively the number of reactant entities disappearing) divided by the number of photons absorbed by the photocatalyst at one single wavelength or within a defined wavelength range. For one wavelength it has the same meaning as quantum yield, whereas within a defined wavelength range it has the same meaning as quantum efficiency.

14043.title: photocatalytic centre
14043.definition: Surface centre, i.e., a surface defect or a regular surface site, in an active or electronically excited state at which a chemical transformation takes place.

14044.title: photocatalytic efficiency
14044.definition: Number of entities (product) formed (alternatively the number of reactant entities disappearing) divided by the number of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared photons incident (prior to absorption) on the system and in a wavelength range \(\lambda_{1}{-}\lambda_{2}\).

14045.title: photocatalytic oxidation
14045.definition: Commonly used to describe the oxidation of pollutants by the action of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation and a catalyst.

16207.title: photochemical aromatic substitution
16207.definition: Photoinduced substitution in an aromatic compound.

P04583.title: photochemical equivalence
P04583.definition: According to the principle of photochemical equivalence, there is a one-to-one relationship between the number of photons absorbed by a system and the number of excited species produced. The principle often fails for light of high intensity (e.g. laser beams), when molecules may absorb more than one photon.

PT07447.title: photochemical funnel
PT07447.definition: Molecular structure where the excited-state reactant or intermediate is delivered to the ground state to initiate product formation.

16209.title: photochemical nucleophile-olefin combination - aromatic substitution
16209.definition: Photoinduced electron-transfer reaction of an aromatic electron-acceptor in the presence of an olefinic electron donor and a nucleophile, leading to aromatic substitution.

P04585.title: photochemical reaction
P04585.definition: Generally used to describe a chemical reaction caused by absorption of ultraviolet, visible or infrared radiation. There are many ground-state reactions, which have photochemical counterparts. Among these are photochemical nitrogen extrusions, photocycloadditions, photodecarbonylations, photodecarboxylations, photoenolizations, photo-Fries rearrangement, photoisomerizations, photooxidations, photorearrangements, photoreductions, photosubstitutions, etc.

PT07448.title: photochemical reaction path
PT07448.definition: Sequence of geometries adopted by a molecule after initial electronic excitation, combined with a specification of the electronic state at each geometry, from radiation absorption to product formation. Theoretically, this usually involves the computation of the MERP connecting the Franck–Condon point, located on the potential-energy surface of the spectroscopic state, to the final photoproducts located on the ground-state potential-energy surface. Experimentally, a photochemical reaction path can be probed by detecting transient species or reaction intermediates.

P04586.title: photochemical smog
P04586.definition: Product of photochemical reactions caused by solar radiation and occurring in polluted air as well as in air contaminated by compounds emitted by natural sources, such as those emitted by vegetation.

P04588.title: photochemistry
P04588.definition: The branch of chemistry concerned with the chemical effects of light (far UV to IR).

P04589.title: photochromism
P04589.definition: Reversible transformation of a molecular entity between two forms, A and B, having different absorption spectra, induced in one or both directions by absorption of electromagnetic radiation. The spectral change produced is typically, but not necessarily, of visible colour and is accompanied by differences in other physical properties. The thermodynamically stable form A is transformed by irradiation into form B. The back reaction can occur thermally (photochromism of type T) or photochemically (photochromism of type P).  The terms 'switch-on' and 'switch-of' are sometimes used to denote the two directions of the photochromic reaction.

08850.title: photoconducting polymer
08850.definition: Polymer exhibiting electrical conductivity or a clear increase in electrical conductivity under irradiation.

P04590.title: photoconductive detector
P04590.definition: In a photoconductive detector an electric potential is applied across the absorbing region and causes a current to flow in proportion to the irradiance if the photon energy exceeds the energy gap between the valence and the conduction band. Depending on their spectral responsivity function, photoconductive detectors are divided into photoconductive detectors for the visible wavelength range e.g. cadmium sulfide or $\ce{CdS}$ photoconductive detectors, photoconductive detectors for the near infrared wavelength range e.g. lead sulfide or $\ce{PbS}$ photoconductive detectors, photoconductive detectors for the infrared wavelength range e.g. silicon doped with arsenide or $\ce{Si:As}$ photoconductive detectors, and the mercury-cadmium-telluride or $\ce{HgCdTe}$ photoconductive detector.

P04591.title: photoconductivity
P04591.definition: Electrical conductivity resulting from photoproduction of charge carriers.

13569.title: photocontact dermatitis
13569.definition: Type of contact dermatitis arising when substances are transformed into either irritants or allergens upon exposure to light.

14046.title: photocorrosion
14046.definition: Decomposition of the photocatalyst or of the electrodes as a result of a photoinduced reaction.

P04592.title: photocrosslinking
P04592.definition: The formation of a covalent linkage between two macromolecules or between two different parts of one macromolecule.

14047.title: photocurrent
14047.definition: Photogeneration and movement of charge between two electrodes in a photovoltaic cell or a photoelectrochemical cell as a result of photoprocesses induced by light absorption.

P04594.title: photocurrent yield
P04594.definition: The quantum efficiency of electron transport between the two electrodes of a photovoltaic cell or photoelectrochemical cell.

PT07450.title: photocyclization
PT07450.definition: Intramolecular photochemical process leading to carbo- or hetero- cyclic ring systems by formation of one new single bond, either by a concerted process (e.g., electrocyclization) or by multi-step processes such as Norrish–Yang reaction, photoinduced electron transfer processes, Yang photocyclization and others.

PT07451.title: photocycloaddition
PT07451.definition: Intermolecular photochemical process leading to carbo- or hetero- cyclic ring systems by formation of two new single bonds, either by a concerted process (e.g., a concerted addition) or by multi-step processes (e.g., the Paternò–Büchi reaction).

PT07455.title: photodeconjugation
