PT07455.definition: Photoinduced reaction of conjugated compounds (e.g., enones and carboxylic acid derivatives) leading to loss of conjugation.

P04595.title: photodegradation
P04595.definition: The photochemical transformation of a molecule into lower molecular weight fragments, usually in an oxidation process. This term is widely used in the destruction (oxidation) of pollutants by UV-based processes.

14048.title: photodesorption
14048.definition: Desorption induced by the absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation either by the adsorbate or by the adsorbent.

14049.title: photodesorption quantum yield
14049.definition: Number of entities evolving into the medium from a surface divided by the number of photons absorbed at a given wavelength by a solid or by an adsorbed entity treated as a surface extrinsic defect (centre).

P04597.title: photodetachment
P04597.definition: Ejection of an electron from a negative ion upon photoexcitation.

08851.title: photodetrapping
08851.definition: Removal of charge carriers from traps in the bandgap by irradiation.

P04598.title: photodiode
P04598.definition: A two-electrode, radiation-sensitive junction formed in a semiconductive material. A junction is formed by two successive regions of a semiconductive material having, respectively, an excess of electrons (n-type) or holes (p-type). A bias potential applied to the detector creates a region at the interface that is depleted of majority carriers. Each incident photon produces electron-hole pairs in the depletion region resulting in a measurable signal current. The photodiode can be operated either with zero bias in the photovoltaic mode where the photodiode is actually generating the electric potential supplied to the load. In a biased mode, the photoconductive mode, the reverse current is proportional to the irradiation. A Schottky-barrier photodiode is constructed by deposition of a metal film on a semiconductor surface in such a way that no interface layer is present. The barrier thickness depends on the impurity dopant concentration in the semiconductor layer. The incident radiation generates electon-hole pairs within the depletion region of the barrier where they are collected efficiently and rapidly by the built-in field. A PIN (p-intrinsic-n) diode is a planar diffused diode consisting of a single crystal having an intrinsic (undoped or compensated) region sandwiched between p- and n-type regions. A bias potential applied across the detector depletes the intrinsic region of charge carriers, constituting the radiation-sensitive detector volume. The number of electron-hole pairs produced is dependent on the energy of the incident photons. An avalanche photodiode is a photodiode in which the photogenerated electron-hole pairs are accelerated by a bias potential near to breakdown potential so that further electron-hole pairs are formed leading to saturation of the photocurrent. This operational mode for photon counting is the so-called Geiger mode, similar to that of the gas filled Geiger counter. Avalanche photodiodes can also be operated in the proportional mode.

P04599.title: photodiode array
P04599.definition: An arrangement of a number of photodiodes on a single chip.

P04600.title: photodynamic effect
P04600.definition: A term used in photobiology to refer to photoinduced damage requiring the simultaneous presence of light, photosensitizer and molecular oxygen. A sensitized photooxidation which involves molecular oxygen.

P04602.title: photoelectric attenuation coefficient
P04602.definition: The attenuation coefficient when only the photoelectric process is taken into account.

P04604.title: photoelectric peak
P04604.definition: Of a spectrum of γ-radiation, the part of the spectral response curve corresponding to the absorption in the radiation detector by the photoelectrical effect of the detected $\upgamma\!\mbox{-}\rm{energy}$. In most cases the peak also contains events caused by multiple processes and use of the expression full energy peak or full energy peak is to be preferred. Synonymous with photopeak.

09345.title: photoelectric work function
09345.definition: Minimum photon energy required to liberate an electron from the surface of a conducting solid by absorption of that photon.

P04601.title: photoelectrical effect
P04601.definition: The ejection of an electron from a solid or a liquid by a photon.

14050.title: photoelectrocatalysis
14050.definition: Electrochemically assisted photocatalysis. The role of the photocatalyst is played by a photoelectrode, often a semiconductor.

P04605.title: photoelectrochemical cell
P04605.definition: An electrochemical cell in which current and a voltage are simultaneously produced upon absorption of light by one or more of the electrodes. Usually at least one of the electrodes is a semiconductor.

P04606.title: photoelectrochemical etching
P04606.definition: The dissolution of a semiconductor in an electrolytic solution upon exposure to light. Used in the photopatterning of semiconductor surfaces.

P04607.title: photoelectrochemistry
P04607.definition: A term applied to a hybrid field of chemistry employing techniques which combine photochemical and electrochemical methods for the study of the oxidation-reduction chemistry of the ground or excited states of molecules or ions. In general, it is the chemistry resulting from the interaction of light with electrochemical systems.

14051.title: photoelectrode
14051.definition: Electrode capable of initiating electrochemical transformations after absorbing ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation.

P04608.title: photoelectrolytic cell
P04608.definition: A cell in which radiant energy causes a net chemical conversion in the cell, e.g. so as to produce hydrogen as a useful fuel. These cells can be classified as photosynthetic or photocatalytic. In the former case, radiant energy provides a Gibbs energy to drive a reaction such as \(\rm{H}_{2}\rm{O}\rightarrow \rm{H}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}\rm{O}_{2}\) , and electrical or thermal energy may be later recovered by allowing the reverse, spontaneous reaction to proceed. In a photocatalytic cell the photon absorption promotes a reaction with \(\Delta G < 0\) so there is no net storage of chemical energy, but the radiant energy speeds up a slow reaction.

P04609.title: photoelectron spectroscopy
P04609.definition: A spectroscopic technique which measures the kinetic energy of electrons emitted upon the ionization of a substance by high energy monochromatic photons. A photoelectron spectrum is a plot of the number of electrons emitted versus their kinetic energy. The spectrum consists of bands due to transitions from the ground state of an atom or molecular entity to the ground and excited states of the corresponding radical cation. Approximate interpretations are usually based on 'Koopmans theorem' and yield orbital energies. PES and UPS (UV photoelectron spectroscopy) refer to the spectroscopy using vacuum ultraviolet sources, while ESCA (electron spectroscopy for chemical analysis) and XPS use X-ray sources.

09346.title: photoelectron X-ray satellite peaks
09346.definition: Photoelectron peaks in a spectrum resulting from photoemission induced by characteristic minor X-ray lines associated with the X-ray spectrum of the anode material.

09347.title: photoelectron X-ray satellite subtraction
09347.definition: Removal of photoelectron X-ray satellite peaks from a spectrum.

P04611.title: photoelectron yield
P04611.definition: The number of photoelectrons emitted by the sample per incident photon.

14052.title: photoelectrosynthesis
14052.definition: Process by which ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation is absorbed by a semiconductor, electron transfer occurs at the interface between the semiconductor and a liquid and the output is chemical energy, i.e., radiant energy is stored as chemical energy.

09348.title: photoemission
09348.definition: Emission of electrons from atoms or molecules caused by the photoelectric effect.

P04612.title: photoemissive detector
P04612.definition: A detector in which a photon interacts with a solid surface, which is called the photocathode, or a gas, releasing a photoelectron. This process is called the external photoelectric effect. The photoelectrons are collected by an electrode at positive electric potential, i.e. the anode.

P04613.title: photoexcitation
P04613.definition: The production of an excited state by the absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation.

P04615.title: photogalvanic cell
P04615.definition: An electrochemical cell in which current or voltage changes result from photochemically generated changes in the relative concentrations of reactants in a solution phase oxidation-reduction couple.

14053.title: photogenerated catalysis
14053.definition: Initiation of chemical transformations through the photochemical formation of molecular species, which (once formed) are catalytically active even without the action of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation.

14054.title: photogenerated charge carrier
14054.definition: Charge carrying entity, especially an electron or a hole, in a semiconductor, produced by the absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation.

PT07456.title: photohydration
PT07456.definition: Photochemical process leading to the addition of water across a $\ce{C–C}$ double (or triple) bond or to a carbonyl (or carbonyl analogue) group.

08852.title: photoinduced discharge
08852.definition: Discharging of an electrically charged material by irradiation.

P04617.title: photoinduced electron transfer
P04617.definition: An electron transfer resulting from an electronic state produced by the resonant interaction of electromagnetic radiation with matter.

P04618.title: photoinduced polymerization
P04618.definition: The polymerization of a monomer by a free radical or ionic chain reaction initiated by photoexcitation.

P04619.title: photoinitiation
P04619.definition: The photoproduction of a free radical or ion capable of initiating a chain reaction such as a polymerization.

14055.title: photoinitiator
14055.definition: Agent initiating certain chemical transformations under the action of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation and consumed therewith.

08853.title: photoinjection
08853.definition: Charge carrier injection by a process induced by irradiation.

P04620.title: photoionization
P04620.definition: The term generally used to describe ionization of any species by photons. The process may, for example, be written  Electrons and photons do not 'impact' molecules or atoms; they interact with them in ways that result in various electronic excitations including ionization. For this reason it is recommended that in mass spectrometry the terms 'electron impact' and 'photon impact' not be used.

09267.title: photoionization cross section
09267.definition: Total ionization cross section for an incident photon of a given energy interacting with a material to produce one or more photoelectrons from all sub-shells that are energetically accessible.

P04621.title: photoionization detector
P04621.definition: Radiation from an ultraviolet lamp ionizes certain species in the carrier gas. A potential difference is applied and the resulting ionization current is detected. The detector is only useful for substances with ionization potentials below about \(11\ \rm{eV}\). This makes it quite useful for detecting one component of a combined eluent when the other component, for instance nitrogen, has a high ionization potential. The detector has a small linear dynamic range and is capable of detecting substances below \(1\ \rm{ppmv}\).

P04622.title: photoisomerization
P04622.definition: Photochemical process leading to an isomerization of the substrate, either by bond rotation, skeletal rearrangement or atom- or group- transfer.

09517.title: photolithography
09517.definition: Lithography performed by exposing a resist to an intense parallel light beam through an image mask.

P04623.title: photoluminescence
P04623.definition: Luminescence from direct photoexcitation of the emitting species.

PT07181.title: photoluminescent polymer
PT07181.definition: Polymer that exhibits luminescence (i.e., fluorescence or phosphorescence arising from photo-excitation).

P04624.title: photolysis
P04624.definition: The cleavage of one or more covalent bonds in a molecular entity resulting from absorption of light, or a photochemical process in which such cleavage is an essential part. For example:  The term is used incorrectly to describe irradiation of a sample, although in the combination flash photolysis this usage is accepted.

P04625.title: photometry
P04625.definition: The measurement of light over wavelengths which produce visual sensation (approximately \(380{-}780\ \rm{nm}\)). Thus photometric quantities do not refer to a specific wavelength but to the light emitted by a standard source (formerly a 'standard international candle', now a blackbody radiator emitting at the temperature of solidifying platinum, \(2042\ \rm{K}\)). luminance and illuminance are the photometric analogues of the radiometric quantities radiance and irradiance, respectively, but conversion from photometric units (e.g. \(\rm{lm cm}^{-2}\)) to radiometric units (e.g. \(\pu{J s-1 cm-2}\)) requires convolution over wavelength of the spectral radiation with the relative spectral response of the human eye. The standard response is called the 'spectral luminous efficiency of radiation', and is tabulated for daylight adapted vision in photopic response tables.

14056.title: photomineralisation
14056.definition: Complete photodegradation of an organic compound into carbon dioxide and water, and other simple inorganic compounds (depending on the hetero-atom in the compound) upon absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation by the photocatalyst or by the adsorbate.

P04626.title: photomultiplier tube
P04626.definition: A vacuum phototube with additional amplification by electron multiplication. It consists of a photocathode, a series of dynodes, called a dynode chain on which a secondary-electron multiplication process occurs, and an anode. According to the desired response time, transit time, time spread, gain, or low dark current, different types of dynode structures have been developed, e.g. circular cage structure, linear focused structure, venetian blind structure, box and grid structure. Some special dynode structures permit combination with additional electric or magnetic fields. A strip dynode photomultiplier tube consists of a photocathode followed by thin dynode material on an insulating substrate. In a continuous-strip photomultiplier, two strip dynodes are arranged in parallel. A potential applied to the ends of the two strips produces an electric field across the continuous strip dynodes, giving rise to electron multiplication along the dynodes. In a resistance-strip magnetic photomultiplier, a uniform magnetic field is applied to the planes of the strips, so that the electrons travel in the crossed electric and magnetic fields. A channel photomultiplier tube photocathode consists of a channel electron multiplier (CEM) system for the photoelectrons, and an anode to collect the final electron current. The basic part of the CEM is a tube with a semiconducting inner surface. In general it is curved in order to inhibit the acceleration of positive ions towards the photocathode. A number of small channels called microchannels can be constructed in arrays for imaging applications.

P04627.title: photon
P04627.definition:
Particle of zero charge, zero rest mass, spin quantum number 1, energy \(h\ 
u \) and momentum \( rac{h\ 
u }{c}\)(\(h\) is the Planck constant, \(
u \) the frequency of radiation and \(c\) the speed of light), carrier of electromagnetic force.

P04629.title: photon counting
P04629.definition: Recording of sequential single photons counted by way of recording and counting sequential electron pulses at the anode of the photomultiplier.

PT07458.title: photon echo
PT07458.definition: Time-resolved optical spectroscopy in which the inhomogeneous broadening of absorbers is eliminated by the proper choice of geometry in a four-wave mixing experiment.

P04631.title: photon exitance
P04631.definition: Photon flux, number basis, \(q_{\rm{p}}\), emitted by an element of the surface containing the source point under consideration divided by the area \(S\) of that element. SI unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{m}^{-2}\).

P04632.title: photon exposure
P04632.definition: Photon irradiance, \(E_{\rm{p}}\), integrated over the time of irradiation for a beam incident from all upward directions. SI unit is \(\rm{m}^{-2}\).

P04633.title: photon flow
P04633.definition: The number of photons (quanta, \(N\)) per unit time. (\(\frac{\rm{d}N}{\rm{d}t}\), simplified expression: \(\mathit{\Phi} _{\rm{p}} = \frac{N}{t}\) when the number of photons is constant over the time considered). The SI unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\). Alternatively, the term can be used with the amount of photons (mol or its equivalent einstein), the SI unit then being \(\pu{mol s-1}\).

P04635.title: photon fluence rate
P04635.definition: Rate of photon fluence. Total number of photons (\(N_{\rm{p}}\)) incident from all directions on a small sphere divided by the cross-sectional area of the sphere and per time interval. SI unit is \(\rm{m}^{-2}\ \rm{s}^{-1}\). Same as photon fluence rate.

P04634.title: photon fluence
P04634.definition: Amount of photons (quanta of radiation) incident on a small sphere from all directions, divided by the cross-sectional area of that sphere and integrated over time. Photons per surface area (\(\rm{quanta m}^{-2}\)). SI unit is \(\rm{m}^{-2}\).

P04636.title: photon flux
P04636.definition: Number of photons (quanta of radiation, \(N_{\rm{p}}\)) per time interval. SI unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\).

P04637.title: photon irradiance
P04637.definition: Number of photons (quanta of radiation, \(N_{\rm{p}}\)) per time interval (photon flux), \(q_{\rm{p}}\), incident from all upward directions on a small element of surface containing the point under consideration divided by the area of the element. SI unit is \(\rm{m}^{-2}\ \rm{s}^{-1}\). Equivalent definition: Integral, taken over the hemisphere visible from the given point, of the expression \(L_{\rm{p}}\, \rm{cos}\:\theta\, \rm{d}\varOmega\) the photon radiance at the given point in the various directions of the incident beam of solid angle \(\varOmega\) and \(\theta\) the angle between any of these beams and the normal to the surface at the given point.

PT07459.title: photon number
PT07459.definition: Total number of photons calculated as \(N_{\rm{p}} = n_{\rm{p}}\, N_{\rm{A}}\) with \(N_{\rm{p}}\) the amount of photons in einsteins and \(N_{\rm{A}}\) the Avogadro constant.

P04638.title: photon quantities
P04638.definition: A group of quantities characterizing electromagnetic radiation in terms of the number of photons. The symbols of photon quantities may be distinguished by adding a subscript p.

P04639.title: photon radiance
P04639.definition: Number of photons (quanta of radiation, \(N_{\rm{p}}\)) per time interval (photon flux), \(q_{\rm{p}}\), leaving or passing through a small transparent element of surface in a given direction from the source about the solid angle \(\varOmega\), divided by the solid angle and by the orthogonally projected area of the element in a plane normal to the given beam direction, \(\rm{d}S_{\perp } = \rm{d}S\, cos\,\theta\), with \(\theta\) the angle between the normal to the surface and the direction of the beam. Equivalent definition: Integral taken over the hemisphere visible from the given point, of the expression \(L_{\rm{p}}\, cos\,\theta\,\rm{d}\varOmega\), with \(L_{\rm{p}}\) the photon radiance at the given point in the various directions of the incident beam of solid angle \(\varOmega\) and \(\theta\) the angle between any of these beams and the normal to the surface at the given point.

09550.title: photonic crystal
09550.definition: Periodic structures consisting of a dielectric material that shows strong interaction with light.

14057.title: photonic efficiency
14057.definition: Ratio of the rate of the photoreaction measured for a specified time interval (usually the initial conditions) to the rate of incident photons within a defined wavelength interval inside the irradiation window of the reactor.

14058.title: photonic yield
14058.definition: Ratio of the rate of the photoreaction measured for a specified time interval (usually the initial conditions) to the rate of incident photons of monochromatic light inside the irradiation window of the reactor.

14059.title: photonic yield spectrum
14059.definition: Plot of the photonic yield of a given photoprocess, measured at the same photon flux of incident (prior to absorption) light, as a function of a measure of the energy of the photons, i.e., for monochromatic irradiation.

09551.title: photonics
09551.definition: Science and technology of the production, transmission, absorption, sensing, and direction of light.

P04640.title: photooxidation
P04640.definition: Oxidation reactions induced by light. Common processes are: 1, the loss of one or more electrons from a chemical species as a result of photoexcitation of that species; 2, the reaction of a substance with oxygen under the influence of light. When oxygen remains in the product this latter process is also called photooxygenation. Reactions in which neither the substrate nor the oxygen are electronically excited are sometimes called photoinitiated oxidations.

P04641.title: photooxygenation
P04641.definition: The incorporation of molecular oxygen into a molecular entity. There are three common mechanisms: Type I: the reaction of triplet molecular oxygen with radicals formed photochemically. Type II: the reaction of photochemically produced singlet molecular oxygen with molecular entities to give rise to oxygen containing molecular entities. The third mechanism proceeds by electron transfer producing superoxide anion as the reactive species.

14911.title: photoperiod
14911.definition: The duration of illumination and darkness over a \(\pu{24\!\mbox{-}h}\) day.

P04645.title: photophoresis
P04645.definition: In aerosol physics, the motion of particles due to the influence of light. In many cases, this amounts to a special form of thermophoresis due to the heating of the particles by the light.

P04646.title: photophosphorylation
P04646.definition: The transformation of light (solar) energy for the reduction of $\ce{CO2}$ and the generation of adenosine 5'-triphosphate, ATP.

P04647.title: photophysical processes
P04647.definition: Photoexcitation and subsequent events which lead from one to another state of a molecular entity through radiation and radiationless transitions. No chemical change results.

P04648.title: photopolymerization
P04648.definition: Polymerization processes requiring a photon for the propagation step.

14060.title: photoradiation catalysis
14060.definition: Radiation catalysis under conditions not allowing a distinction between the effect of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared and of ionising radiation as well as the case in which the ionising radiation alone generates emission of chemically active light (e.g., the 'Cherenkov' light emission).

PT07460.title: photorearrangement
PT07460.definition: Photoisomerization involving changes in the arrangement of the atoms within the molecular species. It may lead to unstable isomers that react further by, e.g., dehydrogenation, deprotonation, or other reactions.

12009.title: photoreceptor cell
12009.definition: Specialized neuron found in the retina, involved in detecting light and transducing the signals of vision

P04650.title: photoreduction
P04650.definition: Reduction reactions induced by light. Common processes are: 1, addition of one or more electrons to a photoexcited species; 2, the photochemical hydrogenation of a substance. Reactions in which the substrate is not electronically excited are sometimes called photoinitiated reductions.

08854.title: photorefractive polymer
08854.definition: Optically nonlinear polymer that changes refractive index when exposed to light.

16214.title: photoremovable protecting group
16214.definition: Release of a reactive species by photolysis of a molecular entity. The release may be induced by direct excitation, by triplet sensitization, or by photoinduced electron transfer.

P04651.title: photoresist
P04651.definition: A photoimaging material, generally applied as a thin film, whose local solubility properties can be altered photochemically. A subsequent development step produces an image which is useful for the fabrication of microelectronic devices (e.g. integrated circuits).

PT07461.title: photoselection
PT07461.definition: Selection of an aligned subset of sample molecules by an exciting light beam. The selected subset will have an orientation distribution that is determined by the electric vector of the beam. If the beam is linearly polarized a uniaxial sample with a known orientation distribution will be produced. Also, the set of remaining molecules will be aligned with a known orientation distribution (residual anisotropy).

PT07182.title: photosensitive polymer
PT07182.definition: Polymer that responds to ultraviolet or visible light by exhibiting a change in its physical properties or its chemical constitution.

13570.title: photosensitivity
13570.definition: Skin reddening due to an abnormal reaction to sunlight, characteristic of systemic autoimmune diseases [e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD)], and cutaneous and subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.

P04652.title: photosensitization
P04652.definition: The process by which a photochemical or photophysical alteration occurs in one molecular entity as a result of initial absorption of radiation by another molecular entity called a 'photosensitizer'. In mechanistic photochemistry the term is limited to cases in which the photosensitizer is not consumed in the reaction.

P04654.title: photostationary state
P04654.definition: A steady state reached by a reacting chemical system when light has been absorbed by at least one of the components. At this state the rates of formation and disappearance are equal for each of the transient molecular entities formed.

16215.title: photostimulated unimolecular radical nucleophilic substitution
16215.definition: Nucleophilic substitution in a substrate through processes that involve electron transfer steps. The reaction occurs through chain steps. The most extensively used method of initiation is photoinitiation.

16216.title: photosubstitution
16216.definition: Photochemical process leading to a substitution reaction.

P04655.title: photosynthesis
P04655.definition: A metabolic process involving plants and some types of bacteria (e.g. Chromatiaceae, Rhodospirillaceae, Chlorobiaceae) in which light energy absorbed by chlorophyll and other photosynthetic pigments results in the reduction of $\ce{CO2}$ followed by the formation of organic compounds. In plants the overall process involves the conversion of $\ce{CO2}$ and $\ce{H2O}$ to carbohydrates (and other plant material) and the release of $\ce{O2}$.

PT06782.title: photosystem
PT06782.definition: A membrane-bound complex in plants and photosynthetic bacteria, responsible for light-harvesting and primary electron transfer. Comprises light-harvesting pigments such as chlorophyll; a primary electron-transfer centre, and secondary electron carriers. In green plant photosynthesis, Photosystem I transfers electrons from plastocyanin to a [2Fe-2S] ferredoxin, and contains iron-sulfur proteins. Photosystem II transfers electrons from the oxygen-evolving complex to plastoquinone, and contains an iron centre.

16217.title: phototautomerisation
16217.definition: Photoisomerization of the general form \[\ce{G-X-Y=Z [h\nu] X=Y-Z-G}\]

P04656.title: photothermal effect
P04656.definition: An effect produced by photoexcitation resulting partially or totally in the production of heat.

08659.title: photothermal spectroscopy
08659.definition: Measurement method of spectroscopy in which the absorption of electromagnetic radiation by a sample is detected as a result of the heat generated by the absorption.

14062.title: photothermocatalysis
14062.definition: Catalysis occurring by the combined action of electronic excitation due to absorption of ultraviolet or visible radiation and thermal energy (infrared radiation or exothermic reactions) including catalytic phenomena.

P04657.title: photothermography
P04657.definition: A process utilizing both light and heat, simultaneously or sequentially, for image recording.

15979.title: phototoxicity
15979.definition: Adverse effects produced by exposure to light energy, especially those produced in the skin.

13571.title: phototoxicity test
13571.definition: Procedure used to identify the phototoxic potential of a test substance. The substance is administered either systemically or topically on the skin, and light is subsequently shone on the skin to photoexcite the substance.

P04658.title: phototransistor
P04658.definition: A bipolar transistor with its base-collector junction acting as a photodiode, which, if irradiated, controls the response of the device. Due to the inherent current gain (of the transistor) the responsivity of the phototransistor is greater than that of photodiodes. A Darlington phototransistor consists of two separate transistors coupled in the high-impedance Darlington configuration with a phototransistor as the input transistor. A field effect phototransistor or photo-FET is a field effect transistor (FET) that employs photogeneration of carriers in the channel region (the neutral region sandwiched between the insulator and the depletion region under the gate of the FET). It is characterized by high responsivity due to the high current gain of the FET.

P04659.title: photovoltaic cell
P04659.definition: A solid state device, usually a semiconductor such as silicon, which absorbs photons with energies higher than or equal to the bandgap energy and simultaneously produces electric power.

08855.title: photovoltaic effect
08855.definition: Phenomenon consisting in converting light to electricity.

P04662.title: phthaleins
P04662.definition: 3,3-Bis(hydroxyaryl)-2-benzofuran-1(3H)-ones generally derived from the condensation of phthalic anhydride with phenols. E.g. phenolphthalein.

14913.title: phylogenetics
14913.definition: Branch of biology that deals with phylogeny, especially with the deduction of the historical relationships between groups of organisms.

14914.title: phylogeny
14914.definition: Pattern of historical relationships between species or other groups resulting from divergence during evolution.

14915.title: phylum
14915.definition: Taxonomic rank at the level below Kingdom and above Class

15980.title: physical map
15980.definition: Map showing how much DNA, measured in base pairs, separates two genes.

P04665.title: physical network
P04665.definition: Polymer network with junction points or zones formed by physically interacting chains which need not be permanent.

14063.title: physical pathway
14063.definition: Set of physical processes leading to the relaxation of the electronically excited system without chemical transformations.

P04666.title: physical quantity
P04666.definition: An attribute of a phenomenon, body or substance that may be distinguished qualitatively and determined quantitatively.

14916.title: physiological adaptation
14916.definition:
Change in an organism, in response to changing conditions of the environment, which takes place without any irreversible disruptions of the given biological system and without exceeding normal (homeostatic) capacities of its response.
Process by which an organism stabilizes its physiological condition after an environmental change.Note: If this process exceeds the homeostatic range, it becomes pathological and results in symptoms of disease (adverse effects).

16234.title: physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling
16234.definition: Mathematical modeling of kinetic behavior of a substance, based on measured physiological parameters.

P04667.title: physisorption
P04667.definition: Adsorption in which the forces involved are intermolecular forces (van der Waals forces) of the same kind as those responsible for the imperfection of real gases and the condensation vapours, and which do not involve a significant change in the electronic orbital patterns of the species involved. The term 'van der Waals adsorption' is synonymous with physical adsorption, but its use is not recommended.

14917.title: phytochelatin
14917.definition: Class of cysteine-rich peptides in plants that are induced by and bind to metals. They can function in the regulation and detoxification of metals by plants.

11090.title: phytoestrogen
11090.definition: Non-steroidal natural product from a plant that, because of a structural similarity to 17\(\upbeta\)-estradiol can exert mild estrogenic effects, or antagonize them.

13572.title: phytohemagglutinin
13572.definition: Plant lectin that acts as a T-cell mitogen.

14918.title: phytoplankton
14918.definition: Photosynthesizing organisms found in the plankton.

P04668.title: phytotoxicant
P04668.definition: An agent which produces a toxic effect in vegetation.

13861.title: π-π stacking
13861.definition: Inter- or intra-molecular alignment of aromatic groups within molecules induced by the interactional overlap of their \(\ce{\uppi\mbox{-}orbitals}\).

12010.title: pia
12010.definition: Innermost of three membranous layers, together composing the meninges, that surrounds and adheres to the brain and spinal cord.

P04671.title: picrates
P04671.definition: Salts or charge-transfer complexes of picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol).

11091.title: piebaldism
11091.definition: Patchy absence of pigmentation of the hair or skin or, depending on the species, of feathers, scales, or other body surfaces.

14920.title: Pielou’s J
14920.definition: Measure of species evenness for a sample from a community. It is calculated from the following equation: \[{\rm{Pielouߴs}}\ J = \frac{H'}{\log S}\] where \(H'\) is the Shannon–Wiener diversity measure and \(S\) is the average species richness.

PT07183.title: piezoelectric polymer
PT07183.definition: Polymer that exhibits a change in dielectric properties on application of pressure.Polymer that shows a change in its dimensions when subjected to an electric field.

P04672.title: piezoluminescence
P04672.definition: Luminescence observed when certain solids are subjected to a change in pressure.

P04673.title: pile-up
P04673.definition: The processing by a radiation spectrometer of pulses resulting from the simultaneous adsorption of independent particles or photons in a radiation detector. As a result they are counted as one single particle or photon with energy between the individual energies and the sum of these energies.

09377.title: pileup
09377.definition: Counts in a backscattering spectrum arising from two or more separate events that occur so closely in time that the signals are not resolved by the detection system and cause counts to be recorded in erroneous channels.

P04676.title: PIN semiconductor detector
P04676.definition: A semiconductor detector consisting of a compensated region between a p and a n region. The compensated region is often referred to as intrinsic.

P04674.title: pinacols
P04674.definition: Tetra(hydrocarbyl)ethane-1,2-diols, $\ce{R2C(OH)–(OH)R2}$, of which the tetramethyl example is the simplest one and is itself commonly known as pinacol (benzpinacol is the tetraphenyl analogue).

11092.title: pineal gland
11092.definition: Pea-sized conical mass of tissue behind the third ventricle of the brain, secreting the hormone-like substance melatonin in some mammals.

11093.title: pinna
11093.definition:
Externally visible portion of the ear.See also: auricle
Feather or fin.

PT06838.title: pinocytosis
PT06838.definition: Type of endocytosis in which soluble materials are taken up by the cell and incorporated into vesicles for digestion.

16245.title: pIon
16245.definition: General mathematical expression form of any ion X activity: \[\rm{p(ion\ X)} = {\rm{pX}} = -\lg {\rm{a_{X}}} = -\lg ({\rm{m_{X}} \gamma_{X}/m^{\circ}})\], analogously to \[\pu{pH} = -\lg {\rm{a_{H}}} = -\lg ({\rm{m_{H}} \gamma_{H}/m^{\circ}})\].

12713.title: pipeline
12713.definition: Discovery and development compound portfolio of a pharmaceutical company or research organization.

11486.title: pipelining programs
11486.definition: Visual programming of the computational execution of sequential operations on a dataset, with each node specifying an operation with options, and the nodes processed sequentially.

14175.title: pipettor
14175.definition: Device that aspirates and dispenses liquid (\(\pu{nL}\) to \(\pu{mL}\) range) for the purposes of transferring from a source to destination.

P04677.title: pitch
P04677.definition: A residue from pyrolysis of organic material or tar distillation which is solid at room temperature, consisting of a complex mixture of numerous, essentially aromatic hydrocarbons and heterocyclic compounds. It exhibits a broad softening range instead of a defined melting temperature. When cooled from the melt, pitches solidify without crystallization.

09552.title: pitch division
09552.definition: Method for making a lithographic pattern smaller than that deemed possible given the wavelength of the imaging radiation.

P04678.title: pitch-based carbon fibres
P04678.definition: Carbon fibres obtained from pitch precursor fibres after stabilization treatment, carbonization and final heat treatment.

P04679.title: pitting corrosion
P04679.definition: A special type of non-uniform corrosion of passive metals, resulting in the formation of pits, which usually occurs in the presence of certain anions at electrode potentials positive to a critical pitting potential.

11094.title: pituitary
11094.definition: Small endocrine gland sitting in a bony cavity (the sella turcica) at the base of the brain and connected to the hypothalamus.

12714.title: pivotal study
12714.definition: Experiment that provides strong support for or against the drug or molecular target under investigation.

11095.title: placenta
11095.definition: Organ of exchange of nutrients and waste products between mother and fetus, having parts derived from both.

11096.title: placental barrier
11096.definition: Multilayered membrane of fetal tissue within the placenta that separates the maternal blood from the fetal blood and allows selective passage of substances between the two.

11097.title: placental circulation
11097.definition: Circulation of blood through the placenta during intrauterine life, serving the needs of the fetus for oxygenation, nutrition, and elimination of waste.

11098.title: placental insufficiency
11098.definition: Inadequate blood flow through the placenta to maintain the needs of the fetus for oxygenation and metabolic balance.

11099.title: placental transfer
11099.definition: Delivery of substances from the maternal circulation to the fetus, across the placental barrier.

15982.title: placentation
15982.definition:
Formation of a placenta in the uterus.
Type or structure of a placenta.
In botany, arrangement of placentas within the plant ovary.

10080.title: Plackett−Burman design
10080.definition: Incomplete experimental design to estimate main effects for which each combination of factor levels for any pair of factors appears the same number of times.

P04681.title: planar chirality
P04681.definition: Term used by some authorities to refer to stereoisomerism resulting from the arrangement of out-of-plane groups with respect to a plane (chirality plane). It is exemplified by the atropisomerism of (E)-cyclooctene (chiral plane = double bond and attached atoms) or monosubstituted paracyclophane (chiral plane = substituted ring). The configuration of molecular entities possessing planar chirality is specified by the stereodescriptors \(R_{\rm{p}}\) and \(S_{\rm{p}}\) (or \(P\) and \(M\)).

P04682.title: planar chromatography
P04682.definition: A separation technique in which the stationary phase is present as or on a plane. The plane can be a paper, serving as such or impregnated by a substrate as the stationary bed (paper chromatography, PC) or a layer of solid particles spread on a support e.g. a glass plate (thin layer chromatography, TLC). Sometimes planar chromatography is also termed open-bed chromatography.

P04683.title: planar film
P04683.definition: A film whose boundaries are represented by ideal parallel planes. The planar film thickness is defined as the distance between these planes. The terms nanometre thick film, micrometre thick film and millimetre thick film refer specifically to film thickness in the ranges \(0.1{-}100\ \rm{nm}\), \(0.1{-}100\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\) and \(0.1{-}100\ \rm{mm}\), respectively.

PT07418.title: planar intramolecular charge transfer
PT07418.definition: In a PICT state formed by intramolecular charge transfer in an electron donor ($\ce{D}$)/acceptor ($\ce{A}$) molecule, the $\ce{D}$ and $\ce{A}$ subgroups have an overall planar configuration, with substantial electronic coupling of $\ce{D}$ and $\ce{A}$.

09553.title: planarising layer
09553.definition: Coating used to create a level surface during lithographic processing.

P04685.title: Planck constant
P04685.definition: The Planck constant, \(h\), is one of seven fixed constants defining the International System of Units, the SI, with \(h = \pu{6.62607015E-34 J s}\). The Planck constant is considered as a fundamental constant of nature.

14924.title: plankton
14924.definition: Organisms living suspended in the water column and incapable of moving against water currents.

14925.title: planktotrophic larva
14925.definition: Planktonic-dispersing larva that derives its nourishment by feeding in the plankton.

13573.title: plantibody
13573.definition: Animal antibody (or fragment thereof), expressed in a genetically modified plant.

13574.title: plaque-forming cell
13574.definition: Antibody-secreting plasma cell detected in vitro by its ability to produce a 'plaque' of lysed antigen-sensitized erythrocytes in the presence of complement.

PT06839.title: plasma
PT06839.definition: Fluid component of blood in which the blood cells and platelets are suspended. Synonym: blood plasma.Fluid component of semen produced by the accessory glands, the seminal vesicles, the prostate, and the bulbo-urethral glands.Cell substance outside the nucleus, i.e., the cytoplasm.

09190.title: plasma assisted desorption ionization mass spectrometry
09190.definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air as a result of the bombardment by a focused plasma.

13576.title: plasma cell
13576.definition: Terminally differentiated B lymphocyte, with little or no capacity for mitotic division, that actively secretes large amounts of antibody.

P04688.title: plasma desorption ionization
P04688.definition: The ionization of any species by interaction with heavy particles (which may be ions or neutral atoms) formed as a result of the fission of a suitable nuclide adjacent to a target supporting the sample.

09554.title: plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition
09554.definition: Process to deposit a solid film on a substrate resulting from plasma-induced reactions of precursor compounds, either in the gaseous state or on the film surface.

09555.title: plasma etch
09555.definition: Plasma processing used in the fabrication of integrated circuits that generates volatile products from the elements of the material etched and the reactive species generated by the plasma.

08519.title: plasma excitation temperature
08519.definition: Temperature governing the number density of atomic species in their ground state and excited states following a Boltzmann distribution.

08520.title: plasma gases
08520.definition: Gas streams used to maintain and stabilize the inductively-coupled plasma. The external stream is the main constituent of the plasma and confines the plasma avoiding melting of the torch walls; the intermediate gas stream keeps the plasma at a given height above the top of the torch and, the central stream carries the aerosol and promotes its injection in the plasma central channel.

P04687.title: plasma
P04687.definition: A gas which is at least partly ionized and contains particles of various types, viz. electrons, atoms, ions and molecules. The plasma as a whole is electrically neutral.

08521.title: plasma induction zone
08521.definition: Inductively-coupled plasma volume where there is a maximum interaction between the electromagnetic field and the plasma gas (mostly argon). This is the plasma’s hottest area and has a toroidal configuration.

08522.title: plasma ionization temperature
08522.definition: Temperature associated with the energy level of plasma ions.

09853.title: plasma lipoproteins
09853.definition: Assemblies of lipids and proteins in blood plasma transporting lipids between tissues.

08523.title: plasma local thermodynamic equilibrium
08523.definition: Condition for which the temperatures estimated from different particles (atoms, molecules, ions, electrons) constituting a plasma are locally coincident.

08524.title: plasma shielding
08524.definition: Prevention of laser pulse energy from reaching a sample surface as a result of the presence of a laser-induced plasma.

08525.title: plasma termination
08525.definition: Extinction of the plasma after a laser pulse as a consequence of self-absorption (quenching) and recombination of electrons and ions.

13575.title: plasmablast
13575.definition: Highly proliferative cell that is a developmental intermediate between small B lymphocytes and immunoglobulin (Ig)-secreting mature plasma cells.

13577.title: plasmacytoid dendritic cell
13577.definition: Dendritic cell of distinct lineage, found in blood and peripheral lymphoid tissue, which secretes large amounts of interferon (IFN) upon activation.

13578.title: plasmacytoma
13578.definition: Mass of neoplastic monoclonal plasma cells growing in bone or soft tissue.

13579.title: plasmapheresis
13579.definition: Technique of extracorporeal separation of blood cells from plasma, with return of the cells to the patient.

P04689.title: plasmid
P04689.definition: An extrachromosomal genetic element consisting generally of a circular duplex of DNA which can replicate independently of chromosomal DNA. R-plasmids are responsible for the mutual transfer of antibiotic resistance among microbes. Plasmids are used as vectors for cloning DNA in bacteria or yeast host cells.

09268.title: plasmon
09268.definition: Excitation of valence-band electrons in a solid in which collective oscillations are generated.

P04690.title: plastic flow
P04690.definition: Steady flow occurring only above a certain finite stress.

P04691.title: plastic transition
P04691.definition: A first-order transition that occurs when a low-temperature phase transforms to an orientationally-disordered high-temperature phase with a strong variation of enthalpy.

14176.title: plate format
14176.definition: Number and configuration of wells on a microplate.

14177.title: plate gripper
14177.definition: Handling device that positions microplates on a workstation.

P04693.title: plate height
P04693.definition: The column length (\(L\)) divided by the plate number: \[H=\frac{L}{N}\] It is also called the height equivalent to one theoretical plate (HETP).

14178.title: plate map
14178.definition: Layout of samples and controls configured on a plate during an assay.

P04694.title: plate number
P04694.definition: A number indicative of column performance, calculated from the following equations which depend on the selection of the peak width expression: \[N=(\frac{V_{\rm{R}}}{\sigma })^{2}=(\frac{t_{\rm{R}}}{\sigma })^{2}\] \[N=16\ (\frac{V_{\rm{R}}}{w_{\rm{b}}})^{2}=16\ (\frac{t_{\rm{R}}}{w_{\rm{b}}})^{2}\] \[N=5.545\ (\frac{V_{\rm{R}}}{w_{\rm{h}}})^{2}=5.545\ (\frac{t_{\rm{R}}}{w_{\rm{h}}})^{2}\] The value of 5.545 stands for \(8\ \ln 2\). These expressions assume a Gaussian (symmetrical) peak. In these expressions the units for the quantities inside the brackets must be consistent so that their ratio is dimensionless: i.e. if the numerator is a volume, then peak width must also be expressed in terms of volume. In former nomenclature the expressions 'number of theoretical plates' or 'theoretical plate number' were used for the same term. For simplification, the present name is suggested.

14179.title: plate reader
14179.definition: Automated device that uses optical and/or computer vision techniques to detect biological, chemical, or physical events in samples stored in microplates.

14180.title: plate stacker
14180.definition: Automated device that loads, unloads, and restacks microplates.

14181.title: plate washer
14181.definition: Automated device used to wash the wells of microplates.

P04692.title: plateau border
P04692.definition: Except for free-floating bubbles, films have to be supported by frames, bulk surfaces or other films. The transition zone separating these from the film proper, always containing some bulk liquid, is called a plateau border.

13580.title: platelet
13580.definition: Small irregular or disc-shaped cell found in large numbers in mammalian blood, essential for blood clotting.

13581.title: platelet-activating factor
13581.definition: Alkyl phospholipid released by a variety of cell types including mast cells and basophils, which has immunoregulatory effects on lymphocytes and monocytes/macrophages, as well as causing platelet aggregation and degranulation.

13582.title: platelet-derived growth factor
13582.definition: Protein synthesized by platelets that is released into the serum during blood clotting.

08526.title: platform atomization
08526.definition: Sample support made of graphite that is inserted into the atomizer tube in electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy. The sample, a liquid or a solid, is deposited onto this platform, from which it undergoes all the transformations leading to atomization. The use of a platform delays atomization, until a more stabilized temperature in the gas phase is reached.

09100.title: platinum electrode
09100.definition: Foil, wire, disc, or mesh electrode made of platinum, which is the most commonly used metallic working electrode in electrochemistry.

P04695.title: pleiotropic gene
P04695.definition: A gene affecting more than one (apparently unrelated) characteristic of the phenotype.

11100.title: pleiotropism
11100.definition:
Having more than one effect.
Relating to a gene, expression of which gives rise to multiple phenotypic traits.

11101.title: pleura
11101.definition: Each of a pair of serous membranes lining the thorax and enveloping the lungs in humans and other mammals.

11102.title: pleural cavity
11102.definition: Potential space between the pleural membranes lining the chest cavity (parietal pleura) and covering the lungs (visceral pleura).

12011.title: plexus
12011.definition: Network of interconnecting nerves, blood vessels or lymphatic vessels.

P04696.title: ploidy
P04696.definition: A term indicating the number of sets of chromosomes present in an organism, e.g. haploid (one) or diploid (two).

11487.title: PLS latent variable
11487.definition: One of the vectors of a linear combination of the input descriptors that a partial least squares calculation extracts from a dataset.

11488.title: PLS loading
11488.definition: The contribution of a particular property to a PLS latent variable.

P04697.title: plug-flow
P04697.definition: A packed bed flow reactor is commonly called a fixed bed reactor and the term plug-flow is also used to indicate that no attempt is made to back-mix the reaction mixture as it passes through the catalyst bed.

15983.title: plumbism
15983.definition: Chronic poisoning caused by absorption of lead or lead salts.

P04700.title: plume
P04700.definition: The gaseous and aerosol effluents which are emitted from a chimney and the volume of space which they occupy (often visible). The shape of the plume and the concentrations of pollutants in it at various points along the path of the plume are sensitive functions of the meteorology, local topography and the chemistry which occurs in the plume. Urban plumes are observed over many urban areas and downwind of these areas in which a combination of man sources of pollution are concentrated.

11103.title: pluripotent
11103.definition: Able to differentiate into a variety of cell types.

13583.title: pluripotent stem cell
13583.definition: Self-replicating cell capable of developing into cells and tissues of the three primary embryonic germ layers.

P04702.title: pneumatic detector
P04702.definition: A pressure-sensitive detector based on the pressure increase of a gas. A special type is the Golay cell where the pressure change is detected by observing the deflection off one of the chamber walls.

08527.title: pneumatic nebulizers
08527.definition: Nebulizers for which the aerosol generation principle is based on the exposure of the liquid sample to a high velocity gas stream.

15984.title: pneumoconiosis
15984.definition: Usually fibrosis of the lungs that develops owing to (prolonged) inhalation of inorganic or organic dusts.

12012.title: pneumotaxic center
12012.definition: Neural network in the brainstem involved in regulating respiration.

09033.title: pnictogen bond
09033.definition: Weak attractive interaction between an electrophilic region on a pnictogen atom in a molecular entity (wherein the pnictogen is involved in other stronger bonds) and a nucleophilic region in another, or the same, molecular entity.

14926.title: poikilotherm
14926.definition: 'Cold-blooded organism' (such as an amphibian, reptile, or fish) with a body temperature varying with, but usually slightly higher than, the temperature of its environment.

P04703.title: point group
P04703.definition: The classification of the symmetry elements of an object. It is denoted in the Schoenflies notation by an italic symbol, such as \(C_{3}\), \(D_{2}\), \(T_{\rm{d}}\), etc.

15986.title: point mutation
15986.definition: Change in a single base pair in DNA.

P04704.title: point of zero charge
P04704.definition: A surface charge is at its point of zero charge when the surface charge density is zero. It is a value of the negative logarithm of the activity in the bulk of the charge-determining ions.

14927.title: point source
14927.definition: Single emission source in a defined location.

P04705.title: poise
P04705.definition: cgs unit of dynamic viscosity, \(\pu{P} = \pu{0.1 Pa s}\).

P04706.title: poison
P04706.definition: An inhibitory substance characterized by its propensity to attach very strongly, by a true chemical bond (e.g. covalent) to the surface atoms or ions constituting the catalytically active sites. Poisons act in minute quantities. Typical poisons are $\ce{S}$, $\ce{As}$, etc. In most cases, activity and/or selectivity cannot be recovered without a drastic change in operating conditions (most often a regeneration). recovery, if at all, takes place very slowly and/or only partially.

15988.title: poisoning
15988.definition: Morbid condition produced by a poison.

P04707.title: Poisson distribution
P04707.definition: A discrete distribution with the differential mass-distribution function of the form: \[f_{\rm{w}}(x)=\frac{x}{a\,+\,1}=\frac{\rm{e}^{-a}\ a^{x-1}}{(x\,-\,1)!}\] where \(x\) is a parameter characterizing the chain length, such as relative molecular mass or degree of polymerization and \(a\) is a positive adjustable parameter.

11489.title: Poisson–Boltzmann equation
11489.definition:
A differential equation that uses a mean-field, continuum model to describe the electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions where both ions and solvent are
 treated implicitly, resulting in less computational effort to describe biomolecules in ionic aqueous solutions.

13584.title: pokeweed mitogen
13584.definition: Plant lectin which is a T-cell-dependent B-cell mitogen.

16218.title: polar driving force
16218.definition: The negative of the standard Gibbs energy change (i.e., \(-\Delta G^{\circ}\)) for outer-sphere electron transfer in polar solvents, where the electrostatic work terms in the expression used for the calculation of the Gibbs energy of photoinduced electron transfer are in general negligibly small.

P04709.title: polar effect
P04709.definition: For a reactant molecule RY, the polar effect of the group R comprises all the processes whereby a substituent may modify the electrostatic forces operating at the reaction centre Y, relative to the standard \(\rm{R}^{\rm{o}}\rm{Y}\). These forces may be governed by charge separations arising from differences in the electronegativity of atoms (leading to the presence of dipoles), the presence of unipoles, or electron delocalization. It is synonymous with electronic effect or 'electrical effect' of a substituent as distinguished from other substituent effects, e.g. steric effects. Sometimes, however, the term 'polar effect' is taken to refer to the influence, other than steric, that non-conjugated substituents exert on reaction rates, i.e. effects connected with electron delocalization between a substituent and the molecular framework to which it is attached are excluded. Polar effect is then not synonymous with electronic effect

11490.title: polar surface area
11490.definition: Surface area over all polar atoms (usually oxygen and nitrogen), including any attached hydrogen atoms, of a molecule.

P04710.title: polarity
P04710.definition: When applied to solvents, this rather ill-defined term covers their overall solvation capability (solvation power) for solutes (i.e. in chemical equilibria: reactants and products; in reaction rates: reactants and activated complex; in light absorptions: ions or molecules in the ground and excited state), which in turn depends on the action of all possible, nonspecific and specific, intermolecular interactions between solute ions or molecules and solvent molecules, excluding such interactions leading to definite chemical alterations of the ions or molecules of the solute. Occasionally, the term solvent polarity is restricted to nonspecific solute/solvent interactions only (i.e. to van der Waals forces).

08195.title: polarity
08195.definition: Characteristic of a bond between atoms of different electronegativity, such that the electrons in that bond are not shared equally.

P04711.title: polarizability
P04711.definition: The ease of distortion of the electron cloud of a molecular entity by an electric field (such as that due to the proximity of a charged reagent). It is experimentally measured as the ratio of induced dipole moment (\(\mu _{\mathrm{ind}}\)) to the field \(E\) which induces it: \[\alpha =\frac{\mu _{\rm{ind}}}{E}\] The units of \(\alpha \) are \(\rm{C}^{2}\ \rm{m}^{2}\ \rm{V}^{-1}\). In ordinary usage the term refers to the 'mean polarizability', i.e., the average over three rectilinear axes of the molecule. Polarizabilities in different directions (e.g. along the bond in $\ce{Cl2}$, called 'longitudinal polarizability', and in the direction perpendicular to the bond, called 'transverse polarizability') can be distinguished, at least in principle. Polarizability along the bond joining a substituent to the rest of the molecule is seen in certain modern theoretical approaches as a factor influencing chemical reactivity, etc., and parametrization thereof has been proposed.

09078.title: polarizable electrode
09078.definition: Electrode whose potential changes with an applied potential.

08856.title: polarization density
08856.definition: Change in electric dipole moment per unit volume of dielectric material in response to its exposure to an electric field.

P04714.title: polarization error
P04714.definition: An error which arises from the fact that the absorbance of a sample (especially a solid) could depend on the polarization of the incident radiation and from the polarization dependent response of the photodetector.

P04713.title: polarization
P04713.definition: The difference of the electrode potential from the corrosion potential. The symbol should not be used for polarization.

16219.title: polarisation spectroscopy
16219.definition: In absorption experiments, polarization spectroscopy is performed with polarized light on anisotropic samples.

P04712.title: polarization
P04712.definition: The relevant material property that couples with the radiation field. May be called optical or dielectric polarization. Optical spectroscopies may be classified according to the dielectric polarization power-law dependence on the external electric field.

P04715.title: polarized interphases
P04715.definition: Ideally, interphases for which there are no common components between the phases or the exchange of these is hindered.

08660.title: polarized Raman band
08660.definition: Raman band with depolarization ratio \(\rho \le 0.75\) for linear polarized incident radiation in normal Raman spectroscopy.

P04716.title: polarography
P04716.definition: A measure of current as a function of potential when the working electrode is a dropping mercury (or other liquid conductor) electrode and unstirred solutions are used.

PT07416.title: polaron
PT07416.definition: Lattice distortion or polarization caused by photoexcitation.

08857.title: poling
08857.definition: Orientation of dipoles or dipolar domains inside a material by using a sufficiently strong electric field.

14928.title: pollutant
14928.definition: Any undesirable solid, liquid, or gaseous matter occurring, as a result of human activities, in a solid, liquid, or gaseous environmental medium and causing adverse effects.

14930.title: pollution tolerance index
14930.definition: Means of measuring environmental quality, usually water quality, by determining the presence of indicator species, classified into three groups—sensitive, facultative, and tolerant. Each group is assigned an index value 1, 2, and 3, with the sensitive group having the highest index value. The number of species present from the list included in each group is identified in a representative environmental sample and the group index multiplied by the number of species in the group. The scores for each group are finally added to give the PTI for the environmental medium under consideration. The environmental quality is directly proportional to the value of the index.

14929.title: pollution-induced community tolerance
14929.definition: Increase in tolerance to pollution resulting from species composition shifts in the community, acclimatization of individuals, and genetic changes in populations in the community.

13588.title: poly I:C
13588.definition: Polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid, a synthetic immunostimulant mimicking viral double-stranded RNA.

13589.title: poly ICLC
13589.definition: Polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid, poly-ʟ-lysine, and carboxymethylcellulose (letter roots of the acronym underlined), a synthetic immunostimulant mimicking viral double-stranded RNA.

13590.title: poly-Ig receptor
13590.definition: Receptor molecule that specifically binds J chain-containing polymeric immunoglobulin (Ig), i.e., dimeric secretory immunoglobulin A (IgA) and pentameric immunoglobulin M (IgM), and transports it across mucosal epithelium.

08890.title: poly(ethene-1,2-diyl)
08890.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules exclusively consisting of ethene-1,2-diyl (formerly called vinylene) constitutional repeating units.

08882.title: polyacetylenes
08882.definition: Polymers prepared from acetylene (ethyne), a substituted acetylene, or both in admixture by a polymerization involving one or more triple bonds (source-based polymer class name).

PT07217.title: polyacid
PT07217.definition: In polymer terminology, polyelectrolyte composed of macromolecules containing acid groups on a substantial fraction of the constitutional units.

P04720.title: polyaddition
P04720.definition: A polymerization in which the growth of polymer chains proceeds by addition reactions between molecules of all degrees of polymerization.

15264.title: polyalkenylene
15264.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alkene-α,ω-diyl (formerly alkenylene) constitutional repeating units: \[\ce{-[-CH=CH-[CH2]_{m}\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\]

15265.title: polyalkylene
15265.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alkane-α,ω-diyl (formerly alkylene) constitutional repeating units: \[\ce{-[-CR^{1}R^{2}\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, or cycloalkyl.

15266.title: polyalkynylene
15266.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alkyne-α,ω-diyl (formerly alkynylene) constitutional repeating units: \[\ce{-[-C#C-[CH2]_m\bond{-}]_n\bond{-}}\]

15267.title: polyamide
15267.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carboxamide groups as linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-NR-CO\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

15268.title: polyamide acid
15268.definition: Polyamide containing pendent carboxy groups:   where \(\ce{R}\) is a constitutional unit with a connectivity three or higher.

15269.title: polyamine
15269.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing imino groups as linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-NR\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

15270.title: polyanhydride
15270.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carboxylic anhydride groupings as linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-CO-O-CO\bond{-}}\]

08883.title: polyanilines
08883.definition: Polymers prepared exclusively from aniline, or substituted aniline, or both in admixture (source-based class name).

13585.title: polyarteritis nodosa
13585.definition: Systemic disease characterized by widespread inflammation of small and medium-sized arteries in which many of the foci are nodular.

08884.title: polyarylenes
08884.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively arenediyl (formerly arylene) or heteroarenediyl (formerly heteroarylene) units in the backbone:  where Ar is a divalent arenediyl or heteroarenediyl group (structure-based polymer class name).

08885.title: polyarylenethynylenes
08885.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating arenediyl or heterarenediyl (formerly arylene or heteroarylene, respectively) and ethynediyl (formerly ethynylene) constitutional repeating units in the backbone:  where Ar is a divalent arenediyl or heterarenediyl group (structure-based polymer class name).

08886.title: polyarylenevinylenes
08886.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating arenediyl or heteroarenediyl (formerly arylene or heteroarylene, respectively) and ethene-1,2-diyl (formerly vinylene) or substituted vinylene constitutional repeating units in the backbone:  where Ar is a divalent arenediyl or heteroarenediyl group and \(\ce{R^{1}}\) and \(\ce{R^{2}}\) are each hydrogen, or an alkyl, aryl or heteroaryl group (structure-based polymer class name).

09412.title: polyatomic fragment
09412.definition: Ion or neutral particle composed of three or more atoms.

08887.title: polyazomethines
08887.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing azomethine (azanylylidenemethanylylidene) linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-N=CR-}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, or an alkyl or aryl group (structure-based polymer class name).

PT07219.title: polybase
PT07219.definition: In polymer terminology, polyelectrolyte composed of macromolecules containing basic groups on a substantial fraction of the constitutional units.

08888.title: polybenzimidazoles
08888.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing benzimidazole groups in the backbone, such as groups (structure-based polymer class name).

15271.title: polybenzothiazole
15271.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing benzothiazole groups in the backbone, such as the groups:

15272.title: polybenzoxazole
15272.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing benzoxazole linkages in the backbone, such as the linkages:

PT07220.title: polybetaine
PT07220.definition: Ampholytic polymer in which pendant groups have a betaine-type structure.

15273.title: polycarbamate
15273.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carbamate (formerly urethane) or N-substituted carbamate linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-NR-CO-O\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, heteroaryl, substituted alkyl, substituted aryl, or substituted heteroaryl.

15274.title: polycarbodiimide
15274.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carbodiimide linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-N=C=N\bond{-}}\]

15275.title: polycarbonate
15275.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carbonate linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-O-CO-O\bond{-}}\]

15276.title: polycarbosilane
15276.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carbon-silicon linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-SiR^{1}R^{2}\bond{-}CR^{3}R^{4}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\), \(\ce{R^2}\), \(\ce{R^3}\), and \(\ce{R^4}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

P04721.title: polychromator
P04721.definition: An extension of a monochromator, a number of exit slits being placed in the focal plane, so allowing a number of discrete bands to pass through (to fall, for example, upon a number of photomultipliers).

13586.title: polyclonal activator
13586.definition: Substance that induces activation of multiple clones of B lymphocytes or T lymphocytes.

15989.title: polyclonal antibody
15989.definition: Antibody produced by a number of different cell types.

P04722.title: polycondensation
P04722.definition: A polymerization in which the growth of polymer chains proceeds by condensation reactions between molecules of all degrees of polymerization.

P04723.title: polycrystalline graphite
P04723.definition: A graphite material with coherent crystallographic domains of limited size regardless of the perfection and preferred orientation (texture) of their crystalline structure.

15277.title: polycyanurate
15277.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing 1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triyltrioxy constitutional units (formerly cyanurate groups) in the backbone:

15432.title: polycyclic macromolecule
15432.definition: Molecule that includes more than one macrocycle, all of which have at least one atom in common with another macrocycle.

P04724.title: polycyclic system
P04724.definition: A molecular system regarded as containing a number of rings equal to the number of scissions required to convert it into an open-chain compound.

11105.title: polydactyly
11105.definition: Congenital occurrence of supernumerary fingers or toes.

08889.title: polydiacetylenes
08889.definition: Polymer prepared from buta-1,3-diyne (diacetylene) or a substituted buta-1,3-diyne or both in admixture (source-based polymer class name).

15252.title: polydiene
15252.definition: Polymer prepared from a diene, or a substituted diene, or both in admixture.

P04726.title: polydisperse medium
P04726.definition: A colloidal system in which many particle sizes occur.

P04728.title: polyelectrolyte
P04728.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules in which a substantial portion of the constitutional units contains ionic or ionizable groups, or both.

PT07222.title: polyelectrolyte complex
PT07222.definition: Neutral polymer-polymer complex composed of macromolecules carrying charges of opposite sign causing the macromolecules to be bound together by electrostatic interactions.

PT07524.title: polyelectrolyte gel
PT07524.definition: Polymer gel in which the polymer network contains ionic or ionizable groups in a significant fraction of its constitutional units.

PT07223.title: polyelectrolyte network
PT07223.definition: Polymer network containing ionic or ionizable groups in a substantial fraction of its constitutional units.

15278.title: polyester
15278.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carboxylic ester linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-O-CO\bond{-}}\]

15279.title: polyether
15279.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing ether linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-O\bond{-}}\]

08892.title: polyfluorenes
08892.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing fluorenediyl or substituted fluorenediyl (mainly 2,7-diyl) constitutional repeating units in the backbone (structure-based polymer class name).

14931.title: polygenic control
14931.definition: Control of a phenotypic trait by several genes.

15280.title: polygermane
15280.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively germanium atoms in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-GeR2\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is alkyl, aryl or heteroaryl.

15281.title: polyglutarimide
15281.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing glutarimide rings in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen or alkyl (usually methyl) and \(\ce{R^1}\) is hydrogen, or an alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl group.

P04730.title: polygranular carbon
P04730.definition: A carbon material composed of grains, which can be clearly distinguished by means of optical microscopy.

P04731.title: polygranular graphite
P04731.definition: A graphite material composed of grains which can be clearly distinguished by means of optical microscopy.

PT06792.title: polyhedral symbol
PT06792.definition: The polyhedral symbol indicates the geometrical arrangements of the coordinating atoms about the central atom. It consists of one or more capital italic letters derived from common geometric terms (tetrahedron, square plane, octahedron, etc.) which denote the idealised geometry of the ligands around the coordination centre, and an arabic numeral that is the coordination number of the central atom. The polyhedral symbol is used as an affix, enclosed in parentheses, and separated from the name by a hyphen. Examples are T-4, SP-4, TBPY-5, SPY-5, OC-6, and CU-8.

P04732.title: polyhedranes
P04732.definition: Polycyclic hydrocarbons of the $\ce{(CH)_{n}}$ series having skeletons corresponding to the regular and semiregular geometrical solids, e.g. cubane,

15282.title: polyhydantoin
15282.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing hydantoin (imidazolidine-2,4-dione) rings in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, or an alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl group.

15283.title: polyhydrazide
15283.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing hydrazide linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-CO-NR^1\bond{-}NR^2\bond{-}CO\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

15284.title: polyimidazole
15284.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing imidazole rings in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen, or an alkyl or aryl group.

08893.title: polyimides
08893.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing cyclic dicarboximide groupings in the backbone:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\), \(\ce{R^{2}}\), \(\ce{R^{3}}\) and \(\ce{R^{4}}\) are groups with connectivity one, two, three, and four, respectively (structure-based polymer class name).

P04733.title: polyions
P04733.definition: Polycations or polyanions — multiply charged ions.

15285.title: polyisocyanurate
15285.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing 2,4,6-trioxo-1,3,5-triazinane-1,3,5-triyl (formerly isocyanurate) rings in the backbone:

P04734.title: polyketides
P04734.definition: Natural compounds containing alternating carbonyl and methylene groups ('$\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}polyketones}$'), biogenetically derived from repeated condensation of acetyl coenzyme A (via malonyl coenzyme A), and usually the compounds derived from them by further condensations. Considered by many to be synonymous with the less frequently used terms acetogenins and ketides.

15286.title: polyketone
15286.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing keto groups as linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-CO\bond{-}}\]

PT07264.title: polymer alloy
PT07264.definition: Polymeric material, exhibiting macroscopically uniform physical properties throughout its whole volume, that comprises a compatible polymer blend, a miscible polymer blend or a multiphase copolymer.

14275.title: polymer bead
14275.definition: Sphere of polymer, usually with a diameter in the range from one-tenth to a few millimeters.

P04736.title: polymer blend
P04736.definition: Macroscopically homogeneous mixture of two or more different species of polymer.

14313.title: polymer colloid
14313.definition: Colloidal dispersion in which at least one of the phases is a polymer, either organic, or inorganic or some combination of the two.

PT07185.title: polymer compatibilizer
PT07185.definition: Polymeric additive that, when added to a blend of immiscible polymers, modifies their interfaces and stabilizes the blend.

PT07142.title: polymer complexation
PT07142.definition: Process that results in the formation of a polymer–polymer complex or a complex composed of a polymer and a low-molar-mass substance.

PT07242.title: polymer composite
PT07242.definition: Composite in which at least one component is a polymer.

14325.title: polymer content
14325.definition: Mass fraction of polymer in a polymer dispersion.

P04737.title: polymer crystal
P04737.definition: A crystalline domain usually limited by well-defined boundaries.

P04738.title: polymer crystallite
P04738.definition: A small crystalline domain. A crystallite may have irregular boundaries and parts of its constituent macromolecules may extend beyond its boundaries. This definition is not identical with that used in classical crystallography.

PT07143.title: polymer cyclization
PT07143.definition: Chemical reaction that leads to the formation of ring structures in or from polymer chains.

PT07144.title: polymer degradation
PT07144.definition: Chemical changes in a polymeric material that usually result in undesirable changes in the in-use properties of the material.

14311.title: polymer dispersion
14311.definition: Dispersion in which the dispersed phase consists of a polymer.

PT07186.title: polymer drug
PT07186.definition: Polymer that contains either chemically-bound drug molecules or pharmacologically active moieties.

14314.title: polymer emulsion
14314.definition: Emulsion in which the dispersed phase is a liquid polymer or a polymer solution.

PT07145.title: polymer functionalization
PT07145.definition: Introduction of desired chemical groups into polymer molecules to create specific chemical, physical, biological, pharmacological, or other properties.

PT07187.title: polymer gel
PT07187.definition: Gel in which the network component is a polymer.

14280.title: polymer gel particle
14280.definition: Particle of gel in which the network component is a polymer.

12793.title: polymer glass
12793.definition: Amorphous polymer at temperatures below its glass-transition temperature.

14328.title: polymer mass fraction
14328.definition: Mass fraction of polymer within the dispersed phase.

12794.title: polymer melt
12794.definition: Polymer in the amorphous state above its glass-transition temperature.

PT07188.title: polymer membrane
PT07188.definition: Thin layer of polymeric material that acts as a barrier permitting mass transport of selected species.
