14276.title: polymer microparticle
14276.definition: Particle of polymer of any shape with an equivalent diameter from approximately \(\pu{0.1 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{100 \upmu m}\).

14278.title: polymer nanoparticle
14278.definition: Particle of polymer of any shape and an equivalent diameter from approximately \(\pu{1 nm}\) to \(\pu{100 nm}\).

14283.title: polymer network particle
14283.definition: Particle having any shape and composed of a polymer network and possibly species of finite molar mass.

14274.title: polymer particle
14274.definition: Particle of polymer of any shape.

PT07160.title: polymer phase-transfer catalyst
PT07160.definition: Polymer that acts as a phase-transfer catalyst and thereby causes a significant enhancement of the rate of a reaction between two reactants located in neighboring phases owing to its catalysis of the extraction of one of the reactants across the interface to the other phase where the reaction takes place.

PT07162.title: polymer reactant
PT07162.definition: Reactant (reagent) that is or is attached to a high-molar-mass linear polymer or a polymer network.

PT07146.title: polymer reaction
PT07146.definition: Chemical reaction in which at least one of the reactants is a high-molar-mass substance.

PT07189.title: polymer solvent
PT07189.definition: Polymer that acts like a solvent for compounds of low molar mass.

PT07190.title: polymer sorbent
PT07190.definition: Polymer that adsorbs or absorbs a certain substance or certain substances from a liquid or a gas.

PT07191.title: polymer support
PT07191.definition: Polymer to or in which a reagent or catalyst is chemically bound, immobilized, dispersed, or associated.

PT07192.title: polymer surfactant
PT07192.definition: Polymer that lowers the surface tension of the medium in which it is dissolved, or the interfacial tension with another phase, or both.

PT07583.title: polymer-derived ceramic
PT07583.definition: Ceramic derived from a polymeric ceramic precursor.

PT07159.title: polymer-metal complex
PT07159.definition: Complex comprising a metal and one or more polymeric ligands.

P04744.title: polymer-poor phase
P04744.definition: That phase of a two-phase equilibrium system, consisting of a polymer and low molecular weight material, in which the polymer concentration is lower. The use of the name 'sol phase' is discouraged. Synonymous with dilute phase.

P04745.title: polymer-rich phase
P04745.definition: That phase of a two-phase equilibrium system, consisting of a polymer and low molecular weight material, in which the polymer concentration is higher. The use of the name 'gel phase' is discouraged. Synonymous with concentrated phase.

PT07161.title: polymer-supported catalyst
PT07161.definition: Catalyst system comprising a polymer support in which catalytically active species are immobilized through chemical bonds or weaker interactions such as hydrogen bonds or donor–acceptor interactions.

PT07147.title: polymer-supported reaction
PT07147.definition: Chemical reaction in which at least one reactant or a catalyst is bound through chemical bonds or weaker interactions, such as hydrogen bonds or donor–acceptor interactions, to a polymer.

P04743.title: polymer–polymer complex
P04743.definition: Complex, at least two components of which are different polymers.

P04746.title: polymer–solvent interaction
P04746.definition: The sum of the effects of all intermolecular interactions between polymer and solvent molecules in solution that are reflected in the Gibbs and Helmholtz energies of mixing.

09715.title: polymerase
09715.definition: Enzyme that catalyses the synthesis of nucleic acids on pre-existing nucleic acid templates.

PT06791.title: polymerase chain reaction
PT06791.definition: A laboratory technique to rapidly amplify pre-determined regions of double-stranded DNA. Generally involves the use of a heat-stable DNA polymerase.

PT07511.title: polymeric sol
PT07511.definition: Sol in which the dispersed phase consists of particles having a polymeric structure.

PT06918.title: polymeric stationary phase
PT06918.definition: Stationary phase (material) based on particles of a cross-linked organic polymeric material. Typical materials are polystyrene divinylbenzene copolymers (PS-DVB) and modified PS-DVB materials.

P04740.title: polymerization
P04740.definition: The process of converting a monomer mixture of monomers into a polymer.

13848.title: polymersome
13848.definition: Vesicle with radius ranging from \(\pu{50 nm}\) to greater than \(\pu{5 \upmu m}\) constructed from an amphiphilic synthetic block copolymer.

15287.title: polymetaloxane
15287.definition: Organometallic polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating metal and oxygen atoms in the main chain: \[\ce{-ML_{x}-O\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{M}\) is a metal atom such as \(\ce{Al}\), \(\ce{Ge}\), \(\ce{Sn}\), or \(\ce{Ti}\), and \(\ce{L}\) is a metal-bonded substituent (ligand).

P04747.title: polymolecularity correction
P04747.definition: A correction applied to relationships between a property and the molar mass or relative molecular mass, obtained from polymers non-uniform with respect to relative molecular mass, in order to obtain the corresponding relationship for polymers strictly uniform with respect to relative molecular mass.

15225.title: polymorph
15225.definition: Solid material that exists at least in two different molecular arrangements, i.e., distinctly different crystal species.

P04748.title: polymorphic transition
P04748.definition: A reversible transition of a solid crystalline phase at a certain temperature and pressure (the inversion point) to another phase of the same chemical composition with a different crystal structure.

11106.title: polymorphism
11106.definition:
Occurrence of a gene in more than one distinct nucleotide sequence in a population, resulting from mutation(s) and potentially producing gene products with different levels of function.
Note: It is sometimes considered that the least frequent of polymorphic gene sequences should be present in at least \(\pu{1\%}\) of the population; otherwise the variant is a mutation rather than a polymorphism.
Occurrence of different phenotypes of a single trait.

13591.title: polymorphonuclear leukocyte
13591.definition: Mature leukocyte with granular cytoplasm and a segmented and irregularly shaped nucleus.

13592.title: polymyositis
13592.definition: Disorder characterized by inflammation and degeneration of skeletal muscle, causing pain, weakness, and wasting in affected (usually proximal) muscles.

12013.title: polyneuritis
12013.definition: Inflammation of several peripheral nerves simultaneously.

12014.title: polyneuropathy
12014.definition: Neuropathy (distal axonopathy) of the peripheral nervous system, often affecting the extremities in a bilateral distribution, and characterized by numbness, tingling, and paresthesia.

08894.title: polyoxadiazoles
08894.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively oxadiazole rings in the backbone (structure-based polymer class name).

15288.title: polyoxyalkylene
15288.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively oxyalkane-α,ω-diyl (formerly oxyalkylene) constitutional repeating units in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-O-Y\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{Y}\) is an alkane-α,ω-diyl (formerly alkylene) or substituted alkane-α,ω-diyl group contributing at least two carbon atoms to the main chain.

15289.title: polyoxyarylene
15289.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively oxyarenediyl (formerly oxyarylene) constitutional repeating units in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-O-Ar\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{Ar}\) is an arenediyl (formerly arylene), heteroarenediyl (formerly heteroarylene), substituted arenediyl or substituted heteroarenediyl.

15290.title: polyoxymethylene
15290.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively oxymethylene or substituted oxymethylene constitutional repeating units in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

15291.title: polyoxyphenylene
15291.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively oxyphenylene or ring-substituted oxyphenylene constitutional repeating units in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R^1}\), \(\ce{R^2}\), \(\ce{R^3}\), and \(\ce{R^4}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl, aryl, or aralkyl group.

15292.title: polyparabanic acid
15292.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing imidazolidine-2,4,5-trione (parabanic acid) rings in the backbone:

P04749.title: polypeptides
P04749.definition: Peptides containing ten or more amino acid residues.

15293.title: polyphenylenemethylene
15293.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating phenylene or substituted phenylene and methylene or substituted methylene constitutional units in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R^1}\), \(\ce{R^2}\), \(\ce{R^3}\), \(\ce{R^4}\), \(\ce{R^5}\), and \(\ce{R^6}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, halogen, trialkylsilyl, etc.

08895.title: polyphenylenes
08895.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively \(\upsigma\)-bonded benzene or substituted benzene rings in the backbone:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\), \(\ce{R^{2}}\), \(\ce{R^{3}}\) and \(\ce{R^{4}}\) are each hydrogen or an univalent group (structure-based polymer class name).

08896.title: polyphenylenethynylenes
08896.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating phenylene or substituted phenylene and ethynediyl (formerly ethynylene) constitutional repeating units in the backbone:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\), \(\ce{R^{2}}\), \(\ce{R^{3}}\) and \(\ce{R^{4}}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, halogen, trialkylsilyl etc. (structure-based polymer class name).

08897.title: polyphenylenevinylenes
08897.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating phenylene or substituted phenylene and ethene-1,2-diyl (formerly vinylene) or substituted ethene-1,2-diyl constitutional repeating units in the backbone:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\), \(\ce{R^{2}}\), \(\ce{R^{3}}\), \(\ce{R^{4}}\), \(\ce{R^{5}}\) and \(\ce{R^{6}}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, heteroaryl, halogen, trialkylsilyl, etc. (structure-based polymer class name).

15294.title: polyphosphate
15294.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing phosphate constitutional repeating units:   where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

15295.title: polyphosphazene
15295.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively nitrilophosphanylylidene (formerly phosphazene) constitutional repeating units in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each a monovalent group, such as a halogen or an alkoxy group.

11107.title: polyploidy
11107.definition: Occurrence of more than two complete sets of chromosomes.

P04750.title: polyprenols
P04750.definition: A subgroup of prenols in which \(n\) in the general formula $\ce{H–[CH2–C(CH3)=CH–CH2]_{n}–OH}$ is greater than four.

08898.title: polypyrroles
08898.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules with backbones composed of pyrrole rings (structure-based polymer class name definition).

15296.title: polypyrrone
15296.definition: Polymer composed of single strand or ladder macromolecules comprising isoindolo[2,1-a]benzimidazole (formerly pyrrone) constitutional repeating units such as:  where \(\ce{Z}\) is a divalent linking group or atom.

P04751.title: polyquinanes
P04751.definition: Saturated or unsaturated, respectively, polycyclic hydrocarbons consisting of fused five-membered rings, commonly but not necessarily incorporating the skeleton of quinacene (tricyclo[5.2.1.04,10]deca-2,5,8-triene): E.g.  bicyclo[3.3.0]octane, dodecahedrane.

15297.title: polyquinoline
15297.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing quinoline moieties in the backbone:

15298.title: polyquinoxaline
15298.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing quinoxaline groups in the backbone:

13850.title: polyrotaxane
13850.definition: Polymer comprising mechanically interlocked molecular architectures typically of a macromolecule threaded through one or more macrocycles.

P04752.title: polysaccharides
P04752.definition: Compounds consisting of a large number of monosaccharides linked glycosidically. This term is commonly used only for those containing more than ten monosaccharide residues. Also called glycans.

08899.title: polysilanes
08899.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively silicon atoms in the backbone:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\) and \(\ce{R^{2}}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl, aryl or heteroaryl group (structure-based polymer class name).

15299.title: polysilazane
15299.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating nitrogen and silicon atoms in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-NR^{1}\bond{-}SiR^{2}\!\,R^{3}\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\), \(\ce{R^2}\), and \(\ce{R^3}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl or aryl group.

15300.title: polysiloxane
15300.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing alternating oxygen and silicon atoms in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-O\bond{-}SiR^{1}\!\,R^{2}\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl or aryl group.

15301.title: polysilsesquioxane
15301.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing silicon and oxygen atoms in the ratio \(1{:}1.5\) (ideal ratio for infinite macromolecule), which alternate in a hyperbranched or ladder structure such as:   where \(\ce{R}\) is alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

15302.title: polystannane
15302.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively tin atoms in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-SnR^{1}\!\,R^{2}\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl or aryl group.

P04753.title: polysulfanes
P04753.definition: Compounds having an unbranched chain of sulfur atoms ($\ce{s2}$ or higher) terminating in H: $\ce{HS_{n}H}$. Some chemists exclude disulfane, $\ce{HS2H}$, from the class polysulfanes.

P04754.title: polysulfides
P04754.definition: Compounds $\ce{R–[S]_{n}–R}$, with a chain of sulfur atoms (\(n\geq 2\)) and $\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$. Some chemists exclude disulfides, $\ce{RS2R}$, from the class polysulfides.

15303.title: polysulfonamide
15303.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing sulfonamide linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-SO2-NR\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen or an alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl group.

15304.title: polysulfone
15304.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing sulfonyl linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-SO2\bond{-}}\]

08900.title: polytetrazines
08900.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing tetrazine or hydrogenated tetrazine rings in the backbone (structure-based polymer class name):

08901.title: polythiadiazoles
08901.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing thiadiazole rings in the backbone (structure-based polymer class name).

08902.title: polythiazoles
08902.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing thiazole rings in the backbone:  where R is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, heteroaryl, substituted alkyl, substituted aryl or substituted heteroaryl (structure-based polymer class name).

15305.title: polythioester
15305.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing thiocarboxylate (thioester) linkages in the backbone:\(\ce{-S-CO\bond{-}}\) or \(\ce{-O-CS\bond{-}}\) or \(\ce{-S-CS\bond{-}}\)

15306.title: polythioether
15306.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing thioether (sulfide) linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-S\bond{-}}\]

08903.title: polythiophenes
08903.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively thiophene rings in the backbone (structure-based polymer class name).

P04755.title: polytopal rearrangement
P04755.definition: Stereoisomerization interconverting different or equivalent spatial arrangements of ligands about a central atom or of a cage of atoms, where the ligand or cage defines the vertices of a polyhedron. For example pyramidal inversion of amines, Berry pseudorotation of $\ce{PF5}$, rearrangements of polyhedral boranes.

15307.title: polytriazine
15307.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing triazine rings in the backbone:

P04756.title: polytypic transition
P04756.definition: A transition of a crystalline structure into one or more forms which differ in the way identical layers of atoms are stacked. Example: $\ce{ZnS}$ consists of two identical close packings, one of $\ce{Zn}$ atoms, the other $\ce{S}$ atoms, with the one displaced to the other along the c-axis through one-quarter of the layer spacing. In sphalerite-type $\ce{ZnS}$ the layers have the face-centred-cubic (ABC ABC) sequence, in wurtzite-type $\ce{ZnS}$ they have the hexagonal-close-packed (AB AB) sequence. The transition of sphalerite-type $\ce{ZnS}$ to wurtzite-type $\ce{ZnS}$ occurs at \(1297\ \rm{K}\).

09854.title: polyunsaturated fatty acids
09854.definition: Fatty acids with more than one double bond.

15308.title: polyurea
15308.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing ureylene or N-substituted ureylene linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-NR-CO-NR\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, heteroaryl, substituted alkyl, substituted aryl, or substituted heteroaryl.

15991.title: polyuria
15991.definition: Excessive production and discharge of urine.

15256.title: polyvinyl acetal
15256.definition: Polymer prepared by acetalization of poly(vinyl alcohol) with an aldehyde.

15257.title: polyvinyl ester
15257.definition: Polymer prepared from a vinyl ester.

15258.title: polyvinyl ether
15258.definition: Polymer prepared from a vinyl ether.

15259.title: polyvinyl halide
15259.definition: Polymer prepared from a vinyl halide (monohalogenoethene).

15260.title: polyvinyl ketone
15260.definition: Polymer prepared from a vinyl ketone.

08904.title: polyvinylcarbazoles
08904.definition: Polymers prepared from a vinylcarbazole or a substituted vinylcarbazole or both in admixture (source-based polymer class name).

08905.title: polyvinylenes
08905.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively ethene-1,2-diyl (formerly vinylene) or substituted ethene-1,2-diyl constitutional repeating units in the backbone: \[\ce{-CR^{1}=CR^{2}-}\] where \(\ce{R^{1}}\) and \(\ce{R^{2}}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl group (structure-based polymer class name).

08906.title: polyzwitterions
08906.definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules consisting of zwitterionic repeating units (structure-based polymer class name).

08858.title: Poole–Frenkel effect
08858.definition: Increase in the electric conductivity of a semiconductor or insulator by exposing it to an electric field.

P04758.title: pooled standard deviation
P04758.definition: A problem often arises when the combination of several series of measurements performed under similar conditions is desired to achieve an improved estimate of the imprecision of the process. If it can be assumed that all the series are of the same precision although their means may differ, the pooled standard deviations \(s_{\rm{p}}\) from \(k\) series of measurements can be calculated as \[s_{\rm{p}}=\sqrt{\frac{(n_{1}- 1)\ s_{1}^{2}+(n_{2}- 1)\ s_{2}^{2}+...+(n_{k}- 1)\ s_{k}^{2}}{n_{1}+n_{2}+...+n_{k}- k}}\] The suffices \(1,2,...,k\) refer to the different series of measurements. In this case it is assumed that there exists a single underlying standard deviation \(\sigma \) of which the pooled standard deviation \(s_{\rm{p}}\) is a better estimate than the individual calculated standard deviations \(s_{1},s_{2},...,s_{k}\), For the special case where \(k\) sets of duplicate measurements are available, the above equation reduces to \[s_{\rm{p}}=\sqrt{\frac{\sum (x_{i1}- x_{i2})^{2}}{2\ k}}\] Results from various series of measurements can be combined in the following way to give a pooled relative standard deviation \(s_{\rm{r,p}}\): \[s_{\rm{r,p}} = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (n_{i}-1)\ s_{\rm{r,}i}^{2}}{\sum n_{i}- 1}} = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (n_{i}-1)\ s_{i}^{2}\ x_{i}^{-2}}{\sum n_{i}-1}}\]

13593.title: popliteal lymph node assay
13593.definition: Test for immunosensitization measuring popliteal lymph node hyperplasia after subcutaneous injection of a test substance into the footpad of the hindpaw of a rodent.

14932.title: population
14932.definition: In ecology, any group of interacting and interbreeding organisms of the same species occupying a given area at the same time.

15992.title: population at risk
15992.definition: Persons who can and may develop an adverse health effect and who are potentially exposed to a substance under study. People already having chronic disease are excluded from the population at risk in studies of the incidence of the adverse effect.

14933.title: population biomass
14933.definition: Total mass or weight of organisms in a population, given by the sum of the masses (or weights) of all the individual members of the population.

15993.title: population critical concentration
15993.definition: Concentration of a substance in the critical organ at which a specified percentage of the exposed population has reached the individual critical organ concentration.

14934.title: population cycle
14934.definition: Changes in the numbers of individuals in a population that repeatedly oscillate between periods of high and low density.

14935.title: population density
14935.definition: Number of individuals divided by area (\(\pu{m-2}\)) or volume (\(\pu{m-3}\)).

14936.title: population dynamics
14936.definition: Variations in time and space in the sizes and densities of populations.

14937.title: population ecology
14937.definition: Study of the variations in time and space in the sizes and densities of populations, and of the factors causing these variations.

15994.title: population effect
15994.definition: Absolute number or incidence rate of cases occurring in a group of people.

14938.title: population fluctuation
14938.definition: Variations over time in the size of a population.

14939.title: population growth rate
14939.definition: Change in population size \(\Delta N\) during a specified time period \(\Delta t\) \[\Delta N/\Delta t = (b - d)N\] where \(N\) is population size, \(b\) is per capita birth rate, and \(d\) is per capita death rate.

P04759.title: population inversion
P04759.definition: A situation in which a higher energy state is more populated than a lower energy state.

14940.title: population pyramid
14940.definition: Diagrammatic illustration of the age structure of a population by depicting the youngest age class at the base and stacking successive age classes above it.

14941.title: population size
14941.definition: Total number of organisms in a population.

P04760.title: pore size distribution
P04760.definition: The distribution of pore volume with respect to pore size; alternatively, it may be defined by the related distribution of pore area with respect to pore size.

11108.title: porencephaly
11108.definition: Occurrence of a cyst in the substance of the brain that usually communicates with one of the lateral ventricles.

P04762.title: porosity
P04762.definition: A concept related to texture, referring to the pore space in a material.

10288.title: porous membrane
10288.definition: Membrane in which permeation occurs through its porous structure.

14942.title: porous pot test
14942.definition: Biodegradation test that simulates the continuous activated sludge (sewage treatment) system.

P04763.title: porous-layer open-tabular column
P04763.definition: A column in which there is a porous layer on the inner wall. porosity can be achieved by either chemical means (e.g. etching) or by the deposition of porous particles on the wall from a suspension. The porous layer may serve as a support for a liquid stationary phase or as the stationary phase itself.

15995.title: porphyria
15995.definition: Disturbance of porphyrin metabolism characterized by increased formation, accumulation, and excretion of porphyrins and their precursors.

15996.title: porphyrin
15996.definition: Natural pigment containing a fundamental skeleton of four pyrrole nuclei united through the α-positions by four methine groups to form a macrocyclic structure.

P04764.title: porphyrinogens
P04764.definition: Hexahydroporphyrins in which the nitrogen atoms and four meso positions are saturated.

P04765.title: porphyrins
P04765.definition: Natural pigments containing a fundamental skeleton of four pyrrole nuclei united through the $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}positions}$ by four methine groups to form a macrocyclic structure (porphyrin is designated porphine in Chemical Abstracts indexes).

11491.title: pose diagram
11491.definition: A 2D diagram that shows the interactions between a ligand and a protein in the 3D structure of the complex.

P04766.title: position-sensitive photomultiplier tube
P04766.definition: In position-sensitive photomultiplier tubes spatial resolution is obtained with the help of a partitioned photocathode.

14182.title: positive assay control
14182.definition: Experimental conditions designed to produce the signal reflective of maximum biological effect in an assay.

P04768.title: positive ion
P04768.definition: This is an atom, radical, molecule or molecular moiety which has lost one of more electrons thereby attaining an electrically positive charge. The use of the term cation as an alternative is not recommended. The use of mass ion is not recommended.

13594.title: positive selection
13594.definition: Selection of those developing T cells in the thymus that are able to recognize self-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules. This occurs by preventing apoptosis in these cells.

09413.title: positive-ion yield
09413.definition: Number of positively-charged secondary ions sputtered from a sample divided by the total number of incident primary particles.

09556.title: positive-tone development
09556.definition: Process for revealing the latent image in a resist in which the exposed regions are more soluble in the developer than are the unexposed regions.

08750.title: positron annihilation analysis
08750.definition: Measurement principle in which the annihilation of positrons is applied to study the microscopic structure of materials.

08751.title: positron emission tomography
08751.definition: Imaging method based on the detection of pairs of gamma rays emitted indirectly by a positron-emitting isotopic tracer.

08752.title: positron lifetime spectrometry
08752.definition: Measurement method of positron annihilation analysis in which the time interval between the emission of positrons from a radioactive source and the detection of gamma rays due to the annihilation of these positrons with electrons from the surrounding matter is the lifetime of the positron or positronium.

P04770.title: positronium
P04770.definition: Atom-like pair of particles consisting of an anti-electron (positron) and an electron.

15997.title: posology
15997.definition: Pharmacological study of the choice of appropriate dose of a drug in relation to the physiological factors, such as age, that may influence its effect.

09557.title: post-apply bake
09557.definition: Thermal annealing step following the coating of a substrate with a resist material.

P04771.title: post-column derivatization
P04771.definition: A version of reaction chromatography in which the separated components eluting from the column are derivatized prior to entering the detector. The derivatization process is generally carried out 'on-the-fly', i.e. during transfer of the sample components from the column to the detector. Derivatization may also be carried out before the sample enters the column or the planar medium; this is pre-column (preliminary) derivatization.

09558.title: post-exposure bake
09558.definition: Thermal annealing step following the exposure of a resist to imaging radiation.

09559.title: post-exposure delay
09559.definition: Pause between successive patterning steps in lithographic processing.

P04772.title: post-filter effect
P04772.definition: This effect arises when the exciting beam does not fill the cell completely and luminescence is absorbed by the analyte and interfering impurities in the non-illuminated region facing the detector.

11109.title: post-implantation
11109.definition: Occurring after the early embryo embeds in the lining of the uterus.

15998.title: post-translational modification
15998.definition: Processes by which proteins are biochemically modified within a cell following their synthesis on the ribosomes.

12015.title: posterior fossa
12015.definition: Pocket in the back of the skull that accommodates the cerebellum and the midbrain.

11492.title: posterior probability
11492.definition:
The conditional probability that is assigned to a quantity after relevant evidence is taken into account. The prior and posterior probabilities are linked by
 the (normalized) likelihood function (Bayes's theorem).

11111.title: postnatal
11111.definition: Referring to events in the life of the mother or fetus following birth.

11112.title: postpartum
11112.definition: Period following the birth of an infant, often considered to be about six weeks in the human.

P04773.title: postprecipitation
P04773.definition: The subsequent precipitation of a chemically different species upon the surface of an initial precipitate usually, but not necessarily, including a common ion.

12016.title: postsynaptic
12016.definition: Event or structure at the distal side of a synaptic cleft.

14183.title: potency
14183.definition: Dose of drug required to produce a specific effect of given intensity as compared to a standard reference.

P04775.title: potential at the point of zero charge
P04775.definition: The value of the electric potential of an electrode at which one of the charges defined is zero. The reference electrode against which this is measured should always be clearly stated. The potential difference with respect to the potential of zero charge is defined by \[E_{\rm{pzc}}=E- E_{\sigma =0}\] where the potential at the point of zero charge is that for the given electrode in the absence of specific adsorption (other than that of the solvent).

08661.title: potential coupling
08661.definition: Coupling of vibrational displacements through terms in the vibrational potential energy. The second-order (quadratic) terms cause harmonic potential coupling while the cubic and higher terms cause anharmonic potential coupling.

P04778.title: potential energy
P04778.definition: Energy of position or orientation in a field of force.

12715.title: potential genotoxic impurity
12715.definition: Confirmed or suspected presence of one or more known genotoxic materials in an active pharmaceutical ingredient.

08196.title: potential of mean force
08196.definition: Free energy as a function of a set of coordinates, the negative gradient of which gives the average force acting on that configuration averaged over all other coordinates and momenta within a statistical distribution. If the averaging is performed within a canonical ensemble (constant volume, temperature, and number of particles), the PMF is equivalent to the Helmholtz energy, but if it is performed within an isobaric-isothermal ensemble (constant pressure, temperature, and number of particles), the PMF is equivalent to the Gibbs energy.

P04787.title: potential temperature
P04787.definition: The temperature that a dry air parcel would have if lowered or raised adiabatically to a level of 1000 \(\rm{mbar}\) pressure (or other arbitrary standard pressure).

P04776.title: potential-determining ions
P04776.definition: Those species which by virtue of their electron distribution between the solid and liquid phase (or by their equilibrium with electrons in the solid) determine the difference in Galvani potential between these phases. This definition requires that adsorbed p.d. ions are part of the adsorbent and belong to the category of surface ions.

P04780.title: potential-energy surface
P04780.definition: A geometric hypersurface on which the potential energy of a set of reactants is plotted as a function of the coordinates representing the molecular geometries of the system. For simple systems two such coordinates (characterizing two variables that change during the progress from reactants to products) can be selected, and the potential energy plotted as a contour map. For simple elementary reactions, e.g. \(\rm{A}\!-\!\rm{B}\,+\,\rm{C}\rightarrow \rm{A}\,+\,\rm{B}\!-\!\rm{C}\) , the surface can show the potential energy for all values of the A, B, C geometry, providing that the ABC angle is fixed. For more complicated reactions a different choice of two coordinates is sometimes preferred, e.g. the bond orders of two different bonds. Such a diagram is often arranged so that reactants are located at the bottom left corner and products at the top right. If the trace of the representative point characterizing the route from reactants to products follows two adjacent edges of the diagram, the changes represented by the two coordinates take place in distinct succession; if the trace leaves the edges and crosses the interior of the diagram, the two changes are concerted. In many qualitative applications it is convenient (although not strictly equivalent) for the third coordinate to represent the standard Gibbs energy rather than potential energy. Using bond orders is, however, an oversimplification, since these are not well-defined, even for the transition state. (Some reservations concerning the diagrammatic use of Gibbs energies are noted under Gibbs energy diagram). The energetically easiest route from reactants to products on the potential-energy contour map defines the potential-energy profile.

P04779.title: potential-energy profile
P04779.definition: A curve describing the variation of the potential energy of the system of atoms that make up the reactants and products of a reaction as a function of one geometric coordinate, and corresponding to the 'energetically easiest passage' from reactants to products (i.e. along the line produced by joining the paths of steepest descent from the transition state to the reactants and to the products). For an elementary reaction the relevant geometric coordinate is the reaction coordinate ; for a stepwise reaction it is the succession of reaction coordinates for the successive individual reaction steps. (The reaction coordinate is sometimes approximated by a quasi-chemical index of reaction progress, such as 'degree of atom transfer' or bond order of some specified bond.)

P04788.title: potentiation
P04788.definition: Dependent action in which a substance or physical agent at a concentration or dose that does not itself have an adverse effect enhances the harm done by another substance or physical agent.

P04789.title: potentiometer
P04789.definition: In electronics, a sensitive voltage measuring device based on a null technique which provides infinite impedance at null.In chemistry, potentiometric methods involve the measurement with a potentiometer of voltage generated in a cell. A high impedance digital voltmeter is often used today as a convenient alternative to a potentiometer.

P04790.title: potentiometric detection method
P04790.definition: A detection method in which the potential of a cell is related to the concentration (activity) of a reactant which is a component of the cell fluid.

09122.title: potentiometric enzyme electrode
09122.definition: Enzyme-modified electrode, or an electrode modified by a substrate, cofactor or inhibitor, in which the activity of a product of the enzyme reaction is measured by an ion-selective electrode.

09123.title: potentiometric gas sensor
09123.definition: Ion-selective electrode cell that is responsive to an analyte gas.

P04791.title: potentiometric selectivity coefficient
P04791.definition: A coefficient which defines the ability of an ion-selective electrode to distinguish a particular ion from others. The selectivity coefficient, \(K_{\rm{A,B}}^{\rm{pot}}\), is evaluated by means of the emf response of the ion-selective electrode in mixed solutions of the primary ion, A, and interfering ion, B (fixed interference method) or less desirable, in separate solutions of A and B (separate solution method). The activities of the primary ion, A, and the interfering ion, B, at which \(K_{\rm{A,B}}^{\rm{pot}}\) is determined should always be specified, as the value of \(K_{\rm{A,B}}^{\rm{pot}}\) is defined by the modified Nikolsky–Eisenman equation. The smaller the value of \(K_{\rm{A,B}}^{\rm{pot}}\) the greater the electrode's preference for the principal ion, A. Comment: The terms selectivity constant and selectivity factor are frequently used instead of selectivity coefficient. However, in order to standardize the terminology associated with ion-selective electrodes, use of the term selectivity coefficient is recommended, as is the fixed interference method for its evaluation. This selectivity coefficient is not identical to the similar term used in separation science.

09154.title: potentiometric stripping analysis
09154.definition: Two-step electrochemical measurement in which 1) material is accumulated at an electrode and 2) the material is removed by chemical reaction or electrochemically at constant current with measurement of electrode potential. The time between changes in potential in step two is related to the concentration of analyte in the solution.

09047.title: potentiometric titration
09047.definition: Redox titration in which the course of the reaction is followed by potentiometry.

09127.title: potentiometry
09127.definition: Electrochemical measurement principle where the potential difference between an indicator electrode and a reference electrode is measured.

09079.title: potentiostat
09079.definition: Measuring instrument for electric current that controls the potential difference between a working electrode and a reference electrode and measures the electric current between a working electrode and an auxiliary electrode.

15227.title: powder
15227.definition: Dry solid material consisting of many, usually free flowing, fine particles. Conventionally, the title 'powder' should be restricted to powder mixes for internal use and alternative terms are used for other powdered formulations presented in this way, e.g., dusting powders, which are for external use.

15226.title: powder grades
15226.definition: Defined for powders used pharmaceutically, according to particle sizes.

08393.title: powder pattern
08393.definition: Very broad and distinctive line shape seen in a static solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment with a typical magnitude of \(\pu{E2}\) to \(\pu{E5 Hz}\).

12292.title: power compensation differential scanning calorimetry
12292.definition: Technique where the difference between the electrical powers into a sample and a reference material is measured.

P04793.title: power level
P04793.definition: Logarithm of the ratio of a power to a reference power. Levels are expressed in different ways: \(L_{P}=\frac{1}{2}\ \ln (\frac{P}{P_{0}})\ \mathrm{Np}\), where \(\mathrm{Np}\) is the symbol for the unit neper coherent with the SI, or \(L_{P}=10\ \log _{10}(\frac{P}{P_{0}})\ \mathrm{dB}\), where \(\mathrm{dB}\) is the symbol for the unit decibel.

14338.title: power-feed emulsion polymerisation
14338.definition: Semi-continuous emulsion copolymerization in which the instantaneous composition of the formed copolymer is the same as that of the added monomer mixture(s).

15347.title: Poynting correction
15347.definition: Factor used to convert experimentally determined Henry’s law constants at the saturation vapor pressure of the solvent \(\ce{A}\), \(p_{\ce{A}}^{\ast}\), to a reference pressure \(p\) \[\begin{array}{c} I_{\rm{p}} = \int_{p_{\ce{A}}^{\ast}}^p \frac{V_{\ce{B}}^{\infty {\rm{l}}}}{RT}{\rm{d}}p \\ k_{\rm{H},\ce{B}}(p) = k_{\rm{H},\ce{B}}(p^{\ast}) \exp \left[I_{\rm{p}}(p) \right]\end{array}\] is the partial molar volume of liquid \(\ce{B}\) at infinite dilution in solvent \(\ce{A}\). The second equation gives the relation between the two Henry’s law constants.

15999.title: practical certainty
15999.definition: Numerically specified low risk of exposure to a potentially toxic substance (e.g., 1 in \(\pu{1000}\)) or socially acceptable low risk of adverse effects from such an exposure applied to decision making in regard to chemical safety.

P04794.title: pre-association
P04794.definition: A step on the reaction path of some stepwise reactions in which the molecular entity C is already present in an encounter pair or encounter complex with A during the formation of B from A, e.g.  In this mechanism the chemical species C may but does not necessarily assist the formation of B from A, which may itself be a bimolecular reaction with some other reagent. Pre-association is important when B is too short-lived to permit B and C to come together by diffusion.

13595.title: pre-B cell
13595.definition: Cell in the B-lymphocyte lineage that has rearranged heavy chain but not light chain genes; it expresses surrogate light chains and \(\upmu\) heavy chain at its surface in conjunction with immunoglobulins Ig _012643_ and Ig _012644_. All these molecules comprise the pre-B-cell receptor (pre-BCR).

11114.title: pre-eclampsia
11114.definition: Pathological condition in pregnancy with symptoms of high blood pressure, kidney dysfunction and edema.

11115.title: pre-embryo
11115.definition: Fertilized ovum up to \(\pu{14 days}\) of age and before implantation.

P04809.title: pre-equilibrium
P04809.definition: Preliminary treatment of a solvent in order to convert the extractants into a suitable chemical form.Notes:The use of equilibration in this sense is confusing and should be avoided.The term conditioning may be used as a synonym for pre-equilibration.Preliminary treatment of either phase with a suitable solution of the other phase (in the absence of main extractable solute(s)) so that when the subsequent equilibration is carried out changes in the (volume) phase ratio or in the concentrations of other components are minimized.

P04810.title: pre-equilibrium
P04810.definition: A rapidly reversible step preceding the rate-limiting step in a stepwise reaction. For example:

P04811.title: pre-exponential factor
P04811.definition: Coefficient in front of the exponential factor expressing the empirical temperature dependence of the rate coefficient, \(k\), on temperature, \(T\), \(k=A\ \exp (- E_{\rm{a}}/R\ T)\), where \(E_{\rm{a}}\) is the activation energy.

P04813.title: pre-filter effect
P04813.definition: This effect arises when the luminescence detector does not see a portion of the luminescent volume where the excitation beam enters the sample. Thus the exciting beam flux is reduced by absorption by the analyte and interfering impurities before it enters the volume observed by the detection system.

PT07506.title: pre-gel regime
PT07506.definition: Stage of a network-forming polymerization or crosslinking process extending up to, but not beyond, the gel point.

PT07507.title: pre-gel state
PT07507.definition: State of a network-forming polymerization or crosslinking process in the pre-gel regime.

11117.title: pre-implantation
11117.definition: Occurring before the early embryo embeds in the lining of the uterus.

P04817.title: pre-polymer
P04817.definition: A polymer or oligomer composed of pre-polymer molecules.

P04818.title: pre-polymer molecule
P04818.definition: A macromolecule or oligomer molecule capable of entering, through reactive groups, into further polymerization, thereby contributing more than one monomeric unit to at least one chain of the final macromolecule. A pre-polymer molecule capable of entering into further polymerization through reactive end-groups, often deliberately introduced, is known as a telechelic molecule.

PT07091.title: pre-reactive complexes
PT07091.definition: Weakly bound complexes with a potential minimum that precedes the activation barrier along the reaction path. In contrast with the van der Waals complexes, which fall apart reversibly into their constituents, the pre-reactive complexes may undergo a vigorous reaction to form different products.

13598.title: pre-T cell
13598.definition: Cell differentiating into a T lymphocyte in the thymus gland.

14943.title: precautionary principle
14943.definition: Approach to risk management that can be applied in circumstances of scientific uncertainty, reflecting a perceived need to take action in the face of a potentially serious risk without waiting for definitive results of scientific research.

08394.title: precession
08394.definition: Classical description of the behaviour of nuclear magnetic moments, in which the vectors rotate about the \(\boldsymbol{B_{0}}\) axis at their Larmor angular frequencies.

13596.title: precipitating antibody
13596.definition: Antibody that is capable of reacting with a soluble antigen with the formation of an insoluble antigenantibody complex.

P04795.title: precipitation
P04795.definition: The sedimentation of a solid material (a precipitate) from a liquid solution in which the material is present in amounts greater than its solubility in the liquid.

P04796.title: precipitation fractionation
P04796.definition: A process in which a macromolecules material, consisting of macromolecules differing in some characteristic affecting their solubility, is separated from solution into fractions by successively decreasing the solution power of the solvent, resulting in the repeated formation of a two-phase system in which the less soluble components concentrate in the polymer-rich phase.

P04797.title: precipitation from homogeneous solution
P04797.definition: The formation of a precipitate which is generated homogeneously and, generally, slowly by a precipitating agent within a solution.

PT07627.title: precipitation
PT07627.definition: Sedimentation of a solid material (a precipitate) from a liquid solution in which the material is present in amounts greater than its solubility in the liquid.

09048.title: precipitation indicator
09048.definition: Visual indicator precipitated, with concomitant color change, by reaction with excess titrant at the end-point of a titration.

14347.title: precipitation polymerisation
14347.definition: Polymerization in which monomer(s), initiator(s) and colloid stabilizer(s) are dissolved in a solvent and this continuous phase that is a nonsolvent for the formed polymer beyond a critical molecular weight.

13597.title: precipitin
13597.definition: Precipitate of antibody and multivalent antigen due to the formation of high-molecular-weight complexes.

P04799.title: precision
P04799.definition: The closeness of agreement between independent test results obtained by applying the experimental procedure under stipulated conditions. The smaller the random part of the experimental errors which affect the results, the more precise the procedure. A measure of precision (or imprecision) is the standard deviation.

08096.title: precision limit
08096.definition: Quantity value, less than or equal to what the absolute difference between two measured quantity values obtained under specified conditions of measurement is expected to be with a given probability.

P04800.title: precision
P04800.definition: The standard deviation of the instrument for the stated load (e.g. \(l_{20}\) for a \(20\ \rm{g}\) load). A statement of the procedure, conditions, and experience of the observer should be included.

P04801.title: precision
P04801.definition: This depends upon the method of weighing and upon the precision of indication, \(l\), for the load in question.

P04802.title: precision of indication
P04802.definition: The standard deviation of the instrumental indication, \(i\), for a stated load.

12716.title: preclinical candidate
12716.definition: Optimised lead compound successfully passing key screening, selectivity, and physicochemical criteria sufficient to warrant further detailed pharmacological and pharmacokinetic evaluation in animal models.

P04804.title: preconcentration coefficient
P04804.definition: This is defined as \[K = \frac{Q_{\rm{T}}/Q_{\rm{M}}}{Q_{\rm{T}}^{\rm{o}}/Q_{\rm{M}}^{\rm{o}}}\] where \(Q_{\rm{T}}\) and \(Q_{\rm{T}}^{\rm{o}}\) are the quantities of the microcomponent in the concentrate and in the sample, respectively (mass units or concentration units), and \(Q_{\rm{M}}^{\rm{o}}\) and \(Q_{\rm{M}}\) and are the quantities of the matrix before and after preconcentration, respectively. If the recovery is 100%, \(K=\frac{Q_{\rm{M}}^{\rm{o}}}{Q_{\rm{M}}}\). The terms enrichment coefficient and enrichment factor are not recommended.

P04803.title: preconcentration
P04803.definition: An operation (process) as a result of which the ratio of the concentration or the amount of microcomponents (trace constituents) and macrocomponents (matrix) increases. The term enrichment is not recommended.

16000.title: precordial
16000.definition: Pertaining to the region over the heart and lower thorax.

P04806.title: precursor complex
P04806.definition: May either indicate an encounter complex or a collision complex, but furthermore implies that this complex undergoes a reaction (e.g. electron transfer).

P04805.title: precursor
P04805.definition: Of a nuclide, any radioactive nuclide which precedes that nuclide in a decay chain.

11113.title: predatory mite test
11113.definition: Procedure in which adult females of the predatory mite (_027814_ considered representative of soil fauna) are exposed to a test substance in artificial soil and the number of surviving females and of juveniles is determined.

14944.title: predicted environmental concentration
14944.definition: Concentration of a substance likely to be found in an environmental compartment calculated from estimates of quantities released, discharge patterns, and inherent disposition of the substance (fate and distribution) as well as the nature of the specific receiving ecosystems.

14945.title: predicted no-effect concentration
14945.definition: Concentration that is expected to cause no adverse effect to any naturally occurring population in an environment at risk from exposure to a given substance.

10104.title: prediction error sum of squares
10104.definition: In multivariate calibration for a prediction set of \(N\) data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the predicted value. \[E_{\rm{PRESS}} = \sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i} - c_{i})^2\]

11493.title: prediction set
11493.definition: Molecules that have been set aside from model development to test the reliability of the derived model.

14946.title: predictive risk assessment
14946.definition: Risk assessment performed for a proposed future action, such as the use of a new chemical or the release of a new effluent.

16001.title: predictive validity
16001.definition: Reliability of a measurement expressed in terms of its ability to predict the criterion.

16002.title: predictive value
16002.definition: Percentage of positive results that are true positives or of negative results that are true negatives.

P04808.title: predissociation
P04808.definition: Dissociation occurring by tunnelling from a 'bound' to an 'unbound' vibronic state. In an absorption spectrum of a molecular entity, the appearance of a diffuse band region within a series of sharp bands is called predissociation, since irradiation with frequencies within the diffuse region leads to effective dissociation. The energy of the band is smaller than that of the dissociation continuum of the bound state.

P04812.title: preferential sorption
P04812.definition: An equilibrium phenomenon, operative in polymer solutions in multicomponent solvents and in polymer networks swollen by multicomponent solvents, that produces differences in solvent composition in the polymer-containing region and in the pure solvent which is in thermodynamic equilibrium with that region. Synonymous with selective sorption.

09269.title: preferential sputtering
09269.definition: Change in equilibrium surface composition of the sample, which can occur when sputtering multicomponent samples.

09016.title: preferred constitutional repeating unit
09016.definition: Constitutional repeating unit (CRU) written with the subunits in a linear series from the highest (higher) seniority to the lowest (lower) or as close as possible by the shortest path.

15228.title: preformulation
15228.definition: Exploratory activity that begins early in pharmaceutics, involving studies designed to determine the compatibility of excipients with the active substance for a biopharmaceutical; physicochemical and bioanalytical investigation in support of promising experimental formulations.

11116.title: pregnancy
11116.definition: State of a female between conception and the termination of gestation.

08528.title: preheating inductively-coupled plasma zone
08528.definition: Inductively-coupled plasma volume where tertiary aerosols suffer from complete solvent evaporation, element salt vaporization and dissociation into atoms.

11118.title: premature birth
11118.definition: Delivery before the expected length of gestation for the species; in humans taken as birth before a gestational age of \(\pu{37 weeks}\).

16003.title: premature ovarian failure
16003.definition: Follicular depletion by the age of 35 years.

P04814.title: premium coke
P04814.definition: An extremely well graphitizing carbon with a high degree of optical anisotropy (isochromatic areas of optical texture above about \(100\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\)) and which is characterized by a combination of the following properties which differ significantly from those of regular coke: high real density, low reversible thermal expansion and low ash content combined, in most cases, with low sulfur content.

P04815.title: premix burner
P04815.definition: A burner in which fuel and oxidant are thoroughly mixed inside the burner housing before they leave the burner ports and enter the primary-combustion or inner zone of the flame. This type of burner usually produces an approximately laminar flame, and is commonly combined with a separate unit for nebulizing the sample.

11119.title: prenatal
11119.definition: Referring to events in the life of the mother or fetus preceding birth.

11120.title: prenatal development study
11120.definition: Procedure in which a substance is administered to pregnant animals (usually rodents or rabbits) from the time of implantation until closure of the hard palate. The animals are killed one to two days before a scheduled delivery, whereupon uterine contents and the fetuses are evaluated for abnormalities.

16004.title: preneoplastic
16004.definition: Before the formation of a tumor.

09855.title: prenol lipids
09855.definition: Lipids containing a linear chain of isoprenoid groups.

P04816.title: prenols
P04816.definition: Alcohols possessing the general formula $\ce{H–[CH2C(Me)=CHCH2]_{n}OH}$ in which the carbon skeleton is composed of one or more isoprene units (biogenetic precursors of the isoprenoids).

11121.title: preoptic area
11121.definition: Region of the anterior hypothalamus primarily involved in regulating body temperature.

PT07163.title: prepolymer
PT07163.definition: Polymer or oligomer the molecules of which are capable of entering, through reactive groups, into further polymerization and thereby contributing more than one structural unit to at least one type of chain of the final polymer.

PT07247.title: prepreg
PT07247.definition: Sheets of a substrate that have been impregnated with a curable polymer, curable polymers, or liquid reactants, or a thermoplastic, and are ready for fabrication of laminates.

11122.title: prepubertal
11122.definition: Stage of human development before the onset of puberty.

11124.title: prepuce
11124.definition: Skin protecting the glans penis in the male (foreskin) or the clitoris in the female (clitoral hood).

11125.title: preputial separation
11125.definition: Separation of the prepuce from the glans penis.

08395.title: presaturation
08395.definition: Technique to suppress a particular nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy signal where a long low-power pulse is applied to that specific resonance prior to the main pulse sequence.

11705.title: presenile dementia
11705.definition: Dementia, often of the Alzheimer type (see Alzheimer disease) developing at or before age 65.

08663.title: pressure broadening
08663.definition: Increase in the line width of a spectral line of a gas due to molecular collisions and other intermolecular interactions that reduce the lifetime of an excited state.

P04821.title: pressure gradient correction factor
P04821.definition: A factor that corrects for the compressibility of the carrier gas. The values of the measured quantities obtained after multiplication by the factor \(j\) are independent of the pressure drop in the column. If \(p_{\rm{i}}\), \(p_{\rm{o}}\) are respectively the pressures of the carrier gas at the inlet and outlet of the column, then \(j\) is given by: \[j=\frac{3\ [(\frac{p_{\rm{i}}}{p_{\rm{o}}})^{2}- 1]}{2\ [(\frac{p_{\rm{i}}}{p_{\rm{o}}})^{3}- 1]}\]

P04822.title: pressure-induced transition
P04822.definition: A transition induced by a change of pressure. Example: The room-temperature transition of $\ce{CdS}$ with a wurtzite-type structure, at \(1.74\ \rm{GPa}\), to $\ce{CdS}$ with a $\ce{NaCl}$-type structure.

P04824.title: pressure-sensitive detector
P04824.definition: A detector which employs the pressure change which results from the absorption of radiation.

P04819.title: pressure
P04819.definition: Normal force acting on a surface divided by the area of that surface. For a mixture of gases the contribution by each constituent is called the 'partial pressure' \(p_{i} = x_{i} p\), where \(x_{i}\) is the amount fraction of the \(i\)th constituent and \(p\) is the total pressure.

10226.title: pressurized hot-water extraction
10226.definition: Extraction by water below its critical point (\(\pu{374.15^{\circ}C}\) and \(\pu{22.064 MPa}\)).

10227.title: pressurized-liquid extraction
10227.definition: Leaching performed at elevated temperature and pressure.Schematic diagram of a typical apparatus for pressurized-liquid extraction. Gas flow is used to displace the extraction solvent from the sample chamber.

12018.title: presynaptic
12018.definition: Event or structure at the proximal (transmitting) side of a synaptic cleft.

P04826.title: pretreatment
P04826.definition: Following the preparation of a catalyst or following its insertion into a catalytic reactor, it is often subjected to various treatments before the start of a catalytic run. The term pretreatment may, in general, be applied to this set of treatments. In some cases the word activation is used. It implies that the material is converted into a catalyst or into a very much more effective one by the pretreatment.

14947.title: prevalence
14947.definition: Number of instances of existing cases of a given disease or other condition in a given population at a designated time; sometimes used to mean prevalence rate.

14948.title: prevalence rate
14948.definition: Total number of individuals who have an attribute or disease at a particular time (or during a particular period) divided by the population at risk of having the attribute or disease at this point in time or midway through the period.

13599.title: prick test
13599.definition: Test carried out by placing a drop of a suspected allergenic extract on the skin of the forearm and gently pricking it into the upper layer of skin. Sensitivity to a substance is indicated if the spot swells slightly and becomes red within about \(\pu{15 min}\).

P04840.title: primary photoproduct
P04840.definition: The first observable chemical entity which is produced in the primary photochemical process and which is chemically different from the reactant.

09270.title: primary beam
09270.definition: Directed flux of beam particles or photons incident on a sample.

13600.title: primary biliary cirrhosis
13600.definition: Autoimmune liver disease that results in the destruction of bile ducts, leading to fibrosis and cirrhosis.

P04827.title: primary crystallization
P04827.definition: The first stage of crystallization, considered to be ended when most of the spherulite surfaces impinge on each other. In isothermal crystallization, primary crystallization is often described by the Avrami equation.

15348.title: primary data
15348.definition: Data reported in peer-reviewed scientific reports of original research which allow an assessment of data quality.

P04829.title: primary electrons
P04829.definition: Electrons generated by a thermal or field emission source used to bombard the specimen for generation of the analytical signals.

10026.title: primary examination standard
10026.definition: Examination standard established using a primary reference examination procedure, or created as an artefact, chosen by convention.

13601.title: primary immune response
13601.definition: Immune response to the first encounter with an antigen, characterized by slow production of antibody molecules and the priming of lymphoid tissue in readiness for the production of a secondary immune response on subsequent challenge with the same antigen.

13602.title: primary immunization
13602.definition: First introduction of a vaccine into the body for the purposes of inducing immunity.

09414.title: primary ion
09414.definition: Ion extracted from a source and directed at a sample.

P04831.title: primary isotope effect
P04831.definition: A kinetic isotope effect attributable to isotopic substitution of an atom to which a bond is made or broken in the rate-controlling step or in a pre-equilibrium step of a specified reaction. The corresponding isotope effect on the equilibrium constant of a reaction in which one or more bonds to isotopic atoms are broken, is called a 'primary equilibrium isotope effect'.

14949.title: primary lamellae
14949.definition: Gill structures extending outward at right angles from the branchial arches.

13603.title: primary lymphoid follicle
13603.definition: Region of a secondary lymphoid organ containing predominantly unstimulated B lymphocytes that develops into a germinal center following antigen stimulation.

13604.title: primary lymphoid organ
13604.definition: Site at which immunocompetent lymphocytes develop, i.e., bone marrow and thymus in mammals.

09806.title: primary metabolite
09806.definition: Metabolite directly involved in the normal life processes of each cell.

P04834.title: primary mixture
P04834.definition: A mixture obtained directly from two or more components intended for the preparation of more dilute calibration mixtures (called secondary or tertiary mixtures).

13605.title: primary myxedema
13605.definition: Atrophic form of diffuse autoimmune thyroiditis.

11041.title: primary oocyte
11041.definition: Oocyte during growth phase before completion of the first meiotic division.

P04837.title: primary pH standards
P04837.definition: Certain substances which meet the criteria of:   reproducible preparation in a highly pure state;   stability of solution over a reasonable period of time;   having a low value of the residual liquid junction potential;   having pH betwen 3 and 11.

P04836.title: primary photochemical process
P04836.definition: Any elementary chemical process undergone by an electronically excited molecular entity and yielding a primary photoproduct.

P04838.title: primary pollutant
P04838.definition: A pollutant emitted directly into the air from identifiable sources (e.g. $\ce{SO2}$, $\ce{NO}$, hydrocarbons, etc.). Secondary pollutants, such as ozone, are generated within the atmosphere through chemical changes which occur in primary pollutants.

14950.title: primary producer
14950.definition: Organism capable of using the energy derived from light or a chemical substance in order to manufacture energy-rich organic compounds.

16006.title: primary protection standard
16006.definition: Accepted maximum level of a pollutant (or its indicator) in the target organism, or some part thereof, or an accepted maximum intake of a pollutant or nuisance into the target under specified circumstances.

14375.title: primary radical
14375.definition: Radicals formed from an initiator molecule.

10023.title: primary reference examination procedure
10023.definition: Reference examination procedure used to obtain an examination result without relation to an examination standard for a nominal property of the same kind-of-nominal-property.

P04841.title: primary sample
P04841.definition: The collection of one or more increments or units initially taken from a population. The portions may be either combined (composited or bulked sample) or kept separate (gross sample). If combined and mixed to homogeneity, it is a blended bulk sample. The term 'bulk sample' is commonly used in the sampling literature as the sample formed by combining increments. The term is ambiguous since it could also mean a sample from a bulk lot and it does not indicate whether the increments or units are kept separate or combined. Such use should be discouraged because less ambiguous alternative terms (composite sample, aggregate sample) are available. 'Lot sample' and 'batch sample' have also been used for this concept, but they are self limiting terms. The use of 'primary' in this sense is not meant to imply the necessity for multistage sampling.

13606.title: primary sclerosing cholangitis
13606.definition: Chronic, non-bacterial, inflammatory narrowing of the bile ducts.

14184.title: primary screen
14184.definition: Initial screen applied to assess the activity of a collection of compounds and identify hits or actives against a biological target of interest.

11126.title: primary sex organ
11126.definition: Gonads, which form gametes; ovaries in the female and testes in the male.

08965.title: primary species
08965.definition: Species that is formed from an initiator or monomer molecule and that is capable of initiating polymerization.

P04843.title: primary structure
P04843.definition: In the context of macromolecules such as proteins, constitutional formula, usually abbreviated to a statement of the sequence and if appropriate cross-linking of chains.

P04844.title: primary structure
P04844.definition: The amino acid sequence of the polypeptide chain(s), without regard to spatial arrangement (apart from configuration at the $\ce{\upalpha\mbox{-}carbon atom}$).

14951.title: primary succession
14951.definition: Sequential colonization by species which begin to colonize the bare ground and modify the environmental conditions after a region is completely denuded; e.g., behind a retreating glacier, early colonizing organisms provide the soils needed by succeeding organisms.

15414.title: primary-radical termination
15414.definition: Termination reaction involving a radical chain carrier and a primary radical.

13607.title: prime
13607.definition: Process of giving an initial sensitization to antigen.

09716.title: primer
09716.definition: Short pre-existing polynucleotide chain attached to a complementary stretch in template deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to which new deoxyribonucleotides can be added by DNA polymerase.

11127.title: primitive axis
11127.definition: Thickening of the embryonic tissue extending forward from the primitive streak.

12271.title: primitive chain
12271.definition: Polymer chain allowed to undergo reptation along the tube created by neighbouring chains.

P04845.title: primitive change
P04845.definition: One of the conceptually simpler molecular changes into which an elementary reaction can be notionally dissected. Such changes include bond rupture, bond formation, internal rotation, change of bond length or bond angle, bond migration, redistribution of charge, etc. The concept of primitive changes is helpful in the detailed verbal description of elementary reactions, but a primitive change does not represent a process that is by itself necessarily observable as a component of an elementary reaction.

11128.title: primitive groove
11128.definition: Shallow depression in the primitive streak that extends anteriorly to communicate with the yolk sac.

11129.title: primitive node
11129.definition: Group of cells at the anterior end of the primitive streak, involved in secreting chemical signals that regulate differentiation of the germ layers during gastrulation.

11130.title: primitive pit
11130.definition: Depression in the primitive node contiguous with the notochord.

11131.title: primitive streak
11131.definition: Structure forming in the blastula during early embryogenesis that establishes bilateral symmetry and determines the site of gastrulation and germ layer formation.

11132.title: primordial follicle
11132.definition: Early stage of the oocyte in which it is surrounded by a single layer of follicular cells.

11133.title: primordial germ cell
11133.definition: Germ cell in the earliest stages of development.

11134.title: primordium
11134.definition: Organ or tissue at its earliest recognizable stage of development.

11494.title: principal component loading
11494.definition: The contribution, scaled between \(\pu{-1.0}\) and \(\pu{1.0}\), of an original variable to a particular principal component.

11495.title: principal component score
11495.definition: A property of a molecule calculated from a principal components analysis of the original properties and the value of these properties for the molecule.

10105.title: principal component-discriminant analysis
10105.definition: Discriminant analysis on a multivariate data set that has been subject to principal-component analysis.

10156.title: principal components regression
10156.definition: Multivariate calibration in which a dependent variable is regressed against the scores of a chosen number of factors obtained from principal-component analysis of the predictor variable.

P04846.title: principal group
P04846.definition: The characteristic group chosen for citation at the end of a name by a suffix or a class name.

P04847.title: principal ion
P04847.definition: A molecular or fragment ion which is made up of the most abundant isotopes of each of its atomic constituents. In the case of compounds that have been artifically isotopically enriched in one or more positions such as $\ce{CH3^{13}CH3}$ or $\ce{CH2D2}$ the principal ion may be defined by treating the heavy isotopes as new atomic species. Thus, in the above two examples, the principal ions would be of masses 31 and 18, respectively.

P04848.title: principal moments of inertia
P04848.definition: Moments of inertia about the principal axes of the molecule chosen so as to make all the products of inertia equal to zero, \(I_{A}\leq I_{B}\leq I_{C}\).

10106.title: principal-component analysis
10106.definition: Factor analysis in which factors are calculated that successively capture the greatest variance in the data set.

10107.title: principal-component factor
10107.definition: Orthogonal factors obtained in a principal-component analysis.

14952.title: principle of allocation
14952.definition: Concept that there exists a cost or trade-off to every allocation of energy resources. Energy spent by an individual organism on one function, process, or structure cannot be spent on another. Optimal allocation of resources enhances Darwinian fitness.

P04849.title: principle of least nuclear motion
P04849.definition: The hypothesis that, for given reactants, the reactions involving the smallest change in nuclear positions will have the lowest energy of activation. (It is also often simply referred to as principle of least motion.)

P04850.title: principle of microscopic reversibility
P04850.definition: In a reversible reaction, the mechanism in one direction is exactly the reverse of the mechanism in the other direction. This does not apply to reactions that begin with a photochemical excitation.

P04852.title: prior distribution
P04852.definition: A product state distribution calculated on the basis of some physical model for the reaction. The distribution usually referred to is that of the products at the instant of their formation.

16005.title: prior informed consent
16005.definition: Concept in law and medicine that states that before one is subjected to a risk, especially a risk of bodily harm, one is entitled to be fully informed well in advance of the nature of that risk in order to make an informed decision about whether to accept it or not.

11496.title: prior probability
11496.definition:
The conditional probability that is assigned to a quantity before relevant evidence is taken into account, for example, the prior probability of an active
 compound would be the fraction of the compounds in the dataset that are active.

12717.title: privileged structure
12717.definition: Substructural feature that confers desirable (often drug-like) properties on compounds containing that feature. They often consist of a semi-rigid scaffold that presents multiple hydrophobic residues without undergoing hydrophobic collapse.

P04867.title: pro-E, pro-Z
P04867.definition: One of a pair of identical groups $\ce{c}$ attached to a double bond (as in $\ce{abC=Cc2}$) is described as pro-E if, when it is arbitrarily assigned CIP priority over the other group c, the stereodescriptor of the molecule becomes E. The other group $\ce{c}$ is then described as pro-Z.

16010.title: pro-pesticide
16010.definition: Substance applied in a form that is not active as a pesticide and which becomes active once it enters an organism and undergoes chemical modification.

P04889.title: pro-R, pro-S
P04889.definition: A stereoheterotopic group $\ce{c}$ (as in tetrahedral $\ce{Xabc2}$) is described as pro-R if, when it is arbitrarily assigned CIP priority over the other stereoheterotopic group $\ce{c}$, the configuration of the thus generated chiral centre is assigned the stereodescriptor R. The other group $\ce{c}$ is then described as pro-S. This method for distinguishing between stereoheterotopic groups can be applied to other kinds of prochiral molecular entities or prochiral parts of molecular entities considered on their own.

P04856.title: probability density
P04856.definition: Product of the wave function and its complex conjugate.

P04855.title: probability
P04855.definition: Number of favourable events divided by the total number of possible events. It is a number between 0 and 1.

P04857.title: probe
P04857.definition: A specific DNA or RNA sequence which has been labelled by radioactivity, fluorescence labels or chemiluminescence labels and which is used to detect complementary sequences by hybridization techniques such as blotting or colony hybridization.

09378.title: probe ion
09378.definition: Ion intentionally produced by an ion source and directed onto the sample surface at a known angle of incidence and a known energy.

14953.title: probit
14953.definition: Probability unit obtained by adding 5 to the normal deviates of a standardized normal distribution of results from a dose-response study.

14954.title: probit log transform
14954.definition: Probability unit obtained from the standardized normal distribution plotted against the logarithm of the concentration or dose of a substance when a quantal or graded response has been measured. A linear plot provides evidence that the distribution is log-normal. Estimates of the \(\pu{L(E)C_{50}}\) and \(\pu{L(E)D_{50}}\), as well as the standard deviation for the distribution, can then be made.

14955.title: problem formulation
14955.definition: Planning and scoping phase that establishes the framework around which the risk assessment is done.

16007.title: procarcinogen
16007.definition: Substance that has to be metabolized before it becomes a carcinogen.

08097.title: procedure validation
08097.definition: Process of defining an analytical requirement and confirming that the procedure under consideration has capabilities consistent with that requirement.

08098.title: procedure verification
08098.definition: Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that the procedure fulfils specified requirements.

P04858.title: process
P04858.definition: A phenomenon by which change takes place in a system. In physiological systems, a process may be chemical, physical or both.

08099.title: process in a state of statistical control
08099.definition: Process subject only to random causes.

P04859.title: prochirality
P04859.definition: This term is used in different, sometimes contradictory ways; four are listed below.The geometric property of an achiral object (or spatial arrangement of points or atoms) which is capable of becoming chiral in a single desymmetrization step. An achiral molecular entity, or a part of it considered on its own, is thus called prochiral if it can be made chiral by the replacement of an existing atom (or achiral group) by a different one. An achiral object which is capable of becoming chiral in two desymmetrization steps is sometimes described as proprochiral. For example the proprochiral $\ce{CH3CO2H}$ becomes prochiral as $\ce{CH2DCO2H}$ and chiral as $\ce{CHDTCO2H}$.The term prochirality also applies to an achiral molecule or entity which contains a trigonal system and which can be made chiral by the addition to the trigonal system of a new atom or achiral group. For example addition of hydrogen to one of the enantiotopic faces of the prochiral ketone $\ce{CH3CH2COCH3}$ gives one of the enantiomers of the chiral alcohol $\ce{CH3CH2CHOHCH3}$; the addition of $\ce{CN^{−}}$ to one of the diastereotopic faces of the chiral aldehyde shown below converts it into one of the diastereoisomers of the cyanohydrin. The two faces of the trigonal system may be described as Re and Si. The term prochiral also applies to a tetrahedral atom of an achiral or chiral molecule which is bonded to two stereoheterotopic groups. For example, the prochiral molecule $\ce{CH3CH2OH}$ can be converted into the chiral molecule $\ce{CH3CHDOH}$ by the isotopic replacement of one of the two enantiotopic hydrogen atoms of the methylene group. The carbon atom of the methylene group is called prochiral. The prochiral molecule $\ce{HO2CCH2CHOHCH2CO2H}$ can be converted into a chiral product by esterification of one of the two enantiotopic $\ce{–CH2CO2H}$ groups. The carbon atom of the $\ce{CHOH}$ group is called prochiral. The chiral molecule $\ce{CH3CHOHCH2CH3}$ can be converted into one of the diastereoisomers of $\ce{CH3CHOHCHDCH3}$ by the isotopic replacement of one of the two diastereotopic hydrogen atoms of the methylene group. The carbon atom of the methylene group is called prochiral. The stereoheterotopic groups in these cases may be described as pro-R or pro-S. Reference to the two stereoheterotopic groups themselves as prochiral, although common, is strongly discouraged.See: chirality centreThe term prochirality is also applied to the enantiotopic faces of a trigonal system.

P04860.title: prochirality centre
P04860.definition: An atom of a molecule which becomes a chirality centre by replacing one of the two stereoheterotopic ligands attached to it by a different ligand, e.g. C-1 of ethanol; C-3 of butan-2-ol.

10108.title: Procrustes analysis
