10108.definition: Comparison of shapes of multi-dimensional objects by a series of geometrical transformations to minimise the sum of squared distances between the transformed and target structures while maintaining the internal structure of the objects.

11135.title: proctodeum
11135.definition: Ectodermal depression of the caudal end of the embryo, where later the anus is formed.

12019.title: prodromal stage
12019.definition: Phase before the onset of full-blown disease.

12020.title: prodrome
12020.definition: Symptom(s) heralding impending onset of a disease.

09030.title: prodrug conjugate
09030.definition: Conjugate in which at least one conjugation includes a bioactive active species to be released by cleavage of the link where its action is desired.

P04861.title: product
P04861.definition: A substance that is formed during a chemical reaction.

P04863.title: product development control
P04863.definition: The term is used for reactions under kinetic control where the selectivity parallels the relative (thermodynamic) stabilities of the products. Product development control is usually associated with a transition state occurring late on the reaction coordinate.

P04866.title: product state distribution
P04866.definition: The distribution of available energy among the vibrational, rotational and translation degrees of freedom in the product molecules. The distribution usually referred to is that of the products at the instant of their formation.

P04862.title: product-determining step
P04862.definition: The step of a stepwise reaction in which the product distribution is determined. The product-determining step may be identical to, or occur later than, the rate-controlling step on the reaction coordinate.

14956.title: product-limit method
14956.definition: Nonparametric method for analyzing time-to-death or survival-time data that does not require a specific model for the survival curve.

P04865.title: productivity
P04865.definition: An economical figure denoting the mass of a product formed per unit reactor volume and unit time. Productivity is often referred to per unit of enzyme or biomass.

13608.title: professional antigen-presenting cell
13608.definition: Highly efficient antigen-presenting cell (APC), generally referring to dendritic cells, B cells, or macrophages.

08100.title: proficiency test item
08100.definition: Sample, product, artefact, reference material, piece of equipment, measurement standard, data set, or other information used for proficiency testing.

08101.title: proficiency testing
08101.definition: Evaluation of the performance of a participant in an interlaboratory comparison against pre-established criteria.

08102.title: proficiency testing provider
08102.definition: Organization which takes responsibility for all tasks in the development and operation of a proficiency testing scheme.

08103.title: proficiency testing round
08103.definition: Single complete sequence from distribution of proficiency test items to reporting of the evaluation results to the participants.

08104.title: proficiency testing scheme
08104.definition: Proficiency testing designed and operated in one or more proficiency testing rounds for a specified area of testing, measurement, calibration, or inspection.

12021.title: profile of mood state test
12021.definition: Procedure in which a test subject is asked to indicate his/her mood during the past week, by quickly marking specified emotional words on a scale between 'not at all' and 'extremely.'

P04868.title: progenitor ion
P04868.definition: Synonymous with precursor ion  in mass spectrometry.

11136.title: progesterone
11136.definition: Steroidal hormone produced in the ovary by the corpus luteum.

11137.title: progestin
11137.definition: Synthetic variant of progesterone, often used in oral contraceptive pills or to suppress hyperplasia of the endometrium.

11138.title: progestogen
11138.definition: Member of a family of hormones, based on the 21-carbon pregnane skeleton, involved in maintaining gestation and regulating the ovarian cycle.

P04869.title: program
P04869.definition: Noun: A set of instructions enabling a device to perform an action. Verb: To provide a set of instructions enabling a device to perform an action.

10313.title: programmable flow extraction
10313.definition: Multi-bidirectional flow (including stopped flow) of sample and/or extractant through an extraction device controlled by a pump.

P04870.title: programmed-flow chromatography
P04870.definition: A procedure in which the rate of flow of the mobile phase is changed systematically during a part or whole of the separation.

P04871.title: programmed-pressure chromatography
P04871.definition: A procedure in which the inlet pressure of the mobile phase is changed systematically during a part or whole of the separation.

P04872.title: programmed-temperature chromatography
P04872.definition: A procedure in which the temperature of the column is changed systematically during a part or the whole of the separation.

16008.title: progression
16008.definition: Increase in the size of a tumor or spread of cancer in the body.

13609.title: progressive systemic sclerosis
13609.definition: Systemic autoimmune disease marked by formation of hyalinized and thickened collagenous fibrous tissue, with thickening and adhesion of skin to underlying tissues, especially of the hands and face and vascular alterations.

13610.title: proinflammatory cytokine
13610.definition: Cytokine that initiates or enhances inflammation.

09271.title: projected range
09271.definition: Distance from the surface at which an energetic ion or atom comes to rest in the sample, projected along the direction of the beam.

P04873.title: projection formula
P04873.definition: A formal two-dimensional representation of a three-dimensional molecular structure obtained by projection of bonds (symbolized as lines) onto a plane with or without the designation of the positions of relevant atoms by their chemical symbols. A projection formula which indicates the spatial arrangement of bonds is called a stereochemical formula or stereoformula. Examples of stereoformulae are Fischer projection, Newman projection, sawhorse projection, wedge projection and zig-zag projection.

16009.title: prokaryote
16009.definition: Unicellular organism, characterized by the absence of a membrane-enclosed nucleus.

11139.title: prolactin
11139.definition: Hormone released from the anterior pituitary gland that stimulates milk production after childbirth.

11140.title: prolapse
11140.definition: Falling or slipping out of place of an organ or other body part.

P04874.title: prolate trochoidal mass spectrometer
P04874.definition: A mass spectrometer in which ions of different mass/charge are separated by means of crossed electric and magnetic fields in such a way that the selected ions follow a prolate trochoidal path. The usual term 'cycloidal' used sometimes is incorrect because the path used is not cycloidal. A cycloid is a special case of a trochoid.

14957.title: proliferation
14957.definition: Multiplication, i.e., an increase by frequent and repeated reproduction or growth by cell division.

13611.title: proliferation assay
13611.definition: Any test that determines the effect on increase in cell number of a test agent such as a cytokine or mitogen.

P04875.title: promoter
P04875.definition: The DNA region, usually upsteam to the coding sequence of a gene or operon, which binds and directs RNA polymerase to the correct transcriptional start site and thus permits the initation of transcription.

P04876.title: promoter
P04876.definition: A relatively small quantity of one or more substances, which when added to a catalyst improves the activity, the selectivity, or the useful lifetime of the catalyst. In general, a promoter may either augment a desired reaction or suppress an undesired one.

P04878.title: prompt coincidence
P04878.definition: The occurrence of two or more events separated by a time interval which is less than a specified small value.

08753.title: prompt gamma radiation
08753.definition: Gamma radiation emitted during the de-excitation of a compound nucleus formed in a nuclear capture reaction.

08754.title: prompt gamma-ray analysis
08754.definition: Measurement principle in which gamma radiation emitted during the de-excitation of the compound nucleus formed by neutron capture is applied to measure the amounts of elements in a material.

P04879.title: prompt neutrons
P04879.definition: Neutrons accompanying the fission process without measurable delay.

11141.title: pronephros
11141.definition: Collection of cells in the vertebrate embryo that represent the earliest stage of development of the kidney.

11142.title: pronucleus
11142.definition: Haploid nucleus formed by either the head of the sperm or the nucleus of the oocyte after fertilization but before their nuclei fuse to form the diploid zygotic nucleus.

12718.title: proof of concept
12718.definition: Procedure by which a specific therapeutic mechanism or treatment/diagnostic paradigm is shown to be beneficial.

08966.title: propagating species
08966.definition: Active species formed by addition to monomer that is capable of adding further monomer.

14958.title: propagule
14958.definition:
Portion of a plant, fungus, etc., that is capable, when detached, of giving rise to a new individual by asexual reproduction (e.g., a cutting, leaf bud, bulbil, seed, or spore).
Less commonly, any of the products of asexual reproduction in certain invertebrates.

14959.title: propagule rain
14959.definition: Relative to metapopulation dynamics, the presence of a seed bank or dormant stage for a species that continually introduces individuals to the patch regardless of the density of occupancy in the surrounding patches. This propagule rain increases the likelihood of population reappearance and decreases the likelihood of patch extinction.

P04882.title: propellanes
P04882.definition: Tricyclic saturated hydrocarbons, systematically named tricyclo[a.b.c.01,(a+2)]alkanes; have been referred to as [a.b.c]propellanes.

13612.title: properdin
13612.definition: Relatively heat-labile, normal serum protein (a euglobulin) that, in the presence of complement component C3 and magnesium ions, is involved in the alternative pathway of complement activation, and acts nonspecifically against Gram-negative bacteria and viruses and may contribute to the lysis of erythrocytes.

P04883.title: property
P04883.definition: A set of data elements (system, component, kind-of-property) common to a set of particular properties, e.g. substance concentration of glucose in blood plasma. Information about identification, time and result is not considered.

08038.title: property value assignment
08038.definition: Determination of property values obtained in the course of the production of a reference material.

P04884.title: prophage
P04884.definition: The latent state of a phage genome in a lysogenic bacterium.

11143.title: prophase
11143.definition: First phase of meiosis or mitosis in which thickening and orientation of the chromosomes occurs.

P04885.title: proportional counter
P04885.definition: A gas-filled X-ray detector in which the electric potential is high enough for the gain to reach a value in the range from \(10^{2}\) to \(10^{5}\). Each electron produced by the initial photo-ionization causes one avalanche. Since the number of avalanche events is proportional to the energy of the incident photons, the charge collected by the anode is proportional to the X-ray photon energy.

P04886.title: proportional counter tube
P04886.definition: A counter tube operated under such conditions that the magnitude of each pulse is proportional to the amount of energy deposited in it.

P04887.title: proportional gas-scintillation counter
P04887.definition: A proportional counter coupled to an ultraviolet sensitive photomultiplier tube. Initial electrons produced by the interaction of the high-energy photon with the counter fill-gas are accelerated by a high electric field where they acquire sufficient energy to excite the noble gas atoms. The resulting UV radiation is observed by a photomultiplier tube.

16011.title: proportional mortality rate
16011.definition: Proportion of observed deaths from a specified condition in a defined population divided by the proportion of deaths expected from this condition in a standard population, expressed either on an age-specific basis or after age adjustment.

12022.title: proprioception
12022.definition: Sense of the movement or position of the body independent of vision.

12023.title: proprioceptor
12023.definition: Sensory organ in a muscle, tendon or joint capsule that senses position or state of contraction.

P04890.title: pros
P04890.definition: The nitrogen atoms of the imidazole ring of histidine are denoted by pros ('near', abbreviated $\ce{\uppi\!}$) and tele ('far', abbreviated $\ce{\uptau\!}$) to show their position relative to the side chain. This recommendation arose from the fact that two different systems of numbering the atoms in the imidazole ring of histidine had both been used for a considerable time (biochemists generally numbering as 1 the nitrogen atom adjacent to the side chain, and organic chemists designating it as 3). The carbon atom between the two ring nitrogen atoms is numbered 2 (as in imidazole), and the carbon atom next to the $\ce{\uptau\!}$ nitrogen is numbered 5. The carbon atoms of the aliphatic chain are designated $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ and $\ce{\upbeta\!}$. This numbering should also be used for the decarboxylation product histamine and for substituted histidine.

11144.title: prosencephalon
11144.definition: Most forward part of the brain that includes most of the cerebral cortex, the thalamus and hypothalamus, and the basal ganglia.

P04891.title: prostaglandins
P04891.definition: Naturally occurring compounds derived from the parent $\ce{C20}$ acid, prostanoic acid.

P04892.title: prostanoids
P04892.definition: The family of natural prostaglandins and prostaglandin-like compounds.

11145.title: prostate
11145.definition: Male exocrine gland whose secretion contributes alkaline fluid to the ejaculate (see ejaculation).

P04893.title: prosthetic group
P04893.definition: The non-amino acid portion of a conjugated protein. Examples include cofactors such as flavines or cytochromes as well as lipids and polysaccharides, which are the prosthetic groups of lipoproteins and glycoproteins, respectively.

11146.title: protamine
11146.definition: Small, basic (arginine-rich) protein involved in sperm maturation and DNA packaging during spermatogenesis.

P04894.title: proteases
P04894.definition: Enzymes that catalyse the hydrolysis of proteins. Usually several proteolytic enzymes are necessary for the complete breakdown of polypeptides to their amino acids.

13613.title: proteasome
13613.definition: Cytoplasmic and nuclear multiprotein proteolytic complex involved in degradation of excess, damaged, or misfolded proteins.

P04895.title: protected lyophobic colloid
P04895.definition: A colloidally stable mixture of a lyophobic and a lyophilic colloid.

13614.title: protectin
13614.definition: Member of the Ly-6 family of cell surface molecules that prevents insertion of the membrane attack complex (MAC) into the membrane, thereby protecting cells from complement-induced lysis.

09560.title: protecting group
09560.definition: Non-reactive group temporarily used to transform a reactive group into one that does not react under conditions where the non-protected group reacts.

PT07148.title: protection of a reactive group
PT07148.definition: Temporary chemical transformation of a reactive group into a group that does not react under conditions where the non-protected group reacts.

P04896.title: protective action
P04896.definition: Addition of small amounts of hydrophilic colloid to a hydrophobic sol may make the latter more sensitive to flocculation by electrolyte. Higher concentrations of the same hydrophilic colloid usually protect the hydrophobic sol from flocculation. This phenomenon is called protective action.

13615.title: protective immunity
13615.definition: Protection against infectious agents conferred by vaccination.

13616.title: protein A
13616.definition: Staphylococcus aureus cell wall protein that binds to the Fc region of immunoglobulin G (IgG).

09762.title: protein complex
09762.definition: Ensemble of two or more different associated proteins, each with a specific function, linked by non-covalent protein-protein interactions.

09763.title: protein complex purification
09763.definition: Set of methods serving to purify the intact protein complex for further analysis.

11497.title: protein data bank
11497.definition: An archive of freely available macromolecular structural data of proteins, nucleic acids, and complex assemblies.

11484.title: protein data bank file
11484.definition: A text file that stores the atomic coordinates of a macromolecule, usually a protein or nucleic acid with associated ligands, solvent molecules and ions.

09764.title: protein database
09764.definition: Collection of protein sequences from several sources, including translations from annotated genetic coding regions, as well as original protein and peptide sequences.

P04897.title: protein engineering
P04897.definition: A technique used to produce proteins with altered or novel amino acid sequences. The methods used are: Transcription and translation systems from synthesized lengths of DNA or RNA with novel sequences.  Chemical modification of 'normal' proteins.   Solid-state polypeptide synthesis to form proteins.

09765.title: protein folding
09765.definition: Physicochemical process by which a polypeptide folds into its characteristic and functional three-dimensional structure from a random coil.

09766.title: protein fractionation
09766.definition: Methodical approach to simplify a complex mixture of proteomic sample.

09767.title: protein fragmentation
09767.definition: Process which happens during tandem mass spectrometry of intact proteins.

13618.title: protein G
13618.definition: Streptococcal cell wall protein that binds to the Fc region of immunoglobulin G (IgG), with a wider species specificity than protein A.

09768.title: protein identification
09768.definition: Analytical approach leading to the identity of a protein.

11147.title: protein kinase
11147.definition: Any enzyme catalyzing protein phosphorylation, often for the purpose of signal transduction.

13619.title: protein kinase C
13619.definition: Member of a kinase family with broad substrate specificity, activated by calcium, diacylglycerol, and (or) phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA).

09769.title: protein machine
09769.definition: Supramolecular interacting system, such as a metabolic circuit, intracellular signal transduction, or cell-to-cell communication.

09770.title: protein purification
09770.definition: Series of processes conducted to isolate either the whole proteome or a subset from a biological sample.

09771.title: protein quantification
09771.definition: Analytical methods and related techniques to measure the protein content.

09772.title: protein sequencer
09772.definition: Equipment designed for the automatic determination of amino acid sequences of peptides using a method of N-terminal analysis.

11547.title: protein sequencing
11547.definition: Determination of the primary structure of a protein.

09773.title: protein staining
09773.definition: Technique used to visualise proteins separated on electrophoretic slab gels.

09646.title: protein-free filtrate
09646.definition: Sample of blood, serum, or plasma from which all proteins have been removed by chemical or physical denaturation, dialysis, ultrafiltration, or solvent extraction.

09878.title: protein–protein interaction
09878.definition: Association of one protein with one or more other proteins to form either homo- or heteromeric proteins or protein complexes.

12719.title: proteinase
12719.definition: Enzyme that catalyses the hydrolysis of proteins.

13617.title: proteinase 3
13617.definition: Multifunctional enzyme of azurophilic granules of neutrophils and monocytes and the major target of antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibodies (ANCA).

P04898.title: proteins
P04898.definition: Naturally occurring and synthetic polypeptides having molecular weights greater than about 10000 (the limit is not precise).

16012.title: proteinuria
16012.definition: Excretion of excessive amounts of protein (derived from blood plasma or kidney tubules) in the urine.

09774.title: proteoform
09774.definition: All of the different molecular forms in which the protein product of a single gene can be found, including changes due to genetic variations, alternatively spliced ribonucleic acid (RNA) transcripts, and post-translational modifications.

09775.title: proteogenomics
09775.definition: Field of biological research in-between proteomics and genomics using proteomic information (mostly derived from mass spectrometry) to improve gene annotations.

P04899.title: proteoglycan
P04899.definition: A subclass of protein in which the carbohydrate units are polysaccharides that contain amino sugars. The protein is glycosylated by one or more (up to about 100) glycosaminoglycans [linear polymers of up to about 200 repeating disaccharide units that consist of a hexosamine (ᴅ-glucosamine or ᴅ-galactosamine) alternating with a uronic acid (ᴅ-glucuronic or ʟ-iduronic) or a neutral sugar (ᴅ-galactose)].

09833.title: proteoglycomics
09833.definition: Systematic study of the structure, expression, and function of proteoglycans.

09856.title: proteolipids
09856.definition: Proteins with covalently linked lipids, e.g. fatty acid or glycophosphatidylinositol (GPI).

09776.title: proteolysis
09776.definition: Protein cleavage to generate proteolytic peptides for bottom-up proteomic analysis, either enzymatic or chemical.

09777.title: proteolytic digestion
09777.definition: Exposure of a sample to proteolytic reactions.

09778.title: proteolytic enzyme
09778.definition: Group of enzymes that cleave the polypeptide into shorter oligopeptides (peptides) and amino acids.

PT06840.title: proteome
PT06840.definition: Complete set of proteins encoded by the genome.

09780.title: proteomics
09780.definition: Complex and comprehensive study of proteomes, particularly proteins, and the way they are expressed, modified, involved in metabolism, as well as of their interactions.

P04903.title: protium
P04903.definition: A specific name for the atom $\ce{^{1}H}$. The cation $\ce{^{1}H^{+}}$ is a proton, the species $\ce{1H}$ is a protide anion, and $\ce{1H}$ is the protio group. The word proton should not be used for $\ce{H^{+}}$ in its natural abundance.

08105.title: protocol for interlaboratory comparison
08105.definition: Detailed set of instructions describing the objectives, design, conduct, and reporting of an interlaboratory comparison.

08197.title: protofugality
08197.definition: Special case of nucleofugality, describing the relative rates of transfer of a proton (more generally: hydron) from a series of Brønsted acids \(\ce{H-X}\) to a common Brønsted base.

P04904.title: protogenic
P04904.definition: Capable of acting as a proton donor (strongly or weakly acidic as a Brønsted acid). The term is preferred to the synonym 'protic' or the more ambiguous expression acidic by itself.

P04905.title: protolysis
P04905.definition: This term has been used synonymously with proton (hydron)-transfer reaction. Because of its misleading similarity to hydrolysis, photolysis, etc., its use is discouraged.

P04906.title: proton
P04906.definition: Nuclear particle of charge number +1, spin quantum number \(\frac{1}{2}\) and rest mass of \(1.007\ 276\ 470(12)\ \rm{u}\).

P04907.title: proton affinity
P04907.definition: The negative of the enthalpy change in the gas phase reaction (real or hypothetical) between a proton (more appropriately hydron) and the chemical species concerned, usually an electrically neutral species to give the conjugate acid of that species. Proton affinity is often, but unofficially, abbreviated as PA.

08860.title: proton doping
08860.definition: Transformation of a semiconducting or insulating material to conducting state by protonation (hydronation) of its molecules.

P04915.title: proton transfer reaction
P04915.definition: A chemical reaction, the main feature of which is the intermolecular or intramolecular transfer of a proton (hydron) from one binding site to another. For example:  In the detailed description of proton transfer reactions, especially of rapid proton transfers between electronegative atoms, it should always be specified whether the term is used to refer to the overall process (including the more-or-less encounter-controlled formation of a hydrogen bonded complex and the separation of the products; see microscopic diffusion control) or just to the proton transfer event (including solvent rearrangement) by itself.

P04908.title: protonated molecule
P04908.definition: An ion formed by interaction of a molecule with a proton abstracted from an ion, as often occurs in chemical ionization according to the reaction: \(\rm{M}+\rm{XH}^{+}\rightarrow \rm{MH}^{+}+\rm{X}\). The symbolism $\ce{[M + H]^{+}}$ may also be used to represent the protonated molecule. The widely used term 'protonated molecular ion' to describe the $\ce{MH^{+}}$ ion is not recommended, since it suggests an associated product of a proton with a molecular ion.

08198.title: protonation
08198.definition: Attachment of the ion \(\ce{^{1}H^{+}}\) of relative isotopic mass approximately equal to 1.

P04909.title: protonation constant
P04909.definition: The equilibrium constant \(K_{\rm{H}n}\) for the addition of the \(n\)th proton to a charged or uncharged ligand. The cumulative protonation constant, \(\beta_{\rm{H}n}\), is the equilibrium constant for the formation of $\ce{H_{n}L}$ from \(n\) $\ce{H^{+}}$ and $\ce{L}$. The same equilibrium constant may be described in several ways, depending on how the ligand, $\ce{L}$, or the acid, has been defined.

08859.title: protonic conductivity
08859.definition: Ionic conductivity mediated by protons (more exactly by hydrogen cations properly called hydrons).

P04916.title: protophilic
P04916.definition: Capable of acting as proton acceptor, strongly or weakly basic (as a Brønsted base). Also called HBA (hydrogen bond acceptor) solvent.

08199.title: protophilicity
08199.definition: Special case of nucleophilicity, describing the relative rates of reactions of a series of Lewis bases with a common Brønsted acid. This term has the advantage over the commonly used 'kinetic basicity' that philicity and fugality are associated with kinetics, while acidity and basicity are associated with thermodynamics.

P04917.title: protoplast
P04917.definition: A spherical, osmotically-sensitive cell without its cell wall but retaining an intact cell membrane. Protoplasts are used to create hybrid cells via protoplast fusion.

P04918.title: prototrophs
P04918.definition: Microoganisms capable of growing at or below a temperature optimum of \(15\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\).

12720.title: prototype drug
12720.definition: Early compound that has biological properties suitable for target validation but may not necessarily be adequate for clinical studies.

11148.title: proximal
11148.definition: Nearer to an anatomical point of origin or attachment, or the midline of the body.

09561.title: proximity effect
09561.definition: Widening of the exposure dose distribution, and hence the developed pattern, caused by the scattering of the primary beam electrons within the resist and substrate.

13620.title: prozone effect
13620.definition: Loss of immunoprecipitation or agglutination that occurs when antibody concentration is increased to an extent that the antibody is in such excess that it is no longer able to effectively cross-link the antigen. A similar phenomenon may occur in antigen excess.

P04920.title: pseudo acids
P04920.definition: Potentially acidic compounds that require some structural reorganization, such as keto–enol tautomerization, having a non-negligible activation energy, in order to show normal acidic properties, e.g. nitroalkanes:

P04923.title: pseudo bases
P04923.definition: Hydroxy compounds that give salts with acids by formation of water accompanied by a change of constitution.

P04933.title: pseudo rate constant
P04933.definition: A term sometimes used for a rate coefficient. For example, if the rate equation is: \[v=k\ \rm{[A]}\ \rm{[B]}\] the function \(k\ \rm{[A]}\) is the pseudo first-order rate constant (or first-order rate coefficient) with respect to B. Similarly, \(k\ \rm{[B]}\) is the pseudo first-order rate constant (or first-order rate coefficient) with respect to A. The term pseudo rate constant is particularly useful when the concentration of one reactant is much greater than that of another.

16013.title: pseudo-acceptable daily intake
16013.definition: Intake for a substance derived by applying a thousandfold uncertainty factor to the lowest low-effect level for noncarcinogenic endpoints.

P04921.title: pseudo-asymmetric carbon atom
P04921.definition: The traditional name for a tetrahedrally coordinated carbon atom bonded to four different entities, two and only two of which have the same constitution but opposite chirality sense. The r/s descriptors of pseudo-asymmetric carbon atoms are invariant on reflection in a mirror (i.e. r remains r, and s remains s), but are reversed by the exchange of any two entities (i.e. r becomes s, and s becomes r). An example is C-3 of ribaric (C-3 is r) or xylaric acid (C-3 is s) or hyoscyamine (C-3 is r). The hyphen in pseudo-asymmetric may be omitted.

14365.title: pseudo-bulk behaviour
14365.definition: Behaviour in an emulsion, mini-emulsion, micro-emulsion, suspension, or dispersion polymerization wherein the kinetics are such that the rate equations are the same as those for polymerization in bulk.

P04924.title: pseudo-catalysis
P04924.definition: If an acid or base is present in nearly constant concentration throughout a reaction in solution (owing to buffering or the use of a large excess), it may be found to increase the rate of that reaction and also to be consumed during the process. The acid or base is then not a catalyst and the phenomenon cannot be called catalysis according to the well-established meaning of these terms in chemical kinetics, although the mechanism of such a process is often intimately related to that of a catalysed reaction. It is recommended that the term pseudo-catalysis be used in these and analogous cases (not necessarily involving acids or bases). For example, if a Brønsted acid accelerates the hydrolysis of an ester to a carboxylic acid and an alcohol, this is properly called acid catalysis, whereas the acceleration, by the same acid, of hydrolysis of an amide should be described as pseudo-catalysis by the acid: the 'acid pseudo-catalyst' is consumed during the reaction through formation of an ammonium ion. The terms 'general acid pseudo-catalysis' and 'general base pseudo-catalysis' may be used as the analogues of general acid catalysis and general base catalysis. The term 'base-promoted', 'base-accelerated' or 'base-induced' is sometimes used for reactions that are pseudo-catalysed by bases. However, the term 'promotion' also has a different meaning in other chemical contexts.

P04925.title: pseudo-co-oligomer
P04925.definition: An irregular oligomer, the molecules of which are derived from only one species of monomer but which display a variety of structural features more appropriate for description in co-oligomer terms.

P04926.title: pseudo-copolymer
P04926.definition: An irregular polymer, the molecules of which are derived from only one species of monomer but which display a variety of structural features more appropriate for description in copolymer terms.

09007.title: pseudo-ionic polymerization
09007.definition: Polymerization proceeding by insertion of a monomer into a polar bond without the generation of ions.

16014.title: pseudoadaptation
16014.definition: Apparent adaptation of an organism to changing conditions of the environment (especially chemical) associated with stresses in biochemical systems that exceed the limits of normal (homeostatic) mechanisms.

13621.title: pseudoallergy
13621.definition: Inflammatory or anaphylactic reaction with symptoms similar to an allergy but not involving an antigen-specific immune response, e.g., salicylate intolerance, reaction to contrast reagents.

12024.title: pseudobulbar affect
12024.definition: Involuntary emotional outburst (typically crying or laughing).

P04930.title: pseudohalogens
P04930.definition: Compounds that resemble the halogen elements, $\ce{X2}$, in their chemistry, e.g. $\ce{(CN)2}$ cyanogen, $\ce{(SCN)2}$ thiocyanogen, $\ce{ICN}$ iodine cyanide. Certain ions that have sufficient resemblance to halide ions are sometimes referred to as pseudohalide ions, e.g. $\ce{N3^{−}}$, $\ce{SCN^{−}}$, $\ce{CN^{−}}$.

11149.title: pseudohermaphrodite
11149.definition: Organism possessing either male (testes) or female (ovaries) gonads, but with ambiguous external genitalia.

12025.title: pseudomeningocele
12025.definition: Part of the cerebrospinal fluid that, in contrast to a meningocele, is not surrounded by dura.

P04932.title: pseudopericyclic
P04932.definition: A concerted transformation is pseudopericyclic if the primary changes in bonding occur within a cyclic array of atoms at one (or more) of which nonbonding and bonding atomic orbitals interchange roles. A formal example is the enol \(\rightarrow \) enol prototropy of pentane-2,4-dione (acetylacetone).  Because the \(\pi \)- and \(\sigma \)-atomic orbitals that interchange roles are orthogonal, such a reaction does not proceed through a fully conjugated transition state and is thus not a pericyclic reaction and therefore not governed by the rules that express orbital symmetry restrictions applicable to pericyclic reactions.

15229.title: pseudopolymorph
15229.definition: Different crystalline form(s) of a solvated compound that differ in the identity and/or the stoichiometry of the solvating molecule.

11150.title: pseudopregnancy
11150.definition: Development of signs of pregnancy in the absence of an embryo.

P04934.title: pseudorotation
P04934.definition: Stereoisomerization resulting in a structure that appears to have been produced by rotation of the entire initial molecule and is superposable on the initial one, unless different positions are distinguished by substitution, including isotopic substitution. One example of pseudorotation is a facile interconversion between the many envelope and twist conformers of a cyclopentane due to the out of plane motion of carbon atoms. Another example of pseudorotation (Berry pseudorotation) is a polytopal rearrangement that provides an intramolecular mechanism for the isomerization of trigonal bipyramidal compounds (e.g. \(\lambda ^{5}\)-phosphanes), the five bonds to the central atom E being represented as \(\rm{e}^{1}\), \(\rm{e}^{2}\), \(\rm{e}^{3}\), \(\rm{a}^{1}\) and \(\rm{a}^{2}\). Two equatorial bonds move apart and become apical bonds at the same time as the apical bonds move together to become equatorial.  A related conformational change of a trigonal bipyramidal structure is described as turnstile rotation. The process may be visualized as follows.  An apical and an equatorial bond rotate as a pair ca. 120° relative to the other three bonds. (Doubts have been expressed about the distinct physical reality of this mechanism.)

13972.title: pseudorotaxane
13972.definition: Rotaxane-like molecular assembly in which the threading component(s) has(have) ends small enough to permit threading or dethreading of the macrocyclic component(s).

13973.title: pseudorotaxane polymer
13973.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules that are macromolecular pseudorotaxanes.

12026.title: pseudotumor cerebri
12026.definition: Disorder with increased intracranial pressure, cerebral edema, and frequently papilledema, symptoms that resemble the effects of a tumor but without the occurrence of one.

13622.title: psoriasis
13622.definition: Skin disorder that has a hereditary component and is characterized by erythematous patches covered with silvery scales, especially on the elbows, knees, and scalp.

13623.title: psoriatic
13623.definition: Of, relating to, or associated with psoriasis; affected with psoriasis.

12027.title: psychoactive
12027.definition: Having the ability to alter mood, behavior, cognitive function or mental state.

11151.title: psychomotor retardation
11151.definition: Delayed development of both cognitive and motor function.

12028.title: psychoneuroimmunology
12028.definition: Study of links between the brain and the immune system, recognizing an interaction between psychological states and the outcome of immune responses to disease.

12029.title: psychosis
12029.definition: Disordered thought processes that may include changes in cognitive function, perception, belief, behavior and personality; altered awareness of reality.

12031.title: psychotropic
12031.definition: Capable of affecting the mind, emotions and behavior.

P04939.title: psychrometric hygrometer
P04939.definition: Instrument by which the relative humidity of the atmosphere may be determined. It is generally composed of two temperature sensors, one of which measures the temperature of the air; the other sensor is moistened with water and senses the cooling due to evaporation of water. The temperature difference between the two sensors is a function of relative humidity; sometimes referred to as a 'wet-and-dry bulb' thermometer.

P04940.title: psychrometry
P04940.definition: The use of a wet-and-dry bulb thermometer for measurement of atmospheric humidity.

09976.title: pterocarpans
09976.definition: Pterocarpans are compounds derived from (6a$R$,11a$R$)-6a,11a-dihydro-6$H$-[1]benzofuro[3,2-$c$][1]benzopyran (15), and their 6a,11a-didehydro derivatives 16 are named coumestans. They are numbered systematically following the numbering rules for fused ring systems.

14960.title: Ptolemaic incongruity
14960.definition: False assertion that any particular level of biological organization holds a more central or important role than any other in the science of ecotoxicology.

11152.title: puberty
11152.definition: Process in which an individual undergoes sexual development, including the onset of gametogenesis, changes in hormonal secretions, secondary sexual characteristics, and reproductive competence.

11153.title: pubescent
11153.definition: Being in the early stage of puberty.

11154.title: pubic
11154.definition: Relating to the region of the most ventral bone of the pelvis (the pubic bone), and thus the region around the genital area, normally showing hair growth (pubic hair) in the adult.

11155.title: pubic symphysis
11155.definition: Cartilaginous joint between the pubic bones forming the front of the pelvis.

16015.title: public health impact assessment
16015.definition: Applying risk assessment to a specific target population of known size, giving as the end product a quantitative statement about the number of people likely to be affected in a particular population.

12032.title: puffer fish
12032.definition: Marine fish of the order Tetraodontiformes and family Tetraodontidae.

P04941.title: puffing
P04941.definition: An irreversible expansion of some carbon artifacts during graphitization heat treatment between \(1650\) and \(2700\ \rm{K}\).

P04942.title: puffing inhibitor
P04942.definition: Metals or metal compounds with a high chemical affinity for the heteroatoms in the carbons. They are distributed as fine particles within the carbon materials to be graphitized.

09879.title: pull-down assay
09879.definition: Approach used for studying protein–protein interactions analogous to immunoprecipitation, using (instead of antibody) one of the interacting proteins (the 'bait') immobilised at a surface to capture the other protein (the 'prey').

11157.title: pulmonary artery
11157.definition: Large vessel that transports blood from the heart to the lungs.

11270.title: pulmonary surfactant
11270.definition: Surface-active layer of phospholipids and proteins coating the pulmonary alveoli that increases lung compliance, facilitates lung expansion, and stabilizes alveolar volume.

11158.title: pulmonary valve stenosis
11158.definition: Condition in which the flow of blood from the heart to the lungs is slowed by a deformity on or near the pulmonary valve that controls the blood flow from the right heart to the lungs.

P04945.title: pulse amplitude analyser
P04945.definition: A sub-assembly for determining the distribution function of a set of pulses in terms of their amplitude. Synonymous with pulse height analyser.

P04946.title: pulse amplitude selector
P04946.definition: A circuit which gives an output pulse for each input pulse whose amplitude lies within a chosen interval. Synonymous with single channel pulse height analyser.

P04947.title: pulse duration
P04947.definition: In pulse polarography, differential pulse polarography, Kalousek polarography, and related techniques, the duration of an interval during which the excitation signal deviates from the base line. This interval includes the sampling interval.

08531.title: pulse energy
08531.definition: Total optical energy content of a laser pulse. Integral of optical power over pulse duration.

08755.title: pulse pile-up
08755.definition: Processing by a radiation counter of pulses resulting from the simultaneous absorption of independent particles or photons in a radiation detector, resulting in them being counted as one single particle or photon with energy between the individual energies and the sum of these energies.

09415.title: pulse rate
09415.definition: Number of ion pulse cycles per second in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

P04951.title: pulse reactor
P04951.definition: In a pulse reactor, a carrier gas, which may be inert or possibly one of the reactants, flows over the catalyst and small amounts of the other reactant or reactants are injected into the carrier gas at intervals. A pulse reactor is useful for exploratory work but kinetic results apply to a transient rather than to the steady state conditions of the catalyst.

08396.title: pulse sequence
08396.definition: Timed series of radiofrequency pulses and magnetic field gradients that define a part or whole of a nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment.

09416.title: pulse width
09416.definition: Full width at half maximum of the time distribution of the pulse of ions generated by a beam chopper and, optionally, the use of beam bunching in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

09417.title: pulsed extraction field
09417.definition: Extraction field around the sample that is pulsed to the working value for extracting ions for the time necessary for operation of a time-of-flight mass spectrometer, but is otherwise at a low value.

08532.title: pulsed laser
08532.definition: Laser system that emits electromagnetic radiation in the form of pulses of a defined and constant duration.

08397.title: pulsed-field gradient
08397.definition: Short, timed pulse in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that momentarily destroys the magnetic field homogeneity within the sample through a spatial-dependent field intensity.

15415.title: pulsed-laser polymerisation
15415.definition: Polymerization initiated by successive pulses of laser light.

PT07465.title: pump-dump-probe technique
PT07465.definition: Transient absorption spectroscopy using three pulses (a strong pump, a dump pulse that can alter the course of the reaction photoinduced by the first pulse, and a weak probe). In general, femtosecond laser pulses are used.

P04952.title: pump-probe technique
P04952.definition: Transient absorption spectroscopy using two pulses (strong pump and weak probe) and capable of achieving a high temporal resolution. A pump pulse excites the sample and triggers the process under investigation. A second delayed pulse, the probe, monitors an optical property. By varying the time delay between the pump and probe pulses, it is possible to assemble measurements as a function of time. The probe pulse is typically a UV, visible or infrared pulse in which case a snap-shot spectrum is taken as a function of the delay time. Often the probe pulse is generated from a portion of the excitation beam, but it can also be an independently generated electromagnetic pulse.

11159.title: pup
11159.definition:
(n) Young or newborn dog, rat or seal.
(v) Give birth to a pup.

08398.title: pure shift yielded by chirp excitation
08398.definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment generating homonuclear spin-spin decoupled spectra.

09349.title: pure-element relative sensitivity factor
09349.definition: In electron spectroscopy, coefficient, proportional to the intensity measured for a pure sample of an element, by which the measured intensity for that element is divided in calculations to yield the atomic concentration or atomic fraction of the element present in the sample.

13624.title: purified protein derivative
13624.definition: Partially purified derivative of tuberculin used in the Mantoux test for tuberculosis.

09717.title: purine
09717.definition: Nitrogen-containing, double-ring, basic compound that occurs in nucleic acids.

P04953.title: purine bases
P04953.definition: Purine and its substitution derivatives, especially naturally occurring examples. The customary numbering shown below is not systematic.purine

12033.title: Purkinje cell
12033.definition: Large neuron forming part of a layer of cells in the cerebellum.

13625.title: purpura
13625.definition: Purple discoloration occurring in patches on the skin, mucus membranes, or organs.

12034.title: pursuit aiming test
12034.definition: Procedure in which a subject is instructed to place a dot in defined sites (such as a number of circles), as quickly as possible.

08200.title: push-pull conjugation
08200.definition: Feature of an extended conjugated \(\ce{\uppi\ system}\) bearing an electron donor group at one end and an electron acceptor group at the other end.

12035.title: putamen
12035.definition: Part of the basal ganglia that plays a role in coordinating movement and learning.

12036.title: pyknosis
12036.definition: Clumping of nuclear chromatin and shrinkage of the cell nucleus during cell degeneration.

11160.title: pyloric stenosis
11160.definition: Narrowing of the sphincter (the pylorus) between the stomach and duodenum.

12037.title: pyramidal cell
12037.definition: Large neuron of the cerebral cortex having a triangular cell body in histological section with several dendrites at the base and one large apical axon.

P04956.title: pyramidal inversion
P04956.definition: A polytopal rearrangement in which the change in bond directions to a three-coordinate central atom having a pyramidal arrangement of bonds (tripodal arrangement) causes the central atom (apex of the pyramid) to appear to move to an equivalent position on the other side of the base of the pyramid. If the three ligands to the central atom are different pyramidal inversion interconverts enantiomers.

P04957.title: pyranoses
P04957.definition: Cyclic hemiacetal forms of monosaccharides in which the ring is six-membered (a tetrahydropyran).

12038.title: pyrethroid
12038.definition: Synthetic molecule with structural similarity to the natural pyrethrins found in plants of the genus Chrysanthemum.

16016.title: pyrexia
16016.definition: Condition in which the temperature of a human being or mammal is above normal.

09718.title: pyrimidine
09718.definition: Nitrogen-containing, single-ring, basic compound that occurs in nucleic acids.

P04958.title: pyrimidine bases
P04958.definition: Pyrimidine and its substitution derivatives, especially naturally occurring examples.

P04959.title: pyro
P04959.definition: A prefix designating compounds formed by heating a compound, usually with the elimination of water, carbon dioxide, or other simple molecule, e.g. pyroglutamic acid from glutamic acid.

P04960.title: pyroelectric detector
P04960.definition: A detector (based on the temperature dependence of ferroelectricity in some crystals) which produces an electrical signal proportional to the energy flux on the collector surface.

13627.title: pyrogen test
13627.definition: Any of various tests used to determine whether an agent, usually an infusion or injection fluid, is free of pyrogens.

14961.title: pyrogenic
14961.definition:
Describing anything that causes fire.
Describing products of fire; e.g., organic compounds produced by the high-temperature combustion of complex organic substances are pyrogenic compounds.Examples: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are examples of pyrogenic compounds.
Describing a substance that produces fever.

P04961.title: pyrolysis
P04961.definition: Thermolysis, usually associated with exposure to a high temperature.

08533.title: pyrolysis curve
08533.definition: Graph of absorbance against pyrolysis temperature in electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy.

P04962.title: pyrolysis-gas chromatography
P04962.definition: A version of reaction chromatography in which a sample is thermally decomposed to simpler fragments before entering the column.

P04963.title: pyrolytic carbon
P04963.definition: A carbon material deposited from gaseous hydrocarbon compounds on suitable underlying substrates (carbon materials, metals, ceramics) at temperatures ranging from \(1000\) to \(2500\ \rm{K}\) (chemical vapour deposition).

P04964.title: pyrolytic graphite
P04964.definition: A graphite material with a high degree of preferred crystallographic orientation of the c-axes perpendicular to the surface of the substrate, obtained by graphitization heat treatment of pyrolytic carbon or by chemical vapour deposition at temperatures above \(2500\ \rm{K}\).

P04965.title: pyrromethenes
P04965.definition: A less preferred term for dipyrrins. (The term 'pyrromethane' has been used for the system with a $\ce{–CH2\bond{–}}$ linkage).

P04385.title: π – π* state
P04385.definition: An excited state related to the ground state by a π → π* transition.

P04386.title: π → π* transition
P04386.definition: An electronic transition described approximately as a promotion of an electron from a 'bonding' $\ce{\uppi\! orbital}$ to an 'antibonding' $\ce{\uppi\! orbital}$ designated as $\ce{\uppi\!^{\ast}}$.

08786.title: π-conjugated system
08786.definition: Molecule or a part of a molecule, of which structure may be represented as a system of alternating single and multiple bonds, in which, eventually, a multiple bond can be replaced by an atom with a pair of non-bonding electrons or an atom carrying a negative charge.

08201.title: π-electron donor
08201.definition: Substituent capable of electron donation by resonance (e.g., \(\ce{OCH3}\)).

12539.title: quadratic field reflectron
12539.definition: Reflectron in which the electric field varies with the square of the distance from the entrance and compensates for kinetic energy spread to all orders.

12540.title: quadrupolar axialization
12540.definition: Technique for axialization in Fourier transform-ion cyclotron resonance-mass spectrometers in which magnetron motion is converted into cyclotron motion by subjecting the trapped ions to a quadrupolar excitation field while they undergo collisions.

12541.title: quadrupole time-of-flight
12541.definition: Hybrid mass spectrometer consisting of a transmission quadrupole mass spectrometer coupled to an orthogonal acceleration time-of-flight mass spectrometer. A collision quadrupole is typically inserted between the two mass spectrometers.

12542.title: quantitation by concatenated tryptic peptides
12542.definition: Method for absolute quantitation of a protein or proteins in a multiplexed fashion using isotope-labeled peptides as surrogate internal standards. The labeled peptides are produced by synthesizing a gene coding for all desired peptides, expressing this gene in E. coli culture containing appropriately labeled substrate, and digesting with trypsin the expressed protein composed of the desired concatenated peptides.

12543.title: quasi-equilibrium theory
12543.definition: Statistical theory of unimolecular reaction rates (isomerization or fragmentation) of molecular species that assumes that reaction occurs from the ground electronic state of the reactant regardless of its mode of formation, at a rate determined by the free statistical redistribution of internal energy into those vibrational and rotational modes that must be activated sufficiently to reach the appropriate transition state for the specified reaction to occur.

15416.title: Q-e scheme
15416.definition: Empirical equations expressing the monomer reactivity ratios in a binary radical copolymerization, \(r_{12}\) and \(r_{21}\), in terms of the empirical parameters \(Q\) and \(e\) for the two monomers, namely, \(\rm{Q}_{1}\), \(\rm{Q}_{2}\), \(\rm{e}_{1}\), and \(\rm{e}_{2}\), with\(r_{12} = (Q_{1}/Q_{2})\exp [-{e_{1}}(e_{1} - e_{2})]\) and \(r_{21} = (Q_{2}/Q_{1}) \exp [-{e_{2}}(e_{2} - e_{1})]\)

Q04967.title: Q-switched laser
Q04967.definition: A laser in which the state of the device introducing important losses in the resonant cavity and preventing lasing operation is suddenly switched to a state where the device introduces very low losses. This increases rapidly the Quality factor of the cavity, allowing the build-up of a short and very intense laser pulse. Typical pulse durations are in the ns range. The Q-switching may be active (a rotating mirror or electro-optic device) or passive (a saturable absorber).

11498.title: q2
11498.definition:
The square of the leave-one-out cross-validation regression coefficient calculated from the variance of the observed versus predicted values of the target
 property, usually potency, of each compound when eliminated during cross-validation.

13628.title: Qa antigen
13628.definition: 'Non-classical' major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecule in mice.

12721.title: QTc interval
12721.definition: Time between the start of the Q wave and the end of the T wave in the heart’s electrical cycle. When corrected for individual heart rate it becomes known as the corrected QT, or QTc interval.

10139.title: quadratic discriminant analysis
10139.definition: Discriminant analysis in which the criterion function is based on the individual within-group covariance matrix.

Q04968.title: quadratic mean
Q04968.definition: The square root of the expression in which the sum of squared observations is divided by the number \(n\). It can be calculated by the formula: \[\overline{x}_{\rm{q}}=\sqrt{\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{n}}\]

08399.title: quadrature detection
08399.definition: Collection of time domain nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy data on both the \(x\) and \(y\) axes of the rotating frame of reference to allow discrimination of positive and negative frequencies.

12039.title: quadriplegia
12039.definition: Paralysis of both upper and both lower limbs.

Q04969.title: quadro-
Q04969.definition: An affix used in names to denote four atoms bound into a quadrangle (e.g. square).

08400.title: quadrupolar nuclide
08400.definition: Nuclide with spin quantum number \(I \gt ½\) and a non-spherical distribution of charge in the nucleus giving rise to a nuclear electric quadrupole moment (\(eQ\)).

08401.title: quadrupolar relaxation
08401.definition: Relaxation mechanism in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy arising from intramolecular quadrupolar interactions with electric field gradients.

Q04970.title: quadrupole ion storage trap
Q04970.definition: An arrangement in which ions with a desired range of quotients mass/charge are trapped by making them describe stable paths under the effect of a static and a high-frequency electric quadrupole field.

Q04971.title: quadrupole mass analyser
Q04971.definition: An arrangement in which ions with a desired quotient mass/charge are made to describe a stable path under the effect of a static and a high-frequency electric quadrupole field, and are then detected. Ions with a different mass/charge are separated from the detected ions because of their unstable paths.

Q04972.title: quadrupole splitting
Q04972.definition: The measured Doppler velocity difference between the two peaks seen in quadrupole split spectra from nuclides such as $\ce{^{57}Fe}$ and $\ce{^{119}Sn}$.

Q04973.title: qualitative analysis
Q04973.definition: Analysis in which substances are identified or classified on the basis of their chemical or physical properties, such as chemical reactivity, solubility, molecular weight, melting point, radiative properties (emission, absorption), mass spectra, nuclear half-life, etc.

Q04974.title: qualitative elemental specificity
Q04974.definition: Ability of a method to detect one element in the presence of another element.

08106.title: quality
08106.definition: Degree to which a set of inherent characteristics of an object fulfils requirements.

Q04975.title: quality assurance
Q04975.definition: The guarantee that the quality of a product (analytical data set, etc.) is actually what is claimed on the basis of the quality control applied in creating that product. Quality assurance is not synonymous with quality control. Quality assurance is meant to protect against failures of quality control.

Q04976.title: quality control
Q04976.definition: The maintenance and statement of the quality of a product (data set, etc.) specifically that it meets or exceeds some minimum standard based on known, testable criteria.

08107.title: quality control material
08107.definition: Material used for the purposes of quality control and subjected to the same or part of the same measurement procedure as that used for analytical samples.

14962.title: quality criteria
14962.definition: Quality guidelines based on the evaluation of scientific data.

Q04977.title: quality factor
Q04977.definition: The linear-energy-transfer dependent factor by which absorbed dose is multiplied to obtain dose equivalent.

14963.title: quality guidelines
14963.definition: Numerical limits or text statements established to support and maintain designated uses of the environment or to protect human health.

08108.title: quality improvement
08108.definition: Part of quality management focused on increasing the ability to fulfil requirements for quality.

08109.title: quality management
08109.definition: Coordinated activities to direct and control an organization with regard to quality.

08110.title: quality management system
08110.definition: Part of a set of interrelated or interacting elements of an organization to establish quality policies and quality objectives and processes to achieve those objectives.

08111.title: quality manual
08111.definition: Specification for the quality management system of an organization.

08112.title: quality objective
08112.definition: Result to be achieved related to quality.

Q04978.title: quality of solvent
Q04978.definition: A qualitative characterization of the polymer–solvent interaction. A solution of a polymer in a 'better' solvent is characterized by a higher value of the second virial coefficient than a solution of the same polymer in a 'poorer' solvent.

08113.title: quality plan
08113.definition: Specification of the procedures and associated resources to be applied when and by whom to a specific object.

08114.title: quality planning
08114.definition: Part of quality management focused on setting quality objectives and specifying necessary operational processes and related resources to achieve the quality objectives.

08115.title: quality policy
08115.definition: Intentions and direction of a laboratory as formally expressed by its top management related to quality.

14964.title: quality standards
14964.definition: Fixed upper limits for exposure to certain chemicals recognized under law by one or more levels of government. Well-known examples include the air, water, and soil quality standards, as well as threshold limit values for air pollutants in the workplace.

16017.title: quantal
16017.definition: Describing a condition that can be expressed only as 'occurring' or 'not occurring', such as death.

14965.title: quantal effect
14965.definition: Condition that can be expressed only as 'occurring' or 'not occurring', such as death or occurrence of a tumor.

Q04980.title: quantitative analysis
Q04980.definition: Analyses in which the amount or concentration of an analyte may be determined (estimated) and expressed as a numerical value in appropriate units. qualitative analysis may take place without quantitative analysis, but quantitative analysis requires the identification (qualification) of the analytes for which numerical estimates are given.

09719.title: quantitative polymerase chain reaction
09719.definition: Polymerase chain reaction to quantify target nucleotide sequences of interest.

14966.title: quantitative structure–metabolism relationship
14966.definition: Quantitative association between the physicochemical and (or) the structural properties of a substance and its metabolic behavior.

QT06977.title: quantitative structure–activity relationship
QT06977.definition: Quantitative structure–activity relationships (QSAR) are mathematical relationships linking chemical structure and pharmacological activity in a quantitative manner for a series of compounds. Methods which can be used in QSAR include various regression and pattern recognition techniques.QSAR is often taken to be equivalent to chemometrics or multivariate statistical data analysis. It is sometimes used in a more limited sense as equivalent to Hansch analysis. QSAR is a subset of the more general term SPC.

Q04981.title: quantitative structure–activity relationships
Q04981.definition: The building of structure–biological activity models by using regression analysis with physicochemical constants, indicator variables or theoretical calculations. The term has been extended by some authors to include chemical reactivity, i.e. activity is regarded as synonymous with reactivity. This extension is, however, discouraged.

08202.title: quantitative structure–property relationship
08202.definition: Regression model to correlate chemical properties such as boiling point or chromatographic retention time with predictor parameters based on measured or calculated features of molecular structure.

Q04982.title: quantity
Q04982.definition: Attribute of a phenomenon, body or substance that may be distinguished qualitatively and determined quantitatively.

Q04983.title: quantity calculus
Q04983.definition: Algebra with quantities where the symbols of quantities represent products of numerical values and their units.

Q04984.title: quantity of dimension one
Q04984.definition: Quantity in the dimensional expression of which all the exponents of the dimensions of the base quantities are zero.

Q04979.title: quantized internal energy
Q04979.definition: The quantized internal energy of a molecule in its electronic ground or excited state can be approximated with sufficient accuracy for analytical purposes by: \[E_{\rm{int}}=E_{\rm{el}}+E_{\rm{vib}}+E_{\rm{rot}}\] where \(E_{\mathrm{el}}\) is the electronic, \(E_{\mathrm{vib}}\) the vibrational and \(E_{\mathrm{rot}}\) the rotational energy, respectively.

08861.title: quantum confinement effect
08861.definition: Effect occurring if at least one dimension of a structure is comparable to the de Broglie wavelength of the electron-hole pair and the motion of charge carriers is thus quantized by the structure boundary.

Q04987.title: quantum counter
Q04987.definition: A medium emitting with a quantum yield independent of the excitation energy over a defined spectral range (e.g, concentrated rhodamine 6G solutions between \(300\) and \(600\ \rm{nm}\)). Also used for devices producing an electrical signal proportional to the photon flux absorbed in a medium.

Q04988.title: quantum efficiency
Q04988.definition: For a primary photochemical process, quantum efficiency is identical to quantum yield.

QT07469.title: quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics
QT07469.definition: Hybrid procedure for the treatment of large molecular systems. A crucial part of the system (e.g., the chromophore and its surroundings) is treated explicitly by quantum mechanical (QM) techniques, whereas the rest of the system is approximated by a classical or molecular mechanics (MM) force field treatment.

Q04986.title: quantum
Q04986.definition: An elementary particle of electromagnetic energy in the sense of the wave-particle duality.

08862.title: quantum tunneling polymer composite
08862.definition: Electrically conducting polymer composite that, however, is conducting only when pressed due to thinning the insulating polymer matrix membranes so much that they allow electron tunneling through them.

Q04991.title: quantum yield
Q04991.definition: The integral quantum yield is \[\mathit{\Phi}(\lambda) = \frac{\rm{number\ of\ events}}{\rm{number\ of\ photons\ absorbed}}\] For a photochemical reaction, \[\mathit{\Phi}(\lambda) = \frac{\rm{amount\ of\ reactant\ consumed\ or\ product\ formed}}{\rm{number\ of\ photons\ absorbed}}\] The differential quantum yield is \[\mathit{\Phi}(\lambda) = \frac{{\rm{d}}x/{\rm{d}}t}{q_{n,{\rm{p}}}^{0}[ 1 - 10^{-A(\lambda)} ]}\] where \({\rm{d}}x/{\rm{d}}t\) is the rate of change of a measurable quantity (spectral or any other property), and \(q_{n\rm{,p}}^{0}\) the amount of photons (\(\pu{mol}\) or its equivalent \(\rm{einstein}\)) incident (prior to absorption) per time interval (photon flux, amount basis). \(A(\lambda)\) is the absorbance at the excitation wavelength.

Q04992.title: quarter-transition-time potential
Q04992.definition: In chronopotentiometry (at constant current density), the potential of the indicator electrode at the instant when the time that has elapsed since the application of current is equal to one-fourth of the transition time. Appropriate correction for double-layer charging is needed in practice.

Q04993.title: quartet state
Q04993.definition: A state having a total electron spin quantum number equal to \(\frac{3}{2}\).

08534.title: quartz atomizer
08534.definition: Atomizer that is used to atomize those elements that form volatile species (e.g., hydrides) at relatively low temperatures (e.g., \(\pu{1000^{\circ}C}\) or below).

Q04994.title: quartz–iodine lamp
Q04994.definition: Wolfram (tungsten) filament high-intensity incandescent lamp containing iodine in a quartz envelope. Used primarily as a source of visible radiation.

Q04996.title: quasi-classical trajectory method
Q04996.definition: A procedure for calculating trajectories in which the quantization of the reactants is taken into account, but in which the course of the reaction is treated classically.

Q04997.title: quasi-enantiomers
Q04997.definition: Constitutionally different yet closely related chemical species MX and MY having the opposite chirality sense of the large common chiral moiety M. For example (R)-2-bromobutane is a quasi-enantiomer of (S)-2-chlorobutane.

Q04999.title: quasi-equilibrium
Q04999.definition: In conventional transition-state theory it is assumed that activated complex are formed in a state of equilibrium with the reactants. They are not in classical equilibrium with the reactants; if they were, addition of more activated complexes to the system would cause the equilibrium to shift in favour of the reactants. This would not occur for an activated complex, and the term quasi-equilibrium is used to denote this special type of equilibrium.

Q05000.title: quasi-molecular ion
Q05000.definition: A protonated molecule or an ion formed from a molecular ion by loss of a hydrogen atom. The use of the term 'pseudo-molecular ion' is not recommended.

Q05001.title: quasi-racemic compound
Q05001.definition: The crystalline product of a 1:1 association between quasi-enantiomers.

09087.title: quasi-reference electrode
09087.definition: Electrode that maintains a constant, but not generally well-defined, potential in an electrochemical cell.

Q05002.title: quasi-single-strand polymer
Q05002.definition: A regular linear polymer that can be described by a preferred constitutional repeating unit in which only one terminal constituent subunit is connected through a single atom to the other identical constitutional repeating units or to an end group.

08863.title: quasiparticle
08863.definition: Discrete disorder in a multi-particulate system that exhibits particle-specific behavior and properties.

Q05003.title: quaternary ammonium compounds
Q05003.definition: Derivatives of ammonium compounds, $\ce{(NH4^{+})Y^{−}}$, in which all four of the hydrogens bonded to nitrogen have been replaced with hydrocarbyl groups.

Q05004.title: quaternary structure
Q05004.definition: The defined organization of two or more macromolecules with tertiary structure such as a protein that are held together by hydrogen bonds and van der Waals and coulombic forces.

10230.title: QuEChERS (quick, easy, cheap, effective, rugged and safe) extraction
10230.definition: Streamlined multiresidue method for extraction and clean-up of analytes in complex matrices.

Q05006.title: quencher
Q05006.definition: A molecular entity that deactivates (quenches) an excited state of another molecular entity, either by energy transfer, electron transfer, or by a chemical mechanism.

Q05007.title: quenching
Q05007.definition: Deactivation of an excited molecular entity intermolecularly by an external environmental influence (such as a quencher) or intramolecularly by a substituent through a non-radiative process.

Q05009.title: quenching correction
Q05009.definition: Correction for errors due to different quenching for standards and test portions. When using liquid scintillation detectors these corrections can be based e.g. on the standard addition or sample channels ratio method or the use of automated external standardization.

11161.title: quickening
11161.definition: Initial awareness of fetal movement by the pregnant mother, usually occurring early in the second trimester.

Q05010.title: quinarenes
Q05010.definition: Mancude assemblies of three carbocyclic rings, a six-membered quinonoid ring bonded at the 1,4-positions to odd-membered rings which differ in ring size by two, e.g.

Q05011.title: quinhydrones
Q05011.definition: Molecular complexes of one equivalent amount of a quinone with one equivalent amount of the corresponding hydroquinone.

Q05012.title: quinomethanes
Q05012.definition: Methylidenecyclohexadienones and dimethylidenecyclohexadienes, formally derived from quinones by replacement of one or both of the quinone oxygens by methylidene groups. (The diradical, triplet state of quinodimethanes can also be called o- or p-xylylenes).

Q05014.title: quinone diazides
Q05014.definition: A potentially confusing term for diazooxides; the presence of an azido group, $\ce{–N3}$, is falsely suggested.

Q05015.title: quinones
Q05015.definition: Compounds having a fully conjugated cyclic dione structure, such as that of benzoquinones, derived from aromatic compounds by conversion of an even number of number of $\ce{–CH=}$ groups into $\ce{–C(=O)–}$ groups with any necessary rearrangement of double bonds (polycyclic and heterocyclic analogues are included).

Q05016.title: quinonimines
Q05016.definition: Imines derived from quinones by replacement of one or both oxygens by $\ce{=NR}$. The term may include both types unless the infix mono or di is included, e.g. o-benzoquinone diimine:

Q05017.title: quinonoximes
Q05017.definition: Mono- or di-oximes of quinones; quinone monooximes are tautomeric with nitrosophenols.

14967.title: quotient method
14967.definition: Calculation of the quotient of the measured or predicted environmental concentration (PEC) of a contaminant and the predicted no-effect level (PNEC), used as an expression of hazard or risk. Higher quotients constitute greater evidence of a hazard or a greater risk.

Q06240.title: θ state
Q06240.definition: The state of a polymer solution for which the second virial coefficient is zero.

R05401.title: rise velocity
R05401.definition: The vertical component of the velocity of the volatilized component in the observation space (in \(\rm{mm s}^{-1}\)). It depends on the flame temperature, the solute nebulized, the observation height and the gas flow rate.

16259.title: retention time
16259.definition: Retention time of a sample component, the molecules of which are smaller than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase but larger than the smallest pores.

14411.title: reversible chain deactivation
14411.definition: Deactivation of a chain carrier in a chain polymerisation, reversibly converting the active center into an inactive one and then, within the lifetime of a growing macromolecule, regenerating an active center on the same original chain carrier.

14213.title: right-handed helix
14213.definition: Helix in which the continuous helical line, approximating the sequence of bonds along the polymer main chain, winds anticlockwise moving towards the observer, i.e., seen from the positive axis direction (see the figures in chain identity period).

14214.title: rod group
14214.definition: Symmetry group of a three-dimensional array of atoms, regularly repeating along one direction.

14215.title: rotation per helix residue
14215.definition: Angle of rotation about the chain axis per helix residue.

14226.title: racemic packing
14226.definition: Packing in a polymer crystal in which stems of opposite helicity coexist in equal numbers.

14242.title: regular adjacent re-entry model
14242.definition: Idealized adjacent re-entry model in which the fold periods are assumed to have all the same length.

12544.title: radial ejection
12544.definition: Ejection of an ion from an ion trap in a direction perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the trap.

12545.title: Rayleigh limit
12545.definition: Limiting droplet size at which self-fragmentation will occur for charged droplets generated in electrospray or other ionization processes. Self-fragmentation occurs when the electrostatic repulsion force generated by the excess charge exceeds the surface tension that maintains the integrity of the droplet.

12546.title: reagent gas
12546.definition: Gas that reacts with ions to produce product ions through ion/molecule reactions; for example, a gas such as methane, ammonia, or isobutane used in chemical ionization to create reagent ions or a gas used in ion traps or collision cells to perform gas-phase ion/molecule reactions.

12547.title: reagent ion
12547.definition: Ion that reacts with a neutral to produce an ionized form of such species through an ion/molecule reaction, for example, as in chemical ionization.

12548.title: recombination energy
12548.definition: Energy released when an electron is added to an ionized molecule or atom.

12549.title: rectilinear ion trap
12549.definition: Quadrupole ion trap whose electrodes form a rectilinear polygon, the simplest form of which consists of two pairs of rectangular electrodes supplied with radio frequency (RF) potentials and a pair of electrodes to which a DC potential is applied. Slits or apertures in the electrodes allow injection and ejection of charged particles.

12550.title: reference ion
12550.definition: Stable ion whose structure or elemental formula is known with certainty. These ions are formed by direct ionization of a molecule of known structure or elemental formula, and are used to verify by comparison the structure or thermochemistry of an unknown ion or to calibrate the m/z scale of the mass spectrometer.

12551.title: relative isotope-ratio difference
12551.definition: Measure of an isotope ratio in a sample of interest relative to a reference defined by the relation \[\delta = (R_{\rm{sample}} - R_{\rm{standard}})/R_{\rm{standard}}\] where \(R\) is the isotope ratio of the element.

12552.title: residual gas analyser
12552.definition: Mass spectrometer used to measure the composition and pressure of gases in an evacuated chamber and to test for leaks in pressurized systems.

12553.title: resolution: 10 per cent valley definition
12553.definition: Value of \((m/z)/\Delta(m/z)\) measured for two peaks of equal height in a mass spectrum at m/z and \(m/z \pm \Delta(m/z)\) that are separated by a valley which at its lowest point is \(\pu{10\%}\) of the height of either peak. For peaks of similar height separated by a valley, let the height of the valley at its lowest point be \(\pu{10\%}\) of the lower peak. Then the resolution (\(\pu{10\%}\) valley definition) is \((m/z)/\Delta(m/z)\) and should be given for a number of values of m/z.

12554.title: resolution: peak width definition
12554.definition: For a single peak corresponding to singly charged ions at mass \(m\) in a mass spectrum, the resolution may be expressed as \((m/z)/\Delta(m/z)\), where \(\Delta(m/z)\) is the width of the peak at a height which is a specified fraction of the maximum peak height. It is recommended that one of three values 50, 5, or \(\pu{0.5\%}\) should always be used.

12555.title: resonance-enhanced multiphoton ionization
12555.definition: Multiphoton ionization in which the ionization cross section is significantly enhanced because the energy of the incident photons is resonant with an intermediate excited state of the neutral.

12556.title: resonance ion ejection
12556.definition: Mode of ion ejection in an ion trap that relies on an auxiliary radio frequency potential that is applied to the end-cap or trapping electrodes. The potential is tuned to the classical oscillation frequency of a particular ion to eject it.

12557.title: retro Diels–Alder reaction
12557.definition: Ion fragmentation mechanism in which the molecular ion \(\ce{M^{+.}}\) of a cyclic alkene fragments to form a neutral diene and an alkene radical cation or a diene radical cation and an alkene. The reaction is the reverse of the Diels–Alder reaction of organic synthesis.

12558.title: reverse geometry
12558.definition: Double-focusing mass spectrometer configuration in which the ion beam traverses the magnetic sector prior to the electric sector.

12559.title: reverse library search
12559.definition: Process of comparing a subset of the peaks in the mass spectrum of an unknown compound with peaks present in the library mass spectrum. Any peaks in the mass spectrum of the unknown compound that are not in the library spectrum are disregarded.

12560.title: RF-only quadrupole
12560.definition: Transmission quadrupole device in which a sinusoidal radio frequency (RF) potential is applied between the connected pairs of opposite rod electrodes in a linear quadrupole, providing a transmission device for all ions with m/z values above a cut-off value.

12561.title: ring and double bond equivalent
12561.definition: Conventional measure of the degree of unsaturation of an organic molecule given by \(X - Y/2 + Z/2 + 1\) where \(X\) is the number of carbon atoms, \(Y\) is the number of hydrogen or halogen atoms and \(Z\) is the number of nitrogen and phosphorus atoms.

14256.title: row structure
14256.definition: Polycrystalline polymer morphology resulting from nucleation of polymer lamellar crystals by multiple fibrillar structures or by macroscopic linear objects such as fibers.

13425.title: residential macrophage
13425.definition: Macrophage stationed at a point where microbial invasion or accumulation of dust is likely to occur.

09586.title: r diad
