09586.definition: Pair of adjacent constitutionally equivalent stereogenic units that are of unlike configuration. Figure 2: Diagrammatic representations of the configurational repeating unit or stereorepeating unit (upper), and the diad sequence (lower) for isotactic poly(oxypropylene), both as a rotated Fischer projections (left) and as a zigzag projection (right). [image2]

11506.title: R-group decomposition
11506.definition:
The process whereby the molecules in a dataset are partitioned into the core ('scaffold'), usually user-specified, and the specific substituents ('R-groups')
 found at each specific position.

15005.title: r-strategy
15005.definition: Opportunistic strategy favoring species that establish themselves quickly, grow quickly to exploit as many resources as possible, and produce many offspring.

R05423.title: R, S
R05423.definition: The approved designations (devised by Cahn, Ingold and Prelog) of absolute configuration at four-coordinate (quadriligant) and six-coordinate (sexiligant) stereogenic centres.

11499.title: r2
11499.definition: The ratio of the sum of squares explained by a regression model (SSR) to the 'total' sum of squares around the mean (SST), or, because SST equals SSR plus the sum of squares of the error or residuals from the fit (SSE): \[R^{2} = \frac{{\rm{SSR}}}{{\rm{SST}}} = 1 - \frac{{\rm{SSE}}}{{\rm{SST}}}\]

R05023.title: rabbit
R05023.definition: A small container propelled pneumatically or hydraulically through a tube leading from the laboratory to a location in a nuclear reactor or other device where irradiation of a sample can take place.

R05025.title: racemate
R05025.definition: An equimolar mixture of a pair of enantiomers. It does not exhibit optical activity. The chemical name or formula of a racemate is distinguished from those of the enantiomers by the prefix (±)- or rac- (or racem-) or by the symbols RS and SR.

R05027.title: racemic compound
R05027.definition: A crystalline racemate in which the two enantiomers are present in equal amounts in a well defined arrangement within the lattice of a homogeneous crystalline addition compound.

R05028.title: racemic conglomerate
R05028.definition: An equimolar mechanical mixture of crystals each one of which contains only one of the two enantiomers present in a racemate. The process of its formation on crystallization of a racemate is called spontaneous resolution, since pure or nearly pure enantiomers can often be obtained from the conglomerate by sorting.

R05029.title: racemic mixture
R05029.definition: The term is confusing since it has been used as a synonym for both racemate and racemic conglomerate. Usage strongly discouraged.

R05030.title: racemization
R05030.definition: The production of a racemate from a chiral starting material in which one enantiomer is present in excess.

11162.title: rachischisis
11162.definition: Failure of the neural tube to close in utero, resulting in a birth defect that leaves a fissure in the vertebral column with part of the spinal cord exposed.

R05032.title: rad
R05032.definition: Non-SI unit of absorbed dose of radiation, \(\rm{rad} = 0.01\ \rm{Gy}\).

12040.title: radial arm maze
12040.definition: Apparatus with a central platform and equidistant arms (usually eight), at the end of which is a reward (e.g., a food pellet).

R05034.title: radial electrostatic field analyser
R05034.definition: An arrangement of two conducting sheets forming a capacitor and giving a radial electrostatic field which is used to deflect and focus ion beams of different energies. The capacitor may be cylindrical, spherical, or toroidal.

R05035.title: radial elution
R05035.definition: A mode of operation in which the sample is spotted at a point source at or near the middle of the plane and is carried outward in a circle by the mobile phase, also applied at that place.

13629.title: radial immunodiffusion
13629.definition: Method for quantifying an antigen by measuring the diameters of circular precipitates around an antigen-spiked cavity in an antibody-containing agar gel.

09272.title: radial sectioning
09272.definition: Sample preparation in which a sample is polished by a cylinder in order to expose compositional changes below the original sample surface, with the intent that the depth of these layers can be related to the position on the surface created by the cylinder.

08535.title: radial viewing mode
08535.definition: Inductively-coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer configuration in which the plasma and the entrance slit are perpendicular and from which the signal is taken perpendicularly to the main plasma axis.

R05036.title: radian
R05036.definition: SI derived unit of plane angle, \(\rm{rad} = 1\).

R05037.title: radiance
R05037.definition: Radiant power, \(P\), leaving or passing through a small transparent element of surface in a given direction from the source about the solid angle \(\varOmega\), divided by the solid angle and by the orthogonally projected area of the element in a plane normal to the given beam direction, \(\rm{d}S_{\perp } = \rm{d}S\, \rm{cos}\,\theta\)

14064.title: radiant dose
14064.definition: Radiant energy (\(Q\), SI unit is \(\pu{J}\)) or amount of photons (in \(\pu{mol}\) or the non-SI unit einstein) absorbed per area or volume by an object irradiated during a given exposure time.

R05040.title: radiant energy density
R05040.definition: Radiant energy divided by the volume.

R05039.title: radiant energy
R05039.definition: The total energy emitted, transferred or received as radiation in a defined period of time (\(Q=\int Q_{\lambda }  \ \mathrm{d}\lambda \)). It is the product of radiant power, \(P\), and time, \(t\): \(Q=P\ t\) when the radiant power is constant over the time considered.

R05041.title: radiant exitance
R05041.definition: Radiant power, \(P\), emitted at all wavelengths by an element of surface containing the source point under consideration divided by the area of the source. SI unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-2}\).

R05042.title: radiant exposure
R05042.definition: Radiant energy, \(Q\), incident from all upward directions on a small sphere divided by the cross-sectional area of that sphere. SI unit is \(\pu{J m-2}\).

R05045.title: radiant intensity
R05045.definition: Radiant power, \(P\), at all wavelengths per solid angle, \(\varOmega\). The @R05046-2@ emitted in a given direction by a source or an element of the source in a small cone containing the given direction divided by the solid angle of the cone. SI unit is \(\rm{W sr}^{-1}\).

R05046.title: radiant power
R05046.definition: Power emitted, transferred or received as radiation. SI unit is \(\pu{J s-1} = \pu{W}\).

R05047.title: radiant quantities
R05047.definition: Group of quantities characterizing electromagnetic radiation in terms of energy. The symbols of radiant quantities may be distinguished by adding a subscript e.

R05048.title: radiation
R05048.definition: A term embracing electromagnetic waves as well as fast moving particles. In radioanalytical chemistry the term usually refers to radiation emitted during a nuclear process (radioactive decay, nuclear reaction, nuclear fission, accelerators).

14066.title: radiation adsorption
14066.definition: The word combination may be misleading. Usually radiation is absorbed.

14067.title: radiation catalysis
14067.definition: Change in the rate of a chemical reaction under the action of ionising radiation in the presence of a radiation catalyst.

14068.title: radiation catalyst
14068.definition: Substance absorbing ionising radiation and able to produce chemical transformations of the reaction partners, repeatedly producing intermediate transformations and regenerating its chemical composition after each cycle of such interactions.

R05050.title: radiation chemistry
R05050.definition: The part of chemistry which deals with the chemical effects of ionizing radiation, as distinguished from photochemistry associated with visible and ultraviolet electromagnetic radiation.

R05051.title: radiation constants
R05051.definition: Fundamental physical constants characterizing black body radiation. The first radiation constant is \(c_{1} = 2\ \pi \ h\ c_{0}^{2}=3.741\,7749(22)\times 10^{-16}\ \rm{W m}^{2}\), the second is \(c_{2} = \frac{h\ c_{0}}{k}=1.438\,769(12)\times 10^{-2}\ \rm{m K}\), where \(h\) is the Planck constant \(c_{0}\) the speed of light and \(k\) the Boltzmann constant.

R05052.title: radiation continuum
R05052.definition: Continuous (in the wavelength, not time sense) radiation arising for example from non-quantized free-free transitions of electrons in the fields of the ions, free-bound transitions or radiative recombinations of electrons and ions, incandescent radiation emitted by hot solids (when the radiation distribution conforms to that described by Planck's law, it is considered black-body radiation) and unresolvable band spectra, i.e. where the spectral lines are wider than the spacings between them.

R05053.title: radiation counter
R05053.definition: Radiation measuring assembly comprising a radiation detector in which individual ionizing events cause electrical pulses and the associated equipment for processing and counting the pulses. Often an expression is added indicating the type of radiation detector (e.g. scintillation, semiconductor).

08402.title: radiation damping
08402.definition: Line-broadening effect on intense signals in high field nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

14070.title: radiation desorption
14070.definition: Desorption from solid or liquid interfaces induced by absorption of radiation by the solid or liquid adsorbent.

R05054.title: radiation detector
R05054.definition: A device in which incident radiation produces a measurable effect. If this effect is a rise in temperature it is called a thermal detector. If it is a rise in pressure it is called a photoacoustic detector. In the case where an electrical signal is produced it is called a photoelectric detector. Photoelectric detectors can be classified as photo-emissive detectors and semiconductor detectors. Where the radiation produces a chemical reaction, it is termed a photochemical detector. A detector yielding an output signal that is independent of the wavelength of the radiation over a specific region is called a nonselective detector. Where it is wavelength specific it is a selective detector. A detector having a quantum efficiency independent of the wavelength is a nonselective quantum counter. Certain detectors are able to distinguish between different quantum energies. This property is described by the energy resolution \(\Delta E\) and the energy resolving power \(\frac{E}{\Delta E}\). These detectors are called energy dispersive detectors. In X-ray spectroscopy, the reciprocal \(\frac{\Delta E}{E}\) is often used but this is discouraged.

08757.title: radiation filter
08757.definition: Material interposed in the path of radiation to modify the energy distribution of the radiation.

R05055.title: radiation hazard
R05055.definition: Hazard that exists in a region where there is a radiation field, other than what is considered to be normal background radiation.

RT07149.title: radiation reaction
RT07149.definition: Chemical reaction that is induced by ionizing radiation with $\upgamma\!\mbox{-}\rm{ray}$, X-ray, electron, or other high-energy beams.

14073.title: radiation sensitisation
14073.definition: Chemical change or physical process occurring in one entity (e.g., biological molecules, cells, and living organisms) as a result of initial absorption of high-energy radiation by the medium in the presence of another entity called the radiation sensitiser.

14074.title: radiation sensitiser
14074.definition: Chemical substance that increases the radiation sensitivity of, in particular, biological molecules, cells and biological organisms.

R05059.title: radiation spectrum
R05059.definition: The components of radiation arranged in order of their wavelengths, frequencies or quantum energies. For particle radiation they are arranged in order of their kinetic energies.

14076.title: radiation thermal catalysis
14076.definition: Radiation catalysis under the action of large radiation fluxes that simultaneously heat the system as a consequence of absorption of energy from radiationless deactivation.

16018.title: radiation toxicology
16018.definition: Scientific study involving research, education, prevention, and treatment of diseases caused by ionizing or nonionizing radiation.

RT07470.title: radiation trapping
RT07470.definition: Process by which the resonance radiation emitted in a lamp is absorbed and re-emitted many times in the plasma prior to striking the phosphor. This process is called radiation trapping or imprisonment.

14065.title: radiation-activation
14065.definition: Increasing of catalytic activity or alteration of selectivity of a substance after its exposure to high-energy radiation.

14069.title: radiation-chemical yield
14069.definition: Number of entities of a product formed (alternatively, the number of entities of a reactant disappearing) generated per \(\pu{100 eV}\) of energy absorbed from ionising radiation.

14071.title: radiation-generated catalysis
14071.definition: Initiation of chemical transformations through the formation, by absorption of high-energy radiation, of substances that are catalytically active even in the absence of the radiation.

14072.title: radiation-induced adsorption
14072.definition: Adsorption of a molecular entity at solid or liquid interfaces induced by absorption of high-energy radiation by the solid or the liquid adsorbent.

14075.title: radiation-stimulated diffusion
14075.definition: Increase of diffusion of an adsorbate under the action of ionising radiation absorbed by either the adsorbent and/or the adsorbate.

R05056.title: radiationless deactivation
R05056.definition: Loss of electronic excitation energy without photon emission or chemical change. Often, ultrafast radiationless decays are mediated by conical intersections.

R05057.title: radiationless transition
R05057.definition: A transition between two states of a system without photon emission or absorption.

R05060.title: radiative absorption
R05060.definition: A process by which a particle in the ground state or an excited state may undergo transition to a higher energy level by absorption of a photon. For a given particle in the lower state of probability per second of such a transition in a field with a continuous spectrum is proportional to the spectral radiant energy density of the absorption line. The proportionality constant is termed the transition probability for absorption. The transition probability for stimulated emission is defined in a similar way for the reverse radiative de-excitation process that is induced by the same radiation field.

R05061.title: radiative capture
R05061.definition: Capture of a particle by a nucleus followed by immediate emission of gamma radiation.

08864.title: radiative charge carrier recombination
08864.definition: Charge carrier recombination in which the energy released is emitted as a photon of corresponding energy.

R05062.title: radiative de-excitation
R05062.definition: The change in the internal energy of a particle may be due to radiative processes, i.e. the emission or absorption of a photon. A particle in an excited state may undergo a transition to a lower energy level by emission of a photon. This is known as radiative de-excitation. If such a transition occurs spontaneously its probability per second for a given excited particle is termed the transition probability for spontaneous emission.

R05063.title: radiative energy transfer
R05063.definition: Transfer of excitation energy by radiative deactivation of a donor molecular entity and reabsorption of the emitted radiation by an acceptor molecular entity.

R05064.title: radiative lifetime
R05064.definition: Lifetime of an excited molecular entity in the absence of radiationless transitions. The reciprocal of the first-order rate constant for the radiative step, or the reciprocal of the sum of these rate constants if there is more than one such step. The equivalent term, natural lifetime, is discouraged.

14077.title: radiative transfer equation
14077.definition: When a photon beam of radiance \(L_{\lambda}\) and angular distribution \(\mathit{\Omega}\) passes along a single direction of propagation through a medium, which is totally absorbing and/or scattering, i.e., the processes occurring are described by the following equation: \[\begin{array} \\ \frac{{\rm{d}}L_{\Omega,\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}{{\rm{d}}s} + \underbrace{\alpha_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t) L_{\mathit{\Omega},\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}_{\rm{adsorption}} + \underbrace{\sigma_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t) L_{\mathit{\Omega},\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}_{\rm{out\mbox{-}scattering}} = \\ \underbrace{j_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}_{\rm{emission}} + \underbrace{\frac{\sigma_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}{4\pi}B_{\lambda}(\mathit{\Omega}' \to \mathit{\Omega}) L_{\mathit{\Omega},\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t){\rm{d}}\mathit{\Omega}'}_{\rm{in\mbox{-}scattering}} \end{array}\] where \(\frac{{\rm{d}}L_{\Omega,\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}{{\rm{d}}s}\) is the directional derivative along the direction \(s\) at a point \(\boldsymbol{x}\) in the reaction space of the incident radiance, \(\alpha_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)\) is the space- and time-dependent spectral linear napierian absorption coefficient, \(\sigma_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)\) is the space- and time-dependent spectral linear napierian scattering coefficient, \(j_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)\) represents the spontaneous and/or induced emission, and \(B_{\lambda}\) is the phase function. All quantities are a function of time. The RTE is written for the direction \(s\).

R05065.title: radiative transition
R05065.definition: A transition between two states of a molecular entity, the energy difference being emitted or absorbed as photons. In principle, radiative and radiationless transitions can be distinguished in molecules. The first occur by absorption or emission of light quanta, and the latter is the result of the transformation of electronic excitation energy into vibrational/rotational energy.

R05066.title: radical
R05066.definition: A molecular entity such as $\ce{^{.}CH3}$, $\ce{^{.}SnH3}$, $\ce{Cl^{.}}$ possessing an unpaired electron. (In these formulae the dot, symbolizing the unpaired electron, should be placed so as to indicate the atom of highest spin density, if this is possible.) Paramagnetic metal ions are not normally regarded as radicals. However, in the 'isolobal analogy' the similarity between certain paramagnetic metal ions and radicals becomes apparent. At least in the context of physical organic chemistry, it seems desirable to cease using the adjective 'free' in the general name of this type of chemical species and molecular entity, so that the term 'free radical' may in future be restricted to those radicals which do not form parts of radical pairs. Depending upon the core atom that possesses the unpaired electron, the radicals can be described as carbon-, oxygen-, nitrogen-, metal-centered radicals. If the unpaired electron occupies an orbital having considerable s or more or less pure p character, the respective radicals are termed $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}}$ or $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}radicals}$. In the past, the term 'radical' was used to designate a substituent group bound to a molecular entity, as opposed to 'free radical', which nowadays is simply called radical. The bound entities may be called groups or substituents, but should no longer be called radicals.

R05069.title: radical centre
R05069.definition: The atom (or group of atoms) in a polyatomic radical on which an unpaired electron is largely localized. attachment of a monovalent atom to a radical centre gives a molecule for which it is possible to write a Lewis formula in which the normal stable valencies are assigned to all atoms.

R05071.title: radical copolymerization
R05071.definition: A copolymerization which is a radical polymerization.

14370.title: radical entry
14370.definition: Irreversible transport of a radical from the continuous to the dispersed phase.

14371.title: radical entry frequency
14371.definition: Average number of entry events per particle per unit interval of time.

14372.title: radical exit
14372.definition: Reversible or irreversible transport of a radical from the dispersed to the continuous phase.

14373.title: radical exit frequency
14373.definition: Average number of exit events per particle per unit interval of time per radical.

R05073.title: radical ion
R05073.definition: A radical that carries an electric charge. A positively charged radical is called a 'radical cation' (e.g. the benzene radical cation $\ce{C6H6^{.+}}$); a negatively charged radical is called a 'radical anion' (e.g. the benzene radical anion $\ce{C6H^{.−}}$ or the benzophenone radical anion $\ce{Ph2C–O^{.−}}$). Commonly, but not necessarily, the odd electron and the charge are associated with the same atom. Unless the positions of unpaired spin and charge can be associated with specific atoms, superscript dot and charge designations should be placed in the order $\ce{^{.+}}$ or $\ce{^{.-}}$ suggested by the name 'radical ion'. (e.g. $\ce{C3H6^{.+}}$).

R05074.title: radical pair
R05074.definition: The term is used to identify two radicals in close proximity in solution, within a solvent cage. They may be formed simultaneously by some unimolecular process, e.g. peroxide decomposition, or they may have come together by diffusion. While the radicals are together, correlation of the unpaired electron spins of the two species cannot be ignored: this correlation is responsible for the CIDNP phenomenon. A radical pair is called geminate provided that each radical partner is a descendant of the same parental pair.

RT07471.title: radical photosubstitution
RT07471.definition: Photo-induced substitution resulting from the reaction of radicals produced by photolysis of an appropriate reagent, such as, e.g., halogenated compounds.

R05075.title: radical polymerization
R05075.definition: A chain polymerization in which the kinetic-chain carriers are radicals.

15417.title: radical reactivity scale
15417.definition: Scale of the values of the rate constants for the reaction of radicals with a reference monomer.

08915.title: radical ring-opening polymerization
08915.definition: Radical polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

12041.title: radiculitis
12041.definition: Inflammation of the spinal nerve roots leading to pain and hyperesthesia radiating along the nerve.

R05077.title: radioactive
R05077.definition: The property of a nuclide of undergoing spontaneous nuclear transformations with the emission of radiation.

R05078.title: radioactive age
R05078.definition: The time, estimated from measurement of the isotopic composition, during which the content of a radioactive species within an object has remained unchanged except for nuclear decay.

R05080.title: radioactive contamination
R05080.definition: A radioactive substance in a material or place where it is undesirable.

R05081.title: radioactive cooling
R05081.definition: Of a strongly radioactive material, the decrease of its activity by nuclear decay.

R05082.title: radioactive dating
R05082.definition: The determination of the radioactive age of an object from its content of radioactive substances and of their daughter products.

R05083.title: radioactive decay
R05083.definition: Nuclear decay in which particles or electromagnetic radiation are emitted or the nucleus undergoes spontaneous fission or electron capture.

R05084.title: radioactive equilibrium
R05084.definition: Among the members of a decay chain, the state which prevails when the ratios between the activities of successive members remain constant. (This is not an equilibrium in the strict sense since radioactive decay is an irreversible process).

R05085.title: radioactive fallout
R05085.definition: The deposition on the ground of radioactive substances from nuclear explosions and other injections of radioactive material into the atmosphere.

R05088.title: radioactive source
R05088.definition: Any quantity of radioactive material which is intended for use as a source of ionizing radiation.

08758.title: radioactive steady state
08758.definition: Among the radionuclides of a decay chain, the state that prevails when the ratios between the activities of successive radionuclides remain constant.

R05089.title: radioactive tracer
R05089.definition: A tracer containing a radioactive label.

R05090.title: radioactive tracer technique
R05090.definition: A technique for investigating recovery and loss of a microcomponent, in which a radioactively-labelled element or compound chemically identical with the microcomponent is added to the sample before preconcentration and its behaviour is followed by sensitive, rapid and selective radioactivity measurements.

R05091.title: radioactive waste
R05091.definition: Unwanted radioactive materials obtained in the processing or handling of radioactive materials.

R05092.title: radioactivity
R05092.definition: The property of certain nuclides showing radioactive decay.

13630.title: radioallergosorbent test
13630.definition: Solid-phase radioimmunoassay (RIA) for detecting immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibody specific for a particular antigen.

R05094.title: radiochemical activation analysis
R05094.definition: A kind of activation analysis in which, after the irradiation, chemical or physical separation is applied.

R05095.title: radiochemical purification
R05095.definition: Chemical separation applied to a radioactive preparation in order to improve the radiochemical purity.

R05096.title: radiochemical purity
R05096.definition: For a material, the fraction of the stated isotope present in the stated chemical form.

R05097.title: radiochemical separation
R05097.definition: Separation by a chemical means of the radioactive isotopes of a specific element from a mixture of radionuclides.

R05098.title: radiochemical yield
R05098.definition: The yield of a radiochemical separation expressed as a fraction of the activity originally present.

R05099.title: radiochemistry
R05099.definition: That part of chemistry which deals with radioactive materials. It includes the production of radionuclides and their compounds by processing irradiated materials or naturally occurring radioactive materials, the application of chemical techniques to nuclear studies, and the application of radioactivity to the investigation of chemical, biochemical or biomedical problems.

R05100.title: radiochromatograph
R05100.definition: A measuring assembly designed to measure the spatial or time distribution of the activity of a mixture of radioactive components after separation by a chromatographic method.

R05101.title: radiocolloid
R05101.definition: A colloid in which some atoms are radioactive.

R05102.title: radioenzymatic assay
R05102.definition: An assay of the catalytic activity of an enzyme based on the use of a radioactive substrate.

08279.title: radiofrequency
08279.definition: Frequency or band of frequencies in the range \(\pu{E4}\) to \(\pu{E12 Hz}\).

08403.title: radiofrequency coil
08403.definition: In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, an inductor-capacitor resonant circuit used to set up \(B_{1}\) magnetic inductions in a sample and to detect the signal from the sample.

08536.title: radiofrequency generator
08536.definition: Component of an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer responsible for the generation of alternating current in the radiofrequency portion of the electromagnetic spectrum (see table).

08537.title: radiofrequency glow discharge optical emission spectroscopy
08537.definition: Optical emission spectroscopy in which a radiofrequency-powered glow discharge is operated with frequencies in the low megahertz range.

R05103.title: radiograph
R05103.definition: A visual representation of an object produced by placing the object between a source of ionizing radiation and a photographic plate or film.

R05104.title: radiogravimetric analysis
R05104.definition: A kind of quantitative analysis in which the activity of a precipitate is used as a measure of its mass.

R05105.title: radioimmunoassay
R05105.definition: An assay based on the reversible and non-covalent binding of an antigen (hapten) by a specific antibody employing radioactivity labelled antigen (hapten) to measure the fraction of the antigen (hapten) bound to a substoichiometric amount of antibody.

13631.title: radioimmunoconjugate
13631.definition: Biochemical conjugate consisting of an immune-targeting molecule such as an antibody or antibody fragment together with a cytotoxic radionuclide.

R05107.title: radioiodination
R05107.definition: The process of incorporating the radionuclides of iodine (usually $\ce{^{125}I}$, $\ce{^{131}I}$ or $\ce{^{123}I}$) into, or of covalently linking a radioiodinated substance to, a substance.

R05108.title: radioisotope
R05108.definition: A radioactive isotope of a specified element.

R05109.title: radioisotope dilution analysis
R05109.definition: A kind of isotope dilution analysis making use of a radionuclide.

R05110.title: radioisotope induced X-ray emission analysis
R05110.definition: A kind of analysis based on the measurement of the energies and intensities of characteristic X-radiation emitted by a test portion during irradiation with a radioactive source.

14185.title: radioligand
14185.definition: Ligand into which a radioisotope has been incorporated as a label.

R05111.title: radioluminescence
R05111.definition: Luminescence arising from excitation by high-energy particles or radiation.

R05112.title: radiolysis
R05112.definition: The cleavage of one or several bonds resulting from exposure to high-energy radiation. The term is also often used loosely to specify the method of irradiation ('pulse radiolysis') used in any radiochemical reaction, not necessarily one involving bond cleavage.

R05113.title: radiometric analysis
R05113.definition: A kind of quantitative analysis in which measurement of the activity is an essential step.

R05114.title: radiometric titration
R05114.definition: A titration in which a radioactive indicator is used to monitor the end-point of the titration.

R05115.title: radiometry
R05115.definition: The measurement of quantities associated with radiant energy. The quantities may also describe the variation of the energy with respect to other variables such as wavelength, time, position, direction (solid angle), area normal to the light or projected area of emitting or receiving surfaces. If the light is monochromatic, it is sometimes convenient to replace the radiant energy by the corresponding number of photons (or quanta) which is obtained by dividing the energy by \(\frac{h\ c}{\lambda }\) where \(h\) is the Planck constant, \(c\) the velocity of light and \(\lambda \) the wavelength of the light.

R05117.title: radionuclidic purity
R05117.definition: For a material, that fraction of the total activity which is present in the form of the stated radionuclide, including daughter products.

R05118.title: radioreceptor assay
R05118.definition: An assay employing a radioactively labelled receptor protein as a tracer.

R05119.title: radiorelease analysis
R05119.definition: A kind of quantitative analysis based on the release of radioactivity from the reagent by reaction with the analyte.

R05120.title: radiosonde
R05120.definition: A miniature radio transmitter with instruments in a package that is carried aloft (e.g. by an unmanned balloon) for broadcasting every few seconds by means of precise tone signals or other suitable method, the humidity, temperature, pressure or other parameter.

R05121.title: radius of gyration

R05122.title: raffinate
R05122.definition: The phase remaining after extraction of some specified solute(s). When necessary it should be further specified, e.g. scrub raffinate. The original meaning of raffinate as a 'refined product' has become extended and changed by common usage. The term should normally be applied only to waste streams but the latter may form the feed to a further extraction process for another solute.

R05123.title: rain out
R05123.definition: The mechanism by which small particles in the clouds are removed by the formation of raindrops; this is a different mechanism from wash out which is a process which occurs below cloud level. Both the terms rain out and wash out have not always been used in accordance with these definitions. For clarity they should be replaced by the terms, in-cloud scavenging and below-cloud scavenging, respectively.

14968.title: rain-out
14968.definition: Removal of pollutants from air by incorporation into developing rain droplets of rain clouds.

08666.title: Raman optical activity
08666.definition: Phenomenon that vibrations in chiral molecules and materials Raman scattering right circularly polarized incident radiation to a different extent than left circularly polarized incident radiation.

08667.title: Raman scattering
08667.definition: Inelastic scattering of electromagnetic radiation by molecules that are excited to higher energy levels.

08668.title: Raman shift
08668.definition: Difference in wavenumber between the incident and scattered electromagnetic radiation in Raman spectroscopy.

08669.title: Raman spectroscopy
08669.definition: Measurement principle of vibrational spectroscopy based on Raman scattering.

08670.title: Raman spectrum
08670.definition: Graph of the intensity of scattered electromagnetic radiation in Raman spectroscopy against Raman shift.

08671.title: Raman wavenumber shift
08671.definition: Wavenumber of exciting electromagnetic radiation minus wavenumber of the scattered radiation.

09143.title: Randles–Ševčík equations
09143.definition:
Equations describing the peak current \(I_{m{p}}\) in linear scan voltammetry and cyclic voltammetry as a function of the amount concentration, \(c_{m{0}}\), of electroactive species in bulk solution. For a reversible charge transfer: \[I_{m{p,rev}} = k\,z\,F\,A\,c_0 (z\,F\,D
u/RT)^{1/2}\] for irreversible charge transfer: \[I_{m{p,irrev}} = k^{\prime}(\alpha z^{\prime})^{1/2} zFA{c_0}(FD
u/RT)^{1/2}\] where \(k\) and \(k^{\prime}\) are numerical constants, \(\alpha\) is the charge transfer coefficient (usually assumed to be close to 0.5), \(z\) the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, \(z^{\prime}\) the number of electrons transferred before the rate determining step, \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(R\) the gas constant, \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature, \(A\) the electrode surface area, \(D\) the diffusion coefficient, and \(
u\) the scan rate.

R05124.title: random coil
R05124.definition: The complete set of spatial arrangements of a chain molecule with a large number of segments that randomly change mutual orientation with time, under conditions in which it is free from external constraints that would affect its conformation. If the solution of the chain molecules is not in a theta state, the segments change mutual orientation only approximately randomly. Synonymous with statistical coil.

R05125.title: random coincidence
R05125.definition: A coincidence of events occurring in not physically connected nuclei.

R05126.title: random copolymer
R05126.definition: A copolymer consisting of macromolecules in which the probability of finding a given monomeric unit at any given site in the chain is independent of the nature of the adjacent units.

R05127.title: random copolymerization
R05127.definition: A copolymerization in which a random copolymer is formed.

R05128.title: random error
R05128.definition: Result of a measurement minus the mean that would result from an infinite number of measurements of the same measurand carried out under repeatability conditions.

11500.title: random forest method
11500.definition:
A classification method that produces many recursive partitioning models, each with a random selection of predictor properties, and then combines the models
 for predictions.

09379.title: random incidence spectrum
09379.definition: Backscattering spectrum recorded with the analysing beam incident on the sample in a direction such as to produce no channelling.

R05129.title: random sample
R05129.definition: The sample so selected that any portion of the population has an equal (or known) chance of being chosen. Haphazard or arbitrary choice of units is generally insufficient to guarantee randomness.

10057.title: random sampling
10057.definition: Sampling in which the sample locations are selected randomly from the whole population.

R05130.title: range
R05130.definition: The difference between the highest and lowest members of a series. This term is not recommended.

R05134.title: range of measurement
R05134.definition: The range of concentration between the measurement threshold and the maximum usable indication.

09273.title: range straggling
09273.definition: Standard deviation of the projected ranges of energetic ions or atoms of a given energy.

15349.title: Raoult’s law
15349.definition: Fugacity (\(\tilde{p}_{\ce{B}}\)) of a gaseous component (\(\ce{B}\)) in equilibrium with a liquid or solid mixture containing \(\ce{B}\) is directly proportional to the activity (\(a_{\ce{B}}\)) of the component in the mixture \[\tilde{p}_{\ce{B}} = \tilde{p}_{\ce{B}}^{\ast} f_{\ce{B}} x_{\ce{B}}\] where \(f_{\ce{B}}\) is the activity coefficient of \(\ce{B}\) referenced to Raoult’s law at mole fraction \(x_{\ce{B}}\) and \(\tilde{p}_{\ce{B}}\) is the fugacity of pure \(\ce{B}\).

08672.title: rapid-scan Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
08672.definition: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy in which the optical path difference is continually changed at a rate of \(\pu{0.05 cm s-1}\) or greater.

09008.title: rare-earth-metal-mediated coordination-addition polymerization
09008.definition: Coordination-addition polymerization with propagation occurring within the coordination sphere of a rare-earth metal complex.

14969.title: rarefaction estimate of richness
14969.definition: Estimate of species richness (\(S\)) expressed relative to that of a sample having a standard number of individuals.

09274.title: raster
09274.definition: Two-dimensional pattern generated by the deflection of a primary beam.

09562.title: raster scan
09562.definition: Rectangular pattern of line-by-line scanning for image capture used in electron beam and ion-beam lithography.

R05136.title: rate
R05136.definition: Derived quantity in which time is a denominator quantity. Rate of \(x\) is \(\frac{\rm{d}x}{\rm{d}t}\).

14970.title: rate constant-based model
14970.definition: Compartment model that employs rate constants to quantify the rate of change in concentration or amount of toxicant.

R05141.title: rate law
R05141.definition: An expression for the rate of reaction of a particular reaction in terms of concentrations of chemical species and constant parameters (normally rate coefficients and partial orders of reaction) only. For examples of rate laws see equations (1)-(3) under kinetic equivalence, and (1) under steady state.

R05144.title: rate of change of a quantity
R05144.definition: The time derivative \(\frac{\rm{d}Q}{\rm{d}t}\) of the value of the quantity. The differential quotient may also be called derivative (or instantaneous) rate of change. Examples are: rate of change of mass, \(\frac{\rm{d}m}{\rm{d}t}\); rate of change of amount of substance, \(\frac{\rm{d}n}{\rm{d}t}\).

R05145.title: rate of change ratio
R05145.definition: The quotient of two rates where the quantities are of the same kind in the same system for different components: \[\frac{\rm{d}Q_{1}/\rm{d}t}{\rm{d}Q_{2}/\rm{d}t}\] For finite time intervals, mean rate of change ratio is: \[\frac{\Delta Q_{1}/\Delta t}{\Delta Q_{2}/\Delta t}=\frac{\Delta Q_{1}}{\Delta Q_{2}}\ \Delta t\] Rate of change ratio has the dimension one. The denominator is often called the reference quantity. Examples are: mass rate ratio, \(\frac{\rm{d}m_{1}/\rm{d}t}{\rm{d}m_{2}/\rm{d}t}\); amount of substance rate ratio, \(\frac{\rm{d}n_{1}/\rm{d}t}{\rm{d}n_{2}/\rm{d}t}\).

R05146.title: rate of consumption
R05146.definition:
The rate of consumption of a specified reactant may be defined in two ways:As the negative of the time derivative of the amount of reactant; thus for a reactant B, present at any time in amount \(n_{m{B}}\), the rate of its consumption may be defined as: \[
u (n_{m{B}}) = - rac{m{d}n_{m{B}}}{m{d}t}\] This definition is particularly appropriate for open systems. Here and elsewhere, when a rate is defined in terms of a time derivative, it must be understood that the definition relates to the process occurring in isolation. In a flow system there may be no actual changes with time, and the time derivative must be inferred. Such an inference is also required for a reaction occurring by a composite mechanism.For kinetics in closed systems it is more usual to define a rate of consumption per unit volume; thus for a reactant B the rate of consumption, \(
u (c_{m{B}}) \) is given by: \[
u (c_{m{B}}) = - rac{1}{V} rac{m{d}n_{m{B}}}{m{d}t}\] When the volume \(V\) is constant this reduces to: \[
u (c_{m{B}}) = - rac{m{d[B]}}{m{d}t}\] When the volume is not constant the relationship \(n_{m{B}} = [m{B}]V\) may be differentiated to give: \[{m{d}}c_{m{B}} = Vm{d[B]} + m{[B]d}V\] and therefore: \[
u (c_{m{B}}) = - rac{m{d[B]}}{m{d}t} -  rac{m{[B]}}{V} rac{m{d}V}{m{d}t}\] In contrast to the rate of conversion and the rate of reaction, the rate of consumption of a reactant may be specified even for a reaction of time-dependent stoichiometry or of unknown stoichiometry. The rate of consumption of a reactant is often called its rate of disappearance. However, the former expression is to be preferred since the word disappearance is not appropriately translatable into certain languages. When English is used the word disappearance might be reserved for cases where the reactant is almost completely removed.

R05147.title: rate of conversion
R05147.definition: The rate of conversion for a reaction occurring in a closed system is defined as the time derivative of the extent of reaction: \[\overset{\rm{.}}{\xi }=\frac{\mathrm{d}\xi }{\mathrm{d}t}\] In view of the definition of extent of reaction it follows that with reference to any species in a reaction showing time-independent stoichiometry \[\overset{\rm{.}}{\xi }=\frac{\mathrm{d}\xi }{\mathrm{d}t}=\frac{1}{\nu _{i}}\ \frac{\mathrm{d}n_{i}}{\mathrm{d}t}\] where \(n_{i}\) is the amount of the species at any time and \(\nu _{i}\) is its stoichiometric coefficient.

09144.title: rate of flow of liquid metal in polarography
09144.definition: Mass of a drop of liquid metal in polarography at the instant when it is detached from the tip of the capillary divided by the drop time \(t_{\rm{d}}\).

R05151.title: rate of fluid consumption
R05151.definition: The volume of fluid consumed by the nebulizer divided by time (in \(\unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{L}\ \rm{s}^{-1}\)). Volume rate has also been called volume flow, flux, aspiration rate, aspiration flow or aspiration flux. The fluid consumed is either aspirated or injected. The volume rate of fluid consumption by nebulizers is usually between \(10\) and \(100\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{L}\ \rm{s}^{-1}\).

R05152.title: rate of formation
R05152.definition:
Like the rate of consumption, the rate of formation of a specified product may be defined in two ways:As the time derivative of the amount of a product. Thus for a product $\ce{Y}$, present at any time in amount \(n_{m{Y}}\). the rate of its formation may be given by: \[
u (n_{m{Y}}) =  rac{m{d}n_{m{Y}}}{m{d}t}\] This definition is particularly appropriate for open systems.For kinetics in closed systems it is more usual to define a rate of formation per unit volume, denoted \(
u (c_{m{Y}}) \): \[
u (c_{m{Y}}) =  rac{1}{V} rac{m{d}n_{m{Y}}}{m{d}t}\] When the volume is constant this reduces to: \[
u (c_{m{Y}}) =  rac{1}{V} rac{m{d}n_{m{Y}}}{m{d}t} =  rac{m{d[Y]}}{m{d}t}\] When the volume is not constant the relationship \(n_{m{Y}} = [m{Y}]V\) may be differentiated to give: \[{m{d}}n_{m{Y}} = Vm{d[Y]} + m{[Y]d}V\] and the rate of formation becomes: \[
u (c_{m{Y}}) =  rac{m{d[Y]}}{m{d}t} +  rac{m{[Y]}}{V} rac{m{d}V}{m{d}t}\] A rate of formation may be specified even for a reaction of time dependent stoichiometry or of unknown stoichiometry.

14078.title: rate of generation
14078.definition: Number of carriers (or electron-hole pairs, or excitons) produced per time interval and per volume of a solid photocatalyst particle due to the absorption of light.

R05153.title: rate of liquid consumption
R05153.definition: The volume of liquid sample that is consumed by the nebulizing system per unit of time.

R05154.title: rate of migration
R05154.definition: The distance of migration divided by time, sometimes called velocity of migration. The symbol \(v\) is also used for velocity.

R05155.title: rate of nucleation
R05155.definition: The number of nuclei formed in unit time per unit volume of the liquid phase.

15418.title: rate of polymerisation
15418.definition: Rate of consumption of monomers in a chain polymerization, or the rate of consumption of the functional groups in the reaction mixture of a polycondensation or polyaddition.

R05156.title: rate of reaction
R05156.definition:
For the general chemical reaction: \[\ce{aA + bB -> pP + qQ + \dots}\] occurring under constant-volume conditions, without an appreciable build-up of reaction intermediates, the rate of reaction \(
u\) is defined as: \[
u = - rac{1}{a} rac{{m{d}}[\ce{A}]}{{m{d}}t} = - rac{1}{b} rac{{m{d}}[\ce{B]}}{{m{d}}t} =  rac{1}{p} rac{{m{d}}[\ce{P]}}{{m{d}}t} =  rac{1}{q} rac{{m{d}}[\ce{Q]}}{{m{d}}t}\] where symbols placed inside square brackets denote amount (or amount of substance) concentrations (conventionally expressed in units of \(\pu{mol dm-3}\)). The symbols \(R\) and \(r\) are also commonly used in place of \(
u\). It is recommended that the unit of time should always be the second. In such a case the rate of reaction differs from the rate of increase of concentration of a product P by a constant factor (the reciprocal of its coefficient in the stoichiometric equation, \(p\)) and from the rate of decrease of concentration of the reactant A by \(\alpha^{-1}\). The quantity: \[\dot{\xi} =  rac{{m{d}}\xi}{{m{d}}t}\] defined by the equation: \[\dot{\xi} = - rac{1}{a}  rac{{m{d}}n_{\ce{A}}}{{m{d}}t} 
= - rac{1}{b}  rac{{m{d}}n_{\ce{B}}}{{m{d}}t} =  rac{1}{p}  rac{{m{d}}n_{\ce{P}}}{{m{d}}t} =  rac{1}{q}  rac{{m{d}}n_{\ce{Q}}}{{m{d}}t}\] (where \(n_{\ce{A}}\) designates the amount of substance A, conventionally expressed in units of mole) may be called the 'rate of conversion' and is appropriate when the use of concentrations is inconvenient, e.g. under conditions of varying volume. In a system of constant volume, the rate of reaction is equal to the rate of conversion per unit volume throughout the reaction. For a stepwise reaction this definition of 'rate of reaction' (and 'extent of reaction', \(\xi \)) will apply only if there is no accumulation of intermediate or formation of side products. It is therefore recommended that the term 'rate of reaction' be used only in cases where it is experimentally established that these conditions apply. More generally, it is recommended that, instead, the terms 'rate of disappearance' or 'rate of consumption' of A (i.e. \(- rac{{m{d}}[\ce{A}]}{{m{d}}t}\), the rate of decrease of concentration of A) or 'rate of appearance' of P (i.e. \( rac{{m{d}}[\ce{P}]}{{m{d}}t}\), the rate of increase of concentration of product P) be used, depending on the concentration change of the particular chemical species that is actually observed. In some cases reference to the chemical flux observed may be more appropriate. The symbol \(
u\) (without lettered subscript) should be used only for rate of reaction; \(
u\) with a lettered subscript (e.g. \(
u_{\ce{A}}\)) refers to a rate of appearance or rate of disappearance (e.g. of the chemical species A).

14079.title: rate of surface recombination
14079.definition: Decay of carriers at the surface of a solid or interface between different phases, e.g., at the crystal surface.

14972.title: rate ratio
14972.definition: Value obtained by dividing the rate in an exposed population by the rate in an unexposed population.

R05139.title: rate-controlling step
R05139.definition:
A rate-controlling (rate-determining or rate-limiting) step in a reaction occurring by a composite reaction sequence is an elementary reaction the rate constant for which exerts a strong effect — stronger than that of any other rate constant — on the overall rate. It is recommended that the expressions rate-controlling, rate-determining and rate-limiting be regarded as synonymous, but some special meanings sometimes given to the last two expressions are considered under a separate heading. A rate-controlling step can be formally defined on the basis of a control function (or control factor) CF, identified for an elementary reaction having a rate constant \(k_{i}\) by: \[m{CF}= rac{\partial (\ln 
u)}{\partial \ln k_{i}}\] where \(
u\) is the overall rate of reaction. In performing the partial differentiation all equilibrium constants \(K_{j}\) and all rate constants except \(k_{i}\) are held constant. The elementary reaction having the largest control factor exerts the strongest influence on the rate \(
u\), and a step having a CF much larger than any other step may be said to be rate-controlling. A rate-controlling step defined in the way recommended here has the advantage that it is directly related to the interpretation of kinetic isotope effects. As formulated this implies that all rate constants are of the same dimensionality. Consider however the reaction of A and B to give an intermediate C, which then reacts further with D to give products:      (1)      (2)   Assuming that C reaches a steady state, then the observed rate is given by: \[
u =  rac{k_{1}\,k_{2}\,\left[m{A}ight]\left[m{B}ight]\left[m{D}ight]}{k_{-1}+k_{2}\left[m{D}ight]}\] Considering \(k_{2}\left[m{D}ight]\) a pseudo-first order rate constant, then \(k_{2}\left[m{D}ight]\gg k_{-1}\), and the observed rate \(
u = k_{1}\ \left[m{A}ight]\left[m{B}ight]\) and \(k_{m{obs}}=k_{1}\). Step (1) is said to be the rate-controlling step. If \(k_{2}\left[m{D}ight]\ll k_{-1}\), then the observed rate: \[
u =  rac{k_{1}\ k_{2}}{k_{-1}}\left[m{A}ight]\left[m{B}ight]\left[m{D}ight]=K\ k_{2}\left[m{A}ight]\left[m{B}ight]\left[m{D}ight]\] where \(K\) is the equilibrium constant for the pre-equilibrium (1) and is equal to \( rac{k_{1}}{k_{-1}}\), and \(k_{m{obs}}=K\ k_{2}\). Step (2) is said to be the rate-controlling step.

R05140.title: rate-determining step
R05140.definition: These terms are best regarded as synonymous with rate-controlling step. However, other meanings that have been given to them should be mentioned, as it is necessary to be aware of them in order to avoid confusion. Sometimes the term rate-determining is used as a special case of rate-controlling, being assigned only to an initial slow step which is followed by rapid steps. Such a step imposes an upper limit on the rate, and has also been called rate-limiting. In view of the considerable danger of confusion when special meanings are applied to rate-determining and rate-limiting, it is recommended that they be regarded as synonymous, with the meaning explained under the entry rate-controlling step.

14971.title: rate-of-living theory of aging
14971.definition: Theory that the total metabolic expenditure of a genotype is generally fixed, and longevity depends on the rate of energy expenditure.

R05142.title: ratemeter
R05142.definition: An electronic sub-assembly which gives a continuous indication proportional to the average counting rate over a predetermined time interval (time constant).

R05157.title: ratio
R05157.definition: Quotient of quantities of the same kind for different components within the same system.

R05158.title: raw coke
R05158.definition: The term raw coke is equivalent to green coke although it is now used less frequently.

10058.title: raw data
10058.definition: Data not yet subjected to analysis.

R05159.title: Rayleigh ratio
R05159.definition: The quantity used to characterize the scattered intensity at the scattering angle \(\theta\), defined as \(R(\theta) = \frac{i_{\theta }\,r^{2}}{I\,f\,V}\), where \(I\) is the intensity of the incident radiation, \(i_{\theta}\) is the total intensity of scattered radiation observed at an angle \(\theta\) and a distance \(r\) from the point of scattering and \(V\) is the scattering volume. The factor \(f\) takes account of polarization phenomena. It depends on the type of radiation employed.   For light scattering, dependent on the polarization of the incident beam, \(f=1\) for vertically polarized light, \(f = 1 - \cos^{2}\theta\) for horizontally polarized light and \(f = 1 + \frac{\cos^{2}\theta}{2}\) for unpolarized light.   For small-angle neutron scattering, \(f=1\).   For small-angle X-ray scattering, \(f \approx 1\), if \(\theta < \rm{ca.}\ 5\,°\).

R05160.title: Rayleigh scattering
R05160.definition: The scattering of light by particles and molecules which are much smaller than the wavelength of the light. In the ideal case, the process is one of pure dipole and induced dipole interactions with the electric field of the light wave. The scattering cross section for light of wavelength \(\lambda \) is proportional to \(\lambda ^{-4}\).

13632.title: Raynaud phenomenon
13632.definition: Intermittent bilateral attacks of vasospasm and ischemia of the fingers or toes and sometimes of the ears and nose, marked by a severe pallor and often accompanied by paresthesia and pain.

R05161.title: rayon-based carbon fibres
R05161.definition: Carbon fibres made from rayon (cellulose) precursor fibres.

R05225.title: re-extraction
R05225.definition: Since the prefix 're' can signify 'back' as well as 'again' this term is ambiguous and should be avoided, except where the process of extraction (e.g. from aqueous solution to an organic phase) in a single direction is repeated (following stripping). It should not be used as a synonym for stripping or back-extraction.

R05308.title: Re, Si
R05308.definition: A stereoheterotopic face of a trigonal atom is designated Re if the ligands of the trigonal atom appear in a clockwise sense in order of CIP priority when viewed from that side of the face. The opposite arrangement is termed Si.

16021.title: reabsorption
16021.definition: Absorption by a living organism of a substance which it has previously absorbed and then released (e.g., the uptake of a substance from the proximal renal tubule following glomerular filtration).

R05163.title: reactant
R05163.definition: A substance that is consumed in the course of a chemical reaction. It is sometimes known, especially in the older literature, as a 'reagent', but this term is better used in a more specialized sense as a test substance that is added to a system in order to bring about a reaction or to see whether a reaction occurs (e.g. an analytical reagent).

R05164.title: reacting bond rules
R05164.definition: For an internal motion of a molecular entity corresponding to progress over a transition state (energy maximum), any change that makes the motion more difficult will lead to a new molecular geometry at the energy maximum, in which the motion has proceeded further. Changes that make the motion less difficult will have the opposite effect. (This rule corresponds to the Hammond principle).For an internal motion of a molecular entity that corresponds to a vibration, any change that tends to modify the equilibrium point of the vibration in a particular direction will actually shift the equilibrium in that direction.Effects on reacting bonds (bonds made or broken in the reaction) are the most significant. The bonds nearest the site of structural change are those most strongly affected.

R05166.title: reaction barrier
R05166.definition: The energy barrier to chemical reaction. In vibrationally adiabatic transition-state theory its height is the zero-point energy of the activated complex minus that of the reactants.

R05167.title: reaction chromatography
R05167.definition: A technique in which the identities of the sample components are intentionally changed between sample introduction and detection. The reaction can take place upstream of the column when the chemical identity of the individual components passing through the column differs from that of the original sample, or between the column and the detector when the original sample components are separated in the column but their identity is changed prior to entering the detection device.

R05168.title: reaction coordinate
R05168.definition: A geometric parameter that changes during the conversion of one (or more) reactant molecular entities into one (or more) product molecular entities and whose value can be taken for a measure of the progress of an elementary reaction (for example, a bond length or bond angle or a combination of bond lengths and/or bond angles; it is sometimes approximated by a non-geometric parameter, such as the bond order of some specified bond). In the formalism of 'transition-state theory', the reaction coordinate is that coordinate in a set of curvilinear coordinates obtained from the conventional ones for the reactants which, for each reaction step, leads smoothly from the configuration of the reactants through that of the transition state to the configuration of the products. The reaction coordinate is typically chosen to follow the path along the gradient (path of shallowest ascent/deepest descent) of potential energy from reactants to products. The term has also been used interchangeably with the term transition coordinate, applicable to the coordinate in the immediate vicinity of the potential energy maximum. Being more specific, the name transition coordinate is to be preferred in that context.

R05169.title: reaction cross-section
R05169.definition: A quantity used in collision theories of reactions in order to interpret calculated or experimental rates. In some collision theories the reaction cross-section is considered to be related to \(b_{\max }\), the maximum value of the impact parameter that allows reaction to occur, by: \[\sigma _{\rm{r}}=P_{\rm{r}}\ \pi \ b_{\max }^{2}\] where \(P_{\rm{r}}\) is the reaction probability.

R05170.title: reaction dynamics
R05170.definition: A branch of chemical kinetics that is concerned with the intermolecular and intramolecular motions that occur in the elementary act of chemical change, and with the details of the relationships between the quantum states of the reactant molecules and those of the product molecules. It is also known as molecular dynamics.

RT07628.title: reaction injection moulding
RT07628.definition: Reactive polymer processing that produces polymer monoliths by low-pressure injection and mixing of low-viscosity precursors into moulds.

R05174.title: reaction path
R05174.definition: A synonym for mechanism.A trajectory on the potential-energy surface.A sequence of synthetic steps.

R05175.title: reaction path degeneracy
R05175.definition: A factor that is introduced into rate theory to take account of the fact that the process may be able to occur in different but equivalent ways. Thus the process:  has a reaction path degeneracy of 2 since the chlorine atom can abstract either of the two hydrogen atoms in the hydrogen molecule. The reaction path degeneracy has also been referred to as the statistical factor for the reaction.

R05176.title: reaction probability
R05176.definition: The probability that a reaction occurs when two particles undergo a collision. If \(N_{\rm{c}}\) is the number of collisions occurring in unit time, and \(N_{\rm{r}}\) the number of reactions occurring in unit time: \(P_{\rm{r}}=\frac{N_{\rm{r}}}{N_{\rm{c}}}\).

R05177.title: reaction stage
R05177.definition: A set of one or more (possibly experimentally inseparable) reaction steps leading to and/or from a detectable or presumed reaction intermediate.

R05178.title: reaction step
R05178.definition: An elementary reaction, constituting one of the stages of a stepwise reaction in which a reaction intermediate (or, for the first step, the reactants) is converted into the next reaction intermediate (or, for the last step, the products) in the sequence of intermediates between reactants and products.

R05179.title: reaction time
R05179.definition: The period of time that elapses between the start of the reaction and the attainment of a given extent of a reaction.

R05180.title: reactive
R05180.definition: As applied to a chemical species, the term expresses a kinetic property. A species is said to be more reactive or to have a higher reactivity in some given context than some other (reference) species if it has a larger rate constant for a specified elementary reaction. The term has meaning only by reference to some explicitly stated or implicitly assumed set of conditions. It is not to be used for reactions or reaction patterns of compounds in general. The term is also more loosely used as a phenomenological description not restricted to elementary reactions. When applied in this sense the property under consideration may reflect not only rate, but also equilibrium, constants.

R05181.title: reactive adsorption
R05181.definition: Reactive adsorption (and its reverse, reactive desorption) resembles dissociative adsorption (and its reverse, dissociative adsorption) but one fragment adds to an adsorbate rather than to a surface site.

13633.title: reactive airways dysfunction syndrome
13633.definition: Syndrome characterized by reversible airflow limitation and complicating bronchial hyperresponsiveness induced by acute exposure to high concentrations of non-sensitizer irritant gases.

11615.title: reactive astrocyte
11615.definition: Astrocyte that, after injury or excessive neural activity, undergoes morphological (including extension of pseudopodia) and biochemical (notably increased synthesis of glial fibrillary acidic protein) changes and participates in astrocytic scar formation.

RT07150.title: reactive blending
RT07150.definition: Mixing process that is accompanied by the chemical reaction(s) of components of a polymer mixture.

R05182.title: reactive complex
R05182.definition: A species of very short life that occurs as an intermediate in a chemical reaction. An activated complex (or transition state) is a special case.

09191.title: reactive desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry
09191.definition: Mode of desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry with reactive chemicals within the spray solution to enhance the analytical specificity.

11790.title: reactive gliosis
11790.definition: Damage-induced proliferation, enlargement and overgrowth of glial cells, often astrocytes in the central nervous system, resulting in an astrocytic scar.

09563.title: reactive ion etching
09563.definition: Etching technology used in microfabrication that uses chemically reactive plasma to remove material from a substrate.

16022.title: reactive nitrogen species
16022.definition: Radical nitrogen-based molecules that can act to facilitate nitrosylation reactions; reactive nitrogen species include dioxidonitrogen(\(\ce{^{.}}\)) (nitrogen dioxide, nitryl radical) \(\ce{NO^{.}}\), oxidonitrogen(\(\ce{^{.}}\)) (nitrogen monoxide, nitrosyl radical) \(\ce{NO^{.}}\) oxidonitrogen(1+) (nitrosyl cation) \(\ce{NO^{+}}\), hydroxyoxidonitrogen (nitrous acid) \(\ce{HNO2}\), and oxidonitrate(1-) \(\ce{NO^{-}}\).

13634.title: reactive oxygen species
13634.definition: Intermediates in the reduction of molecular dioxygen, \(\ce{O2}\), to water.

RT07164.title: reactive polymer
RT07164.definition: Polymer having reactive functional groups that can undergo chemical transformation under the conditions required for a given reaction or application.

RT07630.title: reactive polymer processing
RT07630.definition: Process whereby a polymeric monolith is produced through an in-situpolymerization or polymer modification reaction.

R05184.title: reactive scattering
R05184.definition: If in a molecular-beam experiment a chemical reaction occurs there is said to be reactive scattering.

R05185.title: reactivity index
R05185.definition: Any numerical index derived from quantum mechanical model calculations that permits the prediction of relative reactivities of different molecular sites. Many indices are in use, based on a variety of theories and relating to various types of reaction. The more successful applications have been to the substitution reactions of conjugated systems where relative reactivities are determined largely by changes of $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}electron}$ energy.

R05186.title: reactivity–selectivity principle
R05186.definition: This idea may be expressed loosely as: the more reactive a reagent is, the less selective it is. Consider two substrates \(\rm{S}^{1}\) and \(\rm{S}^{2}\) undergoing the same type of reaction with two reagents \(\rm{R}^{1}\) and \(\rm{R}^{2}\), \(\rm{S}^{2}\) being more reactive than \(\rm{S}^{1}\), and \(\rm{R}^{2}\) more reactive than \(\rm{R}^{1}\) in the given type of reaction. The relative reactivities (in log units) for the four possible reactions may notionally be represented as shown in the diagram.  With the positions of (\(\rm{S}^{1}+\rm{R}^{1}\)), (\(\rm{S}^{2}+\rm{R}^{1}\)) and (\(\rm{S}^{1}+\rm{R}^{2}\)) fixed, there are three types of positions for (\(\rm{S}^{2}+\rm{R}^{2}\)). In position (i) the selectivity of \(\rm{R}^{2}\) for the two substrates, measured by \(a\), is the same as the selectivity of \(\rm{R}^{1}\) for the two substrates, also \(a\). In position (ii) the selectivity of \(\rm{R}^{2}\) for the two substrates, measured by \(b\), is less than the selectivity of \(\rm{R}^{1}\) for the two substrates, i.e. \(b < a\). It is this situation which is in accord with the RSP. In position (iii) the selectivity of \(\rm{R}^{2}\) for the two substrates, measured by \(c\), is greater than the selectivity of \(\rm{R}^{1}\) for the two substrates, i.e. \(c > a\). This situation may be described as anti-RSP. There are many examples in which the RSP is followed, but there are also many examples corresponding to situations (i) and (iii). The RSP is in accord with intuitive feeling and certainly holds in the limiting case when reactivity is controlled by diffusion. However, the validity of the RSP is a matter of great controversy.

R05188.title: readability
R05188.definition: The smallest fraction of a division to which the index scale can be read with ease either by estimation or by the use of a vernier. It should normally be expressed in divisions of the pointer scale.

16023.title: readily biodegradable
16023.definition: Arbitrary classification of substances that have passed certain specified screening tests for ultimate biodegradability; these tests are so stringent that such compounds will be rapidly and completely biodegraded in a wide variety of aerobic environments.

13635.title: reagin
13635.definition: Historic term for antibodies of the immunoglobulin E (IgE) class.

R05192.title: real potential of a species in a phase
R05192.definition: Defined for species $\ce{B}$ in phase $\upbeta\!$ as \[\alpha _{\rm{B}}^{\beta } = \mu _{\rm{B}}^{\beta }\,-\,z_{\rm{B}}\ F\ \psi ^{\beta }\] where \(\mu _{\rm{B}}^{\beta }\) is the electrochemical potential of species $\ce{B}$ in phase $\upbeta\!$, \(z_{\rm{B}}\) is the charge number of species $\ce{B}$, \(F\) is the Faraday constant, and \(\psi ^{\beta }\) is the outer electric potential of phase $\upbeta\!$. Since \(\psi ^{\beta }\) is zero when the charge on the phase $\upbeta\!$ is zero, the real potential may be regarded as the value of the electrochemical potential of the uncharged phase.

08404.title: real spectrum
08404.definition: In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, one of two equally sized blocks of frequency data \(\pu{90\!^{\circ}}\) out of phase to each other produced by Fourier transformation of the time domain signal.

09720.title: real-time polymerase chain reaction
09720.definition: Polymerase chain reaction where data are collected and monitored in real-time as the reaction proceeds.

14973.title: realised niche
14973.definition: Portion of a species’ fundamental niche that it actually occupies.

12042.title: rearing
12042.definition: Of a rodent or other animal raising itself on its hind legs.

R05195.title: rearrangement ion
R05195.definition: An electrically charged species, involving a molecular or parent ion, in which atoms or groups of atoms have transferred from one portion of a molecule or molecular moiety to another during the ionization fragmentation processes.

R05196.title: rearrangement stage
R05196.definition: The elementary reaction or reaction stage (of a molecular rearrangement) in which there is both making and breaking of bonds between atoms common to a reactant and a reaction product or a reaction intermediate. If the rearrangement stage consists of a single elementary reaction, this is a 'rearrangement step'.

14975.title: reasonable maximum exposure
14975.definition: Highest exposure that is reasonably expected to occur.

14974.title: reasonable worst case
14974.definition: Semiquantitative term referring to the lower portion of the high end of the exposure, dose, or risk distribution.

12043.title: rebound
12043.definition: Reappearance of original symptom(s), often exacerbated, following cessation of treatment.

11801.title: rebound headache
11801.definition: Headache caused by stopping analgesics following their overuse to relieve headaches.

R05197.title: rebound reaction
R05197.definition: If in a chemical process, occurring in a molecular beam, the reaction products are scattered backwards with respect to the moving centre of mass of the system, the reaction is called a rebound reaction.

16024.title: recalcitrance
16024.definition: Ability of a substance to remain in a particular environment in an unchanged form.

11501.title: recall
11501.definition: The fraction of the total number of actives, in the top-scoring docking hits, such as the fraction of true actives that are retrieved in the top \(\pu{1\%}\) scoring molecules.

13636.title: recall antigen
13636.definition: Substance recognized by memory cells that stimulates rapid (secondary) immune responses, often associated with hypersensitivity.

08280.title: received radiant flux density
08280.definition: Radiant power incident on unit area.

11502.title: receiver-operator characteristic curve
11502.definition:
A plot that shows the result of a test of the performance of a binary classifier by plotting the fraction of true positives identified versus the fraction of
 false positives as the discrimination threshold is varied.

14976.title: receiving water
14976.definition: Surface water (e.g., in a stream, river, or lake) that has received, or is about to receive, a discharged waste (i.e., the surface water immediately around the discharge point).

RT06841.title: receptor
RT06841.definition: Molecular structure in or on a cell that specifically recognizes and binds to a compound and acts as a physiological signal transducer, or mediator of, an effect.

RT06978.title: receptor
RT06978.definition: A receptor is a protein or a protein complex in or on a cell that specifically recognizes and binds to a compound acting as a molecular messenger (neurotransmitter, hormone, lymphokine, lectin, drug, etc). In a broader sense, the term receptor is often used as a synonym for any specific (as opposed to non-specific such as binding to plasma proteins) drug binding site, also including nucleic acids such as DNA.

16025.title: receptor-mediated endocytosis
16025.definition: Endocytosis of a substance and its receptor following receptor binding.

11164.title: recessive
11164.definition: In genetics, relating to or denoting heritable characteristics controlled by genes which are expressed in offspring only when inherited from both parents.

16026.title: recessive gene
16026.definition: Allele which in the heterozygous state is expected to have no effect on the phenotype of the organism which carries it.

11165.title: reciprocal mesenchymal-epithelial interaction
11165.definition: Process in tissue or organ development in which epithelium induces changes in the mesenchyme and the mesenchyme also induces changes in the epithelium, through paracrine signaling.

15350.title: reciprocal salt system
15350.definition: System containing \(n\) ionic species with or without a single solvent. Because of electrical neutrality, the system has \(n\) components in an aqueous system with a single solvent and \(n - 1\) components in a molten salt system.

11166.title: reciprocal translocation
11166.definition: Chromosomal translocation in which crossing over between two non-homologous chromosomes leads to each carrying genetic material from the other.

R05199.title: recognition site
R05199.definition: A nucleotide sequence to which a protein binds specifically.An amino acid sequence in an antibody molecule to which the specific antigen binds specifically.

R05200.title: recoil
R05200.definition: The motion acquired by a particle through a collision with, or the emission of, another particle or electromagnetic radiation.

R05202.title: recoil labelling
R05202.definition: Labelling by a chemical reaction initiated by recoil.

R05201.title: recoil-free fraction
R05201.definition: The fraction of all Mössbauer gamma rays of the transition which are emitted or absorbed without significant recoil energy loss.

13637.title: recombinant antibody
13637.definition: Antibody fragment manufactured by use of genetically modified microorganisms.

09721.title: recombinant deoxyribonucleic acid
09721.definition: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) molecules joined together using recombinant deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) technology.

09722.title: recombination
09722.definition: Process by which genetic material is broken and joined to other genetic material, which can lead to a rearrangement of genetic sequences.

14081.title: recombination centre
14081.definition: Defect in semiconductors and insulators capable of sequential capture of free charge carriers of both signs with high efficiency.

14080.title: recombination of photocarriers
14080.definition: Two-step transition of an electron from the conduction band to a defect centre and then further to the valence band, or from the defect centre to the valence band (first step) and a subsequent transition of the conduction band electron to the defect centre (second step).

13639.title: recombination signal sequence
13639.definition: Any conserved heptamer (7-nucleotide)-nonamer (9-nucleotide) sequence, separated by a 12 or 23 base spacer, which occurs 3′ of variable gene segments, 5′ and 3′ of diversity gene segments, and 5′ of joining gene segments, in both immunoglobulin (Ig) and T-cell receptor (TCR) genes. It functions as a recognition sequence for the recombinase enzymes that mediate the gene rearrangement process involved in the generation of lymphocyte antigen receptor diversity.

13638.title: recombination-activating gene
13638.definition: Gene whose products are involved in V(D)J recombination in B cells and T cells. Two such genes that have been identified are RAG-1 and RAG-2.

14977.title: recommended limit
14977.definition: Maximum concentration of a potentially toxic substance that is expected to be safe.

14978.title: reconstituted water
14978.definition: De-ionized or glass-distilled water to which reagent-grade chemicals have been added. The resultant synthetic freshwater is expected to be free from contaminants and have the desired \(\rm{pH}\) and hardness characteristics.

16028.title: reconstitution
16028.definition: Restoration to original form of a substance previously altered for preservation and storage.

R05205.title: reconstructive transition
R05205.definition: A transition which involves a major reorganization of the crystal structure and a change of local topology, during which primary bonds are broken and reformed so that there is no immediate relationship between the crystal structures of the parent and product phases.

08039.title: recovered quantity value ratio
08039.definition: Measured quantity value relating a component to a system divided by a reference value.

R05206.title: recovery
R05206.definition: In toxicology, the process leading to partial or complete restoration of a cell, tissue, organ or organism following its damage from exposure to a harmful substance or agent.Term used in analytical and preparative chemistry to denote the fraction of the total quantity of a substance recoverable following a chemical procedure.

08759.title: recovery time
08759.definition: Period of time after the dead time of a radiation counter during which the output pulses are smaller than the original.

R05208.title: recrystallization
R05208.definition: (chemical): The repeated dissolution and precipitation of a solid from a liquid solvent.(metallurgical): The process in which a crystalline solid with a high degree of disorder develops a new microstructure by the nucleation of relatively imperfection-free regions, and their propagation throughout the complete solid.

11168.title: rectum
11168.definition: Terminal part of the large intestine, ending at the anus.

11503.title: recursive partitioning
11503.definition:
A classification method that uses predictor properties to successively divide the data set into subsets such that each resulting subset is enriched in
 molecules that are in one class.

16029.title: recycling
16029.definition: Process or method allowing for the recovery of some value from a waste, either as reusable material or as energy.

13640.title: red pulp
13640.definition: Parenchymal tissue of the spleen consisting of cords of cells and sinuses infiltrated with erythrocytes and responsible for removal of aged or damaged erythrocytes.

09275.title: redeposition
09275.definition: Deposition of sputtered sample material back onto the sample surface.

08865.title: redox doping
08865.definition: Doping of a parent polymer consisting in oxidation or reduction of its molecules.

09049.title: redox indicator
09049.definition: Visual indicator that reacts with excess titrant or titrand with a color change at the end-point of a redox titration.

R05209.title: redox ion exchangers
R05209.definition: Conventional ion exchangers in which reversible redox couples have been introduced as counter-ions either by sorption or complex formation. They closely resemble redox polymers in their behaviour.

09095.title: redox mediation
09095.definition: Detection principle for a chemically modified electrode (CME) in which an immobilized redox couple can shuttle electrons between the electrode and an analyte, for instance, one with difficult access to the electrode surface because of steric reasons.

R05210.title: redox polymer
R05210.definition: Polymer containing groups that can be reversibly reduced or oxidized.

RT06783.title: redox potential
RT06783.definition: Any oxidation-reduction (redox) reaction can be divided into two half-reactions: one in which a chemical species undergoes oxidation and one in which another chemical species undergoes reduction. If a half-reaction is written as a reduction, the driving force is the reduction potential.
