If the half-reaction is written as oxidation, the driving force is the oxidation potential related to the reduction potential by a sign change. So the redox potential is the reduction/oxidation potential of a compound measured under standards conditions against a standard reference half-cell. In biological systems the standard redox potential is defined at pH – 7.0 versus the hydrogen electrode and partial pressure of hydrogen = 1 bar.

R05212.title: reduced adsorption

R05214.title: reduced mass
R05214.definition: Effective mass in equations of motion for a many particle system.

R05215.title: reduced mobile phase velocity
R05215.definition: A term used mainly in liquid chromatography. It compares the mobile phase velocity with the velocity of diffusion into the pores of the particles (the so-called diffusion velocity, \(u_{\rm{D}}\)): \[\nu=\frac{\overline{u}}{u_{\rm{D}}}=\frac{\overline{u}\ d_{\rm{p}}}{D_{\rm{M}}}\] In open-tubular chromatography: \[\nu=\frac{\overline{u}\ d_{\rm{c}}}{D_{\rm{M}}}\]

R05216.title: reduced osmotic pressure
R05216.definition: The osmotic pressure divided by mass concentration.

09908.title: reduced plate height
09908.definition: In liquid chromatography plate height divided by average particle diameter. \[h = H/d_{\rm{p}}\]

15351.title: reduced pressure
15351.definition: Pressure divided by the critical pressure.

R05217.title: reduced sample
R05217.definition: A representative part of the primary (composited or gross) sample obtained by a division and reduction process. Typically the mass approximates that of the final laboratory sample.

R05219.title: reduced species
R05219.definition: A term used to characterize the degree of reduction (or oxidation) in atoms, molecules and ions. An atom in a molecule or an ion which has a low oxidation state. An element or atom in a compound can be reduced by the reaction of an element or compound with hydrogen, while it can be oxidized by reaction with oxygen. A reduced species can be formed also through the gain of electrons (either at the negative electrode in a cell or through transfer from another atom, ion or group of atoms in a chemical reaction). For example, the carbon atom in $\ce{CH4}$ and other hydrocarbons is in a reduced state, while the carbon in $\ce{CO2}$ is in an oxidized state. Similarly the sulfur atom in $\ce{H2S}$ is in a reduced state while that in sulfuric acid ($\ce{H2SO4}$) is in an oxidized state.

15352.title: reduced temperature
15352.definition: Temperature divided by the critical temperature.

R05220.title: reduced viscosity
R05220.definition: The ratio of the relative viscosity increment to the mass concentration of the polymer, \(c\), i.e. \(\frac{\eta _{i}}{c}\), where \(\eta _{i}\) is the relative viscosity increment.

R05221.title: reducing
R05221.definition: Decreasing the size of the laboratory sample or individual particles, or both. Division of the size of the laboratory sample may be accomplished manually by coning and quartering or by riffling or mechanically by rotary dividers. Reduction of particle size may be accomplished by milling or grinding. Simultaneous division and reduction may also be achieved with mills having stream diverters.

R05222.title: reduction
R05222.definition: The complete transfer of one or more electrons to a molecular entity (also called 'electronation'), and, more generally, the reverse of the processes described under oxidation (2) and (3).

R05224.title: reductones
R05224.definition: Compounds containing an enediol structure stabilized by conjugation and hydrogen bonding with an adjacent carbonyl group, $\ce{RC(OH)=C(OH)C(=O)R}$. They are strong reducing agents, fairly strong acids and commonly derived from saccharides by oxidation at the carbon atom alpha to the carbonyl function, e.g. ascorbic acid.

14979.title: redundancy hypothesis
14979.definition: Hypothesis that many species are redundant, and their loss will not influence the community function as long as crucial (e.g., keystone and dominant) species populations are maintained.

13641.title: Reed–Sternberg cell
13641.definition: Large transformed lymphocyte, often binucleate, considered pathognomonic of Hodgkin lymphoma.

R05227.title: reference atom
R05227.definition: The atom to which a primitive change is nucleophilic, electrophilic, nucleofugal or homolytic.

16030.title: reference concentration
16030.definition: An estimate (with uncertainty spanning perhaps an order of magnitude) of a continuous inhalation exposure to the human population (including sensitive subgroups which include children, asthmatics, and the elderly) that is likely to be without an appreciable risk of deleterious effects during a lifetime.

15353.title: reference data
15353.definition: Data that are critically evaluated and verified, obtained from an identified source, and related to a property of a phenomenon, body, or substance, or a system of components of known composition and structure.

RT06912.title: reference dose
RT06912.definition: An estimate (with uncertainty spanning perhaps an order of magnitude) of daily exposure to the human population (including sensitive subgroups) that is likely to be without appreciable risk of deleterious effects during a lifetime.

R05229.title: reference electrode
R05229.definition: An external electrode system which comprises an inner element, usually mercury–mercury(I) chloride (calomel), silver–silver chloride or thallium amalgam–thallium(I) chloride, a chamber containing the appropriate filling solution and a device for forming a liquid junction, e.g. capillary, ceramic plug, fritted disc or ground glass sleeve.

14980.title: reference environment
14980.definition: Generalized description of the environment into which contaminants will be released and in which organisms will be exposed. Reference environments are used when there is no specific site at risk.

10022.title: reference examination procedure
10022.definition: Examination procedure accepted as providing examination results fit for their intended use in assessing examination trueness of examined values) obtained from other examination procedures for nominal properties of the same kind-of-nominal-property, in examination calibration, or in characterizing nominal reference materials.

10028.title: reference examination standard
10028.definition: Examination standard designated for the examination calibration of other examination standards for nominal properties of a given kind-of-nominal-property in a given organization or at a given location.

08538.title: reference flux density
08538.definition: Intensity transmitted by the reference medium in a double-beam spectrometer.

16032.title: reference individual
16032.definition: Person selected with the use of defined criteria for comparative purposes in a clinical study.

16033.title: reference interval
16033.definition: Area between and including two reference limits, for example, the percentiles \(\pu{2.5}\) and \(\pu{97.5}\).

08116.title: reference laboratory
08116.definition: Laboratory that applies a reference measurement procedure, a reference examination procedure, or performs a calibration.

16034.title: reference limit
16034.definition: Boundary value defined so that a stated fraction of the reference values is less than or exceeds that boundary value with a stated probability.

R05230.title: reference material
R05230.definition: A substance or mixture of substances, the composition of which is known within specified limits, and one or more of the properties of which is sufficiently well established to be used for the calibration of an apparatus, the assessment of a measuring method or for assigning values to materials. Reference materials are available from national laboratories in many countries [e.g. National Institute for Standards and Technology (NIST), USA.; Community Bureau of Reference, UK].

08117.title: reference material certificate
08117.definition: Document, issued by a reference material producer, containing the essential information for the use of a certified reference material and confirming that the necessary procedures have been carried out to ensure the validity and traceability of the stated property values.

08118.title: reference material certification
08118.definition: Process that formally establishes the certified property value(s) of a candidate certified reference material.

08119.title: reference material certification report
08119.definition: Document giving detailed information, in addition to that contained in a reference material certificate.

08120.title: reference material producer
08120.definition: Technically competent body that produces a reference material compliant with the appropriate guidance documents and issues the reference material documentation.

R05231.title: reference method
R05231.definition: A method having small, estimated inaccuracies relative to the end use requirement. The accuracy of a reference method must be demonstrated through direct comparison with a definitive method or with a primary reference material.

09998.title: reference nominal property value
09998.definition: Nominal property value used as a basis for comparison with nominal property values of nominal properties of the same kind-of-nominal-property.

16035.title: reference population
16035.definition: Group of all reference individuals used to establish criteria against which a population that is being studied can be compared.

R05232.title: reference procedure
R05232.definition: Agreed method for determining one or more air quality characteristics where it is not practical to produce a reference material; the result obtained is defined as the measure of the air quality characteristic. For example, a gas such as $\ce{NO2}$ may be somewhat unstable when stored in a tank at low mixing ratios, so that the use of a more stable $\ce{NO}$ standard mixture in $\ce{N2}$ may be oxidized to $\ce{NO2}$ by $\ce{O3}$ in a specified manner referred to as the $\ce{NO2}$ reference procedure.

16036.title: reference sample group
16036.definition: Selected reference individuals, statistically adequate numerically to represent the reference population.

14981.title: reference sediment
14981.definition: Whole sediment near an area of concern used to assess sediment conditions in the absence of substances of concern.

14982.title: reference site
14982.definition: Relatively unpolluted site used for comparison with polluted sites in environmental monitoring studies, often incorrectly referred to as a control site.

R05233.title: reference state
R05233.definition: The state in which the element is stable at a chosen standard-state pressure and for a given temperature.

14983.title: reference toxicant
14983.definition: Chemical used in an aquatic toxicity test as a positive control in contrast to the negative control provided by exposure water without the test chemical. Information collected is used to determine the general health and viability of the test organisms and assess consistency in testing protocol implementation.

14984.title: reference toxicity test
14984.definition: Test conducted in conjunction with sediment tests to determine possible changes in condition of the test species.

16037.title: reference value
16037.definition: Quantity value, generally accepted as having a suitably small measurement uncertainty, to be used as a basis for comparison with values of quantities of the same kind.

R05234.title: reference value pH standard
R05234.definition: An aqueous solution of \(\pu{0.05 mol}\) potassium hydrogen phthalate per kg water which is the reference value for the definition of pH(RVS) values in the temperature range \(\pu{0\!{-}\! 95 ^{\circ}C}\).

R05235.title: reflectance
R05235.definition: Fraction of incident radiation reflected by a surface or discontinuity, \(\rho(\lambda) = \frac{P_{\lambda} ^{\rm{refl}}}{P_{\lambda} ^{\rm{0}}}\), where \(P_{\lambda}^{\rm{0}}\) and \(P_{\lambda}^{\rm{refl}}\) are, respectively, the incident and reflected spectral radiant power.

08539.title: reflected power
08539.definition: Incident power that is not absorbed by the plasma.

08281.title: reflection
08281.definition: Process by which electromagnetic radiation is reflected by a sample. For non-scattering samples the term means Fresnel reflection; for scattering samples the term includes regular reflection and volume reflection or diffuse reflection.

R05236.title: reflection electron energy loss spectroscopy
R05236.definition: Any technique in which a specimen is bombarded with a focused low energy (\(E_{0} < 10\ \rm{eV}\)) electron beam and the energy distribution of the reflected electrons is measured. This energy distribution contains features corresponding to discrete losses of energy of the reflected electrons due to excitation of vibrational and plasmon states and provides information on the type and geometric structure of compounds at the surface of the specimen.

R05238.title: reflection high energy electron diffraction
R05238.definition: Any technique which measures the angular intensity distribution of electrons 'reflected' from a crystalline surface under bombardment with high energy electrons near grazing incidence. The diffraction pattern provides very surface sensitive information (information depth \(1\ \rm{nm}\)) on the atomic arrangement of the top layers of a solid.

08673.title: reflection-absorption at grazing incidence
08673.definition: Reflection-absorption with very thin layers of an absorbing material on a metallic substrate and the angle of incidence between \(\pu{70\!^{\circ}}\) and \(\pu{90\!^{\circ}}\).

09418.title: reflector voltage
09418.definition: Electric potential set on the reflector electrode of a reflectron mass spectrometer with the zero referenced, such that an ion emitted from the sample with an energy numerically equal to the reflector voltage would just be on the point of reflection or transmission by the reflector electrode.

11544.title: reflectron
11544.definition: Component of a time-of-flight mass spectrometer that uses a static electric field to reverse the direction of travel of the ions and improves mass resolution by assuring that ions of the same m/z but different translational energy arrive at the detector at the same time.

12044.title: reflex
12044.definition: Involuntary reaction in response to a stimulus applied to the periphery following its transmission to the nervous centers in the brain or spinal cord.

12045.title: reflex sympathetic dystrophy
12045.definition: Diffuse persistent pain usually in an extremity.

R05239.title: refraction effects
R05239.definition: The luminescence flux emitted from the interior of a rectangular sample reaching a photodetector place at some distance from the sample is decreased by a factor of approximately \(n^{2}\) (where \(n\) is the refractive index of the medium) compared with a medium whose refractive index is 1.0. Such effects are termed refraction effects.

R05241.title: refractive index increment
R05241.definition: The change of the solution refractive index, \(n\), with solute concentration, \(C\), i.e. \(\frac{\partial n}{\partial C}\).

R05240.title: refractive index
R05240.definition: The ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to that in a given medium.

R05242.title: regeneration
R05242.definition: Reversal of catalytic deactivation with restoration of the original catalytic activity.

08866.title: regioirregular polymer
08866.definition: Regular polymer or an irregular polymer whose macromolecules contain non-uniformly oriented simple asymmetric repeating units.

14985.title: region
14985.definition: Area of the Earth’s surface differentiated by its specific characteristics.

08867.title: regiorandom polymer
08867.definition: Regioirregular polymer with randomly oriented asymmetric constitutional repeating units in its chains.

08868.title: regioregular polymer
08868.definition: Regular polymer whose chains are composed of uniformly oriented asymmetric constitutional repeating units.

R05243.title: regioselectivity
R05243.definition: A regioselective reaction is one in which one direction of bond making or breaking occurs preferentially over all other possible directions. Reactions are termed completely (100%) regioselective if the discrimination is complete, or partially (x%), if the product of reaction at one site predominates over the product of reaction at other sites. The discrimination may also semi-quantitatively be referred to as high or low regioselectivity. (Originally the term was restricted to addition reactions of unsymmetrical reagents to unsymmetrical alkenes.) In the past, the term 'regiospecificity' was proposed for 100% regioselectivity. This terminology is not recommended owing to inconsistency with the terms stereoselectivity and stereospecificity.

RT06979.title: regression analysis
RT06979.definition: Regression analysis is the use of statistical methods for modeling a set of dependent variables, Y, in terms of combinations of predictions, X. It includes methods such as multiple linear regression (MLR) and partial least squares (PLS).

R05244.title: regular block
R05244.definition: A block that can be described by only one species of constitutional repeating unit in a single sequential arrangement.

R05245.title: regular coke
R05245.definition: A petroleum coke with good graphitizability, characterized by a combination of properties which differ significantly from those of metallurgical coke but do not reach the quality level of premium coke. These properties are: optical anisotropy, medium reversible thermal expansion and low ash content. Regular coke is mainly used for the production of synthetic carbon and graphite materials.

09626.title: regular dendrimer
09626.definition: Substance composed of regular dendrimer molecules.

09627.title: regular dendrimer molecule
09627.definition: Dendrimer molecule comprising only identical regular dendrons.

09628.title: regular dendron
09628.definition: Dendron composed of only one type of constitutional repeating units and of only one type of end-groups.

13974.title: regular macromolecular rotaxane
13974.definition: Macromolecular rotaxane, the structure of which essentially comprises the repetition of a single constitutional unit of the rotaxane type, referred to as the rotaxane constitutional repeating unit, rot-CRU, with all units connected identically with respect to directional sense.

R05247.title: regular macromolecule
R05247.definition: A macromolecule the structure of which essentially comprises the repetition of a single constitutional unit with all units connected identically with respect to directional sense.

R05248.title: regular oligomer molecule
R05248.definition: An oligomer molecule the structure of which essentially comprises the repetition of a single constitutional unit with all units connected identically with respect to directional sense.

R05249.title: regular polymer
R05249.definition: A polymer composed of regular macromolecules, regular star macromolecules or regular comb macromolecules. A polymer consisting of star macromolecules with arms identical with respect to constitution and degree of polymerization is considered to be regular. Analogously, a polymer consisting of comb macromolecules with the sub-chains between the branch points of the main chain and the terminal sub-chains of the main chain identical with respect to constitution and degree of polymerization and the side-chains identical with respect to constitution and degree of polymerization is considered to be regular.

R05250.title: regular single-strand polymer
R05250.definition: A regular linear polymer that can be described by a preferred constitutional repeating unit in which both terminal constituent subunits are connected through single atoms to the other identical constitutional repeating units or to an end group.

14082.title: regular surface
14082.definition: Perfect surface of a solid without heterogeneity or defect.

14083.title: regular surface site
14083.definition: Zero-dimension site (atom, ion, or interstitial position) at a regular surface.

11504.title: regularization
11504.definition:
Introducing additional information in order to solve an ill-posed problem or to prevent overfitting, usually taking the form of a penalty for complexity of the
 model.

10140.title: regularized discriminant analysis
10140.definition: Discriminant analysis in which the criterion function is based on a combination of pooled covariance matrix and the individual within-group covariance matrix.

13642.title: regulated upon activation normal T cell expressed and secreted
13642.definition: Chemokine secreted by T cells and macrophages upon stimulation by mitogens, which acts as a chemoattractant and stimulates eosinophils and basophils.

R05252.title: regulator gene
R05252.definition: A gene which codes for a protein (an activator of repressor) having the ability to induce or repress the transcription of other genes.

16038.title: regulatory dose
16038.definition: Term used by the USEPA to describe the expected dose resulting from human exposure to a substance at the level at which it is regulated in the environment.

13643.title: regulatory idiotope
13643.definition: Antibody or T-cell receptor (TCR) idiotope capable of regulating immune responses via interaction with lymphocytes bearing complementary idiotopes (anti-idiotopes).

16039.title: regulatory sequence
16039.definition: DNA sequence to which specific proteins bind to activate or repress the expression of a gene.

13644.title: regulatory T cell
13644.definition: T cell that controls the maintenance of normal immune homeostasis. Treg cells are involved in controlling (anergizing or counter-regulating) autoreactive cells that escaped from thymic negative selection.

RT07472.title: Rehm–Weller equation
RT07472.definition: Empirical correlation found between the observed second-order rate constant, \(k_{\rm{q}}\), for an intermolecular electron-transfer reaction and the Gibbs energy of the photoinduced electron transfer process within the encounter complex (\(\Delta _{\rm{ET}}G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\)): \[k_{\rm{q}} = \frac{k_{\rm{d}}}{1+ \frac {k_{\rm{d}}}{K_{\rm{d}}\, \rm{Z}}\left [ \rm{exp}\left ( \frac{\Delta G^{\ddagger }}{RT} \right ) + \rm{exp}\left ( \frac{\Delta_{\rm{ET}} G^{o }}{RT} \right ) \right ]}\] with \(k_{\rm{d}}\) and \(k_{\rm{-d}}\) the rate constant for the formation and separation, respectively, of the encounter (precursor) complex, \(K_{\rm{d}} = \: ^{k_{\rm{d}}}\! /_{k_{\rm{-d}}}\), \(Z\) the universal collision frequency factor, \(R\) the gas constant, \(T\) the absolute temperature and \(\Delta G^{\ddagger}\) the activation Gibbs energy of the forward electron transfer reaction.

RT07629.title: reinforced reaction injection moulding
RT07629.definition: Reaction injection moulding within which glass fibres are included to increase the strength of the moulding.

12046.title: reinforcement
12046.definition: Use of a stimulus in operant conditioning to increase the likelihood that a particular behavior will occur.

R05253.title: Reissert compounds
R05253.definition: Compounds formed by formal addition of an acyl group and a cyano group to a nitrogen atom and carbon atom, respectively, of a nitrogen–carbon bond in quinolines, isoquinolines, and related nitrogen heterocycles, e.g.

13645.title: rejection
13645.definition: Immune response leading to destruction of a transplanted organ or tissue.

08121.title: rejection interval
08121.definition: Interval of non-permissible measured quantity values.

R05255.title: relative
R05255.definition: Quotient of quantities having the same kind-of-quantity in different systems.

R05257.title: relative adsorption
R05257.definition: If \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\sigma}\) and \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}^{\sigma}\) are the Gibbs surface concentrations of components i and 1, respectively, with reference to the same, but arbitrarily chosen, Gibbs surface, then the relative adsorption of component i with respect to component 1, is defined as \[\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\left(1\right)} = \mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\sigma}- \mathit{\Gamma}_{1}^{\sigma}\ \frac{c_{i}^{\alpha}- c_{i}^{\beta}}{c_{1}^{\alpha}- c_{1}^{\beta}}\] and is invariant to the location of the Gibbs surface. Alternatively, \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\left(1\right)}\) may be regarded as the Gibbs surface concentration of \(i\) when the Gibbs surface is chosen so that \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\sigma}\) is zero, i.e. the Gibbs surface is chosen so that the reference system contains the same amount of component 1 as the real system. Hence \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{1}^{\left(1\right)}\equiv 0\).

R05258.title: relative atomic mass
R05258.definition: The ratio of the average mass of the atom to the unified atomic mass unit.

R05259.title: relative biological effectiveness
R05259.definition: The ratio of the appropriate value of the biological effectiveness of the radiation in question to that of X-radiation with an average specific ionization of 100 ion pairs per micron of water, for the particular biological effect under consideration and for the condition under which the radiation is received.

R05260.title: relative configuration
R05260.definition: The configuration of any stereogenic (asymmetric) centre with respect to any other stereogenic centre contained within the same molecular entity. Unlike absolute configuration, relative configuration is reflection-invariant. Relative configuration, distinguishing diastereoisomers, may be denoted by the configurational descriptors \(R^{\rm{*}}\), \(R^{\rm{*}}\) (or l) and \(R^{\rm{*}}\), \(S^{\rm{*}}\) (or u) meaning, respectively, that the two centres have identical or opposite configurations. For molecules with more than two asymmetric centres the prefix rel- may be used in front of the name of one enantiomer where R and S have been used. If any centres have known absolute configuration then only \(R^{\rm{*}}\) and \(S^{\rm{*}}\) can be used for the relative configuration.See also: α (alpha), β (beta) (Defs. 1 and 3)Two different molecules Xabcd and Xabce, may be said to have the same relative configurations if e takes the position of d in the tetrahedral arrangement of ligands around X (i.e. the pyramidal fragments Xabc are superposable). By the same token the enantiomer of Xabce may be said to have the opposite relative configuration to Xabcd. The terms may be applied to chiral molecular entities with central atoms other than carbon but are limited to cases where the two related molecules differ in a single ligand.Both definitions can be generalized to include stereogenic units other than asymmetric centres.

08760.title: relative counting efficiency
08760.definition: Absolute counting efficiency of a given radiation counter divided by the absolute counting efficiency of a reference radiation counter.

R05261.title: relative counting
R05261.definition: A measurement in which the activity of a test portion is derived from the ratio between the count rates observed for the test portion and for a radioactive source of known activity.

R05262.title: relative density
R05262.definition: Ratio of density to a reference density, usually the density of water at \(\pu{4^{\circ}C}\); in the older literature this is called specific gravity.

R05263.title: relative detection limit
R05263.definition: (Often incorrectly referred to as sensitivity). Smallest amount of material detectable ($3\upsigma\!$-criterion) in a matrix relative to the amount of material analysed — given in atomic, mole or weight fractions.

R05264.title: relative electrode potential
R05264.definition: The electrode potential of a single electrode is not amenable to direct experimental determination and can only be measured against a reference system. The measured quantity, \(E\), is the relative electrode potential.

R05266.title: relative error
R05266.definition: Error of measurement divided by the true value of the measurand. Since a true value cannot be determined, in practice the conventional true value is used.

16040.title: relative excess risk
16040.definition: Measure that can be used in comparison of adverse reactions to drugs, or other exposures, based solely on the component of risk due to the exposure or drug under investigation, removing the risk due to background exposure experienced by all in the population. The relative excess risk, \(R\), is given by \[R = (R_{1} - R_{0})/(R_{2} - R_{0})\] where \(R_{1}\) is the rate in the population, \(R_{2}\) is the rate in the comparison population, and \(R_{0}\) is the rate in the general population.

RT07092.title: relative hardness
RT07092.definition: The difference between the values of the absolute hardnesses (\(\eta \)) of a given molecule and the corresponding reference structure (\(\eta _{\rm{a}}\)): \(\eta _{\rm{r}} = \eta - \eta _{\rm{a}}\). The values of relative hardnesses correlate well with the resonance energies of cyclic compounds and may be used as an index of aromaticity.

R05267.title: relative humidity
R05267.definition: The ratio, often expressed as a percentage, of the partial pressure of water in the atmosphere at some observed temperature, to the saturation vapour pressure of pure water at this temperature.

09276.title: relative instrument spectral response function
09276.definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy (AES), secondary-ion mass spectrometry, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, the spectrometer response function divided by the response function of a reference instrument, or the average for several such instruments, as a function of energy (AES, XPS, etc.) or mass (SIMS).

09419.title: relative isotopic sensitivity factor
09419.definition: In dynamic secondary-ion mass spectrometry, coefficient for an element by which the measured intensity for an isotope of that element, divided by the measured intensity for a matrix ion, is multiplied to yield the atomic concentration of that isotope of the element present in the sample.

09420.title: relative mass accuracy
09420.definition: Mass accuracy divided by reference mass.

R05269.title: relative micellar mass
R05269.definition: The relative molecular mass (\(M_{\rm{r}}\)) of a micelle is called the relative micellar mass or micellar weight and is defined as the mass of a mole of micelles divided by the mass of \(\frac{1}{12}\) mole of $\ce{^{12}C}$.

R05270.title: relative molar mass
R05270.definition: Molar mass divided by \(\pu{1 g mol-1}\) (the latter is sometimes called the standard molar mass).

R05271.title: relative molecular mass
R05271.definition: Ratio of the mass of a molecule to the unified atomic mass unit. Sometimes called the 'molecular weight' or relative molar mass.

09965.title: relative molecular-mass exclusion limit
09965.definition: Maximum value of the relative molecular masses of components in a specific polymer solvent system that can enter into the pores of the porous non-adsorbing material used in size-exclusion chromatography.

R05272.title: relative permeability
R05272.definition: Ratio of the magnetic flux density in a given medium to that in vacuum.

R05273.title: relative permittivity
R05273.definition: Ratio of the electric field strength in vacuum to that in a given medium. It was formerly called the dielectric constant.

14084.title: relative photonic efficiency
14084.definition: Ratio of the photonic efficiency (\(\xi\)) of a chemical process to the corresponding photonic efficiency of a standard process under otherwise identical conditions in the same reactor configuration and operation.

R05274.title: relative preconcentration
R05274.definition: An operation (process) as a result of which the ratio of concentration or amounts of microcomponents and main macrocomponents increases. This is a particular example of a separation, but at greatly differing concentrations of components. The ratio of the masses of the initial and final samples is not of great importance. Frequently, the main purpose of relative preconcentration is the replacement of a matrix unsuitable for analysis by a suitable medium. In some cases, it is difficult to trace a boundary between the absolute and the relative preconcentrations as, for example, in preconcentration by zone melting.

09781.title: relative quantification
09781.definition: Type of protein/peptide quantification, where the relative amounts of one protein in different samples is determined, i.e. the ratio of the content of a protein/peptide in sample 1 to sample 2.

09277.title: relative resolution
09277.definition: Resolution of a spectrometer at a given energy, mass, or wavelength divided by that energy, mass, or wavelength.

R05276.title: relative retardation
R05276.definition: A term which is equivalent to relative retention used in column chromatography: the ratio of the \(R_{\rm{F}}\) value of a component to the \(R_{\rm{F}}\) value of a standard (reference) substance. Since the mobile phase front is common for the two components, the \(R_{\rm{F}}\) value can be expressed directly as the ratio of the distances travelled by the spot of the compound of interest (\(b_{i}\)) and the reference substance (\(b_{\rm{st}}\)) respectively: \[R_{\rm{rel}}=\frac{R_{\rm{F}\left(i\right)}}{R_{\rm{F}\left(\rm{st}\right)}}=\frac{b_{i}}{b_{\rm{st}}}\] In former nomenclatures the symbol \(R_{\rm{s}}\) was used to express relative retardation in planar chromatography. Because of its identity with the symbol for peak resolution the symbol \(R_{\rm{rel}}\) is suggested for relative retardation in planar chromatography.

R05277.title: relative retention
R05277.definition: The ratio of the adjusted or net retention volume (time) or retention factor of a component relative to that of a standard, obtained under identical conditions: \[r=\frac{V_{\rm{R}i}^{'}}{V_{\rm{R}\left(\rm{st}\right)}^{'}}=\frac{V_{\rm{N}i}}{V_{\rm{N}\left(\rm{st}\right)}}=\frac{t_{\rm{R}i}^{'}}{t_{\rm{R}\left(\rm{st}\right)}^{'}}=\frac{k_{i}}{k_{\rm{st}}}\] Depending on the relative position of the peak corresponding to the standard compound in the chromatogram, the value of \(r\) may be smaller, larger or identical to unity.

14986.title: relative risk
14986.definition:
Ratio of the risk of disease or death among the exposed to the risk among the unexposed.
Ratio of the cumulative incidence rate in the exposed to the cumulative incidence rate in the unexposed.

09278.title: relative sputtering rate
09278.definition: Sputtering rate of a sample divided by the sputtering rate of a reference sample sputtered under the same conditions.

R05280.title: relative standard deviation
R05280.definition: The standard deviation divided by the mean of the series. It can be calculated with the formula: \[s_{\rm{r}}=\frac{s}{\overline{x}}\]

16041.title: relative systemic availability
16041.definition: Quantity of metabolizable substance divided by product of quantity of absorbed substance and exposure.

R05281.title: relative uncertainty
R05281.definition: Uncertainty divided by the mean value.

R05282.title: relative viscosity
R05282.definition: The ratio of the viscosity of the solution, \(\eta \), to the viscosity of the solvent, \(\eta _{\rm{s}}\), i.e. \(\eta _{\rm{r}} = \frac{\eta}{\eta _{\rm{s}}}\). Synonymous with viscosity ratio.

R05283.title: relative viscosity increment
R05283.definition: The ratio of the difference between the viscosities of solution and solvent to the viscosity of the solvent, i.e. \(\eta _{i} = \frac{\eta - \eta _{\rm{s}}}{\eta _{\rm{s}}}\), where \(\eta \) is the viscosity of the solution and \(\eta _{\rm{s}}\) is the viscosity of the solvent. The use of the term 'specific viscosity' for this quantity is discouraged, since the relative viscosity increment does not have the attributes of a specific quantity.

RT07093.title: relativistic effects
RT07093.definition: Corrections to exact non-relativistic energy from the fact that inner shell electrons in heavy atoms move with velocities comparable in order of magnitude to the velocity of light. The most important relativistic effect is spin–orbit coupling.

R05285.title: relaxation
R05285.definition: If a system is disturbed from its state of equilibrium it relaxes to that state, and the process is referred to as relaxation. The branch of kinetics concerned with such processes is known as 'relaxation kinetics'. Relaxation techniques include temperature jump and 'pressure jump'.

09350.title: relaxation energy
09350.definition: Energy associated with intra-atomic or extra-atomic electronic readjustment to the removal of an atomic electron, so as to minimize the energy of the final state of the system.

12795.title: relaxation map
12795.definition: Plot of the logarithm of the relaxation time vs. the reciprocal temperature.

08405.title: relaxation reagent
08405.definition: Paramagnetic species added to a sample in a nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment to promote more rapid spin-lattice relaxation and allow a faster pulse repetition rate.

12796.title: relaxation spectrum
12796.definition: Range of relaxation times describing stress relaxation in a polymer.

R05287.title: relaxation time
R05287.definition: In magnetic resonance spectroscopy the longitudinal relaxation time, \(T_{1}\), is associated with spin-lattice relaxation, and the transverse relaxation time, \(T_{2}\), with spin-spin relaxation. The definitions are: \(\frac{\rm{d}M_{z}}{\rm{d}t} = -\frac{M_{z} - M_{z,\rm{e}}}{T_{1}}\) and \(\frac{\rm{d}M_{x}}{\rm{d}t} = -\frac{M_{x}}{T_{2}}\), where \(M_{z}\) and \(M_{x}\) are the components of magnetization parallel and perpendicular to the static field \(B\) and the subscript e denotes the equilibrium value.

R05288.title: releaser
R05288.definition: A substance which reduces solute-volatilization interferences by forming a compound preferentially with the interferent, thus preventing the reaction of the analyte or interferent from entering a thermally stable compound.

14987.title: remedial investigation
14987.definition: Study that has three parts: characterization or the type and degree of the contamination, human risk assessment, and ecological risk assessment.

14988.title: remedial investigation and feasibility study
14988.definition: For an EPA Superfund site, a study that has as its goal the implementation of 'remedies that reduce, control, or eliminate risks to human health and the environment' or, more specifically, the accumulation of 'information sufficient to support an informed risk management decision regarding which remedy appears to be most appropriate for a given site'.

14989.title: remediation
14989.definition:
Giving a remedy.
Removal of pollution or contaminants from environmental media such as soil, groundwater, sediment, or surface water for the general protection of human health and the environment.

16042.title: remedy
16042.definition: Anything, such as a medicine or therapy, that relieves pain, cures disease, or corrects a disorder.

14990.title: remote sensing
14990.definition: Technologies that allow the acquisition and analysis of data without requiring physical contact with the land or water surface being studied. Most determine qualities or characteristics of areas of interest based on measurements of visible light, infrared radiation, or radio energy coming from them.

16043.title: renal plasma flow
16043.definition: Volume of plasma passing through the kidneys in unit time.

R05290.title: Renner–Teller effect
R05290.definition: Molecular distortion in linear molecular species with degenerate electronic states (e.g. belonging to the \(C_{\infty\rm{v}}\) group). The Renner–Teller effect is a particular case of the Jahn–Teller effect. From the point of view of the potential energy surfaces the Renner–Teller effect generates a surface touching (see scheme below).

R05292.title: reorganization energy
R05292.definition: Gibbs energy dissipated when a system that has undergone 'vertical' electron transfer (i.e., electron transfer obeying the Franck–Condon principle) relaxes to the equilibrium state for its new charge distribution. Commonly the total reorganization energy (\(\lambda\)) is written as the sum of an inner contribution (\(\lambda_{\rm{in}}\)) and an outer contribution (\(\lambda_{\rm{out}}\)) attributed to nuclear reorganizations of the redox partners and their environment (solvent), respectively.

R05291.title: reorganization
R05291.definition: The molecular process by which (i) amorphous or poorly ordered regions of a polymer specimen become incorporated into crystals, or (ii) a change to a more stable crystal structure takes place, or (iii) defects within the crystal decrease.

15230.title: repeat action dosage form
15230.definition: Tablet or capsule distinguished from a sustained-release dosage form, by the fact that it releases the medicinal agent, or part of it, at any time other than promptly after administration as opposed to a slow, controlled manner.

R05293.title: repeatability
R05293.definition: The closeness of agreement between independent results obtained with the same method on identical test material, under the same conditions (same operator, same apparatus, same laboratory and after short intervals of time). The measure of repeatability is the standard deviation qualified with the term: `repeatability' as repeatability standard deviation. In some contexts repeatability may be defined as the value below which the absolute difference between two single test results obtained under the above conditions, may be expected to lie with a specified probability.

09993.title: repeatability condition
09993.definition: Condition of examination out of a set of conditions that includes the same examination procedure, same operators, same examining system, same operating conditions, same location, and replicate examinations on the same or similar objects over a short period of time.

08040.title: repeatability condition of measurement
08040.definition: Condition of measurement, out of a set of conditions that includes the same measurement procedure, same operators, same measuring system, same operating conditions, and same location, and replicate measurements on the same or similar objects over a short period of time.

16044.title: repellent
16044.definition: Substance used mainly to repel blood-sucking insects in order to protect humans and animals.

12048.title: reperfusion
12048.definition: Restoration of the blood supply to an organ or tissue following a period of ischemia.

08540.title: repetition rate
08540.definition: Number of laser pulses emitted by a pulsed laser system per unit time.

08406.title: repetition time
08406.definition: Time duration between repetitions of a nuclear magnetic resonance pulse sequence including the pulse sequence, acquisition time and relaxation delay.

R05297.title: replacement name
R05297.definition: A name in which the replacement of an atom or a group of a parent structure by another atom or group is indicated by affixes attached to or inserted into the name of the parent structure. There are two main types of replacement names.   Skeletal replacement name. A name in which the replacement of skeletal atoms and their associated hydrogen atoms is indicated by non-detachable prefixes. When carbon atoms are replaced by heteroatoms this method has been called 'a' nomenclature since the prefixes end in 'a'. Certain names in which the prefix 'thio-', 'seleno-' or 'telluro-' indicates replacement of a skeletal oxygen atom by a sulfur, selenium or tellurium atom, respectively, are also skeletal replacement names.   Functional replacement name. A name containing prefixes or infixes which indicate the replacement of an oxygen atom or hydroxy group of a characteristic group, functional parent or class name by other atoms or groups.

R05298.title: replacement operation
R05298.definition: The exchange of one group of atoms or a single non-hydrogen atom for another.

R05299.title: replicate sample
R05299.definition: Multiple (or two) samples taken under comparable conditions. This selection may be accomplished by taking units adjacent in time or space. Although the replicate samples are expected to be identical, often the only thing replicated is the act of taking the physical sample. A duplicate sample is a replicate sample consisting of two portions. The umpire sample is usually used to settle a dispute; the replicate sample is usually used to estimate sample variability.

16045.title: replicate sampling
16045.definition: Act of taking multiple samples concurrently under comparable conditions.

R05300.title: replication
R05300.definition: The duplication of DNA as part of the reproductive cycle of a cell or virus. During replication the two DNA strands in the double helix separate, and each strand then acts as a template specifying the base sequence of newly synthesized complementary strands.

12049.title: repolarization
12049.definition: Returning of a cell’s membrane potential to its resting potential following depolarization.

R05301.title: report
R05301.definition: A combination of specimen information and results. The report should contain information about unequivocal identification of the source and type of material analysed and the requesting agency. It may contain such other information that is pertinent to the correct interpretation of a result (e.g. confidence interval, reference data and interpretative information).

09880.title: reporter probe
09880.definition: Specifically designed single-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid (ssDNA) (alternatively, ribonucleic acid (RNA) or a synthetic nucleic acid analogue such as locked nucleic acid (LNA) or peptide nucleic acid (PNA)) with a defined (known) nucleotide sequence used to detect complementary DNA or RNA sequence in a sample.

R05302.title: reprecipitation
R05302.definition: The planned repetition of a precipitation in order to remove chemically different species from a previous precipitate or to improve its stoichiometry.

R05303.title: representative sample
R05303.definition: A sample resulting from a sampling plan that can be expected to adequately reflect the properties of interest of the parent population. A representative sample may be a random sample or, for example, a stratified sample, depending upon the objective of sampling and the characteristics of the population. The degree of representativeness of the sample may be limited by cost or convenience.

R05304.title: repression
R05304.definition: Binding of a protein (repressor) to the operator sequence in an operon thus preventing the transcription of the following structural gene(s) into mRNA and consequently synthesis of protein (cf. enzyme repression).

R05305.title: reproducibility
R05305.definition: The closeness of agreement between independent results obtained with the same method on identical test material but under different conditions (different operators, different apparatus, different laboratories and/or after different intervals of time). The measure of reproducibility is the standard deviation qualified with the term 'reproducibility' as reproducibility standard deviation. In some contexts reproducibility may be defined as the value below which the absolute difference between two single test results on identical material obtained under the above conditions, may be expected to lie with a specified probability. Note that a complete statement of reproducibility requires specification of the experimental conditions which differ.

09995.title: reproducibility condition
09995.definition: Condition of examination out of a set of conditions that includes different locations, operators, examining systems, and replicate examinations on the same or similar objects.

10580.title: reproductive cycle
10580.definition: Cycle of physiological changes in the female reproductive organs, from the time of fertilization of the oocyte through gestation and parturition.

11172.title: reproductive senescence
11172.definition: Progressive decline in reproductive capacity with age, marked by menopause in females.

11173.title: reproductive toxicant
11173.definition: Agent that interferes with reproductive function, including sexual performance, fertility, and development of the fetus and embryo.

14403.title: reproductive toxicity
14403.definition: Ability of a physical, chemical, or biological agent to induce adverse effects in the reproductive system.

11174.title: reproductive toxicity test
11174.definition: Procedure based on specific guidelines in which adverse effects of a substance on reproduction and development are studied either in animals or by use of in vitro assays.

14404.title: reproductive toxicology
14404.definition: Study of the non-heritable adverse effects of substances on male and female reproductive function or capacity and on resultant progeny.

14991.title: reproductive value
14991.definition: Expected contribution of offspring during the life of an individual of an age class \(x\) in a life table.

12268.title: reptation
12268.definition: Snake-like movement of a polymer chain in a semi-dilute or concentrated solution or bulk amorphous polymer through the hypothetical tube created by neighbouring chains.

R05306.title: repulsive potential-energy surface
R05306.definition: A surface for an exergonic reaction $\ce{A + BC}$ in which the col corresponds to considerable separation between the products $\ce{A–B + C}$. The energy barrier in the potential-energy profile is in the later stages of the reaction path. On such a surface most of the energy is released after $\ce{A–B}$ is formed. Repulsive surfaces are also called late-downhill surfaces, and the barrier in such a surface is called a Type-II barrier.

08122.title: requirement
08122.definition: Need or expectation that is stated, generally implied or obligatory.

14992.title: rescue effect
14992.definition: Increased probability of a vacated-patch reoccupation in a metapopulation as the number of nearby, occupied patches increases.

16046.title: reserve capacity
16046.definition: Physiological or biochemical capacity that may be available to maintain homeostasis when the body or an organism is exposed to an environmental change.

16047.title: reservoir
16047.definition: Storage compartment from which a substance may be released with subsequent biological effects.

R05309.title: residence time
R05309.definition: (instrumentation): The time required for air or reagent parcel to pass from the entrance to the exit of an instrument. Often this is approximated as the ratio of the interior volume of the device to the flow rate.(atmospheric): The average time a molecule or aerosol spends in the atmosphere after it is released or generated there. For compounds with well defined sources and emission rates, this is estimated by the ratio of the average global concentration of a substance to its production rate on a global scale. It is a function of not only the emission rates but the loss rates by chemical and physical removal processes.

R05310.title: residence time
R05310.definition: The average time a particle or volume element of the culture resides in a bioreactor (or other device) through which a liquid medium continously flows. residence time of the liquid is the reciprocal of dilution rate.

R05311.title: residual current
R05311.definition: The current that flows, at any particular value of the applied potential, in the absence of the substance whose behaviour is being investigated (i.e. in a blank solution).

08407.title: residual dipolar coupling
08407.definition: Dipolar coupling, but of a reduced magnitude to that seen in solids, observed in a liquid sample between spins in a molecule where there is incomplete averaging of spatially anisotropic dipolar couplings.

RT07473.title: residual emission anisotropy
RT07473.definition: Photoselected molecules hindered in their rotation (e.g., in lipid bilayers or liquid crystals) do not become randomly oriented even after long time periods. Thus, the emission anisotropy does not decay to zero but to a steady value, \(r_{\mathrm{\infty }}\), called residual emission anisotropy. In the case of a single rotational correlation time, \(\tau _{\mathrm{c}}\) or \(\theta \), the decay of emission anisotropy following $\ce{\updelta\!\mbox{-}pulse}$ excitation is given by: \[r\left(t\right)=(r_{0}- r_{\mathrm{\infty }})\ \exp (- \frac{t}{\tau _{\mathrm{c}}})+r_{\mathrm{\infty }}\] where \(r_{0}\) is the fundamental emission anisotropy.

R05312.title: residual fuel/oil
R05312.definition: The liquid or semi-liquid, high-boiling fraction of residue from the distillation of petroleum which is used as a fuel. After removal of the lower boiling fraction of crude oil, sold as petroleum gas, the somewhat higher boiling fraction becomes gasoline and diesel oil. A portion of the higher boiling fraction is 'cracked' to yield additional gasoline. Still heavier oils become lubricants. paraffin, asphalt, etc., are also extracted from the crude oil. It is the remaining residual oil, not economically usable for other industrial purposes, which is then sold as a relatively low cost fuel for burning.

R05313.title: residual liquid junction error
R05313.definition: Error arising from breakdown in the assumption that the liquid junction potential remains constant when solution X is substituted for solution S in the operational cell.

16048.title: residual risk
16048.definition: Health risk remaining after risk reduction actions are implemented.

R05314.title: residual spectrum/background spectrum
R05314.definition: Set of peaks recorded in the absence of a sample and due either to small air leaks or to the presence of molecules desorbed from the walls of the introduction device or the source, or from the pump fluid.

16049.title: residue
16049.definition: Contaminant remaining in an organism or in other material such as food or packaging, following exposure.

14993.title: resilience
14993.definition: Ability of a community to maintain its structure and function in the face of disturbance, and to reorganize following disturbance-driven change.

RT07166.title: resin
RT07166.definition: Soft solid or highly viscous substance, usually containing prepolymers with reactive groups.

09564.title: resist
09564.definition: Material, usually a polymer, that when irradiated either undergoes a marked change in solubility in a given solvent or is ablated.

RT07193.title: resist polymer
RT07193.definition: Polymeric material that, when irradiated, undergoes a marked change in solubility in a given solvent or is ablated.

09570.title: resist profile
09570.definition: Topography of a resist pattern in cross section.

09571.title: resist strip
09571.definition: Subsequent removal of the remaining resist that covers the protected regions of a substrate during development and etch processing.

R05315.title: resistance
R05315.definition: Electric potential difference divided by the electric current when there is no electromotive force in a conductor.

R05316.title: resistivity
R05316.definition: Electric field strength divided by the current density. This quantity is a tensor in an anisotropic medium.

R05318.title: resolution
R05318.definition: (energy): By analogy with the peak width definition for mass resolution, a peak showing the number of ions as a function of their translational energy should be used to give a value for the energy resolution.($\pu{10\%}$ valley definition): Let two peaks of equal height in a mass spectrum at masses \(m\) and \(m- \Delta m\) be separated by a valley which at its lowest point is just $\pu{10\%}$ of the height of either peak. For similar peaks at a mass exceeding \(m\), let the height of the valley at its lowest point be more (by any amount) than ten per cent of either peak height. Then the resolution ($\pu{10\%}$ valley definition) is \(\frac{m}{\Delta m}\). It is usually a function of \(m\). The ratio \(\frac{m}{\Delta m}\) should be given for a number of values of \(m\).(peak width definition): For a single peak made up of singly charged ions at mass \(m\) in a mass spectrum, the resolution may be expressed as \(\frac{m}{\Delta m}\) where \(\Delta m\) is the width of the peak at a height which is a specified fraction of the maximum peak height. It is recommended that one of three values $\pu{50\%}$, $\pu{5\%}$ or $\pu{0.5\%}$ should always be used. For an isolated symmetrical peak recorded with a system which is linear in the range between $\pu{5\%}$ and $\pu{10\%}$ levels of the peak, the $\pu{5\%}$ peak width definition is technically equivalent to the $\pu{10\%}$ valley definition. A common standard is the definition of resolution based upon \(\Delta m\) being Full Width of the peak at Half its Maximum height, sometimes abbreviated 'FWHM'. This acronym should preferably be defined the first time it is used.

R05317.title: resolution
R05317.definition: A characteristic of the separation of two adjacent peaks. It may be expressed according to the equation: \[R_{\rm{AB}} = 2\ \frac{|d_{\rm{R}}\left(\rm{B}\right)\,-\,d_{\rm{R}}\left(\rm{A}\right)|}{|w\left(\rm{B}\right)\,+\,w\left(\rm{A}\right)|}\] where \(R_{\rm{AB}}\) is the resolution, \(d_{\rm{R}}(\rm{A})\) and \(d_{\rm{R}}(\rm{B})\) are the retention distances (time or volume) of each eluted component A and B, and \(w(\rm{A})\) and \(w(\rm{B})\) are the respective widths of each peak at its base.

R05319.title: resolution
R05319.definition: Wavenumber, wavelength or frequency difference of two still distinguishable lines in a spectrum.

R05320.title: resolution
R05320.definition: The separation of a racemate into the component enantiomers.

10081.title: resolution of a design
10081.definition: One more than the smallest nth-order interaction effect that some main effect is aliased with.

12050.title: resolution phase
12050.definition: Return to a sexually unexcited state following orgasm.

R05321.title: resolving power
R05321.definition: The ability to distinguish between ions differing in the quotient mass/charge by a small increment. It may be characterized by giving the peak width, measured in mass units, expressed as a function of mass, for at least two points on the peak, specifically at fifty percent and at five percent of the maximum peak height.

R05322.title: resolving power
R05322.definition: Transition wavenumber (or wavelength or frequency) divided by the resolution.

R05325.title: resolving time correction
R05325.definition: Correction to be applied to the observed number of pulses in order to take into account the number of pulses lost during the resolving time.

R05323.title: resolving time
R05323.definition: The smallest time interval which must elapse between the occurrence of two consecutive ionizing events or signal pulses, in order that the measuring device be capable of fulfilling its function of each of them separately.

R05326.title: resonance
R05326.definition: In the context of chemistry, the term refers to the representation of the electronic structure of a molecular entity in terms of contributing structures. Resonance among contributing structures means that the wavefunction is represented by 'mixing' the wavefunctions of the contributing structures. The concept is the basis of the quantum mechanical valence bond methods. The resulting stabilization is linked to the quantum mechanical concept of 'resonance energy'. The term resonance is also used to refer to the delocalization phenomenon itself.

R05327.title: resonance absorption technique
R05327.definition: The monitoring of atoms or radicals generated in the gas phase by observing the attenuation of the radiation from a lamp emitting the characteristic resonance radiation of the observed species.

R05329.title: resonance cross-section
R05329.definition: The cross-section for resonant absorption of the Mössbauer transition $\upgamma\!\mbox{-}\rm{ray}$.

R05331.title: resonance effect magnitude
R05331.definition: Ratio of the difference in the transmitted or scattered intensity at resonance maximum and off-resonance, relative to the intensity off-resonance.

R05333.title: resonance energy
R05333.definition: The difference in potential energy between the actual molecular entity and the contributing structure of lowest potential energy. The resonance energy cannot be measured, but only estimated, since contributing structures are not observable molecular entities.

R05334.title: resonance energy
R05334.definition: The energy of a particle entering a nuclear reaction, this energy being just sufficiently high to lead to the formation of reaction products in one of their excited states.

R05335.title: resonance fluorescence
R05335.definition: Fluorescence from the primary excited atomic or molecular species at the wavelength of the exciting radiation (no relaxation within the excited manifold). This term is also used to designate the radiation emitted by an atom of the same wavelength as the longest one capable of exciting its fluorescence, e.g. \(122.6\ \rm{nm}\) in the case of the hydrogen atom, and \(253.7\ \rm{nm}\) in the case of the mercury atom.

R05336.title: resonance fluorescence technique
R05336.definition: The monitoring of atoms or radicals generated in the gas phase by observing the intensity of fluorescence (exitance) emitted by the species after excitation with radiation of the same wavelength.

08205.title: resonance form
08205.definition: One of at least two Lewis structures, with fixed single, double, and triple bonds, that is a contributing structure to the valence-bond wavefunction of a molecule that cannot be described by a single Lewis structure.

RT07094.title: resonance hybrid
RT07094.definition: A localized valence bond representation of a molecule. This describes pictorially an electronic wavefunction that makes some contribution to the state wavefunction of the system. resonance hybrids are needed to describe the state of a system when that system is not adequately described by a single Lewis structure.

R05338.title: resonance integral
R05338.definition: The integral, over all or some specified portion of the resonance energy range, of the cross-section divided by the energy of a radiation.

R05337.title: resonance integral
R05337.definition: In Hückel molecular orbital theory, the integral over space of the type \(\int \psi _{r}^{*}\ \hat{H}\ \psi _{s}  \ \rm{d}\tau \) where \(\hat{H}\) is the hamiltonian operator and \(\psi _{r}\) and \(\psi _{s}\) are different wavefunctions.

R05339.title: resonance lamp
R05339.definition: Lamp emitting resonance radiation of atoms and their ions. Depending on the requirements, the lamp is filled either with pure vapour of the element or with a mixture of it and other gases.

R05340.title: resonance line
R05340.definition: The longest wavelength capable of exciting fluorescence in an atom.

R05341.title: resonance line
R05341.definition: The radiative decay of an excitation level may proceed to the neutral ground state and would thus occur at the same energy as the corresponding line in the absorption spectrum. Such a line is called a resonance line and the process is called resonance emission.

R05342.title: resonance neutrons
R05342.definition: Neutrons whose energy corresponds to the resonance energy of a specified nuclide or element. If the nuclide is not specified, the term refers to resonance neutrons of $\ce{^{239}U}$.

08674.title: resonance Raman scattering
08674.definition: Raman scattering that occurs through the polarizability of a molecule, (not the hyperpolarizabilities) and is excited by electromagnetic radiation that is in resonance with electronic transitions or vibronic transitions in the sample.

09380.title: resonance reaction
09380.definition: Nuclear reaction that has a narrow peak in the nuclear reaction cross section as a function of energy, the nuclear reaction cross section at the peak being so much larger than the nuclear reaction cross sections at adjacent energies on either side of the peak that essentially all the particles detected from the reaction are due to the peak.

08541.title: resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
08541.definition: Measurement method of inelastic X-ray spectroscopy that uses a hard or soft X-ray beam to excite transitions of core-level electrons into empty energy levels. The subsequent transition of an electron into the core state is accompanied by X-ray emission with characteristic momentum and energy.

11175.title: resorption
11175.definition:
Removal of mineralized tissue by natural processes, as in the breakdown of bone by osteoclasts or the disappearance of a tooth.
Disintegration and assimilation of an embryo or fetus through a natural process involving lysis and removal of all the products of conception by cells of the maternal immune system.
In multigestational pregnancies, death of one fetus followed by absorption of its tissue by another, sometimes referred to as a 'vanishing twin'.

16050.title: resorptive effect
16050.definition: Action of a substance after its reabsorption from the gut into the blood.

16051.title: respirable dust
16051.definition: Mass fraction of dust (particles) that penetrates to the unciliated airways of the lung (the alveolar region).

13646.title: respiratory burst
13646.definition: Generation of cytotoxic superoxide from dioxygen due to increased NADPH oxidase activity, typically occurring in activated neutrophils.

13647.title: respiratory hypersensitivity assay
13647.definition: Test of the ability of a substance to induce hyperreactivity in the airways, typically measured as an increase in the rate of respiration of guinea pigs during inhalation of the substance.

10042.title: response
10042.definition: Measured or observed quantity in an experimental design.

R05344.title: response constant
R05344.definition: A quantity whose expression includes a current, whose value is characteristic of a charge-transfer process and the experimental conditions under which it is investigated, and whose nature depends on the technique that is employed. Some typical response constants are the diffusion current constant in polarography, the voltammetric constant in linear-sweep voltammetry, and the chronopotentiometric constant in chronopotentiometry.

11505.title: response scrambling
11505.definition:
Evaluation of the robustness of a QSAR or classification model by repeatedly randomizing the target property of compounds, developing models based on this
 randomized property, and comparing the statistics of fit of the scrambled models with those of the true model, which should be superior.

10082.title: response surface methodology
10082.definition: Experimental design in which the response is modelled in terms of one or more factor levels.

R05346.title: response time
R05346.definition: Time which elapses, when there is a stepwise change in the quantity to be measured, between the moment when this change is produced and the moment when the indication reaches a value conventionally fixed at 90% of the final change in indication.

R05345.title: response time
R05345.definition: The time required for the detector output to go from the initial value to a percentage (e.g. 99%) of the final value. In the case of an exponential behaviour of the detector \(\tau _{\rm{R}}\) can be related to the time constant \(\tau _{\rm{c}}\). The rise time \(\tau _{\rm{r}}\) is the time required for the detector output to vary between given percentages (e.g. from 10% to 90%) of the final value. Similarly, the fall time \(\tau _{\rm{f}}\) is the time required for the detector output to vary between given percentages (e.g. from 90% to 10%) of the initial value.

RT07526.title: responsive gel
RT07526.definition: Gel that responds to external electrical, mechanical, thermal, light-induced or chemical stimulation.

R05347.title: responsivity
R05347.definition: Detector input can be e.g. radiant power, irradiation, radiant energy. It produces a measurable detector output which may be e.g. an electrical charge, an electrical current or potential or a change in pressure. The ratio of the detector output and the detector input is defined as the responsivity. It is given in e.g. ampere/watt, volt/watt. The responsivity is a special case of the general term sensitivity. Dark current is the term for the electrical output of a detector in the absence of input. This is a special case of the general term dark output. For photoconductive detectors the term dark resistance is used. If the responsivity is normalized with regard to that obtained from a reference radiation the resulting ratio is called relative responsivity. For measurements with monochromatic radiation at a given wavelength the term spectral responsivity \(R(\lambda)\) is used. In some cases the 'relative spectral responsivity', where the spectral responsivity is normalized with respect to the responsivity at some given wavelength, is used. The dependence of the spectral responsivity on the wavelength is described by the spectral responsivity function. The useful spectral range of the detector should be given as the wavelength range where the relative responsivity does not fall below a specified value.

R05348.title: rest point
R05348.definition: The position of the pointer with respect to the pointer scale when the motion of the beam has ceased.

10253.title: restricted-access sorbent
10253.definition: Porous material with a biocompatible outer surface and a retentive interior surface.

R05350.title: restriction enzymes
R05350.definition: Endonucleases which recognize specific base sequences within a DNA helix, creating a double-strand break of DNA. Type I restriction enzymes bind to these recognition sites but subsequently cut the DNA at different sites. Type II restriction enzymes both bind and cut within their recognition or target sites.

09723.title: restriction fragment length polymorphism
09723.definition: Variation between individuals in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) fragment sizes cut by specific restriction enzymes.

11176.title: restriction site
11176.definition: Short DNA nucleotide sequence that is recognized by a sequence-specific enzyme (restriction enzyme) that cleaves the double stranded DNA.

R05351.title: result
R05351.definition: The final value reported for a measured or computed quantity, after performing a measuring procedure including all subprocedures and evaluations.

09948.title: retainer and eluter
09948.definition: Most important reagents in pH-zone-refining counter-current chromatography. A retainer is added to the stationary organic phase to retain the analytes and the eluter added to the mobile aqueous phase to elute the analytes.

08967.title: retardation
08967.definition: Diminished rate of polymerization brought about by the action of a retarder.

R05352.title: retardation factor
R05352.definition: The fraction of the sample component in the mobile phase at equilibrium; it is related to the retention factor and other fundamental chromatography terms: \[R = \frac{1}{k\,+\,1}\]

R05353.title: retardation factor
R05353.definition: Ratio of the distance travelled by the centre of the spot to the distance simultaneously travelled by the mobile phase: \[R_{\rm{F}}=\frac{b}{a}\] By definition the \(R_{\rm{F}}\) values are always less than unity. They are usually given to two decimal places. In order to simplify this presentation the \(hR_{\rm{F}}\) values may be used: they correspond to the \(R_{\rm{F}}\) values multiplied by 100. Ideally, \(R_{\rm{F}}\) values are identical to the \(R\) values used in column chromatography.

R05355.title: retarder
R05355.definition: This term, used mainly in polymerization kinetics, refers to a substance that reduces the rate of reaction. Synonymous with inhibitor.

11178.title: rete testis
11178.definition: Rete in the testis that carries sperm from the seminiferous tubules.

10289.title: retentate stream
10289.definition: Sample left over in membrane separations after initial contact with the membrane.

14994.title: retention effect
14994.definition: Observed effect of the properties of persistent organic pollutants (POPs) with high lipophilicity which causes them to be bound more firmly than less lipophilic POPs in solid phases such as soil and vegetation; consequently, they spend less time in the atmosphere and are less available for transport in that medium.

R05358.title: retention efficiency
R05358.definition: The ratio of the quantity of particles retained by a separator to the quantity entering it (generally expressed as a percentage).

R05359.title: retention factor
R05359.definition: A measure of the time the sample component resides in the stationary phase relative to the time it resides in the mobile phase; it expresses how much longer a sample component is retarded by the stationary phase than it would take to travel through the column with the velocity of the mobile phase. Mathematically, it is the ratio of the adjusted retention volume (time) and the hold-up volume (time): \[k = \frac{V_{\rm{R}}^{'}}{V_{\rm{M}}} = \frac{t_{\rm{R}}^{'}}{t_{\rm{M}}}\] If the distribution constant is independent of sample component concentration, then the retention factor is also equal to the ratio of the amounts of a sample component in the stationary and mobile phases respectively, at equilibrium: \[k = \frac{\rm{amount\ of\ component\ in\ stationary\ phase}}{\rm{amount\ of\ component\ in\ mobile\ phase}}\] If the fraction of the sample component in the mobile phase is \(R\), then the fraction in the stationary phase is \(1 - R\); thus \[k = \frac{1 - R}{R}\] In former nomenclatures and in the literature one may find the expressions partition ratio, capacity ratio, capacity factor or mass distribution ratio to describe this term. In the literature the symbol \(k^{'}\) is often used for the retention factor, particularly in liquid chromatography. The original reason for this was to clearly distinguish it from the partition coefficient (distribution constant) for which the symbol K had been utilized. Since, however, the distribution constants are all identified with a subscript, there is no reason to add the prime sign to this symbol. It should be emphasized that all the recognized nomenclatures (IUPAC, BS, ASTM) have always clearly identified the capacity factor with the symbol \(k\) and not \(k^{'}\). The logarithm of the retention factor is equivalent to the \(R_{\rm{M}}\) value used in planar chromatography. The symbol \(\kappa \) is suggested to express \[\upkappa = \log_{10} k = \log_{10}\left[\frac{1 - R}{R}\right]\]

R05357.title: retention
R05357.definition: Of atoms undergoing a nuclear transformation, that fraction which remains in or reverts to its initial chemical form.

R05360.title: retention index
R05360.definition: The retention index of a sample component is a number, obtained by interpolation (usually logarithmic), relating the adjusted retention volume (time) or the retention factor of the sample component to the adjusted retention volumes (times) of two standards eluted before and after the peak of the sample component. In the Kováts index or Kováts retention index used in gas chromatography, n-alkanes serve as the standards and logarithmic interpolation is utilized: \[I = 100\left[\frac{\log _{10}X_{i}- \log _{10}X_{z}}{\log _{10}X_{z+1}- \log _{10}X_{z}}+z\right]\] where \(X\) refers to the adjusted retention volumes or times, \(z\) is the number of carbon atoms of the n-alkane eluting before and \(\left(z+1\right)\) is the number of carbon atoms of the n-alkane eluting after the peak of interest: \[V_{\rm{R}z}^{'} < V_{\rm{R}i}^{'} < V_{\rm{R}(z+1)}\] The Kováts (retention) index expresses the number of carbon atoms (multiplied by 100) of a hypothetical normal alkane which would have an adjusted retention volume (time) identical to that of the peak of interest when analysed under identical conditions. The Kováts retention index is always measured under isothermal conditions. In the case of temperature-programmed gas chromatography a similar value can be calculated utilizing direct numbers instead of their logarithm. Since both the numerator and denominator contain the difference of two values, here we can use the total retention volumes (times). Sometimes this value is called the linear retention index. \[I^{\rm{T}} = 100\left[\frac{t_{\rm{R}i}^{\rm{T}}- t_{\rm{R}z}^{\rm{T}}}{t_{\rm{R}(z+1)}^{\rm{T}}- t_{\rm{R}z}^{\rm{T}}}+z\right]\] where \(t_{\rm{R}}^{\rm{T}}\) refers to the total retention times (chart distances) measured under the conditions of temperature programming. The value of \(I^{\rm{T}}\) will usually differ from the value of \(I\) measured for the same compound under isothermal conditions, using the same two phases.

R05363.title: retention temperature
R05363.definition: The column temperature when the peak maximum for a component has been reached in temperature-programmed chromatography.

10040.title: retention time of an unretained compound
10040.definition: Retention time of a sample component the molecules of which are larger than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.

09963.title: retention volume
09963.definition: Retention volume of a sample component, the molecules of which are smaller than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase but larger than the smallest pores.

09962.title: retention volume of an unretained compound
09962.definition: Retention volume of a sample component the molecules of which are larger than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.

09949.title: retention volume of the stationary phase
09949.definition: Volume of the stationary phase, which stays permanently within the column in counter-current chromatography.

R05366.title: retention volumes
R05366.definition: Retention measurements (and measurements of hold-up volume and peak width) may be made in terms of times or chart distances as well as volumes. If flow and recorder speeds are constant, the volumes are directly proportional to the times and chart distances. The following definitions are drawn up in terms of volume, and it is recommended that theoretical discussion should be couched in the same terms wherever possible. The total retention volume, \(V_{\rm{R}}\), is the volume of eluent carrier gas admitted to the column between the injection of the sample and the emergence of the peak maximum of the specified component. It includes the hold-up volume. In gas chromatography, the volume of carrier gas is specified at the outlet pressure and temperature of the column. Note: the word 'total' in this definition allows retention time to be used as a general term when specification of a particular quantity is not required. The adjusted retention volume, \(V_{\rm{R}}^{'}\), is the total retention volume less the hold-up volume, \(V_{\rm{M}}\), i.e. \[V_{\rm{R}}^{'}=V_{\rm{R}}- V_{\rm{M}}=\overline{V}- V_{\rm{I}}\] where \(\overline{V}\) is the peak elution volume and \(V_{\rm{I}}\) the interstitial volume. The net retention volume, \(V_{\rm{N}}\), is the adjusted retention volume multiplied by the pressure-gradient correction factor: \[V_{\rm{N}}=j\ V_{\rm{R}}^{'}\] The specific retention volume, \(V_{\rm{g}}\), is the net retention volume per gram of stationary liquid, active solid or solvent-free gel. In liquid chromatography, except when conducted at very high pressures, the compression of the mobile phase is negligible, and the adjusted and net retention volumes are identical. The specific retention volume is then the adjusted retention volume per gram of stationary liquid, active solid, or solvent-free gel. It is recommended that, when appropriate, authors specify the drying conditions. At \(0\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\), \[V_{\rm{g}}=273\ \frac{V_{\rm{N}}}{w_{\rm{L}}\ T}\] where \(w_{\rm{L}}\) is the mass of the stationary liquid phase.

08869.title: reticulate doped polymer
