08869.definition: Surface-conducting polymer composite obtained by crystallization of a low-molar-mass organic conductor on an insulating or semiconducting polymer support.

11179.title: retina
11179.definition: Multicell-layer membrane in the back of the eye that is sensitive to light and transduces incoming optical information into signals that are necessary for vision.

R05369.title: retinoids
R05369.definition: Oxygenated derivatives of 3,7-dimethyl-1-(2,6,6-trimethylcyclohex-1-enyl)nona-1,3,5,7-tetraene as shown and derivatives thereof.

11181.title: retinopathy
11181.definition: Noninflammatory degenerative disease of the retina.

R05370.title: retro
R05370.definition: A prefix which indicates a shift by one position of all single and double bonds in a conjugated polyene system. It has been applied only to carotenoids and retinoids, e.g. retro-carotenoids, retro-retinoids. A prefix which indicates the reverse sequence of a peptide.

12052.title: retrograde axonal transport
12052.definition: Transport of material from the nerve ending back to the cell body.

11954.title: retrograde neurotransmission
11954.definition: Neurotransmission wherein a neurotransmitter is sent from the postsynaptic to the presynaptic membrane in order to modify a signal.

15354.title: retrograde solubility
15354.definition:
Solubility that decreases with an increase in conditions such as temperature or added component, where an increase is expected as the usual case.
In ternary liquid systems with coexisting phases, where the critical solution point is not a maximum on a ternary diagram, passing from a homogeneous mixture in which the composition of a given component is greater than that of the critical mixture to a heterogeneous mixture and back to a homogeneous mixture by altering the relative amounts of the two other components.

11183.title: retroperitoneal
11183.definition: Outside of and posterior to the peritoneum.

14995.title: retrospective risk assessment
14995.definition: Risk assessment dealing with an existing condition.

16052.title: retrospective study
16052.definition: Research design used to test etiological hypotheses in which inferences about exposure to the putative causal factor(s) are derived from data relating to characteristics of the persons or organisms under study or to events or experiences in their past.

12722.title: retrosynthesis
12722.definition: Process of conceptually deconstructing complex molecules into simpler fragments capable of chemical manipulation to reform the parent compound.

16053.title: returned effect of poisons
16053.definition: Enhancement of the dose–effect relationship for a poison following repeated exposure to decreasing doses.

12053.title: reuptake
12053.definition: Transporter-dependent resequestration of a neurotransmitter by a presynapticneuron, terminating synaptic transmission.

11184.title: reverse genetics
11184.definition: Approach to elucidating the function of a gene by studying the effects on phenotype of expressed variations in a known DNA sequence.

13648.title: reverse immunology
13648.definition: High-throughput procedure where information on potential immunogenic tumor proteins is gained from the amino acid sequences of gene products specifically expressed by the tumor, followed by predicted fitting of putative antigenic peptides to a peptide-binding groove, and finally experimental verification.

08934.title: reverse iodine-transfer polymerization
08934.definition: Iodine-transfer polymerization where the initial polymerization mixture comprises a conventional initiator (e.g., an azo-compound or a peroxide) and molecular iodine.

16054.title: reverse mutation
16054.definition: Mutation in a mutant allele which makes it capable of producing the nonmutant phenotype; this may result from restoration of the original DNA sequence of the gene or from production of a new DNA sequence which has the same effect.

RT06893.title: reverse osmosis
RT06893.definition: Liquid-phase pressure-driven separation process in which applied transmembrane pressure causes selective movement of solvent against its osmotic pressure difference.

09683.title: reverse passive agglutination
09683.definition: Modification of the indirect agglutination assay, where the particles are coated with antibody.

R05378.title: reverse transcriptases
R05378.definition: Enzymes found in retroviruses that can synthesize complementary single-strands of DNA from an mRNA sequence as template. They are used in genetic engineering to produce specific cDNA molecules from purified preparations of mRNA.

16055.title: reverse transcription
16055.definition: Process by which an RNA molecule is used as a template to make a single-stranded DNA copy.

R05375.title: reversed isotope dilution analysis
R05375.definition: Isotope dilution analysis used for the determination of the isotopic carrier in a solution of a radionuclide with the aid of one of its stable isotopes.

R05374.title: reversed direct-injection burner
R05374.definition: A direct-injection burner combines the function of nebulizer and burner. Most commonly the oxidant is also used for aspirating and nebulizing the sample. However, when the fuel is used for this purpose, the term reversed direct-injection burner is applied.

R05376.title: reversed-phase chromatography
R05376.definition: An elution procedure used in liquid chromatography in which the mobile phase is significantly more polar then the stationary phase, e.g. a microporous silica-based material with chemically bonded alkyl chains. The term 'reverse phase' is an incorrect expression to be avoided.

16056.title: reversible alteration
16056.definition: Change from normal structure or function, induced by a substance or other agent(s), that returns to normal status or within normal limits after cessation of exposure.

RT07572.title: reversible network
RT07572.definition: Polymer network that forms or breaks up as the temperature is changed or under the action of a force.

R05379.title: reversible transition
R05379.definition: A transition that returns a system directly to its original state by reversing the process that changed it.

08968.title: reversible-addition-fragmentation chain-transfer agent
08968.definition: Chain-transfer agent that provides chain transfer by a reversible-addition-fragmentation mechanism.

08935.title: reversible-addition-fragmentation chain-transfer polymerization
08935.definition: Degenerate-transfer radical polymerization in which chain activation and chain deactivation involve a degenerative chain-transfer process, which occurs by a two-step addition-fragmentation mechanism.

08922.title: reversible-addition-fragmentation radical polymerization
08922.definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization in which the dormant species is a stable (persistent) radical and the deactivation step involves reversible fragmentation.

08981.title: reversible-deactivation anionic polymerization
08981.definition: Reversible-deactivation polymerization in which the kinetic-chain carriers are anions.

08988.title: reversible-deactivation cationic polymerization
08988.definition: Reversible-deactivation polymerization in which the chain carriers are cations.

08999.title: reversible-deactivation coordination polymerization
08999.definition: Reversible-deactivation polymerization in which the chain carriers are coordination complexes.

08976.title: reversible-deactivation ionic polymerization
08976.definition: Reversible-deactivation polymerization in which the kinetic-chain carriers are ions.

08912.title: reversible-deactivation polymerization
08912.definition: Chain polymerization, propagated by chain carriers that are deactivated reversibly, bringing them into active-dormant equilibria of which there might be more than one.

08916.title: reversible-deactivation radical polymerization
08916.definition: Chain polymerization, propagated by radicals that are deactivated reversibly, bringing them into active-dormant equilibria of which there might be more than one.

12797.title: reversing heat flow
12797.definition: In modulated-temperature DSC the heat-capacity component of the total heat flow that is in-phase with the temperature modulation.

12054.title: Rey–Osterrieth complex figure test
12054.definition: Procedure in which the test subject first copies a complicated drawing and then is asked to draw it from memory.

16057.title: rhabdomyolysis
16057.definition: Acute, fulminating, potentially lethal disease of skeletal muscle that causes disintegration of striated muscle fibers as evidenced by myoglobin in the blood and urine.

R05381.title: rheology
R05381.definition: The study of the flow and deformation of matter under the influence of a mechanical force. It is concerned particularly with material behaviour which cannot be described by the simple linear models of hydrodynamics and elasticity. Some of these departures are due to the presence of colloidal particles or to the influence of surfaces.

RT07527.title: rheopexic gel
RT07527.definition: Gel for which the time of solidification after discontinuation of a relatively high shear rate, is reduced by applying a small shear rate.

R05382.title: rheopexy
R05382.definition: A phenomenon in which the time of solidification, after discontinuation of a relatively high shear rate, is shortened by applying a small shear rate.

11185.title: rhesus factor
11185.definition: Antigen that occurs on the red blood cells of about 85 per cent of humans and can cause hemolytic disease of the newborn (erythroblastosis fetalis) and hemolytic transfusion reactions.

13650.title: rheumatic fever
13650.definition: Inflammatory disease that may develop following a streptococcal infection such as strep throat, and may affect the heart, joints, skin, and brain.

13651.title: rheumatoid arthritis
13651.definition: Episodic inflammatory systemic disease with autoimmune pathogenetic mechanisms.

13652.title: rheumatoid factor
13652.definition: Immunoglobulins IgM, IgG, and IgA autoantibodies to the Fc region of IgG.

13653.title: rhinitis
13653.definition: Inflammation of the mucous membrane of the nose.

R05384.title: rhodamine dyes
R05384.definition: Dyes derived from condensation of phthalic anhydride with m-dialkylaminophenols.

11186.title: rhombencephalon
11186.definition: Posterior portion of the brain that includes the cerebellum, pons, and medulla.

R05385.title: rhombohedral graphite
R05385.definition: A thermodynamically unstable allotropic form of graphite with an ABCABC stacking sequence of the layers. The exact crystallographic description of this allotropic form is given by the space group \(D_{3\rm{d}}^{5}- R\overline{3}m\), (unit cell constants: \(a=256.6\ \mathrm{pm}\), \(c=1006.2\ \mathrm{pm}\)).

16058.title: rhonchus
16058.definition: Harsh crepitation in the throat, often resembling snoring.

RT07095.title: ribbon delocalisation
RT07095.definition: Electron delocalization realized in both acyclic and cyclic $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}conjugated}$, 1, and $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bonded}$, 2, ribbon-like systems.  For cyclic systems, a variety of linkage fashions between several ribbons (pericyclic, spirocyclic, longicyclic and laticyclic) is possible.

R05387.title: ribonucleotides
R05387.definition: Nucleotides in which the glycosyl group is a ribosyl group.

R05388.title: ribosomal RNA
R05388.definition: RNA molecules which are essential structural and functional components of ribosomes, the subcellular units responsible for protein synthesis.

R05389.title: ribosomes
R05389.definition: Subcellular units composed of specific RNA molecules and a large number of proteins that are responsible for protein synthesis.

R05390.title: Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel theory
R05390.definition: A theory of unimolecular gas reactions in which the rate with which the energized reactant molecule breaks down is treated as a function of the energy \(\varepsilon\) that it contains. The theory assumes that the rate is proportional to the number of ways of distributing \(\varepsilon\) among the internal degrees of freedom of the reactant molecule, in such a manner that the critical energy \(\varepsilon_{\rm{c}}\) is localized in one particular degree of freedom.

R05391.title: Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel–Marcus theory
R05391.definition: An improved form of Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel (RRK) theory in which account is taken of the way in which the various normal-mode vibrations and rotations contribute to reaction, and allowance is made for the zero-point energies. In this theory the energy \(\varepsilon^{\rm{*}}\) in an energized molecule is classified as either active, \(\varepsilon^{\rm{*active}}\), or inactive, \(\varepsilon^{\rm{*inactive}}\). The rate depends upon \(\frac{P(\varepsilon^{\rm{*active}})}{N(\varepsilon^{\rm{*}})}\), where \(N(\varepsilon^{\rm{*}})\) is the density of states having energy between \(\varepsilon^{\rm{*}}\) and \(\varepsilon^{\rm{*}}+\rm{d}\varepsilon^{\rm{*}}\), and \(P(\varepsilon^{\rm{*active}})\) is the sum of the active quantum states of the activated complex. This extension of RRK theory brings it in line with transition-state theory.

R05392.title: riffling
R05392.definition: The separation of a free-flowing sample into (usually) equal parts by means of a mechanical device composed of diverter chutes.

12055.title: righting reflex
12055.definition: Reflex that restores the correct orientation of the body when taken out of the upright position.

12056.title: righting test
12056.definition: Experimental measurement of an animal’s (usually a rodent’s) ability to land in an upright position at the end of a fall.

RT06871.title: rigid chain
RT06871.definition: The rod-like chain of an MCPLC (main-chain polymer liquid crystal) with direct links between the mesogenic groups for which the persistence length is at least comparable with the contour length and much greater than the diameter.

09111.title: rigid membranes
09111.definition: Kind of ion-selective membranes used in an ISE comprising synthetic cross-linked polymer with fixed sites or thin glass membrane.

R05393.title: ring assembly
R05393.definition: Two or more cyclic systems (single rings or fused systems) which are directly joined to each other by double or single bonds are named ring assemblies when the number of such direct ring junctions is one less than the number of cyclic systems involved. Examples:

R05397.title: ring reversal
R05397.definition: The interconversion by rotation about single bonds (coupled with angle deformation in the transition state) of cyclic conformers having equivalent ring shapes (e.g. chair → chair) though not necessarily equivalent spatial positions of substituents (e.g. equatorial → axial).

14996.title: ring test
14996.definition: Part of an external quality assurance program for assessment of an analytical method or test. A reference institute sends identical samples, which have to be analyzed or tested for specified parameters, to a number of different laboratories. The laboratory has a deadline before which to provide results. Statistical evaluation and interpretation of the results permits assessment of the reliability of the methods used and a comparison of the laboratories’ proficiency.

R05395.title: ring-opening copolymerization
R05395.definition: A copolymerization which is a ring-opening polymerization with respect to at least one monomer.

08993.title: ring-opening metathesis polymerization
08993.definition: Metathesis polymerization in which an unsaturated cyclic monomer is converted into an unsaturated monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

08983.title: ring-opening nucleophilic chain polymerization
08983.definition: Nucleophilic chain polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

R05396.title: ring-opening polymerization
R05396.definition: A polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit which is acyclic or contains fewer cycles than the monomer.

R05398.title: ring-sector
R05398.definition: A sequence of ring atoms, linked together as an unbranched chain and connecting two bridgehead or junctions, but not itself containing any bridgehead or junction, is termed an atomic ring-sector. A bond linking together directly two bridgeheads or junctions is termed a bond ring-sector.

R05394.title: Ringelmann chart
R05394.definition: A chart which has been used in air pollution evaluation for assigning the degree of blackness of smoke emanating from a source. The observer compares the shades of grey (white to black) with a series of shade diagrams formed by horizontal and vertical black grid lines on a white background. A corresponding number, the Ringelmann number, is then assigned to the describe the best match; numbers range from 0 (white) to 5 (black). This method of pollution evaluation, although relevant to the enforcement of legislation still in force in many countries, is not recommended for use today since more quantitative indicators of the efficiency of the combustion are now available.

RT07529.title: ringing gel
RT07529.definition: Gel with energy dissipation in the acoustic frequency range.

10254.title: rinse solvent
10254.definition: Weak solvent used to displace matrix components from a sorbent without displacing the target analyte(s).

14997.title: riparian
14997.definition: Interface between land and a flowing body of surface water.

R05400.title: rise time
R05400.definition: The difference between the response time and the dead time.

RT06807.title: risk
RT06807.definition: Probability of adverse effects caused under specified circumstances by an agent in an organism, a population, or an ecological system.Expected frequency of occurrence of a harmful event arising from such an exposure.

14998.title: risk analysis
14998.definition: Process for controlling situations where an organism, system, or subpopulation could be exposed to a hazard.

RT06808.title: risk assessment
RT06808.definition: Identification and quantification of the risk resulting from a specific use or occurrence of an agent, taking into account possible harmful effects on individuals exposed to the agent in the amount and manner proposed and all the possible routes of exposure.

14405.title: risk assessment management process
14405.definition: Global term for the whole process from hazard identification to risk management.

16059.title: risk associated with a lifetime exposure
16059.definition: Probability of the occurrence of a specified undesirable event following exposure of an individual person from a given population to a specified substance at a defined level for the expected lifetime of the average member of that population.

16060.title: risk aversion
16060.definition: Tendency of an individual person to avoid risk.

14999.title: risk characterisation
14999.definition: Outcome of hazard identification and risk estimation applied to a specific use of a substance or occurrence of an environmental health hazard.

16061.title: risk communication
16061.definition: Interpretation and communication of risk assessments in terms that are comprehensible to the general public or to others without specialist knowledge.

16062.title: risk de minimis
16062.definition: Risk that is negligible and too small to be of societal concern (usually assumed to be a probability below \(\pu{E-5}\) or \(\pu{E-6}\)).

RT06913.title: risk estimation
RT06913.definition: Assessment with or without mathematical modeling, of the probability and nature of effects of exposure to a substance based on quantification of dose-effect and dose-response relationships for that substance and the population(s) and environmental components likely to be exposed and on assessment of the levels of potential exposure of people, organisms, and environment at risk.

16063.title: risk evaluation
16063.definition: Establishment of a qualitative or quantitative relationship between risks and benefits, involving the complex process of determining the significance of the identified hazards and estimated risks to those organisms or people concerned with or affected by them.

15000.title: risk hypotheses
15000.definition: Clear statements of postulated or predicted adverse effects of a toxicant on an assessment endpoint.

16064.title: risk identification
16064.definition: Recognition of a potential hazard and definition of the factors required to assess the probability of exposure of organisms or people to that hazard and of harm resulting from such exposure.

14406.title: risk management
14406.definition: Decision-making process involving considerations of political, social, economic, and engineering factors with relevant risk assessments relating to a potential hazard so as to develop, analyze, and compare regulatory options and to select the optimal regulatory response for safety from that hazard.

16065.title: risk marker
16065.definition: Attribute that is associated with an increased probability of occurrence of a disease or other specified outcome and that can be used as an indicator of this increased risk.

16066.title: risk monitoring
16066.definition: Process of following up the decisions and actions within risk management in order to check whether the aims of reduced exposure and risk are achieved.

16067.title: risk perception
16067.definition: Subjective perception of the gravity or importance of the risk based on a person’s knowledge of different risks and the moral, economic, and political judgment of their implications.

16068.title: risk phrases
16068.definition: Word groups identifying potential health or environmental hazards required under CPL Directives (European Community); may be incorporated into Safety Data Sheets.

15002.title: risk quotient
15002.definition: Ratio of predicted exposure concentration (PEC) to predicted no-effect concentration (PNEC).

16225.title: risk ratio
16225.definition: Value obtained by dividing the probability of occurrence of a specific effect in one group by the probability of occurrence of the same effect in another group, or the value obtained by dividing the probability of occurrence of one potentially hazardous event by the probability of occurrence of another.

15003.title: risk reduction
15003.definition: Taking measures to protect humans or the environment against identified risks.

15001.title: risk source
15001.definition: Agent, medium, process, procedure, or site with the potential to cause an adverse effect or effects.

16069.title: risk-specific dose
16069.definition: Amount of exposure corresponding to a specified level of risk.

R05402.title: Ritchie equation
R05402.definition: The linear free-energy relation \[\log _{10}k_{\rm{N}} = \log _{10}k_{0}+N_{\rm{+}}\] applied to the reactions between nucleophiles and certain large and relatively stable organic cations, e.g. arenediazonium, triarylmethyl and aryltropylium cations in various solvents. \(k_{\rm{N}}\) is the rate constant for reaction of a given cation with a given nucleophilic system (i.e. given nucleophile in a given solvent). \(k_{0}\) is the rate constant for the same cation with water in water, and \(N_{\rm{+}}\) is a parameter which is characteristic of the nucleophilic system and independent of the cation. A surprising feature of the equation is the absence of a coefficient of \(N_{\rm{+}}\), characteristic of the substrate (cf. the \(s\) in the Swain–Scott equation), even though values of \(N_{\rm{+}}\) vary over 13 log units. The equation thus involves a gigantic breakdown of the reactivity–selectivity principle. The equation has been extended both in form and in range of application.

15004.title: rivet popper hypothesis
15004.definition: Hypothesis that each species in a community contributes to its proper functioning.

R05022.title: RM value
R05022.definition: A logarithmic function of the \(R_{\rm{F}}\) value (retardation factor): \[R_{\rm{M}}=\log _{10}(\frac{1\,-\,R_{\rm{F}}}{R_{\rm{F}}})=\log _{10}(\frac{1}{R_{\rm{F}}}\,-\,1)\]

11187.title: RNA interference
11187.definition: Effect of small, often double-stranded RNA targeting a specific messenger RNA (mRNA), blocking its translation, and thereby silencing expression of the corresponding gene.

11188.title: Robertsonian translocation
11188.definition: Chromosomal translocation in which chromosomes with acrocentric centromeres break the centromere to fuse the long arms into a new large chromosome and the short arms into another small one that may be lost, leaving a karyotype in the human of \(\pu{45}\) chromosomes.

14186.title: robot
14186.definition: Automated device that performs tasks (i.e., screen functions) that would normally be performed by a human.

13655.title: rocket electrophoresis
13655.definition: Technique in which a test antigen is electrophoretically driven through an antibody-containing gel. The rocket-shaped tails of precipitation give information on the antigen concentration.

13852.title: rod-coil copolymer
13852.definition: Copolymer the molecules of which consist of rigid and flexible blocks.

RT07308.title: rod-like morphology
RT07308.definition: Morphology characterized by cylindrical phase domains.

R05404.title: röntgen
R05404.definition: Non-SI unit of exposure to X- or $\upgamma\!\mbox{-}\rm{radiation}$: \(\rm{R} = \pu{2.58E-4 C kg}\).

10109.title: root mean square error of cross validation
10109.definition: Root mean square error of prediction when the predicted data is obtained by cross validation.

10157.title: root mean squared error of calibration
10157.definition: In calibration for \(N\) calibration data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the value predicted by the calibration function. \[E_{\rm{RMSEC}} = \sqrt \frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i,=\,N} (\hat c_{i} - c_{i})^2}{N}\]

10110.title: root mean squared error of prediction
10110.definition: In multivariate calibration or classification for \(N\) evaluation data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the predicted value \[E_{\rm{RMSEP}} = \sqrt {\frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i}\,-\,c_{i})^2}{N}}\]

R05405.title: root-mean-square end-to-end distance
R05405.definition: The square root of the mean-square end-to-end distance of a linear polymer chain averaged over all conformations of the chain. For a freely jointed chain consisting of \(N\) segments each of length \(L\), it is given by: \[\rm{}^{1/2} = \sqrt{N}\ L\] The subscript zero is used to indicate unperturbed dimensions, as in \(\rm{}_{0}^{1/2}\). If this term is used repeatedly, and if it is not confusing, the abbreviated name 'end-to-end distance' may be used.

12200.title: root-mean-square end-to-end distance of a freely rotating chain
12200.definition: Root-mean-square end-to-end distance of a linear freely rotating chain.

12191.title: root-mean-square radius of gyration
12191.definition: For a flexible macromolecule composed of \(n\) mass elements, of masses \(m_{i}\), \(i = 1, 2, \ldots, n\), located at statistical-mechanical mean-square distances \(\lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\) from the centre of mass, the root-mean-square radius of gyration is the square-root of the mass average of \(\lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\) over all mass elements, i.e., \[\lt\!s^{2}\!\gt^{1/2}\;= \left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} m_{i} \lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\!/\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} m_{i} \right)^{1/2}\]

12198.title: root-mean-square unperturbed end-to-end distance
12198.definition: Root-mean-square end-to-end distance of a chain having unperturbed dimensions.

12193.title: root-mean-square unperturbed radius of gyration
12193.definition: Root-mean-square radius of gyration of a macromolecule having unperturbed dimensions.

13656.title: rosette
13656.definition: Particles or cells bound to the surface of a lymphocyte (e.g., sheep erythrocytes around a human T cell).

11189.title: rostral
11189.definition:
Pertaining to, resembling, or having a rostrum or beak.
Situated toward the beak (thus, oral and nasal region), which may mean superior (in relationships of areas of the spinal cord) or anterior or ventral (in relationships of brain areas).
Closer to the head.

R05407.title: rotamer
R05407.definition: One of a set of conformers arising from restricted rotation about one single bond.

12058.title: rotarod test
12058.definition: Experimental observation of an animal’s (usually a rodent’s) ability to stay on a rotating rod without falling off.

09584.title: rotated Fischer projection
09584.definition: Projection formula for macromolecules in which horizontal lines denote polymer backbone bonds. At each individual backbone carbon atom, horizontal lines represent bonds directed below the projection plane and vertical lines represent bonds directed above that plane.

09124.title: rotating disc electrode
09124.definition: A disc electrode that is embedded in the centre of a cylinder which rotates in solution around the longitudinal cylinder axis.

10274.title: rotating disk sorptive extraction
10274.definition: Sorbent-coated disc consisting of a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) base with an integrated magnet and a sorbent film attached to one side.

08408.title: rotating-frame NOE spectroscopy
08408.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy yielding through-space correlations via spin-spin relaxation.

08676.title: rotation-vibration spectrum
08676.definition: Spectrum that shows absorption or emission of radiation during transitions between rotational-vibrational states of a molecule.

R05408.title: rotational barrier
R05408.definition: In a rotation of groups about a bond, the potential energy barrier between two adjacent minima of the molecular entity as a function of the torsion angle.

08675.title: rotational branch
08675.definition: Spectral lines in the rotation-vibration spectrum of a gas that derive from the same change in rotation quantum number, \(J\).

R05409.title: rotational constants
R05409.definition: Coefficients of quantum numbers in the rotational term expression and inversely proportional to the principal moments of inertia. Symbols: \(A\), \(B\), \(C\). \(\overset{˜}{A}=\frac{h}{8\ \pi ^{2}\ c\ I_{\rm{A}}}\) (dimension wavenumber), \(A=\frac{h}{8\ \pi ^{2}\ I_{\rm{A}}}\) (dimension frequency) where \(h\) is the Planck constant and \(c\) the speed of light in vacuum.

RT07474.title: rotational correlation time
RT07474.definition: Parameter describing the time dependence of the tumbling of a molecular entity in a medium of viscosity \(\eta\). The rotational correlation time can be obtained from the decay of the fluorescence or phosphorescence anisotropy and is related to the average molecular rotational diffusion coefficient, \(D_{\rm{r}}\), in turn related to the hydrodynamic molecular volume of the fluorophore, \(V\), and to \(\eta\) (see Note 3).

R05410.title: rotational diffusion
R05410.definition: A process by which the equilibrium statistical distribution of the overall orientation of molecules or particles is maintained or restored. Rotational diffusion may be compared to translational diffusion through which the equilibrium statistical distribution of position in space is maintained or restored.

R05411.title: rotational diffusion coefficient
R05411.definition: Defined by the equation: \[D_{\theta }=\frac{t_{\theta }}{\frac{\partial (f(\theta ,\mathit{\Phi }))}{\partial \theta }\ \sin\,\theta }\] where \(f\left(\theta ,\mathit{\Phi }\right)\:\sin \,\theta \ \rm{d}\theta \ \rm{d}\mathit{\Phi }\) is the fraction of particles whose axes make an angle between \(\theta \) and \(\theta +\mathrm{d}\theta \) with the direction \(\theta =0\), and have an azimuth between \(\mathit{\Phi}\) and \(\mathit{\Phi} + \rm{d}\mathit{\Phi}\); \(t_{\theta }\ \mathrm{d}\mathit{\Phi }\) is the fraction of particles having an azimuth between \(\mathit{\Phi}\) and \(\mathit{\Phi} + \rm{d}\mathit{\Phi}\) whose axis passes from values \(\theta \) in unit time. The axis whose rotational diffusion is considered has to be clearly indicated.

08409.title: rotational echo double resonance
08409.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy allowing recoupling of heteronuclear dipolar coupling under magic angle spinning.

R05412.title: rotational frequency
R05412.definition: The number of rotations divided by time: \[f_{\rm{rot}}=\frac{\rm{d}N}{\rm{d}t}\] The synonyms rate of rotation, rate of revolution, centrifugal speed, centrifugation speed, and the traditional units of rotational frequency such as revolutions per minute, r.p.m., ppm, \(\rm{rev min}^{-1}\), \(\rm{r min}^{-1}\), are not recommended.

12248.title: rotational frictional coefficient
12248.definition: Torque, \(T\), per unit angular velocity, \(\omega\), required for rotation of a body about a given axis in a viscous isotropic fluid, i.e., \(T = \zeta\omega\).

12187.title: rotational isomeric state
12187.definition: Rotamer defined by a relative rotation about a skeletal bond of a single-strand chain.

RT07475.title: rotational relaxation time
RT07475.definition: Parameter describing the time-dependence of the tumbling of a molecular entity in a medium of viscosity \(\eta\) as originally defined by Debye, and used by Perrin in the original development of the theories of rotational motion of fluorophores.

R05413.title: rotational term
R05413.definition: Rotational energy divided by the product of the Planck constant and the speed of light.

R05414.title: rotator phase transition
R05414.definition: A transition from a fully-ordered crystal of globular or quasi-spherical molecules to a crystal that retains translational order but exhibits dynamic orientational disorder and is usually mechanically soft (plastic phase). Example: The transition of $\ce{CBr4}$ to a plastic phase which exists from \(319\) to \(365\ \rm{K}\).

R05415.title: rotatory power
R05415.definition: The quantitative measure of optical activity.

13975.title: rotaxane constitutional repeating unit
13975.definition: Constitutional repeating unit (CRU) that has a rotaxane structure.

13976.title: rotaxane constitutional unit
13976.definition: Constitutional unit (CU) that has a rotaxane structure.

13977.title: rotaxane end-unit
13977.definition: Constitutional unit of a macromolecular rotaxane consisting of an end-group of its macromolecular component and a complementary threading or macrocyclic component.

13979.title: rotaxane monomeric unit
13979.definition: Monomeric unit (monomer unit, mer) that has a rotaxane structure.

13980.title: rotaxane polymer
13980.definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules that are macromolecular rotaxanes.

R05416.title: rotaxanes
R05416.definition: Molecules in which a ring encloses another, rod-like molecule having end groups too large to pass through the ring opening, and thus holds the rod-like molecule in position without covalent bonding.

R05417.title: rotenoids
R05417.definition: Naturally occurring substances containing a cis-fused tetrahydrochromeno[3,4-b]chromene nucleus. Many rotenoids contain an additional ring, e.g rotenone:

R05418.title: rotometer
R05418.definition: A device, based on Stokes law, for measuring rate of fluid flow. It is a tapered vertical tube having a circular cross-section in which a float moves in a vertical path to a height dependent upon the rate of fluid flow upward through the tube.

R05419.title: roughness factor
R05419.definition: The ratio: \[f_{\rm{r}}=\frac{A_{\rm{r}}}{A_{\rm{g}}}\] where \(A_{\rm{r}}\) is the real (true, actual) surface (interface) area and \(A_{\rm{g}}\) is the geometric surface (interface) area.

12267.title: Rouse chain
12267.definition: Hypothetical polymer chain satisfying the assumptions made in the Rouse theory.

12266.title: Rouse theory
12266.definition: Molecular theory for treating polymer chain dynamics based on the bead-spring model assuming the beads (segments) have zero excluded volume and there is no hydrodynamic interaction between the beads.

16071.title: route of exposure
16071.definition: Means by which a toxic agent gains access to an organism by administration through the gastrointestinal tract (ingestion), lungs (inhalation), skin (topical), or by other routes such as intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, or intraperitoneal routes.

R05420.title: rovibronic state
R05420.definition: A state corresponding to a particular rotational sublevel of a particular vibrational level of a particular electronic state.

RT06793.title: rubredoxin
RT06793.definition: An iron-sulfur protein without acid-labile sulfur, in which an iron centre is coordinated by four sulfur-containing ligands, usually cysteine. The function, where known, is an electron carrier.

R05427.title: ruby laser
R05427.definition: A pulsed source of coherent radiation emitting mainly at \(\pu{694.3 nm}\) from chromium ions ($\ce{Cr^{3+}}$) in aluminium oxide.

08123.title: ruggedness of a measurement procedure
08123.definition: Ability of a measurement procedure to maintain acceptable performance under minor changes in operating conditions.

11507.title: rule of five
11507.definition: The rule of five states that molecules that violate two or more of the following rules are likely to have permeability problems; (1) CLOGP calculated octan-1-ol-water log P greater than 5.0; (2) molecular weight greater than 500; (3) more than five hydrogen bond donors; and (4) the sum of oxygen and nitrogen atoms is greater than 10.

12723.title: rule of three
12723.definition: Set of molecular descriptors used to assess the quality of hit or lead molecules.

15006.title: rules of practical causal inference
15006.definition: Fox’s rules of practical causal inference that are used in ecotoxicology (environmental epidemiology) to infer causality for toxicant exposure/effect scenarios.

08041.title: run bias
08041.definition: Contribution to measurement bias that is attributed to systematic effects on measurement results made in a single analytical run.

15007.title: run-off
15007.definition: Portion of the wet precipitation on the land that ultimately reaches streams and, eventually, the sea.

11190.title: runt
11190.definition: Smallest and weakest animal of a litter.

R05428.title: rupture
R05428.definition: The formation of a hole which permits coalescence or direct contact of the two phases which it separates.

R05429.title: Rutherford backscattering
R05429.definition: Any technique using high energy particles directed toward a sample, in which the bombarding particles are detected and recorded as function of energy and/or angle. The technique is mostly used for determining depth distributions of elements based on the energy of the backscattered particle. In general, $\ce{He^{+}}$ or $\ce{H^{+}}$ particles are used at energies in the order of \(100\ \rm{keV}\) to some \(\mathrm{MeV}\). Also referred to as backscattering spectrometry (BSS).

09178.title: Rutherford backscattering spectrometry
09178.definition: Measurement method to elucidate composition and structure of layers at the surface of a solid material, in which principally monoenergetic, singly charged probe ions scattered from the surface with a Rutherford cross section are detected and recorded as a function of their energy or angle of scattering, or both.

09381.title: Rutherford cross section
09381.definition: Elastic scattering cross section calculated using classical mechanics and a Coulomb potential.

R05430.title: Rydberg constant
R05430.definition: Atomic fundamental physical constant \(R_{\infty} = \frac{E_{h}}{2\ h\ c_{0}} = 1.097\ 373\ 1534\ (13)\times 10^{7}\ \rm{m}^{-1}\), where \(E_{h}\) is the Hartree energy, \(h\) the Planck constant, and \(c_{0}\) the speed of light.

R05431.title: Rydberg orbital
R05431.definition: For an atom, an orbital with principal quantum number greater than that of any occupied orbital of the ground state. For a molecular entity, a molecular orbital which correlates with a Rydberg atomic orbital in an atomic fragment produced by dissociation. Typically, the extension of the Rydberg orbital is large compared to the size of the atom or molecular entity.

RT07096.title: Rydberg state
RT07096.definition: An electronic state that arises by the excitation of a valence electron to a diffuse atomic-like orbital. For instance, the lowest lying Rydberg state (n, 3S) of $\ce{NH3}$ can be described as resulting from the excitation of a non-bonding orbital to a 3S Rydberg orbital.

R05432.title: Rydberg transition
R05432.definition: An electronic transition described approximately as promotion of an electron from a 'bonding' orbital to a Rydberg orbital. Spectral bands corresponding to Rydberg transitions approximately fit the Rydberg formula: \[\sigma = I - \frac{R}{(n\,-\,\mathit{\Delta })^{2}}\] where \(\sigma \) is the wavenumber, \(I\) the ionization potential of the atom or molecular entity, \(n\) a principal quantum number, \(R\) the Rydberg constant, and \(\mathit{\Delta}\) the quantum defect which differentiates between s, p, d, etc., orbitals. The notation used is, e.g. \(\pi \rightarrow \mathrm{ns}\).

R02568.title: γ-radiation
R02568.definition: Electromagnetic radiation emitted in the process of nuclear transformation or particle annihilation.

R02570.title: γ-ray spectrometer
R02570.definition: A measuring assembly for determining the energy spectrum of $\upgamma\!\mbox{-}\rm{rays}$.

13921.title: synthetic biopolymer
13921.definition: Copy of a biopolymer man-made using abiotic chemical routes.

13945.title: stealth
13945.definition: Qualifier for a macromolecule, a surface, or a device that is not detected by defense proteins of the complement and the Mononuclear Phagocyte System, especially macrophages, after introduction in parental compartments.

13962.title: sustainability
13962.definition: Developments that meet the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.

14227.title: symmetry breaking
14227.definition: Vanishing, in a specific crystal polymorph, of selected symmetry elements present in other crystal polymorphs, or in selected minimum energy conformations of isolated molecules of a given substance.

14246.title: solidification model
14246.definition: Model of crystalline polymer formed by lamellar crystallization from the melt, in which some stems of a macromolecule belong to one crystal, whilst other stems of the same macromolecule are in different crystals.

12562.title: saddle field gun
12562.definition: Compact ion and fast atom sources for use when small size and high beam intensity are required, as in fast atom bombardment mass spectrometry. The discharge is produced by electrons oscillating between two cold cathodes in an electric field that possesses a single saddle point. To produce and intensify the plasma the electrons must have long path lengths, achieved by allowing the electrons to have an oscillatory motion in the saddle-shaped electric field between the cathodes separated by the anode.

12563.title: sampling cone
12563.definition: Component of a spray ionization interface that consists of a cone with a small orifice through which the spray passes into a differentially pumped chamber

12564.title: scan cycle time
12564.definition: Time required to obtain a mass spectrum (or other mass spectrometric data quantity) such as in a separation coupled to mass spectrometry.

12565.title: secondary neutral mass spectrometry
12565.definition: Mass spectrometry technique in which neutral species ejected from a sample surface as a result of bombardment by a primary beam of atoms or ions are ionized, most often by photoionization, prior to analysis.

12566.title: sector mass spectrometer
12566.definition: Mass spectrometer consisting of one or more magnetic sectors for recording a mass spectrum of a monoenergetic beam of ions. Such instruments may also have one or more electric sectors for energy dispersion that can be arranged for velocity-focusing by compensating for dispersion by the magnetic sector if the beam is not truly monoenergetic. Such a combination provides double focusing of ions of the same m/z, i.e., focusing with respect to both direction and speed.

12567.title: selected ion flow tube
12567.definition: Device in which m/z selected ions are entrained in an inert carrier gas and subsequently undergo ion/molecule reactions with molecules introduced into the gas flow.

12568.title: selected reaction monitoring
12568.definition: Data acquired from one or more specific product ions corresponding to m/z selected precursor ions recorded via two or more stages of mass spectrometry.

12569.title: self-chemical ionization
12569.definition: Chemical ionization of an analyte where the reagent ion is an ionized form of the analyte or one of its product ions.

12570.title: sheath flow interface
12570.definition: Capillary electrophoresis to electrospray ionization interface that uses a coaxial flow of make-up liquid that is introduced through a tube that is concentric with the separation capillary.

12571.title: sheath gas
12571.definition: Gas introduced through a tube that is coaxial with the electrospray emitter to pneumatically assist the formation of the sprayed droplets.

12572.title: sheath liquid
12572.definition: Make-up liquid in a sheath flow interface

12573.title: shotgun proteomics
12573.definition: Protein identification using a combination of high-performance liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry in which the proteins in a mixture are digested, usually by a specific enzyme, and the resulting peptides are separated by liquid chromatography and identified by tandem mass spectrometry.

12574.title: skimmer
12574.definition: Cone with a central orifice that intercepts the center of a spray or jet expansion to sample the central portion of the expansion, for example, as in a momentum separator.

12575.title: soft ionization
12575.definition: Formation of gas-phase ions without extensive fragmentation.

12576.title: sonic spray ionization
12576.definition: Process in which both anions and cations are produced at atmospheric pressure from an ionic solution due to a statistically unbalanced charge distribution in the minute droplets formed by the action of a sonic atomizer.

12577.title: space charge effect
12577.definition: Result of mutual repulsion of particles of like charge (ions, electrons, etc.) that can limit the current in a charged-particle beam and can also cause some motion of ions in a beam or packet in addition to that caused by external fields.

12578.title: spectral skewing
12578.definition: Deviation of the peak intensities in a mass spectrum from their expected values that occurs when the relative concentration of the various analytes change during acquisition of the mass spectrum.

12579.title: spray ionization
12579.definition: General term used to describe a range of ionization techniques for analytes in solution that involve dispersing the liquid into fine droplets as a component step.

12580.title: stable isotope ratio analysis of amino acids in cell culture
12580.definition: Proteomics technique that detects differences in protein abundance between cultured cell samples using stable isotopic labeling achieved with labeled amino acids in one cell culture and unlabeled ones in a separate culture.

12581.title: stable isotope standards and capture by anti-peptide antibodies
12581.definition: Method for absolute quantitation of a protein or proteins in a multiplexed fashion using isotope-labeled peptides as surrogate internal standards. The labeled peptides are produced by synthesizing a gene coding for each desired peptide, cell-free transcription, and translation of this gene in a medium containing \(\ce{^{13}C6}\)-labeled lysine, and digesting with trypsin the expressed protein composed of the desired concatenated peptides. For low-abundance proteins the sensitivity is increased by selective enrichment of the target peptides by antibody capture.

14258.title: subsidiary lamellae
14258.definition: Lamellar crystals nucleated either epitaxially or incoherently on dominant lamellae.

12582.title: static field
12582.definition: Electric or magnetic field that does not change in time.

12583.title: Stevenson’s rule
12583.definition: Rule stating that in competing fragmentations the product ion formed from its neutral species counterpart with the lower ionization energy will usually be the more abundant.

12584.title: stored waveform inverse fourier transform
12584.definition: Technique to create excitation waveforms for ions in Fourier transform-ion cyclotron resonance-mass spectrometers or Paul ion traps. An excitation waveform in the time-domain is generated by taking the inverse Fourier transform of an appropriate frequency-domain programmed excitation spectrum, in which the resonance frequencies of ions to be excited are included.

12585.title: supercritical fluid chromatography-mass spectrometry
12585.definition: Combined technique in which a mixture of analytes is separated into solutions of individual components by chromatography that uses a supercritical fluid as mobile phase, followed by the ionization of the separation effluent in the ion source of a mass spectrometer.

12586.title: surface-enhanced laser desorption/ionization
12586.definition: Variant of matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI) in which the matrix is replaced by a surface coating of a chromatographic stationary phase designed to selectively retain different subsets of proteins or peptides from a mixture depending on their physico-chemical properties or biochemical affinity characteristics.

12587.title: surface-induced dissociation
12587.definition: Fragmentation that results from the collision of an ion with a surface.

12588.title: surface-induced reaction
12588.definition: Process wherein a reactant ion interacts with a surface to produce either chemically different species or a change in the internal energy of the reactant ion.

12589.title: surrogate internal standard
12589.definition: Compound added in accurately known amounts to a sample to be analyzed for a specified analyte. The surrogate internal standard is chemically similar to the analyte so that losses in the analytical procedure are the same for both and thus the analyte concentration can be determined relative to that of the standard.

12590.title: sustained off-resonance irradiation
12590.definition: Procedure associated with Fourier transform-ion cyclotron resonance-mass spectrometers to facilitate ion/neutral reactions such as low-energy collision-induced dissociation in which a radio-frequency electric field, slightly off-resonance with respect to the cyclotron frequency of the reactant ion, cyclically accelerates and decelerates the reactant ion that is confined in the Penning ion trap. As a consequence, the orbit does not exceed the dimensions of the ion trap but maintains a high average translational energy for an extended time that activates an ion/neutral process.

14269.title: secondary nucleation
14269.definition: Nucleation of a new molecular layer on a growing crystal face.Note: Secondary nucleation refers to the further growth of an already-existing crystal.

14270.title: self-nucleation
14270.definition: Heterogeneous nucleation by crystals of the same polymer.

14272.title: supercooled melt
14272.definition: Metastable melt of a crystallizable polymer at temperatures below its equilibrium melting temperature \(T^{\circ}_{\rm{m}}\).

14273.title: supercooling
14273.definition: The process of cooling a melt to a temperature below its equilibrium melting point, without crystallization occurring.

13917.title: solid dispersion
13917.definition: Solid multiphasic mixture with at least one polymer component dominating.

13919.title: stimulus-responsive polymer
13919.definition: Polymer that responds or that is designed to respond to a stimulus like pH, light, heat, etc. change, and provides a predetermined action.

13920.title: sustained delivery
13920.definition: Supply of a substance from a container where it is temporarily entrapped for the sake of achieving a prolonged action.

S05508.title: s-cis, s-trans
S05508.definition: The spatial arrangement of two conjugated double bonds about the intervening single bond is described as s-cis if synperiplanar and s-trans if antiperiplanar. This term should not be applied to other systems such as N-alkyl amides (use E/Z or sp/ap).

16072.title: S9 fraction
16072.definition: Supernatant fraction obtained from an organ (usually liver) homogenate by centrifuging at \(\pu{9000 g}\) for \(\pu{20 min}\) in a suitable medium; this fraction contains cytosol and microsomes.

12059.title: saccadic eye movement
12059.definition: Rapid or jerky movement of the eyes from one line of sight to another, as in reading or correction of a jerky nystagmus.

S05441.title: saccharides
S05441.definition: The monosaccharides (1) and di- (2), oligo- (3 - 10) and polysaccharides (many), which are made up of $n$ monosaccharide units linked to each other by a glycosidic bond. Considered by some to be synonymous with carbohydrates.

09857.title: saccharolipids
09857.definition: Biomolecules where fatty acids are directly bound to a saccharide backbone, thus forming structures similar to glycerolipids or glycerophospholipids, with saccharide substituting for the glycerol.

S05442.title: Sackur–Tetrode constant
S05442.definition: Fundamental physical constant representing the translational contribution to molar entropy; \(\frac{S_{0}}{R} = -1.151\ 693(21)\) at \(1\ \rm{K}\) and standard pressure of \(100\ \rm{kPa}\), where \(R\) is the gas constant.

11191.title: sacral agenesis
11191.definition: Absence or significant underdevelopment of the lower part of the spine and the lower limbs.

S05443.title: sacrificial acceptor
S05443.definition: Molecular entity that acts as the electron acceptor in a photoinduced electron transfer process and is not restored in a subsequent oxidation process but is destroyed by irreversible chemical conversion.

S05444.title: sacrificial donor
S05444.definition: Molecular entity that acts as the electron donor in a photoinduced electron transfer process and is not restored in a subsequent reduction process but is destroyed by irreversible chemical conversion.

15008.title: safe concentration
15008.definition: Concentration of a substance to which prolonged exposure will cause no adverse effect.

14407.title: safety
14407.definition: Reciprocal of risk: practical certainty that injury will not result from a hazard under defined conditions.

14408.title: safety data sheet
14408.definition: Single page giving toxicological and other safety advice, usually associated with a particular preparation, substance, process, use pattern, or exposure scenario.

16073.title: safety pharmacology
16073.definition: Science directed to the discovery, development, and safe therapeutic use of biologically active substances as a result of the identification, monitoring, and characterization of potentially undesirable pharmacodynamic activities of these substances in nonclinical studies.

11192.title: sagittal
11192.definition: Vertical (longitudinal) plane dividing the body into right and left sections.

08542.title: Saha’s ionization equation
08542.definition: Equation that relates the ionization state of an element present in a gas in thermal equilibrium to the temperature and the pressure of the medium.

12060.title: Saint Anthony fire
12060.definition: Referring to inflammatory conditions of the skin such as erysipelas.

15009.title: salinity
15009.definition: Mass of dissolved salts in seawater, brackish water, brine, or other saline solution divided by the mass of the solution.

09647.title: saliva
09647.definition: Clear, viscous secretion from the parotid, submaxillary, sublingual, and smaller mucous glands in the cavity of the mouth.

11193.title: salpingectomy
11193.definition: Surgical removal of the Fallopian tubes.

S05447.title: salt
S05447.definition: A chemical compound consisting of an assembly of cations and anions.

09080.title: salt bridge
09080.definition: Means of making electrolytic connection between two half cells without introducing a significant liquid junction potential.

S05449.title: salt form of an ion exchanger
S05449.definition: The ionic form of an ion exchanger in which the counter-ions are neither hydrogen nor hydroxide ions. When only one valence is possible for the counter-ion, or its exact form or charge is not known, the symbol or the name of the counter-ion without charge is used, e.g. sodium-form or $\ce{Na}$-form, tetramethylammonium-form, orthophosphate-form. When one of two or more possible forms is exclusively present, the oxidation state may be indicated by a Roman numeral, e.g. $\ce{Fe^{II}}$ form, $\ce{Fe^{III}}$ form.

15010.title: salt tolerance index
15010.definition: Quotient calculated as total plant (shoot + root) dry mass at different salt concentrations compared to the total plant dry mass obtained for the controls, as indicated below: \[S_{\rm{T}} = m_{\rm{d}}({\rm{x}})/m_{\rm{d}}({\rm{i}})\] where \(m_{\rm{d}}\) is the total dry mass, and \(x\), \(i\) refer to a control treatment and a defined salt treatment, respectively.

10184.title: salting in
10184.definition: Addition of an electrolyte to an aqueous phase to decrease the distribution ratio of the analyte(s) or matrix.

S05450.title: salting out
S05450.definition: The addition of particular electrolytes to an aqueous phase in order to increase the distribution ratio of a particular solute.

09279.title: sample bias
09279.definition: Electric potential applied to the whole or part of the sample, referenced to the electric potential of the sample holder.

09280.title: sample charging
09280.definition: Change in the electrical potential in the sample or on the sample surface caused by particle or photon bombardment.

12302.title: sample controlled technique
12302.definition: Applied to the technique to indicate that a property of the sample is used either continuously or discontinuously to control the sample heating. Without this term, it is assumed that the experiment is following a controlled-temperature program.

S05456.title: sample error
S05456.definition: An error which arises when the absorbance of some samples changes with time, e.g. as a result of photochemical reaction, formation of aggregates or adsorption on the cell wall.

08543.title: sample flux density
08543.definition: Intensity transmitted by the atomizer when the latter is supplied with the sample solution or a reference solution.

S05457.title: sample handling
S05457.definition: Any action applied to the sample before the analytical procedure. Such actions include the addition of preservatives, separation procedures, storage at low temperature, protection against light and irradiation, loading, etc.

S05451.title: sample
S05451.definition: A portion of material selected from a larger quantity of material. The term needs to be qualified, e.g. bulk sample, representative sample, primary sample, bulked sample, test sample. The term 'sample' implies the existence of a sampling error, i.e. the results obtained on the portions taken are only estimates of the concentration of a constituent or the quantity of a property present in the parent material. If there is no or negligible sampling error, the portion removed is a test portion, aliquot or specimen. The term 'specimen' is used to denote a portion taken under conditions such that the sampling variability cannot be assessed (usually because the population is changing), and is assumed, for convenience, to be zero. The manner of selection of the sample should be prescribed in a sampling plan.

S05458.title: sample injector
S05458.definition: A device by which a liquid or gaseous sample is introduced into the apparatus. The sample can be introduced directly into the carrier-gas stream, or into a chamber temporarily isolated from the system by values which can be changed so as to make an instantaneous switch of the gas stream through the chamber. The latter is a by-pass injector.

09930.title: sample introduction
09930.definition: In isotachophoresis a sample is introduced between a zone of fast leading electrolyte and a zone of slow terminating electrolyte.

08042.title: sample pre-treatment
08042.definition: Collective noun for all procedures used for conditioning a sample to a defined state which allows subsequent chemical analysis or long-term storage (see material stability).

09660.title: sample quality control
09660.definition: Test of the purity of the sample that will be subjected to detailed biochemical analysis.

S05461.title: sample unit
S05461.definition: The discrete identifiable portion suitable for taking as a sample or as a portion of a sample. These units may be different at different stages of sampling.

09281.title: sample voltage
09281.definition: Electric potential difference of the sample referenced to ground.

09145.title: sampled DC polarography
09145.definition: DC polarography with current sampling at the end of each drop life mechanically enforced by a knocker at a preset drop time value. The current sampling and mechanical drop dislodge are synchronized.

S05459.title: sampler
S05459.definition: A device used to withdraw and deliver a volume or an amount of a sample.

08043.title: sampling
08043.definition: Act of taking or constituting a sample.

S05463.title: sampling error
S05463.definition: That part of the total error (the estimate from a sample minus the population value) associated with using only a fraction of the population and extrapolating to the whole, as distinct from analytical or test error. It arises from a lack of homogeneity in the parent population. In chemical analysis, the final test result reflects the value only as it exists in the test portion. It is usually assumed that no sampling error is introduced in preparing the test sample from the laboratory sample. Therefore, the sampling error is usually associated exclusively with the variability of the laboratory sample. Sampling error is determined by replication of the laboratory samples and their multiple analyses. Since sampling error is always associated with analytical error, it must be isolated by the statistical procedure of analysis of variance.

08044.title: sampling increment
08044.definition: Individual portion of material collected by a single operation of a sampling device.

S05465.title: sampling interval
S05465.definition: In Tast polarography, square-wave polarography, and similar techniques, the interval during which the current is measured or recorded.

S05466.title: sampling plan
S05466.definition: A predetermined procedure for the selection, withdrawal, preservation, transportation and preparation of the portions to be removed from a population as samples. Summarizing the test values or observations from the selected portions yields an estimate for the concentration of an analyte or a value for a property determined with a calculable degree of uncertainty at a specified confidence level. A sampling plan includes the designation of the number, location and size of the portions, and instructions for the extent of compositing and for the reduction (in amount and fineness) of the portions to a laboratory sample and to test portions. It may also contain acceptance criteria. Some sampling plans do not include more than instructions for the statistical selection of portions to be removed. Such plans should properly be designated as 'statistical sampling plans'.

08045.title: sampling target
08045.definition: Portion of the material, at a particular time, that the sample is intended to represent.

S05467.title: sampling time
S05467.definition: In Tast polarography, square-wave polarography, and similar techniques, the duration of the sampling interval.

10059.title: sampling unit
10059.definition: Defined quantity of material having a boundary which may be physical or temporal.

S05468.title: sandwich compounds
S05468.definition: Compounds in which a metal atom is located between the faces of two parallel and planar (or nearly so) ring structures, e.g. bis(\(\eta ^{5}\)-cyclopentadienyl)iron (ferrocene), dibenzenechromium.

09684.title: sandwich immunoassay
09684.definition: Immunoassay using chemical or immunochemical binding of analyte to a solid phase carrying antibody and the immunochemical binding of a second (labelled) reagent to the analyte.

09725.title: Sanger sequencing
09725.definition: Method for determining a nucleotide sequence of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) based on incorporating chain-terminating dideoxynucleotides.

S05469.title: sanitary land fill
S05469.definition: An engineered burial of refuse. The refuse is dumped into trenches and compacted by bulldozer, where, it is hoped, aerobic metabolism by microorganisms decomposes the organic matter to stable compounds ($\ce{H2O}$, $\ce{CO2}$, etc.). Moisture is essential for the biological degradation and groundwater assists the process except when it fills air voids and prevents the transport of oxygen to the refuse. Land fills of unsatisfactory design can be major sources of air, water and soil pollution.

12061.title: Santa Ana dexterity test
12061.definition: Procedure in which a test subject stands in front of a plate with 48 square holes and an equal number of fitted pegs, each having a cylindrical upper part and square base, and is asked to fit the pegs into the holes as quickly as possible by turning them 180 degrees, first with one hand and in a subsequent trial with the other hand.

15011.title: saprobic
15011.definition: Living in or being an environment rich in organic matter but lacking oxygen.

15012.title: saprobic index
15012.definition: Means of classifying the saprobic state of running waters, covering the full range from unpolluted to extremely polluted waters.

15013.title: saprobic water classification

15014.title: saprobien spectrum
15014.definition: Characteristic change in community composition at different distances below the discharge of putrescible organic waste to a river or stream.

S05470.title: saprophyte
S05470.definition: A microorganism that feeds on dead and decaying organic matter. Saprophytes excrete enzymes that digest organic residues externally, the low molecular weight compounds formed then being absorbed.

13658.title: sarcoidosis
13658.definition: Chronic, progressive, generalized granulomatous reticulosis of unknown etiology, involving almost any organ or tissue, including the skin, lungs, lymph nodes, liver, spleen, eyes, and small bones of the hands and feet. It is characterized histologically by the presence in all affected organs or tissues of noncaseating epithelioid cell tubercles.

16074.title: sarcoma
16074.definition: Malignant tumor arising in a connective tissue and composed primarily of anaplastic cells resembling supportive tissue.

15015.title: satellite groups
15015.definition: Organisms or groups of organisms treated in a similar fashion to those in standard toxicity tests for the purpose of special additional studies.

16075.title: saturable elimination
16075.definition: Elimination that becomes concentration-independent at a concentration at which the elimination process is functioning maximally.

S05471.title: saturated solution
S05471.definition: A solution which has the same concentration of a solute as one that is in equilibrium with undissolved solute at specified values of the temperature and pressure.

15355.title: saturating solute
15355.definition: Solute that forms a saturated solution.

S05472.title: saturation
S05472.definition: The state of a saturated solution.

S05474.title: saturation activity
S05474.definition: For a specified isotope, the value of the activity of an irradiated element, whence state of saturation is reached.

S05476.title: saturation fraction
S05476.definition: Amount-of-substance of a component (solute) in a solution divided by the amount-of-substance of the component when it is saturating the system at constant temperature and pressure. Also referred to simply as saturation, for example oxygen saturation.

S05473.title: saturation
S05473.definition: Of an irradiated element for a specified isotope, the steady state reached when the disintegration rate of the nuclide formed is equal to its production rate.

11194.title: saturation mutagenesis
11194.definition: Mutagenesis screening in which a large number of mutations are introduced in a target area of the genome with the aim of identifying all the genes or their functions that are associated with that area.

S05478.title: saturation transfer
S05478.definition: A term used in nuclear magnetic resonance. When a nucleus is strongly irradiated, its spin population may partly be transferred to another nucleus by an exchange process.

08410.title: saturation transfer difference spectroscopy
08410.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that allows detection of transient binding of small molecule ligands to macromolecular receptors.

S05479.title: saturation vapour pressure
S05479.definition: The pressure exerted by a pure substance (at a given temperature) in a system containing only the vapour and condensed phase (liquid or solid) of the substance.

08544.title: saturator
08544.definition: Buffer containing interfering element(s) in sufficient quantity to reach the limit of enhancement or dispersion (i.e., saturation) of the interference curve.

16076.title: saturnia
16076.definition: Pain in a joint resulting from lead poisoning.

S05480.title: sawhorse projection
S05480.definition: A perspective formula indicating the spatial arrangement of bonds on two adjacent carbon atoms. The bond between the two atoms is represented by a diagonal line, the left-hand bottom end of which locates the atom nearer the observer and the right-hand top end the atom that is further away. In general a Newman or zig-zag projection is preferred.

S05481.title: Saytzeff rule
S05481.definition: Dehydrohalogenation of secondary- and tertiary-alkyl halides proceeds by the preferential removal of the $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}hydrogen}$ from the carbon that has the smallest number of hydrogens. Originally formulated by A. Saytzeff (Zaitsev) to generalize the orientation in $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}}$elimination reactions of alkyl halides, this rule has been extended and modified, as follows: When two or more olefins can be produced in an elimination reaction, the thermodynamically most stable alkene will predominate. Exceptions to the Saytzeff rule are exemplified by the Hofmann rule.

12724.title: scaffold
12724.definition: Core portion of a molecule common to all members of a chemical library or compound series.

12725.title: scaffold hopping
12725.definition: Exchange of one scaffold for another while maintaining molecular features that are important for biological properties.

S05482.title: scaler
S05482.definition: A sub-assembly for counting electrical pulses and containing one or more scaling circuits.

10060.title: scaling
10060.definition: Element-wise division of a data matrix by a scaling matrix.

S05483.title: scaling circuit
S05483.definition: An electronic circuit which produces an output pulse for each time a specified number of pulses has been received at its input.

15356.title: scaling equation
15356.definition: Dimensionless equation representing mutual solubilities in a number of chemically related liquid systems. Each mutual solubility is subtracted from the solubility at the critical solution point, and the temperature is divided by the critical solution temperature.

ST07097.title: scaling factor
ST07097.definition: A variational parameter used as a multiplier of each nuclear Cartesian and electronic coordinate chosen to minimize the variational integral and to make a trial variation function to satisfy the virial theorem. In practical calculations, the numeral factor to scale computed values, e.g. vibrational frequencies, to those found in experiments.

12233.title: scaling law
12233.definition: Equation of the type \(y = k x^{a}\), relating two physical quantities, \(x\) and \(y\), in which the value of the exponent \(a\) can be predicted by theory.

12303.title: scan
12303.definition: A term used to describe the data produced from a thermal analysis experiment. More correct usage is a thermal analysis curve, or, for a specific technique thermogravimetric curve, etc.

09146.title: scan rate
09146.definition: The rate of change of applied potential with time.

12305.title: scanning calorimetry
12305.definition: Techniques where heat is measured as a function of temperature.

S05484.title: scanning electron microscopy
S05484.definition: Any analytical technique which involves the generation and evaluation of secondary electrons (and to a lesser extent back scattered electrons) by a finely focused electron beam (typically \(10\ \rm{nm}\) or less) for high resolution and high depth of field imaging.

S05485.title: scanning method
S05485.definition: This term refers to the sequence of control over operating parameters of a mass spectrometer that results in a spectrum of masses, velocities, momenta or energies.

09202.title: scanning near-field optical microscopy
09202.definition: Measurement method in microscopy in which spectroscopic data may be collected with the detector closer to the sample than the optical wavelength employed.

08761.title: scanning proton microscopy
08761.definition: Measurement method of X-ray fluorescence analysis in which protons are focused and collimated to form a micro beam to obtain an image of a surface.

12304.title: scanning technique
12304.definition: Indicates that a specified experimental parameter, if not temperature, is changed in a controlled manner.

S05486.title: scanning transmission electron microscopy
S05486.definition: A special TEM-technique in which an electron transparent sample is bombarded with a finely focused electron beam (typically of a diameter of less than $\pu{10 nm}$) which can be scanned across the specimen or rocked across the optical axis and transmitted, secondary, back scattered and diffracted electrons as well as the characteristic X-ray spectrum can be observed. STEM essentially provides high resolution imaging of the inner microstructure and the surface of a thin sample (or small particles), as well as the possibility of chemical and structural characterization of micrometer and sub-micrometer domains through evaluation of the X-ray spectra and the electron diffraction pattern.

09518.title: scanning-probe lithography
09518.definition: Lithographic method in which a microscopic or nanoscopic stylus is moved mechanically across a surface to form a pattern.

11195.title: scaphocephaly
11195.definition: Elongated and narrow head with decrease of the parietal regions and conspicuous frontal and occipital protrusions; a type of craniosynostosis.

13853.title: Scatchard equation
13853.definition: Equation used to calculate the association constant, \(K_{\rm{a}}\), of a ligand with a protein molecule.

13854.title: Scatchard plot
13854.definition: Linear plot of \(r/c\) against \(r\) in accordance with the Scatchard equation.

09382.title: scattered-ion energy
09382.definition: Kinetic energy of a primary ion after a collision.

09383.title: scattered-ion energy ratio
09383.definition: Scattered-ion energy divided by energy of the incident probe ion prior to a collision.

S05487.title: scattering
S05487.definition: A process in which a change in direction or energy of an incident radiation is caused by interaction with a particle, a system of particles, or a photon.

14085.title: scattering albedo
14085.definition: Efficiency of scattering, i.e., ratio of scattering coefficient, \(\sigma(\lambda_{\rm{i}})\), to the total attenuance coefficient, \(\beta(\lambda_{\rm{i}})\), at a particular wavelength \(\lambda_{\rm{i}}\).

S05488.title: scattering angle
S05488.definition: The angle between the forward direction of the incident beam and a straight line connecting the scattering point and the detector. Synonymous with angle of observation.

16251.title: scattering coefficient
16251.definition: Negative Napierian logarithm of the ratio of the intensity of radiation scattered (\(I_{\rm{s}}\)) by a non-absorbing sample to the incident intensity (\(I_{0}\)), divided by the path-length, \(l\). \[s = -\ln(I_{s}/I_{0})/l\]

S05490.title: scattering cross-section
S05490.definition: The scattering coefficient per particle (\(\frac{\rm{cm}^{2}}{\rm{particle}}\)); \[b_{\rm{scat}}=n\ \sigma _{\rm{scat}}\] where \(n\) is the number concentration of particles (\(\rm{particles cm}^{-3}\)) and \(\sigma _{\rm{scat}}\) is the scattering cross-section. \(b_{\rm{scat}}\), the scattering component of extinction due to gas and particles, is measured in the atmosphere using a nephelometer. For a homogeneous atmosphere it is related in theory to the meteorological range (\(L_{\rm{V}}\)): \(L_{\rm{V}}=\frac{3.9}{b_{\rm{scat}}}\); \(b_{\rm{scat}}\) and \(b_{\rm{abs}}\) represent the scattering and absorption coefficients per unit length for a light beam (of path length \(L\)) which has a spectral radiance (intensity) \(I_{0}\) incident on a sample of air and \(I\) is the transmitted spectral radiance (intensity), \(\ln (\frac{I_{0}}{I}) = L\ (b_{\rm{scat}}+b_{\rm{abs}})\).

S05491.title: scattering error
S05491.definition: The presence of particulate matter, emulsions, micelles, etc. may cause radiation scattering which will result in further attenuation of the transmitted beam and the measured absorbance will be too high. This error is called the scattering error.

08677.title: scattering geometry
08677.definition: Relation between the propagation directions, \(k_{\rm{i}}\), \(k_{\rm{s}}\), and the polarization directions, \(p_{\rm{i}}\), \(p_{\rm{s}}\), of the incident and scattered radiation, usually expressed in terms of laboratory-fixed or crystal-fixed Cartesian axes.

S05492.title: scattering matrix
S05492.definition: The Stokes parameters of scattered light are given by the matrix equation \[(s_{0},s_{1},s_{2},s_{3}) = F\ (s_{0}^{0},s_{1}^{0},s_{2}^{0},s_{3}^{0})\] where the 4, 4 scattering matrix \(F\) is comprised of 16 scattering matrix elements. These matrix elements, which may originate in theory or experiment, provide a complete description of the scattered radiation in terms of the incident radiation.

S05493.title: scattering plane
S05493.definition: The plane containing the incident light beam and the line from the centre of the scattering system to the observer.

S05494.title: scattering vector
S05494.definition: The vector difference between the wave propagation vectors of the incident and the scattered beam, both of length \(\frac{2\ \pi }{\lambda }\), where \(\lambda \) is the wavelength of the scattered radiation in the medium.

S05495.title: scavenger
S05495.definition: A substance that reacts with (or otherwise removes) a trace component (as in the scavenging of trace metal ions) or traps a reactive reaction intermediate.

13659.title: scavenger receptor
13659.definition: Cell surface receptor, for example on phagocytes, which recognizes cells or molecules that require clearance from the body.

S05496.title: scavenging
S05496.definition: Binding radicals or free electrons with a receptive (or reactive) material.

13657.title: scFv
13657.definition: Single-chain molecule composed of the variable (V) regions of an antibody heavy and light chain joined together by a flexible linker.

12063.title: schedule of reinforcement
12063.definition: Frequency, duration, dose, and (or) intensity of a conditioning stimulus.

12062.title: schedule-controlled operant behaviour
