12075.definition: Method for visualization of macromolecules such as nucleic acids and proteins, typically in electrophoretic gels or formalin-fixed histological sections, based on the reduction of silver salts to metallic silver or formation of crystalline silver compounds.

S05674.title: silyl groups
S05674.definition: In a strict sense, the silyl group is $\ce{H3Si\bond{–}}$.A name commonly applied to hydrocarbyl derivatives of the silyl group $\ce{R3Si\bond{–}}$.

S05675.title: silyl radicals
S05675.definition: In a strict sense, the silyl radical is $\ce{H3Si^{.}}$.A name commonly applied to the silicon-centered radicals $\ce{R3Si^{.}}$.

09573.title: silylation
09573.definition: Introduction of a substituted silyl group (\(\ce{R3Si}\)) to an alcohol, carboxylic acid, amine, thiol, or phosphate, commonly as a protecting group.

S05673.title: silylene
S05673.definition: Generic name for $\ce{H2Si{:}}$ and substitution derivatives thereof, containing an electrically neutral bivalent silicon atom with two non-bonding electrons. (The definition is analogous to that given for carbene.)The silanediyl group ($\ce{H2Si}$), analogous to the methylene group ($\ce{H2C}$).

11511.title: similarity ensemble approach
11511.definition:
A method that predicts the probability that a molecule or set of molecules will be active against a particular target by considering its pairwise similarities
 to all known ligands for that target.

10141.title: similarity index
10141.definition: Quantity that describes the equivalence of two objects characterised by multivariate data.

11512.title: similarity searching
11512.definition:
A virtual screening method that calculates the molecular similarity of an input 2D or 3D structure to each of the molecules in a database to identify a
 requested number of most similar molecules or those above some similarity threshold.

12076.title: simple reaction time test
12076.definition: Procedure to assess psychomotor speed in which a test subject is presented at irregular intervals with a visual stimulus, such as a coloured dot on a screen, and is asked to press a button immediately after noticing the stimulus.

S05676.title: simple shear
S05676.definition: An idealized treatment of a fluid between two large parallel plates (to permit ignoring edge effects) of area \(A\), separated by a distance \(h\). If one plate moves relative to the other with a constant velocity \(V\), requiring a force \(F\) acting in the direction of movement, and the density, pressure, and viscosity throughout the fluid are constant, the Newtonian equation can be coupled with the equations of motion and of continuity to show that the velocity gradient in the fluid is constant (= \(\frac{V}{h}\)), and that \(\frac{F}{A} = \frac{\eta \ V}{h}\). This idealized case (simple shear) is sometimes used to define shear viscosity.

10111.title: simple-to-use interactive self-modelling mixture analysis
10111.definition: Interactive method to obtain concentrations and pure spectra from spectra of mixtures using directly-measured variables.

11514.title: simplified molecular input line entry system

15034.title: Simpson’s diversity index
15034.definition: Dominance index weighted toward the abundance of the most common species, giving the probability of any two individuals drawn at random from an infinitely large community belonging to different species. The bias corrected mathematical form of Simpson’s index is \[D = \sum \limits_{i=1}^{S} p_{i}^{2}\] where \(p_{i}\) is the fraction of all organisms which belong to the \(i\)-th species and \(S\) is the number of species.

09428.title: SIMS ion image
09428.definition: Two-dimensional surface map of the spatial distribution of the amount of a particular secondary ion emitted from within a specific area of the sample in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

10114.title: simulated annealing
10114.definition: Generic probabilistic meta-heuristic to locate a good approximation to the global optimum of a given function in a large search space, in which there is a slow decrease in the probability of accepting worse solutions as the solution space is explored.

15035.title: simulated field studies
15035.definition: Experimental ecosystem that should be: physically confined; self-maintaining; multitrophic; have a duration time exceeding the generation time of the penultimate trophic level present; and of size sufficient to enable pertinent sampling and measurements to be made without seriously influencing the structure and dynamics of the system.

S05677.title: simulation technique
S05677.definition: A technique for reducing or eliminating analytical errors resulting from interferences, using a reference solution sufficiently similar in quantitative composition to the sample solutions to be analysed that the interferences in the reference and sample solution are equivalent.

16091.title: simulation test
16091.definition: Procedure designed to predict the rate of biodegradation of a compound under relevant environmental conditions.

ST07567.title: simultaneous interpenetrating polymer network
ST07567.definition: Interpenetrating polymer network prepared by a process in which the component networks are formed concurrently.

S05679.title: simultaneous pair transitions
S05679.definition: Simultaneous electronic transitions in two coupled absorbers or emitters. Because of the coupling, transitions which are spin-forbidden in one of the centres might become spin-allowed (spin flip).

S05680.title: simultaneous reactions
S05680.definition: Composite reactions, in which processes like \[\rm{A}\ \overset{1}{\rightarrow }\ \rm{Y}\] and \[\rm{B}\ \overset{2}{\rightarrow }\ \rm{Z}\] occur in parallel, can be called simultaneous or parallel reactions. Sometimes there is competition involved, like in the scheme: \[\rm{A}\,+\,\rm{B}\ \overset{1}{\rightarrow }\ \rm{Y}\] and \[\rm{A}\,+\,\rm{C}\ \overset{2}{\rightarrow }\ \rm{Z}\] where B and C compete with one another for A.

ST07575.title: simultaneous semi-interpenetrating polymer network
ST07575.definition: Semi-interpenetrating polymer network prepared by a process in which the networks and the linear or branched components are formed concurrently.

S05681.title: simultaneous spectrometer
S05681.definition: A spectrometer which has more than one detector and enables the intensities of several spectral bands to be measured at the same time.

10200.title: simultaneous steam distillation-solvent extraction
10200.definition: Extraction in which a sample dispersed in water and a water immiscible organic solvent (extraction phase) in separate flasks are heated simultaneously and their vapours co-condensed and separated into two streams in which water is returned to the sample flask and the extraction phase to the organic solvent flask.Apparatus for simultaneous steam distillation-solvent extraction with a lighter-than-water extraction phase. A = aqueous sample solution or slurry; B = immiscible organic solvent and receiving flask for extracted compounds; C = bowl for phase separation; D, E, F, and G are solvent or vapour transfer arms; and H = entry port for additional solvent or alternative sample introduction position for continuous liquid–liquid extraction. Switching the position of flasks A and B allows extraction with a heavier-than-water extraction solvent.

12306.title: simultaneous technique
12306.definition: Indicates the measurement of two or more properties of a single sample at the same time.

08283.title: single beam spectrum
08283.definition: Output of a single beam spectrometer as a function of wavenumber or wavelength.

S05683.title: single cell protein
S05683.definition: Microbial biomass or proteins extracted therefrom obtained from processes in which bacteria, yeasts, other fungi or algae are cultivated in large quantities as human or animal protein supplement in animal feed or in human nutrition.

08414.title: single crystal nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
08414.definition: Solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy on a single crystal in a similar manner to that used in X-ray diffraction.

S05686.title: single escape peak
S05686.definition: In a $\upgamma\!\mbox{-}\rm{ray\ spectrum}$, the peak due to pair production in the detector and escape, from the sensitive part of the detector, of one of the photons of \(511\ \rm{keV}\) resulting from annihilation.

10142.title: single linkage
10142.definition: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the distance between two clusters is the distance between those two objects (one from each cluster) that are closest together.

09727.title: single nucleotide polymorphism
09727.definition: Variant of nucleotide sequence of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) in which the purine or pyrimidine base of a single nucleotide is replaced by another such base.

S05690.title: single scattering
S05690.definition: Radiation scattering in which there is only one scattering encounter.

S05682.title: single-beam spectrometer
S05682.definition: A luminescence spectrometer in which a single beam of radiation is used for excitation and a single beam of luminescence radiation is taken from the sample.

13679.title: single-chain antibody
13679.definition: Small antibody construct in which the variable fragment (Fv) [see variable (V) region] of a heavy chain is linked via a synthetic peptide to the variable fragment of a light chain.

10218.title: single-drop microextraction
10218.definition: Extraction of analytes from the gas phase or solution by a single drop of extraction solvent.Typical experimental arrangement for single-drop microextraction.

S05685.title: single-electron transfer mechanism
S05685.definition: A reaction mechanism characterized by the transfer of a single electron between the species occurring on the reaction coordinate of one of the elementary steps.

S05687.title: single-focusing mass spectrometer
S05687.definition: An instrument in which an ion beam with a given value of mass/charge is brought to a focus although the initial directions of the ions diverge.

S05689.title: single-photon timing
S05689.definition: Technique that permits recovery of the parameters characterizing a fluorescence decay after pulse excitation (in particular excited-states lifetimes). It is based on the creation of a time histogram of many stochastic events involving the time delay between the electronic excitation of a molecule or material and its emission of a photon from an excited state. A key to the technique is that no more than one photon strike the detector per pulsed excitation. Excitation is commonly achieved with a flash from a repetitive nanosecond lamp or diode laser or a CW operated laser (mode-locked laser). The essential components of the hardware are a device to measure the excitation-emission delay time and another to determine the relative frequency of photons reaching the detector at each delay time. Delay times are usually measured with a time-to-amplitude-converter (TAC), using voltage to measure the delay between a start and a stop signal. The frequency of events with each delay is stored in a multi-channel analyser. This term is preferred to time-correlated single-photon counting.

S05691.title: single-step reaction
S05691.definition: A reaction that proceeds through a single transition state.

S05692.title: single-strand chain
S05692.definition: A chain that comprises constitutional unit connected in such a way that adjacent constitutional units are joined to each other through two atoms, one on each constitutional unit.

S05693.title: single-strand macromolecule
S05693.definition: A macromolecule that comprises constitutional unit connected in such a way that adjacent constitutional units are joined to each other through two atoms, one on each constitutional unit.

S05694.title: single-strand polymer
S05694.definition: A polymer the macromolecules of which are single-strand macromolecules.

S05695.title: singlet molecular oxygen
S05695.definition: Oxygen molecule (dioxygen), $\ce{O2}$, in an excited singlet state. The ground state of $\ce{O2}$ is a triplet (\(^{3}\Sigma_{\rm{g}}^{-}\)). The two metastable singlet states derived from the ground-state configuration are \(^{1}\Delta_{\rm{g}}\) and \(^{1}\Sigma_{\rm{g}}^{+}\) (the latter with the higher energy).

S05699.title: singlet state
S05699.definition: A state having a total electron spin quantum number equal to 0.

S05696.title: singlet-singlet absorption
S05696.definition: Absorption which results in the transition from the singlet ground state of the molecule into singlet excited states (\(\rm{S}_{0}\) → \(\rm{S}_{\rm{n}}\)) and leads to the UV/visible absorption spectrum.

S05698.title: singlet-singlet energy transfer
S05698.definition: Transfer of excitation from an electronically excited donor in a singlet state to produce an electronically excited acceptor in a singlet state.

S05700.title: singlet-triplet absorption
S05700.definition: Absorption which takes place with the transition from the singlet ground state of the molecule to triplet states (\(\rm{S}_{0}\) → \(\rm{T}_{\rm{n}}\)) and results in the singlet-triplet absorption spectrum.

S05701.title: singlet-triplet energy transfer
S05701.definition: Transfer of excitation from an electronically excited donor in a singlet state to produce an electronically excited acceptor in a triplet state.

ST07477.title: singlet–triplet crossing
ST07477.definition: Point of intersection between the potential energy surfaces of states of different multiplicity.

S05702.title: singly labelled
S05702.definition: A specifically labelled compound in which the isotopically substituted molecule has only one isotopically modified atom e.g. $\ce{CH3–CH[^{2}H]–OH}$.

10115.title: singular value decomposition
10115.definition: A factorization of an \(m \times n\) matrix (\(\boldsymbol{M}\)) such that \(\boldsymbol{M} = \boldsymbol{U}\boldsymbol{\Sigma} \boldsymbol{V}^{T}\), where \(\boldsymbol{U}\) is an \(m \times m\) matrix, \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\) is a \(m \times n\) matrix and \(\boldsymbol{V}^{\rm{T}}\) is a \(n \times n\) matrix.

S05703.title: sink
S05703.definition: The receptor for material which is removed from the atmosphere. Because of long range transport of many pollutants such as $\ce{SO2}$, sulfuric acid and its salts, the sink region can be many hundreds of kilometres from the source region of the pollutants.

11220.title: sinoatrial node
11220.definition: Mass of specialized cardiac muscle cells ('pacemaker cells') that spontaneously depolarize to initiate rhythmic contraction of the heart.

S05704.title: sintering
S05704.definition: Temperature-induced coalescence and densification of porous solid particles below the melting points of their major components.

11221.title: sinus
11221.definition:
Hollow or cavity.
Channel for the passage of fluid, lacking the usual lining of a blood or lymphatic vessel; especially a dilatation for the passage of venous blood.

11222.title: sinus venosus
11222.definition: Cavity at the caudal end of the developing embryonic heart where intra- and extra-embryonic veins meet.

11223.title: sister chromatid exchange
11223.definition: Reciprocal exchange of chromatin between two replicated chromosomes that remain attached to each other until anaphase of mitosis.

08678.title: site splitting
08678.definition: Appearance of more than one band in the spectrum of a crystal when only one is seen in that of the gas, when this splitting is attributed to either the molecule lying on a crystal site of lower symmetry than that of the gaseous molecule or to molecules occupying more than one type of crystal site. See crystal field splitting.

12726.title: site-directed mutagenesis
12726.definition: Molecular biology technique in which mutations are created at one or more defined sites in a DNA molecule.

11224.title: situs inversus
11224.definition: Developmental anomaly in which major visceral organs are found in a mirrored position to their normal location.

08874.title: size effect
08874.definition: Effect of size on properties of the material or device which incorporates it.

S05705.title: size-exclusion chromatography
S05705.definition: A separation technique in which separation mainly according to the hydrodynamic volume of the molecules or particles takes place in a porous non-adsorbing material with pores of approximately the same size as the effective dimensions in solution of the molecules to be separated.

13680.title: Sjögren syndrome
13680.definition: Chronic inflammation of the lachrymal and salivary glands, often accompanied by rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and the presence of autoantibodies in the blood, occurring chiefly among women.

S05706.title: skeletal atom
S05706.definition: An atom of a skeletal structure.

S05707.title: skeletal bond
S05707.definition: A bond connecting two skeletal atoms.

08208.title: skeletal formula
08208.definition: Two-dimensional representation of a molecular entity in which bonds are indicated as lines between vertices representing octet carbon atoms with attached hydrogens omitted and in which other atoms are represented by their chemical symbols.

S05708.title: skeletal structure
S05708.definition: The sequence of atoms in the constitutional unit(s) of a macromolecule, an oligomer molecule, a block or a chain which defines the essential topological representation.

13681.title: skin immune system
13681.definition: Skin-associated cells that participate in an immune response, including Langerhans cells, dendritic cells, and keratinocytes (mainly responsible for production of cytokines).

13682.title: skin sensitization test
13682.definition: Any test used to study skin hypersensitivity such as the guinea pig maximization test or the Buehler test.

13683.title: skin test
13683.definition: Procedure for evaluating immunity status, involving the introduction of a reagent into or under the skin.

ST07100.title: Slater determinant
ST07100.definition: The determinantal representation of many-electron wavefunction \(\Psi \) which conforms to the requirement of the antisymmetry principle.

S05710.title: Slater-type orbital
S05710.definition: An approximate atomic orbital attempts to allow for electron-electron repulsion by scaling the nuclear charge for each orbital.

16093.title: slimicide
16093.definition: Substance intended to kill slime-producing organisms.

ST07508.title: slip
ST07508.definition: Ceramic precursor dispersed in a liquid.

ST07633.title: slip casting
ST07633.definition: Procedure in ceramic processing whereby slip is contained in a porous plaster mould prior to pyrolysis.

08284.title: slit width
08284.definition: Distance between the blades of the entrance or exit slits in a monochromator.

16094.title: slope factor
16094.definition: Value, in inverse concentration or dose units, derived from the slope of a dose-response curve; in practice, limited to carcinogenic effects with the curve assumed to be linear at low concentrations or doses.

14392.title: slow coagulation rate
14392.definition: Rate of coagulation in presence of repulsive barriers between particles.

S05712.title: slow neutrons
S05712.definition: Neutrons of kinetic energy less than some specified value. This value may vary over a wide range and depends on the application. In reactor physics, the value is frequently chosen to be \(1\ \rm{eV}\); in dosimetry, the effective cadmium cut-off is used.

13684.title: slow-reacting substance of anaphylaxis
13684.definition: Group of leukotrienes released by mast cells during anaphylaxis, which induces a prolonged contraction of smooth muscle.

12077.title: SLUDDE
12077.definition: Acronym for the constellation of signs salivation, lacrymation, urination, defecation, dyspnea/gastrointestinal upset, and emesis.

15232.title: slugging
15232.definition: Method by which powder particles are compressed into a large tablet, called a slug, which is subsequently dry-screened and compressed into a tablet.

S05715.title: SM-interference
S05715.definition: Interference by a substance that produces a signal by a similar mechanism to the analyte, which in the given procedure (including the apparatus used) can not be distinguished from the signal given by the analyte. For example, in a colour reaction with an organic ligand by also reacting with the ligand and producing a coloured compound absorbing at the same wavelength as the compound produced by the analyte or in an atomic spectrochemical analysis by absorbing or emitting at the same wavelength as the analyte.

13685.title: small G protein
13685.definition: Any member of a family of monomeric G proteins, with molecular mass typically \(\pu{20\!{-}\! 40 kDa}\), that also bind guanine nucleotides and are involved in signal transduction.

12727.title: small inhibitory double-stranded RNA
12727.definition: Small RNA fragments that can combine with specific genes to silence their expression.

12276.title: small molecule
12276.definition: Molecule much smaller than the wavelength of the radiation in the solvent used.

13686.title: small outer capsid protein
13686.definition: Protein from the shell of the bacteriophage T4, commonly used in construction of phage antibody libraries.

S05713.title: small particle
S05713.definition: A particle much smaller than the wavelength of the radiation in the medium. In practice, all dimensions of a particle considered small must be less than about one-twentieth of the wavelength employed.

09203.title: small-angle X-ray scattering
09203.definition: Measurement method in which the elastically scattered intensity of X-rays is measured for small-angle deflections.

11513.title: SMARTS
11513.definition: An expansion of the SMILES language that describes a particular specific or generalized substructure.

13858.title: smectic
13858.definition: Pertaining to the arrangement and orientation of molecules in a smectic mesophase.

13859.title: smectic mesophase
13859.definition: Mesophase that has the molecules arranged in layers with a well-defined layer spacing or periodicity.

ST06980.title: simplified molecular input line entry system
ST06980.definition: SMILES (Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System) is a string notation used to describe the nature and topology of molecular structures.

11515.title: SMIRKS
11515.definition: A derivative of the SMILES language that describes the transformation in a chemical reaction.

S05717.title: smog chamber
S05717.definition: A large confined volume in which sunlight or simulated sunlight is allowed to irradiate air mixtures of atmospheric trace gases (hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide, etc.) which undergo oxidation. In theory these chambers allow the controlled study of complex reactions which occur in the atmosphere. However, ill-defined wall reactions which generate some molecular and radical species (e.g. $\ce{HONO}$, $\ce{CH2O}$, $\ce{HO}$-radicals, etc.) and remove certain products ($\ce{H2O2}$, $\ce{HNO3}$, etc.), the use of reactant concentrations well above those in the atmosphere, ill-defined light intensities and wavelength distribution within the chamber, and other factors peculiar to chamber experiments require that caution be exercised in the extrapolation of results obtained from them to atmospheric systems.

S05716.title: smog
S05716.definition: The term originated in Great Britain as a popular derivation of 'smoke-fog' and appears to have been in common use before World War 1. It originally referred to the heavy pollution derived largely from coal burning (largely smoke filled air, rich in sulfur dioxide), and it probably was largely a reducing atmosphere. More common today in cities is an oxidizing atmosphere which contains ozone and other oxidants.

S05718.title: smog index
S05718.definition: A mathematical correlation between smog and meteorological and/or pollutant concentrations associated with it. These are qualitative indices which are sometimes used in some urban communities to predict the degree of the air pollution which is expected for the coming day.

S05719.title: smoke
S05719.definition: An aerosol originating from combustion, thermal decomposition or thermal evaporation. Its particles may be solid (magnesium oxide smoke) or liquid (tobacco smoke).

10061.title: smoothing
10061.definition: Transformation using an approximating function to capture important patterns in data, while removing noise or other fine-scale structures.

S05721.title: soap
S05721.definition: A salt of a fatty acid, saturated or unsaturated, containing at least eight carbon atoms or a mixture of such salts. A neat soap is a lamellar structure containing much (e.g. $\pu{75\%}$) soap and little (e.g. $\pu{25\%}$) water.

S05722.title: soap curd
S05722.definition: A gel-like mixture of fibrous soap-crystals ('curd-fibres') and their saturated solution (not a mesomorphic phase).

S05723.title: soap film
S05723.definition: A term established by usage for A/W/A films stabilized by surfactants although it is not a film of soap, nor is the stabilizing surfactant necessarily a soap. (A/W/A means water film in air).

12078.title: social interaction test
12078.definition: Behavioral test wherein a rodent stranger is placed in the cage of a domestic rodent and intensities and duration of interactions (e.g., sniffing, aggression, avoidance) between the socially unacquainted animals are observed.

16095.title: societal risk
16095.definition: Total probability of harm to a human population including the probability of adverse effects to health of descendants and the probability of disruption resulting from loss of services such as industrial plant or loss of material goods and electricity.

09574.title: soft bake
09574.definition: Short, low temperature annealing step following the coating of a wafer with a photoresist.

10143.title: soft independent modelling of class analogy
10143.definition: Supervised classification that performs a principal-component analysis on each class, and then an unknown is assigned to the class with which it has the lowest residual variance.

09519.title: soft lithography
09519.definition: Family of techniques for fabricating or replicating structures using elastomeric stamps, molds, and conformable photomasks.

ST07294.title: soft-segment phase domain
ST07294.definition: Phase domain of microscopic or smaller size, usually in a block, graft, or segmented copolymer, comprising essentially those segments of the polymer that have glass transition temperatures lower than the temperature of use.

15036.title: soil
15036.definition: Naturally occurring, unconsolidated mineral and (or) organic material at the surface of the Earth that is capable of supporting plant growth. It extends from the surface to \(\pu{15 cm}\) below the depth at which properties produced by soil-forming processes can be detected.

16096.title: soil partition coefficient
16096.definition: Experimental ratio of a substance’s concentration in the soil to that in the aqueous (dissolved) soil phase at equilibrium: It is valid only for the specific concentration and solid/solution ratio of the test.

S05726.title: soiling
S05726.definition: Visible damage to materials by deposition of air pollutants.

S05727.title: sol
S05727.definition: A fluid colloidal system of two or more components, e.g. a protein sol, a gold sol, an emulsion, a surfactant solution above the critical micelle concentration.

ST07513.title: sol fraction
ST07513.definition: Mass fraction of the dissolved or dispersed material, resulting from a network-forming polymerization or crosslinking process, that is constituted of molecules of finite (statistically definable) relative molecular masses.

ST07587.title: sol-gel coating
ST07587.definition: Coating formed through a sol-gel process.

ST07634.title: sol-gel critical concentration
ST07634.definition: Concentration of an added electrolyte above which a particulate sol undergoes coagulation instead of gelation.

ST07586.title: sol-gel material
ST07586.definition: Material formed through a sol-gel process.

ST07588.title: sol-gel metal oxide
ST07588.definition: Metal oxide formed through a sol-gel process.

ST07151.title: sol-gel process
ST07151.definition: Process through which a network is formed from solution by a progressive change of liquid precursor(s) into a sol, to a gel, and in most cases finally to a dry network.

ST07589.title: sol-gel silica
ST07589.definition: Silica formed through a sol-gel process.

S05731.title: sol-gel transition
S05731.definition: Transition of a sol to a gel at the gel point.

08875.title: solar cell
08875.definition: Device that directly transduces electromagnetic radiation into electricity based on the photovoltaic effect.

S05728.title: solar conversion efficiency
S05728.definition: The ratio of the Gibbs energy gain per unit time per \(\mathrm{m}^{2}\) of surface exposed to the sun and the solar irradiance, \(E\), integrated between \(\lambda = 0\) and \(\lambda = \infty \).

S05729.title: solar flare
S05729.definition: A bright eruption of energy from the sun's chromosphere.

S05730.title: solar radiation
S05730.definition: The electromagnetic radiation emitted by the sun. The total range of wavelengths of light emitted by the sun (99.9% in the range from \(150\ \rm{to}\ 4000\ \rm{nm}\)) is filtered on entering the earth's atmosphere, largely through the absorption by oxygen, ozone, water vapour and carbon dioxide. Near sea level only light of wavelengths longer than about \(290\ \rm{nm}\) is present. The light from \(290{-}400\ \rm{nm}\) is effective in inducing important photochemical processes since absorption by the important trace gases, ozone, nitrogen dioxide, aldehydes, ketones, etc., is significant in this region.

09098.title: solid amalgam electrode
09098.definition: Electrode made of a solid amalgam of an appropriate metal.

09282.title: solid angle of analyser
09282.definition: Solid angle allowing particles or photons to be transmitted from a point on the sample to the detector.

S05732.title: solid angle
S05732.definition: Of a cone, the ratio of the area cut out on a spherical surface (with its centre at the apex of that cone) to the square of the radius of the sphere. It is a quantity of dimension one (dimensionless quantity) with unit steradian (\(\mathrm{sr}=1\)).

S05734.title: solid phase antibody radioimmunoassay
S05734.definition: A kind of radioimmunoassay employing an antibody bound to a solid phase.

ST07227.title: solid polymer electrolyte
ST07227.definition: Electrically conducting solution of a salt in a polymer.

S05736.title: solid state lasers
S05736.definition: CW or pulsed lasers in which the active medium is a solid matrix (crystal or glass) doped with an ion (e.g. $\ce{Nd^{3+}}$, $\ce{Cr^{3+}}$, $\ce{Eu^{3+}}$). The emitted wavelength depends on the active ion, the selected optical transition, and the matrix. Some of these lasers are tunable within a very broad range (e.g. from \(700\) to \(1000\ \rm{nm}\) for $\ce{Ti^{3+}}$ doped sapphire). Pulsed lasers may be free-running, Q-switched, or mode-locked. Some CW lasers may be mode-locked.

S05737.title: solid support
S05737.definition: Normally an inert porous solid, which sorbs the liquid phase. The particle-size range of the support affects column efficiency and the pressure differential necessary to achieve a given flow rate. Modifications have been introduced for the achievement of special separations, in which the solid support is not inert but is an active solid. In capillary columns the inner wall of the column serves as the solid support and obviates the use of additional porous solids for this purpose.

S05739.title: solid volume
S05739.definition: The volume occupied by the solid or the active solid in the column.

10275.title: solid-phase dynamic extraction
10275.definition: Solid-phase microextraction in which the extraction phase is coated on the internal surface of a needle.

10255.title: solid-phase extraction
10255.definition: Extraction of analytes from a gas, liquid, or fluid by transfer to a solid sorbent.

10276.title: solid-phase microextraction
10276.definition: Microextraction where the extraction phase is a solid.

08415.title: solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
08415.definition: Application of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy to solids.

S05733.title: solidification
S05733.definition: The transition of a liquid or gas into a solid.

10219.title: solidified floating organic drop
10219.definition: Droplet of organic solvent recovered from the surface of the sample solution by solidification induced by cooling.

10220.title: solidified floating organic drop microextraction
10220.definition: Microextraction employing a solidified floating organic drop.

14324.title: solids content
14324.definition: Mass fraction of nonvolatile material in a polymer dispersion.

S05738.title: solidus
S05738.definition: A line on a binary phase diagram (or a surface on a ternary phase diagram) that indicates the temperature at which a system becomes completely solid on cooling or at which melting begins on heating under equilibrium conditions.

ST07101.title: soliton
ST07101.definition: Localized excitations propagating in a system with constant velocity and colliding with each other without change in their shapes.

14087.title: Solonitsyn effect
14087.definition: Adsorption (or reaction) after preliminary irradiation of a photocatalyst in vacuum (or in the absence of reagent).

S05740.title: solubility
S05740.definition: The analytical composition of a saturated solution, expressed in terms of the proportion of a designated solute in a designated solvent, is the solubility of that solute. The solubility may be expressed as a concentration, molality, mole fraction, mole ratio, etc.

15359.title: solubility constant
15359.definition: Generalization of solubility product to include, for example, undissociated salt or uncharged cation-anion pair as solute, reaction between solution species and the cation or anion of the solid salt, and gas-solution equilibria.

ST07466.title: solubility parameter
ST07466.definition: Parameter used in predicting the solubility of non-electrolytes (including polymers) in a given solvent.For a substance \(\ce{B}\), \[\delta_{\ce{B}} = \left (\frac{\Delta_{\rm{vap}}E_{\rm{m,B}}}{V_{\rm{m,B}}} \right)^{1/2}\] where \(\Delta _{\rm{vap}}E_{\rm{m,B}}\) is the molar energy of vaporization at zero pressure and \(V_{\rm{m,B}}\) is the molar volume.

S05742.title: solubility product
S05742.definition: The product of the ion activities raised to appropriate powers of an ionic solute in its saturated solution expressed with due reference to the dissociation equilibria involved and the ions present.

15360.title: solubilisation
15360.definition: Process by which an agent increases the solubility or the rate of dissolution of a solid or liquid solute.Modified from entry 'micellar solubilization' in.

15233.title: solubilising agents
15233.definition: Additives making a substance soluble or more soluble, especially in water.

S05744.title: solute
S05744.definition: The minor component of a solution which is regarded as having been dissolved by the solvent.

S05745.title: solute-volatilization interference
S05745.definition: Interference due to changes in the volatilization rate of the dry aerosol particles in the case when volatilization of the analyte is incomplete in the presence and/or absence of the concomitant. This interference can either be specific, if the analyte and interferent form a new phase of different thermostability, as when $\ce{Mg}$ and $\ce{Al}$ form $\ce{MgAl2O4}$ in an air–acetylene flame, or non-specific, if the analyte is simply dispersed in a large excess of the interferent, as when $\ce{Ag}$ is dispersed in $\ce{ThO2}$. If the interferent has a high boiling point, this latter is sometimes referred to as a blocking interference. It is often difficult to make sharp distinctions between the specific and non-specific solute-volatilization interferences.

S05746.title: solution
S05746.definition: A liquid or solid phase containing more than one substance, when for convenience one (or more) substance, which is called the solvent, is treated differently from the other substances, which are called solutes. When, as is often but not necessarily the case, the sum of the mole fractions of solutes is small compared with unity, the solution is called a dilute solution. A superscript attached to the \(\infty \) symbol for a property of a solution denotes the property in the limit of infinite dilution.

15234.title: solvate
15234.definition: Crystalline form of a compound in which one or more solvent molecules are part of the crystal structure.

S05747.title: solvation
S05747.definition: Any stabilizing interaction of a solute (or solute moiety) and the solvent or a similar interaction of solvent with groups of an insoluble material (i.e. the ionic groups of an ion-exchange resin). Such interactions generally involve electrostatic forces and van der Waals forces, as well as chemically more specific effects such as hydrogen bond formation.

ST07102.title: solvation energy
ST07102.definition: The change in Gibbs energy when an ion or molecule is transferred from a vacuum (or the gas phase) to a solvent. The main contributions to the solvation energy come from:  the cavitation energy of formation of the hole which preserves the dissolved species in the solvent;  the orientation energy of partial orientation of the dipoles; the isotropic interaction energy of electrostatic and dispersion origin; and  the anisotropic energy of specific interactions, e.g. hydrogen bonds, donor-acceptor interactions etc.

S05748.title: solvatochromic relationship
S05748.definition: A linear free-energy relationship based on solvatochromism.

S05749.title: solvatochromism
S05749.definition: The (pronounced) change in position and sometimes intensity of an electronic absorption or emission band, accompanying a change in the polarity of the medium. Negative (positive) solvatochromism corresponds to a hypsochromic (bathochromic) shift with increasing solvent polarity.

08209.title: solvatomers
08209.definition: Isomers that differ in their solvation environment.

16097.title: solvent abuse
16097.definition: Deliberate inhalation (or drinking) of volatile solvents, in order to become intoxicated.

08546.title: solvent blank flux density
08546.definition: Intensity transmitted by the atomizer when the latter is supplied with the solvent blank.

10256.title: solvent desorption
10256.definition: Use of a solvent, typically combined with agitation, to remove target analytes from a sorbent.

15037.title: solvent drag
15037.definition: Movement of a solute (e.g., a contaminant) along with the bulk movement of the solvent.

S05752.title: solvent extraction
S05752.definition: The process of transferring a substance from any matrix to an appropriate liquid phase. If the substance is initially present as a solute in an immiscible liquid phase the process is synonymous with liquid-liquid extraction.

S05753.title: solvent front
S05753.definition: The front line of the eluent.

S05751.title: solvent
S05751.definition: The term applied to the whole initial liquid phase containing the extractant.

S05755.title: solvent isotope effect
S05755.definition: A kinetic or equilibrium isotope effect resulting from change in the isotopic composition of the solvent.

S05756.title: solvent migration-distance
S05756.definition: The distance travelled by the solvent front.

15361.title: solvent mole fraction
15361.definition: Mole or mass fraction of a solvent in a solution containing \(s\) solute constituents (\(i = 1, 2, \ldots, s\)) and \(p\) solvent constituents (\(i = s + 1, s + 2, \ldots, p\)). For a solvent \(\ce{A}\), \[x_{{\rm{v}},{\ce{A}}} = x_{\ce{A}}/\sum \limits_{i=s+1}^{p} x_{i}\] where \[\sum \limits_{i=1}^{p} x_{i} = \sum \limits_{i=1}^{s} x_{i} + \sum \limits_{i=s+1}^{p} x_{i} = 1\] and analogously for \(w_{{\rm{v}},{\ce{A}}}\), where the first and last summations are over all solvent constituents.

08547.title: solvent nucleation
08547.definition: Solvent condensation on solid particles or droplets contained in an aerosol.

S05757.title: solvent parameter
S05757.definition: Quantitative measures of the capability of solvents for interaction with solutes. Such parameters have been based on numerous different physicochemical quantities, e.g. rate constants, solvatochromic shifts in ultraviolet/visible spectra, solvent-induced shifts in infrared frequencies, etc. Some solvent parameters are purely empirical in nature, i.e. they are based directly on some experimental measurement. It may be possible to interpret such a parameter as measuring some particular aspect of solvent–solute interaction or it may be regarded simply as a measure of solvent polarity. Other solvent parameters are based on analysing experimental results. Such a parameter is considered to quantify some particular aspect of solvent capability for interaction with solutes.

S05758.title: solvent regeneration
S05758.definition: Treatment of the solvent for re-cycling, e.g. by removal of degradation products or non-strippable solutes. The term solvent purification is synonymous, but the terms scrubbing, stripping and washing should not be used in this context.

S05761.title: solvent shift
S05761.definition: A shift in the frequency of a spectral band of a chemical species arising from interaction with its solvent environment.

08416.title: solvent suppression
08416.definition: In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy reduction or removal of large, unwanted resonances from solvents to improve spectrum quality and dynamic range through selective excitation and exploiting differences in relaxation times between solvent and analyte signals.

08548.title: solvent transport rate
08548.definition: Mass of solvent, both in liquid and vapour forms, reaching an inductively-coupled plasma per unit of time.

09448.title: solvent vapor annealing
09448.definition: Annealing via the exposure of a substrate to solvent vapor.

15362.title: solvent volume fraction
15362.definition: For a solvent \(\ce{A}\), volume fraction of \(\ce{A}\) divided by the sum of the volume fractions of solvent in a solution containing both \(s\) solutes (\(i = 1, 2, \ldots, s\)) and \(p\) solvents (\(i = s + 1, s + 2, \ldots, p\)) \[\varphi_{{\rm{v}},{\ce{A}}} = \varphi_{\ce{A}}/\sum \limits_{i=s+1}^{p} \varphi_{i}\] where the summation is over the \(p\) solvent components only.

ST07478.title: solvent-induced symmetry breaking
ST07478.definition: Breaking of symmetry of a molecular species by interactions with the solvent that can modify the molecular charge distribution, to favour asymmetrical configurations.

S05762.title: solvolysis
S05762.definition: Generally, reaction with a solvent, or with a lyonium ion or lyate ion involving the rupture of one or more bonds in the reacting solute. More specifically the term is used for substitution elimination and fragmentation reactions in which a solvent species is the nucleophile ('alcoholysis' if the solvent is an alcohol, etc.).

13865.title: solvophilic
13865.definition: Qualifier indicating an affinity for solvents.

13866.title: solvophobic
13866.definition: Qualifier indicating a lack of affinity for solvents.

S05763.title: solvophobicity parameter
S05763.definition: A solvent parameter defined by: \[Sp = 1 - \frac{M}{M (\rm{hexadecane})}\] derived from the Gibbs energy of transfer (\(\Delta_{\rm{t}} G^{\circ}\)) of a series of solutes from water to numerous aqueous-organic mixtures and to pure solvents: \[\Delta_{\rm{t}} G^{\circ} ({\rm{to\ solvent}}) = M R_{\rm{T}} + D\] where \(R_{\rm{T}}\) is a solute parameter, and \(M\) and \(D\) characterize the solvent. The \(M\) values are used to define a solvent solvophobic effect so that \(Sp\) values are scaled from unity (water) to zero (hexadecane).

S05764.title: solvus
S05764.definition: A line on a binary phase diagram (or a surface on a ternary phase diagram) that defines the limit of solid solubility under equilibrium conditions.

11226.title: somatic
11226.definition: Pertaining to the body or describing cells that form the body other than germ line cells or undifferentiated stem cells.

13687.title: somatic diversification theory
13687.definition: Theory that very few immunoglobulins (Ig) are inherited, but that extensive antibody diversity arises from mutations in non-reproductive cells.

13688.title: somatic gene conversion
13688.definition: Nonreciprocal exchange of nucleic acid sequences between genes in which part of the donor gene or genes is 'copied' into an acceptor gene, but only the acceptor gene is altered.

11227.title: somatic hypermutation
11227.definition: Programmed process of mutation affecting the variable (V) regions of immunoglobulin (Ig) genes. SHM affects only individual immune cells, and the mutations are not transmitted to offspring.

13689.title: somatic recombination
13689.definition: Process giving rise to increased antibody diversity by cutting and splicing immunoglobulin (Ig) genes during lymphocyte differentiation.

15039.title: somatic risk
15039.definition: Risk of an adverse effect to the exposed individual associated with genetic damage to somatic cells, e.g., damage leading to cancer.

11229.title: somatomedin
11229.definition: Any of a group of peptide growth factors produced by the liver following stimulation by somatotropin.

11230.title: somatotropin
11230.definition: Hormone produced in the pituitary gland that stimulates the liver to produce somatomedin.

11231.title: somite
11231.definition: One of bilaterally paired, segmented masses of mesodermal tissue lying along the notochord that gives rise to the vertebrae and associated muscle and connective tissue.

S05765.title: SOMO
S05765.definition: A Singly Occupied Molecular Orbital (such as the half-filled HOMO of a radical).

11232.title: sonic hedgehog
11232.definition: Protein morphogen produced in the notochord that plays a critical role in early development, including vertebrate organogenesis, brain development and limb formation.

S05766.title: sonication
S05766.definition: Irradiation with (often ultra)sound waves, e.g. to increase the rate of a reaction or to prepare vesicles in mixtures of surfactants and water.

ST07530.title: sonogel
ST07530.definition: Colloidal gel produced by the action of ultrasonically induced cavitation.

14088.title: sonophotocatalytic reactor
14088.definition: Reactor in which a hybrid technique combining 'sonochemical' and photocatalytic reactions is used.

ST07512.title: sonosol
ST07512.definition: Sol produced by the action of ultrasonically induced cavitation.

S05768.title: soot
S05768.definition: A randomly formed particulate carbon material and may be coarse, fine and/or colloidal in proportions depending on its origin. Soot consists of variable quantities of carbonaceous and inorganic solids together with absorbed and occluded tars and resins.

15040.title: sorbate
15040.definition: Noncommittal term used instead of adsorbate or absorbate when the sorption process is undefined.

10163.title: sorbent
10163.definition: Condensed phase where extraction of analytes can occur at the surface and in the bulk.

10201.title: sorbent trap
10201.definition: Tube filled with porous sorbent typically used to extract analytes from the gas phase.

10257.title: sorbent-containing pipette tip
10257.definition: Disposable pipette tip with a small packed bed, disc, or monolithic plug of sorbent at its narrow end.Sorbent containing pipette tips in an array for use with a multiwall sample plate.

ST06784.title: Soret band
ST06784.definition: A very strong absorption band in the blue region of the optical absorption spectrum of a haem protein.

15041.title: sorption constant
15041.definition: Quantity describing the distribution of a substance between a solvent and a sorbent, typically water and sediment, at equilibrium, e.g., \[K_{\rm{d}} = [\pu{C(sediment)}]/[\pu{C(water)}]\]

S05769.title: sorption
S05769.definition: The process by which a substance (sorbate) is sorbed (adsorbed or absorbed) on or in another substance (sorbent).

S05770.title: sorption isotherm
S05770.definition: The concentration of a sorbed species in the ion exchanger, expressed as a function of its concentration in the external solution under specified conditions and at constant temperature.

S05771.title: sorption techniques
S05771.definition: Techniques based on the distribution of components being separated between two phases, one of which is stationary and the other mobile. The advantage of some chromatographic methods is the possibility of combining the preconcentration and determination steps, as well as improving the speed of determination, and the possibility of separation of components with similar properties, and of achieving high values of the preconcentration coefficient. The methods enable analyses of microamounts of substances. ion-exchange chromatography is not widely used owing to the great volumes of solutions being treated and, consequently, to a great degree to the variation in the blank, and to some diffusional limitations. Static ion-exchange, which is much simpler and more readily carried out, is practised quite widely.

S05772.title: sorptive insertion
S05772.definition: This is analogous to the process of ligand insertion in coordination chemistry. $$\ce{H^{\ast} + C2H4(g) -> ^{\ast}C2H5}$$ This reaction might also be imagined to proceed by adsorption of $\ce{C2H4}$ followed by ligand migration (an associative surface reaction).

10258.title: sorptive-tape extraction
10258.definition: Extraction from the surface of a solid by sorbent or polymer film in the form of a tape in direct contact with, or in the headspace above, the sample.

15042.title: source term
15042.definition: Estimate of the total amount released, or the temporal pattern of the rate of release, of a pollutant from a source.

09728.title: Southern blot
09728.definition: Technique based on deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) hybridization used for the detection of a DNA fragment of specific nucleotide sequence.

10228.title: Soxhlet extraction
10228.definition: Leaching with fresh solvent cycled multiple times through a fine solid sample contained in a porous thimble.Typical apparatus for classical Soxhlet extraction.

S05776.title: space charge
S05776.definition: At the surface region of a semiconductor the surface excess or deficiency of electrons constitutes a space charge.

14089.title: space charge region
14089.definition: Region formed within a semiconductor in contact with another phase in which there is a band bending that can be upward or downward.

S05779.title: space velocity
S05779.definition: Defined as \(v_{m}\), \(v_{v}\), and \(v_{a}\) where the \(v_{i}\)s represent the rate of feed of the given reactant fed per unit mass, volume or surface area of the catalyst.

ST06873.title: spacer
ST06873.definition: A flexible segment used to link successive mesogenic units in the molecules of MCPLCs (main-chain polymer liquid crystals) or to attach mesogenic units as side-groups onto the polymer backbone of SGPLCs (side-group polymer liquid crystals).

09031.title: spacer arm
09031.definition: Link used in a conjugation to distance the substrate from the active species that otherwise would have its activity affected by steric or other influences.

12728.title: spare receptor
12728.definition: Residual binding site still available to an endogenous ligand after sufficient sites have already been filled to elicit the maximal response possible for that particular biological system.

S05780.title: spark ionization
S05780.definition: Occurs when a solid sample is vaporized and partially ionized by an intermittent discharge. It is recommended that the word 'source' be dropped from this term.

12080.title: spasm
12080.definition: Sudden involuntary contraction of one or more muscles; includes cramps and contractures.

12081.title: spasmolytic
12081.definition: Agent that relieves smooth muscle spasms.

12083.title: spasticity
12083.definition: Increased muscle tone at rest, characterized by resistance to passive stretch.

S05781.title: spatial-distribution interference
S05781.definition: Interference which may occur when changes in concentration of concomitants affect the mass flow rates or mass flow patterns of the analyte species in the flame. If they are caused by changes in volume and rise velocity of the gases formed by combustion, in extreme cases manifesting themselves by changes in the size and/or shape of the flame, they are non-specific and are called flame-geometry interferences.

08679.title: spatially offset Raman spectroscopy
08679.definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy in which the sample is illuminated at one location, and the Raman signal is collected from a different location on the sample surface.

S05782.title: spatially resolving detector
S05782.definition: A detector for the measurement of the spatial distribution of the radiation. Spatially resolving detectors can be divided into two groups:   the photosensitive area consists of a matrix of discrete photosensitive elements, the pixels (picture elements) forming an array with the facility to separately read out the information, simultaneously or sequentially.   the photosensitive area consists of a single photosensitive element that must be scanned (e.g. image dissection tube.)

11233.title: spawn
11233.definition:
(v) Release gametes. (Of mature adult fish, frogs, molluscs, crustacea, etc.).
(n) Fertilized eggs of mature adult fish, etc.

11234.title: spawning
11234.definition:
(n) Release of gametes (eggs or sperm) from mature adult fish, frogs, molluscs, crustacea, etc.
(adj) Describing behavior related to the readiness of mature adult fish, etc. to release gametes.

15043.title: Spearman–Karber method
15043.definition: Nonparametric method to estimate the \(\pu{LC_{50}}\), \(\pu{EC_{50}}\), or \(\pu{LD_{50}}\) when it is difficult or unnecessary to assume a specific model for the dose- or concentration effect data.

S05783.title: special salt effect
S05783.definition: The initial steep rate increase observed in the kinetic electrolyte effect on certain solvolysis reactions, upon addition of some non-common ion salts, especially $\ce{LiClO4}$.

ST06848.title: speciation analysis
ST06848.definition: Analytical activities of identifying and/or measuring the quantities of one or more individual chemical species in a sample.

ST06861.title: speciation
ST06861.definition: Distribution of an element amongst defined chemical species in a system.

S05786.title: species
S05786.definition: A taxonomic subdivision of a genus; a group of closely related, morphologically and physiologically similar individuals.

15045.title: species assemblage
15045.definition: Operationally defined subset of the entire community.

15047.title: species differences in sensitivity
15047.definition: Quantitative or qualitative differences of response to the action(s) of a potentially toxic substance on various species of living organisms.

15048.title: species diversity
15048.definition: Heterogeneity of an ecological community, considering both species richness (\(S\)) and species evenness.

15049.title: species evenness
15049.definition: Degree to which the individuals in the community are evenly or uniformly distributed among species.

15050.title: species imbalance
15050.definition: Change in the species numbers or diversity in an ecosystem, or in their interactions, which results in change in ecological character and its functions and attributes.

15051.title: species richness
15051.definition: Total number of species in an ecosystem.

15052.title: species sensitivity distribution
15052.definition: Statistical relationship between exposure concentration and a defined effect derived from a combination of single-species test data to predict concentrations affecting only a certain percentage of the total number of species in a defined community.

15044.title: species–area relationship
15044.definition: Common pattern in which the number of species on islands decreases as island area decreases.

15046.title: species–deletion stability
15046.definition: Tendency in a model community for the remaining species to remain at locally stable equilibria after a species is made extinct.

15053.title: species-specific sensitivity
15053.definition: Quantitative and qualitative features of response to the action(s) of a potentially toxic substance that are characteristic for a particular species of living organism.

S05787.title: specific
S05787.definition: Attribute to a physical quantity obtained by division by mass. Specific volume is the volume of a sample divided by its mass.

14091.title: specific absorption coefficient
14091.definition: Linear napierian, \(\alpha_{\lambda}^{\ast}\), or linear decadic, \(a_{\lambda}^{\ast}\), absorption coefficient divided by the mass concentration, \(\rho\).

S05789.title: specific acid–base catalysis
S05789.definition: Catalysis by acids or bases in solution is said to be specific when the only observable catalytic effects are those due to the ions formed from the solvent itself (e.g. if when water is the solvent the only observable catalysis is that due to the $\ce{H^{+}}$ and $\ce{OH^{−}}$ ions).

15054.title: specific action concept
15054.definition: Assumption made in radiotracer usage concerning specificity of action of a radionuclide used to trace or quantify the movement of a stable nuclide (e.g., \(\ce{^{14}C}\) for stable \(\ce{C}\)), implying that the radionuclide behaves identically in chemical and biological processes to its nonradioactive analog (e.g., stable \(\ce{C}\)).

08763.title: specific activity (radionuclide)
08763.definition: Activity of a specified radionuclide (\(\ce{R}\)) per unit mass of that nuclide.

S05790.title: specific activity
S05790.definition: For a specified isotopes, or mixture of isotopes, the activity of a material divided by the mass of the material.

S05791.title: specific adsorption
S05791.definition: Ions become specifically adsorbed when short-range interactions between them and the interphase become important. They are believed then to penetrate into the inner layer and may (but not necessarily) come into contact with the surface. They are usually assumed to form a partial or complete monolayer.

09881.title: specific binding
09881.definition: Binding of proteins to specific sites in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) based on the precise recognition of nucleotide sequence and/or conformation of the DNA.

S05795.title: specific burn-up
S05795.definition: The total energy released through induced nuclear transformations divided by the mass of a nuclear fuel.

S05796.title: specific catalysis
S05796.definition: The acceleration of a reaction by a unique catalyst, rather than by a family of related substances. The term is most commonly used in connection with specific hydrogen-ion or hydroxide-ion (lyonium ion or lyate ion) catalysis.

16098.title: specific death rate
16098.definition: Death rate computed for a subpopulation of individual organisms or people having a specified characteristic or attribute, and named accordingly.

S05798.title: specific detector
S05798.definition: A detector which responds to a single sample component or to a limited number of components having similar chemical characteristics.

S05788.title: specific
S05788.definition: A term which expresses qualitatively the extent to which other substances interfere with the determination of a substance according to a given procedure. Specific is considered to be the ultimate of selective, meaning that no interferences are supposed to occur.

S05801.title: specific ionization
S05801.definition: The number of ion pairs formed per unit distance along the track of an ionizing particle passing through matter.

14092.title: specific napierian attenuance coefficient
14092.definition: Attenuance (napierian), \(D_{\rm{e}}\), divided by the absorption pathlength, \(l\), and the mass concentration, \(\rho\).

14093.title: specific napierian scattering coefficient
14093.definition: Fraction of attenuance (napierian) not due to absorbance, divided by the pathlength, \(l\), within the scattering medium and the mass concentration, \(\rho\).

16099.title: specific pathogen free
16099.definition: Describing an animal removed from its mother under sterile conditions just prior to term and subsequently reared and kept under sterile conditions.

S05802.title: specific permeability
S05802.definition: A term expressing the resistance of an empty tube or packed column to the flow of a fluid (the mobile phase).

14090.title: specific photoadsorption number
14090.definition: Maximum number of entities (molecules, atoms or radicals) adsorbed as a result of irradiation divided by the surface area and by the mass of adsorbent.

S05804.title: specific pore volume
S05804.definition: The total internal void volume per unit mass of adsorbent.

09966.title: specific resolution
09966.definition: Peak resolution also considering the molar masses (\(M_{1}\), \(M_{2}\)) of the two test compounds: \[R_{\rm{sp}} = \left[\frac{V_{\rm{R1}} - V_{\rm{R2}}}{(w_{\rm{b1}} + w_{\rm{b2}})/2} \right] \cdot \left[ \frac{1}{\log (M_{2}/M_{1})} \right]\]

S05806.title: specific surface area
S05806.definition: When the area of the interface between two phases is proportional to the mass of one of the phases (e.g. for a solid adsorbent, for an emulsion or for an aerosol), the specific surface area (\(a\),\(s\) or preferably \(a_{s}\)) is defined as the surface area divided by the mass of the relevant phase.

S05807.title: specific volume
S05807.definition: Volume of a substance divided by its mass. It is the reciprocal of mass density.

S05792.title: specifically absorbing ion
S05792.definition: Ions which possess a chemical affinity for the surface in addition to the Coulomb interaction, where chemical is a collective adjective, embracing all interactions other than purely Coulombic. Examples are van der Waals or hydrophobic bonding, pi-electron exchange and complex formation. Specifically adsorbing ions can adsorb on an initially uncharged surface and hence provide it with a charge. The term specifically adsorbed applies to the sorption of all other ions having an affinity to the surface in addition to the purely Coulombic contribution.

S05793.title: specifically labelled
S05793.definition: An isotopically labelled compound is designated as specifically labelled when a unique isotopically substituted compound is formally added to the analogous isotopically unmodified compound. In such a case, both position(s) and number of each labelling nuclide are defined.

S05794.title: specifically labelled tracer
S05794.definition: A tracer in which the label is present in a specified position.

11516.title: specificity
11516.definition: The ability of a two-class model to detect known inactive or non-toxic molecules.

08129.title: specified requirement
08129.definition: Need or expectation that is stated.

S05809.title: specimen
S05809.definition: A specifically selected portion of a material taken from a dynamic system and assumed to be representative of the parent material at the time it is taken. Although the specimen may not be reproducible in time, e.g. it may be taken from a flowing stream or a portion of blood, no separable sampling error exists since this error is unavoidably included with the corresponding error of the estimate of the property, function or analyte being studied. A specimen may be considered as a special type of sample, taken primarily in time rather than in space. The term 'specimen' has been used both as a representative unit and as a nonrepresentative (often better than most) unit of a population, usually in clinical, biological and mineralogical collections. 'Collections' in this case is used as either a noun or verb. This usage is almost always self-evident, and thus would not be confused with a time-type sample.

09356.title: spectator hole
09356.definition: Electronic configuration of an atom containing an electronic vacancy that can be present during processes, such as Auger electron and X-ray photoelectron emission, but is not created or destroyed in the process.

S05810.title: spectator mechanism
S05810.definition: A pre-association mechanism in which one of the molecular entities, C, is already present in an encounter pair with A during formation of B from A, but does not assist the formation of B, e.g.  The formation of B from A may itself be a bimolecular reaction with some other reagent. Since C does not assist the formation of A, it is described as being present as a spectator, and hence such a mechanism is sometimes referred to as a spectator mechanism.

S05811.title: spectator-stripping reaction
S05811.definition: An extreme type of stripping reaction in which one reaction product has almost the same direction and momentum as one of the reactant molecules had before the reactive collision occurred.

S05814.title: spectral effectiveness
S05814.definition: The reciprocal of the photon fluence rate, \(E_{\rm{p}}^{0}\), at wavelength \(\lambda \), causing identical photoresponse, \(\Delta \rm{y}\), per unit time (\(\frac{\Delta \rm{y}}{\Delta t}\)). The effectiveness spectrum is directly proportional to the conversion spectrum of the sensory pigment, if spectral attenuance is negligible.

08549.title: spectral background
08549.definition: Electromagnetic radiation, within the bandpass used, emitted by, and/or in the case of atomic absorption spectroscopy, absorbed in, the atomizer when nothing is supplied to the atomizer but the gases involved in its operation.

08285.title: spectral band
08285.definition: Region of the absorption/transmission spectrum in which the absorbance/transmission passes through a maximum/minimum.

08286.title: spectral bandwidth
08286.definition: Upper frequency minus lower frequency in a continuous band of frequencies.

S05812.title: spectral bandwidth error
S05812.definition: To measure the true shape, particularly the true maximum of an absorption band, the spectral bandwidth \(\Delta \lambda \) of the instrument must be much less than the width of the absorption band. A spectral bandwidth error results from using too large a bandwidth relative to the absorption band being measured.

S05813.title: spectral distribution
S05813.definition: The variation of the spectral radiance with wavelength.

16221.title: spectral fluence
16221.definition: Derivative of fluence, \(H_{\rm{o}}\), with respect to wavelength, _010366_.

ST07479.title: spectral fluence rate
ST07479.definition: Derivative of fluence rate, \(E_{\rm{o}}\), with respect to wavelength, \(\lambda\). SI unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-3}\); common unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-2}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\).

S05816.title: spectral interference
S05816.definition: Interference due to the incomplete isolation of the radiation emitted or absorbed by the analyte from other radiation detected by the instrument. Its occurrence may be established by comparing the measures of the analyte-free blank solution and the solvent blank.

S05817.title: spectral irradiance
S05817.definition: Irradiance, \(E\), at wavelength \(\lambda \) per unit wavelength interval. The SI unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-3}\), but a commonly used unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-2}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\).

08550.title: spectral line
08550.definition: In atomic spectroscopy, a very narrow band of frequencies of electromagnetic radiation emitted or absorbed by atoms, which undergo a single electronic transition.

S05818.title: spectral overlap
S05818.definition: In the context of radiative energy transfer, the integral, \(J = \int_{0}^{\infty} f_{\rm{D}}^{\prime}(\sigma)\ \varepsilon_{\rm{A}}(\sigma) {\rm{d}}\sigma \), which measures the overlap of the emission spectrum of the excited donor, D, and the absorption spectrum of the ground state acceptor, A; \(f_{\rm{D}}^{'}\) is the measured normalized emission of D, \(f_{\rm{D}}^{'}=\frac{f_{\rm{D}}\left(\sigma \right)}{\int _{0}^{\infty }f_{\rm{D}}\left(\sigma \right)  \ \mathrm{d}\sigma }\), \(f_{\rm{D}}(\sigma)\) is the photon exitance of the donor at wavenumber \(\sigma \), and \(\varepsilon_{\rm{A}}(\sigma)\) is the decadic molar absorption coefficient of A at wavenumber \(\sigma \). In the context of Förster excitation transfer, \(J\) is given by: \[J = \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{f_{\rm{D}}^{^\prime}(\sigma)\ \varepsilon_{\rm{A}}(\sigma)}{\sigma^{4}} {\rm{d}}\sigma \] In the context of Dexter excitation transfer, \(J\) is given by: \[J = \int_{0}^{\infty} f_{\rm{D}}(\sigma)\ \varepsilon_{\rm{A}}(\sigma) {\rm{d}}\sigma \] In this case \(f_{\rm{D}}\) and \(\varepsilon_{\rm{A}}\), the emission spectrum of donor and absorption spectrum of acceptor, respectively, are both normalized to unity, so that the rate constant for energy transfer, \(k_{\rm{ET}}\), is independent of the oscillator strength of both transitions (contrast to Förster mechanism).

S05819.title: spectral photon exitance
S05819.definition: The photon exitance, \(M_{\rm{p}}\), at wavelength per unit wavelength interval. The SI unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{m}^{-3}\), but a commonly used unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{m}^{-2}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\). Alternatively, the term can be used with the amount of photons (mol or its equivalent einstein) the SI unit then being \(\pu{mol s-1 m-3}\) and the common unit \(\pu{mol s-1 m-2 nm-1}\).

S05820.title: spectral photon flow
S05820.definition: The photon flow, \(\varPhi_{\rm{p}}\), at wavelength \(\lambda \) per unit wavelength interval. The SI unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{m}^{-1}\), but a commonly used unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\). Alternatively, the term can be used with the amount of photons (mol or its equivalent einstein), the SI unit then being \(\pu{mol s-1 m-1}\) and the common unit \(\pu{mol s-1 nm-1}\).

S05821.title: spectral photon flux
S05821.definition: The photon irradiance \(E_{\rm{p}}\), at wavelength \(\lambda \) per unit wavelength interval. The SI unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{m}^{-3}\), but a commonly used unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{m}^{-2}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\). Alternatively, the term can be used with the amount of photons (mol or its equivalent einstein), the SI unit then being \(\pu{mol s-1 m-3}\) and the common unit \(\pu{mol s-1 m-2 nm-1}\).

14094.title: spectral photon irradiance
14094.definition: Derivative of photon irradiance, \(E_{\rm{p}}\), with respect to wavelength, \(\lambda\).

S05822.title: spectral photon radiance
S05822.definition: The photon radiance, \(L_{\rm{p}}\), at wavelength per unit wavelength interval. The SI unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{m}^{-3}\ \rm{sr}^{-1}\), but a commonly used unit is \(\rm{s}^{-1}\ \rm{m}^{-2}\ \rm{sr}^{-1}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\). Alternatively, the term can be used with the amount of photons (mol or its equivalent einstein) the SI unit then being \(\pu{mol s-1 m-3 sr-1}\) and the common unit \(\pu{mol s-1 m-2 sr-1 nm-1}\).

14095.title: spectral photonic yield
14095.definition: Dependence of the photonic yield on the photon energy (wavelength, frequency, or wavenumber) of the radiation for a given photoreaction obtained at a certain incident (prior to absorption) photon irradiance in a given spectral range.

S05823.title: spectral quantities
S05823.definition: Quantities characterizing electromagnetic radiation (radiant power, energy, energy density, intensity, exitance, radiance, irradiance, etc.) derived by differentiation with respect to wavelength, frequency or wavenumber, e.g. spectral (concentration of) irradiance is the derivative of the irradiance with respect to wavelength (\(E_{\lambda }\)), frequency (\(E_{\nu }\)) or wavenumber (\(E_{\stackrel{˜}{\nu }}\)).

14096.title: spectral quantum yield
14096.definition: Dependence of the quantum yield on the photon energy (wavelength, frequency or wavenumber) of the radiation absorbed by the reactant for a given photoreaction.

S05824.title: spectral radiance
S05824.definition: The radiance, \(L\), at wavelength \(\lambda \) per unit wavelength interval. The SI unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-3}\ \rm{sr}^{-1}\), but a commonly used unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-2}\ \rm{sr}^{-1}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\).

08287.title: spectral radiant energy density
08287.definition: Radiant energy density in unit wavenumber (wavelength) interval at wavenumber \(\tilde{\nu}\) (wavelength \(\lambda\)).

ST07480.title: spectral radiant energy
ST07480.definition: Derivative of radiant energy, \(Q\), with respect to wavelength \(\lambda \). SI unit is \(\pu{J m-1}\); common unit is \(\pu{J nm-1}\).

S05825.title: spectral radiant exitance
S05825.definition: The radiant exitance, \(M\), at wavelength \(\lambda \) per unit wavelength interval. The SI unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-3}\), but a commonly used unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-2}\ \rm{nm}^{-1}\).

S05827.title: spectral radiant intensity
S05827.definition: The radiation intensity, \(I\) at wavelength \(\lambda \) per unit wavelength interval. The SI unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-1}\ \rm{sr}^{-1}\), but a commonly used unit is \(\rm{W nm}^{-1}\ \rm{sr}^{-1}\).

S05828.title: spectral radiant power
S05828.definition: The radiant power at wavelength \(\lambda \) per unit wavelength interval. The SI unit is \(\rm{W m}^{-1}\), but a commonly used unit is \(\rm{W nm}^{-1}\).

08288.title: spectral range
08288.definition: Wavelength range for which a spectrometer can be used.

08289.title: spectral resolution
08289.definition: Smallest difference between wavenumbers (or wavelengths or frequencies) at which different spectral properties may be distinguished, measured as the full width at half maximum.

S05829.title: spectral responsivity
S05829.definition: The spectral output quantity of a system such as a photomultiplier, diode array, photoimaging device, or biological unit divided by the spectral irradiance \(s(\lambda) = \frac{\rm{d}y\left(\lambda \right)}{\rm{d}E\left(\lambda \right)}\), simplified expression: \(s(\lambda) = \frac{Y_{\lambda }}{E_{\lambda }}\), where \(Y_{\lambda }\) is the magnitude of the output signal for irradiation at wavelength \(\lambda \) and \(E_{\lambda }\) is the spectral irradiance of the parallel and perpendicular incident beam at the same wavelength.

ST07395.title: spectral sensitivity
ST07395.definition: Referred to actinometer based on spectrophotometric measurements, \(S_{\rm{ac}}(\lambda) = \varPhi (\lambda)\ \varepsilon(\lambda _{\rm{obs}}) = \rm{sensitivity\ or\ actinometric\ factor}\). \(\varPhi(\lambda)\) is the quantum yield of the actinometer at the excitation wavelength and \(\lambda_{\rm{obs}}\) is the observation wavelength, which may be the same as or differ from the former.

S05831.title: spectral sensitization
S05831.definition: The process of increasing the spectral responsivity of a (photoimaging) system in a given wavelength region.

S05832.title: spectral spheradiance
S05832.definition: Alternative term suggested for actinic flux.

08290.title: spectral subtraction
08290.definition: Ordinate of one spectrum minus ordinate of another spectrum.

08417.title: spectral width
08417.definition: Frequency range that describes the width of the spectrum window of a specific nucleus in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

S05833.title: spectrochemical buffer
S05833.definition: Buffer added to samples and reference samples with the intention of making the measure of the analytical element less sensitive to changes in concentration of an interferent.

S05834.title: spectrochemical carrier
S05834.definition: An additive which gives rise to a gas which can help to transport the vapour of the sample material into the excitation region of the source, e.g. carbon in an air atmosphere when carbon dioxide is formed.

09171.title: spectroelectrochemistry
09171.definition: Measurement methods combining spectrometric and electrochemical measurements.

S05835.title: spectrogram
S05835.definition: A spectrum as recorded by a spectrometer.

S05836.title: spectrograph
S05836.definition: A combination of a spectral apparatus and a camera, which enables an image of a spectrum to be recorded. Spectra are recorded by a photographic emulsion or other means, e.g. two-dimensional electronic image sensors.

S05837.title: spectrometer
S05837.definition: A general term for describing a combination of spectral apparatus with one or more detectors to measure the intensity of one or more spectral bands.

09283.title: spectrometer response function
09283.definition: Number of particles detected with a spectrometer divided by the number of such particles per solid angle and per interval of the dispersing parameter available for measurement as a function of the dispersing parameter.

09284.title: spectrometer transmission function
09284.definition: Number of particles transmitted by the analyser divided by the number of such particles per solid angle and per interval of the dispersing parameter (e.g. energy, mass, or wavelength) available for measurement as a function of the dispersing parameter.

S05847.title: spectroscope
S05847.definition: A device which enables visual observation and evaluation of optical spectra (usually confined to the visible spectral region).

S05848.title: spectroscopy
S05848.definition: The study of physical systems by the electromagnetic radiation with which they interact or that they produce. Spectrometry is the measurement of such radiations as a means of obtaining information about the systems and their components. In certain types of optical spectroscopy, the radiation originates from an external source and is modified by the system, whereas in other types, the radiation originates within the system itself.

08291.title: spectrum
08291.definition: Graph of a quantity derived from the radiant power at each wavelength (frequency or wavenumber) as ordinate plotted against the wavelength (frequency or wavenumber) of electromagnetic radiation as abscissa.

S05849.title: spectrum analysis
S05849.definition: The interpretation of the information present in an energy spectrum in terms of radiation energy and intensity.

S05851.title: specular reflectance
S05851.definition: Radiant power specularly reflected from the surface of a system, \(P_{\mathrm{refl}}\), divided by the incident power, \(P_{0}\): \[\rho =\frac{P_{\mathrm{refl}}}{P_{0}}\]

08292.title: specular reflection
08292.definition: Reflection of electromagnetic radiation from a surface such that each incident ray is reflected at the same angle to the surface normal as the incident ray, but on the opposing side of the surface normal in the plane formed by incident and reflected rays.

09204.title: specular X-ray reflectrometry
09204.definition: Mode of X-ray reflectrometry in which the angle between the detected beam and the sample surface is equal to that of the incident beam and the sample surface.

S05853.title: speed distribution function
S05853.definition: Probability density of finding a particle with speed within an interval between \(c\) and \(c+\mathrm{d}c\).

S05854.title: speed of light in a vacuum
S05854.definition: The speed of light in vacuum, \(c\), is one of seven fixed constants defining the International System of Units, the SI, with \(c = \pu{299792458 m s-1}\). The speed of light is considered as a fundamental constant of nature.

S05852.title: speed
S05852.definition: Scalar quantity equal to the absolute value of the velocity vector.

11235.title: Spemann organizer
11235.definition: Group of cells in the amphibian embryo that is important in orientation of surrounding cells and facilitates development of the central nervous system.

09649.title: sperm
09649.definition: Seminal fluid containing male reproductive cells.

11236.title: sperm banking
11236.definition: Storage of frozen donor sperm for use in artificial insemination.

10977.title: sperm motility
