09430.definition: Registration of a particle by a time-to-digital converter in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

08553.title: stop-flow conditions
08553.definition: Stoppage to the otherwise constant flow of argon gas to the atomizer in electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy, that can be programmed to occur during atomization, for the purpose of increasing the residence time of the analyte atoms and thus the associated signal.

S06033.title: stopped flow
S06033.definition: A technique for following the kinetics of reactions in solution (usually in the millisecond time range) in which two reactant solutions are rapidly mixed by being forced through a mixing chamber. The flow of the mixed solution along a uniform tube is then suddenly arrested. At a fixed position along the tube the solution is monitored (as a function of time following the stoppage of the flow) by some method with a rapid response (e.g. photometry).

S06034.title: stopped-flow cell
S06034.definition: A small-volume absorption cell connected to a rapid mixing chamber.

13983.title: stopper
13983.definition: Group bulky enough to prevent dethreading of a given macrocyclic component from a threading component or its translocation to another linear section of the threading component.

09387.title: stopping cross section
09387.definition: Rate of energy loss of a particle with distance along its trajectory in a sample divided by the atomic density of sample atoms for a sample of infinitesimal thickness.

09386.title: stopping cross section factor
09386.definition: Energy loss of a particle scattered at a given depth in the sample, and detected at a given angle, by the product of the atomic density of the sample atoms and the depth of scattering.

S06035.title: stopping power
S06035.definition: Of a substance, for charged particles of specified energy, the average energy loss in passing through a thin layer of that substance, divided by the thickness of that layer.

12802.title: storage modulus
12802.definition: Ratio of the amplitude of the stress in phase with the strain (\(\sigma_{0} \cos \delta\)) to the amplitude of the strain (\(\gamma_{0}\)) in the forced sinusoidal oscillation of a material. \[M^{\prime} = \frac{\sigma_{0} \cos \delta}{\gamma_{0}}\]

S06036.title: STP
S06036.definition: Abbreviation for standard temperature (\(273.15\ \rm{K}\) or \(0\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\)) and pressure (\(10^{5}\ \rm{Pa}\)); usually employed in reporting gas volumes. Note that flow meters calibrated in standard gas volumes per unit time often refer to volumes at \(25\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\), not \(0\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\).

S06037.title: strain
S06037.definition: Strain is present in a molecular entity or transition structure if the energy is enhanced because of unfavourable bond lengths, bond angles or dihedral angles ('torsional strain') relative to a standard. It is quantitatively defined as the standard enthalpy of a structure relative to a strainless structure (real or hypothetical) made up from the same atoms with the same types of bonding. (The enthalpy of formation of cyclopropane is \(\pu{53.6 kJ mol-1}\), whereas the enthalpy of formation based on three 'normal' methylene groups, from acyclic models, is \(\pu{-62 kJ mol-1}\). On this basis cyclopropane is destabilized by ca. \(\pu{115 kJ mol-1}\) of strain energy.)

ST07108.title: strain energy
ST07108.definition: The excess energy due to steric strain of a molecular entity or transition state structure, i.e. distortions relative to a reference (real or hypothetical) 'strainless' structure with the standard bond lengths, bond angles and dihedral angles. The strain energy components involve the following destabilizing terms: non-bonded repulsions, bond-angle distortions, bond stretch or compression, rotation around or twisting of double bonds, and electrostatic strain. In general, the contributions of these components are inseparable and interdependent. A quantitative assessment of strain and strain energies can be made by taking the difference between the heat of formation of the substance under consideration and that of a hypothetical strain-free model. Several approaches to the assessment of strain energies have been developed based on the use of energies of isodesmic and homodesmotic reactions and on the so-called 'strainless increments', i.e. heats of formation of certain groups ($\ce{CH3}$, $\ce{CH2}$, $\ce{CH}$, $\ce{C}$ etc).

S06038.title: strain-induced transition
S06038.definition: A transition in a solid that is initiated by plastic strain.

09729.title: strand break
09729.definition: Interruption of the sugar-phosphate backbone of a polynucleotide chain.

15063.title: stratification
15063.definition: Process by which materials form or are deposited in layers, as in sedimentary rocks and some igneous rocks. The atmosphere and the ocean also exhibit stratification, with the warmer air or water occupying the upper layers.

S06039.title: stratified film
S06039.definition: A film in which more than two thicknesses coexist in a fixed configuration over significant periods of time.

S06040.title: stratified sample
S06040.definition: A sample consisting of portions obtained from identified subparts (strata) of the parent population. Within each stratum, the samples are taken randomly. The objective of taking stratified samples is to obtain a more representative sample than that which might otherwise be obtained by random sampling.

15064.title: stratified sampling
15064.definition: Sampling of individual subgroups (strata) of a population after its division into homogeneous strata.

S06041.title: stratocumulus cloud
S06041.definition: A layer of patches composed of laminae or globular masses arranged in groups, lines or waves and having a soft, grey appearance; very often the rolls are so close together that their edges join and give the undersurface a wavy character; the process of formation (cumulogenesis) involves the spreading out of the tops of cumulus clouds, the latter having disappeared; \(

S06042.title: stratopause
S06042.definition: That region of the atmosphere which lies between the stratosphere and the mesosphere and in which a maximum in the temperature occurs.

S06043.title: stratosphere
S06043.definition: The atmospheric shell lying just above the troposphere which is characterized by an increasing temperature with altitude. The stratosphere begins at the tropopause (about \(10{-}15\ \rm{km}\) height) and extends to a height of about \(50\ \rm{km}\), where the lapse rate changes sign at the stratopause and the beginning of the mesosphere.

S06044.title: stratus cloud
S06044.definition: A uniform, featureless layer of cloud resembling fog but not resting on the ground; when this very low layer is broken up into irregular shreds, it is designated as fractostratus; \(300{-}600\ \rm{m}\); widespread irregular stirring and lifting of the shallow layer of cool, damp air near the ground.

08293.title: stray light
08293.definition: Electromagnetic radiation that does not follow the usual path through a spectrometer and consequently appears in a spectrum at a frequency or wavenumber different from its initial value. The term is also used to refer to radiation that passes around the sample instead of through it, and consequently is not modified by the sample and seriously affects absolute and relative intensities.

S06045.title: stray radiation error
S06045.definition: A spectrometer set to pass radiation of a particular wavelength band always has a small amount of stray radiation of other wavelengths. Since the sample may absorb more (or less) of this stray radiation than of the radiation at the selected wavelength an error can occur. This error is called a stray radiation error.

S06047.title: streak tube
S06047.definition: An image converter adapted to provide scanning or time-resolved images. If the image is recorded the whole device is an example of a streak camera.

10291.title: stream
10291.definition: The sample in membrane separations prior to contact with the membrane.

S06048.title: streaming birefringence
S06048.definition: The birefringence induced by flow in liquids, solutions and dispersions of optically anisotropic, anisometric or deformable flow molecules or particles due to a non-random orientation of the molecules or particles. Synonymous with flow birefringence.

S06049.title: streaming current
S06049.definition: The electric current \(I\) flowing in a streaming cell if the electrodes, which are supposed to be ideally depolarized, are short-circuited. \(I\) is positive if the current in the membrane, plug, etc., is from high to low pressure side (and in the outside lead from low to high pressure side).

S06050.title: streaming potential difference
S06050.definition: The potential difference \(E_{\mathrm{st}}\) or \(E\) at zero current caused by the flow of liquid under a pressure gradient through a membrane, plug or capillary. Identical electrodes must be used on both sides of the membrane, plug, etc. \(E\) is positive if the higher potential is on the high pressure side.

15065.title: stress
15065.definition: Any condition that results in reduced growth of an organism or that prevents an organism from realizing its 'genetic potential'.

S06052.title: stress graphitization
S06052.definition: The solid-state transformation of non-graphitic carbon into graphite by heat treatment combined with application of mechanical stress, resulting in a defined degree of graphitization being obtained at a lower temperature and/or after a shorter time of heat treatment than in the absence of applied stress.

15068.title: stress proteins
15068.definition: Several classes of proteins coded by genes transcriptionally activated by acute stresses, generally serving a protective or adaptive function.

12803.title: stress relaxation
12803.definition: Change in stress with time after the instantaneous application of a constant strain.

15069.title: stress theory of aging
15069.definition: Theory that stress shortens longevity by accelerating energy expenditure. Selection takes place for resistance to stress, and as an epiphenomenon, individuals resistant to stress will predominate in extreme age classes of a population. The diminution of homeostasis under stress with age should be slowest in individuals with highest longevity.

S06051.title: stress-assisted transition
S06051.definition: A transition that takes place when an applied stress assists the transition to the new phase.

15067.title: stress-protein fingerprinting
15067.definition: Proposed use of the patterns of stress-protein induction seen in the field to suggest the particular toxicant inducing the response, after patterns from organisms sampled in the field are compared with those obtained with single-candidate toxicants in the laboratory.

11263.title: stress-response pathway
11263.definition: Signaling events induced when normal cell function or development is disrupted by environmental (physical or chemical) factors.

15066.title: stressor
15066.definition: Any physical, chemical, or biological factor causing an adverse response on any component of an ecosystem.

12097.title: striatum
12097.definition: Subcortical structure of striations of gray matter and white matter in the forebrain that serves as the major input to the basal ganglia, specifically the caudate nucleus, the putamen and the striated structure linking them.

S06054.title: stripping
S06054.definition: The process of removing solute(s) from a loaded solvent or extract. Generally this refers to the main solute(s) present.

10292.title: stripping phase
10292.definition: Extraction phase in a membrane separation.

S06057.title: stripping reaction
S06057.definition: A chemical process, studied in a molecular beam, in which the reaction products are scattered forward with respect to the moving centre of mass of the system.

S06058.title: stripping solution
S06058.definition: A solution (usually aqueous, sometimes water alone) used for back-extracting the distribuend from the extract (usually organic).

09155.title: stripping voltammetry
09155.definition: Two-step electrochemical measurement in which 1) material is accumulated at an electrode and 2) the amount of an accumulated species is measured by voltammetry. The measured electric current in step 2 is related to the concentration of analyte in the solution by calibration.

12098.title: stroke
12098.definition: Acute impairment of circulation to a part of the brain, lasting more than \(\pu{24 h}\).

11264.title: stromal cell
11264.definition: Cell producing the connective tissue framework of an organ or other anatomical structure.

S06059.title: strong collision
S06059.definition: A collision between two molecules in which the amount of energy transferred from one to the other is large compared with \(k_{\rm{B}}\ T\), where \(k_{\rm{B}}\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(T\) the absolute temperature.

12804.title: strong glass
12804.definition: Glass characterised by a small value of the fragility index (\(m\)).

12729.title: structural alert
12729.definition: Chemical features present in a hit or lead molecule indicative of potential toxicity.

S06060.title: structural disorder
S06060.definition: Any deviation from the ideal three-dimensional regularity of the crystal structure.

15070.title: structural diversity
15070.definition: Range of types of physical structure in a community that may provide habitats for species.

S06061.title: structural formula
S06061.definition: A formula which gives information about the way the atoms in a molecule are connected and arranged in space.

11519.title: structural keys
11519.definition:
A pre-established set of substructures the presence or absence of which are used to describe a molecule and are used during substructure searching as a filter
 to eliminate molecules that cannot match a query, for clustering or similarity searching, or for developing classification or regression models.

09862.title: structural lipids
09862.definition: Lipids (mainly glycerophospholipids, sterols and sphingolipids) involved in the formation of biological membranes.

09783.title: structural proteomics
09783.definition: Field in proteomics which focuses on higher orders of the protein structure, mainly tertiary or quaternary.

ST07109.title: structural stability
ST07109.definition: Within the Born–Oppenheimer (adiabatic) approximation, this is associated with an energy minimum on a potential energy surface. Structural stability implies that any change in the coordinates of the nuclei can only increase the total energy.

S06062.title: structural transition
S06062.definition: A reversible or irreversible transition that involves a change of the crystal structure. Example: The transition of $\ce{NH4Cl}$ at $\pu{469 K}$ from a $\ce{CsCl}$-type structure to a $\ce{NaCl}$-type structure.

11520.title: structure diagram
11520.definition: A 2D drawing that shows the atoms of a molecular structure and the bonds that connect them.

S06063.title: structure
S06063.definition: The distribution in space of the atoms or ions in the material part of the catalyst and, in particular, the distribution at the surface.

ST06981.title: structure-based design
ST06981.definition: Structure-based design is a design strategy for new chemical entities based on the three-dimensional (3D) structure of the target obtained by X-ray or nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) studies, or from protein homology models.

11509.title: structure-data format file
11509.definition:
A computer text file that follows a specified format in which each molecule is described by 2D or 3D coordinates, atom type, and connectivity to other atoms
 and also specific user-definable fields that contain other information such as name and biological or chemical properties.

15071.title: structure–metabolism relationship
15071.definition: Association between the physicochemical and (or) the structural properties of a substance and its metabolic behavior.

ST06982.title: structure-property correlations
ST06982.definition: Structure-property correlations (SPC) refer to all statistical mathematical methods used to correlate any molecular property (intrinsic, chemical or biological) to any other property, using statistical regression or pattern recognition techniques.

ST06845.title: structure–activity relationship
ST06845.definition: Association between specific aspects of molecular structure and defined biological action.

12099.title: stupor
12099.definition: State of impaired consciousness showing diminution in response to environmental stimulation.

15072.title: Sturm test
15072.definition: Biodegradation test based on the measurement of \(\ce{CO2}\) production.

15073.title: stygobiont
15073.definition: Organism that lives only in groundwater.

15074.title: stygophile
15074.definition: Organism that lives in groundwater and in surface water.

S06064.title: styphnates
S06064.definition: Salts or charge-transfer complexes of styphnic acid (2,4,6-trinitrobenzene-1,3-diol).

15261.title: styrene polymer
15261.definition: Polymer prepared from styrene, or a substituted styrene, or both in admixture.

09357.title: sub-shell photoionization cross section
09357.definition: Cross section for an incident photon interacting with a material to produce one or more photoelectrons from a given sub-shell.

13698.title: subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
13698.definition: Chronic remitting form of dermatitis characterized by severe photosensitivity and Ro/SS-A and La/SS-B autoantibodies.

12101.title: subarachnoid hemorrhage
12101.definition: Loss of blood into the space between the arachnoid membrane and the pia mater.

S06065.title: subchain
S06065.definition: An arbitrarily chosen contiguous sequence of constitutional units in a chain.

16105.title: subchronic
16105.definition: Repeated over a short period, usually about \(\pu{10\%}\) of the life span; an imprecise term used to describe exposures of intermediate duration.

16106.title: subchronic effect
16106.definition: Biological change resulting from an environmental alteration lasting about \(\pu{10\%}\) of the lifetime of the test organism.

16107.title: subchronic toxicity test
16107.definition: Animal experiment serving to study the effects produced by the test substance when administered in repeated doses (or continually in food, drinking water, air) over a period of up to about 90 days.

16108.title: subclinical effect
16108.definition: Biological change with detectable symptoms following exposure to an agent known to cause disease either before symptoms of the disease occur or when they are absent.

15075.title: subcooled
15075.definition: Term applied to a substance that is a liquid at a temperature lower than the saturation temperature for the existing pressure.

15076.title: subcooled liquid vapour pressure
15076.definition: Vapor pressure of a subcooled liquid.

12102.title: subdural
12102.definition: Between the dura mater and the arachnoid membrane.

16109.title: subfertility
16109.definition: Fertility below the normal range for a given species.

S06066.title: subgroup-supergroup transition
S06066.definition: A transition in which the space-group symmetry of the lower symmetry phase is a subgroup of that of the higher symmetry phase. Example: The transition of the low-temperature polymorph of quartz characterized by space-group symmetry \(P3_{1}2\) (trigonal), to the high temperature polymorph of quartz with space-group symmetry, \(P6_{2}22\) (hexagonal). Synonymous with 'symmetry-breaking transition' (note: this term, strictly speaking, is no longer in use).

S06067.title: subjacent orbital
S06067.definition: The Next-to-Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital ('NHOMO', also called 'HOMO') and the Second Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (SLUMO). Subjacent orbitals are sometimes found to play an important role in the interpretation of molecular interactions according to the frontier orbital approach.

16110.title: subjective environment
16110.definition: Surrounding conditions as perceived by persons living in these conditions.

S06068.title: sublation
S06068.definition: A flotation process in which the material of interest, adsorbed on the surface of gas bubbles in a liquid, is collected on an upper layer of immiscible liquid. There is no liquid-phase mixing in the bulk of the system; as a result recoveries can approach 100%.

14195.title: sublibrary
14195.definition: Portion of a library that is grouped or selected based on similarity of structure or biological effect.

S06069.title: sublimation
S06069.definition: The direct transition of a solid to a vapour without passing through a liquid phase. Example: The transition of solid $\ce{CO2}$ to $\ce{CO2}$ vapour.

15237.title: sublingual tablets
15237.definition: Usually small, flat, and soft tablets, which are designed to be placed under the tongue to allow direct absorption of the active ingredient through the mucosa for systemic effect.

S06071.title: subsample
S06071.definition: A subsample may be: (a) a portion of the sample obtained by selection or division; (b) an individual unit of the lot taken as part of the sample; (c) the final unit of multistage sampling. The term 'subsample' is used either in the sense of a 'sample of a sample' or as a synonym for 'unit'. In practice, the meaning is usually apparent from the context or is defined.

S06073.title: substance content
S06073.definition: Amount-of-substance of a component divided by the mass of the system.

S06074.title: substance flow rate
S06074.definition: Amount-of-substance of a component crossing a surface divided by the time. For clinical chemistry the term component is recommended. ISO uses 'substance'.

S06075.title: substance fraction
S06075.definition: Ratio of the amount-of-substance of the component to the total amount-of-substance in the system containing the component.

12103.title: substantia nigra
12103.definition: Component of the basal ganglia involved in production of the neurotransmitterdopamine.

S06076.title: substituent atom
S06076.definition: An atom (group) that replaces one or more hydrogen atoms attached to a parent structure or characteristic group except for hydrogen atoms attached to a chalcogen atom.

08972.title: substitution chain transfer
08972.definition: Chain-transfer process that proceeds by a one-step substitution reaction.

S06078.title: substitution reaction
S06078.definition: A reaction, elementary or stepwise, in which one atom or group in a molecular entity is replaced by another atom or group. For example,

S06079.title: substitutive name
S06079.definition: A name which indicates the exchange of one or more hydrogen atoms attached to a skeletal atom of a parent structure or to an atom of a characteristic group for another atom or group, which may be expressed by a suffix or by prefixes.

S06080.title: substoichiometric extraction
S06080.definition: Solvent extraction in which the amount of reagent used is lower than that dictated by stoichiometry. If the constants of formation and extraction of the complexes are high, the amount of extracted metal is dictated by the amount of extractant introduced.

S06081.title: substoichiometric isotope dilution analysis
S06081.definition: A kind of isotope dilution analysis in which the final isotopic abundance is estimated from the amount of the nuclide present in a known quantity of the relevant element separated from the test portion, where this quantity is smaller than the total amount of that element present in the test portion.

S06082.title: substrate
S06082.definition: A chemical species, the reaction of which with some other chemical reagent is under observation (e.g. a compound that is transformed under the influence of a catalyst). The term should be used with care. Either the context or a specific statement should always make it clear which chemical species in a reaction is regarded as the substrate.

S06083.title: substrate
S06083.definition: The chemical entity whose conversion to a product or products is catalysed by one or several enzymes.A solution or dry mixture containing all ingredients which are necessary for the growth of a microbial culture or for product formation.Component in the nutrient medium, supplying the organisms with carbon (C-substrate), nitrogen (N-substrate), etc.

S06084.title: substrate
S06084.definition: The terms substrate and subphase refer to a condensed phase that physically supports a film or layer. The term substrate should be used with care in the light of the existing double meaning of the term substrate in film science and technology, on the one hand, and in biochemistry, on the other. The term subphase applies, mainly, to a liquid phase underlying an adsorption layer or a floating spread monolayer.

11521.title: substructure searching
11521.definition:
A virtual screening method that uses a graph-based method to discover which molecules in a chemical structure database contain the substructure specified in
 the query.

11265.title: subthalamus
11265.definition: Part of the diencephalon, of which the major part is the subthalamic nucleus, and which connects to the globus pallidus, part of the telencephalon.

S06085.title: subtractive name
S06085.definition: A name for a modified parent structure in which prefixes and/or suffixes indicate the removal of atoms or groups and, where required, replacement by an appropriate number of hydrogen atoms.

09017.title: subunit
09017.definition: Largest main-chain (backbone) segment of the constitutional repeating unit (CRU) that can be named a single unit under organic nomenclature rules. This may be a ring or a ring system, a heteroatom or a heteroatom chain, or an acyclic carbon chain.

15077.title: succession
15077.definition: Orderly sequential progression of changes in community composition that occurs during development of new populations in any area, from initial colonization to the attainment of the climax typical of a particular geographic area.

S06086.title: successor complex
S06086.definition: The radical ion pair which forms by the transfer of an electron from the donor D to the acceptor A after these species have diffused together to form the precursor or encounter complex: \[\rm{A}+\rm{D}\rightarrow (\rm{A D})\rightarrow (\rm{A}^{\cdot - }\rm{D}^{\cdot +})\]

ST07110.title: sudden polarization
ST07110.definition: The occurrence of a large intramolecular charge separation in the singlet excited state of polyenes and their derivatives twisted about a double bond. Non-symmetrical substitution or geometrical distortion is effective in polarizing the system. An example is the stabilization of the zwitterionic structure of 90° twisted ethene with one methylene group pyramidalized:

16111.title: sufficient evidence
16111.definition: According to the USEPA’s Guidelines for Carcinogen Risk Assessment, sufficient evidence is a collection of facts and scientific references that is definite enough to establish that an adverse effect is caused by the agent in question.

09834.title: sugar
09834.definition: Term frequently applied to monosaccharides and lower oligosaccharides.

S06088.title: sugars
S06088.definition: A loose term applied to monosaccharides and lower oligosaccharides.

16112.title: suggested no-adverse-response level
16112.definition: Maximum dose or concentration that on current understanding is likely to be tolerated by an exposed organism without producing any harm.

16113.title: suicide reaction
16113.definition: Formation of irreversible cleavage complexes (also referred to as 'suicide complexes') leading to cell death.

11266.title: sulcus
11266.definition: Any long, narrow groove, furrow or shallow depression, specifically referring to one of the fissures on the surface of the brain.

S06091.title: sulfamic acids
S06091.definition: $\ce{H2NS(=O)2OH}$ (sulfamic acid) and its N-hydrocarbyl derivatives. Sulfamic acid is called sulfamidic acid in inorganic chemistry.

S06092.title: sulfanes
S06092.definition: A term including hydropolysulfides, polysulfanes, polysulfides. Use is discouraged because of confusion with the newer systematic name sulfane, $\ce{H2S}$, and the numerous names derived therefrom.

S06093.title: sulfatides
S06093.definition: Hydrogen sulfate esters of glycosphingolipids. Specific compounds should be named as glycerosphingolipid derivatives, e.g.

S06094.title: sulfenamides
S06094.definition: Compounds derived from sulfenic acids, $\ce{RSOH}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$), by replacement of $\ce{–OH}$ by $\ce{–NR2}$. May alternatively be considered as alkylsulfanylamines, e.g. $\ce{C2H5SNH2}$ ethanesulfenamide or ethylsulfanylamine.

S06096.title: sulfenic acids
S06096.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RSOH}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$), e.g. $\ce{PhSOH}$ benzenesulfenic acid.

S06097.title: sulfenium ions
S06097.definition: A term sometimes erroneously used for sulfenylium ions.

S06098.title: sulfenyl groups
S06098.definition: Groups having the structure $\ce{RS–}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$). This term is derived from sulfenic acids. The synonymous term sulfanyl groups is derived from sulfane, $\ce{H2S}$. E.g. $\ce{CH3–S–}$ methanesulfenyl, methylthio or methylsulfanyl.

S06101.title: sulfenyl radicals
S06101.definition: Sulfur-centered radicals having the structure $\ce{RS^{.}}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$). This term is derived from sulfenic acids. The synonymous term sulfanyl radicals is derived from sulfane, $\ce{H2S}$. E.g. $\ce{CH3S^{.}}$ methylsulfanyl or methanesulfenyl radical. An older synonymous term is alkylthio radical.

S06099.title: sulfenylium ions
S06099.definition: Cations having the structure $\ce{RS^{+}}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$). This term is derived from sulfenic acids. The synonymous term sulfanylium ions is derived from sulfane, $\ce{H2S}$. E.g. $\ce{CH3S^{+}}$ methylsulfanylium or methanesulfenylium ion.

S06102.title: sulfides
S06102.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RSR}$ ($\ce{R \neq H}$). Such compounds were once called thioethers.See also: thioacetalsIn an inorganic sense, salts or other derivatives of hydrogen sulfide.A term used in additive nomenclature, see imides (2).

S06104.title: sulfimides
S06104.definition: $\ce{H2S=NH}$, sulfimide, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives. They are thus related to sulfoxides in the same way that imines are related to aldehydes or ketones, e.g. $\ce{(C2H5)2S=NPh}$ S,S-diethyl-N-phenylsulfimide.A term used in Chemical Abstracts Service Index Nomenclature for sulfonylamines, $\ce{RN=S(=O)2}$.

S06106.title: sulfinamides
S06106.definition: Amides of sulfinic acids, $\ce{RS(=O)OH}$; thus $\ce{RS(=O)NR2}$, e.g. $\ce{PhS(=O)NHCH3}$ N-methylbenzenesulfinamide.

S06107.title: sulfinamidines
S06107.definition: Amidines of sulfinic acids, $\ce{RS(=O)OH}$; thus $\ce{RS(=NR)NR}$, e.g. $\ce{PhS(=NH)NH2}$ benzenesulfinamidine.

S06109.title: sulfinic acids
S06109.definition: $\ce{HS(=O)OH}$, sulfinic acid, and its S-hydrocarbyl derivatives, e.g. $\ce{(CH3)2CHS(=O)OH}$ propane-2-sulfinic acid.

S06112.title: sulfinylamines
S06112.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RN=S=O}$. Formerly called thionylamines.

S06114.title: sulfonamides
S06114.definition: Amides of sulfonic acids $\ce{RS(=O)2NR'2}$, e.g. $\ce{PhS(=O)2NHCH3}$ N-methylbenzenesulfonamide.

S06115.title: sulfonamidines
S06115.definition: A term abandoned because of its ambiguous use to mean either $\ce{RS(=O)=NH2}$ (sulfonimidamide) or $\ce{RS(=NH)2=NH2}$ (sulfonodiimidamide).

S06116.title: sulfonediimines
S06116.definition: Compounds having the structure, $\ce{RS(=NR)2R}$, formally derived from sulfones by replacing $\ce{(=O)2}$ by $\ce{(=NR)2}$, e.g. $\ce{Ph2S(=NH)2}$ diphenyl sulfonediimine.

S06117.title: sulfones
S06117.definition: Compounds having the structure, $\ce{RS(=O)2R}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$), e.g. $\ce{C2H5S(=O)2CH3}$ ethyl methyl sulfone.

S06118.title: sulfonic acids
S06118.definition: $\ce{HS(=O)2OH}$, sulfonic acid, and its S-hydrocarbyl derivatives.

S06119.title: sulfonic anhydrides
S06119.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RS(=O)2OS(=O)2R'}$, e.g. $\ce{PhS(=O)2OS(=O)2Ph}$ benzenesulfonic anhydride.

S06121.title: sulfonium compounds
S06121.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R3S+}$ and associated anion (generally, but not necessarily, all three $\ce{R}$ groups are hydrocarbyl). E.g. $\ce{[(CH3)3S]^{+}Cl^{−}}$, trimethylsulfonium chloride, or

S06122.title: sulfonphthaleins
S06122.definition: 3,3-Bis(hydroxyaryl)-3H-2,1-benzoxathiole S,S-dioxides, formed by condensation of o-sulfobenzoic acid with phenols or related compounds, e.g.

S06123.title: sulfonylamines
S06123.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RN=S(=O)2}$. (Indexed by Chemical Abstracts Service at the heading sulfimide). E.g. $\ce{CH3N=S(=O)2}$ N-sulfonylmethylamine.

S06124.title: sulfoxides
S06124.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R2S=O}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$), e.g. $\ce{Ph2S=O}$ diphenyl sulfoxide.

S06125.title: sulfoximides
S06125.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R2S(=O)=NR}$. (Indexed by Chemical Abstracts Service at the heading sulfoximines). E.g. $\ce{(CH3)2S(=O)=NPh}$ S,S-dimethyl-N-phenylsulfoximide.

S06127.title: sulfur diimides
S06127.definition: The parent compound $\ce{HN=S=NH}$ and hydrocarbyl derivatives.

S06128.title: sultams
S06128.definition: Sulfonamides in which the S-N bond is part of a ring.

S06129.title: sultims
S06129.definition: Tautomeric forms of sultams, having a sulfur–nitrogen double bond as part of a ring.

S06130.title: sultines
S06130.definition: Intramolecular cyclic esters of hydroxy sulfinic acids. (Named by supposed analogy with lactones and sultones; but the -ine ending is unfortunate).

S06131.title: sultones
S06131.definition: Intramolecular cyclic esters of hydroxy sulfonic acids, analogous to lactones.

08684.title: sum band
08684.definition: Band resulting from a sum transition.

09205.title: sum frequency generation spectroscopy
09205.definition: Measurement method from non-linear optics in which a structurally-ordered sample at an interface between two phases is irradiated by single frequency visible and variable frequency infrared pulses of light to generate a sum frequency vibrational spectrum of the interfacial species without any bulk phase contribution.

S06134.title: sum of states
S06134.definition: The total number of states for a system corresponding to an energy \(\varepsilon\) less than or equal to a specified value.

08685.title: sum transition
08685.definition: Combination transition between the ground state and a state in which more than one vibration is excited; i.e., a transition from the ground state in which more than one quantum number increases.

08686.title: sum-frequency spectroscopy
08686.definition: Nonlinear optical technique in which pulsed lasers at frequencies \(\omega_{1}\) and \(\omega_{2}\) are overlapped at a surface and light emitted at the sum of the two frequencies, \(\omega_{1} + \omega_{2}\), is detected. One laser is normally in the mid-infrared and the other in the visible or near-infrared.

16114.title: summary sheet
16114.definition: Two-to-four page summary of a risk assessment.

16115.title: summation
16115.definition: Process of addition of separate postsynaptic responses caused by stimuli that are adjacent in time and space.

S06132.title: summit current
S06132.definition: In ac polarography, differential pulse polarography, derivative polarography, square-wave polarography, and similar techniques, the maximum value of the component of the current that is associated with the presence of a substance B. Normally this component of the current is faradaic, and the maximum arises because the rate of variation (with applied potential) of the rate of the charge-transfer process passes through a maximum. Similar maxima arise when this component is non-faradaic (and when B is surface-active rather than electroactive). In a case known to be of the latter type, the term apex current is recommended as being more specific.

S06133.title: summit potential
S06133.definition: In ac polarography, differential pulse polarography, derivative polarography, and similar techniques, the potential of the indicator electrode at which the summit current is attained.

ST07195.title: superabsorbent polymer
ST07195.definition: Polymer that can absorb and retain extremely large amounts of a liquid relative to its own mass.

S06135.title: superacid
S06135.definition: A medium having a high acidity, generally greater than that of 100 wt.% sulfuric acid. The common superacids are made by dissolving a powerful Lewis acid (e.g. $\ce{SbF5}$) in a suitable Brønsted acid such as $\ce{HF}$ or $\ce{HSO3F}$. (An equimolar mixture of $\ce{HSO3F}$ and $\ce{SbF5}$ is known by the trade name 'magic acid'.) In a biochemical context 'superacid catalysis' is sometimes used to denote catalysis by metal ions analogous to catalysis by hydrogen ions. By analogy, a compound having a very high basicity, such as lithium diisopropylamide, is called a 'superbase'.

13699.title: superantigen
13699.definition: Antigen which reacts with all the T cells belonging to a particular T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V) region family, and which therefore stimulates (or deletes) a much larger number of cells than does conventional antigen.

S06137.title: superconducting transition
S06137.definition: A transition at the critical temperature, \(T_{\rm{c}}\), below which the resistance of electrical conductors becomes zero and magnetic flux is excluded.

15078.title: supercooled
15078.definition: Term describing a substance that persists as a liquid at a temperature below its freezing point without solidification or crystallization.

12805.title: supercooled polymer melt
12805.definition: Metastable melt of a crystallisable polymer at temperatures below its equilibrium melting temperature.

ST07636.title: supercritical drying of a gel
ST07636.definition: Drying of a gel using a supercritical fluid.

S06138.title: supercritical fluid
S06138.definition: The defined state of a compound, mixture or element above its critical pressure (\(p_{\rm{c}}\)) and critical temperature (\(T_{\rm{c}}\)).

S06139.title: supercritical fluid chromatography
S06139.definition: A separation technique in which the mobile phase is a fluid above and relatively close to its critical temperature and pressure. In general the terms and definitions used in gas or liquid chromatography are equally applicable to supercritical fluid chromatography.

10229.title: supercritical fluid extraction
10229.definition: Use of a supercritical fluid to extract analytes from a solid or supported liquid sample.

S06140.title: superequivalent adsorption
S06140.definition: This occurs when the specifically adsorbed amount of charge in the inner Helmholtz plane is higher than the charge on the metal phase, taken with the reverse sign.

S06141.title: superexchange interaction
S06141.definition: Electronic interaction between two molecular entities mediated by one or more different molecules or ions.

13700.title: superfamily
13700.definition: Large group of proteins related by structural homology and function. The term also refers to the genes that encode them.

11267.title: superfecundation
11267.definition: Fertilization of two or more ova released in the same period of ovulation, either by different males or by the same male in separate acts of intercourse.

11268.title: superfetation
11268.definition: Presence of two fetuses in the uterus at different stages of development, resulting from fertilization of ova released in two successive periods of ovulation.

S06142.title: superficial work
S06142.definition: The reversible work of formation of unit area of new surface by cleavage. It has previously been called specific surface work, surface energy, surface tension or surface free energy. The symbol recommended is \(\gamma _{\pi }\) in preference to \(\sigma \) because of the confusion with surface charge density. The superficial work \(\gamma _{\pi }\) is a scalar quantity and consequently is isotropic.

16116.title: Superfund
16116.definition: Federal authority, established by the U.S. Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in 1980, to respond directly to releases or threatened releases (such as from landfills or waste disposal areas) of hazardous substances that may endanger health or welfare.

S06143.title: superlattice
S06143.definition: A periodic multilayer which is synthetic and where a unit cell, consisting of successive layers that are chemically different from their adjacent neighbours, is repeated. The term quantum well multilayer applies to the superlattices with artificially created electronic band structures.

11269.title: supernumerary
11269.definition: Exceeding the usual number; thus, in anatomy, anomalies such as a sixth finger on one hand or a third nipple (in a human).

16117.title: superoxide dismutase
16117.definition: Enzymatic antioxidant that removes the potentially toxic superoxide ion (\(\ce{O2^{-}}\)) by disproportionating it to \(\ce{O2}\) and hydrogen peroxide (\(\ce{H2O2}\)).

S06144.title: superposability
S06144.definition: The ability to bring two particular stereochemical formulae (or models) into coincidence (or to be exactly superposable in space, and for the corresponding molecular entities or objects to become exact replicas of each other) by no more than translation and rigid rotation.

S06145.title: superradiance
S06145.definition: Spontaneous emission amplified by a single pass through a population inverted medium. It is distinguished from true laser action by its lack of coherence. The term superradiance is frequently used in laser technology.

12730.title: supersaturated solution
12730.definition: Solution that has a greater composition of a solute than one that is in equilibrium with undissolved solute at specified values of temperature and pressure.

S06146.title: supersaturation
S06146.definition: In chemistry, an unstable system which has a greater concentration of a material in solution than would exist at equilibrium is said to be supersaturated.In meteorology, supersaturation of an air mass with respect to $\ce{H2O}$ vapour is of special interest. It is the saturation ratio minus one, or the percent supersaturation is the percent relative humidity minus 100.

10144.title: supervised classification
10144.definition: Classification in which, in a first step, a model is built using data from objects of known classes, and in a second step, the model is applied to new data to assign a class to unknown objects.

11522.title: supervised learning
11522.definition:
A machine learning method that aims to discover a relationship between the predictor and the response values, such as exists in a QSAR or recursive
 partitioning model.

S06147.title: support
S06147.definition: In multiphase catalysts, the active catalytic material is often present as the minor component dispersed upon a support sometimes called a carrier. The support may be catalytically inert but it may contribute to the overall catalytic activity.

S06150.title: support plate
S06150.definition: The plate that supports the thin layer in thin-layer chromatography.

S06148.title: support-coated open-tubular column
S06148.definition: A version of a porous-layer open-tabular (PLOT) column in which the porous layer consists of support particles and was deposited from a suspension.

S06149.title: supporting electrolyte
S06149.definition: An electrolyte solution, whose constituents are not electroactive in the range of applied potentials being studied, and whose ionic strength (and, therefore, contribution to the conductivity) is usually much larger than the concentration of an electroactive substance to be dissolved in it.

15238.title: suppositories
15238.definition: Dosage form, semi-solid, used for the administration of drugs via the rectal route, for systemic or local effect. When application is via other routes (e.g., the vaginal route), suppositories are termed differently, inserts, pessaries, etc.

13701.title: suppression
13701.definition: Dominant immunological tolerance, a phenomenon that plays an active role in regulating T-cell and B-cell responses to both foreign antigens and autoantigens.

S06151.title: suppressor
S06151.definition: A substance which reduces emission, absorption, or light scattering by an interferent, thus removing or lowering spectral interference.

13702.title: suppressor cell
13702.definition: T cell that suppresses the immune response of B cells and other T cells to an antigen. In more current usage classified as a regulatory T cell.

13703.title: supramolecular adhesion complex
13703.definition: Collection of molecules forming at the contact point of a T cell and an antigen-presenting cell (APC), enriched in T-cell receptor (TCR), adhesion molecules, and signaling molecules.

09576.title: supramolecular assembly
09576.definition: Molecular system comprising two or more self-assembled molecular, or molecular and ionic, entities held together by means of non-covalent intermolecular binding interactions.

13867.title: supramolecular association
13867.definition: Self-assembly involving reversible, noncovalent, directional interactions of molecules that result in a high-molecular-mass entity.

ST07111.title: supramolecular chemistry
ST07111.definition: A field of chemistry related to species of greater complexity than molecules, that are held together and organized by means of intermolecular interactions. The objects of supramolecular chemistry are supermolecules and other polymolecular entities that result from the spontaneous association of a large number of components into a specific phase (membranes, vesicles, micelles, solid state structures etc.)

S06153.title: supramolecule
S06153.definition: A system of two or more molecular entities held together and organized by means of intermolecular (noncovalent) binding interactions.

12104.title: supratentorial
12104.definition: Intracranial contents located above the tentorium of the cerebellum, notably the white matter of the cerebrum, often describing functional symptoms of diseases of the white matter that lead to physical and mental disability.

12105.title: supratentorial herniation
12105.definition: Abnormal protrusion of brain structures into compartments above the tentorium, or over the edge of the tentorium, due to increased intracranial pressure.

S06154.title: surface
S06154.definition: The boundary between two phases. It is recommended that for the purpose of surface analysis a distinction be made between 'surface' in general, 'physical surface' and 'experimental surface': Surface — The 'outer portion' of a sample of undefined depth; to be used in general discussions of the outside regions of the sample. Physical Surface — That atomic layer of a sample which, if the sample were placed in a vacuum, is the layer 'in contact with' the vacuum; the outermost atomic layer of a sample. Experimental Surface — That portion of the sample with which there is significant interaction with the particles or radiation used for excitation. It is the volume of sample required for analysis or the volume corresponding to the escape for the emitted radiation or particle, whichever is larger.

S06163.title: surface excess conductivity
S06163.definition: The excess conductivity in a surface per unit length and width, symbol \(\kappa ^{\sigma }\).

S06156.title: surface amount
S06156.definition: Amount of substance adsorbed on a surface.

09370.title: surface approximation energy
09370.definition: Simplification of calculations involving the energy of an ion passing through a solid sample, where the energy of the ion at the surface is used in place of a properly averaged energy.

S06157.title: surface barrier semiconductor detector
S06157.definition: A semiconductor detector utilizing a junction due to a surface inversion layer.

S06159.title: surface charge density
S06159.definition: Electric charge on a surface divided by the surface area.

S06161.title: surface chemical potential

S06162.title: surface concentration
S06162.definition: Amount of substance adsorbed on a surface divided by the surface area.

S06164.title: surface contamination
S06164.definition: Material in the experimental surface which is either not characteristic of the sample or which would not be present if the sample had been prepared in an absolute vacuum by methods not contacting other substances to the sample.

09358.title: surface core-level shift
09358.definition: Energy shift observed in core-level photoelectron spectroscopy arising from the reduced coordination of the surface or near-surface atoms compared to bulk atoms.

S06165.title: surface coverage
S06165.definition: Number of adsorbed molecules on a surface divided by the number of molecules in a filled monolayer on that surface.

S06166.title: surface crossing
S06166.definition: In a diagram of electronic energy versus molecular geometry, the electronic energies of two states of different symmetry may be equal at certain geometrical parameters. At this point (unidimensional representation), line or surface (more than one dimension), the two potential-energy surfaces are said to cross one another.

S06169.title: surface dipole layer
S06169.definition: Particles in the surface region of a phase are subjected to orienting forces as a result of the anisotropic force field. Polar molecules (e.g. permanent dipoles) may thus be preferentially oriented in the surface region, while polarizable molecules may be polarized (induced dipoles). The array of oriented polar and/or polarized molecules is called the surface dipole layer with which an electric potential drop is associated, called the surface potential of the phase.

S06170.title: surface electric potential
S06170.definition: Given by \[\chi ^{\beta} = \mathit{\Phi }^{\beta} - \psi ^{\beta}\] where \(\psi ^{\beta }\) and \(\mathit{\Phi} ^{\beta}\) are the outer and inner electric potentials of phase $\ce{\upbeta\!}$, respectively.

09292.title: surface excess amount
09292.definition: For an interface, the difference between the amount of component actually present in the system and that which would be present (in a reference system) if the bulk concentration in the adjoining phases were maintained up to a chosen geometrical dividing surface (Gibbs dividing surface).

S06172.title: surface excess concentration
S06172.definition: A quantity defined by \[\mathit{\Gamma}_{i} = \frac{n_{i}^{\sigma }}{A_{\rm{s}}}\] where \(n_{i}^{\sigma}\) is the surface excess (or adsorption) of component \(i\) and \(A_{\rm{s}}\) is the area of the dividing surface or interface.

S06173.title: surface excess energy
S06173.definition: Defined by: \[U^{\unicode[Times]{x3C3} } = U - U^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }- U^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }= U - V^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }\ \frac{U_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }}{V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }} - V^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\ \frac{U_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }}{V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }}\] where \(V^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }\) and \(V^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\) satisfy the condition \(V^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} } + V^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} } = V\), the total volume of the system. (\(\frac{U_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }}{V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }}\)) and (\(\frac{U_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }}{V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }}\)) are the energy densities in the two bulk phases where \(U_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }\) and \(U_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\) are the mean molar energies and \(V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }\) and \(V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\) are the mean molar volumes of the two phases.

S06174.title: surface excess enthalpy
S06174.definition: Defined by: \[H^{\sigma }=U^{\sigma }- \gamma \ A_{\rm{s}}\] where \(U^{\sigma }\) is the surface excess energy, \(\gamma \) is the surface tension, and \(A_{\rm{s}}\) is the area relative to a Gibbs surface.

S06175.title: surface excess entropy
S06175.definition: Defined by: \[S^{\unicode[Times]{x3C3}} = S - S^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }- S^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }=S- V^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }\ \frac{S_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }}{V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }}- V^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\ \frac{S_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }}{V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }}\] (\(\frac{S_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }}{V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }}\)) and (\(\frac{S_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }}{V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }}\)) are the entropy densities in the two bulk phases, where \(S_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }\) and \(S_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\) are the mean molar entropies and \(V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }\) and \(V_{\rm{m}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\) are the mean molar volumes of the two phases.

S06176.title: surface excess Gibbs energy
S06176.definition: Defined by \[G^{\sigma }=H^{\sigma }- T\ S^{\sigma }=A^{\sigma }- \gamma \ A_{\rm{s}}\] where \(H^{\sigma }\) is the surface excess enthalpy, \(T\) is the thermodynamic temperature, \(S^{\sigma }\) is the surface excess entropy, \(A^{\sigma }\) is the surface excess Helmholtz energy, \(\gamma \) is the surface tension, and \(A_{\rm{s}}\) is the area relative to a Gibbs surface.

S06177.title: surface excess Helmholtz energy
S06177.definition: Defined by: \[A^{\sigma }=U^{\sigma }- T\ S^{\sigma }\] where \(U^{\sigma }\) is the surface excess energy, \(T\) is the thermodynamic temperature, and \(S^{\sigma }\) is the surface excess entropy.

S06178.title: surface excess isotherm
S06178.definition: The function relating, at constant temperature and pressure, \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\left(\rm{n}\right)}\), \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\left(\rm{l}\right)}\) or \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\left(\rm{v}\right)}\), or the respective specific quantities \(\frac{n^{\rm{l}}\ \Delta x_{i}^{\rm{l}}}{m}\), \(\frac{A_{\rm{s}}\ \mathit{\Gamma }_{i}^{\left(\rm{l}\right)}}{m}\) or \(\frac{V^{\rm{l}}\ \Delta c_{i}^{\rm{l}}}{m}\) to the mole fraction (or concentration) of component \(i\) in the equilibrium liquid phase. With solutions of more than two components such isotherms are unequivocal functions only when the ratios of the mole fractions (or concentrations) of all other components except \(i\) are kept constant. (\(A_{\rm{s}}\) is the area of interface, \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\left(\rm{n}\right)}\), \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\left(\rm{l}\right)}\), \(\mathit{\Gamma}_{i}^{\left(\rm{v}\right)}\) are relative adsorptions, \(\Delta x_{i}^{\rm{l}}\) is the change in mole fraction of \(i\) resulting from bringing a specified mass \(m\) of solid into contact with a specified amount of solution \(n^{\rm{l}}\), \(\Delta c_{i}^{\rm{l}}\) is the change in concentration resulting from bringing a specified mass of solid into contact with a specified amount of solution of volume \(V^{\rm{l}}\).)

S06171.title: surface excess
S06171.definition: For an interface, the adsorption or surface excess of a given component is defined as the difference between the amount of component actually present in the system, and that which would be present (in a reference system) if the bulk concentration in the adjoining phases were maintained up to a chosen geometrical dividing surface (Gibbs dividing surface). For a solid/liquid interface in which no component of the liquid phase penetrates into the solid, the surface excess (or adsorption) of component i is defined as: \[n_{i}^{\sigma }=n_{i}- V^{\rm{l}}\ c_{i}^{\rm{l}}\] where \(n_{i}\) is the total amount of i in the system, \(V^{\rm{l}}\) is the volume of an arbitrarily chosen amount of bulk liquid (in the framework of the so-called algebraic method) and \(c_{i}^{\rm{l}}\) is its bulk concentration in the liquid.

09206.title: surface extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy
09206.definition: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy in which, instead of measuring X-ray absorption, electron emission arising from that absorption is measured.

ST07152.title: surface grafting
ST07152.definition: Process in which a polymer surface is chemically modified by grafting or by the generation of active sites that can lead to the initiation of a graft polymerization.

S06179.title: surface ionization
S06179.definition: Takes place when an atom or molecule is ionized when it interacts with a solid surface. ionization occurs only when the work function of the surface, the temperature of the surface, and the ionization energy of the atom or molecule have an appropriate relationship.

S06180.title: surface ions
S06180.definition: Ions that are constituents of the surface or which have a particularly high affinity for the surface or surface sites.

S06181.title: surface layer
S06181.definition: The region of space comprising and adjoining the phase boundary within which the properties of matter are significantly different from the values in the adjoining bulk phases.

09293.title: surface map
09293.definition: Two- or three-dimensional representation of the sample surface where the information at each point in the representation, given by a brightness or colour or as a length in a third dimension, is related to the output signal from a detector or processed intensity information from the available software.

S06182.title: surface of a phase
S06182.definition: The plane ideally marking the boundary between a phase and its environment.

S06183.title: surface of tension
S06183.definition: The mechanical properties of an interfacial layer between two fluid phases may be expressed in terms of those of a geometrical surface of uniform tension called the surface of tension, whose location is dependent on the distribution of the stress tensor within the interfacial layer.

09294.title: surface plasmon
09294.definition: Collective motion of electrons on an interface of two phases which have different permittivity, of which one must have electrical conductivity to sustain the collective motion.

09444.title: surface plasmon resonance
09444.definition: Resonant interaction between the natural frequency of a surface plasmon and incident light of the same frequency.

14196.title: surface plasmon resonance assay
14196.definition: Assay in which the binding of a ligand to a target immobilized on the gold surface of a chip is detected by changes in the angle of the light reflected from the surface.

S06185.title: surface pressure
S06185.definition: The change of interfacial tension caused by addition of a given species to a base solution. When an area of liquid covered with a spread substance is separated from a clean area of surface by a mechanical barrier, the force acting on unit length of the barrier is called the surface pressure, \(\pi \) or \(\pi _{\rm{s}}\), and is equal to \(\gamma ^{0} - \gamma \) where \(\gamma ^{0}\) is the surface tension of the clean surface and \(\gamma \) that of the covered surface.

14098.title: surface recombination
14098.definition: Recombination of charge carriers at a solid surface or at an interface between different phases.

S06187.title: surface region
S06187.definition: The tridimensional region, extending from the free surface of a condensed phase towards the interior, where the properties differ from the bulk. The term surface may also be used in this sense.

12057.title: surface righting test
12057.definition: Test animal is placed on its back and the time to retain an uprate position with four paws in contact with the surface is measured.

09577.title: surface roughness
09577.definition: Measure of the texture of a surface that is quantified by vertical deviations from its ideal location.

09295.title: surface segregation
09295.definition: Partitioning of a species from the bulk of a material to the surface as a result of kinetic or thermodynamic effects.

S06189.title: surface shear viscosity
S06189.definition:
For steady state deformations a surface shear viscosity \(\eta ^{m{s}}\), and an area viscosity or surface dilatational viscosity \(\zeta ^{m{s}}\) can be defined. In a Cartesian system with the x-axis normal to the surface, they are defined by the equations: \[\eta ^{m{s}} =  rac{\sigma _{xy}}{ rac{\partial 
u_{y}}{\partial 
u_{x}}}\] \[\zeta ^{m{s}}= rac{\Delta \gamma }{ rac{\mathrm{d}(\ln A)}{\mathrm{d}t}}\] where \(\sigma _{xy}\) is the shear component of the surface stress tensor, \(
u_{x}\) and \(
u_{y}\) are the \(x\) and \(y\) components of the surface velocity vector, respectively, \(A\) is the surface area, \(t\) is the time, and \(\Delta \gamma \) is the difference between the (steady state) dynamic surface tension and the equilibrium surface tension.

S06190.title: surface states
S06190.definition: Energy levels localized in the surface region of semiconductors, which do not bear any direct relation to the bulk energy distribution, but which can exchange electrons with the bulk. In such a case a space charge may arise even when \(\sigma \) (the free charge density) is zero, i.e. \(\sigma =\sigma _{\mathrm{sc}}+\sigma _{\mathrm{ss}}\), where \(\sigma _{\mathrm{sc}}\) is the space charge density and \(\sigma _{\mathrm{ss}}\) is the charge density associated with the surface states.

S06191.title: surface stress
S06191.definition: The work required to form unit area of new surface by stretching under equilibrium conditions. It is numerically equal to the force acting in the jth direction per unit length of exposed edge, the edge being normal to the ith direction, that must be applied to a terminating surface to keep it in equilibrium, the ith and jth directions lying in the plane of the surface.

S06192.title: surface tension
S06192.definition: Work required to increase a surface area divided by that area. When two phases are studied it is often called interfacial tension.

S06193.title: surface work
S06193.definition: Surface tension is the intensive factor in the differential expression for the work required to increase the area of the surface of tension. Measured under reversible conditions at constant temperature (and normally constant pressure) and referred to unit area, this work, the so-called (differential) surface work, is equal to the static surface tension.

14097.title: surface-active site
14097.definition: Surface regular or defect site that can initiate the chemical transformation of reagents.

09194.title: surface-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry
09194.definition: Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry using a combined liquid and particulate matrix.

14292.title: surface-average particle diameter
14292.definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[\left\langle {d_{\rm{s}}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{s}} = \frac{\Sigma {N_{i}} {d_{i}^{3}}}{\Sigma {N_{i}} {d_{i}^{2}}}\]

10260.title: surface-bound macrocyclic sorbent
10260.definition: Porous sorbent with surface-bound macrocyclic ligands designed for the extraction of metal ions and some anions from aqueous solution.

10261.title: surface-bound phenylboronic acid sorbent
10261.definition: Porous sorbent with surface-bound phenylboronic acid groups for the selective extraction of bifunctional compounds by reversible formation of 5- or 6-membered covalent cyclic boronic acid complexes.

08687.title: surface-enhanced hyper-Raman spectroscopy
08687.definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy by which the Raman spectrum is significantly enhanced simultaneously by both the hyper-Raman (see hyper-Raman spectroscopy) and surface-enhanced Raman (see surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy) effects.

08688.title: surface-enhanced infrared absorption
08688.definition: Measurement method of infrared spectroscopy by which the intensity of absorption bands of molecules within a few nanometers of the surface of metal particles is increased by interactions with surface plasmons (the collective resonance of electrons near the surface of metal islands).

09207.title: surface-enhanced infrared spectroscopy
09207.definition: Measurement method giving enhanced infrared absorption in the measured infrared spectrum of a sample adsorbed on a roughened thin metal substrate. The metal substrate is deposited onto a prism and data is collected by total internal reflection.

08689.title: surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy
08689.definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy by which the intensity of vibrational bands in the Raman spectra of molecules within a few nanometers of the surface of microscopically rough metals, metal colloids and metal nanoparticles is increased by several orders of magnitude.

08690.title: surface-enhanced resonance Raman spectroscopy
08690.definition: Measurement method of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) by which the Raman spectrum is significantly enhanced when the conditions occur that whilst undergoing SERS the molecules are excited by radiation that is in resonance with electronic transitions in the sample.

09209.title: surface-enhanced resonant Raman spectroscopy
09209.definition: Measurement method of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) by which the Raman spectrum is significantly enhanced under the conditions that, whilst undergoing SERS, the molecules are excited by radiation that is in resonance with electronic transitions in the sample.

08691.title: surface-enhanced, spatially offset Raman spectroscopy
08691.definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy that combines spatially offset Raman spectroscopy and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) enabling the detection of a SERS signal deep within diffusely scattering samples.

S06194.title: surfactant
S06194.definition: A substance which lowers the surface tension of the medium in which it is dissolved, and/or the interfacial tension with other phases, and, accordingly, is positively adsorbed at the liquid/vapour and/or at other interfaces.

14377.title: surfmer
14377.definition: Monomer with the properties of a surfactant.

S06196.title: surprisal analysis
S06196.definition: The study of product state distributions in terms of surprisal has been referred to as surprisal analysis.

S06195.title: surprisal
S06195.definition: A function relating the prior distribution \(P_{0}\) of product states to an observed or calculated product distribution P. It is defined by: \[s=- \ln (\frac{P}{P_{0}})\]

16118.title: surrogate
16118.definition: Relatively well studied toxicant whose properties are assumed to apply to an entire chemically and toxicologically related class.

13704.title: surrogate light chain
13704.definition: Light chain-like structure formed when the proteins encoded by the \({\rm{V}}_{\rm{preB}}\) and \(\uplambda_{5}\) genes associate with each other. It can form immunoglobulin (Ig)-like complexes which are expressed on the surface of pre-B cells at different stages of development.

15079.title: surrogate organism
15079.definition: Test organism, or population that is cultured under laboratory conditions to serve as a substitute in toxicity testing for indigenous organisms, communities, or populations.

15080.title: surrogate toxicant
15080.definition: Relatively well-studied substance whose properties are assumed to apply to an entire chemically and toxicologically related class.

15081.title: surveillance
15081.definition: Systematic ongoing collection, collation, and analysis of data and the timely dissemination of information to those who need to know in order that action can be taken to initiate investigative or control measures.

15082.title: survival time
15082.definition: Time interval between initial exposure of an organism to a harmful substance and death.

15083.title: survivorship
15083.definition: Proportion of animals surviving between two specified ages.

15084.title: survivorship curve
15084.definition: Graph showing how survivorship from birth varies with age.

15085.title: susceptibility
15085.definition: Condition of an organism or ecological system that makes it more vulnerable to a given exposure than the majority of the population or group of ecological systems to which it belongs.

16119.title: susceptible
16119.definition: Describing a group of organisms more vulnerable to a given exposure than the majority of the population to which they belong.

S06197.title: suspended matter
S06197.definition: All particulate material which persists in the atmosphere or in a flue gas stream for lengthy periods because the particles are too small in size to have an appreciable falling velocity.

S06198.title: suspension
S06198.definition: A liquid in which solid particles are dispersed.

16246.title: suspension pH
16246.definition: Readings on a pH-meter scale obtained for a suspension of soil (in water or electrolyte) by any method for potentiometric pH measurement, performed in a manner analogous to the pH measurement in solutions.

S06199.title: suspension effect
S06199.definition: An effect which occurs when ion-selective electrodes are used in concentrated, space-filled suspensions while the external reference electrode remains in the supernatant (suspension-free) solution. The suspensions are specifically solvent-swollen ion exchangers or other materials, like soils and clays, that concentrate ions by adsorption and absorption. Space-filled, gravity-packed suspensions act like a second phase and form apparently an interfacial potential difference (PD) with respect to the supernatant. The measured ion activity in the suspension differs from the value in the supernatant by the interfacial PD, and corresponds to a higher value approximating the activity inside the ion exchanger gel. The effect nearly disappears when the outer reference electrode is placed in the same region of the suspension as the sensor electrode. There are some changes in the junction potential differences of the reference electrode, between suspension and supernatant.

15086.title: suspension feeder
15086.definition: Animal that feeds by straining suspended matter and food particles from water, typically by passing the water over a specialized structure, such as the baleen of baleen whales.

16242.title: suspension of solid charged particles
16242.definition: Dispersion of solid electrically charged particles, commonly larger in size range than colloidal particles (of approximate diameter range \(\pu{{1}{-}{1000} nm}\)) (dispersed phase), in water or an aqueous solution (continuous, liquid phase).

14354.title: suspension polymerisation
14354.definition: Polymerization in which polymer is formed in monomer, or monomer-solvent droplets in a continuous phase that is a nonsolvent for both the monomer and the formed polymer.

16243.title: suspension potentiometric cell
16243.definition: Galvanic cell containing, as its essential component, a uniform or combined suspension or one of its separated parts alone, the eqs or sediment.

15239.title: sustained release
15239.definition: Dosage form designed to release the drug contained therein at a continuous and controlled rate for a longer period of time that can normally be achieved with its conventional, nonsustained counterpart.

S06200.title: Swain–Lupton equation
S06200.definition: A dual parameter approach to the correlation analysis of substituent effects, which involves a field constant (\(F\)) and a resonance constant (\(R\)). The original treatment was modified later. The procedure has been considerably applied, but also much criticized.

S06201.title: Swain–Scott equation
S06201.definition: The linear free-energy relation of the form: \[\log _{10}(\frac{k}{k_{0}})=s\ n\] applied to the variation of reactivity of a given electrophilic substrate towards a series of nucleophilic reagents. \(n\) is characteristic of the reagent (i.e. a measure of its nucleophilicity) and \(s\) is characteristic of the substrate (i.e. a measure of its sensitivity to the nucleophilicity of the reagent). A scale of \(n\) values is based on the rate coefficients \(k\) for the reaction of methyl bromide with nucleophiles in water at \(25\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\), \(s\) being defined as 1.00 for these reactions and \(n\) being defined as 0.00 for the hydrolysis of methyl bromide. (Other scales have been devised.)

09650.title: sweat
09650.definition: Fluid excreted by the sweat glands in the skin of mammals during perspiration.

ST07538.title: swelling agent
ST07538.definition: Fluid used to swell a gel, network or solid.

S06202.title: swelling
S06202.definition: The increase in volume of a gel or solid associated with the uptake of a liquid or gas.

S06203.title: swelling pressure
S06203.definition: That pressure difference \(\mathit{\Pi} _{\rm{sw}}\) or \(\mathit{\Pi}\) which has to be established between a gel and its equilibrium liquid, to prevent further swelling of the gel.

09388.title: swift ion
09388.definition: Ion moving with a velocity exceeding the Bohr speed of \(c/137\), where \(c\) is the velocity of light.

12106.title: swimming test
12106.definition: Procedure in which a test animal (rodent) is forced to swim to avoid drowning.

09578.title: swing curve
09578.definition: Sinusoidal variation in the lithographic clearance dose arising from changes in the phase difference between incoming and outgoing radiation that is induced by variations in resist thickness.

13705.title: switch sequence
13705.definition: Highly conserved repetitive sequence that mediates class switching in the immunoglobulin (Ig) heavy chain gene locus.

S06204.title: switchboard model
S06204.definition: A model of crystallinity in which the crystallized segments of a macromolecule belong to the same crystal, although the stems are connected randomly.

S06205.title: switching transition
S06205.definition: A transition in semiconductive glasses in which, beyond a critical applied voltage, there is an avalanche breakdown of conducting electrons that causes local melting and hence local crystallization that gives metallic conductivity.

S06206.title: sydnone imines
S06206.definition: Imines of sydnones (i.e. having an imino group in place of the exocyclic oxygen atom).  (These structures represent only two canonical forms.)

S06207.title: sydnones
S06207.definition: Mesoionic compounds having the 1,2,3-oxadiazole skeleton bearing an oxygen atom attached to the 5 position.  (These structures represent only two canonical forms).

S06208.title: sym-
S06208.definition: An affix used in names to denote symmetrical.

S06209.title: symbiosis
S06209.definition: The term was originally applied to describe the maximum flocking of either hard or soft ligands in the same complexes. For hydrocarbon molecules, symbiosis implies that those containing a maximum number of $\ce{C–H}$ bonds (e.g. $\ce{CH4}$) or $\ce{C–C}$ bonds (e.g. $\ce{Me4C}$) are the most stable.

S06210.title: symbol
S06210.definition: Conventional sign designating a quantity or a unit of measurement.

08692.title: symmetric
08692.definition: Term used in at least two senses in vibrational spectroscopy. In general usage, a symmetric molecule is a molecule with high symmetry. In more specific usage, a property is symmetric with respect to a symmetry element if it remains unchanged by the action of the corresponding symmetry operation.

08693.title: symmetric top
08693.definition: Molecule that has two equal principal moments of inertia with the third one different.

S06211.title: symmetrical films
S06211.definition: The properties of fluid films depend on the nature of the film phase and that of each of the two neighbouring bulk phases. These films should be described, where appropriate, by three capital letters such as A for air, W for water, O for oil, and S for solid, separated by solidi, the middle letter indicating the film phase. For symmetrical films the first and last symbols are the same, e.g. A/W/A: water film in air, or W/O/W: oil film in water, whereas for unsymmetrical films these are different, e.g. W/O/A: oil film between water and air.

09941.title: symmetrical flow field-flow fractionation
09941.definition: Flow field-flow fractionation in which the speed of mobile phase is constant along the length of the channel due to constant channel width.

08428.title: symmetrization
08428.definition: Method of removing artefacts from a two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum that are symmetrical about the diagonal (e.g., HH COSY) or the \(\rm{f}1\) axis (e.g., tilted J-resolved spectra). Values equidistant from midline are compared and replaced the lower (or average) value of the two.

08694.title: symmetry coordinate
08694.definition: Each \(S_{i}\) is a linear combination of general coordinates, usually internal coordinates, constructed to take advantage of the molecular symmetry. The \(S_{i}\) are elements of the vector \(\boldsymbol{S}\). They have the same units as the general coordinates from which they were constructed.

S06214.title: symmetry number
S06214.definition: The symmetry number of a molecule is obtained by imagining all identical atoms to be labelled, and then counting the number of different but equivalent arrangements that can be obtained by rotating (but not reflecting) the molecule. In the statistical-mechanical treatment of chemical equilibrium, the partition function for each molecular species must be divided by its symmetry number.

S06213.title: symmetry-conserving transition
S06213.definition: A transition in which the cell dimensions and/or angles of the one phase differ from those in the other phase, but where the space-group symmetry is conserved. Example: The transition of face-centred cubic $\ce{Ce}$, upon cooling, to a face-centred cubic phase that is $\pu{10\%}$ denser. Upon cooling, enough contraction takes place to allow an overlap of the \(\rm{fsp}^{2}\) configuration and the change from an isolated non-bonding magnetic f electron to a bonding non-magnetic electron pair.

08695.title: symmorphic space group
08695.definition: Space group that does not contain screw-axes and glide planes.

12107.title: sympathetic nervous system
12107.definition: Part of the autonomic nervous system originating in the thoracic and lumbar regions of the spinal cord that tends to inhibit or oppose the physiological effects of the parasympathetic nervous system, as in tending to reduce digestive secretions, increase the heart rate, and contract blood vessels.

13706.title: sympathetic ophthalmia
13706.definition: Autoimmune injury to one eye that occurs after penetrating injury or surgery to the other eye.

16120.title: sympatholytic
16120.definition:
adj., Blocking transmission of impulses from the adrenergic (sympathetic) postganglionic fibers to effector organs or tissues.
n., Agent that blocks transmission of impulses from the adrenergic (sympathetic) postganglionic fibers to effector organs or tissues.

12108.title: sympathomimetic
12108.definition:
n., Substance that produces effects resembling those of impulses transmitted by the postganglionic fibers of the sympathetic nervous system.
adj., Having the property of producing such effects.

16121.title: symptom
16121.definition: Any subjective evidence of a disease or an effect induced by a substance as perceived by the affected subject.

16122.title: symptomatology
16122.definition: General description of all of the signs and symptoms of exposure to a toxicant.

S06216.title: syn
S06216.definition: See: torsion angleSee: endo, exo, syn, antiSee: antiFormerly used to describe the stereochemistry of oximes and related systems.See: E, Z

12109.title: synapse
12109.definition: Functional junction between two neurons, where a nerve impulse is transmitted from one neuron to another, by neurotransmitters.

11271.title: synapsis
11271.definition: Point-wise pairing of homologous chromosomes during the prophase of meiosis.

12110.title: synaptic cleft
