12110.definition: Narrow gap between the presynaptic and postsynaptic regions of two communicating neurons, into which neurotransmitters are secreted.

12112.title: synaptic plasticity
12112.definition:
Ability of synapses to form and reform continually, including to allow learning.
Malleability of signal strength arising at the level of synaptic transmission.

12114.title: synaptic transmission
12114.definition: Neurotransmitter release, diffusion, and receptor binding, propagating an impulse across a synapse.

11272.title: synaptonemal complex
11272.definition: Structure of filamentous proteins that forms between homologous chromosomes when they pair during meiosis; it may contribute to synapsis and genetic recombination.

11273.title: syncephalus
11273.definition: Conjoined twins with two bodies and a fused head.

S06218.title: synchronization
S06218.definition: This principle applies to reactions in which there is a lack of synchronization between bond formation or bond rupture and other primitive changes that affect the stability of products and reactants, such as resonance, solvation, electrostatic, hydrogen bonding and polarizability effects. The principle states that a product-stabilizing factor whose development lags behind bond changes at the transition state, or a reactant-stabilizing factor whose loss is ahead of bond changes at the transition state, increases the intrinsic barrier and decreases the 'intrinsic rate constant' of a reaction. For a product-stabilizing factor whose development is ahead of bond changes, or reactant factors whose loss lags behind bond changes, the opposite relations hold. The reverse effects are observable for factors that destabilize a reactant or product.

S06219.title: synchronous
S06219.definition: A concerted process in which the primitive change concerned (generally bond rupture and bond formation) have progressed to the same extent at the transition state is said to be synchronous. The term figuratively implies a more or less synchronized progress of the changes. However, the progress of the bonding change (or other primitive change) has not been defined quantitatively in terms of a single parameter applicable to different bonds or different bonding changes. The concept is therefore in general only qualitatively descriptive and does not admit an exact definition except in the case of concerted processes involving changes in two identical bonds.

S06220.title: synchronously excited spectrum
S06220.definition: A two-dimensional spectrum obtained by varying both the excitation and emission wavelengths simultaneously and which corresponds to the curve where a plane, parallel to the z-axis, intersects the excitation-emission spectrum (EES).

S06221.title: synchrotron radiation
S06221.definition: X-Radiation which results from the acceleration of charged particles in circular orbits by strong electric and magnetic fields.

08764.title: synchrotron radiation induced X-ray fluorescence analysis
08764.definition: Measurement method of X-ray fluorescence analysis in which synchrotron X-radiation is used to irradiate the substance.

08554.title: synchrotron X-ray spectroscopy
08554.definition: X-ray spectroscopy performed using a high intensity, continuous polychromatic synchrotron X-ray source.

11274.title: syncytiotrophoblast
11274.definition: Outer syncytial layer of trophoblast cells that invades the endometrium during implantation.

11275.title: syncytium
11275.definition: Referring to a large multinucleated mass of cellular contents that arises from the fusion of originally individual cells.

11276.title: syndactyly
11276.definition: Congenital occurrence of fusion or webbing of the fingers or toes.

S06223.title: syndet
S06223.definition: A synthetic detergent; a detergent other than soap.

S06224.title: syndiotactic macromolecule
S06224.definition: A tactic macromolecule, essentially comprising alternating enantiomeric configurational base units, which have chiral or prochiral atoms in the main chain in a unique arrangement with respect to their adjacent constitutional units.

S06225.title: syndiotactic polymer
S06225.definition: A polymer composed of syndiotactic macromolecules.

11277.title: syndrome
11277.definition: Group of signs and symptoms occurring together, having a common cause and defining a disease.

S06227.title: syneresis
S06227.definition: Spontaneous shrinking of a gel with exudation of liquid.

S06228.title: synergism
S06228.definition: A term describing the co-operative effect of two (or more) extractants where the distribution ratio for the combination is greater than the largest individual distribution ratio (measured under comparable conditions).

S06229.title: synergism
S06229.definition: Pharmacological or toxicological interaction in which the combined biological effect of two or more substances is greater than expected on the basis of the simple summation of the toxicity of each of the individual substances.

16123.title: synergist
16123.definition: Substance that contributes more than additively to a mutual effect with another substance.

13707.title: syngeneic
13707.definition: Genetically identical, e.g., a fully inbred strain of mice.

15087.title: syngenetic
15087.definition: Describing mineral deposits formed at the same time as the enclosing rocks; characterized by or pertaining to a formation contemporaneous with the enclosing or surrounding rock.

16124.title: synomone
16124.definition: Semiochemical that is produced by one organism inducing a response in an organism of another species that is favorable to both the emitter and the responding organism.

11278.title: synophthalmia
11278.definition: Congenital fusion of the orbits in the midline, which then contains one eyeball.

S06230.title: synoptic scale
S06230.definition: In meteorology, the size or scale of ordinary weather systems or cyclones; typically \(1000\ \rm{km}\) horizontally.

11279.title: synotia
11279.definition: Congenital malformation characterized by the union or approximation of the ears in front of the neck, often accompanied by the absence or defective development of the lower jaw.

S06232.title: syntectic reaction
S06232.definition: A reversible reaction that involves the conversion of two liquid phases, \(\rm{l}^{'}\) and \(\rm{l}^{''}\), into a solid phase $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ on cooling: \[\rm{l}^{'}+\rm{l}^{''}\rightleftharpoons \unicode[Times]{x3B1} \] The maximum temperature at which this reaction can occur is the congruent melting point of the solid phase. Example: The conversion of co-existing $\ce{K}$-rich and $\ce{Zn}$-rich phases in the $\ce{K-Zn}$ system to form an intermediate solid phase $\ce{KZn13}$.

16125.title: synteny
16125.definition: Property of genes which reside on the same chromosome.

S06233.title: synthetic graphite
S06233.definition: A material consisting of graphitic carbon which has been obtained by graphitizing of non-graphitic carbon by chemical vapour deposition (CVD) from hydrobcarbons at temperatures above \(2500\ \rm{K}\), by decomposition of thermally unstable carbides or by crystallizing from metal melts supersaturated with carbon.

14289.title: synthetic latex
14289.definition: Latex obtained as a product of an emulsion, mini-emulsion, micro-emulsion, or dispersion polymerization.

15364.title: synthetic method
15364.definition: Class of experimental procedures for solubility determination in which a solution of known composition is prepared. Two major subclasses are recognized. In the isothermal method, one liquid component is titrated with a second liquid component at constant temperature until persistent turbidity is observed (i.e., to the cloud point). In the polythermal method, a mixture of known composition is heated above its solution temperature and monitored visually during cooling until turbidity (the cloud point) is observed.

12115.title: syringomyelia
12115.definition: Cyst occurring within the spinal cord as a result of accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid.

15240.title: syrup
15240.definition: Liquid preparation of high sugar concentration with or without medicinal and additional flavoring substances.

S06234.title: system
S06234.definition: Arbitrarily defined part of the universe, regardless of form or size, e.g. for clinical chemistry, patient, patient plasma, patient urine.

S06237.title: system of units
S06237.definition: Set of base units, together with derived units, defined in accordance with given rules, for a given system of quantities, e.g. Système International d'Unités (SI).

09389.title: system resolution
09389.definition: Energy resolution or depth resolution measured in a backscattering spectrum for a monoenergetic incident-ion beam.

08048.title: systematic effect
08048.definition: Recognized effect of an influence quantity on a measured quantity value.

S06235.title: systematic error
S06235.definition: Mean that would result from an infinite number of measurements of the same measurand carried out under repeatability conditions minus a true value of the measurand.

10011.title: systematic examination error
10011.definition: Fraction of examined values with examination error that in replicate examinations remains constant or varies in a predictable manner.

S06236.title: systematic name
S06236.definition: A name composed wholly of specially coined or selected syllables, with or without numerical prefixes; e.g. pentane, oxazole.

16126.title: systematic sample
16126.definition: Subset selected according to some simple rule such as specified date or alphabetic classification.

10062.title: systematic sampling
10062.definition: Sampling in which individual samples are taken at equal intervals in location.

15088.title: systematics
15088.definition: Study of the diversity of past and present life forms and of relationships among them through time.

13708.title: systemic
13708.definition:
1) Relating to the body as a whole.
2) Occurring at a site in the body remote from the point of contact with a substance.

13709.title: systemic autoimmune disease
13709.definition: Autoimmune disease affecting a number of organs or tissues, or the whole body.

ST06802.title: systemic effect
ST06802.definition: Consequence that is either of a generalized nature or that occurs at a site distant from the point of entry of a substance.

13710.title: systemic lupus erythematosus
13710.definition: Chronic autoimmune disease that is potentially debilitating and sometimes fatal as the immune system attacks the body’s cells and tissues, with inflammation and tissue damage.

13711.title: systemic sclerosis
13711.definition: Fibrosing disease of unclear etiology that affects multiple organ systems.

12731.title: systems biology
12731.definition: Integration of high-throughput biology measurements with computational models that study the projection of the mechanistic characteristics of metabolic and signalling pathways onto physiological and pathological phenotypes.

S06239.title: Szilard–Chalmers effect
S06239.definition: The rupture of the chemical bond between an atom and the molecule of which the atom is part, as a result of a nuclear reaction of that atom.

S04387.title: π → σ* transition
S04387.definition: An electronic transition described approximately as a promotion of an electron from a 'bonding' orbital $\ce{\uppi\!}$ to an 'antibonding' orbital $\ce{\upsigma\!}$ designated as $\ce{\upsigma\!^{\ast}}$. Such transitions generally involve high transition energies and appear close to or mixed with Rydberg transitions.

S05435.title: σ → σ* transition
S05435.definition: An electronic transition described approximately as promotion of an electron from a 'bonding' $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}orbital}$ to an 'antibonding' $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}orbital}$ designated as \(\sigma ^{\rm{*}}\). Such transitions generally involve high transition energies, and appear close to or mixed with Rydberg transitions.

S05434.title: σ, π
S05434.definition: The terms are symmetry designations, $\ce{\uppi\! molecular orbitals}$ being antisymmetric with respect to a defining plane containing at least one atom (e.g. the molecular plane of ethene) and $\ce{\upsigma\! molecular orbitals}$ symmetric with respect to the same plane. In practice the terms are used both in this rigorous sense (for orbitals encompassing the entire molecule) and also for localized two-centre orbitals or bonds, and it is necessary to make a clear distinction between the two usages. In the case of two-centre bonds, a $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}bond}$ has a nodal plane that includes the internuclear bond axis, whereas a $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bond}$ has no such nodal plane. (A $\ce{\updelta\!\mbox{-}bond}$ in organometallic or inorganic molecular species has two nodes.) Radicals are classified by analogy into $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}}$ and $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}radicals}$. Such two-centre orbitals may take part in molecular orbitals of $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}}$ or $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}symmetry}$. For example, the methyl group in propene contains three $\ce{C–H}$ bonds, each of which is of local $\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}symmetry}$ (i.e. without a nodal plane including the internuclear axis), but these three '$\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}bonds}$' can in turn be combined to form a set of group orbitals one of which has $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}symmetry}$ with respect to the principal molecular plane and can accordingly interact with the two-centre orbital of $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}symmetry}$ ($\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}bond}$) of the double-bonded carbon atoms, to form a molecular orbital of $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}symmetry}$. Such an interaction between the $\ce{CH3}$ group and the double bond is an example of what is called hyperconjugation. This cannot rigorously be described as '$\ce{\upsigma\!\mbox{-}\uppi\!}$ conjugation' since $\ce{\upsigma\!}$ and $\ce{\uppi\!}$ here refer to different defining planes, and interaction between orbitals of different symmetries (with respect to the same defining plane) is forbidden.

08429.title: t1
08429.definition: Time domain arising from the regular increments of the delay period in two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

08431.title: t1 noise
08431.definition: Streaks of spurious artefact signals in a two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum parallel to the \(\rm{f}1\) axis at the \(\rm{f}2\) of a strong resonance.

08430.title: t2
08430.definition: Time domain in two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy arising from direct free induction decay detection.

13922.title: theoretical degree of biodegradation
13922.definition: Degree of biodegradation that corresponds to conversion of all the organic matter present in an original polymer-based item to minerals and biomass.

13946.title: targeting
13946.definition: Exploitation of specific or nonspecific interactions to target a particular part of a living system, or a particular type of cells.

13947.title: therapeutic polymer
13947.definition: Polymer aimed at helping therapists in treating diseases or trauma.

13948.title: thrombogenicity
13948.definition: Property of a material (or substance) that induces and/or promotes the formation of a thrombus.

13949.title: tissue engineering
13949.definition: Use of a combination of cells, engineering and materials methods, and suitable biochemical and physico-chemical factors to improve or replace biological functions.

13950.title: transplant
13950.definition: Complete structure, such as an organ that is transferred from a site in a donor to a site in a recipient for the purpose of the reconstruction of the recipient site.

16258.title: total mobile-phase volume in column
16258.definition: Sum of the interparticle volume of the column and intraparticle volume of the column: \(V_{\rm{t}} = V_{0} + V_{\rm{i}}\)

16260.title: total mobile phase time
16260.definition: Retention time of a sample component the molecules of which are smaller than the smallest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.

14205.title: two-phase model
14205.definition: Model based on the assumption that the polymer sample consists only of domains of a crystalline phase and of an amorphous phase.

14216.title: translational chain repeating unit
14216.definition: Smallest structural unit of a polymer chain that is repeated by translation in the crystal lattice along the chain axis.

14259.title: transcrystalline layer
14259.definition: Polycrystalline layer nucleated and shaped by a pre-existing planar surface within or in contact with a polymer melt.

14260.title: twinned polymer crystal
14260.definition: Polymer crystal in which two or more single crystalline domains of the same crystal polymorph, with different lattice orientations, coexist.

12591.title: tandem mass spectrometry in space
12591.definition: Tandem mass spectrometry procedure in which product ion spectra are recorded for ion beams in m/z analyzers separated in space. Specific m/z separation functions are designed so that in one section of the instrument ions are selected, dissociated in an intermediate region, and the product ions are then transmitted to another analyzer for m/z separation and data acquisition.

12592.title: tandem mass spectrometry in time
12592.definition: Tandem mass spectrometry procedure in which product ion spectra are recorded in a single m/z analyzer (such as a Paul ion trap, linear ion trap, or Fourier transform-ion cyclotron resonance-mass spectrometer) in discrete steps over time. Ions in a specific m/z range are selected, dissociated, and the product ions analyzed sequentially in time.

12593.title: Taylor cone
12593.definition: Conical shape of the liquid emanating from a capillary under high potential, as in electrospray or other electrohydrodynamic spray processes.

12594.title: thermospray ionization
12594.definition: Spray ionization in which a liquid is flowed through a heated capillary to produce a spray of droplets and solvent vapor. Ions are formed due to the statistical imbalance of charges in the droplets or by a heated filament.

12595.title: thin layer chromatography-mass spectrometry
12595.definition: Technique by which a mixture of analytes is separated into individual components by liquid chromatography, followed by the ionization of the separated species by an ion source of a mass spectrometer.

12596.title: time-lag focusing
12596.definition: Energy focusing of ions formed in the gas phase in a time-of-flight mass spectrometer that is accomplished by introducing a time delay between the formation of the ions and the application of the accelerating potential pulse.

12597.title: tolyl ion
12597.definition: Even-electron \(\ce{C7H7^{+}}\) ion with the same carbon skeleton as toluene that has lost a hydrogen atom from one of the ring carbons that carries the positive charge.

12598.title: toroidal ion trap
12598.definition: Ion trapping device based on the three-dimensional structure formed by rotating the cross-section of a quadrupole ion trap about the edge perpendicular to the plane of the ring electrode. The resulting trapping region is toroidal.

12599.title: total ion current electropherogram
12599.definition: Plot of the total ion current in each of a series of mass spectra that are recorded as a function of electrophoresis time.

12600.title: total ion current profile
12600.definition: Any plot of total ion current in a series of mass spectra recorded as a function of time, including total ion current chromatogram, total ion current electropherogram, flow injection mass spectrometry, or any other time dependent sampling.

12601.title: transmission efficiency
12601.definition: Ratio of the number of ions leaving a region of a mass spectrometer to the number entering that region.

12602.title: transmission quadrupole mass spectrometer
12602.definition: Mass spectrometer that consists of an array of four parallel rod electrodes whose centers form the corners of a square and whose opposing electrode pairs are connected. The electric potential applied between the connected pairs of rods is a superposition of a static potential and a sinusoidal radio frequency potential. The motion of an ion in the \(x\mbox{-}y\) plane perpendicular to the length direction of the rod electrodes is described by the Mathieu equation whose solutions show that ions in a particular m/z range can be transmitted along the \(z\mbox{-}\rm{axis}\).

12603.title: transport region
12603.definition: Region in a mass spectrometer in which an ion beam is transported from the ion source to the ion optics or from one ion optical element to the next.

12604.title: triple quadrupole mass spectrometer
12604.definition: Tandem mass spectrometer comprising two transmission quadrupole mass spectrometers in series, with a (non-selecting) RF-only quadrupole (or other multipole) between them to act as a collision cell.

12878.title: therapeutic antibody
12878.definition: Antibody administered with the aim of treating a disease.

13724.title: T lymphocyte
13724.definition: Lymphocyte that matures in the thymus and has the ability to recognize specific peptide antigens through the receptors on its cell surface.

13714.title: T-cell receptor
13714.definition: Antigen-specific receptor on T cells composed of one set of heterodimeric chains. Two types of TCR heterodimers are known (\(\upalpha/\upbeta\) and \(\upgamma/\updelta\)).

13713.title: T-cell-dependent antibody response
13713.definition: Immunotoxicity test that evaluates the ability of animals to produce antibodies to a T-dependent antigen [e.g., sheep red blood cells (SRBCs) or keyhole limpet hemocyanin (KLH)].

13715.title: T-dependent antigen
13715.definition: Antigen that requires helper T lymphocytes (Th) in order to elicit an antibody response.

13723.title: T-independent antigen
13723.definition: Antigen that is able to elicit an antibody response in the absence of T cells.

12116.title: T-maze
12116.definition: Simple type of test apparatus with three arms shaped like the letter 'T.' After placing a rodent in the middle, it is recorded how often the animal enters each arm.

13862.title: T-stacking
13862.definition: Orthogonal alignment of constitutional units within molecules that lead to favourable interactions.

15241.title: tablet
15241.definition: Solid dosage form compressed into a specific shape containing medicinal substances with or without suitable diluents.

15242.title: tablet coating
15242.definition:
Solid layers based typically on cellulose derivatives and may include plasticizers and pigments. They are usually employed for one or more of the following reasons:

Protection of the ingredients (from light or moisture).
Masking the bad taste of the drug.
Masking possible batchwise differences in the appearance of raw materials and hence allaying possible patient concern over tablets of differing appearance.
Coating confers mechanical strength and facilitates handling.
Colored coating aids in the rapid identification of a product.
Functional film coating is used to impart enteric or controlled-release properties to the tablet.

16127.title: tachy-
16127.definition: Prefix meaning rapid as in tachycardia and tachypnoea.

T06242.title: tactic block
T06242.definition: A regular block that can be described by only one species of configurational repeating unit in a single sequential arrangement.

T06243.title: tactic block polymer
T06243.definition: A polymer, the molecules of which consist of tactic blocks connected linearly.

T06245.title: tactic macromolecule
T06245.definition: A regular macromolecule in which essentially all the configurational repeating unit are identical.

T06246.title: tactic polymer
T06246.definition: A polymer composed of tactic macromolecules.

T06244.title: tacticity
T06244.definition: The orderliness of the succession of configurational repeating units in the main chain of a regular macromolecule, a regular oligomer molecule, a regular block or a regular chain.

T06247.title: Taft equation
T06247.definition: Various equations are associated with R.W. Taft, but the term is most often used to designate the family of equations that emerged from Taft's analysis of the reactivities of aliphatic esters, and which involved the polar substituent constant \(\sigma^{\ast}\) and the steric substituent constant \(E_{\rm{s}}\): \[\log_{10}k = \log_{10}k_{0} + \rho^{\ast} \sigma^{\ast} + \delta E_{\rm{s}}\] or the one-parameter forms applicable when the role of either the polar term or the steric term may be neglected. Nowadays \(\sigma^{\ast}\) is usually replaced by the related constant \(\sigma_{I}\).

11280.title: tail bud
11280.definition: In the vertebrate embryo, mass of proliferating cells at the caudal end that arises from the primitive node.

12118.title: tail flick test
12118.definition: Procedure in which the tail of a rodent is heated and the time taken for the animal to flick its tail (latency) is taken as a measure of the relative degree of antinociception.

12119.title: tail immersion test
12119.definition: Procedure in which the tail of a rodent is placed in a hot water bath (typically between \(\pu{54^{\circ}C}\) and \(\pu{58^{\circ}C}\)) and the time it takes the animal to remove the tail from the water is interpreted as a measurement of the relative degree of antinociception.

12120.title: tail suspension test
12120.definition: Procedure in which a mouse is suspended by its tail and the time spent attempting to right itself is observed.

09905.title: tailing factor
09905.definition: Width of the back of a peak (\(b\)) divided by the width of the front (\(f\)) of the peak measured at \(\pu{10\%}\) of the peak height. See figure in asymmetry factor.

T06249.title: tailing
T06249.definition: Asymmetry of a peak such that, relative to the baseline, the front is steeper than the rear. In paper chromatography and in thin-layer chromatography, the distortion of a zone showing a diffuse region behind the zone in the direction of travel.

10063.title: take-it-or-leave-it data
10063.definition: Happenstance data that must be processed, or not processed, as is.

09296.title: take-off angle
09296.definition: Angle between the trajectory of a particle as it leaves a surface and the local or average surface plane.

12806.title: Tammann’s 2/3rd rule
12806.definition: Empirical rule that states that in a partially crystalline polymer the glass-transition temperature can be reasonably approximated by a value equal to two-thirds of the melting temperature, \(T_{\rm{m}}\)/\(\pu{K}\).

12309.title: tan $\delta$
12309.definition: The dimensionless ratio of energy lost to energy returned during one cycle of a periodic process.

13726.title: tandem conjugate
13726.definition: Molecular construct with two fluorochromes where the first excites the second by its emission.

T06250.title: tandem mass spectrometer
T06250.definition: An arrangement in which ions are subjected to two or more sequential stages of analysis (which may be separated spatially or temporally) according to the quotient mass/charge. A hybrid mass spectometer is an instrument which combines analysers of different types, e.g. magnetic plus electric sector combined with quadrupole. The study of ions involving two stages of mass analysis has been termed mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry.

09730.title: tandem repeat sequence
09730.definition: Multiple consecutive copies of the same nucleotide sequence on a chromosome.

11523.title: Tanimoto similarity
11523.definition: A scale that ranges from \(\pu{0.0}\) to \(\pu{1.0}\) when calculated as the ratio of the fingerprint bits or structural keys that both molecules have set divided by the number of bits or keys set in both molecules plus those set either molecule.

10145.title: Tanimoto similarity index
10145.definition: Fraction of variables that are considered to agree between two objects.

11735.title: tardive dyskinesia
11735.definition: Involuntary, repetitive body movement of slow onset.

13727.title: target cell
13727.definition: Cell killed by one of the body’s killer cells, such as a cytotoxic T lymphocyte or natural killer (NK) cell.

10013.title: target examination uncertainty
10013.definition: Examination uncertainty specified as an acceptable fraction and decided on the basis of the intended use of examination results.

TT06812.title: target
TT06812.definition: Any organism, organ, tissue, cell, or cell constituent that is subject to the action of an agent.

08133.title: target measurement uncertainty
08133.definition: Measurement uncertainty specified as an upper limit and decided on the basis of the intended use of measurement results.

16130.title: target population
16130.definition:
Collection of individuals, items, measurements, etc. about which inferences are required: The term is sometimes used to indicate the population from which a sample is drawn and sometimes to denote any reference population about which inferences are needed.
Group of persons for whom an intervention is planned.

12733.title: target validation
12733.definition: Process by which a protein, RNA, or DNA is implicated in a biological pathway thought to be of relevance to a disease or adverse pathology.

12732.title: targeted drug delivery
12732.definition: Approach to target a drug to a specific tissue or molecular target using a prodrug or antibody recognition systems.

14197.title: targeted library
14197.definition: Library designed, on the basis of preexisting information, to generate enhanced activity or hit rate against a particular biological target or target class.

09863.title: targeted lipidomics
09863.definition: Analytical technique focusing on the quantification of specific lipids of interest.

09784.title: targeted proteomics
09784.definition: Approach in proteomics focused on the selected proteins of a sample.

12122.title: tau protein
12122.definition: One of a class of proteins that stabilizes microtubules, particularly in neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes of the central nervous system.

12121.title: tauopathy
12121.definition: One of a class of neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer disease, associated with abnormal aggregation of tau proteins.

12734.title: tautomer
12734.definition: Structural isomer that can readily convert to another form that differs only by the attachment position of a hydrogen atom and the location of double bond(s).

T06252.title: tautomerism
T06252.definition: Isomerism of the general form:  where the isomers (called tautomers) are readily interconvertible; the atoms connecting the groups $\ce{X}$, $\ce{Y}$, $\ce{Z}$ are typically any of $\ce{C}$, $\ce{H}$, $\ce{O}$ or $\ce{S}$, and $\ce{G}$ is a group which becomes an electrofuge or nucleofuge during isomerization. The commonest case, when the electrofuge is H+, is also known as 'prototropy'. Examples, written so as to illustrate the general pattern given above, include: keto-enol tautomerism, such as:   The grouping Y may itself be a three-atom (or five-atom) chain extending the conjugation, as in:  The double bond between $\ce{Y}$ and $\ce{Z}$ may be replaced by a ring, when the phenomenon is called ring-chain tautomerism, as in:

T06253.title: tautomerization
T06253.definition: The isomerization by which tautomers are interconverted. It is a heterolytic molecular rearrangement and is frequently very rapid.

08213.title: tautomers
08213.definition: Constitutional isomers that can interconvert more or less rapidly, often by migration of a hydron.

15089.title: taxocene
15089.definition: Taxonomically defined subset of an entire community.

09982.title: taxon
09982.definition: Category indicating a class of organisms within a recognized hierarchically structured nominal property value set.

15090.title: taxonomy
15090.definition: Science applied to the allocation of biological names and the rules of naming.

11281.title: Tay–Sachs disease
11281.definition: Autosomal recessive inheritance of hexosaminidase A deficiency leading to a lysosomal storage disease characterized by central and peripheral neuronal involvement and early death.

12123.title: TDP-43 transcription factor
12123.definition: Cleavage product (\(\pu{43 kDa}\)) of the transactive response (TAR) DNA binding protein (TARDBP) that targets TAR DNA and transcriptionally represses HIV-1.

13716.title: TdT-dependent dUTP-biotin nick end labeling assay
13716.definition: Method for detecting apoptotic cells in situ based on characteristic DNA fragmentation. It is based on the ability of terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT) to transfer a labeled deoxyuridine triphosphate to the terminal ends arising from DNA cleavage.

09651.title: tears
09651.definition: Clear salty liquid that is secreted by the lachrymal gland of the eye to lubricate the surface between the eyeball and eyelid and to wash away irritants.

T06256.title: tele-substitution
T06256.definition: A substitution reaction in which the entering group takes up a position more than one atom away from the atom to which the leaving group was attached:

TT07167.title: telechelic polymer
TT07167.definition: Prepolymer capable of entering into further polymerization or other reactions through its reactive end-groups.

11283.title: telencephalon
11283.definition: Embryonic structure that develops into the cerebrum.

T06257.title: tellurides
T06257.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RTeR}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$). Thus tellurium analogues of ethers.Metal salts of tellurane, $\ce{H2Te}$.

T06258.title: tellurones
T06258.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R2Te(=O)2}$. Thus tellurium analogues of sulfones.

09731.title: telomerase
09731.definition: Enzyme that directs the replication of telomeres.

09732.title: telomere
09732.definition: Repetitive nucleotide sequences present at the ends of a chromosome that protect the chromosome from deterioration.

T06260.title: telomerization
T06260.definition: The formation of an addition oligomer, having uniform end groups $\ce{X'\ldots X^{''}}$, by a chain reaction in which a chain transfer limits the length of the polymer ('telomer') produced. An example is the polymerization of styrene in bromotrichloromethane solution ($\ce{X'} = \ce{CCl3}$, $\ce{X^{''}} = \ce{Br}$), where $\ce{Cl3C^{.}}$ radicals are formed in the initiation step to produce $\ce{Cl3C[CH2CHPh]_{n}Br}$, with \(n\) greater than 1 and often less than ca. 10:

11284.title: telophase
11284.definition: Final phase of both meiosis and mitosis in which distinct nuclei form in each daughter cell.

T06261.title: temperature
T06261.definition: Short form for thermodynamic, Celsius or Fahrenheit temperature.

T06262.title: temperature coefficient
T06262.definition: The dependence of a detector on temperature can be described by the temperature coefficient of responsivity and is expressed as percentage change in output per \(\mathrm{K}\). In the case of a nonlinear dependence the temperature and the temperature range should also be stated for which the stated temperature coefficient of responsivity is applicable.

T06263.title: temperature effect
T06263.definition: A term used for changes in the luminescence parameters caused by changes in temperature, since the type of solvent and its temperature can effect the luminescence yield from an analyte as a result of quenching, exciplex formation, aggregation, etc.

T06264.title: temperature inversion
T06264.definition: A departure from the normal decrease of temperature with increasing altitude. A temperature inversion may be produced, for example, by the movement of a warm air mass over a cool one. Intense surface inversions may form over the land during nights with clear skies and low winds due to the radiative loss of heat from the surface of the earth. The temperature increases as a function of height in this case. Poor mixing of the pollutants generally occurs below the inversion, since the normal convective process which drives the warmer and lighter air at ground level to higher altitudes is interrupted as the rising air parcels encounter the warmer air above. Temperature inversions near the surface are particularly effective in trapping ground level emissions.

T06265.title: temperature jump
T06265.definition: A relaxation technique in which the temperature of a chemical system is suddenly raised. The system then relaxes to a new state of equilibrium, and analysis of the relaxation processes provides rate constants.

T06266.title: temperature lapse rate
T06266.definition: The rate of change of temperature with altitude (\(\frac{\rm{d}T}{\rm{d}z}\)). The rate of temperature decrease with increase in altitude which is expected to occur in an unperturbed dry air mass is \(9.8\times 10^{3}\ ^{\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C min}^{-1}\). This is called the dry adiabatic lapse rate. The lapse rate is taken as positive when temperature decreases with increasing height. For air saturated with $\ce{H2O}$, the lapse rate is less because of the release of the latent heat of water as it condenses. The average tropospheric lapse rate is about \(6.5\times 10^{3}\ ^{\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\ \min ^{-1}\). The lapse rate has a negative value within an inversion layer.

12124.title: temperature sensitivity
12124.definition:
Adverse responsiveness to heat or cold.
Note: It is associated with a number of medical conditions, some physiologically well-defined (as in cold intolerance in hypothyroidism) and others less so (as in reported chronic fatigue syndrome).
Phenotype arising from engineered or selected gene mutations in experimental organisms characterized by an altered temperature permissive for optimal growth or survival.

T06267.title: temperature-programmed chromatography
T06267.definition: A procedure in which the temperature of the column is changed systematically during a part or the whole of the separation.

12310.title: temperature-programmed desorption
12310.definition: EGA using an inert atmosphere or vacuum, in the absence of sample decomposition.

12311.title: temperature-programmed oxidation
12311.definition: Experiment using an oxidising atmosphere, usually oxygen. Oxidation is monitored by any appropriate technique (EGA, TGA, gas sorption, etc.).

12312.title: temperature-programmed reduction
12312.definition: Experiment using a reducing atmosphere, usually hydrogen. Reduction is monitored by any appropriate technique (EGA, TGA, gas sorption, etc.).

T06269.title: template
T06269.definition: The nucleic acid single strand that is copied during replication or transcription.

13868.title: template polymerization
13868.definition: Polymerization of monomer molecules adsorbed and oriented (a) on a surface, (b) in a polymer lattice, (c) on polymer molecules in solution, or (d) round a metal ion whereby the structure of the polymer chains formed is controlled by the orientation of the monomer molecules.

12125.title: temporal lobe
12125.definition: One of the four major lobes of each cerebral hemisphere, situated at the base of the brain.

16131.title: temporary acceptable daily intake
16131.definition: Value for the acceptable daily intake (ADI) proposed for guidance when data are sufficient to conclude that use of the substance is safe over the relatively short period of time required to generate and evaluate further safety data, but are insufficient to conclude that use of the substance is safe over a lifetime.

16132.title: temporary maximum residue limit
16132.definition: Regulatory value established for a specified, limited time when only a temporary acceptable daily intake has been established for the pesticide concerned or, with the existence of an agreed acceptable daily intake, the available residue data are inadequate for firm maximum residue recommendations.

T06270.title: temporary poisoning
T06270.definition: Weak and reversible adsorption of a poison, such that removal of the poison from the fluid phase results in restoration of the original catalytic activity.

11802.title: tension headache
11802.definition: Headache associated with anxiety or other states of distress, associated with chronic contraction of the scalp muscles.

12126.title: tentorium
12126.definition: Fold of the dura mater separating the cerebrum from the cerebellum.

11285.title: teratocarcinoma
11285.definition: Malignant teratoma, occurring most often in the testis.

11286.title: teratogen
11286.definition: Chemical, physical, or biological agent that, when administered to a parent either prior to conception or before birth of the child, induces permanent structural malformations or birth defects in the offspring.

11287.title: teratogenesis
11287.definition: Process of development of malformations or birth defects.

11288.title: teratogenetics
11288.definition: Study of how genes and teratogens interact to cause birth defects.

15091.title: teratogenic
15091.definition: Capable of causing nonheritable permanent structural malformations or defects in the offspring of an exposed parent.

11289.title: teratogenic index
11289.definition: Mortality of eggs expressed as a lethal concentration divided by the threshold concentration for production of abnormal embryos with nonheritable permanent structural malformations or defects following exposure to a teratogen.

11290.title: teratogenicity
11290.definition: Inherent ability to act as a teratogen.

11291.title: teratology
11291.definition: Study of the causes, mechanisms, and manifestations of developmental deviation of either structure or function.

11292.title: teratoma
11292.definition: Benign germ cell-derived tumor containing embryonic elements of the three primary germ layers, such as skin, hair, and muscle, occurring most frequently in the ovary.

T06273.title: term
T06273.definition: A set of levels which have the same electron configuration and the same value of the quantum numbers for total spin \(S\) and total orbital angular momentum \(L\).

T06277.title: term symbols
T06277.definition: Symbols characterizing the states of atoms and molecules in terms of multiplicity, symmetry of the total electronic wavefunction, and sometimes total (orbital + spin) angular momentum. Examples: \(^{2}\rm{P}_{1/2}\) denotes an atomic state of multiplicity 2 (doublet), electron orbital angular momentum quantum number \(L=1\), and orbital plus spin angular momentum quantum number \(J=\frac{1}{2}\).

T06272.title: term
T06272.definition: Energy divided by the product of the Planck constant and the speed of light, when of wavenumber dimension, or energy divided by the Planck constant, when of frequency dimension.

09630.title: terminal constitutional repeating unit
09630.definition: Constitutional repeating unit connected to only one other constitutional repeating unit.

13728.title: terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase
13728.definition: Enzyme that inserts non-coded nucleotides at the junctions of V, D, and J gene segments of immunoglobulin (Ig) and T-cell receptor (TCR) locus DNA, thus increasing the diversity of antigen-specific recognition.

T06274.title: termination
T06274.definition: The steps in a chain reaction in which reactive intermediates are destroyed or rendered inactive, thus ending the chain.

T06275.title: terminator
T06275.definition: A sequence of DNA lying beyond the 3' end of the coding segment of a gene which is recognized by RNA polymerase as a signal to stop synthesizing mRNA.

15365.title: ternary diagram
15365.definition: Triangular plot (usually an equilateral or right-angled triangle) whose vertices represent the pure components of a ternary system at constant temperature and pressure. Any point within the triangle represents the composition in terms of the two independent mole (or mass) fractions. Lines parallel to the sides of the triangle represent constant proportions of the respective components (isopleths).

T06278.title: terpenes
T06278.definition: Hydrocarbons of biological origin having carbon skeletons formally derived from isoprene $\ce{[CH2=C(CH3)CH=CH2]}$. This class is subdivided into the $\ce{C5}$ hemiterpenes, $\ce{C10}$ monoterpenes, $\ce{C15}$ sesquiterpenes, $\ce{C20}$ diterpenes, $\ce{C25}$ sesterterpenes, $\ce{C30}$ triterpenes, $\ce{C40}$ tetraterpenes (carotenoids) and $\ce{C5_{n}}$ polyterpenes.

T06279.title: terpenoids
T06279.definition: Natural products and related compounds formally derived from isoprene units (see isoprenoids). They contain oxygen in various functional groups. This class is subdivided according to the number of carbon atoms in the same manner as are terpenes. The skeleton of terpenoids may differ from strict additivity of isoprene units by the loss or shift of a fragment, generally a methyl group.

15092.title: terrestrial
15092.definition: Relating to land, as distinct from water or air.

08555.title: tertiary aerosol
08555.definition: Aerosol that reaches an inductively-coupled plasma.

13731.title: tertiary lymphoid tissue
13731.definition: Ectopic lymphoid aggregates that accumulate during the process of chronic immune stimulation, and exhibit characteristics usually associated with the secondary lymphoid organs.

T06282.title: tertiary structure
T06282.definition: The spatial organization (including conformation) of an entire protein molecule or other macromolecule consisting of a single chain.

09785.title: tertiary structure of a protein
09785.definition: Arrangement of all atoms of a protein molecule or a subunit of a protein molecule in space, without regard to its relationship with neighbouring molecules or subunits.

T06283.title: tesla
T06283.definition: SI derived unit of magnetic flux density, \(\pu{T} = \pu{Wb m-2} = \pu{kg s-2 A-1}\).

11293.title: Tessier classification
11293.definition: Classification of bony and soft tissue facial clefts based on their anatomic location.

T06284.title: test portion
T06284.definition: The amount or volume of the test sample taken for analysis, usually of known weight or volume.

T06285.title: test sample
T06285.definition: The sample, prepared from the laboratory sample, from which test portions are removed for testing or for analysis.

11524.title: test set
11524.definition: The set of molecules not used in any way to devise a computational model but instead are used to test its predictivity.

T06286.title: test solution
T06286.definition: The solution prepared from the test portion for the analytical procedure. The proportions of test portion and solvent are normally known.

11294.title: testicular feminization
11294.definition: Type of male pseudohermaphroditism in which the individual has a male karyotype and testes present within the abdominal cavity, but develops external female genitalia and female secondary sexual characteristics.

08049.title: testing
08049.definition: Determination of one or more characteristics of an object of conformity assessment, according to a specified procedure.

16133.title: testing of chemicals
16133.definition:
In toxicology, evaluation of the therapeutic and potentially toxic effects of substances by their application through relevant routes of exposure with appropriate organisms or biological systems so as to relate effects to dose following application.
In chemistry, qualitative or quantitative analysis by the application of one or more fixed methods and comparison of the results with established standards.

11295.title: testis
11295.definition: Gonad of a male animal, involved in the secretion of androgens and the site of sperm production.

11296.title: testosterone
11296.definition: Androgenic steroid hormone produced primarily in the testis, responsible for the development of the male sexual organs and male secondary sexual characteristics.

12127.title: tetanic
12127.definition: Pertaining to tetanus, characterized by tonic muscle spasm.

12128.title: tetanus
12128.definition:
Sustained muscle contraction.
Disease caused by tetanus toxin and characterized by painful, sustained muscle contraction with spasticity and paralysis.

12129.title: tetanus toxin
12129.definition: Neurotoxin produced by the bacterium Clostridium tetani growing in anaerobic conditions, producing the disease tetanus.

12130.title: tetanus toxin-binding ganglioside
12130.definition: Ganglioside that binds tetanus toxin, facilitating its internalization at the presynapticneuronal membrane.

13729.title: tetanus toxoid
13729.definition: Detoxified tetanus toxin used to produce active immunity (see active immune response) against tetanus.

12131.title: tetany
12131.definition: Neurological syndrome characterized by muscle twitches, cramps, and spasms; and in severe forms, by spasm of the muscles of the larynx (laryngospasm) and seizures.

T06287.title: tetracyclines
T06287.definition: A subclass of polyketides having an octahydrotetracene-2-carboxamide skeleton, substituted with many hydroxy and other groups, e.g. chlortetracycline:

12132.title: tetrad test
12132.definition: Battery of tests typically for the effects of cannabinoids in rodents that includes hypomotility assessed by an open field test, catalepsy assessed by the bar test, hypothermia measured by rectal temperature, and analgesia measured by avoidance of heat, e.g., in the tail immersion test.

T06289.title: tetrahedral intermediate
T06289.definition: A reaction intermediate in which the bond arrangement around an initially double-bonded carbon atom (typically a carbonyl carbon atom) has been transformed from trigonal to tetrahedral. For example, aldol in the condensation reaction of acetaldehyde (but most tetrahedral intermediates have a more fleeting existence).

T06290.title: tetrahedro-
T06290.definition: An affix used in names to denote four atoms bound into a tetrahedron.

11297.title: tetralogy of Fallot
11297.definition: Set of four congenital cardiac defects involving an opening in the wall that should separate the right and left ventricles (ventricular septal defect), allowing the aorta to receive venous as well as arterial blood: including stenosis of the pulmonary artery, hypertrophy of the right ventricle, and displacement of the aorta. Right ventricular hypertrophy is the fourth part of the tetralogy, although it may also be a consequence of the other defects.

13730.title: tetramer staining
13730.definition: Technique used for selective staining of antigen-specific T lymphocytes in vitro or in situ. The antigen is presented to T cells by peptide tetramer constructs of major histocompatibility (MHC) class I molecules. It is also used to isolate antigen-specific T-cell populations for clonal expansion.

T06291.title: tetrapyrroles
T06291.definition: Natural pigments containing four pyrrole rings joined by one-carbon units linking position 2 of one pyrrole ring to position 5 of the next. porphyrins are macrocyclic tetrapyrroles. E.g. bilin (a linear tetrapyrrole).

12133.title: tetrodotoxin
12133.definition: Neurotoxin that inhibits action potentials by blocking sodium ion channels.

12134.title: tetrodotoxin-insensitive
12134.definition: Denoting a class of sodium ion channels, found mainly in the heart, that is not blocked by tetrodotoxin.

T06293.title: texture
T06293.definition: The detailed geometry of the void space in the particles of a catalyst.

13717.title: Th0 cell
13717.definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) with a less restricted cytokine profile than Th1 and Th2 cells.

13718.title: Th1 cell
13718.definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) producing mainly interleukin-2 (IL-2), interferon (IFN-$\ce{\upgamma\!}$), and tumor necrosis factor $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ ($\ce{TNF\mbox{-}\upbeta\!}$), and thereby responsible for phagocyte-dependent host responses.

13722.title: Th17 cell
13722.definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th), distinct from Th1 and Th2 cells, that secretes the interleukin IL-17.

13719.title: Th2 cell
13719.definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) in mice producing interleukins IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-9, IL-10, and IL-13.

13720.title: Th3 cell
13720.definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) producing and responding to transforming growth factor $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ ($\ce{TGF\mbox{-}\upbeta\!}$) and helping immunoglobulin A (IgA) antibody responses.

13721.title: Th9 cell
13721.definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) producing interleukin IL-9, which stimulates mast cells.

11298.title: thalamus
11298.definition: Either of two masses of grey matter, the largest part of the diencephalon, lying between the cerebral hemispheres on either side of the third ventricle, relaying sensory information and acting as a centre for pain perception.

11299.title: thalidomide
11299.definition: Teratogenic indole-based drug with sedative and anti-angiogenic properties.

11300.title: theca
11300.definition: Bilayer covering of the ovarian follicle (thus theca interna and externa), of which the theca interna is involved in production of androstenedione.

TT07544.title: theoretical ceramic yield
TT07544.definition: Ceramic yield based on the stoichiometry of the ceramization process.

16134.title: theoretical maximum daily intake
16134.definition: Predicted maximum daily intake of a residue, assuming that it is present at the maximum residue level and that average daily consumption of foods per person is represented by assessed regional diets: It is expressed in milligrams of residue per person per day.

09390.title: theoretical scattered-ion intensity
09390.definition: Calculated intensity for probe ions scattered into a specified solid angle at a given direction.

16135.title: therapeutic cloning
16135.definition: Generation and manipulation of stem cells with the objective of deriving cells of a particular organ or tissue to treat a disease.

12735.title: therapeutic index
12735.definition: Ratio of the exposure/concentration of a therapeutic agent that causes beneficial effects to that which causes the first observed adverse effect.

T06295.title: thermal analysis
T06295.definition: A group of techniques in which a physical property of a substance and/or its reaction product is measured as a function of temperature while the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program.

09449.title: thermal annealing
09449.definition: Annealing in which a heating step is used to activate chemical processes in a resist that depend on diffusion.

T06296.title: thermal black
T06296.definition: A special type of carbon black produced by pyrolysis of gaseous hydrocarbons in a preheated chamber in the absence of air. Thermal black consists of relatively large individual spheres (\(100{-}500\ \rm{nm}\) diameter) and aggregates of a small number of pseudospherical particles. The preferred alignment of the layer planes is parallel to the surface of the spheres.

14099.title: thermal bleaching
14099.definition: Loss of absorption by the colour centres because of heating of the solid semiconductor or insulator.

T06297.title: thermal column
T06297.definition: A large body of moderator, adjacent to or inside a reactor to provide thermal neutrons for experiments.

T06298.title: thermal conductance
T06298.definition: Heat flow rate divided by the temperature difference.

T06300.title: thermal conductivity detector
T06300.definition: In general, two cells arranged in a bridge configuration detect the change in thermal conductivity of the gas at the output of the column. This detector is sensitive to any substance with thermal conductivity different from that of the carrier gas. The lowest detectable limit is between \(0.5\) and \(100\ \rm{ppmv}\). The linear dynamic range is of the order of \(10^{3}\). This type of detector is often used for measuring components at relatively high concentrations.

T06299.title: thermal conductivity
T06299.definition: Tensor quantity relating the heat flux, \(J_{q}\), to the temperature gradient, \(J_{q}=- \lambda \ \nabla T\).

12313.title: thermal curve
12313.definition: Any graph of any combination of property, time, temperature derived from a thermal analysis technique.

08696.title: thermal diffusion depth
08696.definition: In photoacoustic spectroscopy, \(L = \sqrt{(D/\pi f)}\), where \(D\) is thermal diffusivity and \(f\) is modulation frequency of the electromagnetic radiation.

08697.title: thermal diffusivity
08697.definition: Thermal conductivity divided by the product of the specific heat and the density.

08556.title: thermal dispersion
08556.definition: Procedures whereby an aerosol is produced at a high temperature, for example by sparks, arcs, furnaces, lasers, cathodic sputtering or electron-beam.

10203.title: thermal extraction
10203.definition: Release of volatile compounds from a sample by heat.

09942.title: thermal field-flow fractionation
09942.definition: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is created by a temperature difference across the channel.

12807.title: thermal history
12807.definition: Thermal treatment a polymer material has experienced before its characterisation or measurement of its properties.

08877.title: thermal injection
08877.definition: Charge carrier injection by a thermally activated processes.

T06303.title: thermal ionization
T06303.definition: Takes place when an atom or molecule interacts with a heated surface or is in a gaseous environment at high temperature. Examples of the latter may be a capillary arc plasma, a microwave plasma or an inductively coupled plasma.

12808.title: thermal lag
12808.definition: Delay of the response of a system to a change in temperature.

T06304.title: thermal lensing
T06304.definition: A technique that determines the alteration in the refractive index of a medium as a result of the temperature rise in the path of a laser beam absorbed by the medium. The lens produced (usually divergent) causes a change (usually a decrease) in the irradiance measured along the laser beam axis.

T06307.title: thermal neutrons
T06307.definition: Neutrons in thermal equilibrium with the medium in which they exist, in general at room temperature.

08557.title: thermal volatilization
08557.definition: Process in glow-discharge atomic emission spectroscopy in which sample volatilization occurs by heating due to sample bombardment with argon ions.

08698.title: thermal wave decay coefficient
08698.definition: Reciprocal of the thermal diffusion depth (\(L\)). \(a_{\rm{s}} = 1/L\).

12314.title: thermally stimulated current
12314.definition: Electrical current observed during heating and caused by the thermally initiated relaxation of the frozen-in electrical polarization of a sample.

12315.title: thermally stimulated depolarisation
12315.definition: Relaxation of frozen-in electrical polarization caused by a temperature increase.

T06306.title: thermally-induced transition
T06306.definition: A transition that is induced by a change in temperature.

09297.title: thermionic work function
09297.definition: Parameter describing the apparent work function of a solid that controls the electronic current density, \(J\), emitted from a conductor at temperature \(T\). \(W = -kT\ln(J/AT^{2})\), where \(k\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(A\) is the Richardson constant.

12316.title: thermo- technique
12316.definition: Indicating the use of changing temperature during the experiment, when in the name of a thermal analysis technique.

T06309.title: thermoacoustimetry
T06309.definition: A technique in which the characteristics of imposed acoustic waves are measured as a function of temperature after passing through a substance (and/or its reaction product(s)) whilst the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program.

12317.title: thermoanalytical
12317.definition: Of, or pertaining to, thermal analysis.

T06312.title: thermochromism
T06312.definition: A thermally induced transformation of a molecular structure or of a system (e.g. of a solution), thermally reversible, that produces a spectral change, typically, but not necessarily, of visible colour.

T06313.title: thermocouple
T06313.definition: A device based on the thermoelectric effect, by which two junctions between dissimilar conductors (metallic or heavily doped semiconductors) kept at different temperatures generate an electric potential.

12318.title: thermodiffractometry
12318.definition: A technique where the X-ray diffraction of the sample is measured.

T06314.title: thermodilatometry
T06314.definition: A technique in which a dimension of a substance under negligible load is measured as a function of temperature while the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program. Linear thermodilatometry and volume thermodilatometry are distinguished on the basis of the dimensions measured.

T06316.title: thermodynamic control
T06316.definition: The term characterizes conditions that lead to reaction products in a proportion governed by the equilibrium constant for their interconversion and/or for the interconversion of reaction intermediates formed in or after the rate-limiting step. (Some workers prefer to describe this phenomenon as 'equilibrium control'.)

T06319.title: thermodynamic isotope effect
T06319.definition:
The effect of isotopic substitution on an equilibrium constant is referred to as a thermodynamic (or equilibrium) isotope effect. For example, the effect of isotopic substitution in reactant A that participates in the equilibrium: \[\rm{A}+\rm{B}\rightleftharpoons \rm{C}\] is the ratio \(\frac{K^{\rm{l}}}{K^{\rm{h}}}\) of the equilibrium constant for the reaction in which A contains the light isotope to that in which it contains the heavy isotope. The ratio can be expressed as the equilibrium constant for the isotopic exchange reaction: \[\rm{A}^{\rm{l}}+\rm{C}^{\rm{h}}\rightleftharpoons \rm{A}^{\rm{h}}+\rm{C}^{\rm{l}}\] in which reactants such as B that are not isotopically substituted do not appear. The potential energy surfaces of isotopic molecules are identical to a high degree of approximation, so thermodynamic isotope effects can only arise from the effect of isotopic mass on the nuclear motions of the reactants and products, and can be expressed quantitatively in terms of partition function ratios for nuclear motion: \[\frac{K^{\rm{l}}}{K^{\rm{h}}} = \frac{(Q_{\rm{nuc}}^{\rm{l}}/Q_{\rm{nuc}}^{\rm{h}})_{\rm{C}}}
{(Q_{\rm{nuc}}^{\rm{l}}/Q_{\rm{nuc}}^{\rm{h}})_{\rm{A}}}\] Although the nuclear partition function is a product of the translational, rotational and vibrational partition functions, the isotope effect is determined almost entirely by the last named, specifically by vibrational modes involving motion of isotopically different atoms. In the case of light atoms (i.e. protium vs. deuterium or tritium) at moderate temperatures, the isotope effect is dominated by zero-point energy differences.

T06321.title: thermodynamic temperature
T06321.definition: Base quantity in the system of quantities upon which SI is based.

T06315.title: thermodynamically equivalent sphere
T06315.definition: A sphere, impenetrable to other spheres, displaying the same excluded volume as an actual polymer molecule.

T06322.title: thermoelectrometry
T06322.definition: A technique in which an electrical characteristic of a substance (and/or its reaction product(s)) is measured as a function of temperature whilst the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program. The most common measurements are of resistance, conductance or capacitance.

12319.title: thermogravimetric analysis
12319.definition: A technique where the mass of the sample is measured, also known as thermogravimetry.

T06324.title: thermogravimetry
T06324.definition: A technique in which the mass of a substance (and/or its reaction product(s)) is measured as a function of temperature whilst the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program.

T06325.title: thermoluminescence
T06325.definition: Luminescence arising from a reaction between species trapped in a rigid matrix and released as a result of an increase in temperature.

12810.title: thermoluminescence analysis
12810.definition: Technique that monitors the light that is emitted from a sample against time or temperature while the temperature of the sample, in a specified atmosphere, is heated in a controlled manner.

T06326.title: thermolysis
T06326.definition: The uncatalysed cleavage of one or more covalent bonds resulting from exposure of a compound to a raised temperature, or a process in which such cleavage is an essential part.

T06327.title: thermomagnetometry
T06327.definition: A technique in which a magnetic characteristic of a substance (and/or its reaction product(s)) is measured as a function of temperature whilst the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program.

12320.title: thermomanometry
12320.definition: A technique where the gas pressure is measured.

12321.title: thermomechanical analysis
12321.definition: A technique where the deformation of the sample is measured under constant load.

T06328.title: thermomechanical measurement
T06328.definition: A technique in which the deformation of a substance (and/or its reaction product(s)) under non-oscillatory load is measured as a function of temperature whilst the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program.

12812.title: thermomechanical properties
12812.definition: The temperature dependence of deformability or mechanical properties of a polymer sample.

T06331.title: thermometric titration
T06331.definition: An analytical method in which one reactant (the titrant) is added continuously or stepwise to an adiabatic or isoperibol vessel containing another reactant. The enthalpy change(s) of the ensuing reaction(s) causes a temperature change which, when plotted versus volume of titrant, may be used to find the titration endpoint(s). This is the preferred term for experiments producing plots of temperature versus volume of titrant in which the main goal is a quantitative determination. Nonetheless, when a calorimetric vessel is used, such that the heat capacity is known, thermodynamic parameters may also be estimated from such experiments. An acceptable synonym in that case is enthalpimetric titration. The use of the adjective thermometric is justified because of widespread historical and current usage, and because a titration of necessity implies a chemical reaction. The term  'thermometric enthalpy titration' has been used, but is not recommended. A method in which the titrant is a catalyst for an indicator reaction that occurs after the endpoint for the analyte reaction should be called a thermometric titration with catalytic endpoint detection, not a 'catalytic thermometric titration'.

12322.title: thermomicroscopy
12322.definition: A technique where the optical properties of the sample are observed and measured through a microscope.

T06332.title: thermoparticulate analysis
T06332.definition: A thermoanalytical technique in which the release of particulate matter from a substance (and/or its reaction product(s)) is measured as a function of temperature whilst the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program.

T06333.title: thermophile
T06333.definition: An organism that can tolerate high temperatures and that grows optimally at temperatures above \(45\ ^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\).

14100.title: thermophotocatalysis
14100.definition: A photocatalytic phenomenon occurring when the system is also heated by the ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation.

T06335.title: thermopile
T06335.definition: Several thermocouples connected in series to increase the magnitude of the electric potential.

T06336.title: thermoptometry
T06336.definition: A technique in which an optical characteristic of a substance (and/or its reaction product(s)) is measured as a function of temperature whilst the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program. Measurements of total light, light of specific wavelength(s), refractive index and luminescence lead to thermophotometry, thermospectrometry, thermorefractometry and thermoluminescence, respectively; observation under the microscope leads to thermomicroscopy.

TT07531.title: thermoreversible gel
TT07531.definition: Swollen network in which the junction points are thermally reversible.

TT07600.title: thermoreversible junction point
TT07600.definition: Junction point in a polymer network that can be destroyed and formed reversibly by a change of temperature.

TT07573.title: thermoreversible network
TT07573.definition: Reversible network that forms or breaks up as the temperature is changed.

TT07168.title: thermosetting polymer
TT07168.definition: Prepolymer in a soft solid or viscous state that changes irreversibly into an infusible, insoluble polymer network by curing.

T06337.title: thermosonimetry
T06337.definition: A technique in which the sound emitted by a substance (and/or its reaction product(s)) is measured as a function of temperature whilst the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program.

12323.title: thermospectrometry
12323.definition: A group of techniques where a spectrum of the sample is measured.

T06338.title: thermosphere
T06338.definition: Atmospheric shell extending from the top of the mesosphere to outer space. It is a region of more or less steadily increasing temperature with height, starting at \(70\) or \(80\ \rm{km}\). It includes the exosphere and most or all of the ionosphere (not the D region).

TT06897.title: thermotropic mesophase
TT06897.definition: A mesophase formed by heating a solid or cooling an isotropic liquid, or by heating or cooling a thermodynamically stable mesophase.

T06342.title: thickness of diffusion layer
T06342.definition: The distance from the electrode where the ratio \[\frac{c\,-\,c_{\rm{e}}}{c_{0}\,-\,c_{\rm{e}}}\] reaches a given value. (\(c_{\rm{e}}\) is the interfacial concentration, \(c\) is the concentration, \(c_{0}\) is the value in the bulk solution.) If this ratio is selected as, say, 0.99 the corresponding thickness of the diffusion layer is denoted by \(\delta_{0.99}\).

T06343.title: thickness of electrical double layer
T06343.definition: The length characterizing the decrease with distance of the potential in the double layer = characteristic Debye length in the corresponding electrolyte solution = \(\kappa^{-1}\):\[\frac{1}{\kappa } = \sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\varepsilon_{0}RT}{F^{2}\sum _{i}c_{i}z_{i}^{2} }}\]  \[\frac{1}{\kappa } = \sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}RT}{4\pi F^{2}\sum _{i}c_{i}z_{i}^{2} }}\](rationalized four-quantity system)  (three-quantity electrostatic system) where \(\varepsilon\) = static permittivity = \(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\varepsilon_{0}\), \(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\) = relative static permittivity of solution; \(\varepsilon_{0}\) = permittivity of vacuum, \(R\) = gas constant, \(T\) = thermodynamic temperature, \(F\) = Faraday constant, \(z_{\rm{i}}\) = concentration of species \(i\), \(z_{\rm{i}}\) = ionic charge on species \(i\).

T06344.title: thickness of reaction layer
T06344.definition: When a kinetic current flows, the concentrations of the electroactive substance B and its precursor C at very small distances from the electrode surface are influenced both by mass transfer and by the finite rate of establishment of the chemical equilibrium. As the distance from the electrode surface increases, the chemical equilibrium is more and more nearly attained. The thickness of the reaction layer is the distance from the electrode surface beyond which deviations from the chemical equilibrium between C and B are taken to be negligibly small.

12135.title: thigmotaxis
12135.definition: Movement of an organism toward or away from a mechanical stimulus, physical contact, or spatial discontinuity, as in movement away from touch by a physical stimulus or exploring close to a wall.

T06345.title: thin film
T06345.definition: A film whose thickness is of the order of a characteristic scale or smaller. Since a film may 'look' operationally thin or thick, according to the procedure applied, it is also recommended that the measurement procedure employed be specified (e.g. ellipsometrically thin film, optically thin film, etc.). It is recommended that the physical specification of the film thickness be used, whenever possible (e.g. thick compared to the electron mean free path, thin compared to the optical wavelength, etc.)

10277.title: thin film format
10277.definition: Solid-phase microextraction where the sorbent is in the form of a thin film on a support or self supported membrane.

09391.title: thin target
09391.definition: In energetic-ion analysis and Rutherford backscattering spectrometry, sample whose thickness is sufficiently small that the variation in energy of particles backscattered from atoms of each constitutive element is small with respect to the system resolution.

T06346.title: thin-layer chromatography
T06346.definition: Chromatography carried out in a layer of adsorbent spread on a support e.g. a glass plate.

10204.title: thin-layer headspace analysis
10204.definition: Dynamic headspace analysis of a flowing sample solution in the form of a thin film on the surface of a heated tube.

T06347.title: thio
T06347.definition: This prefix properly denotes replacement of an oxygen by a sulfur, e.g. $\ce{PhC(=S)NH2}$, thiobenzamide. See also entries prefixed thio-.

T06348.title: thioacetals

T06350.title: thioaldehyde S-oxides
T06350.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RC(=S=O)H}$. (Also known by the disapproved term 'sulfines' which includes thioaldehyde S-oxides and thioketone S-oxides).

T06349.title: thioaldehydes
T06349.definition: Compounds in which the oxygen of an aldehyde has been replaced by divalent sulfur, $\ce{RC(=S)H}$, e.g. $\ce{CH3CH2C(=S)H propanethial}$.

T06351.title: thioanhydrides
T06351.definition: Compounds having the structure acyl-S-acyl. Also called diacylsulfanes, e.g. $\ce{CH3C(=O)SC(=S)CH2CH3}$ acetic thiopropanoic thioanhydride.

T06352.title: thiocarboxylic acids
T06352.definition: Compounds in which one or both oxygens of a carboxy group have been replaced by divalent sulfur $\ce{RC(=O)SH}$ or $\ce{RC(=S)OH}$ monothiocarboxylic acids, $\ce{RC(=S)SH}$ dithiocarboxylic acids.

T06353.title: thiocyanates
T06353.definition: Salts and esters of thiocyanic acid $\ce{HSC#N}$, e.g. $\ce{CH3SC#N}$ methyl thiocyanate.

T06357.title: thioketone S-oxides
T06357.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{R2C=S=O}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$). (Also known by the disapproved term 'sulfines' which comprises thioaldehyde S-oxides and thioketone S-oxides.)

T06356.title: thioketones
T06356.definition: Compounds in which the oxygen of a ketone has been replaced by divalent sulfur $\ce{R2C=S}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$), e.g. $\ce{CH3C(=S)CH2CH3}$ butane-2-thione.

T06358.title: thiolates
T06358.definition: Derivatives of thiols, in which a metal (or other cation) replaces the hydrogen attached to sulfur, e.g. $\ce{CH3S^{-}Na^{+}}$ sodium methanethiolate.

T06359.title: thiols
T06359.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{RSH}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$), e.g. $\ce{MeCH2SH}$ ethanethiol. Also known by the term 'mercaptans' (abandoned by IUPAC).

T06361.title: third body
T06361.definition: A species, other than the reactant itself, which brings about the energization of a molecule that can undergo a unimolecular process, or brings about a combination reaction between atoms or radicals. In the latter case a third body is also called a chaperon.

TT07532.title: thixotropic gel
TT07532.definition: Gel which has a reduced viscosity on the application of a finite shear but which recovers its original viscosity when the shear is discontinued.

11301.title: thoracic duct
11301.definition: Largest of the lymphatic vessels; it conducts lymph from its origin in the abdomen to the venous circulation at the junction of the left subclavian and jugular veins.

12136.title: thoracic spine
12136.definition: Portion of the vertebral column of the upper back, between the cervical spine and lumbar spine, in humans consisting of 12 vertebrae designated T1 to T12.

13984.title: threadable ring
13984.definition: Key part of a macrocyclic component: molecular ring (cycle) large enough to be threaded onto a linear subchain of a threading component.

13985.title: threading component
13985.definition: Molecule with at least one linear section onto which at least one macrocyclic component is threaded.

08432.title: three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
08432.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in which data are collected in three time domains.

09081.title: three-electrode cell
09081.definition: Electrochemical cell with a working electrode, reference electrode, and auxiliary electrode.Schematic of a three-electrode cell. 1 - working electrode, 2 - reference electrode, 3 - auxiliary electrode. The potential between 1 and 2 is set while passing and measuring current between 1 and 3.

16136.title: threshold
16136.definition: Dose or exposure concentration below which a defined effect will not occur.

T06366.title: threshold energy
T06366.definition: Potential energy gap between reactants and the transition state, sometimes involving the zero point energies, but usually not.

TT06915.title: threshold limit value
TT06915.definition: The concentration in air to which it is believed that most workers can be exposed daily without an adverse effect (i.e., effectively, the threshold between safe and dangerous concentrations). The values were established (and are revised annually) by the ACGIH and are time-weighted concentrations (TWA) for a 7- or 8-h workday and 40-h workweek, and thus are related to chronic effects. A short-term exposure limit (STEL) is defined as a 15-min TWA exposure, which should not be exceeded at any time during a workday even if the 8-h TWA is within the TLV-TWA.

16137.title: threshold limit value–ceiling
16137.definition: As defined by ACGIH, concentration of a potentially toxic substance that should not be exceeded during any part of the working exposure.

16138.title: threshold limit value–short-term exposure limit
16138.definition: As defined by ACGIH, concentration to which it is believed that workers can be exposed continuously for a short period of time without suffering from (1) irritation, (2) chronic or irreversible tissue damage, or (3) narcosis of sufficient degree to increase the likelihood of accidental injury, impair self-rescue or materially reduce work efficiency, and provided that the daily TLV-TWA is not exceeded.

16139.title: threshold limit value–time-weighted average
16139.definition: As defined by ACGIH, time-weighted average concentration for a conventional \(\pu{8\!\mbox{-}h}\) workday and a \(\pu{40\!\mbox{-}h}\) workweek, to which it is believed nearly all workers may be repeatedly exposed, day after day, without adverse effect.

16140.title: threshold of toxicological concern
16140.definition: Human exposure threshold value for a group of chemicals below which there should be no appreciable risk to human health.

12137.title: threshold potential
12137.definition: Level of depolarization that must be reached to trigger an action potential in an excitable cell.

15094.title: threshold theory
15094.definition: Theory that, for a given substance, no toxic effect can occur below a defined low dose.

15093.title: threshold-effect concentration
15093.definition: Concentration calculated as the geometric mean of no-observed-effect concentration (NOEC) and lowest-observed-effect concentration (LOEC).

11302.title: thrombocytopenia
11302.definition: Abnormally low concentration of platelets (thrombocytes) in the blood.

13732.title: thromboxane
13732.definition: Any of several substances (predominantly thromboxanes A2 and B2) synthesized by platelets from arachidonic acid precursor, that cause vasoconstriction of vascular and bronchial smooth muscle and facilitates platelet aggregation.

12138.title: thrombus
12138.definition: Clot in the cardiovasculature formed from components of the blood, which may be attached to the vessel wall and (or) occlusive.

T06367.title: through-bond electron transfer
