T06367.definition: Intramolecular electron transfer for which the relevant electronic interaction between the donor and acceptor sites is mediated by through-bond interaction, i.e. via the covalent bonds interconnecting these sites, as opposed to through-space interaction.

08214.title: through-conjugation
08214.definition: Phenomenon whereby electrons can be delocalized from any of three (or more) groups to any other.

T06369.title: through-space electron transfer
T06369.definition: Electron transfer for which the relevant electronic interaction between the donor and acceptor sites is mediated either by direct orbital overlap or by superexchange interaction via intervening molecular entities not covalently bound to the donor or acceptor sites.

13733.title: thrush
13733.definition: Oral infection with Candida albicans, often in patients with immunosuppression.

13735.title: thymic atrophy
13735.definition: Involution of the thymus gland leading to a diminished capacity to generate new T cells.

13736.title: thymic education
13736.definition: Process by which T cells, developing in the thymus, are screened for potentially harmful self-reactive T cells (which are removed), while potentially beneficial T cells are promoted.

13737.title: thymoma
13737.definition: Rare, usually benign, tumor arising from tissue of the thymus gland.

11303.title: thymus
11303.definition: Pyramid-shaped organ in the thoracic or cervical region of mammals, composed of lymphatic tissue in which minute concentric bodies (thymic corpuscles, the remnants of epithelial structures) are found.

13738.title: thymus-dependent antigen
13738.definition: Antigen that requires the participation of T lymphocytes to elicit an immune response in B lymphocytes.

13739.title: thymus-independent antigen
13739.definition: Antigen that does not require the participation of T lymphocytes to elicit an immune response in B cells.

13740.title: thyroglobulin
13740.definition: Glycoprotein secreted by thyroid follicular cells that is a major autoantigen in autoimmune diseases of the thyroid.

11304.title: thyroglossal duct
11304.definition: Connection in the embryo between the site of initiation of development of the thyroid gland and its final location in the neck.

11305.title: thyroid gland
11305.definition: Bilobar endocrine gland, located below the prominence of cartilage surrounding the larynx (the Adam’s apple), that produces and secretes the hormones triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxin (T4), and calcitonin.

13743.title: thyroid peroxidase
13743.definition: Thyroid enzyme that is a major autoantigen in autoimmune diseases of the thyroid.

11307.title: thyroid stimulating hormone
11307.definition: Pituitary hormone that stimulates the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine (T4), and then triiodothyronine (T3).

13742.title: thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor
13742.definition: Main autoantigenic target in patients with Graves disease.

16141.title: thyrotoxicosis
16141.definition: Condition resulting from excessive concentrations of thyroid hormones, as in hyperthyroidism, characterized by bulging eyes and rapid heart rate.

T06371.title: TICT emission
T06371.definition: Electronic emission emanating from a TICT state.

T06372.title: TICT state
T06372.definition: The acronym derives from Twisted Internal Charge Transfer state, proposed to be responsible for strongly Stokes-shifted fluorescence from certain aromatics, particularly in a polar medium.

16142.title: tidal volume
16142.definition: Quantity of air or test gas that is inhaled and exhaled during one respiratory cycle.

T06373.title: tie molecule
T06373.definition: A molecule that connects at least two different crystals.

15367.title: tie-line
15367.definition: Straight line connecting compositions of independent coexisting phases in equilibrium on a phase diagram.

15095.title: tiered testing
15095.definition: Structured approach to assessment of the fate and effects of substances, where a tier of relatively simple tests is used initially to select substances of concern and to define their toxicity. If the information from these tests is inadequate for regulatory decisions, further more complex tests (higher tier tests) may be required. For example, under a tiered structure, testing might progress from acute studies to chronic laboratory studies to field studies.

T06376.title: time constant
T06376.definition: If the output of a detector changes exponentially with time, the time required for it to change from its initial value by the fraction \(1 - \exp(-t/\tau _{\rm{c}})\) (for \(t=\tau _{\rm{c}}\)) of the final value, is called the time constant.

08433.title: time domain
08433.definition: Condition in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy where the independent variable of all functions is time.

08434.title: time domain nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
08434.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy run at low magnetic field strengths where data analysis is performed directly on the free induction decay, often through the extraction of relaxation time constants

T06380.title: time of centrifugation
T06380.definition: The time difference from switching on until switching off. The time for deceleration is not included.

T06383.title: time
T06383.definition: The time in which a certain viscosity or yield stress is reached after discontinuation of a shear. These times depend on the values of viscosity or yield stress chosen by the experimenter.

T06377.title: time-correlated single photon counting
T06377.definition: A technique for the measurement of the time histogram of a sequence of photons with respect to a periodic event, e.g. a flash from a repetitive nanosecond lamp or a CW operated laser (mode locked laser). The essential part is a time-to-amplitude-converter (TAC) which transforms the arrival time between a start and a stop pulse into a voltage. Sometimes called single photon timing.

TT07484.title: time-dependent density functional theory
TT07484.definition: Methods for computing accurate excitation energies at a low computational cost in large molecular species within the time-dependent scheme and the density functional theory. It is the only available DFT-based method for computing electronic excitation energies.

T06378.title: time-dependent stoichiometry
T06378.definition: A state in which if intermediates are formed in significant amounts during the course of a reaction, the overall stoichiometric equation does not apply throughout.

T06379.title: time-independent stoichiometry
T06379.definition: A state in which the stoichiometric equation applies throughout the course of the reaction.

15096.title: time-independent test
15096.definition: Acute toxicity test with no predetermined temporal endpoint.

T06382.title: time-of-flight mass spectrometer
T06382.definition: An arrangement using the fact that ions of different mass/charge need different times to travel through a certain distance in a field-free region after they have all been initially given the same translational energy.

08558.title: time-resolved laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy
08558.definition: Measurement method of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy in which the emitted radiation is monitored with time resolution sufficiently high to resolve different stages in the lifetime of the laser-induced plasma.

T06384.title: time-resolved microwave conductivity
T06384.definition: Technique allowing the quantitative and qualitative detection of radiation-induced changes in the real, \(\Delta \rm{Re}\sigma\), and imaginary, \(\Delta \rm{Im}\sigma\), components of the conductivity of a medium by time-resolved measurement of changes in the microwave absorption resulting from the formation of mobile charges or from changes in the dipole moment or polarizability of molecules on excitation.

T06385.title: time-resolved spectroscopy
T06385.definition: The recording of spectra at a series of time intervals after the excitation of the system with a light pulse (or other perturbation) of appropriately short duration.

12813.title: time–temperature superposition principle
12813.definition: Principle stating that the value of a viscoelastic property measured at a given temperature, after a given length of time or at a given frequency, is equal to the value of the property at a different temperature after a length of time or at a frequency equal to the given length of time or given frequency multiplied by a shift factor, \(a_{T}\) , with the value of the shift factor being independent of length of the time or frequency.

10189.title: time-weighted average sampling
10189.definition: A passive sampling or active sampling strategy over a relatively long time, during which the amount of analyte(s) extracted is proportional to its average (mean) concentration over that time.

16143.title: time-weighted-average-exposure
16143.definition: Concentration in the exposure medium at each measured time interval multiplied by that time interval and divided by the total time of observation.

T06375.title: time
T06375.definition: Base quantity in the system of quantities upon which SI is based.

12140.title: tinnitus
12140.definition: Continual noise in an ear, such as ringing, buzzing, roaring, or clicking.

09210.title: tip enhanced raman spectroscopy
09210.definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy combining surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy and scanning using an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope to produce maps of a surface.

08699.title: tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy
08699.definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy combining surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy and scanning using an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope to give complementary maps of a surface.

09652.title: tissue
09652.definition: Group of biological cells that perform a specific function.

16144.title: tissue dose
16144.definition: Amount of a substance or physical agent (radiation) absorbed by a tissue.

13744.title: tissue transglutaminase
13744.definition: Main target of autoantibodies in celiac disease.

13745.title: titer
13745.definition: Reciprocal of the highest dilution of a titration of an antigen with an antibody that gives a measurable effect (e.g., agglutination), and thus an empirical measure of the avidity of an antibody.

09051.title: titrand
09051.definition: Reactant solution being titrated in a titration.

T06386.title: titrant
T06386.definition: The solution containing the active agent with which a titration is made.

T06387.title: titration
T06387.definition: The process of determining the quantity of a substance A by adding measured increments of substance B, with which it reacts (almost always as a standardized solution called the titrant, but also by electrolytic generation, as in coulometric titration) with provision for some means of recognizing (indicating) the endpoint at which essentially all of A has reacted. If the endpoint coincides with the addition of the exact chemical equivalence, it is called the equivalence point or stoichiometric or theoretical endpoint, thus allowing the amount of A to be found from known amounts of B added up to this point, the reacting weight ratio of A to B being known from stoichiometry or otherwise. Terms for varieties of titration can reflect the nature of the reaction between A and B. Thus, there are acid–base, complexometric, chelatometric, oxidation–reduction, and precipitation titrations. Additionally, the term can reflect the nature of the titrant, such as acidimetric, alkalimetric, and iodometric titrations as well as coulometric titrations, in which the titrant is generated electrolytically rather than being added as a standard solution.

T06388.title: titration curve
T06388.definition: A plot of a variable related to a relevant concentration (activity) as the ordinate vs. some measure of the amount of titrant, usually titration volume (titre) as the abscissa. If the variable is linearly related to concentrations, such as the electrical conductance or the photometric absorbance, the term linear titration curve is used. When a logarithmic expression of the concentration or activity is used, such as the \(\rm{pH}\), \(\mathrm{pM}\), or the electrical potential in \(\mathrm{mV}\), the curve is referred to as a logarithmic titration curve.

T06389.title: titration error
T06389.definition: The difference in the amount of titrant, or the corresponding difference in the amount of substance being titrated, represented by the expression: (end-point value - equivalence-point value).

T06391.title: titre
T06391.definition: The reacting strength of a standard solution, usually expressed as the weight (mass) of the substance equivalent to \(1\ \rm{cm}^{3}\) of the solution.

09052.title: titrimetric analysis
09052.definition: Methods of quantitative analysis employing titration.

16145.title: tolerable daily intake
16145.definition: Estimate of the amount of a potentially harmful substance (e.g., contaminant) in food or drinking water that can be ingested daily over a lifetime without appreciable health risk.

16146.title: tolerable risk
16146.definition: Probability of suffering disease or injury that can, for the time being, be tolerated, taking into account the associated benefits, and assuming that the risk is minimized by appropriate control procedures.

16147.title: tolerable weekly intake
16147.definition: Estimate of the amount of a potentially harmful substance (e.g., a contaminant) in food or drinking water that can be ingested weekly over a lifetime without appreciable health risk.

08134.title: tolerance
08134.definition: Difference between upper and lower tolerance limits.

15097.title: tolerance index
15097.definition: Quotient of an adequate parameter acquired under treated and control environments, multiplied by \(\pu{100}\), thus: \[\rm{TI} = (\rm{parameter\ treated}/\rm{parameter\ control}) \times 100\]

08136.title: tolerance limit
08136.definition: Specified upper or lower bound of permissible quantity values of a property.

13747.title: toll-like receptor
13747.definition: Member of a family of pattern recognition receptors involved in the detection of structures associated with pathogens or damaged host tissues.

12141.title: tomography
12141.definition: Construction of an image of a three-dimensional structure from a series of planar sections obtained with penetrating waves.

16148.title: tonic
16148.definition:
Characterized by tension, especially muscular tension.
Medical preparation that increases or restores normal muscular tension.

11308.title: tonsil
11308.definition: Small, rounded mass of tissue, especially of lymphoid tissue; generally used to designate one of the paired palatine tonsils.

15098.title: top-down ecotoxicological study
15098.definition: Approach to investigating ecotoxicological effects that starts with a determination of the presence and nature of any adverse effects via responses at community and ecosystem levels of organization rather than the suborganismal levels of organization.

09580.title: top-down patterning
09580.definition: Pattern formation using lithographic (also embossing) methods.

09786.title: top-down proteomics
09786.definition: Approach to identify proteins and characterise their amino acid sequences or post-translational modifications either by direct mass spectrometric analysis of an ionised protein molecule or by sequential combination of protein/peptide fragmentation in the ion source or mass analyser with ion trapping mass spectrometers.

09581.title: top-surface imaging
09581.definition: Lithographic process in which the exposed region of resist is silylated and the image then formed through reactive oxygen etch.

09579.title: topcoat
09579.definition: Protective layer spun directly on top of a resist.

16149.title: topical
16149.definition: Applied directly to the surface of the body.

TT06846.title: topical effect
TT06846.definition: Consequence of application of a substance to the surface of the body which occurs at the point of application.

15423.title: topochemical polymerisation
15423.definition: Solid-state polymerization, resulting in the formation of a polymer having essentially the same crystal structure as that of the monomer.

T06395.title: topochemical reaction
T06395.definition: A reversible or irreversible reaction that involves the introduction of a guest species into a host structure and that results in significant structural modifications to the host, for example, the breakage of bonds. Example: The insertion of lithium at \(50\,^{\unicode{x26ac}}\rm{C}\) into the spinel $\ce{Li[Mn2]O4}$ with symmetry \(F\,\rm{d3m}\) to yield a layered structure with symmetry \(P\bar{3}\,\rm{m1}\).

09298.title: topographic contrast
09298.definition: Contrast in a surface map or image arising from the topography of the sample surface.

11525.title: topological index
11525.definition: A numerical value associated with chemical constitution for correlation of chemical structure with various physical properties, chemical reactivity or biological activity. The numerical basis for topological indices is provided (depending on how a molecular graph is converted into a numerical value) by either the adjacency matrix or the topological distance matrix. In the latter the topological distance between two vertices is the number of edges in the shortest path between these.

11526.title: topological polar surface area
11526.definition: An approximation to polar surface area that is calculated from the 2D structure.

T06396.title: topomerization
T06396.definition: The identity reaction leading to exchange of the positions of identical ligands. The indistinguishable molecular entities involved are called topomers. For example in the reaction below the two identical ligating atoms $\ce{N_{\rm{a}}}$ and $\ce{N_{\rm{b}}}$ are interchanged by rotation about the $\ce{C-aryl}$ bond but may be identified by NMR spectroscopy. This is a degenerate isomerization.

T06399.title: topotactic transition
T06399.definition: A transition in which the crystal lattice of the product phase shows one or more crystallographically equivalent, orientational relationships to the crystal lattice of the parent phase. Example: Transitions in which the anionic array is unchanged during the transition but cation reorganization occurs, as in:

T06400.title: torque
T06400.definition: Sum of moments of forces not acting along the same line.

T06401.title: torquoselectivity
T06401.definition: The preference for 'inward' or 'outward' rotation of substituents in conrotatory or disrotatory electrocyclic ring opening reactions.

16150.title: torsade de pointes
16150.definition: Potentially lethal form of ventricular tachycardia following chronic abuse of alcohol and mainly due to hypomagnesemia.

T06406.title: torsion angle
T06406.definition: In a chain of atoms A-B-C-D, the dihedral angle between the plane containing the atoms A,B,C and that containing B,C,D. In a Newman projection the torsion angle is the angle (having an absolute value between 0° and 180°) between bonds to two specified (fiducial) groups, one from the atom nearer (proximal) to the observer and the other from the further (distal) atom. The torsion angle between groups A and D is then considered to be positive if the bond A-B is rotated in a clockwise direction through less than 180° in order that it may eclipse the bond C-D: a negative torsion angle requires rotation in the opposite sense. Stereochemical arrangements corresponding to torsion angles between 0° and ±90° are called syn (s), those corresponding to torsion angles between ±90° and 180° anti (a). Similarly, arrangements corresponding to torsion angles between 30° and 150° or between -30° and -150° are called clinal (c) and those between 0° and 30° or 150° and 180° are called periplanar (p). The two types of terms can be combined so as to define four ranges of torsion angle; 0° to 30° synperiplanar (sp); 30° to 90° and -30° to -90° synclinal (sc); 90° to 150°, and -90° to -150° anticlinal (ac); ±150° to 180° antiperiplanar (ap).  The synperiplanar conformation is also known as the syn- or cis-conformation; antiperiplanar as anti or trans and synclinal as gauche or skew. For macromolecular usage the symbols \(\rm{T}\), \(\rm{C}\), \(\rm{G}^{+}\), \(\rm{G}^{-}\), \(\rm{A}^{+}\) and \(\rm{A}^{-}\) are recommended (ap, sp, +sc, -sc, +ac and -ac respectively).

12814.title: torsion pendulum
12814.definition: Device consisting of a disc or other body of large moment of inertia mounted on one end of a torsionally flexible elastic rod or wire, the other end of which is fixed.

T06403.title: torsional braid analysis
T06403.definition: A particular case of dynamic thermomechanometry in which the material is supported on a braid.

12815.title: torsional pendulum analysis
12815.definition: Dynamic mechanical analysis performed using a torsion pendulum.

T06404.title: torsional stereoisomers
T06404.definition: Stereoisomers that can be interconverted (actually or conceptually) by torsion about a bond axis. This includes E,Z-isomers of alkenes, atropisomers and rotamers.

12142.title: torticollis
12142.definition: Spasmodic contraction of neck muscles drawing the head to one side with the chin pointing to the other side.

T06409.title: total consumption time
T06409.definition: The time necessary to consume the prepared sample completely (in \(\mathrm{s}\)). It is equal to the volume of the prepared sample divided by the rate of fluid consumption.

08435.title: total correlation spectroscopy
08435.definition: Two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance homonuclear correlation experiment, which creates correlations between all protons within a given spin system, not just between geminal or vicinal protons as in COSY.

16151.title: total diet study
16151.definition:
Study designed to establish the pattern of pesticide residue intake by a person consuming a defined diet.
Study undertaken to show the range and amount of various foodstuffs in a typical diet or to estimate the total amount of a specific substance in a typical diet.

08700.title: total internal reflection
08700.definition: Internal reflection from a non-absorbing material at angles of incidence at or above the critical angle.

14198.title: total internal reflection fluorescence
14198.definition: Spectroscopic technique that discriminates between labeled molecules in the homogeneous phase and those interacting with binding partners immobilized at a surface.

T06410.title: total ion current
T06410.definition: (after mass analysis): The sum of the separate ion currents carried by the different ions contributing to the spectrum (this is sometimes called the reconstructed ion current).(before mass analysis): The sum of all the separate ion currents for ions of the same sign before mass analysis.

09299.title: total ion yield
09299.definition: Number of ions of both signs sputtered from a sample divided by the number of incident particles.

09964.title: total mobile phase volume
09964.definition: Retention volume of a sample component, the molecules of which are smaller than the smallest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.

15099.title: total organic carbon
15099.definition: Organic matter content of soil, sediment, or water determined by measurement of organic carbon as the ratio of mass of organic carbon/mass of solid or of water.

08137.title: total quality management
08137.definition: Organization-wide efforts to install a permanent climate in which an organization continuously improves its ability to deliver high-quality products and services to customers.

09440.title: total reflection of X-rays
09440.definition: Condition where the glancing angle for the incident X-rays is at or less than the critical angle and the X-rays are either reflected or absorbed in a region very close to the surface.

08765.title: total reflection X-ray fluorescence analysis
08765.definition: Measurement method of X-ray fluorescence analysis in which a collimated X-ray flux impinges on a smooth surface under a grazing angle; rendering total reflection is used to excite atoms in the top layers of the material for measurement of the amounts of elements.

09211.title: total reflection X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy
09211.definition: Measurement method in which an X-ray spectrometer is used to measure the energy distribution of fluorescence X-rays emitted from a surface irradiated by primary X-rays under the condition of total reflection.

10039.title: total retention time
10039.definition: Time between sample injection and the emergence of the peak maximum of the sample component of interest.

T06413.title: total retention volume
T06413.definition: The volume of mobile phase entering the column between sample injection and the emergence of the peak maximum of the sample component of interest, or the corresponding time. It includes the hold-up volume (time): \[t_{\rm{R}}=\frac{V_{\rm{R}}}{F_{\rm{c}}}\] where \(F_{c}\) is the mobile phase flow rate at column temperature.

08559.title: total sample consumption system
08559.definition: Liquid-sample introduction system able to achieve \(\pu{100\%}\) transport efficiency.

09359.title: total secondary-electron yield
09359.definition: Total number of electrons emitted from a sample divided by the total number of electrons incident at a given energy and angle of incidence. \(\sigma = \delta + \eta\), where \(\delta\) is the secondary-electron yield and \(\eta\) is the backscattering coefficient.

08436.title: total suppression of spinning sidebands
08436.definition: Technique to suppress spinning sidebands in solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy with cross polarization in magic angle spinning experiments.

16152.title: total terminal residue
16152.definition: Summation of levels of all the residues of a defined pesticide in a food.

TT06926.title: total velocity of the analyte
TT06926.definition:
The sum of electrophoretic velocity, \(
u_{m{ep}}\), of an ion and the electroosmotic velocity, \(
u _{m{eo}}\). \[
u_{m{tot}} = 
u_{m{ep}}\,+\,
u_{m{eo}}\] This quantity can be measured experimentally as the effective length of the capillary divided by the migration time (\(L_{m{eff}}/t_{m{m}}\)).

T06411.title: totally porous packing
T06411.definition: Packing in which the stationary phase permeates each porous particle.

09360.title: Tougaard background
09360.definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, intensity distribution of the background due to inelastic scattering obtained from the differential inelastic scattering cross section with respect to energy loss and the three-dimensional distribution of the emitting atoms in the surface region.

16153.title: toxemia
16153.definition:
Condition in which the blood contains toxins produced by body cells at a local source of infection or derived from the growth of microorganisms.
Pregnancy-related condition characterized by high blood pressure, swelling, and fluid retention, and proteins in the urine.

15100.title: toxic
15100.definition: Able to cause injury to living organisms as a result of physicochemical interaction.

16154.title: toxic dose
16154.definition: Amount of a substance that produces intoxication without lethal outcome.

13748.title: toxic epidermal necrolysis
13748.definition: A severe form of Stevens–Johnson syndrome with extensive detachment of the skin, often as a result of an allergic adverse drug reaction.

13749.title: toxic shock syndrome
13749.definition: Systemic reaction produced by the toxin derived from the bacterium Staphylococcus aureus; the toxin acts as a superantigen, which activates a high proportion of CD4+ T lymphocytes to produce cytokines.

12143.title: toxic substance
12143.definition: Substance causing injury to living organisms as a result of physicochemical interactions.

15101.title: toxic unit
15101.definition: Dose or concentration of a toxicant expressed in units of lethality such as units of \(\pu{LD_{50}}\) or \(\pu{LC_{50}}\).

16240.title: toxicant
16240.definition: This is the preferred term for a substance that is considered to be toxic under circumstances which are thought likely to happen.

T06414.title: toxicity
T06414.definition: Capacity to cause injury to a living organism defined with reference to the quantity of substance administered or absorbed, the way in which the substance is administered (inhalation, ingestion, topical application, injection) and distributed in time (single or repeated doses), the type and severity of injury, the time needed to produce the injury, the nature of the organism(s) affected and other relevant conditions.Adverse effects of a substance on a living organism defined with reference to the quantity of substance administered or absorbed, the way in which the substance is administered (inhalation, ingestion, topical application, injection) and distributed in time (single or repeated doses), the type and severity of injury, the time needed to produce the injury, the nature of the organism(s) affected, and other relevant conditions.Measure of incompatibility of a substance with life: this quantity may be expressed as the reciprocal of the absolute value of median lethal dose (\(\frac{1}{\rm{LD}_{50}}\)) or concentration (\(\frac{1}{\rm{LC}_{50}}\)).

15102.title: toxicity curve
15102.definition: Curve obtained by plotting the median survival times of a group of test organisms against the concentration of a substance on a logarithmic scale.

15103.title: toxicity equivalency factor
15103.definition:
Ratio of the toxicity of a chemical to that of another structurally related chemical (or index compound) chosen as a reference.
In risk assessment, ratio of the toxicity of a chemical to that of another structurally related chemical (or index compound) chosen as a reference. Factor used to estimate the toxicity of a complex mixture, commonly a mixture of chlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins [oxanthrenes], furans, and biphenyls: in this case, TEF is based on relative toxicity to 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin [2,3,7,8-tetrachlorooxanthrene] for which the \(f = 1\).

15104.title: toxicity equivalent
15104.definition: Contribution of a specified component (or components) to the toxicity of a mixture of related substances.

16226.title: toxicity exposure ratio
16226.definition: Ratio of the measure of the effects (e.g., \(\pu{LD_{50}}\), \(\pu{LC_{50}}\), NOEC) to the estimated exposure.

15105.title: toxicity identification and evaluation
15105.definition: Systematic pretreatment (e.g., \(\rm{pH}\) change, filtration, or aeration) of a sample to obtain defined fractions that are subsequently tested for their toxicity. This fractionation is designed to separate out defined substances and thus to identify the agent(s) primarily responsible for lethal or sublethal toxicity of a complex mixture.

16155.title: toxicity test
16155.definition: Experimental study of the adverse effects of exposure of a living organism to a substance for a defined duration under defined conditions.

15106.title: toxicity value
15106.definition: Factor used to estimate risk. It may be a reference dose or it may be calculated from the following equation: \[T_{\rm{x}} = m\ C\] where \(m\) is the slope of a published dose-effect relationship and \(C\) is the toxicant concentration.

T06415.title: toxicodynamics
T06415.definition: Study of toxic actions on living systems, including the reactions with and binding to cell constituents, and the biochemical and physiological consequences of these actions.

14402.title: toxicogenetics
14402.definition: Study of the influence of hereditary factors on the effects of potentially toxic substances on individual organisms.

16156.title: toxicogenomics
16156.definition: Scientific subdiscipline that combines toxicology with genomics to determine how an organism’s genetic make-up influences its response to a toxic substance.

T06416.title: toxicokinetics
T06416.definition: Process of the uptake of potentially toxic substances by the body, the biotransformation they undergo, the distribution of the substances and their metabolites in the tissues, and the elimination of the substances and their metabolites from the body. Both the amounts and the concentrations of the substances and their metabolites are studied. The term has essentially the same meaning as pharmacokinetics, but the latter term should be restricted to the study of pharmaceutical substances.

16157.title: toxicological data sheet
16157.definition: Document that gives in a uniform manner data relating to the toxicology of a substance, its production and application, properties and methods of identification.

T06417.title: toxicology
T06417.definition: Scientific discipline involving the study of the actual or potential danger presented by the harmful effects of substances (poisons) on living organisms and ecosystems, of the relationship of such harmful effects to exposure, and of the mechanisms of action, diagnosis, prevention and treatment of intoxications.

16158.title: toxicometry
16158.definition: Term sometimes used to indicate a combination of investigative methods and techniques for making a quantitative assessment of toxicity and the hazards of potentially toxic substances.

16160.title: toxicophoric group
16160.definition: Structural moiety that upon metabolic activation exerts toxic effects: The presence of a toxicophoric group indicates only potential and not necessarily actual toxicity of a drug or other substances.

16161.title: toxicovigilance
16161.definition: Active process of identification, investigation, and evaluation of various toxic effects in the community with a view to taking measures to reduce or control exposure(s) involving the substance(s) which produces these effects.

16162.title: toxification
16162.definition: Metabolic conversion of a potentially toxic substance to a product that is more toxic.

T06418.title: toxin
T06418.definition: Poisonous substance produced by a biological organism such as a microbe, animal or plant.

T06419.title: toxinology
T06419.definition: Scientific discipline involving the study of the chemistry, biochemistry, pharmacology and toxicology of toxins.

13750.title: toxoid
13750.definition: Chemically or physically modified toxin that is no longer harmful but retains immunogenicity.

11309.title: toxoplasmosis
11309.definition: Infection with the parasite Toxoplasma gondii that, when acquired by the fetus, can lead to a variety of congenital abnormalities that may include hydrocephalus or microcephaly, mental retardation, and problems with vision and hearing.

13725.title: Tr1 cell
13725.definition: T lymphocyte that regulates Th1 cell responses. It resembles the regulatory T cell (Treg) and is possibly related to the Th3 cell.

T06421.title: trace element
T06421.definition: Any element having an average concentration of less than about 100 parts per million atoms (\(\rm{ppma}\)) or less than \(100\ \frac{\unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{g}}{\rm{g}}\).

15107.title: trace nutrient
15107.definition: Substance required in very small quantities by a defined organism to maintain health.

T06420.title: traceability
T06420.definition: The property of a result or measurement whereby it can be related to appropriate standards, generally international or national standards, through an unbroken chain of comparisons.

T06422.title: tracer
T06422.definition: A foreign substance mixed with or attached to a given substance to enable the distribution or location of the latter to be determined subsequently. There are several types of tracers which are used: (i) A physical tracer is one that is attached by physical means to the object being traced; (ii) A chemical tracer is a chemical with properties similar to those of the substance being traced with which it is mixed homogeneously; (iii) An isotopic tracer is a unique isotope, either radioactive or an enriched, uncommon stable isotope, of the element to be traced; (iv) A radioactive tracer is a physical or chemical tracer having radioactivity as its distinctive property which allows detection at small concentrations and hence after large transport distances. The composition of aerosols in the troposphere has been used as a qualitative tracer of air masses. The elemental analyses (determined by neutron activation, X-ray fluorescence, etc.) of the aerosols transported from various sources or source regions sometimes have characteristic patterns which are used to define qualitatively the origin of tropospheric aerosols collected in other geographical regions.

16163.title: tracer substance
16163.definition: Substance that can be tracked through one or more reactions or systems, often by detecting an incorporated isotope.

11310.title: trachea
11310.definition: Thin-walled, cartilaginous tube descending from the larynx to the bronchi and carrying air to the lungs.

T06429.title: track
T06429.definition: The path of an ionizing particle as revealed by a track detector.

T06430.title: track detector
T06430.definition: A detector which makes the paths of ionizing particles visible, either directly (e.g. cloud chamber) or after suitable treatment (photographic emulsion, polymers).

15108.title: trade-off
15108.definition: Exchange of one advantageous character for another.

T06431.title: trajectory
T06431.definition: A path taken by a reaction system over potential-energy surface or a diagram or mathematical description that represents that path. A trajectory can also be called a reaction path.

12144.title: tranquilizer
12144.definition: Drug that calms and pacifies with minimal sedating or depressant effects.

T06433.title: trans-
T06433.definition: A prefix designating two groups directly across a central atom from each other, i.e. in the polar positions on a sphere, not now generally recommended for precise nomenclature purposes.

T06434.title: transannular strain
T06434.definition: In medium-sized ring compounds, the strain due to repulsive nonbonded interactions between substituents or hydrogen atoms attached to non-adjacent ring atoms.

11311.title: transcription factor
11311.definition: DNA-binding protein that is involved in regulating gene expression.

T06436.title: transcription
T06436.definition: The process by which the genetic information encoded in a linear sequence of nucleotides in one strand of DNA is copied into an exactly complementary sequence of RNA.

16164.title: transcriptome
16164.definition: Total mRNA expressed in a cell or tissue at a given point in time.

16165.title: transcriptomics
16165.definition: Global analysis of gene expression to identify and evaluate changes in synthesis of mRNA after chemical exposure.

12145.title: transcutaneous electronic nerve stimulation
12145.definition: Electrical stimulus applied across the skin to excite nerves for therapeutic purposes.

13751.title: transcytosis
13751.definition: Vesicular transport of macromolecules from one side of a cell to the other, through the cell’s interior.

T06437.title: transducer
T06437.definition: An analytical instrument which provides an output quantity having a given relationship to the input quantity.

T06438.title: transduction
T06438.definition: The transfer of genetic information from one bacterium to another by means of a transducing bacteriophage. When the phage is grown on the first host, a fragment of the host DNA can be incorporated into the phage particles. This foreign DNA can be transferred to the second host upon infection with progeny phage from the first experiment.

T06439.title: transfer
T06439.definition: Movement of a component within a system or across its boundary. It may be expressed using different kinds of quantities, e.g rates of change \(\frac{\rm{d}Q}{\rm{d}t}\) or \(\frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t}\). Examples are: mass rate, \(\frac{\rm{d}m_{\rm{B}}}{\rm{d}t}\) or \(\frac{\Delta m_{\rm{B}}}{\Delta t}\); substance rate, \(\frac{\rm{d}n_{\rm{B}}}{\rm{d}t}\) or \(\frac{\Delta n_{\rm{B}}}{\Delta t}\).

T06442.title: transfer activity coefficient
T06442.definition: A term used to quantify the difference in the free energy of a solute ion in two different standard states often in two different liquid phases. The relationship is \(\Delta _{\rm{t}}G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}} = \nu \ R\ T\ \ln \mathit{\gamma}_{\rm{t}}\) where \(\Delta _{\rm{t}}G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) is the transfer Gibbs energy and \(\nu \) is the number of ions in the solute.

12283.title: transfer coefficient
12283.definition:
The anodic transfer coefficient \(\alpha_{\rm{a}}\) and the cathodic transfer coefficient \(\alpha_{\rm{c}}\) are defined by the following equations: \[\alpha_{\rm{a}} = (RT/F)({\rm{d}}\ln\! j_{\rm{a}}/{\rm{d}}E); \quad \alpha_{\rm{c}} = -(RT/F)({\rm{d}}\ln\!\vert {j_{\rm{c}}} \vert /{\rm{d}}E)\]
In these equations, \(j_{\rm{a}}\) and \(j_{\rm{c}}\) are the anodic and cathodic current densities, respectively, corrected for any changes in the reactant concentration at the electrode surface with respect to its bulk value; incidentally, the symbols \(\ln\! j_{\rm{a}}\) and \(\ln\!\vert j_{\rm{c}}\vert\) imply that the argument of the logarithm is of dimension one, obtained by division with the corresponding unit, e.g., \(\ln\! j_{\rm{a}}\) meaning \(\ln(j_{\rm{a}}/\pu{A m^{-2}})\), and similarly for the other quantities \(\vert j_{\rm{c}}\vert\), \(k_{\rm{a}}\) and \(k_{\rm{c}}\). \(E\) is the applied electric potential, \(R\) is the gas constant, \(T\) is the thermodynamic temperature, and \(F\) is the Faraday constant. In practice, \(\alpha_{\rm{a}}\) and \(\alpha_{\rm{c}}\) are defined as the reciprocal of the corresponding Tafel slopes, \({\rm{d}}E/{\rm{d}}\ln\! j_{\rm{a}}\) and \(-{\rm{d}}E/{\rm{d}} \ln\! \vert j_{\rm{c}} \vert\), made dimensionless by the multiplying factor \(RT/F\). Both the transfer coefficient and the Tafel slope are determined at constant temperature and pressure.

10031.title: transfer examination device
10031.definition: Device used as an intermediary to compare examination standards.

T06440.title: transfer
T06440.definition: The action of moving material between containers, or containers between transport devices. This term is of particular importance in clinical chemistry.

T06444.title: transfer line
T06444.definition: Line provided to carry the sample to be analysed from the sample point to the analytical unit without altering the composition of the sample.

T06445.title: transfer RNA
T06445.definition: A single-stranded RNA molecule containing about 70-90 nucleotides, folded by intrastrand base pairing into a characteristic secondary ('cloverleaf') structure that carries a specific amino acid and matches it to its corresponding codon on an mRNA during protein synthesis.

T06441.title: transferability
T06441.definition: Transferability assumes invariance of properties, associated conceptually with an atom or a fragment present in a variety of molecules. The property, such as electronegativity, nucleophilicity, NMR chemical shift, etc. is held as retaining a similar value in all these occurrences.

T06443.title: transferases
T06443.definition: Enzymes that catalyse reactions in which a group is transferred from one compound to another. Groups that are transferred are $\ce{C}$, aldehydic or ketonic residues, acyl, glycosyl, alkyl, nitrogenous, phosphorus and sulfur containing groups.

08701.title: transflectance
08701.definition: Spectral intensity of a transflected beam divided by spectral intensity of the incident beam in a transflection experiment.

08702.title: transflection
08702.definition: Reflection absorption at near-normal incidence when the thickness of the absorbing medium is large enough to yield an interpretable spectrum. The substrate is usually a mirror for mid-infrared measurements and a ceramic disk for near-infrared measurements. The angle of incidence is typically between \(\pu{0\!^{\circ}}\) and \(\pu{45\!^{\circ}}\).

T06446.title: transformation
T06446.definition: The conversion of a substrate into a particular product, irrespective of reagents or mechanisms involved. For example, the transformation of aniline ($\ce{C6H5NH2}$) into N-phenylacetamide ($\ce{C6H5NHCOCH3}$) may be effected by use of acetyl chloride or acetic anhydride or ketene. A transformation is distinct from a reaction, the full description of which would state or imply all the reactants and all the products.

T06447.title: transformation
T06447.definition: A process for genetic alteration of a cell following incorporation of foreign DNA.

09431.title: transformation probability
09431.definition: Probability of a defined charged or neutral species being produced, by consumption of a defined parent atomic or molecular configuration at a surface, as a result of sputtering in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

16166.title: transformed cell
16166.definition: Cell that has become genetically altered spontaneously or by incorporation of foreign DNA to produce a cell with an extended lifetime in culture.

13752.title: transforming growth factor β
13752.definition: Secreted member of the protein superfamily of the same name that functions in controlling the cell cycle and apoptosis.

16167.title: transgene
16167.definition: Gene from one source that has been incorporated into the genome of another organism.

11312.title: transgenic
11312.definition: Describing an organism that is genetically changed by the addition or deletion of genetic material or whose existing genes are altered by gene targeting.

T06451.title: transient species
T06451.definition: Relating to a short-lived reaction intermediate. It can be defined only in relation to a time scale fixed by the experimental conditions and the limitations of the technique employed in the detection of the intermediate. The term is a relative one. Transient species are sometimes also said to be 'metastable'. However, this latter term should be avoided, because it relates a thermodynamic term to a kinetic property, although most transients are also thermodynamically unstable with respect to reactants and products.

TT07595.title: transient crosslink
TT07595.definition: Crosslink formed by intermolecular or intramolecular interactions that are unstable under the conditions of use of the material formed.

TT07601.title: transient junction point
TT07601.definition: Junction point in a polymer network that exists only for a finite period of time.

T06450.title: transient phase
T06450.definition: This expression relates to the period of time that elapses prior to the establishment of a steady state. Initially the concentration of a reactive intermediate is zero, and it rises to the steady-state concentration during the transient phase.

T06453.title: transient spectroscopy
T06453.definition: A technique for the spectroscopic observation of transient species (excited-state molecular entities or reactive intermediates) generated by a pulse of short duration.

TT07487.title: transient-stimulated emission pumping
TT07487.definition: Transient-spectroscopy technique in which the excited state dynamics is probed via stimulating the molecular species from the photo-excited state (produced by a short pump pulse) back to the ground state by means of a short dump pulse at various pump–dump time delays.

14199.title: transiently transfected cells
14199.definition: Eukaryotic cells into which recombinant DNA has been introduced and expressed by cellular transcription, but without incorporation into the stable genome.

T06474.title: transit time
T06474.definition: The time needed for the component to pass through the observation space (in \(\mathrm{s}\)). It depends on the geometry of the observation space, the flame temperature and the solute nebulized.

T06460.title: transition moment
T06460.definition: An electromagnetic wave may induce an oscillating electric moment in a molecule (possibly leading to absorption if the oscillation frequency is equal to the light frequency). The amplitude of this moment is the transition moment between the initial (i) and final (f) states (here assumed to be non-degenerate): \[M_{\rm{if}} = \, < \rm{f} \mid M_{\rm{op}}\mid \rm{i} >\] where \(M_{\rm{op}}\) is the electric dipole moment operator, a vector operator that is the sum of the position vectors of all charged particles weighted with their charge. The transition moment \(M_{\rm{if}} \) is a vector in the molecular framework, characterized both by its direction and its probability.

T06455.title: transition coordinate
T06455.definition: The reaction coordinate at the transition state corresponding to a vibration with an imaginary frequency. Motion along it in the two opposite senses leads towards the reactants or towards the products.

T06456.title: transition element
T06456.definition: An element whose atom has an incomplete d sub-shell, or which can give rise to cations with an incomplete d sub-shell.

T06457.title: transition interval
T06457.definition: The range of concentration over which the eye is able to perceive change in hue, colour intensity, fluorescence or other property of a visual indicator arising from the varying ratio of the two relevant forms of the indicator.

T06462.title: transition polarization
T06462.definition: The direction of the transition moment in the molecular framework.

09053.title: transition potential
09053.definition: Potential at the end-point of a redox titration.

T06467.title: transition species
T06467.definition: Any intermediate species in an elementary reaction. An activated complex is an example of a transition species, but the latter term also includes other intermediate species. Transition species have also been called transition states, but there is then danger of confusion with a true activated complex, which is also commonly known as a transition state.

T06468.title: transition state
T06468.definition: In theories describing elementary reaction it is usually assumed that there is a transition state of more positive molar Gibbs energy between the reactants and the products through which an assembly of atoms (initially composing the molecular entities of the reactants) must pass on going from reactants to products in either direction. In the formalism of 'transition state theory' the transition state of an elementary reaction is that set of states (each characterized by its own geometry and energy) in which an assembly of atoms, when randomly placed there, would have an equal probability of forming the reactants or of forming the products of that elementary reaction. The transition state is characterized by one and only one imaginary frequency. The assembly of atoms at the transition state has been called an activated complex. (It is not a complex according to the definition in this Compendium.) It may be noted that the calculations of reaction rates by the transition state method and based on calculated potential-energy surfaces refer to the potential energy maximum at the saddle point, as this is the only point for which the requisite separability of transition state coordinates may be assumed. The ratio of the number of assemblies of atoms that pass through to the products to the number of those that reach the saddle point from the reactants can be less than unity, and this fraction is the 'transmission coefficient' \(\kappa \). (There are also reactions, such as the gas-phase colligation of simple radicals, that do not require 'activation' and which therefore do not involve a transition state.)

T06469.title: transition state analogue
T06469.definition: A substrate designed to mimic the properties or the geometry of the transition state of reaction.

T06470.title: transition state theory
T06470.definition: A theory of the rates of elementary reactions which assumes a special type of equilibrium, having an equilibrium constant \(K^{\ddagger }\), to exist between reactants and activated complexes. According to this theory the rate constant is given by: \[k=\frac{k_{\rm{B}}\ T}{h}\ K^{\ddagger }\] where \(k_{B}\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(h\) is the Planck constant. The rate constant can also be expressed as: \[k=\frac{k_{\rm{B}}\ T}{h}\ \exp (\frac{\Delta ^{\ddagger }S^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}}{R})\ \exp (- \frac{\Delta ^{\ddagger }H^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}}{R\ T})\] where \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}S^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\), the entropy of activation, is the standard molar change of entropy when the activated complex is formed from reactants and \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}H^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\), the enthalpy of activation, is the corresponding standard molar change of enthalpy. The quantities \(E_{a}\) (the energy of activation) and \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}H^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) are not quite the same, the relationship between them depending on the type of reaction. Also: \[k=\frac{k_{\rm{B}}\ T}{h}\ \exp (- \frac{\Delta ^{\ddagger }G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}}{R\ T})\] where \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\), known as the Gibbs energy of activation, is the standard molar Gibbs energy change for the conversion of reactants into activated complex. A plot of standard molar Gibbs energy against a reaction coordinate is known as a Gibbs-energy profile; such plots, unlike potential-energy profiles, are temperature-dependent. In principle the equations above must be multiplied by a transmission coefficient, \(\kappa \), which is the probability that an activated complex forms a particular set of products rather than reverting to reactants or forming alternative products. It is to be emphasized that \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}S^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\), \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}H^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) and \(\Delta ^{\ddagger}G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) occurring in the former three equations are not ordinary thermodynamic quantities, since one degree of freedom in the activated complex is ignored. Transition-state theory has also been known as absolute rate theory, and as activated-complex theory, but these terms are no longer recommended.

T06471.title: transition structure
T06471.definition: A saddle point on a potential-energy surface. It has one negative force constant in the harmonic force constant matrix.

TT06898.title: transition temperature
TT06898.definition: The temperature at which the transition from mesophase X to mesophase Y occurs.

T06472.title: transition time
T06472.definition: In chronopotentiometry and related techniques, the time that elapses between the instant at which current is applied and the instant at which the concentration of an electroactive substance B at the electrode-solution interface becomes indistinguishable from zero. In experimental practice the latter time is often taken to be the instant at which the rate of variation of the potential of the indicator electrode attains a maximum value.

T06473.title: transition wavenumber
T06473.definition: Difference of term values for the corresponding states (upper minus lower).

08928.title: transition-metal-mediated radical polymerization
08928.definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization mediated by transition-metal complexes or organometallic compounds.

T06475.title: translation
T06475.definition: The unidirectional process that takes place on the ribosomes whereby the genetic information present in an mRNA is converted into a corresponding sequence of amino acids in a protein.

12245.title: translational diffusion
12245.definition: Process by which the equilibrium statistical distribution of positions of molecules or entities in space is maintained or restored due to their translational Brownian motion.

12247.title: translational diffusion coefficient
12247.definition: Proportionality constant relating the flux per unit area, \(J_{n}\), in unidirectional flow of amount, \(n\), of entities \(\ce{B}\) to their concentration gradient in the direction (\(x\)) of flow, \({\rm{d}}c_{\ce{B}}/{\rm{d}}x\), i.e., \(J_{n} = -D{\rm{d}} c_{\ce{B}}/{\rm{d}}x\).

12246.title: translational frictional coefficient
12246.definition: Frictional force, \(F\), per unit velocity, \(u\), experienced by an isolated spherical body moving unidirectionally in a viscous isotropic fluid, i.e., \(F = fu\).

T06476.title: translational spectroscopy
T06476.definition: A technique to investigate the distribution of the velocity of product ions from reactions of ions and neutral species.

T06480.title: transmission electron energy loss spectroscopy
T06480.definition: Any technique in which an electron transparent specimen is bombarded with a finely focused electron beam and the energy distribution of the transmitted electrons is measured. This energy spectrum contains features corresponding to discrete losses of energy of the transmitted electrons due to excitation of electronic or plasmon states and provides information on the identity (and in some cases) chemical bonding of the elements in the sample.

T06481.title: transmission electron microscopy
T06481.definition: Any technique in which an electron transparent sample is bombarded with an electron beam and the intensity of the transmitted electrons which is determined by scattering phenomena (electron absorption phenomena) in the interior of the sample is recorded. TEM essentially provides a high resolution image of the microstructure of a thin sample. This technique is often just called 'electron microscopy'. The term transmission electron microscopy is however recommended for the sake of a clear distinction from other electron microscopic techniques.

T06483.title: transmission high energy electron diffraction
T06483.definition: Any technique which is based on the diffraction of high energy electrons (\(E_{0} = 10{-}200\ \rm{keV}\)) in crystalline materials and evaluation of the angular distribution of the transmitted electrons. The diffraction pattern represents an image of the reciprocal lattice and therefore contains information about crystal structure. This technique is also often called selected area electron diffraction (SAED). For consistency with other electron diffraction techniques, however, the term THEED is recommended.

T06478.title: transmission
T06478.definition: The ratio of the number of ions leaving a region of a mass spectrometer to the number entering that region.

08703.title: transmission Raman spectroscopy
08703.definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy in which the sample is illuminated on one side and the Raman signal is collected from the opposite side.

08294.title: transmission spectrum
08294.definition: General term for the spectrum of transmitted electromagnetic radiation.

T06484.title: transmittance
T06484.definition: The ratio of the transmitted radiant power (\(P_{\lambda }\)) to that incident on the sample (\(P_{\lambda }^{0}\)): \[T=\frac{P_{\lambda }}{P_{\lambda }^{0}}\] Internal transmittance refers to energy loss by absorption, whereas the total transmittance is that due to absorption, reflection, scatter, etc.

11314.title: transplacental carcinogen
11314.definition: Substance that crosses the placenta and subsequently causes cancer in the child or young adult.

13754.title: transplantation
13754.definition: Grafting solid tissue (e.g., cornea) or organ (e.g., kidney or heart), or cells (particularly bone marrow), from one individual to another.

08560.title: transport efficiency
08560.definition: Mass of analyte entering the atomizer of a flame atomic spectrometer or the plasma of an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer divided by the mass of analyte entering the dispersion device.

T06486.title: transport
T06486.definition: The action of moving materials within the analytical instrument. Transport can involve any of several means including pressure flow, where the materials are moved by fluid pressure, either continuously or discontinuously; centrifugal flow, where the materials are moved by centrifugal force; spontaneous motion, where the materials are moved due to their intrinsic properties, e.g. diffusion, capillarity; and discrete transport, where materials are enclosed within a moving container.

T06488.title: transport interference
T06488.definition: Transport interferences affect the amount of desolvated sample passing through the horizontal flame cross-section per unit time at the observation height. They include factors affecting the rate of liquid consumption, \(F_{\rm{l}}\), the efficiency of nebulization, \(\varepsilon_{\rm{n}}\), and the fraction desolvated \(\beta_{\rm{s}}\). They may be classified as non-specific (and physical).

T06489.title: transport number
T06489.definition: Of ions $\ce{B}$, the current density due to ions $\ce{B}$ divided by the sum of current densities of all the ions in the electrolyte. ISO recommends the name current fraction of ions $\ce{B}$.

13755.title: transporters associated with antigen processing
13755.definition: Molecules that carry antigenic peptides from the cytoplasm into the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum for incorporation into major histocompatibility (MHC) class I molecules.

11315.title: transposition of the great arteries
11315.definition: Congenital cardiovascular malformation in which the position of the chief blood vessels of the heart (aorta and pulmonary artery) is reversed.

T06490.title: transposon
T06490.definition: A movable DNA element that can be inserted at new sites into plasmids or chromosomes independently of the host cell recombination system. Prokaryotic transposons can carry genes that confer new phenotypic properties, such as resistance to antibiotics on the host.

12146.title: transsynaptic
12146.definition: Referring to an event, such as transmission of a nerve impulse, across a synapse.

T06491.title: transtactic polymer
T06491.definition: A tactic polymer in which the main-chain double bonds of the configurational base units are entirely in the trans-arrangement.

12147.title: transtentorial herniation
12147.definition: Bulging of brain tissue from the cerebrum through the notch of the tentorium, caused by increased intracranial pressure.

14379.title: transurf
14379.definition: Chain-transfer agent with the properties of a surfactant.

08437.title: transverse relaxation optimized spectroscopy
08437.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, usually in protein NMR, that improves peak sharpness for molecules having a molecular mass of greater than \(\pu{100 kDa}\).

T06492.title: trapping
T06492.definition: The interception of a reactive molecule or reaction intermediate so that it is removed from the system or converted into a more stable form for study or identification.

T06493.title: travel time
T06493.definition: The time needed for the component to be carried from the burner tip to the observation space (in \(\mathrm{s}\)). Travel time depends on the observation height and the flame rise velocity.

10030.title: travelling examination standard
10030.definition: Examination standard, sometimes of special construction, intended for transport between different locations.

11316.title: Treacher Collins syndrome
11316.definition: Congenital deformity characterized by structural abnormalities of the head and face.

12148.title: treadmill test
12148.definition: Procedure used to assess limb function and strength, often to evaluate models of peripheral neuropathy, in which a rodent is placed in an enclosed lane upon a surface that can be made to move at variable speed in a retrograde manner, thus allowing observation of the animal’s gait dimension during sustained attempt at forward motion.

16168.title: treatability
16168.definition: In relation to waste water, the amenability of substances to removal without adversely affecting the normal operation of biological treatment processes (such as a sewage treatment plant).

T06494.title: treated solution
T06494.definition: The test solution that has been subjected to reaction or separation procedures prior to measurement of some property.

12149.title: tremor
12149.definition: Repetitive, often regular and usually involuntary oscillatory movement caused by alternating contractions of opposing muscle groups.

16169.title: triage
16169.definition:
Process for sorting people into groups based on their need for or likely benefit from immediate medical treatment.
Note: Triage is used in hospital emergency rooms, on battlefields, and at disaster sites when limited medical resources must be allocated.
System used to allocate a scarce commodity, such as food, to those most likely to benefit from it.
Process in which things are ranked in terms of importance or priority.

T06496.title: triangulo-
T06496.definition: An affix used in names to denote three atoms bound into a triangle.

T06499.title: triboluminescence
T06499.definition: Luminescence resulting from the rubbing together of the surface of certain solids. It can be produced, for example, when solids are crushed.

12150.title: trigeminal nerve
12150.definition: Fifth cranial nerve, supplying sensation to the face and controlling motor activity of mastication.

12151.title: trigeminal neuralgia
12151.definition: Severe, paroxysmal bursts of pain in one or more branches of the trigeminal nerve, often induced by touching trigger points in or about the mouth.

15109.title: trigger values
15109.definition: Criteria applied to results from tests (for fate or effects) which prompt further studies, e.g., moving to the next tier of tests, which are generally more complex.

11317.title: trilaminar embryo
11317.definition: Disc-like embryonic stage in which differentiation into three layers (endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm) has occurred.

11318.title: trimester
11318.definition: In pregnancy, one of three equal timed divisions of the normal human gestation period, each lasting approximately three months.

T06500.title: trimethylenemethanes
T06500.definition: The diradical $\ce{CH2=C(C^{.}H2)2}$, 2-methylenepropane-1,3-diyl, for which no Kekulé structure can be written, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives.

T06501.title: trioxides
T06501.definition: Organic derivatives of trioxidane, $\ce{HOOOH}$, e.g. $\ce{ROOOR'}$. When $\ce{R'} = \ce{H}$, the compound is a hydrotrioxide.

T06502.title: triple point
T06502.definition: The point in a one-component system at which the temperature and pressure of three phases are in equilibrium. If there are \(p\) possible phases, there are \(\frac{p!}{(p\,-\,3)!\ 3!}\) triple points. Example: In the sulfur system four possible triple points (one metastable) exist for the four phases comprising rhombic $\ce{S}$ (solid), monoclinic $\ce{S}$ (solid), $\ce{S}$ (liquid) and $\ce{S}$ (vapour).

11319.title: triple screen
11319.definition: Measurement of maternal serum levels of alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and estriol, usually in the second trimester of pregnancy, that can serve as an indicator of risk for certain fetal chromosomal abnormalities and neural tube defects.

08438.title: triple-resonance nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
08438.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy using three NMR-active nuclei.

T06503.title: triplet state
T06503.definition: A state having a total electron spin quantum number of 1.

T06504.title: triplet-triplet absorption
T06504.definition: Absorption which takes place with the transition from the lowest triplet state of the molecule to higher triplet states (T → \(T_{n}\)) thus leading to the triplet-triplet absorption spectrum.

T06505.title: triplet-triplet annihilation
T06505.definition: Two atoms or molecular entities both in a triplet state often interact (usually upon collision) to produce one atom or molecular entity in an excited singlet state and another in its ground singlet state. This is often, but not always, followed by delayed fluorescence.

T06506.title: triplet-triplet energy transfer
T06506.definition: Energy transfer from an electronically excited triplet donor to produce an electronically excited acceptor in its triplet state.

T06507.title: triplet-triplet transitions
T06507.definition: Electronic transitions in which both the initial and final states are triplet states.

11320.title: triploidy
11320.definition: Presence of three haploid sets of chromosomes in the cell.

T06508.title: triprismo-
T06508.definition: An affix used in names to denote six atoms bound into a triangular prism.

12152.title: triptan
12152.definition: Member of a class of drugs based on tryptamine that act as serotonin receptor agonists.

11321.title: trisomy
11321.definition: Condition of having three homologous chromosomes in each somatic cell instead of the normal pair.

11323.title: trisomy 13
11323.definition: Presence of part or all of an extra chromosome 13 from nondisjunction during meiosis.

11324.title: trisomy 18
11324.definition: Presence of part or all of an extra chromosome 18 from nondisjunction during meiosis.

T06509.title: tritactic polymer
T06509.definition: A tactic polymer that contains three sites of defined stereoisomerism in the main chain of the configurational base unit. Example:

T06513.title: tritium
T06513.definition: A specific name for the atom $\ce{^{3}H}$. The cation $\ce{^{3}H^{+}}$ is a triton, the species $\ce{^{3}H^{−}}$ is a tritide anion and $\ce{^{3}H}$ is the tritio group.

T06516.title: trivial name
T06516.definition: A name having no part used in a systematic sense.

15243.title: troche
15243.definition: Applied to compressed lozenges. In lay language, lozenge and troche are used interchangeably.

T06517.title: Troe expression
T06517.definition: A semiempirical description of the rate coefficient for a specific three body reaction [e.g. ] which represents well its pressure and temperature dependence in the region of transition between second and third order kinetics.

11326.title: trophectoderm
11326.definition: Outer layer of the blastocyst that contacts the endometrium, establishes nutrition for the embryo, and differentiates into the trophoblast.

15111.title: trophic cascade
15111.definition: Situation arising when predators in a food chain suppress the abundance of their prey, thereby releasing the next lower trophic level from predation (or herbivory if the intermediate trophic level is an herbivore).

15112.title: trophic dilution
15112.definition: Decrease in contaminant concentration as trophic level increases; this results from a net balance of ingestion rate, uptake from food, internal transformation, and elimination processes favoring loss of contaminant that enters the organism via food.

15113.title: trophic level
15113.definition: Position in a food chain, assessed by the number of energy-transfer steps to reach that level.

15114.title: trophic structure
15114.definition: Organization of an ecological community described in terms of energy flow through its various trophic levels.

15115.title: trophic transfer
15115.definition: Transfer of a substance from one trophic level to another.

15116.title: trophic transfer factor
15116.definition: Ratio between the concentration of a compound in a predator and in its prey.

11327.title: trophoblast
11327.definition: Outer layer of the blastocyst that invades the endometrium and establishes nutrition for the embryo.

T06518.title: tropilidenes
T06518.definition: This term has inconsistently been used to mean cyclohepta-1,3,5-trienes or to mean cyclohepta-1,3,5-trienes in dynamic equilibrium with bicyclo-[4.1.0]hepta-2,4-dienes, so that the structure of the bulk substance is indeterminate in the time scale of the method of observation. Use of this term is therefore discouraged.

T06520.title: tropones
T06520.definition: Compounds that contain the cyclohepta-2,4,6-trienone ring system.

T06521.title: tropopause
T06521.definition: The region of the atmosphere which joins the troposphere and stratosphere, and where the decreasing temperature with altitude, characteristic of the troposphere ceases, and the temperature increase with height which is characteristic of the stratosphere begins.

T06522.title: troposphere
T06522.definition: The lowest layer of the atmosphere, ranging from the ground to the base of the stratosphere (tropopause) at \(10{-}15\ \rm{km}\) of altitude depending on the latitude and meteorological conditions. About 70% of the mass of the atmosphere is in the troposphere. This is where most of the weather features occur and where the chemistry of the reactive anthropogenic species released into the atmosphere takes place.

T06524.title: tropyl radicals
T06524.definition: The delocalized radicals derived formally by abstraction of one hydrogen from the $\ce{CH2}$ group of cyclohepta-1,3,5-triene and substitution derivatives thereof.

T06523.title: tropylium ions
T06523.definition: The delocalized carbenium ion, cycloheptatrienylium, $\ce{C7H7^{+}}$, derived formally by detachment of one hydride ion from the $\ce{CH2}$ group of cyclohepta-1,3,5-triene and substitution derivatives thereof.

T06525.title: true coincidence
T06525.definition: A coincidence of events occurring in the same atom or in physically connected atoms.

11527.title: true negative
11527.definition: A model prediction of a negative result, such as no biological activity, when the true result is also negative.

10001.title: true nominal property value
10001.definition: Nominal property value consistent with the definition of a nominal property.

11528.title: true positive
11528.definition: A model prediction of a positive result, such as biological activity, when the true result is also positive.

T06527.title: true value
T06527.definition: The value that characterizes a quantity perfectly in the conditions that exist when that quantity is considered. It is an ideal value which could be arrived at only if all causes of measurement error were eliminated, and the entire population was sampled.

16170.title: trueness
16170.definition: Closeness of agreement between the average of a theoretically infinite number of replicate measured quantity values and a reference quantity value.

11328.title: truncus arteriosus
11328.definition: Arterial trunk, opening from the fetal heart and developing into the aorta and pulmonary artery.

09787.title: trypsin
09787.definition: Serine protease with highly specific primary endoproteolytic activity that serves to generate proteolytic peptides in bottom-up proteomics analysis.

13756.title: tryptophan
13756.definition: Essential amino acid for humans, and required for T-cell proliferation.

T06528.title: tub conformation
T06528.definition: A conformation (of symmetry group \(D_{\rm{2d}}\)) of an eight-membered ring in which the four atoms forming one pair of diametrically opposite bonds in the ring lie in one plane and all other ring atoms lie to one side of that plane. It is analogous to the boat conformation of cyclohexane.

12269.title: tube model
12269.definition: Model to describe the motion of a polymer chain confined in the hypothetical tube created by neighbouring chains.

12270.title: tube renewal
12270.definition: Dynamic renewal of tubes by the disentanglement and re-entanglement of polymer chains.

13757.title: tuberculin
13757.definition: Antigen found in extracts of Mycobacteria, used in a skin test for tuberculosis (Mantoux test).

13758.title: tuberculin test
13758.definition: Diagnostic test in which antigens derived from the organism causing tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis) are injected subcutaneously; individuals who have been exposed to the organism develop a delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) response at the injection site \(\pu{24}\) to \(\pu{48 h}\) later.

11329.title: tuberoinfundibular pathway
11329.definition: Group of dopaminergic neurons in the hypothalamus involved in regulating prolactin secretion from the anterior pituitary gland.

10848.title: tubular fertility index
10848.definition: Percentage of seminiferous tubules containing identifiable spermatogonia.

16171.title: tubular reabsorption
16171.definition: Transfer of solutes from the renal tubule lumen to the tubular epithelial cell and normally from there to the peritubular fluid.

10116.title: Tucker tri-linear analysis
10116.definition: Decomposition of a three-way data matrix into a three-way core matrix, and three, two-way loadings matrices.

11330.title: tumor
11330.definition: Any abnormal swelling or growth of tissue, whether benign or malignant.

13759.title: tumor antigen
13759.definition: Antigen whose expression is associated with tumor cells.

13760.title: tumor immunology
13760.definition: Application of immunology to understanding tumor biology, immune system avoidance by tumors, and immunotherapy directed against tumors.

13762.title: tumor necrosis factor
13762.definition: Protein produced and secreted by several of the body’s cell types, including leukocytes.

13763.title: tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor
13763.definition: Family of proteins involved in regulating inflammation and apoptosis through interaction with the tumor necrosis factor receptor.

16173.title: tumor progression
16173.definition: Sequence of changes by which a benign tumor develops from the initial lesion to a malignant stage.

13764.title: tumor rejection antigen
13764.definition: Antigen present specifically on a tumor cell that may target it for destruction by the immune system or for antibody therapy.

16174.title: tumor suppressor gene
16174.definition: Gene that serves to protect cells from entering a cancerous state.

13761.title: tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte
13761.definition: Mononuclear lymphocyte derived from the inflammatory infiltrate of a solid tumor.

13765.title: tumor-specific transplantation antigen
13765.definition: Antigen, present only on a tumor cell, and targetable by the immune system or by antibody therapy in order to destroy the tumor.

T06529.title: tunable laser
T06529.definition: A high intensity source with narrow spectral bandwidth, with and without frequency doubling and/or Raman shifting. Its use may enable the spectral apparatus to be omitted. Tunable lasers may be either continuous (CW) or pulsed in nature.

09883.title: Tunel test
09883.definition: Method for the determination of strand breaks and DNA fragmentation in cells based on labelling and quantification of free 3′-OH ends of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).

T06530.title: Tung distribution
T06530.definition: A continuous distribution with the differential mass-distribution function of the form: \[f_{\rm{w}}(x)\ \rm{d}x = a\ b\ x^{b-1}\ \rm{e}^{-a\ x^{b}}\ \rm{d}x\] where \(x\) is a parameter characterizing the chain length, such as relative molecular mass or degree of polymerization and \(a\) and \(b\) are positive adjustable parameters.

11331.title: tunica albuginea
11331.definition: Dense, collagenous fibrous coat surrounding an anatomical structure, and in particular surrounding the ovaries, testicles, and corpora cavernosa of the penis.

11332.title: tunica vaginalis
11332.definition: Membranous sheath, derived from the peritoneum, surrounding the testis and epididymis.

T06531.title: tunnelling
T06531.definition: The process by which a particle or a set of particles crosses a barrier on its potential-energy surface without having the energy required to surmount this barrier. Since the rate of tunnelling decreases with increasing reduced mass, it is significant in the context of isotope effects of hydrogen isotopes.

T06532.title: turbidimetric titration
T06532.definition: The process in which a precipitant is added incrementally to a highly dilute polymer solution and the intensity of light scattered by, or the turbidity due to, the finely dispersed particles of the polymer-rich phase is measured as a function of the amount of precipitant added.

T06533.title: turbidity
T06533.definition: The apparent absorbance of the incident radiation due to scattering. For small particles, direct proportionality exists between turbidity and the Rayleigh ratio.

15117.title: turbidity of water
