15117.definition: Extent to which the clarity of water is reduced by the presence of suspended or other matter that causes light to be scattered and absorbed rather than transmitted (in straight lines) through the sample.

11333.title: turner syndrome
11333.definition: Phenotypic female lacking one X chromosome, the genotype being designated XO.

T06534.title: turnover frequency
T06534.definition: Commonly called the turnover number, \(N\), and defined, as in enzyme catalysis, as molecules reacting per active site in unit time.

14101.title: turnover number
14101.definition: Number of times, \(n\), that the overall reaction (the photochemical transformation) goes through a photocatalytic cycle.

11529.title: Tversky similarity
11529.definition: An asymmetric measure in which a target structure is compared to a reference structure with user-selectable weighting of the relative importance of the fingerprint bits or structural keys that are present only in the reference versus the fingerprint bits or structural keys that are only in the target, weightings for which the Tanimoto coefficient uses \(\pu{1.0}\).

15118.title: twin-tracer technique
15118.definition: Experimental method for evaluating assimilation that introduces simultaneously a radiotracer of the substance being assimilated and an inert tracer that will not be assimilated, thus providing a basis for evaluating the assimilation.

T06537.title: twisted intramolecular charge transfer
T06537.definition: In a TICT state formed by intramolecular charge transfer in an electron donor ($\ce{D}$)/acceptor ($\ce{A}$) molecule, the $\ce{D}$ and $\ce{A}$ subgroups have a mutually perpendicular configuration that leads to electronic decoupling of $\ce{D}$ and $\ce{A}$.

09884.title: two hybrid system
09884.definition: Molecular biology method for studying protein–protein or protein–deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) interactions in cellular (yeast or bacterial) milieu.

16175.title: two-compartment model
16175.definition: Product of compartmental analysis requiring two compartments.

T06540.title: two-dimensional chromatography
T06540.definition: A procedure in which parts or all of the separated sample components are subjected to additional separation steps. This can be done e.g. by conducting a particular fraction eluting from the column into another column (system) having different separation characteristics. When combined with additional steps, this may be described as multi-dimensional chromatography. In planar chromatography two-dimensional chromatography refers to the chromatographic process in which the components are caused to migrate first in one direction and subsequently in a direction at right angles to the first one; the two elutions are carried out with different eluents.

08295.title: two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy
08295.definition: Measurement principle of spectroscopy in which spectra are recorded at different magnitudes of an applied external perturbation of the sample and are processed to yield a 2-D correlation spectrum.

08296.title: two-dimensional correlation spectrum
08296.definition:
Three-dimensional surface in which two of the dimensions show frequency axes (\(
u_{1}\), \(
u_{2}\)) and the third axis shows a correlation function of the spectral intensities observed at \(
u_{1}\) and \(
u_{2}\).

09788.title: two-dimensional gel electrophoresis
09788.definition: Technique used to separate proteins using isoelectric focusing in a gel. The proteins are then further separated in the second dimension using denaturing PAGE.

08439.title: two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
08439.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in which data are collected in two time domains: acquisition of the free induction decay (\(t_{2}\)) and a successively incremented delay (\(t_{1}\)).

11334.title: two-generation reprotox study
11334.definition: Procedure in rodents wherein parents (P0 generation) and their offspring (F1 generation) are both exposed to a test substance and the second generation (F2) is examined for possible toxic effects.

10223.title: two-phase aqueous partition
10223.definition: Distribution in a biphasic system formed by two aqueous solutions containing structurally incompatible components (two polymers or a polymer and a salt) above a critical concentration.

T06541.title: two-photon excitation
T06541.definition: Excitation resulting from successive or simultaneous absorption of two photons by an atom or molecular entity. This term is used for successive absorption only if some of the excitation energy of the first photon remains in the atom or molecular entity before absorption of the second photon. The simultaneous two-photon absorption can also be called biphotonic excitation.

TT07491.title: two-photon photochromism
TT07491.definition: Photochromic process involving a two-photon process. The process might involve the simultaneous or the sequential absorption of two photons.

T06542.title: two-photon process
T06542.definition: A photophysical or photochemical event triggered by a two-photon excitation.

T06543.title: two-site immunoradiometric assay
T06543.definition: Immunoradiometric assay involving two sets of antibodies, one of which is labelled, that combine with different immunoreactive sites of an antigen molecule.

11335.title: tympanic
11335.definition: In anatomy, relating to the resonant cavity and membrane of the inner ear.

15119.title: type A organism
15119.definition: Animal or plant living in contact with sediments but unable to ingest particulates.

15120.title: type B organism
15120.definition: Animal or plant living in contact with sediments and capable of ingesting particulates.

09950.title: type-J coil planet centrifuge
09950.definition: Centrifuge that provides type-J synchronous planetary motion to the column holder, the axis of which is parallel to the centrifuge axis (see figure in high-speed counter-current chromatography).

09951.title: type-J synchronous planetary motion
09951.definition: Unique type of planetary motion (so named because the flow tubes form a letter J figure, as shown in the figure in high-speed counter-current chromatography) of the column holder, which rotates around its own axis once during one revolution around the central axis of the centrifuge in the same direction.

13766.title: tyrosine kinase
13766.definition: Any member of a family of enzymes that phosphorylates target proteins on tyrosine residues, thus playing a crucial role in signal transduction.

T06241.title: θ temperature
T06241.definition: The temperature at which a solution is in the θ state.

T03420.title: λ-transition
T03420.definition: A second-order or higher-order transition, in which the heat capacity shows either a discontinuity (second-order) or a vertex (higher-order) at the transition temperature. Example: The transition at \(846\ \rm{K}\), accompanied by a finite change in specific heat capacity at constant pressure \(C_{p}\), of the low-temperature polymorph of quartz to the high-temperature polymorph.

13923.title: ultimate biodegradation
13923.definition: Complete breakdown of a compound to either fully oxidized or reduced simple molecules (such as carbon dioxide/methane, nitrate/ammonium, and water).

12605.title: unimolecular dissociation
12605.definition: Fragmentation reaction in which the molecularity of the reaction system is unity. The dissociation may arise from the extra energy acquired by a metastable ion produced in the ion source or that provided by collisional excitation of a stable ion.

12606.title: unit mass resolution
12606.definition: Mass resolution such that it is possible to clearly distinguish a peak corresponding to a singly charged ion from its neighbors \(\pu{1 u}\) away, usually with no more than \(\pu{5\!-\! 10\%}\) overlap.

13767.title: ubiquitin
13767.definition: Highly conserved 76 amino acid peptide abundant in eukaryotic cells. Its covalent attachment to a protein by a ubiquitin ligase complex targets that protein for destruction by the proteasome.

16176.title: ulcer
16176.definition: Defect, often associated with inflammation, occurring locally or at the surface of an organ or tissue owing to sloughing of necrotic tissue.

U06546.title: ultimate capacity
U06546.definition: The theoretical maximum capacity of a solvent containing a given concentration of extractant for a solute under any conditions. Where appropriate the term stoichiometric capacity can be used.

14200.title: ultra-high throughput
14200.definition: Relative term, currently applied to the screening of \(\pu{E5}\) test samples in a \(\pu{24\!\mbox{-}h}\) period.

09432.title: ultra-shallow depth profile
09432.definition: Depth profile in secondary-ion mass spectrometry where the depth over which significant changes occur is less than \(\pu{10 nm}\).

U06547.title: ultrafiltrate
U06547.definition: The solution obtained by ultrafiltration, in general not of the same composition as the equilibrium solution.

U06548.title: ultrafiltration
U06548.definition: A separation process whereby a solution containing a solute of molecular size significantly greater than that of the solvent molecule is removed from the solvent by the application of a hydraulic pressure which forces only the solvent to flow through a suitable membrane, usually having a pore size in the range \(0.001{-}0.1\ \unicode[Times]{x3BC}\rm{m}\).

14401.title: ultrafine particle
14401.definition: Particle in air of aerodynamic diameter \(\pu{\lt 0.1 \upmu m}\).

09085.title: ultramicroelectrode
09085.definition: Electrode with smallest dimension of less than 25 micrometre.

U06549.title: ultrasonic detector
U06549.definition: Sound is generated in a reference cell and a measuring cell. An eluted component passing through the measuring cell changes the velocity of sound in the cell. This change is detected by a phase shift of acoustic signals between the two cells. This detector is usually employed for inorganic gases in the region where thermal conductivity detectors are not sufficiently sensitive. The detection threshold is of the order of \(0.1\ \rm{ppmv}\). The linear dynamic range is of the order of \(10^{3}\).

08561.title: ultrasonic nebulizers
08561.definition: Nebulizers whose aerosol generation principle is based on the transfer of the energy from a vibrating transducer to the liquid sample.

11336.title: ultrasonography
11336.definition: Imaging technique that creates a picture of internal body structures from differentially reflected ultrasound waves.

11337.title: ultrasound
11337.definition:
Sound waves of frequency higher than the range audible to the human ear.
Imaging technique that uses such sound waves to create a picture of internal body structures.

10231.title: ultrasound-assisted extraction
10231.definition: Extraction in which ultrasound energy is used to increase the extraction rate by enhancing the contact area between the sample and solvent and by promoting efficient agitation.

UT07492.title: ultraviolet
UT07492.definition: Region of the electromagnetic spectrum extending from about \(100\ \rm{nm}\) to \(400\ \rm{nm}\). This region is divided into four sub-bands as follows: Vacuum UV (VUV) \(100{-}200\ \rm{nm}\)UV-C \(200{-}280\ \rm{nm}\)UV-B\(280{-}315\ \rm{nm}\)UV-A\(315{-}400\ \rm{nm}\).

11338.title: umbilical artery
11338.definition: Paired artery that, in the fetus, returns deoxygenated blood from each half of the fetal body to the placenta, via the umbilical cord.

11339.title: umbilical cord
11339.definition: Cord-like structure connecting the fetus with the placenta and housing the umbilical artery and umbilical vein that carry nutrients from the mother and remove wastes from the fetus.

11340.title: umbilical hernia
11340.definition: Protrusion of bowel or omentum through the abdominal wall at the umbilicus.

11341.title: umbilical vein
11341.definition: Vessel within the umbilical cord, entering the fetus at the umbilicus and carrying oxygenated blood from the placenta.

16263.title: umbilicus
16263.definition: Feature marking the point in the abdominal wall where the umbilical cord entered the fetus.

U06550.title: umpire sample
U06550.definition: A sample taken, prepared and stored in an agreed upon manner for the purpose of settling a dispute. The agreement usually extends beyond the sample to the basis for reaching a decision (e.g. quantity of material from which taken, use of a third party and criteria serving as the basis for acceptance, rejection or economic adjustment). The term 'reference sample' has been used in this context but this term more properly should be used in conjunction with a 'reference material' or 'reference standard' which has a true or assigned value for a constituent or property. One of the characteristics of a reference material or reference standard is that it must have a negligible sampling error between test portions.

U06551.title: umpolung
U06551.definition: Any process by which the normal alternating donor and acceptor reactivity pattern of a chain, which is due to the presence of $\ce{O}$ or $\ce{N}$ heteroatoms, is interchanged. Reactivity umpolung is most often achieved by temporary exchange of heteroatoms ($\ce{N}$, $\ce{O}$) by others, such as $\ce{P}$, $\ce{S}$ and $\ce{Se}$. The original meaning of the term has been extended to the reversal of any commonly accepted reactivity pattern. For example, reaction of $\ce{R–C#CX}$ ($\ce{X}$ = halide) as a synthon for $\ce{'R–C#C^{+}}$ (i.e. electrophilic acetylene) is an umpolung of the normal more common acetylide, $\ce{R–C#C^{−}}$ (i.e. nucleophilic) reactivity.

U06552.title: unactivated adsorption process
U06552.definition: If the temperature coefficient of the rate of adsorption is very small, the adsorption process is said to be unactivated (i.e. to have a negligible activation energy). In this case the sticking coefficient at low coverages may be near unity particularly for smaller molecules.

12092.title: unbiased stereology
12092.definition: Stereological method that uses systematic analysis of defined spatial fractions of a sample to estimate numbers of neuronal nuclei independent of changes in size and shape that may occur during tissue processing.

16177.title: uncertainty
16177.definition: Parameter characterizing the dispersion of the quantity values being attributed to a measurand, based on the information used.

15121.title: uncertainty factor
15121.definition:
In assay methodology, confidence interval or fiducial limit used to assess the probable precision of an estimate.
In toxicology, value used in extrapolation from experimental animals to humans (assuming that humans may be more sensitive) or from selected individuals to the general population.Example: A value applied to the no-observed-effect-level (NOEL) or no-observed-adverse-effect-level (NOAEL) to derive an acceptable daily intake (ADI) or tolerable daily intake (TDI).Note: The NOEL or NOAEL is divided by the value to calculate the ADI or TDI.

U06553.title: uncertainty of measurement
U06553.definition: Parameter, associated with the result of a measurement, that characterizes the dispersion of the values that could reasonably be attributed to the measurand (the quantity being measured).

12096.title: unconditioned stimulus
12096.definition: Stimulus that automatically elicits a paired response, such as food eliciting salivation in a hungry animal.

12153.title: unconscious
12153.definition:
Not in a conscious state.
In psychoanalytic theory, describing feelings and motivations of which one is unaware that nevertheless shape behavior.

12154.title: uncus
12154.definition: Anterior projection of the gray matter surrounding the hippocampus, covered by a region of the temporal lobe, involved in olfaction.

11530.title: underdetermined system
11530.definition: A system in which the number of descriptors is much larger than the number of observations.

10158.title: underfitting
10158.definition: Condition in which a model fails to describe the data adequately.

08297.title: undersampling
08297.definition: Sampling less frequently than is required by the Nyquist criterion.

11342.title: undescended testis
11342.definition: Testis that has failed to descend completely from its developmental origin in the lower abdominal cavity into the scrotum.

UT07638.title: uniaxial pressing
UT07638.definition: Application of pressure in one direction during ceramization to achieve a uniform densification and the production of a compact monolith.

UT07493.title: uniaxial sample
UT07493.definition: Sample characterized by a (unique) sample axis Z with all directions perpendicular to Z being equivalent. In other words, the sample properties are invariant to rotation around Z. Uniaxiality exists in many anisotropic samples and simplifies the interpretation of their spectra considerably.

U06554.title: unified atomic mass unit
U06554.definition: Non-SI unit of mass (equal to the atomic mass constant), defined as one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom in its ground state and used to express masses of atomic particles, \(\rm{u} \approx \pu{1.6605402(10)E-27 kg}\).

U06555.title: uniform corrosion
U06555.definition: Corrosion is uniform if the time average of the corrosion current through a unit area of any macroscopic dimension is independent of the position on the surface.

12272.title: uniform dispersion
12272.definition: Dispersion of particles of identical size, shape, and constitution.

U06558.title: uniform polymer
U06558.definition: A polymer composed of molecules uniform with respect to relative molecular mass and constitution.

U06556.title: uniformly labelled
U06556.definition: A selectively labelled compound where all atoms of a particular element are labelled in the same isotopic ratio.

U06557.title: uniformly labelled tracer
U06557.definition: A tracer in which the label is uniformly distributed over its possible positions.

08971.title: unimer
08971.definition: Species comprising only one monomer unit.

16248.title: unimolecular
16248.definition: Feature of a reaction in which only one molecular entity is involved.

U06560.title: unit
U06560.definition: Each of the discrete, identifiable portions of material suitable for removal from a population as a sample or as a portion of a sample, and which can be individually considered, examined or tested, or combined. In the case of sampling bulk materials (or large packages), the units are increments, created by a sampling device. In the case of packaged materials, the unit may vary with the level of commercial distribution. For example, an individual piece of candy is the sampling unit at the consumer level; a package of individual pieces is the sampling unit at the retail level; a carton of packages is the sampling unit at the wholesale level; a pallet of cartons is the shipping unit at the distribution centre level; and a truckload of pallets is the consignment unit at the manufacture level. Before packaging, the bin containing the individual pieces would be the bulk lot (or batch) for sampling.

U06562.title: unit cell
U06562.definition: The smallest, regularly repeating material portion contained in a parallelepiped from which a crystal is formed by parallel displacements in three dimensions.

U06561.title: unit
U06561.definition: Particular quantity, defined and adopted by convention, with which other quanitities of the same kind are compared in order to express their magnitudes relative to that quantity. Units have conventionally assigned names and symbols.

16178.title: unit risk
16178.definition: Upper-bound excess lifetime cancer risk estimated to result from continuous exposure to an agent at a concentration of \(\pu{1 \upmu g L-1}\) in water, or \(\pu{1 \upmu g m-3}\) in air.

U06563.title: unit system
U06563.definition: Set of base units, together with derived units, defined in accordance with given rules, for a given system of quantities.

08050.title: unitary quantity
08050.definition: Quantity with a magnitude expressed as a reference quantity multiplied by a number.

U06564.title: universal calibration
U06564.definition: A calibration of a size-exclusion chromatography set-up based on the finding that the retention volume of a molecular or particulate species is a single-valued function of an appropriate size parameter of this molecule or particle, irrespective of its chemical nature and structure. The product of the intrinsic viscosity and molar mass, \([\eta]M\), has been widely used as the size parameter.

U06565.title: universal detector
U06565.definition: A detector which responds to every component in the column effluent except the mobile phase.

09054.title: universal indicator
09054.definition: Visual indicator composed of a solution of several pH indicators (main components are thymol blue, methyl red, bromothymol blue and phenolphthalein) that changes color through a range of pH values, usually from 1 to 14.

12736.title: unmet medical need
12736.definition: Term used for diseases or other disorders for which no optimal therapeutic options exist.

12189.title: unperturbed conformational state
12189.definition: Chain conformation corresponding to unperturbed dimensions.

U06566.title: unperturbed dimensions
U06566.definition: The dimensions of an actual polymer random coil in a θ state.

12196.title: unperturbed end-to-end distance
12196.definition: Magnitude of the unperturbed end-to-end vector.

12195.title: unperturbed end-to-end vector
12195.definition: Vector connecting the two ends of a linear chain in a particular conformation, with the chain having unperturbed dimensions.

12190.title: unperturbed radius of gyration
12190.definition: Radius of gyration of a macromolecule in an unperturbed conformational state.

U06567.title: unreactive
U06567.definition: Failing to react with a specified chemical species under specified conditions. The term should not be used in place of stable, since a relatively more stable species may nevertheless be more reactive than some reference species towards a given reaction partner.

13768.title: unresponsiveness
13768.definition: Inability to respond to an antigenic stimulus.

15369.title: unsaturated solution
15369.definition: Solution that has a lower proportion of a solute than one that is in equilibrium with undissolved solute at specified values of temperature and pressure.

09864.title: unsaturation index
09864.definition: Measure of the number of double bonds in fatty acids moieties of phospholipids, calculated as the fraction of each unsaturated fatty acid multiplied by the number of double bonds within that fatty acid.

U06569.title: unstable
U06569.definition: The opposite of stable, i.e. the chemical species concerned has a higher molar Gibbs energy than some assumed standard. The term should not be used in place of reactive or transient, although more reactive or transient species are frequently also more unstable. (Very unstable chemical species tend to undergo exothermic unimolecular decompositions. Variations in the structure of the related chemical species of this kind generally affect the energy of the transition states for these decompositions less than they affect the stability of the decomposing chemical species. Low stability may therefore parallel a relatively high rate of unimolecular decomposition.)

U06571.title: unstable ion
U06571.definition: An ion which is sufficiently excited to dissociate within the ion source.

10146.title: unsupervised classification
10146.definition: Classification in which no prior information about membership of groups is known.

10147.title: unweighted pair group method with arithmetic mean
10147.definition: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the distance between two clusters is the average of all distances between pairs of objects.

U06574.title: upconversion
U06574.definition:
The process by which two photons with frequencies \(
u _{2}\) and \(
u _{3}\) combine in a non-linear medium to produce a higher energy photon with frequency \(
u _{1}\) such that \(
u _{1}=
u _{2}+
u _{3}\).

UT06884.title: uphill transport
UT06884.definition: Process in which diffusion of a component occurs from a less concentrated stream to a more concentrated permeable stream.

16179.title: upper boundary
16179.definition: Estimate of the plausible upper limit to the true value of a quantity.

UT07280.title: upper critical solution temperature
UT07280.definition: Critical temperature above which a mixture is miscible.

U06576.title: upper limit of measurement
U06576.definition: Highest value of the air quality characteristic which can be measured by an instrument; its variations, caused for example by instability, are expected to lie within specified limits. The difference between the lower detection limit and the upper limit of measurement constitutes the dynamic range of the instrument.

12155.title: upper motor neuron
12155.definition: Neuron whose cell body lies in the cerebral cortex or brainstem and whose axon carries impulses to a lower motor neuron.

UT06882.title: upstream
UT06882.definition: Side of a membrane into which penetrants enter from the feed stream.

15122.title: upstream water
15122.definition: Water in a rivulet, river, or lake that is situated above a defined point, in a direction opposite to that of the current flow.

UT06806.title: uptake
UT06806.definition: Entry of a substance into the body, into an organ, into a tissue, into a cell, or into the body fluids by passage through a membrane or by other means.

15123.title: uptake rate constant
15123.definition: First-order one-compartment constant to describe the uptake of a substance by an organism from water.

U06578.title: urethanes
U06578.definition: An alternative term for the compounds $\ce{R2NC(=O)OR'}$ ($\ce{R} \neq \ce{H}$), esters of carbamic acids, $\ce{R2NC(=O)OH}$, in strict use limited to the ethyl esters, but widely used in the general sense, e.g. 'polyurethane resins'.

11343.title: urethra
11343.definition: Duct by which urine is conveyed out of the body from the bladder, and which in male vertebrates also conveys semen.

09653.title: urine
09653.definition: Fluid containing metabolic products that is excreted by the kidneys, stored in the bladder, and normally discharged by way of the urethra.

11344.title: urogenital
11344.definition: Concerning the urinary and genital organs.

11345.title: urogenital sinus
11345.definition: Embryonic structure that forms in the ventral part of the cloaca when it separates from the anal canal to give rise to the genitourinary organs.

U06579.title: uronic acids
U06579.definition: Monocarboxylic acids formally derived by oxidation to a carboxy group of the terminal $\ce{–CH2OH}$ group of aldoses, e.g. ᴅ-glucuronic acid.

U06580.title: uronium salts
U06580.definition: Salts of O-hydronated urea, having the structure $\ce{[HOC(=NH2)NH2]^{+}X^{−}}$ (and O- and N- hydrocarbyl derivatives).

16180.title: urticaria
16180.definition: Vascular reaction of the skin marked by the transient appearance of smooth, slightly elevated patches (wheals, hives) that are redder or paler than the surrounding skin and often attended by severe itching.

09433.title: useful ion yield
09433.definition: In secondary ion mass spectrometry, number of ions of a particular isotope detected divided by the number of atoms of the same element sputtered from the sample.

09434.title: useful spatial resolution
09434.definition: Image resolution in secondary ion mass spectrometry obtained in practice.

11346.title: uterine crypt
11346.definition: Chamber on the interior surface of the uterus that serves as a site of embryo homing and implantation.

11347.title: uterine cycle
11347.definition: Regular, periodic changes that occur in the uterus and, together with the ovarian cycle constitute the menstrual cycle necessary for female fertility.

11348.title: uterotrophic
11348.definition: Having an effect on the uterus.

11349.title: uterotrophic assay
11349.definition: Procedure in which immature female rodents are treated for three days with a test substance. A resultant increase in uterine wet weight suggests an estrogenic activity of the substance.

11350.title: uterus
11350.definition: Hollow muscular organ of the female reproductive system that receives the fertilized ovum (see implantation) and supports the subsequent development of the fetus.

10237.title: UV photochemical digestion
10237.definition: Formation of free metal ions in aqueous solution by oxidation under the influence of UV light and possibly an oxidizing agent (e.g. hydrogen peroxide or peroxodisulfate) in order to break down dissolved organic matter and metal complexes.

U06584.title: ultraviolet stabilizer
U06584.definition: A substance added to a sample to prevent photodeterioration by ultraviolet (UV) light.

11351.title: uvula
11351.definition: Muscular projection from the posterior edge of the soft palate.

12607.title: v-ion
12607.definition: High-energy product ion of a protonated peptide formally equivalent to a y-ion with the ionizing proton on the \(\ce{N}\)-terminus, but with elimination of \(\ce{HR}\) from the \(\ce{N}\)-terminus where \(\ce{R}\) is the side-chain on the \(\ce{C}\)-atom of the \(\ce{N}\)-terminal residue, to give a (\(\ce{H2N^{+}=CH-CO\bond{-}}\)) structure.

12608.title: volumetric internal standard
12608.definition: Compound added in a fixed reproducible amount to a solution to be analyzed by gas chromatography to permit corrections for uncontrolled variations in injected volumes.

13770.title: V(D)J recombination
13770.definition: Mechanism for generating antigen-specific receptors of T cells and B cells; it involves the joining of V, D, and J gene segments, mediated by the enzyme complex V(D)J recombinase, and products of the recombination-activating genes.

13771.title: vaccination
13771.definition: Immunization with a vaccine against a pathogen.

V06585.title: vaccine
V06585.definition: An agent containing antigens produced from killed, attenuated or live pathogenic microorganisms, synthetic peptides or by recombinant organisms, used for stimulating the immune system of the recipient to produce specific antibodies providing active immunity and/or passive immunity in the progeny.

09300.title: vacuum level
09300.definition: Energy level of an electron positioned at rest just outside a solid, i.e. with zero kinetic energy with respect to the sample surface.

09301.title: vacuum level at infinity
09301.definition: Electric potential of the vacuum at a point in space.

09361.title: vacuum level referencing
09361.definition: Method of establishing the kinetic energy scale in which the zero point corresponds to an electron at rest at the vacuum level.

V06586.title: vacuum phototube
V06586.definition: A photo-emissive detector inside an evacuated envelope with a transparent window, the photocathode, and the anode. The photocathode can be opaque or semitransparent.

V06587.title: vacuum system
V06587.definition: Those components used to lower the pressure within a mass spectrometer are all parts of the vacuum system. This includes not only the various pumping components but also valves, gauges and associated electronic or other control devices, the chamber in which ions are formed and detected, and the vacuum envelope.

11352.title: vagina
11352.definition: Fibromuscular canal passing between the uterine cervix and the opening to the vulva.

11353.title: vaginal cornification
11353.definition: Conversion of the normal epithelium of the vagina to a keratinized squamous (flattened) epithelium.

11354.title: vaginal patency
11354.definition: Referring to the opening of the vagina that usually occurs at sexual maturity and is maintained by hormonal influences pre-menopausally.

11355.title: vaginal smear
11355.definition: Examination by light microscopy of a sample of a vaginal discharge, used in the diagnosis of a vaginal infection.

12156.title: vagus nerve
12156.definition: Tenth cranial nerve, arising from the medulla oblongata.

V06588.title: valence
V06588.definition: The maximum number of univalent atoms (originally hydrogen or chlorine atoms) that may combine with an atom of the element under consideration, or with a fragment, or for which an atom of this element can be substituted.

V06589.title: valence band
V06589.definition: Highest energy continuum of energy levels in a solid that is fully occupied by electrons at \(0\ \rm{K}\).

08878.title: valence bond theory
08878.definition: Quantum mechanics theory of chemical bonding that treats electrons as being assigned to individual bonds between particular atoms.

V06590.title: valence isomer
V06590.definition: A constitutional isomer interrelated with another by pericyclic reactions. For example, Dewar benzene, prismane and benzvalene are valence isomers of benzene.

V06591.title: valence tautomerization
V06591.definition: The term describes simple reversible and generally rapid isomerizations or degenerate rearrangements involving the formation and rupture of single and/or double bonds, without migration of atoms or groups; e.g.

V06592.title: valence transition
V06592.definition: A transition observed in certain rare-earth and actinide materials in which the electronic occupation of the 4f or 5f orbital changes with external conditions for example, temperature and pressure. Example: The transition at approximately \(0.65\ \rm{GPa}\) where black, semiconducting $\ce{Sm^{2+}S^{2−}}$ changes to golden metallic $\ce{(Sm^{3+} + e^{−})S^{2-}}$.

09362.title: valence-band spectrum
09362.definition: X-ray photoelectron energy distribution arising from the excitation of electrons from the valence band of the sample material.

08138.title: validation
08138.definition: Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that the requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled.

11531.title: validation set
11531.definition:
The molecules not used to devise a computational model but instead are used during model development to test for possible over-fitting as seen when additional
 properties are added to a model but the predicted potencies of the validation set become less accurate.

16182.title: validity of a measurement
16182.definition: Expression of the degree to which a measurement measures what it purports to measure.

16183.title: validity
16183.definition: Degree to which the inferences drawn, especially generalizations extending beyond the study sample, are warranted when account is taken of the study methods, the representativeness of the study sample, and the nature of the population from which it is drawn.

V06594.title: value of a division
V06594.definition: The reciprocal of the sensitivity; like the latter, it usually varies with load. It is determined by empirical calibration.

V06593.title: value
V06593.definition: Magnitude of a particular quantity generally expressed as a unit of measurement multiplied by a number.

V06597.title: van der Waals forces
V06597.definition: The attractive or repulsive forces between molecular entities (or between groups within the same molecular entity) other than those due to bond formation or to the electrostatic interaction of ions or of ionic groups with one another or with neutral molecules. The term includes: dipole–dipole, dipole-induced dipole and London (instantaneous induced dipole-induced dipole) forces. The term is sometimes used loosely for the totality of nonspecific attractive or repulsive intermolecular forces.

09582.title: vapor deposition
09582.definition: Growth of solid materials on a substrate by deposition from the gas phase.

V06598.title: vaporization temperature
V06598.definition: The temperature of the atomization surface at which analyte loss becomes statistically significant.

V06599.title: vapour phase interference
V06599.definition: Interference caused by a change in the fraction of analyte dissociated, ionized or excited in the gaseous phase. (Note: here 'dissociation' means the formation of free neutral atoms from free molecules in the gaseous phase. The term atomization is here not appropriate because the latter also covers the formation of free atomic ions.) These interferences may be called dissociation, ionization and excitation interference, respectively.

13772.title: variable gene
13772.definition: Gene, segment(s) of which rearrange together with diversity (D) gene and joining (J) gene segments in order to encode the variable (V) region amino acid sequences of immunoglobulins (Ig) and T-cell receptors (TCRs).

V06601.title: variable pathlength cell
V06601.definition: A cell whose pathlength can be varied either continuously or in steps by means of spacers.

13773.title: variable region
13773.definition: N-terminal portion of an immunoglobulin (Ig) or T-cell receptor (TCR) that contains the antigen-binding region of the molecule. V regions are formed by the recombination of V(D) and J gene segments.

V06600.title: variable
V06600.definition: The quantity or characteristic measured or computed. The corresponding numerical value may be taken for statistical handling; it may, for example, be a measured value or result.

10064.title: variance scaling
10064.definition: Scaling in which the scaling matrix is the standard deviation of each variable across the objects. \[a_{i,j}^{\ast} = \frac{a_{i,j}}{s_{j}}\]

V06602.title: variance
V06602.definition: The sum of the squares of the standard deviations, expressing the contributions to the overall precision from various sources of uncertainty.

V06603.title: variational transition state theory
V06603.definition: This expression is applied to modifications of conventional transition state theory in which the position of the dividing surface in the potential-energy surface is varied. The rate is calculated with the surface at various positions, and the lowest rate calculated is taken to be closest to the truth.

11358.title: vas deferens
11358.definition: Secretory duct of the testis running between the epididymis and the ejaculatory duct.

13774.title: vascular addressin
13774.definition: Cell adhesion molecule present on the luminal surface of blood and lymph vessel endothelium, recognized by homing molecules that direct leukocytes to tissues with the appropriate 'address'.

13775.title: vascular cell adhesion molecule
13775.definition: Molecule, expressed on the surface of endothelial cells that functions in the adhesion of lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils to vascular endothelium to the vascular surface.

13776.title: vasculitis
13776.definition: Group of disorders that share a common underlying problem of inflammation of a blood vessel or vessels.

11357.title: vasculogenesis
11357.definition: De novo development of blood vessel endothelium in absence of preexisting vessels, e.g., during fetal development or in connection with tissue repair, initiated by migration of mesodermal precursor cells.

11359.title: vasectomy
11359.definition: Surgical removal of all or part of each vas deferens, typically as a means of sterilization.

13777.title: vasoactive amine
13777.definition: Substance containing amino group(s) that increases vascular permeability and smooth muscle contraction.

12157.title: vasoconstriction
12157.definition: Decrease in the diameter of the lumen of a blood vessel (especially in the arteries and arterioles) as a result of contraction of smooth muscles in the vessel walls.

16184.title: vasodilation
16184.definition: Increase in the caliber of the blood vessels, leading to an increased blood flow.

11360.title: vasopressin
11360.definition: Pituitary hormone that acts to promote the retention of water by the kidneys and to increase blood pressure.

12160.title: vasorelaxation
12160.definition: Increase in the diameter of the lumen of the blood vessels as a result of relaxation of smooth muscles in the vessel walls.

12161.title: vasospasm
12161.definition: Contraction of the muscular wall of blood vessels with sustained vasoconstriction possibly leading to tissue ischemia.

V06606.title: vector
V06606.definition: A DNA molecule (plasmid, virus, bacteriophage, artificial or cut DNA molecule) capable of being replicated and bearing cloning sites for the introduction of foreign DNA, used to introduce this DNA into host cells.Any organism that transmits a disease between two hosts.

09583.title: vector scan
09583.definition: Pattern formation using a directed electron beam or ion beam that skips from region to region requiring exposure but is otherwise turned off.

16185.title: vehicle
16185.definition: Substance(s) used to formulate active ingredients for administration or use.

V06608.title: velocity
V06608.definition: The flux density \(N_{\rm{B}}\) is related to the velocity by the equation \[N_{\rm{B}}=c_{\rm{B}}\ v_{\rm{B}}\] The vector \(v_{\rm{B}}\) is the macroscopic average velocity at which the species B moves (which is to be distinguished from the random molecular velocity); \(c_{\rm{B}}\) is the concentration of species B (\(\pu{mol m-3}\)). Note that the velocity is defined with respect to a frame of reference.

V06607.title: velocity
V06607.definition: Vector quantity equal to the derivative of the position vector with respect to time (symbols \(u\), \(v\), \(w\) for components of \(c\)).

11361.title: velopharyngeal insufficiency
11361.definition: Inability to achieve closure of the velopharyngeal sphincter (closure of the muscle of the soft palate) during speech, owing to muscular dysfunction, cleft palate, or other disorders.

11362.title: vena cava
11362.definition: Large vein returning deoxygenated blood to the right heart.

12162.title: venom
12162.definition: Animal toxin generally used for self-defense or predation and usually delivered by a bite or sting.

16186.title: ventilation
16186.definition:
Process of supplying a building or room with fresh air.
Process of exchange of air between the ambient atmosphere and the lungs.
In physiology, the amount of air inhaled per day.
Oxygenation of blood.

11363.title: ventral
11363.definition: Situated to the anterior side of the trunk; in humans, to the front of the body.

12163.title: ventricle
12163.definition: Normal cavity within an organ, as in the brain or heart.

16187.title: ventricular fibrillation
16187.definition: Irregular heartbeat characterized by uncoordinated contractions of the ventricle.

11365.title: ventricular septal defect
11365.definition: Congenital defect with an opening in the wall separating the right and left ventricles of the heart (see ventricular septum).

11364.title: ventricular septum
11364.definition: Dividing wall between the two lower chambers (ventricles) of the heart.

12164.title: ventriculo-atrial shunt
12164.definition: Surgical shunt draining cerebrospinal fluid into a cardiac atrium, to relieve pressure in hydrocephalus.

12167.title: ventriculo-peritoneal shunt
12167.definition: Surgical shunt draining cerebrospinal fluid into the peritoneum of the abdominal cavity, to relieve pressure in hydrocephalus.

V06609.title: verdazyl radicals
V06609.definition: Relatively stable delocalized radicals, derived from hydrazyl, $\ce{H2NN^{.}H}$, of the types shown, in particular the six-membered ring:

08139.title: verification
08139.definition: Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that specified requirements have been fulfilled.

16188.title: vermicide
16188.definition: Substance intended to kill intestinal worms.

12168.title: vermis
12168.definition: Narrow central part of the cerebellum between the two cerebellar hemispheres.

11366.title: vertebra
11366.definition: One of the bony segments that together make up the bony column surrounding the spinal cord.

12169.title: vertebral column
12169.definition: Bony structure consisting of the vertebrae and enclosing the spinal cord.

11367.title: vertebrate
11367.definition: Denoting an animal that has as part of its nervous system a spinal cord that is surrounded by a bony vertebral column.

V06610.title: vertical ionization
V06610.definition: A process whereby an electron is removed from a molecule in its ground or an excited state so rapidly that a positive ion is produced without change in the positions or momenta of the atoms. The resultant ion is often in an excited state.

12170.title: vertigo
12170.definition: Dizziness; an illusion of movement as if the external world were revolving around one’s self or as if one’s self were revolving in space.

V06612.title: Verwey transition
V06612.definition: An electron-ordering transition occurring in a mixed-valent system that results in an ordering of formal valence states in the low-temperature phase. Example: The prototype system, first identified by Verwey, is the ferrospinel magnetite, $\ce{Fe^{3+}[Fe^{3+}Fe^{2+}]O4}$ in which an ordering of $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ and $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ ions within octahedral sites is thought to occur below \(T_{\rm{v}}\approx 120\ \rm{K}\).

13778.title: very early activating antigen
13778.definition: Specific antigen expressed on lymphocytes very soon after activation by phorbol myristate acetate (PMA).

13779.title: very late activation antigen
13779.definition: T-cell surface antigen, named for its delayed appearance after T-cell activation; a member of the integrin superfamily involved in cell adhesion.

16189.title: vesicant
16189.definition:
adj., Producing blisters on the skin.
n., Substance that causes blisters on the skin.

11368.title: vesicle
11368.definition: Small fluid-filled sac, bladder-like structure, or blister.

14341.title: vesicle polymerisation
14341.definition: Polymerization inside the bilayer of a vesicle leading to formation of polymer inside the bilayer.

11369.title: vestigial
11369.definition: In anatomy, pertaining to a remnant of an embryonic or fetal structure persisting in the adult.

13780.title: vetoing
13780.definition: Elimination by apoptosis of a self-peptide-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecule recognizing lymphocyte by a self-peptide-presenting (veto) cell.

15124.title: viability selection
15124.definition: Component of the life cycle of an individual in which natural selection can occur through the differential survival of individuals. It begins at the formation of the zygote and continues throughout the life of the individual.

08704.title: vibrational circular dichroism
08704.definition: Circular dichroism, \(k^{\rm{L}} – k^{\rm{R}}\), for vibrational transitions.

08705.title: vibrational eigenvector
08705.definition:
Part of the solution of the matrix equation of normal coordinate analysis, \(\boldsymbol{G\!F\!L} = \boldsymbol{L \lambda}\). Each element \(L_{ik}\) of \(\boldsymbol{L}\) is a vibrational eigenvector, and gives the change in internal coordinate \(R_{i}\) during unit change in the normal coordinate \(Q_{k}\), as shown in matrix form by \(\boldsymbol{R} = \boldsymbol{LQ}\), i.e., \(L_{ik} = \partial R_{i}/\partial Q_{k}\).
Eigenvectors are sometimes expressed in terms of symmetry coordinates or Cartesian coordinates.

08706.title: vibrational kinetic energy
08706.definition: Kinetic energy of the molecule as a function of the displacements of the atoms from equilibrium positions. For Cartesian displacement coordinates (\(x, y, z\)), \[T = \sum_{\alpha}½m_{\alpha}(\dot x_{\alpha}^{2} + \dot y_{\alpha}^{2} + \dot z_{\alpha}^{2})\] where the sum is over all atoms and \(\dot{x}_{\alpha}\), etc., are the displacement velocities. For internal coordinates \[T = ½\boldsymbol{P}^{t}\boldsymbol{GP} = ½\dot{\boldsymbol{R}}^{t}{\boldsymbol{G}}^{-1}\dot {\boldsymbol{R}} = ½\sum_{ij}G_{ij}^{-1}\dot R_{i}\dot R_{j}\] where \(\dot {\boldsymbol{R}}^{t}\) and \(\dot {\boldsymbol{R}}\) are the row and column vector, respectively, of the \(\partial R_{i}/\partial t\), \(\boldsymbol{P}^{t}\) and \(\boldsymbol{P}\) are the row and column vector, respectively, of the momenta conjugate to the \(R_{i}\), \(\boldsymbol{G}^{-1}\) is the inverse of the \(\boldsymbol{G}\) matrix and \(G_{ij}^{-1}\) is the \(ij^{\rm{th}}\) element of \(\boldsymbol{G}^{-1}\). The elements of the \(\boldsymbol{G}\) matrix are defined by \[G_{ij} = \sum_{\alpha} \frac{1}{m_{\alpha}} B_{i\alpha} B_{j\alpha}\] where \(B_{i\alpha}\) and \(B_{j\alpha}\) relate the \(i^{\rm{th}}\) and \(j^{\rm{th}}\) internal coordinate to the \(\alpha^{\rm{th}}\) Cartesian coordinate through the equation \(\boldsymbol{R} = \boldsymbol{BX}\) in which \(\boldsymbol{X}\) is the column vector of the Cartesian coordinates.

08707.title: vibrational potential energy
08707.definition:
Potential energy of the molecule as a function of the displacements of the atoms from equilibrium positions. The harmonic terms are quadratic in the displacements and the anharmonic terms are of cubic, quartic and higher orders in the displacements.
\(Q\) are normal coordinates \[2V = \sum\limits_{k}\lambda_{k}Q_{k}^{2} + \sum\limits_{ijk}k_{ijk}Q_{i}Q_{j}Q_{k} + higher\,order\,terms\]
In terms of internal coordinates, \[2V = \sum\limits_{i} F_{ii} R_i^{2} + \sum\limits_{i,j\ne i} F_{ij} R_{i} R_{j} + \sum\limits_{i,j,k} F_{ijk} R_{i} R_{j} R_{k} + higher\,order\,terms\]

V06614.title: vibrational redistribution
V06614.definition: Intramolecular redistribution of energy among the vibrational modes usually giving a statistical distribution of their populations, characterized by the 'vibrational temperature'. For large molecules, this process does not require collisions.

V06615.title: vibrational relaxation
V06615.definition: The loss of vibrational excitation energy by a molecular entity through energy transfer to the environment caused by collisions. The molecular entity relaxes into vibrational equilibrium with its environment.

08708.title: vibrational spectroscopy
08708.definition: Measurement principle of spectroscopy to analyse molecular properties based on vibrations (bond stretching or deformation modes) in chemical species.

08709.title: vibrational term value
08709.definition: Vibrational energy, \(E\), expressed in wavenumber units. \(G = E/(hc)\), where \(h\) is the Planck constant and \(c\) is the speed of light in vacuum.

V06616.title: vibrational term
V06616.definition: Vibrational energy divided by the product of the Planck constant and the speed of light.

V06617.title: vibronic coupling
V06617.definition: Interaction between electronic and vibrational motions in a molecular entity.

V06618.title: vibronic transition
V06618.definition: A transition which involves a change in both the electronic and vibrational quantum numbers of a molecular entity, as opposed to purely electronic or purely vibrational transitions. The transition occurs between two states, just as in a purely electronic transition, but involves a change in both electronic and vibrational energy.

12816.title: Vicat softening temperature
12816.definition: Temperature at which a thermoplastic polymer reaches a specific degree of softness as measured by a standard test.

V06619.title: vidicon
V06619.definition: A vacuum tube containing a photosensitive area, or target, and an electron gun to read the signal from the target. The silicon target consists of a two-dimensional array of Si-photodiodes having a common cathode and isolated anodes. irradiation of the target causes the production of electron-hole pairs which, by recombination, leads to a depletion of the surface charge.

12171.title: vigilance
12171.definition: Ability to maintain concentration or sustain attention over prolonged periods of time.

12172.title: vigilance decrement
12172.definition: Decreased vigilance measured as a decline in the ability to maintain an accurate voluntary response to signals with time.

11371.title: villus
11371.definition:
Projection from the surface, typically of a mucous membrane.
Elongated projection of the dermis into an epidermal space.

11372.title: vimentin
11372.definition: Intermediate filament protein that is expressed in mesenchymal cells, e.g., fibroblasts, leukocytes, and blood vessel endothelial cells.

V06620.title: vinyl carbenes
V06620.definition: Carbenes having a vinylic group on a carbenic carbon atom $\ce{R2C=CRC{:}R  R2C^{+}–CR=C^{−}R}$. E.g. $\ce{H2C=CHC{:}H}$, prop-2-en-1-ylidene.

15262.title: vinyl polymer
15262.definition: Polymer prepared from a monomer containing the vinyl group \(\ce{-CH=CH2}\).

V06622.title: vinylic groups
V06622.definition: The vinyl group ($\ce{CH2=CH\bond{–}}$) and derivatives formed by substitution. Informally, a group, such as $\ce{–OH}$, attached to the free valence of a (substituted) vinyl group is sometimes referred to as 'vinylic'.

15263.title: vinylidene polymer
15263.definition: Polymer prepared from a monomer containing the ethene-1,1-diyl group \(\gt\!\ce{C=CH2}\), formerly called vinylidene.

V06623.title: vinylidenes
V06623.definition: Carbenes in which the carbenic carbon atom has a double bond to another carbon atom $\ce{R2C=C{:}}$, e.g. $\ce{H2C=C{:}}$ ethenylidene.

V06625.title: virial coefficients
V06625.definition: Coefficients (\(B\rm{,}C\rm{,}\,...\)) in the virial equation of state for a real gas \(p\ V_{\rm{m}}=R\ T\ (1+\frac{B}{V_{\rm{m}}}+\frac{C}{V_{\rm{m}}^{2}}+\,...)\) where \(p\) is the pressure, \(V_{\rm{m}}\) the molar volume, \(R\) the gas constant and \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature.

11373.title: virilization
11373.definition: Possession or acquisition of characteristics of a male body, especially by a female or prepubescent male.

12737.title: virtual chemical library
12737.definition: Collection of chemical structures constructed solely in electronic form or on paper.

11532.title: virtual reaction
11532.definition:
The computer encoding of a possible chemical reaction between two explicit or Markush structures or substructures, often with a mapping between the atoms in
 the starting material and those in the product.

11533.title: virtual screening
11533.definition: Computational methods that rank the molecules in a database by their forecast continuous or categorical biological or chemical properties.

V06626.title: virtual transition
V06626.definition: A non-observable liquid-crystal transition that occurs below the crystallization temperature and is determined by extrapolation in binary phase diagrams.

16190.title: virtually safe dose
16190.definition: Human exposure over a lifetime to a carcinogen which has been estimated, using mathematical modeling, to result in a very low incidence of cancer, somewhere between zero and a specified incidence (e.g., 1 cancer in \(\pu{1000000}\) exposed people).

11374.title: viscera
11374.definition: Soft and hollow organs of the body, in vertebrates particularly those found in the thoracic and abdominal cavities.

12817.title: viscoelastic spectrum
12817.definition: Double logarithmic plot of a viscoelastic property vs. frequency of measurement or interval of time of measurement at constant temperature.

V06628.title: viscosity function
V06628.definition: A coefficient connecting the intrinsic viscosity, the radius of gyration and the molar mass of a chain macromolecule, according to the equation: \[\rm{[}\eta \rm{]} = \frac{\mathit{\Phi }\ 6^{3/2}\ ( < s^{2} > )^{3/2}}{M}\] where \(\rm{[}\eta \rm{]}\) is the intrinsic viscosity, \(s\) is the radius of gyration and \(M\) is the molar mass. The viscosity function is often referred to as the Flory constant.

12220.title: viscosity-average molar mass
12220.definition:
The equation for viscosity-average molar mass is \[M_{\rm{v}} = \left[\sum\limits_{M} w_{M}M^{a} \right]^{1/a}\]
The equation for viscosity-average molecular weight is \[M_{\rm{r,v}} = \left[\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}}M_{\rm{r}}^{a} \right]^{1/a}\] where \(a\) is the exponent in the Mark–Houwink equation, \([\eta] = KM^{a}\)

VT07640.title: viscous sintering
VT07640.definition: Sintering process by which it is possible to densify gels to glasses and ceramics at elevated temperatures.

V06631.title: visibility
V06631.definition: Defined as the greatest distance at which a black object of suitable dimensions can be seen and recognized against the horizon sky, or, in the case of night observations, could be seen and recognized if the general illumination were raised to the normal daylight level. The criterion of recognizing the object, not just seeing the object without recognition, is used. Transmissometers, telephotometers and sun photometers are devices used to measure the degree of transmission of light. Nephelometers (integrating) are used to measure visibility by way of the light scattering from aerosols in the air mass.

VT07496.title: visible
VT07496.definition: Region of the electromagnetic spectrum extending from about \(400\ \rm{nm}\) to \(760\ \rm{nm}\). This is the wavelength region to which the human eye is sensitive. There are no precise limits for the spectral range of visible radiation since they depend upon the amount of radiant power reaching the retina and on the responsivity of the observer.

12173.title: visual cortex
12173.definition: Part of the cerebral cortex located in the occipital lobe, responsible for processing the images of sight.

15125.title: vital rates
15125.definition: Measures of how fast vital statistics change in a population (usually expressed per \(\pu{1000}\) individuals).

11375.title: vitellogenin
11375.definition: Protein that forms part of the yolk of egg-laying vertebrates.

12818.title: vitrification
12818.definition: Formation of a polymer glass from a polymer melt.

12819.title: Vogel–Fulcher–Tammann equation
12819.definition: Equation describing the time-dependence of a relaxation time that deviates from an Arrhenius-type temperature dependence. \[\tau = \tau_{0} \exp\!\left({\frac{B}{T - T_{0}}}\right)\] \(\tau\)/\(\pu{s}\) = relaxation time; \(\tau_{0}\)/\(\pu{s}\) = relaxation time at the Kauzmann temperature, \(B\)/\(\pu{K}\) = constant; \(T\)/\(\pu{K}\) = temperature; \(T_{0}\)/\(\pu{K}\) = Kauzmann temperature.

08298.title: Voigt function
08298.definition: Convolution of Gaussian and Lorentzian (Cauchy) functions.

14103.title: volatile organic chemical/compounds
14103.definition: Term commonly used to designate organic gas-phase pollutants frequently degraded by photocatalytic procedures.

V06632.title: volatilization
V06632.definition: The conversion of a solid or liquid to a gas or vapour by application of heat, by reducing pressure, by chemical reaction or by a combination of these processes.Example: \(\rm{W(s)}+\frac{3}{2}\rm{O}_{2}\:\rm{(g)}\:\rightarrow \:\rm{WO}_{3}\:\rm{(g)}\)

V06633.title: volatilizer
V06633.definition: Material added to a sample to increase its volatilization or that of some component of it. Volatilizers increase the fraction volatilized either by forming more volatile compounds or by increasing the total surface area of all analyte particles (e.g. by explosive disintegration or by dispersal of the analyte in a highly volatile matrix).

V06634.title: volt
V06634.definition: SI derived unit of electric potential, \(\pu{V} = \pu{J C-1} = \pu{m2 kg s-3 A-1}\).

V06635.title: voltage
V06635.definition: The use of this term is discouraged, and the term applied potential should be used instead, for non-periodic signals. However, it is retained here for sinusoidal and other periodic signals because no suitable substitute for it has been proposed.

14201.title: voltage-activated channel
14201.definition: Ion channel that is specifically activated, or gated, by the surrounding potential difference across the cell membrane near the channel (or near the cell, neuron, or synapse).

12174.title: voltage-gated ion channel
12174.definition: Ion channel that opens and closes in response to changes in membrane potential.

V06639.title: voltammetric constant

09148.title: voltammetry
09148.definition: Electrochemical measurement principle in which the electrode potential of a working electrode is controlled and the electric current measured.

09149.title: voltammogram
09149.definition: Current-potential curve in a voltammetry experiment.

V06641.title: volume content
V06641.definition: The volume of an (isolated) specified component (C) divided by the mass of the system (S), e.g. patient–blood volume content. Volume content should not be confused with specific volume (or massic volume), which is the volume of the system divided by the mass of the system.

V06642.title: volume flow rate
V06642.definition: Volume of a component crossing a surface divided by the time.

V06643.title: volume fraction
V06643.definition: Volume of a constituent of a mixture divided by the sum of volumes of all constituents prior to mixing.

V06644.title: volume of activation
V06644.definition: A quantity derived from the pressure dependence of the rate constant of a reaction (mainly used for reactions in solution), defined by the equation: \[\Delta ^{\ddagger }V=- R\ T\ (\frac{\partial (\ln k)}{\partial p})_{T}\] providing that the rate constants of all reactions (except first-order reactions) are expressed in pressure-independent concentration units, such as \(\pu{mol dm-3}\) at a fixed temperature and pressure. The volume of activation is interpreted, according to transition state theory, as the difference between the partial molar volumes of the transition state (\(V\)) and the sums of the partial volumes of the reactants at the same temperature and pressure, i.e. \[\Delta ^{\ddagger}V = ^{\ddagger}V- \sum \left(r\ V_{\rm{R}}\right)\] where \(r\) is the order in the reactant R and \(V_{\rm{R}}\) its partial molar volume.

12738.title: volume of distribution
12738.definition: Apparent (hypothetical) volume of fluid required to contain the total amount of a substance in the body at the same concentration as that present in the plasma assuming equilibrium has been attained.

V06645.title: volume of the stationary phase
V06645.definition: The volume of the stationary liquid phase or of the active solid or of the gel in the column. The volume of any solid support is not included.

08710.title: volume reflection
08710.definition: Re-emergence of electromagnetic radiation from the surface of incidence after penetrating into a powdered sample.

V06648.title: volume strain
V06648.definition: The change of volume divided by the original volume.

12820.title: volume thermodilatometry
12820.definition: Technique in which the volume of a substance under negligible load is measured as a function of temperature while the substance is heated or cooled in a controlled programme.

V06650.title: volume viscosity
V06650.definition: A quantity $\upzeta\!$ which enters into equations at any point where the flow involves a change in volume, i.e. is dilatational. If the deformation is purely dilatational, the average of three normal stress components is: \[\sigma =\frac{1}{3}\ (\sigma _{xx}+\sigma _{yy}+\sigma _{zz})=- p+\zeta \ (\frac{\partial v_{x}}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial v_{y}}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial v_{z}}{\partial z})\] where \(p\) is the hydrostatic pressure at the point considered in the absence of motion.

09302.title: volume yield
09302.definition: Volume sputtered from a sample divided by number of incident particles.

14295.title: volume-average particle diameter
14295.definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[\left\langle d_{\rm{v}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{v}} = \left(\frac{\Sigma N_{i} d_{i}^{3}}{\Sigma N_{i}}\right)^{1/3}\]

V06649.title: volumetric flowrate
V06649.definition: The flowrate of the mobile phase (\(\pu{cm3 min-1}\)), normally specified at the column temperature and outlet pressure, although the measurement may be made at ambient temperature and must be corrected accordingly (and possibly also for water vapour present in the flowmeter).

09055.title: volumetric titration
09055.definition: Titration in which the titrant is added by volume.

V06651.title: volumic
V06651.definition: Attribute to a physical quantity obtained by division by volume. charge density may thus be called volumic charge which is the electric charge in a section of space divided by the volume of that section.

09056.title: von Weimarn ratio
09056.definition: Difference between the concentration of the supersaturated solution (see supersaturation) required for nucleation (\(Q\)) and its solubility (\(S\)), divided by the solubility, \((Q − S)/S\).

VT07153.title: vulcanization
VT07153.definition: Chemical crosslinking of high-molar-mass linear or branched polymers to give a polymer network.

13769.title: Vα-Jα rearrangement
13769.definition: Preferential partnering of \(\ce{J\upalpha\ gene}\) segments with \(\ce{V\upalpha\ gene}\) segments during rearrangement in the T-cell receptor (TCR) gene, possibly following deletion of the \(\ce{V\updelta\ gene}\) region.

V05019.title: ρ-value
V05019.definition: A measure of the susceptibility to the influence of substituent groups on the rate constant or equilibrium constant of a particular organic reaction involving a family of related substrates. Defined by Hammett for the effect of ring substituents in meta- and para-positions of aromatic side-chain reactions by the empirical '\(\rho \sigma \)-equation' of the general form: \[\log _{10}(\frac{k_{\rm{X}}}{k_{\rm{H}}}) = \rho \ \sigma _{\rm{X}}\] in which \(\sigma _{\rm{X}}\) is a constant characteristic of the substituent X and of its position in the reactant molecule. More generally (and not only for aromatic series), \(\rho \)-values (modified with appropriate subscripts and superscripts) are used to designate the susceptibility of reaction series for families of various organic compounds to any substituent effects, as given by the modified set of \(\sigma \)-constants in an empirical \(\rho \sigma \)-correlation. Reactions with a positive \(\rho \)-value are accelerated (or the equilibrium constants of analogous equilibria are increased) by substituents with positive \(\sigma \)-constants. Since the sign of \(\sigma \) was defined so that substituents with a positive \(\sigma \) increase the acidity of benzoic acid, such substituents are generally described as attracting electrons away from the aromatic ring. It follows that reactions with a positive \(\rho \)-value are considered to involve a transition state (or reaction product) so that the difference in energy between this state and the reactants is decreased by a reduction in electron density at the reactive site of the substrate.

13963.title: waste
13963.definition: Residue left when a compound or a product reaches the end of its initial usefulness.

13964.title: waste management
13964.definition: Control of the collection, treatment and disposal of wastes.

12609.title: Wahrhaftig diagram
12609.definition: Diagram illustrating the relative contributions in unimolecular dissociation of an ion, for example, by homolytic cleavage of a single bond, and fragmentation following rearrangement. The diagram is in two parts with a common horizontal axis representing the internal energy of the ion. The vertical axis in one part of the diagram shows the two types of rate constant on a logarithmic scale, and that for the other portion of the diagram indicates the distribution function for internal energy of the ion.

12610.title: Wien filter
12610.definition: Mass spectrometer in which m/z separation is achieved using crossed electric and magnetic fields.

12611.title: w-ion
12611.definition: High-energy product ion of a protonated peptide formally equivalent to a z-ion that has lost the part of the \(\ce{N}\)-terminal side-chain starting at the \(\ce{\upgamma\mbox{-}carbon}\) (if any).

15127.title: Wahlund effect
15127.definition: Net deficit of heterozygotes when two populations, each in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium but with different allele frequencies, are mixed and the genotype frequencies quantified in a combined population sample.

W06653.title: Walden inversion
W06653.definition: Retention of configuration is the preservation of integrity of the spatial arrangement of bonds to a chiral centre during a chemical reaction or transformation. It is also the configurational correlation when a chemical species Xabcd is converted into the chemical species Xabce having the same relative configuration. The configurational change when a chemical species Xabcd (where X is typically carbon), having a tetrahedral arrangement of bonds to X, is converted into the chemical species Xabce having the opposite relative configuration (or when it undergoes an identity reaction in which Xabcd of opposite configuration is produced) is called a Walden inversion or inversion of configuration. The occurrence of a Walden inversion during a chemical transformation is sometimes indicated in the chemical equation by the symbol shown below in place of a simple arrow pointing from reactants to products.

15128.title: waldsterben
15128.definition: Widespread and substantial decline in growth and the change in behavior of many softwood and hardwood forest ecosystems in central Europe.

08562.title: wall atomization
08562.definition: Electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy in which the sample is deposited directly onto the wall of the electrothermal atomizer tube, from which it undergoes all the transformations leading to atomization.

W06654.title: wall-coated open-tubular column
W06654.definition: A column in which the liquid stationary phase is coated on the essentially unmodified smooth inner wall of the tube.

09125.title: wall-jet electrode
09125.definition: A disc electrode with a thin circular jet of fluid impinging on its centre.

10148.title: Ward’s minimum variance method
10148.definition: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the within-cluster variance is minimized.

13781.title: warm autoantibody type
13781.definition: Autoantibodies that react optimally at higher temperatures (\(\pu{37^{\circ}C}\)) with surface antigens of erythrocytes. They mediate autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

W06655.title: wash out
W06655.definition: The removal from the atmosphere of gases and sometimes particles by their solution in or attachment to raindrops as they fall.

08563.title: wash out time
08563.definition: Time required for the output signal of an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer for a given analyte to fall back to baseline levels from the end of sampling time and/or after introducing a blank solution.

15129.title: waste-water
15129.definition: General term describing effluents, leachate, and elutriates which enter the natural environment.

16192.title: wasting syndrome
16192.definition: Disease marked by weight loss and atrophy of muscular and other connective tissues that is not directly related to a decrease in food and water consumption.

12175.title: water maze test
12175.definition: Procedure in which a rat or mouse is placed in a pool of water and observed to swim, using visual environmental clues, to an invisible submerged platform that allows escape from the water.

16193.title: water potential
16193.definition: Difference in free energy or chemical potential (per unit molal volume) between pure water and water in cells and solutions.

W06656.title: watt
W06656.definition: SI derived unit of power, \(\pu{W} = \pu{J s-1} = \pu{m2 kg s-3}\).

W06658.title: wave height
W06658.definition: The limiting current of an individual wave, frequently expressed in arbitrary units for convenience.

09441.title: wave vector
09441.definition: Vector in reciprocal space describing the direction of propagation of X-rays and equal in magnitude to \(2\uppi/\lambda\), where \(\lambda\) is the wavelength of the X-rays.

W06657.title: wavefunction
W06657.definition: The solution of the Schrödinger equation, eigenfunction of the hamiltonian operator. Complex conjugate functions are denoted by an asterisk read as 'star'.

W06660.title: wavelength converter
W06660.definition: A wavelength converter converts radiation at one wavelength to radiation at another detectable wavelength or at a wavelength of improved responsivity of the detector. The classical wavelength converter consists of a screen of luminescent material that absorbs radiation and radiates at a longer wavelength. Such materials are often used to convert ultraviolet to visible radiation for detection by conventional phototubes. In X-ray spectroscopy a converter that emits optical radiation is called a scintillator. In most cases wavelength conversion is from short to long wavelength, but in the case of conversion of long to short wavelength the process is sometimes called upconversion. Wavelengths of coherent sources can be converted using nonlinear optical techniques. A typical example is frequency doubling.

W06661.title: wavelength dispersion
W06661.definition: Spatial separation of characteristic X-rays according to their wavelengths.

W06663.title: wavelength error
W06663.definition: The error in absorbance which may occur if there is a difference between the (mean) wavelength of the radiation entering the sample cell and the indicated wavelength on the spectrometer scale.

08299.title: wavelength in medium
08299.definition: Distance travelled by a wave of electromagnetic radiation in one cycle in a non-absorbing medium of real refractive index \(n\). \(\lambda = \lambda_{0}/n\).

08300.title: wavelength in vacuum
08300.definition: Distance travelled by a wave of electromagnetic radiation in one cycle in vacuum.

W06662.title: wavelength-dispersive X-ray fluorescence analysis
W06662.definition: A kind of X-ray fluorescence analysis involving the measurement of the wavelength spectrum of the emitted radiation e.g. by using a diffraction grating or crystal.

W06659.title: wavelength
W06659.definition: Distance in the direction of propagation of a periodic wave between two successive points where at a given time the phase is the same.

08301.title: wavenumber in medium
08301.definition: Reciprocal of wavelength of electromagnetic radiation. \(\sigma = 1/\lambda\).

08302.title: wavenumber in vacuum
08302.definition: Reciprocal of the vacuum wavelength of electromagnetic radiation. \(\tilde{\nu} = 1/\lambda_{0}\).

W06664.title: wavenumber
W06664.definition: The reciprocal of the wavelength, \(\lambda \), or the number of waves per unit length along the direction of propagation. The SI unit is \(\rm{m}^{-1}\), but a commonly used unit is \(\pu{cm-1}\). Symbols \(\overset{˜}{\nu }\) in a vacuum, \(\sigma \) in a medium.

W06665.title: weak collision
W06665.definition: A collision between two molecules in which the amount of energy transferred from one to the other is not large compared to \(k_{\rm{B}}\ T\) (\(k_{\rm{B}}\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(T\) the absolute temperature).

15130.title: weakest-link incongruity
15130.definition: Questionable extension of the critical life-stage concept (see critical life-stage testing) that protection of the most sensitive life stage will ensure protection of all life stages; it assumes that exposure of field populations to concentrations identified in laboratory testing as causing significant mortality at a critical stage of life will result in significant impact on the field population

11377.title: wean
11377.definition: Accustomize a young mammal to independence from its mother’s milk as a source of nutrition.

WT06852.title: weathering
WT06852.definition: Exposure of a polymeric material to a natural or simulated environment.

11378.title: web
11378.definition: Tissue or membrane present between adjacent structures where it is not usually found, e.g., between fingers or toes, or between the neck and shoulder, representing a congenital abnormality.

W06666.title: weber
W06666.definition: SI derived unit of magnetic flux, \(\pu{Wb} = \pu{V s} = \pu{m2 kg s-2 A-1}\).

W06667.title: wedge projection
W06667.definition: A stereochemical projection, roughly in the mean plane of the molecule, in which bonds are represented by open wedges, tapering off from the nearer atom to the farther atom. It is mainly used to illustrate the conformation of larger cycloalkanes e.g. cyclotetradecane:   equivalent to

13782.title: Wegener granulomatosis
13782.definition: Granulomatous inflammation involving the respiratory tract, and necrotizing vasculitis affecting small to medium-sized vessels (e.g., capillaries, venules, arterioles, and arteries).

15131.title: Weibull model
15131.definition: Dose–response model of the form \[P(d) = \gamma + (1 - \gamma)(1 - e^{-\beta d^{\alpha}})\] where \(P(d)\) is the probability of a tumor (or other response) from lifetime, continuous exposure at dose \(d\) until age \(t\) (when tumor is fatal), \(\alpha\) is a fitted dose parameter (sometimes called the Weibull parameter), \(\beta\) is a fitted dose parameter, and \(\gamma\) is the background response rate.

15132.title: weight composition
15132.definition: Distribution of organisms among the various weight classes present in a population.

15133.title: weight of evidence
15133.definition:
(in general) Quantitative, semiquantitative, or qualitative estimate of the degree to which the evidence supports or undermines a given conclusion.
(in toxicology) Estimate of the extent to which the available biomedical data support the hypothesis that a substance causes a defined toxic effect such as cancer in humans.

16194.title: weight-of-evidence for toxicity
16194.definition: Extent to which the available biomedical data support the hypothesis that a substance causes a defined toxic effect such as cancer in humans.

W06668.title: weight
W06668.definition: Force of gravity acting on a body, \(G=m\ g\), where \(m\) is its mass and \(g\) the acceleration of free fall.

10159.title: weighted least squares regression
10159.definition: Least squares regression in which a nonnegative constant is associated with each value of the dependent variable.

W06670.title: weighted mean
W06670.definition: If in a series of observations a statistical weight (\(w_{i}\)) is assigned to each value, a weighted mean \(\overline{x}_{w}\) can be calculated by the formula: \[\overline{x}_{w}=\frac{\sum w_{i}\ x_{i}}{\sum w_{i}}\]

15134.title: Weismannism
15134.definition: Theory of evolution and heredity propounded by the German biologist, August Weismann, especially in regard to the continuity of the germ-plasm and the nontransmission of acquired characteristics.

W06671.title: Weller correlation
W06671.definition: Empirical correlation for the energy of full charge-transfer exciplex relative to the ground state in n-hexane as a function of the electrochemical one electron standard reduction potential of the cation radical produced upon electron donation and standard reduction potential of the acceptor measured in a polar solvent for the donor (D) and the acceptor (A) involved \[\Delta H(\rm{D}^{+}\rm{A}^{-},\rm{hexane}) = e\left [ E^{0}(\rm{D}^{+\bullet }/\rm{D}) - E^{0}(\rm{A}/\rm{A}^{-\bullet }) \right ]+e\Delta E\] with \(E^{0}(D^{+\bullet }/D)\) and \(E^{0}(A/D^{-\bullet })\) the standard electrode potentials of the donor and acceptor, respectively.

12176.title: Wernicke aphasia
12176.definition: Type of aphasia associated with damage to Wernicke’s area or alternatively the medial temporal lobe of the brain, characterized by preservation of speech but with loss of meaningful language and language comprehension.

12178.title: Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome
12178.definition: Co-existence of Wernicke encephalopathy (with gait, ocular and mental disturbances) and Korsakoff psychosis (severe memory loss, often with aphasia, apraxia or agnosia) caused by vitamin B1 deficiency in the context of chronic alcohol abuse.

12177.title: Wernicke’s area
12177.definition: Region of the brain in superior temporal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere, associated with comprehension of written and spoken language.

09789.title: Western blot
09789.definition: Immunoanalytical technique for the identification of polypeptides separated using gel electrophoresis.
