The polypeptide is transferred by blotting to a membrane, where it undergoes specific interaction with primary antibody that is specific to the protein of interest. The peptides are detected as complexes by a label and/or enzymatic reaction, which may be conjugated to the primary antibody directly or via a separate (secondary) antibody.

12179.title: Western Pacific amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and parkinsonism–dementia complex
12179.definition: Neurodegenerative disease observed in the islands of Guam, Indonesia, Japan and Papua New Guinea, showing combinations of characteristics of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, atypical parkinsonism with dementia, or dementia alone that may present sequentially during life.

W06673.title: wet bulb temperature
W06673.definition: In psychrometry, the temperature of the sensor or the bulb of a thermometer in which a constantly renewed film of water is evaporating. The temperature of the water used to renew the film must be at the temperature of the gas.

15135.title: wet deposition
15135.definition: Transfer of chemicals from the atmosphere to the Earth’s surface in atmospheric water precipitation (atmospheric deposition), e.g., rain, snow, or hail, of pollutants that occur in the precipitation, e.g., as a result of Brownian capture, nucleation, dissolution, or impaction.

09491.title: wet etching
09491.definition: Process of removal of material, typically of a masked pattern on a semiconductor, by exposing it to a corrosive liquid.

15371.title: wet residue method
15371.definition: Method for determining composition of a solid phase in a ternary system at constant temperature and pressure by analysis of the total mixture of solid and liquid in equilibrium.

15136.title: wetland
15136.definition: Area of land consisting of soil that is saturated with moisture, such as a swamp, marsh, or bog.

WT07250.title: wetting
WT07250.definition: Process by which an interface between a solid and a gas is replaced by an interface between the same solid and a liquid.

W06674.title: wetting tension
W06674.definition: The work done on a system when the process of immersional wetting involving unit area of phase $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ is carried out reversibly: \[w_{\rm{W}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }=\gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }- \gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\] where \(\gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\) and \(\gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }\) are the surface tensions between two bulk phases $\ce{\upalpha\!}$, $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ and $\ce{\upbeta\!}$, $\ce{\updelta\!}$, respectively.

11379.title: Wharton’s jelly
11379.definition: Gelatinous substance that embeds the vessels of the umbilical cord.

13783.title: wheal
13783.definition: Circumscribed papule or plaque of edema of the skin, occurring as an urticarial lesion.

13784.title: wheal and flare
13784.definition: Dermatological reaction at a skin site where an antigen is injected into an allergic individual. The reaction is characterized by a 'flare' of erythema and a wheal produced by serum exuding into tissue, causing local edema.

11380.title: white matter
11380.definition: Portion of the brain and spinal cord consisting mainly of myelinated axons (see myelination) and glial cells.

13785.title: white pulp
13785.definition: Collections of lymphocytes in the spleen, responsible for its immune function.

11381.title: whole embryo culture
11381.definition: Technique, used prior to embryo transfer during in vitro fertilization, in which embryos undergoing organogenesis are maintained in formulated medium outside the body.

15138.title: whole sediment
15138.definition: Sediment and associated interstitial water that have had minimal manipulation.

15137.title: whole-effluent toxicity
15137.definition: Total toxic effect of an effluent measured directly with aquatic organisms in a toxicity test.

08440.title: wideband, alternating-phase, low-power technique for residual splitting
08440.definition: Cluster of pulses applied repeatedly for heteronuclear decoupling.

W06676.title: Wiegner effect
W06676.definition: Synonymous with suspension effect (in an ion-selective electrode).

11382.title: wild type
11382.definition: Of an allele or phenotype, the naturally occurring, unaltered, or most frequent; if several alleles occur, the most frequent one is considered to be the wild type.

12739.title: wild-type receptor
12739.definition: Receptor that occurs naturally in human and other species.

11383.title: Williams syndrome
11383.definition: Congenital disorder with characteristic facies (described as elf-like), short stature, outgoing personality and mild mental retardation; associated with contiguous gene deletions on chromosome 7.

12821.title: Williams–Landel–Ferry equation
12821.definition: Equation describing the temperature dependence of the shift factor, \(a_{T}\), for time–temperature superposition \[\log_{10}a_{\rm{T}} = \frac{-C_{1}(T_{1} - T_{0})}{C_{2} + (T_{1} - T_{0})}\] \(C_{1}\) and \(C_{2}\) are empirical constants, \(T\) is the temperature of measurement, and \(T_{0}\) is the reference temperature.

W06678.title: Wilzbach labelling
W06678.definition: Labelling of a substance by exposing it to tritium gas.

W06679.title: wind rose
W06679.definition: A diagram designed to show the distribution of wind direction experienced at a given location over a considerable period of time. Usually shown in polar coordinates (distance from the origin being proportional to the probability of the wind direction being at the given angle usually measured from the north). Similar diagrams are sometimes used to summarize the average concentrations of a given pollutant seen over a considerable period of time as a function of direction from a given site (sometimes called a pollution rose).

12180.title: Wisconsin card sorting test
12180.definition: Procedure in which cards, depicting different arrangements, numbers, and colors of symbols, are presented to the test subject, who is asked to make the most appropriate match of a test card without further instructions.

13786.title: Wiskott–Aldrich syndrome
13786.definition: Condition characterized by chronic eczema, chronic suppurative otitis media, anemia, and thrombocytopenic purpura (accompanied by bloody diarrhea); it is an immunodeficiency syndrome transmitted as an X-linked recessive trait, in which there is poor antibody response to polysaccharide antigens and dysfunction of cell-mediated immunity.

12181.title: withdrawal
12181.definition: Cessation of exposure to a substance, being characterized by adverse symptoms.

12182.title: withdrawal effect
12182.definition: Adverse event following withdrawal from a person or animal of a drug to which they have been chronically exposed or on which they have become dependent.

11384.title: Wnt
11384.definition: Family of genes important in development, the proteins they encode, or the signal transduction pathways they determine.

12183.title: Wolfgram protein
12183.definition: Acidic proteolipid protein component of central nervous systemmyelin.

WT07499.title: wolfram lamp
WT07499.definition: Incandescent lamp that generates light by passing an electric current through a thin filament wire (usually of wolfram) until it is extremely hot. The lamps are often filled by a halogen gas such as iodine and bromine that allow filaments to work at higher temperatures and higher efficiencies.

W06681.title: Wood horn
W06681.definition: A mechanical device that acts by absorption as a perfect photon trap.

W06682.title: Wood lamp
W06682.definition: Term used to describe a low-pressure mercury arc possessing a fluorescing layer, which emits in the UV-A region (from \(315\) to \(400\ \rm{nm}\)).

08879.title: work function
08879.definition: Minimum thermodynamic work (energy) needed to remove an electron from a solid to a point in the vacuum nearby the solid surface.\[\mathit{\Phi} = -e{\mathit{\Psi}} - \mu\]where \(e\) is the elementary charge (\(-e\) is charge of electron), \(\mathit{\Psi}\) is the electric potential nearby the surface and \(\mu\) is the energy of Fermi level.

W06685.title: work hardening
W06685.definition: Opposite of work softening, in which shear results in a permanent increase of viscosity or consistency with time.

W06687.title: work of adhesion
W06687.definition: The work of adhesion per unit area, \(w_{\rm{A}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }\), is the work done on the system when two condensed phases $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ and $\ce{\upbeta\!}$, forming an interface of unit area are separated reversibly to form unit areas of each of the $\ce{\upalpha\!\updelta\!\mbox{-}}$ and $\ce{\upbeta\!\updelta\!\mbox{-}}$ interfaces. \[w_{\rm{A}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }=\gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }+\gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }- \gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\] where \(\gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B2} }\), \(\gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }\) and \(\gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B2} \unicode[Times]{x3B4} }\) are the surface tensions between two bulk phases $\ce{\upalpha\!}$, $\ce{\upbeta\!}$; $\ce{\upalpha\!}$, $\ce{\updelta\!}$ and $\ce{\upbeta\!}$, $\ce{\updelta\!}$ respectively. The work of adhesion as defined above, and traditionally used, may be called the work of separation.

W06688.title: work of cohesion per unit area
W06688.definition: Of a single pure liquid or solid phase $\ce{\upalpha\!}$, \(w_{\rm{C}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }\) is the work done on the system when a column $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ of unit area is split, reversibly, normal to the axis of the column to form two new surfaces each of unit area in contact with the equilibrium gas phase. \[w_{\rm{C}}^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }=2\ \gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }\] where \(\gamma ^{\unicode[Times]{x3B1} }\) is the surface tension between phase and its equilibrium vapour or a dilute gas phase.

W06689.title: work of immersional wetting per unit area

W06691.title: work softening
W06691.definition: The application of a finite shear to a system after a long rest may result in a decrease of the viscosity or the consistency. If the decrease persists when the shear is discontinued, this behaviour is called work softening (or shear breakdown), whereas if the original viscosity or consistency is recovered this behaviour is called thixotropy.

W06684.title: work
W06684.definition: Scalar product of force, \(\boldsymbol{F}\), and position change, \(\rm{d}\boldsymbol{r}\), \(w = \int \boldsymbol{F}\cdot \rm{d}\mathbf{r}\).

11534.title: workflow
11534.definition: The sequence of steps used to perform a certain task.

W06686.title: working electrode
W06686.definition: An electrode that serves as a transducer responding to the excitation signal and the concentration of the substance of interest in the solution being investigated, and that permits the flow of current sufficiently large to effect appreciable changes of bulk composition within the ordinary duration of a measurement.

10029.title: working examination standard
10029.definition: Examination standard that is used routinely to calibrate or verify examining systems.

08051.title: working interval
08051.definition: Set of quantity values over which a measuring instrument or measuring system provides measurement results with acceptable measurement uncertainty under defined conditions.

09082.title: working potential range
09082.definition: Range of electrode potentials of a given working electrode in a given electrolyte, where the electric current from reactions of the electrode or electrolyte is negligible compared with the current from reactions of the system under investigation.

08303.title: working range
08303.definition: Range of absorbance or intensity which a spectrometer can measure with accuracy and precision.

16195.title: working zone
16195.definition: Space measuring up to \(\pu{2 m}\) over the level of the floor or platform that contains a worker’s permanent or temporary station.

14202.title: workstation
14202.definition: Programmable device used to automate a single operation (such as liquid handling) on a microplate supplied to the device by a robot (automated stacker system or a robotic manipulator).

W06692.title: worm-like chain
W06692.definition: A hypothetical linear macromolecule consisting of an infinitely thin chain of continuous curvature; the direction of curvature at any point is random. The model describes the whole spectrum of chains with different degrees of chain stiffness from rigid rods to random coils, and is particularly useful for representing stiff chains. In the literature this chain is sometimes referred to as a Porod–Kratky chain. Synonymous with continuously curved chain.

09960.title: wrap-around
09960.definition: Occurrence of second dimension peaks in subsequent elution sequences, caused by second-dimension retention times that exceed the modulation time in comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography.

12184.title: wrist drop
12184.definition: Inability to extend the wrist as a result of peripheral nerve damage, causing drooping of the hand.

12612.title: x-ion
12612.definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{C}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{C-C}\) bond.

11385.title: X chromosome
11385.definition: Chromosome determining female sex in the absence of a Y chromosome.

16196.title: x-disease
16196.definition: Hyperkeratotic disease in cattle following exposure to chlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins, naphthalenes, and related compounds.

11386.title: X-linked
11386.definition: Carried by a gene located on the X chromosome.

13787.title: X-linked agammaglobulinemia
13787.definition: Sex-linked impairment of the ability to produce mature B cells, thus characterized by recurrent infections.

13788.title: X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency
13788.definition: Sex-linked trait carried on the X-chromosome of severe combined immunodeficiency syndrome resulting from nonfunctional B lymphocytes and lack of T lymphocytes and natural killer (NK) lymphocytes, leading to recurrent, persistent, and severe infections.

X06703.title: X-radiation
X06703.definition: Radiation resulting from the interaction of high energy particles or photons with matter.

08766.title: X-ray absorption analysis
08766.definition: Measurement principle of X-ray analysis in which the absorption spectrum is used to measure the number of atoms, species, and other parameters of chemical elements.

08767.title: X-ray absorption edge
08767.definition: Increase in X-ray absorption observed at the energy at which a strongly bound electron is released.

09212.title: X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy
09212.definition: Measurement method to measure the absorption of X-rays at energies near and above (typically several hundred \(\pu{eV}\) greater) an absorption edge, over which fine structure (modulation of the X-ray absorption coefficient) can be detected.

08768.title: X-ray absorption near edge structure
08768.definition: Measurement method of X-ray absorption analysis in which the fine structure of the adsorption spectrum in the range \(\pu{30 eV}\) below to \(\pu{50 eV}\) above the absorption edge is used to measure parameters describing the chemical state, coordination environment, and local geometry distortion for the X-ray absorbing atom.

09213.title: X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy
09213.definition: X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy in the energy region near (within approximately \(\pu{100 eV}\)) an absorption edge.

08769.title: X-ray analysis
08769.definition: Measurement principle in which characteristic X-radiation, produced upon irradiation of a material with elementary particles or photons, is applied to measure amounts of elements in a material.

08770.title: X-ray computed micro-tomography
08770.definition: Measurement method based on the transmission of X-rays to obtain three-dimensional images of a sample.

08771.title: X-ray diffraction analysis
08771.definition: Measurement method using diffraction of X-radiation to obtain the spatial arrangement of atoms in a crystalline sample.

08564.title: X-ray emission spectrum
08564.definition: Spectrum comprising the continuum Bremsstrahlung and the most energetic characteristic spectral lines defined by differences in binding energy between electron energy levels.

X06709.title: X-ray escape peak
X06709.definition: In a gamma or X-ray spectrum, the peak due to the photoelectric effect in the detector and escape, from the sensitive part of the detector, of the X-ray photon emitted as a result of the photoelectric effect.

X06710.title: X-ray fluorescence
X06710.definition: The emission of characteristic X-radiation by an atom as a result of the interaction of electromagnetic radiation with its orbital electrons.

X06711.title: X-ray fluorescence analysis
X06711.definition: A kind of analysis based on the measurement of the energies and intensities of characteristic X-radiation emitted by a test portion during irradiation with electromagnetic radiation.

08772.title: X-ray fluorescence microscopy
08772.definition: Measurement method of X-ray fluorescence to obtain quantitative and spatial information about elements in a sample.

X06714.title: X-ray intensity
X06714.definition: Essentially all X-ray measurements are made by photon counting techniques but the results are seldom converted to radiant flux or irradiance or radiant exposure. The term photon flux would be appropriate if the measurements were corrected for detector efficiency but this is seldom done for X-ray chemical analysis. Therefore the term X-ray intensity, \(I\), is commonly used and expressed as photons/unit time detected. Likewise the term relative X-ray intensity, \(I_{\rm{r}}\), is used to mean the intensity for the analyte in an unknown specimen divided by the intensity for a known concentration of the analyte element.

09442.title: X-ray jump ratio
09442.definition: X-ray absorption coefficient at an energy just above an absorption edge divided by that at an energy just below the edge.

X06715.title: X-ray level
X06715.definition: An electronic state occuring as the initial or final state of a process involving the absorption or emission of X-ray radiation. It represents a many-electron state which, in the purely atomic case, has total angular momentum (\(J = L + S\)) as a well defined quantum number.

09303.title: X-ray linewidth
09303.definition: Energy width of the principal characteristic X-ray line.

09520.title: X-ray lithography
09520.definition: Lithography performed by exposing a resist to X-radiation through an image mask.

09304.title: X-ray monochromator
09304.definition: Device used to eliminate photons of energies other than those in a narrow energy or wavelength band.

X06716.title: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy
X06716.definition: Any technique in which the sample is bombarded with X-rays and photoelectrons produced by the sample are detected as a function of energy. ESCA (Electron Spectroscopy for Chemical Analysis) refers to the use of this technique to identify elements, their concentrations, and their chemical state within the sample.

09214.title: X-ray reflectometry
09214.definition: Measurement method for surface and interface roughness and density, layer thickness of thin layers, and electron density profile achieved by reflecting X-rays from a flat sample and analysing the reflected intensity as a function of angle.

09569.title: X-ray resist
09569.definition: Resist optimized for use under X-ray irradiation.

X06717.title: X-ray satellite
X06717.definition: A weak line in the same energy region as a normal X-ray line. Another name used for weak features is non-diagram line. Recommendations as to the use of these two terms have conflicted. Using the term diagram line as defined here, non-diagram line may well be used for all lines with a different origin. The majority of these lines originate form the dipole-allowed de-excitation of multiply ionized or excited states, and are called multiple-ionization satellites. A line where the initial state has two vacencies in the same shell, notably the K-shell, is called a hypersatellite. Other mechanisms leading to weak spectral features in X-ray emission are, e.g. resonance emission, the radiative Auger effect, magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole transitions and, in metals, plasmon excitation. Atoms with open electron shells, i.e. transition metals, lanthanides and actinides, show a splitting of certain X-ray lines due to the electron interaction involving this open shell. Structures originating in all these ways as well as structures in the valence band of molecules and solid chemical compounds have in the past been given satellite designations.

X06718.title: X-ray spectroscopy
X06718.definition: X-ray spectroscopy consists of three steps: (a) excitation to produce emission lines characteristic of the elements in the material, (b) measurement of their intensity, and (c) conversion of X-ray intensity to concentration by a calibration procedure which may include correction for matrix effects.

09215.title: X-ray standing waves
09215.definition: Measurement method based on the interference of X-rays that occurs near the Bragg condition at the surface of a crystalline solid, which leads to intensity maxima in yields of photoelectrons as the Bragg condition is scanned by tilting the sample.

X06695.title: xanthene dyes
X06695.definition: Dyes derived by condensation of phthalic anhydride with resorcinol (and derivatives) or m-aminophenol (and derivatives), of which fluorescein is the prototype (all such dyes have the xanthene nucleus).

X06696.title: xanthic acids
X06696.definition: Compounds having the structure $\ce{ROC(=S)SH}$. Thus O-esters of dithiocarbonic acid. Salts and esters of xanthic acid are 'xanthates'. Use of this term is not recommended.

X06697.title: xanthophylls
X06697.definition: A subclass of carotenoids consisting of the oxygenated carotenes.

XT06755.title: xenobiotic
XT06755.definition: A xenobiotic (Greek, xenos 'foreign'; bios 'life') is a compound that is foreign to a living organism. Principal xenobiotics include: drugs; carcinogens; and various compounds that have been introduced into the environment by artificial means.

13790.title: xenograft
13790.definition: Tissue or organ graft between individuals of different species.

X06699.title: xenon lamp
X06699.definition: An intense source of ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared light produced by electrical discharge in xenon under high pressure.

13791.title: xenophagy
13791.definition: Autophagy selective for degradation of intracellular bacteria and viruses.

X06700.title: xerogel
X06700.definition: Open network formed by the removal of all swelling agents from a gel.

X06693.title: ξ-
X06693.definition: A symbol used to denote unknown configuration at a chiral centre.

12613.title: y-ion
12613.definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{C}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{C-N}\) bond.

YT07500.title: Yang photocyclization
YT07500.definition: Intramolecular coupling of diradicals of different sizes (1,4-, 1,5-, 1,6-, 1,7-, 1,8-diradicals, as well as very remote diradicals) formed through intramolecular hydrogen abstraction by an excited ketone, yielding cyclic alcohols of different sizes.

Y06723.title: year
Y06723.definition: Non-SI unit of time, \(\rm{a}=31\ 556\ 952\ \rm{s}\). The year is not commensurable with the day and not a constant. The value given corresponds to the Gregorian calendar year (\(\rm{a}=365.2425\ \rm{d}\)).

09733.title: yeast artificial chromosome
09733.definition: Vector used to clone large deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) fragments.

Y06724.title: yield
Y06724.definition: Ratio expressing the efficiency of a mass conversion process. The yield coefficient is defined as the amount of cell mass (\(\pu{kg}\)) or product formed (\(\pu{kg}\),\(\pu{mol}\)) related to the consumed substrate (carbon or nitrogen source or oxygen in \(\pu{kg}\) or \(\pu{moles}\)) or to the intracellular ATP production (\(\pu{moles}\)).

Y06727.title: yield stress
Y06727.definition: The shear stress \(\sigma _{0}\) or \(\tau _{0}\) at which yielding starts abruptly. Its value depends on the criterion used to determine when yielding occurs.

Y06728.title: ylides
Y06728.definition: Compounds in which an anionic site $\ce{Y^{−}}$ (originally on carbon, but now including other atoms) is attached directly to a heteroatom $\ce{X^{+}}$ (usually nitrogen, phosphorus or sulfur) carrying a formal positive charge. They are thus 1,2-dipolar species of the type $\ce{R_{m}X^{+}–Y^{−}R^{n}}$. If $\ce{X}$ is a saturated atom of an element from the first row of the periodic system, the ylide is commonly represented by a charge-separated form; if $\ce{X}$ is a second, third, etc. row element uncharged canonical forms are available $\ce{R_{m}X=YR_{n}}$. If $\ce{X}$ is an unsaturated atom, doubly bonded to another first row element $\ce{Z}$, the negative charge on $\ce{Y}$ may be stabilized by $\ce{\uppi\!\mbox{-}}$conjugation, $\ce{Z=X^{+}–Y^{−}Rn  Z^{−}–X^{+}=YR_{n}}$. Such ylides belong to the class 1,3 dipolar compounds. However, 1,3-dipolar compounds with only sextet-containing canonical forms (e.g. vinylcarbenes) are not ylides. E.g. $\ce{Ph3P^{+}–C^{−}H2  Ph3P^{+}=CH2}$ (often called a Wittig reagent), $\ce{(CH3)3N^{+}–C^{−}H2}$, $\ce{RC#N^{+}N^{−}–R}$, $\ce{(CH3)2S=CHPh  (CH3)2S^{+}–C^{−}HPh}$. Note that ylide is a complete word, not to be confused with the suffix -ylide, used for some radical anions. Subclasses of ylides: Ylides $\ce{R_{m}X^{+}–C^{−}R2}$ having the negative charge on carbon are classified by citing the name of the element $\ce{X}$ before the word ylide. E.g. nitrogen ylide, phosphorus ylide, oxygen ylide, sulfur ylide. A further specification may be achieved by citing the class name of $\ce{R_{m}X}$ before the word ylide. Thus nitrogen ylides include amine ylides, $\ce{R3N^{+}–C^{−}R2}$, azomethine ylides $\ce{R2C=N^{+}R–C^{−}R2}$, nitrile ylides, $\ce{RC#N^{+}–C^{−}R2}$. Some authors, who wish to express the positive charge on $\ce{X}$, prefer e.g. ammonium ylides over amine ylides; such usage varies according to the heteroatom $\ce{X}$ and to national custom. The ylides $\ce{R_{m}X^{+}–Y^{−}  R_{m}X=Y}$ ($\ce{Y} = \ce{O}, \ce{S}, \ce{Se}, \ce{Te}, \ce{NR}$) are usually named by citing the name of $\ce{R_{m}X}$ followed by the additive nomenclature term for $\ce{Y}$ (oxide, sulfide, selenide, telluride, imide, respectively). E.g. amine imides; use of the less systematic synonyms amine imines and aminimines is discouraged. Some classes of ylides are known by trivial names e.g. nitrones, Wittig reagents (synonymous with phosphonium ylides).

Y06729.title: ynamines
Y06729.definition: N,N-Disubstituted alk-1-yn-1-amines, $\ce{RC#CNR2}$. By usage, restricted to this type of acetylenic amine.

11388.title: yolk
11388.definition: Nutritive material stored in the ovum for the nourishment of the embryo.

11389.title: yolk sac
11389.definition: Fluid-filled, membrane-bound pouch on the ventral side of the early embryo that provides nourishment until the circulatory system develops.

11390.title: yolk stalk
11390.definition: Narrow tubular support that connects the yolk sac to the middle of the digestive tract of an embryo.

08140.title: Youden plot
08140.definition: Graphical technique for evaluating an interlaboratory comparison when each participant has made two measurements on the same sample or one measurement on each of two different samples.Figure 1: Youden plot of the \(z\) scores of samples #9 and #10 of Round 5 of U39 of the proficiency testing program held by the RCPA Australia for the analysis of creatinine in urine by 218 laboratories. (Reproduced with permission).

Y06734.title: Yukawa–Tsuno equation
Y06734.definition: A multiparameter extension of the Hammett equation to quantify the role of enhanced resonance effect on the reactivity of meta- and para-substituted benzene derivatives, e.g. \[\log _{10}k = \log _{10}k_{0}+\rho \ [\sigma +r\ (\sigma^{+}-\sigma)]\] The parameter \(r\) gives the enhanced resonance effect on the scale (\(\sigma ^{+}\,-\sigma\)) or (\(\sigma\,-\sigma \)), respectively.

12614.title: z-ion
12614.definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{C}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{N-C}\) bond.

14203.title: Z factor
14203.definition: Dimensionless statistical parameter that provides a practical assessment of assay performance in the presence of test compounds. \[Z = 1 - 3(\sigma_{\rm{s}} + \sigma_{\rm{c}})/\vert\mu_{\rm{s}} - \mu_{\rm{c}}\vert\] where \(\mu_{\rm{s}}\) denotes the mean of the library sample signal, \(\mu_{\rm{c}}\) the mean of the control signal and \(\sigma_{\rm{s}}\), \(\sigma_{\rm{c}}\) the corresponding standard deviations. \(1 \gt Z \ge 0.5\) generally categorizes an excellent assay.

12218.title: z-average molar mass
12218.definition:
The equation for z-average molar mass is \[M_{\rm{z}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{M} w_{M}M^{2}}{\sum\limits_{M} w_{M}M}\]
The equation for z-average molecular weight is \[M_{\rm{r,z}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}}M_{\rm{r}}^{2}}{\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}}M_{\rm{r}}}\]

14294.title: z-average particle diameter
14294.definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[\left\langle d_{\rm{z}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{z}} = \frac{\Sigma N_{i} d_{i}^{5}}{\Sigma N_{i}d_{i}^{4}}\]

Z06737.title: Z-value
Z06737.definition: An index of the ionizing power of a solvent based on the frequency of the longest wavelength electronic absorption maximum of 1-ethyl-4-methoxycarbonylpyridinium iodide in the solvent. The Z-value is defined by: \[Z = \frac{\pu{2.859E4}}{\lambda}\] where \(Z\) is in \(\pu{kcal mol-1}\) and \(\lambda \) is in \(\pu{nm}\).

14204.title: Z′ factor
14204.definition:
Dimensionless statistical parameter used extensively in biomolecular screening, and a characteristic of an assay without the intervention of test compounds. It provides a practical index of the quality and reliability of the assay, and can be used as a guide to assay development and optimization. \[Z' = 1 - 3(\sigma_{\rm{c^{+}}} + \sigma_{\rm{c^{-}}})/(\vert\mu_{\rm{c^{+}}} - \mu_{\rm{c^{-}}}\vert)\] where \(\sigma_{\rm{c^{+}}}\) and \(\sigma_{\rm{c^{-}}}\) are the standard deviations of the high and low controls and \(\mu_{\rm{c^{+}}}\) and \(\mu_{\rm{c^{-}}}\) are the means of the high and low controls, respectively.
A graphical illustration of the parameters used in the calculation of \(Z'\) is provided below.

ZT07501.title: $\pu{\rm{Z}_{50}}$
ZT07501.definition: Number of cycles required to reduce by 50% the initial absorbance of the coloured form of a photochromic compound at a specific wavelength.

12185.title: zebrafish
12185.definition: Tropical fish (Danio rerio) about \(\pu{4 cm}\) long, commonly used as a model organism in developmental biology.

Z06739.title: Zeeman effect
Z06739.definition: The splitting or shift of spectral lines due to the presence of an external magnetic field.

08441.title: Zeeman levels
08441.definition: Energy levels of a nucleus arising from the interaction of its magnetic dipole with an external magnetic field.

ZT07132.title: zero differential overlap approximation
ZT07132.definition: An approach to the systematic neglect of the small-in-value electron repulsion integrals which is used in a number of approximate self-consistent field molecular orbital schemes. It means that all the products of atomic orbitals \(\upchi_{\upmu} \upchi_{\upnu}\) are set to zero and the overlap integral \(\rm{S}_{\upmu\upnu} = \updelta_{\upmu\upnu}\) (where \(\updelta_{\upmu\upnu}\) is the Kronecker delta). The ZDO approximation greatly simplifies the computation of wavefunctions by eliminating many of two-electron integrals. At the ZDO approximation all three- and four-centered integrals vanish.

Z06741.title: zero field splitting
Z06741.definition: The separation of multiplet sublevels in the absence of an external magnetic field.

08304.title: zero filling
08304.definition: Addition of zeros to a free induction decay or interferogram to decrease the frequency or wavenumber spacing between points in the Fourier-transformed spectrum.

08305.title: zero path difference
08305.definition: In a Michelson interferometer or other two-beam interferometer, the position of the moving mirror at which the optical paths are equal.

Z06742.title: zero point
Z06742.definition: Value of the pH of a solution, which in combination with a stated outer reference electrode, gives zero emf from the operational cell.

Z06743.title: zero point of scale
Z06743.definition: The rest point of the properly adjusted balance with no load on the pans and the rider (or chain) in the zero position.

08442.title: zero-field nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
08442.definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in which nuclear magnetic resonance spectra are acquired in an environment carefully screened from magnetic fields, including from the Earth’s field allowing the direct detection of J-spectra in the absence of Zeeman interactions (see Zeeman levels).

14363.title: zero-one behaviour
14363.definition: Limiting behaviour in an emulsion, mini-emulsion, or micro-emulsion polymerization during which the entry of a radical into a particle that contains a growing radical results in termination before significant propagation has occurred.

16197.title: zero-order kinetics
16197.definition: Kinetics of a reaction in which the rate is independent of the concentration(s) of the reactants.

08215.title: zero-point energy
08215.definition: Extent, in consequence of Heisenberg’s Uncertainty Principle, by which a particle or a set of particles has an energy greater than that of the minimum on the potential-energy surface.

Z06744.title: zero–zero absorption or emission
Z06744.definition: A purely electronic transition occurring between the lowest vibrational levels of two electronic states.

13792.title: Zeta chain-associated protein kinase-70 kDa
13792.definition: T-lymphocyte-specific tyrosine kinase involved in T-lymphocyte activation.

Z06747.title: zig-zag projection
Z06747.definition: A stereochemical projection for an acyclic molecule (or portion of a molecule) where the main chain is represented by a zig-zag line in the plane and the substituents are shown above or below the plane.

Z06748.title: Zimm plot
Z06748.definition: A diagrammatic representation of data on scattering from large particles, corresponding to the equation: \[\frac{Kc}{\Delta R (\theta)} = \frac{1}{\bar{M}_{\rm{w}} P(\theta)} + 2\ A_{2}c + \ldots\] and used for the simultaneous evaluation of the mass average molar mass, \(\bar{M}_{\rm{w}}\), the second virial coefficient of the chemical potential, \(A_{2}\), and (usually) the z-average radius of gyration, \(< s^{2} > _{\rm{z}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\); \(c\) is the mass concentration of the solute, \(\Delta R(\theta)\) the excess Rayleigh ratio, and \(P (\theta )\) the particle scattering function that comprises (usually) the z-average radius of gyration. \(K\) depends on the solute, the temperature and the type of radiation employed. Several modifications of the Zimm plot are in frequent use; the most common one uses the excess scattering instead of the excess Rayleigh ratio.

11391.title: zinc finger
11391.definition: Small tertiary protein structure in which parts of the protein, typically with cysteine and histidine residues, link to a divalent zinc ion, forming a loop or 'finger' that attaches proteins to DNA.

11392.title: zona pellucida
11392.definition: Acellular glycoprotein-rich membrane surrounding the mature ovum.

Z06749.title: zone
Z06749.definition: A region in the chromatographic bed where one or more components of the sample are located. The term band may also be used for it.

Z06750.title: zone melting method of preconcentration
Z06750.definition: A technique based on the different solubility of microcomponents in the liquid and solid matrix. It has a limited field of application for the analysis of fusible (and stable) substances.

11548.title: zone pH
11548.definition: pH of the solute zone in pH-zone-refining counter-current chromatography. \[{\rm{pH}}_{\rm{zone}} = \pu{p}K_{\rm{a}} + \log[(K_{\rm{DS}}/K_{\rm{S}}) - 1]\], where \(K_{\rm{DS}}\) is the partition ratio of solute $\ce{S}$ (an indicator for solute hydrophobicity) and \(K_{\rm{S}}\), the dissociation constant of the solute.

15139.title: zooplankton
15139.definition: Small floating or weakly swimming animals that drift with water currents and which, with phytoplankton, make up the planktonic food supply upon which almost all oceanic organisms ultimately depend.

Z06751.title: Zucker–Hammett hypothesis
Z06751.definition: This hypothesis states that, if in an acid catalysed reaction, \(\log _{10}k_{1}\) (first-order rate constant of the reaction) is linear in \(H_{0}\) (Hammett acidity function), water is not involved in the transition state of the rate-controlling step. However, if \(\log _{10}k_{1}\) is linear in \(\log _{10}\left[\rm{H}^{+}\right]\) then water is involved. This has been shown to be incorrect by Hammett himself.

Z06752.title: zwitterions
Z06752.definition: Neutral compounds having formal unit electrical charges of opposite sign. Some chemists restrict the term to compounds with the charges on non-adjacent atoms. Sometimes referred to as inner salts, dipolar ions (a misnomer). E.g. $\ce{H3N^{+}CH2C(=O)O^{−}}$ ammonioacetate (glycine), $\ce{(CH3)3N^{+}–O^{−}}$ trimethylamine oxide.

15427.title: zwitterionic copolymerisation
15427.definition: Copolymerization that is a zwitterionic polymerization.

ZT07228.title: zwitterionic polymer
ZT07228.definition: Ampholytic polymer containing ionic groups of opposite sign, commonly on the same pendant groups.

15428.title: zwitterionic polymerisation
15428.definition: Chain polymerization in which a growing macromolecule bears two ionic chain carriers of opposite signs, at one or both of its ends.

11393.title: zygosis
11393.definition: Sexual union of two cells with fusion of their nuclei.

Z06753.title: zygote
Z06753.definition: The cell obtained as a result of complete or partial fusion of meiotically (cf. meiosis) produced cells.

11394.title: zygote intrafallopian transfer
11394.definition: Introduction of a zygote fertilized in vitro into one of the Fallopian tubes.

13793.title: zymosan
13793.definition: Crude preparation of yeast cell walls, consisting chiefly of polysaccharide, activating the alternative pathway of the complement system in the presence of properdin and used in the immunoassay of this compound.
